units.tr: On the tribute to be exacted from church goods.

units.la: INdicimus, ut omnes Ecclesiæ Regni nostri tertiam partem fructuum fisco dissolvant. Quod Edictum omnes Episcopi consenserunt & subscripserunt.
units.tr: We decree that every church in our kingdom shall pay a third part of its revenues into the royal treasury. This edict all the bishops have agreed to and signed.

units.la: CLOTHARII I. REGIS AUG. DECRETVM De electione & depositione Episcopi.
units.tr: Decree of King Chlothar I Augustus, on the election and deposition of a bishop.

units.la: Tronici facto consensu in Eufronium Presbyterum, ad Regem pergunt, dataq; suggestione respondit Rex: Praeceperam, ut Cato Presbyter illic ordinaretur, & eius est spreta jussio nostra? Responderunt ei: Petivimus eum, sed noluit venire. Haec illis dicentibus, advenit subito Cato Presbyter, deprecans Regem, ut ejecto Cantino Episcopo, ipsum * Arverno juberet institui. Quod Rege inridente, petiit iterum ut Turonis ordinaretur, quod antè desperarat. Cui Rex ait: Ego primum praecepi, ut Turonis te ad Episcopatum consecrarent: sed quantum audio, despectui habuisti Ecclesiam illam; ideoq; elongaberis à dominatione ejus.
units.tr: When consent had been given to Tronicus for Eufronius the presbyter, they went to the king, and when the matter was put to him the king replied: "Did I not order that Cato the presbyter should be ordained there, and has my command been scorned? They answered him: "We sought him, but he would not come." While they were saying this, Cato the presbyter arrived suddenly, begging the king to eject Bishop Cantinus and to order that he himself be installed at Arverna. The king mocked him, and Cato then asked again that he be ordained at Tours, which he had earlier given up hope of. The king said to him: "I first ordered that they consecrate you as bishop at Tours; but, as I hear, you have held that church in contempt, and so you will be kept far from its authority."

units.la: CHARIBERTI REGIS AUG. DECRETVM De electione & depositione Episcopi.
units.tr: Decree of King Charibert Augustus, concerning the election and deposition of a bishop.

units.la: Apud urbem Sanctonicam Leontius congregatis Provinciae suae Episcopis, Emerium ab Episcopatu depulit, adferens non Canonicè cum fuisse hoc honore donatum. Decretum enim Regis Clotharii habuerat, ut absque Metropolitani consilio benediceretur, qui non erat praesens. Quo ejecto consensum fecere in Heraclium tunc Burdegalensis urbis Presbyterum, quod Regi Chariberto libscriptum propriis manibus per nuncupatum Presbyterum transmiserunt. Qui Regis praesentiam adiens haec effatus est: Salve Rex gloriose: sedes Apostolica eminentiae tuae salutem mittit uberrimam. Cui ille: Numquid, ait, Turonicam adisti urbem, ut Patris illius nobis salutem deferas? Pater, inquit Presbyter, tuus Leontius cum Provincialibus suis salutem tibi mittit, indicans Emerium ejectum ab Episcopatu, pro eo quòd praetermissa Canonum sanctione urbis Sanctonicae Episcopatum ambivit: ideoque consensum ad te direxerunt, ut alius in loco ejus substituatur: quò fiat, ut dum transgressores Canonum regulariter arguuntur, Regni vestri potentia avis prolixioribus propagetur. Haec eo dicente Rex eum à suis conspectibus extrahi jussit, & plausftro spinis suppleto imponi desuper, & in exilium protrudi praecepit, dicens: Putásne quòd non est super quisquam de filiis Chlotharii Regis, qui patris facta custodiat, quòd hi Episcopum, quem ejus voluntas elegit, abs que nostro judicio projecerunt? Et statim directis viris religiosis, Episcopum in loco restituit, dirigens etiam quosdam de Camerarus suis, qui exactis à Leontio Episcopo mille aureis, reliquos juxta possibilitatem condemnarent Episcopos.
units.tr: At the city of Saintes, Leontius, having gathered the bishops of his province, drove Emerius from the episcopate, alleging that he had not been granted this office canonically. For he had a decree of King Clotharius that he be blessed without the counsel of the metropolitan, who was not present. With him removed, they agreed upon Heraclius, then presbyter of the city of Bordeaux, and sent him to King Charibert in writing, delivered by their own hands through a presbyter named for the purpose. This presbyter, coming into the king's presence, spoke thus: "Greetings, glorious King: the Apostolic See sends your eminence its most abundant salutation." To which he replied: "Have you, then, gone to the city of Tours, so as to bring us greetings from that father of yours?" "Father," said the presbyter, "your Leontius, with his provincial bishops, sends you greeting, informing you that Emerius has been ejected from the episcopate, because, passing over the sanction of the canons, he sought the bishopric of the city of Saintes; and therefore they have sent their consent to you, that another be substituted in his place. Thus it will come about that, while transgressors of the canons are duly called to account, the power of your kingdom will be spread more widely over the lands." While he was speaking thus, the king ordered him to be taken out of his sight, and, a cart having been filled with thorns, he commanded that he be placed upon it and thrust into exile, saying: "Do you suppose that there is no one among the sons of King Clotharius who would keep his father's acts, since these men have cast out a bishop whom his will chose, without our judgment?" And at once, having sent religious men, he restored the bishop to his place, also sending some of his chamberlains, who, having exacted a thousand gold pieces from Bishop Leontius, were to condemn the remaining bishops according to their means.

units.la: CHILPERICI REGIS AUGUSTI MANDATUM DE ASYLIS.
units.tr: The Mandate of King Chilperic Augustus concerning Asylums.

units.la: Chilpericus Rex Francorum Gregorio Turonensis Ecclesiae Archiepiscopo salutem. Merovcum filium meum, qui contra fas legemq; Canonicam, uxorem patrui sui accepit, & relicto sacro Presbyterali ordine apostatans in beati Martini templum confugit, ejice de sancta Basilica: sin autem aliud, totam regionem illam igni succendam.
units.tr: Chilperic, King of the Franks, to Gregory, Archbishop of the Church of Tours, greeting. Eject from the holy basilica my son Merovech, who, against divine law and canon law, has taken his uncle's wife, and who, abandoning the sacred presbyteral order as an apostate, has fled into the temple of blessed Martin. But if you do not, I will set that whole region on fire.

units.la: EIVSDEM LEX CANONICA.
units.tr: The Canon Law of the same.

units.la: Episcopus in homicidio, adulterio, & perjurio deprehensus, à sacerdotio divellatur.
units.tr: A bishop caught in homicide, adultery, or perjury shall be stripped of the priesthood.

units.la: EIVSDEM DECRETVM IN ECCLESIASTICOS BENEFICIARIOS.
units.tr: The Decree of the same concerning ecclesiastical beneficiaries.

units.la: Chilpericus Rex de pauperibus & junioribus Ecclesiae vel Basilicae bannos iussit exigi, pro eo quòd in exercitu non ambulantes, nec exsolvissent publicam functionem.
units.tr: King Chilperic ordered that fines (bannus) be exacted from the poor and younger men of the Church or basilica, because they did not go on campaign and had not paid the public service.

units.la: EIVSDEM STATVTVM DE DESCRIPTIO- NIBUS CENSUUM FISCALIUM.
units.tr: The Statute of the same concerning the assessments of fiscal dues.

units.la: Statuimus, ut possessor de propria terra unam amphoram vini per aripennem reddat. Similiter tam de reliquis terris, quàm de mancipiis, functiones publicae exigantur.
units.tr: We ordain that a possessor shall render one amphora of wine per arpent from his own land. Likewise, public dues shall be exacted both from the remaining lands and from slaves.

units.la: EIVSDEM INDICVLVS DE SVMMA TRINITATE.
units.tr: The Little Edict of the same concerning the Supreme Trinity.

units.la: Sancta Trinitas non in personarum distinctione, sed tantum Deus nominetur. Indignum enim est, ut Deus petiona, licut homo carneus, nominetur. Ipse enim est Pater, qui est Filius: idemque ipse est Spiritus sanctus, qui Pater & Filius. Sic Prophetis & Patriarchis apparuit: sicut ipsa Lex nunciavit. Et hic volumus ut Archiepiscopi, Episcopi & reliqui Doctores Ecclesiarum credant ac doceant.
units.tr: The Holy Trinity is not to be named with a distinction of persons, but simply as God. For it is unworthy that God be named a person, as a fleshly man is. For he is the Father who is the Son, and the same is the Holy Spirit, who is both Father and Son. Thus he appeared to the prophets and patriarchs, as the Law itself declared. And here we wish that the archbishops, bishops and the other teachers of the Churches believe and teach this.

units.la: EIVSDEM EDICTVM DE LITERIS ALPHABETO ADDENDIS.
units.tr: The Edict of the same concerning letters to be added to the alphabet.

units.la: ADDIDIT literas literis nostris, id est Ω, sicut Graeci habent, ae, the, vuui: quarum characteres subscripsimus. hi sunt; O. Ψ. Z. Π. Et misit Epistolas in universas Civitates Regni sui, ut sic pueri docerentur, ac libri antiquitus scripti, planati pumice rescriberentur.
units.tr: He added letters to our alphabet: namely Ω, as the Greeks have it, ae, the, and wi, whose shapes we have written below. These are: O, Ψ, Z, Π. And he sent letters to all the cities of his kingdom, so that boys might be taught in this way, and books written long ago be rewritten on parchment smoothed with pumice.

units.la: EIVSDEM SANCTIO CONTRA RE- giorum mandatorum contemptores.
units.tr: The Sanction of the same against despisers of royal mandates.

units.la: SI quis Judicum praecepta nostra, quae ad eos pro nostris utilitatibus dirigimus, contempserit, oculorum avulsione multetur.
units.tr: If anyone among the judges despises our precepts, which we send to them for our advantage, let him be punished by the tearing out of his eyes.

units.la: EIVSDEM REVOCATIONES IN OFFICIO- farum donationum Episcopis & Ecclesiis factarum.
units.tr: The Revocations of the same, of offices and gifts made to bishops and churches.

units.la: ECCE pauper remansit fiscus noster, ecce divitiae nostrae ad Ecclesias sunt translatae. Nulli penitus, nisi soli Episcopi, regnant. Periit honor noster, & translatus est ad Episcopos Civitatum. Haec agens assidue, testamenta, quae in Ecclesiis conscripta erant, plerumque diruptit, ipsaque patris sui praeceptiones saepe calcavit.
units.tr: Behold, our treasury has been left poor; behold, our riches have been transferred to the churches. No one at all reigns except the bishops alone. Our honour has perished and been transferred to the bishops of the cities. In doing this continually, he often tore up the wills that had been drawn up in the churches, and often trampled underfoot the precepts of his own father.

units.la: GUNTHCRAMNI REGIS AU- GUSTI SANCTIO IN PAR- RICIDAS REGUM.
units.tr: The decree of King Guntram Augustus against the murderers of kings.

units.la: GUNTHCRAMNUS Rex iuravit omnibus Optimatibus, quod non modo ipsum Eberulfum Cubicularium, Chilperici Regis fratris sui interfectorem, verum etiam progeniem eius in novam generationem deleret, ut per horum necem consuetudo auferretur iniqua, ne Reges amplius interficerentur. Factum Parisiis in Conventu Principum tam Ecclesiasticorum quam Secularium.
units.tr: King Guntram swore to all the nobles that he would destroy not only Eberulf the chamberlain, the murderer of his brother King Chilperic, but also his offspring to the new generation, so that by the killing of these men an unjust custom might be abolished, namely that kings should be murdered. This was done at Paris, in the assembly of princes, both ecclesiastical and secular.

units.la: EIVSDEM MANDATVM IN ECc- lesiasticos heribannitos.
units.tr: The same king's mandate concerning ecclesiastics who failed to answer the military summons.

units.la: DICTUM a Rege datum est, ut qui in expeditione contra hostem tardi fuerint, a Judicibus damnarentur. Sed & Episcopi, & ipsi homines Ecclesiastici precia dissolverent pro eo, quod Regis imperium neglexerint.
units.tr: The king issued a ruling that those who were slow to join an expedition against the enemy should be condemned by the judges. But the bishops and the ecclesiastics themselves were also to pay fines for having neglected the king's command.

units.la: EIVSDEM DECRETVM DE CRASSATIONIBVS MILITVM.
units.tr: The same king's decree concerning the misdeeds of soldiers.

units.la: GUNTHCRAMNUS Rex convocatis Episcopis & Maioribus laicorum ad Basilicam S. Symphoriani Martyris, Duces atque Comites discutere coepit super sceleribus per viam, homicidiis, praedis, direptionibus per regionem gestis, & segetibus provinciae igni succensis, dicens: Qualiter nos hoc tempore victoriam obtinere possumus, qui ea, quae patres nostri consecuti sunt, non custodimus? Illi vero ecclesias aedificantes, in Deum spem omnem ponentes, Martyres honorantes, Sacerdotes venerantes, victorias obtinuerunt, gentesque adversas divino opitulante adiutorio, ensis & parma saepius subdiderunt. Nos vero non solum Deum non metuimus, verumetiam sacra eius vastamus, Ministros interficimus, ipsa quoque Sanctorum pignera in ridiculo disccerpinus ac vastamus. Non enim potest obtineri victoria, ubi talia perpetrantur. Ideo manus nostrae sunt invalidae, ensis tepescit, nec clypeus nos, ut erat solitus, defendit ac protegit. Ergo si hoc meae culpae adscribitur, iam id Deus capiti meo restituat. Certe si vos Regalia iussa contemnitis, & ea, quae praecipio, implere differtis, iam debet securis capiti vestro submergi. Erit enim documentum omni exercitui, cum unus de Prioribus fuerit interfectus: verumtamen iam experiri debemus, quid agi oporteat. Si quis iustitiam sequi destinat, iam sequatur. Si quis contemnit, iam ultio publica cervici eius imminet. Satius est enim, ut pauci contumaces pereant, quam ira Dei super omnem regionem dependat innoxiam.
units.tr: King Guntram, having summoned the bishops and the chief laymen to the basilica of the martyr St Symphorian, began to examine the dukes and counts about the crimes committed throughout the region along the roads, the murders, plunderings and robberies, and the fields of the province set on fire. He said: "How can we obtain victory at this time, when we do not keep what our fathers obtained? They, building churches, placing all their hope in God, honouring the martyrs and venerating the priests, obtained victories, and with the help of God's aid they often subjected hostile nations to the sword and shield. But we not only do not fear God; we also lay waste his sacred places, we kill the ministers, and we tear apart and waste the very relics of the saints as a mockery. Victory cannot be obtained where such things are committed. For this reason our hands are weakened, the sword grows cold, and the shield no longer defends and protects us as it used to. So if this is ascribed to my fault, may God now restore it to my own head. Certainly, if you despise my royal commands and delay in carrying out what I order, then the axe should now be buried in your heads. For it will be a lesson to the whole army when one of the leaders is killed. Yet now we must test what ought to be done. If anyone intends to follow justice, let him follow it now. If anyone scorns it, public vengeance now hangs over his neck. For it is better that a few stubborn men perish than that the wrath of God fall upon the whole innocent region."

units.la: 2. Haec Rege dicente, responderunt Duces: Bonitatis tuae magnanimitas, Rex optime, narrari facile non potest: qui timor tibi in Deum sit, qui amor in ecclesias, quae reverentia in Sacerdotes, quae pietas in pauperes, quaeve dispensatio in egenos: sed quia omnia, quae gloria vestra profert, rebus vestraque esse censentur. Quid faciemus, quod populus omnis in vitia est dilapsus? Omnemque hominem agere, quae sunt iniqua, delectat, nullus regem metuit; nullus Ducem, nullus comitem reveretur. Et si fortasse alicui ista displicent, & ea pro longaevitate vitae vestrae emendare conatur, statim sed in populo, statim tumultus exoritur, & in tantum unusquisque contra Seniorem saeva incentione grassatur, ut vix se credat evadere, si tandem silere nequiverit.
units.tr: 2. When the king had said this, the dukes replied: "The greatness of your goodness, best of kings, cannot easily be described: what fear of God you have, what love for the churches, what reverence for the priests, what piety towards the poor, and what generosity towards the needy. But since everything that your glory produces is considered to belong to your affairs and property, what shall we do, when the whole people has slipped into vice? Every man delights in doing what is wicked; no one fears the king, no one respects the duke or the count. And if perhaps someone is displeased by these things and tries to correct them for the sake of your long life, at once a tumult arises among the people, and everyone rages so savagely against his elder that he hardly believes he can escape, if at last he cannot keep silent."

units.la: 3. Ad haec Rex ait: Si quis sequitur iustitiam, vivat: si quis legem mandatumque nostrum respuit, iam percat, ne nos diutius hoc blasphemium prosequatur.
units.tr: 3. To this the king said: "If anyone follows justice, let him live; if anyone rejects our law and command, let him now perish, so that this blasphemy does not go on any longer against us."

units.la: GUNTHERAMNI, ET CHILDE- BERTI II. REGUM, ET BRU- NICHILDIS Reginæ Francorum CONSTITUTUM PACTIONIS DE PACE PVBLICA, IN Comitiis Andelavensibus sanctitum.
units.tr: Agreement concerning public peace between the kings Guntram and Childebert II and Brunhild, queen of the Franks, sanctioned at the assembly of Andelau.

units.la: CUm in Christi nomine præcellentissimi Domini GUNTHERAMNUS, & CHILDEBERTUS Reges, & gloriosissima Domna BRUNICHILDIS Regina, * Andelaum charitatis studio convenissent, ut omnia, quæ undecunque inter ipsos scandalum poterant generare, plenori consilio definirent: id inter eos mediantibus Sacerdotibus atq; Proceribus, Deo medio, charitatis studio sedit, complacuit, atque convenit, ut quamdiu eos Deus omnipotens in præsenti sæculo superesse voluerit, fidem & charitatem puram, & simplicem, sibi debeant conservare.
units.tr: When the most excellent lords Guntram and Childebert, kings, and the most glorious lady Brunhild, queen, had met at Andelau, out of zeal for charity, to settle with full deliberation all the matters that could give rise to offence between them, it was agreed, pleased, and resolved between them, with the mediation of the bishops and nobles and with God as mediator, out of zeal for charity, that as long as Almighty God wills them to survive in this present age, they shall keep faith and charity between them, pure and sincere.

units.la: 2. Similiter quia Dominus GUNTHERAMNUS iuxta pactionem, quam cum bonæ memoriæ Domno Sygiberto inierat, integram portionem, quæ est de regno Chariberti, illis fuerat consecutus, sibi diceret in integrum redhibeti, & pars Domni Childeberti, ea quæ pater suus possederat, ad se vellet ex omnibus revocare, id inter ipsos constat fixa deliberatione finitum, ut in illam tertiam portionem de Parisiensi civitate cum terminis & populo suo, quæ ad Domnum Sygibertum de regno Chariberti conscripta Pactione pervenerat, cum castellis Duno & Vindocino, & quicquid de pago Stampensi, vel Carzoteno in pervio illo antefactus Rex cum terminis & populo suo perceperat, in iure & dominatione Domni GUNTHERAMNI, cum eo quod superstite Domno Sygiberto de regno Chariberti antea tenuit, debeant perpetualiter permanere: pari conditione civitates Meldonenses, & duas portiones de Silvanectis, Turonos, Pictavos, Abrincatas, vicum Julienfem cum Sorannis, Lapurdo & Albige, Domnus Childebertus Rex cum terminis à præsenti die suæ vindicet potestati. Ea igitur conditione servata, ut quem Deus de ipsis Regibus superstitem esse præceperit, regnum illius, qui absque filiis de præsentis sæculi luce migraverit, ad se integritatem iure perpetuo debeat revocare, & posteris suis, Domino auxiliante, relinquere.
units.tr: 2. Likewise, since Lord Guntram, under the agreement he had made with the late Lord Sigibert, had obtained the whole portion of Charibert's kingdom that fell to them, and claimed that it should be restored to him in full, and wished to recall from all sources the part of Lord Childebert that his father had possessed, it has been settled between them by firm decision that the third portion of the city of Paris, with its boundaries and people, which had come to Lord Sigibert from Charibert's kingdom under the written agreement, together with the castles of Dun and Vendôme, and whatever the aforesaid king had taken in the district of Étampes or Carzoten, in that passage, with its boundaries and people, shall remain perpetually in the right and lordship of Lord Guntram, together with what he held before from Charibert's kingdom while Lord Sigibert was alive. On the same condition, Lord King Childebert shall claim for his own power, from this day, the cities of Meaux, two portions of Senlis, Tours, Poitiers, Avranches, the vicus of Jublains with Sorans, Lapurdum, and Albi. This condition being observed: whomever God shall ordain to survive those kings, he shall with perpetual right recall to himself the entire kingdom of whichever of them departs from the light of this present age without sons, and leave it, with the Lord's help, to his own descendants.

units.la: 3. Illud specialiter placuit per omnia inviolabiliter conservari, ut quicquid Domnus Guntheramnus Rex filiæ suæ Chlothieldi contulit, aut adhuc Deo propitiante contulerit, in omnibus rebus atque corporibus, tam in civitatibus, quam agris vel reditibus, in iure & dominatione ipsius debeant permanere: & si quid de agris fiscalibus, vel speciebus atque præsidio pro arbitrii sui voluntate facere, aut quicquam conferre voluerit, in perpetuo auxiliante Domino conservetur, neque à quocumque ullo unquam tempore convellatur, & sub tuitione ac defensione Domni Childeberti, cum his omnibus, quæ ipsam translitus genitoris sui invenerit possidentem, sub omni honore & dignitate securâ debeat possidere.
units.tr: 3. It has been especially agreed that the following be kept inviolate in all respects: whatever Lord Guntram the king has bestowed upon his daughter Chlodechild, or shall yet bestow, God being gracious, in all goods and persons, whether in cities, fields, or revenues, shall remain in her right and lordship. And if she wishes to do anything, or to grant anything, from the crown lands, or from the rights and protection, at her own pleasure, it shall be preserved in perpetuity with the Lord's help, and shall never at any time be overturned by anyone; and under the protection and defence of Lord Childebert, she shall hold all that she has found in her possession from her father's time, with all honour and dignity, in safety.

units.la: 4. Pan conditione repromisit Domnus Guntheramnus Rex, ut si, ut habet humana fragilitas, quod divina pietas non permittat, nec ille videre desiderat, si contigerit Domnum Childebertum, eo superstite, de hac luce migrare, filios suos THEODOBERTUM & THEODORICUM Regem, vel ii adhucalios ipsi Deus dare voluerit, ut pius pater sub sua tuitione & defensione recipiat, ita ut regnum patris eorum sub omni solliditate possideant: & genitricem Domni Childeberti, Domnam BRUNICHILDEM Reginam, vel filiam eius Chlodosindam, germanam Domni Childeberti Regis, quandam intra regionem Francorum fuerit, vel eius Reginam Faileubam, ranquam sororem bonam, & filias, in sua tuitione & defensione, spiritali dilectione recipiat, & sub omni honore & dignitate cum omnibus rebus earum, cum civitatibus, agris, reditibus, vel cunctis titulis, & omni corpore facultatus, tam quod præsenti videntur tempore possidere, quam quod adhuc Christo præsule iuste potuerint augmentare, sub omni securitate & quiete possideant: ut si quid de agris fiscalibus vel speciebus atque præsidio pro arbitrii sui voluntate facere, aut cuiquam conferre voluerint, fixa stabilitate in perpetuo conservetur, nec à quibuscunque voluntas illarum ullo tempore convellatur.
units.tr: 4. On this condition, Lord King Guntram promised that if, as human frailty has it (which divine goodness forbid, and which he himself does not wish to see), Lord Childebert should die while Guntram is still alive, he will receive Childebert's sons Theudebert and Theuderic, the kings, or any other children God may wish to give him, as a loving father, under his protection and defence, so that they may hold their father's kingdom in full security. He will also, in spiritual affection, receive under his protection and defence the mother of Lord Childebert, Lady Brunhild the queen, or her daughter Chlodosind, the sister of Lord King Childebert, wherever she may be within the land of the Franks, or his queen Faileuba, as a good sister, and their daughters; and he will let them hold, with all honour and dignity, with all their goods, cities, fields, revenues, and all their titles and every kind of property, both what they seem to hold at present and what they may rightly augment with Christ's help, in full security and peace. And whatever they wish to grant or bestow upon anyone from the crown lands, or from the rights and protection, at their own pleasure, shall be preserved in perpetuity with firm stability, and their will shall never at any time be overturned by anyone.

units.la: 5. De Civitatibus verò, hoc est, Burdegala, Lemonica, Cadurco, Benarno, & Begorra, quas Gaifesuindam germanam Domnæ Brunichildis, tam in dote, quàm in morganegiba, hoc est, matutinali dono, in Franciam venientem certum est adquisisse: quas enim per iudicium gloriosissimi Domni Guntheramni Regis, vel Francorum superstitibus Chilperico & Sygiberto Regibus, Domna Brunichildis noscitur adquisisse: ita convenit, ut Cadurcum civitatem cum terminis & cunctopulo suo, Domna Brunichildis de præsenti in sua proprietate percipiat: reliquas verò civitates ex hac conditione superius nominatas Domnus Guntheramnus, dum advixit, possideat, ita ut quandoque post eius transitum, in dominationem Domnæ Brunichildis hæredumque suorum cum omni solliditate De propiopinio revertantur. Nec superstite Domno Guntheramno, neq; à Domna Brunichilde, neque à filio suo Childeberto Rege, filiisque suis, quolibet ingenio, vel tempore repetantur.
units.tr: 5. As for the cities, namely Bordeaux, Limoges, Cahors, Bigorre, and Bagnères, which it is certain Gailswintha, sister of Lady Brunhild, acquired when she came into Francia, both as dowry and as morgengabe, that is, the morning gift, and which it is known Lady Brunhild acquired by the judgment of the most glorious Lord King Guntram, or while the kings Chilperic and Sigibert were alive: it is agreed that Lady Brunhild shall take the city of Cahors, with its boundaries and all its people, now, into her own property. As for the remaining cities named above under this condition, Lord Guntram shall hold them as long as he lives, so that after his death they shall return, with full security and by their own right, to the lordship of Lady Brunhild and her heirs. While Lord Guntram lives, they shall not be reclaimed, either by Brunhild, or by his son King Childebert, or by his sons, by any device or at any time.

units.la: 6. Similimodo convenit, ut Silvanectum Domnus Childebertus in integritate teneat, & quantum tertia Domni Guntheramni exinde debita competit, de tertia Domni Childeberti, quæ est in Rossoutensi, Domni Guntheramni partibus compensetur.
units.tr: 6. Likewise it is agreed that Lord Childebert shall hold Senlis in full, and that as much of the third of Lord Guntram that is due from it shall be compensated from Lord Childebert's third in Rouxou, on the side of Lord Guntram.

units.la: * Andelaw in Alsatia, olim Civitas Imperialis, nunc sub ditione Ducis Bipontini.
units.tr: * Andelau in Alsace, formerly an imperial city, now under the rule of the Duke of Zweibrücken.

units.la: 7. Simili modo convenit, ut secundum pactiones inter Domnum Guntheramnum & bonæ memoriæ Domnum Sygibertum initas, leudes illi, qui Domno Guntheramno post transitum Domini Chlotharii sacramenta primitus præbuerunt, & si postea cóvincentur se in parte alia tradidisse, de locis, ubi commanere videntur, convenit ut debeant removeri. Similiter & qui post transitum Domni Chlotharii convincuntur Domno Sygiberto sacramenta primitus præbuisse, & se in aliam partem transtulerunt, modo simili removeantur.
units.tr: 7. In the same way it is agreed that, according to the agreements made between Lord Guntram and the late Lord Sigibert, those vassals who first gave their oaths to Lord Guntram after the death of Lord Chlothar, and who, if they are later shown to have transferred themselves to another party, shall be removed from the places where they seem to be staying. Likewise, those who, after the death of Lord Chlothar, are shown to have first given their oaths to Lord Sigibert, and have transferred themselves to another party, shall be removed in the same way.

units.la: 8. Similiter quicquid antefati Reges ecclesiis aut fidelibus suis contulerint, aut adhuc conferre cum iustitia, Deo propitiante, voluerint, stabiliter conservetur, & quicquid unicuique fidelium in utriusque regno per legem & iustitiam redhibetur, nullum ei præjudicium patiatur, sed licet res debitas possidere, atque recipere. Et si aliquid cuiuscunque per interregna sine culpa sublatum est, audientia habita restauretur. Et de eo, quod per munificentias præcedentium Regum unusquisque usque ad transitum gloriosæ memoriæ Domni Chlotharij Regis possedit, cum securitate possideat. Et quod exinde fidelibus personis ablatum est, de præsenti recipiat.
units.tr: 8. Likewise, whatever the aforesaid kings have granted, or shall yet, God being gracious, justly wish to grant, to churches or to their own faithful, shall be firmly preserved; and whatever is restored to anyone of the faithful in either kingdom by law and justice shall suffer no prejudice to him, but he may hold and receive his due goods. And if anything of anyone's was taken away without fault during the interregnum, it shall be restored after a hearing. And what each man held by the bounty of the earlier kings up to the death of the glorious Lord King Chlothar, he shall hold in security. And what has been taken from faithful persons since then, he shall recover at once.

units.la: 9. Et quia inter præfatos Reges pura & simplex est in Dei nomine concordia inligata, convenit ut in utroque regno utriusque fidelibus, tam pro causis publicis quàm privatis, quicunque voluerit ambulare, pervium nullis temporibus denegetur.
units.tr: 9. And since a pure and sincere concord has been bound between the aforesaid kings in the name of God, it is agreed that in either kingdom, the faithful of each, whether for public or private causes, may travel wherever they wish, and passage shall never at any time be denied.

units.la: 10. Similiter convenit, ut nullus alterius leudes nec sollicitet, nec venientes excipiat. Quod si forsitan pro aliqua amissione parte altera crediderit expetendam, juxta qualitate culpæ excusati reddatur.
units.tr: 10. Likewise it is agreed that no one shall entice the vassals of the other, nor receive those who come over. But if at any time one party believes that something of the kind should be demanded for some loss, the offender shall be made to pay according to the degree of his fault.

units.la: 11. Hoc etiam huic addi placuit Pactioni, ut si qua pars præsentia statuta sub quacunque calliditate, tempore quocunque transcenderit, omnia beneficia, tam repromissa, quàm in præsenti collata, amittar, & illi proficiat, qui inviolabiliter omnia suprascripta servaverit: & sit de sacramentorum obligatione in omnibus absoluta.
units.tr: 11. It has also been pleased to add to this agreement that if any party, by whatever trickery, at any time goes beyond the present statutes, it shall lose all benefices, both those promised and those now conferred, and they shall pass to him who has inviolably kept all the things written above; and he shall be absolved from the obligation of his oaths in all matters.

units.la: 12. His itaque omnibus definitis, jurant partes per Dei omnipotentis nomen, & inseparabilem Trinitatem, vel Divina omnia, ac tremendum diem judicii, se omnia, quæ superius scripta sunt, absque ullo dolo malo, vel fraudis ingenio inviolabiliter servaturos.
units.tr: 12. With all these things thus settled, the parties swear by the name of Almighty God and the inseparable Trinity, and by all things divine and the dread day of judgment, that they will inviolably keep everything written above, without any evil deceit or fraudulent contrivance.

units.la: 13. Facta Pactio sub die quarto Kalendis Decembris, anno vicesimo sexto regni Domni GUNTHERAMNI Regis, Domni CHILDEBERTI vero duodecimo anno.
units.tr: 13. The agreement was made on the fourth day before the Kalends of December, in the twenty-sixth year of the reign of Lord Guntram the king, and the twelfth year of Lord Childebert.

units.la: CHILDEBERTI II. REGIS AUGUSTI DECRETVM
units.tr: CHILDEBERT II, KING AUGUSTUS: A DECREE

units.la: De divisione hereditatis inter matrem & filiam.
units.tr: Concerning the division of an inheritance between mother and daughter.

units.la: INIMICITIA orta inter Ingeltrudem, & filiam eius Berthegundem, dum sæpius Regis præsentiam adeunt, & hæc res patris defensare cupiens, hæc verò Berthegundis donationem mni germani sui ostendit, dicens: Quia hæc & hæc mihi germanus meus contulit. Sed mater eius non admittens donationem, omnia sibi vendicare cupiens, misit qui effracta domo ejus, omnes testilius cum hac donatione diriperet. Unde seipsam genitrix reddidit comprobatam, cum de rebus ipsi in sequenti filiæ quædam repetenti districta restituit. Sed cum sæpius Gregorius Turonensis Archiepiscopus & Maroveus Pictavensis Episcopus, acceptis Regalibus epistolis, ut eas pacificare deberent, Berthegundis advenit Turonos. In judicium quoque accedentem cogerunt eam, in quantum potuerunt, rationem sequi: mater verò ejus flecti non potuit. Tunc accensa felle ad Regem abiit, quali filiam exheredem datura de facultate paterna. Ac in præsentia Regis exponens causas, filia absente, judicatum est ei, ut quarta parte filiæ restituta, tres cum nepotibus suis, quos de filio uno habebat, reciperet. Factum Decretum in urbe, quam Stratæburgum vocant.
units.tr: There arose enmity between Ingeltrudis and her daughter Berthegunda, since they repeatedly came into the presence of the King: the daughter, wishing to defend her father's property, showed the gift made to her by her brother, saying: "These and those things were given to me by my brother." But her mother, not accepting the gift and wishing to claim everything for herself, sent men who broke into her house and tore apart all the documents, including this gift. Thus the mother herself was shown to be at fault, since she was compelled to restore some of the goods to her daughter, who was demanding them back. But when Gregory, Archbishop of Tours, and Maroveus, Bishop of Poitiers, had repeatedly received royal letters ordering them to make peace between them, Berthegunda came to Tours. They also compelled her, as far as they could, to come to a hearing and to follow reason; but her mother could not be bent. Then, inflamed with bitterness, she went to the King, as if she intended to disinherit her daughter from her paternal estate. Setting out the case in the King's presence, with the daughter absent, it was judged that the daughter should be restored a quarter, and that the mother should receive back three parts together with her grandchildren, whom she had by one son. The decree was made in the city which they call Strasbourg.

units.la: EIVSDEM SANCTIO DE ASYLIS.
units.tr: The same king's ordinance concerning sanctuaries.

units.la: SEPTIMINA & Droctulfus, qui nutritores erant infantum Regis, delati ad Regem de parricidio in eum & Reginam matrem, atque Reginam conjugem machinato, conscientia terrente, latebrâ intra ecclesiarum sepța petiere. Quibus Rex mandatum misit in hæc verba: Egredimini in judicio ut cognoscamus de his, quæ vobis objiciuntur, si vera sint, an falsa. Nam (ego ut opinor) in hanc ecclesiam fuga dilapsi non fuissetis, nisi vos conscientia terruisset. Verum tamen, pusillonè habete de vita, etiam culpabiles inveniamini. Christiani enim sumus, nefas est enim vel criminosos ab ecclesia eductos punire.
units.tr: Septimina and Droctulfus, who had been nurses of the King's infants, were accused before the King of plotting parricide against him and the Queen mother, and against the Queen his wife. Terrified by their conscience, they sought hiding inside the enclosure of a church. The King sent them an order in these words: "Come out to judgment, so that we may learn whether the things objected to you are true or false. For (I suppose) you would not have fled into this church unless your conscience had terrified you. Yet, take heart concerning your life, even if you are found guilty. For we are Christians, and it is wrong to punish even criminals once they have been led out of the church."

units.la: CAROLI MARTELLI PRINCIPIS FRANCORUM ET PATRITII ROMANORUM EDICTVM
units.tr: EDICT OF CHARLES MARTEL, PRINCE OF THE FRANKS AND PATRICIAN OF THE ROMANS

units.la: De fide publica vel salvo conductu dato, Bonifacio Episcopo Moguntino Legato Sedis Romanæ in Franciam venienti, ea ratione, ut justitiam redderet, & ut similiter justitiam acciperet.
units.tr: Concerning public faith, or a safe-conduct given to Boniface, Bishop of Mainz, legate of the Roman See, coming into France, on the principle that he should render justice and likewise receive it.

units.la: DOMINIS sanctis & Apostolicis in Christo Patribus, Episcopis, Ducibus, Comitibus, Vicariis, Domesticis, seu omnibus Agentibus, Iunioribus nostris, seu Missis decurrentibus, & amicis nostris, Illustris Vir CAROLUS Majordomus, bene cupiens vester. Cognoscatis, qualiter Apostolicus vir in Christo pater Bonifacius Episcopus, Missus Sancti Petri, ad nos venit, & nobis. mihi suggestit, quod sub nostro mundiburdio vel defensione eum recipere deberemus. Quod ita nos gratanti animo fidelitate cognoscite. Proinde nos taliter vi, fecimus eim anum nostram toboratam dare, ut ubique, ubi & ubi ambulare videtur, cum nostro amore vel sub nostro mundiburdio & defensione quietus vel conservatus esse debeat in ea ratione, ut iustitiam reddat, & ut similiter accipiat. Et si quis eiusdem vel necessitas advenerit, quae per legem definiri non poterit, usque ad nos quaeratur, vel conservatus esse debeat, tam ipse, quam qui per ipsum sperare videntur, ut ei nullam ullam ... vel damnationem adversus eum facere non debeat, nisi omni tempore sub nostro mundiburdio vel defensione quietus vel conservatus residere debeat. Et ut certius credatur, manu propria subscripsimus, & de annulo nostro subterfigillavimus.
units.tr: To the lords, the holy and apostolic fathers in Christ, bishops, dukes, counts, vicars, domestics, or all our agents, juniors, or running messengers, and our friends: Charles, the illustrious mayor of the palace, who wishes you well. Know that the apostolic man, the father in Christ Bishop Boniface, sent of Saint Peter, has come to us and has put it to me that we ought to receive him under our protection and defence. You should know that we receive this with a glad mind and in good faith. Accordingly, we have decided, by our authority, to give him our firm letter of protection, so that wherever he seems to go, he may be safe and preserved under our love and under our protection and defence, on the understanding that he renders justice and likewise receives it. And if any need concerning him or those who seem to hope through him should arise, which cannot be settled by law, let it be sought up to us. No one shall do any harm or bring any condemnation against him, but he must always remain safe and preserved under our protection and defence. And so that it may be believed the more surely, we have subscribed with our own hand and sealed beneath with our ring.

units.la: CAROLOMANNI I. FRAN- CORUM PRINCIPIS ET Patricii Romanorum EDICTUM DE REFORMATIONE COLLAPSAE RELIGIONIS Christianae, & adscriptis in Ecclesiastica, & morum Cleri ac populi.
units.tr: Edict of Carloman I, Prince of the Franks and Patrician of the Romans, concerning the reform of the collapsed Christian religion, and of the additions made in the Church, and of the morals of clergy and people.

units.la: IN nomine Domini Dei nostri Iesu Christi. * CAROLOMANNUS Dux & Princeps Francorum: anno a nato Christo Servatore & authore nostro, sepringente tuno quadragesimo secundo, undecimo Calendas Maii: suatu & consilio Sacerdotum Dei Optimi Maximi & amicorum nostrorum, Pontificum Regni nostri, maximos, minores, cum Presbyteris, nimirum Bonifacium Archiepiscopum, Burchardum Reginoldum, Vicanum, Wilevaldum, Dadanum, & Addanum, cum collegis eorum, & sacerdotibus, ut Christiano convocavi, ut mihi consulant, quo pacto iustitia & Christiana devotio instauretur, quae neglegentia & ignavia superiorum Principum labefactata, collapsa, terris depulsa corrunt. Quapropter in populis Christi, a fallis & pravis sacerdotibus hactenus deceptus, & peranfractibus confragosos & devios seductos, ad veritatis sermonem reducantur. Juxta igitur religiosorum Sacerdotum, & Procerum nostrorum consilium rogavimus, iussimus, decrevimus, voluimus, haecque placita praescriptimus.
units.tr: In the name of the Lord our God Jesus Christ. * Carloman, Duke and Prince of the Franks, in the year from the birth of Christ our Saviour and Author 742, on the eleventh day before the Kalends of May, by the advice and counsel of the priests of God Most Good and Greatest and of our friends, the bishops of our kingdom, both greater and lesser, with the elders, namely Boniface the archbishop, Burchard, Reginold, Vicanus, Wilevald, Dadan and Addan, with their colleagues and priests, whom I have summoned in Christ's name, that they might advise me how justice and Christian devotion may be restored, which, through the negligence and sloth of the former princes, have been weakened, have collapsed, and are falling to the ground. Therefore, let the peoples of Christ, hitherto deceived by false and wicked priests, and led astray along winding and rough paths, be brought back to the word of truth. Accordingly, following the counsel of our religious priests and nobles, we have asked, ordered, decreed, willed, and prescribed these decrees.

units.la: 1. Episcopi omnes, quos per civitates designavimus, Bonifacio Archiepiscopo, Nuncio Christi, & Legato Divi Petri, dicto audientes sunto.
units.tr: 1. All the bishops whom we have appointed through the cities shall obey Boniface the archbishop, messenger of Christ and legate of St Peter, as they would obey us.

units.la: 2. Quorannis Concilia celebrentur, in hisce pieratem Christianam, candoremque germanum, a malis Sacerdotibus polluram exparo.
units.tr: 2. Councils shall be held every year, in which Christian piety and genuine purity, polluted by bad priests, shall be cleansed.

units.la: 3. Decimas, bona Ecclesiastica, occupata a prophanis, restituimus.
units.tr: 3. We restore the tithes and church property that have been seized by profane persons.

units.la: 4. Falsi Diaconi, Presbyteri, sacrificuli adulteri, scortatores, sacris opibus nequaquam alantur, quos omnes in ordinem redegimus, atque exauguravimus; ad poenasque pro criminibus luendis compulimus.
units.tr: 4. False deacons, presbyters, adulterous little priests, and fornicators shall in no way be supported from sacred resources. All of them we have reduced to order and deprived of office, and we have compelled them to pay penalties for their crimes.

units.la: 5. Nemo sacris initiatus, divinoque ministerio mancipatus, arma omnino ferat, aut in bellum, aut in hostem pergat. Unus, aut ad tumultum deo Episcopi, delectu suffragio cum suis Sacerdotulis Principem comitentur ac bella sacrificandi comprecandique causa. Cuique tribuno unus duntaxat a sacris, poenitentia & confessionibus esto.
units.tr: 5. No one who has been initiated into sacred orders and bound to the divine ministry shall carry weapons at all, or go to war or against the enemy. One or two bishops, chosen by vote, shall accompany the prince with their little priests to battle, for the purpose of sacrifice and prayer. For each tribune, only one from the sacred ministry shall be there, for penance and confessions.

units.la: 6. Initiati, canes, accipitres, & huiusmodi aves ad venandum nequaquam alunto. Aris & templis deditus, venarus si fuerit, duis devotus esto.
units.tr: 6. Those who are initiated shall by no means keep dogs, hawks, and such birds for hunting. If a man devoted to altars and temples is found hunting, let him be ...

units.la: 7. Quisquis Sacerdos Episcopo suo pareat, in quadragesima rationem suscepti muneris reddat.
units.tr: 7. Every priest shall obey his bishop, and in Lent he shall give an account of the office he has undertaken.

units.la: 8. Ignoti Presbyteri, Episcopi, nisi in conventibus solennibus eruditio eorum, & mores comprobati fuerint, repulsam ferant.
units.tr: 8. Unknown presbyters and bishops, unless their learning and morals have been approved in solemn assemblies, shall receive rejection.

units.la: 9. Quisquis Pontifex dei operam, Praefectus quem Franci Graphionem vocant, summo studio adnitatur, ut incantationes, auguria, fornicationes, & huiusmodi praestigiae impune non habeant; quare etiam auspicio Dei Optimi Maximi Divorumque eius fuit: quos huiusmodi contaminationibus magis ad iracundiam provocari certum est.
units.tr: 9. Whatever bishop, or the prefect whom the Franks call the Graphio, shall strive with the utmost zeal that enchantments, auguries, fornications, and such magic tricks do not go unpunished. For this was also done under the auspices of God Most Good and Greatest and of his saints, since such pollutions are certainly provoking to anger.

units.la: 10. Sacerdos ... ibidemque mancipium in carcere, pane & aqua pastus, poenas luat.
units.tr: 10. The priest ... and the servant there, shall be placed in prison, fed on bread and water, and pay the penalties.

units.la: 11. Hoc quoque, concilium Mystarum & populi Christiani sciunus, ut propter crebra bella, & fe-ractissimarum gentium, quibus undique cingimur, afflictas in nos incursiones, pars Ecclesiasticae pecuniae nempe duodecim denarii, quem solidum vocamus, contribuant nihil, quo militibus nostris praemia condigna laboribus solvantur.
units.tr: 11. We also make known to this council of the initiated and the Christian people that, because of frequent wars and the savage incursions made against us from the most ferocious nations surrounding us on every side, a portion of Church money, namely twelve pence, which we call a solidus, shall be contributed, so that our soldiers may be paid worthy rewards for their labours.

units.la: 12. Adulterna, incesta matrimonia si vetus coibeto.
units.tr: 12. Incestuous and adulterous marriages shall be forbidden.

units.la: CAROLOMANNI I. ET PIPINI EDICTUM DE METROPOLI MOGUNTINA.
units.tr: The Edict of Carloman I and Pippin concerning the Metropolis of Mainz.

units.la: GREGORIUS Moguntinum Pontificem, qui quod hominis caede pollutus sit, sacerdotio tunc non potest, quod eum avibus & canibus luserit, quod Episcopo fas non est, cuius omnium Episcoporum calculis exauctoravimus ac depositimus.
units.tr: Gregory deposed and removed the Pontiff of Mainz, who, because he was polluted by the slaughter of a man, could not then hold the priesthood, and because he played with birds and dogs, which is not permitted to a bishop, by the votes of all the bishops.

units.la: B 2 1. Eg 2. Eo autem depositio, Bonifacium Moguntinæ Sedi præfecimus. Et ut eius dignitas aliquanto emineret, statuimus hoc perpetuo edicto, ut Ecclesia Moguntina amplius alteri fidelecta non sit, sed in totius Germaniæ capita ac metropolim levata existat. Actum in Synodo.
units.tr: B 2 1. Eg 2. After that deposition, we placed Boniface over the see of Mainz. And so that its dignity might rise somewhat higher, we decree by this perpetual edict that the Church of Mainz shall no longer be subject to another, but shall stand raised up as the head and metropolis of all Germany. Done in the Synod.

units.la: PIPINI REGIS AUGUSTI DECRETA ECCLESIASTICA
units.tr: PIPPIN THE KING'S ECCLESIASTICAL DECREES

units.la: COMITIORUM IN GENTILIACO HABITORUM ANNO DOMINI DCCLXVII. contra errores Graecorum de processione Spiritus sancti, & adoratione imaginum.
units.tr: Of the assemblies held at Gentilly in the year of the Lord 767, against the errors of the Greeks concerning the procession of the Holy Spirit and the adoration of images.

units.la: ORTA quæstione de sancta Trinitate, & de Sanctorum imaginibus, tunc Orientalium & Occidentalem Ecclesiam, id est, Romanos & Græcos, Rex Pipinus Conventum Gentiliaco congregato, Synodum de ipsa quæstione habuit.
units.tr: When a question arose concerning the holy Trinity and concerning the images of the saints, King Pippin, since the Eastern and Western Church, that is, the Romans and the Greeks, were at odds, gathered a meeting at Gentilly and held a synod on that very question.

units.la: 2. De Trinitate, utrum Spiritus Sanctus, sicut procedit a Patre, ita procedat a Filio. Et Patris præsentia Regis definierunt, processionem Spiritus Sancti ex Patre & Filio æque fieri, ideoque recte in Symbolo adiectum esse FILIOQUE.
units.tr: 2. Concerning the Trinity: whether the Holy Spirit, just as he proceeds from the Father, so also proceeds from the Son. In the presence of the King and the Father, they defined that the procession of the Holy Spirit is equally from the Father and the Son, and therefore that the word FILIOQUE was rightly added to the Creed.

units.la: 3. De Sanctorum imaginibus, utrum nec fingendæ an pingendæ essent in ecclesiis. Et Patres decreverunt, Sanctorum imagines factas aut pictas ira ad ornatum & decus ecclesiarum sed non ad cultum, veneratiónem & adorationem, quod idololatriæ facit, non habeantur.
units.tr: 3. Concerning the images of the saints: whether they should neither be fashioned nor painted in churches. And the Fathers decided that images of the saints, made or painted, are to be kept only for the adornment and honour of churches, but not for worship, veneration and adoration, which would make them idolatry.

units.la: CAROLI MAGNI IMPERATORIS AUG. FORMULÆ JURAMENTORUM.
units.tr: The Formulae of Oaths of the Emperor Augustus Charles the Great

units.la: JURAMENTUM DUCUM IN ITALIA.
units.tr: The Oath of the Dukes in Italy

units.la: PROMITTO, me Domino meo Carolo, & filiis eius fidelem futurum in tota vita, sine fraude, doloque malo.
units.tr: I promise that I will be faithful to my lord Charles and to his sons all my life, without deceit or evil trickery.

units.la: JURAMENTUM COMITUM, CAPITANEORUM VALVASORUM.
units.tr: The Oath of the Counts, Captains and Vavassors

units.la: JURO per hæc sancta Dei Evangelia, me in posterum fidelem ei futurum, ut vasallum Domino, nec id quod mihi sub nomine fidelitatis commiserit, enunciaturum in eius detrimentum scientem.
units.tr: I swear by these holy Gospels of God that henceforth I will be faithful to him as a vassal to his lord, and that I will not knowingly disclose to his detriment what he has entrusted to me under the name of fidelity.

units.la: JURAMENTUM CIVITATUM.
units.tr: The Oath of the Cities

units.la: PROMITTO, me Domino meo Carolo & filiis eius fidelem futurum in tota vita sine fraude, doloque malo: & vitam, membrum, mentem, & rectum eris honorem servaturum.
units.tr: I promise that I will be faithful to my lord Charles and to his sons all my life, without deceit or evil trickery; and that I will preserve life, limb, mind and lawful honour.

units.la: SENATUSCONSULTUM ROMANUM
units.tr: SENATUS-CONSULTUM ROMANUM

units.la: DE LEGE REGIA, QUA A PAPA SENATU POPULOQUE ROMANO JUS DOMINII ET POTESTATIS CAROLO MAGNO & eius successoribus concessum est, item de electione Romani Pontificis, & investituris Episcoporum, &c. CUM SCHOLIIS THEODORICI A NIEM EPISCOPI FERDENSIS & Cameracensis, Protonotarii Apostolici, &c.
units.tr: CONCERNING THE ROYAL LAW, BY WHICH THE POPE, THE SENATE AND THE ROMAN PEOPLE GRANTED THE RIGHT OF LORDSHIP AND POWER TO CHARLEMAGNE AND HIS SUCCESSORS; ALSO CONCERNING THE ELECTION OF THE ROMAN PONTIFF AND THE INVESTITURE OF BISHOPS, ETC. WITH THE SCHOLIA OF THEODORIC OF NIEM, BISHOP OF VERDEN AND OF CAMBRAI, APOSTOLIC PROTONOTARY, ETC.

units.la: ROMÆ constituit Sancta Synodus a beato Adriano Papa in Patriarchio Lateranensi, vt delectetur in Ecclesia sanctorum, quæ reverendissime celebrata est a centum & quinquaginta episcopis, & Abbatibus, Judicibus etiam & Legis Doctoribus, ab universis regionibus & urbibus huius almæ Urbis, ac uncto etiam Clero huius sanctæ Romanæ Ecclesiæ exquirentibus usus, leges, & mores eiusdem Ecclesiæ & Imperii: quemadmodum etiam hactenus seditiones ibidem pellerent de Apostolica Sede & dignitate Patriciatus & Romani Imperii, ut quod omnibus nominis esset crescebat in universo orbe. Populus itaque Romanus legem condere tunc solito. Sed difficile erat pro unoquoque negocio torrenstn unum congregari: unde sua in nos testatum Imperatori concessit, quemadmodum legitur. Populus itaque Romanus concessit et in eum transtulit omne ius suum & potestatem.
units.tr: At Rome, the holy synod was convened by the blessed Pope Hadrian in the Lateran Patriarchate, so that he might take delight in the Church of the saints. It was most solemnly celebrated by one hundred and fifty bishops and abbots, also judges and doctors of law, from all the regions and cities of this kindly City, and with the clergy of this holy Roman Church, seeking the customs, laws and usages of the same Church and Empire. Likewise, as hitherto seditions had there driven out the Apostolic See and the dignity of the Patriciate and the Roman Empire, so that what was of the name of all grew throughout the world. The Roman people therefore then customarily enacted law. But it was difficult to gather everyone together for each matter; whence by their testimony they granted their right to the Emperor, as is read. The Roman people therefore granted and transferred to him all their right and power.

units.la: SCHOLIUM.
units.tr: SCHOLIUM.

units.la: Nota qualiter Adrianus Papa cum Clero & Populo & universa sancta Synodo, concessit eidem Carolo Regi imperii gladium. fuerunt, ut haberetur 63. dist. Adrianus. Et illud privilegium renovatur & confirmatur per Papam, Cardinalis & Presbyteros Romanum, ac generale Concilium, in personam Ottonis Primi Magni Augusti, suosq; successores in Romano Imperio in perpetuum, ut sequitur inferius.
units.tr: Note how Pope Hadrian, with the clergy and the people and the whole holy synod, granted to the same King Charles the sword of empire. These things were so that it might be held in Dist. 63, Hadrian. And that privilege is renewed and confirmed by the Pope, the Cardinals and the Roman Presbyters, and the general council, in the person of Otto the First, the Great Augustus, and his successors in the Roman Empire forever, as follows below.

units.la: 2. Ad eorum quoque exemplum prædictus Adrianus Papa cum omni Clero & Populo, acuniversa Sancta Synodo, concessit Carolo Augusto omne suum ius & potestatem eligendi Summum Pontificem, & ordinandi Apostolicam Sedem, dignitatemque Patriciatus: insuper Archiepiscopos & Episcopos per singulas provincias ab eo accipere investituras diffinivit. Post hoc vero consecrationem si quis peccaverit, unde scitur. Unde tamen abolita fit veterum scientia, moresq; in posterum, quatenus nemo per cognationem, vel amicitiam, aut per pecuniarum acceptionem, sibi eligat Episcopum: sed soli Regi Romanorum huiusmodi reverentiæ tribuatur facultas. Verùmtamen si ab universo Clero & toto Populo aliqua præsumptione & religionis causa eligatur Episcopus, nisi à Rege laudetur & investiatur, à nemine consecretur.
units.tr: 2. In imitation of these, the aforesaid Pope Hadrian, with all the clergy and people and the whole holy synod, granted to Augustus Charles all his right and power of electing the Supreme Pontiff and of ordering the Apostolic See, and the dignity of the Patriciate. Moreover, he decreed that the archbishops and bishops in each province should receive their investitures from him. After this, if anyone sins in the consecration, it is known from this. Hence indeed the knowledge of the ancients is abolished, and the customs for the future, so that no one, by kinship or friendship, or by the acceptance of money, should choose a bishop for himself; but the faculty of such reverence shall be granted to the King of the Romans alone. However, if a bishop is elected by the whole clergy and the whole people, by any presumption and for the sake of religion, unless he is approved and invested by the King, he shall be consecrated by no one.

units.la: 3. Ex hoc prolatis sententiis ab universis, qui in hac Sancta Synodo congregati fuerunt, In nomine Sanctæ Trinitatis, Adrianus Papa pro omnibus hoc concessit, laudavit, & affirmando constituit. Adhuc etiam totum toborandum decrevit, ut si quis posthæc contra hanc Sanctam Synodum temerator repertus fuerit, sive contra hoc totum, quod prædiximus, repugnaverit, cuiuscumque fit gradus, ordinis, vel officij, aut dignitatis, vel generis, sciat se in iram beati Petri Principis Apostolorum, & omnium Sanctorum, & prædecessorum nostrorum, casurum, & anathematis vinculo damnatum perpetualiter victurum, excommunicationem quoque universalis Ecclesiæ & cuncti Populi Christiani facturum. Insuper, nisi à malo relipuerit, irrevocabili exilio prematur, vel ultimis supplicis serviatur, & bona eius publicentur. Qui vero pio intuitu custos horum & observator in omnibus extiterit, bene dictionis gratiam vitamque æternam à Deo cum omnibus Sanctis suis sine fine habere merebitur in secula seculorum. Amen.
units.tr: 3. Then, with the sentences pronounced by all who were gathered in this Holy Synod, in the name of the Holy Trinity, Pope Hadrian granted this for all, approved it, and established it by affirmation. Furthermore, he decreed that the whole be strengthened, so that if anyone hereafter is found to be a violator against this Holy Synod, or sets himself against the whole of what we have said, of whatever degree, order, office, dignity or kind, let him know that he will fall into the wrath of blessed Peter, Prince of the Apostles, and of all the Saints and of our predecessors, and will live condemned forever under the bond of anathema, and will incur excommunication from the universal Church and all the Christian people. Moreover, unless he turns back from evil, let him be pressed with irrevocable exile, or be subjected to the ultimate punishment, and let his goods be confiscated. But whoever, with a pious regard, has been the guardian and observer of these things in all respects, shall deserve to have from God, with all His saints, the grace of blessing and eternal life without end, for ages of ages. Amen.

units.la: CAROLI MAGNI IMP. AUG. CONSTITUTIO DE METALLIFODINARUM PRIVILEGIO Comitibus Glichensibus concesso.
units.tr: Constitution of Emperor Charles the Great, Augustus, on the privilege of the metal mines, granted to the Counts of Glichen.

units.la: CAROLUS divina favente gratia Romanorum ac Francorum Rex &c. Terræque Saxonum & Turingorum Dominator, Dilectis ac Nobilibus filiis, Ludoico seniori, Equiti & Militi nostro Christiano, exercitusque enim Capitaneo generali in Hispania contra incredulos: necnon eiusdem hæredibus Carolo & Ludoico salutem.
units.tr: Charles, by the favour of divine grace King of the Romans and the Franks, etc., and ruler of the lands of the Saxons and Thuringians, to our beloved and noble sons: Ludwig the Elder, our knight and soldier Christian, and general captain of our army in Spain against the unbelievers; and likewise to his heirs Charles and Ludwig, greetings.

units.la: Considerata devotione vestra, quam geritis circa Deum, propter quam non tantum laborum & rerum, verum etiam proprii sanguinis effusione ad propulsandos & extirpandos Saracenos & evacuandum gentilitatis errorem. Tu hli, dilecte Ludoice, indifferenter te exposuisti, ideoque ob hanc T. strenuitatem non minora commoda Imperio, nobis & Ecclesia præparasti. Comprobatâ igitur & experta fidelitate tuâ, quam indefessam invenimus, operæ pretium nobis factUrum iudicamus, tuis exigentiis & laboribus Imperiali nostrâ authoritate & munificentiâ subvenire. Propterea tibi tuisque hæredibus concedimus. Tractum Regionis in saltu nostro Thuringiaco ad 20. Milliana in longitudine & latitudine Jure hæreditario possidendum & facultatem damus in territorio districtis illius domini quærere & fodere aurum argentumque, atque omnia alia Metalla uti debeatis & possitis. Dominiam oppida Gliehou & Alchk cum omnibus requisitis & Regaliis, quæ ad nos obitu viri Nobilis, Domini in Gleicho pervenere. Et ad evidentiam & perpetuitatem omnium promulgationem hanc paginam nostri Sigilli magni appensione munitam vobis decernimus indulgendam. Datæ ad portum Naonis in Francia. Anno incarnatæ salutis. 746.
units.tr: Considering your devotion towards God, on account of which you have exposed yourself not only to the outpouring of your labours and goods but also of your own blood, to drive out and root out the Saracens and to remove the error of heathenism; you, dear Ludwig, have exposed yourself without reserve. Therefore, on account of this your strenuous service, you have prepared no small advantages for the Empire, for us and for the Church. Your fidelity, having been proven and tested, and found tireless, we judge it worthwhile to assist your needs and labours with our imperial authority and generosity. Accordingly, we grant to you and your heirs a tract of territory in our Thuringian forest, twenty miles in length and breadth, to be possessed by hereditary right; and we give you the faculty to seek and dig gold, silver and all other metals in the territory of that district, and to use them as you ought and are able. We also grant the towns of Gliehou and Alchk, with all their appurtenances and regalia, which came to us on the death of the noble lord of Gleich. And, for the evidence and perpetuity of all these things, we decree that this charter, secured by the appending of our great seal, be granted to you. Given at the port of Naon in France, in the year of the incarnate salvation 746.

units.la: CAROLI MAGNI IMP. AUG. ET ORDINUM IMPERII DECRETUM IN REBELLES IMPERII ET lasæ Majestatis reos, Thessalonicenses Boiorum Regem, & socios eius, latum in Comitiis Ingelheimensibus, Anno DCCLXXXVIII.
units.tr: The Decree of Charlemagne, Emperor Augustus, and the Orders of the Empire against the rebels of the Empire and the guilty of high treason, Thessalo, King of the Bavarians, and his associates, issued at the Diet of Ingelheim in the year 788.

units.la: CAROLUS Concilium Angilemos cogit: Pontifices maiores, minores, Sacerdotes, prophanos, Regulos, Duces, Tetrarchas, Præfectos, Cives, Oppidanos, ad se venire iubet: in re maxima eorum consilio opus esse. Nemo non paret: omnes certatim iussa capessunt. Nobiles, ignobiles, prophani, quicunque in aliquo numero aut honore erant, die dicto frequentes coëunt atque... Illuc quoque Thessalonus proficiscitur: quem etiam paucis post diebus Litopyrei subsequitur. Præstò fuit & Boiorum, ut iussa erat, legatio. Posteaquam consedere Duces, Oratores Boiorum introduƈti, in consessu Procerum paucis ita locuti sunt: Non tam impudentes nec tam obstinati sumus, Patres Consultissimi, ut ea, quae luce clariora sunt, omnibusque patent, more perditorum negemus: illud oramus, ne perpaucorum crimen in omnes diffundatur. Maxima pars adhuc syncera erit, quae dum iustitiae & aequitati omnes nervos intendit, & fidem Regi optimo servare conantur, capitis periculum adivit. Aut malos fieri necesse est, aut exterres patria sine pignore, sine lare, sine tribu errabimus, nisi quid vestra providentia profuerit. Linquenda tellus, domus, uxor, liberi. Esse fidem, nefas esse ducitur. Regi a Deo optimo maximo coelitus demisso parere crimen est. Pax exultat, arma parantur: cum hostibus crudelissimis foedus ictum est: amicis bellum indicitur. Bonorum omnium vita in extremo versatur discrimine. Dux & autor horum malorum, quo magis pudear, femina est: ille, quem prohibere oporteret, uxorius est, & noluit consilia aspernatur. Suasu coniugis suae Hunnos & Avares nostrae religionis acerrimos hostes, & sanguinis nostri avidissimos, adversus pientissimum Principem concitat. Huius amicis insidiae struuntur, mors denique intentatur. Saepius data fides Regibus optimis, saepius (nullo nostro merito, nulla culpa, omnibus bonis dissuadentibus) fracta, nunquam servata est. Melior fortasse speranda sunt. Illud ultimo, quod in concione omnes audivimus, praeterire non possumus, satius esse decem filios amittere, quam obsequium Regi praestare, in servitutemque (ira adpellar) redigi. Fallitur, egregio quisquis sub Principe credit servitium: nunquam libertas gratior exstat, quam sub Rege pio.
units.tr: Charles convenes a council at Angilemos and summons to himself the greater and lesser bishops, priests, laymen, kings, dukes, tetrarchs, prefects, citizens and townsmen. He says that his counsel is needed in a matter of the greatest importance. No one fails to obey; all eagerly carry out the command. Nobles, commoners, laymen, and all who held any rank or office come in crowds on the appointed day... Thessalo sets out there too, and a few days later Lytopyrga follows him. A Bavarian embassy was also present, as it had been ordered to be. When the dukes had taken their seats, the Bavarian envoys were brought in and, before the assembly of the nobles, spoke briefly as follows: "We are not so shameless or so obstinate, most learned fathers, as to deny in the manner of the wicked what is clearer than light and lies open to everyone. We ask only this: that the crime of a very few not be spread over all. Most of us are still innocent. While we strain every nerve for justice and fairness and try to keep faith with our excellent king, we have faced the danger of our lives. Either we must become wicked, or we shall wander as exiles from our country, without pledge, without home, without tribe, unless your foresight helps us. We must leave the land, the house, the wife, the children. To keep faith is judged a crime; to obey a king set over us by God, the best and greatest, is counted a crime. Peace is trampled, arms are being prepared; a treaty has been struck with the cruelest enemies; war is declared on friends. The lives of all good men are in the greatest peril. The leader and author of these evils, to my shame, is a woman; he whom it would be fitting to restrain is under his wife's thumb and does not wish to reject her counsels. At his wife's urging he stirs up the Huns and Avars, the fiercest enemies of our religion and the greediest for our blood, against the most devout prince. Plots are laid against his friends, and death is finally threatened. Faith has often been pledged to the best kings, and often broken (through no merit or fault of ours, with all good men advising otherwise), and never kept. Better things may perhaps be hoped for. Finally, what we all heard in the assembly we cannot pass over: that it is better to lose ten sons than to render obedience to the king and be reduced to servitude (may it not be so). Whoever believes that servitude exists under an excellent prince is mistaken: liberty never appears more pleasing than under a pious king."

units.la: Haec ubi dicta sunt, & Thessalonus ite inficias non potuit, quippe quae testibus praesentibus comprobata erant, ex Codice lex recitata est, qua fidem Regi non servare, cum hostibus foedus adversus Regem inire, capitale erat. Secundum legem itaque Salicam ex veteri instituto Thessalonus crimine laesae maiestatis reus peractus, capitali supplicio condemnatur, Boiaria Regi adiudicatur. Ubi haec sententia ritu solenni renunciata est, Thessalonus ad genua CAROLI accidit. CAROLUS eundem rolli iuber, rogatque quidnam facturus sit, si vita donetur? Ille se in contubernio Monachorum omnem aetatem acturum, scelera sua atque crimina deprecaturum. CAROLUS igitur ipsum tonderi more Religiosorum iubet, in monasterium Divi Nazarii in Bergoftraffa, VVormatiensium agro situm, Laureacum literatores vocant, relegat. Theodo filius Thessaloni sacris initiatur. Sacerdotum tribui cooptatur. Uxor Lytopyrga in sacratarum foeminarum coetu degere iussa est. Pauci Boiorum, qui cum Thessalono senserant, in exilium acti sunt.
units.tr: When these things had been said, and Thessalo could not deny them, since they had been proved by witnesses present, a law was read aloud from the Code, by which it was a capital offence not to keep faith with the king and to enter into a treaty with enemies against the king. Accordingly, in keeping with the ancient custom and the Salic law, Thessalo was convicted of high treason and condemned to capital punishment, and Bavaria was adjudged to the king. When this sentence had been announced in the customary solemn form, Thessalo fell at the knees of Charles. Charles ordered him to be raised up and asked what he would do if his life were granted to him. He replied that he would spend the whole of his life in the fellowship of monks, and would beg pardon for his wickedness and crimes. Charles therefore ordered that he be shorn in the manner of the religious and sent into exile to the monastery of St. Nazarius at Bergoftraffa, situated in the territory of the Worms people, which the scholars call Laureacum. Theodo, the son of Thessalo, was initiated into holy orders and admitted to the ranks of the priests. His wife Lytopyrga was ordered to live in the company of consecrated women. A few Bavarians who had sided with Thessalo were driven into exile.

units.la: CAROLI MAGNI IMP. AUG. DECRETA ECCLESIASTICA
units.tr: Decrees of the Emperor Charlemagne, Augustus, on Ecclesiastical Matters

units.la: COMITIORVM FRANCONOFORTENSIVM, IN QVIBVS CCC. circiter Episcopi Elipandum & Felicem, eorumque haeresim de Filio Dei condemnarunt; actaque Nicaeni Concilii II. Pseudosepti mi in causa imaginum infirmarunt. A.D. 794.
units.tr: The Frankfurt Assembly, in which some 300 bishops condemned Elipandus and Felix, and their heresy concerning the Son of God; and the acts of the Second Council of Nicaea, the Pseudo-Seventh, were weakened in the matter of images. A.D. 794.

units.la: CAPITVLVM I.
units.tr: Chapter I.

units.la: CONVENIENTIBUS, Deo favente, Apostolica auctoritate, atque piissimi Domini nostri CAROLI Regis iussione, anno vigesimo sexto Principatus sui, cunctis Francorum, Italiae & Aquitaniae Episcopis ac Sacerdotibus, Synodali Consilio, inter quos ipse mitissimus sancto interfuit Conventui. Ubi in primordio capitulum exorsum de impia ac nefanda haeresi Elipandi Toletanae Sedis Episcopi, & Felicis Orgelitanae, eorumque sequacibus, qui male sentientes in Filio Dei adscribebant adoptionem. Quam omnes, qui supra, sanctissimi Patres respuentes, una voce contradixerunt, atque hanc haeresim funditus a sancta Ecclesia eradicandam statuerunt.
units.tr: Assembled by the favour of God, under apostolic authority and at the command of our most pious lord Charles the King, in the twenty-sixth year of his reign, with all the bishops and priests of the Franks, Italy and Aquitaine in synodal council, among whom the most gentle Charles himself took part in the assembly. At the beginning of the proceedings the chapter took up the impious and abominable heresy of Elipandus, bishop of the see of Toledo, and of Felix of Urgel, and of their followers, who, holding wrong opinions, ascribed adoption to the Son of God. All the most holy Fathers named above rejected this and spoke against it with one voice, and resolved that this heresy be uprooted from the holy Church.

units.la: CAPITVLVM II.
units.tr: Chapter II.

units.la: ALLATA est in medium quaestio de nova Graecorum Synodo, quam de adorandis imaginibus Constantinopoli fecerunt, in qua scriptum habetur, ut qui imagines Sanctorum ita ut Deificam Trinitatem servitio aut adoratione non impenderent, anathema iudicarentur. Quam omnes, qui supra, sanctissimi Patres nostri omnimodis, & adorationem & servitium respuentes, contempserunt, atque consentientes condemnaverunt.
units.tr: A question was brought forward concerning the new synod of the Greeks, which they held at Constantinople about the adoration of images, in which it is written that those who did not render service or adoration to the images of the saints in the same way as to the Deified Trinity should be judged anathema. All the most holy Fathers named above, rejecting both the adoration and the service in every way, despised this and, in agreement, condemned it.

units.la: CAPITVLVM III.
units.tr: Chapter III.

units.la: HIs peractis.
units.tr: These things being done,

units.la: CAROLI
units.tr: of Charles

units.la: CAROLI MAGNI, REGIS FRANCORUM, &c. CONSTITVTIO DATA FRANCOFURTI IN CONCILIO CCC. E- PISCOPORUM EX ITALIA, LIGURIA, ÆMILIA, HESPERIA, GAL- LIA, AQUITANIA, BRITANNIA, GERMANIA, & AUSTRIA PROVINCIIS A REGE CONVOCATORUM, ANNO DOMINI DCCLXXXIV.
units.tr: Capitulary of Charlemagne, King of the Franks, etc., issued at Frankfurt in the council of three hundred bishops summoned by the king from the provinces of Italy, Liguria, Aemilia, Hesperia, Gaul, Aquitaine, Britain, Germany and Austria, in the year of the Lord 784.

units.la: CONTRA HAERESIN ELIPANDINAM ET FELICIANAM, asserentem, Christum secundum carnem esse Dei Patris filium adoptivum.
units.tr: Against the Elipandan and Felician heresy, which asserts that Christ according to the flesh is an adoptive son of God the Father.

units.la: CAROLUS GRATIA DEI REX FRANCORUM ET LONGOBARDORUM, ac Patricius Romanorum, Filius & defensor sanctæ Dei Ecclesiæ, Elipando Toletanæ Civitatis Metropolitano, & cæteris in partibus Hispaniæ Constitutis Episcopis, Orthodoxæ fidei & fraternæ caritatis in Christo Dei Filio proprio & vero optamus salutem.
units.tr: Charles, by the grace of God King of the Franks and the Lombards, and Patrician of the Romans, son and defender of the holy Church of God, to Elipandus, Metropolitan of the city of Toledo, and to the other bishops established in the parts of Spain: we wish you health in the orthodox faith and in fraternal love, in Christ the true and proper Son of God.

units.la: Audet pietas Christiana divinæ scilicet atq; fraternæ per lata terrarum spatia duplices caritatis alas extendere, ut materno foveat affectu, quos sacro genuerat baptismate. Et maxima est sanctæ matris Ecclesiæ exultatio suorum adunatio filiorum, ut sint consummati in unum, qui redempti sunt ab uno, dicente eodem Redemptore nostro Jesu Christo: Pater sancte serva eos in nomine tuo, quos dedisti mihi, ut omnes unum sint sicut & nos unum sumus. Unde & in Cantico Canticorum de sancta dicitur Ecclesia: Terribilis ut castrorum acies ordinata. Constipata exercitus ordinatio & unanimis belatorum fortitudo magno solet hostibus esse terrori: sic filiorum sanctæ matris Ecclesiæ intra murum Catholicæ fidei pacifica adunatio aereis potestatibus nimium constat terribilis, & ignitis maligni perfidiæ spiculis omnino impenetrabilis extat, sicut & veratissimus Gentium prædicator & fortissimus Ecclesiæ proeliator præcipit, dicens: In omnibus sumentes scutum fidei, in quo possitis omnia tela Nequissimi ignita extinguere, & hoc sæculum nequam libero ad cœlestia volatu evadere. Sine fide enim impossibile est placere Deo: impossibile est, quod omnino ab homine fieri non potest. Principium est salutis nostræ Fidei, qua intemerata & integra sanitate confirmata, totus vitæ cursus per bonorum vestigia operum feliciter finetenus currit. Per fidem enim (sicut idem præfatus doctor in epistola ad Hebræos testatur) omnes sancti placuerunt Deo.
units.tr: Christian devotion, that is, divine and fraternal love, is eager to spread its twofold wings across the wide spaces of the lands, so that it may cherish with a mother's affection those whom it has begotten in sacred baptism. The greatest joy of our holy mother the Church is the gathering of her children into one, that they may be made perfect in one, since they have been redeemed by one, as our Redeemer Jesus Christ said: "Holy Father, keep them in your name, those whom you have given me, that they may all be one, as we are one" (John 17:11). Hence also the Song of Songs says of the holy Church: "Terrible as an army set in array" (Song 6:4). An ordered and compact army, and the united strength of fighters, is usually a great terror to enemies. So too the peaceful union of the children of our holy mother the Church, within the wall of the Catholic faith, is very terrible to the powers of the air, and is wholly impenetrable to the fiery darts of the wicked treachery. The most truthful preacher to the Gentiles and the most valiant fighter of the Church commands this too, saying: "Taking up in all things the shield of faith, by which you may be able to quench all the fiery darts of the most wicked one" (Eph. 6:16), and to escape this evil age by a free flight to heavenly things. For without faith it is impossible to please God (Heb. 11:6); it is impossible, that is, which cannot be done at all by man. Faith is the beginning of our salvation, and when it is confirmed in unimpaired and whole soundness, the whole course of life runs happily to the end by the footsteps of good works. For through faith (as the same teacher testifies in the Epistle to the Hebrews) all the saints have pleased God.

units.la: 2. Hanc igitur Fidem Orthodoxam & ab Apostolicis traditam Doctoribus, & ab universali servatam Ecclesia, nos pro virium nostrarum portione ubique in omnibus servare & prædicare confitemur: quia non est in alia aliqua salus, nisi in illa, quam pacifica ab initio salutis nostræ unanimitate semper servabat Ecclesia. Pro qua etiam, viri fratres, & vestra bona devotio, quam vos habere decet in Domino, his partibus fidei vestræ litteras dirigere * curastis, nempe & generales ad Sacerdotales sanctissimas aures, ad nos quoq; speciales: in quarum utriq; serie litterarum non satis nobis elucebat, an quali ex auctoritate magistrorum vos vestra docere disposuistis, an ex humilitatis discipulatu nostra discere desideratis: tamen live hoc sive illud vestris inesset animis, petitionem vestram, caritate Christianæ religionis cogente, non spernendam esse censuimus, valde desiderantes, Deumq; ex intimo corde deprecantes, quatenus in veræ fidei solliditate firmiter utrimq; permaneamus, contra huius sæculi ictus, Spiritu Sancto navigium vestri cursus regente, ad portum perpetuæ tranquillitatis pervenire mereamur.
units.tr: 2. Therefore we confess that this orthodox faith, handed down by the apostolic teachers and kept by the universal Church, we keep and proclaim everywhere in all things, as far as the measure of our powers allows; for there is no salvation in any other, except in that which the Church has always kept in peaceful unanimity from the beginning of our salvation. For this faith, brothers, and for your good devotion, which becomes you in the Lord, you have taken care to send letters to these parts of the faith, both general ones to the most holy ears of the priests and special ones to us also. In the sequence of both letters it did not sufficiently appear to us whether you had decided to teach your own doctrine on the authority of masters, or whether you desired to learn from us in the discipleship of humility.
