Yet, whether this or that was in your minds, we have judged that your petition, compelled by the charity of the Christian religion, is not to be despised, earnestly desiring, and praying to God from the depth of our heart, that we may remain firmly on both sides in the solidity of the true faith, and that, against the blows of this age, with the Holy Spirit steering the ship of your course, we may deserve to reach the harbour of perpetual tranquillity.

units.la: 3. Ad hanc tranquillitatem capiendam oculus cordis fide purificandus est, & assiduis sanctorum orationum precibus mentis acies illustranda, ut puræ veritatis lumen, omni errorum nube expulsa, contemplari valeat, ne in opiniones noxiæ falsitatis temerias motdinata incautius gradientes præcipitet. Non pudeat Christianum, ubi hæsitat, quærere; ubi nescias, discere: quoniam pia humilitas discendi sapientiæ nimirum secreta: & melius est, discipulum esse veritatis, quam doctorem existere falsitatis. Ille ad altiora semper provehitur; iste ad inferiora semper dilabitur, & inde magister efficitur erroris, unde auditor contemplit esse veritatis. Hanc igitur, Fratres, perniciosam devitantes externam, sanctorum Patrum & sanctorum Doctorum sacris inhæreamus sensibus: dicēamus, quæ scripserunt; credamus, quæ docuerunt, & nō declinemus ad dexteram neq; ad sinistram, sed per viam regiam ad Regem & Redemptorem & Deum & Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum concordi fidei & veritatis curramus profectione. Corde enim creditur ad iustitiam, ore autem confessio fit ad salutem, eodem Apostolo. Iustus autem ex fide vivit: si justus ex fide vivit, quomodo, qui fidem non habet revivere æternam? Nos nempe non sumus infidelitatis in perditionem, sed fidei ad acquisitionem animæ. Suntur sanctorum Patrum venerabilia in caritate præcepta.
units.tr: 3. To attain this tranquillity, the eye of the heart must be cleansed by faith, and the sight of the mind enlightened by the constant prayers of the saints, so that it may be able to contemplate the light of pure truth, with every cloud of error driven away, lest rashness, walking more carelessly into the opinions of harmful falsehood, plunge it headlong. A Christian should not be ashamed to seek where he hesitates, and to learn where he does not know; for it is a pious humility that learns the secrets of wisdom, and it is better to be a disciple of truth than to become a teacher of falsehood. The one is always carried up to higher things; the other always slides down to lower things, and from there becomes a master of error, whence he ought to have been a hearer of truth. Therefore, brothers, avoiding this pernicious novelty, let us cling to the sacred senses of the holy Fathers and the holy teachers: let us say what they have written, let us believe what they have taught, and let us not turn aside to the right or to the left, but run by the royal way, in agreement of faith and truth, to Christ, our King, Redeemer, God and Lord. For, as the same Apostle says, "with the heart one believes unto righteousness, and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation" (Rom. 10:10). "The just shall live by faith" (Hab. 2:4; Heb. 10:38). If the just lives by faith, how shall he who has no faith live again to eternity? For we are not of unbelief unto perdition, but of faith unto the gaining of the soul. Thus the venerable precepts of the holy Fathers are given in charity.

units.la: 4. Decet enim ut omnium Christianorum una sit fides & unus animus, sicut est unum ovile & unus pastor. Qui enim extra Ecclesiam ovilis septa invenientur, lupina rabie devorabuntur, qui vocem boni pastoris non audiunt, qui ante suas oves ingredietur & egredietur, ut eos ad pascua vitæ perducat æternæ. Nobis itaq; dictum intelligamus, quod egregius prædicator suis carissimis filiis præcipiebat.
units.tr: 4. For it is fitting that all Christians have one faith and one mind, just as there is one sheepfold and one shepherd. For those who are found outside the Church, outside the fold, will be devoured with wolfish rage; they do not hear the voice of the good shepherd, who goes in and out before his sheep, that he may lead them to the pastures of eternal life. Let us therefore understand as spoken to us what the eminent preacher commanded his dearest sons.

units.la: {y} Ecclesiam, Ilanam ad usum nostra. cipiebat, dicens: Obsecro vos per nomen Domini nostri Iesu Christi, ut unum dicatis omnes, & non sint in vobis schismata. Sitis autem perfecti in uno sensu & in eadem sententia. Haec habentes Apostolicae auctoritatis praecepta, concordare nobiscum. Diligimus vos: hoc vobis volumus in Domino, quod & nobis: quia perfecta, quam habemus in Christo, cantas congregare gaudet non spargere, adunare non sciudere, & inconsutilem Salvatoris nostri tunicam integram servare non dividere, praevidentes hoc idem in pace Christi custodire, quod milites in passione ejus observabant.
units.tr: {Misreadings aside} The Apostle commanded, saying: "I beseech you, brothers, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you; but that you be perfect in the same mind and in the same judgement" (1 Cor. 1:10). Having these precepts of apostolic authority, agree with us. We love you; we wish for you in the Lord what we wish for ourselves, because the perfect charity which we have in Christ rejoices to gather, not to scatter, to unite, not to tear apart, and to keep the seamless tunic of our Saviour whole, not divided, foreseeing that we should keep this same unity in the peace of Christ which the soldiers observed at his passion.

units.la: 5. His ita praelibatis, vestris in Domino valde congaudemus profectibus, ita ut in cordibus nostris fraterno vulnerati amore vestram, quam patimini, lachrymabili gemitu condoleamus oppressionem; sed majore multo tristitia lugemus, si aliquid Diabolica fraude interius oppressionis perinsidelitatem vel cujuslibet schismatici erroris patiamur cordibus. Ipse est continuus dolor pectoribus nostris, & pene irremediabile vulnus, nisi per ejus misericordiam, a qui sanat contritos corde, & b vult omnes homines salvos fieri & ad agnitionem veritatis pervenire, illi nos laetificent, qui tristaverunt. Veltra·gi· tur correctio, nostra est laetificatio. Desiderantes vos socios habere in fide Catholica, & cooperatores in praedicatione veritatis, ut gaudium, quod Christus suis promisit discipulis, habitet in nobis, & gaudium nostrum impleatur in vobis.
units.tr: 5. Having thus said these preliminary words, we rejoice greatly in your progress in the Lord, so that, wounded in our hearts by fraternal love, we grieve with tearful sighs over the oppression which you suffer. But we mourn with a much greater sorrow if we suffer, through the devilish fraud, any inward oppression of unbelief or of any schismatic error in our hearts. This is the continual pain of our breasts, and an almost irremediable wound, unless by his mercy, who heals the broken in heart (Ps. 147:3), and who wills that all men be saved and come to the knowledge of the truth (1 Tim. 2:4), those who have caused us sorrow should make us glad. Your correction, therefore, is our joy. We desire you as companions in the Catholic faith and co-workers in preaching the truth, so that the joy which Christ promised to his disciples may dwell in us, and our joy may be fulfilled in you (John 15:11).

units.la: 6. Ad implementum vero hujus gaudii, fraterna cogente caritate, justissimus sanctorum Patrum Synodale ex omnibus undiq; nostrae ditionis Ecclesiis congregari Concilium, quatenus sanctorum unanimitas firmiter decerneret, quid credendum sit de adoptione carnis Christi, quam nuper novis assertionibus, & sanctae Dei universali Ecclesiae antiquis temporibus inauditis vos ex verbis scriptis intulisse cognovimus: immo & ad beatissimum Apostolicae Sedis Pontificem de hac nova inventione nostrae devotionis ter quateraq; direximus Missos, scire cupientes, quid sancta Romana Ecclesia, Apostolicis edocta traditionibus, in hac respondere voluisset inquisitione. Necnon & de Britanniae partibus aliquos Ecclesiasticae disciplinae viros convocavimus, ut ex multorum diligenti consideratione veritas Catholicae Fidei investigaretur, & probatissimis sanctorum Patrum hinc & inde roborata testimoniis aliq; illa dubitatione teneatur.
units.tr: 6. To fulfil this joy, compelled by fraternal charity, we have ordered a most just synod of the holy Fathers to be gathered from all the churches of our dominion on every side, so that the unanimity of the saints might firmly decide what is to be believed concerning the adoption of the flesh of Christ, which, as we have learned, you have introduced from the written words with new assertions, and which was unheard of in the holy universal Church of God in ancient times. Indeed, we have also sent envoys, three and four times, to the most blessed Pontiff of the Apostolic See concerning this new invention of ours, wishing to know what the holy Roman Church, taught by the apostolic traditions, had wished to answer in this inquiry. We have also summoned some men from the parts of Britain who are versed in ecclesiastical discipline, so that the truth of the Catholic faith might be investigated by the careful consideration of many, and that, strengthened by the most approved testimonies of the holy Fathers on both sides, it might be held without any doubt.

units.la: 7. Idcirco vobis per singulos libellos dirigere curavimus, quid praedictorum Patrum pia unanimitas & pacifica perscrutatio auctoritate Ecclesiastica invenire, statuisset, confirmaret. Primo quid Dominus Apostolicus cum sancta Romana Ecclesia, & Episcopis in illis partibus quaqua versum commorantibus, & Catholicis Doctoribus, sentiret, sub unius libelli tenore statuimus. Deinde secundo loco, quid Ecclesiastici Doctores & Sacerdotes Ecclesiarum Christi de propinquioribus Italiae partibus cum Petro Mediolanensi Archiepiscopo, & Paulino Foro-Juliensi vel Aquilejensi Patriarcha, viris a Domino valde venerabilibus, intelligi vel firmiter credi voluissent, suis propriis responsionibus exaratum posuimus libellum; quia ipsi quoq; praesentes nostro Synodali Conventui adfuerant. Post haec tenet & terminus libellus Orthodoxorum sanctorum Patrum Episcoporum & virorum venerabilium fidem, qui in Germania, Galliae, Aquitaniae, & Britanniae partibus, dignis Deo deserviunt officiis, vestrisq; objectionibus sanctarum scripturarum testimoniis roboratas obtinet responsiones. Deinde quarto loco mex propriae unanimitatis cum his sanctissimis praedictorum Patrum decretis & Catholicis statutis consensum subnexui, sicut vosmetipsi in vestra epistola, quam meo speciali designatis nomini, rogare curastis, id est, ne subdolis paucorum assertionibus consentirem, sed plurimorum testimonus roboratam fidem tenerem.
units.tr: 7. Accordingly, we have taken care to send you, in separate little books, what the holy unanimity and peaceful inquiry of the aforesaid Fathers have determined under ecclesiastical authority, and what they confirm. First, under the wording of one book, we have set out what the lord Pope, together with the holy Roman Church, the bishops dwelling everywhere in those regions, and the Catholic teachers think. Second, we have set down in its own answers a book in which the ecclesiastical teachers and priests of the churches of Christ from the nearer parts of Italy, with Peter, Archbishop of Milan, and Paulinus, Patriarch of Friuli or Aquileia, men greatly venerated by the Lord, wished to be understood and firmly believed. They were also present at our synodal assembly. After this comes a third book, that of the orthodox holy Fathers, bishops and venerable men, who serve God worthily in the regions of Germany, Gaul, Aquitaine and Britain. It contains responses supported by testimonies of Holy Scripture to your objections. Fourth, I have added my own agreement with the most holy decrees of the aforesaid Fathers and the Catholic statutes, just as you yourselves asked in your letter, which you directed to my name, namely that I should not consent to the deceitful assertions of a few, but should hold the faith confirmed by the testimony of many.

units.la: 8. Facio certissime, Deo Domino meo Jesu Christo donante, horum me sanctissimae multitudini & probatissimae auctoritati veritatis fidei professione assocans, nec vestrae me paucitati in contentione hujus novae assertionis socium admitto, sed Apostolicae Sedi, & antiquis ab initio nascentis ecclesiae & Catholicis traditionibus, tota mentis intentione, tota cordis alacritate conjungo. Quicquid in illorum legitur libris, qui divino Spiritu afflati, toti orbi a Deo Christo dati sunt Doctores, indubitanter teneo, hoc ad salutem animae meae sufficere credens, quod sacratissimae Evangelicae veritatis pandit historia, quod Apostolica in suis epistolis confirmat auctoritas, quod eximii sanctae Scripturae tractatores & praecipui Christianae Fidei Doctores, ad perpetuam posteritatis scriptarum reliquerunt memoriam. Cum his quoq; Doctoribus, & sanctae Ecclesiae Patribus veram praedico fidem, quos in praesenti tempore ille nobis dedit luminaria, qui dixit: Ecce ego vobiscum sum omnibus diebus usq; ad consummationem saeculi. Hi sunt propugnatores fidei nostrae, hi sunt rectores per diversas sedes civitatis Christi, cujus antemurale est Fides Catholica, & caritas firmissimus murus, & propugnacula divinarum testimonia scripturarum, & divitiae salutis in ea sunt sapientia & scientia, & spes portarum custodia, quae quatuor clavibus, id est prudentia, justitia, fortitudine, & temperantia piis aperiuntur animis. Hujus vero civitatis ipse Dei verus & proprius filius, Deus verus homo verus Iesus Christus Dominus noster Regali praesidet potentia, cujus gratia totam illius civitatis structuram regit, defendit, & exaltat. Quisquis ad hanc civitatem, recta sibi praeviante fide, manus bonorum operum habens plenissimas pervenire festinat, aperras inveniet portas, & Regem Regum cum multitudine sanctorum agnoscendum obviare sibi gaudebit.
units.tr: 8. I do most assuredly, with the Lord my God Jesus Christ granting it, join myself to the most holy multitude of these men and to their most approved authority by profession of the faith of truth. Nor do I admit myself as a partner of your small number in contending for this new assertion. Rather, with my whole mind's intention and my whole heart's eagerness, I join myself to the Apostolic See and to the ancient traditions of the Church from its beginning, and to the Catholic traditions. Whatever is read in those books, which were given to the whole world by God Christ as teachers, inspired by the divine Spirit, I hold without doubt, believing that what the most sacred history of the Gospel truth sets forth is sufficient for the salvation of my soul, as is what the apostolic authority confirms in its epistles, and what the distinguished interpreters of holy Scripture and the chief teachers of the Christian faith have left to the lasting memory of posterity in their writings. Together with these teachers and the Fathers of the holy Church, I proclaim the true faith. These are the lights which He has given us at the present time, He who said: "Behold, I am with you all days, even to the end of the world" [Matth. 28.20]. These are the defenders of our faith, these are the rulers throughout the various seats of the city of Christ, whose bulwark is the Catholic faith, whose most firm wall is charity, whose ramparts are the divine testimonies of Scripture, and in which are the riches of salvation, wisdom and knowledge, and the hope which guards the gates. These gates are opened to pious minds by four keys, namely prudence, justice, fortitude and temperance. Over this city the true God and proper Son of God, true God and true man, Jesus Christ our Lord, presides with royal power, by whose grace He rules, defends and exalts the whole structure of that city. Whoever hastens to come to this city, with right faith going before him and with hands full of good works, will find the gates open, and will rejoice to meet the King of kings with the multitude of the saints.

units.la: 9. Sed & gratias vobis agimus de instantia orationum vestrarum, quibus memoriam nostri assidue vos habere dixistis, optantes ut preces vestrae acceptabiles sint Domino Deo Salvatori nostro, & ut ipse per suam misericordiam dignos vos efficiat exaudiri, & ad unitatem sanctae suae Ecclesiae revocare dignetur, & ejusdem pietatis humeris in sanctae matris Ecclesiae reportet ovile, qui de coelis veniens ovem requirere perditam, inventamq; cum triumpho gloriae ad sedem paternae Majestatis revexit.
units.tr: 9. We also thank you for the earnestness of your prayers, by which you said you constantly keep us in your memory, wishing that your prayers may be acceptable to the Lord God our Saviour, that He may make you worthy to be heard through His mercy, and that He may deign to call you back to the unity of His holy Church, and may, with the shoulders of His own mercy, bring back into the fold of the holy mother Church the sheep that was lost, He who came down from heaven to seek the lost sheep and, having found it, carried it back with the triumph of glory to the seat of the Father's majesty.

units.la: [illegible, ~20 letters] quod vobis nostram pietatem flagitare placuit, quatenus in praesentia nostra libelli vestri textus, & perscrutantes plurimorum consilio, quid in eo recte fidei sanctionibus consentaneum sit, quam diligentissime, sicut petitis, collectis, undique, velut praefati fumus, Ecclesiasticis Doctoribus & pluribus Christiani Rectoribus, nobisque omnibus pacifico unanimiter choro consentientes, ut illum a capite calcatum per diversas interpretationes uniuscujusque sententiae, & per interpretationes [?] prout cuique libuit, perlegere jussimus. Quod vero de illo libello Praesulum [?] Catholicae Doctores intellexissent, non est opus mihi in hac mea epistola ostendere, cum ipse libellus proprius hoc vobis evidenter ostender.
units.tr: [illegible, about twenty letters] it has pleased us to ask of you that, in our presence, the texts of your book be examined, and that, by the counsel of many, we consider with the greatest diligence, as you requested, what in it agrees with the sanctions of the right faith. These have been gathered from everywhere, as we said before, from the ecclesiastical teachers and many rulers of Christians, and from all of us, agreeing together in one peaceful chorus. We have ordered that it be read through, trampled from its head through various interpretations of each opinion, and through interpretations [?] as each one pleased. As for what the Catholic teachers of the prelates [?] understood concerning that book, there is no need for me to show it in this my letter, since the book itself shows this to you clearly.

units.la: In epistolis veltra hujusmodi obsecrationem invenimus: Posentes vos per eum, qui ... extendit, & pro te suscepit ... pretio sum effudit, & pro te mortem pertulit & sepultus ... ad infernum descendit, & pro te resurgens ... viam ad caelo revertendi, si licet ad caelestia ... per ipsum ... fideas etc. Ecce ego vestris petitionibus satisfaciens, consentio ... editor & arbiter ad fidei. Discernimus, & Deo donante decrevimus, quid ... sit deliberandum ... honorare, quae humana fragilitas temere perscrutando invenire non valet.
units.tr: In your letter we found an entreaty of this kind: Beseeching you through him who ... stretched out, and who took up [your cause] for you ... poured out his blood as the price, and endured death for you, and having been buried ... descended into hell, and rising again for you ... the way of returning to heaven, if it is lawful to [go] to the heavenly things ... through him ... you believe, etc. Behold, satisfying your petitions, I consent ... editor and arbiter of the faith. We discern, and by God's grant we have decided, what ... is to be deliberated ... to honour, which human frailty cannot find by rashly searching.

units.la: Exemplum mihi Constantini Imperatoris propositum, cujus initium beatum Isidorum ... quod ne mihi accidat, per quendam Beatum quem per antiquam ... praecavere satago, non abil- ... ex filiis sanctae matris Ecclesiae valeo, mihi in hac petitione ... conjungo, ne me aliquis verbis adulatio, vel tandulenta laudatio decipiens ... via vernatus cum Propheta decantans: Corripiet me justus in misericordia & increpabit me, oleum autem peccatoris non impinguet caput meum.
units.tr: The example of the Emperor Constantine is set before me, whose beginning the blessed Isidore ... which lest it happen to me, through a certain blessed man whom through the ancient ... I strive to guard against, I am not able ... of the sons of the holy mother Church, I join myself to you in this petition, lest any flattery of words, or deceiving thin praise, ... I, with the Prophet singing: Let the righteous strike me in mercy and rebuke me; but let the oil of the sinner not anoint my head. [Ps. 141.5]

units.la: Vos vero vobismetipsis cavete quos vos fraterno monuistis amore, procurantes diligenter ... hoc in potentia Dei vobis assidue precibus clementissimam convocate gratiam, ne calcida ... hostis vestrum ... mentis ... ex advenientis ... cumque expectare Redemptorem, quem salutis vellitis habuistis ... Illum glorificate in corde & portate in corpore, & dignam in vobis illam praeparate habitationem in fide, quae per dilectionem operatur, quatenus vos illius gloriosa potentia & ineffabili miseria ab utroque ... vivunt molestia, exteriore scilicet & interiore, liberet & custodiat, & in magno ... ante conspectum gloriae suae cum multiplicibus laboris vestri divitiis stare concedat, & ... sabilem cum operatoribus Apostolicae Fidei audire faciat: Venite benedicti Patris mei, percipite regnum ... paratum vobis ab origine mundi. Pa... tunc igitur vobis regnum ab origine mundi indubitanter ... Catholicae fidei ... in conspectu nostro ... adjungere curam exter-... molestia interna hdelitatis ipse contemplamini: oculos mentis vestrae ad eum dirigere, ... de potestate tenebrarum, & instituere in regnum filii dilectionis suae.
units.tr: But you yourselves, beware of those whom you have admonished out of brotherly love, taking diligent care ... by this power of God, call upon His most merciful grace for yourselves with constant prayers, lest the crafty ... enemy of yours ... of mind ... from the one who is coming ... and when you have looked to await the Redeemer, whom you have wished to have for salvation ... Glorify him in your heart and bear him in your body, and prepare for him in yourselves a dwelling worthy of him, in the faith which works through love, so that his glorious power and ineffable mercy may free and keep you from both ... live in trouble, that is, outward and inward, and grant that you may stand in great ... before the sight of his glory with the many riches of your labour, and ... may cause you to hear, with the workers of the Apostolic Faith: Come, you blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom ... prepared for you from the foundation of the world [Matth. 25.34]. Pa... then, therefore, the kingdom from the foundation of the world without doubt ... of the Catholic faith ... in our sight ... take care to add ... the inward trouble of faithfulness itself you behold: to direct the eyes of your mind to him ... from the power of darkness, and to be established in the kingdom of the Son of his love.

units.la: Hactenus antequam Filius adoptionis in Christo nomen a vobis exortum non nostrum vos ... in fide et amore dilectionis, & in nos vestrum unum corporale servitium contribuerit, tamen Ecclesia Catholica laetificavit in nobis. Nunc vero ... pro vobis afflictimur ... Christi ... fratum ... deceptione ... de eo, & inimica servitute oppressus in corpore. Sed redite, ... Ecclesiae ... ut vos eruat de angustiis ... vinculo liberavit ... ex illis peccatum. Expolitus vero ... houlaecis quomodo ... multitudinem illum: Adoptionis filii Deo Patris facti estis per eum, qui ... adoptionis dono. Stare per fidei inviolabilem confessionem in libertate filiorum Dei, & ... subiacere, expellite vinculum Diaboli deceptionis de cordibus, quae ... compeditos, excutite catenam generis inimicae de manibus vestris ... cooperatores gaudii vestri, si vos nobiscum Catholicae Fidei ... Christianum namque est divinae misericordiae auxilium: ubi una est totius ... fidei confessio.
units.tr: Hitherto, before the Son of adoption, the name having arisen among you in Christ, ... you ... in faith and in the love of charity, and contributed to us your one bodily service, nevertheless the Catholic Church has rejoiced in us. But now ... we are afflicted for you ... of Christ ... of the brethren ... by deception ... of him, and oppressed in body by hostile servitude. But return, ... of the Church ... so that he may rescue you from distress ... has freed you from the bond ... from those sins. Moreover, ... how ... that multitude: You have become sons of adoption to God the Father through him who ... by the gift of adoption. To stand by the inviolable confession of faith in the liberty of the sons of God, and ... to be subject, cast out the bond of the Devil's deception from your hearts, which ... shackled, shake off the chain of the hostile race from your hands ... fellow-workers of your joy, if you with us [hold to] the Catholic Faith ... For the help of divine mercy is Christian: where there is one confession of the whole ... faith.

units.la: Admonitionem ... populi Christiani & ad Sacerdotalis Concilii unanimitatem revertimini ... voluntate ... ut quod nos ... confessionem, secundum ... ad nos ... dubitamus, quia ubi tot sanctissimi fratres, tot filii matris Ecclesiae in nomine ... cognoscunt ... dubitandum ... illorum ... quod in laudem ... quaerere dignoscuntur. Ad confirmandum ... cuius ... ad ... aeternam ... cantare, qui ... habemus ... fide Catholica, proficiat devotio, & vos divina clementia ad ... Christum.
units.tr: You return to the admonition of the Christian people and to the unanimity of the sacerdotal council, that what we ... confession, according to ... to us ... we doubt, because where so many most holy brothers, so many sons of Mother Church in the name of ... recognize ... must be doubted ... of them ... which they are known to seek in praise. To confirm ... whose ... to ... eternal ... to sing, who ... we have ... by the Catholic faith, may devotion profit, and may the divine clemency turn you to Christ.

units.la: Ante ... Quasi ... ipsum dicti scandali ... vobis ... oppressionis ... dupliciter ... pradicamus ... dilectissimi, ... est in ... orationibus nostris per omnes ... regni nostri Ecclesiae ... laborantes ... Amen.
units.tr: Before ... As if ... of the said scandal ... to you ... of oppression ... doubly ... we proclaim, most beloved, ... is in ... our prayers through all ... of our kingdom's Church ... labouring ... Amen.

units.la: {*} Sylv. Tinct. & Cathol. socios, & veltri memoriam quotidie facientes: itidem quoq;, & Deo auxiliante, voluntate mus vos liberare à servitio secularis necessitatis secundum temporis opportunitatem, & adhortationem: nunc vero hac duplice caritate (quod sine dolore non dicimus) fraudatis vos ipsos, non intelligentes, fraude Diabolica esse deceptos, ut utroque juvamine vos denudarer, participatione fidei & orationum nostrarum, vel solatio auxilii nostri. Videte, videte, quam graviter malum adversus vosmetiplos habetis factum, quod nequaquam aliud fumus orare pro vobis: pro fidelibus sanctae Dei Ecclesiae filius, nec vos adjuvare, quomodo fratres in veltris maximis necessitatibus. Quapropter reverumini ad hanc duplicem consolationem, & abjicite à vobis hanc magnam Diabolicae fraudis versutiam, ut pollitis nobiscum consortium habere in omni caritate & studio opportuno.
units.tr: {*} Sylvester, Tinctus and Catholic companions, and remembering you daily; likewise also, with God helping, we are willing to free you from the service of worldly necessity, according to the opportunity of the time and by exhortation. But now, by this double charity (which we do not say without grief), you defraud yourselves, not understanding that you have been deceived by a diabolical fraud, so that you would be stripped of both aids: the participation of faith and of our prayers, and the solace of our help. See, see how grievously you have done evil against yourselves, since we on our part do not cease to pray for you, the sons of the holy Church of God, and you do not help us, as brothers, in your greatest necessities. Therefore return to this double consolation, and cast far from you this great subtlety of diabolical deceit, so that you may have fellowship with us in all charity and fitting zeal.

units.la: 17. Post hanc vero correctionem sive admonitionem Apostolicae auctoritatis & Synodal sanctae ... non relipisci tis ab errore veltro: scitote omnino vos pro Haereticis haberi, nec ullam vobiscum communionem pro Deo audeamus habere. Currite dum lucem habetis, ne tenebrae vos anathematis comprehendant, unde non poteritis pedes vestros explicare, sed interna damnatione ... ritos esse lugebitis. Adhuc enim pia mater revocat vos in gremium suae misericordiae, volens vos Deo nutrire in filios. Tantum nolite vos abstrahere ab ejus pietate, qui vos vocavit in regnum suum dilectionis suae.
units.tr: 17. After this correction, or admonition, of apostolic authority and of the holy synod ... unless you turn back from your error, know for certain that you are held as heretics, and we dare to have no communion with you before God. Run while you have the light, lest the darkness of anathema seize you, so that you cannot extricate your feet, but you will lament that you have been cast down into inward condemnation. For still the pious mother calls you back into the bosom of her mercy, wishing to nourish you in God as her sons. Only do not withdraw yourselves from the piety of him who called you into his kingdom of love.

units.la: 18. Credimus in Deum unum, Patrem omnipotentem, factorem caeli & terrae, visibilium omnium & invisibilium.
units.tr: 18. We believe in one God, the Father almighty, maker of heaven and earth, of all things visible and invisible.

units.la: 19. Credimus & in unum Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, filium Dei unigenitum, natum ex Patre ante omnia saecula, & ante omnia tempora; lumen de lumine, Deum verum de Deo vero; natum, non factum; naturalem, non adoptivum; per quem omnia condita sunt caelestia & terrestria, unius essentiae & unius substantiae cum Patre.
units.tr: 19. We also believe in one Lord, our Jesus Christ, the only-begotten Son of God, born of the Father before all ages and before all time; light of light, true God of true God; begotten, not made; natural, not adoptive; through whom all things in heaven and on earth were made; of one essence and one substance with the Father.

units.la: 20. Credimus & in Spiritum S. Deum verum, vivificatorem omnium, a patre & filio procedentem, cum patre & filio coadorandum & conglorificandum.
units.tr: 20. We also believe in the Holy Spirit, the true God, the giver of life to all, proceeding from the Father and the Son, to be adored together with the Father and the Son and glorified together.

units.la: 21. Credimus eandem sanctam Trinitatem, Patrem & Filium & Spiritum sanctum, unius essentiae, substantiae, unius potentiae & unius essentiae tres personas, & singulam quamque in Trinitate personam, plenum Deum: & totas tres personas unum Deum omnipotentem; Patrem ingenitum, Filium genitum, Spiritum sanctum procedentem ex Patre & Filio: nec Patrem aliquando coepisse, sed sicut semper est Deus, ita semper & patet est, quia semper habuit filium. Aeternus Pater, aeternus Filius, aeternus & Spiritus sanctus, ex patre filioque procedens. Unus Deus omnipotens, Pater & Filius & Spiritus sanctus: ubique praesens, ubique totus. Deus aeternus, ineffabilis, incomprehensibilis. In qua sancta Trinitate, nulla est persona vel tempore posterior, vel gradu inferior, vel perfectione minor: sed per omnia aequalis Patri Filius, aequalis Patri & Filio Spiritus sanctus divinitate, voluntate, operatione & gloria. Alius tamen Pater, alius in persona Filius, alius persona Spiritus sanctus. Non aliud, sed unum, natura, potentia, & essentia Deus Pater, & Filius, & Spiritus sanctus.
units.tr: 21. We believe that the same holy Trinity, the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, is of one essence, one substance, and one power; and that the three persons of one essence, and each single person in the Trinity, is full God; and that the three persons together are one almighty God: the Father unbegotten, the Son begotten, the Holy Spirit proceeding from the Father and the Son. The Father never began, but as he is always God, so he is always Father, because he always had the Son. The Father is eternal, the Son is eternal, the Holy Spirit is eternal, proceeding from the Father and the Son. One almighty God, Father and Son and Holy Spirit: present everywhere, whole everywhere; eternal, ineffable, incomprehensible God. In this holy Trinity no person is either later in time, or lower in rank, or less in perfection; but the Son is equal to the Father in all things, and the Holy Spirit is equal to the Father and the Son in divinity, will, operation and glory. Yet the Father is one person, the Son is another person, the Holy Spirit is another person. They are not other, but one: God the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, one in nature, power and essence.

units.la: 22. Credimus ex hac sancta Trinitate Filii tantummodo personam, pro salute generis humani de Spiritu sancto & Maria Virgine incarnatam: ut quemadmodum divinitate Dei Patris Filius, effectus in humanitate hominis matris filius: perfectus in divinitate Deus, perfectus in humanitate homo: Deus ante omnia saecula, homo in fine saeculi verus in utraque, subsistentia Dei filius; non putativus, sed verus; non adoptione, sed proprietate. Una persona Deus & homo, unus mediator Dei & hominum, in forma Dei aequalis Patri, in forma servi minor Patre: in firma Dei creator, in forma servi redemptor. Unus in utroque Dei filius proprius & perfectus, ad implendam humanae salutis dispensationem passus est vera carnis passione, mortuus vera corporis suo morte. Surrexit vera carnis suae resurrectione & vera animae resumptione: & eodem corpore, quo passus est, & resurrexit. Ascendit in caelum, sedens in dextera Dei Patris: & in eadem forma, qua ascendit, venturus judicare vivos ac mortuos. Cuius regni non erit finis.
units.tr: 22. We believe that from this holy Trinity the person of the Son alone was incarnate, from the Holy Spirit and the Virgin Mary, for the salvation of the human race; so that, just as the Son of God the Father is by divinity, so he was made by humanity the son of a human mother: perfect God in divinity, perfect man in humanity; God before all ages, man at the end of the age; true in both; the Son of God in subsistence; not seeming, but true; not by adoption, but by property. One person, God and man, one mediator between God and men: in the form of God equal to the Father, in the form of a servant less than the Father; in the form of God the creator, in the form of a servant the redeemer. One and the same, the proper and perfect Son of God, to fulfil the dispensation of human salvation, suffered in the true passion of the flesh, and died in the true death of his body. He rose by the true resurrection of his flesh and by the true reunion of his soul, and rose in the same body in which he suffered. He ascended into heaven, sitting at the right hand of God the Father; and in the same form in which he ascended he will come to judge the living and the dead. Of his kingdom there will be no end.

units.la: 23. Praedicamus unam sanctam Dei Ecclesiam toto orbe diffusam locis separatam, fide & charitate conjunctam: & veram remissionem peccatorum in eadem Ecclesia, live per baptismum, live per poenitentiam, divina donante gratia, & bona voluntate hominis cooperante.
units.tr: 23. We proclaim one holy Church of God, spread through the whole world, separated in places but joined in faith and charity; and a true remission of sins in the same Church, whether through baptism or through repentance, with divine grace granting and the good will of man cooperating.

units.la: 24. Credimus & omnes homines resurrecturos esse, & singulos secundum sua opera judicari, impios aeternis supplicis damnandos cum Diabolo & Angelis ejus; sanctos vero aeterna gloria coronandos cum Christo & sanctis Angelis ejus in saeculorum saecula.
units.tr: 24. We believe also that all men will rise again, and that each will be judged according to his works: the impious to be condemned to eternal punishments with the devil and his angels, but the holy to be crowned with eternal glory with Christ and his holy angels, for ages of ages.

units.la: 25. Haec est fides Catholica, & ideo nostra: optamus etiam & vestra: quia unus Deus baptisma, & unus Dominus noster Jesus Christus, qui est Deus verus & verus homo, verus Deus & verus Dei filius, in utraque natura unus idemque mediator Dei & hominum, homo Iesus Christus, qui sit Deus nedum in saeculum.
units.tr: 25. This is the Catholic faith, and therefore ours; we desire that it be yours also: because there is one God, one baptism, and one our Lord Jesus Christ, who is true God and true man, true God and true Son of God, in both natures one and the same mediator between God and men, the man Jesus Christ, who is God, not only for this age.

units.la: 26. Hanc ipsam vos, Fratres carissimi, firmiter tenere in communi praedicamus: & si aliquem ut in quolibet verbo sensus corrigere vosmetipsos, & ad unitatem sanctae Dei Ecclesiae pura lectio... firmate, & contentiones nominum novitatesque vocum devitate, quia juxta Apostolum, novi haereticus sui ... porte, quam quod ... de tali solo orbe diffusa tenet Ecclesia: Sub tegmine ... requiescite, ne vos a diabolo rapacitas (ut fors universi) nefando gutture devorent. Reduce ad ... pium matris Ecclesiæ gremium; illa vos foveat & nutriat, donec accurratis in virum perfectum, & in plenitudinem corporis Christi. Habere nos cooperatores salutis vestræ, Catholicæ pacis auxiliatores; & societas vestra sit in Christo Jesu Domino nostro, qui vos nobiscum incorruptos & immaculatos fide pariter & opere custodiat, & constituat ante conspectum gloriæ suæ incontaminatos & irreprehensibiles, & perpetuæ hæreditatis hæredes pariter perficiat in æternum, AMEN.
units.tr: 26. We proclaim to you, dearest brothers, that you hold this same faith firmly in common; and if anyone ... in any word of sense, correct yourselves, and to the unity of the holy Church of God ... hold fast, and avoid contentions over names and novelties of words; for according to the Apostle, ... of a new heretic ... the gate, which the Church holds spread throughout the whole world. Rest under the covering, lest the devil's rapacity (as a wolf of the universe) devour you with his wicked throat. Return to the pious bosom of Mother Church; let her cherish and nourish you, until you grow into a perfect man, and into the fullness of the body of Christ. May we be fellow workers for your salvation and helpers of catholic peace; and may your fellowship be in Christ Jesus our Lord, who keeps you with us, uncorrupted and unblemished in faith and in deed alike, and sets you, unstained and blameless, before the sight of his glory, and makes you heirs together of eternal inheritance for ever. AMEN.

units.la: CAROLI MAGNI IMP. AUG. CAPITULARE De non adorandis imaginibus, CONTRA CONSTANTINI VII. IMP. CONSTANT- INOPOLITANI ET HIRENÆ MATRIS DECRETUM ET SYNODUM Nicænam II. Pseudoseptimam Oecumenicam sive universalem: composi- tum & publicatum in Concilio Francofordiensi, & Hadria- no Papæ missum, Anno Domini DCCXCIV. IN NOMINE DOMINI ET SALVAT- ORIS NOSTRI JESU CHRISTI. INCIPIT OPVS
units.tr: The Capitulare of the Emperor Charles the Great, Augustus, on not adoring images, against the decree and the synod of Constantine VII, emperor of Constantinople, and of his mother Irene, which they call the Second Nicene Synod, the Seventh Ecumenical or universal one. Composed and published at the Council of Frankfurt and sent to Pope Hadrian, in the year of the Lord 794. IN THE NAME OF THE LORD AND OF OUR SAVIOUR JESUS CHRIST. HERE BEGINS THE WORK

units.la: Illustrissimi et excellentissimi seu spectabilis viri Karoli nutu Dei, Regis Francorum, Gallias, Germaniam, Italiamque, sive earum finitimas provincias Domino opitulante regentis, contra synodum quæ in partibus Græciæ pro adorandis imaginibus stolide sive arroganter gesta est.
units.tr: Of the most illustrious, most excellent, or respected man Charles, by the will of God King of the Franks, who by the Lord's help rules Gaul, Germany and Italy, or the provinces bordering them, against the synod which was foolishly or arrogantly held in the regions of Greece in favour of adoring images.

units.la: PRÆFATIO.
units.tr: PREFACE.

units.la: Ecclesia mater nostra, preciosissimo sponsi Christi sanguine redempta, & regeneratione salutaris gurgitis lota, & salutifero edulio corporis, & haustu sanguinis sanctificata, & nectareo liquoris unguine delibuta, & per universum orbem terrarum in pace diffusa: aliquando externa, aliquando intestina perpetitur bella, aliquando exterorum concurrit incursibus, aliquando civium pulsatur tumultibus. Nonnunquam videlicet incredulorum vel hæreseorum impellitur infestationibus, nonnunquam vero schismaticorum vel arrogantium turbatur simultatibus. Est enim arca salvanda intra se continens animas, cujus rypum antiqui illius patris arca gerebat, quæ in hujus sæculi fluctuans diluvii absque naufragii periculo transigit procellas, & nescit mortiferis præsentis sæculi allurementibus cedere, nec infestantium diversarum potestatum obsidione fatiscere, sed illo pro ea & maxime ea pugnante, qui positus est in ea murus, dicente propheta, Urbs fortitudinis nostræ Salvator, ponetur in ea murus, & antemurale, & qui super eius muros constituit custodes, qui tota die & tota nocte in perpetuum non tacebunt, ad versus resistens, & tumultuosas inquietudines tolerat, & ad veræ fidei confessionem convenientibus in gremio suscepti, & eidem confessioni obstinata mente reluctantibus abdicans, inconcussa et intemerata perseverat, & cum David canere non cessat, Sæpe expugnaverunt me à juventute mea, sæpe expugnaverunt me à juventute mea, etenim non potuerunt mihi: quæ mecum sancta per partes mysterium sanctæ Trinitatis exponit, dum & verba sua auribus divinæ majestatis psallendi melodiam, quam sine intermissione exhibet, deprecatur; & clamorem intelligendum, cordis affectum, qui non auribus carnalibus, sed ineffabilibus divinæ majestatis audibus mirabiliter excipitur, devota mente exorat, & orationis suæ vocem intendendam expostulat, ut scilicet declaret hanc esse orationem perfectam, quam mentis affectus ardentis inflammat. Et quamquam metaphoricos mutatis verbis sensus nostros immisceat, diviuam tamen naturam credit non partibus membrorum discernenda discernere, sed una virtute cuncta peragere, qui ea quæ à nobis vidente audit, & quæ cogitavimus sive cogitaturi sumus, intro inspicit: nec quicquam ejus ineffabili lumini potestatis condi. Auribus etenim verba percipere, clamorem intelligere, vociferationis intendere, quamquam iterate sub varietate verborum, per id locutionis genus, quod ârhetoribus metaphorice dicitur, proferantur: trina tamen repetitio unum idemque significat, quæ etiam in invocatione recte & Deus, sive Domini, dum dicit, Rex meus & Deus meus, quoniam ad te orabo Domine. Tres personas & substantiam in divinitate se credere & fateri demonstrat, cum trium nominum invocationi, non pluralia, sed singularia verba interserit. Est enim sancta mater, et tunc maculata, est præclara, est mater, est & fecunda, quæ & virginitatem amittere nescit, & filios generare non definit: quæ supra omnia mundi advertitatibus ferunt, tanto auctoribus sive excellentioribus virtutibus diquanto plus præmitur, tanto altius exaltatur, quam propheta per ethopœiam Deo sic introducit, Cum invocarem te, exaudisti me Deus iustitiæ meæ, in tribulatione dilatasti me. Cujus quorum regni gubernacula domino tribuente suscepimus, necesse est, ut in ejus defensione, & ab ea expositione, Christo auxiliante, toto annisu certemus, ut ab eo boni servi & fideles nominomine censeri valeamus. Quod quidem non solùm nobis, quibus in hujus sæculi procellosis fluctibus ad regendum commissa est, sed etiam cunctis ab ejus uberibus enutritis sollicitè observandum est: ita tamen ut ab ejus unione, qui ejus membrum esse dinoscitur nullatenus abscedat. Quoniam qui cum ea non est, adversus eam est: & qui cum ea non colligit, spargit. Hujus ergo rei causa loqui compellit, quod non fine quodam animi mœrore prosequimur, quippe qui cum infirmantibus infirmari, & cum scandalizantibus uri Apostolico perdocemur exemplo. Inflammavit igitur ventósæ arrogantiæ inflata ambitio, & vanæ laudis infolentissimus appetitus, quosdam orientalium partium non solùm reges, sed etiam sacerdotes, adeò ut postposita sana sobriaque doctrina, & parvi pendentes illud Apostolicum, Siquis Evangelizaverit vobis, praeter id quod Evangelizatum est, & sit Angelus sit, anathema sit, & transgredientes contra propheticam institutionem terminos majorum, per infames & ineptissimas synodos Ecclesiæ inferre conentur, quod nec Salvator, nec Apostoli intulisse noscuntur: & dum sublimare conantur sinè laudis fastigium, magnum adcumulent suis animabus deliquium: dumq; sinorum gestorum ordinem volunt mandare memoriæ posteritatis, discindunt vinculum Ecclesiasticæ unitatis. Gesta sanè est ante hos annos in Bithiniæ partibus quædam synodus tam incautæ tamq; indiscretæ procacitatis, ut imagines in ornamentis Ecclesiæ & memoria rerum gestarum ab antiquis positas incautè abolerent abdicatione: quodq; Dominus de idolis præcepit, hoc illi de cunctis imaginibus perpetrarent: nescientes, imaginem esse genus, idolum verò speciem: & speciem ad genus, genus ad speciem referri non posse. Nam cùm penè omne idolum imago sit, non omnis imago idolum. Alterius & longè alterius definitionis est idolum, alterius imago: cùm videlicet istæ ad ornamentum vel ad res gestas monstrandas fiant: illud autem nunquam nisi ad miserorum animas sacrilego ritu, & vana superstitione injiciendas: & imago ad aliquid, idolum ad seipsum dicatur. Qui nimirum tantæ excæcatis caligine obtenebrati fuerunt, ut cunctis, qui eas habere in Ecclesiis noscebantur, vel habituri erant, anathematizatis, inter cæteros errores hoc etiam suo errori inferetent, quòd Rex eorum Constantinus eos ab idolis liberâsset: & ei qui exultavit, ut gigas ad currendam viam de quo dictum est, Ecce vicit leo de tribu Juda, radix David, & triumphanti mundi spolia secum reportavit, Victoriæ titulum derogare cupientes, Regi suo adnectererunt: cùm non de eorum rege, sed de vero triumphatore Christo propheta prædixerit, Ecce Dominus ascendet super nubem levem, & ingrediétur Ægyptum, & commovebuntur simulacra Ægypti à facie ejus: Nubem levem, corpus videlicet humanum, quod ex virgine adsumpserat, nulla humanæ commixtionis sorde prægravatum: Ægyptum mundum volens intelligi: quod & per Hieremiam penè iisdem verbis se dudum facturum esse promiserat, dicens, Disperdam simulacra, & cessare faciam idola de Memphis. Gesta præterea est ferme ante trienium & altera synodus illis in partibus, ab eorum qui priorem gesserant successoribus, vel à plurisque, qui in priore fuisse narrantur: quæ tamen quamquam à priore distet voto, non tamen distat errore: & si dilpar est negotio, est tamen compar flagitio: & cùm fit posterior tempore, non tamen est posterior crimine. Nec immeritò in unius baratri cœnosum lacum, quamquam per diversa fluitantes, confluere videntur, quæ ab unius jactantiæ & vanæ laudis fonte scaturiisse creduntur. Hæc enim, anathematizata & abominata cum suis auctoribus priore, imagines, quas prior nec etiam cernere permiserat, adorare compellit: & ubicumq; sive in divinæ Scripturæ locis, sive in sanctorum patrum commentariis, quamcunque repererunt imaginum mentionem ergo suæ voluntatis arbitrium verterunt in adorationem. Nec minoris absurditatis spiritus hi connectuntur in habere & adorare, quam illi connexi sunt in imagine & idolo, cùm illi imaginem & idolum, isti habere & adorare, unum esse putarunt, quæ tamen à se invicem distant, & diversitate rei, & societate prædicamenti: quippe cum unum illorum sit habitus, alterum agere. Nam illa etsi magna distent differentia, saltem in eo jungVuntur, quòd unum species, alterum genus est: hæc verò necgenere, nec specie, nec ulla hujuscemodi societate sibi cohærent, cùm & adorari possint, quæ non habentur, & habere, quæ non adorantur. Sicque rejectis moderaminis reliquaculis, & neglecto quod ab antiquis non incongruè dictum est proverbio, Ne quid nimis, mediocritatis callé transmisso, per devia gradiuntur: veluti siquis cuidam multiloquio vacanti, temperamentum in loquendo indicere curans, ille è contrario adeò silentio studeat, ut mutus efficiatur, & cui dedecus ingerebat inordinata loquacitas, dedecus nihilominus ingerat desidiosa taciturnitas. Aut si quis medicus agrotantem temulentiæ arguat, ille putans, se medici partes dictis, non solùm vini, sed etiam laticum sibi interdicat humorem: adeò ut qui dudum languebat nimio vini hausta maceratus, omni sibi liquore interdictio, langueat sit arefactus: cum tamen, etsi diversa sit causa langnoris, unus tamen sit effectus defidiosi erroris. Interea cùm in neutra parte neque isti, neque illi temperantiæ teneantur habenis, sed utrique præcipites per abrupta discurrant, & disparı cursu ferantur: uno tamen occursu ispronsæ Christi Ecclesiæ, cui ipse dicit in Canticis Canticorum, Tota speciosa es amica mea, & macula non est in te, maculam inferre conantur: dum & illi ei bene habita abjicere, & isti bene habitis male uti suadent: dum scilicet & illi ei ornamenta auferre studeant: & isti eam imagines adorare permovent: quæ duo mala, ut præfati sumus, de jactantiæ fonte pullularunt. Dumque volunt humanos favores, & vocari ab hominibus Rabbi, & suas laudes suis apicibus præfigunt, nec attendunt, quòd per quendam sapientem dicitur: Laudent te aly, & non os tuum, extranei, & non lingua tua: reliquis prioribus Patrum traditionibus, qui imagines non colere sanxerunt, sed in ornamento Ecclesiarum habere siverunt, novas & insolitas Ecclesiæ nituntur inferre constitutiones, quibus ei maculam potius quam decorem adscribant. Nam si novas constitutiones Ecclesiæ ingerere jactantia est, (chisina schisma est: quod tamen in Ecclesia fieri non debet, quod si schisma est, macula est quae in sponsa esse negatur. Signatur novas constitutiones Ecclesiae ingerere jactantia est, macula proculdubio est, quae in sponsa esse negatur. Unde datur intelligi non cum esse amicum sponsi, qui adeo suae laudis vult cumulare cacumen, ut per errorum notas non vereatur Ecclesiasticum obtundere acumen: ac per hoc sponsam maculam non decet, eam ei nullus conari debet imprimere: quam si nullus conari debet imprimere, qui conatur, sponso injuriam facit. Signatur sponsam macula non decet, & revera non decet, qui conatur imprimere, sponso injuriam facit. Nos denique propheticis, Evangelicis & Apostolicis Scripturis contenti, & sanctorum orthodoxorum patrum, qui nullatenus in suis dogmatibus ab eo, qui est via, veritas & vita deviaverunt, institutis inburi, & sanctas & universales sex synodos, quae pro variis haereticorum infestationibus a sanctis & venerabilibus patribus gestae sunt, sapientes, omnes novitates vocum, & shultiloquas adinventiones abjicimus: & non solum non suscipimus, verum etiam tanquam purgamenta despicimus, licut & eam, quae propter adorandarum imaginum impudentissimam traditionem in Bithiniae partibus gesta est, synodum. Cujus Scripturae textus eloquentia sensuque carens ad nos usque pervenit. Contra cujus errores ideo scribere compulli sumus, ut licubi forte aut manus renentium, aut aures audientium inquinare tentaverit, nostyli divinarum Scripturarum authoritate armari invectione pellatur: & inertem, vel potius interim orientali de parte venientem hostem occidua in parte per nos favente Deo allata sanctorum patrum sententia feriat. Quod opus adgrelli sumus cum conhibentia sacerdotum in regno a Deo nobis concesso Catholicis gregibus praelatorum, non arrogantiae supercilio, sed zelo Dei & veritatis studio quoniam licet justis & honestis rebus inhaerere sanctum, ita nimirum pessimis & inordinatis animum addommodare peccare est. Unde & David, quod societates malorum fugerit, Deo quasi purum sacrificium offert, cum dicit, Odio habui congregationes malignantium, & cum impiis non sedebo. Et Josaphat Rex Juda, eo quod Israelitice gentis pessimo regi amicitiis junctus sit, a Domino non arguitur per prophetam. Cum igitur praefatarum duarum synodorum conditores, nec illius imperitiae sermonem habeant, quae se Apostolus impetritum dicit sermone, sed non scientia: necillius eloquentiae cum spiritali sensu nitorem, de quo ex persona sanctorum praedicatorum, in Canticis Canticorum Ecclesiae dicitur, Murenulas aureas faciemus tibi vermiculatas argento: mitum ducimus quae tantae vanitatis vento inflati sint, ut eas non solum agitare praesumpserint, sed etiam sex venerabilibus synodis adnumerare conati sint: quarum neutra quomodo non septima post Nicenam, sed aut tertia, priore servata post Ariminensem, aut secunda priore destructa conputari debeat, in sequentibus, cum res exegerit, diligentius adnuente Domino disputabimus, quae scilicet haud secus sex synodi quiparanda sunt, quam Rubenitarum & Gaditarum, & dimidiae tribus Manasse altari, quod per legislatorem Domino jubente conditum est, aequiparari potuit: cujus autores Israelitici gladium furere vastaret, nisi fraternas iras supplex confessio mixta precibus praeveniret. Nos denique Esaiae vaticinio doctus, qui dicit, Hac via ambulate in ea, non declinabitis ab ea, neque ad dexteram, neque ad sinistram: Esai.30. & doctoris gentium praedicatione admoniti, qui nos viam regiam tenere instituit, imagines in ornatu Ecclesiarum & memoria rerum gestarum habentes; & solum Deum adorantes & ejus sanctis opportunam venerationem exhibentes, nec cum illis frangimus, nec cum istis adoramus, sed illius inepti... synodi Scripturam, quae non solum illa locutione caret, qua parva submisse, mediocria temperate, magna granditer proferuntur; sed etiam pedestris sermonis modum negligit, abnuentes, sed tutoris nostri, sermonis videlicet Dominici nitinunt fieri usquequaque sequaces. Quoniam igitur & patrum anathematizantium filios, & filiorum anathematizantium patres, mixtum in praefata synodo hebetudinis continentur discursus, mixtam utrisque reprehensionem nostram, favente Domino, dirigit stylus, nihil indiscussum, nihil intactum, nihil silenti cavernis obstrusum praeteriens: nisi quae forte difficultas inordinati sermonis nostro intellectui impertire negaverit, aut pueriles disputationes cohibente nostro sermone persequi despexerit.
units.tr: Our mother the Church, redeemed by the most precious blood of the Bridegroom Christ, washed in the regenerating flood of salvation, sanctified by the life-giving food of his body and the draught of his blood, and anointed with the nectar-like oil, and spread in peace throughout the whole world, sometimes suffers external wars, sometimes internal ones; sometimes she is attacked by the incursions of outsiders, sometimes battered by the tumults of her own citizens. Sometimes she is assailed by the hostility of unbelievers and heretics, sometimes troubled by the rivalries of schismatics and the proud. For she is an ark that must be saved, containing souls within itself; the ark of that ancient father bore her image. Tossed by the flood of this age, she passes through the storms without danger of shipwreck, and does not yield to the deadly allurements of the present age, nor does she grow weary under the siege of the various hostile powers. For he who is the wall set in her, fighting for her and above all in her, the Saviour (as the prophet says, "Salvation will be the city of our strength; a wall and a bulwark will be set in her"), has placed guards on her walls, who will not be silent day or night for ever. They resist and endure the tumultuous disturbances; they receive into the bosom those who come to the confession of the true faith, and with a steadfast mind they reject those who struggle against that confession. She remains unshaken and undefiled, and does not cease to sing with David, "Often they have attacked me from my youth, often they have attacked me from my youth; yet they have not prevailed against me." She, the holy one, sets forth with her own parts the mystery of the holy Trinity, while she prays that her words be heard by the ears of the divine majesty, to which she offers without interruption the melody of the psalm. With a devout mind she pleads that her cry be understood as the affection of the heart, which is received wondrously not by carnal ears but by the ineffable hearing of the divine majesty, and she asks that the voice of her prayer be attended to, that is, that this be declared to be the perfect prayer, which the flame of an ardent mind kindles. And although she mixes in our senses with metaphorical language, changing the words, she believes that the divine nature, which is not to be distinguished by parts of members, accomplishes all things by one power; it hears what we see, and it looks within at what we have thought or are about to think, and nothing is hidden from its ineffable light. For to receive words with the ears, to understand a cry, to attend to a shout, though these are expressed in varied words, and repeated, by that kind of speech which rhetoricians call metaphorical, the threefold repetition nevertheless signifies one and the same thing. This also rightly demonstrates, in the invocation, "God" and "Lord," when she says, "My King and my God, for to you I will pray, O Lord," that she believes and confesses three persons and one substance in the Godhead, since in the invocation of the three names she inserts not plural but singular verbs. She is holy mother, and yet she is stained; she is glorious, she is mother, and she is fruitful, who never loses her virginity and never ceases to bear children. Those things which bear the adversities of the world above all else, are exalted the higher, with the more excellent virtues of their authors, the more they are pressed down; as the prophet introduces God speaking in this manner, by prosopopoeia: "When I called upon you, you heard me, O God of my righteousness; in tribulation you enlarged me." Since by the Lord's gift we have taken up the reins of the kingdom whose governance has been entrusted to us, it is necessary that we strive with all our effort, with Christ's help, in its defence and in its exposition, so that we may be counted by him as good and faithful servants. This must be carefully observed not only by us, to whom the task of ruling has been committed amid the stormy waves of this age, but also by all who have been nourished at her breasts; yet in such a way that no one separates himself from her unity, which is recognised as her member. For whoever is not with her is against her, and whoever does not gather with her scatters. For this reason the matter compels me to speak, which I pursue not without some sorrow of mind; for we are taught by the apostolic example to be weakened with the weak and to burn with those who cause offence. Therefore the swollen ambition of windy arrogance and the most insolent desire for empty praise have inflamed certain men of the eastern regions, not only kings but also priests, to such an extent that, putting aside sound and sober teaching, and making little of that apostolic word, "If anyone preaches to you a gospel other than what has been preached, let him be anathema," and transgressing against the prophetic command the boundaries set by our forefathers, they try to bring into the Church, through infamous and most foolish synods, things which neither the Saviour nor the apostles are known to have introduced. While they strive to raise their own glory to a height without praise, they heap up for their souls a great deficit; and while they wish to commit the order of their own acts to the memory of posterity, they sever the bond of ecclesiastical unity. Indeed, some years ago in the regions of Bithynia there was held a synod of such careless and indiscreet boldness that they recklessly abolished by an edict the images which the ancients had placed in the ornaments of the Church and in the memory of past deeds; and what the Lord commanded about idols, they carried out against all images, not knowing that an image is the genus, while an idol is the species, and that the species cannot be referred to the genus, nor the genus to the species. For although almost every idol is an image, not every image is an idol. The idol is of a quite different definition from the image: images are made for ornament or for showing forth deeds done, whereas idols are never made except for the souls of the wretched to be seized by sacrilegious rite and vain superstition. And an image is said to be relative to something, an idol to itself. Those men were so blinded by the darkness of such great blindness that, having anathematised all who were known, or were about to be, to have such images in their churches, they added among their other errors this also: that their king Constantine had freed them from idols. And since he who rejoiced, like a giant to run his course, of whom it is said, "Behold, the lion of the tribe of Judah, the root of David has conquered," and who carried back the spoils of the triumphant world with him, they, wishing to take away the title of victory, attached it to their king; whereas the prophet foretold, not of their king but of the true conqueror Christ: "Behold, the Lord will ascend upon a light cloud, and will enter Egypt, and the idols of Egypt will be moved at his presence." The light cloud is the human body which he took from the Virgin, not burdened by any filth of human mixture; and by Egypt he means the world. Through Jeremiah he had long before promised that he would do this almost in the same words, saying, "I will destroy the images, and will cause the idols to cease from Memphis." Moreover, about three years ago another synod was held in those regions, by successors of those who had held the former one, or by many who are said to have been in the former one. Although this one differs from the former in intention, it does not differ in error; and if it is unlike in its business, it is equal in its disgrace; and although it is later in time, it is not later in crime. Nor without reason do they seem to flow together into the muddy pool of one abyss, though wandering by different ways, since they are believed to have gushed from the one fountain of boastfulness and empty praise. For this later synod, the former one, with its authors, having been anathematised and abominated, compels us to adore images, which the former would not even allow to be looked at; and wherever they have found any mention of images, whether in the places of divine Scripture or in the commentaries of the holy Fathers, they have turned it into adoration according to the arbitrary will of their own choice. Nor are these spirits joined in having and adoring by a less absurd connection than that by which the others were joined in image and idol; for those thought image and idol to be one, and these think having and adoring to be one, though these are distinct both in the difference of the thing and in the relation of the category. For the one is a state of having, the other a doing. For although those two differ greatly, at least they are joined in this, that one is species and the other genus; but these are not bound together by genus, nor species, nor any such relation, since things which are not had can be adored, and things which are not adored can be had. And so, rejecting the restraints of moderation and neglecting the proverb, not inaptly used by the ancients, "Nothing in excess," they pass by the path of the mean and go astray through byways. It is like someone who, when a man given to much talk seeks to prescribe restraint in speaking, is so eager for silence in reply that he becomes dumb, and the disgrace which unbridled talkativeness brought on him is equalled by the disgrace of idle taciturnity. Or as when a physician rebukes a patient for drunkenness, and the patient, thinking he has taken up the physician's role, forbids himself not only wine but also the drink of water, so that he who was languishing from excessive wine, soaked in drink, now, forbidden every liquid, languishes and is dried up; though the cause of the languor is different, the effect of idle error is one. Meanwhile, since neither party holds to the reins of temperance, but both rush headlong through precipices and are carried on unequal courses, they nevertheless attempt, by one encounter, to bring a stain upon the beautiful Church of Christ, to whom he himself says in the Song of Songs, "You are all fair, my love, and there is no spot in you." For these men persuade her to cast away the good things she has, and those men persuade her to misuse the good things she has; they strive, that is, to remove her ornaments, while these urge her to adore images. These two evils, as we have said, have sprouted from the fountain of boastfulness. And while they wish for human favours, and to be called Rabbi by men, and set their own praises on their own letters, they do not heed what a certain wise man says: "Let others praise you, and not your own mouth; strangers, and not your own lips." Leaving aside the earlier traditions of the Fathers, who decreed that images should not be worshipped but allowed to be kept as ornaments of the churches, they strive to introduce new and unusual constitutions into the Church, by which they attribute to her a stain rather than a beauty. For if to introduce new constitutions into the Church is arrogance, it is schism; but this ought not to happen in the Church; and if it is schism, it is a stain, which is denied to be in the bride. Undoubtedly, to introduce new constitutions into the Church is arrogance, a stain indeed, which is said not to be in the bride. Hence it is clear that he is not a friend of the Bridegroom who wishes so greatly to heap up the peak of his own praise that, through the marks of errors, he does not hesitate to blunt the ecclesiastical edge; and therefore it does not befit the bride to be stained, and no one ought to attempt to impress a stain upon her; and if no one ought to attempt to impress it, he who attempts it does an injury to the Bridegroom. Finally, we, content with the prophetic, Gospel and apostolic Scriptures, and with the orthodox Fathers, who in their doctrines never turned aside from him who is the way, the truth and the life, instructed by them, and we reject all novelties of words and all wordy inventions, and the six holy and universal synods, which were held by the holy and venerable Fathers against the various assaults of heretics, we wise men not only do not receive but despise as refuse; and likewise that synod which was held in the regions of Bithynia on account of the most shameless tradition of adoring images. Its text, lacking eloquence and sense, has come down to us as far as this. We have been compelled to write against its errors, so that wherever it may have tried to defile either the hands of those who handle it or the ears of those who hear it, it may be driven off by the authority of the divine Scriptures, armed by our invective, and so that, with the favour of God, the sentence of the holy Fathers, brought from the western part, may strike that enemy which comes, sluggish, from the eastern part. We have undertaken this work with the consent of the priests and of the prelates of the Catholic flocks in the kingdom conceded to us by God; not with the haughtiness of arrogance, but with zeal for God and devotion to the truth. For although it is holy to cling to just and honourable things, so surely it is sinful to apply the mind to the most wicked and disorderly things. Hence David, because he fled the company of evildoers, offers himself to God as a pure sacrifice, when he says, "I have hated the assembly of the wicked, and I will not sit with the ungodly." And Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, because he joined himself in friendship to the worst king of the Israelite people, is rebuked by the Lord through the prophet. Since therefore the authors of the two synods mentioned have neither the unskilled speech of which the apostle says he is "rude in speech, but not in knowledge," nor that eloquence with spiritual sense and brightness, of which the Church is spoken of in the Song of Songs, in the person of the holy preachers, "We will make you chains of gold, inlaid with silver," we marvel that men so swollen with the wind of such vanity have not only presumed to bring these synods forward, but have even tried to count them among the six venerable synods; neither of which, in what way it ought not to be counted as the seventh after the Nicene, but rather as the third (the former being kept after the Ariminian) or as the second (the former being destroyed), we shall, in what follows, when the matter requires it, discuss more carefully with the Lord's assistance. For they are to be equated with the six synods no more than the altar which the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh built, by the Lawgiver's command, could be equated with the altar of the Lord; for the Israelites, its authors, were ready to waste the sword in fury, unless a suppliant confession mixed with prayers had anticipated their brotherly anger. Finally, taught by the prophecy of Isaiah, who says, "Walk in this way, and do not turn aside from it, either to the right hand or to the left" (Isa. 30), and admonished by the preaching of the teacher of the nations, who taught us to keep the royal way, having images in the ornament of the churches and in the memory of past deeds, and worshipping God alone while giving fitting honour to his saints, we neither break with those men nor adore with these; but we strive to be in every way followers of the Scripture of that foolish synod, which not only lacks that style by which small things are set forth humbly, middle things with moderation, great things with grandeur, but also neglects the manner of plain speech, and refuses, but of our guardian, that is, of the Lord's word. Since therefore the synod's discourse, confused and dull, contains both the sons of the anathematising fathers and the fathers of the anathematising sons, our pen, with the Lord's favour, directs a mixed rebuke at both, passing over nothing unexamined, nothing untouched, nothing hidden in the caves of silence; except perhaps what the difficulty of the disordered speech has refused to make intelligible to our understanding, or what, restraining our speech, we have disdained to pursue as childish disputes.

units.la: LIBER PRIMUS. CAPUT I. De eo quod Constantinus & Harenā in suis scriptis dicunt, Per eum qui conregnat nobis Deus.
units.tr: BOOK I, CHAPTER I. On what Constantine and Harenā say in their writings: God who co-reigns with us.

units.la: Plerumque humana fragilitas suae impossibilitatis metas excedit, & quanto se ultra quam debet extollit, tanto ab eo, qui in altis habitat, & humilia respicit in caelo & in terra, recedit: quanto quoque ad eum, qui excelsus super omnes gentes est, perfublimitatem adpropinquare conatur, tanto ab eo propensius elongatur. Quae si quidem suae conditionis non negligat, & superate petere nitens, ad humiliora se devota mente submittat, poterit se inclinando eo conscendere, quo exaltando nosceba-tur descendere: & quanto se prostraverit humo, tanto fiat proxima caelo. Cum ergo nostrum esse tantum differt a Dei esse, & nostrum vivere ab ejus vivere, & nostrum regnare ab ejus regnare, dolenda potius quam admirenda est illorum vecordia, qui inter caetera quae libet dicere ut usurpant, Deum sibi conregnare etiam dicunt. Illius enim esse, esse tantum novitatis fuisse vel futurũ esse, non novit. Non habet n. partè æternitatis, quâ nos tempus dicimus. & in præsens, præteritum & futurũ dividimus, sed totius æternitatis in suæ essentiæ incommutabilitate integritatem habens, esse tantum ei est. Unde & sancto Moysi dixit: Ego sum, qui sum, &c., Qui est, misit me ad vos. Nostrũ autem esse, quibus præterita in recordatione, præsentia in intuitu, futura in expectatione, illius essentiæ conparatum non esse est. Vivere namq; ejus, nec initiũ, nec finem, nec mutabilitate ullo modo sentit.
units.tr: Human frailty often oversteps the limits of its own capacity, and the more it raises itself beyond what it ought, the further it withdraws from him who dwells on high and looks down on the lowly in heaven and on earth. The more it strives to approach the supreme height of him who is exalted above all nations, the more it is driven far from him. But if it does not neglect its own condition, and, straining to seek what is above, humbly submits itself to lower things, it will be able, by bowing down, to rise to where it would have been brought low by exalting itself; and the more it casts itself down to the ground, the nearer it will become to heaven. Since, then, our being differs so greatly from God's being, our living from his living, and our reigning from his reigning, the folly of those who, among the many other things they presume to say, also say that God co-reigns with them is to be lamented rather than admired. For God does not know being merely as having been new or as about to be. He has no part of eternity, which we call time, and divide into present, past and future; but possessing the whole of eternity in the unchangeable integrity of his essence, to him being is simply being. Hence he also said to the holy Moses: I am who I am, etc.; He who is has sent me to you. Our being, however, to which the past is present in memory, the present in perception, and the future in expectation, is not comparable to his essence. For his living feels neither beginning, nor end, nor change in any way.

units.la: Unde & in prophetis scribitur; Vivo ego, dicit Dominus, & quidam sanctorum, Vivit Dominus dicere ausi sunt, id est, qui in ea vita vivit, quam nec initium cepit, nec mutabilitas movet, nec finis intercipit. Nostrum autem vivere, ortum & occasum & mutabilitatem patitur: quamquam anima immortalis sit, tamen mutabilis esse dinoscitur: quæ mutabilitas ei plærunque pro morte adscribitur. Unde & primo hominem dictum est, In quacunque die comederis ex eo, morte morieris.. Non quòd statim ut præceptum Domini est transgressus, carnis sit morte multatus, sed quia ab ea sanctitate, in qua Deo proximus stabat, per animi mutabilitatem sit longè digressus. Porrò ejus regnare à nostro regnare, non minùs quàm ejus esse à nostro esse, & ejus vivere à nostro vivere dictat: quippe cujus essentia sicut semper habuit esse & vivere, ita etiam & regnare. Nostrum enim regnare à nostro esse & vivere præcedit, à nostro interire succeditur: quæ dum ita se habeant, magnæ præsumptionis est, Deum sibi quenquam dicere coregnare: cum hoc nec David dicere ausus est, de quo Dominus dixit, Inveni virum secundum cor meum; & illud, Inveni David servum meum: oleo sancto meo unxi eum: nec Salomon, cui à Domino dictum est, Sapientia & scientia data sunt tibi, divitias autem, & subsistentiam & gloriam dabo tibi, ita ut nullus in regibus nec ante te nec post te fuerit similis tui: qui de se quoq; ipse loquitur confidenter, Deus docuit me sapientiam, & intellectum sanctorum cognovi. Nec quisquam de regibus, nec de his, quos meritorum prærogativa suffultos, nec de his, quos superbia usos fuisse Scriptura commemorat, tale quid legitur dixisse. Interea consyllaba in conponendis verbis secundum eos, qui terrariæ collectiam disciplinæ nō nescinunt, pene nihil aliud quàm simul significat ut est, Congregetur omnis Ecclesia Israel: &, convenient ad diem festum, id est, simul in gregem glomeretur, simul veniant: & Apostolus, Si tamen compatiamur, ut & simul glorificemur, id est, conglorificemur; & illud, Super vitrei margiem fontis utere q; consedit, id est, simul sedit: & confessor dicitur simul sedens.
units.tr: Hence it is also written in the prophets: As I live, saith the Lord, and some of the saints have dared to say, The Lord liveth; that is, he who lives in that life which neither had a beginning, nor is moved by change, nor is cut off by an end. Our living, however, suffers rising, setting and change; although the soul is immortal, it is nonetheless known to be changeable, and this change is most often ascribed to it as death. Hence it was also said of the first man: In whatever day you eat of it, you shall surely die. Not that he was punished with death of the flesh as soon as he transgressed the Lord's command, but because through the change of his mind he had wandered far from that holiness in which he stood near to God. Moreover, his reigning, no less than his being and his living, is said to differ from ours; for his essence, just as it always had being and living, so also has reigning. For our reigning is preceded by our being and living, and succeeded by our dying. Since these things stand so, it is a sign of great presumption for anyone to say that he co-reigns with God, since not even David, of whom the Lord said, I have found a man after my own heart, and I have found David my servant; I have anointed him with my holy oil, dared to say this; nor Solomon, to whom the Lord said, Wisdom and knowledge are given to you, and I will give you riches, substance and glory, so that there shall be none like you among the kings before you or after you, who also speaks confidently of himself: God has taught me wisdom, and I have known the understanding of the saints. Nor is any such thing read as having been said by any of the kings, either by those supported by the prerogative of merit, or by those whom Scripture records as having been puffed up with pride. Meanwhile, the particle con- in compounding words, according to those who are not ignorant of the collecting of the earthly discipline, means almost nothing other than together, as in Let all the Church of Israel be gathered together; and they shall come together to the feast day, that is, they shall be crowded together into one flock, they shall come together at once; and the Apostle, If indeed we suffer with him, that we may also be glorified together, that is, be glorified with him; and that other, He sat down upon the brink of the glassy spring, that is, sat together with him; and one who sits with another is called a fellow-sitter (consessor).

units.la: Simul namq; quædam juxta eos, qui sagacissimæ logicæ arcana scrutantur, tribus modis dicuntur: tempore, natura, & genere. Tempore, natura, & genere. Tempore vel apparent, ita ut neutrum de duobus vel prius sit, vel alterum consequatur, sed utriq; ortus videtur esse communis. Secundum quem modum, nobis simul minimè regnare dicendus est: quippe cum ille sit sempiternus, nos temporales. Ille sine initio, nos cum initio. Natura, cum quædam naturaliter simul sunt, nullum tamen eorum præest alteri: ut verbi gratia simplum & duplum ponamus, necesse simul esse naturaliter: sed neq; duplum facit ut simplum sit, neq; simplum efficit duplum. Sed nec secundum hunc modum nobis simul regnare dici potest: cum tot distantiis natura ejus nostræ naturæ prior sit, totq; modis creatrix creatam præcedat. Genere, quoniam ex eodem genere manantia simul videntur esse natura, sed specie discernitur, ut est animal. Nam & pedestre & aquatile animal dicitur, sed specie discernitur: nullumq; alteri aliud prius est, sed simul omnia ab animali, id est, ab uno genere orta noscuntur.
