Coming to him, a living stone, rejected indeed by men but chosen and honoured by God, and a little later: To you therefore who believe, honour; but to those who do not believe, the stone which the builders rejected has become the head of the corner, and a stone of stumbling and a rock of offence to those who stumble at the word, and do not believe, for which they were also appointed. By this teaching it is shown that he is an honour of strength to believers and a scandal of hardness to unbelievers. This was also foretold in this sense by the righteous Simeon, who says: This child is set for the fall and rising again of many in Israel: the fall, namely, of unbelievers, and the rising again of believers. He is also called fire, either because he illuminates believers with the brightness of eternal light, or because he will scorch unbelievers with the heat of eternal fire. The anointing of this stone was also declared in the oracles of David a little earlier, and now the testimony of the chief minister of the Church must be brought forward, who says: Jesus of Nazareth, whom God anointed with the Holy Spirit and with power. Since the Holy Spirit is often signified in the divine Scriptures by the name of oil, the Apostle John is a witness who says: As his anointing teaches you about all things. If they have been anointed with the unspeakable nectar of that anointing, they ought by no means to convene synods to establish the adoration of images, nor to appropriate the holy Scriptures to foreign senses.

units.la: CAP. XI.
units.tr: CHAPTER XI.

units.la: De eo quod præfatus Iohannes dixit, In hominis forma luctatus est cum ipso, & vocavit eum Israhel, quod est interpretatum, mens videns Deum.
units.tr: Concerning what the aforesaid John said: "In the form of a man he wrestled with him, and called him Israel, which is interpreted, the mind seeing God."

units.la: Sed necillud quidem à reprehensione vacat quod idem Iohannes presbyter & legatus Orientalium inter cætera deliramenta de Iacob dixisse fertur, In hominis forma luctatus est cum ipso, & vocavit cum Israhel, quod est interpretatum, mens videns Deum: cùm hoc dictum & à re propósita longe distet, & in nominis interpretatione usitatiorem quandam omittens, pene inusitatum quid persónet. Nàdum quidam id nomen interpretentur, vir videns Deum, quidam verò, fortis cum Deo, nonnulli etiam veracius, princeps cum Deo: nescio tamen an ullus eorum qui in canone recipiuntur, reperiatur hoc, mens videns Deum, interpretatus fuisse: unde non solum ille reprehendendus est qui usitatioribus interpretationibus præteremissis pene inusitatum quid protulit, sed & omnis illa synodus, quæ e in pluribus so-mnianti adsensum præbuit, quæ non solù dicenti non restitit, sed etiam dicta in volumine taxavit. Cùm ergo sancta ecclesia secundum sanctorum patrum institutionem omne quod inreprehensibile est recipiat: omne verò quod reprehensibile abiciat, hanc quoque eorum synodum, quæ utique reprehensibilis est, abicit: & si hanc quæ reprehensibilis est non abicit, neque eas quæ inreprehensibiles sunt suscipit: suscipit autem eas quæ inteprehensibiles sunt: hanc igitur quia reprehensioni patet, penitus suscipere non debet. Illas enim synodos sancta & universalis recipit ecclesia, quæ pro diversis fidei, sive religionis causis diversis locis, seu temporibus, à doctis & catholicis viris celebratæ, à sana sobriaque doctrina nullatenus deviare perhibentur. Præterea tanti patriarchæ cum angelo luctatio non quandam imaginum adorationem, sed dominicam præfiguràsse dicitur in eodem populo passionem: qui populus & ei luctando prævaluit, quia crucifixit: & ab eo benedictionem in his qui iaeum crediderunt accepit: & in his claudus qui in eum credere contempserunt, remansit, dicente beato Augustino, Quod ab illo angelo desiderat benedici Iacob cui luctando prævaluit, magna est de CHRISTO prophetia. Nam eo ipso ammonet mysticum aliquid sapere, quia omnis homo à majore vult benedici. Quomodo ergo ab eo ipse voluit quem luctando superavit? prævaluit enim Iacob Christo, vel potius prævalere visus est per eos Israhelitas à quibus crucifixus est Christus: & ab eo tamen benedicitur in eis Israhelitis qui crediderunt in Christum, ex quibus erat qui dicebat, Nam & ego Israhelita sum ex genere Abrahæ & tribu Benjamin. Unus ergo atq; idem Iacob & claudus & benedictus. Claudus in latitudine fœmoris tanquam in multitudine generis, de quibus dictum est, Et claudicaverunt à senitus sui: benedictus autem in eis de quibus dictum est. Reliquiæ per electionem gratiæ salvæ factæ sunt.
units.tr: Yet it is not free from blame that the same John, presbyter and legate of the Easterners, is reported to have said, among his other absurdities about Jacob, "In the form of a man he wrestled with him, and called him Israel, which is interpreted, the mind seeing God," since this saying is far removed from the matter at hand. By omitting the more usual interpretation of the name, he put forward something almost unheard of. Some interpret that name as "a man seeing God," some as "strong with God," and some, more accurately, as "prince with God." Yet I do not know whether any of those received in the canon is found to have interpreted it as "the mind seeing God." Hence not only is he to be blamed who, passing over the more usual interpretations, put forward something almost unheard of, but also that whole synod which gave assent to this dreamer in many matters. It did not merely fail to resist him when he spoke, but even censured in its volume the things he had said. Since the holy Church, following the teaching of the holy Fathers, accepts everything that is irreproachable and rejects everything that is reproachable, she rejects also that synod of theirs, which is certainly reproachable. And if she did not reject the reproachable synod, she would not receive those that are irreproachable; but she does receive those that are irreproachable. Therefore this one, because it lies open to reproach, she ought not to receive at all. For the holy and universal Church receives those synods which were celebrated in various places or times by learned and catholic men, for various causes of faith or religion, and which are said in no way to deviate from sound and sober doctrine. Moreover, that wrestling of so great a patriarch with the angel is said to have prefigured, not some adoration of images, but the Lord's passion in the same people. That people also prevailed over him in the wrestling, because it crucified him; and from him it received the blessing among those who believed in him, while among those who scorned to believe in him it remained lame. As blessed Augustine says: "That Jacob desires to be blessed by that angel, with whom he wrestled and prevailed, is a great prophecy about Christ. For by that very fact it warns that something mystical is signified, since every man wishes to be blessed by a greater. How then did he wish to be blessed by him whom he overcame in wrestling? For Jacob prevailed over Christ, or rather seemed to prevail, through those Israelites by whom Christ was crucified; yet he is blessed by Christ in those Israelites who believed in Christ, out of whom was the one who said, 'For I too am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham and of the tribe of Benjamin.' So one and the same Jacob is both lame and blessed. Lame in the breadth of the thigh, as in the multitude of the race, of whom it is said, 'And they limped from their own path'; blessed, however, in those of whom it is said, 'A remnant is saved by the election of grace.'"

units.la: CAP. XII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XII.

units.la: Quod non ad adorationem imaginum pertineat, nec in nostris codicibus qui ex Hebraica veri- tate translati sunt, inveniatur, quod illi in sua synodo dicunt, Iacob suscipiens à fi- liis suis vestem talarem tabefactam Ioseph osculatus est cum lachrymis, & propriis oculis inposuit.
units.tr: That this does not pertain to the adoration of images, and is not found in our codices, which were translated from the Hebrew truth, what they say in their synod: "Jacob, receiving from his sons a long robe, torn and wasted, kissed Joseph's tunic with tears and placed it on his own eyes."

units.la: Non mirandum est si Iacob accuserut ab illis tunicam Ioseph osculatus fuisse, & oculis inposuisse, à quibus etiam Pharaonem accusatur adorasse. Accidere erenim plerumque solet, ut qui semel falli cæperit, crebro fallatur: & qui semel à via recesserit, & tramitem sui itineris ducem sequi neglexerit, per abrupta & invia affatim errore duce feratur. Tunica enim Ioseph nec & in eadem virga filium adorasse transtulerit: quis sanctæ legis studiosissimus indagator eum virgam filii vel filium potius quàm Deum adorasse tractaverit: & cum hunc invenire nequiverint, depravatricem, sive refragatricem potius, quàm indagatricem suam intellegentiam divinarum scripturarum esse persentiant. Iam verò quia pene omnis divinæ legis series ab illis ob imaginum adorationem aut mutilatur aut permutatur, nova necesse est post Moysen legis tradatur scriptio: nova post Eziam gis reperiatur restauratio: nova post septuaginta interpretes, Theodotionem & Symmachum & Aquilam, sive etiam beatum Hieronymum legis quæ-ratur translatio: nova post Apostolos & Apostolicos viros Spiritu sancto repletos scriptura tractatio, quæ adeo divinis scripturis refragari queat, ut omnes imaginum adorationem spernentes anathematis vinculo nectat. Quæ sit præsens differentia crucis Christi & imaginum pictorum arte pictarum, vel quanto mysterio crux imaginibus eminet, sive quomodo humanum genus non per imagines, sed per crucem Christis redemptum sit, quæ duo illi vel paria vel æqualia putant, in sequentibus loco suo Domino favente explicabimus.
units.tr: It is no wonder if they accuse Jacob of kissing Joseph's tunic and placing it on his eyes, the same people who also accuse Pharaoh of having worshipped. It usually happens that whoever has once begun to be deceived is deceived again and again, and whoever has once strayed from the road and neglected to follow the guide of his own path is carried headlong by error through precipices and trackless places. For who, most diligent searcher of the holy law, would have interpreted the rod or the son, rather than God, as the object of the adoration that was offered to the same rod? And when they cannot find this, they perceive that their understanding of the divine Scriptures is a corrupter, or rather a refuter, and not a searcher. Indeed, since nearly the whole series of the divine law is either mutilated or altered by them on account of the adoration of images, it is necessary that a new writing of the law be handed down after Moses, a new restoration be found after Ezra, a new translation of the law be sought after the Seventy, Theodotion, Symmachus and Aquila, or even after blessed Jerome, and a new treatment of Scripture after the Apostles and apostolic men filled with the Holy Spirit, which can so oppose the divine Scriptures that it binds with the chain of anathema all who despise the adoration of images. What the present difference is between the cross of Christ and images painted by the art of painters, or how much mystery the cross surpasses images by, or how the human race was redeemed not by images but by the cross of Christ, these two things they think equal or alike; we will explain them in what follows, in their proper place, with the Lord's favour.

units.la: CAP. XIV. Non pertinere ad imaginum adorationem, ut illi dicunt, quod scriptum est, Iacob Pharaonem benedixit.
units.tr: CHAP. XIV. That the words "Jacob blessed Pharaoh" do not pertain to the adoration of images, as they say.

units.la: Quo o sæpe memoratus patriarcha Iacob Pharaonem non adorasse, sed benedixisse legatur, superius dictum est. Nunc vero quia in alia ejusdem vanissima synodi lectione benedictio quodammodo posita est pro adoratione, breviter exsequendum est. Quoniam quidem tantis est illius vanitatis scriptura ignorantiæ obsita caliginibus, ut nec sequentia præcedentibus, nec præcedentia convenire videantur sequentibus, & ut se habet vanitas mendacium, semper fugitiva, semper caduca, semperque labentia sequitur, dicente Salomone; Qui ventum mendacii, hic pascit ventos, ipse autem sequitur aves volantes. Ut ergo imaginum adorationem, in quantum antiquitus eorum mens pendet, & totius sanctitatis propositum est, stabiliant, plurima verba vel sensus quæ ad aliud pertinent, in adorationem mutare affectant. Nam & hæc, quod idem sanctus vir Pharaonem benedixit, non ad eandem benedictionem pertinere putant, quam solemni ple minque exsules civibus, subditis præsatis, pauperiores ditioribus, & quam maxime senes, qui sibi quædam commoda impendunt exhibere, sed ad nescio quam adorandarum imaginum pictuarum: quæ nimirum tanto inutilis est, quanto minus suæ utilitatis efficaciam potest loquendo edicere. Ajunt enim, Benedixit Iacob Pharaonem, sed non ut Deum benedixit: adoramus nos imaginem, sed non ut Deum adoramus. O inconveniens comparatio! O hebes conjectura! O stolidissima dictio! Similem dicis benedictionem, quam sanctus patriarcha regi exhibuit, qui pro ceteris dilectissimo filio insigne contulit potestatis: qui sibi cum universa prole uberem ad inhabitandum gebam concessit: qui sibi non cuiuscunque provinciæ portionem, sed totius sui imperii tetræ donavit optionem, adorationi quam imaginibus exhibes? quæ adorantibus nihil præter rei memoriam cujus sunt, exhibere valent. Benedixit itaque Iacob Pharaonem, non ut Deum quem omnis creatura benedicit & laudat, neque ut picturam quam manus artificis aptat, sed ut hominem cui propter sublimitatem concessa a Deo potestatis honor est exhibendus. Benedixit, inquam, eum, non ut imaginem insensatam, sed ut rationem hominem: non ut industria pictoris conpaginatum, sed ut ad Dei imaginem & similitudinem conditum: non ut in parietibus immobiliter stantem, sed ut sibi vel proli pro peta commodum. Et ut ita dixerim, benedixit Israhel regem qui ejusdem spiritus nectare delibutus erat: qui per Apostolum dicturus esset, Benedicite & nolite maledicere: qui non solum pro eo qui se persequentibus, sed pro calumniantibus & persequentibus orare debeat. Non itaque huiusmodi benedictio, quæ profecto bonæ retributionis causa extitit celebrata, imaginum adorationi congruit: quæ neque se adorantibus, neque adorare spernentibus quandam pro qualitate meritorum possunt inferre retributionem.
units.tr: It was said above that the patriarch Jacob, often mentioned, is read not to have worshipped Pharaoh but to have blessed him. Now, because in another reading of that most vain synod the blessing is somehow put in place of adoration, it must be briefly set forth. For the Scripture of that vanity is so wrapped in the darkness of ignorance that neither what follows seems to agree with what precedes, nor what precedes with what follows; and as falsehood is, vanity always follows what is fleeting, always falling and always slipping away, as Solomon says: He who feeds on the wind of lies, feeds the winds, and he himself follows the flying birds. So, in order to establish the adoration of images, to the extent that their minds hang upon it from of old and it is the purpose of all their sanctity, they strive to turn very many words or senses that pertain to something else into adoration. For they also think that this, that the same holy man blessed Pharaoh, does not pertain to that blessing which is commonly shown to exiles by citizens, subjects to superiors, the poorer to the richer, and especially the old, who lend certain advantages to themselves, but to I know not what blessing of painted images to be adored; which is surely as useless as it is less able to declare the efficacy of its usefulness in speaking. For they say, Jacob blessed Pharaoh, but not as he blessed God: we adore the image, but not as we adore God. O unsuitable comparison! O dull conjecture! O most stupid expression! You speak of a blessing like that which the holy patriarch showed to the king, who above the others conferred the mark of power on his most beloved son; who granted to himself with all his offspring a fertile land to dwell in; who gave to himself not a portion of some province but the choice of the whole of his realm, to the adoration which you show to images? Which can give to those who adore them nothing except the memory of the thing whose they are. Jacob therefore blessed Pharaoh, not as God, whom every creature blesses and praises, nor as a picture which the hand of the craftsman fits together, but as a man to whom honour of power granted by God on account of his eminence is to be shown. He blessed him, I say, not as an insensate image, but as a rational man; not as one put together by the skill of a painter, but as one formed in the image and likeness of God; not as one standing immovably on walls, but as one who was useful to himself and his offspring in turn. And, so to speak, he blessed the king of Israel, who was imbued with the nectar of the same Spirit, who would say through the Apostle, Bless and do not curse; who ought to pray not only for those who persecute him, but for those who slander and persecute. Therefore a blessing of this kind, which has indeed been celebrated as the cause of a good recompense, does not agree with the adoration of images; which can bring to those who adore them, or to those who despise adoring them, no recompense according to the quality of their merits.

units.la: CAP. XV. Quam absurde agant qui ad confirmandas imagines exemplum divinæ legis proferunt dicentes, propitiatorium & duos cherubim aureos & archam testamenti pr- æcipiente Domino Moysen fecisse.
units.tr: CHAPTER XV. How absurdly they act who, to confirm images, cite the example of the divine law, saying that the Lord commanded Moses to make the mercy seat, the two golden cherubim and the ark of the covenant.

units.la: Fecisse sanctus Moyses, præcipiente Domino, propitiatorium & arcam testamenti, & duos cherubim aureos, necnon & excidisse tabulas lapideas legitur: non tamen adorare jussisse, nec ob præteritarum quarundam rerum memoriam, sed ob futurorum mysteriorum sacratissimorum figuram conditum est. Quæ dum ita se habeant, quantæ sint absurditatis quantæ demenție illi qui his sacratissimis & summo honore dignis rebus, præcipiente Domino, à legislatore conditis, imagines æquiparare conantur, illarum adorationem his exemplis stabilire moliuntur. Nec ferrea vox explicare, nec nostri sensus existimatio poterit indagare: præsertim cum illa sacratissimorum sensuum exuberent archanis, hæc parum utilitatis habeant, excepta recordatione rei cujus sunt. Cum ergo archa testamenti Domini de lignis Setthim, jubente Domino, per legislatorem condita & inaurata sit, & introtus habeat tabulas nihilominus fœderis & manna sive virgam Aaron: propitiatorium vero sit aureum in modum tabulæ, quod supernnponebatur archæ, ejusdem que longitudinis & latitudinis, tantæque formæ fieri iu jussum, qua & archa, ut eodem propitiatorio archa tegeretur, & duo cherubim aurei ductiles super ipsum propitiatorium essent, hincatque inde alterutrum ad tendentes, ita ut vultus eorum in propitiatorium essent, & pinnis suis obumbrarent propitiatorium, & inde Deus loquereturad Moysen, de propitiatorio videlicet sive de medio cherubim: quis tam hebes tamque est demens, ut non solum habendarum, sed etiam adorandarum imaginum insolentissimum usum, horum tam terribilium tamque insignium mysteriorum conparatio ne concturad uere? Nam dum istæ nihil aliud innuant, nisi interdum rerum gestarum ordinem, interdum non gestarum, sed fictarum mentiantur errorem: illa vero semper sanctis & excellentibus radiant mysteriis & rutilant sacramentis. Archa namque fœderis secundum quosdam Dominum & salvatorem nostrum, in quo solo fœdus pacis apud patrem habemus, designat: qui post resurrectionem suam ascendens in cælum carnem quam adsumpserat ex virgine, in patris dextera collocavit. In quo sunt duæ tabulæ legis, duo videlicet testamenta: in quo est virga Aaron, quæ fronduerat ei, quia ipse est rex & sacerdos: Rex, quia de eo scriptum est; Virgam virtutis tuæ emittet Dominus ex Sion, & dominabitur in medio inimicorum tuorum. Sacerdos vero, quia de eo scriptum est; Tu es sacerdos in æternum secundum ordinem Melchisedech: in quo est manna, cælestis videlicet pabuli edulium, de quo edulio David egregius propheta dicit; Panem de cælo dedit eis, panem angelorum manducavit homo: sicut & ipse in Evangelio dicit, Ego sum panis vivus qui de cælo descendi. Cui propitiatorium superponitur, quia scilicet legalibus sive evangelicis præceptis, quæ in eo fundata sunt, superemimet misericordia ejusdem mediatoris, per quam non ex operibus legis quæ fecimus nos, neque volentes, neque currentes, sed ejus miseratione salvamur: de quo etiam voce paterna dicitur, Veritas mea & misericordia mea cum ipso, & in nomine meo exaltabitur cornu ejus: & qui per Prophetam dicit, Misericordiam volo & non sacrificium: & cui per Psalmistam dicitur, Miserationes tuæ multæ Domine: qui secundum Apostolum propitiatio est pro peccatis nostris. In quo sunt duo cherubim, scientiæ videlicet plenitudo, quæ in duobus testamentis, cujus revelatione, monstrata est: qui invicem se adtendunt, quia lex & evangelium magnam inter se consonantiam habent, dicente Domino, Non veni legem solvere, sed adimplere. Qui cherubim ideo versos vultus habent in propitiatorium, quia duo testamenta spem semper in Dei misericordia ponendam omnino commendant. Desuper quo propitiatorio, id est, de medio cherubim loquitur Deus, quia idem filius est verbum patris, per quem facta sunt omnia: & cum sit unius cum patre substantiæ, sicut ipse in evangelio ait, Ego & pater unum sumus, sive ut Philippo ait, Qui videt me, videt & patrem, Dei patris in eo semper de medio duorum testamentorum vox auditur: secundum plerosque vero divinæ legis doctores qui hæc moraliter tractant, aurum sapientiam significat, archa secretum Dei. In archa julia sunt poni lex & manna & virga Aaron. Per virgam potestas significatur, per manna gratia: quia nisi cum gratia non est potestas præcepta faciendi. Verumtamen quia lex à quovis proficiente non ex omni parte completur, propitiatorium est desuper ad hoc enim opus est, ut propitius sit Deus: & ideo desuper ponitur, quia superexaltat misericordia judicio. Duo vero cherubim pinnis suis obumbraut propitiatorium, id est, honorant velando, quorum nil mysteria ista sunt, & invicem se adtendunt, quia consonant. Duo quippe ibi testamenta figurantur, & vultus eorum sunt in propitiatorium: quia misericordiam Dei, in qua una spes est, vel le commendant. Denique hinc se promisit locuturum Deus ad Moysen, de medio cherubim, de sursum propitiatorii. Porro si creatura rationalis in multitudine scientiæ, quoniam hanc interpretationem habent cherubim, duobus ipsis animalibus significatur: ideo duo sunt ut societatem charitatis commendent: ideo pinnis suis propitiatorium obumbrant, quia Deo, non sibi tribuunt pinnas suas, id est, Deum honorant virtutibus quibus præstant. Et vultus eorum non sunt nisi in propitiatorium, quia cuicumque profectui ad multitudinem scientiæ spes non est, nisi in Dei misericordia. Quia igitur tabulæ per quas duo testamenta significant supeius diximus, nullo terrore dantur, nullo spiritu ignium, nulla commotione nubium, nullo mugitu tubarum, sicut illæ quæ prius à Domino data & à Moyse conminutæ fuisse leguntur: quæ dum darentur Moysi, à populo dictum est; Loquere tu nobiscum, & non loquatur ad nos Deus, ne forte moriamur: hoc evidenter innuitur, quod priores vetus testamentum in quo terror erat, significaverunt: posteriores vero novum, in quo dilectio. Quod vero priores opus Dei fuerint, secundo opus hominis: & illæ conscriptæ digito Dei, istæ scriptæ ab homine narrentur, hoc apertissime declaratur, quod in illis vetus testamentum, ut prætati sumus, significatum est: quia Deus ibi præcepit, sed homo non fecit. Lex enim posita est in veteri testamento, quæ convinceret transgressores: unde & egregius prædicator ait, Lex autem subintravit, ut abundaret peccatum. Non enim implebatur timore, quæ non impletur nisi charitate: & ideo dicitur opus Dei, quia Deus legem constituit, Deus conscripsit: nullum opus hominis, quia homo Deo non obtemperavit, & eum potius reum lex fecit. In secundis autem tabulis homo per adjutorium Dei tabulas fecit atque confecit, quia novi testamenti characteres legem facit. Unde mediator Dei & hominum legem non solvit, sed adimplere venit. Dicit autem & idem egregius prædicator, Plenitudo legis charitas & fides quæ per dilectionem operatur. Factum est itaque hominis facile in novo testamento quod veteri dissiluit, habenti fidem quæ per dilectionem operatur: atque illi dei, hoc est spiritu Dei, intus eam in corde scribente, non foris in lapide. Unde dicit Apostolus, Non in tabulis lapideis, sed in tabulis cordis carnalibus. pedes, sed in tabulis cordis carnalibus: quoniam charitas Dei qua veracitèr impletur præceptum, diffusa est in cordibus nostris per Spiritum sanctum, qui datus est nobis. Hoc ergo quòd primo data est lex, ubi significatur vetus testamentum, quod est opus tantummodo Dei, & conscriptio digiti Dei, quod Apostolus dicit, Itaque lex quidem sancta, & mandatum sanctum & justum & bonum. Lex ergo sancta & bona Dei opus est, ubi homo nihil agit: quia non obtemperat, sed reatu potius premitur legem minante atque damnante. Peccatum enim, inquit, ut appareat peccatum per bonum mihi operatum est mortem: beatus autem homo est, cùm hoc mandatum sanctum & justum & bonum adimplet. Est etiam opus ejus, sed per gratiam Dei. Hic enim sensus aptatur translationi veteri, in qua secundæ tabulæ à legislatore scriptæ fuisse memorantur. Cæterum quia in Hebraica veritate utraque prima videlicet & secunda à Deo scribuntur, hoc significatur, quia & vetus & novum testamentum sancti Spiritus gratia, quod digitus Dei dicitur, conscriptum est, & in illo accipitur spiritus servitutis in timore, quia Deus jugum legis hominai imponit, homo ferre non valer. In illo verò ubi tabulæ ab homine fiunt, à Deo scribuntur, homo obœdiendo accipit spiritum adoptionis. Hæc igitur insignia, archa videlicet & quæ in ea sunt, propitiatorium sive cherubim, semper à nobis spirituali intuitu cernantur, & tota mentis intentione quærantur. Nec ea in depictis tabulis sive parietibus quæramus, sed in penetralibus nostri cordis mentis oculo aspiciamus: & qui secundum Apostolum, revelata facie gloriam Dei speculantes in ejusdem imaginem transformamur, à claritate in claritatem, tanquam à Domini spiritu non ambulantes in astutia, neque adulterantes verbum Dei, sed in manifestatione veritatis: non jam veritatem per imagines & picturas quæramus, qui ipse, fide & charitate ad eandem veritatem quæ Christus est, ipso auxiliante pervenimus.
units.tr: It is read that the holy Moses, at the Lord's command, made the mercy seat, the ark of the covenant and the two golden cherubim, and also broke the stone tablets. Yet he was not ordered to worship them, and they were not established for the sake of remembering certain past events, but as figures of the most sacred future mysteries. Since this is so, how great is the absurdity, how great the madness, of those who try to set images on a level with these most sacred things, which were made by the lawgiver at the Lord's command and are worthy of the highest honour, and who strive to establish the worship of images by these examples. No spoken word can explain, and no judgment of our mind can search out, how great the difference is, especially since those things overflow with the most sacred secrets of meaning, while these images have little use except to remind us of the things they represent. Therefore, since the ark of the covenant was made by the lawgiver of acacia wood, at the Lord's command, and overlaid with gold, and since it contains the tablets of the covenant and the manna, or the rod of Aaron; and since the mercy seat is of gold in the form of a plate, placed over the ark, of the same length and breadth, and was commanded to be made in such a shape that the ark was covered by that same mercy seat, and the two golden cherubim, beaten work, were upon the mercy seat itself, facing one another from either end, so that their faces looked toward the mercy seat and they shaded the mercy seat with their wings, and from there God spoke to Moses, that is, from the mercy seat or from between the cherubim: who is so dull and so foolish that he does not see that the comparison of these most terrible and remarkable mysteries with images does not merely lead to the having of images, but even to the most outrageous practice of worshipping them? For while those things (the images) signify nothing else than sometimes the order of deeds done, and sometimes, not deeds done but invented, they tell a falsehood; whereas the others shine always with holy and excellent mysteries and gleam with sacraments. For the ark of the covenant, according to some, designates our Lord and Saviour, in whom alone we have the covenant of peace with the Father, who, ascending into heaven after his resurrection, placed in the right hand of the Father the flesh which he had taken from the virgin. In it are the two tablets of the law, that is, the two testaments; in it is the rod of Aaron, which had put forth leaves, because he is both king and priest: king, because it is written of him, The Lord shall send forth the rod of your strength out of Zion, and rule in the midst of your enemies; priest, because it is written of him, You are a priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek. In it is the manna, the food of heavenly bread, concerning which food the outstanding prophet David says, He gave them bread from heaven; man ate the bread of angels; just as he himself says in the Gospel, I am the living bread which came down from heaven. Over this is placed the mercy seat, because the mercy of the same Mediator rises above the precepts of the law and of the gospel which are founded in it, by which we are saved not by works of the law which we have done, nor by willing or running, but by his mercy. Of him it is said by the Father's voice, My truth and my mercy shall be with him, and in my name shall his horn be exalted; and he who says through the prophet, I desire mercy and not sacrifice; and to whom it is said by the Psalmist, Your mercies are many, O Lord; who, according to the Apostle, is the propitiation for our sins. In it are the two cherubim, that is, the fullness of knowledge, which was shown by revelation in the two testaments; they look toward one another, because the law and the gospel have great agreement with each other, the Lord saying, I came not to destroy the law but to fulfil it. These cherubim have their faces turned toward the mercy seat, because the two testaments wholly commend that hope must always be placed in God's mercy. God speaks from above that mercy seat, that is, from between the cherubim, because the same Son is the Word of the Father, through whom all things were made; and since he is of one substance with the Father, as he himself says in the Gospel, I and the Father are one, or as he says to Philip, He who sees me sees also the Father, the voice of God the Father is always heard in him from the midst of the two testaments. But according to most teachers of the divine law who treat these things morally, the gold signifies wisdom, and the ark the secret of God. In the ark are placed the law, the manna and the rod of Aaron. The rod signifies power, the manna grace, because power to do what is commanded does not exist except with grace. Nevertheless, because the law is not fulfilled in every part by anyone who makes progress, the mercy seat is placed above it; for this work requires that God be propitious, and therefore it is placed above, because mercy exalts itself above judgment. The two cherubim shade the mercy seat with their wings, that is, they honour it by covering it, and these are the mysteries of it; and they look toward one another, because they agree. Indeed the two testaments are signified there, and their faces are toward the mercy seat, because they commend the mercy of God, in which alone is hope. Finally, from there God promised that he would speak to Moses, from between the cherubim, from above the mercy seat. Further, if the rational creature is signified by the two animals, the cherubim, since they bear this interpretation, in respect of the multitude of knowledge: therefore they are two, so that they may commend the fellowship of love; therefore they shade the mercy seat with their wings, because they do not ascribe their wings to themselves, that is, they honour God by the virtues in which they excel. And their faces are turned only toward the mercy seat, because for anyone advancing to a multitude of knowledge there is no hope except in God's mercy. Therefore, since the tablets by which the two testaments are signified, as we said above, were given with no terror, no spirit of fire, no commotion of clouds, no blast of trumpets, unlike those which are read to have been first given by the Lord and broken by Moses; when these were being given to Moses, the people said, Speak to us yourself, and let not God speak to us, lest perhaps we die: it is plainly indicated that the former signified the old covenant, in which there was terror, and the latter the new, in which there is love. That the former were the work of God, and the second the work of man, and that the former were written with the finger of God while the latter are said to have been written by man, is most clearly declared by this, that in the former the old covenant was signified, as we have said: for there God commanded, but man did not do. For the law was set in the old covenant to convict transgressors; whence also the excellent preacher says, The law entered that sin might abound. For that is not fulfilled by fear which is not fulfilled except by love; and therefore it is called the work of God, because God established the law and God wrote it: it is no work of man, because man did not obey God, and the law rather made him guilty. But in the second tablets man, with the help of God, made and completed the tablets, because the law is written in the characters of the new covenant. Whence the Mediator of God and men did not come to dissolve the law but to fulfil it. The same excellent preacher also says, The fulfilling of the law is love and faith, which works through love. Thus what was made by man has easily come to pass in the new covenant, which failed in the old, for he who has faith which works through love, and God, that is, the Spirit of God, writes it within the heart, not outside on stone. Whence the Apostle says, Not on tablets of stone, but on the fleshly tablets of the heart; because the love of God, by which the precept is truly fulfilled, has been poured out in our hearts through the Holy Spirit, who has been given to us. Therefore, in that the law was first given, which signifies the old covenant, which is only the work of God, and the writing of the finger of God, the Apostle says, So the law indeed is holy, and the commandment holy and just and good. The law then, holy and good, is the work of God, in which man does nothing, because he does not obey, but is rather crushed by guilt, the law threatening and condemning. For sin, he says, that it might appear to be sin, worked death in me through that which is good: but a man is blessed when he fulfils this commandment, which is holy and just and good. It is also his work, but by the grace of God. For this sense fits the old translation, in which the second tablets are recorded as having been written by the lawgiver. But since in the Hebrew truth both the first and the second are written by God, this signifies that both the old and the new covenant were written by the grace of the Holy Spirit, which is called the finger of God; and in the one is received the spirit of bondage in fear, because God lays on man the yoke of the law which man cannot bear; but in the other, where the tablets are made by man, they are written by God, and man receives the spirit of adoption by obeying. Therefore let these emblems, that is, the ark and what is in it, the mercy seat or the cherubim, always be beheld by us with a spiritual gaze, and sought with the whole intention of the mind. Nor should we seek them in painted tables or walls, but behold them with the eye of the mind in the innermost chambers of our heart; and, as the Apostle says, beholding the glory of God with unveiled face, we are transformed into his image from glory to glory, as by the Spirit of the Lord, not walking in craftiness, nor adulterating the word of God, but by the manifestation of the truth; let us no longer seek the truth through images and pictures, since by faith and love we have come, with his help, to that same truth which is Christ.

units.la: CAP. XVI.
units.tr: CHAP. XVI.

units.la: Quod nec inde adorandarum imaginum usus adstrui possit, ut illi stultissimè & irrationabiliter dicunt, eo quod in lege scriptum est: Ecce vocavi ex nomine Beseleel filii Ur filii Hor de tribu Iuda, & replevi eum spiritu sapientiæ & intelligentiæ, ad perficiendum opus ex auro & argento, & dedi ei Oeliab Achisama.
units.tr: That the use of adoring images cannot be supported from this either, as those men foolishly and irrationally claim, because it is written in the law: "Behold, I have called by name Bezaleel, the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, and I have filled him with the spirit of wisdom and understanding, to make the work in gold and silver, and I have given him Oholiab the son of Ahisamach."

units.la: LEX, ut ait Apostolus, spiritalis est. Est enim nobis in præsentis sæculi caliginoso itinere ad dirigendos nostrarum mentium gressus à Deo conlata, cujus jubare mentis acies perlustrata mysticorum sensuum possit intueri secreta. Præceptum nameq; Domini lucidum, ait Propheta, illumi-nans oculos: atque idem, Lucerna pedibus meis verbum tuum Domine, & lumen semitis meis. De hac itaque per quandam sapientem dicitur; Lucerna est mandatum legis, & lux vita, & increpatio & disciplina. Et Esaias De nocte spiritus meus vigilat ad te Deus: quia lux præcepta tua sunt super terram. cujus lucis cùm omnes cæcum non rectè intellegentes expertes sint, hi nimirum prorsus expertes esse creduntur, qui ob nescio quam imaginum adorationem cam violenter ad suos sensus flectere nituntur, & in suo errore eam quasi modo sibi adminiculari affectant: cùm ex ea, quamquam ad rem non pertinentia, tamen testimonia proferre tentant. Quia ergo Beseleel ad faciendum opus ex auro & argento à Domino electus, & spiritu sapientiæ & intellegentiæ & scientiæ repletus, ita hoc illi ad suum errorem reundum in testimonium trahunt, ac si ea quæ per eum Domino jubente fiebant, & mysticas typicas figuras redolebant, adoranda forent. Beseleel igitur interpretatur, in umbra Dei: Ur, ignis lumen intellegitur. Cujus ergo ipse Beseleel, qui, ut diximus, in umbra Dei interpretatur, typicum: nisi illius cui semper ecclesia clamat, Sub umbra alarum tuarum protege me: &, Sub umbra ala-rum tuarum, donec transeat iniquitas: & de quo in Canticis Canticorum sponsa dicit, Sub umbra illius quem desideravi sedi. Hic enim filius Ur filii Hor dicitur: quia est splendor inenarrabilis, Deus ex lumine: de quo per Abacuc prophetam dicitur, Splendor ejus ut lumen erit. Deus namque ignis, ut Moyses, ignis consumens est: quod & Apostolus Paulus in epistola ad Hebræos iisdem verbis: & idem Dominus per Zachariam Prophetam dicit, Absque muro habitabitur Hierusalem præ multitudine hominum & jumentorum, & ego ero in circuitu ejus murus & ignis. Qui cùm sit unius cum patre substantiæ: & ad Moysen in igne loquitur, & ad discipulos in Evangelio ait, Ignem veni mittere super terram: & quid volo nisi ut ardeat? Numquid non illo igne illorum pectora inflammata erant qui dicebant, Nonne cor nostrum ardens erat in nobis, dum loqueretur in via, & aperiret nobis scripturas? Is ergo Beseleel ex nomine vocatur, quia ei paterna voce per Esaiam Prophetam dicitur, Et vocavi te nomine tuo, Esa. 43. & de quo per Moysen dicitur, Ecce mittam angelum qui præcedat te, & custodiat in via, & introducat ad locum quem præparavi. Observa eum, & audi vocem ejus, nec contemnendum putes, quia non dimittet cum peccaveris, & est nomen meum in illo. Sed nec genus hujus Beseleel, qui ex nomine vocatus est, tacetur. Ait enim scriptura, Filium Ur filii Hor de tribu Iuda. Hic est enim de quo Israhelitica voce ante prædictum est: Catulus leonis Iuda ad prædam fili mi ascendisti: id est, in crucem prædaturus infernum, requiescens ut leo, id est, in sepulchro: & quasi leæna, quis suscitabit eum? quia per virtutem patris tertia die à mortuis resurrexit. Per virtutem autem patris illum resurrexisse audi Apostolum dicentem; Hunc Deus suscitavit post diem tertium, & dedit illum manifestum fieri non omni populo. Dic, rogo, sancte Iohannes, qui supra mediatoris Dei & hominum pectus recumbens, de æterni luminis fonte luciflua po-culâ. cula hauriebas, unde quotidie ambrosci liquoris nectar Christicolis mentibus propinas, si nostri unde genus ducat iste Befeleel, cujus rypum ille antiquus legalis quondam Befeleel gerebat. Vidi, inquam, in dextera sedentis super thronum librum scriptum intus & foris, signatum sigillis septem: & vidi Angelum fortem praedicantem voce magna: Quis dignus est aperire librum, & solvere signacula ejus? & nemo poterat neque in caelo, neque in terra, neque subtus terra aperire librum; neque respicere illum: & ego flebam multum, quoniam nemo dignus inventus est aperire librum, nec videre eum. Et unus de senioribus dixit mihi: Ne fleveris: ecce vicit leo de tribu Iuda, radix David, aperire librum, & solvere septem signacula ejus. Nam dum iste Befeleel, quem Christi figuram gestasse diximus, tantis virtutum praerogativis ornetur, ut & a Deo electus, & ex nomine vocatus, & Spiritu sancto replerus, & cujus filius vel de qua stirpe fit describatur, incassum ob imaginum adorationem firmandam in exemplum trahitur: cum videlicet cunctis pictoribus excellentior, cunctisque artificibus imagines formantibus credatur fuisse praestantior: cujus si operibus pictura vel cujusliber opificio imagines conditae adsimilandae sunt, illi quoque pictores vel cujuslibet artis opifices imagines condentes adsimilandi sunt: & si illi pictores vel eujuslibet opificii homines imagines condentes adsimilandi sunt, ipsi quoque opifices sive ab his conditae imagines suturorum insignem praefigurationem gerunt: non autem pictores vel cujuslibet opificii homines nec opera eorum futurorum quandam praefigurationem gerunt: non igitur illius operibus pictura vel cujuslibet opificio imagines conditae adsimilandae sunt. Quia vero iste novus Befeleel, redemptor videlicet humani generis, spiritum sapientiae, scientiae & intellegentiae habuerit, qui utique unius cum patre & filio substantiae est, & a patre filioque procedit: Esaias Propheta testis est. Ait enim, Exiet virga de radice Iesse, & flos de radice ejus ascendet & requiescet super eum spiritus Domini, spiritus sapientiae & intellectus, spiritus consilii & fortitudinis, spiritus scientiae & pietatis, & replebit eum spiritus timoris Domini. Et idem Dominus per eundem Prophetam dicit, Spiritus Domini super me, propter quod unxit me. Hic ergo quod facit ex auro & argento, facit in ornamentis tabernaculi: cum videlicet sanctos viros auro conflantes, id est, interiori intellegentia, argento niteres, id est, divinis eloquiis ornatos, & ut ita dixerim, aurum in corde habentes, juxta illud, Corde creditur ad justitiam: argentum in confessione oris, juxta illud, Ore autem confessio fit ad salutem: in tabernaculo Dei, sancta scilicet Ecclesia, ad aeternam patriam transituros constituit. Quae duo aurum & argentum, id est, fidem & confessionem, Apostolus quaerebat cum dicebat, Quia prope est verbum in ore tuo & in corde tuo: quia si confessus fueris Dominum Iesum Christum, & credideris in corde tuo quod Deus illum suscitavit a mortuis, salvus eris. Quae etiam ad exornandum tabernaculum Moyses quaerebat, cum dicebat, Sumite a vobis ipsis emptionem Domino: omnis qui conceperit corde, offerat initia Domino, aurum, argentum, & caetera. Qui etiam cum sit sapientia Dei patris, in sanctis hominibus spiritali sensu exuberantibus habitare dinoscitur, dicente Scriptura, Sapientia Dei super lapides pretiosos est, habitatio ejus in vasis aureis. De qua sapientia alias per Salomonem dicitur, Beatus homo qui invenit sapientiam, & affluit prudentia: melior est adquisitio ejus negotiatione argenti & auro primo: fructus ejus pretiosior est cunctis opibus: & omnia quae desiderantur huic non valent comparari. Quia ergo in argento eloquiorum divinorum nitor intelligitur, Psalmistae testimonio adpiobandum est dicentis, Eloquia Domini eloquia casta, argentum igni examinatum terra purgatum septuplum. Huic namque Befeleel ad peragendum opus in adjutorium datur Achisama. Quem namque Achisama iste qui adjutorium Christo praebet, nisi sanctos Apostolos & Apostolicos viros significat? qui nimirum dum per praedicationem, studia & bonorum operum exempla homines in ecclesiae gremio & virtutibus coruscare faciunt, & ad aeternam patriam perrexerunt, Christi adjutores exstiterunt. De quibus profecto erat ille qui dicebat, Dei adjutores sumus: Dei agricultura estis: Dei aedificatio estis. Quae igitur omnia dum allegoricis plena sint sensibus, & ropicis per legislatorem prolata figuris, non solum dementissimum, sed etiam insanissimum est ea imaginibus, quas unusquisque opifex pro captu ingenii sui quales voluerit, immo quales potuerit, effecit, adsimilare conari.
units.tr: THE LAW, as the Apostle says, is spiritual. For it has been given to us by God on the dark road of this present age to direct the steps of our minds, so that by its light the eye of the mind may survey and see the hidden mystical senses. For the commandment of the Lord is bright, says the Prophet, enlightening the eyes; and again, Your word, O Lord, is a lamp to my feet and a light to my paths. Of this it is said by a certain wise man: The commandment is a lamp, and the law a light of life, and reproof and discipline. And Isaiah: My spirit watches for you in the night, O God, for your commandments are light upon the earth. Since all those who do not understand rightly are blind to this light, those are surely believed to be utterly blind who, for I know not what adoration of images, strive to bend it violently to their own senses, and in their error try to lend it some support, as though it were a help to them; for they try to bring forward testimonies from it, though these have nothing to do with the matter. Therefore, because Bezaleel was chosen by the Lord to make the work in gold and silver, and was filled with the spirit of wisdom, understanding and knowledge, they drag this into their error as a testimony, as if the things made through him at the Lord's command, which breathed mystical and typical figures, were to be adored. Bezaleel therefore means in the shadow of God, and Uri is understood as the light of fire. Therefore, what is Bezaleel, who, as we have said, is interpreted in the shadow of God, a type of, unless of him for whom the Church always cries, Protect me under the shadow of your wings; and, Under the shadow of your wings, until iniquity passes away; and of whom the bride in the Song of Songs says, I sat under the shadow of him whom I desired. For he is called the son of Uri, the son of Hur, because he is the ineffable splendour, God from light, of whom it is said through the prophet Habakkuk, His splendour will be as light. For God is a fire, as Moses says, a consuming fire; which the Apostle Paul also says in his Epistle to the Hebrews in the same words; and the same Lord says through the prophet Zechariah, Jerusalem will be inhabited without walls, because of the multitude of men and beasts, and I will be to it a wall of fire round about. Since he is of one substance with the Father, and speaks to Moses in the fire, and says to the disciples in the Gospel, I came to send fire upon the earth; and what do I desire but that it be kindled? Were not the hearts of those who said, Did not our heart burn within us while he spoke to us on the way, and opened to us the Scriptures? inflamed by that fire? So Bezaleel is called by name, because the Lord says to him through the prophet Isaiah in a paternal voice, And I have called you by your name, Isa. 43; and of whom it is said through Moses, Behold, I will send an angel to go before you and keep you in the way, and bring you into the place which I have prepared. Observe him and hear his voice, and do not think him to be despised, because he will not forgive your sins, and my name is in him. But the lineage of this Bezaleel, who was called by name, is not passed over either. For Scripture says, the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah. For this is he of whom it was foretold by the Israelite voice: Judah is a lion's whelp; you have gone up to the prey, my son; that is, going to plunder hell on the cross, resting as a lion, that is, in the sepulchre; and like a lioness, who will rouse him? because by the power of the Father he rose from the dead on the third day. Hear the Apostle saying that he rose by the power of the Father: God raised him up on the third day, and granted that he should be made manifest, not to all the people. Tell me, I ask you, holy John, who lay on the breast of the mediator of God and men, and drew the shining cups from the fountain of eternal light, whence you daily pour out to Christian minds the nectar of ambrosial liquor: whence our Bezaleel is descended, whose type that ancient Bezaleel of the law once bore. I saw, I say, in the right hand of him who sat upon the throne, a book written within and without, sealed with seven seals; and I saw a strong angel proclaiming with a loud voice: Who is worthy to open the book and loose its seals? And no one in heaven, nor on earth, nor under the earth, was able to open the book or even look at it; and I wept much, because no one was found worthy to open the book or see it. And one of the elders said to me: Do not weep; behold, the lion of the tribe of Judah, the root of David, has conquered to open the book and loose its seven seals. For since that Bezaleel, whom we have said bore the figure of Christ, is adorned with such great prerogatives of virtue, so that he is both chosen by God and called by name, and filled with the Holy Spirit, and his son or the stock from which he comes is described, he is drawn in vain as an example to strengthen the adoration of images: when he is evidently believed to have been more excellent than all painters, and superior to all craftsmen who form images. If images made by his works or any craft are to be compared with him, then painters, or men of any craft who make images, are also to be compared with him; and if those painters or men of any craft who make images are to be compared with him, then the craftsmen themselves, or the images made by them, bear a notable figure of things to come; but painters, or men of any craft, do not bear any figure of things to come, nor do their works. Therefore images made by painting or any craft are not to be compared with his works. Moreover, that this new Bezaleel, that is, the redeemer of the human race, had the spirit of wisdom, knowledge and understanding, who is surely of one substance with the Father and the Son, and proceeds from the Father and the Son, the prophet Isaiah is witness. For he says, A shoot will come forth from the root of Jesse, and a flower will rise from his root, and the spirit of the Lord will rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and fortitude, the spirit of knowledge and godliness, and the spirit of the fear of the Lord will fill him. And the same Lord says through the same prophet, The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me. Therefore he who makes things of gold and silver makes them for the ornaments of the tabernacle; that is, he sets holy men, who are fused with gold, that is, with inner understanding, and shine with silver, that is, adorned with divine utterances, and, so to speak, have gold in their heart, according to that saying, With the heart one believes unto righteousness; and silver in the confession of the mouth, according to that saying, With the mouth confession is made unto salvation; in the tabernacle of God, namely the holy Church, destined to pass to the eternal fatherland. These two, gold and silver, that is, faith and confession, the Apostle sought when he said, The word is near you, in your mouth and in your heart; for if you confess the Lord Jesus Christ, and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved. Moses also sought these things for adorning the tabernacle when he said, Take from yourselves an offering to the Lord: everyone whose heart is moved, let him offer to the Lord the first fruits, gold, silver, and the rest. Since he is also the wisdom of God the Father, he is known to dwell in holy men who abound in spiritual sense, as Scripture says, The wisdom of God is above precious stones; its dwelling is in golden vessels. Of this wisdom it is said elsewhere through Solomon, Blessed is the man who finds wisdom, and abounds in prudence: its gain is better than the trading of silver and its profit better than first gold; it is more precious than all riches, and all things that are desired cannot be compared with it. Since therefore the lustre of the divine utterances is understood in the silver, it must be approved by the testimony of the Psalmist who says, The words of the Lord are chaste words, silver tried in the fire, purified from the earth, sevenfold. For Oholiab is given to this Bezaleel as a helper in carrying out the work. For whom does this Oholiab, who gives help to Christ, signify, unless the holy Apostles and apostolic men? These, indeed, while by their preaching, their zeal and the examples of good works they make men shine in the bosom of the Church and in virtues, and have gone on to the eternal fatherland, have been helpers of Christ. Of whom surely was he who said, We are God's fellow-workers; you are God's field; you are God's building. Since therefore all these things are full of allegorical senses, and figures spoken by the lawgiver in a typical manner, it is not only most mad but also most insane to try to make them resemble images which each craftsman has made as his talent allowed, or rather as he was able, of whatever kind he wished.

units.la: CAP. XVII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XVII.

units.la: Quòd non recte sentiant qui dicunt, Si secundum Moysi legitimam traditionem praecipitur populo purpura hyacinthina in fimbriis, in extremis vestimentis poni ad memoriam & custodiam praeceptorum, multò magis nobis est per adsimilatam picturam sanctorum virorum videre exitum conversationis eorum, & eorum imitari fidem secundum Apostolicam traditionem.
units.tr: That those are wrong who say: if, according to Moses' lawful tradition, the people are commanded to put hyacinthine purple on the fringes, on the extreme garments, as a memorial and guard of the precepts, then much more for us it is by a likened picture of holy men to see the outcome of their conduct, and to imitate their faith according to Apostolic tradition.

units.la: TOTUM hoc capitulum commaticè est considerandum, & per singula unicuique particulae respondendum: quoniam quamquam ad unius erroris tendat propositum, ex multis tamen particulatim est erroribus conpaginatum. Primo namque discutiendum est, cur purpuram hyacinthinam in eodem capitulo dixerint: cum videlicet alius color fit purpureus, & alius hyacinthinus: & sicut non poterit recte dici rubeus candor & candens rubor, velut si quis dicar argenteum aurum vel aureum argentum, ita necrecte dici poterit purpura hyacinthina, ut converso ordine dici queat purpurea hyacinthus: quoniam talis derivatio reciprocata nullius sensus vigore manere potest inconvnlsa: quoniam quidem, ut praefati sumus, alius color est hyacinthinus & alius purpureus, testis est ipsa lex a Domino per Moysen data, quae singillatim haec quatuor, hyacinthum videlicet, purpuram & coccum seu etiam byssum ad indumenta pontificis conficienda, vel caetera quae ad facrarium praeparandum essent offerenda, designar: quibus quatuor materiis majores nostri quatuor elementorum figuram, ex quibus mundus sive humanum corpus constat, significari dixerunt, & singulas tropologice virtutes innuere docuerunt. Hyacinthum ergo ad aërem referunt, quod & ipse in aërcat color, sicut & coccum ad ignem: purpuram aquae accommodant, eo quod de aquis accipiat fucum: byssum terrae, quia oritur ex terra. Denique & illud discutiendum est quod imaginum usum exemplo fimbriarum hyacinthinarum munire niruntur: cum praesertim illas priscae legis in mysterium series in extremis vestibus poni jubeat: istas vero ut adorentur nec veteris nec novi testamenti pagani uspiam in factariis poni praecipiat. Neque enim tanti erroris hoc exemplo valet adstruere, quod per legislatorem idcirco conlatum est, ut quaedam archani sensus immeret indicia: nec res bene justa beneque gestata tanto deliramento poterit convenire conlata. Inlaus igitur Dominus per Moysen mandatis legis ad extremum intulit, Ligabis ea in manu tua & erunt immota ante oculos tuos. Quae nos spiritaliter dum opere complemus in manibus immota tenemus: & cum dic ac nocte meditamur in eis, ante oculos conlocara gestamus. Iussit quoque fimbrias hyacinthinas fieri in quatuor angulis palliorum, sive ad dinoscendum populum Israel, ut essent signum in veste, sicut circumcisio signum in corpore: sive ut nos, qui spiritalis Israhel sumus, habeamus pro indumento justitiam & sanctam conversationem: hujus indumenti extremitas fimbriis hyacinthinis sit ornata, quatenus vita nostra sanctarum scripturarum sit testimoniis erudita. Hic enim fimbriarum bonus usus & bene per legislatorem sive illi carnali Israheli, sive nobis spirituali bene concessus, malc ab illis abutus potius quam habimus est. De quibus veritas in evangelio dicit, Dilatant enim phylacteria & magnificant fimbrias. Cujus quaesio isti, cujus exemplum tenent? nisi Pharisaeorum qui dum volunt vocari ab hominibus Rabbi, & quaerunt primas in foro salutationes, primas in conventibus cathedra, dumque per appetitum vanae laudis sua dicta vel facta cupiunt mandare memoriae posteritatis, imagines quae bene a quibusdam in basilicarum ornamentis constitutae fuerunt, per ineptas & inutiles synodos male & ipsi adorant & alios adorare compellunt. Illi per inanem gloriam simbrias magnificant, isti nihilominus per jactantiam imagines adorant: illi bene institutas male magnificando dilatant, isti bene conditas male adorando exaltant: illi putant Moysi praeceptis parere fimbrias magnificando, isti putant se sanctis omnibus placere imagines adorando: ac per hoc quamquam per diversa discurrant & diversa diversis modis sequantur, ad unius erroris destinatam tendere noscuntur: nec inmerito, cum horum effectuum causae sive efficientia nil aliud sint nisi ventosae laudis gloria sive arrogantia. Ut ergo istius vanissimi capituli quod discutere commaticè propositum, errorem expressius discutiatur, necesse est ut illius textus ex ordine repetatur. Garriunt enim, Si secundum Moysi legitimam traditionem praecipitur populo purpura hyacintina in fimbriis in extremis vestimentis poni, ad memoriam & custodiam praeceptorum, multo magis nobis est per adsimilatam picturam sanctorum virorum videre exitum conversationis eorum. Hoc quod dicunt, multo magis, quod pertinet ad praecipitur, ut subaudiatur, si populo praecipitur, multo magis nobis, nullum declevem sensum quidem habere potest: quippe cum non solum multo magis non praecipitur, sed nec aeque quidem nec minus uspiam hic error praecipi videatur. Quod vero dicunt, Per adsimilatam picturam videre exitum conversationis sanctorum virorum, quantae sit absurditatis quantaeque dementiae, pene infinitum est persequi: cum videlicet in imaginibus non possit sanctae conversationis virtus videri, sed solummodo illae materiae quibus ipsae imagines formatae sunt. Nunc quidnam virtutes & meritorum insignia, quae illis utique in subjecto fuerunt, hoc est in animo, ut hic ea clut in subjecto quodam videri possunt? cum tamen in his non sit anima quae subjacens esse possit virtutibus, in subjecto autem istis hoc est in materiali corpore quodammodo colores sint virtutem autem his nec de subjecto, nec in subjecto esse possunt. Numquid igitur sapientiam, & eloquentiam in istis cernere possumus, quam plerique illorum habuerunt? numquidnam prudentiam afficere in istis valemus, per quam agnitio verae fidei & scientia divinorum apicum in illis fuit? per quam trimodum illud intelligentiae genus in divinis libris a prudentibus intellegitur. Quorum primum est, per quod quaedam ita accipiuntur historialiter, sepositis aenigmaticis vel allegoricis figuris, ut est decalogus legis. Secundum, per quod quaedam in scripturis mystice accipiuntur, tam secundum fidem rerum gestarum, quam etiam juxta figuram allegoricorum sensuum: sicut petra ex qua legislator latices elicuit & historialiter cautis fuit, & aquas evomuit, & allegorice Christi figuram gestit, qui cum sit lapis in fundamento Sion fundatus, mellifluo spiritalis vitae poculo credentium metes sitiat. Tertium genus est, quod tantum spiritaliter accipitur, sicut de canticis canticorum, in quibus nil historialiter, sed tantum spiritaliter accipiendum est. An justitia in istis intueri potest? per quam sancti Deum timebant, religionem venerabantur, cunctis prodesse, nulli nocere curabant, fraternae charitatis vincula ampleati, sive alicna pericula suscipere, vel etiam opem ferre misetis, nec non & boni accepti vicissitudinem rependere, seu aequitatem in judiciis conservare studebant. An illorum fortitudinem in pictorum coloribus perspicere possumus? per quam magnanimes adversa aequanimiter tolerarent, & his patienter ceciere, & spretis inlecebris fortiter restitere: per quam
units.tr: The whole of this chapter must be examined piece by piece, and each part answered separately, for although its purpose tends to one error, it is made up of many errors put together. First, then, we must ask why they speak of "hyacinthine purple" in the same chapter, since clearly one colour is purple and another hyacinthine. Just as one cannot rightly speak of "reddish whiteness" or "glowing redness", as if one were to call silvery gold or golden silver, so "hyacinthine purple" cannot rightly be said, nor can the order be reversed to "purple hyacinth", for such a reciprocal derivation cannot stand unshaken by the force of any sense. As we have said, hyacinthine is one colour and purple another. The law given by the Lord through Moses bears witness to this, for it names these four singly: hyacinth, purple, scarlet (coccum) and fine linen (byssus), to be used in making the high priest's garments or in the other things to be offered for preparing the sanctuary. To these four materials our forefathers said the figure of the four elements, of which the world or the human body consists, was signified, and they taught that each indicates a tropological virtue. So they refer hyacinth to air, because it is itself of the colour of air, as scarlet is to fire; they fit purple to water, because it takes its dye from waters; fine linen to earth, because it grows from the earth. Finally, we must also examine what they strive to do. They seek to defend the use of images by the example of the hyacinthine fringes, especially since the law of the old covenant commands those fringes to be placed on the extreme garments for a mystery, whereas neither the Old nor the New Testament anywhere commands that images be placed in sanctuaries to be adored. Nor does this example avail to establish so great an error, since the lawgiver brought it in only so that it might be a sign of some hidden sense; nor can a thing rightly ordained and rightly done be compared to such a delirium. Therefore the Lord through Moses at last added to the commandments of the law: You shall bind them on your hand, and they shall be unmoved before your eyes. When we fulfil these spiritually in our works, we hold them unmoved in our hands, and when we meditate on them day and night, we carry them set before our eyes. He also ordered hyacinthine fringes to be made on the four corners of the cloaks, either so that the people of Israel might be distinguished, the fringe being a sign on the garment as circumcision is a sign on the body, or so that we, who are the spiritual Israel, might have righteousness and holy conduct for a garment, its edge adorned with hyacinthine fringes, so that our life may be instructed by the testimonies of the holy Scriptures. This good use of the fringes, well granted by the lawgiver both to that carnal Israel and to us spiritual, has been abused by them rather than used. Of such people the truth says in the Gospel: For they enlarge their phylacteries and magnify their fringes. Whose example do these men hold? Surely that of the Pharisees, who wish to be called Rabbi by men, who seek the first greetings in the marketplace and the first seats in assemblies, and who, through desire for empty praise, want to commit their sayings and deeds to the memory of posterity. So these men wickedly adore, and compel others to adore, the images which some have rightly set up in the decoration of basilicas, through foolish and useless synods. The Pharisees magnify the fringes through vainglory; these men, nonetheless, adore images through boasting. The former enlarge well-instituted things by magnifying them wrongly; these exalt well-made things by adoring them wrongly. The former think they obey the precepts of Moses by magnifying the fringes; these think they please all the saints by adoring images. Thus, although they run in different directions and follow different things in different ways, they are known to tend toward one destined error, and not undeservedly, since the causes or efficient causes of these effects are nothing other than the glory of windy praise, or arrogance. So, in order to examine more clearly the error of this most vain chapter, which we have proposed to discuss piece by piece, its text must be repeated in order. For they babble: If, according to Moses' lawful tradition, the people are commanded to put hyacinthine purple on the fringes, on the extreme garments, as a memorial and guard of the precepts, much more for us it is, by a likened picture of holy men, to see the outcome of their conduct. What they say, "much more", which goes with "is commanded", is to be understood as: if it is commanded to the people, much more to us. This can have no clear sense at all, since not only is it not commanded "much more", but nowhere here does this error appear to be commanded equally or even less. As to what they say, "to see by a likened picture the outcome of the conduct of holy men", it would be nearly endless to pursue how great its absurdity and how great its madness: namely, because in images the virtue of holy conduct cannot be seen, but only the materials of which the images are formed. Now, what are the virtues and marks of merit, which indeed were in their subject, that is in the mind, so that they could be seen here as in some subject? In these images there is no soul that could underlie virtues; in what underlies them, the material body, there are, in a manner of speaking, only colours, and virtues can be neither from such things nor in them. Can we, then, discern in these images the wisdom and eloquence which most of the saints had? Can we perceive in them the prudence through which they knew the true faith and the understanding of divine writings, by which the prudent grasp the threefold kind of understanding in the divine books? The first of these is that by which some things are taken historically, with enigmatic or allegorical figures set aside, as the Decalogue of the law. The second is that by which some things in the Scriptures are taken mystically, both according to the faith of the deeds done and also according to the figure of allegorical senses: as the rock from which the lawgiver drew water, which was historically a rock and poured forth waters, and allegorically bears the figure of Christ, who, being the stone founded in the foundation of Zion, slakes the thirst of believers with the honeyed cup of spiritual life. The third kind is that which is taken only spiritually, as in the Song of Songs, where nothing is to be taken historically but only spiritually. Can justice be seen in these images, by which the saints feared God, revered religion, cared to benefit all and harm none, embraced the bonds of brotherly charity, undertook the dangers of others, brought help to the wretched, repaid in turn the good they had received, and strove to preserve equity in judgements? Can we discern their fortitude in the colours of painters, by which the magnanimous bore adversity with equanimity, endured patiently, and bravely resisted allurements, having scorned them: by which

units.la: Matth. 23. mordaces gazas & gloriæ appetitus effugerunt: per quam etiam nec adversis frangebantur, nec celebrabantur secundis: cujus lorica induti fortes ad labores existentes, ad pericula contra improbos molestiis nullis cedentes, animos paravere. An illorum temperantia in his imaginibus cernitur? per quam affectionem carnis moderantes restringebant appetitum. Cum ergo nil horum quæ prædiximus in iis videri possit, magnæ est temeritatis dicere, In adsimilata pictura videre exitum conversationis sanctorum. Sequitur in eodem vanissimo capitulo, Et eorum imitari fidem secundum Apostolicam traditionem. Num quidnam eorum fides quæ secundum Apostolum per dilectionem operatur in imaginibus imitari potest? Sicut ergo non potest videri in his exitus conversationis sanctorum, sic nec fides imitari: quoniam quæ illis desunt in his nec videri nec per has imitari possunt. Omne quod caret vita, caret sensu: omne quod caret sensu, caret fide: omne igitur quod caret vita, caret fide. Nam cum sint spes fides & charitas invisibiles & incorporalis qualitatis secundum proprietatem suæ substantiæ, in vero homine qui has habet, videri non possunt, nisi forte in operibus demonstrentur: fides enim earum sicut & ceterarum virtutum, in anima est, quam constat esse invisibilem. Et si in vero, qui has utique habet, videri non possunt, multo minus in pictio videri poterunt, qui non solum his, ut præfati sumus sed etiam vita caret: & si in his videri non possunt, multo igitur minus imitari poterunt. unde datur intellegi, vanam esse eorum fidem qui per imagines sanctorum fidem imitaturos se dicunt. Iam vero quia dicunt, secundum Apostolicam traditionem, dicant ubi ab Apostolis aut exemplis aut verbis traditum sit. Per imagines videre exitum conversationis sanctorum & eorum imitari fidem. Exitum ergo conversationis sanctorum hoc modo demonstrat Apostolus, cum dicit, Sancti omnes juxta fidem defuncti sunt non acceptis repromissionibus, sed a longe aspicientes & salutantes & confitentes quia peregrini & hospites sunt super terram: sive cum dicit, Sancti per fidem vicerunt regna, operati sunt justitiam, adepti sunt repromissiones, extinxerunt impetum ignis, convaluerunt de infirmitate, fortes facti sunt in bello, vel cetera quæ sequuntur. Quid ergo debeamus imitari evidentissime idem Apostolus demonstrat, cum dicit, Estote imitatores Dei sicut filii charissimi: & in alio loco dicit, Imitatores mei estote sicut & ego Christi. Unde liquido patet hanc esse Apostolicam traditionem, ut non in picturis, sed in virtutibus videri possit sanctorum exitus conversationis, & eorum imitari fides, non imaginum fucis, sed in operibus bonis.
units.tr: Matth. 23. They fled from biting avarice and the appetite for glory; by which they were not broken by adversity nor exalted by prosperity; clad in whose breastplate they stood strong for labours, yielding to no hardship, and prepared their minds against the wicked in dangers. Can their temperance be seen in these images, by which they restrained the appetite and moderated the affections of the flesh? Since none of these things we have named can be seen in them, it is great rashness to say, In a likened picture one may see the outcome of the conduct of the saints. There follows in the same most vain chapter: And to imitate their faith according to Apostolic tradition. Can the faith of these men, which according to the Apostle works through love, be imitated in images? Just as the outcome of the holy men's conduct cannot be seen in these, so their faith cannot be imitated, since what they lacked cannot be seen in these nor imitated through them. Whatever lacks life lacks sense; whatever lacks sense lacks faith; therefore whatever lacks life lacks faith. For since hope, faith and charity are invisible and of an incorporeal quality according to the nature of their substance, they cannot be seen in a true man who has them, unless perhaps they are shown in works; for their faith, like that of the other virtues, is in the soul, which is plainly invisible. And if they cannot be seen in a true man, who indeed has them, much less can they be seen in a painted image, which lacks not only these, as we have said, but also life. And if they cannot be seen in these, much less can they be imitated through them, whence it may be understood that the faith of those who say they will imitate the faith of the saints through their images is vain. Now, since they say "according to Apostolic tradition", let them say where it was handed down by the Apostles, either by examples or by words, that one may see by images the outcome of the saints' conduct and imitate their faith. The outcome of the saints' conduct is indeed shown in this way by the Apostle, when he says: All these died according to faith, not having received the promises, but seeing them from afar and greeting them, and confessing that they are strangers and pilgrims on the earth; or when he says: Through faith the saints conquered kingdoms, wrought righteousness, obtained promises, quenched the power of fire, were made strong out of weakness, became mighty in war, and the rest that follows. What we ought to imitate the same Apostle shows most clearly, when he says: Be imitators of God as beloved children; and in another place he says: Be imitators of me, as I am of Christ. Whence it is plainly evident that this is the Apostolic tradition: that the outcome of the saints' conduct may be seen not in pictures but in virtues, and their faith imitated not by the dyes of images but in good works.

units.la: CAP. XVIII. Quod vana sit spes eorum qui salutem suam in imaginibus ponunt, dicentes, Sicut Israeli- ticus populus serpentis æneî inspectione servatus est, sic nos sanctorum effigies aspicientes salvabimur.
units.tr: CAP. XVIII. That the hope of those who place their salvation in images is vain, who say, As the Israelite people were saved by looking upon the bronze serpent, so we shall be saved by looking upon the images of the saints.

units.la: SPes eorum qui salutem suam in imaginibus ponunt ab Apostolo reprobatur qui spem non in his quæ videntur, sed in his quæ non videntur esse differt. ait enim, Spes quæ videtur non est spes: quod enim videt quis, quid speret? Si autem quod non videmus speramus, per patientiam expectamus. Nam dum æneus serpens præcipiente Domino à Moyse conditus, & in sublimi fuerit, non ut adoraretur, positus, sed ut ad tempus ignitorum serpentium virosis obsisteret morbis, falsæ spei ludificatione deluduntur, qui ira se manu factarum imaginum inspectione sanandos arbitrantur, sicut Israeliticus populus illius æneî serpentis inspectione ab ignitarum pestium mortiferis ictibus sanabatur: præsertim cum ille ut fieret, Moysi à Domino imperatum est: hæ vero ut fiant nullius scripturæ textu sit institutum. Quid ergo serpens ille, cujus inspectione à serpentibus vulneratis sanabantur, significaverit ipso redemptore nostro docente cognovimus, qui ait, Sicut Moyses exaltavit serpentem in deserto, ita exaltari oportet filium hominis: quem videlicet dum sedula mente interius oculis aspicimus, malignorum spirituum mortiferis tentationum morbis superatis, æternæ mortis periculæ evitamus. Præterea sicut in divinæ legis verbis ea quæ à sancto Spiritu bene in lege, Prophetis, evangelio sive Apostolis dicta sunt, plerumque perversa intentione ab schismaticis male intelliguntur, itâ etiam pleraque quæ idcirco à patribus ut prodessent instituta vel facta sunt, decursis prolixorum temporum curriculis, à posteris male habita & in perversum mutata fuisse creduntur, sicut de phylacteriis & fimbriis, de quibus paulo superius dictum est, vel etiam de æneo serpente, de quo nunc dicere instituimus, qui, ut præfati sumus, ad tempus ut vulneratis à serpentibus prodesset, fuit necessarius, per quem postmodum inolevit excelsorum insolentissimus usus: cui cum differet Ezechias rex justus incensa adolere & quasdam culturas exhibere, magnaque ex parte populum periclitari, tanto persuasum errore, eum non distulit frangere, quem & per legislatorem ad profectu novterat conditum fuisse, & à populo cernebat celebrari vano cultu & superstitiosa religione. Laus ergo ejusdem Ezechiæ sanctissimi regis eo quod vanas superstitiones abstulerit, eundemque serpentem confregerit, hoc modo in divinis literis habetur: Fecit, inquit, Ezechias quod bonum erat coram Domino, juxta omnia quæ fecerat David pater suus: ipse dissipavit excelsa & contrivit statuas, & succidit lucos, confregitque serpentem æneum quem fecerat Moyses: siquidem usque ad illud tempus filii Israel adolebant ei incensum, vocavitque eum Nachstan. In Domino Deo Israel speravit, itaque post eum non fuit similis ei de cunctis regibus Iuda, sed neque in his qui ante eum fuerunt: & adhaesit Domino, & non recessit à vestigiis ejus, fecitque mandata ejus quæ præceperat Dominus Moysi, & erat Dominus cum eo & in cunctis ad quæ procedebat sapienter agebat.
units.tr: The hope of those who place their salvation in images is rejected by the Apostle, who distinguishes hope placed in things that are seen from hope placed in things that are not seen. For he says, Hope that is seen is not hope: for what a man sees, why does he hope for it? But if we hope for what we do not see, we wait for it with patience. For when the bronze serpent, made by Moses at the command of the Lord and set up on high, was placed there not to be worshipped but to resist for a time the deadly bites of the fiery serpents, those are deluded by a false hope who think they will be healed by looking at images made by human hands, just as the Israelite people were healed from the deadly strikes of the fiery plagues by looking at that bronze serpent. This is especially so since Moses was commanded by the Lord to make the serpent, whereas no text of Scripture has ever instituted that images be made. What that serpent, by whose sight those bitten by serpents were healed, signified we have learned from our Redeemer himself, who teaches, As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of man be lifted up. If with a diligent mind we look upon him inwardly, then, with the deadly diseases of the evil spirits' temptations overcome, we escape the danger of eternal death. Moreover, just as in the words of divine law, those things that the Holy Spirit has rightly spoken in the Law, the Prophets, the Gospel or the Apostles are often misunderstood by the schismatics through a perverse intention, so also many things that the fathers instituted or did for the sake of benefit are believed, after long lapses of time, to have been ill-treated by posterity and turned into perversion. This is so with the phylacteries and fringes, of which we spoke a little above, and also with the bronze serpent, of which we now intend to speak.
