As we have said, it was necessary for a time, so that it might benefit those wounded by serpents, and through it there later grew up the most insolent custom of the high places. When King Ezechias, a righteous man, hesitated to burn incense and offer certain worship to it, and saw the people, to a great extent, in danger, persuaded by so great an error, he did not hesitate to break it, though it had been made, as he knew, by the lawgiver for a good purpose, and he saw it being honoured by the people with vain worship and superstitious religion. The praise of that most holy king Ezechias, because he removed vain superstitions and broke that serpent, is recorded in the divine letters in this way: Ezechias, he says, did what was good in the sight of the Lord, according to all that David his father had done. He himself removed the high places, broke the statues, cut down the groves, and broke the bronze serpent that Moses had made; for until that time the children of Israel burned incense to it, and they called it Nehushtan. He trusted in the Lord God of Israel, so that after him there was none like him among all the kings of Judah, nor among those who were before him. He clung to the Lord and did not depart from following him, and kept his commandments which the Lord had commanded Moses; and the Lord was with him, and in all that he undertook he acted wisely.

units.la: blxc Haec praeterea & hujusmodi superstitiones, quas se quidem putant ob amorem Dei facere: sicut hi qui ob sanctorum amorem imaginibus luminaria accendunt, easque adorant. Hoc modo beatus Hieronymus dum de fimbriis & phylacteriis Pharisaeorum sancti evangelii lectionem exponeret, reprehendit dicens: Hoc apud nos, inquit, superstitiose multerculae in parvulis evangelium & in crucis ligno & in ißusmodi rebus, quae habent quidem zelum Dei, sed non juxta scientiam neque bodie factitant, culicem liquantes, & camelum glutientes. Iam vero quia se imaginum inspectione salvandos credunt, sicut serpentis inspectione Ifrahelitieus populus a serpentium morsibus sanabatur, si qua forte eis quaedam corporis inclementia accesserit, recurrant ad imagines, easque adspiciant, quatenus dum illarum inspectione mitiores lapsi fuerint, revertantur ad Dominum, & per sanctorum intercessiones ab eo sanitatem se accepisse credant, qui totius sanitatis & vitae est auctor.
units.tr: Moreover, these and similar superstitions, which people think they do out of love for God, are like those who, out of love for the saints, light candles before images and worship them. In this way blessed Jerome, while expounding the Gospel reading about the fringes and phylacteries of the Pharisees, rebuked it, saying: Among us, he says, superstitious old women make a gospel of little children, and a cross of wood, and such things, which indeed have a zeal for God, but not according to knowledge, nor do they act wisely, straining out a gnat and swallowing a camel. Now, since they believe they will be saved by looking at images, just as the Israelite people were healed from the bites of serpents by looking at the serpent, if by chance some bodily infirmity should befall them, they run to the images and look upon them, so that, when they have been made milder by looking at them, they may return to the Lord, and believe that they have received health through the intercession of the saints from him who is the author of all health and life.

units.la: CAP. XIX. Quod magna sit temeritatis dicere, Sicut Iudaeis tabulae & duo cherubim: sic nobis Christianis donata est crux & sanctorum imagines, ad scribendum & adorandum.
units.tr: CHAPTER XIX. That it is great rashness to say: as the tablets and the two cherubim were given to the Jews, so the cross and the images of the saints were given to us Christians, for writing and for adoration.

units.la: Sape in hoc opere dicere compellimur, quod neque tabulae neque duo cherubim, nec caetera huiuscemodi adorandum in veteri testamento facta fuisse credantur: quae quidem isti omnia recto medio gitatis & rectitudinis calle in eo ultra quam ordo exposcit, extollunt, quod ea ad adorandum fuisse conlata proclamant: in eo vero ultra quam res exigit submittunt, quod illis imagines aequipararefferent. Cum ergo dicunt, Sicut Iudaeis tabulae & duo cherubim, ita nobis Christianis data est crux & sanctorum imagines ad adorandum & ad scribendum: quid aliud faciunt, nisi ut imagines exaltent, Christianorum res extenuent? praesertim cum illos qui sub lege erant dicant habuisse duos cherubim a Moyse conditos, de quorum medio Deus loquebatur, nos autem qui sub gratia sumus dicant habere cruces, quae a quibuslibet artificibus efficiuntur: illos qui umbram legis sequebantur habuisse fixdemos tabulas, continentes legis decalogum, nos qui veritatem quae Christus est sequimur, habere opera quorumlibet artificum: illos qui spiritum servitutis acceperunt, in timore dicant habuisse ea quae Moyses faciebat, Domino insinuante, nos qui spiritum adoptionis accepimus, in quo clamamus Abba pater, habere imagines quas quilibet pictor condit, mundanae tantum artis experientia perdocente. Nos enim, qui non sequimur literam mortificantem, sed spiritum vivificantem, qui non carnalis, sed spiritalis Israhel sumus, qui spretis visibilibus invisibilia contemplamur, non solum imaginibus majora mysteria, quae omni mysterio carent, sed ipsis tabulis seu duobus cherubim majora & eminentiora mysteriorum insignia a Domino accepisse nos gratulamur: cum videlicet tabulae & duo cherubim exemplaria fuerint futurorum: & cum Iudaei habuerint carnaliter, resque typicis operatae praefigurationes fuerint futurorum, nos habemus in veritate spiritaliter ea, quae illis exemplaribus et praefigurationibus carnalibus praefigurabantur. Quantum ergo eminet umbrae corpus, imago veritas, figurae res gesta, tantum eminet veteri testamento novum: quippe cum illud dedicatum Moyse cum lecto omni mandato legis universo populo, accipiens sanguinem vitulorum & hircorum cum aqua & lana coccinea & hyssopo: ipsum quoque librum & omnem populum adspersit, Hic sanguis testamenti quod mandavit ad vos Deus: istud vero dedicatum fit a mundi redemptore nostro Iesu Christo, qui in qua nocte tradebatur, accepit panem & benedixit ac fregit dedit, dicens, Hoc est corpus meum quod pro vobis tradetur: hoc facite in meam commemorationem: similiter & calicem postquam caenavit, dicens, Hic calix novum testamentum est in meo sanguine, qui pro vobis & pro multis effunditur in remissionem peccatorum. In illo sanguis hircorum & taurorum, & cinis vitulae adspersus coinquinatos sanctificabat, ad emundationem carnis: in isto sanguine Christi qui per Spiritum sanctum semetipsum immaculatum Deo, & mundat conscientias nostras ab operibus mortuis, ad serviendum Deo vivo & vero. In illo agnus per familias occidebatur, ejusque carnibus pascha celebrabatur, in isto agnus Dei qui tollit peccata mundi, qui est vere agnus immaculatus, Deo etiam est in sacrificium oblatus, dicente Apostolo, Pascha nostrum immolatus est Christus. In illo Cananitidis gentis terram quae lacte et melle fluit: in isto pollicetur patria caelestis, in qua datur quod oculus non vidit, nec auris audivit, nec in cor hominis ascendit. In illo neomeniae, id est, novae lunae primitiae colebantur: in isto nova creatura in Christo accipitur, vase electionis Paulo adtestante, Si qua nova in Christo creatura, vetera transierunt, ecce facta sunt nova. In illo sabbati otium & requies in isto sabbati requies, in Christo habetur qui dixit, Venite ad me omnes qui laboratis & onerati estis, & ego vos reficiam, et invenietis requiem animabus vestris. In illo pecoribus inmolatis carnes oblatae hostiae offerebantur: in isto sacrificium carnis & sanguinis Christi offertur, quod per illa animalia figurabatur. In illo jugum grave legis cervicibus impositum faciebat servos: in isto jugum Christi leve & onus suave per spiritum adoptionis facit filios. His ita se habentibus pervertum & ultra quam perversum est, ut alternatim converso ordine praestantioribus deteriora, deterioribusve praestantiora dentur, & adeo imaginum usus magnificetur ut Christianorum res quodam modo extenuentur.
units.tr: Often in this work we are compelled to say that the tablets, the two cherubim, and other things of this kind are not believed to have been made for adoration under the Old Testament. Those people, indeed, in this matter go beyond the straight middle path of truth and rightness, raising these things above what order requires, when they proclaim that they were provided for adoration. In the matter of images, however, they lower them beneath what the case demands, when they set images on a level with those objects. So when they say, As the tablets and the two cherubim were given to the Jews, so the cross and the images of the saints were given to us Christians for adoration and for writing, what else do they do but exalt images and belittle the things of the Christians? Especially since they say that those who were under the law had two cherubim made by Moses, between which God spoke, while we, who are under grace, have crosses made by any craftsmen whatever; that those who followed the shadow of the law had two fixed tablets containing the decalogue of the law, while we, who follow the truth which is Christ, have the work of any craftsmen whatever; that those who received the spirit of bondage had in fear the things Moses made at the Lord's direction, while we, who have received the spirit of adoption, by which we cry, Abba, Father, have images which any painter makes, taught only by the experience of worldly art. For we, who do not follow the letter that kills but the Spirit that gives life, who are not the fleshly but the spiritual Israel, who, having set aside the visible, contemplate the invisible, rejoice that we have received from the Lord not only greater mysteries in images, which lack all mystery, but also, in the very tablets or the two cherubim, greater and more eminent signs of the mysteries. For the tablets and the two cherubim were patterns of things to come; and while the Jews had them in the flesh, and the things wrought in types were foreshadowings of the future, we have in truth, in the Spirit, those things which were foreshadowed by those carnal patterns and prefigurations. Therefore, as the body excels the shadow, the image the truth, and the reality the figure, so the New Testament excels the Old. Indeed, when Moses had dedicated that covenant, after reading every commandment of the law to the whole people, taking the blood of calves and goats with water, scarlet wool and hyssop, he sprinkled both the book itself and all the people, saying, This is the blood of the covenant which God has commanded to you. But that covenant is dedicated by our Redeemer of the world, Jesus Christ, who, on the night in which he was betrayed, took bread, blessed it, broke it, and gave it, saying, This is my body, which is given for you; do this in remembrance of me. Likewise also the cup, after supper, saying, This cup is the new covenant in my blood, which is poured out for you and for many for the remission of sins. In that covenant the blood of goats and bulls, and the ashes of the heifer sprinkled, sanctified the defiled, for the cleansing of the flesh; in this covenant, the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without blemish to God, cleanses our consciences from dead works, to serve the living and true God. In that covenant a lamb was slain by households, and the Passover was celebrated with its flesh; in this covenant the Lamb of God, who takes away the sins of the world, who is truly the unblemished Lamb, was also offered to God as a sacrifice, the Apostle saying, Christ our Passover is sacrificed for us. In that covenant the land of the Canaanite nation, which flows with milk and honey; in this covenant the heavenly fatherland is promised, in which is given what eye has not seen, nor ear heard, nor has entered into the heart of man. In that covenant the new moons, that is, the first fruits of the new moon, were observed; in this covenant the new creature is received in Christ, Paul, the chosen vessel, bearing witness: If anyone is in Christ, he is a new creature; the old things have passed away; behold, they have become new. In that covenant the rest and leisure of the Sabbath; in this covenant the rest of the Sabbath is found in Christ, who said, Come to me, all you who labour and are heavy laden, and I will refresh you, and you will find rest for your souls. In that covenant the flesh of the slain beasts was offered as sacrificial victims; in this covenant the sacrifice of the flesh and blood of Christ is offered, which was prefigured by those animals. In that covenant the heavy yoke of the law laid on the neck made servants; in this covenant the yoke of Christ is light and its burden sweet, and by the spirit of adoption it makes sons. With these things so set, it is perverse, and more than perverse, that the order is reversed, so that the lesser things are given for the greater, or the greater for the lesser, and so the use of images is magnified that the things of the Christians are in a manner belittled.

units.la: CAP. XX.
units.tr: CHAPTER XX.

units.la: Quod non minus omnibus, sed pene cunctis plus Tarasius delirasse dinoscitur, dicens: Sicut veteres habuerunt cherubim obumbrantem propitiatorium; & nos imagines Domini nostri Jesu Christi & sanctæ Dei genetricis & sanctorum ejus habeamus obumbrantes altare.
units.tr: That Tarasius is shown to have raved not less than nearly everyone else, saying: Just as the ancients had the cherubim overshadowing the mercy seat, so we should have images of our Lord Jesus Christ, of the holy Mother of God and of his saints, overshadowing the altar.

units.la: NON est inconsequens ut Tarasius, qui, ut fertur, à populari conversatione ad sacerdotale culmen, à militari habitu ad religiosum, à circo ad altarium, à forensi tumultu ad prædicationem, ab armorum strepitu ad sancta mysteria peragenda extraordinarie provectus est, subditarum sibi plebium mentes ab spiritalibus ad carnalia, ab invisibilibus ad invisibilia, à veritate ad imaginem, à corpore ad umbram, ab spiritu vivificante ad literam mortificantem, ab spiritu adoptionis ad spiritum timoris, denuo redire conpellat: ut quoniam ille spretis his quæ ei fortasse inlicita non erant in laicali conversatione, ad sacerdotalis culminis gradum convolavit, quod ei inlicitum erat ob subitaneam conversationem, cietiam subditæ plebes à licitis spiritalium observationum mysteriis ad inlicitas corporalium rerum observantias convolent per ejus prædicationem. Quia ergo melioribus contemptis, pejoribus uti hortatur, & quia veteres habuerunt cherubim qui per Moysen facti sunt, de quorum medio loquebatur Deus, obumbrantes propitiatorium: ideo fideles hortatur habere imagines, quæ à quibuslibet opificibus conduntur obumbrantes altare. modo aberrasse creduntur. Facies eorum erant versæ ad exteriorem domum: quia nos ab hujus peregrinationis ærumna ereptos ad suum desiderant pervenire consortium. Stabant ergo erectis pedibus,alas ad auro textos oraculi parietes extentas, & facies habebant versas ad domum exteriorem:quia videlicet ita angeli suam perpetuò innocentiam conservant: sic de animarum sanctarum in cælis beatitudine congaudent, ut eis quoque, quos in terris adhuc peregrinari conspiciunt electis opem ferre non desinant,donec & illos ad cælestem patriam introducant. Possunt etiam,sicut iam in superiori capitulo exsequuti sumus, per duos Cherubim duo testamenta significari. Ideo igitur in oraculo sunt facti, quia in consilio divinæ provisionis nobis utique inaccessibili atque inconprehensibili ante secula dispositum est, quando & qualiter quibusve auctoribus sacra scriptura conderetur. De lignis vero olivarum sunt facti, sive quia per viros misericordiæ unctione Spiritus sanctí inlustratos divini conscripti sunt libri: sive quia lucem scientiæ tribuunt, juvante flamma charitatis Dei,quæ per Spiritum sanctum diffunditur in cordibus nostris. Decem cubitis sunt alti, quia per observantiam decalogi legis Deo serviendum prædicant: quia Deo fideliter servientes,denario se remunerandos esse regni cælestis ostendunt. Geminas habent alas, quia testamenta per asperaæque & prosperainde fesso proposito semper ad cælestia tetendisse ac pervenisse declarant: quia hoc idem suis auctoribus faciendum esse demonstrant. Quinque cubitorum ala cherub vna, & quinque cubitorum ala cherub altera: quia in omni labentium rerum varietate sancti universos corporis sui sensus in obsequium sui conditoris extendunt, oculos habentes semper ad Dominum, audire desiderantes vocem laudis ejus, & enarrare universa mirabilia ejus, dulcia faucibus suis habentes eloquia illius super mel & favum ori suo:currentes in odore unguentorum ejus & donec superest halitus in eis,& Spiritus Dei in naribus ipsorum, non loquentes labiis iniquitatem, nec in lingua sua stultitiam personantes:sicque per arma justitiæ à dextris & à sinistris incedētes ad perceptionem cælestis denarii, quem summus paterfamilias cultoribus suæ vineæ repromisit, perveniunt. Quia ergo opus unum erat in duobus cherubim, hoc innuebat, quia utriusque instrumenti scriptores una eademque castitate operis & charitatis devotione Deo serviebant,una & consona Deum voce ac fide prædicant. Quaéque novum testamentum de dominica incarnatione, passione,resurrectione,ascensione,gentium vocatione,ludæorum expulsione, multimoda ecclesiæ tribulatione faEta narrat:hæc eadem vetus testamentum si recte intellegitur veraciter facienda prædicebat. Adventum verò Antichristi,finem seculi extremi, discrimen judicii & æternam bonorum gloriam,pœnamque reproborum,concordi utrumque testamentum veritate profatur. Alæ igitur cherubim interiores super archam se invicem contingebant, quia testamenta pari de domino adtestatione consentiunt. Item alis exterioribus iste unum parietum,ille alterum contingebat: quia vetus testamentum proprie antiquo Dei populo scriptum est: novum vero nobis qui post incarnationem dominicam ad fidem venimus,& secundo pariete, hoc est, septemtrionali, recte conparamur, quibus post figuram ac tenebras idolatriæ lucem veritatis cognoscere datum est. Nam etsi primitiva ecclesia maxime de Iudæis efflorurit,& omnis Israhel circa finem sæculi salvandus esse credatur, plurimi tamen fidelium hujus temporis de gentibus congregantur ad evangelii suscipienda sacramenta. Quibus hocetiam divinitus donatum est, ut revelatis oculis sui cordis manifeste cognoscant literam veteris testamenti evangelicæ gratiæ plenam esse mysteriis. Versas habentes facies cherubim ad exteriorem domum:quia nos qui adhuc foris stamus non re ipsa,sed spe salvi facti sumus. Divini sunt libri conditi,quia scriptores eorum jam regnantes cum domino illumque conlaudantes in cælis curam nostræ gerunt salutis proque nostris erratibus apud ejus pietatem interpellant. Circumdati sunt auro cherubim,quia præclaris scriptorum suorum operibus confirmatur auctoritas testamentorum,manifestata autem per orbem cognitione divinarum scripturarum,sive interna gloria cœlestium agminum.Vterque enim cherub,vt diximus,& angelos & testamenta designant.
units.tr: It is not inconsistent that Tarasius, who, as is reported, was raised out of ordinary life to the summit of the priesthood, from a soldier's dress to a religious one, from the circus to the altar, from the clamour of the law courts to preaching, and from the clash of arms to the performance of the holy mysteries, should compel the minds of the peoples subject to him to turn back again from spiritual things to carnal, from invisible things to visible, from truth to image, from body to shadow, from the life-giving Spirit to the letter that kills, and from the Spirit of adoption to the spirit of fear. For just as he, having scorned those things which in lay life were perhaps not forbidden to him, flew up to the rank of the priestly summit, which was forbidden to him because of his sudden change of life, so, through his preaching, the subject peoples too fly from the lawful mysteries of spiritual observances to unlawful observances of bodily things. Therefore, since he urges them to use the inferior things after despising the better, and since the ancients had the cherubim which were made through Moses, about whose midst God spoke, overshadowing the mercy seat, he therefore urges the faithful to have images, made by whatever craftsmen, overshadowing the altar. They are believed to have gone astray just now. Their faces were turned towards the outer house, because they desire to bring us, freed from the hardship of this pilgrimage, to their own fellowship. They therefore stood with upright feet, their wings stretched out to the walls of the oracle, which were covered with gold, and they had their faces turned towards the outer house: because, clearly, in this way the angels always keep their innocence; and they so rejoice in the blessedness of holy souls in heaven that they never cease to bring help also to those of the elect whom they see still wandering on earth, until they lead them too into the heavenly homeland. They can also be signified, as we have already explained in the previous chapter, by the two cherubim as the two covenants. They were made in the oracle therefore because in the counsel of divine providence, which is certainly inaccessible and incomprehensible to us, it was arranged before the ages when and how, and by what authors, the sacred Scripture should be composed. They were made of olive wood, either because the books of God were written by men enlightened by the anointing of the Holy Spirit of mercy, or because they bestow the light of knowledge, with the flame of God's love, which is poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit, helping them. They are ten cubits high, because they proclaim that God is to be served by observing the law of the Decalogue; because, serving God faithfully, they show that they will be rewarded with the denarius of the heavenly kingdom. They have two wings, because they declare that the covenants, through adversities and prosperities, have always stretched towards and reached heavenly things with an unwearied purpose; because they show that the same thing is to be done by their authors. One cherub's wing is five cubits, and the other cherub's wing is five cubits: because, in all the variety of passing things, the saints stretch out all the senses of their body in the service of their Creator, having their eyes always on the Lord, desiring to hear the voice of his praise and to tell of all his wonders, having his sayings sweet in their mouths, above honey and the honeycomb to their mouth, running in the odour of his ointments; and while breath remains in them and the Spirit of God is in their nostrils, they do not speak iniquity with their lips, nor utter folly with their tongue; and thus, walking through the arms of righteousness on the right hand and on the left, they arrive at the receiving of the heavenly denarius, which the great householder promised to the workers of his vineyard. Therefore, because there was one work in the two cherubim, this signifies that the writers of both instruments served God with one and the same purity of work and devotion of love, and proclaim God with one and the same consonant voice and faith. And whatever the New Covenant relates concerning the Lord's incarnation, passion, resurrection, ascension, the calling of the Gentiles, the expulsion of the Jews, and the many-fold tribulation done to the Church, this same Old Covenant, if it is rightly understood, truly foretold would be done. And both covenants with one accord speak the truth concerning the coming of Antichrist, the end of the last age, the crisis of judgement, the eternal glory of the good, and the punishment of the reprobate. Therefore the inner wings of the cherubim touched one another above the ark, because the covenants agree in the same testimony concerning the Lord. Likewise, with their outer wings, the one touched one wall and the other touched the other: because the Old Covenant was written properly for the ancient people of God, while the New Covenant, we who came to faith after the Lord's incarnation are rightly compared to the second wall, that is, the northern one, to whom, after figure and the darkness of idolatry, it has been given to know the light of truth. For although the primitive Church flourished chiefly from the Jews, and all Israel is believed to be destined to be saved near the end of the age, nevertheless very many of the faithful of this time are gathered from the Gentiles to receive the sacraments of the gospel. To them this too has been divinely granted, that, with the eyes of their heart revealed, they may clearly recognise that the letter of the Old Covenant is full of the mysteries of evangelical grace. The cherubim have their faces turned towards the outer house, because we, who still stand outside, have been made saved not in reality but in hope. The divine books were composed, because their writers, now reigning with the Lord and praising him in the heavens, take care of our salvation and intercede before his mercy for our errors. The cherubim are overlaid with gold, because the authority of the covenants is confirmed by the splendid works of their writers; and the knowledge of the divine Scriptures, made manifest throughout the world, is their inner glory, as is that of the heavenly hosts. For each cherub, as we have said, designates both the angels and the covenants.

units.la: CAP. XXI.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXI.

units.la: Quod non bene Iohannes presbyter senserit qui ut imaginum adorationem adstrueret, dixit, Et Iesu Nave duodecim lapides statuit in Dei memoria.
units.tr: That John the presbyter did not reason well when, to support the adoration of images, he said: "And Joshua set up twelve stones in the memory of God."

units.la: CUm in eadem synodo quæ pro adorandis imaginibus facta est, cujus nos errores summatim discutiendos arripuimus, nullum testimonium ex divinis apicibus prolatum ad eandem rem pertinere constet, nec hoc quoque pertinere constat, quod Iohannes presbyter & legatus orientalium protulit dicens, Iesu Nave duodecim lapides statuit in Dei memoria. Quorum si historialiter quur ab amnis alveo educti & in Galgalis fuerunt positi, causa quæratur, ab eodem Iosue aperitur: qui his non ad adorandas imagines instruendam fore Israhelitarum posteritatem edocuit, sed memorem stupendo miraculo arefacti fluminis esse debere permonuit, qui ad posteros hanc sine voce legationem proclamantes deferrent: Nos quos cernitis liquentis quondam elementi suimus habitatores, qui arida terra nunc sumus exsules, quiq; tot seculis Iordanis suimus indigenæ, ipsi exempti gurgitibus telluris nunc sumus advena. Quoniam cum ante faciem arche domini, immo ante faciem Dei Iacob, sacerdotum perstrepentibus caterva, & populi cum magna exultatione admirantibus cuneis, cuneu,novum ille pateretur dissidium,inferiorem partem fuga lapsam aquoreu undis immergeret,superioremq; in aera fastigiaret,obslupescentibusq; populu lymphaticos ad alta montes sustolleret & plantis insolitum Israhelitieus transitum arenti alveo prastaret ab antiquis sumus sedibus educti,& islic Israhelitarum humeru adlati istiq; positi, isliq; sumus diu permansuri. Si verò typicè quid isti lapides præfiguraverint quæratur, novo Iolue, Domino videlicet & salvatore nostro IesuChristo qui æternæ nobis patriæ habitationem distribuit docente,panditur,qui ut baptismi sacramentum per quod ad æternam patriam pervenitur , stabiliret, duodecim Apostolos elegit, quibus & dixit, Euntes docete omnes, baptizantes eos in nomine patris & filii & spiritus sancti: qui usque in perpetuum sanctæ Ecclesiæ posteritati perhibent testimonium, dum eam ad cœlestia regna provocant per baptismi sacratissimum sacramentum. Per alios ergo duodecim nihilominus lapides qui in Iordanis alveo positi sunt, sanctorum patriarcharum & prophetarum prosećto figura prætenditur:qui nimirum dum baptismi sacramentum sub umbra legis positi non aperte prædicaverint,sed per quasdam mysticas & obumbratas figuras innuerint, quasi flumineis fluctibus obruti sunt:quia videlicet quanquam aperte non videantur baptismum instituisse, non tamen creduntur eius mysterio caruisse.pro quibus patribus sanctæ ecclesiæ nati sunt filii, id est, Apostoli,quos constituit principes super omnem terram qui memores sunt nominis Domini in omni progenie & generatione:ut tam per illos quam etiam per istos sacrosanctis charismatibus referta & dogmatibus edocta,non imaginum fucis vel quibuslibet superstitiosis rebus,sed fide & operibus dominum quærere non desistat.
units.tr: Since in that same synod which was held concerning the adoration of images, whose errors we have undertaken to examine briefly, it is established that no testimony brought forward from the divine letters pertains to that matter, nor is it established that this also pertains to it, which John the presbyter and legate of the Easterns brought forward, saying: "And Joshua set up twelve stones in the memory of God." If someone asks, from the historical standpoint, why they were taken from the bed of the river and set up at Gilgal, Joshua himself makes this clear. He taught that these stones were not meant to instruct the posterity of Israel toward adoring images, but warned that they ought to be a memorial of the astonishing miracle of the dried-up river, and that they should carry this message to posterity without a voice, proclaiming it: "We whom you see were once inhabitants of the liquid element; we who are now exiles from dry land, and who for so many ages were natives of the Jordan, now ourselves taken out of the flood are strangers to the land. For when, before the face of the ark of the Lord, or rather before the face of the God of Jacob, with a throng of priests making a noise and the people admiring in great exultation in their ranks, he suffered that strange discord: he made the lower part, fallen in flight, sink in the watery waves, and raised the upper part into the air; and while the people stood amazed, he lifted the watery mountains on high and gave the Israelites an unaccustomed passage on dry ground with their feet. We were led from our ancient seats, carried there on the shoulders of the Israelites and placed here, and here we shall remain for a long time." But if one asks what these stones prefigured typically, it is revealed by the new Joshua, namely our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, who teaches us and grants us a dwelling in our eternal homeland. To establish the sacrament of baptism, through which one comes to the eternal homeland, he chose twelve apostles, and said to them: Go and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit. These bear witness to the posterity of the holy Church forever, while they call her to the heavenly kingdoms through the most sacred sacrament of baptism. Through the other twelve stones likewise, which were placed in the bed of the Jordan, the figure of the holy patriarchs and prophets is surely put forward. While living under the shadow of the law, they did not openly proclaim the sacrament of baptism but only hinted at it through certain mystical and shadowed figures, and so they are as it were overwhelmed by the river's waves. For although they do not seem openly to have instituted baptism, they are not believed to have been without its mystery. In place of these fathers the sons of the holy Church were born, that is, the apostles, whom he has made princes over all the earth, who are mindful of the name of the Lord in every generation and age; so that the Church, filled with holy gifts and taught by doctrine both through them and through these, may not cease to seek the Lord by faith and works, not by the paint of images or any superstitious things.

units.la: CAP. XXII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXII.

units.la: Quod non sit æqualis adoratio vt illi dicunt, Nathan prophetæ erga David re- gem,adorationi imaginum.
units.tr: That the worship which they speak of, that Nathan the prophet paid to King David, is not equal to the worship of images.

units.la: NON esse æqualem adorationem,quam Nathan propheta David æque prophetæ regique sanc-tissimo exhibuit,adorationi quam quidam imaginibus exhibent, non necesse est multis adprobare documentis: quoniam evidentissimis est adprobatum indiciis, nec nostra indiget disputatione res quæ tam aperta tamque clara elucet ratione. Sed ne hoc silentio præteresse videamur,oportet vt quiddam inde strictim breviterque exsequamur. Adoravit, inquam, Nathan propheta David regem,non ut colorum fucis conpaginatam imaginem, sed ut à Deo in regni apice sublimatam potestatem. Quippe qui ejusdem doni cœlestis munere satiatus erat, quo ille satiandus foret qui dićturus erat : Omnibus potestatibus sublimioribus subditi estote. Non est enim potestas nisi à Deo,quæ autem sunt à Deo, ordinatæ sunt.Itaque qui resistit potestati,Dei ordinationi resistit:qui autem resistunt ipsi sibi damnationem adquirunt.Nam principes non sunt timori boni operis,sed mali. Vis autem non timere potestatem : bonum fac,& habebis laudem ex illa. Dei enim minister est tibi in bonum, si autem malum feceris,time.Non enim sine causa gladium portat. Dei enim minister est,vindex in iram ei qui malum agit. Ideoq; necessitati subditi estote non solum propter iram,sed propter conscientiam. Ideo enim & tributa præstatis : ministri enim Dei sunt , in hoc ipsum servientes.Reddite ergo omnibus debita:cui tributum,tributum:cui većtigal, većtigal: cui timorem , timorem : cui honorem,honorem:nemini quicquam debeatis nisi ut invicem diligatis. De hac etiam re idem vas elećtionis per spiritum sanćtum discipulum Titum sic instruit, Admone illos, principibus & potestatibus subditos esse, dićto obedire,admone ad opus bonum paratos esse,neminem blasphemare, litigiosos non esse , sed modestos, omnem ostendentes mansuetudinem ad omnes homines. Adoravit itaque propheta regem:spiritu sanćto repletus, spiritu sanćto repletum;vaticinii munere fretus,vaticinii munere fretum;meritorum insignibus coruscans,meritorum insignibus coruscantem. Non enim in eo quandam insensatam rem superstitiosæ vanitatis cultu adoravit,sed virum inventum secundùm cor Domini,virum sacri unguinis liquore delibutum, virum in Dei laudibus supra omnes excitatum, virum qui de Christi incarnatione , passione , à mortuis resurrećtione,in cœlum ascensione,cunćtis præcellentius prophetavit : virum qui non solum Dei filium venturum prophetavit,sed eius etiam typum gessit:virum qui non solum eius typum gessit,sed etiam secundum formam servi germinis prosapiam ministravit. Dilećtionis affećtu, humilitatis obsequio,prælationis debito,officiosa adoratione honorificavit, quem si non ei se subdendo eiusque monitis parendo honorificaret,illi spiritui contraire videretur, qui per pastorem ecclesiæ dićturus erat,Subditi estote omni humanæ ordinationi propter Dominum, sive regi tamquam præcellenti, sive ducibus tamquam ab eo in hoc ipsum missis ad vindićtam malorum, laudem verò bonorum : quia sic est voluntas Dei vt benefacientes obmutescere faciatis stultorum hominum ignorantiam : vt liberi,non ut velamen malitiæ habentes libertatem, sed sicut servi Dei. Omnes honorate , fraternitatem diligite, Deum timete,regem autem honorificate. Cùm ergo tot indiciis, tantisque Apostolorum prædicationibus reges honorificandi sint,absurdissimum est adorationem, quæ imaginibus aniliter fit, adorationi quæ sanctissimo regi per prophetam fiebat, æquiparare velle: cùm videlicet ille Dei famulum,& vt ita dixerim,sancti spiritus habitaculum & divinæ incarnationis ministrum salutando adoraverit:isti verò in imaginibus nil aliud nisi easdem materias,de quibus illæ siant adorent. Nam si æ-qualis est adoratio quæ David à propheta exhibita est,adorationi quæ imaginibus exhibetur,ipse quo-que David imaginibus æqualis est:& si imaginibus æqualis est, non solum tot meritorum insignibus, sed etiam ipsa humana ratione caruisse credendus est:non autem tot meritorum insignibus, nec ipsa humana ratione caruisse credendus est: non igitur æqualis est adoratio quę illi à propheta exhibita est,adorationi quę imaginibus exhibetur.
units.tr: That the worship which Nathan the prophet paid to David, equally a prophet and a most holy king, is not equal to the worship which some give to images, does not need to be proved by many arguments. It has been proved by the plainest evidence, and the matter, which shines out so openly and clearly, does not need our discussion. Yet, so that we may not seem to pass it over in silence, we should briefly and concisely set out something about it. I say that Nathan the prophet worshipped King David, not as a painted image put together from colours, but as a power raised up by God to the height of a kingdom. For he himself had been filled with the same heavenly gift by which he who was to say, Let every soul be subject to the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God. Whosoever therefore resisteth the power, resisteth the ordinance of God: and they that resist shall receive to themselves damnation. For rulers are not a terror to good works, but to the evil. Wilt thou then not be afraid of the power? do that which is good, and thou shalt have praise of the same: for he is the minister of God to thee for good. But if thou do that which is evil, be afraid; for he beareth not the sword in vain: for he is the minister of God, a revenger to execute wrath upon him that doeth evil. Wherefore ye must needs be subject, not only for wrath, but also for conscience sake. For this cause pay ye tribute also: for they are God's ministers, attending continually upon this very thing. Render therefore to all their dues: tribute to whom tribute is due; custom to whom custom; fear to whom fear; honour to whom honour. Owe no man any thing, but to love one another, was to be filled. The same chosen vessel, through the Holy Spirit, instructs his disciple Titus on this matter in these words: Put them in mind to be subject to principalities and powers, to obey magistrates, to be ready to every good work, to speak evil of no man, to be no brawlers, but gentle, shewing all meekness unto all men. So the prophet worshipped the king: filled with the Holy Spirit, relying on the gift of prophecy, shining with the distinguished marks of merit. For he did not worship in him some senseless thing with the cult of superstitious vanity, but a man found according to the heart of the Lord, a man anointed with the oil of holy anointing, a man raised above all others in the praises of God, a man who prophesied of the incarnation of Christ, of his passion, of his resurrection from the dead, and of his ascension into heaven, more excellently than all others; a man who not only prophesied that the Son of God would come, but also bore his type; a man who not only bore his type, but also, according to the form of a servant, supplied the lineage of the seed. With the affection of love, with the duty of humility, with the due respect owed to one set above him, he honoured him with a dutiful worship. Had he not honoured him by submitting to him and obeying his admonitions, he would seem to be opposed to that Spirit who was to say through the minister of the Church, Be subject to every human ordinance for the Lord's sake, whether to the king as supreme, or to governors as sent by him for the punishment of evil men and the praise of the good: for so is the will of God, that by well-doing ye may put to silence the ignorance of foolish men: as free, yet not using your liberty as a cloak of maliciousness, but as the servants of God. Honour all men. Love the brotherhood. Fear God. Honour the king. Since, therefore, by so many indications and by such great preaching of the Apostles, kings are to be honoured, it is most absurd to want to make equal the worship which is given to images in a foolish way with the worship which was paid by the prophet to the most holy king. For the one saluted and worshipped the servant of God, the habitation, so to speak, of the Holy Spirit and the minister of the divine incarnation; whereas these, in images, worship nothing but the very materials of which the images are made. For if the worship which the prophet paid to David is equal to the worship which is paid to images, then David himself is equal to images; and if he is equal to images, he must be believed to have lacked not only so many marks of merit, but even human reason itself. But he did not lack so many marks of merit, nor human reason itself. Therefore the worship which the prophet paid to him is not equal to the worship which is paid to images.

units.la: Matth.26.
units.tr: Matth.26.

units.la: CAP. XXIII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXIII.

units.la: Quod in eo quod scriptum est, Signatum est super nos lumen vultus tui Domine: sive, Vultum tuum Domine requiram, nihil manufactae imaginis intelli- gendum est, ut illi dicunt.
units.tr: That what is written, "The light of your countenance, Lord, is signed upon us," or "I will seek your face, Lord," is not to be understood of images made by hands, as they claim.

units.la: Nihil ad manufactarum imaginum vultus pertinet, quod Psalmographus dicit, Signatum est super nos lumen vultus tui Domine: nec illud, Vultum tuum Domine requiram, ut in ejusdem vanissimi synodi lectione habetur, quae pro adorandis imaginibus facta est: cujus textus nihil aliud quam signa est, ubi stultitia magnitudinem suam exercuit. Nam si hic vultus cujus super nos lumen signatum esse propheta decantat, et quem se requisituum esse denunciat, in manufactarum imaginibus intellegendus est, quaerendum magnopere est, quale lumen habeant, aut quo modo illumen super nos signatum sit, aut ubi idem Propheta talem requisierit vultum. In corde etenim idem sanctus vir Deum non in manufactis vultibus quaerebat, cum dicebat: In toto corde meo exquisivi te. Deus, ne repellas me a mandatis tuis. Vultus ergo Dei cognitio Dei est, id est, filius, per quem ad cognitionem divinitatis pervenimus.
units.tr: Nothing that the Psalmist says about the face pertains to images made by hands: neither "The light of your countenance, Lord, is signed upon us," nor "I will seek your face, Lord," as is read in the reading of that same most vain synod, which was held in favour of adoring images. Its text is nothing but a sign of where folly has shown its greatness. For if this face, whose light the prophet sings is signed upon us, and which he declares he must seek, is to be understood as in images made by hands, it must be asked earnestly what light they have, or how that light has been signed upon us, or where the same Prophet sought such a face. For the same holy man did not seek God in faces made by hands when he said: "With my whole heart have I sought you; O God, do not drive me from your commandments." The face of God, therefore, is the knowledge of God, that is, the Son, through whom we come to the knowledge of the divinity.

units.la: Psal. 119. & Coloss. 1. Hebr. 1. Ioan. 14. Psal. 119. Psal. 115. Psalm. 105. Psalm. 34. Ephes. 4.
units.tr: Psal. 119. & Coloss. 1. Hebr. 1. Ioan. 14. Psal. 119. Psal. 115. Psalm. 105. Psalm. 34. Ephes. 4.

units.la: CAP. XXIV.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXIV.

units.la: Quod non ad ullam manufactam imaginem pertineat quod scriptum est, Vultum tuum deprecabuntur omnes divites plebis, sicut illi autumant.
units.tr: That the words "All the rich among the people shall entreat your favour" do not refer to any man-made image, as they suppose.

units.la: Sed nec illud quod scriptum est, Vultum tuum deprecabuntur omnes divites plebis, de quodam manufacto vultu intellegendum est: praesertim cum manufacti vultus, ideo non deprecandi sint, quia nec exaudire queunt: Omne quod deprecatur ideo deprecatur ut exaudiat: et omne quod exaudit
units.tr: But neither should the words "All the rich among the people shall entreat your favour" be understood of some man-made face, especially since man-made faces should not be entreated for the very reason that they cannot hear. Everything that is entreated is entreated so that it may hear, and everything that hears must be sentient.

units.la: Psalm. 4. audit intrationale esse non debet: omne igitur quod deprecatur intrationale esse non debet: quod si deprecari non debet, multo minus adorari: cum videlicet adoratio deprecationi emineat. Namque manufacti vultus deprecandi & adorandi sunt, ut illi garriunt, necesse est ut deprecantes exaudire, & adorantibus favere credantur: & si deprecantes exaudire, adorantibusque favere creduntur, necesse est ut vita eis sensuum capax inesse credatur. Non autem inest eis vita sensuum capax: non igitur, ut illi garriunt, adorandi vel deprecandi sunt. Nam haec duorum membrorum, quae quidem commata nuncupant, sententia, id est, Vultum tuum deprecabuntur omnes divites plebis, non Deo cujus imago & vultus filius est, sed ecclesiae quae corpus Christi est, per Prophetam dicitur. Dixerat enim superius per energiam, Audi filia & vide, & inclina aurem tuam, & obliviscere populum tuum, & domum patris tui: quoniam concupivit rex speciem tuam, quia ipse est dominus meus: & adorabunt eum filiae Tyri in muneribus. & in eadem energia perseverans subjunxit eidem cujus speciem concupiscere regem dixerat, dicens, Vultum tuum deprecabuntur omnes divites plebis.
units.tr: Psalm. 4. Therefore everything that is entreated must not be insensible. If it must not be entreated, much less must it be worshipped, since worship clearly surpasses entreaty. For if man-made faces must be entreated and worshipped, as those babblers say, then they must be believed to hear those who entreat them and to favour those who worship them. And if they are believed to hear the entreaty and favour the worship, then they must be believed to have a life capable of sense. But they have no life capable of sense; therefore they are not to be worshipped or entreated, as those babblers say. For this sentence of the two members, which they call the commata, namely "All the rich among the people shall entreat your favour," is spoken by the Prophet not to God, whose image and face is the Son, but to the Church, which is the body of Christ. For above he had said by way of energy: "Hearken, O daughter, and consider, and incline your ear, and forget your people and your father's house: for the king has greatly desired your beauty, for he is your lord; and the daughters of Tyre shall worship him with gifts." And continuing in the same energy, he added to her whose beauty the king had said he desired: "All the rich among the people shall entreat your favour."

units.la: Vultus ergo ecclesiae doctrinae spiritalis eruditio est: quare ideo a divitibus deprecari dicitur, quia multi propter eam omnibus pompis saeculi & divitiis renunciaverunt, qualiter ad eam pervenire & per eam ad aeternam patriam convolare valerent: hae sunt enim filiae Tyri adorantes in muneribus: hi divites plebis, qui ejus vultum deprecantur. Una enim est ecclesia cujus vultus deprecatur, & a quibus deprecatur, mater videlicet cum filiis, una sponsa, una regina, omnes ad Christum unum caput pertinentes, qui est aeternus & inmortalis sponsus: cujus amicus erat ille, qui eosdem divites plebis ficalloquebatur; Pracipe divitibus hujus mundi, non superbe sapere, neque speraare in incerto divitiarum, sed in Deo vivo qui praestat nobis omnia abundanter ad fruendum. Hi semper a sanctis praedicationibus exhortantur, ut thesaurizent sibi fundamentum bonum in futurum, ut adprehendant veram vitam adorando in muneribus. Vultum ergo hujus reginae deprecantur divites plebis, cum ad eam concurrunt, & in ejus sinu eleemosynas faciunt, ne extra ejus collegium fiant. Hujus itaque reginae vultum, non imaginum fucos deprecabantur, qui ad eam in muneribus veniebant, & ea quae portabant ad pedes Apostolorum ponebant, huius reginae vultus desiderio, non alicujus pietatis, aestuabant illi, eamque in muneribus non aliquam infensam imaginem deprecabantur. De quibus scriptum est, Multitudini vero credentium erat cor & anima una, & nemo eorum quae possidebat quicquam suum proprium esse dicebat, sed erant eis communia omnia. Hujus reginae vultum, non alicujus tabulae coloribus divitum opibus decorare volebat sponsus, cum dicebat; Vendite quae possidetis, & date eleemosynam: facite vobis sacculos qui non veterescunt, thesaurum non deficientem in caelis, quo fur non appropinquat, neque tinea corrumpit: ubi enim fuerit thesaurus tuus, illic erit & cor tuum: sive cum dicebat, Verumtamen date eleemosynam, & ecce omnia munda sunt vobis. Quia ergo ad eandem reginam divites in hypocrisi cum falsis munibus quasi vultum ejus deprecaturi venire non debent, ipsa veritas inhibet, cum dicit, Carete facie justitiam vestram coram hominibus, ut videamini ab eis. Quia vero ejus vultum semper clarioremque & in paululo splendidiorem fieri delectet, evidenter ostendit, cum dicit, Luceat opera vestra coram hominibus, ut videant bona vestra, & glorificent patrem vestrum qui est in caelis. In quibus omnibus non imaginum adoratio, nec deprecatio, nec earum gloria, sed aut sponsi qui caput est, aut sponsae quae corpus est, indubitanter ostenditur. A quibus sensibus & a quorum ornamentorum insignibus quam expectes sint qui, Vultum tuum deprecabuntur omnes divites plebis, ad manufactarum imaginum vultus referunt non nobis est judicandum, sed lectoris arbitrio relervandum.
units.tr: The face of the Church, therefore, is the teaching of spiritual instruction. It is said that the rich entreat it for this reason: many, for its sake, have renounced all the pomp and riches of the world, so that they might be able to come to it and through it hasten to the eternal homeland. For these are the daughters of Tyre who worship with gifts, and these are the rich among the people who entreat her face. For there is one Church whose face is entreated and by whom it is entreated, that is, the mother together with her children, one bride, one queen, all belonging to Christ the one head, who is the eternal and immortal bridegroom. His friend was he who spoke to those same rich among the people: "Charge those who are rich in this world not to be proud, nor to trust in the uncertainty of riches, but in the living God, who gives us all things richly to enjoy." These are always exhorted by the holy preachings to lay up for themselves a good foundation for the future, that they may lay hold on the true life by worshipping with gifts. Therefore the rich among the people entreat the face of this queen when they come together to her and make almsgivings into her bosom, lest they be cut off from her fellowship. Those who came to this queen with gifts, and set what they carried at the feet of the Apostles, did not entreat the paint of images, but were burning with desire for the face of this queen, not for any piety of their own, and they did not entreat in gifts some hostile image. Of them it is written: "And the multitude of those who believed were of one heart and one soul; and none of them said that anything he possessed was his own, but they had all things in common." The bridegroom did not wish the face of this queen to be adorned with the colours of some panel or with the riches of the wealthy, when he said: "Sell what you have and give alms; make for yourselves purses which do not wear out, a treasure in the heavens that does not fail, where no thief comes near nor moth destroys; for where your treasure is, there will your heart be also." Or when he said: "But give alms, and behold, all things are clean for you." Because therefore the rich should not come to this same queen in hypocrisy with false gifts, as if about to entreat her face, the truth itself forbids it, when it says: "Take heed that you do not do your righteousness before men, to be seen by them." Because it delights her that her face should always be brighter, and in a little while more splendid, he clearly shows this when he says: "Let your light shine before men, that they may see your good works and glorify your Father who is in heaven." In all these things there is clearly shown not the worship or entreaty of images, nor their glory, but that of the bridegroom, who is the head, or of the bride, who is the body. It is not for us to judge how far from these meanings, and from the adornments of these ornaments, are those who refer "All the rich among the people shall entreat your favour" to the faces of man-made images; this must be left to the judgment of the reader.

units.la: CAP. XXV.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXV.

units.la: Inopportuna & deliramento plena dictio Leonis Focia Episcopi, qui in eo quod ad imaginum ad- orationem conversus est, sibi versiculum Psalmistae accommodat dicentis, Convertisti planctum meum in gaudium mihi, conscidisti saccum meum, & circundedisti lae- titia.
units.tr: An inopportune statement, full of nonsense, by Leo Phocas, bishop, who, because he turned to the adoration of images, applies to himself the verse of the Psalmist: "Thou hast turned my mourning into dancing for me; thou hast put off my sackcloth and girded me with gladness."

units.la: Cum pene nullum divinorum apicum testimonium competenter in saepissime memorata sanodo fuerit positum, nec hoc quoque competenter a Leone Focia episcopo constat esse prolatum: qui videlicet si quiddam sale conditum aut ad rem pertinens proferret, caeteris apparere dissimilis, cunctorumque sententiis refragator exstitisset. Sed dum se inaniter flevisse fallus est, eo quod imagines non adoraverit, & laetari, eo quod inanius se ad earum adorationem diverterit, quam fit delinus, quamque caeterorum consortio nexus evidentissime adparuit. Habuit enim, ut idem praefatus est, sine damno tristitiam, sine profectu laetitiam, sine perditione lachrymarum decutius, sine adquisitione cachinnabiles risus, tras sine calumniis, placationes sine honorificentiis: impote puer in quadam ludicra peragenda iubians, si a nutrice coerceatur, singulis verba intentibus ejulat, ad quae perpetranda si ei fuerit a nutrice concessa facultas, semiplenis vociferando sermonibus exultat: siqueque coercitus habet vanos fletus, & ea peragere permissus vanos nihilominus risus: cum videlicet nec in prohibitione fuerit causa deflendi, nec in data licentia causa ridendi.
units.tr: Since almost no testimony from the divine writings was competently set forth in the synod so often mentioned, and it is not established that Leo Phocas, the bishop, brought forward even this one competently, he would clearly have appeared unlike the rest, and opposed the opinions of all, had he put forward anything seasoned with wit or pertinent to the matter. But while he falsely claims that he wept in vain because he did not adore images, and rejoiced because he turned more emptily to their adoration, he is foolish, and his association with the others most clearly shows it. For he had, as he himself said, sorrow without loss, joy without gain, weeping without destruction of tears, a dimness without acquiring laughable laughter, agitation without slander, and appeasements without honours. It is like a boy who, when ordered to perform some playful task, if his nurse restrains him, wails and pays attention to each word; if she grants him the freedom to carry out those things, he exults, shouting half-formed words. So when restrained he has empty tears, and when allowed to do those things, he nonetheless has empty laughter, since there was no cause for weeping in the prohibition, nor cause for laughing in the permission given.

units.la: Versiculus namque iste, quem ille sibi in hac parte uncassum adcommodavit, id est, Convertisti planctum meum in gaudium mihi, & conscidisti saccum meum, & praecinxisti me laetitia, in persona totius ecclesiae a Propheta per ethiopeam dictus est: quae scilicet dum in hujus saeculi mortalitate & aerumnis versatur, plangere dicitur: cùm verò ad æternam remunerationem pervenerit, tunc lætitia præcingetur. Unde & idem sanctissimus Prophetarum in eodem Psalmo paulo superius dixit, Ad vespe- rum demorabitur fletus, & ad matutinum lætitia, vesperum scilicet hanc nostri temporis ætatem, in quo hones seculorum devenerunt, sive extremi judicii diem: matutinum verò resurrectionis tempus & sanctorum retributiones volens intelligi. Quod & per Esaiam Prophetam sanctis hoc modo promit- titur, Sanctin terra sua duplicia possidebunt, id est, post resurrectionem in æterna patria animæ & carnis jucunditate fruentur: unde & subditur, Lætitia sempiterna erit electis meis, dum dedero opera eorum in veritate. Tuncergo saccus noster conscindetur, & præcingemur lætitia, cùm secundum Apostolum.corruptibile hoc indutum fuerit incorruptela, & mortale hoc indutum fuerit immortalitate, & fuerit sermo qui scriptus est, Absorpta est mors in victoria: sive cum in his membris, quæ nunc mortificamus super terram, Christo adparente vita nostra, nos quoque adparuerimus cum illo in gloria.
units.tr: For that little verse, which he has wrongly applied to himself in this matter, namely, Thou hast turned my mourning into joy for me, and hast rent my sackcloth, and hast girded me with gladness, was spoken by the Prophet through an Ethiopian figure in the person of the whole Church. Indeed, while the Church lives in the mortality and miseries of this age, it is said to mourn; but when it has come to eternal reward, then it shall be girded with gladness. Hence the same most holy Prophet, a little earlier in the same Psalm, said, Weeping may endure for the night, but joy comes in the morning, meaning by the night this age of our time, in which the ends of the ages have come, or the day of the last judgment, and by the morning the time of resurrection and the rewards of the saints. This is also promised to the saints through the Prophet Isaiah in this way: In their land they shall possess double, that is, after the resurrection in the eternal fatherland, soul and flesh shall enjoy delight; hence it is also added, Everlasting joy shall be to my elect, when I shall give their works in truth. Then, therefore, our sackcloth will be rent, and we shall be girded with gladness, when, according to the Apostle, this corruptible shall have put on incorruption, and this mortal shall have put on immortality, and the word that is written shall come to pass, Death is swallowed up in victory; or when, Christ appearing, our life, we too shall appear with him in glory, in those members which we now mortify upon the earth.

units.la: CAP. XXVI.
units.tr: CAP. XXVI.

units.la: Quòd non pertineat ad imaginum adorationem contemnentes illud quod Psalmographus cecinit, Vana locuti sunt unusquisque ad proximum suum, labia dolosa in ore, &c.
units.tr: That the verse the Psalmist sang, "They have spoken vanity every one with his neighbour, with lying lips and a double heart," etc., does not apply to those who despise the adoration of images.

units.la: OMNE quod sine profectu est, inutile est: & omne quod inutile est, vanum est: omne igitur quod sine profectu est, vanum est. & omne quod inofficiosum est, profectu caret: & omne quod profectu caret, vanitate non caret: omne igitur quod inofficiosum est, vanitate non caret. Quoniam ubi nulla utilitas, nullum emolumentum: ubi nullum emolumentum, summa vanitas: ubi igitur nulla utilitas, summa vanitas est. In imaginum ergo adoratione ubi nullus profectus, nullum emolumentum, nulla utilitas est, summa vanitas esse credenda est. Ob quam staruendam & mu- nendâ quicunque conventus faciunt, & concilia adgregant, & eas prorsus adorare instituunt, proculdubio vana loquuntur, unusquisque ad proximum suum. Nam neque in eo à vanitate sejunguntur, quòd divinorum apicum testimonia ad suos sensus violenter inflectere niruntur. Sicut & hunc Psalmistæ versiculum, quem quidem ille alio sensu divino afflatus spiritu cecinit, alio isti vanitatis supercilio inflati intellegunt. Si ergo quærimus de quibus Prophera dixerit, Vana locuti sunt unusquisque ad proximum suum, labia dolosa in ore, & corde locuti sunt mala; relegamus sanctorum evangelio- rum textum, & inveniemus Pharisæos & Sadducæos, vel cæteras Iudæorum catervas semper Dominum tentasse, & adversus eum consilia vana iniisse. Qui dum obstinata mente in Christum credere renuerunt, vana loqui non desierunt. De quibus & in alio Psalmo legitur, Quia exacuerunt ut gladium linguas suas: intenderunt arcum, rem amarum, ut sagittent in occultis immaculatum: subito sagittabunt eum, & non timebunt. Linguas enim acuere, & labia dolosa habere, unum est quia & uno dicendi genere di- cum est, quo plerumque aut per id quod continet hoc quod continetur, aut per hoc quod continetur id quod continet demonstratur. Item in alio Psalmo de eisdem scriptum est; Sepulchrum patens est guttur eorum, linguis suis dolose agebant, venenum aspidum sub labiis eorum, quorum os maledictione & amaritudine plenum est. Sepulchrum ergo patens eorum, ora mendacia dixit, qui exitiabile malum contra Dominum loquentes, mortem ei infligere cupiebant. quod ideo patens dictum est, propter eorum apertam nequitiam, quæ foetorem potius quàm odorem exaggerabat. Est enim rerum dissimilium facta comparatio per tropum qui nuncupatur parabole à Grammaticis. Vana, inquit, locuti sunt unusquisque ad proximum suum. Hæc est ergo vanitas omnes vanitates excellens, hic est dolus omnibus dolis renuntiantium & redemptor mundi non creditur, & idem ab hominibus iniquis, quamquam ad aliorum ... ad illorum tamen damnationem crucifigitur. Porro etiam hic versiculus & de haereticis intelligi: qui dum sint mundanæ sapientiæ versutia imbuti, & ad vanas inventiones et superfluas contentiones potius quàm ad credendum prompti, vana loquuntur unusquisque ad proximum suum: quoniam dum male de Christo aut de ecclesia sentiunt, ad eundem errorem proximos suos, id est, cæteros hæreticos invitare non desinunt, quatenus majori infestatione ecclesiam quæ Christi vinea est, demoliri possint. De quibus in Canticis Canticorum dicitur, Capite nobis vulpes parvulas quæ demoliuntur vineas. nam vinea nostra floruit: quia videlicet dum hæreses sive caeres sequaces, hæresei hæreseorum ve discipuli à sanctis & catholicis viris in suis erroribus capiuntur, vinea domini, id est, ecclesia, sacrosanctis charismatibus semper magis magisque exuberat: quatenus suo agricolæ qui pro ea sanguinem fudit, nectarei odoris pocula perpetim ministret.
units.tr: All that is without profit is useless, and all that is useless is vain; therefore all that is without profit is vain. And all that is without duty lacks profit, and all that lacks profit is not free from vanity; therefore all that is without duty is not free from vanity. For where there is no usefulness, there is no advantage; where there is no advantage, there is supreme vanity; therefore where there is no usefulness, there is supreme vanity. So in the adoration of images, where there is no gain, no advantage, and no usefulness, supreme vanity must be believed to be present. Those who hold assemblies and gather councils to establish and fortify this adoration, and who resolve to adore images altogether, undoubtedly speak vanity every one with his neighbour. Nor are they separated from vanity in this alone, that they strive to twist the testimonies of the divine oracles violently to their own meanings. So too with this verse of the Psalmist, which he sang inspired by the divine Spirit in one sense, while those puffed up with the arrogance of vanity understand it in another. If then we ask of whom the Prophet spoke, They have spoken vanity every one with his neighbour, lying lips in the mouth, and with the heart they have spoken evil, let us re-read the text of the holy Gospels, and we shall find that the Pharisees and Sadducees, and the other bands of the Jews, always tempted the Lord and devised vain plots against him. While with a stubborn mind they refused to believe in Christ, they did not cease to speak vain things. Of these it is also read in another Psalm: For they have sharpened their tongues like a sword; they have bent their bow, a bitter thing, to shoot in secret at the blameless; they shall shoot at him suddenly, and they shall not fear. For to sharpen tongues and to have lying lips is one and the same thing; it is said in a figure of speech by which the container is often shown through what it contains, or the thing contained through what contains it. Likewise in another Psalm it is written of the same men: Their throat is an open sepulchre; they dealt deceitfully with their tongues; the venom of asps is under their lips; whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness. By "an open sepulchre" he meant their lying mouths, who, speaking the deadly evil against the Lord, desired to bring death upon him. It is called "open" because of their manifest wickedness, which gave off a stench rather than a fragrance. For this is a comparison of unlike things, made by the trope which the grammarians call parable. They have spoken vanity, he says, every one with his neighbour. This, then, is the vanity that surpasses all vanities, this is the deceit that renounces all deceits; and the Redeemer of the world, though not believed, and himself crucified by wicked men, is crucified to the damnation of those men. Moreover, this verse may also be understood of heretics, who, being steeped in the cunning of worldly wisdom and more ready for vain inventions and superfluous disputes than for belief, speak vanity every one with his neighbour: for while they think ill of Christ or of the Church, they do not cease to invite their neighbours, that is, the other heretics, to the same error, so that they may be able to pull down with greater hostility the Church, which is Christ's vineyard. Of these it is said in the Song of Songs: Catch us the little foxes that destroy the vineyards, for our vineyard has flowered. For when heretics and their followers, or the disciples of heresies, are caught in their errors by holy and catholic men, the Lord's vineyard, that is the Church, grows ever more and more abundant in holy graces, so that it may continually serve to its husbandman, who shed his blood for it, cups of nectared fragrance.

units.la: CAP. XXVII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXVII.

units.la: Quòd non ad eorum parentes pertineat, sicut illi dicunt, Disperdat Dominus universa labia dolosa, & linguam magniloquam.
units.tr: That it does not pertain to their parents, as they say, "May the Lord destroy all deceitful lips and the proud tongue."

units.la: VERSICULUM etiam quem Psalmographus de perfidorum Iudæorum labiis dolosis & linguis magniloquis protulit, qui consilium inierunt, ut salvatorem mundi dolo tenerent & occiderent, illi in sua synodo propriis parentibus adscribunt: qui quanquam fuerint cujusdam temetitemeritatis in imaginibus ab ornamentis ecclesiæ abolendis, majoris tamen & inconparabiliter iniquitatis non dicam temeritatis, sed etiam crudelitatis illi fuerunt in Domino crucifigendo. Isti enim habuerunt zelum Dei, sed non secundum scientiam, cùm imagines penitus abdicaverunt: illi simulantes se habere zelum legis, habuerunt zelum livoris & perfidiosissimæ iniquitatis, cùm Dominum patibulo adfixerunt: isti ecclesiarum indiscretè ornamenta quassavere. illi malitiosè semetipsos Dominum contemnentes fregere. Labia ergo dolosa & linguam magniloquam perfidiosissima Judæorum cohors habebat, cum dicebat; Scimus quia Moysi locutus est DEVS, hunc autem unde sit, nescimus. Nonne magniloquam &c, ut ita dixerim, magniloquam linguam habebant? cùm dicebant, Nos legem habemus, & secundum legem mori debet, quia filium Dei se fecit. Nonne magniloquam linguam habebant, cùm dicebant? Et hunc scimus, & unde sit scimus: Christus autem cum venerit, nemo scit unde sit. Nonne magniloquam linguam habebant, cum dicebant? Nulli scribere regem: nos non habemus regem nisi Cæsarem. Unde liquido paret, quod probrosò imaginum institutionem amore, qui ob earum abolitionem ea quæ de perfidis Judæis per Prophetam dicta sunt, patentibus suis non erubescunt adnectere, & eisdem jaculis cives perfodere, quibus Propheta ecclesiæ, immo Christi hostes nosci tur perfodile.
units.tr: The verse also which the Psalmist uttered concerning the deceitful lips and proud tongues of the faithless Jews, who plotted to seize and kill the Saviour of the world by guile, they ascribe in their synod to their own parents. Although these men were guilty of a certain rashness in removing the images from the ornaments of the church, the Jews were guilty of a far greater and incomparably greater iniquity, I will not say rashness but even cruelty, in crucifying the Lord. For those men had a zeal for God, but not according to knowledge, when they utterly rejected images. The others, pretending to have zeal for the law, had a zeal of envy and most faithless wickedness, when they nailed the Lord to the gibbet. Those men rashly shook the ornaments of the churches; the others maliciously broke them, despising the Lord himself. The deceitful lips and the proud tongue, then, were those of the most faithless band of Jews, when they said: We know that God spoke to Moses, but as for this man, we do not know where he is from. Did they not have a proud tongue, so to speak, when they said: We have a law, and by the law he ought to die, because he made himself the Son of God. Did they not have a proud tongue when they said: We know this man, and we know where he is from, but when the Christ comes, no one will know where he is from. Did they not have a proud tongue when they said: We have no king but Caesar; whoever makes himself a king opposes Caesar. Whence it is plainly evident that those who, out of love for images and for the sake of their abolition, do not blush openly to attach to their own people what the Prophet said about the faithless Jews, and to pierce their fellow citizens with the same darts with which the Prophet is known to have pierced the enemies of the Church, or rather of Christ, are themselves the ones pierced.

units.la: CAP. XXVIII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXVIII.

units.la: Quod non in eorum parentibus, ut illi dicunt, impletum sit, quod scriptum est, Inimici detec- cerunt framea in finem, & civitates eorum destru- xisti.
units.tr: That it was not fulfilled in their parents, as they claim, what is written: The enemies have come to an end of swords, and you have destroyed their cities.

units.la: SED nec hujus versiculi, ut illi ajunt, prophetia in eorum prodecessoribus sive parentibus quòd imagines abdicaverint, est completa: qui ergo incaute loca divinis cultibus mancipata nantentis expoliavere, longè tamen ab antiqui hostis nequitia, de quo hæc prophetia est, dicere: quippe cum nequitia quæ per ejus suasionem accidit humano generi, minor sit nequitia, qui & suæ humanæ auctor est artificis fraudulenti, qui sicut est natura subtilior, ita & sagacior callidior: & quem non gravat corporis fragilitas, acuit vafræ perversitatis iniquitas. Hujus inimici framea defecerunt in finem, quia tentamenta nequissima mox ut ad Christum qui est legis ad justitiam omni credenti, qui est finis sine fine: ad quem cum venerimus, nihil ulterius quæramus habemus, conlata fuerint, omnino deficiunt. Et ideo Propheta beatum dicit, qui pos los, id est, cogitationes inrationabiles, ad lapidem, ad Christum videlicet qui est lapis angularis, sive etiam, ut quidam volunt, inimici defecerunt framea in finem: quando gladius quo antiquus hostis bacchatur in consummatione seculi omnipotentis Dei gladio interimendus est: de quo Psalmo dicit, Nisi convertamini, gladium suum vibrabit: & de quo per Prophetam Ezechielem dicit, vo ego, dicit Dominus, acuam sicut fulgur gladium meum, & reddam ultionem inimicis meis. Framea namque braicus sermo est, quo in hoc loco antiqui hostis gladius innuitur. Inimici igitur in hoc loco minativus pluralis, ut plerique arbitrantur, sed genitivus singularis est, id est, inimici diaboli deferunt framea. & est schema quod prolepsis nuncupatur, id est, præoccupatio sive præsumptio, per ea quæ sequi debent anteponuntur. Quæ & in exordio Ezechielis Prophetæ invenitur, cùm Et factum est in tricesimo anno. Et in Psalmo habetur, cùm dicitur, Fundamenta ejus in montibus sanctis. Civitates igitur destructas non in hoc loco Psalmographus, ut illi arbitrantur, eorum prodecessoribus parentes pro imaginum abolitione eversos decantat, sed infideles populos, sive malorum acervos, quos diabolus tanquam suæ civitatis mœnia inhabitat, Christi manifestatione dicit eliminatos. Inanis igitur & vanus imaginum amor illorum pectora invasit, qui ut illarum adorationem staruanr, ea quæ de antiquo hoste vel de incredulis Judæis prophetata sunt, de suis parentibus prodecessoribus dicta fuisse existimant.
units.tr: Nor, as they say, was the prophecy of this verse fulfilled in their predecessors or parents, who cast out images. Those who carelessly tore down places dedicated to divine worship were far from speaking of the wickedness of the ancient enemy, of whom this prophecy speaks. For the wickedness that came upon the human race through his persuasion is greater, since he is the author of the human artifice of fraud, who is more subtle by nature and also keener and more cunning, and whom the frailty of the body does not burden, since the iniquity of his crafty perversity sharpens him. The swords of this enemy have failed to the end, because his most wicked attempts, once they were brought against Christ, who is the end of the law for righteousness to everyone who believes, who is an end without end, to whom when we have come we seek nothing further, altogether fail. And therefore the Prophet calls him blessed who dashes, that is, unreasonable thoughts, against the rock, namely against Christ, who is the corner stone. Or, as some want, the enemies have failed to the end of the swords: when the sword with which the ancient foe rages is to be destroyed at the consummation of the age by the sword of almighty God, of which the Psalm says: Unless you turn, he will brandish his sword; and of which the prophet Ezekiel says: Behold, I, says the Lord, will sharpen my sword like lightning, and will render vengeance to my enemies. For framea is a Hebrew word, by which in this place the sword of the ancient foe is meant. So inimici in this place is not the nominative plural, as most suppose, but the genitive singular, that is, the enemies of the devil fail with swords. This is a figure called prolepsis, that is, anticipation or presumption, by which things that ought to follow are put first. It is also found at the beginning of the prophet Ezekiel, where it says And it came to pass in the thirtieth year; and it is found in the Psalm where it says His foundations are in the holy mountains. Therefore the Psalmist does not, in this place, as they suppose, lament that cities destroyed were overthrown for the abolition of images in the time of their predecessors or parents; rather he declares that unbelieving peoples, or heaps of evildoers, whom the devil inhabits as the walls of his city, were cast out by the manifestation of Christ. Therefore a vain and empty love of images has taken hold of their hearts, and in order to defend the worship of images, they think that what was prophesied of the ancient foe or of the unbelieving Jews was said of their own parents and predecessors.

units.la: CAP. XXIX.
units.tr: CAP. XXIX.

units.la: Quomodo intellegendum sit quod scriptum est, Domine dilexi decorem domus tuæ, quem decorem isti imagines intellegunt.
units.tr: How the words "Lord, I have loved the beauty of your house" are to be understood, and what the images take this beauty to be.

units.la: DOMUS Dei aut secundum allegoriam ecclesia est, aut secundum anagogen cœlestis aut secundum tropologiam animæ hominis: & idcirco in plerisque scripturæ sanctæ locis domus Dei legitur, non parietes nec quædam materialis ædificatio, sed spiritualis & immobilis Dei intellegenda est habitatio: quorum sensuum archanis illorum mens penitus jejuna, qui decoreni domus Domini non ecclesiæ existimant virtutes, sed materiales imagines. Namque idem eximius vates quasdam imagines, vel certe pariterum pulchritudines, aut ministeriorum pretiosissimos apparatus viderat, cum dicebat, Domine dilexi decorem domus tuæ, & locum habitationis gloriæ tuæ. Numquidnam locus habitationis gloriæ Domini in manufactis quoquam credendus est? Habet ergo sancta ecclesia decorem quem Propheta diligebat, id est, spiritales virtutes: habet argentum, id est, fidem sive interiorem sensum: habet argenteum, id est, confessionem sive eloquii veritatem; habet columnas argenteas, id est, sanctos viros patientia rationabili & eloquiorum pulchritudine con-quaesita. quæ columnæ habent bases argenteas, cùm supra stabilitatem verbi Dei quod per prophetas & apostolos nobis traditur, conlocantur. Hæc etiam habent caput deauratum, quia caput aureum fides est Christi, Apostolo adtestante qui ait, Omnis namque viri caput Christus est. Habet etiam pro lignis imputribilibus scientiam quæ per lignum venit, sive incorruptionem castitatis quæ vetustatem nescit. Habet & pro bysso virginitatem, pro cocco confessionis gloriam: pro purpura charitatis fulgorem, pro hyacintho spem regni cælorum. His materis ejus sacerdotes induuntur, juxta David vocem, qui ait, Sacerdotes tui induantur justitiam: quos & Paulus his verbis hortatur, cum dicit, Induite vos viscera misericordiæ. habent etiam ejus sacerdotes alia nobiliora indumenta, quæ idem vas electionis designat, cum dicit; Induite vos dominum Jesum Christum, & carnis curam ne feceritis in concupiscentiis vestris. habet & bibliothecam, id est, sanctos viros divinæ legis documentis eruditos: de quibus per Prophetam dicitur, Beati immaculati in via, qui ambulant in lege Domini: beati qui scrutantur testimonia ejus, in toto corde exquirunt ea: & iterum beatos dicit eos qui memoria tenent mandata ejus ut faciant ea. Habet decem alia distensa, cum non in uno tantum verbo legis, neque in duobus aut in tribus, sed in toto decalogo legis spiritualis intellectus amplitudine dilatatur: sive cum fructum spiritus, id est, gaudium, pacem, patientiam, benignitatem, bonitatem, modestiam, fidem, continentiam, adjecta quæ est major omnium charitate profert. Habet etiam altare, id est firmitatem fidei, in qua orationum holtias & misericordiæ victimas offert Deo: in qua continentiæ cultro superbiam quasi tauram immolat, jucunditatem quasi arietem jugulat, luxuriam omnemque libidinem tanquam hircos & hædos, quibus dextrum brachium & pectusculum & maxillas sacerdotibus separat, id est, opera bona, opera dextra, in quibus siniistrum quiddam nullatenus reperitur. Habet & candelabrum luminis, sive quia Dominus lumen ejus est, sive quia sancti viri quorum lucernæ sunt ardentes &ludentes adventum, qui expectant dominum suum quando revertatur à nuptiis, lucivomaine ea prædicationes dogmata fundunt. Quod candelabrum lucernarum in austrum habet conlocatum ut ad aquilonem respiciat, id est, ut sancti viri vigilanter & sollicitus intueantur semper astutias diaboli, & pavida mente aspiciant unde sit ventura tentatio: quia & Propheta vidisse se dicit fuccensum, lebetem vel ollam & faciem ejus à facie aquilonis: & in alio loco dicitur, Ab aquilone enim pandetur malum super universam terram. & Petrus Apostolus dicit, Quia adversarius vester diabolus sicut leo rugiens circuit quærens quem devoret. Habet & mensam propositionis habentem duodecim panes conlocatas in parte aquilonis quæ respicit ad austrum, id est, duodecim Apostolos quos quotidie indesinenter jubetur adponere quæ ad austrum respicit, quia videlicet quotidie adventum Domini præstolatur. Dominus enim, ait Propheta, ab austro veniet. Habet alrare incensi, quia de ejus ædei firmitatem per orationum sanctarum fumus in conspectu Domini ascendit, & quotidie cum David clamat, Dirigatur oratio mea sicut incensum in conspectu tuo: sive quia secundum Apostolum, Christi bonus odor Deo. Habet propitiatorium & archam & duos cherubim, de quibus superius in quodam capitulo disputatum est.
