units.la: Notum esse non ambigimus vestrae spiritali dilectioni, scriptum esse, a omne datum optimum, & omne donum perfectum, descendens a patre luminum. Et iterum ait Spiritus sanctus per sanctissimum Salomonem: b Per me reges regnant, & potentes scribunt justitiam. Et per quendam Prophetam ait: c Ego sufficiam eis cum justitia regem. Nam quidem haec a Deo data Domini & Salvatoris nostri dona suscepimus, propterea hoc dignum putamus omnibus unius tribus nostrae fidelibus & orthodoxis Christianis, & maxime vestrae Christo dilectae & pacificae gloriae, omnia, si possibile est, subtiliter adnuntiare. Attamen ut non multa loquamur, brevem in sermone hoc rationem vobiscum faciemus. Duo mus. Duo enim capitula magna & præcipua est nobis cordi intimare. Unum, quia dispositor omnium bonarum rerum dominus Iesus Christus verus Deus noster adduxit ad Imperii dignitatem. Alterum, quod permisit propter quædam peccata subjecti populi sui provenire quasdam tribulationes. Sed ut facilius intelligi possit, breviori sermone comprehendi potest. Attamen necesse nobis videtur, ut initium rei quam prosequuturi sumus, tractare incoemus hoc modo.
units.tr: We do not doubt that it is known to your spiritual love that it is written: "Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of lights." And again the Holy Spirit says through the most wise Solomon: "By me kings reign, and princes decree justice." And through a certain prophet he says: "I will give them a king in righteousness." Since we have received these gifts from God, the gifts of our Lord and Saviour, we think it fitting to set out, if it is possible, all things carefully for all the faithful and orthodox Christians of our one empire, and especially for your glory, beloved of Christ and peaceful. Yet, so that we do not speak at length, we shall give you a brief account in this discourse. There are two great and principal points that we wish to make known to you. The first is that the Lord Jesus Christ, the true God and disposer of all good things, has brought us to the dignity of empire. The second is that, on account of certain sins, he has permitted certain tribulations to come upon his subject people. But so that this may be more easily understood, it can be summarised in a shorter account. Nevertheless, it seems necessary to us to begin with the origin of the matter we are about to pursue, and to treat it in this way.

units.la: Igitur tempore Leonis, qui ante nos hoc imperium tenuit, quidam homo, Thomas nomine, antiqui diaboli discipulus, & ejus operum promptus perpetrator fuit. Is cum esset cuiidam ex maximis Patriciis subjectus, tempore quo Herena imperium tenuit, fraudem operatus est in dominum suum, scilicet concubuit cum uxore domini sui. Cum hæc res ad notitiam pervenisset, profugitin Persas, mens legalem subire sententiam. Qui cum illic moras fecisset, a diebus prædictæ Herenæ, usque ad prædictum Leonem, fidem Christi abnegans, & hoc modo proditor fidei Christianæ fuit, quo facilius potuisset multos infideles Sarracenorum & cæterarum aliarum gentium ad suam perducere voluntatem. Suggerebatque eis quòd ipse esset Constantinus, filius sæpe dictæ Herenæ Imperatricis, & quod alter pro eo esset oculis privatus, & ipse inlexis oculis sanus evasisset. Pro quare prædicti gentiles ei adhæserunt. Primùm quidem cœpit cum eis exercere latrocinia & alios vi sibimet sociare, quoniamdam vero perditione pecuniarum, quosdam quidem honorum & dignitatum promissionibus solicitavit. Et ut hæc compendiosius expediam, idem Thomas exiens de Persida cum Sarracenis & Persis, Hiberis, Armeniis & Avasgis, & reliquis gentibus alienigenarum tempore prædicti Leonis subito cum prædicta manu valida perpræliaret, direptione sibi subdidit totum Armeniæ Ducatum, simul & Ducatum Chaldeæ, quæ gens montem Caucasum incolit, nec non & Ducem Armeniacorum cum manu valida devicit.
units.tr: Therefore, in the time of Leo, who held this empire before us, a certain man named Thomas, a disciple of the ancient devil and a ready perpetrator of his works, was. Being subject to one of the greatest patricians, at the time when Irene held the empire, he committed a fraud against his lord, namely he lay with his lord's wife. When this matter came to light, he fled to the Persians, fearing to undergo the sentence of the law. Having stayed there, from the days of the aforesaid Irene down to the aforesaid Leo, denying the faith of Christ, and in this way becoming a betrayer of the Christian faith, he was able more easily to bring many unbelieving Saracens and other nations to his own will. He told them that he himself was Constantine, son of the Empress Irene, and that another had been blinded in his place, while he himself had escaped unharmed by the blinding of eyes that had been arranged. For this reason the aforesaid heathens joined him. At first he began to carry on robberies with them and to bind others to himself by force, and then, by the lure of money, he tempted some with promises of honours and offices. To dispatch these matters more briefly: the same Thomas, setting out from Persia with Saracens and Persians, Iberians, Armenians, Avasgians, and the other foreign nations, in the time of the aforesaid Leo suddenly fought a battle with that strong band, and by plunder he subdued to himself the whole Duchy of Armenia, together with the Duchy of Chaldea, a people who dwell on Mount Caucasus, and he also conquered the Duke of the Armeniacs with his strong band.

units.la: His ergo ita gestis, ut plurima omittamus propter superfluitatem verborum, quæ in hac tempestate tribulationum contigerunt, cujus tyranni impetum non valens memoratus Leo Imperator sustinere, & in his angustiis constitutus de recuperatione desperans, à quibusdam improbis conjurationem in eum facta subito occisus est. Quo interfecto, & cum nemo tunc imperaret, per adjutorium patris & filii & spiritus sancti, unius consubstantialis divinitatis, & per intercessiones dominatricis & intemeratæ Dei genetricis & omnium sanctorum, convenit universa multitudo secundum antiquum morem, videlicet beatissimus Patriarcha, gloriosi Patricii nostri, inlustres senatores & Principes, qui illic tunc affuerunt diversarum provinciarum, quorum omnium consensu ad hoc imperium elevatus sumus, maximè propter imminentes angustias & tribulationes, quas faciebat homicida ille & proditor patriæ. Fuimus enim noti inlustribus Principibus nostris & cœn.
units.tr: These things having thus been done, that we may omit many things for the sake of brevity, which happened in this time of tribulation, the aforesaid Emperor Leo, unable to withstand the assault of that tyrant, and placed in these straits, despairing of recovery, was suddenly killed by a conspiracy formed against him by some wicked men. When he had been slain, and when no one then held the empire, through the help of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, one consubstantial divinity, and through the intercessions of the Lady and immaculate Mother of God and of all the saints, the whole assembly gathered according to the ancient custom: namely the most blessed Patriarch, our glorious patricians, the illustrious senators and princes of the various provinces who were then present there. By the consent of all of them we were raised to this empire, chiefly on account of the imminent distress and tribulations which that murderer and traitor to his country was causing. For we were known to our illustrious princes and ...

units.la: Hoc modo ad imperium provecti, invenimus Christianos divisos & discordantes, & ut verius dicamus, plurimos invenimus illius impii Tyranni errorem & impietatem sequentes, & ob hoc non potuimus facilè illos fideles nostros Christianos ad hoc adunare, ut eum expugnare valuissemus. Quibus calibus nos impediti, ille hac occasione accepta, solicitando sibi plurimos sociavit, & ex clientibus nostris & dromoniis collectis potestatem habuit veniendi partibus Thraciæ & Macedoniæ, & festinus veniens civitatem nostram obsedit, & navali exercitu circundedit eam in Mense Decembri xv. Indictione. Nos autem, quamvis nobiscum paucitas militum & pugnatorum esset, non præterimus, cum semper cum eis congrederemur in certamine, & eos à civitate repelleremus. Sed cùm ille, (ut superius dictum est,) hostium validam manum habuisset, non solùm de his, quos suprà moravimus, sed etiam de Asiæ & Europæ partibus Thraciæ, Macedoniæ, Thessalonicæ & circumcentibus Sclaviniis; hæc causa prolongavit obsidionem nostram, hæc eadem obsidio modò propiore modò longior usque ad unius anni spatium perseveravit.
units.tr: Raised to the empire in this way, we found the Christians divided and at odds, and, to speak more truly, we found very many following the error and impiety of that wicked tyrant. For this reason we could not easily unite those faithful Christians of ours so as to be able to overthrow him. Hindered by these difficulties, he seized the opportunity, gathered many to his side, and, having assembled soldiers from our clients and dromons, he had the power to come to the regions of Thrace and Macedonia. Hastening there, he besieged our city and surrounded it with a naval force in the month of December, in the fifteenth indiction. We, although the number of our soldiers and fighting men with us was small, did not hold back, but always engaged them in conflict and drove them away from the city. But since he (as said above) had a strong force of enemies, not only from those whom we have already mentioned but also from the parts of Asia and Europe, from Thrace, Macedonia, Thessalonica and the surrounding Slavic peoples, this circumstance prolonged our siege, and this same siege, now closer and now more distant, continued for the space of a whole year.

units.la: Nos autem videntes illius diaboli & homicidæ longam pertinaciam & ignaviam, & seductionem Christianorum, qui ab eo seducti sunt, posuimus spem nostram & virtutem in Christum verum Deum nostrum adjutorem & corroboratorem, atque cum sincera fide civitatem nostram ingressi sumus adversus illum tyrannum, qui tunc fere triginta milibus ab urbe nostra resedebat. Cumque prælium committeremus, ipse Dominus Deus noster, qui semper adjutor & protector imperii nostri est, misit principem militiæ virtutis suæ, sicut legitur fecisse Iesu Nave, & dissolvit ac dissipavit virtutem eorum, & prævalere nos fecit adversus eum. Volentes Christianis parcere, receptui canere jussimus, & nostros à cæde coërcuinius. Et hac occasione pagani & alienigenæ, qui cum Thoma perditionis eorum auctore fuerant, evaserunt, & in fugam versi sunt, & à nobis persecuti, in quadam civitate provinciæ Thraciæ nomine Arcadiopoli inclusi sunt. Quidam autem ipsorum dispersi in montibus se occultaverunt. Pars autem eorum intraverunt in Panadus civitatem.
units.tr: But we, seeing the long obstinacy and cowardice of that devil and murderer, and the deception of the Christians who had been led astray by him, placed our hope and strength in Christ, the true God, our helper and strengthener. With sincere faith we entered our city against that tyrant, who at that time was encamped about thirty thousand paces from our city. When we joined battle, the Lord our God himself, who is always the helper and protector of our empire, sent the leader of his host, of his power, as is read to have been done by Joshua the son of Nun, and he broke and scattered their strength, and made us prevail against him. Wishing to spare the Christians, we ordered the recall to be sounded, and we restrained our men from slaughter. On this occasion the heathens and foreigners who had been with Thomas, the author of their ruin, escaped, turned to flight, and, pursued by us, were shut up in a city of the province of Thrace called Arcadiopolis. Some of them, scattered, hid themselves in the mountains. Part of them entered the city of Panadus.

units.la: Nos autem, missis exercitibus nostris, eos obsideri fecimus. Sed ipsa civitas, in qua Deo odibilis & immemorabilis erat, cum suis sequacibus per quinque menses obsessa est, volentes sicut diximus populo nostro parcere & civitati, vivum tum cepimus, & omnes, qui cum eo erant, tā contribules quā etiam alienigenas. Et ipsum quidem Thomam, amputatis manibus & pedibus, patibulo suspendi jussimus. Duo verò, qui dicebantur ei filii esse adoptivi, alter eorum in Asiaà fidelibus nostris interemtus est, & alterum eadem morte, qua pseudopatrem ejus, condemnare jussimus. Et hoc modo deleta est memoria eorum de terra in seculorum secula, juxta id quod scriptum est; inimici defecerunt framea in finem. Sarracenos quoque omnes & Armenios & reliquos, qui de prælio evaserunt, omnes vivos cepimus, & secundùm Dei dispositionem nos in eis ulti sumus. Deinde profecti pervenimus ad castellum, quod dicitur Panidus, in quo suprà memoratam partem inimicorum nostrorum confugisse diximus,
units.tr: We, sending out our armies, had them besieged. But that city, where he was hateful to God and unremembered, was beset for five months together with his followers. Wishing, as we have said, to spare our people and the city, we took alive him and all who were with him, both fellow countrymen and foreigners. Thomas himself, having had his hands and feet cut off, we ordered to be hanged on a gibbet. As for the two who were said to be his adopted sons, one of them was killed in Asia by our faithful men, and we ordered the other to be condemned to the same death as his pseudo-father. In this way their memory has been blotted out from the earth for ever and ever, according to what is written: the enemies have come to an end, with the sword, for ever. We also took alive all the Saracens, Armenians and the rest who had escaped from the battle, and we avenged ourselves on them according to God's disposition. Then, setting out, we came to the fortress called Panidus, into which, as we said, the aforesaid part of our enemies had fled,
Josh. 1.

units.la: Psal. 9. iunus, quibus nos vitam promisimus, si ad fidem nostram venire voluissent. Sed Illi nost is jussionibus parere nolentes, quia magis mori quàm in dedition̉m venire maluerunt, im̄nifit eis Deus terræ motum, qui concussit civitatem, à quo muri ejus d̔ruti sunt, sicut de Hierico accidisse legitur, Josu. 6. & eo modo traditi sunt in manus nostras. & hoc omnipotentis Dei miraculum in nobis factum est, quod miraculum nequaquam existimavimus esse celandum, sed ubique gloriam Dei & magnalia ejus adnuntiandum. Et hoc modo cum triumpho victoriæ ad palatium nostrum reversi sumus.
units.tr: Ps. 9. To them we promised life, if they had been willing to come to our faith. But they, unwilling to obey our commands, and preferring to die rather than come into surrender, God sent upon them an earthquake, which shook the city, by which its walls were thrown down, as is read to have happened at Jericho, Josh. 6. and so they were delivered into our hands. This miracle of almighty God was wrought in us, and we did not think this miracle ought to be concealed, but that the glory of God and his great works should be proclaimed everywhere. And in this way we returned with triumph of victory to our palace.

units.la: Et ex eo tempore omnes Christiani imperii nost i adunitatem pacis & pristinam concordiam tenuerunt, glorificantes & magnificantes propugnatorem nostrum, Dominum Jesum Christum, quia adunitatem fidei coadunare populum suum dignatus est, in subjectionem, quod ab eo est, imperii nostri. Quocirca dignum existimavimus, hæc quasi pacifico amico & spirituali fratri nostro, & ut credimus socio gaudii à Deo imperii nostri manifesta facere, quæ nobiscum acta sunt, ut pariter, sicut unus ejusdemque fidei & religionis cultoribus facere oportet, laudibus & hymnis conlaudemus & glorificemus Salvatorem nostrum Dominum Jesum Christum. Opportuerat enim statim in exordio imperii nostri sicut spiritali fratri nostro & pacifico amico, per veros apices nostros, quæ erga nos gesta sunt, vobis manifestare: Sed, sicut supra dictum est, præfati tyranni & rebellis ac turpi morte condemnati Thomæ seditio nos facere prohibuit.
units.tr: And from that time all the Christians of our empire have kept the unity of peace and the former harmony, glorifying and magnifying our champion, the Lord Jesus Christ, because he has deigned to unite his people in the unity of faith, in subjection to our empire, which comes from him. Wherefore we have thought it right to make known to you, as to our peaceful friend, our spiritual brother, and, as we believe, a sharer in our joy granted by God to our empire, what has been done by us, so that, as becomes those who worship one and the same faith and religion, we may together praise and glorify our Saviour, the Lord Jesus Christ, with hymns and songs. For we ought at the very beginning of our reign to have made known to you, our spiritual brother and peaceful friend, by our true letters, what has been done concerning us; but, as was said above, the aforesaid tyrant and rebel Thomas, condemned to a shameful death, prevented us by his sedition.

units.la: At vero nunc dedit Deus nobis hoc præsens opportunum tempus, post ejus interfectionem, & coadunationem & concordiam populi nostri. Et ideo justum existimavimus, mittere ad vestrum gloriam Theodorum Protospatharium nostrum & Stratigon, Nicetam sanctissimum Metropolitanum Myrdensem Licæ, Fortunatum Archiepiscopum Venetiæ, Theodorum reverendissimum Diaconum & Oeconomum istius sanctissimæ Dei Catholicæ & magnæ Ecclesiæ sanctæ Sophiæ, & Leonem nostrum Candidatum. Et non tantum per has syllabas, sed & per ipsos viros adnuntiamus ve-stræ gloriæ omnia, quæ præposita sunt, ut tam per eos, quàm quæ & per missos vestros iterum scire possimus vestræ dilectionis sanitatem, simulque fidelium vestrorum incolumitatem, nec non & omnium rerum vestrarum apud vos consistentium prosperita em. Potrò nunc per has nostras veras & fideles syllabas corroboramus & confirmamus priorem pacem & amicitiam inter vos & nos constitutam, deprecantes mediatorem ejusdem pacis Dominum qui dixit; Pacem meam do vobis, pacem meam relinquo vobis, eandem pacem & charitatem splendidiorem & robustiorem facere, & ostendere temporibus & potestatibus præterens, quoniam & nos sic tenemus & speramus, quòd & vestra gloriosissima potestas ita consentiat, sicut & nostra. Charitas enim & pax utramque potestatem secundum Dominicam vocem potest & servatrices mandatorum ejus efficere. Dixit enim; Qui diligit me, mandata mea custodit. Et iterum; In hoc cognoscent omnes, quia mei discipuli estis, si dilectionem habueritis ad invicem.
units.tr: But now God has given us this present fitting time, after his death, and after the union and concord of our people. And therefore we have judged it right to send to your glory Theodore our Protospatharius and Strategus, Nicetas the most holy Metropolitan of Myra in Lycia, Fortunatus Archbishop of Venice, Theodore the most reverend deacon and steward of that most holy Catholic and great Church of God, Holy Sophia, and our Leo the Candidatus. And we announce to your glory everything that has been set before us, not only by these few syllables but also through the men themselves, so that through them, as well as through your envoys, we may again learn of the health of your love, and likewise of the safety of your faithful subjects, and of the prosperity of all your affairs existing among you. Now therefore by these our true and faithful syllables we confirm and establish the former peace and friendship made between you and us, praying the Lord, the mediator of that peace, who said: My peace I give unto you, my peace I leave with you, to make this same peace and charity more splendid and more robust, and to show it to times and powers to come; since we hold and hope that your most glorious power agrees in this just as ours does. For charity and peace, according to the Lord's word, can both make the two powers keepers of his commandments. For he said: He who loves me keeps my commandments. And again: By this shall all men know that you are my disciples, if you have love one for another.

units.la: Sed & hoc vestræ Christo amabili dilectioni manifestamus, quia multa de Ecclesiasticis seu & laicis viris alieni de apostolicis traditionibus facti, & neque paternos terminos custodientes, facti sunt inventores malarum rerum. Primum quidem honoríficas & vivificas cruces de sacris templis expellebant, & in eadem loca imagines statuebant, ponebantque lucernas coram eis, simul & incensum celebrant, atque eas in tali honore habebant, sicut honorificum & vivificum lignum, in quo Christus Deus noster crucifigi dignatus est propter nostram salutem. Psillebant & adorabant, atque ab eldem imaginibus auxilium petebant. Psærique autem linteaminibus easdem imagines circundabant, & filiorum suorum de baptismatis fonte susceptrices faciebant. Alii vero religiosum habitum sumere volentes, religiosiores personas postponebant, qui priùs comam capitis eorum solebant, adhibitis imaginibus quasi in sinum earum decidere capillos illorum sinebant. Quidam vero sacerdotum & clericorum colores, de imaginibus radentes, immiscuerunt oblationino, & ex hac oblatione post missarum celebrationem dabant communicare volentibus. Alii Domini in manus imaginum ponebant, unde communicare volentes accipere feceunt. Alii vero spreta Ecclesia, in communibus domibus, tabulis imaginum pro altaris usu, per eas sacrum ministerium celebrabant, & alia multa his similia illicita, & nostræ re-ligioni contraria, in Ecclesiis fiebant, quæ à doctioribus & sapientioribus vitæ sacris indigna esse videbantur.
units.tr: But we also make this known to your love, beloved in Christ, that many of the ecclesiastical and lay men, having been turned aside from the apostolic traditions and not keeping the paternal bounds, have become inventors of evil things. First, they drove the honourable and life-giving crosses out of the sacred temples, and set up images in the same places, and placed lamps before them, and celebrated incense, and held them in such honour as the honourable and life-giving wood on which Christ our God deigned to be crucified for our salvation. They kissed and adored them, and sought help from those same images. Some surrounded these images with linen cloths, and made them sponsors of their sons at the baptismal font. Others, wishing to take the religious habit, put more religious persons before them, who used to cut their hair; with the images present, they let their hair fall, as it were, into the bosom of the images. Some priests and clerics scraped colours from the images, mixed them into the oblation, and after the celebration of the Mass gave this oblation to those who wished to communicate. Others placed the Lord's body into the hands of the images, from which they made those who wished to communicate receive it. Others, despising the Church, celebrated the sacred ministry in private houses, using panels of images in place of the altar; and many other things like these, unlawful and contrary to our religion, were done in the churches, which seemed to the more learned and wiser men unworthy of the sacred life.

units.la: Propterea statuerunt orthodoxi Imperatores, & doctissimi sacerdotes, locale adunare Concilium ad inquisitionem siper his habendam, qui in idipsum convenerunt, sancto spiritu inspirante. Ta-bnique commune consilio fieri prohibuerunt, & imagines de humilioribus locis vesteri si fecerunt, &c., quæ in sublimioribus locis positæ erant, ut ipsa pictura pro scriptura haberetur, in suis locis statuere permiserunt, ne ab indoctioribus & infirmioribus adorarentur, sed neque eis lucernas accendere, neque incensum adolerent, prohibuerunt. Quemadmodum & nos nunc sentimus & tenemus abs cientes de Ecclesia Christicos, qui hujusmodi malignis inventionibus student.
units.tr: Therefore the orthodox Emperors and the most learned priests resolved to gather a local council to examine these matters; and they came together for this purpose, inspired by the Holy Spirit. They forbade the matter to be settled by common counsel, and had the images taken down from the lower places, and allowed those that were placed in higher positions to remain in their places, so that the painting itself might be regarded as Scripture, and they forbade that they be adored by the less learned and weaker folk, and likewise forbade lamps to be lit before them or incense to be burnt. Just as we also now think and hold, expelling from the Church those Christians who labour at such wicked inventions.

units.la: Propterea quidam illorum, qui noluerunt suscipere Concilia localia, & à veritate redargui, sugerunt hinc, & venerunt ad antiquam Romam à Deo conservatam, injuriam & calumnias ecclesiæ mileres, & veræ religioni detrahentes, quorum pelliima verba & blasphemiis plena postponentes potius orthodoxa gloriæ tuæ manifesta facimus, quia nos symbolum sanctorum & universalis Synodorum, quod ab omnibus orthodoxis Christianis tenetur, non tantùm prædicamus, sed & inviolabiliter corde tenemus.
units.tr: Therefore some of those who refused to accept the local councils and to be refuted from the truth fled from here and came to ancient Rome, which God has preserved, and spread injuries and calumnies against the Church, detracting from the true religion. Setting aside their wicked words, full of blasphemies, we rather make plain to your orthodox glory that we not only proclaim but also inviolably hold in our hearts the creed of the holy and universal Synods, which is held by all orthodox Christians.

units.la: Trinitatem in tribus personis divisam colimus, unitatem unius divinitatis naturam confitentes, ex virgine temporalem Verbi nativitatem praedicamus, divinitatis & humanitatis duas voluntates operationes * glorificamus: Postulante intercessiones & interpellationes inviolatae dominae nostrae Dei genitricis semper virginis Mariae & omnium Sanctorum. Gloriosas autem & sanctas, eorum cum fide veneramur, & quicquid aliud a beatissimis Apostolis traditum, & a sanctis Patribus in eisdem sex synodis constitutum est, & confitemur & tenemus.
units.tr: We worship the Trinity divided in three persons, confessing the unity of the one divine nature; we proclaim the temporal birth of the Word from the Virgin; we glorify the two wills and two operations of divinity and humanity; at the request of the intercessions and pleas of our inviolate Lady, the Mother of God, ever Virgin Mary, and of all the Saints. We venerate with faith their glorious and holy images, and we confess and hold whatever else has been handed down by the most blessed Apostles and established by the holy Fathers in those six Synods.

units.la: Unde honorem ecclesiae Christi quaerentes, fecimus literas ad sanctissimum Papam Romae, & eas misimus per praedictos missos nostros ad eum, dantes eis evangelium aureum ex bus pretiosis ornatum, similiter & patenam auream, & ipsam ex lapidibus pretiosis, ornatum cem simili modo ornatum, ambobus inscripta imperii nostri nomina, ut Deo jubente illuc pro entes offerant ea ad templum sanctissimi & beatissimi Apostolorum principis Petri, qui pro nobis & vobis.
units.tr: Therefore, seeking the honour of the Church of Christ, we have written letters to the most holy Pope at Rome, and sent them by our aforesaid envoys to him, giving them a golden gospel book adorned with precious stones, likewise a golden paten, and also a chalice adorned with precious stones in the same manner, both inscribed with the names of our empire, so that, God willing, they may offer them there to the temple of the most holy and most blessed prince of the Apostles, Peter, who [is] for us and for you.

units.la: De caetero ordinet vestra spiritualis dilectio, ut cum omni honore & illaesione ad eum auxilium eis ferentes in his, quae Deo placeant, & ad honorem ejus pertineant in satisfactionem, quae inter nos est, jubentes ei, ut si amodo manifestum fuerint quidam seductores Pseudo ecclesiae calumniatores, illuc eos expellere, ut quod scriptum est, de his adimpleatur. Dicit ptura; Ejicite malum de medio vestri, ut non tantum in republica ad invicem concordemus, sed de magna re, quae ad salutem animae pertinet, id est, ecclesiastica & Deo amabilia consentiamus.
units.tr: For the rest, let your spiritual love arrange that, with all honour and without harm, they be helped to him in those things which please God and pertain to his honour, in confirmation of the peace which is between us; and let him be instructed that, if from now on certain seducers and false calumniators of the Church are made manifest, he should expel them from there, so that what is written concerning them may be fulfilled. The Scripture says: Put away the evil from among you, so that we may agree not only in public affairs with one another, but also in the great matter which pertains to the salvation of the soul, that is, in things ecclesiastical and pleasing to God.

units.la: Causa memoriae dilectionis, quae inter nos est, misimus per praedictos Missos nostros pra vultrim unum, milinovultum unum, ryrea duo blattas veras duas * dirodina duo, diventa duo.
units.tr: In memory of the love which is between us, we have sent by our aforesaid envoys: pra vultrim one, milinovultum one, two ryrea, two genuine blattae, two dirodina, two diventa.

units.la: Absoluta mense Aprili die x. Indict. xi. a Deo * conservata regia urbe.
units.tr: Completed in the month of April, on the tenth day, in the eleventh indiction, in the royal city preserved by God.

units.la: LUDOVICI PII ET LOTHARII IMP. P. A. U. G.
units.tr: Of Louis the Pious and Lothar, Emperors, Pious, Fortunate, Venerable, Augustus

units.la: SYNODUS PARISIENSIS De Cultu imaginum, habita sub Anno Domini DCCCXXV. SYNODVS PARISIENSIS, EXCELLENTISSIMIS AC VICTORIOSISSIMIS DEOQUE AMABILIBUS AUGUSTIS DO- MINIS HLUDOVVICO & HLUDHARIO Serenissimis Imperatoribus.
units.tr: The Synod of Paris on the Worship of Images, held in the year of the Lord 825. THE SYNOD OF PARIS, TO THE MOST EXCELLENT AND MOST VICTORIOUS, AND GOD-BELOVED AUGUSTUS LORDS, LUDWIG AND LOTHAR, THE MOST SERENE EMPERORS.

units.la: NOs servi ac fidelissimi oratores vestri, qualiter proximis Kalendis Novembris apud urbem juxta praeceptum vestrae magnitudinis in unum convenimus, qualiter quoque à vestra pietate nobis injuncto, de causa videlicet imaginum, egerimus, ad vestrae cellitudinis reducimus. Sed ut melius nobis manifestum fieret, ob quam causam vestrae quae ergo Dei sanctaeque suae ecclesiae amorem ardentissime flagrat, ad hoc inquirendum primum epistolam Hadriani Papae, quam pridem pro imaginibus erigendis Constantino Imperatori & Herculi jus ad eorum deprecationem in transmarinis partibus direxit, coram nobis legi fecimus, & nostrae pa vitati res patuit, sicut juste reprehendit illos, qui imagines Sanctorum et memoria abolere pattibus confringere, & penitus abolere praesumserunt, sicut diu discrete noscitur fecisse in eo, quod perstitiose eas adorare jullit. Pro quatum etiam causa synodum congregari praecepit, & sua vestrae sub jurejurando censuit, ut erigerentur & adorarentur, & sanctae nuncupatentur, cum sit licitum, adorare vero nefas sit. Inserunt etiam in eadem epistola quaedam testimonia sanctorum quantum nobis datur intelligi, valde absona, & ad rem de qua agebatur, minime pertinentia.
units.tr: We, your servants and most faithful envoys, report to your Highness how, on the nearest Kalends of November, we assembled in the city, as your majesty had commanded, and how we dealt with the matter of images, which your piety had enjoined upon us. But so that it might become clearer to us for what reason your Highness, who burns with the most ardent love of God and of his holy Church, wished this to be inquired into, you first had the letter of Pope Hadrian read before us. He had lately sent it to the Emperor Constantine and to Irene concerning the setting up of images in the eastern regions, urging them to pray to these images. From it our minds were made clear: he rightly rebuked those who had presumed to destroy and utterly abolish images of the saints, breaking them and erasing their memory, as is well known to have been done for a long time, unwisely, in that they ordered them to be adored as superstition demanded. For this reason he also ordered a synod to be convened, and by his judgment he decided that images should be set up and adored and called holy, since this is permitted, whereas adoration is wicked. In the same letter they also insert certain testimonies of the saints, which, as far as we are able to understand, are altogether discordant and in no way pertinent to the matter under discussion.

units.la: Ex hujus namque epistolae textu, Imperator & clerus, simulque & populus, auctoritatem synodum fecerunt, in qua sicut illi multum deviaverunt, qui imagines Sanctorum in illo odo, quae sub Constantino avo memorati Constantini facta est, penitus abdicandas esse decreverunt: sic illi non mediocriter erraverunt, qui eas non solum coli & adorari, & sanctas nuncupari decreverunt: verum etiam sanctimoniam ab eis se adipisci professi sunt. Et ut id verum esse quod notum est adstruere, demonstrarent, quaedam sanctarum scripturarum testimonia & sanctorum patrum suum superstitiosum errorem confirmandum violenter sumserunt, & eidem suo operi inaptaverunt, quoniam non eo sensu, quo dicta, nec eo intellectu, quo a sanctis patribus expositia esse producuntur prolata vel intellecta.
units.tr: From the text of this letter, the Emperor, the clergy and also the people made the authority of a synod, in which, just as those erred greatly who decreed that the images of the saints should be utterly abandoned, as was done under the grandfather of the Constantine mentioned above, in that council, so too those erred no small amount who decreed that they should not only be venerated and adored and called holy, but also professed that holiness is obtained from them. And so that they might demonstrate that what is well known is true, they violently took up certain testimonies of the holy Scriptures and of the holy Fathers to confirm their superstitious error, and fitted them to their own work, though they were neither produced nor understood in the sense in which they were spoken, nor in the meaning in which they have been expounded by the holy Fathers.

units.la: Eandem porro synodum cum sanctae memoriae genitor vester coram se fuisset, perlegi fecit et ibi in locis, ut dignum erat, reprehendisset, & quaedam capitula, quae reprehensionem pateret, tradidit, eaque per Angilbertum Abbatem eidem Hadriano Papae direxisset, ut illius judicio & auctoritate corrigerentur, ipse rursus fivendo illis, qui ejus institutu tam super stitiosa tamque inconsiderata monita memorato operi inseruerant, per singula capitula in illorum excusationem respondere voluit, non tamen quae decuit, conatus est. Talia quippe quaedam sunt, quae in illorum oppositum, quae remota pontificali auctoritate, & veritati & auctoritati refragantur. Sed objectionibus aliquando absona, aliquando inconvenientia, aliquando etiam reprehensione testimonia defensionis gratia proferre nisus sit, in fine tamen ejusdem apologiae sic se sentire & praedicare ac praecipere de his quae agebantur, professus est, sicut a beato Papa Gregorio ... te constabat. Quibus verbis liquidò colligitur, quòd non tantum scienter, quantum ignoranter, in eodem facto à recto tramite deviaverit. Nisi enim in conclusione objectionum suarum retinaculis veritatis, beati scilicet Gregorii institutis, adstrictus iter devium praecavisset, in superstitionis praecipium omninò labi potuisset.
units.tr: When your father of holy memory was present before him, he had this same synod read through and, as was fitting, reproved it at the relevant places, and he handed over certain chapters which deserved rebuke, and sent them by Abbot Angilbert to that same Pope Hadrian, so that they might be corrected by his judgment and authority. He himself, however, in reply to those who had inserted such superstitious and such thoughtless admonitions in the aforementioned work, wished to answer each chapter in their defence, yet he did not do so as he ought. Indeed, there are some things which are opposed to them, which, apart from papal authority, conflict with both truth and authority. But at times with objections that were discordant, at times unsuitable, and at times even rebuked testimonies, he strove to bring forward testimonies in defence; yet at the end of the same apology he professed that he thought, taught and commanded concerning the matters at issue as it was known the blessed Pope Gregory had done. From these words it is clearly gathered that he went astray from the straight path in this matter not so much knowingly as ignorantly. For unless, at the close of his objections, he had been bound by the reins of truth, namely the institutions of blessed Gregory, and had guarded against the devious path, he could have fallen altogether into the chief of superstitions.

units.la: Hisigitur pro captu ingeniranimadversis & intellectis, ut plenius etiam nobis cuncta patescecent, fecimus epistolam nobis relegi, quam vobis Legati Graecorum anno praeterito detulerunt. Venerabilis namque Freculfus Episcopus subtiliter prudenterque, qualiter ipse & Adegarius socius illius, de hac re cum domino Apostolico & cum venerandis Episcopis & ministris illius egissent, viva voce patefacti nostrae innotuit. Sed cùm prudenti relatu illius cuncta cognovissemus, qualiter partim veritatis ignorantia, partim pessimae consuetudinis usu hujus superstitionis pestis illis in partibus inolevisset, & priora & posteriora studiosissimè consideràssemus, intelleximus, quantum nobis resparuit, quo zelo ad haec consideranda vestra sancta devotio excitata fuerit. Non enim ignoramus, animum vestrum magno raedio posse affici, cùm illos à recto tramite quoquomodo conspicitis deviare, qui summa auctoritate praediti, deviantesque quosque debuerant corrigere. Illo nempe zelo accensi estis, de quo beatus Paulus Apostolus dicit; Quis scandalizatur, & ego non uror? Cùm enim duos in periculo constitutos conspexistis, & à via regia declinantes, unum scilicet ad sinistram in abruptum confringendarum imaginum prolapsum: alterum verò ad dexteram in superstitiosam videlicet earundem imaginum adorationem proclivem, voluistis vos affectu piaratis medium opponere, & utrumque partis morbo salutiferam medicinam conferre.
units.tr: Having therefore considered and understood these matters as far as our capacity allowed, and so that all things might be made more fully clear to us, we had the letter read back to us which the envoys of the Greeks delivered to you last year. For the venerable Bishop Freculf, with prudence and skill, set forth to us in living voice how he and his companion Adegar had dealt with this matter with the lord Apostolic and with the venerable bishops and ministers of his. And when we had learned all these things from his prudent report, and had most carefully considered both what had come before and what followed, we understood how greatly your holy devotion must have been stirred to consider these matters with such zeal. For we are not unaware that your spirit must be greatly moved when you see those who are endowed with the highest authority, and who ought to correct those who go astray, turning aside from the straight path in any way. Indeed you were kindled with that zeal of which the blessed Apostle Paul says: "Who is offended, and I do not burn?" For when you saw two men placed in danger and departing from the royal way, one, indeed, on the left, falling headlong into the breaking of images, and the other on the right, inclined to the superstitious adoration of the same images, you wished, with pious affection, to set a middle course against both, and to offer a healing remedy against the disease of each side.

units.la: Sed quoniam maximum vobis in eo obstaculum erat, eò quòd pars illa quae debebat errata corrigere, suaque auctoritate hujusce superstitionis errori obniti, ipsa prorsus eidem superstitioni non solùm resistere, verùm etiam incauta defensione contra auctoritatem divinam & sanctorum patrum dicta nitebatur suffragari: aperuit vobis dominus ostium juxta optatum vobis desiderium, ut licentia vobis ab eadem tribueretur auctoritate tantae rei cum vestris quaerendi familiariter veritatem, ut quoniam inerat vobis voluntas consulendi, & deerat auctoritas quaerendi, ejus auctoritate quaereretis veritatem, cujus auctoritas deviare videbatur ab ipsa veritate, quatenus sancto vestro desiderio ac vigilanti studio veritas patefacta, dum se in medium ostenderet, etiam ipsa auctoritas volens nolensque veritati cederet atque succumberet. Verum quoniam fratrum salus non est negligenda, & eminens auctoritas non est facilè reprehendenda, visum est extremitati nostrae, ut omnis vestrae serenitatis sermo ad illos specialiter ex Apostolicarum auctoritate literarum dirigatur, quorum primum causa ad haec quaerenda estis excitati, & quicquid reprehensione in utrisque partibus dignum cognoscitur, ad illorum personam potius referatur, qui liberè admoneri possunt, & quorum scandalum, si pro veritatis tecortum fuerit, faciliùs tolerari potest.
units.tr: But since there was a very great obstacle for you in this, namely that the party which ought to correct errors and to resist this superstition with its authority, itself not only resisted that superstition altogether but, with rash defence, strove to support it against the divine authority and the sayings of the holy Fathers, the Lord opened to you a door according to your desired wish, so that by that authority the freedom to seek the truth together with your own men in so great a matter might be granted to you. Thus, since there was in you the will to consult and lacked the authority to inquire, you might seek the truth by the authority of those whose authority seemed to have turned aside from the truth itself, so that, as your holy desire and watchful zeal brought the truth to light, and as it showed itself openly, even that authority, willing or unwilling, might yield to the truth and give way. But since the salvation of the brethren is not to be neglected, and an eminent authority is not easily to be reproved, it seemed good to our humble selves that the whole discourse of your serenity should be directed specially, by the authority of apostolic letters, to those by whom you were first stirred to seek these things, and that whatever is recognised as deserving rebuke on either side should be referred rather to the persons of those who can be admonished freely, and whose scandal, if it arises for the sake of truth, can more easily be tolerated.

units.la: Credimus itaque, quod illos reprehendendo, illisque compatiendo, istos vero demulcendo, laudando & praeferendo, eorumque auctoritatem magnis laudum praeconiis efferendo, & sanctae Romanae ecclesiae condignam laudem deferendo, veritatem tamen ex testimoniis sanctarum scripturarum & sententiis sanctorum patrum in medium proferendo, & veraciter sobrieque exponendo, potent vestra sanctissima devotio, sicut optat, utrisque consulere. Sic quippe refragatur vinculis veritatis modò blandiendo, modò honorando, modò secundùm rationem veritatem demonstrando subtiliter adstrictus, non audebit aliter docere, quàm quod veritas habet, nec poterit aliter tenere, quàm quod veritas habet, nec poterit aliter tentare quàm ф veritatis documenro aliis tenendum tradiderit.
units.tr: We believe, therefore, that by rebuking those men, and showing compassion to them, but by soothing, praising and favouring those others, and by extolling their authority with great praises, and paying the fitting honour due to the holy Roman Church, yet by bringing forward the truth from the testimonies of the holy Scriptures and the sentences of the holy Fathers, and by expounding it truthfully and soberly, your most holy devotion may, as it desires, be able to consult both parties. For he who resists the bonds of truth, now by flattering, now by honouring, now by demonstrating the truth reasonably and subtly, being bound fast, will not dare to teach otherwise than truth has, nor will he be able to hold otherwise than truth has, nor will he be able to attempt otherwise than as the teaching of truth has handed down to be held by others.

units.la: Tali nempe modo visum est nostrae mediocritati, ut utriusque partis saluti commodissimè prodesse, magnamque vobis à Domino remunerationem hujus rei gratia praeparare potestis. Credimus sane, quia quanquam aliqua ex parte superstitiosam sibi consuetudinem forte vindicare velint, nullatenus tamen ab eadem Sede aliter quàm auctoritas & veritas se habet, mandare in aliquam partem praesumet. Verebitur siquidem, potestatem vestram, auctoritatem Sedis, & testimonia veritatis. Cùm igitur à vestra sancta devotione ita peracta fuerint, licet, quod non optamus, in aliquo aut isti aut illi deviare voluerint, & vestram salubertimam admonitionem, quae tota ex auctoritate veritatis profertur, audire contemserint, non minor ob id vobis à Domino recompensatio fiet, quia totum secundum verba beati Heliae Prophetae, quod vestrum fuit facere studuistis.
units.tr: In such a manner it has seemed good to our modest selves that you may most conveniently serve the salvation of each party, and prepare for yourselves a great reward from the Lord for this matter. We indeed believe that, although they may perhaps wish to defend some superstitious custom on their part, they will in no way presume to send anything to any party otherwise than as the authority and truth of the same See stand. For he will fear your power, the authority of the See, and the testimonies of truth. Therefore, when these things have been carried out by your holy devotion, even if, which we do not wish, either one or the other should choose to deviate in any respect, and should disdain to hear your most salutary admonition, which is wholly drawn from the authority of truth, no less recompense will be made to you by the Lord on that account, since you have striven to do, in everything, according to the words of the blessed prophet Elijah: "What was yours to do, you have endeavoured to do."

units.la: Nos denique servi vestri, sicut superiùs praemissum est, in unum convenientes, & de nobis injunctis pro captu intelligentiae nostrae familiariter conferentes, testimonia ex auctoritate divina & sententias sanctorum patrum, quas prout temporis angustia permisit, collegimus, & coram nobis legi fecimus, & quicquid in his de negotio, de quo agitur, necessarium aprumq; judicavimus, & in unum congetere studuimus, vestraque imperiali potentiae per venerabiles viros Halitgarium & Amalarium dirigere praesumsimus, ut videlicet vestra à Deo vobis collata sapientia ex his eligat, quicquid necessarium dignumq; ad idem negotium pertinens judicaverit. Obsecramus itaq; humiliter abundantissimam pietatem vestram, ut non nobis adscribatur, quicquid ibi minus aut indecens, aut inventum fuerit. Verè enim fatemur, quia angustia temporis praepediente, nec quanta voluimus, nec quanta potuimus, collegimus: sed tantùm vestris sacris justionibus, ut decet & oportet, totis nitibus parere cupientes, quae parvo in tempore ad manus nobis occurrere potuerunt, breviatim collegimus, & huic operi usque ad vestram sagacissimam examinationem inseruimus. Nam quidam nostrorum de longe venientes non habuerunt spatium temporis quaerendi: quidam verò nec causam, pro qua ad hunc conventum venire justi sunt, donec pervenerunt veraciter nosse potuerunt. Modum namq; infirmitate, in qua diutissimè laborat, detentus venire nequivit. Scit itaque plenissimè excellentia vestra; quia illud, quod per omnes catholicorum libros in-ri necessitas urget, prolixi temporis spatio ad legendum indiget. Nam si sufficiens spatium temnobis tributum fuisset, tanta domino opitulante poteramus colligere, quæ huic operi copiorant abundare. Tamen in his, quæ collecta sunt, summam hujus negotii, de quo agitur, com-prehensam esse juxta auctoritatem divinam & sanctorum patrum sententias arbitramur, sci-licet, ut unusquisque fidelis ea perlegens animadvertere queat, quòd imagines sanctorum præsumptione non sunt confringendæ, & ad injuriam sanctorum abolendæ, & penitus dispiciennec assertione superstitiosa colendæ aut adorandæ, sed potius hujusmodi superstitione remjuxta veram religionem memoriæ & amoris causa, ob recordationem eorum, quorum imagines pingendæ, sicut à beatissimo Gregorio satis catholicè perspicuèque dictum declaratur.
units.tr: We, your servants, as was set out above, have met together and conferred familiarly about the matters enjoined upon us, according to the measure of our understanding. We have gathered the testimonies from divine authority and the sayings of the holy Fathers, as the shortness of time allowed, and have had them read before us. Whatever we judged necessary and fitting concerning the business at hand, we have striven to bring together, and we have presumed to send it to your imperial power through the venerable men Halitgar and Amalarius, so that your wisdom, given you by God, may choose from these whatever it judges necessary, worthy and pertinent to this matter. We therefore humbly beseech your most abundant piety that whatever is found there lacking or unfitting not be imputed to us. For we truly confess that, the shortness of time being an obstacle, we have collected neither as much as we wished nor as much as we could. Yet, desiring to obey your holy commands with all our effort, as is right and proper, we have briefly gathered what could come to hand in a short time, and inserted it into this work for your most discerning examination. For some of our number came from far away and had no time to seek anything, and some could not truly learn the cause for which they were bound to come to this assembly until they arrived. One man, detained by an illness in which he has long laboured, was unable to come at all. Your excellency therefore knows full well that what the need of this matter requires to be searched through all the books of the Catholics needs a long span of time for reading. For if sufficient time had been granted us, with the Lord's help we could have gathered much more, which would abundantly enrich this work. Nevertheless, in what has been collected, we judge that the sum of the matter under discussion is comprehended in accordance with divine authority and the sentences of the holy Fathers: namely, that each faithful reader, reading these through, may perceive that the images of the saints are not to be presumptuously broken and destroyed to the injury of the saints, nor utterly despised, nor honoured or worshipped with superstitious assertion; but rather, with such superstition removed, they are to be painted according to true religion, for the sake of memory and love, to recall those whose images they are, as the most blessed Gregory has declared, saying it sufficiently, catholically and clearly.

units.la: Quia igitur nos his, qui in sacra sede beati Petri Apostoli residentibus, dignam honoris reverentiamre tribuendam non dubitamus, & illorum ergo imagines superstitiosam venerationem quidam omnes verò aliorum relatu cognoscimus, voluimus primum contra illos sententias ponere, quæ imagines præsumptiosè temeritate confringere præsumserunt, quatenus inde isti animati aliorumta valentius vobiscum corrigerent, & ad suam superstitionem cognoscendam veritatis testimo-cipienda animum facilius flecterent. Sicut igitur nobis videtur, & superiùs præmisimus, apertæ vestræ correctionis contra illos usquequaque dirigi potest, à quibus vobis illa epistola, quam misimus, directa esse cognoscitur. quoniam ejus textu utramque partem reprehensione dignam defravit, & illam scilicet, quæ indebito ac superstitioso cultu imagines venerabatur, & illam, quæfenoribus locis easdem imagines evertere ac delere præcepit. Et ideò credimus, quanquam cæteræ secundum auctoritatem veritatis, sicut in suis scriptis continetur, idem Imperator fecerit, proptertamen factum quosdam illarum partium infirmos scandalizâsse, nec non quosdam nostræ urbis manæ perturbâsse.
units.tr: Since, therefore, we do not doubt that due reverence and honour is to be rendered to those who sit in the holy see of the blessed Apostle Peter, and since we know that some pay superstitious veneration to their images, while all of us know this from the report of others, we wished first to set out against those who rashly presumed to break the images the sentences that would be most effective, so that, being admonished by them, these men might the more readily be moved to recognise their superstition and to receive the testimonies of truth with a willing mind. As it seems to us, and as we have said above, your open correction can be directed everywhere against those from whom it is known that the letter we sent you was addressed, since in its text it condemns both parties as deserving reproof: both the one which venerated images with undue and superstitious worship, and the one which ordered the images to be overthrown and destroyed in several places. We therefore believe that, although the same Emperor acted otherwise in accordance with the authority of truth, as is contained in his writings, nevertheless the deed scandalised some of the weak in those regions and also disturbed the minds of some in our city.

units.la: · Ad exaltationem & pacem sanctæ suæ ecclesiæ humilimam Deoque amabilem, ac Christianæ religioni necessariam Dominationem serenitatis vestræ Dominus Jesus Christus incolumem de-sinæ pietatis tueri, ac felici protectione per immensum conservare, & post hujus vitæ cursum suicivibus consortem dignetur efficere.
units.tr: May the Lord Jesus Christ, for the exaltation and peace of his holy Church, which is humble and pleasing to God and necessary to the Christian religion, keep safe the serene dominion of your majesty, guard it with his devoted protection, preserve it through immense time by his happy shelter, and after the course of this life deign to make it a fellow citizen of his own.

units.la: CAPUT PRIMUM.
units.tr: CHAPTER I.

units.la: CONGRUUM NECESSARIUMVE JUDICAVIMUS PRIMUM SENTENTIAS SAN- CTORUM PATRUM COLLIGERE CONTRA EOS QUI IMAGINES NON SOLUM A BÆDIBUS SED ETIAM A SACRIS VASIS INDISCRETE ABOLERE PRÆSUMUNT. Ex libro Eusebii Ecclesiasticæ historiæ VII. Cap. XV.
units.tr: WE HAVE THOUGHT IT FITTING AND NECESSARY FIRST TO GATHER THE SENTENCES OF THE HOLY FATHERS AGAINST THOSE WHO PRESUME TO REMOVE IMAGES INDISCRIMINATELY, NOT ONLY FROM THE WALLS BUT ALSO FROM THE SACRED VESSELS. From the book of Eusebius, Ecclesiastical History, Book VII, chapter 15.

units.la: VERUM quia urbis hujus fecimus mentionem, justum videtur commemorare etiam illud in ea gestum historia dignum duximus, mulierem quam sanguinis profluvio laborantem à Salvatore curatam Evangelii tradiderunt, hujus urbis civem constat fuisse, domusque ejus in ea etiam nunc ostenditur. Pro foribus domus ipsius basis quædam in loco editiore collocata monstratur, in qua mulieris ipsius velut genibus provoluta, quæ simpliciter tendentis imago ære videtur expressa. Adstat vero alia ære nihilominus fusa statua habitu virili amicta circumdata, & dexteram mulieri porrigens. hujus ad pedem statuæ, e basi herba quædam nova ipsi nequa cum exorta fuerit, excrescere usque ad stolæ illius ærei indumenti fimbriam solet, quam cum summo tactu herba contigerit, vires inde ad depellendos omnes morbos languoresque conquirit, ita ut quacumque illa firmitas corporis hanc lu exiguo madefacti salutaris graminis depellatur, nihil omnino virium gerens, si -ærea fimbria summitatem crescendo contigerit decerpatur. Hanc statuam ad similitudinem vultus Jesus fortam tradebant, quæ permansit ad nostra usque tempora, sicut ipsi oculis nostris inspeximus, & nihil mirum si ex gentibus crediderunt, pro beneficiis quæ à Salvatore fuerant consecuti, hujusmodi velut munus videbantur. Cum videamus etiam nunc & Apostolorum Petri & Pauli vel ipsius Salvatoris imagines designari, tabulisque di-gi, sed & antiquas ipsorum imagines à quibusdam conservatas nos vidimus. Quod mihi videtur ex gentilis con-suetudine indifferenter observatum, quod ita soleant honorare quos honore dignos duxerunt. insignia etenim veterum referri ad posterorum memoriam, illorum honoris, horum vero amoris indicium est.
units.tr: BUT since we have mentioned this city, we think it right to record also a deed done there which is worth telling. The woman who, as the Gospels relate, was healed by the Saviour of a flow of blood was a citizen of this city, and her house is still shown there. In front of the doors of her house stands a base set on a rather high place, on which is shown a statue of the woman kneeling, as if prostrate, and it appears to be cast in bronze, in the posture of one stretching out her hands. Opposite her stands another bronze statue of a man in a cloak, reaching out his right hand to the woman. At the foot of this statue there grows a certain strange herb, which rises up to the fringe of the bronze garment that covers the statue. It is said to have the power to drive out all diseases and weaknesses, so that whatever illness it is that afflicts the body is driven away by a small amount of this healing herb moistened with water. But if the herb grows up and touches the bronze fringe, it is plucked, having no power at all. They used to say that this statue was made in the likeness of Jesus, and it has remained to our own time, as we ourselves have seen with our own eyes. It is no wonder that people of the Gentiles, who had received benefits from the Saviour, believed that such a thing was a gift. We see even now that images of the Apostles Peter and Paul, and of the Saviour himself, are painted and kept on panels, and we have seen old images of them preserved by some people. This, it seems to me, has been done in imitation of the custom of the Gentiles, who in that way honour those whom they judged worthy of honour. For the likenesses of the men of old, set up to keep their memory among posterity, are a mark of honour for the former and of love for the latter.

units.la: In Actibus Sylvestri Papæ leguntur.
units.tr: Read in the Acts of Pope Sylvester.

units.la: APPARUISSE Constantino Imperatori in visione Apostoli Sanctus Petrus & Paulus ciquenta dixisse: Ni-am flagitius tuus posuisti terminum & effusionem innocentium sanguinis horruisti, misi sumus à Christorum domino, dare tibi sanitatis recuperandæ consilium. Audi ergo monita nostra, & fac quæcumque jucansus tibi. Sylvester Episcopus civitatis Romanæ ad montem Syrapti persecutiones tuas fugiens, in cavernis pecum suis clericis latebram fovet. Hunc cum ad te adduxeris, ille tibi pietatis piscinam ostendet, in quam dum te immersefis, omnis te valetudo ista deseret lepræ. quod dum factum fuerit, hanc vicissitudinem tuo Salvatori comomnes jussu tuo per totum orbem Romanum Ecclesiæ restaurantur, tu autem in hac parte purifica te, ut relictatione idolorum, Dominum unum, qui solus & verus est, adores & excolas, & ad ejus voluntatem attingas. Esitaque à somno, statim convocat eos qui observabant palatium & secundum tenorem somni sui, misit ad montem rapti, ubi sanctus Sylvester in cujusdam Christiani agrum persecutionis causa cum suis clericis receptus lectionibus & orationibus insistebat. Acubi a militibus se conventum vidit, credidit se ad martyrium coronam vocari. Et ad [illegible, ~60 letters] Profectio Dei ... [illegible, ~80 letters] [illegible, ~70 letters] [illegible, ~90 letters] [illegible, ~80 letters] [illegible, ~60 letters]
units.tr: In a vision, the holy Apostles Peter and Paul appeared to the Emperor Constantine and said: "Because you have set a limit to your cruelty and have shrunk from the shedding of innocent blood, we have been sent by the Lord of Christians to give you counsel for recovering your health. Listen therefore to our warnings and do whatever we tell you. Sylvester, bishop of the city of Rome, fleeing your persecutions, is hiding in the caves of Mount Soracte with his clergy. When you have brought him to yourself, he will show you a pool of piety, in which, when you have been immersed, all this leprosy of yours will leave you." When this had been done, by your command the churches of the whole Roman world are to be restored to their former state, and you yourself are to be purified in this respect, so that, abandoning idols, you may worship and honour the one Lord, who alone is true, and attain to his will." Constantine, waking from sleep at once, summoned those who kept watch over the palace, and according to the tenor of his dream sent them to Mount Soracte, where holy Sylvester, received on the field of a certain Christian because of the persecution, was devoting himself to reading and prayer with his clergy. And when he saw himself surrounded by soldiers, he believed that he was being called to the crown of martyrdom. [The rest of this passage is illegible in the scan: the Profectio Dei ... (remaining text unreadable).]
