units.la: Isidori ex libr. Etymologiarum:
units.tr: Isidore, from the book of Etymologies:

units.la: Pictura autem est imago exprimens speciem rei alicujus, quae dum visa fuerit, ad recordationem mentem reducit. Pictura autem dicta quasi fictura. Est enim imago ficta, non veritas, hinc & fucata, id est, quodam fuco inlita, nihil fidei & veritatis habens. Unde & sunt quaedam picturae, quae corpora veritatis studio coloris excedunt, & fidem dum augere conantur, ad mendacium provocant.
units.tr: A picture is an image expressing the appearance of some thing, which, when it has been seen, brings the thing back to the memory. It is called a picture (pictura) as if it were a fiction (fictura). For it is a made image, not the truth; hence also it is "painted over" (fucata), that is, smeared with a certain dye, having nothing of faith or truth. Hence there are some pictures which, through their eagerness for colour, go beyond the truth of bodies, and while they try to increase belief, they provoke to falsehood.

units.la: Item ipse post pauca:
units.tr: Likewise he himself, a little later:

units.la: Picturam autem Aegyptii excogitaverunt, primum umbram hominis lineis circumductam, itaque initio talis, singulis coloribus, postea diversis, sicque paulatim sese ars ipsa distendit, & invenit lumen atque umbras differentes colorum, &c.
units.tr: The Egyptians invented painting: first they drew the outline of a man's shadow with lines; at first it was of this kind, with single colours, later with various colours; and so gradually the art itself expanded and discovered light and shades of differing colours, etc.

units.la: Item Hieronymus in expositione Ezechiel. Prophetae:
units.tr: Likewise Jerome in the exposition of the prophet Ezekiel:

units.la: Et septuaginta viri de senioribus domus Israel & Jechonias filius Saphan stabat in medio eorum stantium ante eos, & unusquisque habebat thuribulum in manu sua, & vapor nebulae de thure consurgebat. Quando dicit seniores viros fuisse de senioribus domus Israel, qui tenebant thuribula manibus, ostendit multos & alios fuisse proinde qui haec in facie bant, sed forsitan peccatu aliis tenebantur, unumque nomen Jechoniam filium Saphan sterilisse in medio eorum quasi principem sceleris eorum atque sacrilegii, qui omissa religione Dei colebant idola, & in templo non adorabant Deum, cujus erat templum, sed picturas parietum.
units.tr: "And seventy men of the elders of the house of Israel, and Jechonias the son of Saphan, stood in the midst of them, standing before them, and each one had a censer in his hand, and the vapour of the cloud of incense rose up." When he says that these were seventy men of the elders of the house of Israel who held censers in their hands, he shows that there were many others too who were doing these things in secret, but perhaps were held by other sins; and that one name, Jechonias the son of Saphan, stood in the midst of them as the leader of their wickedness and sacrilege, who, having abandoned the worship of God, worshipped idols, and in the temple did not adore God, whose temple it was, but the pictures on the walls.

units.la: Firmianus Lactantius in libr. 1. de falsa religione, inter caetera inquit:
units.tr: Firmianus Lactantius, in the first book of On False Religion, among other things, says:

units.la: Illa quae sunt extra hominem, quid opus est ea colere quibus careas? Virtus enim colenda est, non imago virtutis, & colenda ipsa est, non sacrificio aliquo, aut thure, aut precatione solenni, sed voluntate sola atque proposito. Nam religio ac veritas nulla alia nisi unius Dei tenenda est. Quid igitur opus est, o vir sapientissime, tantos suntus vel fingendis vel colendis imaginibus impendere: firmius & incorruptius templum est pectus humanum: hoc potius ornetur: hoc verum illis imbuis implearetur. Haec enim falsas consecrationes sequitur quod necesse est, qui enim sic virtutes colunt, id est, quos ipsas & imagines virtutum consectantur, ea ipsa, quae vera sunt, tenere non possunt, &c caetera.
units.tr: Why is there any need to worship those things which are outside man, and which you lack? Virtue is to be worshipped, not the image of virtue; and it is to be worshipped not with some sacrifice, or incense, or solemn prayer, but with the will and purpose alone. For religion and truth are to be held in no other way than through the one God. What need is there, O most wise man, to spend so much money either on making or on worshipping images? The human breast is a firmer and more incorruptible temple: let this be adorned; let this be filled with true things. For what follows false consecrations is necessary: those who worship virtues in this way, that is, who pursue the very images of virtues, cannot hold those things which are true, etc., and the rest.

units.la: Augustin. in libr. Quaestion. veteris & novi testamenti:
units.tr: Augustine, in the book of Questions on the Old and New Testament:

units.la: Christiani, utpote pauperes, quos stultos vocant, unum Deum colunt in mysterio, ex quo sunt omnia: nec aliquod ab eo conditum est, venerantur. Ipsum enim solum sufficere sibi & abundare sciunt ad salutem.
units.tr: Christians, as poor men, whom they call foolish, worship in mystery the one God from whom all things are, and they do not venerate anything created by him. For they know that he alone is sufficient for himself and abundant for salvation.

units.la: Item idem post pauca:
units.tr: Likewise the same, a little later:

units.la: Non ergo nobis videtur, ut quod homo fecit, adorari debeat. Factor enim a factura, non factura a factore adoranda judicatur.
units.tr: It does not seem right to us, then, that what man has made should be adored. For the maker is judged to be worthy of adoration rather than the thing made by the maker.

units.la: Item Firmiani Lactantii de falsa religione libr. 2.
units.tr: Likewise Lactantius, On False Religion, book 2:

units.la: Duplici ergo ratione peccatur ab insipientibus, primum, quod elementa, id est, Dei opera Deo praeferunt. Deinde quod elementorum ipsorum figuras humana specie comprehensas colunt.
units.tr: Therefore the unwise sin in a twofold way: first, because they put the elements, that is, the works of God, before God; then, because they worship the figures of the elements themselves, shaped in human form.

units.la: Item ipse in eodem libro:
units.tr: Likewise he himself in the same book:

units.la: Nihil aliud adoremus, nihil colamus, nisi solius artificis, parentisque nostri unicum nomen.
units.tr: Let us adore nothing else, let us worship nothing, except the one name of the Maker and our Parent alone.

units.la: Item ipse in eodem libro:
units.tr: Likewise he himself in the same book:

units.la: Supra ergo non infra est Deus, nec in ima potius, sed in summa religione, quae credenda est.
units.tr: God is therefore above, not below, nor in the lowest but in the highest religion, which is to be believed.

units.la: Et infra:
units.tr: And below:

units.la: Non potest esse coelestis in eare, quae fit ex terra. Quicquid enim simulatur, falsum esse necesse est, nec potest unquam accipere, quod veritatem fuco & imitatione mentitur.
units.tr: What is made of earth cannot be heavenly. For whatever is counterfeited must necessarily be false, and what lies in the guise of truth through dye and imitation can never receive the truth.

units.la: Idem ipse eodem libro:
units.tr: The same himself, in the same book:

units.la: Ulligas nihil coleudum esse, quod oculis mortalibus cernitur.
units.tr: Understand that nothing is to be worshipped which is seen by mortal eyes.

units.la: Augustin in psalm. 113.
units.tr: Augustine on Psalm 113:

units.la: Nolli ergo addiris manus hominum, ut ex eo metallo quod fecit verus Deus, velis facere falsum Deum, imo salsum, quem pro vero venerari Deo, quem quisquis pro vero homine in auxilium reciperet, insanuiret. Ducit enim quodam infirmo rapit infirma corda mortalium formae similitudo & membrorum imitata compago.
units.tr: Do not, therefore, let the hands of men be applied, so that you wish to make from that metal which the true God made a false god, or rather a counterfeit one, which whoever received as a true man for help would be out of his mind to worship as the true God. For the likeness of a form and the imitated structure of limbs attracts and captures the weak hearts of mortals with a certain feebleness.

units.la: Fulgentius in libr. de fide ad Donatum:
units.tr: Fulgentius in the book On Faith, to Donatus:

units.la: Quia ipse Deus sibi soli praecipiens tantum modo serviendum, seque jubens a fidelibus adorandum, prorsus interdicit ne audeat creaturam adorare, creatoris atque servire. Propterea in fine primi illius praecepti de omnibus, quae create loquitur; non adorabis ea, nec servies eis.
units.tr: Because God himself, commanding that he alone be served and bidding himself be adored by the faithful, utterly forbids anyone to dare to adore or serve a creature instead of the Creator. Therefore, at the end of that first precept, speaking of all things that are created, he says: "You shall not adore them, nor serve them."

units.la: Et post pauca:
units.tr: And after a few words:

units.la: Vera enim religio in unius consilut Dei servitio.
units.tr: For true religion lies in the service of the one God's will.
Exod. 20.

units.la: Item ipse post pauca:
units.tr: Again, the same author, after a few words:

units.la: Sic veraciter unum Deum cum patre filium vera fide adorat, quae sic Deo novit a creaturis omnibus serviendum, ut noverit creaturae non debere divinae servitutis obsequium.
units.tr: Thus truly, with true faith, he adores the one God together with the Father and the Son, who knows that God is to be served by all creatures in such a way that he knows creatures ought not to be given the obedience of divine service.

units.la: Augustinus in epistola ad Maximum Grammaticum:
units.tr: Augustine in the letter to Maximus the Grammarian:

units.la: Sces a Christianis catholicis, quorum in vestro oppido etiam Ecclesia constituta est, nullum coli mortuorum, nihil denique adorari, quod sit factum et conditum a Deo, sed unum ipsum Deum qui fecit et condidit omnia.
units.tr: You know that among Catholic Christians, whose Church is established even in your town, no dead are worshipped, and nothing at all is adored that was made and created by God, but only the one God who made and created all things.

units.la: Item Augustinus in libro de Quantitate animae:
units.tr: Again, Augustine in the book On the Greatness of the Soul:

units.la: Deus autem immortalem animam fecit, ut opinor, nisi forte tibi aliter videtur. Ergo tu velles talia fieri dixerim, sed quemadmodum ipse immortalis immortale quiddam fecit ad similitudinem suam, sic et non immortales facti a Deo, ad similitudinem nostram quod facimus immortale esse deberet. Recte duceres, si ad ejus imaginem pingeres tabulam, quod in te immortale esse credis: nunc vero in ea exprimis similitudinem corporis, quod profecto mortale est. Quomodo ergo sumus similes Deo cum immortalitatis nulla possum facere ut ille? quomodo nec imago corporis potest hoc valere, quod tuum corpus valet, sic anima non mirandum est, si potentiam tantam non habet, quantam ille ad cujus similitudinem facta est, etc.
units.tr: God, I suppose, made the soul immortal, unless perhaps it seems otherwise to you. So I would say that you wish such things to be made. But just as the immortal God made something immortal in his own likeness, so we, who were made by God and are not immortal, ought to make what we make immortal, in our likeness. You would be right to paint a picture in his image of what you believe to be immortal in you; but now you express in it the likeness of the body, which is certainly mortal. How then are we like God, when I can make nothing immortal as he does? Just as the image of the body cannot have the power that your body has, so it is no wonder if the soul does not have as great a power as he to whose likeness it was made, etc.

units.la: Si enim imago humani corporis nectantum valere asseritur, quantum veraciter ipsum corpus valere perhibetur, qua causa tibi sufragari posse putant nonnulli reprehensione digni, qui in illa Synodo Graecorum mediationem imaginum, tibi necessariam esse dicere praesumserunt?
units.tr: For if the image of the human body is not claimed to be worth as much as the body itself is truly said to be worth, what reason do some men, deserving of reproach, have for thinking they can support you, those who presumed to say in that Synod of the Greeks that the mediation of images was necessary for you?

units.la: August. lib.8. de civitate Dei:
units.tr: Augustine, On the City of God, book 8:

units.la: Quapropter merito homo deficit ab illo qui eum fecit, cum sibi praeficit ipse quod fecit. Demonstrat enim idem Ermes, quod homines mortui divino colebantur honore, velut Aesculapius atque Mercurius, quem suum esse dicit avum, et reliqui. Hac enim occasione accepta, daemones ut intercessores exsisterent apud bonos Deos, quos nos Angelos sanctos aut Archangelos, vel Potestates dicimus, ta i enim ratione, nubilo velamine sapientes gentilium sua mumima obtexere nitebantur.
units.tr: Therefore man rightly falls away from him who made him, when he sets over himself what he himself made. For the same Hermes shows that dead men were worshipped with divine honour, like Aesculapius and Mercury, whom he says was his grandfather, and the rest. For by this occasion being seized, demons came to be intercessors with the good gods, whom we call holy angels, or archangels, or powers. For by this reasoning they strove to cover the wise of the Gentiles with their own falsehoods under a cloudy veil.

units.la: Ambrosius in expositione epist. ad Romanos:
units.tr: Ambrose in his exposition of the Epistle to the Romans:

units.la: Numquid tam demens est aliquis, aut salutis sua immemor, ut honorificentiam Regis vindicet Comiti, cum de hac re, si qui etiam tractare fuerint inventi, jure ut rei damnantur majestatis, et ipsi se non cogitant reos, qui honorem nominis Dei deferunt creaturae, et relicto domino conservos adorant, quasi fit aliquid quod plus referret domino. Nam ideo ad Regem per Tribunos aut Comites itur, quia homo utique est Rex, et nesciat quibus debeat rempublicam credere. Ad Deum autem promerendum, quem nihil utique latet, omnium enim merita novit, suffragatione non est opus, sed mente devota.
units.tr: Is anyone so foolish, or so forgetful of his own salvation, as to claim for a count the honour due to the king? In this matter, if any were found to treat it, they are rightly condemned as guilty of treason; and yet they do not consider themselves guilty who transfer the honour of God's name to a creature, and, leaving the Lord, adore their fellow servants, as if there were something that would bring more to the Lord. For one goes to the king through tribunes or counts because man is indeed king, and does not know to whom he should entrust the commonwealth. But to win over God, from whom nothing is hidden, for he knows the merits of all, there is no need of intercession, but of a devout mind.

units.la: Item Augustinus in libro de Vera religione, inter caetera dicit:
units.tr: Again, Augustine in the book On True Religion, among other things, says:

units.la: Ad percipiendam veritatem nihil magis impedire quam vitam hebdinibus deditam et falsas imagines rerum sensibilium, quae nobis ab hoc sensibili mundo per corpus impressae, varias opiniones errorésque generant. Nec errorem ullum in religione esse potuisse, si anima pro Deo suo non coleret animam aut corpus, aut phantasmata sua, quae nihil sunt aliud, quam de specie corporis corporeo sensu attracta figmenta.
units.tr: Nothing hinders the perception of truth more than a life given over to pleasures and false images of sensible things, which, impressed upon us from this sensible world through the body, generate various opinions and errors. Nor could any error in religion have arisen if the soul did not worship as its God a soul, or a body, or its own phantasms, which are nothing other than figments drawn from the appearance of a body by bodily sense.

units.la: Item in eodem:
units.tr: Again in the same work:

units.la: Non sit nobis religio humanorum operum cultus. Meliores enim sunt ipsi artifices, qui talia fabricant, quos tamen colere non debemus. Non sit nobis religio in phantasmatibus nostris. Melius enim qualemcunque virum, quam omne quicquid pro arbitrio fingi potest, et tamen animam ipsam, quamvis anima vera sit, cum falsa imaginatur, colere non debemus. Melior est vera stipula, quam lux mea cogitatione pro suspicantis voluntate formata, et tamen stipulam quam sentimus, et tangimus, dementis est credere colendam.
units.tr: Let the worship of human works not be our religion. For the craftsmen who fashion such things are better than them, and yet we ought not to worship them. Let our religion not rest in our phantasms. For any man whatever is better than whatever can be imagined at will; and yet we ought not to worship the soul itself, though it is a true soul, when we imagine it falsely. A true straw is better than my light formed in thought according to the wish of the one who imagines it; and yet it is madness to believe that the straw we perceive and touch is to be worshipped.

units.la: Item idem libro decimo de Civitat. Dei:
units.tr: Likewise, the same author, in the tenth book of the City of God:

units.la: Multa denique de cultu divino usurpata sunt, quae honoribus deferrentur humanis, sive humilitate nimia, sive adulatione pestifera, ita tamen ut quibus ea deferrentur, homines haberentur, qui decuntur colendi et venerandi; si autem eis multum addatur, adorandi. quis vero sacrificandum censuit, nisi ei quem Deum aut fecit, aut putavit, aut finxit.
units.tr: Many things, in fine, have been transferred from divine worship to human honours, whether through excessive humility or pernicious flattery, yet in such a way that those to whom these things were paid were regarded as men who ought to be honoured and revered; but if much more were added to them, they were to be worshipped. Who, indeed, has thought that sacrifice should be offered except to him whom he believed to be God, or whom he made, or whom he imagined?

units.la: Item August. in libr. Quaest. 84.
units.tr: Likewise Augustine, in the book of Questions, question 84.

units.la: Minoribus rebus intenta anima, quae per corpus corporaliter facit, minus inhaeret ipsi summae sapientiae, qui vero talia opera colunt, quantum deviaverint a veritate, hinc colligi potest, quia si ipsa animalium corpora colerent, quae multo excellentius fabricata sunt, et quorum sunt ea imitamenta, quid eis infelicius diceremus?
units.tr: The soul, occupied with lesser things, which through the body acts in a bodily way, clings less to the highest wisdom itself. How far those who worship such works have strayed from the truth can be inferred from this: if they were to worship the bodies of animals themselves, which were made far more excellently and of which those works are imitations, what could we call more unhappy than them?

units.la: CAPUT QUINTUM.
units.tr: CHAPTER V.

units.la: Qua ratione quave auctoritate imagines sanctorum adorandae sint, eisque, ut fertur, incensum ponendum, cum ipsi angeli vel sancti homines vivos se adorari noluerint.
units.tr: By what reasoning and what authority the images of the saints are to be adored, and incense is to be offered to them, as is said, when the angels themselves and holy men, while alive, did not want to be adored.

units.la: Unde beatus Augustinus in libr. 11. de Civitate Dei sic ait:
units.tr: Whence the blessed Augustine says in book 11 of The City of God:

units.la: Putaverunt quidem deferendum angelis honorem vel adorando, vel sacrificando, qui debetur Deo, & eorum sint ammonitione prohibiti, justiq; hoc ei deferre, cuius uni fas esse noverunt, imitati sunt angelos sanctos, & jam sancti homines Dei. Nam Paulus & Barnabas in Lycaonia facto quodam miraculo sanitatis, putati sunt Dii, eisq; Lycaonii victimas immolare voluerunt, quod à se humili pietate removentes, eum in quem crederent annuntiaverunt Deum.
units.tr: Indeed, men have thought that the honour due to God, whether of adoration or of sacrifice, should be paid to angels. Having been forbidden by their admonition, and rightly so, to render it to one whom they knew it was lawful to serve alone, they imitated the holy angels and the holy men of God. For when Paul and Barnabas in Lycaonia had performed a certain miracle of healing, they were taken for gods, and the Lycaonians wished to sacrifice victims to them. But they, removing this from themselves with humble piety, announced that the God in whom they believed was the one God.

units.la: Et post pauca:
units.tr: And a little later:

units.la: Quicunq; igitur mortalis potestas quantalibet virtute praedita, sinos diligit sicut seipsam ei vult esse subditos, ut beati simus, cui & ipsa subdita beata est. Si ergo non colit Deum, misera est, quia privatur Deo. Si autem colit Deum, non vult se coli pro Deo: illi enim potius divinae sententiae suffragatur, & delectioni viribus favet, quia scriptum est, sacrificans Diis, eradicabitur, nisi Domino soli. Nam ut alia nunc taceam, quae pertinent ad religionis obsequium, quo colitur Deus, sacrificium certe nullus hominum est, qui audeat dicere debere nisi Deo.
units.tr: Therefore, whatever mortal power, however endowed with virtue, loves us as itself and wishes us to be its subjects, so that we may be blessed, to whom it too is blessed in being subject. If then it does not worship God, it is wretched, because it is deprived of God. But if it worships God, it does not want to be worshipped in place of God. For it rather supports the divine sentence and favours the love of God with its strength, because it is written: "He who sacrifices to gods shall be utterly destroyed, unless to the Lord alone" (Exod. 22.). For, to pass over for now the other matters that belong to the service of religion by which God is worshipped, there is certainly no one of men who would dare to say that sacrifice is to be offered to anyone but God.

units.la: Item idem in Psalm. 96. inter caetera:
units.tr: Likewise the same, on Psalm 96, among other things:

units.la: Homines autem sanctos attendite, qui sunt similes angelis. cum invenieris hominem aliquem sanctum servum Dei, si voluerit illum colere & adorare pro Deo, prohibet te, non vult sibi arrogare honorem Dei, non vult tibi esse pro Deo, sed tecum esse sub Deo.
units.tr: But consider the holy men, who are like the angels. When you have found some holy man, a servant of God, if he should wish you to worship and adore him in place of God, he forbids you. He does not want to claim for himself the honour of God; he does not want to be in God's place for you, but to be with you under God.

units.la: Et post pauca:
units.tr: And a little later:

units.la: Sic & sancti angeli illius gloriam quaerunt quem diligunt, ad ejus cultum, ad ejus orationem, ad ejus contemplationem, omnes quos diligunt rapere & inflammare student, ipsum illi adnuntiant non se, quoniam angeli sunt, & quia mulites sunt, non noruut gloriam quaerere nisi Imperatoris sui.
units.tr: So too the holy angels seek the glory of him whom they love, and they strive to draw and inflame all whom they love to his worship, his prayer and his contemplation. They announce him to them, not themselves, since they are angels; and since they are soldiers, they know not how to seek glory except for their Emperor.

units.la: Item post pauca:
units.tr: Likewise, a little later:

units.la: Nemo dicat, Timeo ne irascatur mihi angelus si non illum colo pro Deo meo. Tunc tibi irascitur, quando ipsum colere volueris. bonus est cum, & Deum amat. quomodo daemones irascuntur si non colantur, sic angeli indignantur, si pro Deo colantur.
units.tr: Let no one say, "I fear that the angel will be angry with me if I do not worship him as my God." He is angry with you when you wish to worship him. He is good with you, and he loves God. As demons become angry if they are not worshipped, so angels are offended if they are worshipped as God.

units.la: Item libr. 10. de Civitate Dei:
units.tr: Likewise in book 10 of The City of God:

units.la: Non itaq; debemus metuere, ne in mortales & beatos uni Deo subditos, non eis sacrificando offendamus, quod enim non nisi uni vero Deo debere sciunt, cui & ipsi adhaerendo beati sunt, procul dubio neq; per ullam significantem figuram neq; per ipsam rem, quae sacramentis significatur, exhiberi sibi volunt. Daemonum est hac arrogantia, superborum miserorum, à quibus longe diversa est pietas subditorum Deo.
units.tr: Therefore we ought not to fear that we offend the mortal and blessed beings, who are subject to the one God, by not sacrificing to them, since they know that it is due only to the one true God, to whom they too are blessed by adhering. Without doubt they do not want to be offered anything either through any signifying figure or through the very thing which is signified by the sacraments. This arrogance belongs to demons, miserable proud spirits, from whom the piety of those subject to God is far different.

units.la: Nos autem martyribus nostris non templa sicut Diis, sed memorias sicut hominibus mortuis, quorum apud Deum spes fabricamus: nec ibi erigimus altaria, in quibus sacrificemus martyribus, sed unum Deo, & martyrum & nostro; ad quod sacrificium sicut homines Dei, qui mundum in ejus confessione vicerunt, suo loco, vice & ordine nominantur. Non tamen a sacerdote, qui sacrificat, invocantur; Deo quippe non ipsis sacrificat; quamvis in memoria sacrificet, quia Dei sacerdos est, & non illorum; ipsum vero sacrificium corpus est Christi, quod non offertur ipsis, quia hoc sunt & ipsi.
units.tr: But we do not build temples for our martyrs as for gods, but memorials as for dead men, whose hope we establish with God. Nor do we raise altars there on which we sacrifice to martyrs, but one sacrifice to God, of the martyrs and of ourselves; in which sacrifice the men of God, who conquered the world in its confession, are named in their own place, rank and order. Yet they are not invoked by the priest who sacrifices; for he does not sacrifice to them but to God, although he celebrates at their memorial, because he is the priest of God and not of them. The sacrifice itself is the body of Christ, which is not offered to them, because they themselves are this.

units.la: Item August. in sermone Evangelico, de potestate quam dedit daemoni- bus, ut abirent in porcos:
units.tr: Likewise Augustine in a gospel sermon, on the power that he gave to the demons to go into the swine:

units.la: Noli inclinari angelis, ut eis sacrificandum putes, nec bonus & sancti is nolunt enim, quando facis non te diligunt; diligunt autem si cum eis adores quem adorant.
units.tr: Do not bow yourself down to angels so that you think sacrifice should be offered to them; the good and holy ones do not want it. For when you do so, they do not love you; but they love you if you adore with them the one whom they adore.

units.la: Item idem in libro de Quantitate animae:
units.tr: Likewise the same, in the book On the Greatness of the Soul:

units.la: Homo autem quilibet alius quanquam sapientissimus & perfectissimus, vel profusus qualibet anima rationis compatiatissima est amanda tantummodo atq; unitanda est, eig; pro merito atq; ordine quod ei congruit deferendum. Nam Dominum Deum tuum adorabis, & illi soli servies.
units.tr: Any other man, however wise and most perfect, or however lavish with any rational soul, is to be loved and united with only as a fellow, and to him is to be rendered what is fitting according to his merit and rank. For "You shall worship the Lord your God, and serve him alone" (Matt. 4.).

units.la: Origenes in epist. ad Romanos:
units.tr: Origen in the epistle to the Romans:

units.la: Cum possent homines Deum aufugere ab ejus cultu declinantes ad imagines hominum adorandas, & animalium deverterunt. ut enim breviter & omni munium collecta definitione diximus, adorare alium praeter Patrem & Filium & Spiritum sanctum, impietatis est crimen.
units.tr: Although men could have fled from the worship of God, turning aside to adore the images of men, they have also turned to animals. For, as we have said briefly, with a definition gathered from all the rest, to adore anyone other than the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit is the crime of impiety.

units.la: Item August. in lib. de Vera relig:
units.tr: Likewise Augustine, in the book On True Religion:

units.la: Non sit ergo nobis religio cultus corporum aetheriorum atq; caelestium, sed ejus, cujus contemplatione beati sunt. Nam enim & nos videndo angelum beati simus, sed videndo veritatem, qua etiam ipsos diligimus angelos, nec inridemus quod ea parationes, & nullis molestiis interpellantibus perfruuntur, sed vagis eos diligemus, quoniam & nos tale aliquid sperare à communi Domino justi simus. quare honoramus eos caritate, non servitute, neccis templa constituimus. nolumus enim sic honorari à nobis, quia nos ipsos cum boni sumus templa summi Dei esse noverunt.
units.tr: Let our religion, then, not be the worship of the heavenly and celestial bodies, but of Him in contemplating whom they are blessed. For we too would be blessed by seeing an angel, but by seeing the truth, by which we also love the angels themselves; nor do we mock them because they enjoy those delights and are not disturbed by any troubles, but we love them as companions, since we too are just enough to hope for something of the same kind from the common Lord. Therefore we honour them with love, not with servitude, and we do not set up temples to them. For they do not wish to be honoured by us in that way, since they know that we too, when we are good, are the temples of the highest God.

units.la: Item ipse in libr. 8. de Civitate Dei:
units.tr: Likewise the same author, in the eighth book of The City of God:

units.la: Sane nec martyribus templa, sacerdotia, sacra & sacrificia constituimus, quoniam non ipsi, sed Deus eorum nobis est Deus, honoramus sane memorias eorum tanquam sanctorum hominum Dei, qui usque ad mortem corporum fuerant pro veritate certarunt, ut innotesceret vera religio, falsis fictisque convictis, quod etiamsi qui aut ita sunt timebant timendo reprimebant, quis autem audivit aliquando fidelium plantam sacerdotem ad altare, & jam. jam super sanctum corpus martyris ad Dei honorem cultumq; constructum dicere in precibus; Offero tibi sacrificium Petre vel Paule, vel Cypriane, cum apud eorum memorias offeratur Deo, qui eos & homines & martyres fecit, & sanctu suis angelis coelesti honore sociavit: ut ea celebritate & Deo vero de illorum victoriis gratias agamus, & nos ad rationem talium coronarum atq; palmarum eodem invocato in auxilium ex illorum memoria renovatione adhortemur. Quacunq; igitur adhibentur religiosorum obsequia in martyrum locis, ornamenta sunt memoriarum, non sacrificia mortuorum tanquam Deorum.
units.tr: Indeed we do not set up temples, priesthoods, sacred rites and sacrifices to the martyrs, since they are not our God, but God is their God as well as ours. We certainly honour the memories of them as holy men of God, who even unto death of the body fought for the truth, so that the true religion might become known, the false and feigned being refuted; although some who were such were afraid, and by fear restrained the fear of others. But who has ever heard of a faithful priest standing at the altar, and already over the holy body of a martyr built for the honour and worship of God, saying in his prayers: "I offer sacrifice to you, Peter, or Paul, or Cyprian"? For sacrifice is offered to God alone, who made them both men and martyrs, and who joined them to his holy angels in heavenly honour; so that with that solemnity we may give thanks to the true God for their victories, and be encouraged, by the remembrance of them, to seek such crowns and palms, invoking the same God for help. Therefore whatever services of religious people are performed in the places of the martyrs are ornaments of the memorials, not sacrifices to the dead as to gods.

units.la: Hieronymus ad Riparium presbyterum:
units.tr: Jerome to Riparius the presbyter:

units.la: Accepti primum literis tuis, non respondere superbia est, respondere temeritatis. De his enim rebus interrogasti, quae & proferre & audire sacrilegium est. Au Vigilantium, qui κατ' ἀντίφρασιν hoc vocatur nomine, nam Dormitantius rectius diceretur, os foetidum rursus aperire, & putorem spurcissimum contra sanctorum martyrum profanas reliquias, & nos, qui eas suscepimus, appellare cinerarios & ululatras, qui mortuorum hominum ossa veneramur. Infelicem hominem, & omni lacrymarum fonte plangendum, qui haec dicens non se intelligit esse Samaritani & Judaei, qui corpora mortuorum pro immundis habent, & etiam vasa quae in eadem domo ruerint pollui suspicantur. Sequentem occidentem literam, & non spiritum vivificantem. Nos autem non dico martyrum reliquias, sed ne Solem quidem & Lunam, non angelos, non archangelos, non Seraphim, non Cherubim, non omne nomen quod nominatur, & in praesenti saeculo, & in futuro colimus & adoramus, ne serviamus creaturae potius quam creatori, qui est benedictus in saecula. Honoramus autem reliquias martyrum, ut eum cujus sunt martyres adoremus: honoramus servos, ut honor servorum redundet ad dominum, quia qui vos suscipit, me suscipit.
units.tr: Having first received your letter, not to reply would be pride, to reply would be rashness. For you have asked about things which it is sacrilege even to mention or to hear. Shall I once more open my foul mouth against Vigilantius, who is called by a name that is the opposite of his nature (for he should rather be called Dormitantius, "the Sleeper"), and against the filthiest stench of his, to malign the holy relics of the martyrs, and to call us who receive them "ash-worshippers" and "howlers," who venerate the bones of dead men? Unhappy man, to be mourned with a fountain of tears, who in saying these things does not understand that he is like the Samaritans and Jews, who hold the bodies of the dead to be unclean and suspect that even the vessels which have fallen in the same house are polluted! He follows the letter that kills, and not the Spirit that gives life. But we do not, I say, worship and adore the relics of the martyrs alone; we do not worship the sun and moon, nor angels, nor archangels, nor Seraphim, nor Cherubim, nor any name that is named, in this age or in the age to come, lest we serve the creature rather than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. We honour the relics of the martyrs so that we may adore Him whose martyrs they are; we honour the servants so that the honour of the servants may redound to the Lord, since he who receives you receives me.

units.la: Idem ipse adversus Vigilantium:
units.tr: The same author against Vigilantius:

units.la: Quis enim, o insanum caput, aliquando martyres adoravit? quis hominem putavit Deum? nonne Paulus & Barnabas cum Lycaonibus Jupiter & Mercurius putarentur, & eis vellent hostias immolare, sciderunt vestimenta sua, & se homines esse dixerunt, non quo meliores non essent olim mortuis hominibus Jove atq; Mercurio, sed quod sub gratia errore honor eis Deo debitus deferretur, quod & de Petro legimus, qui Cornelium se adorare cupientem manu sublevavit & dixit; Surge, nam & ego homo sum.
units.tr: For who, you foolish head, ever worshipped the martyrs? Who thought a man to be God? Were not Paul and Barnabas, when they were taken for Jupiter and Mercury by the Lycaonians, and they wished to sacrifice victims to them, tearing their garments and saying that they were men? Not that the men Jove and Mercury of old were not better than others, but because under the appearance of grace the honour due to God would be paid to them in error. We read the same of Peter too, who, when Cornelius wished to worship him, raised him up with his hand and said: "Rise, for I too am a man."

units.la: Augustinus in lib.de Solutione quaestionum cap.3.
units.tr: Augustine, in the book On the Resolution of Questions, chapter 3:

units.la: Proinde sicut impia superbia sive hominum, sive daemonum, sibi hos divinos honores exhiberi vel iubet vel cupit, ita pia humilitas vel hominum vel Angelorum sanctorum, haec sibi oblata recusavit, & cui deberentur ostendit.
units.tr: Therefore, just as proud impiety, whether of men or of demons, either orders or desires these divine honours to be paid to itself, so holy humility, whether of men or of holy angels, has refused what was offered to itself and has shown to whom they are due.

units.la: In libr.19. De civit. Dei dicit Augustinus:
units.tr: Augustine says in the nineteenth book of The City of God:

units.la: Sed Deus ille, quem coluerunt sapientes Hebraeorum, & jam caelestibus sanctis angelis & virtutibus Dei, quos beatissimos tanquam cives in hac nostra peregrinatione mortali veneramur & amamus, sacrificari vetat & coli, interdicens in lege sua, sacrificans Dis eradicabitur.
units.tr: But that God whom the wise men of the Hebrews worshipped, and whom we, now that the holy angels and the powers of God are in heaven, whom we venerate and love as most blessed fellow citizens in this mortal pilgrimage of ours, forbids to be sacrificed to and worshipped, forbidding in his law: "He who sacrifices to gods shall be utterly destroyed."

units.la: CAPUT SEXTUM.
units.tr: CHAPTER SIX.

units.la: HÆC CONTRA EOS, QVI ANNORUM NUMERO SUPERSTITIONEM IMAGINIS VINDICARE VOLUNT, CONSUETUDINEM SEQUI CUPIUNT POTIUS, QUAM VERITATIS AUCTORITATEM.
units.tr: These things are said against those who wish to defend the superstition of images by the number of years, and who prefer to follow custom rather than the authority of truth.

units.la: Augustinus in libro Quaestion.veteris & novi Testamenti:
units.tr: Augustine, in the book Questions on the Old and New Testament:

units.la: Irrationabile, inquit, vulgus, aut apparentes umbras, aut daemonia, aut simulacra mortuorum, ut Deos colere coeperunt. quae res in consuetudine vetustatis deducta arbitratur rationis sibi veritatem posse defendi, cum veritatis non ex consuetudine atq; ex vetustate, sed ex Deo sit, quia non vetustate Deus probatur, sed aeternitate. quamobrem fides non capta res, sed sine inurio est. In Deum enim credere nostrum incipere est: nam quod creditur aeternum est.
units.tr: "The uneducated crowd," he says, "began to worship either apparent shadows, or demons, or images of the dead, as gods. This practice, carried on through the custom of antiquity, supposes that the truth of reason can be defended by it, whereas truth comes not from custom and antiquity but from God, since God is proved not by antiquity but by eternity. Therefore faith is not a thing grasped by reason but is without reproach. For to believe in God is for us to begin; for what is believed is eternal."

units.la: Et post pauca:
units.tr: And a little after:

units.la: Quod colunt Pagani post Deum est, opus post opificem est, pagani colunt opera, nos opificem, illi creaturam, non creatorem, factus homo coepit venerari suum conditorem, quia & dignum est, & causa hoc exegit.
units.tr: "What the pagans worship is after God: the work is after the maker. The pagans worship works, we the Maker; they worship the creature, not the Creator. Man, having been made, began to venerate his Creator, because this is both fitting and required by the cause."

units.la: Hieremias Propheta:
units.tr: The prophet Jeremiah:

units.la: Post Baalim, inquit, abierunt, quos didicerunt a patribus suis.
units.tr: "They went after the Baalim," he says, "which they had learned from their fathers."

units.la: Unde Hieronymus:
units.tr: Whence Jerome:

units.la: Ergo nec parentum, nec majorum error sequendus est, sed auctoritas scripturarum, & Dei docentis imperium.
units.tr: "Therefore neither the error of parents nor of ancestors is to be followed, but the authority of the Scriptures and the command of God who teaches."

units.la: August. in Psalm.113.
units.tr: Augustine, on Psalm 113.

units.la: Videntur autem sibi purgatorii esse religiosi, qui dicunt, nec simulacrum, nec daemonium colo, sed effigiem corporalem ejus rei signum intueor quam colere debeo.
units.tr: "Those who say, 'I do not worship the image nor the demon, but I look upon the bodily likeness, a sign of that thing which I ought to worship,' seem to themselves to be scrupulously religious."

units.la: Item post pauca:
units.tr: Likewise, a little after:

units.la: Audent respondere, non ipsa corpora colere, sed quae illis regendis praesident numina.
units.tr: "They dare to reply that they do not worship the bodies themselves, but the divinities who preside over the governing of them."

units.la: Si enim sunt praemissa sanctorum Patrum documenta declarant, sancti angeli & sancti viri non sunt colendi nec adorandi, hoc enim & ipsi refugiunt, sed sola caritate, non autem servitute honorandi, nec sanctis martyribus tum pla, [illegible, ~40 letters]
units.tr: "For if the teachings of the holy Fathers have been set forth, they declare that holy angels and holy men are not to be worshipped or adored; for they themselves also reject this, but are to be honoured with love alone, not with servitude, nor are the holy martyrs to be ... [illegible]"

units.tr: [illegible] choosing. Finally, as to what in these matters must be held for the salvation of the universal Church, we give counsel pleasing to God and confirm the same counsel. And although, as is fitting, divine authority surpasses all, yet first we wish, by reasoning, to satisfy everyone and to soften and unite minds tending in different directions, so that they may more easily and in harmony accept the divine authority according to the sound understanding of the Catholic faith, and then may more gladly embrace the counsel we have settled upon and keep it embraced in time to come.

units.la: Apud omnes igitur hujus sanctæ Occidentalis Ecclesiæ, quæ se auctoritate beatorum Apostolorum Petri & Pauli, largiente Domino fidei, spei, & charitatis sumsisse exordium gloriatur, ita hactenus per eosdem Apostolos protegente Spiritu sancto, & ipsis intercedentibus ac protegentibus, ab omni hæresi inlibata, nunc usque conservata est, ut non solum ipsa ad quodlibet erroris diverticulum declinaret, sed potius omnes à recto fidei tramite quoquo modo deviantes, per orthodoxos successores toto orbe terrarum ad rectitudinem potius revocaret. Testis enim hujus rei liber angulus, sed orbis terrarum universus, quia quotiens tales per mundum perceptiones sunt, quæ ad periculum fidei universalis Ecclesiæ imminere putabantur, ob inveniendam interque conservandam catholicæ fidei veritatem, semper hoc universalis Ecclesia, præsente ob hujus sanctitatem Sedis Pontifice, aut certe cum consensu illius verbis vel litteris protecto corrigere, correctumque ad conservandum statuere consuevit.
units.tr: Among all, then, of this holy Western Church, which glories that it took its beginning from the authority of the blessed Apostles Peter and Paul, the Lord granting faith, hope and charity, and the Holy Spirit protecting it through the same Apostles, and they interceding and protecting, it has been kept until now unstained by any heresy. So not only has it itself never turned aside into any byway of error, but it has rather, through its orthodox successors, called back to the right path all who in any way strayed from the straight road of the faith throughout the whole world. For the witness of this is not a corner of the earth but the whole world. Whenever such disputes have arisen throughout the world which seemed to threaten the peril of the universal Church's faith, the universal Church has always been accustomed, to find and preserve the truth of the Catholic faith, to correct them, with the Pope of this holy See presiding because of its sanctity, or at least with his consent, by word or letter, and, once corrected, to establish them for preservation.

units.la: Simili modo etiam & in his, quæ ad conservandum in humanis actibus ejusdem Ecclesiæ incontaminabilem statum, moderante non qualibet dolosa vel sophistica, nec non duplici calliditate, sed veritate subnixa, simplici ratione, ipsaque discretione, honestate, utilitate, pariter in radiata ratione, non solum noxia vel nociva, verum quoque & ipsa superflua & non necessaria resecare consuevit, & ea, ut prædictum est, quæ ad salutem totius Ecclesiæ pertinent, & insuper merito cavere non debuit, diffe-rendo & ordinando sancire solita fuit. Et hoc non tantum modo de causa fidei, vel, sicut præmissum est, de statu humani generis, vel cursu rectitudinis, verum quoque de omni dissensione in Ecclesia Dei Ecclesia, quæ pacem illam turbare videbatur, quam Dominus Apostolis & per Apostolos nobis omnibus vicariam præsentiæ suæ dereliquit, dicens; Pacem meam do vobis, pacem meam relinquo vobis. Ubicunque per quodlibet pietatis argumentum pertingere potuit, semper hujus sanctæ sedis vicarii Apostolorum quædam mulcendo, quædam vero, si ita res popposcisset, sublimi ac vemenda auctoritate, ut dignum erat, docendo pariterque prædicando ad pacis concordiam revocare studuit.
units.tr: In the same way also, in those matters which pertain to preserving the undefiled state of the same Church in human affairs, the Church has been accustomed to cut away not only what is harmful or hurtful but also what is superfluous and unnecessary, governing itself not by any deceitful or sophistical cleverness nor by double cunning, but by a simple reason resting on truth, shining with discretion, honesty and utility; and it has been accustomed to ordain, by deferring and arranging, what it ought not to have failed to guard against, as has been said, those things which pertain to the salvation of the whole Church. And this has been the custom not only in matters of faith, or, as has been said, of the state of the human race or the course of rectitude, but also in every dissension in the Church of God which seemed to disturb that peace which the Lord left to us all through the Apostles as a vicar of his presence, saying: My peace I give unto you; my peace I leave with you. Wherever it could reach by any argument of piety, the Church has always, with the vicars of the Apostles of this holy See, soothing some matters and, where the case required it, with lofty and vehement authority, as was fitting, teaching and preaching at the same time, laboured to bring them back to the concord of peace.

units.la: Quorum vicem, qualescunque simus, ministerium tamen auctoritate subeuntes, caritate pariter & eadem auctoritate roborati dissensionem illam, quæ infra ipsam semper Deo amabilem Romanorum Græcorumque ecclesiam exortam durius eandem ecclesiam, quam salutis illius ullo modo venire posset, scindentem diuturno tempore cognovimus non audemus declinare, ut non illam auctoritate tantorum Apostolorum ad pacis concordiam ipsis mediantibus non debeamus advocare. Maxime vero in eo quod ejusdem misericordiæ dissensio ea sit materia, sine qua, sicut multis videtur, per fidem, spem, & caritatem incunctanter & in hoc sæculo, & in futuro salvari potest ecclesia. Quorum sensus & sententia talis est. Quid fidei, spei, & caritati obesse potuisset, si imago nulla toto orbe terrarum vel ficta fuisset? Et quanquam idem filii nostri, qui hæc dicunt, rationabiliter se ostendere posse nullus dubitant, melius illud nunquam fuisse, sine cujus cultu perfecta fide, spe, & caritate universa Dei Ecclesia salva potuisset consistere, quam sub hac occasione non dubium, sed certissimum illud malum discordiæ debere incurrere, quod nisi correctum fuerit, nullatenus cum hac dissensione ad Dominum, qui est pax, omnium sibi placitam pacem habentium, nunquam in perpetuo posse ... ingere. Et quamvis devotio illorum hoc constanter postulet, ut eis ratiocinando qualiter de iisdem omnibus discrete & rationabiliter sentiant, postea differre liceat. Quod si est, qui suscipere jugum sine velit, salubre omni hominii esse non dubitant, ad comparationem tamen tanti mali imaginum causam pro vilo computant, si pax illa, quæ ad æternam vitam, quæ est via, veritas ducit, ad eandem viam, veritatemque perductæ non fuerit.
units.tr: Taking up their place, however we may be, in a ministry of authority, yet strengthened by charity and the same authority, we do not dare to shun that dissension which we have known for a long time to have arisen within the Roman and Greek churches, which are always beloved of God, and which tears that church apart more harshly than any means by which salvation could come. Lest we should not summon it, through the authority of such great Apostles, to the concord of peace with their mediation. Especially since this dissension concerns that matter without which, as many think, the Church can be saved without hesitation both in this age and in the future through faith, hope and charity. Their meaning and opinion is this: What could have harmed faith, hope and charity, if there had been no image at all throughout the whole world, even a false one? And although our sons who say these things, no one doubts, can show reasonably that it was never better that there should be no cult of images, without which the whole Church of God could have remained in perfect faith, hope and charity, yet under this pretext there must arise not a doubtful but a most certain evil of discord, which, unless it is corrected, can in no way, with this dissension, ever be brought to the Lord, who is peace, for all who have the peace pleasing to him. And although the devotion of those men constantly asks that we should defer to a later time the discussion of how they may judge all these things wisely and reasonably. But if there are some who are unwilling to take up this yoke, they do not doubt that it is wholesome for every man; yet, compared with so great an evil, they reckon the cause of images as worthless, if that peace which leads to eternal life, which is the way, the truth, has not been brought to that same way and truth.

units.la: Ideireo cunctus chorus sacerdotum, necnon & omnis Senatus totius gentis seu Imperii Francorum universa ecclesia per totam Galliam cum cæteris provinciis eidem à Deo conservando Imperio salutis, audita fama delendæ dissensionis fratrum suorum, inrevocabiliter postulant, ut prius sanctæ Sedis à Deo conservatam in futuroque usque in finem sæculi, sicut ipsi indubitanter, & non omnes per merita Apostolorum confidimus, conservandam auctoritatem, illud summopere testinemus, ut quia auctore Deo hæc duo regna in toto orbe terrarum principalia mutua sibi caritate devincta sunt, illud Diaboli telum ab eadem Ecclesia dissipetur, ut pax Dei, quæ exuperat omnem sensum, in eadem beata plebe pleniter restituatur.
units.tr: Therefore the whole choir of priests, and also the whole Senate of the entire nation or Empire of the Franks, and the whole church throughout all Gaul with the other provinces, having heard the report of the dissension among their brethren that is to be destroyed, earnestly and irrevocably ask that the authority of the holy See, preserved by God before and to be preserved to the end of the age, be upheld, as they trust without doubt, and not all through the merits of the Apostles. They most earnestly testify that, since by the ordering of God these two kingdoms are the principal ones in the whole world, bound together by mutual charity, that weapon of the Devil be scattered from the same Church, so that the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, may be fully restored among that blessed people.

units.la: Vt enim tantum in cælum uno ore & uno corde omnipotentis Dei judicium inevitabiliter cumbere, si auctoritate summorum in toto orbe terratum Apostolorum, quorum doctrinis & eorum ecclesiasticis flectitur mundus, discordiam vestram ad veram concordiam non certanius reducere. Dicunt enim, quid acturi essent de tam præcipuo coram Deo amisso solatio, si illos, quos post sedis immutabilem tuitionem, illud in tam præcipue carissimis fratribus solatium petdiderunt, qui similiter in universa Ecclesia nullum habebunt? Si enim cum illis veram fidem, integrumque caritatis ardorem non servaverint, quid in judicio Domini tanta neglecta caritate & in nomine Domini certissime confirmata neglexerint? Sed nos diuturnæ lectioni vestroque fastigio in legendo
units.tr: For they say that, if with one voice and one heart the judgment of almighty God must inevitably fall on heaven, we shall not labour to lead your discord back to true concord by the authority of the highest Apostles of the whole world, by whose teachings and ecclesiastical doctrines the world is swayed. For they say, what would they do, having lost so great a comfort before God, if they have lost that comfort in regard to the most dear brethren, after the unchanging protection of the See, which likewise will have no such comfort in the whole Church? For if they do not keep with them the true faith and the whole ardour of charity, what will they have neglected in the judgment of the Lord, when so great charity has been neglected and what has been most certainly confirmed in the name of the Lord? But we, sparing your long reading and your lofty station in reading

units.la: Q legendo parcentes, ubi tanta ab eis caritate urgente, de Deo placita mutua dilectione vestra, plorando, immo lugendo conquesti sunt, quae in unum colligi difficile possunt, omissis, ad eandem seriem decexendam, quam ipsi de imaginum reddenda ratione spoponderant, redeamus. Ajunt enim:
units.tr: [illegible] sparing in reading, where, with such charity urging them, they have complained, or rather lamented, with weeping, of your mutual love which is pleasing to God, things which can hardly be gathered into one. Leaving these aside, let us return to the same sequence which they had promised to give on the rendering of an account concerning images. For they say:

units.la: Oramus ergo sanctissime atque beatissime Pontifex, ut nobis antiquorum parrum nostrorum hac de causa vitae cursum recitare liceat, simulque prout rationis ordo poposcerit, census suis affectum in hac duntaxat re, cur ita vel ita tenuerint interserendo adjungere. Nec vobis taedium fiat, si ad ostendendam rationem veritatis, veritatemque rationis sese paulo longius sermo protraxerit, dum modo linea veritatis, quae ab antiquis patribus nostris usque ad nos inflexibiliter ducta est, beato Dionysio scilicet, qui a sancto Clemente beati Petri Apostoli in Apostolatu primus ejus successor exstitit, in Gallias cum duodenario numero primus praedicator directus, & post aliquod tempus una cum sociis suis huc illuc que praedicationis gratia per idem regnum dispersis martyrio coronarus est. Er quanquam plures exstitant, quidam martyres, quidam etiam confessores, quorum merita, quae apud Deum habeantur, quamvis quotidianis miraculis corruscent, quia tamen propter longitudinem terrarum vobis minus cogniti fortasse exstiterunt intermissis, sanctum tamen Hilarium antiquum ecclesiasticum doctorem, nec non & beatum Martinum toto orbe venerandum, vobis notissimos esse minime dubitantes, ad memoriam reducere necessarium aestimamus, quorum vitae magisterio edocti, haec ita tenenda atque servanda suscepimus. Sed quia apud nos vel majores nostros, ex quo ulla praesens aetas recordari potest, nunquam ejusmodi quaestio mota vel ventilata fuit, ideo sempertalis exinde mos ex praedictis antiquis temporibus retentus, in universa istius regni ecclesia exstitit, ut nullus, ac si ex auctoritate ejusdem sanctae Dei ecclesiae juberer, nullus cuicunque imaginem volenti pingere aut fingere prohiberet. Unde usque hodie eadem apud nos confuetudo tenetur, ut quia hoc auctoritas nulla jubet, nemo jubeat: similiter quia auctoritas nulla prohibet, nemo prohibeat. Quia vero propter praemissam rationem aliter esse non potest, mutatio inde habeatur, fortasse eadem ratio tale exordium non inconvenienter habere poterit. Si igitur imago in toto orbe rerarum nulla picta vel ficta esset, numquid aliquid fidei, spei, vel charitati sanctae Dei ecclesiae obesset? Rursus si ita, ut in quibusdam locis, maxime ecclesiis seu palatiis principum, ob nullam aliunde catholicae fidei seu religionis cultum, sed tantummodo scientibus pro amotis pii memoria seu ornamento eorundem locorum; nescientibus vero pro ejusdem pietatis doctrina pictae vel fictae sunt, ita per reliqua ejusdem imaginibus congrua domicilia ad eundem sensum pertinentes pictae vel fictae essent, quid praefatis virtutibus unquam aut usquam obesse potuisset? Et ideo quia res ita se habet, quid superest, nisi ut qui nolunt, ita non faciant, ut tamen eis, qui illas eo sensu (ut praemissum est) habere volunt vel facunt, in faciendo vel habendo minime contradicant. Et illi similiter, qui nias habere volunt, nolentes ad habendum vel faciendum nullatenus cogant. Atque ita auctore Deo, uterque inlaesus servatur, dum & habere volens * propter cautelam inliciti cultus, & habere nolens propter cautelam inliciti contemtus salvus permanere indubitanter poterit. Atque ita miserante Deo majorum nostrorum imaginibus vel picturis morem imitantes, in jubendo vel prohibendo, in habendo vel non habendo, in colendo vel non colendo, inlaesus hactenus hac de causa Domino opitulante nos transisse, & ipso gubernante transitus nequaquam dubitamus. Quamobrem monendi sunt omnes, qui illas habere volunt, ne amando, vel quolibet modo orando vel complectendo, ultra quam oportet, cultum eis inlicere rum nullatenus impendant. Similiter * & illis, qui eas habere noluerunt, sicubi eas aspexerint, qualibet ignominiosa vel probrosa detestatione spernere, contumeliare, vel lacerare praesumant. Hinc ergo indubitanter colligi poterit, quae illum ratio hoc cum periculo quocunque compellat habere, quod illum procul dubio sine ullo periculo licet non habere. Ideo ergo totius hujus rationis talis est summa, ut qui volunt propria memoria vel sana doctrina, in locis competentibus absque ullo inlicito cultu pietas vel fictas habeant imagines. Qui autem nolunt absque ullo inlicito concretu taliter habentes, vel habitas imagines nullatenus spernant.
units.tr: We therefore ask, most holy and most blessed Pontiff, that we may be allowed to recite the course of life of our ancient fathers on this matter, and, as the order of reason requires, to add, interspersed, their feeling on this one point, why they held this or that. Nor let it weary you if our discourse stretches somewhat further in order to show the reason of the truth and the truth of the reason, provided only that the line of truth, which has been drawn unwaveringly from our ancient fathers down to us, is kept: namely blessed Dionysius, who was the first successor of St Clement, the blessed Apostle Peter's successor in the apostolate, and was sent as the first preacher into Gaul with the twelve, and after some time, scattered with his companions here and there through that kingdom for the sake of preaching, was crowned with martyrdom. And although there have been many others, some martyrs and some also confessors, whose merits are held before God, though they shine with daily miracles, yet because they may be less known to you on account of the length of the lands, we think it necessary to call to mind St Hilary, the ancient ecclesiastical teacher, and also blessed Martin, venerated throughout the whole world, whom we do not doubt are very well known to you; taught by the example of whose lives we have undertaken to hold and keep these things as we do. But because among us or our elders, as far back as any present age can remember, such a question was never raised or debated, therefore a custom has always been retained from those aforesaid ancient times throughout the whole church of this kingdom, that no one forbade anyone wishing to paint or carve an image, as though he were ordered to do so by the authority of the same holy Church of God. Hence even today the same custom is kept among us: since no authority orders it, no one orders it; likewise, since no authority forbids it, no one forbids it. Since, because of the reasoning set out above, it cannot be otherwise, if a change is to be made from this, perhaps the same reasoning could fittingly have such an opening. If then no picture or image were painted or made anywhere in the whole world, would anything harm the faith, hope or charity of the holy Church of God? Again, if, as in certain places, especially churches or princes' palaces, they were painted or made not for any other cult of the Catholic faith or religion, but only for those who know, as a memorial or ornament of the pious for those places, and for those who do not know, for the teaching of that same piety; and if, in the same way, other dwellings suited to such images were painted or made with the same meaning, what could ever or anywhere have harmed the aforesaid virtues? And therefore, since the matter stands thus, what remains but that those who do not wish to should not do so, yet should in no way contradict those who wish to have or make them in that sense (as has been said)? Likewise those who wish not to have them should not in any way force those who are unwilling to have or make them. And thus, with God as author, each is kept unharmed: the one who wishes to have them, for caution against unlawful worship, and the one who does not wish to have them, for caution against unlawful contempt, can doubtless remain safe. And so, by the mercy of God, imitating the custom of our elders with images or pictures, in commanding or forbidding, in having or not having, in venerating or not venerating, we have so far passed through this matter unharmed, with the Lord helping us, and with him governing we doubt not that the passage will continue. Wherefore all who wish to have them must be warned not to give them any worship at all, by loving them, or praying to them in any way, or embracing them, beyond what is fitting. Likewise, let those who have not wished to have them not presume, whenever they see them, to spurn, insult or tear them with any shameful or disgraceful detestation. Hence it can be indubitably inferred that the reason which compels anyone to have them at whatever risk is the same reason which without doubt permits him not to have them without any risk. So the sum of this whole reasoning is this: those who wish, for the sake of their own memory or sound teaching, may have painted or carved images in suitable places without any unlawful worship; but those who do not wish to have them must not in any way spurn images that are had or held in that way.

units.la: Essent utique plura, quae hic ratiocinando, his per omnia congrua dici vel scribi potuissent, si aut brevitas temporis permitteret, aut id aliqua, si ea confirmando scribi necessitas popposcisset.
units.tr: There would indeed be more things that could have been said and written here, reasoning in agreement with these in every respect, if either the brevity of the time allowed, or some necessity had demanded it by confirming them in writing.

units.la: AUCTORITAS.
units.tr: AUTHORITY.

units.la: His etiam pro satisfactione praedictorum fratrum nostrorum, vel Ecclesiae superius commemorati regni, in sua, quia aliter esse non potuit, separatim relatione vel serie competenter praemissis, ut quicunque ratiocinando animo suo satisfacere voluerit, cur eadem Ecclesia tali se moderamine hac in re ex antiquis temporibus in habendis vel non habendis imaginibus tractare voluerit, tanto compendiosius facere possit, quanto non sparsim, sed simul sensum illorum opportune collectum legendo addiscere poterit. Modo autem eadem ratio docet, sicut supra significatum est, ut nunc ad auctoritatem sanctorum Patrum, qui inde aliquid scripserunt, nobisque scriptum reliquerunt, recurramus, & videamus, si eadem auctoritas praemissam rationem congruendo affirmare debeat, an non. Videtur igitur nobis, quamvis plures inde in reliquis * contractibus suis, quos de statu sanctae Dei Ecclesiae inspirante Spiritu sancto studiose texuerunt, nonnulla interserant, juxta quod sensus ille postulat unde agebatur: merito tamen illi ad hujusmodi examinationem primiponantur, qui de hac re specialiter & ob hanc solummodo solvendam quaestionem scripsisse reperiuntur. untur. E quibus nobis beatus Papa Gregorius hujus sanctæ Dei Ecclesiæ Pontifex primus occurrit, qui ad Serenum Massilienfem episcopum hoc specialiter scripsit, sicut & in epistola illius ad eum facta in armario sanctæ Dei nostræ ecclesiæ continetur, eo quod audiret illum propter, ut sibi videbatur, superfluum imaginarium cultum, tali zelo succensum, omnes imagines, quas in ecclesia sua receperat, depositte, confregisse, & extra eandem ecclesiam funditus projecisse, ut hoc facto à cultura vel adoratione inlicita populum compesceret. Qua de re, nihil congruentius in hac causa posse fieri arbitrati sumus, quam ut prima eadem epistola huic nostro operi, quod maxime ob amorem verae pacis sanctæ Ecclesiæ texere, ordinare, de meritis beatorum Apostolorum confisi, fideliter adgressi sumus, credentes per eos posse obtinere, ut tam per necessarium ecclesiasticum opus à Deo placitam consummationem debeamus perducere. Scribit enim ita.
units.tr: His also, in satisfaction of the aforesaid brethren of ours, and of the Church of the kingdom mentioned above, I have set out, as it could not be otherwise, separately in their own account and sequence, so that whoever wishes to satisfy his mind by reasoning why this Church from ancient times has chosen to deal with the having or not having of images in such a measured way, may do so all the more briefly, because he will be able to learn their sense by reading it gathered together at the right place, not scattered. Now, however, the same reasoning teaches, as has been said above, that we should now have recourse to the authority of the holy Fathers, who wrote something on this subject and left writings to us, and see whether that authority ought to confirm the reasoning set out above, or not. It seems to us, then, that although many of them in their other treatises, which they diligently composed on the state of the holy Church of God under the inspiration of the Holy Spirit, insert some matter on this point, as the sense of the subject under discussion requires, yet those should rightly be placed first for such an examination who are found to have written specially and solely to resolve this question. Of these, the blessed Pope Gregory, first Bishop of this holy Church of God, presents himself to us, who wrote on this point specifically to Serenus, bishop of Marseilles. This is also contained in a letter of his to him, kept in the archive of the holy church of our God, because he had heard that the bishop, kindled with such zeal, as it seemed to Gregory, against superfluous image-worship, had removed all the images which he had received into his church, had broken them and thrown them utterly out of the same church, so that by this act he might restrain the people from unlawful veneration or adoration. For this reason we judged that nothing more fitting could be done in this matter than to begin faithfully with that same first letter for this our work, which we have undertaken chiefly out of love of true peace in the holy Church, trusting in the merits of the blessed Apostles, believing that through them we may obtain that this necessary ecclesiastical work be brought to a conclusion pleasing to God. For he writes thus.

units.la: Indico, inquit, ad nos dudum pervenisse, quod fraternitas vestra quosdam imaginum adoratores aspiciens, eadem ecclesiis imagines confregit, atque projecit. Et quidem zelum vos, ne quid manufactum adorari posset, habuisse laudavimus, sed frangere eas dem imagines non debuisse judicamus. Idcirco enim pictura in ecclesiis adhibetur, ut hi, qui literas nesciunt, saltem in parietibus videndo legant, quae legere in codicibus non valent. Tua ergo fraternitas, & illa servare, & ab eorum adoratu populum prohibere debuit, quatenus & literarum nescii habentes, unde scientiam historiae colligerent, & populus in pictura adoratione minime peccaret.
units.tr: He says: "We have lately learned that your brotherhood, seeing some adorers of images, broke those same images in the churches and threw them out. We indeed commended your zeal, that nothing made by hand might be adored, but we judge that you ought not to have broken those images. For pictures are placed in churches so that those who do not know letters may at least read by looking at the walls what they cannot read in books. Your brotherhood therefore ought both to have preserved those images and to have forbidden the people from adoring them, so that the illiterate might have something from which to gather knowledge of history, and the people might not sin at all by worship of a picture."

units.la: Item idem ad eundem:
units.tr: Likewise the same to the same:

units.la: Perlatum, inquit, siquidem ad nos fuerat, quod inconsiderato zelo succensus, sanctorum imagines sub hac quasi excusatione, ne adorari debuissent, confringeres, & quidem quia eas adorare vetuisses, omnino laudavimus, fregisse vero reprehendimus. Dic, frater, a quo factum sacerdote aliquando auditum est quod fecisti? Si non aliud, vel aliud te non debuit revocare, ut dispectus alius fratribus solum te sanctum, & esse credetes sapientem? Aliud est enim picturam adorare, aliud pictura historia quid sit adorandum addiscere. Nam quod legentibus scriptura, hoc idiotis praestat pictura cernentibus, quia in ipsa ignorantes vident quod sequi debeant, in ipsa legunt qui literas nesciunt. Unde praecipue gentibus pro lectione pictura est, quod magnopere a te, qui inter gentes habitas, attendi decenter, ne dum recto zelo incaute succenderis, ferocibus animis scandalum generares. Frangi ergo non debuit, quod non ad adorandum in ecclesiis, sed ad instruendas solummodo mentes fuit nescientium collocatum. Et quia in locis venerabilibus sanctorum depingi historias, non sine ratione vetustas admisit, si zelum discretione condisses, sine dubio & ea, quae intendebas, salubriter obtinere, & collectum gregem non dispergere, sed potius poteras congregare, ut pastoris in te merito nomen excelleret, non culpa dispersoris incumberet. Huc autem dum in hoc animi tui incaute unus motus exsequeris, ita tuos scandali zasse filios perhiberis, ut maxima eorum pars a tua se communione suspenderet. Quando ergo ad ovile dominicum errantes oves adducas, qui quas habes, detinere non praevales? Proinde hortamur, ut vel nunc studeas esse sollicitus, atque ab hac te praemissione compescas, & eorum animos, quos a tua disjunctos unitate cognoscis, paterna ad te dulcedine omni adusque omniqe studio revocare festines. Convocandi enim sunt diversi ecclesiae filii, eique scripturae testimonium ostendendum, quia omne manufactum adorare non liceat, quoniam scriptum est: Dominum Deum tuum adorabis, & illi soli servies. Ac deinde subjungendum, quia picturas imaginum, quae ad aedificationem imperitii populi facta fuerant, ut nescientes literas, ipsam historiam intendentes, quod actum sit discerent, transisse in adorationem videras, idcirco commotus es, ut eas imagines frangi praeciperes, atque eis dicendum, si ad hanc instructionem, ad quam imagines antiquitus facta sunt, habere vultus in ecclesiis, eas modis omnibus & offerri & haberi permittas. At indica, quod non tibi ipsa visio historia, quia pictura teste pandebatur, displicuerit, sed illa adoratio, quae picturis fuerat incompetenter exhibita. Atque in hiis verbis eorum mentes demulcens, eos ad concordiam revoca, & si quis imagines facere voluerit, minime prohibe. Adorare vero imagines, omnimodis devita. Sed hoc sollicite fraternitas tua admoneat, ut ex visione rei gestae ardorem compunctionis percipiant, & in adorationem soli illius omnipotentis sanctae Trinitatis humiliter prosternantur.
units.tr: He says: "For it has been reported to us that you, kindled by an ill-considered zeal, broke the images of the saints under the pretext, as it were, that they ought not to be adored; and indeed because you had forbidden their adoration, we wholly commended you, but we blame you for breaking them. Tell me, brother, has it ever been heard from any priest that you did this? If not, let another not have been the one to recall you from it, lest, having scorned the others, you should seem to yourself alone holy and wise. For it is one thing to adore a picture, another thing to learn from a picture what is to be adored. For what Scripture offers to readers, that picture offers to the unlearned who look at it, since in it the ignorant see what they ought to follow, in it those who do not know letters read. Hence a picture is chiefly a kind of reading for the Gentiles, which you, who dwell among the Gentiles, ought to have considered carefully, lest while you were rashly inflamed with a right zeal, you should give offence to fierce minds. What was placed not for adoring in churches but solely for instructing the minds of the unlearned ought not to have been broken. And since antiquity has not without reason admitted that histories of the saints be painted in venerable places, if you had tempered your zeal with discretion, without doubt you could also have obtained what you intended, salutarily, and instead of scattering the flock gathered together, you could rather have gathered it, so that the name of minister might rightly stand out in you, and the fault of a scatterer not rest upon you. But now, since you pursue an unrestrained movement of your mind in this way, you are reported to have caused such scandal among your sons that the greater part of them has withdrawn from your communion. When, then, will you lead wandering sheep to the Lord's fold, when you cannot hold those you have? Therefore we exhort you that now at last you take care, and restrain yourself from this course, and hasten with all earnestness and diligence to recall to yourself with paternal sweetness the minds of those whom you know to be separated from your unity. For the various sons of the Church must be called together, and the testimony of Scripture shown to them, that it is not lawful to adore everything made by hand, since it is written: 'You shall adore the Lord your God, and serve him alone.' And then it must be added that, since you saw that pictures of images, which had been made for the edification of the unlearned people, so that those who do not know letters might learn, by attending to the history itself, what had been done, had passed into adoration, you were therefore moved to order those images to be broken; and to them must be said that, if you permit images to be in churches for that instruction for which images were made of old, you may in every way permit them both to be offered and to be kept. But declare that it was not the sight of the history itself, which was disclosed by means of the picture, that displeased you, but that adoration which had been improperly offered to the pictures. And soothing their minds with these words, call them back to concord, and by no means forbid anyone who wishes to make images. But to adore images, avoid entirely. Yet let your brotherhood take care to admonish them diligently, so that from seeing the deeds done they may perceive the fervour of compunction, and may humbly prostrate themselves in adoration of him alone, the almighty holy Trinity."

units.la: Item idem ad Januarium Episcopum:
units.tr: Likewise the same, to Januarius, Bishop:

units.la: Judaei, inquit, de civitate vestra huc venientes questi nobis sunt, quod synagogam eorum, quae Caralis sita est, Petrus, qui ex eorum superstitione ad Christianae fidei cultum Deo volente perductus est, albibitus sibi quibusdam disciplinatu, sequenti die baptismatis sui, hoc est dominica ipsa festivitate Paschali, cum gravi scandalo sine vestra voluntate occupasset, atque imaginem illic genetricis Dei, Dominique nostri & venerandam crucem vel byrrum album, quo fonte surgens, mundatus fuerat, appositum, & cetera. Et post pauca inquit: Confulerites hac de re vestrae voluntatis intentum ac magis judicium his hortamur affectibus, ut sublata exinde cum ea, quia dignum est, veneratione imagine atque cruce debeatis quod violenter ablatum est reformare.
units.tr: The Jews, he says, coming here from your city, have complained to us that their synagogue, which is situated at Caralis, was occupied, against your will and to great scandal, by Peter, who had been brought by God's will from their superstition to the worship of the Christian faith. He had put on some white garments provided for him, on the day after his baptism, that is, on the very feast of Easter Sunday; and an image of the Mother of God and of our Lord, and the venerable cross, and the white cloak in which he had risen mundified from the font, had been placed there, and so on. And after a little he says: We exhort you, having consulted your will and judgment on this matter, that the image and the cross, which were violently taken away, should be restored with the veneration that is fitting.

units.la: Item idem ad Secundinum servum Dei Inclusum:
units.tr: Likewise the same, to Secundinus, a servant of God, an Inclusus:

units.la: Imagines, inquit, quas à nobis tibi dirigendas per Dulcidium diaconem tuum rogasti, valde nobis tua postulatio placuit, quia illum in corde tota intentione quaeris, cujus imaginem praeoculis habere desideras, ut visio corporalis quotidiana reddat exortum, ut dum picturam vides, animo mardescas, cujus te imaginem videre confiderás. Abs re non facimus, si per visibilia invisibilia demonstramus, sic homo, qui alium ardenter videre desiderat, aut sponsam amando desiderat quam videre conatur, si contingit, aut ad balneum ire, aut ad ecclesiam procedere, festinus in via se praeparat, ut de visione hilaris recedat. Scimus quia tu imaginem Salvatoris nostri ideo non petis, ut quasi Deum colas, sed ob recordationem filii Dei, ut in ejus amore recaleseas, cujus te imaginem videre confiderás. Et nos quidem non quasi ante divinitatem ante ipsam prosternimur, sed illum adoramus, quem per imaginem aut natum, aut passum, vel in throno sedentem recordamur. Et dum nos ipsa pictura, quasi scriptura, ad memoriam filii Dei reducimus animum no-strum, aut de resurrectione laetificat, aut de passione mulcet. Ideoque direximus tibi fysternas duas, & imaginem Salvatoris & sanctæ Mariæ Dei genetricis, beati Petri & Pauli Apostolorum, per supradictum filium nostrum Diaconem, & una cruce clavem pro benedictione, ut ab ipso maligno defensus sis, cuius sancto ligno te esse munitum credis.
units.tr: The images, he says, which you asked us to send to you through Dulcidius your deacon, your request has pleased us greatly, because you seek with your whole heart Him whose image you desire to have before your eyes, so that the daily sight of the body may kindle the feeling; so that as you look at the picture, you may be inflamed in spirit by Him whose image you trust you are looking at. We do not act unreasonably if through visible things we show forth invisible ones. So a man who ardently desires to see another, or who loves a bride whom he tries to see, if it happens, either prepares himself quickly on the way to go to the bath or to proceed to church, so that he may leave the sight with joy. We know that you do not ask for the image of our Saviour so that you may worship it as God, but for the remembrance of the Son of God, so that you may be warmed in His love, whose image you trust you are seeing. And we indeed do not prostrate ourselves before the image as before the divinity itself, but we worship Him whom we remember through the image as born, or suffering, or sitting on the throne. And while the picture itself, like Scripture, brings our mind back to the memory of the Son of God, it either gladdens us about the resurrection or soothes us about the passion.
