Therefore we have sent you two veils, both the image of the Saviour and of holy Mary, Mother of God, and of the blessed Apostles Peter and Paul, through our aforesaid son the deacon, and a cross and a key for a blessing, so that you may be defended from that very evil one, by whose holy wood you believe you are fortified.

units.la: Hucusque epistola Gregorii.
units.tr: Thus far the letter of Gregory.

units.la: Sed quia hi cordo verborum ita præposterus atque à non intelligentibus confusus videri poterit, ut nisi caute consideretur, ita à nonnullis minus capacibus inrelligi possit, quasi beatus Gregorius id, quod prius omnibus inlicitum esse prædixit, se fecisse, sibique faciendi licitum esse testetur, quod quam absurdum, quamque contra sanctæ Dei ecclesiæ religionem de tanto ecclesiastico doctore sentire indignum sit, nullus, qui dicta ejus scrutando vel legendo cognovit, ignorare permittitur. Nam ut sibimetipsi contrarius esse debeat, justitia vel rectitudo sanctæ Dei maximeque Romanæ ecclesiæ sustinere non valet, quod & si paupertas insipientiæ nostræ id intelligere non valet, meliusque contra insipientiam, quam contra tantam à Deo datam sapientiam insurgere præsumar. Sed & ipsum modicum sensum nostrum virtus misericordiæ Dei aliquantulum illuminate dignatur, quomodo idipsum contrarium sibi non sit facillime intelligitur. Nam quia ab imaginum adoratione adorantes compescuerit, nulla dubitatio est. In eo vero, quod ad Secundinum scripsit, nos quidem non quasi ante divinitatem ante ipsam prosternimur, sed illum adoramus, quem per imaginem natum, aut passum, vel in throno sedentem recordamur, ubi ut præmissum est, ac sibimet contraria dixerit, intelligentiæ nostræ se caligo confundit. Sed ne nos non necessaria ignorantia ad non intelligendo diutius torqueat, sensus ejusdem sententiæ talis est.
units.tr: But since these words of his may seem so inverted, and so confused by those who do not understand, that unless they are carefully considered, they may be understood by some less capable people as if blessed Gregory were testifying that he had done what he had before declared to be forbidden to all, and that it was lawful for him to do it: no one who has learned his words by searching or reading is allowed to be ignorant how absurd this is, and how unworthy it is to think so of so great an ecclesiastical teacher, contrary to the religion of the holy Church of God. For that he should contradict himself, the justice and uprightness of the holy Church of God, and especially of the Roman Church, cannot endure; and even if the poverty of our folly cannot understand this, I would rather rise up against folly than against such great wisdom given by God. But the power of God's mercy also deigns to illuminate our own small understanding somewhat, so that it is very easily understood how this same thing is not contrary to itself. For that he restrained the worshippers from worshipping images, there is no doubt. But in what he wrote to Secundinus, we indeed do not prostrate ourselves before the image as before the divinity itself, but we worship Him whom we remember through the image as born, or suffering, or sitting on the throne, where, as has been premised, he seems to contradict himself, the darkness confounds our understanding. But lest unnecessary ignorance torment us longer by not understanding, the sense of that same sentence is such as follows.

units.la: Nos quidem ante ipsam non prosternimus, quasi ante divinitatem, sed illum adoramus, & cætera. Quod tale est, ac si regi in throno sedenti dicas: Nos quidem, ô Rex, non quasi ante divinitatem ante te prosternimus, sed illum adoramus, quem per imaginem tuam, quia homo es, Dominum Jesum Christum hominem recordamur natum, aut passum, vel in throno sedentem, cujus imitator es tu sedens in throno. nunquid tali dicto mox consequens est, ut eundem regem adorare compellar sedentem in throno? Ita nec in eo, quod dicitur: Nos quidem non quasi ante divinitatem ante ipsam prosternimur, sed illum adoramus, & cætera: ad imaginum adorationem invitamur, quia sicut in multis divinæ auctoritatis voluminibus sententias ordine verborum præposterò scriptas invenimus, ita quoque factum esse eo sensu, ut supra dictum est, hoc in loco minime dubitamus.
units.tr: We indeed do not prostrate ourselves before the image itself, as before the divinity, but we worship Him, et cetera. This is as if you were to say to a king sitting on his throne: We indeed, O King, do not prostrate ourselves before you as before a divinity, but we worship Him whom we remember, through your image, since you are a man, as the Lord Jesus Christ, born as man, or suffering, or sitting on the throne, whose imitator you are, sitting on the throne. Does it immediately follow from such a saying that I am compelled to worship that same king sitting on his throne? So also in what is said: We indeed do not prostrate ourselves before the image itself, as before the divinity, but we worship Him, and so on, we are not invited to the worship of images; since, just as in many volumes of divine authority we find sentences written with the order of words inverted, so we have no doubt that this has happened in this place in the sense stated above.

units.la: Cum enim ibi scriptum sit: Nos quidem non quasi ante divinitatem ante ipsam prosternimus, quis non animadvertat, idipsum magis refutando, vel imperando, vel adorando, eandem adorationem imaginum dictum esse, ita ut dictum est? quanto magis, licut supra factum est, ordo verborum suo restituatur in ordine, omnemque quemcumque ob nimiam simplicitatem etrantem, in eo quod beatum sanctæ Dei ecclesiæ doctorem adversum seipsum sensisse æstimabat, corrigere poterit. Insuper etiamsi quemquam subtilius intelligentem hoc negligentius minusve intente legere contigisset, facilime seipsum dijudicante, cur aliquando aliter senserit, ad sobrium intellectum revocare poterit. Si quis autem, quod quidem à sane sapientibus omnibus ablit, magis suum sensum sequendo illum voluerit condemnare quam se corrigere, nullo dubium, quin merito ab universa, maxime tamen à sancta Dei Romana ecclesia debeat condemnari. Nequaquam enim fieri potest, ut hæc duæ sententiæ sibimet contrariæ non exstiterunt, una qua populus ab adoratione imaginum, ne criminis id agendo reus appareat, prohibeatur: altera vero, quæ illum ad ipsum egisse, caeterosque ut hoc faciant docuisse perhibeatur. Sed abtiu hoc à tanto tali que generali catholicæ ecclesiæ magistro, ut qui universas perplexas scripturæ quæstiones, quæ sibi contrariæ videbantur, eique ad explanandum vel tractandum occurrerunt, nunquam diffidentes relinquere consuevit, sua sibimet dicta discordantia reliquisset.
units.tr: For since it is written there: We indeed do not prostrate ourselves before the image itself, who does not notice that the same worship of images was spoken of, by refuting, or commanding, or adoring it, in the way it has been said? All the more, as has been done above, if the order of words is restored to its proper order, anyone who went astray through excessive simplicity, thinking that the blessed teacher of the holy Church of God had felt against himself, will be able to correct himself. Moreover, even if someone more subtle in understanding should happen to read this less carefully or with less attention, he will be able, by judging it very easily for himself, to recall himself to a sober understanding of why he sometimes thought otherwise. But if anyone, which is far from all truly wise men, should wish to condemn Gregory by following his own opinion rather than correct himself, there is no doubt that he ought to be condemned, rightly, by the whole Church, but above all by the holy Roman Church of God. For it cannot possibly be that these two opposing sentences did not exist: one by which the people are forbidden to worship images, lest by doing so they appear guilty of a crime; the other, which is said to show that he himself did so, and taught others to do so as well. But far be it that such a great and universal teacher of the Catholic Church, who was accustomed never to leave unresolved, distrustful, all the perplexing questions of Scripture which seemed to contradict themselves and which occurred to him to explain or treat, should have left his own words in contradiction with one another.

units.la: His ita propter vitandam hujusmodi temeritatem suminatim præmissis; nunc videndum, utrum ei quisquam Catholicorum Patrum, quamvis ei specialiter fortasse talis scribendi necessitas minime incumberet, in cæteris tractatibus suis tale aliquid inditum habeat, in quo ejusdem patris sensui de imaginibus concors esse videatur.
units.tr: Having thus briefly premised these things, in order to avoid this kind of rashness, let us now see whether any one of the Catholic Fathers, although perhaps such a necessity of writing did not specially press upon him, has in his other treatises something inserted of this kind, in which he may seem to agree with the opinion of that same Father about images.

units.la: Ecce enim beatus Ambrosius antiquus ecclesiæ Dei probabilis doctor, ita in epistola Pauli ad Romanos tractans ait: Qua ratione, quæ auctoritate imagines Angelorum, vel aliorum Sanctorum adorandæ sint, cum ipsi sancti Angeli vel sancti homines vivos se adorari noluerunt?
units.tr: For behold, blessed Ambrose, an ancient and approved teacher of the Church of God, treating the Epistle of Paul to the Romans, says thus: By what reason, by what authority, are the images of Angels, or of other Saints, to be worshipped, when the holy Angels themselves, or holy men, did not wish to be worshipped while they were alive?

units.la: CONSILIUM.
units.tr: COUNSEL.

units.la: Auctoritate ergo, ut propositum secundo loco inserta, non quidem quantum ex thesauro uberrimo ecclesiastico potuit: sed quantum epistolaris brevitas tite permisit, monere vos & exhortari, ô venerandi mundi Principes, cum universa sancta Dei, quam Domino dispensante & committente gubernatis, Ecclesia, ut ea quæ vobis non quælibet temeritas, sed vera humilitas nostra intimare studuerit, attentius audiatis, & ob illorum reverentiam, qui cum Domino ipso promittente in die novissimo totius mundi venturi sunt judices reverenter suscipiatis, & ad salutem omnium vestrum strenue conservare studeatis. Præmisimus enim paulo superius, ut post redditam rationem, post insertam auctoritate, propter adunandum, quā Domino Deo ordinante regitis, Ecclesiā, consilium vobis non nostra adinventione, sed divina auctoritate illud dare debuissemus, perq eadem sancta mater Ecclesia ita sibi mutuoin vera pace fœderari debuisset, qualiter & in hoc seculo, & in futuro ei placere potuisset, qui ascensurus de mundo suis promisit dicens, Pacem meam do vobis, pacem relinquo vobis. Et quia attestante Paulo inter cætera verum est, Si quis tradiderit corpus suum ut ardeat, charitatem autem non habuerit, nihil est. Ideo prædictam sanctam Dei ecclesiam in veræ pacis concordiam adunari totis viribus optamus, quia quomodo sine illa charitatem mutuam habere posset, nullo modo intelligimus. Poterit enim fieri, ut aliquis cum altero ex parte vel fictam pacem temporaliter habeat, quomodo autem sine vera mutua pace habita cum altero veram posset habere charitatem, nulla docet auctoritas. Unde magnopere considerandum est, quanta temeritate, quantaque audacia ad æternam ille pervenire se posse existimat, qui præsentem in hoc sæculo pacem Domini per quamlibet occasionem sciens restaurare cum proximo non curat, quam primum munus humano generi conlatum Angeli nuntiant mox nato Domino in mundo, eandemque novissime fidelibus suis in vice sua idem Dominus reliquit discessurus de mundo. Et quanquam multa & pene innumerabilia essent, quæ de tanta re subtiliter, sublimiter, & nimis terribiliter dici potuissent, cavendum est unicuique, ne hoc quisquam de illa solummodo pace intelligendum putet, quæ habetur in cœlis. Quia & Dominus recedens ait: Pacem meam relinquo vobis. Et Angeli præmittentes: Gloria in excelsis Deo, nioc non in cœlis subjungunt, sed in terra pax hominibus bonæ voluntatis. Cogita igitur tecum, o plebs & populus Dei si ad perpetuam vis pervenire salutem, ut in hoc sæculo non fictam, sed veram habere mutuam itudeanuis pacem.
units.tr: Therefore, as the matter proposed in the second place requires, I have inserted an authority. It is not drawn from the rich storehouse of the Church, as it might have been, but only so far as the brevity of a letter allows. I admonish and exhort you, O venerable Princes of the world, whom the Lord has placed in charge of the holy Church of God, to listen more attentively to what our humble concern, not any rashness, has tried to make known to you. Out of reverence for those who, as the Lord himself promised, will sit as judges at the last day of the whole coming world, receive these words with respect and take care to keep them diligently for the salvation of all of you. Shortly before this, we said that after giving our reasons and inserting an authority, we ought to offer you counsel, not from our own invention but on divine authority, concerning the gathering of the Church, which the Lord has ordered you to rule. For this holy mother, the Church, ought to be bound to itself in true peace, so that it might be pleasing to him who, about to leave the world, made this promise: My peace I give to you, my peace I leave to you. And since, as Paul attests among other things, it is true that if someone gives his body to be burned, but has not love, it profits him nothing. Therefore we earnestly wish that the aforesaid holy Church of God be gathered into the harmony of true peace, for we cannot understand how it could have mutual love without it. A man may indeed have a feigned peace with another for a time, but no authority teaches how one could have true love with another without true mutual peace. Hence we must consider with great care what recklessness and what audacity it is for a man to think he can reach eternity, when he knows that he can restore the Lord's peace in this world with his neighbour on any occasion, yet does not care to do so. This is the gift that the angels announced to the human race as soon as the Lord was born into the world, and the same Lord, about to leave the world, finally left it to his faithful in his place. And although there are many, almost countless, things that could be said about so great a matter, subtly, loftily and very terribly, each one must take care not to think that this peace is to be understood only as the peace that is in heaven. For the Lord, withdrawing, said: My peace I leave to you. And the angels, going before him, add: Glory to God in the highest, not in heaven, but on earth peace to men of good will. Consider therefore within yourselves, O people and populace of God, if you wish to attain eternal salvation, that in this world you should have not a feigned but a true mutual peace.

units.la: Sed minus fortasse prodesse poterit, licet merito tanta talisque auctoritas causa consilii sufficere debuisset, necesse erit, ut huic adsertioni cætera adjungantur, quæ nequaquam juste adderentur, si à Deo ab initio catholicæ fidei data vobis sapientia, sicut oportuit, pro vobis sollicita esse studuisset. Dicit enim Apostolus, Judæi signa petunt, Græci sapientiam quærunt, ubi est ergo sapientia vestra, qui propter quamlibet occasionem illud habere contemnitis, sine quo ad regna cœlestia pervenire nullo modo valebitis? Et hæc non arguendo vel increpando, sed admonendo interim dicimus, ut vos ad interiorem hominem vestrum, in quo Deus per fidem, spem, & charitatem inhabitare consuevit, revocemus. Quem si ita secundum, ut supra dictum est, sapientiam vobis à Deo datam, cogitare, diligere, vel metuere vultis, mirum est, quomodo cum fratribus invicem tanto jam tempore scandalum & discordiam habere non metuitis. Ecce etenim, si non amplius, jam annus est, ex quo hanc inter vos miserrimam dissensionem publicatam audivimus. Quam videlicet discordiam Deo (ut dignum est,) semper odibilem, diabolo vero, ut ei decet, semper amabilem, omnes antecessores mei ad corrigendum prout eis possibile fuit, multum laborasse non ignoratur.
units.tr: But perhaps this will be of little benefit. Although such an authority, rightly considered, ought to be sufficient reason for counsel, it will be necessary to add other matters to this assertion, which would not be rightly added at all if the wisdom given to you by God from the beginning of the Catholic faith had been careful, as it ought, for your sake. For the Apostle says: The Jews ask for signs, the Greeks seek wisdom. Where, then, is your wisdom, when on any pretext you despise that without which you will by no means be able to reach the heavenly kingdom? We say this not by arguing or rebuking, but by admonishing, that we may call you back to your inner man, in whom God is accustomed to dwell through faith, hope and love. If, as has been said above, you wish to think, love or fear him with the wisdom given you by God, it is strange how you are not afraid to keep up scandal and discord with your brothers for so long. For behold, it is now a year, if not more, since we heard that this most wretched dispute has been made public among you. It is not unknown that all my predecessors, as far as was possible for them, laboured much to correct this discord, which is always hateful to God (as is fitting) and always pleasing to the devil, as is also fitting.

units.la: Hæc in paucis ad excitanda Deo amabilia corda vestra ideo præmittere curavimus, ut ea, quæ vobis studiosius pro salute omnium animarum nostrarum dicenda providimus, auctiores vos ad audiendum & per omnia sollicitos in Domino redderemus. Sed sicut non solum sacra auctoritate discimus, verum quoque & humana quotidiana bene consuetudine agendo cernimus, quia arbor fructus malos faciens, nullo modo salubrius extirpatur, quam si radicitus evellatur: melius sæpe dictam discordiam vestram omnipotente Domino opitulante una vobiscum, qui huic miserrimæ numinimque infelici conditioni prostrati non succumbitis, sed auctoritate bonorum omnium Domino Deo tantæ spurcitiæ celso in cacumine præeminentis corrigere valemus, si quæ sit hujus perditionis origo vel tomes detegendo pandamus.
units.tr: We have taken care to set out these few things in advance, to stir your hearts, which are dear to God, so that the things we have carefully prepared to say to you for the salvation of all our souls might make you more eager to listen and more attentive in all things in the Lord. But as we learn not only from sacred authority, but also see from the daily custom of human affairs, that a tree bearing bad fruit is in no way more healthily removed than when it is torn up by the roots, so we can correct this discord of yours, which we have often mentioned, with the Lord almighty helping us, and with you, who are not overcome, but cast down by this most wretched and unhappy condition of the Church. We can do so with the authority of all good men and with the Lord God, who stands high above such filth, if we uncover and reveal what the origin or root of this destruction is.

units.la: Nullus nempe sana sapientium fideliumque in Domino fratrum vestrorum dubitare permittitur esse plures in hac sancta & à Deo conservanda Ecclesia, qui tantæ miseriæ succumbere dedignentur, licet eis manus humana validior, nec id, quod exinde justum esse non dubitant, restaurare vel perficere valeant, obsistat. Quamobrem amabiliter ammonendi estis, ut totis viribus omnipotentem Dominum exorare studeatis, ut tantam ab hoc regno infelicitatem amovere jubeat, & illam, quam mundus dare non poterit, pacem sua vobis immensa clementia concedat.
units.tr: Surely no wise man who is sound and faithful in the Lord, among your brothers, is allowed to doubt that there are many in this holy Church, which God must preserve, who disdain to yield to such misery, even though human power may be stronger than they, and even though they cannot restore or accomplish what they do not doubt is just in this matter. Therefore you must be lovingly admonished to strive with all your strength to beseech the almighty Lord, that he may command this great unhappiness to be removed from this kingdom, and that by his boundless mercy he may grant you that peace which the world cannot give.

units.la: Et quia tantæ auctoritatis ordo, vel tantæ sublimitatis ratio necdum poscebat, ut prius quam illa omnia, quæ merito præmittenda erant, præponeretur, ut facilius quovis in loco secundum sui qualitatem haberentur illa, quibus salva fide, ipse, vel charitate totius Ecclesiæ status carere potuisset, propter satisfactionem tamen in hoc opere laborantium principalis hujus sæpedictæ discordiæ vestræ, causa imaginum exstitisse traditur. Ejusdem quoque causæ origo in eo contigisse fertur, quod Imperator, considerans quosdam in eadem plebe indiscreto zelo inflammatos ultra quam oportuisset, vel unquam prius actum esset, in imaginum cultura, veneratione vel adoratione ultra progredere, quam ut antea unquam in universa ecclesia factum esset, volens ut tunc sibi cum illis, qui ei favebant, eandem superstitionem qualiscunque esset, ab Ecclesia penitus amoveret, postposita hac in re salubri discretione, sine qua omnis humanæ actionis virtus in vitium vertitur, elegit prætermittam superstitionem aliter emendari non posse, nisi omnes imagines penitus delerentur. Atqui si ita erat, ut dictum est, nulicitum cultum in hominibus, vel ab hominibus compescendum erat, non in imaginum destructione, quæ nihil peccaverunt: immo eo sensu, quo supra præmissum est, scientibus pro pia memoria, nescientibus vero pro doctrina utiles erant, infringendo vel dissipando sinistram extendit pro dextera. & qui ita hac in re incautos reducere debuit, sicut forte, quia recens erat causa, facilime potuit, instigante qui nunc late patet, ecclesiasticæ pacis vel charitatis inimico.
units.tr: Since the order of so great an authority, or the reason for so great a height, did not yet require that all those things which rightly had to be put first should be placed before it, so that those things by which the faith or charity of the whole Church might have been kept safe, in whatever place and according to their nature, could more easily be had, nevertheless the cause of this discord of yours, which I have often mentioned, is said to have arisen because of the images, for the sake of the satisfaction of those labouring in this work. The origin of this same cause is also said to have happened in this way: the Emperor, considering that certain people in the same populace, inflamed with indiscreet zeal beyond what was proper, or beyond what had ever been done before, were advancing in the cultivation, veneration or adoration of images further than had ever been done in the whole Church before, wished, together with those who favoured him, to remove this superstition, whatever it might be, from the Church entirely. Setting aside in this matter that wholesome discretion, without which the power of every human action turns into vice, he chose, since he thought the superstition could not be corrected in any other way, to destroy all images completely. But if things were as has been said, the unlawful worship among men, or practised by men, ought to have been restrained, not by destroying images, which had done no wrong. Indeed, in the sense set out above, they were useful to those who know them for pious remembrance and to those who do not know them for instruction. By breaking up and scattering them he stretched out his left hand instead of his right. And he who ought to have led the unwary back in this matter, as perhaps he could very easily have done, since the cause was recent, was driven on by the enemy of ecclesiastical peace and charity, who now spreads widely.

units.la: Hanc ei * ac si luculentissimam ostendit sententiam, heu quam longe ab illa sinistris anfractibus incedenté, quæ de semetipso ait: Ego sum via, veritas, & vita, quid putas quam dulcia quamque religiosi illa, Joan. 14. imo sanctus. imò sanctissima satagebat fingere itinera, ut per illa ad hæc, quæ nunc omnes plangimus, perttahere potuisset discidia? sed nec hoc ullo modo aliter æstimatur peragere potuisse, nisi illum prius cum sequacibus suis illius impiæ dulcedinis demulcendo cor tangeret, cujus idem diabolus pestifero telo perforatus, de cœlo merito cecidisset.
units.tr: He showed this as a most clear opinion. Alas, how far from it was the one who walked on crooked paths, who said of himself: I am the way, the truth, and the life (Joan. 14.). What sweet and devout, indeed holy, indeed most holy, paths do you think he was busy making, so that by them he might bring about the divisions which we now all lament? Yet it does not seem that he could have accomplished this in any way, unless he had first touched the heart of himself and his followers by soothing them with that impious sweetness, by which the devil himself, pierced by the deadly weapon, had justly fallen from heaven.

units.la: Sed quid agimus, quid dicimus? Ad comparationem namque malorum omnium, quæ hic congruente spatio, quod omnino non decet, non solum de diabolo, sed etiam de ipso Imperatore cum fautoribus suis dici poterant, nihil est quod dicimus. Universa denique mala, quæ ex eo usque in præsentem diem per hujusmodi discordiam in vobis perpetrata sunt, hinc sumsere principium. Quamvis enim propter singultum plorationis tacere non permittamus, licet propter arctissimum temporis spatium, & propter innumeritatem earundem miseriarum, ut lugentibus mos est, innumera ad dicendum flebilia occurrerint, paucis ad incoationem hujus infelicitatis redire placet, ut contueamur diabolum in hujus vitæ excursu in bivio stantem, ubi Imperator e duobus unum ad eligendum indeclinabiliter cogitur, aut cultui inlicito favendo imaginibus contra jus ecclesiasticum cei vicem flectere, aut certe hujusmodi cultoribus contradicendo, vel non favendo ingratus exsistere. & qui facilius poterat ad imitationem antiquiorum principum vel patrum suorum, & illos ab inlicito cultu revocare, & cum cæteris omnibus morem antiquum sine offensione Dei prosequentibus pacem vel charitatem leniter retinere; persuadit eum prædictus pacis semper & charitatis inimicus, illud iter in destruendis imaginibus arripere, per quod omnes per discretionem sane sapientes atq; servantes perturbando confunderet, & illos, qui sæpe dicta discretione vel temperantia, quæ una de cardinalibus ecclesiasticis virtutibus esse cognoscitur, spreta, elegit ultra quam unquam Deo placuit, vel placere debeat, imaginum cultui deservire, ut eisdem, qui hoc electum habebant, potuissent placere. Non considerans illud quod terribiliter scriptum est, Qui hominibus placent confusi sunt, quoniam Deus sprevit illos.
units.tr: But what are we doing, what are we saying? Compared with all the evils, which could be spoken of here, though the space is too short, as it certainly ought not to be, not only of the devil but also of the Emperor himself and his supporters, what we say is nothing. In short, all the evils that have been committed among you from that time down to the present day through this kind of discord took their beginning here. Although we cannot keep silent for the sobbing of our lament, and although, because the time is very short and the miseries are countless, as is the custom of mourners, countless sad things present themselves for telling, we are pleased to return briefly to the beginning of this misfortune, so that we may behold the devil standing at the fork in the road in the course of this life. There the Emperor is inescapably forced to choose one of two things: either by favouring unlawful worship, to turn toward images against ecclesiastical law, or else, by opposing or not favouring those who practise such worship, to show himself ungrateful. He could more easily, in imitation of the older princes and his own fathers, both call them back from unlawful worship and gently keep peace and charity with all the others who follow the ancient custom without offence to God. But the aforesaid enemy of peace and charity always persuades him to take up that path of destroying images, by which he would confound and throw into disorder all who are wise and preserve the faith through discretion, and those who, having scorned the aforesaid discretion or temperance (which is known to be one of the cardinal virtues of the Church), chose to serve the worship of images beyond what ever pleased God or ought to please, so that they might please those who had made this choice. Not considering what is terribly written: Those who please men are confounded, because God has despised them.

units.la: Sicque factum est, ut ex die illo ab eodem antiquo semper Deo placens populo fidelium exilia non cessarent, cruces & cruciatus non quiescerent, &, ut fertur, membrorum detruncationes, ipsa etiam homicidia, causa earundem imaginum, nimia perpetrata sint. Et hæc diu cucurrerunt, quousque idem humani generis antiquus hostis, quasi in hac parte satiatus, convertit se ad alia perditionis argumenta, ut denuo suscitaret libi contra cultores imaginum, Herenam videlicet cum filio, tam pestifera infusione decipiens, ut absque ulla misericordia vel metus superni spiciens omnipotentis Dei majestate, talis ab eis promulgaretur sententia, ut omnis homo eorum ditioni subjectus imagines adoraret, aut certe exilio pœnisve diversis cruciaretur, & si non adquiesceret, ab universali Ecclesia anathematis vinculo sequestratus teligaretur. Sed quid nunc denuo è diverso agat, ad priorem iterum recurrens semitam, præsentem denuo incitans Imperatorem, ut eas pietas vel scriptas habere quempiam volendo permittat. Quis igitur tam eloquens sub cœlo habetur, qui hanc pestiferam cladem enumerare prævaleat? Quis tam ferrea habeat præcordia, cui non dico scribendi, verum quoque per defectum lacrymarum vocem non tollat ejulandi?
units.tr: And so it came about that from that day onward, among the people who always pleased the God of old, exiles did not cease, crosses and tortures did not rest, and, as is reported, mutilations of limbs and even murders were committed in excess on account of those same images. These went on for a long time, until that ancient enemy of the human race, as if sated on this front, turned himself to other instruments of ruin, so as to stir up again against the worshippers of images, namely Irene together with her son, deceiving them with such a pestilent infusion that, without any mercy or fear, not looking upon the majesty of almighty God, such a sentence was proclaimed by them that every man subject to their rule should adore images, or else be tormented with exile and various punishments; and if he did not consent, he would be cut off from the universal Church and bound with the chain of anathema. But what he now does on the opposite side, returning again to the former path, again urging the present Emperor, is to permit someone to have those writings... Who is held so eloquent under heaven as to be able to enumerate this pestilent disaster? Who has a heart so hard that he cannot, I will not say write, but at least raise his voice in wailing for lack of tears?

units.la: Catera desunt.
units.tr: The rest is missing.

units.la: SANCTISSIMO AC REVEREN- DISSIMO DOMNO ET IN CHRI- STO PATRI EUGENIO SUMMO PONTIFICI, & universali Papæ HLudovicus & HLudarius, divina ordinante providen- tia Imperatores & Augusti, spiritales filii vestri sempiternam in Domino nostro Jesu Christo salutem.
units.tr: To the most holy and most reverend lord and father in Christ, Eugenius, Supreme Pontiff and universal Pope: Ludovicus and Lotharius, by the ordaining providence of God Emperors and Augustuses, your spiritual sons, send eternal greetings in our Lord Jesus Christ.

units.la: QUIA veraciter nos debitores esse cognovimus, ut his quibus regimen ecclesiarum, & ovium dominicarum cura commissa est, in omnibus cautis ad divinum cultum pertinentibus opem atque auxilium pro qualitate virium nostrarum & intellectus nostri capacitate feramus. Idcirco prætermittere nequivimus, quin tunc, quando Legati Græcorum nobis manifestaverunt, qualem ad vos deberent perferre legationem, summa cura ac sollicitudine tractatemus, quale vobis adjutorium in hoc negotio cum Dei auxilio exhibere potuissemus. Et ob hoc vestra sanctitate petimus, ut sacerdotibus nostris liceret de libris sanctorum Patrum sententias quærere atque colligere, quæ ad eandem rem, pro qua idem Legati vos consulturi erant, veraciter definiendam convenire potuissent.
units.tr: Since we have truly recognised that we are debtors to those to whom the governance of the churches and the care of the Lord's flock have been entrusted, to bring aid and help in all matters pertaining to divine worship, according to the measure of our strength and the capacity of our understanding, we could not omit to consider with the utmost care and concern, when the envoys of the Greeks made known to us what embassy they were to bring to you, what help we might be able to give you in this business, with God's assistance. For this reason we ask your holiness that our priests be permitted to seek out and gather from the books of the holy Fathers the opinions which could fittingly serve to settle truly the very matter on which those envoys were to consult you.

units.la: Quas cum illi juxta concessam etiam à vobis licentiam solerter inquirerent, & divina opitulante gratia quicquid invenire tam brevi temporis spatio potuerunt, collegissent, nobis ea perlegenda direxerunt. Quibus perlectis, ea vestræ sanctitati legenda atq; examinanda per hos legatos nostros Hieremiam scilicet & Jonam, venerabiles Episcopos, mittere curavimus. Cum quibus si vestra paternitas dignum duxerit, de eadem legatione, quæ in Græciam à vobis mittenda est non inutilem, sed potius proficuam conlatione habere poteritis, quia & in sacris sunt literis admodum eruditi, & in rationibus disputandi. bus disputatoriis non minimum exercitati. Quos non ob hoc ad vestræ almitatis præsentiam commemoratis sententiarum collectionibus misimus, ut hic aliquo velut magisterii officio fungerentur, aut huc docendi gratia directi purarentur: quia, sicut jam commemorati sumus, nos debitores exist ere, ut huic sacratissimæ sedi in quibuscunq; negotiis auxilium ferre debeamus. Ideo & hos Missos, & quas deferunt literas, si quid vobis adjutorii conferre potuissent, mitterte dignum duximus. Hos vestræ sanctitati commendamus, ut & benignam apud vos receptionē, & familiariter vobiscum loquendi locum inveniant.
units.tr: When they had diligently searched these, under the permission granted by you, and by the aid of divine grace had gathered whatever they could find in so short a space of time, they sent them to us to be read through. When these had been read, we took care to send them, by our legates Hieremias and Jonas, reverend bishops, for your holiness to read and examine. With them, if your paternity thinks fit, you may hold a conference about this embassy which is to be sent by you into Greece, not unprofitable but rather advantageous, since they are both very learned in the sacred letters and not a little practised in the methods of disputation. We have not sent them to your almighty presence with these collections of opinions so that they might act here in some office of teaching, nor were they sent hither to be instructed; for, as we have already said, we are debtors to help this most sacred see in whatever business it may have. Therefore we have thought fit to send these envoys, and the letters they bring, in case they might contribute some aid to you. We commend them to your holiness, that they may find both a kind reception among you and an opportunity of speaking familiarly with you.

units.la: Novit quippe sanctitas vestra qualiter populus Græcorum in hac imaginum veneratione divisus sit. Ideo rogamus, ut almitas vestra curam & diligentiam adhibere dignetur, quomodo per vestram salubertimam doctrinam atque admonitionem magis ad concordiam & unitatem revocetur, quam propter hoc ad majorem discordiam & dissensionē impellatur. Et ideo cautissime considerare debetis, ut legatio vestra, quam illuc dirigere disponitis, tanta prudentia, tantoq; moderamine sulfulta sit, ut à nemine neq; à Græco neq; Romano juste valeat reprehendi: sed talis sit, qualem semper decet in omnibus causis ab ista facratissima Sede proficisci. Et si vestræ sanctitati placet, ut pro hac ipsa legatione Missi nostri simul cum vestris illis in partes dirigantur, & hoc nos tempore congruo scire permittite. Et non solum hoc, sed etiam si iturí fuerit, ubi & quando cum vestris Missis se jungere debeant. Non ideo tamen de nostris Missis illuc dirigendis interrogamus, quasi necessarium nobis videatur, aut nos vestros Missos hanc legationem per se perficere dubitemus, sed potius propter hoc eos vobis offerimus, ut sciatis nos in omnibus esse paratos, quæ hujus sacratissimæ sedis necessitas aut voluntas postulaverit. Optamus sanctam & venerabilem, ac piam paternitatem vestram, semper in Christo bene valere, & nostri ac nostrorum omnium in sacrosanctis orationibus meminisse, sanctissime ac beatissime Pater.
units.tr: Your holiness knows well how the people of the Greeks is divided over this veneration of images. Therefore we ask that your almighty self deign to apply care and diligence, how, through your most salutary teaching and admonition, they may be recalled rather to concord and unity than driven by this to greater discord and dissension. And so you must consider most cautiously that your embassy, which you intend to direct thither, be supported by such prudence and such moderation that it may justly be reproved by no one, neither Greek nor Roman; but let it be such as always befits proceeding from this most sacred See in all causes. And if it pleases your holiness that our envoys be sent into those parts together with your own envoys for this same embassy, permit us to know this at a suitable time; and not only this, but also, if they are to go, where and when they ought to join themselves with your envoys. Yet we do not ask about sending our envoys thither as though it seemed necessary to us, or as though we doubted that your envoys could accomplish this embassy by themselves; rather we offer them for this reason, that you may know we are ready in all things which the necessity or the will of this most sacred see may require. We pray that your holy, venerable and pious paternity may always fare well in Christ, and remember us and all ours in your most sacred prayers, most holy and most blessed Father.

units.la: Hieremiæ & Jonæ venerabilibus Episcopis in Domino salutem.
units.tr: To the reverend bishops Hieremias and Jonas, greetings in the Lord.

units.la: Venerunt ad præsentiam nostram Halitgarius & Amalarius Episcopi VIII. Idus Decembris, deferentes collectiones de libris sanctorum Patrum, quas in conventu apud Parisios habito simul positi collegistis, quas etiam coram nobis perlegi fecimus. Et quia placuerunt, ad id, propter quod collectæ sunt, necessariæ atq; utiles à nobis judicantur, sub omni celeritate censuimus dirigendas. Idcirco admonendo præcipimus solertiæ vestræ, ut priusquam de his aliquid Domno Apostolico indicetis, diligenti cura eadem vos recensere curetis, & ea quæ melius & aptius præsenti negotio convenire inveneritis, excerpere atque describere, illiusque ad legendum offerre studeatis, quia enim, ut nostis, nos ab eo petere voluimus licentiam, quatenus has collectiones à sacerdotibus nostris fieri permitteret; & ideo non poterit prætermitti, quin ostendatur, quod ex ipsius permissione collectum est.
units.tr: The bishops Halitgarius and Amalarius came into our presence on the eighth day before the Ides of December, bringing the collections from the books of the holy Fathers which you gathered together when you were assembled at the council held at Paris; these we have also had read through in our presence. And since they pleased us, we have judged them necessary and useful for the purpose for which they were gathered, and we have thought fit to send them on with all speed. We therefore admonish and command your diligence that, before you report anything of these to the lord Apostolic, you take care diligently to review them yourselves, and be eager to select and copy out those things which you find to agree better and more aptly with the present business, and to offer them to him for reading; for, as you know, we wished to ask him for permission that these collections be made by our priests; and therefore it cannot be omitted that it be shown what has been gathered by his permission.

units.la: Illud tamen summopere prævidete, ut ea illi de his ostendatis, quæ rationi de imaginibus habendæ per omnia conveniunt, & quod ipse vel sui minime rejicere valeant. Sed & vos ipsi tā patienter ac modeste cum eo de hac causa disputationem habeatis, ut summopere caveatis, ne nimis ei resistedo eum in aliquam inrevocabilem pertinaciam incidere compellatis, sed paulatim verbis ejus quasi obsequendo magis quam aperte resistendo ad mensuram, quæ in habendis imaginibus tenenda est, eum deducere valeatis. Et ideo potius efficere cōtendatis, ut negotium, de quo agitur ad meliorem, quam ad pejorem statum cum Dei adjutorio perducatur.
units.tr: Yet above all take care to show him those things about this matter of holding images which agree in every respect with reason, and which he himself and his people can by no means reject. And you yourselves should so patiently and modestly hold the debate with him about this cause that you take great care not to resist him too strongly and drive him into some irrevocable obstinacy; but rather, by gradually yielding somewhat to his words as if complying, rather than openly opposing, you may be able to lead him to the measure which is to be observed in the holding of images. And so you should strive rather to bring the business in question, with God's help, to a better rather than a worse state.

units.la: Postquam vero hancrationem de earundem imaginum causa consummaveritis, si tamen hoc ad nihilum Romana pertinacia permiserit, ut ratio inter vos habita, aliquo bono & convenienti fine claudatur, & ille vobis indicaverit, quod Legatos suos ob eandem causam in Græciam permitere velir, volumus, ut eum interrogetis, si ei placeat, ut nostri legati pariter cum suis in Græciam pergant. Et si hoc ei melius visum fuerit, seque hoc omnino velle responderit, tunc volumus, ut sub omni festinatione literis vestris à vobis ad nos directis nos inde certos faciatis, simulque & de vestro adventu ad nos, ut eo tempore, quo vos ad nostram veneritis præsentiam, Halitgarium & Amalarum nobiscum inveniatis. Vos autem cum Domno Apostolico considerate, ubi ille vel quando velit, ut sui ac nostri Legati ad naves conscendendas se jungere debeant, & hoc nobis per vosmetipsos cum Deo volente, veneritis, adnuntiare poteritis.
units.tr: Moreover, when you have finished this discussion about the cause of these images, if nevertheless Roman obstinacy allows nothing, so that the reasoning held between you is concluded with some good and fitting end, and he has told you that he is willing to send his legates into Greece for the same cause, we wish you to ask him whether it pleases him that our legates go together with his into Greece. And if this seems better to him, and he replies that he wishes this altogether, then we wish you to make us certain of it with all haste, by letter sent from you to us, and at the same time of your coming to us, so that at the time when you come into our presence you may find Halitgarius and Amalarius with us. But do you, with the lord Apostolic, consider where and when he wishes that his legates and ours should join themselves for embarking on the ships; and you will be able to announce this to us yourselves, God willing, when you come.

units.la: LOTHARII I. IMPERA- TORIS AUGUSTI CONSTITUTIO De Electione Romani Pontificis, & Legibus Romanorum.
units.tr: THE CONSTITUTION OF THE EMPEROR LOTHAIR I AUGUSTUS On the Election of the Roman Pontiff, and the Laws of the Romans.

units.la: Volumus ut ad electionem Pontificis nemo audeat venire neque liber neque servus, qui aliquod impedimentum inferat, exceptis illis tantum Romanis, quibus antiqua fuit consuetudo concessa per constitutionem sanctorum Patrum eligendi Pontificem. Quod si quis contra nostram justionem facere ausus fuerit, exilio afficiatur.
units.tr: We will that no one, whether free or slave, dare to come to the election of the Pontiff so as to hinder it in any way, except only those Romans to whom the ancient custom of electing the Pontiff has been granted by the constitution of the holy Fathers. If anyone presume to act against our command, let him be punished with exile.

units.la: a Volu-
units.tr: Volu-

units.la: 2. * Volumus ut cunctus populus Romanus interrogetur, qua lege velit vivere, aut ea, qua professus sit vivere velle, vivat; eiq; denuntietur, ut hoc unusquisq; sciat, tam Duces, quam Judices, vel reliquus populus. Quod si in offensionem suam contra eamdem legem fecerint, eidem legi, quam profitentur, ex constitutione Pontificis & nostra subjacebunt.
units.tr: 2. * We will that the whole Roman people be asked under what law they wish to live, or that they live under the law which they have professed they wish to live under; and let it be announced to them, so that everyone, both dukes and judges and the rest of the people, may know this. If they offend against that same law, they shall be subject to that same law which they profess, under the constitution of the Pontiff and of ourselves.

units.la: 3. De rebus Ecclesiarum injustè occupatis per occasionem, quasi licentia accepta à Pontifice, & de iis quæ necdum reddita sunt, & tamen fuerunt * à potestate Pontificum occupatæ, volumus ut per Legatos nostros restituantur.
units.tr: 3. Concerning the property of the Churches unjustly seized on the occasion, as if licence had been received from the Pontiff, and concerning those things which have not yet been restored and yet were * seized by the power of the Pontiffs, we will that they be restored through our envoys.

units.la: 4. Placet nobis ut cuncti Judices, sive ii qui cunctis præesse debent, per quos judiciaria potestas in hac Urbe Roma exercetur, aut in cæteris provinciis exerceri debet, in præsentiam nostram veniant. Volumus numerum & nomina eorum scire, & singulos de munere sibi credito admonere.
units.tr: 4. It pleases us that all judges, both those who ought to preside over all others, through whom judicial power is exercised in this city of Rome or ought to be exercised in the other provinces, come into our presence. We wish to know their number and names, and to remind each one of the office entrusted to him.

units.la: 5. Novissimè admonemus, ut omnes homines, licut Dei gratiam & nostram habere desiderant, ita præstent in omnibus obedientiam ac reverentiam huic Pontifici.
units.tr: 5. Lastly, we admonish that all men, just as they desire to have the grace of God and ours, so likewise show obedience and reverence in all things to this Pontiff.

units.la: Papæ ut omnes Romani obediant in Ecclesiasticis, tanquam suo Episcopo.
units.tr: That all Romans obey the Pope in ecclesiastical matters, as their own bishop.

units.la: DECRETA COMITIORUM IMPERIALIUM, Pro confirmanda Libertate Germanica & Gallicana contra Lotharii Cesaris & Gregorii IV. Papæ machinationes in Ludovicum Pium Imperatorem.
units.tr: DECREES OF THE IMPERIAL ASSEMBLIES, for confirming German and Gallican liberty against the machinations of the Emperor Lothar and Pope Gregory IV against the Emperor Louis the Pious.

units.la: Papirius Massonus JC. in Synopsi vitæ & doctrinæ Agobardi Lugdunensis Episcopi.
units.tr: Papirius Masson, JC, in his Synopsis of the life and teaching of Agobard, Bishop of Lyons.

units.la: Defectio Lotharii abripuerat omnem pene Italiam, Pontificem, multosq; etiam Episcopos Gallos, quorum opera Patri eripere Imperium. Veri Galli recalcitrant, citant Agobardum; recusat. Habent conventum; cujus hæc fuerunt Capita, adversum ipsius contumaciam, pro confirmanda Gallicana Libertate.
units.tr: The revolt of Lothar had carried off almost all of Italy, the Pope, and also many Gallic bishops, by whose work they snatched the empire from the father. The true Gauls kick back and summon Agobard; he refuses. They hold an assembly, whose heads were these, against his obstinacy, for confirming Gallican liberty.

units.la: EPISCOPUM Romanum, vocandum Papam, Fratrem, non autem Patrem, neque Summum Pontificem.
units.tr: The Roman bishop is to be called Pope, Brother, but not Father, nor Supreme Pontiff.

units.la: 2. Imperialem Majestatem plus posse in administranda Ecclesia, quàm Pontificiam.
units.tr: 2. The imperial majesty has more power in administering the Church than the papal.

units.la: 3. Cæsarem non dehonestandum præsumptuosa excommunicatione.
units.tr: 3. The Emperor is not to be dishonoured by presumptuous excommunication.

units.la: 4. Posse unum aliquem Pontificem abjici sine injuria Sedis Apostolicæ.
units.tr: 4. One Pope may be deposed without injury to the Apostolic See.

units.la: 5. Episcopos in causa Fidei jusjurandum præstare solitos Imperatori.
units.tr: 5. Bishops are accustomed to render an oath to the Emperor in a matter of faith.

units.la: 6. Agobardum Primatem Aquitaniæ, nullam deinceps habiturum potestatem in excommunicando, nullamque jurisdictionem in cæteras Parochias, si obedire potius Pontifici quàm Cæsari.
units.tr: 6. Agobard, Primate of Aquitaine, shall henceforth have no power in excommunicating, and no jurisdiction over the other parishes, if he obeys the Pope rather than the Emperor.

units.la: 7. Privandum Episcopum consortio & honore, qui potius Pontifici quàm Ecclesiæ Gallicanæ Concilio obedierit.
units.tr: 7. A bishop who has obeyed the Pope rather than the council of the Gallican Church is to be deprived of fellowship and honour.

units.la: LUDOVICI PII IMPER. AUG. SACRA
units.tr: Sacred Writings of Louis the Pious, Emperor Augustus

units.la: De Colligendis & transferendis S. Dionysii monumentis.
units.tr: On the gathering and transferring of the relics of St. Dionysius.

units.la: IN nomine Domini Dei & Salvatoris nostri Jesu Christi, Ludovicus divina propitiante clementia Imperator Augustus Hilduino venerabili Abbati monasterii sanctissimorum Martyrum ac specialium protectorum Dionysii pretiosi, sociorumq; ejus, æternam in Christo salutem.
units.tr: In the name of the Lord God and our Saviour Jesus Christ, Louis, by the merciful favour of God Emperor Augustus, to Hilduin, the venerable abbot of the monastery of the most holy martyrs and special protectors, Dionysius the precious and his companions, eternal salvation in Christ.

units.la: 1. quantum muneris atq; præsidii non modò nobis ac prædecessoribus, seu progenitoribus nostris, verum etiam totius Imperii nostri populis, Domini providentia, per beatissimum Dionysium sæpenumero, immò continuè in magnis gratiarum ubertatibus contulerit, cunctæ per transacta tempora Gallicæ nationes senserunt, quæ ejus insigni Apostolatu Fidei rudimenta sumpserunt. Prædecessores autem nostri gloriam hujus eximii testis & amici Dei non inaniter coluerunt: qui dum ejus sacras exuvias in terris ob amorem & honorem Domini nostri Jesu Christi, opibus, quibus poterant, honoraverunt: per ejus preces dignissimas, honoris privilegio potiri & in terris, & cælestibus meruerunt. Ut videlicet unus ex priscis Francorum Regibus Dagobertus, qui eumdem pretiosissimum Christi Martyrem veneratus non mediocriter fuerat, & immortali est vita sublimatus, & per ejus adjutorium (sicut divina ac cælestis ostensio perhibet) à pœnis est liberatus, inque vita perenni desiderabiliter constitutus.
units.tr: 1. How much of service and protection the Lord, by the providence of the most blessed Dionysius, has bestowed again and again, indeed continually, in great abundance of graces, not only upon us and our predecessors or forefathers, but also upon the peoples of our whole Empire, all the Gallic nations have experienced through the ages past, which received the first elements of the faith through his distinguished apostolate. Our predecessors, moreover, did not vainly honour the glory of this outstanding witness and friend of God: for while they honoured his sacred relics on earth out of love and reverence for our Lord Jesus Christ, with whatever resources they had, they merited, through his most worthy prayers, to obtain the privilege of honour both on earth and in heaven. Thus, for example, Dagobert, one of the ancient kings of the Franks, who had venerated that most precious martyr of Christ not a little, was raised up to immortal life, and through his help (as a divine and heavenly vision attests) was freed from punishments and placed in eternal life, longed for.

units.la: 2. Progenitores quoq; nostri mellifluum nomen Domini Dionysii (sic enim verbis & scriptis suis cum appellare consuevere) non incongruè pia dilectione & dilectissima pietate amplexi sunt. Quia proavus noster Carolus Princeps Francorum inclytus, per orationes ipsius excellentissimi Martyris indeptum se fuisse gratulatus est apicem Principatus, eidemque decursu mortalitatis tempore, quod carnus potuit habere depositum, corpus scilicet proprium in magni dei judicii suscitandum, & animam Domino præsentandam fideliter commendavit, ac pro hoc maximè devotionem atq; fiduciam cordis sui erga peculiarem patronum patenter ostendit.
units.tr: 2. Our forefathers also embraced the honeyed name of the Lord Dionysius (for so they were accustomed to call him in their words and writings) with pious affection and most loving devotion, and not without reason. For our great-grandfather Charles, the illustrious prince of the Franks, rejoiced that through the prayers of this most excellent martyr he had obtained the summit of princely power, and he faithfully commended to him, at the close of his mortal course, the part of himself that he could best entrust, namely his own body, to be raised at the great judgment of God, and his soul, to be presented to the Lord; and in this he openly showed his particular devotion and trust of heart towards his special patron.

units.la: 3. Sanctæ nihilominus recordationis avus noster Pipinus, propter altare, quod ante sepulchrum sæpè sepè fati, sæpiusq; dicendi domini Dionysii, per divinam & memorabilem revelationem, jussu ipsius sanctissimi Martyris, in honorem Dei & Apostolorum Petri & Pauli, qui præsentes ostendebantur, à beato & Angelico viro Stephano summo Pontifice dedicatum est, intrà sacra Missarum solemnia, unà cum duobus filiis Carolomanno videlicet & divæ memoriæ domino ac genitore nostro Carolo, jure prænominato Magno, ab eodem Apostolico Papa in Regem Francorum unctus superni inneris benedictionem percepit. Quiq; cùm quanta se humilitate ante limina basilicæ SS. Martyrum, defuncto ipsius vitæ curriculo, sepeliri præceperit, titulus etiam ipsius conditorii innotescit.
units.tr: 3. Likewise our grandfather Pepin, of holy memory, received the blessing of heavenly grace, being anointed King of the Franks, within the solemn celebration of Mass, together with his two sons, Carloman and our lord and father Charles, of blessed memory, who is rightly called the Great, by the same Apostolic Pope. This was on account of the altar, dedicated in honour of God and of the Apostles Peter and Paul, who were shown present, before the tomb of the lord Dionysius, often mentioned and often to be mentioned, through a divine and memorable revelation, by command of that most holy martyr himself, and dedicated by the blessed and angelic man Stephen, the supreme Pontiff. And when, at the end of his earthly course, he gave orders to be buried, with such humility, before the threshold of the basilica of the Holy Martyrs, the inscription of his tomb is also made known.

units.la: 4. Sed & nos multis ac frequentibus largitionibus beneficia ejus sumus experti, præcipuè tamen in humanæ varietatis eventu, quo Dei (ut semper farendum est) justo judicio in virga eruditionis suæ visitari & baculo speciosæ misericordiæ ejus ante præscriptum altare per merita & solatium domini ac piissimi patris nostri Dionysii virtute divinâ erecti & restituti sumus, cingulumq; militare judicio atq; auctoritate Episcopali resumpsimus, & utq; ad præsens ipsius gratioso adjutorio sustentamur.
units.tr: 4. We too have experienced his benefits in many and frequent bounties, especially in the event of human vicissitude, when, by the just judgment of God (as must always be said), we were visited with the rod of his correction and, by the staff of his lovely mercy, were raised up and restored, through the merits and comfort of the lord and most pious father of ours, Dionysius, by divine power, before the altar aforesaid; and we took up again the military belt by episcopal judgment and authority, and are still sustained by his gracious help.

units.la: 5. Idcirco, venerabilis cultos ac cultor ipsius provisoris & adjutoris nostri domini Dionysii, monere te volumus, ut quicquid de ejus notitia ex Græcorum historiis per interpretationem sumprum, vel quod ex libris ab eo patrio sermone conscriptis, & auctoritaris nostræ jussione, ac tuo sagaci studio, interpretumq; sudore in nostram linguam explicatis, huic negotio inseri fuerit congruum; quodque etiam Latinis codicibus jam inde habes inventum, adjunctis eis quæ in libello ejus passionis continentur, nec non illis quæ in tomis vel chartis vetustissimis armarii Parisiacæ Ecclesiæ, sacræ videlicet sedis suæ prolatis inveneras, & obtutibus nostræ serenitatis ostenderas, secundùm quod rerum, causarum etiam & temporum convenientiam noveris: in corpus unum redigas, atq; uniformem textum exinde componas; quatenùs devotis compendiosius valeat innotescï, & fastidiosis minusve capacibus vel studiosis lectionis possit tædium sublevari, pariterq; omnibus ædificationis utilitas proviæderi.
units.tr: 5. Therefore, venerable worshipper and devotee of Lord Dionysius, our provider and helper, we wish to admonish you that whatever is suitable to be inserted into this business from the knowledge of him drawn from Greek histories by translation, or from books written by him in his native tongue and explained in our language by our authority, by your wise diligence and the labour of translators, and whatever you have already found in Latin codices, together with those things which are contained in the little book of his passion, as well as those things which you have found and shown to our serenity in the very ancient volumes or papers of the cabinet of the Church of Paris, namely of his own holy see, you are to reduce into one body and compose from them a uniform text, according to your knowledge of the fitness of things, causes and times; so that it may be known more conveniently to the devout, and the tedium of the fastidious, less capable, or studious readers may be relieved, and the benefit of edification may be provided for all alike.

units.la: 6. His ita contextis, volumus ut revelationem ostensam beato Papæ Stephano in Ecclesia ejusdem sanctissimi Dionysii, sicut ab eo dictata est, & gesta quæ eidem subnixa sunt, unà cum hymnis, quos de gloriosissimo Martyre atq; Pontifice habes, & officium nocturnale subjungas. Sed & dissererer ac cum integritate tua quæcumq; ex eo reperta sunt, in altero volumine colligas; nobisq; diligenter & correctè transcripta quantocyus dirigas, aut præsentes: quoniam maximum, valdeque dulcissimum pignus desiderabilis præsentiæ illius domini & solatiatoris nostri, ubicumq; simus, habere nos credimus, si cum eo, vel de eo, aut ab eo dictis, oratione, collatione, lectione colloquimur. Vale in Christo vir Dei, in sacris orationibus jugiter memor nostri.
units.tr: 6. Having thus assembled these materials, we wish you to add to them the revelation shown to the blessed Pope Stephen in the church of the same most holy Dionysius, as it was related by him, and the deeds which are attached to it, together with the hymns which you have concerning the most glorious martyr and pontiff, and the nocturnal office. Also, whatever has been found concerning him, with its integrity, you are to gather into a second volume and send to us as quickly as possible, carefully and correctly transcribed, or bring it yourself; for we believe that, wherever we may be, we have a very great and most sweet pledge of the desired presence of that lord and comforter of ours, when we speak with him, or about him, or with words spoken by him, in prayer, conference or reading. Farewell in Christ, man of God, ever mindful of us in holy prayers.

units.la: EX EDICTIS PIISSIMORUM IMPERATORUM
units.tr: EX EDICTIS PIISSIMORUM IMPERATORUM

units.la: De electione Episcopi.
units.tr: On the election of a bishop.

units.la: JURENT majores civitatis ad Evangelia de persona electa ad Episcopatum, quòd neq; uxorem habuerit procertam, neq; concubinam, neq; sit curialis vel taxiota; sed sanctus & literarus, & Canonicas leges intelligens, & in Clero vel Monasterio nutritus, & tunc ordinetur. Sin autem hi, qui debent Episcopū eligere, talia decreta intra sex menses non fecerint, tunc Metropolitanus propter periculum animæ suæ omnibus his exquisitis, quæ diximus, ordinet & consecret sua potestate clero & populis Episcopum.
units.tr: Let the greater men of the city swear on the Gospels concerning the person chosen to the episcopate, that he has neither a lawful wife nor a concubine, that he is neither a member of the curia nor a taxiota; but that he is holy and learned, understands the canonical laws, and has been brought up in the clergy or in a monastery; and then let him be ordained. But if those who ought to elect the bishop have not made such decrees within six months, then the Metropolitan, on account of the peril to his own soul, shall ordain and consecrate a bishop for the clergy and people by his own authority, with all these requirements which we have mentioned having been sought out.

units.la: Nescio, an Ludovicum & Lotharium intelligat quanquam stilus non sapiat hanc ætatem Francicam, sed priscos illos Imperatores redoleat. vide l. 53. in pr. C. de Episcop. & Cleric. Novel. 123. c. 15.
units.tr: I do not know whether he means Ludovicus and Lotharius, although the style does not smack of this Frankish age but breathes of those ancient emperors. See l. 53 in pr. C. de Episcop. & Cleric., and Novel. 123, c. 15.

units.la: LOTHARII I. IMP. AUG. EDICTUM
units.tr: THE EDICT OF LOTHAR I, AUGUSTUS EMPEROR

units.la: DE RESTITUTIONE ARCHIEPISCOPI IN SEDEM ET DIOE- CESIM SUAM EX CRIMINE INFIDELITATIS AMISSAM.
units.tr: CONCERNING THE RESTORATION OF THE ARCHBISHOP TO HIS SEE AND DIOCESE, WHICH HE HAD LOST THROUGH THE CRIME OF INFIDELITY.

units.la: IN nomine Domini nostri Jesu Christi Dei æterni: Lotharius divina ordinante providentia Imperator Augustus. Quia confessio delictorum non minus in adversis necessaria est, quàm in prosperis, & cor contritum & humiliatū Deus nō despicit; gaudium etiam esse Angelorum, in cælo super uno peccatore pœnitentiam agente non dubitamus: Nos mortales in terris eos nequaquam despicimus, pro quibus gaudere Angelos in cælo, divino testimonio, non ignoramus. Accusantes & reprehendentes in excessibus semetipsos divina nos benignitas non condemnare, sed recreare docuit, qui meretricem non solùm à legali damnatione eripuit; verùm etiam publicanum humiliarum & accusantem se non condemnavit; sed magis justificando exaltavit. qui non dixit, omnis qui se humiliat condemnabitur, sed exaltabitur. Potestatem ergo, quam pro causa nostra raptus perditi, repetentibus Ecclesiæ tuæ filiis, præsentibus quoq;, adstantibus ac decernentibus Præsulibus, sedem ac diœcesim Remensis urbis tibi, Ebo, restituimus, ut pristino sanctæ largitatis Apostolicæ pallio indutus concordiam atq; gratiam divini officii a nobis, cum humili satisfactione expleta solemni nostra à largitate recipiendo exerceas.
units.tr: IN the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, the eternal God: Lothar, Emperor Augustus by the ordaining providence of God. Since the confession of sins is no less necessary in adversity than in prosperity, and God does not despise a contrite and humbled heart, we do not doubt that there is joy among the angels in heaven over one sinner doing penance. We mortals on earth by no means despise those for whom, as we know from the divine testimony, the angels rejoice in heaven. God's kindness, which accuses and reproves themselves for their excesses, has taught us not to condemn but to restore, for he rescued the harlot not only from legal condemnation, but also did not condemn the humbled publican who accused himself, but rather exalted him by justifying him. He did not say, "everyone who humbles himself will be condemned, but will be exalted." Therefore, the power which was seized by the lost for our cause, the sons of your Church demanding it back, and with the prelates present, standing by and deciding, we have restored the see and diocese of the city of Reims to you, Ebo, so that, clothed with the pallium of the former holy apostolic bounty, you may exercise the harmony and grace of the divine office, received from us with our solemn bounty, once humble satisfaction has been made.

units.la: Drogo Dtogo Episcopus Metensis Otgarius Archiepiscopus Hecti Archiepiscopus Amaluuinus Archiepiscopus Audax Atchiepiscopus Joseph Episcopus Adalulphus Episcopus David Episcopus Rodingus Episcopus Gifelbertus Episcopus Flotarius Episcopus Badaradus Episcopus Hagano Episcopus Hartgarius Episcopus Ado Episcopus Samuel Episcopus Rambertus Episcopus Haiminus Episcopus Ratoldus Presbytet vocatus Episcopus Amalricus vocatus Episcopus, cum caeteris plurimis Presbyteris ac Diaconis publicè assistentibus. Actum in Engilenheim palatio publico, in mense Junii, VIII. Kal. Julii, regnante & imperante Domino LOTHARIO Caesare, anno reversionis ejus primo cum esset successor factus patris in Francia, indictione III.
units.tr: Drogo, Dtogo, Bishop of Metz; Otgarius, Archbishop; Hecti, Archbishop; Amaluuinus, Archbishop; Audax, Archbishop; Joseph, Bishop; Adalulphus, Bishop; David, Bishop; Rodingus, Bishop; Gifelbertus, Bishop; Flotarius, Bishop; Badaradus, Bishop; Hagano, Bishop; Hartgarius, Bishop; Ado, Bishop; Samuel, Bishop; Rambertus, Bishop; Haiminus, Bishop; Ratoldus, the so-called elder, Bishop; Amalricus, the so-called bishop; with very many other elders and deacons publicly assisting. Done at the public palace at Engilenheim, in the month of June, on the 8th day before the Kalends of July, in the reign and under the rule of our Lord Lothar Caesar, in the first year of his return, when he had become successor to his father in Francia, indiction III.

units.la: LUDOVICI II. ET KAROLI II. REGUM AUGUSTORUM COMPOSITIO
units.tr: The Agreement of the Kings Louis II and Charles II, the August Kings

units.la: Pro tuenda Regnorum Germaniae & Galliae libertate contra usurpationem & oppressionem LOTHARII Imperatoris Romanorum, facta in Comitiis Argentinensibus, A. D. DCCCXLII.
units.tr: To defend the liberty of the kingdoms of Germany and France against the usurpation and oppression of Lothair, Emperor of the Romans, made at the Diet of Strasbourg, A.D. 842.

units.la: ERGO XVI. KAL. Martii HLODVVICUS & KAROLUS in civitate, quae olim Argentaria vocabatur, nunc autem Strazburg vulgò dicitur, convenerunt, & sacramento, quae subternotata sunt, HLODVVICUS Romana, KAROLUS verò Teudisca lingua juraverunt. Acta cum te sacramenta circumfusam plebem alter Teudisca, alter Romana allocuti sunt.
units.tr: So on the 14th day before the Kalends of March, Louis and Charles met in the city formerly called Argentaria and now commonly called Strasbourg, and swore the oaths written below: Louis swore in the Romance tongue, and Charles in the Teutonic tongue. When the oaths were completed, each addressed the surrounding people, one in Teutonic and the other in Romance.

units.la: 2. HLODVVICUS autem, quia major natu, prior exorsus sic coepit: Quotiens LOTHARIUS me & hunc fratrem meum post obitum patris nostri infestando usque ad internecionem delere conatus sit, nostis. Cùm autem nec fraternitas, nec Christianitas, nec quodlibet ingenium, salva justicia, ut pax inter nos esset, adjuvare posset, tandem coacti rem * ad judicium omnipotentis Dei delimus, ut suo nutu, quid cuiq; deberetur, contenti essemus. In quo nos, sicut nostis, per misericordiam Dei victores extitimus. Is autem victus unà cum suis, quò valuit, secessit. Hinc verò fraternoamore cotrepti, necnon & super populum Christianum compassi, persequi atq; delere illos noluimus, sed hactenus, sicut & antea, ut saltem deinde cuiq; sua justicia cederetur, mandavimus. At ille posthac non contentus judicio divino, sed hostili manu iterum & me & hunc fratrem meum persequi non cessat. Insuper & populum nostrum incendiis, rapinis, caedibusq; devastat. Quamobrem nunc necessitate coacti convenimus. Et quoniam vos de nostra stabili fide ac firma fraternitate dubitare creditis, hoc sacramentum inter nos in conspectu vestro jurate decrevimus. Non qualibet iniqua cupiditate illecti hoc agimus, sed ut certiores, si Deus nobis vestro adjutorio quietem dederit, de communi profectu simus. Si autem, quod absit, sacramentum, quod fratri meo juravero, violare praesumpseto, ab subditione mea, necnon & à juramento, quod mihi juraistis, unumquemque vestrum absolvo.
units.tr: 2. Louis, as the elder, began first and spoke thus: "You know how often Lothair has tried, since the death of our father, to destroy me and my brother here by harassing us to the point of annihilation. But since neither brotherly affection, nor Christian faith, nor any ingenuity could, with justice preserved, bring about peace between us, we were at last compelled to refer the matter to the judgement of almighty God, so that, by his will, each of us might be content with what was due to him. In this, as you know, we were made victors by the mercy of God. Lothair, however, defeated, withdrew with his men as far as he could. Then, moved by brotherly love and also taking pity on the Christian people, we did not want to pursue and destroy them, but up to now, as before, we have ordered that at least afterwards each should receive his right. But he, not content with the divine judgement, has not ceased to persecute both me and my brother here with hostile hand. Moreover, he lays waste our people with fires, plunder and slaughter. Therefore, now compelled by necessity, we have met. And since you believe that we may doubt our steadfast faith and firm brotherhood, we have decided to swear this oath between ourselves in your sight. We do this not led by any unjust desire, but so that, if God grants us quiet with your help, we may be more certain of our common advantage. But if, which God forbid, I should presume to violate the oath that I have sworn to my brother, I absolve each of you from your allegiance to me and from the oath that you have sworn to me."

units.la: 3. Cumq; KAROLUS haec eadem verba Romanâ linguâ peroraret, LODHVVICUS, quoniam major natu erat, prior haec deinde se servaturum testatus est: Pro don amur, & pro Xristian poblo, & nostro commun salvamēt, disi di en avant, in quant Deus savir & potir me dunat, si salvarai eo cest meon fradra KARLO, & in adjudha & in cadhuna cosa, si cum hom per dreit son fradra salvar dist, ino quid il imi altre si faret, & ab LUDHER nul plaid nunquam prindrat, qui meon vol cist meon fradre KARLE in damno sit.
units.tr: 3. When Charles had delivered these same words in the Romance tongue, Louis, since he was the elder, then first bore witness that he would keep them: "For the love of God, and for the Christian people, and for our common salvation, from this day forward, insofar as God grants me knowledge and power, I will support this my brother Charles, both in aid and in every matter, as a man ought by right to support his brother, provided that he does the same for me; and I will never enter into any agreement with Lothair which, by my will, would be to the harm of this my brother Charles."

units.la: 4. Quod cùm LODHVVICUS explesset, KAROLUS Teudisca lingua sic haec eadem verba testatus est: In Godes minna, ind durh tes Xristianes folches, ind unser bedhero gehaltnisse, son thesemo dage frammordes, so fram so mir Got gervizei indi mahd furgibit, so hald ih tesan minan bruodber ....... sofo man mit rehtu sinan bruoder scal, mithiu thaz er mig so fo maduo, indi mit LUTHEREM inno theimni thing ne gegango, zhe minan vvillon imo ce sf adhen vverhen.
units.tr: 4. When Louis had finished, Charles bore witness to these same words in the Teutonic tongue: "For the love of God, and for the sake of the Christian people and our common salvation, from this day forward, as far as God grants me knowledge and power, I will keep this my brother ....... as a man ought by right to keep his brother, provided that he does the same for me; and I will enter into no discussion with Lothair which, by my will, would be to the harm of my brother."

units.la: 5. Sacramentum autem, quod utrorumque populus quiq; propria lingua testatus est, 'Romanâ lingua sic se habet: Si Lodhuvigs sacrament, quæ son fratre Karlo jurat, conservat, & Karlus meo sendra de suo part non los tanit, si io returnar non lint pois, ne io, ne neuls cui eo returnar nit pois, in nulla adjudha contra Lodhuvig nun li iver.
units.tr: 5. The oath that the people of each side swore in their own tongue reads, in the Romance language: "If Louis keeps the oath which he swears to his brother Charles, and Charles, my lord, does not hold back on his part from it, if I cannot turn him from it, neither I nor anyone whom I can turn from it will in any way give aid against Louis."

units.la: 6. Teudiscaautem lingua: Oba Karl then eid, then er sinemo bruodher Ludhuvig egesuor, geleistit, inde Ludhuvig nun herro, then er imo gesuor, forbrichit, ob ih manes arvvenden nemag, noh ih, noh thero thein her arvvenden mag, imo ce follinsti vvidhar Karle ne vvrdin.
units.tr: 6. In the Teutonic tongue: "If Charles keeps the oath which he swore to his brother Louis, and Louis, my lord, breaks the oath which he swore to him, if I cannot turn him from it, nor can he whom I can turn from it, then I will not be against Charles in any way."

units.la: KAROLI. II. REGIS AUG. CONSTITUTIO
units.tr: Constitution of Charles II, King and Augustus

units.la: De rebus Ecclesiæ ablatis restituendis, & in posterum ad seculares usus non transferendis.
units.tr: On restoring the goods of the Church that were taken away, and on not transferring them again to secular uses in future.

units.la: IN nomine sanctæ & individuæ Trinitatis, Karolus Rex. Si ea, quæ à prædecessoribus nostris vel fidelium devotione bene tradita, statuta ac confirmata sunt, nostris oraculis roboramus; si etiam illa, quæcunque necessitate corrupta sunt, Regia nostra auctoritate corrigimus, & in melius commutamus, saluti nostræ consulimus, & Regum ministerium susceptum à Domino exercemus. Proinde noverit omnium fidelium Dei ac nostrorum solertia, quia res ex Episcopatu Remensi, quas magna necessitate, & per omnia invitus, dum à Pastore sancta sedes illa vacaret, fidelibus nostris ad tempus, unde temporale quoddam solatium in nostro haberent servitio, commendavimus, ordinato & electo, munere sancti Spiritus, per Dei & nostram dispositionem in eadem sancta Sede Hincmaro Archiepiscopo, hoc nostræ auctoritatis præcepto cum integritate, quidquid exinde nos fidelibus nostris beneficiavimus, præsentaliter restituimus, sive etiam illa omnia, quæ tam Clerici quàm Laici, qui in nostra dominatione aliquandiu fuerunt, quosque jam dicto Episcopo commendavimus habebant.
units.tr: In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Charles the King. If we confirm by our decrees those things which were well handed down and established and ratified by our predecessors or by the devotion of the faithful, and if we correct by our royal authority those things which have been corrupted by necessity and change them for the better, we are looking to our own salvation, and we exercise the ministry of kings which we have received from the Lord. Therefore let the diligence of all the faithful of God and of ours know that the properties of the Archbishopric of Reims, which out of great necessity, and quite against our will, we had committed for a time to our faithful men, so that they might have some temporal comfort in return for their service to us, while that holy see was vacant of its pastor, have now been restored in full by this precept of our authority, as soon as, by the gift of the Holy Spirit and by the arrangement of God and of ourselves, Hincmar was ordained and elected Archbishop in that same holy see; and likewise whatever we had granted from them as benefices to our faithful men, and also all those things which both clergy and laity who had been under our dominion for some time possessed, and which we had already committed to the said Bishop.

units.la: 2. Et, ut in calce omnia concludamus, quidquid ex eodem Episcopatu, quando de manu N.. illum recepimus, alicui præstito beneficio concessimus, per hanc nostræ confirmationis auctoritatem in conspectu Dei, coram coetu fidelium nostrorum tam Ecclesiastici quàm laicalis ordinis, restamento præsentaliter calæ S. Mariæ & S. Remigii, atque Hincmaro Archiepiscopo, cum omni integritate reddimus vel restituimus, ut absque ulla refragatione cassatis quibuscunque aliis conscriptionibus easdem res per hanc nostram auctoritatem recipiat, ut, sicut res Ecclesiæ Dei, tam ipse quàm successores ipsius disponant.
units.tr: 2. And, to sum up everything at the end: whatever from the same Bishopric, since we received it from the hand of N., we have granted to anyone as a benefice, we now, by this authority of our confirmation, in the sight of God and before the assembly of our faithful men of both the ecclesiastical and the lay order, give back and restore in full to the church of St. Mary and St. Remigius, and to Archbishop Hincmar, with complete integrity, by the restitution of this present charter; so that, with all other writings set aside without any objection, he may receive the same properties by this our authority, and that he, as well as his successors, may dispose of them as the goods of the Church of God.

units.la: 3. Quam auctoritatem, in qua nos ulterius tale quiddam erga ipsam casam Dei non acturos spondemus, &, ut nemo successorum nostrorum agere moliatur, per omnipotentem Dominum ejusdem Virginis filium obsecramus, ut per ventura tempora certior habeatur, & contra æmulos ipsius Ecclesiæ sui noticia valeat, manu nostra subter firmavimus, & annuli nostri impressione roboravimus decrevimus. Data Kal. Octobris, anno VI. regnante Karolo glorioso Rege, Indictione VIII. Actum in pago Andegavensi in villa N...
units.tr: 3. We pledge that we shall not in any further way act against that house of God in such a manner, and, so that none of our successors may attempt to do so, we beseech, through the almighty Lord, the Son of that same Virgin, that for times to come it may be held more securely and that its knowledge may be a safeguard for the Church against its adversaries. We have confirmed this with our own hand below and strengthened it with the impression of our ring, and have decreed it. Given on the Kalends of October, in the sixth year of the reign of Charles the glorious King, in the eighth indiction. Done in the district of Anjou, in the village of N...

units.la: LUDOVICI. II. REGIS AUG. ET POSTEA III. IMP. ROM. DECRETUM
units.tr: THE DECREE OF LUDWIG II, KING AND AUGUSTUS, AND AFTERWARDS OF THE THIRD EMPEROR OF ROME

units.la: Comitiorum Moguntinensium, de Anno DCCCL.
units.tr: Of the Assembly of Mainz, concerning the year 850.
