units.la: LUdovicus maximum Concilium sacratorum & prophanorum Moguntiaci cogit. Singulorum controversiæ auditæ, causæ cognitæ, lites dirempta sunt. Pax per universam Germaniam jurejurando firmata. Inter fuere Bulgarorum, Sclavorum Legati.
units.tr: Ludwig held a great council of the sacred and secular men at Mainz. The disputes of individuals were heard, the causes examined, and the lawsuits settled. Peace was confirmed by oath throughout all Germany. Envoys of the Bulgarians and of the Slavs were among those present.

units.la: ALIUD DECRETUM.
units.tr: ANOTHER DECREE.

units.la: IN Saxonia Conventum judicum ad amnem Visurgim agit, prædia Regia, quibus Procerum quidam incubabant, neq; quicquam tribuebant, recuperat, fiscoq; adjecit.
units.tr: In Saxony he held an assembly of judges at the river Weser, and recovered the royal estates, which certain nobles had occupied and paid nothing for, and he added them to the treasury.

units.la: Leges Saxonum emendat, Judices avaritia notatos, jura venditare, munera accipere solitos, albo Praetorum eradit, bona eorum confiscat, institutorum veterum atq; legum peritos, pecuniæ contemptores, provinciis juris dicundi præfecit.
units.tr: He amended the laws of the Saxons. Judges marked for greed, who were accustomed to sell justice and accept bribes, he struck from the list of praetors and confiscated their goods; in their place he set over the provinces men skilled in the ancient institutions and laws, who despised money.

units.la: DECRETUM COMITIORUM ERDFVRTENSIVM.
units.tr: DECREE OF THE ASSEMBLY OF ERFURT.

units.la: ERdfurdiæ apud Turogos Concilium gentis cogit. Ibi vetiti sunt Magistratus patrocinia vendere, aut cuiquam in sua Praefectura adesse. Diminuta sunt Causidicorum merces, quorum perfidia nihil venalius.
units.tr: At Erfurt, among the Thuringians, he held a council of the people. There it was forbidden for magistrates to sell their patronage, or to appear for anyone within their own jurisdiction. The fees of advocates were reduced, men whose treachery was nothing if not for sale.

units.la: LOTHARII. I. IMP. AUG. RESCRIPTUM
units.tr: LOTHAIR I, EMPEROR AUGUSTUS: A RESCRIPT

units.la: AD LEONEM IV. PAPAM DE PRESBYTERO ECCLESIAM suam relinquente per Papam citato ad Synodum.
units.tr: To Pope Leo IV, concerning the presbyter who left his church, summoned by the Pope to the Synod.

units.la: VESTRÆ denique Serenitatis industria cognoscat de a Anastasio Presbytero, cur ad vos noua pervenerit, nostro satis animo displicuisse: quem nunc per clarissimos Missos nostros, Ioseph videlicet reverendissimum b Episcopum, atque dilecti filii nostri Archicapellanum, necnon & Petrum sanctæ sedis Spoletinæ venerabilem Episcopum, & Aldegisum illustrem Comitem nostrum præsentialiter vobis misimus: quidquid canonicè & secundum Deum per illum vestra deliberaverit sententia, nihil contradicentes. Tantum solicitè cavere acprudenter tractare curate, ne hoc facto divina voluntas offendatur in aliquo.
units.tr: Let Your Serenity's diligence finally understand that the arrival of Anastasius the presbyter with you was, in our judgment, quite displeasing; we have now sent him to you in person through our distinguished envoys, namely the most reverend Bishop Joseph, our beloved son the Archchaplain, and also Peter, venerable Bishop of the holy see of Spoleto, and Aldegis, our illustrious Count. Whatever your judgment decides through him canonically and according to God, let it stand without objection from us. Only take care with all diligence and deal prudently, so that the divine will is not offended in any way by this act.

units.la: RECESSUS
units.tr: RECESS

units.la: COMITIORUM CONFLUENTA- NORUM, DE PACE PUBLICA, ET CONCOR- DIA INTER REGES FRANCORUM STABILITA,
units.tr: ## Of the Assemblies of Coblenz, concerning Public Peace and the Concord Established Between the Kings of the Franks

units.la: LUDOVICUM II. REGEM GERMANIARUM ET SCLAVONIARUM, CAROLUM II. Regem Galliarum, LUDOVICUM Imperatorem Romanorum & Regem Longobardorum, LOTHARIUM REGEM Lotharingiæ, & CAROLUM Regem Burgundiæ ac Provinciæ.
units.tr: Louis II, king of the Germans and Slavs; Charles II, king of the Franks; Louis, emperor of the Romans and king of the Lombards; Lothar, king of Lotharingia; and Charles, king of Burgundy and Provence.

units.la: HÆC sunt nomina Episcoporum, qui Anno Incarnationis Dominicæ octingentesimo sexagesimo, Nonis Junii, in Secretario basilicæ S. Castoris considerarunt cum Nobilibus Laicis hæmitatem, quam gloriosissimi Reges nostri Ludovicus, Carolus, atque Lotharius inter se secerunt octavo Idus Junii in eodem Monasterio, & qui hæc capitula ab omnibus observanda acceptarunt. Hincmarus, Theudericus, Juntherius, Leutbertus, Alefridus, Gedebartus, Salomon, Christianus, Adventius, Vulfadus Abbas, Atto, Witgarius Abbas Hæc nomina Laicorum: Conradus, *Exstangarius, Luitharius, Everhardus, Arnulphus, Luthardus, Vicarnarius, Berengarius, Hunfriardus, Leuthulphus, Rithuenus, Adalbertus, Hernodulphus, Bernoldus, Sigeri, Adalardus, Burchardus, Harmainus, Luitfridus, Hessi, Wigricus, Gislebertus, Arnustus, Atto, Huto, Hynodulphus, Christianus, Matfridus, Ratbotus, Herimannus, Bofo, item Chuanradus, Sigardus.
units.tr: These are the names of the bishops who, in the year of the Lord's Incarnation 860, on the Nones of June, met in the secretary of the basilica of St Castor together with the lay nobles to consider the partition which our most glorious kings Louis, Charles and Lothar had made between themselves on the eighth day before the Ides of June in the same monastery, and who accepted these chapters to be observed by all: Hincmar, Theuderic, Juntherius, Leutbert, Alefrid, Gedebart, Solomon, Christian, Adventius, Abbot Vulfad, Atto, Abbot Witgar. These are the names of the laymen: Conrad, *Exstangar, Luithar, Everhard, Arnulf, Luthard, Vicarnar, Berengar, Hunfriard, Leuthulf, Rithuen, Adalbert, Hernodulf, Bernold, Sigeri, Adalard, Burchard, Harmain, Luitfrid, Hessi, Wigric, Gislebert, Arnust, Atto, Huto, Hynodulf, Christian, Matfrid, Ratbot, Herimann, Bofo; likewise Chuanrad and Sigard.

units.la: * Archangelsius.
units.tr: * Archangelsius.

units.la: 1. Ludovicus & Rex Carolus frater ejus, nepos que eorum Lotharius cum primatibus suis in Confluenta castello convenientes, pacem inter se & fidelitatem mutuam singuli juramento confirmarunt, cujus sacramenti series hujusmodi fuit: Amodo & quamdiu vixero, illum fratrem meum Carolum, & nepotes meos Ludovicum & Lotharium atque Carolum, ad Dei voluntatem & sanctæ Ecclesiæ statum & honorem atque defensionem, & ad nostram communem salutem & honorem, & ad populi Christiani nobis commissi salvamentum & pacem, & ad legis & justitiæ & rectæ rationis conservationem (quantum mihi Dominus scire & posse donaverit, & ipsi me obaudierint) vero consilio, & secundum quod mihi rationabiliter & salubriter possibile fuerit, recipiens, sincero auxilio adjutor ero ad regnum illorum continendum, & nec in vita, nec in membris, neque in regno illorum eos forsconsiliabo in hoc, ut ipsi erga me similem promissionem faciant, & conservent, sicme Deus adjuvet & istæ sanctæ reliquiæ.
units.tr: 1. King Louis and his brother King Charles, and their nephew Lothar, meeting with their chief men at the castle of Coblenz, each confirmed by oath the peace and mutual fidelity between them. The form of this oath was as follows: "From now on, and as long as I live, I will help that brother of mine Charles, and my nephews Louis and Lothar and Charles, in sincere aid, for the will of God, for the state and honour and defence of the holy Church, for our common welfare and honour, for the safety and peace of the Christian people committed to us, and for the preservation of law, justice and right reason (as far as the Lord shall grant me to know and to be able, and as they shall obey me), receiving their counsel, and as far as it shall be reasonably and profitably possible for me to keep their kingdom; and neither in their life, nor in their limbs, nor in their kingdom will I plot against them; and I will ensure that they make and keep a similar promise to me, so help me God and these holy relics."

units.la: 2. Ut omnium præteritorum malorum, & contrarietatum, & supplantationum, atq; malarum machimachinationum, atque molitionum, seu nocumentorum invicem actorum abolitio, ita inter nos & apud nos fiat, & à nostris cordibus penitus avellatur communi malitia & rancore, & nec in memoriam ad retribuendum duntaxat mali, vel contrarietatis, atq; exprobrationis, seu improperii de cetero exinde quidquam veniat.
units.tr: 2. That the abolition of all past evils, oppositions, plots, wicked machinations and schemes, or injuries done to one another, be made between us and among us in this way, and be utterly torn from our hearts, along with common malice and rancour; and that nothing from now on arise from them, neither in memory, for the sole purpose of repaying evil, opposition, reproach or insult.

units.la: 3. Ut tanta inter nos, Domino cooperante, verae charitatis benignitas abhinc inante semper manet de corde puro, conscientia bona, & fide non ficta, sine dolo & simulatione, ut nemo suo fratri suum regnum, aut suos fideles, & quod ad salutem sive prosperitatem ac honorem Regum pertinet, discupiat, aut forconsiliet, aut per occultos susurrones libenter composita mendacia seu detractiones acceptet.
units.tr: 3. That, with the Lord's cooperation, such a degree of true charity among us shall always remain from now on, from a pure heart, a good conscience and unfeigned faith, without deceit or pretence, so that no one desires his brother's kingdom or his faithful subjects, or whatever pertains to the safety, prosperity and honour of kings, nor plots against them, nor willingly accepts invented lies or slanders from secret whisperers.

units.la: 4. Ut unusquisq; fideliter suum fratrem, ubicūq; necessitas illi fuerit, & ipse potuerit, aut per se, aut per filium, aut per fideles suos & consilio & auxilio adjuvet, ut regnum fidele, prosperitatem, atq; honorem regium debitè valeat obtinere; & veraciter unusquisq; erga alterum certatim demonstret, quia in fratris sui adversitate, si sic venerit, fraterno modo contristetur, & in prosperitate illius laetetur; & talem fidem sicut inter nos modò abhinc inante conservaturos confirmatū habemus, sic unusquisque infantibus fratris sui, si obierit, qui superfuerit, conservabit.
units.tr: 4. That each one faithfully help his brother, wherever need arises for him and he is able to do so, whether in person, through his son, or through his faithful men, by counsel and by aid, so that his brother may properly obtain his faithful kingdom, prosperity and royal honour; and that each one, in truth, strive to show towards the other that, if adversity comes upon his brother, he will be saddened in brotherly fashion, and rejoice in his prosperity. And we hold it confirmed that, just as we shall keep such faith among ourselves from now on, so each one shall keep it towards the children of his brother, if he dies, to whichever of them survives.

units.la: 5. Et quia per vagos & tyrannica consuetudine incuentes homines pax & tranquillitas regni perturbari solet: volumus, ut si ad quemcumq; nostrum talis venerit, ut in his quae egit, rationem ac justitiam subterfugere non possit, nemo ex nobis illum ad aliud recipiat & retineat, nisi ut ad rectam rationem & debitam emendationem perducatur. Et si rationem recta subterfugerit, omnes in commune, in cujus regnum venit, illum persequantur, donec ad rationem perducatur, aut de regno deleatur. Similiter de eo agendum est, qui pro aliquo capitulo & publico crimine à quolibet Episcopo corripitur & excommunicatur, aut de excommunicatione crimen faciens, regnum & Regis regimen mutat, ne debitam poenitentiam suscipiat, ut suscep tam legitimè peragat; interdum etiam incestam propinquā suam, aut sanctimonialem, & raptam, sive adulteram, quam illi ei non licebat habere, fugiens secum duxit: hic talis cùm Episcopus, ad cujus curam pertinebit, nobis notū fecerit, diligenter perquiratur, ne morandi & latitādi locum in regno alicujus nostrum inveniat, & Dei ac nostros fideles suo morbo inficiat, sed à nobis & ministris Reipub. constringatur, ut & simul cum diabolica praeda, quam secum duxit, ad Episcopum suum redeat, & de quocumq; crimine publico poenitentiam, ut suscep tam legitimè peragat, compellatur.
units.tr: 5. Since the peace and tranquillity of the kingdom are usually disturbed by vagrant men and by those who bring in a tyrannical custom, we will that if any such man comes to any one of us, and cannot escape reason and justice for what he has done, none of us shall receive and retain him for any other purpose than that he be brought to right reason and due amendment. And if he flees from right reason, all of us in common, in whose kingdom he has come, shall pursue him until he is brought to reason or is driven from the kingdom. The same is to be done with one who, for some chapter offence or public crime, is rebuked and excommunicated by any bishop, or who, making a crime of his excommunication, changes kingdom and royal government so as not to undergo the penance due; and sometimes also with one who, fleeing, has carried off with him an incestuous kinswoman, or a nun, or a woman seized or adulterous, whom he was not permitted to have. When the bishop in whose care such a man falls has made him known to us, let him be diligently sought out, lest he find a place to stay and hide in the kingdom of any of us, and infect God's and our faithful people with his disease; but let him be constrained by us and by the ministers of the commonwealth, so that he may return, together with the diabolical prey he has carried off with him, to his bishop, and be compelled to perform legitimately the penance for whatever public crime he has committed."

units.la: 6. Ut nemo Episcoporum hominem peccantem ab Ecclesia Christiana alienet, donec illum secundum Evangelicum praeceptum, ut ad emendationem & poenitentiam redeat, cōmonitum habeat. Qui peccans si commonitus inobediens & incorrigibilis permanserit, & ad emendationem redire noluerit, Regiam & Reip. potestatem per se ipsos & per ministros suos adeant, ut constringatur, & ad emendationem & poenitentiam peccator redeat. Qui etiam si ita ad correctionem perduci nequiverit, tunc secundum leges Ecclesiasticas medicinali separatione communionis Ecclesiasticae segregetur.
units.tr: 6. That no bishop shall alienate from the Christian Church a man who sins, until he has admonished him, according to the evangelical precept, to return to amendment and repentance. If the sinner, having been admonished, remains disobedient and incorrigible, and refuses to return to amendment, let the bishops approach the royal and civil power, either in person or through their ministers, so that he may be constrained and the sinner may return to amendment and repentance. And if he cannot be brought to correction in this way, then, according to the ecclesiastical laws, he is to be separated from the communion of the Church by the medicinal sentence of excommunication.

units.la: 7. Ut illis hominibus, qui in talibus perturbationibus (sicut in his praeteritis annis accidit) in Deū & in sanctam Ecclesiam atq; in eos peccaverunt, si ex veritate recognoscentes veniam petierint, & deinceps nobis veraciter fideles esse voluerint, & in regnis nostris pacifici & quieti, & legibus ac justitiae obedientes extiterint, rationabilis misericordia impendatur, non solum in indulgentia commissorum & in concessione proprietatum, verum etiam & in largitione honorum secundum nostram rationabilem possibilitatem.
units.tr: 7. That, to those men who in such disturbances (as happened in the past years) have sinned against God, the holy Church and those persons, if they acknowledge the truth, seek pardon, and wish from now on to be truly faithful to us, and have been peaceful and quiet in our kingdoms and obedient to the laws and justice, reasonable mercy be shown, not only in the forgiveness of their offences and the restoration of their property, but also in the bestowal of honours, according to our reasonable ability.

units.la: 8. Ut de rapinis ac depraedationibus, & de conspirationibus, ac seditionibus, & de raptis foeminarum, sicut Ecclesiasticae & Christianae leges atq; progenitorum Capitula continent, ita in omnibus & ab omnibus conserventur.
units.tr: 8. That concerning robberies and plunderings, and concerning conspiracies and seditions, and concerning the abduction of women, the ecclesiastical and Christian laws and the chapters of our forefathers be preserved in all things and by all, as they contain.

units.la: 9. Ut alia etiam Capitula eorundem progenitorum nostrorum de sanctae Ecclesiae honore & immunitate ac conservatione, & de Regis etiam honore, & populi nobis commissi lege & justitia in omnibus & ab omnibus conserventur.
units.tr: 9. That the other chapters of the same forefathers of ours concerning the honour, immunity and preservation of the holy Church, and likewise concerning the honour of the king and the law and justice owed to the people committed to us, be preserved in all things and by all.

units.la: 10. Ut nostri fideles unusquisq; in suo ordine & statu veraciter sint de nobis securi, quia nullum abhinc inante contra legem, justitiam, & auctoritatem, ac justam rationem aut damnabimus, aut dehonorabimus, aut opprimemus, & indebitis machinationibus affligemus, sed illorū scilicet veraciter nobis fidelium communi consilio, secundum Dei voluntatem & commune salvamentū, ad restitutionem sanctae Dei Ecclesiae, & ad statum regni, & ad honorem Regium, atq; pacem populi commissi pertinenti assensum praebebimus in hoc, ut non illi solùm non sint nobis contradicentes & resistentes ad ista consequenda verum etiam sic sint nobis fideles & obedientes, ac veri adjutores atq; cooperatores vero consilio atq; sincero auxilio ad ista peragenda quae praemisimus, licut per rectum in suo ordine ac statu suo Principi & Seniori esse debent.
units.tr: 10. That each of our faithful men, in his own rank and station, may truly feel secure with regard to us, because from now on we will not condemn, dishonour or oppress anyone contrary to law, justice, authority and right reason, nor afflict them with unjust machinations; but we will give our assent, with the common counsel of those of our faithful men who truly belong to this, according to the will of God and the common welfare, to the restoration of the holy Church of God, the state of the kingdom, the royal honour and the peace of the people committed to us, on the condition that they not only do not contradict or resist us in attaining these things, but are also faithful and obedient to us, and true helpers and co-workers in carrying out, by sound counsel and sincere aid, the things we have set forth, just as they ought to be to a rightful prince and lord in their own rank and station.

units.la: 11. Ut sic simul & conjuncti & nos fratres & nepos nostri ad invicem, & nos cum fidelibus nostris, & fideles nostri nobilcum, & omnes simul cum Deo nos conjungamus, & ut nobis sit propitius, illi pro devoto munere offeramus, & unusquisq; omnium nostrum absq; sua propria excusatione & justificatione recognoscamus, in quibus aut sigillatim, aut communiter, aut contra illius mandata, & decreta suorum Sanctorum fecimus, aut consensimus in ordine Ecclesiastico & statu regni, & per singula in medium illa producamus; & nemo nostrum suo aut amico aut propinquo & confoederato, immo nec sibi ipsi saeculariter parcat, ut spiritualiter & salubriter parcere possit; quoniam, sicut praemisimus in praecedenti capitulo, vero consilio & sincero auxilio illa in commune certatim emendari totis viribus procuremus, quantocyus rationabiliter poterimus. 11. Et si aliquis de subditis in quocunq; ordine & statu de hac convenientia exierit, aut se tetraxerit, & huic communi decreto cōtradixerit; Seniores cum veraciter fidelibus suis hanc secundum Dei voluntatem & legem & justam rationem, velit nolit ille, qui divino consilio & decreto, & huic convenientiæ resistens & contradicens fuerit, exequantur. Et si aliquis de Senioribus de hac convenientia exierit, aut se tetraxerit, & huic communi decreto (quod absit) contradixerit; complurium Seniorum nostrorum concilio, & Episcoporum judicio, ac communi consensu, qualiter de eo, qui debitè admonitus incorrigibilis perseveraverit, agendum sit, favente Domino decernatur, & ut obnixius suprascripta Capitula à nobis, auxiliante Domino inviolabiliter observentur, & nos illa observaturos ut certius credatur, manibus propriis subterfirmavimus.
units.tr: 11. So that we, together with our nephews and brothers, and we with our faithful men, and our faithful men with our nobles, and all of us together, may join ourselves to God, so that He may be gracious to us, and offer Him this as a devoted gift; and so that each one of us, without any excuse or self-justification, may acknowledge those things in which we have acted, either individually or collectively, against His commands and the decrees of His saints, or have consented to them, in the ecclesiastical order and in the state of the kingdom, and bring them forward one by one into the open. Let no one of us spare his kinsman, friend, or ally, or even himself in a worldly way, so that he may be able to spare in a spiritual and salutary way. For, as we said in the preceding chapter, we shall strive with all our strength, by true counsel and sincere aid, to have these things corrected in common, as quickly as we reasonably can. 11. And if any of the subjects, in any order or rank, departs from this agreement, or withdraws himself, and contradicts this common decree, the elders, together with their faithful men, shall enforce this according to the will of God, the law, and right reason, whether he wills it or not, against the one who, resisting and contradicting this agreement, has done so against the divine counsel and decree. And if any of the elders departs from this agreement, or withdraws himself, and (God forbid) contradicts this common decree, it shall be decided, by the favour of the Lord, by the counsel of several of our elders, the judgment of the bishops, and common consent, how one who, though duly admonished, persists incorrigibly, is to be dealt with. And so that the aforesaid chapters may be observed more earnestly and inviolably by us, with the Lord's help, and so that it may be more firmly believed that we shall observe them, we have confirmed them with our own hands.

units.la: ANNVNTIATIONES DOMNI LVDOVICI REGIS apud confluentem, lingua Theotisca.
units.tr: The announcements of Lord King Louis at Confluence, in the Teutonic language.

units.la: 13. Vos scitis, quid in isto Regno evenit. Et ideò huc convenimus, ut de Dei voluntate, & sanctæ ejus Ecclesiæ statu & nostra ac vestra communi salute & honore, & de pace populi Christiani cum Dei adjutorio & fidelium nostrorum consilio tractaremus. Et nimimus hoc super Episcopos & cæteros fideles nostros, ut illi hoc invenirent, qualiter nos ad hæc quæ diximus exequenda adunaremus. Et volumus ut sciatis, quia sicut illi invenerunt, & scripto nobis nunciaverunt, ad invicem adunati sumus, sicut fratres per rectum esse debent, & vos simul cum isto nepote nostro, & ille nobiscum, & etiam suos fratres & nepotes nostros in hac adunationis firmitate nobiscum tecepimus, ita tamen ut si ipsi hanc firmitatem erga nos fecerint & observaverint.
units.tr: 13. You know what has happened in this kingdom. Therefore we have come together here, so that we might deal, with God's help and the counsel of our faithful men, concerning God's will, the state of His holy Church, and our common salvation and honour and yours, and concerning the peace of the Christian people. And we commissioned the bishops and our other faithful men to find out how we might come together to carry out the things we have spoken of. And we want you to know that, just as they have found and reported to us in writing, we have been united with one another, as brothers ought to be united according to what is right. You too, together with this nephew of ours, and he with us, and also his brothers and nephews, we have received into this firm union with us, on the condition, however, that they make and keep this firm pledge towards us.

units.la: 14. Et scratis, quia non volumus, ut ullus inter nos abhinc inante alia verba portet nisi talia, quæ Deo sint placita, & ad nostram communem salutem & ad nostrum honorem pertineant; ut sic sinius sicut fratres invicem, & patrui cum nepotibus, & nepotes cum patruis esse debent. Et si aliquis fuerit, qui hoc facere tentaverit, perducatur in medium ad rationem, & taliter inde castigetur, ut nemo alius similiter agere tentet.
units.tr: 14. And we say that we do not want anyone among us from now on to carry words other than such as are pleasing to God and pertain to our common salvation and our honour, so that we may live as brothers towards one another, and uncles with nephews, and nephews with uncles, as they ought to. And if anyone should try to do otherwise, he shall be brought forward to give an account, and be so punished that no one else will attempt to act in the same way.

units.la: 15. Volumus ut Ecclesiæ & Casæ Dei, & Episcopi, & Dei homines, Clerici & Monachi & Nonnæ, talem mundeburdem & honorem habeant, sicut tempore nostrorum antecessorum habuerunt.
units.tr: 15. We wish that the churches and houses of God, and the bishops, and the men of God, clerics, monks and nuns, have such protection and honour as they had in the time of our predecessors.

units.la: 16. Et volumus, ut vos & cæteri homines fideles nostri talem legem & rectitudinem, & tale salvamentum in regnis nostris habeatis, sicut antecessores vestri tempore antecessorum nostrorum habuerunt: & justitia & lex omnibus conservetur; & pauperes homines talem defensionem habeant, sicut tempore antecessorum nostrorum lex & consuetudo fuit, & sicut fideles nostri communiter consenserunt, & scripto nobis demonstraverunt, & nos cum illorum consilio consentimus, & communiter volumus. Et si aliquis hoc perturbare voluerit, à nullo nostrum receptiatur, nisi ad rectam rationem aut rationabilem indulgentiæ concessionem deducatur.
units.tr: 16. And we wish that you and our other faithful men have in our kingdoms such law, rightful treatment and safeguard as your predecessors had in the time of our predecessors; and justice and law are to be preserved for all; and poor men are to have such defence as was the law and custom in the time of our predecessors, and as our faithful men have agreed in common, and have shown to us in writing; and we, with their counsel, consent and wish this in common. And if anyone wishes to disturb this, let him not be received by any of us, unless he is brought back to right reason or to a reasonable grant of pardon.

units.la: 17. Sed de istis rapinis & depredationibus, quas jam quasi pro lege multi per consuetudinem tenent, ab hodie & deinceps de Dei banno & nostro bannimus, ut nemo hoc amplius præsumat, sed unusquisque intra patriam cum pace & sine oppressione pauperum & circummanentium consistat, & in hostem, & ad placitum, seu ad curtem veniens de suo sicuvarmitacs, & de domo sua moveat, ut cum pace venire & nobiscum stare, & ad domum suam redire possit. Et qui hoc transgressus fuerit, sicut tempore antecessorum nostrorum fuit, & in illorum Capitulis continetur, volumus ut hoc in illis transgressionibus emendetur.
units.tr: 17. But concerning those plunderings and depredations, which many now hold almost as law by custom, from today onwards we proclaim, by God's ban and ours, that no one is to presume to do this any longer; rather let each man remain within his country in peace and without oppressing the poor and his neighbours, and when he comes to the host, or to the assembly, or to the court, let him move with his equipment and from his house, so that he can come in peace, stand with us, and return to his home. And whoever has transgressed in this, as was the case in the time of our predecessors and is contained in their capitularies, we wish that he be amended in those transgressions.

units.la: 18. Similiter & de conspirationibus, & de raptis fœminarum tam viduarum quàm puellarum atque nonnarum, bannimus ex Dei & nostro verbo, ut nullus hoc in nostris regnis agere præsumat. Et si quis hoc præsumpserit, secundum legem & sicut in Capitularibus progenitorum nostrorum continetur, sic hoc emendare cogatur.
units.tr: 18. Likewise, concerning conspiracies and the abduction of women, whether widows or maidens or nuns, we proclaim by the word of God and of ourselves that no one is to presume to do this in our kingdoms. And if anyone presumes to do so, he shall be compelled to make amends in this way, according to the law and as is contained in the capitularies of our forefathers.

units.la: 19. Hæc eadem Carolus Romana lingua pronuntiavit, & maxima parte lingua Theotisca recapitulavit.
units.tr: 19. The same things Charles pronounced in the Romance language, and summarised for the greater part in the Teutonic language.

units.la: 20. Posthæc Domnus Ludovicus ad Domnum Carolum fratrē suum lingua Romana dixit: Hoc si vobis placet, vestrum verbum habere volo de illis hominibus, qui ad meam fidem venerunt. Et Domnus Carolus excelsiore voce lingua Romana dixit: Illis hominibus, qui contra me fecerunt, &, sicut scitis, ad meum fratrem venerunt, propter Deum & propter illius amorem, & pro illius gratia totum perdono quod contra me nimis fecerunt; alodes de hæreditate & de conquisita, & quod de donatione nostri Senioris habuerunt; excepto illo, quod de mea donatione venit, illis concedo, si mihi fidelitatem fecerint, quod in regno meo pacifici sint, & sic vivant sicut Christiani in Christiano Regno vivere debent: in hoc si frater meus meis fidelibus, qui contra illum nihilo minus fecerunt, & me, quando opus fuit, adjuverint, similiter illorum alodes, quos in Regno illius habent, concessit. Sed & de illis alodibus, quos de mea donatione habuerunt, & etiam de honoribus, sicut cum illo melius considerabo, illis, qui ad me retornabunt, voluntatè faciam.
units.tr: 20. After this, Lord Louis said to Lord Charles his brother in the Romance language: "If it pleases you, I wish to have your word concerning those men who have come to my faith." And Lord Charles, in a louder voice, said in the Romance language: "To those men who acted against me and, as you know, came to my brother for God's sake and out of love for him, and by his grace, I forgive them entirely whatever they did against me: the allods from inheritance and from acquisition, and what they had from the gift of our lord; except what came from my gift, I grant to them, if they swear fealty to me, that they may be peaceful in my kingdom and live as Christians ought to live in a Christian kingdom. In this matter, if my brother, for his part, has granted the allods which they have in his kingdom to those of my faithful men who nonetheless acted against him, and have helped me when need arose, likewise [I grant them]. But concerning those allods which they hold from my gift, and also concerning offices, I will act according to my will toward those who return to me, after I have considered this more carefully with him."

units.la: 21. Et Domnus Lotharius lingua Theotisca in supraannunciatis Capitulis se consentire dixit, & se observaturum illa promisit. Et tunc Domnus Carolus iterum lingua Romana de pace commonuit, ut cum Dei gratia sani & salvi sint, & ut eos sanos revideret oravit, & annuntiationi finem imposuit.
units.tr: 21. And Lord Lothar, in the Teutonic language, said that he agreed to the chapters announced above, and promised that he would observe them. Then Lord Charles again, in the Romance language, reminded them about peace, and prayed that they might be restored safe and sound with the grace of God; and he brought the announcement to an end.

units.la: LUDOVICI II. ET CAROLO- MANNI REGG. AUGG.
units.tr: Louis II and Charles Manno, Kings and Augusti

units.la: Recessus SYNODI VVormatiensis, contra cultum imaginum à Gracis & Papa Rom. assertum.
units.tr: The recess of the Synod of Worms, asserted against the worship of images by the Greeks and by the Roman Pope.

units.la: ECclesiasticus conventus Teutonum & Venedorum, jussu Regis, apud Vangiones actus est. Mystę & Pontifices Germaniæ, Græcorum ineptiis, quas ad eos Romanus Episcopus retulerat, responsa reddiderunt.
units.tr: An ecclesiastical assembly of the Teutons and Venedi was held at Worms by the king's command. The mystagogues and bishops of Germany gave their replies to the foolishness of the Greeks, which the Roman bishop had referred to them.

units.la: LUDOVICI. II. REGIS AUG. DIFFIDATIO
units.tr: The Defiance of Louis II, King and Augustus

units.la: Decreta in Comitiis Francofurtensibus contra CAROLUM CALVUM Gallorum Regem, Regni Lotharingii invasorem & usurpatorem.
units.tr: Decrees of the Diet of Frankfurt against Charles the Bald, King of the Gauls, invader and usurper of the Kingdom of Lotharingia.

units.la: LUdovicus Calendis Februariis Francofordiam festinat. Confugiunt ad eum plerique omnes ex Gallia, Germania, Belgio & Celtica, quibus Rex CAROLUS cordi non erat. Luitpertus Archiepiscopus Moguntinus, Adelfridus Saxonû Hyldeshaimensis Pontifex, vitæ probitate, morum sanctimonia, sapientiaq; nobilissimi, ad CAROLUM Legati proficiscuntur: hancq; orationem habuerunt: Quoniam hactenus tibi ludibrio fuimus, tuq; animo indulgens consilia, postulara nostra floccifacis, neq; ulla juris, pietatis, sanguinis ratione habita aliena intercipis, nihil ultra, verbis frustra tempus teremus, factis opus est, armis præreptα repetemus, vi ablata ferro adscremus. Vulgò apud nos dici solet: Qui aliena appetit, sui est negligens: & nimis multa concupiscens, perpauca adipiscitur. Proinde pacem & bellum hic offerimus. Utrum vis, mox tibi sume. aut continuò cum omnibus comitibus in tuum Regnû, quovis gentiû ex hisce discede terris, aut jam aciê instrue. Jam jam invictissimus Rex noster, Regiiq; juvenes, CAROLUS, LUDOVICUS, CAROLOMANNUS, fulmina belli, victrices copiæ aderunt. Ingruent cum his bellicosissimi & ferocissimi Germaniæ pugnacis populi, nationesq; ne sociis satis quidem notæ, Sclavi, Venedi, Cimbri, Dani, Nordmanni, Abroditæ, Bojemi, Zechi, Sorabes, Moravi, Bolii, Velatabi, Turogi, Franci, Saxones, Boii, Suevi, Chariones, & cæteri, quos scrupulosius referre supervacuum est. Hi, superis faventibus, frenos aviditati imponent, te ferro docebunt, quidnam periculi sit fratrem fallere, & alienam hæreditatem præripere.
units.tr: King Louis hastens to Frankfurt on the Kalends of February. Almost all those from Gaul, Germany, Belgium and Celtica, whom King Charles did not hold dear, take refuge with him. Luitpert, Archbishop of Mainz, and Adelfrid, Bishop of Hildesheim, men of notable uprightness of life, sanctity of manners and wisdom, set out as envoys to Charles and delivered this speech: "Since until now we have been the butt of your mockery, and since you indulge your own mind, make light of our requests, and seize what belongs to others without regard to law, piety or kinship, we will waste no more time with words in vain. Deeds are needed. We will recover what was snatched away and reclaim by the sword what was taken by force. It is commonly said among us: whoever covets what belongs to others neglects his own, and whoever desires too much gains very little. Therefore we offer you peace and war here. Choose whichever you wish, and choose now: either leave our lands at once, with all your companions, for your own kingdom, or draw up your battle line immediately. Our most invincible king is already at hand, with his young sons Charles, Louis and Carloman, thunderbolts of war, and victorious forces. With them will come the most warlike and fierce peoples of pugnacious Germany, and nations too little known even to their neighbours: the Slavs, Wends, Cimbrians, Danes, Northmen, Abroditae, Bohemians, Czechs, Sorbs, Moravians, Bolii, Velatabi, Turogi, Franks, Saxons, Boii, Suevi, Chariones, and others whom it would be superfluous to list in detail. These, with the gods favouring us, will curb your greed, and will teach you with the sword what danger there is in deceiving a brother and snatching away another's inheritance."

units.la: EJUSDEM DECRETVM CONCILII COLONIENSIS DE anno DCCCLXX.
units.tr: The decree of the same concerning the Council of Cologne, in the year 870

units.la: COgitur VI. Kl. Octobris jussu Regis Conventus Ecclesiasticus apud Coloniam Agrippinensem. Interfuere Archiepiscopi Luitperdus Mogontinus, Bertulphus Treverorum, Willebertus Agrippinensis, Adelvinus Juvavensis, cum Episcopis, Sacrificulis, Sacerdotibus, Monachis suis. Divi Pauli ad Timotheum Titumq; de libro epistolæ recitatæ sunt. Sacerdotes, Episcopi, avari, Veneri venique dediti, ignominia notati, tribuq; moti sunt. Cæteri jussi sunt vivere juxta Christi Servatoris nostri placita. Imperatum Mystis, ut literis sacræ philosophiæ operam darent, ut oves pascerent, névegregem a Deo creditum malis exemplis trucidarent, neu lac consumerent, de lanis se contegerent. Ante omnia ut curam pauperum agerent Episcopi, Patrochiq;, præceptum fuit.
units.tr: By the king's order an ecclesiastical assembly is convened at Cologne (Colonia Agrippina) on the sixth day before the Kalends of October. Present were the archbishops Luitperd of Mainz, Bertulf of Trier, Willibert of Cologne and Adalwin of Salzburg (Juvavum), with their bishops, sacrificers, priests and monks. Letters of the blessed Paul to Timothy and Titus were read from the book. Priests and bishops who were greedy, given over to Venus and wine, were marked with disgrace and removed from their order. The rest were ordered to live according to the precepts of Christ our Saviour. The Mystae were commanded to devote themselves to the letters of sacred philosophy, to feed the sheep, not to slaughter by evil examples the flock entrusted to them by God, not to consume the milk, and to clothe themselves with the wool. Above all, it was prescribed that the bishops and the patrochi should take care of the poor.

units.la: LUDOVICI. II. IMP. AUG. RESCRIPTUM
units.tr: LUDOVICUS II, EMPEROR AUGUSTUS: A RESCRIPT

units.la: AD BASILIVM IMPERATOREM CON- STANTINOPOLITANUM.
units.tr: TO BASIL, EMPEROR OF CONSTANTINOPLE.

units.la: IN nomine Domini nostri Jesu Christi Dei æterni, Ludovicus divina ordinante providentia Imperator Augustus Romanorum, dilectissimo spiritualiqe fratri nostro Basilio gloriosissimo ac pulcherrimo æquè Imperatori Novæ Romæ.
units.tr: In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, the eternal God, Louis, by the ordaining providence of God Emperor Augustus of the Romans, to our most beloved and spiritual brother Basil, the most glorious and most excellent Emperor likewise of New Rome.

units.la: 1. Probabile quidem & laudabile constat, aliquem fratrem fratris monitis, quasi quibusdam flabris ad ignem charitatis accendi: probabilius autem est, sic ipsius ultroneæ voluntatis ad hoc moribus inflammari; sed probabilissimum est, quandocunq; viam quemquam virtutis arripere, & magis magisq; miris successibus in sublime proficere. Nam ille semper miles a Duce magis diligitur, qui post reniens hostium vires fortiter premit, quàm is qui maturus quidem accessit, sed forte aut nihil, aut certe modicum gessit. Secundum quam regulam divinitus stabilitum Imperium nostrum, ex die qua coepit erga fraternitatem tuam dilectionis radicem in corde suo plantare, multiplices fructus exhibere non destitit, non minus quæ vestra tanquam quæ nostra sunt procurans & vendicans. Quamvis quæ ita Missos nostros in causa familiaritatis & benignitatis te gloriaris egisse: nos priùs erga Joannem gloriosissimum Patricium gestisse patescat; quem revera non sicut amicum, vel quemadmodum fratris, id est Imperii tui hominem, sed quasi consanguineum nostrum, & tanquam excellentiæ tuæ sobolem tractavimus & dileximus: nec hunc penes nos positum aut tarditas umquam temporis, aut tima locorum à penetralibus nostris fecere extorrem.
units.tr: 1. It is generally agreed to be a commendable thing when one brother is kindled to the fire of love by the admonitions of a brother, as if by bellows. It is more probable that a man is inflamed to this by his own willing disposition. But most probable of all is that whoever takes up the way of virtue advances ever higher and higher by remarkable successes. For a soldier is always more valued by his commander if, after routing the enemy's forces, he presses on bravely, than one who came up in good time but perhaps achieved nothing, or at most very little. By this rule, our Empire, established by God, from the day it began to plant the root of love in its heart toward your brotherhood, has not ceased to bear manifold fruits, caring for and claiming your affairs no less than its own. You boast that our envoys acted in this way out of friendship and kindness; but it is plain that we first showed such feeling toward John, the most glorious Patrician, whom we treated and loved not as a friend, or as a brother, that is, a man of your Empire, but as our own kinsman and as the offspring of your excellency. Neither the slowness of time nor the distance of places has ever made him an exile from our inner circle.

units.la: 1. Cæterùm spiritualem fraternitatem tuam mitamur, tot sermonum ambages cõtentiosius adversus Apostolum prætendentem, qui dicit; Si quis vult contentiosus esse, nos talem consuetudinem non habemus: nec Ecclesia Dei, cùm Imperii dignitas apud Deum non in vocabuli voce, sed in culmine pie gloriosa existat; nec nobis quid appellatu mirandū, sed quid sumus providendum. Verùm quia de Imperatorio nomine multa nobis cœpisti, cogimur & nos quoq; ad scripta tua quædam respondere, usquequaq; super hoc siluerimus, non ut contentionem vitantes, sed quasi ratione convicti stultis insipientibus videamur.
units.tr: 1. Moreover, we admonish your spiritual brotherhood that you put forward so many verbal circumlocutions, contending more fiercely against the Apostle who says: If anyone wishes to be contentious, we have no such custom. Nor does the Church of God, since the dignity of the Empire before God exists not in the sound of a word but in the height of piety and glory, have any reason to marvel at a name; rather, we must consider what we are. But since you have begun to say much to us about the imperial name, we too are compelled to make some reply to your writings. Hitherto we have kept silent on this altogether, not to avoid contention, but lest we seem, like fools, to have been convicted by reason.

units.la: 3. Indicat itaq; dilectio tua, se * maledictū legis pavescere, & idcirco terminos æternos trásferre veterum Imperatorū formas cōmutare, ac præter Canonica & paterna præcepta cóversari, tennuare recusct. Et tamen qui sunt illi, vel ubi, aut unde fuerūt prolati termini æterni, vel veteres formæ, aut Canonica & paterna præcepta, minus apertè declarat. Nisi forte super Imperatoris nomine velut cūcta sentiti. Verū apud nos multa lecta sunt, multa quidē indefessè legūtur, nunquā tamē inventi terminos positos, aut formas, aut præcepta piata, neminé appellandū Basilea, nisi enim, quē in urbe Constantinopoli Imperii tenere gubernacula cōtigisset, cùm gentiū singularū monumentis interpositis, sacræ nobis affluenter historiæ mōstrent, plurimos fuisse Basileos nūcupatos, & non electos quosq;, quales fuere Melchisedech & David, verū etiā reprobos, quales primores Assyriorum, Ægyptiorum, Moabitarum, & cæterarum nationum, quas enumerare longum est, extitisse probant.
units.tr: 3. Your love indicates that it fears the curse of the law, and therefore hesitates to move the eternal boundaries, to change the forms of the ancient emperors, and to go beyond the canonical and paternal precepts. Yet it declares less clearly who they are, or where or whence the eternal boundaries, the ancient forms, or the canonical and paternal precepts were brought forth. Unless perhaps you think all this follows from the name of Emperor. Many things have indeed been read among us, and they are read tirelessly, yet we have never found boundaries set, forms laid down, or pious precepts forbidding anyone to be called Basileus. For the sacred histories, showing by the records of individual nations, prove abundantly that many have been called Basileus, not only the chosen, such as Melchizedek and David, but also the reprobate, such as the chiefs of the Assyrians, Egyptians, Moabites, and other nations, too many to list.

units.la: 4. Ergo cùm ita sit, frustrà cauśandum ducit prudentia tua, alios præter se Basileos appellandos nisi forte radendos ducat totius codices mundi, in quibus pene cunctarum gentium Principes à primis temporibus & deinceps Basilei inveniūtur scripti. Et certè, ut de Latinis codicibus interim taceamus, si Græcos & novitèr editos revolvas codices, invenies proculdubio plurimos tali nomine vocatos, & non solùm Græcorum, sed & Persarum, Epirotarum, Indorum, Bithyniensium, Parthorum, Armeniorum, Sarracenorum, Æthiopum, Vuandalorum, & Gothorum, & aliarum gentiū Principum Basileorum appellatione venerator. Intuere igitur Frater, & considera, qu multi fuerunt, qui diversis temporibus, & in diversis locis & nationib. nuncupati sunt, vel hactenus nuncupantur: & non vel nobis, quod dicimur, invidere, vel tibi singulariter usurpare, quòd non solùm nobiscū, sed & cum ribus Præpositis aliarū gentium possides Grave namq; vitium est singularis dignitatis fastigium, quod in principio ambierit, quid ei ambiendo talia contigerit, commemorare nolumus, ne fraternitas commemoratum ad injuriam suam exiit met.
units.tr: 4. Therefore, since this is so, your prudence is wrong to object that others besides yourself should not be called Basileis, unless perhaps you think that every codex in the world should be scraped, in which nearly all the princes of the nations, from the earliest times onward, are found written as Basileis. Indeed, to say nothing for now of Latin codices, if you turn over the Greek and recently published codices, you will undoubtedly find very many called by that name: not only princes of the Greeks, but also of the Persians, Epirots, Indians, Bithynians, Parthians, Armenians, Saracens, Ethiopians, Vandals, Goths, and other nations, honored with the title of Basileus. Consider therefore, brother, how many there have been who in different times, places and nations have been so named, or are still so named. Do not begrudge us, who are so called, nor claim for yourself alone what you hold not only in common with us but also with the rulers of other nations. For it is a grave fault to recall what a man set out to seek as the summit of singular dignity, and what came to him from such ambition. We do not wish to mention this, lest your brotherhood take the recollection as an injury to itself.

units.la: 5. Dicis autē, quod quatuor Patriarchales sedes, unā Imperium inter sacra mysteria memorari, à Delferis Apostolis ulq; nunc traditum habeant; moxq; hortaris, ut persuadeamus eis, quod nos Imperatores appellent, quod tamen nec ratio dictat, nec est opus. Primò quidē, quia nobis nō congruit, alios modo nos vocent instruere; deinde verò, quia nobis etiā minimè suadentibus, tā Patriarchas singulos q; cæteros homines, qui sub cælo sunt, excepta fraternitate tua, tam honoratos quamq; privatos, nos nominis appellare cognomine, quoties eorū accepimus epistolas & litteras, invenimus. Pr cùm & ipsi patrui nostri, g'o.iosi Reges, absq; invidia Imperatorem nos vocitent, & Imperatorem proculdubio fatentur, non profectò ad ætatē, quā nobis majores fuit, attendentes, sed ad unctionem & sacrationem, quā per summi Pontificis manus impositione divinitus sumus ad hoc culmen pervenit & ad Romani Principatus Imperium, quo superno nutu potimur, aspiciens es. Porrò si nunc Imperatoris Patriarchæ inter sacrosancta sacrificia memorant, laudandi sunt, non utiq; incovenienter agentes. Imperium Patris & Filii & Spiritus sancti, cujus pars est Ecclesia constituta in terris; quamen Deus nec per te solùm, nec per me tantùm gubernari disposuit, nisi quia tanta sumus ad unitatem charitate connexi, ut non jam divisi, sed unum esse videamur.
units.tr: 5. You say that the four patriarchal sees, from the holy Apostles until now, have handed down that the Empire is recorded together with them among the sacred mysteries; and then you urge us to persuade them to call us Emperors, which neither reason requires nor is there any need for. First, because it does not befit us to instruct others how they should address us. Then, because even without our urging, whenever we have received their letters we find that they address each of the patriarchs and all other men under heaven, both honored and private, except your brotherhood, by our name with an added title. Moreover, since our uncles, the glorious kings, without envy call us Emperor and undoubtedly acknowledge us as Emperor, they do not look to the age by which we are older than they, but to the anointing and consecration by which, through the laying on of the hands of the supreme Pontiff, we were divinely raised to this height and to the Empire of the Roman principate, which we hold by heavenly will. Further, if the Patriarchs now mention the Emperor among the most holy sacrifices, they are to be praised, for they are certainly not acting unfittingly. The Empire of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, of which the Church established on earth is a part, God has ordained to be governed not by you alone, nor by me alone, but because we are so closely joined by love in unity that we seem no longer divided but one.

units.la: 6. Nonautem credimus, sanctissimos Patriarchas sic tui mentionem facere, ut aliorū quoq; Principum (ut omittamus nostram) mentionem prætereant, cùm pro hujusmodi etiam * Apostolus juserit, cùm perseq̃uerentur Ecclesiam, ut securam & tranquillam vitam agerent cum omni pietate. Præterea cùm eos etiam pro impiis orare non dubitamus, sub quorum ditione consistunt, sicut Jerem. quoq; populus in Babyloniam ductus pro Rege Babyloniæ per * Jeremiam jubetur orare. Nam eorum pace etiam populi constituitur pacem.
units.tr: 6. We do not believe that the most holy Patriarchs make mention of you in such a way as to pass over the mention of other princes, not to mention ourselves; for the Apostle also commanded, when they were persecuting the Church, that prayers be made for such men, that we might lead a secure and tranquil life in all piety. Moreover, we do not hesitate to pray even for those impious men under whose rule they stand, just as the people led captive into Babylon were commanded by Jeremiah to pray for the King of Babylon. For by their peace the peace of the people is also established.

units.la: 7. Illud autem mirari merito possumus, q; sublimitas tua ad novam & recentiorē appellationem aspirare nos autumat; cùm quantū ad lineā generis pertinet, non sit novis vel recens, q; jam ab avo stro non usurpante, ut pei hibes, sed Dei nutu, & Ecclesiæ judicio, Summiq; Pontificis per impositionem & unctionē manus obtinuit, sicut in codicib. tuis invenire facilè poteris. Verū quid mirum, si novum, cùm omne vetus à novo principiū habeat, & nō novū à veteri? Et certè cùm primi Romani Principes serare cœperunt, novum fuit, sed de die in diem devenit in vetustatē. Non ergò quæcumq; novitas culpa est, scilicet irreprehensibilis novitas. Unde & Apostolus cùm dilecto filio scriberet, non ait voces novitates devita, sed profanas vocū novitates devita. Sanè antiquā esse Imperii nostri dignitatē nullā ambigit, qui vel nos successores antiquorū Imperatorū esse nō nescit, vel divinæ pietatis divitias nō ignorat. Nā quid mirū, si in fine téporis palā exhibuit, quod ante tempora in abdito cōsilio suo, prædestinavit.
units.tr: 7. But we may rightly marvel that your sublimity claims we aspire to a new and more recent title, when, as far as the line of descent goes, it is neither new nor recent. It was already obtained, not by our grandfather usurping it, as you assert, but by the will of God and the judgment of the Church, through the laying on of hands and anointing by the supreme Pontiff, as you can easily find in your own codices. But what wonder if it is new, since every old thing has its beginning from something new, and nothing new from something old? Indeed, when the first Roman princes began to reign, it was new, but day by day it grew into antiquity. Therefore not every novelty is a fault, certainly not a blameworthy novelty. Hence also the Apostle, writing to his beloved son, did not say avoid the novelties of words, but avoid the profane novelties of words. Surely no one doubts that the dignity of our Empire is ancient, since he knows that we are successors of the ancient emperors, or does not ignore the riches of divine goodness. For what wonder if, at the end of time, he has openly displayed what before time he predestined in his hidden counsel.

units.la: 8. Sed nec hoc admiratione caret, quod alleris, Principem Arabum Protosymbolum dici, cùm in voluminibus nostris nihil tale reperiatur, & vestri codices modò Architòa, modò Regem, vel aliquando vocabulo nuncupent. Verùm nos omnibus litteris Scripturas sanctas præferimus, * quæ per Dei non Protosymbolos, sed Reges Arabum & Saba perspicuè confitentur. Chaganum verò non Avarum, non Cazarorum, aut Northmannorum nuncupari reperimus, neque Principem Bulgarum, sed Regem vel Dominum Bulgarum. Quæ omnia idcirco dicimus, ut quàm alteri se habe-ant quæ ipsi ... gentes in Græcis voluminibus ipse cognoscas. Quos nimirum suis cognominibus ... perhibes, nec tamen propria ipsorum cognomina recolis. Verùm idcirco ab iis & ab omnibus ... debitum vocabulum adimis, ut hoc tibi soli non tam propriè quàm violenter intelectas.
units.tr: 8. But this is not without cause for wonder either: you allege that the Prince of the Arabs is called Protosymbolus, yet nothing of the kind is found in our books, while your codices now call him Architoa, now King, and sometimes give him other names. We, however, prefer the holy Scriptures to all other writings, and these openly confess that the Arabs and Saba had kings, not protosymboli. As for the Khagan, we find he is not called Avar, nor of the Khazars or Northmen, nor Prince of the Bulgars, but King or Lord of the Bulgars. We say all this so that you may learn from the Greek books how the other peoples stand. You name them by their own surnames, yet you do not recall their proper surnames. But you take from them, and from all of them, their due title, so that this name may be understood as belonging to you alone, not so much properly as by force.

units.la: Illud autem videre libuit, quod de IMPERATORIS nomine dixisti, neque paternum esse, neque venire. Quomodo enim paternum no est, quod jam in avo nostro paternum fuit? Quomodo autem non convenit, cum Iclamus ut de cæteris brevitatis causa taceamus ex Hispanorum, Gothorum, & Cazarorum gente Imperatores Romanos effectos? Neque enim veraciter affirmabis ... gente Francorum aut religione aut virtutibus clariores, & tamen admittere non rennuus ... ratores, & eos prædicare non dubitas. Porro de eo quod dicis, non in tota nos Francia imperare, ... Frater, breve responsum. In tota nempe imperamus Francia, quia nos procul dubio retinemus, ... renuent, cum quibus una caro & sanguis sumus, & unus per Dominum spiritus.
units.tr: We were pleased to note also what you said about the name of Emperor, that it is neither paternal nor rightly acquired. For how is it not paternal, when it was already paternal in our grandfather? And how is it not fitting, when we know, to say nothing of others for the sake of brevity, that Roman Emperors have been made from the peoples of the Spaniards, the Goths and the Khazars? For you will not truly affirm that the nation of the Franks is more distinguished than these in religion or in virtues, and yet you do not refuse to admit them, and you do not hesitate to proclaim them. As to what you say, that we do not rule the whole of Francia: brother, a brief reply. We do indeed rule the whole of Francia, since we undoubtedly hold it, ... though they refuse, with whom we are one flesh and blood, and one spirit through the Lord.

units.la: Præterea miraris fe dilecta fraternitas tua significat, quòd non Francorum, sed Romanorum Imperator appellemur; sed scire te convenit, quia nisi Romanorum Imperatore essemus, utique nec Francorum. A Romanis enim hoc nomen & dignitatem assumpsimus, apud quos proscò primo tantæ culmen sublimitatis & appellationis effulsit, quorumq; gentem & Urbem divinitus gubernandam, & ... in omnem Ecclesiarum Dei defendendam atq; sublimandam suscepimus, ex qua & regnandi ... & post nodum imperandi auctoritatem prosapiæ nostræ fœminarium sumpsit. Nam Francorum Primo Reges, deinde verò Imperatores dicti sunt, ii duntaxat qui a Romano Pontifice ad hoc ... unctio perfusi sunt, in qua etiam Carolus Magnus abavus noster unctione ejusmodi per Summum Pontificem delibutus, primus ex gente & genealogia nostra, pietate in eo abundante, & Imperator dictus, & Christus Domini factus est. Præterea cum tales sæpe ad Imperium sunt adsciti, qui nulla ... operatione per Pontificum ministerium, propositi solùm à Senatu & populo, nihil horum ... ibus, Imperatoria dignitate potiti sunt; nonnulli verò nec sic, sed tantùm à militibus sunt clamati, & in Imperio stabiliti sunt, ita ut etiam eorum quidam à fœminis, quidam autem aut hoc aut alio ... ad Imperii Romani sceptra promoti sunt.
units.tr: Besides, you wonder, as your beloved brotherhood signifies, that we are called Emperor of the Romans and not of the Franks. But you should know that if we were not Emperors of the Romans, we would certainly not be of the Franks either. For from the Romans we have taken this name and dignity, among whom first of all the summit of such sublimity and title shone forth, and whose people and City, to be governed under divine providence ... we have undertaken to defend and exalt in all the Churches of God; from this too, both the power of reigning ... and afterwards the authority of ruling, our line has taken as its inheritance. For the first kings of the Franks, and afterwards those who were anointed with the unction of the Roman Pontiff, were called emperors, for this purpose ... In this unction Charles the Great, our great-grandfather, anointed with such unction by the Supreme Pontiff, was the first of our people and lineage, abounding in piety, to be called Emperor and to be made the Christ of the Lord. Moreover, since men have often been admitted to the empire by no ... operation through the ministry of the Pontiffs, merely proposed by the Senate and the people, and without any of these ... they obtained the imperial dignity; some indeed not even in this way, but were merely acclaimed by soldiers and established in the empire, so that some of them were promoted by women, and some by this or that ... to the sceptres of the Roman Empire.

units.la: Porrò si calumniaris Romanum Pontificem, quod gesserit, calumniari poteris & Samuel, ... pneto Saule, quem ipse unxerat, David in Regem ungere non rennuerit. Verùm super hoc si est, ... Summo Pontifici talem unum faciat mutuum, congruo profecto illius non carebit responso. Sed si paginas revolvas Græcorum Annalium, utiq; discriminatos ab alienis, per quos nequaquam ... et si quæ veltrantibus Pontifices Romani pertulerint, perseveraveris, profecto invenies unde ... te non valeas redarguere. Verùm hæc illi, quæ extrinsecus agebantur, facilè parvipenderunt, nisi ... intrinsecus, quæ per diversas hæreses perimere conantur molimina deprehenderunt. Unde merito ... defectis (quæ enim * communicatio Christi cum Belial?) adhæserunt genti adhærenti Deo, ... regni fructus facienti: quoniam non est personarum acceptor Deus, sed ut eximius Apostolus * innuit, in omni gente, qui timet Deum, acceptus est illi. Ergo cum ita sit, cur nos satagis reprehendere ... iam ex Francis oriundi, Romani moderamur habenas Imperii, cum in omni gente, qui timet ... ... acceptus est illi: Et certè Theodosius major, & filii Arcadius & Honorius, & Theodosius ... Arcadii filius, ex Hispanis ad Imperii Romani culmen assumpti sunt, & non invenimus quod ... averunt vel reprehenderunt Theodosium, quòd non Romanus, sed Hispanus existeret, vel ... vel prohibuerunt filios ejus in locum patris & honores succedere, quemadmodum ut cum ... camus) nunc tua conatu videtur diligeda fraternitas & sufficienda dilectio, quasi gens Franc... pertineat ad hæreditatem, de qua Pater ad Filium loquitur; * Postula a me, & dabo * hæreditatem tuam, &c. Et alibi; * Glorificantes me glorificabo. Et alia innumerabilia.
units.tr: Moreover, if you accuse the Roman Pontiff of what he did, you may also accuse Samuel, ... Saul having been rejected, whom he himself had anointed; David he did not refuse to anoint as king. But if there is ... if you were to make such an exchange to the Supreme Pontiff, he would not lack a fitting answer. But if you turn over the pages of the Greek Annals, which are indeed distinct from foreign ones, through whom by no means ... and if you persist in whatever the Roman Pontiffs have endured from persecutors, you will surely find whence ... you cannot refute. But those things which were done from outside they lightly esteemed, unless ... they discovered from within the schemes which through various heresies they strive to destroy. Whence rightly ... defections (for what fellowship has Christ with Belial?) they clung to the nation that clings to God, ... bearing the fruit of the kingdom; for God is no respecter of persons, but, as the eminent Apostle declares, in every nation he who fears God is acceptable to him. Therefore, since it is so, why do you labour to reprehend ... now sprung from the Franks, we Romans guide the reins of the Empire, since in every nation he who fears ... is acceptable to him? And indeed Theodosius the Elder, and his sons Arcadius and Honorius, and Theodosius ... son of Arcadius, were raised from the Spaniards to the summit of the Roman Empire, and we do not find that ... they censured or reprehended Theodosius because he was not a Roman but a Spaniard, or ... or forbade his sons to succeed their father in place and honours, as ... Now, as we say, your beloved brotherhood and deserving affection seems to strive, as if the nation of the Franks ... belongs to the inheritance of which the Father speaks to the Son: Ask of me, and I will give you the inheritance, etc. And elsewhere: Those who glorify me I will glorify. And countless other passages.

units.la: Ergo, Frater charissime, desinem in hoc contentionis agere; desine adulatoribus quibuscunque ... ritatis inflectere. Denique gens Francorum justos & fecundissimos Domino attulit fructus, ... rò credendo verum etiam nullos alios salutifere convertendo. Verùm vobis à Domino ... om est; * Auferetur a vobis regnum, & dabitur genti facienti fructus ejus. Sicut ergo potuit Deus de ... tare filios Abrahæ, ita potuit de Francorum duntaxat Romani iniscitare successores Imperii.
units.tr: Therefore, dearest brother, I will cease to contend on this point; cease to listen to any flatterers ... Finally, the nation of the Franks has brought forth just and most fruitful fruits to the Lord, ... not only in believing the truth but also in converting others to salvation. But from the Lord to you ... it is: The kingdom shall be taken from you and given to a nation that bears its fruit. Therefore, just as God was able to raise up the sons of Abraham, so from the Franks alone could He raise up the successors of the Roman Empire.

units.la: Christi fumus, secundum * Apostolum, Abrahæ semen existimus. Ita si fumus Christi, omnia ... gratiam ipsius, quæ pollunt illi, qui evidenter existunt Christi. Et sicut nos per hæc Christi ... men existimus, et Judæi per perfidiam Abrahæ filii esse dicitur, ita quoq; nos propter bo- ... id est orthodoxiam, regimen Imperii Romani suscepimus; Græci verò propter caco- ... malam opinionem, Romanorum Imperatores existere cessaverunt: desertes scilicet ... de urbem & sede Imperii, sed & gentem Romanam, & ipsam quoq; linguam penitus amitten- ... urbem, eodem gentem, & linguam per omnia transmigrantes.
units.tr: We are the seed of Abraham, according to the Apostle, because we are Christ's. So if we are Christ's, all ... the grace of Him, which avails those who clearly belong to Christ. And just as we are Christ's through these things ... seed, and the Jews are said to be sons of Abraham only through unbelief, so also we, on account of good ... that is, orthodoxy, have taken up the government of the Roman Empire; but the Greeks, on account of their bad ... evil opinion, have ceased to be Roman Emperors: deserting, of course, ... not only the city and seat of the Empire, but also the Roman people and the language they have entirely lost ... the city, the people and the language, migrating completely.

units.la: Sed nos frater delinquo habilis, tamen cor eorum replicat, audi frequentia, quia * non repulit Deus ple- ... Dic ergo, numquid sic offenderunt ut caderent? Absit; sed illorum delictum honor nostrer, & ... plenitudo nostra effecta est. Cum ... fumus, nos inferi fumus in illis, cum ... quidem ... fulleus, & focum indicum & pinguedinem olivæ sumus effecti. Dicimus ergo: ... ... nemus, inferamur. Et bene. Non enim nihil propter credulitatem non rectam sumus. ... mentitus est. Qui habet aures audiendi, audiat. 14. Sed dicis, quòd esset tempus secundùm quod fraternitati nostræ promiseris, quando hoc potiremur appellatione, si Deus ad finem ea, quæ constiliati sumus, perducere voluisset. Eundem consilio quod asseris, quæ diximus, hæc ipsa & nunc dicimus. Non enim est in nobis, Est & Non verbo nostro neq; ad dexteram neq; ad sinistram divertimus, sed in ipso immou pei sistimus: appellationem autem illam, sicut hactenus nec nos nec patres nostri per carnem & sanguinem pollidere gnoscimur, ita quoq; de catero non immerito pollidere contendimus. Per patres enim nos per filios consuevimus honorari, & apud nos gloria non à filiis ad patrem, sed à patribus filios dicimus. Quod enim nos à patre luminum, à quo omne datum optimum, & omne donum perfectum sunt filio, neq; per hominem aut ab hominibus accipere volumus.
units.tr: But we, brother, ... yet their heart is turned back; hear the frequent words, that God has not cast off his people ... Say then, did they stumble so as to fall? Far from it; but by their offence salvation has come to the Gentiles ... fullness has been made. Since ... we are grafted in among them, ... have become partakers of the root and the fatness of the olive. We say therefore: ... Well said. For they were not broken off for nothing, because of their unbelief ... has lied. He who has ears to hear, let him hear. 14. But you say that there would be a time, according to what you promised our brotherhood, when we would obtain this title, if God had willed to bring to an end those things which we have resolved. In the same counsel which you assert, we now also say these same things. For it is not in us to say Yes and No; neither do we turn to the right hand or the left, but in Him we stand fixed. As for that title, just as hitherto neither we nor our fathers are known to have possessed it through flesh and blood, so henceforth too we rightly contend that we possess it. For we are used to being honoured through our fathers, and among us glory is said to pass not from sons to fathers but from fathers to sons. For since we are from the Father of lights, from whom comes every good gift and every perfect gift, we are unwilling to receive it through a man or from men.

units.la: 15. Postremò scito, quia qui Riga quemq; appellat, quid dicat, nec ipse novit. Si quidem si linguis omnibus, more Apostolorum, immò Angelorum loquaris, cujus linguæ sit Riga, vel gnitati sonus ille barbarus congruit, quod Rex dicitur, interpretari non poteris. Nihil enim dioma proprie linguæ, tractum Riga, Regé significare monstraveris. Quod si ita est, qui non barum, sed Latinum est, oportet ut cum ad manus vestras pervenerit, in linguam vernam ideo latione vertatur. Quod si factū fuerit, quid aliud nisi hoc nomine βασιλεὺς interpretabitur. Quod non solùm veteris, sed & novi Testamenti omnes Interpretes attestantur. Unde in alio hocde restaris vocabulū, stude ex omnibus tam Latinis libris quàm Græcis, sive Regis, sive βασιλεὺς nomen eradere.
units.tr: 15. Finally, know this: whoever calls him "Riga" does not himself know what he is saying. Even if you spoke in all languages, as the Apostles did, or rather as the Angels do, you would not be able to explain what the word "Riga" means, or how that barbarous sound corresponds to the meaning of "king." For you could not show that the native idiom of the language, the word "Riga" as it is used, signifies "king." If that is so, then the word that is not barbarian but Latin must, when it reaches your hands, be turned into your own tongue. And once that is done, what else would it be rendered, except by the word βασιλεύς [basileus]? All the translators of the Old and New Testament bear witness to this. Therefore, in your other documents, take care to erase the word "Riga" from all books, Latin and Greek alike, whether it is "Rex" or "basileus."

units.la: 16. His igitur super hoc ita prælibatis, obstupescimus in iis, quæ Serenitas tua prosequitur, id est Græcis Barum ex parte tua debellantibus, & elidere decertantibus, nostros vel solū vel prandiis dissolutos nullū auxilio præstitisse: hancq; ideò civitate minimè capi potuit; cum sive intuendo tantū, sive prandendo, sive aliud quid agédo Barum tamen licet perpauci, & impugnasse, & opte divina cepisse nolscantur. Veltri autè sicut bruchi niultitudine apparentes, locultæ primū impetū danres, eo ipso, quo conatum suū in prima fronte monstraverunt, pusillate superati, protinus infirmati sunt, & more locutarū repente quidē fallerunt, sed ostendit quasi à nitibus volandi decidérunt, ac per hoc neq; intuēdo, neq; prandēdo, neq; bellando, quibus insignibus triumphi monstratis, motu subitaneo & clandestino recesserunt & ineflicaces; ne contra, Christianis solùmodò captivatis, ad propria repedarunt. Ergo, Frater, noli de catero ridere, quia etiā inter mortis vicina studēt & prandia & omnia charitatis indicia proximis exhibere tamen à proposito nō lentescere, quoniā, sicundum Apostolum, sciunt abundare & penuriam & saturari & esurire. Et(ut compendio dicamus)omnia possunt in eo, qui illos confortat.
units.tr: 16. Having thus touched on these matters in advance, we are astonished at what Your Serenity reports: that the Greeks, on your side, have been fighting against Bari and striving to drive it out, while our men, either alone or at their meals, have given no help; and that for this reason the city could not be taken, since, whether they were looking on, or dining, or doing something else, they did not, as far as we know, attack Bari at all, though very few of them did; and did not capture it by divine aid. But they appeared like a swarm of locusts, and at their first onslaught, by the very act of showing their effort at the front, they were quickly overcome by a small force, and at once lost heart. Like locusts, they vanished suddenly, and as if they had fallen from the wings of flight, they withdrew by a sudden and secret movement, and without accomplishment, without showing any sign of triumph, and returned to their own territory, having captured only Christians. So, brother, do not laugh at them any more. For even among the nearness of death they strive to show their neighbours both their meals and all the signs of charity, and they do not slacken in their purpose, since, according to the Apostle, they know how to abound and to be in want, to be full and to be hungry. And (to sum up briefly) they can do all things in him who strengthens them.

units.la: 17. De paucitate verò, quid miraris si pauci fuerunt, & tamen multa lucra detulerūt. Præterea de re pauci fuerunt nostri, pridè patefecimus dilectioni tuæ. Sed quoniā nos super hoc pulsati, nostrum fume reponsuni. Cùm. n. diu demorante Stolo fraternitatis tuæ, & illius jam Stolaremur advenū, & in anno ipso de obsidione Bari nihil omnino fieri putaremus, omnes dire permiseramus, his solū retentis, quos ad prohibitionē recipiendorum alimentorū debamus. Et hoc est quòd stolus insperatus apparens, non nisi paucos nostros inven-runt. Verum isti pauci & adhuc pauciores, quibusdam horum diverso languore gravatis, effectis, antequam caperetur, tres Ammuredas, qui tota Calabriam depopulabantur, & numerosam multitudinem cenorum prostraverunt, & magna vestratibus salute divino beneficio cōtulerunt. Quare nō labritanorum Ismaelitarū ingens ex tunc facta est diminutio, sed & Barensium potentatu dissoluto, ac per id ad capiendum faciisadinventio. Cujus facti trophæa vestros credimus tuo retulisse, & opera Dei, quæ tacere non debent, mirabiliter enarrasse.
units.tr: 17. As for their small number, why do you wonder that they were few, and yet brought back many gains? Besides, we have already made clear to Your Love how few of our men there were in this matter. But since we were urged on this point, we shall give our answer. For when the fleet of Your Fraternity had long delayed, and we were already growing anxious at its arrival, and we thought that nothing at all would be done that year regarding the siege of Bari, we had let all the men go, keeping back only those whom we had to retain to prevent the supply of food. And it is for this reason that the fleet, appearing unexpectedly, found only a few of our men. But these few, and even fewer, some of them weighed down by various sicknesses, before Bari was taken, destroyed three Emirs, the Ammurades, who were laying waste all of Calabria, and overthrew a numerous multitude of their followers, and by God's goodness brought great safety to your people. Therefore, not only was there a great diminution of the Ishmaelite raiders of Apulia from that time, but also the power of the Barensians was broken, and so the way was opened for taking the city. We believe your people have reported the trophies of this deed to you, and have wondrously recounted the works of God, which ought not to be kept silent.

units.la: 18. Cæterùm fraternitatis tuæ dilectionē rogamus, nullam Nicetæ Patricio molestiā irrogare eo quòd nostrū infoleter offenderit animū. Nam licet adeò protervus & contumax in nobis causā tui honoris pariter & amoris præventa cōpescceretur, tamen malū pro malo retribuere, nec debemus. Et idcirco deposcimus, si quid minarū super ipsum potestatis tuæ fortiter minet, celerī benignitatis tuæ manu pro nostro removeatur amore.
units.tr: 18. Moreover, we ask Your Brotherly Love to inflict no harm on the patrician Nicetas, because he has grievously offended our spirit. For although he was so insolent and obstinate towards us, he was restrained by the prior concern for your honour and love; yet we ought not to repay evil with evil. And therefore we beg that, if your power threatens him with any penalties, they be removed by the swift hand of your kindness, for the sake of our love.

units.la: 19. Non autē tales Apocrisarios Apostolicæ Sedis esse, vel professio docet, vel eruditio conversatio anteacta demonstrat: quales illos scripta prædicant, q nobis fraternitas tua direxit, & approbatos eos tā spiritualis pater noster Summus Pontifex, quæ Ecclesia per diuturna tempora, & Ecclesiasticæ correctionis negotia strenuē peragentes, ad preces sublimis à Deo fer rii tui illos direxisse noscūtur. Unde & decuerat excellētiam tuam ita munitos eos remittere, ut los vel piratarū vel aliorum pravorum incuriūs inciderent. Grave namq; contra te super hac tualis patris nostri Apostolici Papæ, quàm totius Ecclesiæ Romanæ murmur accenditur, q à Sede Apostolica tam desiderabiliter expetierī, sed tam improvida dispensatione remiser.
units.tr: 19. Now, that such men are not the envoys of the Apostolic See, either their profession teaches, or their former learning and conduct demonstrate. Such as the writings which your Fraternity sent to us declare them to be, and as our spiritual father, the Supreme Pontiff, and the Church, through long periods of time and in the business of ecclesiastical correction, have approved them as acting vigorously, it is known that they were sent by him at the lofty prayer of your servant to God. Hence your Excellency too ought to have sent them back so well equipped that they did not fall into the hands of pirates or other wicked men through carelessness. For a grave murmur is kindled against you, not only from the Apostolic Pope, our father, but from the whole Roman Church, because those men were so eagerly sought from the Apostolic See, and yet were sent back with such an improvident arrangement.

units.la: 20. Et Nicetas quidē Patricius, Hadriatici freti servator, cū classibus destinatus, accepta hujusmodi rem occasione, multas prædas ab ipsis Sclavinis abstulit, & quibusdam castris dirrenit homines captivos abduxit, nec tamē quæ præfati venerabiles Apocrisarii perdiderunt, hactenus sunt. Sanè spiritalem tuā nolumus ignorare fraternitatē, super castra nostra desti uēta, tot populi vōnæ nostræ in captivitate fine qualibet parcitate subtractis, supra q dici potestanimum nostrarum motum. Non n. congrue gestū est, ut usdē Sclavinis nostris cum navibus suis apud Barinum in communis utilitatis cōsistentibus, & nihil sibi adversi aliunde immuere putantibus, tā impie dispetetur, sibi, cōtingerent, quæ si ptænoscerét, nequaquam prorsus incurrerent. Qua de re dilectionem tuam hortamur & admonemus, ut mox id corrigere jubeat, & ipsos ad propria cum suis reduci præcipiat, si charitatis vinculum numquam inter nos fore cupiat dissoluendum. Nullas morialium hactenus Imperium vestrum talia commisisse recolit, ac per hoc nisi correctionem jussio tua prævenat, justè severitatis nostrae proxima ultio proculdubio subsequatur; ... scerit tamen penitus impunitum, quod in contemptum nostrum tanta temeritate constat factum.
units.tr: 20. And the patrician Nicetas, guardian of the Adriatic sea, was sent out with the fleets, and seizing the occasion of this affair, he carried off many spoils from the very Slavs, and from certain fortresses he led away men as captives; yet what the aforesaid venerable envoys lost has not been recovered to this day. Certainly we do not wish Your Spiritual Brotherhood to be ignorant concerning our fortresses, which have been laid waste, and so many of our people carried off into captivity without any mercy, such that the motion of our spirits can scarcely be described. For it was not fitting that the same Slavs of ours, who were with their ships at Bari, engaged in common service and thinking that nothing adverse could come to them from elsewhere, should be so impiously treated, and should suffer what, had they known beforehand, they would never have incurred. For this reason we exhort and admonish Your Love to order that this be corrected at once, and to command that they be brought back to their own homes with their people, if you desire that the bond of charity between us never be dissolved. Our memory recalls that no mortal has hitherto committed such things against our Empire; and therefore, unless your command anticipates the correction, undoubtedly the near vengeance of our just severity will follow. ... Yet it cannot be that what has been done with such temerity in contempt of us should go wholly unpunished.

units.la: Nihilominus etiam te existimare scimus, obstupuisse nos talia de Missis nostris audientes, ... nobis dulcedinis literarum intimarunt: adeò quippe illos mordinatè significans ambisse, ut vagarentur adho deposto, non solùm jumenta sed & homines interficerent.
