Quæ res si ita ... cti ... nostræ valde displiceat, & ut ad certitudinem perducatur, vehementer exoptat. Vtrum & ipsi diligenter à nobis inquisitum, tale quid egisse modis omnibus negaverunt. Et quia non est, ... in tacem arguat, non est probatò eis neq; convictis neq; confessis iustæ correctionis aliquid ... ndum. Verum nos illos nec ita educavimus, nec ita docuimus, ut ad talia, qualia perhibes, labe-... ideò de illis quidquam eorum credere non facile judicarius. Cæterum ... eorum sonuit, ... tenitas tua perhibuit, dicens, non gladus sed dentibus nostros dilaniandos esse, nisi causa ... ncerentur, cum si non essent in Imperio tuo, nihil tale sibi præsumerent. Sed nec ... quidquam hominum penitus formidarent, quin immo nec tantum aunas viros & ad-... videntur, Deo gratias, expavescerent.
units.tr: Nevertheless, we know that you too will think that we were astonished on hearing such things about our envoys ... they made known to us by the sweetness of their letters; for they, signifying in a disordered way, had so pursued that, with the deposed one, they should wander about, and slay not only beasts of burden but also men. If this thing is so ... it displeases our ... very much, and we earnestly desire that it be brought to certainty. Both they and we have diligently inquired, and they have denied in every way that they did any such thing. And since it is not ... let him who accuses be convicted; no just correction is to be applied to them, since they have neither been convicted nor confessed. Yet we did not so bring them up, nor so teach them, that they would fall into such crimes as you assert; therefore we do not easily judge that anything of that kind should be believed of them. Moreover, ... of them sounded, as Your Highness reported, saying that they were to be torn apart not by the sword but by our teeth, unless ... were not in your Empire, they would presume nothing of the kind. But they do not fear any men at all; nay, they would not even be terrified, thanks be to God, by ... men of ... so great.

units.la: Vastrenò de Neapoli nobis in Christo fraternitas tua monuit, quasi miserimus populum nostrum incidendas arbores, & messes igne cremandas, & hanc ditionem nostram subdendam. Cum ... nostra fuerit, & parentibus nostris, piis Imperatoribus, tributa persolverit; verum nos ab ... præter solitas functiones nihil exegimus, nisi salute ipsorum, videlicet ut desisterent contra ... perdutum, & plebem desiderent in sequi Christianorum. Nam infidelibus arma, & alimenta, ... subsidia tribuentes, per totius Imperii nostri litora eos ducunt, & cum ipsis tones beati Petri Apostolorum Principis fines sui tui depraedari conantur: ita ut facta videatur Neapolis Panormus vel ... edes Saracenorum. Cumq; nostri quoq; Saracenos insequuntur, ipsi ut possint evadere, Nea-... fugiant. Quibus non est nec ssitum Panormum reperere, sed Neapolim fugientes, ibidemq; ... sq; pervideruntlatitantes, ruisus improuiso ad certamina redeunt. Super quibus sæpe illos mo-... sed ex admonitione pejores effectu sunt, adeo ut Episcopum proprium (quoniam eos, ut vita-... consortia malignorum, monitabat) ex urbe projicerent, illustres ac proceres civitatis compedi-... obligarent. Ergo si sociatam non dissoluentur infidelium secundum Apostolum, qui præcepit ...; Nolite jugum ducere cum infidelibus; & Episcopum proprium & pastorem non receperint, portio-... corum ponemus cum us, quorum libenter amplexi sunt unionem, & uno lance appendemus ... que. Quoniam non solùm qui faciunt talia, sed qui consentiunt facientibus, dignos morte judi-... moratus iniquus Apostolus, præsertim cum unanimiter arma contra Christianos ferant, & di-... e, & si quos fidelium capere possunt, Saracenorum manibus tradant, cum ipsis ad bella uno ... tu procedentes.
units.tr: Moreover, Your Fraternity has warned us in Christ concerning Naples, as if we had sent our people to cut down trees and burn the harvests with fire, and to subject this province of ours. ... has been ours, and has paid tribute to our parents, the pious emperors; but we have exacted nothing beyond the usual dues from them ... except for their own salvation, namely that they might desist from ... and desire to follow the people of the Christians. For giving arms and provisions to the unbelievers, they lead them along the shores of our whole Empire, and together with them they try to plunder the territories of the blessed Peter, the Prince of the Apostles, so that Naples seems to have become Palermo or ... the house of the Saracens. And when our men also pursue the Saracens, they flee to Naples so that they may escape; ... they do not have the means to find Palermo, but fleeing to Naples, and there lurking ... they return again unexpectedly to battles. Concerning these matters we often admonished them, but by admonition they became worse in deed, so much so that they cast out their own bishop from the city (because he warned them to shun the company of wicked men) and bound the illustrious men and nobles of the city in chains. Therefore, if they do not break off the alliance with the unbelievers, as the Apostle commands, saying: "Be not unequally yoked with unbelievers," and if they do not receive their own bishop and pastor, we shall place their portion with those whose union they have gladly embraced, and we shall weigh them in the same scale ... For not only those who do such things, but those who consent to those who do them, the wicked Apostle judges worthy of death, especially since they bear arms unanimously against Christians, and if they can seize any of the faithful, they hand them over to the hands of the Saracens, proceeding with them to war as one ...

units.la: 23. De cætero, Fratet charillime, noveris, cum virtute summi Opificis nostri exercitu nostrum præ notato, Bari triumphis nostris submissa, Saracenos Tarenti pariter & Calabriæ moxmi-... sumiliasse, simul & comminuuile, ac hos celeriter, duce Deo, penitus contiuuerunt, si à mari ... facinnt escarum admittere copias, vel etiam classibus à Panormo vel Africa suscipere multitudi-... Quapropter spiritalis fraternitas tua, quia per totum nostrorum cunei populorum in utrisq; lo-... nunquam studeat, necesse est sufficientem stolum destinare, qui illos ab acceptendis ali-... man coerceat: & si plurimas contigerit sicut sæpe nuntiatur, pessimæ gentis advenire cater-... illis resistere, divino munitus brachio, valeat. Nam iste ... stratigus Georgius licet solerter ... & strenuè pro suo posse decerteet, non tamen sufficit obviare, si plures ini micorum naves ex ... sper apparerent, non videlicet nisi pauca protsus e chalendina possidens. Et quia nonnulli miserunt ... Panormi latitunculi cum d sagenis, solatio & refugio jam memoratorum Neapolitano-... Tyrrhenum mare debacchantur, oportet ut ad hos capiendos tuæ fraternitatis stolus si... ssitant. Ibi sunt, qui cum Calabrianis Saracenis indefessa stipendia præbent, & iis, ... st, at auxilia quotidiana ministrant. Unde si capiantur sagenæ, maxima ex parte Saracenorum ... qui im Calabriæ constringentur.
units.tr: 23. Furthermore, dearest brother, know that with the power of the Supreme Maker, our army, sent forth in advance, having been subjected to our triumphs at Bari, has also overcome the Saracens of Taranto and of Calabria, and has put them to flight, and with God leading, has quickly and completely hemmed them in, if from the sea they should admit troops of the enemy, or receive multitudes by fleets from Palermo or from Africa. Wherefore your spiritual brotherhood, since throughout all the peoples of our realm... (the Latin here is badly garbled), must of necessity send a sufficient fleet which may restrain them from receiving other forces; and if, as is often reported, a great host of this most wicked nation should arrive, it may be able, fortified by the divine arm, to resist them. For that commander Georgius, though he strives skilfully and bravely with all his power, is not sufficient to meet them if more enemy ships should appear, since he holds only a few ships in the port. And because some have sent little nets from Palermo, as a relief and refuge for the aforesaid Neapolitans... the Tyrrhenian Sea rages. It is necessary that your brotherhood's fleet be stationed to capture these. There are those who give unwearied pay to the Calabrian Saracens and supply them daily with aid. Hence, if the nets are seized, the greater part of the Saracens... will be bound in Calabria.

units.la: 24. Nam enim Calabria, Deo auctore, expugnata, Siciliam disposuimus, secundùm commune ... liberati restituere. quod tantum erit utrumq; facilius, quantum illi, divina dextera captis ... si nescunt, succumbendo sunt, sed celerius institurint. Nulla ergo tarditas, nulla mora, Frater ... a mirendo stolo proveniat, ne vel per escarum à mari tectè ptarum abundantiam, vel per ... Agareuorum classium nimerositatem hiorum vires non infirmentur, sed roborentur: ... ostiem postea difficilius infirmentur, sed & frustrà nostræ pei siccum indefessè certamen ... per aquora factum alqua stipendia vel copiosam multitudinem consequuti.
units.tr: 24. For, Calabria being conquered by the author of all, we have arranged to restore Sicily, liberated according to the common... This will be all the easier for both, as much as those (who are held captive by the divine right hand)... if they do not know how, they yield by succumbing, but they have been more quickly... Let there therefore be no delay, no hindrance, brother... let it come from the fleet, lest their strength be weakened rather than strengthened, through the abundance of nets properly... by the sea, or through the numerous Saracen fleets; ... afterwards, they are weakened with greater difficulty, and our unceasing struggle on land is in vain... made over the waters, they obtain pay and a large multitude.

units.la: Postremo multum desiderabili fraternitati tuæ Autprandum fideleni & familiarem homi... qui quendam, quæ luce desinit epistolæ, viva voce tuo a Deo ruendo in perio referebit, ... obis in Christo fraternitate tua susceptæ benignè, non exceptis o so diebus, qu tu-... e scedetur, sed celerius ad nos, quia ita convers, nulla impediente mora. Christo pro-...
units.tr: Finally, to your most desirable brotherhood, we send our faithful and familiar man, who, by the living voice, will report to you, concerning the letter which ends here, what has been done under God in your empire... to be received kindly by your brotherhood in Christ, not delayed for only a few days, but sent back to us more quickly, since so it is agreed, with no hindrance of delay. To Christ...

units.la: CAROLI II. REGIS AUG. RESCRIPTUM
units.tr: THE RESCRIPT OF CHARLES II, KING AND AUGUSTUS

units.la: DE POTESTATE REGIA SEV IMPERATO- RIA, auctoritate Papæ, & iurisdictione utriusque regiminis.
units.tr: ON ROYAL OR IMPERIAL POWER, THE AUTHORITY OF THE POPE, AND THE JURISDICTION OF EACH GOVERNMENT.

units.la: SANCTISSIMO acreverentissimo Patri * Hadriano, Summo Pontifici & Papæ, CAROLVS Dei gratia Rex & Spiritualis filius vester.
units.tr: To the most holy and most reverend Father Hadrian, Supreme Pontiff and Pope, from CHARLES, by the grace of God King and your spiritual son.

units.la: Legimus in libro Paralipomenon, filios Israel mente pacifica misse ad proelium, quia nostris vindicta, sed obtinendæ pacis gratia dimicarunt. Quod rursum dicimus, quia cogitationes, indignitatibus potestati Regiæ literis vestris inhonoratum, inconvenientibus Episcopali modestiæ ... datis gravatum, contumeliis & opprobriis dehonestatum, aliter quàm vellemus mente pacificabere, ut tandem animadvertatis, quamquam pertinacionibus humanis obnoxium, in imagine Dei ambulantem esse nos hominem, habetè sensium paterna & avita successione, Dei gratia Regni nomine ac culmine sublimatum; & quod his majus est, Christianum, Catholicum, fidei orthodoxae cultorem, sacris literis ac legibus, tam Ecclesiasticis quàm Sæcularibus, ab infantia eruditum, nullo crimine publico in audientia Episcopali legaliter ac regulariter accusatum, minime autem con-
units.tr: We read in the Book of Chronicles that the sons of Israel went out to battle with a peaceful mind, because they fought not for vengeance but to win peace. We say this again, because our thoughts, dishonoured by the slights done to royal power in your letter, burdened by things unbecoming to episcopal moderation ... given, and disgraced by insults and reproaches, have been disturbed otherwise than we wished. We ask that you may at last consider that we are a man, subject to human frailties yet walking in the image of God, raised to the name and summit of kingship by the grace of God through paternal and ancestral succession; and, what is greater than this, a Christian, a Catholic, a defender of the orthodox faith, taught from infancy in sacred letters and in laws, both ecclesiastical and secular, never legally or regularly accused of any public crime in an episcopal hearing, and not in any way ... convicted.

units.la: cet legamus Apostolum pluta de se dixisse ob aliorum salutem necessitate compulsum: quippe humiliter vobis locuti, benigna & pacifica atque honorabilia nobis scripta impetrare ut quietem pacis & veneratione, quam apud autecessores vestros nostri decessores & nos ... quoquo modo obtinere possumus. Scripsimus vobis per Actardum Episcopum & manifestam nostrae Legatum lingullatum ac vitium, quam inconvenientia pro Hincmaro quondam ... Episcopo ex nomine vestro nobis scripta fuerunt: quæ nos à vobis processisse non credebamus ... tantes nos ratione competit ... incompetentibus, quæ aliorum instinctu nobis extenuè scripsérunt, calamum revocare. Sed ipsa vana fallacitatis aliter nobis, quàm sperabamus, evenit. ... quippe litterarum, quos per ... Actardum Episcopum nobis vestra direxit paternitas, laudabilem charitatis & fraternitatis nostræ magnitudinem vos præstitisse invenimus, & mox dicentes perto murmure & tumultuoso clamore indebitae reprehensionis adversus paternitatem vestram denotatos repertimus: siccque audiatur nostram sapientiam collaudastis, ut quasi honestius & rectius onustius nos solitus contumeliis afficere voluéritis, quem non per insipientiam, sed per murmuratione & clamore contra debitam charitatem delinquere demonstrabatis, & quasi vasculi melle illiti, & de eodem fonte, quo & ante missæ litteræ ... postea iniuriis, nobis permisculum propinaverunt, fatentes illa, quæ aliorum instinctu & non à vobis processisse credebamus, ... stra fuisse.
units.tr: Yet we read that the Apostle said many things of himself, compelled by necessity for the salvation of others. Indeed, speaking to you humbly, we asked for letters that were kind, peaceful and honourable to us, so that we might obtain, in whatever way we can, the quiet of peace and the reverence which our predecessors and we have held before your predecessors. We wrote to you through Bishop Actardus and your legate ..., and we recalled our pen from the inconsistent things which were written to us in your name for the late Bishop Hincmar, which we did not believe had come from you but had been written to us in a disparaging way at the urging of others. But the vain outcome of this deceit turned out otherwise than we hoped. For in the letters which your fatherhood sent us through Bishop Actardus, we found that you had shown a praiseworthy greatness of charity and brotherhood towards us; yet soon, on reading them, we found that you had been denounced with a murmur and tumultuous clamour of undue reproach against your fatherhood. Thus you praised our wisdom, as though you wished to load us with insults more honourably and more rightly, when you showed that we offended not through folly but through murmuring and clamour against due charity. As if from a little vessel smeared with honey, and from the same fountain as the earlier letter, you poured out to us, mixed with injuries, the things which we believed had come not from you but at the instigation of others ... were.

units.la: 2. Nam in præcedentibus litteris nos perjurum, tyrannum, ac perfidum, & distractores Ecclesiasticarum, non confessum nec ordine judiciario legaliter ac regulariter convictum, ... in istis autem murmurationis crimen nobis impegistis, & tumultuosi clamoris nævum impositum ... guente Domino carnalem Israel per Prophetam, unde nos coarguitis; Quia non fecerit judicium ... morem. Et Apostolus; Omnis, inquit, clamor & indignatio tollatur à vobis. Et non leviis malum ... muratio his, quibus nos antea denotastis, dicente Apostolo; Neque murmuraveritis, sicut quidam ex eis murmuraverunt, & à serpentibus perierunt. Et, ut beatus dicit Gregorius; Nullus murmurator regnum Dei intrare permittitur. Hinc colligendum est, quantum peccatum sit murmurando, quæ ... Dei intercludit; sicut & illa peccata gravia, post quorum enumerationem dicit Apostolus, ... agunt, regnum Dei non possidebunt. Et non, ut scriptum est, tumultuoso clamore paternitatem vestram debitè reprehendimus, sed quæ nobis ex vestro nomine scripta fuerunt, non multorum ... quibus tumultus fieri solet, sed nostra tantum voce retulimus. Et quoniam talia vomitiss ... sancta Romana Ecclesia, in omnibus semper discretissima atque camillima, dictata fuisse ... quàm credidimus: quia ipsa sancta Sedes cum modestia & discretione semper corrigere, & ... bitè corrigere, secundum uniuscujusque personam & ordinem solita lit, suggesserimus. Igitur ... locuti sumus, testimonium perhibere de malo; si autem bene, quid nobis successeritis?
units.tr: 2. For in the preceding letter you called us perjurer, tyrant, traitor and despoiler of Church property, though we had not been convicted by confession or legally and regularly by judicial process ... but in these letters you charged us with the crime of murmuring and stained us with the mark of tumultuous clamour ... The Lord, speaking through the Prophet to carnal Israel, reproves you: "Because he has not done judgment ..." And the Apostle: "Let all clamour and indignation be put away from you." And not lightly is the evil of murmuring ... to those whom you earlier denounced us, as the Apostle says: "Neither murmur, as some of them murmured, and were destroyed by serpents." And, as blessed Gregory says: "No murmurer is permitted to enter the kingdom of God." From this it must be gathered how great a sin murmuring is, which ... shuts out the kingdom of God; just as those grave sins, after whose listing the Apostle says that those who commit them shall not inherit the kingdom of God. Nor, as is written, have we reproved your fatherhood with tumultuous clamour; but what was written to us in your name we reported with our own voice, not with the noise of many ... by which tumult is usually made. And since such things were vomited forth ... the holy Roman Church, always most discreet and most calm in all things, is believed not to have dictated them ... rather than we believed; for that holy See has always been accustomed to correct with modesty and discretion, and to correct ... according to each person and rank. Therefore we have spoken, bearing witness to evil; but if well, why have you struck us?

units.la: 3. Scriptum est, Abraham licet sanctum, ut à Deo sanctificatum hominem, tamen ... dixisse: Num perdes justum cum impio: non hoc est tuum, qui judicas omnem terram; & non tagarci ... num fulcepisse. Et nos arguimus, quoniam humili placatione vobis suggesserimus, non esse vestram confessum vel legaliter ac regulariter convictum, Regia etiam potestate (gratia Dei, prædicto, tali ... plebeio & de criminibus confutato, scribendo impingere: sciens, quàm grave lit fratri ... bis impactis minus est dicere fatue, nulliqué detrahendum, vel contra fas maledicendum ... autem Regi, a Apostolica doctrina, atque b sancti David in Saulis jam à Domino reprobati, & c Salomonis Sapientia, ac d Nabuhæ prodit historia.
units.tr: 3. It is written that Abraham, though holy, as a man sanctified by God, nevertheless said: "Will you destroy the righteous with the wicked? Far be it from you, who judge all the earth." And ... he took it up. And we charge that, since we suggested to you with humble submission that it is not your confession nor legally and regularly proven, and with royal power (by the grace of God, as said above, such ... a plebeian and refuted by crimes) you would strike by writing, knowing how grave it is for a brother ... It is less to call a man fool when such charges are laid, nor should one be slandered or cursed contrary to right ... but to the King, from a the apostolic teaching, and b the example of David against Saul, already rejected by the Lord, and c the wisdom of Solomon, and d the history of Naboth.

units.la: 4. In eodem enim et eisdem literis nobis datum consilium, (si forte dicipiatis consulimus quod est Domini exemplis contrarium, & Decretis Sanctorum inveniturab vestris dicamus) omnia, quæ à Sede Apostolica, cui per Dei gratiam præsidetis, directa sunt, alacri mente, ... pere, animo grato amplecti, & humili semper debemus intentione recipere. Scriptum est enim ... nomine, nos perjurum, tyrannum, ac pertidum, & distractorem esse rerum Ecclesiasticarum. Et hæc alacri mente percipere, animo grato amplecti, & humili semper debemus intentione recipere? Nisi scriptor forte velit nos cum vulgo Æthiopes vocare argenteos: & ideo quis nobis pulcher videatur, qui a nomine Bellus vocatur, & sibi cantare cum Persio ——Quicquid * calcaverit hic, rosa fiat:
units.tr: 4. For in the same letters we were given advice (if perhaps we are advised of what is contrary to the Lord's example, and what is found contrary to the decrees of the saints, let us say it with you) that everything which is sent from the Apostolic See, over which by the grace of God you preside, we ought always to receive with a ready mind, with a grateful spirit, and with humble attention. For it is written ... in your name, that we are a perjurer, a tyrant, a traitor, and a despoiler of Church property. And should we receive these things with a ready mind, embrace them with a grateful spirit, and always accept them with humble attention? Unless perhaps the writer wishes us to be called, with the common crowd, Ethiopians of silver; and so whatever is pleasing to us, which is called Bellus, and to sing with Persius: "Whatever this man tramples, let it become a rose."

units.la: Illudque Propheticum incurrere: Væ his, qui ponunt amarum in dulce: cùm Dominus dicentibus ad se Judæis: Nonne bene dicimus nos, quia Samaritanus es tu, & Dæmonium habes? quod recognovit, tacendo consensit; & patienter repulit, quod fallaciter audivit, dicens; Ego Dæmonium non habeo. Cujus promodulo nostro in hoc exemplum secuti, qui nos dignatus est ex ratione ostendere se peccatorem non esse, qui ex virtute divinitatis poterat peccatores justificare: de his, quæ in nobis non recognovimus, liter & patienter apud paternitatem vestram excusavimus, ne si penitus taceremus, tales, quales tabamur, tacendo & consentiendo esse nos fateremur, & quasi confessi & nostra confessione convicti judicaremur.
units.tr: And we run into that prophetic word: "Woe to those who put bitter for sweet," since the Lord, when the Jews said to him, "Do we not say well that you are a Samaritan and have a demon?", acknowledged it, by keeping silent consented; and patiently repelled what he had falsely heard, saying, "I have no demon." Following this example, which he who deigned to show by reason that he was not a sinner, though by the power of his divinity he could justify sinners, we have patiently and calmly excused before your fatherhood the things which we did not acknowledge in ourselves, lest, if we kept wholly silent, we should be taken to confess by silence and consent that we are such as we were charged with being, and be judged as though confessing and convicted by our own confession.

units.la: 5. Et hoc hortamentum, quod in litteris ex nomine vestro ab Actardo Episcopo nobis delatis invenimus, scilicet ut omnia, quæ a Sede Apostolica nobis veniunt, humili semper debeamus intentione recipere, non solum (ut præmisimus) Evangelicæ veritati sed etiam decretis Sanctorum inventur adversum. In quorum Decretis legimus, eum absolvi non posse, qui in se ipsum dixerit mortis causam, qua edicta in alium puniretur, * falsum videlicet testimonium: cùm omnis, qui sibi fuerit mortis causa, major homicida sit. Et hinc decreverunt, ut quicumque sub ordinatione vel Diaconatus vel Presbyteri vel Episcopatus, mortali crimine dixerint se esse pollutos, à supradictis ordinationibus submovendos. Et nos, si ad talia nobis impacta tacendo consentiremus, non solum à regimine Regio, verum & à Catholicæ Ecclesiæ communione nos ipsos sequestraremus. Non igitur talia nobis ex parte Sedis Apostolicæ & nomine vestro scripta, mente alacri percipere, & animo grato amplecti, & humili semper debemus intentione recipere, quæ, sicut in eisdem litteris ex sententia Salomonis subjungitur, quasi stimuli & sicut clavi in altum defixi esse viderentur, quia culpas delinquentium nesciunt palpare sed pungere. Cui sententiæ item † Sapientis verba * referimus, quibus dixit: Priusquam interroges, ne vituperes quemquam; & cum interrogaveris, (id est, probaveris) corripe juste. Sicut † Nathan David Regem prius interrogavit, & interrogatione probatum corripuit: & cùm causa correptionis defuit, humiliter adoravit, velut in sacra Historia legimus. Mandate & scribite, quæ vestro & nostro ministerio congruunt, ut defessores vestri nobis & nostris decessoribus mandaverunt, atque scripserunt, & alacri mente gratoque animo accipiemus.
units.tr: 5. And this exhortation, which we found in the letter delivered to us from your name by Bishop Actardus, namely that everything that comes to us from the Apostolic See we ought always to receive with humble attention, is opposed not only to the Gospel truth (as we have said) but also to the decrees of the saints. In those decrees we read that one cannot be absolved who has named himself the cause of death, by which another would be punished, that is, by false witness; since everyone who is the cause of death for himself is a greater murderer. And hence they decreed that whoever, under ordination as deacon, presbyter or bishop, has said he is defiled by mortal crime, must be removed from those ordinations. If we were to consent by silence to such charges laid upon us, we would separate ourselves not only from royal government but also from the communion of the Catholic Church. Therefore we ought not to receive with a ready mind, embrace with a grateful spirit, and always accept with humble attention such things as have been written to us on behalf of the Apostolic See and in your name, which, as the sentence of Solomon is added in the same letters, seem to be like goads and nails fixed deep, because they do not know how to soothe the faults of offenders but to prick them. To this saying we also refer the words of the Wise Man, in which he said: "Before you question, do not blame anyone"; and "when you have questioned" (that is, proved) "reprove justly." As Nathan first questioned King David, and reproved him once the matter was proven; and when there was no cause for reproof, he humbly worshipped, as we read in sacred history. Command and write what befits your ministry and ours, as your predecessors commanded and wrote to us and to our predecessors, and we will receive it with a ready mind and a grateful spirit.

units.la: 6. Litteræ autem ex nomine vestro semper sine interrogatione, id est probatione, nos pungunt, & peccata, pro quibus invitum pungunt, sponte confessa vel ordine judiciario legaliter acregulariter comprobata, non ostendunt: & cùm peccata manifesta & probata desinr, fomentis benignæ adhortationis & allocutionis non refovent: reprehendente hinc Domino populorum Rectores peros, atque dicente: Vos autem cum auctoritate imperabitis eis & cum potentia. Quibus Apostolus recitam dedit commonitionis, singulis dicens: Argue, obsecra, increpa in omni patientia & doctrina, miscens temporibus tempora, terroribus blanditmenta. Dirum magistri, & pium patris ostendentes affectum, id est disciplinatos & inquietos debent durius arguere; obedientes autem ac patientes, ut in melius proficiant, obsecrate; negligentes autem & contemnentes debent utique increpare atque corripere; & de criminalibus peccatis aut ultrò confessos, aut ordine judiciario comprobatos atque convictos, secundum modum culpæ legaliter ac regulariter judicare. Noluit Apostolus, inquit beatus Augustinus, hominem ex hoc homine judicari ex arbitrio suspicionis, vel etiam extraordinario usurpato judicio: sed potius ex lege Dei secundum ordinem Ecclesiæ, sive ultrò confitentem, sive accusatum atq; convictum. Alioquin illud cur dixit: Si quis frater nominatur, aut fornicator, aut idolis servitus &c? nisi quia eam nominationem intelligi voluit quæ fit in quemquam, cum sententia ordine judiciario atq; integritate proferetur. Nam si nominatio deficit, multi damnandi sunt innocentes; quia sæpe falsò in quemquam crimen nominatur. Plerique tamen boni Christiani propterea tacent & sufferunt aliorum peccata, quæ noverunt, quia doceri sæpe deferuntur, ut ea quæ sciunt judicibus Ecclesiasticis probare non possint. Quamvis autem quædam, non tamen indici facile credenda sunt, nisi certis indicis demonstrentur, nisi ordine judiciario comprobentur, ut, si per judicium mali ab Ecclesiæ communione auferri non possunt, tolerentur potius, ne perverse malos evitando quisq; ab Ecclesia ipse discedens, eos, quos fugere videtur, vincat ad gehennam.
units.tr: 6. But letters written in your name always prick us without first examining the matter, that is, without proof. They do not show the sins for which they prick us, whether those sins were freely confessed or legally and regularly proved through judicial process. And when manifest and proven sins are left unpunished, they do not soothe us with the warm comfort of kindly exhortation and address. In this the Lord rebukes the rulers of peoples, saying: But you shall rule over them with authority and with power. To these the Apostle gave a fitting admonition, saying to each: Reprove, entreat, rebuke in all patience and teaching, mixing times with times, threats with flatteries. Showing the harshness of a teacher and the loving feeling of a father, the teachers ought to rebuke more sharply those who are undisciplined and restless. Those who are obedient and patient they should entreat, that they may make greater progress. Those who are negligent and contemptuous they should certainly reprove and correct. And for criminal sins, judges ought to judge, according to the measure of the fault, those who have either confessed freely or have been convicted and proved by judicial process, and to do so legally and regularly. The Apostle, says the blessed Augustine, was unwilling that one man be judged by another on the basis of suspicion, or even by an extraordinary judgment seized upon outside the rules; but rather according to the law of God and the order of the Church, either against one who confesses freely or one accused and convicted. Otherwise, why did he say: If anyone who is named a brother is a fornicator, or an idolater, or a servant of idols, etc.? Unless he meant that naming which is made against someone when sentence is pronounced in due judicial order and with a fair hearing. For if the naming lacks such process, many innocent people would be condemned, since a crime is often falsely imputed to someone. Yet many good Christians therefore keep silent and endure the sins of others which they know, because they are often taught that such sins are reported so that those things which they know cannot be proved before the church judges. However, certain matters, though not to be readily believed on mere indications, are not to be believed unless they are demonstrated by certain signs and proved by judicial process; so that if wicked persons cannot be removed from communion with the Church by judgment, they are rather to be tolerated, lest anyone, in avoiding the wicked in a perverse way, withdraw from the Church himself and so be overcome by those whom he seems to flee, and be drawn to gehenna.

units.la: 7. Quod scriptum est in eisdem ex nomine vestro litteris, quia sane non patienter Pontificii vestri monita & correctiones nos audisse comperimus, liquidò patet adhuc perfectæ aliquid charitatis minus duntaxat habere, de qua dicit Apostolus: Charitas patiens est, benigna est, non inflatur, non irritatur, non agit perperam, omnia suffert, omnia sustinet. Cujus charitatis modum & perfectionem in benignitate ac patientia, in humilitate & sufferentia, exemplo sanctæ paternitatis vestræ in litteris vestris dicere admodum cupieremus, si Deus nos inde honorare dignaretur.
units.tr: 7. As for what is written in the same letters in your name, that our hearing of your pontifical monitions and corrections was not patient, it is plainly evident that we still lack something of perfect charity, of which the Apostle says: Charity is patient, is kind, is not puffed up, is not provoked, does not act perversely, bears all things, endures all things. We would very much like to speak, from the example of your holy fatherhood in your letters, of the measure and perfection of this charity in kindness and patience, in humility and forbearance, if God were pleased to honour us with it.

units.la: 8. Quod & in hoc posse mus addiscere, si in his, quæ ex nomine vestro nobis scripta sanctitati vestræ nprimus, sustinentes modicum quid insipientiæ nostræ, & supportaretis nos, sicut magnus Petrus, Apostolicæ & primæ Sedis primus Episcopus non solum patienter sed & gaudenter adeo fulcepit reprehensionem suam à coapostolo suo Paulo sibi ostensam, ut ejus epistolas, in quibus se reprehensum legerat, cum maximo favore laudaverit. Non enim ita suppurare eas laudare poterat, nisi legisset; & quia legx
units.tr: 8. This too we could learn from you, if you, the first of the holy see, would bear with us a little in our folly in those matters which have been written to us in your name, and would put up with us, just as the great Peter, the first bishop of the apostolic and first see, not only patiently but even gladly received the rebuke given him by his fellow apostle Paul, so much so that he praised with the greatest favour the epistles in which he had read that he was rebuked. For he could not have praised them so warmly unless he had read them; and by praising them so greatly he showed how patiently he received, with joy, his own just rebuke.

units.la: * al. calcaveris, ref. Satyr. 5. v. 40
units.tr: * Another reading: calcaveris; cf. Satire 5, v. 40.

units.la: Johan. 8. v. 48. ibid. v. 49.
units.tr: John 8. v. 48. Ibid. v. 49.

units.la: Ezechiel. 34. 2. Timoth. 4.
units.tr: Ezekiel 34. 2 Timothy 4.

units.la: 1. Corinth. 13.
units.tr: 1 Corinthians 13.

units.la: Galat. 1. 1. Petr. 3. legit scriptum, reprehensum se in eis invenit: & quoniam eas tam granditer laudavit, quàm gratantes justam reprehensionem suam accepto tulerit patienter, ostendit. Et cùm à minoribus suis reprehensus fuit, cur ad Gentiles intraverit, non eis nudo & tumido sermone respondit, ut omnia, quæ egerat, patientissimè sustinerent; necaliquid in eorum querela de sua potestate dixit, sed humili ejus ratione placavit, atque in causa reprehensionis suæ etiam testes adhibuit. Quia si in querela fidelium, ut beatus dicit Gregorius, aliquid de sua potestate diceret, profecto doctor mansuetudinis non fuisset.
units.tr: Galatians 1. 1 Peter 3. He read what was written and found himself rebuked in them; and because he praised them so greatly, he shows how patiently he accepted, with thanks, his just rebuke. And when he was rebuked by his inferiors for going in to the Gentiles, he did not answer them with a bare and swollen speech, so that they should endure all that he had done with the greatest patience; nor did he say anything about his own authority in answer to their complaint, but he soothed them with a humble explanation, and in the matter of his rebuke he even called witnesses. For if in answer to the complaint of the faithful, as the blessed Gregory says, he had spoken of his own authority, he would surely not have been a teacher of gentleness.

units.la: 9. Si igitur pastor Ecclesiæ Apostolorum Princeps, signa & miracula singulariter faciens, non dedignatus est in causa reprehensionis suæ rationem humiliter reddere, quanto magis, inquit Gregorius Apostolicæ Sedis Pontifex, nos peccatores, cùm de re aliqua reprehendimur, nostros rationes humili placare debemus? Litteræ autem ex nomine vestro nobis directæ non humili nos ratione placarunt, sed indebita increpatione os nostrum oppilare studuerunt, quum, Deo gratia, libera adhuc fronte de his, quæ nobis per litteras ex nomine vestro directas impacta sunt, loqui possimus.
units.tr: 9. If then the minister of the Church, the Prince of the Apostles, who worked signs and miracles in a singular way, did not disdain humbly to give an account of his reasoning in the matter of his rebuke, how much more, says Gregory, Pontiff of the apostolic see, ought we sinners, when we are reproved about some matter, to soothe our reproachers with humble reasoning? But the letters directed to us in your name did not soothe us with humble reasoning; they strove to stop our mouth with undue reproof, although, thanks be to God, we can still speak with a free brow about those things which have been thrust upon us by the letters directed to us in your name.

units.la: 10. Scriptum est etiam in præfatis litteris nobis ex nomine vestro directis de Hincmaro, hoc modo: Volumus & auctoritate Apostolica jubemus, ipsum Hincmarum Landunensem Episcopum, vestra fretum potentia, ad lumina Sanctorum nostramque venire clementiam. Quo sanè veniente, venmat pariter accusator idoneus, qui nullâ possit auctoritate legitima respui. Et tunc in præsentia nostra, & totius Sedis Romanæ Synodali Collegio, causa illius prudenti ventilata examinue, ac diligenter inquisita, secundum Deum & sacrorum canonum constitutiones Spiritu Dei prolatas, sine protelatione aliqua finietur. Quæ relegentes, licet contra morem decessorum ac prædecessorum vestrorum hoc dictum invenerimus, id est, umbrosum seculi typhum inducere in Ecclesiam suam, quæ lucem simplicitatis & humilitatis diem Domini videre desiderantibus præfert, amen de voluntate non dubitavimus. Quia humano animo facilè potest subrepi, quod ex deliberatione conveniat immutari. Sed valde mirati sumus, ubi hoc dictator epistolæ, nobis per Adtardum Episcopum delatæ, scriptum invenerit, esse Apostolica auctoritate præcipiendum, ut Rex corrector iniquorum & distrigitor reorum, ac secundum leges Ecclesiasticas atque mundanas altior criminum, reum legaliter ac regulariter pro excessibus suis damnatum, sua fretum potentia, Romam dirigat; maximè autem illum, qui & ante depositionem contra custodiam publicam & contra quietem moliri in tribus Synodis extitit deprehensus, sicut in Gestis Episcopalibus paternitati vestræ directis continetur; & post depositionem suam, & per se & per quoscumque potuit, à sua pervicacia non quievit. Sed non miramur, si in posterioribus litteris ex nomine vestro nobis directis, est infulcitum, ut legaliter ac regulariter damnatus, qui nullis legibus decernitur quoquam gradu seu rebus ac facultatibus redonandus, antequam si contra custodiam & pacem publicam moliri non fuerit deprehensus, renovato Apostolicæ Sedis auctoritate judicio Provincia, qua fuerat judicatus, forte inveniatur innoxius, Regia nostra potentia ad vestrum veniat fretus, cùm se auctore damnato debeatur zelus rectitudinis, non clementia resolutionis. Quæ si non de eodem foramine, de eodem tamen conamine manarunt, de quo & anteriores fluxerunt, in quibus continetur, ut res omnes Hincmaro commissæ Ecclesiæ, donec ad propria revertetur, nobis committeretis, ut indemnes consisterent, & aliquod dispendium non incurrerent.
units.tr: 10. It is also written in the aforesaid letters directed to us in your name concerning Hincmar, in this way: We wish, and by apostolic authority we command, that Hincmar, bishop of Laon, relying on your power, come to the light of the saints and to our clemency. And when he comes, let there come with him a fit accuser, who cannot be rejected by any lawful authority. Then in our presence and that of the whole synodal college of the Roman See, his cause, having been weighed prudently and examined diligently, shall be settled according to God and the canonical constitutions brought forth by the Spirit of God, without any delay. In reading these, although we found this said contrary to the custom of your predecessors and forerunners, namely, that it introduces into its Church a shadowy pride of the world, whereas the Church of the Lord prefers the light of simplicity and humility to those who desire to see the day of the Lord, nevertheless we did not doubt the good will. For it can easily creep into a human mind that what was agreed upon in deliberation may be changed. But we were greatly astonished that, in the letter brought to us by Bishop Adtard, the drafter of the letter has written that by apostolic authority it must be commanded that the King, corrector of the wicked and punisher of the guilty, and, according to ecclesiastical and secular laws, the higher judge of crimes, should, relying on his power, send to Rome the man legally and regularly condemned for his excesses; and especially him who, both before his deposition, was found in three synods plotting against public custody and public peace, as is contained in the episcopal acts sent to your fatherhood; and who, after his deposition, has not ceased from his obstinacy, either himself or through whomsoever he could. But we are not surprised that in the later letters directed to us in your name it has been inserted that the man legally and regularly condemned, who by no laws is decreed to be restored to any rank or to goods and resources, should, before, if he has not been found to plot against public custody and peace, be sent by our royal power to you, relying on it, so that by a renewed judgment of the apostolic see in the province where he was judged he may perhaps be found innocent, since zeal for righteousness, and not clemency of release, is owed to the one who has been condemned by his own authority. And if these did not flow from the same channel, yet they flowed from the same effort from which the earlier ones flowed, in which it is contained that you would commit to us all the goods entrusted to Hincmar to the Church, until he returns to his own, so that they might remain unharmed and suffer no loss.

units.la: 11. Unde, sicut vobis rescripsimus, & nunciterum vobis scribere non piguit, sed exigente causa necessarium est: quia Reges Francorum, ex Regio genere nati, non Episcoporum Vicedominì, sed terræ domini hactenus summus computati. Et, in Leo ac Romana Synodus scripsit, Reges & Imperatores, quos terris divina potentia præcepit præesse, jus dislmguendorum negociorum Episcopi sanctus juxta Divalia constituta permiserunt, non autem Episcoporum villici extiterunt. Et sanctus Augustinus dicit: Per jura Regum possidentur possessiones, non autem per Episcopale imperium Reges villici suos actoresque Episcoporum. Et Dominus, Quæ sunt Cæsaris, Cæsari; & quæ sunt Dei, Deo reddi pit, qui etiam b Censum Regi reddidit. Et c Apostolus voluit servire * Regibus: voluit honorari & non conculcari Reges: Regem, inquit, honorificare. Et iterum: d Omnis, inquiens, anima potestatibus sublimioribus subdita sit. Et: Reddite ergo omnibus debita. Et paulò superius: Idcò necessitate subditi estote, non solum propter iram, sed etiam propter conscientiam. Et si revolveritis Regesta decessorum ac prædecessorum vestrorum, talia mandata, sicut habentur in litteris ex nomine vestro nobis directis per Adtardum Episcopum, decessores nostros à decessoribus vestris accepisse nullatenus invenietis. Unde pauca de pluribus vobis scribere necessarium duximus.
units.tr: 11. Therefore, as we have replied to you, and it does not trouble us to write to you again, but the cause requires it, since the kings of the Franks, born of royal stock, have hitherto been reckoned not stewards of bishops but lords of the land. And the Leo and Roman Synod wrote: Kings and emperors, whom divine power has commanded to rule the lands, have, according to the holy divine decrees, allowed the right of settling affairs to the bishops; they were not, however, stewards of the bishops. And the holy Augustine says: Possessions are held by the laws of kings, not by episcopal command, the kings being not stewards and agents of the bishops. And the Lord said: Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's, and he himself paid the tax to the king. And the Apostle willed that we should serve kings: he willed that kings be honoured and not trodden down: Honour the king, he says. And again: Let every soul be subject to the higher powers. And: Render therefore to all their dues. And a little earlier: Therefore be subject of necessity, not only because of wrath, but also for conscience' sake. And if you look through the records of your predecessors and forerunners, you will find that our predecessors never received from yours such commands as are contained in the letters directed to us in your name through Bishop Adtard. Therefore we thought it necessary to write to you a few things out of many.

units.la: 12. Sanctus Gregorius meritò vitæ & sapientiæ doctrina Apostolicæ Sedis Pontifex, & toti orbi colendus ac imitandus, Francorum Regibus Theodorico & Theoberto, prædecessoribus nostris, de præjudicio cujuldam Episcopi non ita, ut vos nobis scripsistis pro eo, qui pro meritis suis legaliter ac regulariter juste depositus est, scripsit hoc modo: Frater & Coëpiscopus noster Urfiomus, Taurinæ civitatis Antistes, in parrochiis suis, quæ intra Regni vestri sunt terminos constituta, grave omnino dicitur præjudicium sustinere, adeò ut contra Ecclesiasticam observantiam, contraque sacerdotalem gravitatem, & contra sacrorum canonum definita, nullo ejus exigente crimine, alter illic meruerit ordinari. Et quia parum visum est, si inlicitus non jungerentur mlicita, etiam res Ecclesiæ suæ, ut fertur, ablatæ sunt. Quod si fe veritas habet, quoniam nimiu intolerabile est, ut virtute opprimeretur, cui culpa non nocuit, præmisso paternæ salutationis alloquio petimus, ut quod Excellentia vestra, amore Ecclesiasticæ reverentiæ & æquitatis contemplatione, sponte potest impendere, nostra studeat benignius intercessione concedere, & justitiam illi, sicut de æquitatis ejus bono confidimus, faciat in omnibus usflodiri, custodiri atq; patefacta veritate, quod illicite actum est, corrigi. Pro utilitate ergo anima vestra hac apud vos nostra exhortatio locum inveniat, &c.
units.tr: 12. Saint Gregory, rightly Pope of the Apostolic See, admirable for the holiness of his life and the wisdom of his teaching, and to be honoured and imitated by the whole world, wrote to the Frankish kings Theoderic and Theudebert, our predecessors, about the wrong done to a certain bishop. He did not write as you have written to us concerning one who was lawfully, regularly and justly deposed for his deserts. He wrote in this manner: Our brother and fellow bishop Urfiomus, bishop of the city of Turin, is said to suffer a very grave wrong in his parishes, which lie within the bounds of your kingdom, so that, contrary to ecclesiastical custom, contrary to the dignity of the priesthood and contrary to the decrees of the sacred canons, another has been ordained there, though no crime demanded it. And since it seemed too little that unlawful acts should not be joined to unlawful acts, his church's property has also, it is said, been taken away. If this is true, since it is quite intolerable that one should be crushed by force when no fault has harmed him, we ask, with a greeting of fatherly address, that what your Excellency, out of love for ecclesiastical reverence and consideration of equity, can freely bestow, you will be pleased to grant more kindly at our intercession, and that you will cause justice to be maintained for him in all things, as we trust in the goodness of your equity, and that, once the truth is made known, what was done unlawfully be corrected. Let this our exhortation, for the good of your soul, find a place with you, etc.

units.la: 13. Sed & ad Romanum Exarchum, minoris dignitatis quàm simus Dei gratia Regiæ potestatis, de quodam Episcopo scripsit hoc modo: Perveniit ad nos, Blandum Ortonensis civitatis Episcopum, longo jam tempore in civitate Ravennati à vestra Excellentia detineri: & fit ut Ecclesia sine rectore, & populus quasi sine pastore grex fuit: & ibidem infantes pro peccatis absque baptismate moriuntur. Et rursus: Quia non credimus, quod eum Excellentia vestra, nisi ex aliqua probabilit exceßus causa tenuerit, oportet ut habita Synodo palàm fiat, si quod in eum crimen intenditur, & si talis in eo culpa reperitur, quæ adusque degradationem Sacerdotis deducatur: aliam ordinationem necesse est inquiramus, ne Ecclesia Dei in his, sine quibus eam Christiana non putatur esse religio, inculta ac destituta maneat. Sui autem Excellentia vestra aliter se habere, quàm de eo quod dicitur esse, perspexerit, enim ad ecclesiam suam reverti concedat, ut officium suum in communis sibi animabus adimpleat. Quibus mandatis beati Gregorii prædecessoris vestri de his, qui nondum judicio Synodali legaliter ac regulariter pro criminibus suis fuere depositi, collatis cum scriptis ex nomine vestro nobis directis, ex eo quòd legaliter ac regulariter pro suis excessibus judicio Synodali habetur depositus, ut eum nostra fretum potentia Romam mittamus, quæ potius sequenda sint, judicate. Nos autem auctoritatem vestram judicaturam potius credimus, ut ea sequamur, quæ decessores ac prædecessores vestri secundum scripturarum tramitem prædicationemq; majorum scripserunt, quàm illa, quæ scriptor sæpe dictæ epistolæ ex nomine vestro nobis directæ, continxit.
units.tr: 13. Likewise he wrote to the Roman Exarch, of lesser dignity than we who by the grace of God hold royal power, about a certain bishop, in this manner: It has come to us that Blandus, bishop of the city of Orte, has for a long time been detained in the city of Ravenna by your Excellency, and so the church is without a ruler, and the people are like a flock without a shepherd, and infants there die without baptism because of their sins. And again: Since we do not believe that your Excellency has held him except for some probable cause of offence, it is necessary that, a synod having been convened, it be made plain openly what crime is charged against him, and if such a fault is found in him as would lead to the degradation of a priest, then we must seek another ordination, lest the Church of God remain neglected and destitute in those things without which the Christian religion is not thought to exist. But if your Excellency finds that he is otherwise than he is said to be, let him allow him to return to his church, so that he may fulfil his office toward the souls committed to him. Now judge which of these commands of the blessed Gregory, your predecessor, concerning those who have not yet been lawfully and regularly deposed for their crimes by synodal judgment, when compared with the writings sent to us in your name, should rather be followed: whether, because he has been lawfully and regularly deposed for his offences by synodal judgment, we should send him to Rome relying on our power. We, however, believe that your authority would rather judge that we should follow those things which your predecessors and forefathers wrote according to the path of the Scriptures and the teaching of the elders, rather than those which the writer of the aforesaid letter, sent to us in your name, has set forth.

units.la: 14. Ait enim beatus Augustinus libro ad Januarium: Omnia talia, quæ neque sanctarum scripturarum authoritatibus continentur, nec conciliis Episcoporum statuta inveniuntur, nec consuetudine universalis ecclesia roborata sunt, reseccanda existimo. Et sanctus Leo de his, quæ à sacris canonibus habentur ita præfixa, & eisdem Apostolicæ Sedis sunt pronulgata decretis, ut nulla possint ratione convelli, constituuntur ut omni penitus authoritate sint vacuum, quicquid ab illorum fuerit constitutione diversum. Ac si cum Paulo diceret, quia sibi ipsi Apostolica Sedes in suis constitutionibus non potest esse contraria, licet nos aut Angelus de cælo evangelicet, vobis, præter quod evangelii annuimus vobis, anathema sit. Sed, ut in controversia Quintiliani legitur, floribus vafricia nebulonum venefica apes mortuas, quibus mellificandum fuerat. De scipturis sacris beatus Petrus adgi demonstrat, loquens de Pauli epistolis; quæ indocti & instabiles, inquit, depravant, sicut & cæteras scripturas ad suam ipsorum perditionem. Et de traditionibus Ecclesiasticis sanctus Innocentius: Dum, inquiens, unusquisque non quod traditum est, sed quod sibi visum fuerit, hoc existimat esse tenendum, inde diversa in diversis locis vel ecclesiis aut teneri aut celebrari cernuntur, ac fit scandalum populis: quas dum ut sciunt traditiones authoritate humana præsumptione corruptas, putant sibi aut Ecclesiis non convenire, aut ab Apostolis vel Apostolicis viris contrarietatem induciam. Contra quem morbum sanctus Cælestinus salubre cunctis celebravit antidotum, dicens: Nulli sacerdoti suos liceat canones ignorare, nec quicquam facere, quod Patrum regulis possit obviare. Quæ enim à nobis res digne servabitur, si decretalium norma constitutorum pro aliquorum libitu, licentia populi permissa, frangatur? Et sanctus Gelasius in Decretis suis: Patres nostri, Catholici videlicet & docti Pontifices, mnnaquaque secta quolibet tempore suscitata, quicquid pro fide, pro veritate, pro communione Catholica atque Apostolica, secundum scripturarum tramitem prædicationemque majorum, facta semel congregatione sanxerunt, inconsulsum voluerunt denuceps firmumq; constare, nec in hac eadem causa denuò, quæ præfixa fuerant, retractari qualibet recenti præsumptione permiserunt.
units.tr: 14. For the blessed Augustine says in his book to Januarius: I judge that all such things as are not contained in the authority of the holy Scriptures, nor found in the decrees of the councils of bishops, nor confirmed by the custom of the universal Church, should be cut away. And Saint Leo, concerning those things which are held as fixed by the sacred canons and proclaimed by the decrees of the same Apostolic See, so that they cannot be overturned on any ground, decrees that whatever is contrary to their enactment is to be made entirely void of authority. It is as if he were saying with Paul that the Apostolic See cannot be contrary to itself in its own constitutions: Though we, or an angel from heaven, preach to you anything beyond what we have preached to you, let him be anathema. But, as is read in Quintilian's controversy, by flowers the cunning of scoundrels, poisonous, makes dead bees, which ought to have made honey. Concerning the holy Scriptures, the blessed Peter also shows, speaking of the epistles of Paul: which the unlearned and unstable, he says, distort, as they do the other Scriptures, to their own destruction. And concerning ecclesiastical traditions, Saint Innocent says: While each person thinks that to be held not what has been handed down but what seems right to himself, hence different things are seen to be held or celebrated in different places or churches, and scandal arises for the people; and since they know these traditions have been corrupted by human authority and presumption, they think they do not agree with themselves or with the Churches, or they suppose a contrariety was introduced by the Apostles or apostolic men. Against this disease Saint Celestine offered a healthful antidote to all, saying: Let no priest be allowed to be ignorant of his canons, nor to do anything that might oppose the rules of the Fathers. For what matter will be worthily kept by us, if the norm of the decretal constitutions is broken at the pleasure of some, with licence granted to the people? And Saint Gelasius in his Decrees: Our Fathers, namely the Catholic and learned Pontiffs, whatever any sect, raised up at any time, they decided, in a single gathering, concerning faith, truth and Catholic and Apostolic communion, according to the path of the Scriptures and the teaching of the elders; they willed that it should stand from then on as unshaken and firm, and they did not permit those things which had been settled to be reopened in this same cause by any recent presumption.

units.la: 15. Videndum est igitur, quid hic tramites sanctarum Scripturarum & prædicatio majorum definiant. Scriptum quippe legimus in sacra Historia, dixisse Dominum per Prophetam Iosaphat Regi: Impio præbes auxilium, & his, qui oderunt Dominum, amicitia jungeris: & idcirco iram quidem Domini merebaris, sed bona opera inventa sunt in te, eò quod abstuleris lucos de terra Iuda. Et in Evangelio semel & secundò ac tertio monitum & non obedientem ad correctionem debitam, Dominus sicut Ethnicum & publicanum habeti.
units.tr: 15. We must therefore see what the path of the holy Scriptures and the teaching of the elders here define. We read in the sacred history that the Lord spoke through the Prophet to king Jehoshaphat: You give help to the ungodly, and you are joined in friendship with those who hate the Lord; therefore indeed you deserved the wrath of the Lord, but good works have been found in you, because you have removed the groves from the land of Judah. And in the Gospel the Lord bids that one who, once, twice and a third time admonished, does not obey the due correction, be regarded as a heathen and a tax collector.

units.la: 16. Et beatus Gregorius in Decretis suis, sicut in gestis Synodi invenire potestis, pervasorem non solùm rerum alienarum, sed etiam ecclesiæ sibi commissæ, anathematizatum decrevit: verùm & si alius hoc egerit, is qui præest ecclesiæ, si hoc vel ipse fieri præcipit, vel sine sua præceptione factum digna punire animadversione neglexerit, eum anathematizat. Satis ergo mirari non possumus, unde scriptor epistolæ nobis ex nomine vestro delatæ hanc legem apud se auro sculptam produxit, quam Dominus digito suo non scripsit, nec scribendam cuiquam inspiravit, neque ordinatam per Angelos in manu Mediatoris illius dedit: quam non Paganus indixit, non Christianus seduxit, non Ecclesiasticus vir decrevit, quæ de se sub illo cœlo sicut non atramento manu justitiæ, ita nec Spiritu Dei vivi scripta personuit: quàm me Regem à Deo constitutum, & gladio ex utraque parte acuto, ultore scilicet nocentium & defensore innocentium insignitum ad vindictam malefactorum, ut exponit Apostolus, laudem verò bonorum, reiatque damnati atque anathematizati fautorem esse præcipit, jubens ut Hinematum sacrarum legum prævaricatorem, sancti Sacerdotii vituperatorem, Regiæ dignitatis contra regulam Apostolicam dehortatorem, regni perturbatorem, perjurum, & seditionum authorem, Ecclesiæ sibi commissæ afflictorem, facultatum ecclesiasticarum sacrilegii fundatorem, ac stipatorem Episcoporum, ac totius populi nostrarum partium scandalizatorem, alienarum rerum pervasorem, & veniendo contra subscriptiones & professiones suas à scripto damnatum, potentia Regia fretum Romam venire faciamus.
units.tr: 16. And the blessed Gregory, in his Decrees, as you may find in the acts of the Synod, decreed that an intruder not only upon the goods of others but also upon the church committed to him should be anathematized. Indeed, if another does this, he who presides over the church, if he either commands it himself or, having neglected to punish with due censure what was done without his command, anathematizes him too. We cannot therefore sufficiently wonder whence the writer of the letter sent to us in your name has brought forth this law, as if engraved in gold by himself, which the Lord did not write with his finger, nor inspired anyone to write, nor gave, ordained through angels, into the hand of that Mediator; which no pagan proclaimed, no Christian led astray, no churchman decreed, and which, speaking of itself beneath that heaven, was written not with ink by the hand of justice, nor by the Spirit of the living God. I, a king appointed by God and invested with the sword sharpened on both sides, that is, the avenger of the wicked and the defender of the innocent for the punishment of evildoers, and, as the Apostle explains, for the praise of the good, and who commands that the one damned and anathematized be regarded as a favourer of such men, bid that the following be sent to Rome, relying on royal power: the transgressor of the sacred laws; the reviler of the holy priesthood; the one who dissuades a king's dignity contrary to the apostolic rule; the disturber of the kingdom; the perjurer and author of sedition; the oppressor of the Church committed to him; the perpetrator of sacrilege against ecclesiastical goods; the supporter of bishops, and the scandaliser of the whole people of our parts; the intruder upon the goods of others; and one who, in coming against his own signatures and professions, stands condemned by his own writing.

units.la: 17. Quis igitur hanc inversam legem Infernus evomuit? Quis Tartarus de suis abdiris & renebrolis. nebrosis cuniculis eructavit? Contra quam litteris sacris ostensa nobis est via, quam sequamur, apponita formae, cui imprimimur. Clamavit, inquit, Propheta ad Regem Israel, & ait: Servus tuus egressus est ad proelianduni cominus, cumque fugisset vir unus, adduxit eum quidam ad me & dixit: Custodi virum istum, qui fuerit lapsus, erit anima tua pro anima ejus, aut talentum argenti appendes. Dum autem ego turbatus huc illucque me verterem, subito non comparuit. Et ait Rex Israel ad eum: Hoc est judicium tuum, quod ipse decrevisti. At ille statim abstersit pulverem de facie sua, & cognovit eum Rex Israel, quod esset de Prophetis, qui aut ad eum: Haec tibi dicit Dominus: quia dimisisti virum dignum morte de manu tua, erit anima tua pro anima ejus, & populus tuus pro populo ejus. Reversus est igitur Rex Israel in domum suam audire contemnens, & furibundus venit in Samariam.
units.tr: 17. What then has Hell vomited forth this inverted law? What has Tartarus belched out from its dark and gloomy burrows? Against it the sacred letters have shown us the way we should follow, a pattern to which we are to be conformed. The prophet cried out to the King of Israel, and said: Thy servant went out into the midst of the battle; and when a man had fled, a certain one brought him to me and said: Keep this man; if he be found missing, thy life shall be for his life, or thou shalt pay a talent of silver. But while I was busy turning this way and that, he suddenly disappeared. And the King of Israel said to him: This is thy judgment, which thou thyself hast decreed. But he immediately wiped the dust from his face, and the King of Israel recognized him, that he was one of the prophets. And he said to him: Thus says the Lord: because you have let go out of your hand a man worthy of death, your life shall be for his life, and your people for his people. So the King of Israel returned to his house sullen and refusing to listen, and came furious into Samaria.

units.la: Quae nam vos dementia cepit? scientes dixisse Christum, Dei virtutem & Dei sapientiam; Per me Reges regnant, & conditores legum justa decernunt? Et sacri Canones, sicut credimus, & in Apostolicis litteris saepius legimus, Spiritu Dei conditi, & totius mundi reverentia sunt consecrati. Propterea videamus, quid de hujusmodi sancti Canones & sacrae Leges decernant.
units.tr: What madness has seized you? Knowing that Christ said, "I am the power of God and the wisdom of God," "By me kings reign, and lawgivers decree just things"? And the sacred canons, as we believe and as we often read in the apostolic letters, were framed by the Spirit of God and consecrated by the reverence of the whole world. Let us therefore see what such holy canons and sacred laws decree.

units.la: 18. Ait enim sanctum Aphricanum Concilium: Et illud petendum, quod apud terrae Principes statuere dignentur, ut si quis cujuslibet honoris Clericus judicio Episcoporum quocumque crimine fuerit damnatus, non liceat eum sive ab ecclesiis, quibus praefuit, sive a quolibet homine defensari, interposita poena damni, pecuniae & honoris; quae necatatem nec sexum excusandum esse praecipiant.
units.tr: 18. For the holy Council of Africa says: And this is also to be sought, that the princes of the earth deign to enact that if any clergyman of whatever rank has been condemned by the judgment of bishops for any crime, he may not be defended either by the churches over which he presided or by any person, under the penalty of loss of money and office; and they order that neither rank nor sex be excused.

units.la: 19. Ettunc Valens, Gratianus, & Valentinianus constituerunt, ut quicumque residentibus Sacerdotibus fuerit Episcopali loco detrusus & nomine, si aliquid contra custodiam publicam vel contra quietem moliri fuerit deprehensus, rursumque sacerdotum petere, a quo videtur expulsus, procul ab urbe, quam a infecit, secundum legem divae memoriae Gratiani, centum millibus vitam agat; sit ab eorum coetibus separatus, a quorum est societate discretus; hujusmodi personis illicitum, hujus legis tenore, sacra nostra adire secreta, & impetrare b scripta; omnibus abjectis per culpam sacerdotio personis, quae impetrata sunt, infecta cpermaneant, sciturus his, quorum defensione nituntur, que sunt prehensione non fuerunt, si hoc eis pollicentur suffragium, quod divinum non videntur meruisse judicium. Leo Papa apud Principalem potestatem petiit de Eutyche scandali & pravitatis authore, ut ab eo loco, qui Constantinopolitanae urbi nimis vicinus erat, longius transferretur, ne frequentionibus solaciis eorum, quos ad impietatem suam traxit, uteretur.
units.tr: 19. Then Valens, Gratian and Valentinian decreed that whoever, while the priests were residing, has been thrust into the episcopal place and name, if he is caught plotting anything against public custody or public peace, and again seeks to obtain the priesthood from which he seems to have been expelled, shall live far from the city he infected, for a hundred miles, according to the law of Gratian of divine memory; he shall be separated from the assemblies of those from whose fellowship he has been set apart. By the tenor of this law it is unlawful for such persons to approach our sacred secrets and obtain rescripts. The things obtained by persons removed from the priesthood through their fault shall remain void, knowing that those whose defence they rely on will not have been seized, if they promise them this support, which they do not seem to have deserved from divine judgment. Pope Leo petitioned the Imperial power concerning Eutyches, the author of scandal and perversity, that he be transferred further away from that place which was too close to the city of Constantinople, lest he use the frequent comforts of those whom he drew into his impiety.

units.la: 20. Et Gregorius Paulum Diadinae civitatis quondam Episcopum quousque omne, quod dilapidavit vel de substantia tulit Ecclesiae, restitueret, in Monasterium mittendum esse decrevit. Et si forte post depositionem suam inverecunde acmente perversa aliquando de Episcopatu loqui, aut rursus ad hoc qualibet aspirare praesumptione tentaverit, Dominici corporis & sanguinis communione privatum, in Monasterio cum usque ad diem obitus sui ad agendam poenitentiam retrudi, studio Joannis Primae Justinianae Episcopi jussit, ut perpetrati sceleris maculas dignis diseceret fletibus emendare, juxta legem Justiniani Imperatoris; qui in libro Constitutionum decrevit, ut si quis Episcopus excessus fuerit ingredi civitatem, de qua repulsus est, vel exire de loco, in quo degere jussus est, jubemus eum in Monasterio in alia provincia constituto tradi, ut qua in sacerdotio peccavit, degens ut Monasterio corrigat.
units.tr: 20. Gregory also decreed that Paul, once bishop of the city of Diadina, should be sent into a monastery until he restored whatever he had squandered or taken from the substance of the Church. And if perhaps, after his deposition, he shamelessly and with a perverse mind ever spoke of the episcopate again, or attempted with any presumption to aspire to it, he ordered him, deprived of communion in the Lord's body and blood, to be shut up in a monastery to do penance until the day of his death, at the zeal of John, bishop of Prima Justiniana, so that he might amend the stains of the crime he committed with worthy tears, according to the law of the Emperor Justinian. In his book of Constitutions Justinian decreed that if any bishop should presume to enter the city from which he was driven out, or leave the place where he was ordered to dwell, we order him to be handed over to a monastery established in another province, so that, living there, he may correct the sin he committed in the priesthood.

units.la: 21. Quas leges ab Imperatoribus & Regibus, nostris videlicet praedecessoribus, promulgatas & decretas nos immutilate & irrefragabiliter convenit conservare, sicut Apostolicae Sedis Antistites ad Dominos & terrae Principes scripserunt. Ait enim Leo ad Leonem Augustum: Debes, inquiens, immutilanter advertere Regiam potestatem tibi non ad solum mundi regimen, sed maxime ad Ecclesiae praesidium esse constitutam, ut ansus nefarios comprimendo, quae bene sunt statuta, defendas, et veram pacem his, quae sunt turbata, restituas. Et Gelasius ad Anastasium: Etenim Imperator Augustae, si contra leges publicas aliquid (quod absit) quispiam fortasse tentaret, nulla id ratione potuisset admitti.
units.tr: 21. These laws, promulgated and decreed by emperors and kings, our predecessors, we are rightly bound to keep unchanged and unbroken, as the bishops of the Apostolic See have written to the lords and princes of the earth. For Leo says to the Emperor Leo: You ought, he says, to observe unchangeably that royal power has been established for you not only for governing the world but chiefly for protecting the Church, so that by checking impious attempts you may defend what has been well established, and restore true peace to what has been disturbed. And Gelasius to Anastasius: For if the Emperor Augustus should attempt anything against public laws (which God forbid), it could by no reasoning be admitted.

units.la: 22. Quas etiam leges Principali authoritate promulgatas non solum a quibuscumque Episcopis, sed etiam ab ipsis Apostolicae Sedis Pontificibus, ipsius primae Sedis Antistites observari debere scripserunt, sicut B. Leo ad Leonem Augustum scribens demonstrat, dicens, non se refragari deberec dicta Imperialia vel ea, quae sui decessores secundum tramitem scripturarum praedicationemque majorum statuerant: Si qua, inquiens, destruxi, hac aedifico; praevaricatorem me constituo, & cum me ultionum conditionibus subdo, quas non solum authores beatae memoriae Principi Martiani, sed etiam ego inea consensione firmasti. Et sanctus Gelasius ad Anastasium Imperatorem: Si, inquit, quantum ad ordinem publica pertinet disciplina cognoscentes Imperium tibi superna dispositione collatum, legibus tuis ipsi quoque parent religionis Antistites, ne vel in rebus mundanis exclusa videantur obviare sententiae; quo, oro te, affectu eis convenit obedire, qui pro erogandis venerabilibus sunt attributi mysteriis?
units.tr: 22. Moreover, the first bishops themselves wrote that these laws, promulgated by princely authority, ought to be observed not only by any bishops but also by the Pontiffs of the Apostolic See themselves. Blessed Leo, writing to the Emperor Leo, shows this, saying that he ought not to oppose the imperial sayings or those which his predecessors had established according to the course of Scripture and the preaching of the elders: If I have destroyed anything, here I rebuild it; I make myself a transgressor, and I subject myself to the conditions of punishments, which not only the authors of blessed memory, Prince Marcian, but I myself too have confirmed in agreement. And holy Gelasius to the Emperor Anastasius: If, he says, knowing that the Empire has been conferred on you by heavenly disposition, the bishops of religion obey your laws as far as public discipline pertains, lest they seem to oppose the sentence even in worldly matters; with what affection, I beg you, ought those to obey who have been appointed to dispense the venerable mysteries?

units.la: 23. Quod & nos, juxta hortamentum B. Gelasii, incunctanter atque libenter exequi cupimus in his, quae ad suum ministerium pertinent, cunctis generaliter Sacerdotibus recte divina tractantibus & potissimae Sedis illius Praesulis, quae cunctis Sacerdotibus divinitas summa voluit praeminere, & subsequens Ecclesiae jugiter pietas celebravit: sicut nostri decessores ac progenitores orthodoxi Imperatores & Reges egerunt, ut & Apostolicae Sedis Pontifex, & reliqui Domini Sacerdotes, nobis, quae a Deo sunt consecuta, exhibeant: scientes, sicut idem B. Gelasius dicit, quoniam Christus memor fragilitatis humanae, quorum salutem congrueret, dispensatione magnifica temperavit, sic actionibus propriis dignitatibusque; distinctis officia potestatis utriusque; discrevit, suosque volens medicinali humilitate salvari, non humana superbia rursus intercipi; ut & Christiani Principes pro aeterna vita Pontificibus indigerent, & Pontifices pro temporalium cursu rerum Imperialium dispositionibus uterentur, quatenus spirituali actio
units.tr: 23. This we also, according to the exhortation of Blessed Gelasius, desire to carry out without delay and gladly in those matters which pertain to their ministry, for all priests who rightly handle divine things, and for the prelate of that chief See, to which the highest divinity willed pre-eminence over all priests, and which the continual piety of the Church has celebrated; just as our predecessors and forefathers, orthodox emperors and kings, did, so that both the Pontiff of the Apostolic See and the other lord priests may render to us what has been obtained from God. We know, as the same Blessed Gelasius says, that Christ, mindful of human frailty, tempered with a magnificent dispensation what would befit the salvation of his people; so he distinguished the offices of each power by their own actions and dignities, willing his own to be saved by a medicinal humility and not to be intercepted again by human pride; so that Christian princes might need Pontiffs for eternal life, and Pontiffs might use imperial dispositions for the course of temporal affairs, insofar as spiritual action

units.la: Reg. 20. Virgil. Eclog. 1. Proverb. 8. infra 13. 1.14. C. de Episcop. & Cleric. l. 16. C. Theod. li. 16. tit. 2. unde & huc est tralata. a. d. l. 14. conturbaverit. b. dd. ll. rescripta. c. al. permoveant. d. C. Th. reprehensione. Novel. 123. C. 11. in fi. auth. fi quis Episcop. C. de Episcop. & Cleric. Papa legibus Imperialibus subjectus. Imperii & Ecclesiae distincta officia. actio à carnalibus distaret incursibus: & ideò militans Deo minimè se negotiis secularibus implicaret; ac vicissim non ille rebus divinis præsidere videretur, qui esset negotiis secularibus implicatus, ut & modestia utriusque otdinis curaretur, ne extolleretur utroque suffultus, & competens qualitatibus actionum speciali ter profellio aptaretur. Omnis Pontifex, inquit Apostolus, ex hominibus assumptus, pro hominibus constituitur in his, quæ sunt ad Deum, ut offerat dona & sacrificia pro peccatis, videlicet non solùm pro populi, sed quia & ipse circumdatus est infirmitate, pro suis. Et Regis est, regni negotia dispensare, licet inculcant litteræ divinitus inspiratæ. Quia ergo sanctarum Scripturarum tramite, & prædicatione majorum ostenditur, sancto etiam attestante Gelasio, quia duo sunt, quibus principaliter mundus hic regitur, authoritas sacra Pontificum & Regalis potestas: & per Regem Regum, ac Summum Pontificem conditorum Pontificum, qui solus Rex & Sacerdos fieri potuit, condiderunt legum justa decernunt. Quas Principales potestates appellaverunt æternas: & sacri Canones Spiritu Dei sunt conditi, & totius reverentia consecrati. Et, ut B. Ambrosius ad Valentinianum dicit; Leges Imperator, quas primus ipse constituit, quia quod præscripsit aliis, præscripsit sibi, nec cui esset liberum aliud judicare. Et B. Augustinus dicit; Quæ posteà quàm leges subscriptæ fuerint & firmatæ, non licet judici de ipsis judicare, sed secundum ipsas.
units.tr: 1 Kings 20. Virgil, Eclogue 1. Proverbs 8. Below 13, 1.14. C. de Episcopis et Clericis. Law 16, C. Theod. book 16, title 2, whence this is also transferred here. a. Law 14: "has disturbed". b. The rescripts of the said laws. c. Others: "may move". d. C. Th.: "reprehension". Novel 123, c. 11 at the end; authentic "si quis episcopus", C. de Episcopis et Clericis. The Pope is subject to imperial laws. The offices of Empire and Church are distinct. "Every high priest," says the Apostle, "taken from among men, is appointed for men in things pertaining to God, that he may offer gifts and sacrifices for sins" (Heb. 5.1), namely not only for the people's sins, but since he himself is also compassed with infirmity, for his own. And it belongs to the king to dispense the affairs of the kingdom, as the divinely inspired letters also insist. Therefore, since it is shown by the path of the holy Scriptures and the preaching of the elders, and since holy Gelasius also attests that there are two things by which this world is principally governed, the sacred authority of Pontiffs and the royal power, and since through the King of kings and the Supreme Pontiff they who alone could become both King and Priest established the Pontiffs, and decree just things as lawgivers, they call these laws the principal powers eternal. The sacred canons were framed by the Spirit of God and consecrated by the reverence of all. And as Blessed Ambrose says to Valentinian: An emperor is bound by the laws which he himself first made, since what he prescribed to others he prescribed to himself, nor is it free for anyone to judge otherwise. And Blessed Augustine says: Once laws have been signed and confirmed, it is not lawful for a judge to judge concerning them, but according to them.

units.la: 24. Quia secundum Pontificale ministerium vestrum Regio ministerio nostro monita vestræ paternitatis obedienter ac libenter cupimus obaudire, patimini nos ea servare, quæ prædecessores vestri ac nostri de hujusmodi, unde agitur, constituerunt; & roborantes servando, quæ gesta sunt, rata doceamus esse debere quæ geritis. Nam quomodo leges Principum ritè vocabuntur æternæ, si transcuntibus Principibus unà cum eis constitutio legis tranlibit? Et Papa Symmachus ad Eonium: Dum, inquit, ad Trinitatis mysterium, cui una est atque individua potestas, unum fit per diversos Antistites sacerdotium, quomodo prioruin statuta a sequentibus conveniat violari? Hoc accedit, quòd si hæc eveniat sententiarum varietas, ad ipsam sacrosanctam religionem credimus pertinere, cujus omnis potestas infringitur, nisi universa, quæ à Domini Sacerdotibus semel statuuntur, perpetua sint. Quid aliàs contingere poterit, si succellor decessoris actibus non tribuerit firmitatem, & roborando quæ gesta sunt, faciat rata esse quæ gesserit? Quanta enim Vicariis B. Petri Apostoli judicabitur esse reverentia, si quæ in sacerdotio præcipiunt, eisdem transeuntibus dissolvantur? Universa, inquit, perpetua sint, quæ à Domini sacerdotibus statuuntur: qui, ut Moyses, ea, quæ statuunt, ab Oraculo divino susciaiunt: non quæ ab his statuuntur, de quibus per Prophetam dicitur: Væ his, qui condunt leges iniquas, & scribentes injustitiam scripserunt. Ea nihilominus, quæ à Vicariis B. Petri constituuntur, maneant inconvulsa: quia, ut Leo dicit, nec nimia est severitas vel remissio, ubi nihil constituitur, nisi quod ex B. Petri æquitate profertur.
