units.tr: 24. Since, according to your pontifical ministry, we desire to obey obediently and gladly the admonitions of your paternity with our royal ministry, allow us to keep those things which your predecessors and ours established concerning the matter at hand, and by keeping what has been done we confirm, and teach that what you do ought to be ratified. For how will the laws of princes rightly be called eternal, if, when princes pass away, the enactment of the law passes away with them? And Pope Symmachus, writing to Eonius: While, he says, the priesthood is made one through different bishops for the mystery of the Trinity, to which there is one and the same power, how can the statutes of predecessors be lawfully violated by successors? This is added: if such variety of opinions should arise, we believe it pertains to the sacred religion itself, whose whole power is undermined unless all those things which have once been decreed by the priests of the Lord are perpetual. What else could happen if a successor did not give firmness to his predecessor's acts, and by confirming what has been done, did not make valid what he himself has done? For with how much reverence will the vicars of the blessed apostle Peter be judged to be regarded, if the things they prescribe in the priesthood are dissolved when they themselves pass away? Let all things, he says, which are decreed by the priests of the Lord be perpetual: those priests who, like Moses, receive what they decree from the divine oracle, not those of whom the Prophet says: Woe to those who make unjust laws, and who have written injustice in writing. Nevertheless, let those things which are established by the vicars of blessed Peter remain unshaken, because, as Leo says, there is neither excessive severity nor excessive leniency where nothing is decreed except what proceeds from the equity of blessed Peter.

units.la: 25. Hæc enim scimus esse canonicè, scimus esse Apostolica authoritate roborata, & Apostolicæ Sedis decreta, quæ, ut Gelasius dicit, Unamquamque Synodum & sua auctoritate confirmat, & continua modo custodit, pro suo sciscet principatu, quem B. Petrus Apostolus Domini voce præceptum Ecclesiam nihilominus frequente & tenuit & semper retinet. Et paulò superius: Confidimus, quod nullus jam veraciter Christianus errat, unusquisque Synodi constitutum, quod universalis Ecclesia probavit assensus, nullam magis exequi sedem pro oportere quàm primam. Et item idem: Cumq; nobis contra salutarium reverentiam regularum cupiamus vere licere, & cùm Sedes Apostolica super his omnibus, favente Domino, quæ paternis canonibus sunt præfixa, pio desiderio studeat tenere propositio, satisq; indignum est, quemquam vel Pontificum vel ordinum subsequentium hanc observantiam refutare, quam B. Petri Sedem & sequi videat & docere, satisq; conveniens sit, ut totum corpus Ecclesia in hac observatione concordet, quam illic videre conspiciat, ubi Dominus Ecclesiæ totius principatum. Et de sanctis Legibus, quas unà cum sanctis Canonibus Catholica observat Ecclesia, idem Gelasius, ut præmi-dicit in epistola ad Anastasium Imperatorem: Quantum, inquiens, ad ordinem publicæ pertinet disciplina, cognoscentes Imperium tibi superna dispositione collatum, legibus tuis ipsi quoque parent religionis Antistites, ne rebus mundanis exclusæ videantur obviare sententiæ.
units.tr: 25. For we know these things to be canonical, we know them to be confirmed by apostolic authority, and they are decrees of the apostolic see, which, as Gelasius says, each synod both confirms by its own authority and keeps in continual observance, and sanctions according to its own principate, which the blessed apostle Peter, commanded by the voice of the Lord, both held and always retains, the Church also frequently holding it. And a little above: We trust that no one who is truly a Christian now errs; each one should follow the decision of the synod, which the assent of the universal Church has approved, and should obey no see more than the first. And again the same: Since we desire truly to be permitted to act against the reverence of the wholesome rules, and since the Apostolic See, by the favour of the Lord, strives with pious desire to keep the proposal concerning all these things which have been laid down by the fathers' canons, and since it is quite unworthy for anyone, whether of the bishops or of the subsequent orders, to refuse this observance, which he sees the See of blessed Peter both follow and teach, and since it is fitting that the whole body of the Church agree in this observance, which it sees there, where the Lord has given the primacy of the whole Church. And concerning the holy laws, which the Catholic Church observes together with the holy canons, the same Gelasius says, as I said before, in his letter to the emperor Anastasius: As far as concerns the order of public discipline, knowing that the empire has been conferred on you by heavenly disposition, the ministers of religion also obey your laws, lest they seem to be excluded from worldly affairs and to oppose the judgment.

units.la: 26. Et cùm ita faciæ leges, tam Ecclesiasticæ quàm mundanæ, de damnato Episcopali & Synodali decernant, non est nostri Regii ministerii, rerum & sacrorum Canonum judicio condemnare, atque Apostolicæ Sedis definitione, sicut in gestis Synodi invenire potestis, anathematizatione potentia fretum quoquam dirigere: cùm apertissimè sacri Canones definiant, & leges Justinianaeorum Imperatorum Catholicorum edicta, qualiter, & pro quibus, & à quibus debeat Episcopus judicari; & post judicium, quid, & qualiter, & per quos sit inde Apostolicæ Sedis agendum, quæ non abnuimus, sed incunctanter ac competenter annuimus. A quibus definitionibus nulli est licitum deviare, quia, ut S. Hilarius dicit, non minus in sanctarum traditionum deliquitur sanctiones, quàm in injuriam ipsius Domini prosilitur.
units.tr: 26. And since laws, both ecclesiastical and secular, thus decree concerning the condemnation of a bishop and of a synod, it is not for our royal ministry, by the judgment of the matters and the holy canons, to condemn anyone, nor, relying on power, to direct anything by anathematization according to the definition of the apostolic see, as you may find in the acts of the synod; since the holy canons most clearly define, and the laws and edicts of the Catholic emperors Justinian define, in what manner, for what causes, and by whom a bishop ought to be judged; and after judgment, what, how, and through whom is to be done by the apostolic see in the matter. These things we do not refuse, but readily and fittingly grant. It is lawful for no one to deviate from these definitions, because, as Saint Hilary says, an offence against the decrees of the holy traditions is no less than an injury done to the Lord himself.

units.la: 27. Quocirca, quia Dominus dicit per Prophetam: Labia sacerdotis custodient scientiam, & legem requirent ex ore ejus, quia Angelus, (id est, nuncius) Domini exercituum est: nolite permittere nobis scribi ex verbo authoritatis nomine, quæ in legibus sacris Dei sapientia conditis, & in sanctis regulis ejusdem Spiritu non promulgatis non continentur, dicente item Propheta, id est Sacerdoti præcipiente; Audiens audiet eis ex me, ex me, inquit, & non, exte: & redarguuntur, qui de corde suo loquuntur: quoniam ipse loquitur, gloriam propriam quærit. Nolite igitur, ut præmisimus, ex vestro nomine Apostolicæ Sedis authoritate,* visiones vel excommunicationum intentationes contra sacrarum Scripturarum tramitem, prædicationemque majorum, ac sacrarum legum sanctorumque Canonum constitutiones, nobis de cætero scribi cujusCUMQUE instinctu permittere precamur.
units.tr: 27. Wherefore, since the Lord says through the Prophet: The lips of the priest shall keep knowledge, and they shall seek the law at his mouth, for he is the messenger (that is, the angel) of the Lord of hosts: we ask you not to permit anything to be written to us in your name, under the authority of the Word, which is not contained in the sacred laws established by the wisdom of God, and in the holy rules not promulgated by his Spirit. As the Prophet also says, that is, to the priest commanding: He who hears, let him hear from me, from me, he says, and not from you; and they are refuted who speak from their own heart, since he himself speaks and seeks his own glory. Therefore, as we have said before, do not permit, in your name and under the authority of the apostolic see, any visions or threats of excommunication to be written to us from now on, at anyone's instigation, against the path of the holy Scriptures and the teaching of the fathers, and against the constitutions of the sacred laws and the holy canons.

units.la: 28. Quia scitis, & scimus, totum esse irritum, quicquid ab eorum fuerit constitutione diversum. Dicitur, inquit sanctus Leo, à Domino beatissimo Petro: Tibi dabo claves regni cælorum, & quæcumque solveris super terram erunt soluta.
units.tr: 28. For you know, and we know, that whatever is contrary to their constitution is wholly void. It is said, says Saint Leo, by the most blessed Lord to Peter: To you I will give the keys of the kingdom of heaven, and whatsoever you shall loose on earth shall be loosed.

units.la: * Visiones, ut sunt Constantini Magni, & Stephani Papæ, quas hîc non obscurè perstringit. per terram, erunt soluta & in coelis. Transfiunt quidem etiam in alios Apostolos jus ipsius potestatis, & ad omnes Ecclesiae Principes decreti hujus constitutio commeavit: sed non frustrà unì commendatur, quod omnibus insinuatur. Petro enim idcò hoc singulariter creditur, quia cunctis Ecclesiae rectoribus Petri fama praeponitur. Manet ergo Petri privilegium, ubicumq; ex ipsius aequitate fertur judicium. Qua sente outia constat, qui non manet Petri privilegii, ubi ex ipsius aequitate non fertur judicium. Cùm enim ubicumq; dicitur, sicuti nullus locus, ita nemo rector Ecclesiae, ex Petri aequitate judicium ferens, excipitur: vel contra illius aequitatem judicium proferens, commendatur. Et quia ubicumq; sine ulla exceptione non manet Petri privilegium, ibi ipsius aequitate non fertur judicium prolatum, obaudiemus jussum, vel recipiemus judicium, quod non ex Petri aequitate fuerit prolatum, ac per hoc ipsius privilegio fuerit destitutum. De quo Epi-scopali judicio quid cunctis Episcopis sequendum, & quid Ecclesiae filiis sit tenendum atque tenendum, B.Gregorius sufficienter inculcat.
units.tr: * Visions, such as those of Constantine the Great and of Pope Stephen, which he here obscurely glances at. On earth, shall be loosed also in heaven. Indeed the right of that same power passes also to the other apostles, and the constitution of this decree has passed to all the leaders of the Church; but what is commended to one is not in vain, when it is announced to all. For it is believed that this is given to Peter singularly, because the fame of Peter is placed before all the rulers of the Church. Therefore the privilege of Peter remains wherever judgment is pronounced from his equity. From which it is clear that he who does not remain under the privilege of Peter is one where judgment is not pronounced from his equity. For when it is said wherever, just as no place is excepted, so no ruler of the Church who pronounces judgment from the equity of Peter is excepted; or who pronounces judgment against his equity is commended. And because wherever, without any exception, the privilege of Peter does not remain, there judgment is not pronounced from his equity; we shall obey the command, or receive the judgment which has not been pronounced from the equity of Peter, and which, by that very fact, has been deprived of his privilege. Concerning this episcopal judgment, what all bishops ought to follow, and what the sons of the Church ought to hold and maintain, blessed Gregory sufficiently inculcates.

units.la: 29. Ergo jubete & judicate privilegio magni Petri, juxta aequitatis ejus judicium, quae judicanda sunt, ne, ut dicit ejus coapostolus, vimperetur ministerium vestrum: quia & nos secundùm Regium ministerium nostrum, quantum ex nobis est, cupimus servare quod scriptum est: Filii, obedite parentibus vestris in Domino, videlicet quod fuerit jussum vel indicarum à Domino, dicere illo singuli, qui pro patribus Apostolis Ecclesiae nati sunt filii Apostolici viri: Tu autem audiens nunciabis eis ex me. Divina quippe nos lectio docet, quia nec etiam Balaam satis superque à Rege Balaach petitus, licet medicamento avaritiae delinitus in consilio dando corruptus offenderit, ullo tamen aut ullius instinctu in dicio justitiae aliud loqui adversus Israel persuaderi vel extorqueri potuit, quam quod à Domino audivit.
units.tr: 29. Therefore, command and judge, by the privilege of great Peter, according to the judgment of his equity, the things that are to be judged, lest, as his fellow apostle says, your ministry be blamed; for we also, according to our royal ministry, as far as lies in us, desire to keep what is written: Children, obey your parents in the Lord, that is, whatever shall have been commanded or decreed by the Lord, let each one who is born, by the apostles' fathers, of the Church, the sons of an apostolic man, say: And you, hearing, shall announce to them from me. For sacred reading teaches us that not even Balaam, though sufficiently and more than sufficiently sought by king Balak, although softened by the medicine of avarice, and corrupted in giving counsel, could be persuaded or drawn, by any instigation or any means, in the judgment of justice, to speak against Israel anything other than what he heard from the Lord.

units.la: 30. De eo quod in litteris ex nomine vestro nobis directis habetur, ut veniente Hincmaro Romam, venirat accusator idoneus, qui nulla possit authoritate legitima reppulit, rescribimus: quia licet haec commendatio nulla sit ratione atque authoritate suffulta, si forte apud vos exlex solus Hincmarus nova lege, priscis tam publicis quàm ecclesiasticis contraria, imò ordine novo, more habetur, ut non nisi a vobis & Romae valeat judicari pro his excessibus, de quibus habentur certa sacrorum canonum actum decreta, quae, ut Leo ait, nulla possunt ratione convelli, cùm etiam de causa fidei, ut dicit Gelasius, cunque Pontifici licet secundum regulam errorus ante damnati quemlibet Catholica communione discernere: & ego exors ab omnibus accusationibus non solùm ab his, quibus legaliter & regulariter accusandi adversus ipsum denegatur licentia, verùm & ab his, quibus in propriis causis accusario non negatur, sicut leges & regulae jubenr in Provincia, in qua sunt orta negocia, terminari non valeant, & secundum Antiochenos canones, Provincialium Synodorum non debeant experiri examen; si vobis cum voluntate & consensu dilectissimi nepotis nostri, Imperatoris vestri, contra cujus dilectionem & debitum honorem, si tamen mutuam dilectionem & congruum honorem nobis exhibere studuerit, illuc ire non volumus, obtinueritis, cooperante Domino, pace in regno nostro contra Paganos virtute vel quacumq; dispositione Dei obtenta, Romam venire congruo tempore non differemus. Et quia illum legaliter aut regulariter in Synodo Episcoporum plurimatum Provinciarum de certis causis accusavimus, idoneum nos accusatorem illius ostendemus, & rantos testes idoneos diversi ordinis ac dignitatis nobiscum ducemus, cum quibus eum legaliter ac regulariter nos accusasse & comprobasse sufficientissimè comprobabimus.
units.tr: 30. Concerning what is contained in the letter sent to us in your name, that when Hincmar came to Rome an suitable accuser came, who by no legitimate authority repelled him, we reply: although this recommendation is supported by no reason or authority, if perhaps Hincmar alone is held by you to be outside the law, under a new law contrary to ancient laws both public and ecclesiastical, or rather in a new order and custom, so that for those offences, concerning which there are certain decrees of the holy canons established, he can be judged only by you and at Rome, which, as Leo says, cannot be overturned by any reason, since even in a matter of faith, as Gelasius says, it is permitted to the Pontiff to separate from Catholic communion anyone previously condemned for error according to the rule; and I, free from all accusations, not only from those by whom the licence to accuse him legally and regularly is denied, but also from those by whom accusation in one's own causes is not denied; as the laws and rules command that matters arising in the province in which they arose ought not to be decided, and, according to the canons of Antioch, ought not to be examined by provincial synods; if you obtain with the will and consent of our most beloved nephew, your emperor, against whose love and due honour (if indeed he has striven to show us mutual love and fitting honour) we are unwilling to go there, and with the Lord cooperating, peace being obtained in our kingdom against the pagans by virtue or by whatever disposition of God, we shall not delay to come to Rome at a suitable time. And since we have accused him legally or regularly, in a synod of many bishops of several provinces, on certain charges, we shall show ourselves a suitable accuser of him, and we shall bring with us witnesses of suitable rank and dignity of various orders, with whom we shall most sufficiently prove that we have accused him legally and regularly and have proved it.

units.la: 31. Tandem quia vos non legisse vel audisse collegimus ex litteris ab Actardo Episcopo nobis delatis, quae antea per illum paternitati vestrae direximus, iteratò scribimus ea, quae tunc scripseramus, deprecantes vos in omnipotentis Dei honore, & sanctorum Apostolorum veneratione, ut tales honorationis nostrae epistolas taliaque mandata, licut hactenus ex nomine vestro suscepimus, & regni nostri Episcopis ac primoribus de caetero non mandetis, & non compellaris nos mandare epistolas vestras inhonorandas contemnere, & Miilos vestros dehonorare, qui nobis in his, quae vestrum ministerium pertinent, si tamen ministerium vestrum cupimus obtemperare.......... Quo pro vestri honore privilegii vobis dicimus: quia vobis, sicut revera Vicario B. Petri Apostolorum principis, in omnibus debite ac competenter obedire desideramus, & ne aliter eveniat cavere per omnia cupimus, ac vestram sanctitatem id ipsum cavere humili prece depositimus: ne nos & nostros saeris invitos ad id cogatis convertere, quod in Quinta universali Synodo à Sede Apostolica, ut in Apostolicis litteris, praecipue aurem in Synodica B. Gregorii ad quatuor Patriarchas, & in aliis ejus epistolis una cum quatuor praecedentibus, legimus collaudatum atque suscepturum, invenitur nobis tenendum: quod adhuc nostris litteris ad exemplum inferre noluimus, donec sciamus, si duritiam mandatorum vestrorum erga nos aliter ad benignitatem inflectere poterimus. Quia quod ex Apostolicae Sedis nomine secundum sanctarum scripturarum tramitem praedicationemq; majorum & orthodoxorum decreta scribuntur, sequendum & tenendum non ignoramus; & quod secus à quoquam fuerit conspectum sive confictum, non solùm respuendum, sed & redarguendum esse cognoscimus. Si denique alirer, quàm & nos & vos decuerat, reverentissimae paternitati vestrae rescribendo factus sum insipiens, vos me coegistis. Perimus autem omnipotentem Dominum, ut inspiret cordi vestro sic nos benigne tractare, quatenus ulterius nobis non sit necesse vobis ita rescribere; sed, ut cupimus in venerationem Apostolorum, Apostolico Pontificio vestro humiliter ac devotè colla & corda summittere.
units.tr: 31. Finally, since we have gathered from the letter delivered to us by Bishop Actardus, which we previously sent to your paternity through him, that you have not read or heard what we wrote then, we write again what we had written, and we beseech you, in the honour of almighty God and the veneration of the holy Apostles, that you no longer send us such letters and such commands, of the kind you have hitherto sent us in your name, to us and to the bishops and nobles of our kingdom, and that you do not compel us to despise your letters as unworthy of honour and to dishonour your messengers, who, in matters that belong to your ministry, serve us, if indeed we desire to obey your ministry.......... Therefore, for the honour of your privilege, we say to you: since we desire to obey you duly and fittingly in all things, as the Vicar of blessed Peter, prince of the Apostles, and since we wish to guard against the contrary in every way, we humbly beg your holiness to take the same care, so that you do not compel us, against our will and often, to turn to that which we find we must hold, as we have read it praised and accepted by the Apostolic See in the Fifth Universal Synod, as in the Apostolic letters, especially in the synodical letter of blessed Gregory to the four patriarchs, and in his other letters together with the four preceding councils. We have not wished to introduce this into our own letters as an example until we know whether we can by some means turn the harshness of your commands towards us to kindness. For we know that what is written in the name of the Apostolic See, in accordance with the path of holy Scripture and the teaching of the elders and the orthodox decrees, is to be followed and held; and whatever has been devised or fabricated otherwise by anyone, we recognise must not only be rejected but also refuted. Finally, if I have written in reply to your most reverend paternity otherwise than became both us and you, I have been made foolish; you have forced me to it. We pray to almighty Lord that He may inspire your heart to treat us so kindly that it will no longer be necessary for us to answer you in this way; but, as we desire, out of reverence for the Apostles, that we humbly and devoutly bow our necks and hearts to your Apostolic Pontifical authority.

units.la: Deus omnipotens, ad honorem & salvationem atque exaltationem sanctae suae Ecclesiae, vos per multa annorum curricula conservare dignetur, Domine sanctissime & reverendissime Pater in Domino.
units.tr: May almighty God deign to preserve you through many courses of years, to the honour, salvation and exaltation of His holy Church, most holy and most reverend Father in the Lord.

units.la: ADDITIO
units.tr: ADDITION

units.la: ADDITIO.
units.tr: ADDITIO.

units.la: SANCTISSIMO AC REVERENTISSIMO PATRI HADRIANO SVMMO Pontifici & universali Papæ, Carolus Dei gratia Rex & spiritualis filius vester.
units.tr: To the most holy and most reverend father Hadrian, highest Pontiff and universal Pope, Charles, by the grace of God King, and your spiritual son.

units.la: Quia litteris ex nomine sanctæ paternitatis vestræ ab Actardo venerabili Archiepiscopo nobis delatis, necessitate cogente, prolixiùs respondere compulsi sumus, contra morem nostrum in quaterniunculo annulo nostro signato, responsionem nostram scribere necessarium duximus, quatenus legi planiùs valeat, & quæ vobis ratio respondere coegit, legenti plenius innotescat. Quam responsionem sancta paternitas vestra non aspernanter sed benignè suscipiat, quæ à nobis nō contumaciter sed mente pacifica, ut in eodem quaterniunculo invenietis, contexta. Deprecamur autem vos in omnipotentis Dei honore, & sanctorum Apostolorum veneratione, ut tales in honorationis nostræ epistolas, taliaque mandata, sicut hactenus ex nomine vestro suscepimus, nobis & nostris Episcopis ac Primoribus de cætero non mandetis: sed liceat nobis Apostolico Pontificio vestro, in veneratione Dei & sanctorum Apostolorum, humiliter ac devotè, ut cupimus, colla & cordia summittere. Deus omnipotens ad honorem & salvationem atque exaltationem sanctæ suæ Ecclesiæ, vos per annorum curricula conservare dignetur, Domine sanctissime atque reverentissime pater in Domino.
units.tr: Since, compelled by necessity, we have been obliged to reply at greater length to the letter delivered to us in the name of your holy fatherhood by the venerable Archbishop Actardus, we have judged it necessary, contrary to our custom, to write our reply in a small quire sealed with our ring, so that it may be read more easily and so that the reader may more fully understand the reasons which compelled us to answer you. We ask that your holy fatherhood receive this reply not disdainfully but kindly, since it has been composed by us not in obstinacy but in a peaceable spirit, as you will find in the same little quire. We beseech you, in honour of almighty God and in reverence for the holy Apostles, that you no longer send to us and to our bishops and nobles such letters and such commands in your name as we have hitherto received; but may it be permitted to us, in reverence for God and the holy Apostles, to bow our necks and hearts humbly and devotedly to your apostolic papal see, as we desire. May almighty God deign to preserve you through the course of many years, for the honour and salvation and exaltation of his holy Church, most holy and most reverend Father in the Lord.

units.la: LUDOVICI BALBI IMPERATORIS ET REGIS FRANCORUM CONSTITUTIO
units.tr: The Constitution of Louis the Stammerer, Emperor and King of the Franks

units.la: CONTRA SACRILEGOS: LATA IN CONCILIO TRECASENSI coram Joanne VIII. Papa & LIII. Episcopis.
units.tr: AGAINST SACRILEGIOUS PERSONS: ENACTED AT THE COUNCIL OF TROYES, before Pope John VIII and fifty-three bishops.

units.la: Quisquis invétus fuerit reus sacrilegii, Episcopis, vel Abbatibus, sive personis, ad quas quemonia sacrilegii justè pertinuerit, triginta libras examinati argenti purissimi componat.
units.tr: Whoever is found guilty of sacrilege shall pay thirty pounds of the purest assayed silver to the bishops or abbots, or to the persons to whom the composition for the sacrilege rightly belongs.

units.la: 2. Sacrilegium committitur, si quis infregerit ecclesiam, vel triginta ecclesiasticos passus, qui in circuitu ecclesiæ fuerint, vel domos, quæ intra prædictos passus fuerint, aliquid inde diripiendo vel auferendo: seu qui injuriam, vel ablationem rerum iutulerit Clericis arma non ferentibus, vel Monachis, sive Deo devotis, omnibusque ecclesiasticis personis. Capellæ, quæ sunt intra ambitum monasteriorum, castellorum, non ponuntur in hac triginta passuum observatione. Similiter sacrilegium committitur auferendo sacrum de sacro, vel non sacrum de sacro, sive sacrum de non sacro.
units.tr: 2. Sacrilege is committed if anyone breaks into a church, or carries off or plunders anything from the thirty ecclesiastical paces that lie around the church, or from the houses that lie within those paces; or if anyone inflicts injury upon, or takes goods from, clerics who do not bear arms, or monks, or those devoted to God, and all ecclesiastical persons. Chapels that lie within the precinct of monasteries or castles are not included in this rule of thirty paces. Likewise sacrilege is committed by removing a sacred thing from a sacred place, or a non-sacred thing from a sacred place, or a sacred thing from a non-sacred place.

units.la: 3. Si quis domum Dei violaverit, & aliqua sine licentia illius, cui commissa esse dignoscitur, inde laeserit, vel ecclesiasticis personis injuriam fecerit, donec in conventu admonitus legitimè satisfaciat se communione privatum. Si verò post secundam & tertiam conventionem coram Episcopis facere detrectaverit, sacrilegii periculo ab omnibus obnoxius teneatur, ita ut secundum Apostolum, nemini fidelium misceatur.
units.tr: 3. If anyone violates the house of God and takes anything from it without the permission of the one to whom it is known to be entrusted, or does injury to ecclesiastical persons, let him be deprived of communion until, admonished in the assembly, he makes lawful satisfaction. But if, after the second and third summons, he refuses to appear before the bishops, let him be held liable to the danger of sacrilege before everyone, so that, according to the Apostle, no one of the faithful may associate with him.

units.la: 4. Si qui monasteria, & loca Deo dedicata, & ecclesias infringunt, & deposita, vel alia quælibet de abstrahunt, damnum novies componant, & emunitatem tripliciter, & velut sacrilegi canonicenti subjugantur. Dat. Trecassibus, Anno Domini DCCCLXXVIII. Indict. II.
units.tr: 4. If anyone breaks into monasteries, places dedicated to God, and churches, and carries off deposits or anything else whatsoever, let him pay ninefold damages, and let him make threefold restitution of the immunity, and let him be subjected to the canonical penalties as a sacrilegious person. Given at Troyes, in the year of the Lord 878, indiction II.

units.la: CAROLI III. IMP. AUG. CONSTITUTIO DE EXPEDITIONE ROMANA.
units.tr: CHARLES III, AUGUSTUS EMPEROR: CONSTITUTION CONCERNING THE ROMAN EXPEDITION.

units.la: In nomine sanctæ & individuæ Trinitatis.
units.tr: In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity.

units.la: Karolus divina favente gratia, Rex Francorum & Romanorum.
units.tr: Charles, by the favour of divine grace, King of the Franks and of the Romans.

units.la: 1. Si prædecessorum nostrorum morem sequimur, non solum præsentibus, sed & successoribus subvenire nitimur. Hac de causa universorum cognoscat experientia, qualiter dum pro consecratione coronaque perceptione proficiscendi tempus ad Apostolicam Sedem instaret, multis Principibus annum Vuormatiæ transegimus, ibique omnem Reipubl. statum uniformem & honestum confirmare; nocivum atque contrarium radicitus extirpare decrevimus. Interim haec agerentur, calu contigit, Principes cum Militibus de Romana expeditione, quæ tunc instabat, acerbè contendere, constringentes eos multò plures halspergas de beneficiis suis ducere, quàm sibi videntur se posse vel jure debere. Sed quando hoc non ab aliquo antecessorum nostrorum termini fuerit, duximus dignum, ut eorum altercationi finem commodum imponerenus, atq; decertam aliquam legem super omni Romana Expeditione concederemus.
units.tr: 1. If we follow the custom of our predecessors, we strive to help not only those who are present but also our successors. For this reason let the experience of all men know that, while the time for setting out to the Apostolic See for consecration and the receiving of the crown was pressing, we spent a year at Worms with many princes. There we decided to confirm the whole state of the commonwealth as uniform and honourable, and to root out utterly what was harmful and contrary to it. Meanwhile, while these things were being done, it happened by chance that the princes and the knights disputed bitterly about the Roman expedition, which was then imminent, since the princes compelled them to bring many more hauberks from their benefices than they seemed able, or were bound by right, to do. But since this had not been fixed by any of our predecessors, we thought it fitting to put a suitable end to their dispute and to grant some fixed law concerning every Roman expedition.

units.la: 2. Statuimus ergo & decrevimus cum consensu tam Spiritualium quàm Sæcularium Principum, nobilium aßidentium, quando pro corona nostra vel aliqua regni utilitate aut honore Romana expeditio à nobis vel à successoribus nostris præparetur, ad omnium nobiscum euntium præparationem annus cum sex hebdomadibus pro induciis detur, & per totum taliter regnum hdeliter nostris indicetur. Cuicunq; autem secundum hanc legem eadem expeditio imperetur, si ad CuGallorum, hoc est, in Campum, qui vulgò Rungalle, Dominum suum non comitetur, & ibi cum apparatu non repræsentetur, feodo, præter hos, qui cum gratia Dominorum suorum remanserunt, in conspectu nostro absq; spe recuperationis priveitur.
units.tr: 2. We therefore establish and decree, with the consent of both spiritual and secular princes and of the assenting nobles, that whenever a Roman expedition is prepared by us or by our successors for our crown or for some benefit or honour of the kingdom, a year with six weeks is to be given as a truce for the preparation of all who go with us, and it is to be faithfully announced throughout the whole kingdom. Whoever is commanded to this expedition under this law, and does not accompany his lord to the Campus Gallorum, that is, to the field commonly called Rungalle, and is not presented there with equipment, shall, apart from those who have remained with the favour of their lords, be deprived of his fief in our sight, without hope of recovery.

units.la: 3. Qui autem per hominium sive liberi sive famuli Dominis suis adhæserint, quot decem mansos in beneficio possideant, tot brunias cum duobus scutariis singulas marcas accipiant: & sic cum redeundo cum hoc stipendio sine omni Dominorum damno vel expensa, nisi quantum ipsis Dominis placuerit, fideliter serviant.
units.tr: 3. Those who have attached themselves to their lords by homage, whether free men or servants, shall, for every ten manses they hold in benefice, each take a byrnie with two shield-bearers and a mark apiece; and thus, on the return journey, they shall serve faithfully with this pay, without any loss or expense to their lords, except as far as the lords themselves may please.

units.la: 4. Si autem forte (quod absit) accidat, ut iidem Milites diversos Dominos propter diversa beneficia acquirant, ne aliquod beneficium indebitum vel sine servitio remaneat, singuli singula debita singulis Dominis persolvant: videlicet quantum ab ipsis, si irent, acceptuli erant, tantum se cognoscant, vel in præfato loco (ut dictum est) feodum amittant: sed stipendia, nisi voluntate Dominorum, non prætermittant.
units.tr: 4. If it should happen (which God forbid) that the same knights acquire different lords on account of different benefices, then, so that no benefice remains undischarged or without service, each shall pay each lord what is due. Namely, they shall acknowledge that they owe just as much as they would have received from those lords had they gone; otherwise they forfeit the fief in the aforesaid place, as has been said. But they shall not omit the pay, unless it is by the will of the lords.

units.la: 5. Similiter de Ecclesiarum filiis vel domesticis, id est ministerialibus, vel quorumcumque Principum clientela, qui quotidie ad serviendum parati esse debent, statuimus, ut quicumq; quinque in beneficio possideant, Domino suo, ad quem pertinent, bruniam cum uno scutario ducant, in arbitrio Dominorum pendeat, quos ducant, à quibus stipendia accipiant, quibus halispergat dant. Ipsis & ad itineris præparationem quinque libras suæ monetæ in stipendiü tribuantur, & duo equi, unus currens, alter ambulans, addantur, ac duobus socijs foumarius victualibus bene oneratus, qui ab ipsis ad opus Dominorum diligenter custodiatur. Ipsi quoq; in Dominorum tam diversis procurationem, quàm diu in incepta vadant expeditione: & quicquid à rebellibus regni pugnando acquisierint, partes duas ad Dominos deferant, tertiam sibi pro consolatione retineant. Quantum non pascunt Domini, ad ipsos reportent tertiam partem sui acquisiti.
units.tr: 5. Likewise, concerning the sons of the churches or household men, that is, the ministerials, or the clients of any princes, who ought to be ready to serve every day, we decree that whoever holds five in benefice shall lead a byrnie with one shield-bearer to his lord, to whom they belong. It shall rest with the discretion of the lords whom they lead, from whom they receive their pay, and to whom they give hauberks. For the preparation of the journey, five pounds of their money shall also be assigned to them as pay, and two horses, one for running and one for walking, shall be added, and to the two companions a wagon well loaded with provisions, which shall be carefully kept by them for the lords' use. They too shall be under the care of the lords, in their various affairs, for as long as they go on the expedition that has been undertaken. And whatever they win by fighting against the rebels of the kingdom, they shall bring two parts to their lords and keep the third part for themselves as a consolation. As far as the lords do not provide for their keep, they shall take back to them a third part of what they have acquired.

units.la: 6. Singuli verò Principes suos habeant officionarios speciales, Marscalcum, Dapiferum, Pincernam, & Camerarium. Qui quatuor quanto plus sunt laboraturi, tanto plus in stipendio, in vestitu & equitatu, præ cæteris sunt honorandi scilicet; & unicuique istorum decem libræ cum tribus equis tribuantur; quartus Marscalco addatur: quorum unum ad præcurrendum, alterum ad pugnandum, tertium ad spatiandum, quartum ad lorcam portandum. Isti verò tales remanere cupientes, si a Dominos impetrare valeant, quot mansos possideant ........... monetæ, vel totum fructum feodi illo anno pro stipendio persolvant.
units.tr: 6. Each prince shall have his own special officials: a marshal, a steward, a cupbearer and a chamberlain. The more these four are going to labour, the more they are to be honoured above the others, namely in pay, clothing and horses. To each of them ten pounds with three horses shall be given, and a fourth horse is to be added to the marshal: one to ride ahead, one for fighting, a third for riding out, and a fourth for carrying the lance. Such men, if they wish to remain and can obtain it from their lords, shall pay for their pay, for as many manses as they hold, a sum of money, or the whole yield of the fief for that year.

units.la: 7. Ut autem nostrum Imperium ab omnibus habeat supplementum, hoc constituimus & firmiter præcipimus, ut singuli buningi decem, cum duodecim funibus de canapo, solidos Dominis impendant, & insuper foumarium cum capistro concedant, quem, si Domini voluerint, ipsi mam navalem aquam usq; perducant. Mansionarius quinq; solidos, Abfarius triginta denarios, Najarius quindecim, quorumlibet larium possessores sex suppleant.
units.tr: 7. So that our empire may have support from all, we decree and firmly order that each group of ten buningi, with twelve hempen ropes, shall give shillings to the lords, and in addition shall grant a wagon-horse with its halter, which, if the lords wish, they shall bring as far as the navigable water. A mansionarius shall supply five shillings, an abfarius thirty pence, a najarius fifteen, and the holders of each farm (larium) shall supply six.

units.la: 8. Et ut hæc nostri Decreti auctoritas inviolabilem & incorruptam in Dei nomine apud omnes successores nostros obtineat emunitatem, cunctis Principibus, qui aderant, astipulatibus, manu propria subter eam roborare decrevimus, & annuli nostri signo assignari jussimus.
units.tr: 8. And so that this authority of our decree may hold an inviolable and uncorrupted immunity before all our successors, in the name of God, we have decided that all the princes who were present and agreed shall strengthen it below with their own hand, and we have ordered it to be marked with the sign of our ring.

units.la: Signum Karuli gloriosissimi Regis.
units.tr: Sign of Karl, most glorious King.

units.la: Hernulfus Notarius ad vicem Lutuuardi Cancellarii recognovi. Data VIII. Idus Junij, anno incarnatione Domini N. I. X. DCCCXC. Regni autem ejus xxii. ante consecrationem. Actum Vormatiæ feliciter, Amen.
units.tr: Hernulf, notary, recognized it in place of Liutward, the chancellor. Given on the eighth day before the Ides of June, in the year of the incarnation of our Lord Jesus Christ 890, and in the twenty-second year of his reign, before his consecration. Done happily at Worms. Amen.

units.la: ARNULPHI IMPER. AUG. DECRETVM COMITIORVM FRANCOFVRTENSIVM IN REBELLES Imperio Regis ac Tyrannos per Galliam & Italiam.
units.tr: The Decree of the Diet of Frankfurt of Emperor Arnulf against the rebels against the kingdom's authority and the tyrants throughout Gaul and Italy.

units.la: Berengarius Forovilianus Præses Italiam intercipit, se Regem adpellat. Ranulphus Aquitaniæ sibi diadema imponit. Radulphus Dux Galliæ Lugdunensis, superiorem Burgundiam inter Juram montem & Alpes Cottias invadit, Rex salutatur. Galliam Narbonensem Ludovicus Arelatensis Comes ambit. Belgis inhiat Vido Dux Spoletanus. Otto Franciæ Occidentalis Procurator à Celtis Galliæ Lugdunensi imponitur. Arnulphus Imp. intellecta periidia hominum Francofordiæ Concilium agit: superiores Tyrannos, nisi ad præscriptum diem prætò Wormatiæ sint, proscribit: eos contra Rempublicam Francorum fecisse viderijudicat.
units.tr: Berengar of Friuli, the margrave, seizes Italy and calls himself king. Rudolf of Aquitaine has a diadem placed on his own head. Rudolf, duke of Lyonnais Gaul, invades upper Burgundy between the Jura mountains and the Cottian Alps and is hailed as king. Louis, count of Arles, aims at Narbonese Gaul. Guy, duke of Spoleto, covets the Belgic lands. Otto is appointed by the Celts as procurator of Western Francia in Lyonnais Gaul. Emperor Arnulf, the treachery of these men having been discovered, holds a council at Frankfurt. He outlaws the above-named tyrants unless they appear in Worms on the appointed day, and he judges that they have acted against the commonwealth of the Franks.

units.la: EJVSDEM EDICTVM AD PRINCIPES IMPERII IN EXPEDITIO- NE ROMANA.
units.tr: The same emperor's edict to the princes of the Empire concerning the Roman expedition.

units.la: NVICTI orbis Christiani Proceres, nierierrix impudica, pancorum scelere, Romam terrarum caput, mercedem stupri tenet: Pontificem Maximum, communem mundi parentem, in vinculis habet, vestrasque victrices dextras scortum contemnit. Agite Principes & Milites Optimi motus vestri... vestro, facinus antehac inauditum, ne syncera pars trahatur, ad vivum ferro resecate. Quae sit imbecillitas adversariorum, satis foemina imbellis, quae eis dominatur, ostendit ipsi ne vultum quidem vestrum atque aciem oculorum, nedum arma ferre poterunt: modo expugnationem simulate, & diffugient.
units.tr: Proud leaders of the unconquered Christian world: an unchaste harlot, by the crime of a few, holds Rome, the head of the world, as the wages of her debauchery. She keeps the supreme pontiff, the common father of the world, in chains, and despises your victorious right hands, a whore. Come, princes and best soldiers, move your forces; cut out with the sword, down to the living flesh, this deed unheard of until now, so that the sound part is not dragged down with it. What the weakness of the adversaries is, a weak and unwarlike woman who rules over them shows well enough: they will not be able even to lift their eyes to your face, let alone bear arms. Only feign an assault, and they will scatter.

units.la: ARNULPHI IMP. AUG. CONFIRMATIO
units.tr: ARNULPH EMPEROR AUGUSTUS, CONFIRMATION

units.la: CONTRACTVS CONCAMBIALIS, CVM ECCLESIA FACTI, QVI sine auctoritate Imperatoris ratus esse non poterat.
units.tr: CONTRACT OF EXCHANGE (?) WITH THE CHURCH, MADE BY ONE WHO, AS HE THOUGHT, COULD NOT BE VALID WITHOUT THE EMPEROR'S AUTHORITY.

units.la: IN nomine sanctae & individuae Trinitatis, ARNULPHUS divina favente clementia Imperator Augustus. Regalem condecet dignitatem, ut facta fidelium suorum, quae communi ipsorum conguunt utilitati, & pie eis consulendo prospiciat, & in posterum mansura gratanter corroboret. Inde omnium Christianae religionis fidelium, instantis temporis ac futuri, agnitum esse volumus noticiae, qualiter Tuto honorabilis Radesponensis Ecclesiae Praesul, & commissi gregis nomine ac merito tutissimus provisor, & femina quaedam N..quandam complacitationis inter se more populari perpetratae chartam nostris praesentarunt obtutibus, supplicantes nostri edicti tenore eam consolidari: quod ita fieri decrevimus. Iussimus igitur hoc praesens muniminis nostri praeceptum inde fieri, per quod decernimus, atque omnino praecipimus, ut hujusmodi complacitationis confirmatio a nullo unquam successore nostro violetur, sed in Christi nomine usque in finem consolidetur, manu nostra subtus eam roborantes, annulo nostro iussimus insigniri.
units.tr: In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Arnulph, by the favouring clemency of God Emperor Augustus. It befits royal dignity to look after the affairs of its faithful subjects which tend to their common advantage, to provide for them by devoutly consulting their interests, and gladly to strengthen what is to endure in future. Therefore we wish it to be made known to all the faithful of the Christian religion, present and future, in what manner the honourable Tuto, prelate of the church of Regensburg, and the most trustworthy guardian by the name and merit of the flock committed to him, together with a certain woman N., presented to our eyes a charter of an agreement made between them in the customary manner of the people, and asked that it be confirmed by the tenor of our edict; which we have decided to do. We have therefore ordered this present precept of our protection to be drawn up, by which we decree and altogether command that the confirmation of such an agreement shall never be violated by any of our successors, but shall remain firm in the name of Christ until the end; and, confirming it below with our own hand, we have ordered it to be sealed with our ring.

units.la: ZUENDEBOLDI REGIS AUG. DECRETUM
units.tr: ZUENDEBOLDUS, KING AND AUGUSTUS: DECREE

units.la: DE RESTITVENDA POSSESSIONE PER INIVSTITIAM ablata.
units.tr: CONCERNING THE RESTORATION OF POSSESSION TAKEN AWAY BY INJUSTICE.

units.la: In nomine sanctae & individuae Trinitatis.
units.tr: In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity.

units.la: ZUENDEBOLDUS divina providentia Rex. Si antecessorum nostrorum, gloriosorum Regum, pium morem sequentes, ecclesiarum statum Regalis auctoritatis rigore inviolatum servatus, ac servorum Dei utilitatibus provida dispositione consulimus, id nobis ad tranquillitatem Regni nostri, & ad beatitudinem aeternam promerendam liquido credimus profuturum.
units.tr: Zuendebold, king by divine providence. If, following the pious custom of our predecessors, the glorious kings, we preserve the condition of the churches inviolate by the strictness of royal authority, and provide with careful arrangement for the advantage of God's servants, we clearly believe this will serve the tranquillity of our kingdom and help us merit eternal blessedness.

units.la: 1. Noverit igitur omnium nostrorum fidelium, praesentium & futurorum, notitia, qualiter de Abbatia S. Servatii Trajectensis Monasterii, in pago Haspaniensi juxta Mosam, & in Comitatu Maslend, quam Dominus genitor noster ARNULPHUS gloriosus Rex ad Ecclesiam B. Petri Treverensedis, Regiae potestatis jure tradiderat, ac perpetua stabilitate firmaverat, Rathbodus ejusdem Ecclesiae venerabilis Archiepiscopus in generali placito nostro querelosis se precibus proclamavit, plagens eam a Ragennatio sub obtentu precariae contra libitum suum suorumque fidelium usurpatam, ac de supradicta Ecclesia violenter abstractam. Protulit quoque quomodo in supradicto Monasterio Misli nostri accepti per potestatem, in Numagam ad nostram praesentiam deducti, ibique minis territi & violentia oppressi ob assensum ex sua parte, illo Cleroque sibi commisso nesciente, hujusmodi usurpativae precariae invite assensum praebuerunt, ac per argumentosas suggestiones (id) nostra auctoritate retulit firmatum.
units.tr: 1. Let it therefore be known to all our faithful, present and future, how the venerable Rathbod, archbishop of the church of Trier, made complaint before us at our general assembly. He declared that the abbey of St Servatius, the monastery of Maastricht (Trajectum), in the district of Haspengau beside the Maas and in the county of Maslend, which our father, the glorious King Arnulf, had handed over to the church of St Peter at Trier by royal right and confirmed in perpetual possession, had been seized by Ragennatius under the pretext of a precarial grant, against the will of that church and of its own people, and forcibly taken from the said church. He also set out how certain of our ministers, having been received into the said monastery by authority and brought to our presence at Nijmegen, were there terrified by threats and overpowered by violence. Thus they gave their unwilling consent to this usurping precarial grant, on their own part, without the knowledge of that abbey and clergy committed to them; and by specious suggestions the grant was confirmed by our authority.

units.la: 2. Nos vero omnia transacta per ordinem recolentes, fallentium jam calliditatibus detectis, quemoniam illius veram esse agnovimus. Perpendentes igitur & verentes, ne forte (quod absit) de eleemosyna genitoris nostri detrimentum animae nostrae faceremus, pro conservanda ejus pietatis munificentia ipsam Abbatiam cum consilio & judicio Episcoporum & Comitum nostrorum memoratae Treverensi Ecclesiae reddidimus, & venientes ad ipsum Monasterium, in quo B. Servatii corpus quiescit, manu propria cum assistentibus pluribus fidelibus nostris restituimus, & hos nostrae redditionis ac confirmationis apices exinde fieri iussimus, per quos enixius jubemus firmiterque sancimus, ut neque in praesenti, neque per succedentia tempora ullatenus alicui in precatiam concedatur, nec aliquo alio ordine cuiquam ex ea quidpiam largiatur, praeterquam iis, qui eidem Treverensi Ecclesiae deservierint: & qui dederit, & qui acceperit, anathematis periculo perpetualiter constringatur. Ut autem praesens nostrae reformationis scriptum inviolabilem per succedentia temporaim Dei nomine obtineat stabilitatem, manu propria subter eam firmavimus, & sigilli nostri impressione jussimus insigniri.
units.tr: 2. We, indeed, going over all the proceedings in order, and the deceits of those who schemed being now exposed, found that his account was true. Weighing and fearing therefore that, which God forbid, we might bring loss to our soul through our father's alms, for the sake of preserving the generosity of his piety, we restored that abbey, with the counsel and judgement of our bishops and counts, to the aforesaid church of Trier. Coming to the monastery itself, where the body of St Servatius rests, we gave it back with our own hand, in the presence of many of our faithful. We have ordered these letters of our restitution and confirmation to be drawn up, by which we earnestly command and firmly decree that in the present time and in succeeding times no one shall in any way be granted anything from it by way of precarium, nor shall anything be bestowed from it upon anyone by any other arrangement, except upon those who have served the said church of Trier. Whoever gives and whoever receives shall be bound perpetually under peril of anathema. So that this writing of our restitution may keep an inviolable stability through the times to come, in the name of God, we have confirmed it below with our own hand and ordered it to be marked with the impression of our seal.

units.la: Signum Domini ZUENDEBOLDI gloriosissimi Regis
units.tr: Sign of the Lord Zuendebold, most glorious king.

units.la: Waltgerus Notarius ad vicem Rathbodi Archiepiscopi Archiquecancellarii recognovi. Data 3. Idus Maij, ipsa die S. Servatii festivitatis, anno Dominicae incarnationis DCCCXCVIII. Indict. prima, anno vero Regis piissimi quarto. Actum Aquisgrani palatio: investitura vero in ipso Monasterio à Rege cum multitudine populi facta, in Dei nomine, Amen.
units.tr: I, Waltgerus, notary, have recognised this on behalf of Rathbod, archbishop and archchancellor. Given on the 3rd day before the Ides of May, on the very day of the feast of St Servatius, in the year of the Lord's incarnation 898, indiction first, in the fourth year of the most pious king. Done at the palace of Aachen; the investiture, however, was made in the monastery itself by the king, in the presence of a crowd of people, in the name of God, Amen.

units.la: LUDOVICI IV. IMP. AUG. LEGES PORTORIÆ, SANCITAE IN COMITIIS RASVELSTADIANIS, LOCVMTENENTE Aribone Marchione Austriae, cum frequentissimo Consilio Episcoporum & Optimatu- m Regni; Anno Domini DCCCCIV.
units.tr: The Laws on Tolls of the Emperor Louis IV, Augustus, Enacted at the Diet of Rasvelstadt, under the Governorship of Aribo, Margrave of Austria, with the Very Full Council of the Bishops and Nobles of the Kingdom; in the Year of the Lord 904.

units.la: MERCES, naves improfessae publicae sunto.
units.tr: Merchandise and ships that have not been declared shall be liable to the public dues.

units.la: 2. Navis, quae ab Occidentali Regno venit, posteaquam sylvam Bathavensem praetergressa est, sive Rosdorphii, sive alibi venundandi gratia appellitur, semidrachmam, hoc est, unum scutatum pendat: si infra Lintzium tendit, semimodios tres, hoc est, tres scaphulas salis solvat: copia postea sit cuique, quò libet versus Boiemiam, distrahendi gratia vehi.
units.tr: 2. A ship that comes from the western kingdom, once it has passed the Bathavian forest, shall pay half a drachma, that is, one shield-piece, whether it puts in at Rosdorf or elsewhere for the purpose of selling. If it sails on as far as Linz, it shall pay three half-measures of salt, that is, three small tubs of salt. After that, each may carry his goods wherever he likes towards Bohemia for the purpose of selling.

units.la: 3. De mancipiis caeterisque rebus nihil penditur. Boios domum salem transvehens, nihil pendit. Boii, Sclavi, bobus, caballis, clitellis, ut victum emant commeantes, immunes sunto.
units.tr: 3. Nothing is charged on slaves or other goods. Bavarians who carry salt home pay nothing. Bohemians, Slavs, and those travelling to buy food for their oxen, horses and pack-saddles are to be exempt.

units.la: 4. Naves a Tranorum nihil praestant.
units.tr: 4. Ships of the Tranae pay nothing.

units.la: 5. Carri, clitellarii, qui Anaslum transeunt, scaphulam praebent.
units.tr: 5. Carts and pack-carriers who cross at Enns give one small tub.

units.la: 6. Venedi, qui de Rugiis, Boiemis mercādi gratia veniunt, de clitella unum scutatum tribuunt: de mancipio, caballis venditis, saicam unam. Venedi vero in Boiaria incolentes, ementes, vendentes nil tribuunt.
units.tr: 6. Wends who come from Rugia or Bohemia for the purpose of trade shall give one shield-piece for a pack-saddle; for a slave or horses sold, one sheep. But Wends living in Bavaria pay nothing when they buy or sell.

units.la: 7. Naves salinariae sylvam Bathavensem egressae, nihil pendant, donec ad Eberspeerg veniant. Si quis ad Moraviam navigat, de nave solidum solvat.
units.tr: 7. Salt ships that have left the Bathavian forest pay nothing until they reach Eberspeerg. If anyone sails towards Moravia, he shall pay a solidus on the ship.

units.la: 8. Mercatores, Judaei, undecunque sint, de rebus & mancipiis justum pendant vectigal.
units.tr: 8. Merchants, Jews, from wherever they come, shall pay the just toll on goods and slaves.

units.la: CONRADI I. IMP. AUG. DECRETA CONCILII ALTHAIMENSIS de anno DCCCCXVI.
units.tr: Decrees of the Council of Althaim of the Emperor Conrad I, Augustus, in the year 916

units.la: QUISQUIS Regi fidem non servarit, aut eidem rebellare conatus fuerit, diris devotus esto.
units.tr: Whoever has not kept faith with the King, or has attempted to rebel against him, let him be devoted to curses.

units.la: 2. Erchingerus quandoquidem cum sociis vitae Regis, Domini sui, & Christi Dei infidiatus est, à classibus Reipublicae armorumque exors esto, in monasterio captus perpetuò archiois religionis disciplina scelus expiato.
units.tr: 2. Since Erchinger has plotted against the life of the King, his lord, and against Christ the God, together with his associates, let him be excluded from the ranks of the Commonwealth and from arms; let him be taken and held in a monastery, and let him atone for his crime forever under the discipline of the archbishop's religious life.

units.la: 3. Richwinus Argentoratensis aedis occupator Herigero Moguntino Archimystae satisfacito. Quod si contempserit, curia Sacerdotum exaugurator.
units.tr: 3. Richwin, occupier of the church of Strasbourg, shall make satisfaction to Herigar, Archbishop of Mainz. But if he despises this, let him be deprived of his office by the court of the priests.

units.la: 4. Episcopi Saxonum, qui praesto esse recusarunt, sacrificiis abstinentor, donec Romam ad eluendum facinus perveniant.
units.tr: 4. The bishops of the Saxons who refused to be present shall abstain from the sacred offices until they come to Rome to wash away the crime.

units.la: 5. a Erchingerus, a Berchtoldus, b Burckhardus, c Arnulphus, quòd nostro Decreto nō steterunt, nec dicto audientes fuerunt, in numero impiorum atque sceleratorum habentor: nemo non eorum aditum atque sermonem defugiro, ne quid ex contagione incommodi accipiatur.
units.tr: 5. Erchinger, Berchtold, Burkhard and Arnulf, because they did not abide by our decree and did not heed what was said, are to be counted among the impious and the wicked; let no one avoid their approach or their speech, lest any harm be taken from the contagion.

units.la: Apud Althaim in pago Rhetiae, anno ab orbe servato, noningentesimo super sextumdecimum, Indictione quarta, duodecimo Calendas Octobris, Regni Conradi piissimi & Christianissimi Regis quinto.
units.tr: Given at Althaim in the district of Rhaetia, in the year of the world saved, nine hundred and sixteen, in the fourth indiction, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of October, in the fifth year of the reign of Conrad, most pious and most Christian King.

units.la: CHUONRADI I. IMP. AUG. CONFIRMATIO CONCAMBII PRAEDIORVM CVM ECCLESIA INITI, QVOD SINE licentia Imperatoris ratum esse non poterat.
units.tr: Charter of Emperor Conrad I Augustus confirming the exchange of estates concluded with the Church, which could not be valid without the Emperor's permission.

units.la: IN nomine sanctae & individuae Trinitatis, Chuonradus Dei gratia Rex. Si Dei Ecclesiis nostro videlicet regimine procurandis dignos adhibere curamus honores, non solùm terreni, sed & caelestis regni non dubitamus honore & fastigio nos sublimari. Inde volumus in nostrorum, praesentium futurorumque pervenire noticiam, qualiter convenit inter Venerabilem virum Radespone sis Ecclesiae Episcopum Tutonem, & quendam a hominem nostrum, ut aliquas ies eorum inter se pro ambarum opportunitate partium, concambire deberent: quod & fecerunt. Tradidit igitur N. proprietatem suam sancto Emmeramnino Martyri, qualem visus est habere, cum omnibus ad praedictum locum rite pertinentibus, in manum Episcopi & Advocati sui N. in perpetuam proprietatem: è contrario vero retradente eodem Advocato unà cum manu Episcopi accepit praedictus N. de rebus S. Emmeramni locum N. cum omnibus appendiciis in perpetuam proprietatem. Et ut hujus concambii præceptum firmum stabileq; permaneat, manu propria subtus illud firmavimus, annuliq; nostri impressione signari jussimus.
units.tr: In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Conrad, King by the grace of God. If we take care to bestow fitting honours on the churches of God, to be governed by us, we do not doubt that we are raised up to the honour and dignity not only of the earthly kingdom but also of the heavenly one. Therefore we wish it to come to the knowledge of our present and future subjects how it was agreed between the venerable man Tuto, bishop of the church of Regensburg, and a certain man of ours, that they should exchange certain possessions between themselves, as suited the advantage of both parties; and this they did. Accordingly N. handed over his property, such as he was seen to hold, with all its rightful appurtenances to the holy martyr Emmeram, into the hand of the bishop and of his advocate N., in perpetual ownership. On the other hand, when the same advocate handed it back together with the bishop's hand, the aforesaid N. received from the goods of St Emmeram the place N. with all its appurtenances, in perpetual ownership. And so that the precept of this exchange may remain firm and stable, we have confirmed it below with our own hand and ordered it to be sealed with the impression of our ring.

units.la: HAINRICI I. IMP. AUG. RESCRIPTUM DE SVA ELECTIONE ET PROMOTIONE AD IMPERIVM, Arnulpho Duci Boiariæ, rebelli ac æmulo suo.
units.tr: ## HENRY I, AUGUSTUS EMPEROR, RESCRIPT CONCERNING HIS OWN ELECTION AND ELEVATION TO THE EMPIRE, to Arnulf, Duke of Bavaria, his rebel and rival.

units.la: NON te tam barbarum aut imperitum religionis nostræ existimo, quin planè intelligas, Regem non à fortuna temerè dari, nec à patris imponi, sed à supremo cœli numine constitui. Cujus mandata qui non facit, is haud dubiè cœlo naturæq; repugnat. Senatus, Proceres, populus, plebes, quæ multorum capitum bellua est, me Regem uno omnium consensu declararunt. Horum mentibus nisi unus & summus Deus author pacis & concordiæ incubaret atq; moderaretur, haud unquam fieri posset, ut non suus cuiq; mos esset: non tot sententiæ, quot homines essent. Undiq; inimici imminent, Galli, Burgundi, Itali, Ugri lacerant, diripiunt, in nos sæviunt, incursant. Si quis gregem ab immortali majestate sibi creditum non tutaretur, non universa ad plebis utilitatem, veluti patens communis à Deo datus refert, nihil aliud quàm latro, & ejus Regnum publicum est latrocinium. Proinde si Senatus Populusq; Francus me hoc facere levarit, tibiq; hoc oneris imposuerit, libens cessero, libentissimè tibi pareto. Atq; ut apertè rute sentias, quàm nihil minus mihi cordi, quàm dominandi libido sit, non solùm Boiariæ Regnum locupletissimum, Narifcos, Alemannos, Chamabos, Boëhos, Suevos, Illissos, Marcomannos, Quados, Vindelicos, Noricos, Austriacos, Tyrollios, Athefinos, Vennonas, Stirios, Chatinos, Venedos, Carnos, Pannonias tibi, sicuti possides, permitto: verùm sacratarum ædium quoque, opum ecclesiasticarum, Episcoporum, Sacerdotum, Mystarium, Monachorum, Antistitum omnium curatorem te esse jubeo & patronum, illos tibi in clientulos dico, modò nomen Regis inutile abdicato: Cuncta alia tibi habeto. Quid nunc aliud tibi vis? Quid ultrà desideras? quæ concupiscis? quæ postulas? Universa tibi favore & gratia mea absq; periculo, sine vi, sine armis obtinere licet.
units.tr: I do not think you so barbarous or unlearned in our religion that you fail to understand clearly that a king is not given by chance, nor imposed by a father, but is appointed by the supreme power of heaven. Whoever does not carry out its commands plainly sets himself against heaven and nature. The Senate, the nobles, the people, and the commons, which is a beast of many heads, have declared me king with one common consent. Unless the one and highest God, the author and guardian of peace and harmony, had brooded over their minds and governed them, it could never happen that each would not have his own way, and that there would not be as many opinions as there are men. Enemies press on every side: the Gauls, Burgundians, Italians and Hungarians tear at us, plunder us, rage against us and attack us. If anyone did not protect the flock entrusted to him by the immortal Majesty, and did not refer everything to the welfare of the people, as the common possession given by God, he would be nothing but a robber, and his kingdom would be a public robbery. Therefore, if the Franconian Senate and people have raised me to this and laid this burden on you, I will gladly yield and most willingly obey you. And so that you may clearly see how far the lust for domination is from my heart, I grant you the most wealthy kingdom of Bavaria, the Narisci, Alemanni, Chamavi, Bohemians, Suevi, Illyrians, Marcomanni, Quadi, Vindelici, Norici, Austrians, Tyrolese, Athesini, Vennones, Styrians, Chatti, Wends, Carinthians, and Pannonia, to hold as you now possess them. Moreover, I order you to be the overseer and patron of the sacred buildings, the ecclesiastical goods, and all the bishops, priests, mystics, monks and prelates, and I declare them your little clients, provided you give up the useless title of king. Keep everything else for yourself. What more do you want now? What do you still desire? What do you seek? You may obtain everything through my favor and grace, without danger, without force, without arms.

units.la: HENRICI I. IMP. AUG. INSTITUTA.
units.tr: HENRY I, EMPEROR AUGUSTUS, INSTITUTES.

units.la: JUBEMUS ex militibus, qui in villis sunt, nonum quemq; in oppidis collocari; cui reliqui agrū colendo victum quærant: nonus tertiam omnium frugum partem conditam asservet, suisque sociis intra muros, horrea & domicilia extruat: sed vice cæterorum ipse, quoties opus erit, militet; & pro patriâ pericula suscipiat, aliis domi servantibus. Hujus instituti commoda hæc sunt, primùm, ut propter incursiones perpetuas, agris spoliatis, non sit timenda penuria: deinde ut in urbibus miles ne deficiat, quæ bellis jam pluribus exhaustæ habitatoribus sunt.
units.tr: We ordain that, of the soldiers who are in the villages, every ninth man be settled in the towns, and that the rest work the fields to earn their living; let the ninth keep a third part of all the produce, stored away, and let him build granaries and dwellings within the walls for his comrades; but in turn he himself shall serve in the army, whenever there is need, while the others remain at home, and he shall undertake dangers for the fatherland. The advantages of this institution are these: first, that because of constant raids and fields despoiled, there need be no fear of want; second, that the soldiery in the cities should not fail, cities which by now have been drained by many wars and are left with few inhabitants.

units.la: 2. Suburbia jubemus esse nulla, aut exigua: tuti casas ratas & viles.
units.tr: 2. We ordain that suburbs be none, or only small ones: let the houses be cheap and humble, and safe.

units.la: 3. Conventus solennes volumus esse tantùm in oppidis; quales sunt dierum festorum, nuptiarū, encæniorum, mercaturum: ut ea ratione oppidorum incrementa fiant: quæ aut diruta resici, aut minùs firma præcipimus muniri.
units.tr: 3. We wish solemn assemblies to be held only in the towns, such as those of festival days, weddings, dedications and markets; in this way the towns may grow. We order that those which have been destroyed be rebuilt, and those which are less secure be fortified.

units.la: 4. E fratribus natu maximum militare volumus, ut homines certos & exercitatos habeat.
units.tr: 4. We wish the eldest of the brothers to serve in the army, so that he may have men who are reliable and experienced.

units.la: 5. Cives itaq; faciendo opere cotidiano, in pace discant eas artes, quibus necessitate compulsi, ad sui incolumitatem utantur. Disciplina enim & labor magnum ad virtutem afferunt momentum.
units.tr: 5. Let the citizens, then, by doing their daily work, learn in peacetime those skills which, when compelled by necessity, they may use for their own safety. For discipline and labour contribute greatly to virtue.

units.la: HENRICI I. IMP. AUG. STATVTA ET PRIVILEGIA LVDORVM EQVESTRIVM, sive Hastiludiorum.
units.tr: The Statutes and Privileges of Henry I, Emperor Augustus, concerning Equestrian Games, or Tourneys.

units.la: PRIMÙM, ut urbs, oppidum, civitas, municipium, pagus, locus deniq; quicunque, ludis hujusmodi designatus, hospitiaq; ipsius, non intra muros tantùm, sed extra muros etiam, quà se jus & limites ejus porrigunt, liberè pateant omnibus & quibuscunq; ludos illos cœlebrare; spectareve cupientibus, exceptis hæreticis, latronibus & proditoribus. Aliis omnibus cujuscunque status hominibus immunitas sit, & liber cômeatus, non tantum iis diebus, quibus ludi edentur, sed & quatuordecim ante, ac totidem post eosdem ludos; de quo voce præconis omnes sint admonendi.
units.tr: First, that any city, town, state, municipality, village, or indeed any place whatever designated for games of this kind, and its lodgings, shall lie freely open to all, not only within the walls but also outside them, as far as its right and boundaries extend, for all who wish to celebrate those games or to watch them, except heretics, robbers and traitors. Let there be immunity and free passage for men of every other rank, not only on the days on which the games are held but also fourteen days before and as many after the same games; and all are to be reminded of this by the voice of a herald.

units.la: II. Inde ut area ludorum, octo diebus ante solennem & indictum eorum diem, sepiatur & munitur; inferneque etiam æquetur, præparetur, sternatur, ut sepiri, muniri, æquari, præparari, sterniri loca similia ab omni tempore motis esset.
units.tr: II. Then let the field of the games be enclosed and fortified eight days before their solemn and announced day, and let it also be levelled below, prepared and laid smooth, so that places of this kind may be enclosed, fortified, levelled, prepared and smoothed as they were at any time in the past.

units.la: III. Ut eodem hoc temporis spatio non alio jure decursuri, quàm equestribus ludis solito & familiari utantur; exceptione adversus eos tuti, qui aliud eos subire jubeant.
units.tr: III. That during this same span of time, those who are to ride shall use no other law than the customary and familiar law of the equestrian games, and shall be protected against those who order them to submit to anything else.

units.la: IV. Ut ne quis sub sacramenti violatione areæ equestri decursurus se immittat, qui non priùs peccata sua expiaverit, & Deo se reconciliaverit.
units.tr: IV. That no one shall enter the equestrian course to ride, under violation of his oath, who has not first expiated his sins and reconciled himself to God.

units.la: V. Uti ne quis ignobilis galeam fortitioni offerat, aut ad decurrendum se præpatet; nisi incurrere velit pœnam viginti marcarum argenti; præter armorum, & equi jacturam; quorum hic cedet familiæ, illa Heroltis sive Regibus armorum.
units.tr: V. That no commoner shall offer a helmet for the lot, nor present himself to run, unless he is willing to incur the penalty of twenty marks of silver, besides the loss of his arms and horse; of which the former shall go to the family and the latter to the heralds, or Kings of Arms.

units.la: VI. Ut quià stirpe nobilis duxerit uxorem imparem, & non ex nobilitate; perinde sciat interdictos sibi hos ludos, atq; ignobilibus, impunitate data, si talis aliquis eis se inmiscuerit, huic more solemni verberibus multandi, & aliis consuetis pœnis afficiendi, cum neque filii ex hujusmodi inæqualibus nuptiis nati, neque nepotes in tertiam usque stirpem ad eosdem ludos admittendi, conatuesque se intrudere, iisdem quibus parentes pœnis plectendi sint: nisi si hi tales fratrem aut consanguineum habeant, ludorum jure fruentem, quod ex insignium ratione palam fit, quo casu is vicem agnati sui luere poterit.
units.tr: VI. That a nobleman who has married a wife of unequal rank, not of noble birth, shall know that these games are forbidden to him just as they are to commoners, with impunity granted if any such man mixes himself in with them; he is to be punished with flogging in the customary manner and with the other usual penalties. Since neither the sons born of such unequal marriages nor their grandsons down to the third generation are to be admitted to the same games, and whoever attempts to intrude is to be punished with the same penalties as the parents, unless such persons have a brother or blood relative who enjoys the right of the games, as is made plain by the display of arms; in which case he may pay the penalty in place of his agnate.

units.la: VII. Ut in ludis singulis singuli quoque ex unaquaque familia tantum admittantur, nisi si qui alii erunt, qui jam ante equestri dignitate condecorati, pro se rem peculiariter gerant, cum alii pro familiæ suæ fama & gloria in certamen prodire cogantur.
units.tr: VII. That in each game only one man from each family be admitted, unless there are others who, already adorned with equestrian dignity, fight on their own account in a special way, since the others are compelled to come forward for the fame and glory of their family.

units.la: VIII. Uti in ludis, communibus expensis & sumptibus, nemo comitatior prodeat, quam serius in equo, si Comes sit; quartus, si Baro; tertius, si Eques; secundus, si ex Nobilitate quilibet; præter quos si plures quis adduxerit, privatis eos sibi sumptibus alendos ne ignoret.
units.tr: VIII. That in the games, at common expense, no one shall come forward with a larger retinue than the following: six mounted attendants if he is a count; four if a baron; three if a knight; two if he is any nobleman. Beyond these, if anyone brings more, let him know that they must be maintained at his own private expense.

units.la: IX. Uti si quis tatæ nobilitatis erit, qui in unum aut plures *Duodecim Articulorum, in ludis equestribus observandorum, commiserit, & nihilominus cum reliquis decurrere præsumat, pro familiæ suæ gloria: hunc Sodalitii, in quo nomen dederit, servus publicus uni ex Heroltis indicet; ut simul insignia ejus in harena conspecta fuerint, veniberibus de more multetur; nisi si quis ex eadem familia culpam consanguinei sui purgare paratus erit; quod Heroltus Regi Circuli, sub quo succedaneus censetur, indicare tenetur, ut ita cum priore illo mitius agatur. Similiter idem Heroltus, ubi arma insigniaque ejus agnoverit, qui pro altero pœnæ & decurrioni se offert, proclamare debet, talem aut talem, adjecto nomine & cognomine ejus, pro alio consanguineo suo, cum & sub his armis pœnæ & juri equestri se submittere; ut spectatores, & præcipuè matronæ virginesque Aulicæ pro alio eum hæc pati, non pro se, intelligant. Quod si vero aliquis animadversione dignus pro se ipse decurrere velit, ejus rei facilè ei fit gratia; sed ita, ut priore loco de incuria pœna admoneatur. Cujus devitandæ causa si mox emanserit, & decursum, ut spospondera ut non venerit, ad proximos inde ludos citatur. quos si item non obierit, rursum ad alios proximos ludos citatur familia ejus universa, admonita, ut aut ipsum emansorem, aut ejus loco duos alios suæ familiæ, nominis & insignium, pœnæ ludorum sistat; sciens, si secus fecerit, se jure decurrendi in talibus ludis in posterum spoliandam. nec se tantum, sed & eos, qui ex ea conjuges sibi optaverint, liberosque ex tali conjugio natos; licet primi illi retrò in ludis huiusmodi certaverint, in quibus deinde admittendi non sunt, nisi rité Regi sui Circuli se purgaverint, & digni venia visi fuerint; quod cùm accidit, perinde ac si nunquam ludis adhuc decurrissent, pro novitiis excipiendi & septis inducendi sunt.
units.tr: IX. That if anyone of noble birth has transgressed one or more of the Twelve Articles to be observed in the equestrian games, and yet presumes to run with the rest for the glory of his family, the public servant of the fellowship in which he has enrolled shall report him to one of the heralds; so that when his arms and insignia have been seen in the arena, he shall be punished with flogging in the customary way, unless someone of the same family is prepared to atone for the fault of his kinsman. The herald is bound to report this to the King of the circle under whom he is considered deputy, so that the former case may be dealt with more leniently. Likewise, the same herald, when he recognizes the arms and insignia of one who offers himself in place of another for the penalty and the course, must proclaim: "such and such a one," adding his name and surname, presents himself in place of another kinsman of his, and under these arms submits to the penalty and to equestrian law; so that the spectators, and especially the court matrons and maidens, may understand that he suffers this for another and not for himself. But if someone deserving of punishment wishes to run on his own behalf, that favour is easily granted to him; but in such a way that, first, he is warned about the penalty for his negligence. If he withdraws at once in order to avoid it, and as he promised does not come to the course, he is summoned to the next games. If he again fails to appear, the whole family is summoned to the next games, and warned that it must produce either the absconder himself or two others of his family, of the same name and arms, to undergo the penalty of the games in his place; knowing that if they act otherwise, they will be stripped of the right to run in such games in future. Not only they, but also those who have chosen wives from that family, and the children born of such marriages, are to be stripped of this right; even though those first ones fought in such games earlier, they are not to be admitted to them thereafter unless they have duly purged themselves before the King of their circle and seem worthy of pardon. When this happens, they are to be received as novices and introduced into the lists, just as if they had never run in the games before.

units.la: X. Die verò ipso ludorum, tenentur decurrere ad suum quisq; Regem devenire, & nomen profiteri, non minus tribus Heroltis præsentibus, ut illud marticibus inscribatur. atque ibi monetur, ne in ludis equo mordaci, calcitroso, sternacique utantur; nisi pœna huic rei statuta, & verberibus multari velint: deinde ita aptata omnia sua arma habeant, ut nemini illa nocere possint, aut exantlibus acuminibus, præacutisque extremitatibus lædere quenquam valeant. Telis etiam non aliis utantur, quàm clava equestri, & gladio; quæ ipsa quoque ad solitum ludis morem haberi & inspici debeant. Hæc qui ita, ut diximus, providerit, is demum galeam fortitioni offerre, in certamen descendere, & observato ludorum jure ac cerimoniis, cum quovis decurrere, & vires suas periclitari poterit.
units.tr: X. On the actual day of the games, each man is bound to come to his own King and declare his name, in the presence of at least three heralds, so that it may be inscribed on the roll. There he is warned not to use in the games a horse that bites, kicks or throws, unless they wish to be punished by the penalty established for this and by flogging. Then let all his arms be so fitted that they cannot harm anyone, and let them not be able to injure anyone with unblunted points or sharp extremities. Let them use no weapons other than the equestrian club and the sword, and these too must be held and inspected in the customary manner of the games. He who has provided thus, as we have said, may then offer his helmet for the lot, descend into the contest, and, with the law and ceremonies of the games observed, run against anyone and test his strength.

units.la: XI. Atque hactenus de iis, quæ ante decurrionem fieri par est; quæ ubi erit celebrata, rursum quisque ad sui Circuli Regem accedet, testimonium decursionis scripto comprehensum petiturus; quod tamen non nisi duobus Regibus ludorum, duobusque Heroltis præsentibus datur, qui in hac re ei, qui ipse non decurrerit, sub periurii & violati sacramenti pœna gratificari prohibentur. Scriptum autem hujusmodi ipsi Reges, cum adjectione Circuli, cujus nomine præsident, nominis sui subscriptione muniunt. Sed hoc Regiæ, Ducalis, aut Principalis dignitatis personæ non indigent: quoniam Reges sui Regni corona, Principes & Duces ferto caput adumbrare contenti, non solent perinde ut alii in his ludicris pugnis illud adornare; quemadmodum nec sodalitati ulli se inferre; quod tamen inferioris dignitatis omnes non solum faciunt, verum etiam facere tenentur.
units.tr: XI. So far concerning what must be done before the course. When that has been celebrated, each man shall again approach the King of his circle, to seek a written testimony of the course. This, however, is given only in the presence of two Kings of the games and two heralds, and they are forbidden to grant it to anyone who has not himself run, under penalty of perjury and violated oath. The Kings themselves confirm such a writing with their own signature, adding the circle in whose name they preside. But persons of royal, ducal or princely dignity do not need this. Since kings are content to shade their head with the crown of their kingdom, and princes and dukes with a cap, they are not accustomed, as others are, to adorn it in these mock fights, nor to enter any fellowship; which, however, all those of lower dignity not only do but are even bound to do.
