units.la: 2. Post solemnes autem hos ludos, qui sunt gravis armaturæ; aliæ quoque digladiationes sequi solent, & puris hastis concursiones, deque cursu certamina. Chori item, & tripudia, ad numerosque saltationes.
units.tr: 2. After these solemn games, which are of heavy armour, other sword fights usually follow, and encounters with blunt lances, and races on foot. Likewise choruses and dances, with leaps to the rhythm of music.

units.la: 3. Præterea gratiarum actiones dicuntur, & bravia donantur iis, qui de singulis Circulis armorum laude primi judicati fuerint.
units.tr: 3. Moreover, thanks are given, and prizes are bestowed on those who have been judged first in the praise of arms from each circle.

units.la: 4. Reges quoque ludorum, novis ad hoc officium designatis, administrationis suæ rationes reddunt; præsentibus ex quoque Circulo minimum tribus, qui iis ludis decurrerint; quorum etiam est acta Regum suorum suis subscriptionibus & signis communire.
units.tr: 4. The Kings of the games also render an account of their administration, once new men have been designated for this office, with at least three from each circle who have run in those games present; and it is their duty to confirm the acts of their Kings with their own signatures and seals.

units.la: XII. Hoc quoque observandum, ut omnibus jam ad ludos exhibendos præparatis, deliganturex singulis Circulis duo, quorum quatuor disciplinæ ludicræ, quatuor septorum custodiæ deputentur, ut hi, ordinibus jam partitis & distributis, funes incidant, atque ita viam decurrentibus aperiant, animadvertantq; in eos, qui animadversione dignū aliquid admiserint; isti cum videbitur signū receptui tuba dari jubeant; quo audito depugnantes omissis clavis suis, gladiis rem gerere incipiant, & alia aliorum clenodiaconscindere & diloricare contendant. quo facto septa recluduntur, utpote rite omnibus, quae ad ludorum solemnia pertinent, administratis. Statutum in Maidenburgo, die Sabbathi post Octavam Trium Regum, Anno Dominicae Incarnationis MDCCCXXXVIII. in praesentia omnium Procerum & Optimatum Imperii ex Germania, Gallia & Sclavorum gentibus convocatorum, quorum haec sunt nomina juxta distributionem exercituum, quos Imperator contra hostes Imperii ordinaverat ad ejus magnitudinem conservandam & augmentandam:
units.tr: XII. This too is to be observed: when everything has been prepared for holding the games, two men are chosen from each circle, of whom four are assigned to the discipline of the games and four to guarding the enclosures. With their ranks now divided and distributed, they are to cut the ropes and so open the way for those riding, and to watch for those who have committed anything deserving punishment. When the signal for retreat is sounded by trumpet, then, on hearing it, those fighting lay down their clubs and begin to fight with swords, and strive to tear apart and unlace each other's ornaments. When this is done, the enclosures are opened, since everything pertaining to the solemnities of the games has been duly carried out. Enacted at Magdeburg, on the Saturday after the Octave of the Three Kings, in the year of the Lord's Incarnation MDCCCXXXVIII, in the presence of all the nobles and magnates of the Empire, summoned from Germany, Gaul and the Slavic peoples, whose names are these, according to the distribution of the armies which the Emperor had ordered against the enemies of the Empire to preserve and increase its greatness:

units.la: PROCESSUS IN OTTONIS I. IMP. AUG. INAUGURATIONE AQUISGRANENSI OBSERVATUS, Anno Domini DCCCCXLVI.
units.tr: THE PROCEEDINGS OBSERVED AT THE AACHEN INAUGURATION OF OTTO I, AUGUSTUS EMPEROR, IN THE YEAR OF OUR LORD 946

units.la: ANno Dominicæ Nativitatis DCCCCXLVI. Indictione X. Otto Primus per manus Hildeberti Archiepiscopi Moguntini, Aquisgrani in Regem unctus est. Cum enim duo Pontifices, Treverensis videlicet & Coloniensis inter se contenderent, quis hoc munus consecratione peragere debuisset, Procerum judicio ad Hildebertum Moguntinum Pontificem delatum est.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord's Nativity 946, in the tenth indiction, Otto I was anointed king at Aachen by the hands of Hildebert, Archbishop of Mainz. For when two bishops, those of Trier and of Cologne, disputed between themselves which of them ought to perform this office by consecration, the matter was referred by the judgment of the nobles to Hildebert, bishop of Mainz.

units.la: Qui accedens ad altare, & sumens inde gladium Imperialem cum baltheo, conversusque ad Reantene genua flectentem, dixit: Accipe hunc gladium, in quo deiicias omnes adversarios, barbaros, & malos Christianos, tibi authoritate divina traditum, cum omni potestate totius Imperii Francorum, ad firmissimam pacem Christianorum, Amen. Deinde sumptis armillis & chlamyde induit eum, dicens: His cornibus humeris demissis, monearis quo zelo fidei fervere debeas, & in tuenda pace usque, in finem constans perseveres. Exinde sceptro baculoque, dixit: His signis monitus esto, quatenus paterna castigatione subjectos corripias, prirte Dei Ministris, deinde etiam viduis, orphanis & pupillis protectorem ac defensorem semper exhibeas, eisque misericordia clementer porrigas. Posthæc fulso super caput ejus oleo consecrationis, ait; Unxit te Dominus Regem super populum suum, ut numquam de capite tuo oleum miserationis deficiat, quo hic & in futuro mi ab ipso creatore tuo consequaris, Amen. Postremo imposuit capiti ejus Regalem coronam, dicens: Accipe coronam justitiæ, qua moneris te justitiam debere subditis, quatenus hoc ornamento præmunitus, & tuis reverendus, & inimicis terribilis appareas, & post hujus vitæ terminum cum Angelis præmio coroneris, Amen.
units.tr: He approached the altar, took from it the imperial sword with its belt, and turning to Otto, who was kneeling, said: Receive this sword, with which you may cast down all adversaries, barbarians and bad Christians, handed to you by divine authority, together with all the power of the whole Frankish empire, for the most firm peace of Christians. Amen. Then, taking up the armbands and the cloak, he clothed him, saying: With these hanging down from your shoulders, you are reminded with what zeal for the faith you ought to burn, and that you should be steadfast in maintaining peace, persevering to the end. Then, with the sceptre and the staff, he said: Be warned by these signs, that you should correct those subject to you with a father's chastisement, showing yourself always a protector and defender first of the ministers of God, then also of widows, orphans and wards, and extending mercy to them kindly. Afterwards, pouring the oil of consecration on his head, he said: The Lord has anointed you king over his people, so that the oil of mercy may never fail from your head, that you may obtain this from your Creator both here and in the future life, Amen. Lastly, he placed the royal crown on his head, saying: Receive the crown of justice, by which you are reminded that you owe justice to your subjects, so that, fortified by this ornament, you may appear reverend to your own people and terrible to your enemies, and after the end of this life may be crowned with a reward together with the angels, Amen.

units.la: 3. Completa benedictione Pontificis, Regem in solium Regale cum omni lætitia posuerunt.
units.tr: 3. When the bishop's blessing was complete, they placed the king on the royal throne with all rejoicing.

units.la: OTTONIS I. IMP. AUG. CONSTITUTIO
units.tr: OTTO I, EMPEROR AUGUSTUS: CONSTITUTION

units.la: DE LOCATIONE ET PRIVILEGIO CAMERAE IMPERIALIS Magdenburgensis.
units.tr: CONCERNING THE SITE AND PRIVILEGE OF THE IMPERIAL CHAMBER AT MAGDEBURG.

units.la: IN nomine Domini, amen. Nos Otto, Romanorum Imperator Semper Augustus, significamus scripto nostro omnibus, qui illud vel visuri vel audituri fuerint, quod accedentes nostram Cæsaream Majestatem fideles ac strenui, Imperii Romani subditi egregii Saxones declararunt constanti animo, in tranquillitate Dei sedes simul locare suas, civitatemque extruere, ubi & auctoritate ... locum sibi delegerunt, quem colere inhabitareque vellent, supplicantes, ut gratiæ prærogativis primùm condonati, simul & perpetua pace firmata à Majestate nostra, legibus quoque & juribus instituerentur. Nos illorum precibus moniti, simulque expendentes, tum illorum amorem & ardorem, quem erga fidem Christianam gerunt, tum etiam illorum strenuè gesta atque indefessa obsequia, quæ & nunc præstant, & antea Romano Imperio præstiterunt, cum scientia sanctissimi patris nostri Papæ Martini, qui ad hæc auctoritate sua & Sancti Petri, pacem suam largitus est, quam nos confirmamus de scitu & consilio Principum Imperii, & accedente consensu terræ; eisdem Saxonibus, fidelibus nostris dilectis, facultatem concessimus concedimusque civitatem extruendi, muniendi, atque in ea jus municipale instituendi, ita ut antiquitus jus municipale observari solitum est.
units.tr: In the name of the Lord, amen. We, Otto, Emperor of the Romans, ever Augustus, make known by this our writing to all who shall see or hear it that the faithful and vigorous subjects of the Roman Empire, the distinguished Saxons, approaching our imperial Majesty, declared with steadfast mind that they wished to settle their seats together in the peace of God and to build a city, and that by their own authority ... they had chosen for themselves a place which they wished to cultivate and inhabit. They begged that, first pardoned by the privileges of grace, and at the same time with perpetual peace confirmed by our Majesty, they might also be established with laws and rights. Moved by their prayers, and weighing both the love and zeal which they bear toward the Christian faith, and also their vigorous and tireless services, which they both now render and formerly rendered to the Roman Empire, with the knowledge of our most holy father Pope Martin, who by his authority and that of Saint Peter has granted his peace, which we confirm with the knowledge and counsel of the princes of the Empire and with the consent of the land, we have granted and do grant to the same Saxons, our beloved faithful subjects, the faculty of building and fortifying a city and of establishing municipal law in it, just as municipal law has been customarily observed from of old.

units.la: 2. Concedimus præterea fidelibus nostris dilectis atque illorum successoribus, perpetuam in civitate pacem, gratiam & libertatem, quòd eo jure, prout à nobilibus & generosis CONSTANTINO & CAROLO, egregiis Saxonibus atque Provinciæ datum est, uti & frui debeant ad honorem & emolumentum civitatis, secundum juris formam, generaliter & specialiter, nisi forte quis jus habere carere declararus fuerit, juréq; exîstat privatus.
units.tr: 2. Furthermore, we grant to our beloved faithful subjects and their successors perpetual peace, grace and liberty in the city, so that they may hold and enjoy that right, just as it was given by the noble and generous Constantine and Charles, to the distinguished Saxons and the province, for the honour and advantage of the city, according to the form of law, both generally and specifically, unless perhaps someone shall have been declared to have no right to it and stands deprived of the law.

units.la: 3. Insuper liberos pronunciamus illos perpetuò à nobis & successoribus nostris, ita ut civitatis ejus incolæ perpetuò liberi sint ab Imperio, quamdiu ipsi suam libertatem, ut juris est, servare sint.
units.tr: 3. Moreover, we declare them perpetually free from us and our successors, so that the inhabitants of that city may be perpetually free from the Empire, for as long as they keep their liberty, as is right.

units.la: 4. Adhæc illi civitati, quæ Maydeburgum vocatur, ex nostra concessione liberum esse voluerunt, ut quidquid illius Præfecti cum insigniorum ac prudentium consilio & populi assensu, ad civitatis honorem, emolumentum, rum & tranquillitatem statuerint, id firmum & stabile esse debebit, perinde ac si ab ipso Imperio concessum & statutum foret. atque illud ipsum plebiscitum, si annuum diem duraverit, servari debet, si ipsimet voluerint. Quod si pacificè post id tempus judicialiter fuerit, robur juris scripti obtinebit, siquidem non repugnet jure scripto & sacrosanctæ fidei Christianæ.
units.tr: 4. Besides, to that city which is called Magdeburg they wished, by our grant, to be free, so that whatever its prefect, with the counsel of the more distinguished and prudent men and with the assent of the people, shall have decreed for the honour, advantage, wealth and tranquillity of the city, that shall be firm and stable, just as if it had been granted and decreed by the Empire itself. And that same plebiscite, if it has lasted for a year's day, ought to be observed, if they themselves so wish. But if after that time it has been peacefully adjudicated, it shall obtain the force of written law, provided it does not conflict with written law and the most holy Christian faith.

units.la: 5. Quare auctoritate nostra Cæsarea mandamus omnibus Principibus nostris & Imperii subditis, Dominis, Equitibus Auratis, Ministerialibus, & omnibus Officialibus tam spiritualibus quam secularibus, ne eandem civitatem Maydeburgensem atque ejus incolas, in illorum jure, libertatibus & immunitatibus à nobis gratiosè concessis impediant, aut ulla ratione gravent, sive violentia, mandatis, exactionibus, sive etiam bellicis subsidiis, aut aliis quibuscunque gravaminibus.
units.tr: 5. Therefore by our imperial authority we command all our princes and the subjects of the Empire, lords, gilded knights, ministerials, and all officials, both spiritual and secular, not to hinder that city of Magdeburg and its inhabitants in their rights, liberties and immunities graciously granted by us, nor to burden them in any way, whether by violence, mandates, exactions, or even military subsidies, or any other grievances.

units.la: 6. Damus insuper illis potestatem dominandi jure municipali, circa quod conservare illos volumus; & proinde nemo huic contravenire audeat. Alioquin quisquis id fecerit, succumbet potestati nostræ Cæsareæ; & si quid præjudicii eis inde accideret, volumus nos & successores nostri, eandem civitatem atque ejus incolas indemnes reddere.
units.tr: 6. We moreover give them power of lordship under municipal law, which we wish them to keep; and therefore let no one dare to act against this. Otherwise, whoever does so shall submit to our imperial power; and if any harm should befall them from this, we wish both ourselves and our successors to make that city and its inhabitants whole and unharmed.

units.la: 7. Ceterum damus eidem civitati atque ejus incolis in verum tutorem, sacrosanctum jus, etiam, Romanum denique Imperatorem cum Principibus, [Electoribus] spiritualibus & secularibus, qui adstent clypeo militari in omnibus utilitatibus atque emolumentis.
units.tr: 7. Moreover, to that same city and its inhabitants we give, as true protector, the inviolable right; and finally the Roman Emperor himself, with the princes, spiritual and secular electors, who shall stand by with the military shield, in all benefits and advantages.

units.la: 8. Ad perpetuam igitur memoriam, cum assensu sacri Romani Principum Imperii, cumque unanimitate rerum, juxta illorum laudum, omnes gratiarum prærogativas, libertates, jura, articulos, privilegia, statuta, & plebiscita confirmavimus, ratificavimus, & obsignavimus sigillo aureo Majestatis nostræ Cæsareæ, quod appensum est. Datum à Nativitate Christi, anno noningentesimo quadragesimo septimo; Imperii nostri anno secundo, die septima mensis Junij, eo in loco, ubi nunc civitas Maydeburgensis situata est.
units.tr: 8. Therefore, for perpetual memory, with the assent of the holy princes of the Roman Empire, and with the unanimous agreement of the matters, according to their praise, we have confirmed, ratified and sealed with the golden seal of our imperial Majesty, which is appended, all the privileges of grace, liberties, rights, articles, charters, statutes and plebiscites. Given from the Nativity of Christ in the year nine hundred and forty-seven, in the second year of our reign, on the seventh day of the month of June, in that place where the city of Magdeburg is now situated.

units.la: LUDOLPHI REGIS ROMA- NORUM
units.tr: LUDOLPH, KING OF THE ROMANS

units.la: SUPPLICATIO AD OTTONEM I. IMP. UNDE LIQUERE POTEST, in quantum Rex Romanorum debeat esse Imperatori fidelis & subjectus.
units.tr: THE SUPPLICATION OF LUDOLPH TO OTTO I, EMPEROR, FROM WHICH IT CAN BE SEEN HOW FAR THE KING OF THE ROMANS OUGHT TO BE FAITHFUL AND SUBJECT TO THE EMPEROR.

units.la: UNDE initium dicendi faciam? nam, quod solet ad deprecandum aliis esse subsidio, nomen paternum; id me nunc exhorrescere facit. Filii tui nomine indignus sum, qui nullam filio dignam pietatem præstiti. Tu mihi, Pater, honores Regni dedisti: tu Imperium daturus es, sed omnibus beneficiis contra re usus sum. Membrum Imperii appellari non debeo, qui gentes externas, & immanes barbaros in mediam Germaniam inimici: qui meâ manu sacra prophanaque vastavi; qui nulli dignitati aut religioni peperci: qui armis impiis urbes exhausi, cæde agros & urbes vastavi. Nullus hostis tantum mihi dedecoris infligere, tantum turpitudinis afferre potuit, quantum mea mihi temeritas & insania nunc conflavit: nec peccati excusationem, nec maleficiorum prætextum invenio. Utere tu (audebo enim ferò dicere) Pater, tuo summo jure in me, modò supplicis preces non plane averteris: & quo pacto satisfacere tibi debeam, per infimum aliquem ex ministris tuis, qui meæ miseriæ hîc sunt spectatores, nutu significa: modò tantum veniæ impetrem, ut in tua gratia moriar.
units.tr: Where shall I begin my speech? For the name of father, which usually serves as a help in pleading with others, now makes me shrink from using it. I am unworthy of the name of your son, for I have shown no filial devotion worthy of a son. You, Father, gave me the honours of the kingdom; you are about to give me the empire; yet I have made use of all your benefits to the contrary. I ought not to be called a member of the Empire, I who have called in foreign peoples and savage barbarians into the middle of Germany; I who have laid waste sacred and profane things alike with my hand; who have spared no dignity or religion; who with impious arms have drained cities, and laid waste fields and towns with slaughter. No enemy could have inflicted on me so much disgrace or brought so much shame as my own rashness and madness have now kindled. I find neither an excuse for my sin nor a pretext for my wrongdoing. Use your supreme right over me, Father (for I will dare to say it late), provided you do not utterly turn away from a suppliant's prayers; and by a nod signify to me, through some lowest one of your ministers who are here as witnesses of my misery, in what way I ought to make amends to you. Only let me obtain pardon, so that I may die in your favour.

units.la: OTTONIS I. IMP. AUG. RESPONSUM

units.la: DE IOHANNIS XII. PAPAE ROMANI INIQVITATE, datum Legatis ejus Leoni S. Rom. Eccl. Protoscriniario, & Demetrio Optimati Romanae Civitatis.
units.tr: CONCERNING THE WICKEDNESS OF JOHN XII, ROMAN POPE, given to his legates Leo, first secretary of the Holy Roman Church, and Demetrius, a nobleman of the Roman city.

units.la: Pro correctione ac morum immutatione, quam promittit, gratias ago. De promissis vero fidem mutare, cujus me arguit, an verum sit, ipsi perpendire. Omnem terram sancti Petri, quae nostrae potestati subjecta est, Ecclesiae promisimus reddere; atque id rei est, quòd ex hac munitione {b}RENGARIUM cum omni familia pellere laboramus. Quo enim pacto {c}terram hanc ei reddere possumus, si non prius eam ex violentorum manibus ereptam potestati nostrae subdamus?
units.tr: I give thanks for the correction and change of morals which he promises. As to the promises, whether it is true that I have broken faith, as he accuses me, let him weigh that himself. We have promised to restore to the Church all the land of St Peter which is subject to our power; and this is the very reason why we are labouring to drive Berengar, with his whole household, out of this stronghold. For how could we restore this land to him, unless we first bring it under our own power, having snatched it from the hands of violent men?

units.la: 2. Leonem Episcopum, & Joannem Cardinalem Diaconum, suos infideles, quos nos suscepimus, accusasti, his temporibus non vidimus, nedum suscepimus. Constantinopolim Domino Papa eos ad injuriam nostram proficiscentes dirigente, Capuae sunt, ut audivimus, capti. Quibus cum etiam Salecenum, natione Bulgarum, educatione Hungarum, Domini Papae familiarissimum, & Zachaeum virum reprobatum, divinarum atque humanarum iuscium literarum, à Domino Papa Episcopum noviter consecratum, & Hungaris ad praedicandum, ut super nos irruant, destinatum, eodem captos esse loco audivimus.
units.tr: 2. You accuse us of receiving Leo the bishop and John the cardinal deacon, his faithless men. In these times we have neither seen them, much less received them. When our lord the Pope sent them on their way to Constantinople to our injury, they were, as we have heard, taken at Capua. Along with them we have heard that Salecenus, a Bulgar by birth, brought up among the Hungarians, a very close friend of the lord Pope, and Zachaeus, a reprobate man learned in divine and human letters, newly consecrated bishop by the lord Pope and sent to the Hungarians to preach, so that they might fall upon us, were likewise taken in the same place.

units.la: 3. Haec Dominum Papam nullis narrantibus fecisse crederemus, nisi literae fidem admitterent, quae plumbo signatae ejus nominis characteres monstrant.
units.tr: 3. We would believe that the lord Pope had done these things only if he were not told so by others; but the letters, sealed with lead, which show the characters of his name, lend them credibility.

Georgius Secundicerius, Stephanus Adminiculator, Andreas Arcarius, Sergius Primicerius Defensorum, Joannes Sacellarius, Stephanus, Theophylactus, Adrianus, Stephanus, Benedictus, Azo, Adrianus, Romanus, Leo, Benedictus, item Leo, & Leo, Leo Primicerius Scholæ Cantorum, Benedictus Subdiaconus & Oblationarius, Azo, Benedictus. Demetrius, Joannes, Amicus, Sergius, Benedictus, Urio, Joannes,
units.tr: Stephanus, Cardinal Archpriest, of the title of Balbina; Dominicus, of the title of Anastasia; Petrus, of the title of Damasus; Theophylactus, of the title of Chrysogonus; Joannes, of the title of Equitius; Joannes, of the title of Susanna; Petrus, of the title of Pammachius; Adrianus, of the title of Callistus; Joannes, of the title of Cecilia; Adrianus, of the title of Lucina; Benedictus, of the title of Sixtus; ... of the title of the Four Crowned Martyrs; Stephanus, of the title of Sabina; Benedictus, Cardinal Archdeacon; Joannes, deacon; Bonifilius, Cardinal Deacon and Primicerius; Georgius, Secundicerius; Stephanus, Adminiculator; Andreas, Arcarius; Sergius, Primicerius of the Defenders; Joannes, Sacellarius; Stephanus, Theophylactus, Adrianus, Stephanus, Benedictus, Azo, Adrianus, Romanus, Leo, Benedictus, likewise Leo and Leo; Leo, Primicerius of the Schola Cantorum; Benedictus, subdeacon and oblationarius; Azo, Benedictus, Demetrius, Joannes, Amicus, Sergius, Benedictus, Urio, Joannes,

units.la: Benedictus Subdiaconus & Subpulmentarius,
units.tr: Benedictus, subdeacon and subpulmentarius,

units.la: Stephanus * Archiacolythus,cum omnibus Acolythis & Regionariis.
units.tr: Stephanus, Archacolythus, with all the acolytes and regionaries.

units.la: Ex Primatibus Romanæ civitatis:
units.tr: From the chief men of the Roman city:

units.la: Stephanus filius Joannis Superista, Demetrius Meliosi, Crescentius Caballi Marmorei, Joannes cognomento Nuzina, Stephanus de Muza, Theodorus de Rufina, Joannes de Primiceno, Leo de Carmizuli, Richardus . . . . . . . . Petrus de Canaparia, Benedictus cum Bulgamino filio suo.
units.tr: Stephanus, son of Joannes Superista; Demetrius of Meliosus; Crescentius of Caballus Marmoreus; Joannes, surnamed Nuzina; Stephanus de Muza; Theodorus de Rufina; Joannes de Primiceno; Leo de Carmizuli; Richardus ...; Petrus de Canaparia; Benedictus with his son Bulgaminus.

units.la: Ex plebe:
units.tr: From the people:

units.la: Petrus, qui & Imperiola est dictus, astitit cum omni Romanorum militia.
units.tr: Petrus, who is also called Imperiola, attended with the whole Roman militia.

units.la: 1. His itaque residentibus, silentiumque summum tenentibus, ita sanctus est Imperator exorsus: Quoniam decorum esset, tam claro sanctoque Dominum Papam Joannem interesse Concilio, quur tantum declinaverit coetum, vos, o sancti Patres, consulimus, quibus communis labor Ecclesiasticus, ac commune negotium exististi.
units.tr: 1. With these men seated and keeping the deepest silence, the holy Emperor began thus: since it would be fitting for the most illustrious and holy Lord Pope John to be present at the Council, we ask you, holy Fathers, to whom the common ecclesiastical labour and common business belong, why he has so long avoided the assembly.

units.la: 2. Tunc Romani Pontifices, [Episcopi scilicet Suffraganei, ] & Cardinales Presbyteri ac Diaconi cum universa plebe dixerunt: Miramur sanctissimam prudentiam vestram nos hoc velle percontari, quod nec Ibericos, nec Babylonicos, nec Indicos incolas latet. Non hic jam de illis est, qui veniunt in vestimentis ovium, intus autem sunt lupi rapaces: ita aperte Diabolica perractat negotia, ut nihil circuitionis utatur. Imperator respondit: Justum nobis videtur, ut accusationes nominatim exprimantur. Deinde quod agendum est, communi consilio pertractetur.
units.tr: 2. Then the Roman pontiffs [that is, the suffragan bishops], the cardinal presbyters and deacons, together with the whole people, said: We marvel that your most holy wisdom wishes to ask this, which is not hidden even from the inhabitants of Iberia, Babylon or India. This is no longer a matter of those who come in sheep's clothing but inwardly are ravening wolves; he so openly carries on diabolical business that he makes no use of any circumlocution. The Emperor replied: It seems right to us that the accusations be stated by name, and that what must be done be then considered by common counsel.

units.la: 3. Tunc consurgens Petrus Cardinalis Presbyter, se vidisse illum missam celebrasse, & non communicasse, testatus est. Joannes Episcopus Narniensis, & Joannes Cardinalis Diaconus, se vidisse illum, Diaconum ordinasse in equorum stabulo non certis temporibus, sunt professi. Benedictus cum Pueris Condiaconis & Presbyteris dixit, se scire quod ordinationes Episcoporum faceret pretio, & quod annorum decem Episcopum in Tudertina civitate ordinarit. De sacrilegio non est necesse perscrutari, e quia plus videndo quam audiendo scire potuissemus. De adulterio dixerunt, quod oculis viderant, sed pro certo scirent, viduam d Rainarii, & Stephanam patris concubinam, & Annam viduam cum nepte sua abusum esse, & sanctum Palatium lupanar & prostibulum fecisse. Venationem dixerunt publice exercuisse. Benedictum spiritualem patrem suum lumine privasse, & mox mortuum Joannem Cardinalem Subdiaconum, virilibus amputatis occidisse: incendia fecisse; ense accinctum, galea & lorica indutum fuisse, testati sunt. Diaboli in amorem vinum bibisse, omnes tam Clerici quam Laici, acclamaverunt. In ludo aleae, Jovis, Veneris, caeterorumque Daemonum auxilium poposcisse dixerunt. Matutinas & Canonicas horas cum non celebrasse, nec signo Crucis se munisse professi sunt.
units.tr: 3. Then Peter, cardinal presbyter, rising, testified that he had seen him celebrate Mass and not communicate. John, bishop of Narni, and John, cardinal deacon, professed that they had seen him ordain a deacon in a stable at no fixed times. Benedict, with the boys, the subdeacons and the presbyters, said that he knew he sold ordinations of bishops for money, and that he had ordained a bishop in the city of Todi ten years ago. Concerning sacrilege there is no need to inquire, since we could have known it more by seeing than by hearing. Concerning adultery they said that they had seen with their own eyes, but for certain they knew that the widow of Rainerius and Stephana, his father's concubine, and Anna, a widow, had been abused with her niece, and that he had made the sacred Palace a brothel and a stew. They said he had openly practised hunting. They testified that he had blinded his spiritual father Benedict, and soon after killed John, the cardinal subdeacon, by cutting off his genitals; that he had committed arson; that he went about girded with a sword, wearing helmet and cuirass. All, both clergy and laity, cried out that he had drunk wine to the honour of the devil. They declared that at dice he had invoked the aid of Jupiter, Venus and the other demons. They professed that he had not said Matins and the canonical hours, nor armed himself with the sign of the Cross.

units.la: 4. His auditis Imperator, quia Romani ejus loquelam propriam, id est Saxonicam, intelligere nequibant, Luitprando Cremonensi Episcopo praecepit, ut Latino sermone haec Romanis omnibus exprimeret. Surgens itaque sic coepit:
units.tr: 4. When these things had been heard, since the Romans could not understand his own language, that is, Saxon, the Emperor ordered Liutprand, bishop of Cremona, to set these things out for all the Romans in Latin. Rising, then, he began as follows:

units.la: 5. Persaepe contigit, & nobis expertis credimus, ut in dignitatibus constitutis in vidorum infamiam mictatur. Displicet bonus malis, quemadmodum & malus bonis. Atque hoc rei est, quod hanc accusationem, quam modo Benedictus Cardinalis Diaconus legit, & vobiscum fecit, animadvertimus, incerti utrum e zelo justitiae, an impietatis livore proruperit. Unde mihi indigno concessae dignitatis auctoritatem omnes obtestor per Deum, quem fallere, etsi vult, nemo potest, sanctamque ejus Genitricem intemeratam Virginem Mariam, perque pretiosissimum Apostolorum Principis corpus, in cujus haec recitantur Ecclesia, ut nulla in Dominum Papam jaculentur convicia, quae non sint ab ipso patrata, atque a viris probatissimis visa.
units.tr: 5. It has often happened, and we who have experienced it believe, that people in high office are slandered for the infamy of the good. The good displease the wicked, just as the wicked displease the good. And this is the point: we notice that this accusation, which Benedict the cardinal deacon has just read out and made with you, has burst forth, we are unsure whether from zeal for justice or from the spite of impiety. Therefore I, unworthy, beseech you all, by God, whom no one can deceive, though he may wish it, and by his holy Mother, the inviolate Virgin Mary, and by the most precious body of the Prince of the Apostles, in whose church these things are recited, that no reproaches be hurled against the Lord Pope which were not committed by him and seen by most approved men.

units.la: 6. Tunc Episcopi, Diaconi, Clerus, & cunctus Romanorum populus, quasi vir unus, dixerunt: Si ea quae per Benedictum Diaconum lecta sunt, hisque turpiora & ampliora Joannes Papa indigna facinora non nos a peccatorum vinculis absolvat Apostolorum Princeps B. Petrus, qui verbum indignis claudit, justis aperit: sinus anathematis vinculo innodati, atque in die novissimum in parte positi cum eis, qui dixerunt Domino meo: Recede a nobis, scientiam viarum tuarum nolumus. Quod si fidem nobis non adhibetis, exercitui Domini Imperatoris saltem debetis credere, cui ante quem dies ense accinctus, clypeo, galea, lorica indutus occurrit. Solus Tyberis, qui interfluxit, ne ... natus ab exercitu caperetur, impedivit. Mox S. Imperator dixit: Tot sunt hujus rei restes, quot ... noltro in exercitu bellatores. S. Synodus dixit: Si placet Domino Imperatori, mittantur litterae Domino Papae, ut adveniat, sequeque ex his omnibus purget. Tunc eidem sunt litterae destinatae, quae ...
units.tr: 6. Then the bishops, deacons, clergy and the whole Roman people, as one man, said: If what has been read out by Benedict the deacon, and worse and greater crimes than these committed by John the Pope, do not absolve us from the bonds of sin, may the Prince of the Apostles, blessed Peter, who shuts the word to the unworthy and opens it to the just, bind us in the chains of anathema and place us in the last day with those who said to my Lord: Depart from us, we do not desire the knowledge of your ways. But if you do not give us credit, you should at least believe the army of the Lord Emperor, which, girded with a sword and wearing shield, helmet and cuirass, came to meet him on the day before. Only the Tiber, which flowed between, prevented him from being captured by the army... Immediately the holy Emperor said: There are as many witnesses of this matter as there are fighters in our army. The holy Synod said: If it pleases the Lord Emperor, let letters be sent to the Lord Pope, that he may come and clear himself of all these things. Then letters were sent to him, which...

units.la: SVMMO PONTIFICI ET VNIVERSALI PAPAE, DO- MINO IOANNI, OTTO divina respectu Clementia Imperator Augustus, cum Archiepiscopis Liguriae, Tusciae, Saxoniae, Franciae, in Domino salutem.
units.tr: ## TO THE SUPREME PONTIFF AND UNIVERSAL POPE, THE LORD JOHN: Otto, by the merciful favour of God Emperor Augustus, together with the Archbishops of Liguria, Tuscany, Saxony and France, greetings in the Lord.

units.la: 7. Romam ob servitium Dei venientes, dum filios vestros, Romanos scilicet Episcopos, Cardinales, Presbyteros, Diaconos, & universam plebem de vestra absentia percontaremur, & quid esset, quod nos Ecclesiae vestrae vestriq; Defensores videre noluisse tis, talia de vobis tamque obscura protulerunt, ut ii de historionibus dicerentur, a nobis verecundiam ingereret. Quae ne magnitudinem vestram lateant omnia, quaedam vobis sub brevitate describimus, quoniam si cuncta nominatim primere cuperemus, dies nobis non sufficeret unus. Noveritis itaque, non a paucis, sed ab omnibus tam vestri quam alterius ordinis, vos homicidii, perjurii, sacrilegii, & ex propria cognatione, atque duabus sororibus incestis crimine esse accusatos. Dicunt & aliud audita ipso horridum, Diaboli amorem vinum bibisse: in ludo aleae, Jovis, Veneris, ceterorumque Daemonum auxilium populo. Oramus itaque paternitatem vestram obnixe, venire, atque ex his vos omnibus purgare non diffiteamini. Si forte vim temeratiae multitudinis formidatis, juramento vobis affirmamus, nihil fieri praeter sanctorum canonum sanctionem. Data VIII. Idus Novembris.
units.tr: 7. When we came to Rome on the service of God, we asked your sons, namely the Roman bishops, cardinals, priests, deacons and the whole people, about your absence, and why you had refused to see us, your Church and your defenders. They told us such things about you, so shameful and so obscure, that they would be called the tales of actors, and they would bring disgrace upon us to repeat them. So that all of them may not remain hidden from your Greatness, we describe some of them to you briefly, since if we wished to set out everything by name, one day would not be enough for us. Know, then, that you have been accused, not by a few but by all, both of your own clergy and of the other order, of murder, perjury, sacrilege, incest with your own relative, and with two sisters. They also say something else, too dreadful to hear: that you drank wine to the love of the Devil, and that at dice games you called on the aid of Jupiter, Venus and the other demons. We therefore earnestly beg your fatherhood to come and not refuse to clear yourself of all these charges. If perhaps you fear the violence of the unruly crowd, we affirm to you on oath that nothing will be done beyond the sanction of the holy canons. Given on the 8th day before the Ides of November.

units.la: 8. Hanc epistolam quum legisset, hujusmodi apologeticum scripsit.
units.tr: 8. When he had read this letter, he wrote an apology of this kind.

units.la: IOANNES Episcopus Servus servorum Dei, omnibus Episcopis.
units.tr: ## JOHN, Bishop, servant of the servants of God, to all the bishops.

units.la: Nos audivimus dicere, quod vos vultis alium Papam facere. Si hoc feceritis, excommunico vos de Deo omnipotente, ut non habeatis licentiam nullum ordinare, & missam celebrare.
units.tr: We have heard it said that you wish to make another pope. If you do this, I excommunicate you by almighty God, so that you have no licence to ordain anyone or to celebrate mass.

units.la: 9. Quum haec epistola in sancta Synodo legeretur, advenerunt, qui prius defuerant, Reginaldus Lotharingiae, Herricus Trevirensis Archiepiscopus, ab Aemilia & Liguria Vido Mutinensis, Gerardus Tortonensis, Sigulfus Placentinus. Quorum consilio Domino Papae ita rescribunt:
units.tr: 9. When this letter was read in the holy Synod, there arrived those who had been absent before: Reginald of Lorraine, Herric, Archbishop of Trier, Vido of Modena from Aemilia and Liguria, Gerard of Tortona, and Sigulf of Piacenza. On their advice they sent the following reply to the Lord Pope:

units.la: SVMMO PONTIFICI ET VNIVERSALI PAPAE DO- MINO IOANNI, OTTO divina respectu Clementia Imperator Augustus, sed & sancta Synodus Roma ob servitium Dei congregata, in Domino salutem.
units.tr: To the most high Pontiff and universal Pope, Lord John, Otto, by the grace of divine clemency Emperor Augustus, and also the holy Synod gathered at Rome for the service of God, greetings in the Lord.

units.la: 10. Praeterita Synodo, quae celebrata est octavo Idus Novembris, litteras vobis direximus, quibus accusatorum vestrorum verba atque accusationis causae continebantur. Rogavimus etiam dein litteris magnitudinem vestram, quemadmodum justum est. A vobis, non quales temporis quantas, sed inconsultorum vanitas exposcit hominum, litteras accepimus. Non veniendi ad Synodum rationabilis esse excusatio debuit: sed & praesentes magnitudinis vestrae debuerunt Nuntii interesse, aut aegritudinis, aut certae difficultatis causa satisfacerent, sanctam vos Synodum declinasse. Est & aliud vestris in litteris scriptum, quod non Episcopum, sed puerilem ineptiam scribere decet. Excommunicastis enim omnes, ut non habeamus licentiam canendi missam, ordinandi Ecclesiasticas dispositiones, si aliam Romanae Sedi constitueremus Episcopum. Ita enim scriptum erat: Non habeatis nullum ordinare. Nunc usque putavimus, immo credimus, duo negativa unum facere dedicatio vestra auctoritas prisco rum sententias infirmare auctorum. Nos vero intentioni vestrae non respondeamus. Si ad Synodum venire, & objecta purgare non differtis, auctoritati vestrae prae biobediemus: sed si (quod abiit) venire, & objecta vobis capitalia crimina purgare dissimulatis, praesertim vos venire nihil impediat, non maris navigatio, non corporis aegritudo, non timor: tunc excommunicationem vestram parvipendemus; eam potius in vos retorquebimus, quam quidem juste facere potestis. Judas Domini nostri Jesu Christi proditor, immo venditor ceteris prius ligandi atque solvendi potestatem a Magistro in haec verba acceperat: Amen dico vobis, quaecumque ligaveritis super terram, &c. Quamdiu enim bonus inter discipulos fuit, ligare atque solvere valebat: postquam vero cupiditatis veneno homicida factus, vitam occidere voluit, quem postea ligare solvere, solutum ligare potuit, nisi seipsum, quem infelicissimo laqueo strangulavit? Data X. Kal. Decemb. & missa per Hadrianum Cardinalem Presbyterum, & Benedictum Cardinalem Diaconum.
units.tr: 10. After the Synod held on the eighth of the Ides of November, we sent you letters containing the words of your accusers and the grounds of the accusation. We then also asked your greatness by letter, as is right. From you we have received letters that are not such as the times and the matter demand, but such as the vanity of ill-advised men requires. A reasonable excuse for not coming to the Synod ought to have been offered, and your envoys ought to have been present, to show that you had avoided the holy Synod because of sickness or some definite difficulty. There is also something else written in your letter, which befits not a bishop but a childish fool. For you have excommunicated us all, so that we would have no licence to celebrate mass or to make ecclesiastical appointments, if we should appoint another bishop to the Roman See. For it was written thus: "Do not let anyone ordain." Hitherto we thought, indeed we believe, that your dedicated authority, as two negatives make one, weakens the opinions of the ancient authors. We, however, will not comply with your intention. If you do not delay to come to the Synod and clear yourself of the charges, we will obey your authority in front of others. But if (which God forbid) you put off coming and clearing yourself of the capital charges laid against you, when nothing at all, neither the voyage by sea, nor bodily sickness, nor fear, should stop you from coming, then we will make light of your excommunication and will rather hurl it back upon you, as indeed you could justly do. Judas, the betrayer, or rather the seller, of our Lord Jesus Christ, had received from the Master before the others the power of binding and loosing, in these words: "Amen I say to you, whatever you bind upon earth," etc. For while he was good among the disciples, he could bind and loose. But after he became a murderer by the poison of greed and wished to destroy life, how could he who was later bound bind the loosed, except himself, whom he strangled with a most unhappy noose? Given on the tenth day before the Kalends of December, and sent by Hadrian, Cardinal Priest, and Benedict, Cardinal Deacon.

units.la: 11. Qui quum ad Tyberim pervenissent, eum non invenerunt (Pharetratus enim in campo abierat:) nec quisquam erat, qui his ubi ipse esset, indicare posset. Quumque eum invenire possent, cum eisdem litteris ad sanctam Synodum, quae tunc tertio est habita, sunt reversi.
units.tr: 11. When they came to the Tiber, they did not find him (for the Quiver-bearer had gone off into the field), nor was there anyone who could tell them where he was. And when they could find him, they returned with the same letters to the holy Synod, which was then held for the third time.

units.la: 12. Mox Imperator ait: Expectavimus adventum ejus, ut praesente eo, quod nobis egerit, reremur. Verum quoniam eum non affuturum certo scimus, quam perfide nobiscum egerit, ut genter agnoscatis, etiam atque etiam flagitamus. Notum itaque vobis facimus Archiepiscopis, Episcopis, Presbyteris, Diaconis, reliquoque Clero, necnon & Comitibus, & Judicibus, omniq; Plebi, quod Joannes Papa oppressus a Berengario atq; Adelberto rebellibus nostris, militi in Saxoniam Nuntiis rogans, ut pro amore Dei in Italiam veniremus, & Ecclesiam S. Petri ac seipsum ex faucibus eorum liberaremus. Nos vero, Deo adjuvante, quantum fecerimus non est necesse dicere, ut in praesentia videtis. Ereptus vero mea opera ex eorum manibus, & honori debito restitutus, oblitus juramenti fidelitatis, quam mihi supra corpus S. Petri promulsit, eumdem Adelbertum Romam venire fecit, & contra me defendir, seditiones fecit, & videntibus nostris militibus Dux belli factus, lorica & galea indutus. Quid super hoc sancta Synodus decernat, edicat.
units.tr: 12. Presently the Emperor said: We have waited for his arrival, so that with him present we might consider what he has done to us. But since we know for certain that he will not come, we demand again and again that you recognise how treacherously he has dealt with us. We therefore make known to you, Archbishops, Bishops, Presbyters, Deacons, the rest of the clergy, and also Counts and Judges, and all the common people, that John the Pope, oppressed by Berengar and Adalbert, our rebels, sent messengers to us in Saxony, asking that for the love of God we would come into Italy and free the Church of St Peter and himself from their jaws. We, with God's help, need not say how much we did, as you see for yourselves. Snatched from their hands by my work and restored to his due honour, he forgot the oath of fidelity which he had pledged to me over the body of St Peter. He brought that same Adalbert to Rome and defended him against me, stirred up seditions, and, with our soldiers looking on, became a leader in war, clad in breastplate and helmet. What the holy Synod decrees and proclaims upon this, let it state.

units.la: 13. Ad haec Romani Pontifices, [Suffraganei scilicet Episcopi] reliquusq; Clerus & cunctus populus dixerunt. Inaudita vulnus maudito est cauterio exurendum. Si corruptis morbi, sibi soli, & non... divebesset, quoquo modo tolerandus esset. Quot prius casti, hujus facti sunt imitatione incasti? Quot exemplo conversationis sunt reprobi? Petimus itaque magnitudinem Imperii vestri, monstrum illud nulla virtute redemptum à vitiis, à sancta Romana Ecclesia pelli, aliunque loco ejus constitui, qui nobis exemplo bonæ conversationis præesse valeat, & prodesse sibi: recte vivat, ac bene vivendi in bis exemplum præbeat.
units.tr: 13. To this the Roman prelates [namely the suffragan bishops], the rest of the clergy and all the people said: "An unheard-of wound must be burned out with the cautery. If the disease touched only himself, it could be endured in whatever way; but how many chaste men have been made unchaste by imitating this deed? How many have been reprobated by the example of his conduct? We therefore beg your Imperial Majesty that that monster, not redeemed from his vices by any virtue, be driven out of the holy Roman Church, and that another be set in his place, who can preside over us by the example of good conduct and profit himself; let him live rightly and give an example of living well to them."

units.la: 14. Tunc Imperator: Placet, inquit, quod dicitis, nihilque gratius nobis, quàm ut talis, qui huic sancto & universali Sedi præponatur, inveniri possit.
units.tr: 14. Then the Emperor said: "It pleases me, as you say, and nothing is more welcome to us than that someone such as this may be found to be placed over this holy and universal See."

units.la: 15. His dictis omnes una voce dixerunt: Leonem venerabilem sanctæ Romanæ Ecclesiæ Protectorem, verum approbatum, ad Summi Sacerdotii gradum nobis in pastorem eligimus, ut fit Summus & Universalis Papa Romanæ Ecclesiæ, reprobato ob mores improbos Joanne Apostata. Quo hoc omnes tertio dixissent, annuente Imperatore, nominatum Leonem ad Lateranense Palatium, secundum consuetudinem cum a Cardinalibus ducunt, & certo tempore in Ecclesia sancti Petri Summum Sacerdotium sancta consecratione attollunt, & fideles se crassuturos jurejurando promiserunt.
units.tr: 15. When these things had been said, all with one voice said: "We choose as our minister to the height of the Supreme Priesthood the venerable Leo, Protector of the holy Roman Church, a true and approved man, so that he may be the Supreme and Universal Pope of the Roman Church, John the Apostate having been rejected on account of his wicked morals." When all had said this three times, with the Emperor assenting, they lead the named Leo to the Lateran Palace, according to custom, with the Cardinals, and at a fixed time in the church of St Peter they raise him to the Supreme Priesthood by holy consecration. And they promised with an oath that they would prove themselves faithful.

units.la: SENATUSCONSULTUM ROMANUM DE LEGE REGIA, QUA A PAPA SENATU POPULOQUE Romano jus omne & potestas Ottonis I. Imperatori & in cum confertur: item de electione Romani Pontificis, & investituris Episcoporum, &c.
units.tr: Senatus-consultum Romanum on the Lex Regia, by which all right and power of the Pope, Senate and Roman people is conferred on the Emperor Otto I and on him; likewise on the election of the Roman Pontiff, the investitures of bishops, etc.

units.la: Cum Scholiis Theodorici ANTIEM EPISCOPI Verdensis & Cameracensis, Protonotarii quondam Apostolici &c.
units.tr: With the scholia of Theodoric Antiem, Bishop of Verdun and Cambrai, formerly Apostolic Protonotary, etc.

units.la: Convenit Apostolico moderamini, petentibus benevola compassione succurrere, & poscentium animis alacri devotione præbere assensum. Ex hoc enim lucri potissimum præmium apud conditorem omnium reperitur. Deinde quoque & cunctum Clerum, & omnem populum asserimus esse concordem, & ad ineliotem statum fore productum. Atque ideo, quia juste & tanquam abiliter vestra humilitas à nostro Apostolatu humiliter postulat, quatenus gratulanter peragentes sanctam Synodum vestro consilio congregaram in Patriarchio Lateranensi, in Ecclesia sancti Salvatoris constitutam à pluribus viris Catholicis, Episcopis, & Abbatibus, insuper Judicibus & Legis Doctoribus, promulgantes qualiter quietè & pacificè stare & vivere valeamus, præsentibus omnibus & regionibus hujus almæ urbis Romæ, & ex omnibus ordinibus Cleri & populi, asserentibus & firmantibus per omnia, ut hæresi & altercatione ac omni errore expulso (quoniam his temporibus ex hoc accrescere cernitur,) discernatur tam de Romano Imperio, quàm de Apostolica Sede ac Patriciatus, & de investituris Episcopatuum. Idcirco ad exemplum beati Adriani, Sedis Apostolicæ hujusmodi Episcopi, cujus vitam & actionem satis discretam audivimus, & rationabilem in suis spiritualibus sanctionibus recognovimus. Idem enim sanctus vir sanctam Synodum congregavit, & in præsentia omnium, eorumque auctoritate, Domino Carolo invictissimo Francorum & Longobardorum, ac Patricio Romano, suisque successoribus, Regnum Italiæ atque dignitatem ac ordinationem Sedis Apostolicæ concessit: insuper & Episcopatuum vellet, velut ipsi cum discretione & reverentia libitum fuerit, [præter quos tam Pontifici summi quàm Archiepiscopis ipse Carolus reliquit.]
units.tr: It befits the apostolic government to help with kindly compassion those who petition, and to give assent with eager devotion to those who ask. For from this the chief reward of gain is found with the Creator of all. Next we also declare that the whole clergy and every people are of one mind and have been brought to a better state. And therefore, since your humility justly and fittingly asks humbly of our Apostolate that, gladly carrying it out, we should convene by your counsel a holy synod in the Lateran Patriarchate, in the church of the Holy Saviour, composed of many Catholic men, bishops and abbots, and also judges and doctors of law, and should proclaim how we may stand and live quietly and peacefully, with all present and from all the regions of this nourishing city of Rome, and from all orders of clergy and people, affirming and confirming in all things that, with heresy, contention and every error expelled (since in these times it is seen to increase from this), there be decided both concerning the Roman Empire and the Apostolic See and the patriciate, and concerning the investitures of bishoprics. Therefore, following the example of the blessed Adrian, bishop of the Apostolic See, whose life and conduct we have heard to be sufficiently discreet, and whom we have acknowledged as reasonable in his spiritual decrees. For this holy man convened a holy synod, and in the presence of all, and by their authority, granted to the Lord Charles, most invincible of the Franks and Lombards, and Roman patrician, and to his successors, the kingdom of Italy and the dignity and ordering of the Apostolic See; moreover he willed that the bishoprics be given as they themselves should please, with discretion and reverence [except those whom Charles himself left to the Supreme Pontiff and the archbishops].

units.la: Igitur nos Leo Servus servorum Dei, Episcopus, ad idem exemplum beati Adriani, cum omnibus Clero & universo populo Romano, omnibusque ordinibus hujus almæ Urbis, sicut constituimus, confirmamus, & corroboramus, & per nostram Apostolicam auctoritatem concedimus atque largimur Domno Ottoni Primo Augusto, Teutonicorum Regi piissimo.
units.tr: Therefore we, Leo, servant of the servants of God, bishop, following the same example of the blessed Adrian, with all the clergy and the whole Roman people, and all the orders of this nourishing City, just as we have established, confirm and strengthen, and by our apostolic authority grant and bestow on Lord Otto the First Augustus, most pious King of the Teutons.

units.la: Scholium
units.tr: Scholium

units.la: Fuerat cum Ottonem Primum, quæ volut esse certus, quòd regnum Italiæ sibi suisque successoribus, Imperatoribus, qui essent pro tempore usque in perpetuum, per eandem Papam & suos successores, etiam qui essent posset aut deberet conferri. Nihil enim aut modicum invenit quod spectaret ad jus & proprietatem Imperii, dum illud in se assumpsit. Erat enim propter impotentiam & negligentiam Galliconum, defenso Carolo Rege, Græcis & Barbaris nationibus atque Paganis illud ubique impugnantibus, quasi totaliter consulum. Erat ergo, ille Ottho Primus Augustus, filius Henrici Primi, ad quem Ludovicus tunc impe-rator Francorum, qui ultimus fuit de successione dicti Caroli Primi Augusti, tunc debilis, acceperat Ludovicum Veteris, & Saxonum ex occasionibus multiplicem pro arte, & suum adjecit Henricum Domestica Veterum Regum Francorum mei parte præsenta, quæ meliorem & nobiliorem constituunt, non seqatur modo. Qui quidem Comes fraternum sequendo mandatum, ad eum Papam ad Matrimonium, Thomas hujus duo vocavit: cui venienti illic meritem dissitis fratris sui aperuit, eundem vocavit. tantum domum sibi oblatum nullatenus refutaret. Ipse autem Henricus, convocatus illic Principis & Procerum Galliæ & Saxoniæ, & eorum omnium accedentibus exhortationibus & precibus, sede regnum Imperii & regni intromisit. Noluit tamen in Regem ungi, asserens non mereri ungi, pro eo quod dicto regno obvius aliquando extitit. Qui sic assumpto in se regno, laudabiliter & strenue ipsum rexit Imperium, Alemanniam reintegrando quod omnia munia, quæ prius Reges Francorum & Imperatores illius nationis in ipsa Germania aut jure belli vel aliis quibusdam tenuerunt usque ad illa tempora tenuerunt. Et ultra dictus Ottho Primus Augustus, filius ut prædicitur Henrici Primi, tanquam fidelis & constans Imperator, sibi addidit Imperio Lotharingiam, & etiam Burgundiæ in partibus Galliarum, quæ extunc sub jure & proprietate Romani Imperii hactenus permanserunt.
units.tr: Otto the First had wished to be certain that the kingdom of Italy could be conferred on him and his successors, the emperors who should be in office for the time being, for ever, by the same Pope and his successors, even those who should be. For he found little or nothing pertaining to the right and property of the Empire when he took it upon himself. For, through the powerlessness and negligence of the Gauls, with King Charles having been defended, the Greeks, barbarian nations and pagans attacking it everywhere, it was as though almost wholly without counsel. So that Otto the First Augustus, son of Henry the First, to whom Louis, then emperor of the Franks, who was the last of the succession of the said Charles the First Augustus, then being weak, had entrusted, by many occasions and by his skill, the Saxons, and added his own Henry, and the matters of the ancient Kings of the Franks, present in my part, which make the better and nobler, does not follow now. This Count, following his brother's command, called the Pope to the marriage of Thomas, and when he came there, he disclosed to him the merit of his brother's distant affairs, and called him; he should by no means refuse the kingdom offered to him. Henry himself, summoned there with the princes and nobles of Gaul and Saxony, and at the exhortations and prayers of all of them, took up the kingdom of the Empire and the realm. He was unwilling, however, to be anointed king, asserting that he did not deserve to be anointed, because he had at some time opposed the said realm. Having thus taken up the kingdom, he ruled the Empire laudably and vigorously, recovering Alemannia, which, with all the offices that previously the Kings of the Franks and emperors of that nation had held in Germany itself, whether by right of war or by other means, they had held until those times. And moreover the said Otto the First Augustus, son, as has been said, of Henry the First, as a faithful and steadfast emperor, added to the Empire Lorraine, and also Burgundy in the regions of Gaul, which from then on have remained under the right and property of the Roman Empire until now.

units.la: 3. Spirituali in Christo filio nostro, ejusque successoribus hujusmodi regni Italiæ in perpetuum sibi facultatem eligendi successorem, quam summæ Sedis Apostolicæ Pontificem ordinandi hoc Archiepiscopos seu Episcopos, ut ipsi tantum ab eo investituram accipiant, & consecrationem bicunque permanent; exceptis his, quos Imperator Pontifici & Archiepiscopis concessit. Interea asserimus, quod nemo deinceps, cujuscunque gradus vel conditionis, aut dignitatis seu religionis, ligendi Regem vel Patricium sive Pontificem summæ Sedis Apostolicæ, aut quemcunque Episcopum vel ordinandi habeat facultatem, sed soli Regi Romani Imperii hanc reverendam cultatem, quam absque omni pecunia disponet.
units.tr: 3. To our spiritual son in Christ, and to his successors of this kingdom of Italy for ever, the faculty of electing a successor, which the Pontiff of the supreme Apostolic See ordains; that archbishops or bishops should receive investiture from him alone, wherever they are consecrated; excepting those whom the Emperor has granted to the Pontiff and the archbishops. Meanwhile we declare that no one henceforth, of whatever rank, condition, dignity or religion, shall have the faculty of electing the King, Patrician or Pontiff of the supreme Apostolic See, or of ordaining any bishop, but this reverend right belongs to the King of the Roman Empire alone, which he shall dispose of without any payment.

units.la: SCHOLIUM.
units.tr: SCHOLIUM.

units.la: Nota, quod semper excipitur Simonia in concessionibus Episcopatuum, & etiam majorum sedium. Fit, cur igitur ita introductum sit per Ecclesiam & Ecclesiasticos, qui Romanæ Ecclesiæ præfuerunt, scilicet Papæ natales, qui tunc in Avinione residerunt, quod per eos promovendi in Archiepiscopos, Episcopos, & Abbates concedantur cum Camera Apostolica, & pro communi servitio Dominorum Cardinalium: & alias nullus extunc providebatur, nullus creabatur Antistes, nisi hac solveret, sen se sub horribilibus pœnis ad id obligaverit?
units.tr: Note that simony is always excepted in grants of bishoprics, and even of the greater sees. The question arises why it was then introduced by the Church and by the churchmen who presided over the Roman Church, namely the Popes' natives, who at that time resided at Avignon: that those to be promoted as archbishops, bishops and abbots were granted with the Apostolic Chamber and for the common service of the lords Cardinals. Otherwise no one was then provided for, and no prelate was created, unless he paid this or bound himself to it under horrible penalties?

units.la: 4. Ac reget, utpote Rex, & Patricius Romanus. Quod si a cunctis Clero & universis quis eligatur Episcopus, nisi a dicto Rege laudetur & investiatur, non consecretur. Si quis contra regulam, & authoritatem Apostolicam & traditionem aliquid molitus, aut temerator in aliquo tus fuerit, sive contra hoc nostrum Concilium agens, sciat se in iram sancti Petri Principis Apostolorum, & filii nostri Domini Ottonis, cujusque successorum, & omnium prædecessorum nostrorum furam, & anathematis vinculum incurruram, ac per hoc excommunicationi universalis Ecclesiæ omnisque populi Christiani cum subjacere decernimus. Insuper, nisi a malo resipiscat, irrevocabiliter puniatur, vel ultimis supplicis feriatur. Qui vero pio intuitu custos & observator in omnibus tenet, benedictionis gratiam vitamque æternam cum omnibus Sanctis sine fine mereatur habere culaæ sæculorum, Amen. In his actis interfuere Senatores, Proconsules, Exarchatus Vicemtenentes, Legionarii Scholæ Græcorum.
units.tr: 4. And he shall rule, as king and patrician of Rome. If anyone is elected bishop by the whole clergy and all the people, he shall not be consecrated unless he is approved and invested by the said King. If anyone shall attempt or presume anything against the rule, the apostolic authority and tradition, or acting against this our council, let him know that he will incur the wrath of St Peter, prince of the apostles, of our lord Otto and his successors, and of all our predecessors, and the bond of anathema. Thereby we decree that he is also subject to the excommunication of the universal Church and of the whole Christian people. Moreover, unless he repents of his wrongdoing, let him be punished without remission, or struck with the final penalty. But whoever holds and observes all these things with pious intent, may he deserve the grace of blessing and eternal life with all the saints without end, for ever and ever, Amen. Present at these acts were the senators, the proconsuls, the vice-holders of the exarchate, and the legionaries of the Greek school.

units.la: SCHOLIUM.
units.tr: SCHOLIUM.

units.la: Et nunc est titulus Cardinalis prædicta Scholæ, & olim in ea legebantur Septem artes liberales, & præcipua theorica. Et etiam in ea legit quandoque beatus Augustinus, & Joannes vocatus de Anglia. Et fuit mulier de Mantua natus, quæ fuduit Athenis sub viris habitu, & in tantum profecit in artibus ipsis, quod tandem venerit ad Romam per biennium in eadem Schola artes ipsas liberales legit, & adeo sufficiens fuit, quod etiam majores & nobiles ejus lectiones frequenter audiverunt. Et postea in Papam elegitur concorditer a Romanis, & Papatum bienio plus tenuit. Sed tunc diutius otio & deliciis vacans non potuit continere, sicut prius fecit, dum ardenter in papam positus literarum studio insistebat. Unde dum quadam die in rogationibus cum Clero Romano, sicut tunc moris erat, solemni processione incederet, Papalibus ornata dritcis, edidit filium suum primogenitum, ex quodam ejus Culmen conceptum, prope templum Pacis in Urbe, ut adhuc vetus statua marmorea illic posita figuratio monstrat. Unde Pontifices dum ad Lateranensem de basilica Principis Apostolorum & e contra radunt, illud rectum iter sunt, imo per alias vias per indirectum transierunt, illud aliquantulum prolongando.
units.tr: And now the title of Cardinal belongs to the aforesaid School, and formerly the seven liberal arts and chiefly theoretical subjects were taught in it. Blessed Augustine also sometimes lectured in it, and John, called of England. And there was a woman, born at Mantua, who studied at Athens disguised in man's dress, and advanced so far in these arts that at last she came to Rome, and for two years lectured in this same school on the liberal arts. She was so competent that even greater and noble men often attended her lectures. Afterwards she was elected Pope by the Romans with one accord, and held the papacy for more than two years. But then, being idle and given to pleasures for too long, she could not restrain herself as she had before, when, placed in the papacy, she devoted herself zealously to the study of letters. Hence, while one day she was going in solemn procession with the Roman clergy for the Rogations, as was then the custom, adorned with papal insignia, she gave birth to a first-born son, conceived from a certain [man], near the temple of Peace in the City, as an old marble statue placed there still shows. Hence, when the Popes go from the basilica of the Prince of the Apostles to the Lateran and back, they do not take that straight road, but cross by other routes indirectly, lengthening the journey somewhat.

units.la: 5. Arabum, Judæorum, & Paganorum, & de majoribus omnium plateatum: insuper Cardinales, Archiepiscopi, omnes Presbyteri & Episcopi de finitimis civitatibus, Processionani, Notarii, cellarii, & ex omni plebe Romani Imperii. Datum in Patriarchio Lateranensi, indict. vi. anno dicti Domini Ottonis secundo, feliciter.
units.tr: 5. Of the Arabs, Jews and pagans, and of the greater men of all the streets; in addition, the Cardinals, archbishops, all presbyters and bishops of the neighbouring cities, the notaries, cellarers, and the whole common people of the Roman Empire. Given at the Lateran Patriarchate, in the sixth indiction, in the second year of the said lord Otto, happily.

units.la: SENATUSCONSULTUM ROMANUM DE RESTITUENDIS ROMANO IMPERIO OMNIBUS temporalibus, quæ per Reges ac Imperatores Ecclesiæ Romanæ in damnum Imperii simul & ipsius Ecclesiæ collata fuerant.
units.tr: ROMAN DECREE CONCERNING THE RESTORATION TO THE ROMAN EMPIRE OF ALL TEMPORAL POSSESSIONS which had been conferred on the Roman Church by kings and emperors, to the loss of the Empire and of the Church itself.

units.tr: We, Leo, servant of the servants of God, Bishop, to Otto, our spiritual son in Christ, the August Emperor, and to all his successors as emperors and kings of the kingdom of Italy. units.la: Nota, quomodo Papa in generali Concilio super ipsa venerabilibus reliquiis abjuravit perpetuo illa regalia & tenenda, quæ transtulit in ipsum Ottonem Primum Augustum ejusq; successores, ac Romano Imperio restituit irrevocabiliter in perpetuum. Et advertendum est, cum quanta authoritate & solemnitate etiam illa restitutio processit, pro- inde & causa potissime, prout habetur in textu: sed fuerunt multa alia majora & potiores, sicut præcipue in Sancta communione continentur.
units.tr: Note how the Pope, in a general council, concerning these same venerable relics, renounced forever those regalia and holdings which he had transferred to Otto the First, Augustus, and his successors, and irrevocably restored them to the Roman Empire for all time. And it should be noted with how great authority and solemnity that restitution also proceeded, and especially for what cause, as is found in the text; but there were many other and greater matters, which are chiefly contained in the Holy Communion.

units.la: 5. De Cruce Domini, & de Caligis pedum suorum, & de vestimento inconsutili, & super Corpore Petri, cum tetribilibus sacramentis, à Papa prædicto & suis Cardinalibus, per contentium & totius populi Romani, tam Clericorum quam Laicorum, de omnibus ordinibus Romanorum, & in omni regione præsentibus, laudantibus & confirmantibus pro nimia persecutione Paganorum.
units.tr: 5. Concerning the Cross of the Lord, and the shoes of his feet, and the seamless garment, and over the body of Peter, together with the awe-inspiring sacraments, by the aforesaid Pope and his Cardinals, with the consent and in the presence of the whole Roman people, both clergy and laity, of all the orders of the Romans and in every region, praising and confirming it because of the excessive persecution by the pagans.

units.tr: SCHOLIUM.

units.la: Quæ igitur ista sint oblata eidem Imperio Romano, & nunc per diversos tenentur occupata, tanquam si sint de sui Ecclesiæ Romanæ? Et illa forsan est causa, quare tam sinistre procedunt in capitibus negotia Catholi- corum.
units.tr: What, then, are those properties which were offered to the same Roman Empire and are now held by various occupants, as if they belonged to the Church of Rome? Perhaps this is the reason why the affairs of the Catholics go so badly at the heads of things.

units.la: 7. Et possideatis in perpetuum ad usus Curiæ & militiarum vestrarum ad bellandum & expugnandum contra prædictos Paganos, & contra rebelles Romani Imperii. Idcoq; per hujus nostri authoritatis confirmamus, & corroboramus in omnibus progeniebus vestris, de genera- tione in generationem in perpetuum. Quod si quisquam hanc authoritatem nostram destruxerit, & violatorē esse repertus fuerit, sive contra hoc agens, sciat se in iram beati Petri Principis Apostolo- rum & nostram nostrorumq; prædecessorum casuram. Insuper, nisi à malo reliquerit, subjacebit reus Regiæ Majestatis & Reipublicæ, ut hujus, qui contra Rempublicam, vel contra Imperatorem aliquid moliti fuerint, animæ amissionem sustineant, & bona eorum publicentur.
units.tr: 7. And you shall possess them in perpetuity for the use of your Court and your armies, to wage war and to subdue the aforesaid Pagans and the rebels against the Roman Empire. Therefore by this our authority we confirm and strengthen it for all your descendants, from generation to generation, in perpetuity. But if anyone shall destroy this our authority, and be found to be a violator, or act against it, let him know that he will incur the wrath of blessed Peter, Prince of the Apostles, and of ourselves and our predecessors. Moreover, unless he desists from evil, he shall be liable to the Royal Majesty and the Commonwealth, so that those who have planned anything against the Commonwealth or against the Emperor shall suffer the loss of their life, and their goods shall be confiscated.

units.tr: The archbishops, bishops, and others from the neighbouring counties were present at these proceedings.

units.la: Scripta per manum Gregorii Archinotarii nostri. Datum in Patriarchio Lateranensi, tertio Kal. Maij, Indict. V I. Anno Sedis nostræ secundo, & dicti Domini Ottonis Secundo, felicitér.
units.tr: Written by the hand of Gregory, our chief notary. Given at the Lateran Patriarchate, on the third day before the Kalends of May, in the sixth indiction, in the second year of our see and of the said Lord Otto, happily.

units.la: OTTONIS I. IMPER. AUG. DECRETA COMITIORVM VVORMACIENSIVM.
units.tr: DECREES OF THE DIET OF WORMS OF OTTO I, EMPEROR AUGUSTUS.

units.la: ANno Christi supra noningentesimum sexagesimo sexto, Imperator Principes Germaniae VVormaciam vocat. Ibi de rebus duabus praecipuis consultatum est: primùm de confirmatione Ottonis filii in Imperio: deinde de nova rursus in Italiam expeditione. Prima deliberatio nem est in sententiam Imperatoris, quam ipse proposuit, nullo homine dissentiente: altera decretum, ut Principes Imperatorem in Italiam sequantur, aut dignos Legatos mittant.
units.tr: In the year of Christ 966, the Emperor summoned the princes of Germany to Worms. Two main matters were discussed there: first, the confirmation of Otto's son in the Empire; second, a new expedition into Italy. The first was decided according to the Emperor's own proposal, which he put forward, and no one dissented. On the second, it was decreed that the princes should either follow the Emperor into Italy or send suitable envoys.

units.la: EIVSDEM EDICTA ROMAE PROPOSITA.
units.tr: EDICTS OF THE SAME EMPEROR PUBLISHED AT ROME.

units.la: NEquis aut Imperatoris aut Pontificis justa decretáve violet, aut otium Urbis turbet, aut factiones alat, aut clandestina arma inferat, aut loca munita sine consensu teneat.
units.tr: Let no one violate the just decrees of the Emperor or of the Pope, disturb the peace of the City, foment factions, bring in secret arms, or hold fortified places without consent.

units.la: 1. Similiter poenas starnimus capitales in contumaces, seditiosos, rebelles.
units.tr: 1. Likewise we decree capital punishments against the contumacious, the seditious and the rebellious.

units.la: 3. Qui Magistratus aut Decuriones potestate sua publica nimis libidinose utuntur, neq; praescripto legum, sed suo libitu agunt, non solùm in civitate, sed etiam in ecclesia, factis ipsorum & impunitate examinatis debito rigore justitiae, nocentes reperti restibus jugulentur.
units.tr: 3. Those magistrates or councillors who abuse their public power too lustfully, and act not according to the prescription of the laws but at their own pleasure, both in the civil state and in the Church, shall have their deeds examined and their impunity judged with the due rigour of justice; and if they are found guilty, let them be throttled with ropes.

units.la: 4. Qui templis Divorum, aut laribus domesticis, aut fortunis civium vim infert, capite luat.
units.tr: 4. Whoever uses violence against the temples of the saints, or against household shrines, or against the property of citizens, shall pay with his head.

units.la: 5. Quantò obscoenitatis furore & licentia abripitur, ut nec corporibus hominum ingenuorum parcendum putet, propter criminis foeditatem strangulatus flammis è medio populi Dei auseratur.
units.tr: 5. Whoever is carried away by such a frenzy and licence of obscenity that he thinks the bodies of freeborn men should not be spared, shall, on account of the foulness of his crime, be strangled, consumed by flames, and removed from the midst of the people of God.

units.la: OTTONIS I. IMPERAT. AUG. EDICTVM, AD DVCES ET PRAEFECTOS GERMANIAE.
units.tr: Edict of the Emperor Otto I Augustus, to the dukes and prefects of Germany.

units.la: OTto divino nutu Imperator Augustus, Hermanno & Theodorico * Ducibus, caeterisque publicae rei nostrae Praefectis omnia amabilia.
units.tr: Otto, Emperor Augustus by the will of God, to Hermann and Theodoric, dukes, and to the other prefects of our public affairs: all good wishes.

units.la: Deo volente, salus omniaq; prosperè succedunt. Caeterum nuntii Constantinopolitani Regis dignitate satis insignes nos adeunt, pacem (ut intelleximus) admodùm quaerentes. Quoquo modo res geratur, bello, Deo volente, nos nullo modo temptare audebunt. Apuliam & Calabriam provincias, quas hactenus tenuere, nisi conveniamus, dabunt. Si verò voluntati nostrae paruerint, praesenti aestate conjungem cum aequivoco nostro Ottone scilicet Juniore in Franciam dirigemus per Fraxinetum ad destruendos Saracenos, Deo comite, iter arripiemus, & sic ad vos disponemus.
units.tr: By God's will, all is well and everything turns out prosperously. Moreover, envoys of the King of Constantinople, notable enough for their rank, have approached us, seeking peace (as we have understood) very earnestly. However the matter goes, with God's will they will not dare to attack us in war in any way. They will give up the provinces of Apulia and Calabria, which they have held until now, unless we come to terms. But if they have obeyed our will, we shall send our son, Otto the Younger, our co-regent, into France this coming summer by way of Fraxinetum, to destroy the Saracens; with God as our companion we shall set out on the journey, and so we shall make arrangements for you.

units.la: Praeterea volumus, si * Redares (sicut audivimus) tantam stragem passi sunt, (scitis enim quàm fidem fregerint, quas injurias attulerint) ut nullam nobiscum pacem habeant. Unde haec cum anno Duce ventilanies totis viribus instare, ut in destructione eorum finem operi imponatis. In necesse fuerit, ad eos ibimus.
units.tr: Furthermore, we wish that, if the Redarii (as we have heard) have suffered such a great slaughter (for you know how they broke faith and what injuries they inflicted) that they have no peace with us, you should, with the dukes of the year, press on with all your strength, so that you put an end to the work by their destruction. If it should be necessary, we will go against them ourselves.

units.la: * Sc. Saxoniae. * Gens Sclavica nunc sub ditione Electoris Brandeburgii, ut putatur.
units.tr: * That is, of Saxony. * A Slavic people now under the dominion of the Elector of Brandenburg, as is thought.

units.la: Filius noster in Nativitate Domini coronam à Domino Apostolico in Imperii dignitatem suscipiet. Scripta decimo quinto Kal. Febr. in Campania, juxta Capuam.
units.tr: Our son will receive the crown of the imperial dignity from the Apostolic Lord at the Nativity of the Lord. Written on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of February, in Campania, near Capua.

units.la: OTTONIS II. IMPER. AUG. CONSTITVTIO
units.tr: The Constitution of the Emperor Otto II Augustus

units.la: Super confirmatione juris municipalis Maydeburgensium, ac praerogati- va Scabinorum.
units.tr: On the confirmation of the municipal law of Magdeburg, and the prerogative of the Scabini.

units.la: NOs Otto Dei gratia Romanorum Rex Semper Augustus, significamus publicè per praesentes, quòd honesti & fideles civitatis nostrae Maydeburgensis incolae ad nos venientes, humiliter declararunt nobis, patrem nostrum vita functum, Caesarem OTTONEM Magnum, civitatem Maydeburgum jure municipali instituisse, ad utilitatem & emolumentum regionis Saxoniae, Imperii nomine illud jus manutenent, & injusticiam comprimant omnium civitatum & oppidum, quae à Maydeburgo initium & fundationis originem ducunt suam, utiq; omnibus jura permissis sententiam suam pronunciant: rogaruntq; nos, ut eaillis confirmaremus. Nos itaq; habentes ratione illorum fidei & prudentiae confirmamus Maydeburgensibus, & potissimum terrae Saxonicae libertates & privilegia, quibus sunt nominanter à patre nostro instituti: & praesertim consules illis, quòd debeant civitatis commodo consulere, & civitatis nostrae officia sub juramento suscipere: quod equidem juramentum seniores & prudentissimi quique ejusdem civitatis suscipere debeant cum auctoritate, perinde ac si nos praesentes adessemus.
units.tr: We, Otto, by the grace of God King of the Romans, ever Augustus, make known publicly by these present letters that the honest and faithful inhabitants of our city of Magdeburg, coming to us, humbly declared to us that our father, the Emperor Otto the Great, now deceased, had established the city of Magdeburg with municipal right, for the benefit and advantage of the region of Saxony; that they, in the name of the Empire, maintain that right and suppress injustice among all the cities and towns that take their beginning and origin from Magdeburg, and that they pronounce their judgment, granting the laws to all. They asked us to confirm these rights for them. We therefore, having regard to their loyalty and prudence, confirm to the Magdeburgers, and above all to the land of Saxony, the liberties and privileges by which they were expressly instituted by our father. And in particular we advise them that they ought to look to the good of the city, and undertake the offices of our city under oath; which oath the elders and the most prudent men of the same city ought to take with authority, just as if we were personally present.

units.la: 2. Adhaec concedimus ejusdem civitatis Scabinis eam facultatem, quòd possint & debeant suscipere ab Episcopo, siquidem ille sua regalia seu feudum à Romanorum Rege collatum habet.
units.tr: 2. Furthermore, we grant to the Scabini of the same city the power that they may and ought to receive (the investiture) from the Bishop, provided that he holds his regalia or fief conferred by the King of the Romans.

units.la: 3. Pot. 3. Portò Scabini nulla ratione à functione sua tejiciendi sunt, nisi eorum quispiam contra sua deliquerit, vel jus amittat suum. Verùm ad Sedem Scabinalem succedere debent jure feudali.
units.tr: 3. Pot. 3. Moreover, the Scabini are by no means to be removed from their office, unless one of them has offended against their duties or forfeits his right. But they ought to succeed to the Scabinal seat by feudal right.

units.la: 4. Quin eam quoque gratiam illis concedimus. Si contingat Scabinales sententias reprehendi, illos non posse propterea ad ulla alia loca protrahi, praeterquam ad Palatiam nostram, Principes nostros, qui ad eam citandi sunt. quòd si Principes non comparuerint, Imperio erunt noxii.
units.tr: 4. Indeed, we also grant them this favour: if it should happen that the Scabinal judgments are challenged, they may not for that reason be summoned to any other place except our Palatinate, to which our princes are to be cited. But if the princes do not appear, they shall be liable to the Empire.

units.la: 5. Praeterea hac praerogativa & auctoritate eos insignitos esse volumus, quòd propter latas sententias nihil prorsus damni perpeti cogantur; imò quicquid ipsi pro jure invenerint, huic nos & successores nostri assensum praestare, & id pro rato habere volumus.
units.tr: 5.
