Besides, we wish them to be distinguished by this prerogative and authority: that on account of judgments pronounced they are not compelled to suffer any loss whatever; indeed, whatever they have found in law, we and our successors wish to give our assent to it and to hold it as ratified.

units.la: 6. Quare mandamus omnibus Imperii subditis, sive sint spirituales, sive saeculares, ne supra moratae Civitatis juribus & libertatibus voluntate, verbis, operibus aut permissione aliqua inde modent. Omnes verò edictum hoc nostrum transgredientes, poena corporis & facultatum omnium erunt multandi, perinde ac si convicti forent.
units.tr: 6. Wherefore we command all subjects of the Empire, whether spiritual or secular, not to act in any way against the rights and liberties of the aforesaid city by will, word, deed or any permission. All who transgress this our edict shall be punished in body and in all their property, just as if they had been convicted.

units.la: 7. Et ad perpetuam hujus rei testimonium praesens hoc privilegium cum appensili Majestatis nostrae sigillo corroboravimus. Datum cum consilio Praefectorum Imperii, & prudentissimorum quorumvis, denique cum consensu etiam terrae, anno post Christi nativitatem DCCCLXXVIII, anno primo Imperii nostri, feria secunda ante Pentecosten, in Palantia Magdeburgensi.
units.tr: 7. And as a perpetual witness of this matter, we have confirmed this present privilege with the appended seal of our Majesty. Given with the counsel of the princes of the Empire and of the most prudent men of every kind, and finally with the consent also of the land, in the year after the birth of Christ 878 [sic], in the first year of our Empire, on the Monday before Pentecost, in the palace at Magdeburg.

units.la: OTTONIS II. IMPER. AUG. DECRETA COMITIORVM VERONENSIVM.
units.tr: Decrees of the Diet of Verona of Otto II, Emperor and Augustus.

units.la: IMPERATOR in Conventu Veronensi, quò Principes vocari praeceperat, calamitate a Saracenis exposita, Principes rogat & hortatur, in commune ut consulerent: ne Respublica domi afflicta majoribus incommodis afficeretur, aut magna ex parte interiret. Capira deliberarant, quo modo esset Italia defendenda; & quibus rationibus posset Germania esse salva. Unum Principum mens & sententia fuit, non deserendam Italiam: & Germaniam viro alicui meritis spectato, tanquam Imperatoris Vicario committendam.
units.tr: At the assembly at Verona, to which he had ordered the princes to be summoned, the Emperor, with the disaster caused by the Saracens laid before them, asked and urged the princes to deliberate together, so that the commonwealth, afflicted at home, would not suffer greater losses or perish for the most part. They deliberated at length on how Italy should be defended and by what means Germany could be kept safe. The mind and opinion of the princes was unanimous: Italy must not be abandoned, and Germany must be entrusted to a man of proven merit, as the Emperor's vicar.

units.la: 1. In hac verba cum consensissent Duces & Praesules; & essent operam, industriam, fidem ... pollicit: Imperator se in Italia mansurum dicit: ipsis suum commendat b filium, & Othoni Suevo, & Bernhardo Luneburgio, viris fortunatis & fortissimis.
units.tr: 1. When the dukes and prelates had agreed to these words, and had pledged effort, diligence, and loyalty ..., the Emperor says that he will remain in Italy. He commends to them his son, and Otto of Swabia and Bernhard of Lüneburg, men of good fortune and great courage.

units.la: 3. Matri Adelheidi Papiam habitandam concedit: eiq; custodes ac ministros praesidiaque gnat, & potestatem in Insubres tribuit.
units.tr: 3. He grants his mother Adelheid Pavia as her residence, gives her guards, attendants and garrisons, and grants her authority over the Insubrians.

units.la: 4. Henrico patrueli Bavariae Duci, ne quid novi suo more ageret, metum omnem demit, plane ignoscit: tum filio ejus c Henrico jus succedendi in avita ditione tradit.
units.tr: 4. He removes all fear from his cousin Henry, Duke of Bavaria, that he might do anything new in his accustomed manner, and fully pardons him. Then he hands over to Henry's son, also named Henry, the right of succession to the ancestral domain.

units.la: 5. Othonem Suevia Ducem, cum potestate Legati atq; Vicarii remittit in Germaniam.
units.tr: 5. He sends Otto, Duke of Swabia, back into Germany with the authority of legate and vicar.

units.la: 6. Deliberatis aliis rebus quàm plurimis, & constituto Reipublicae statu, cum valedixisset singulis & universis Imperator, patriam eis summa gravitate & contentione commendat: ipse Romam cum selecta manu militum proficisci statuit, ut retineret in officio Italiam; & hostibus religionis Saracenis terrori in propinquo esset.
units.tr: 6. After very many other matters had been settled and the state of the commonwealth arranged, the Emperor bade farewell to each and all, and commended the fatherland to them with the utmost seriousness and earnestness. He himself resolved to set out for Rome with a picked band of soldiers, so as to keep Italy in obedience and to be near at hand as a terror to the Saracens, enemies of the religion.

units.la: OTTONIS III. IMPER. AUG. CONSTITUTIO De otiosis Civibus.
units.tr: Constitution of the Emperor Otto III Augustus, concerning idle citizens.

units.la: SANCIMUS, ne otiosi in civitate locum habere permittantur. Dat. Florentiae ad mandatum Imperatoris.
units.tr: We decree that idle persons are not to be permitted to have a place in the city. Given at Florence, by command of the Emperor.

units.la: Hugo Marchio Brandenburgensis & Vicarius Imperii in Tuscia & Hetruria.
units.tr: Hugo, Margrave of Brandenburg and Vicar of the Empire in Tuscany and Etruria.

units.la: OTTONIS III. IMPER. AUG. CONSTITUTIO
units.tr: OTTO III, EMPEROR AUGUSTUS: CONSTITUTION

units.la: De Jure ac potestate Imperii, de donatione Constantini & Caroli Calvi, de assignatione bonorum, quibus Pontifices Romani ad sui sustentationem uti frui debeant.
units.tr: Concerning the right and power of the Empire, concerning the donation of Constantine and of Charles the Bald, and concerning the assignment of goods by which the Roman Pontiffs ought to be sustained and enjoy them.

units.la: IN nomine sanctae & individuae Trinitatis. OTTO servus Apostolorum, & secundum voluntatem Dei Salvatoris Romanorum Imperator Augustus. Romam caput mundi profitemur Romanam Ecclesiam matrem omnium Ecclesiarum esse testamur; sed incuria & inscientia Pontificum, longè suae claritatis titulos obfuscasse. Nam non solum, quae extra Urbem esse videbantur, averunt, & quibusdam colludiis à lare sancti Petri alienaverunt, sed (quod absque dolore non dicimus) si quid in hac nostra urbe Regia habuerunt, ut majori licentia evagerentur, omnibus indicatis peccatis. pecunia in commune dederunt, & sanctum Petrum & sanctum Paulum, ipsa quoq; altaria spoliaverunt, & pro reparatione semper confusionem duxerunt. Confusis vero Papaticis legibus, & jam abject Ecclesia Romana, in tantum quidam Pontificum irruerunt, ut maximam partem Imperii nostri Apostolatui suo cōjungerent, jam non quærentes quæ & quanta suis culpis perdiderunt, non curantes quanta ex voluntaria vanitate effuderunt; sed sua propria, utpote ab illis ipsis dilapidata, dimittentes, quali culpam suam in Imperium nostrum retorquentes ad aliena, id est, ad nostra & nostri Imperii, maxime migraverunt.
units.tr: In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity. Otto, servant of the Apostles, and by the will of God the Saviour, Augustus Emperor of the Romans. We profess that Rome is the head of the world, and we testify that the Roman Church is the mother of all churches; but by the negligence and ignorance of the Pontiffs, she has greatly obscured the titles of her brightness. For they not only alienated, and by certain collusions removed from the hearth of St Peter, whatever seemed to lie outside the City, but also (which we do not say without grief) whatever they held in this our royal city, that they might wander with greater licence, with all their sins laid bare, they gave away as common property; they despoiled the holy Peter and the holy Paul, and even the altars themselves, and they regarded restoration as always a confusion. Indeed, with the Papal laws thrown into confusion and the Roman Church now brought low, some of the Pontiffs rushed on so far that they joined the greater part of our Empire to their Apostolate, no longer asking what and how great things they had lost through their own faults, not heeding how much they had poured out through voluntary vanity; but, dismissing their own property, as though squandered by those very men, they shifted their guilt onto our Empire, as though turning it back, and migrated especially to what belongs to others, that is, to ours and to our Empire.

units.la: 1. Hæc sunt enim commenta ab illis ipsis inventa, quibus Johannes Diaconus cognomento Digitorum mutuis præceptū aureis literis scripsit, sub titulo Magni Constantini, longi mendacii tempora finxit. Hæc sunt etiam commenta, quibus dicunt quendam 4 Carolum sancto Petro nostra publica tribuisse. Sed ad hæc respondemus ipsum Carolū nihil dare jure potuisse, utpote jam à b Carolo fugatum, jam Imperio privatum, jam destitutum & annullatum. Ergo quod non habuit, dedit, licut nimirum dare potuit, utpote qui male acquisivit, & dici se posse furum non fecit.
units.tr: 1. For these are the fictions devised by those very men, by whom John the Deacon, surnamed Digitorum, wrote a golden-lettered precept under the title of Great Constantine, and invented long periods of falsehood. These are also the fictions by which they say that a certain Charles gave our public possessions to St Peter. But to these we reply that Charles himself could give nothing by right, since he had already been put to flight by Charles, already deprived of the Empire, already removed and annulled. Therefore what he did not have, he gave, just as indeed he could give, since he had acquired it wrongly and did not make himself one who could be called a thief.

units.la: 4. Spretis ergo commenticiis præceptis & imaginariis scriptis, ex nostra liberalitate sancto Petro donamus, quæ nostra sunt; non sibi, quæ sua sunt, veluti nostra conferimus. Sicut enim pro amore sancti Petri Dominum Silvestrum, magistrum nostrum, Papam elegimus, & Deo volente ipsum se-renissimum ordinavimus & creavimus, ita pro amore ipsius Domini Silvestri Papæ, sancto Petro de publico nostro dona conferimus, ut habeat magister, quod principi nostro Petro a parte sui discipuli essent. Octo igitur Comitatus pro amore Magistri Domini Silvestri Papæ, sancto Petro offerimus & donamus, ut ad honorem Dei & sancti Petri cum sua & nostra salute habeat & teneat, & ad incrementa sui Apostolatus nostrique Imperii ordinet. Hos autem sibi ad ordinandum concedimus, Pisaurium, Forum, Senogalliam, Anconam, Follabrum, Callium, Hesium, & Aufimum, ut nullus unquam ei & sancto Petro audeat aliquam inquietationem facere, aut eum aliquo ingenio fatigare. Quicumque vero præsumpserit, omnia, quæ habet, amittat: & sanctus Petrus, quæ sua sunt, recipiat.
units.tr: 4. Therefore, with spurious precepts and imaginary writings set aside, out of our generosity we give to St Peter what is ours; we do not confer on him what is his own, as though it were ours. For just as, for love of St Peter, we chose Lord Sylvester, our teacher, as Pope, and by God's will ordained and created him most serene, so, for love of this same Lord Sylvester, the Pope, we confer gifts from our public domain on St Peter, so that the teacher may have what our prince Peter would have from the part of his disciple. Therefore we offer and give eight counties to St Peter for love of our teacher Lord Sylvester, the Pope, so that he may have and hold them, to the honour of God and St Peter, with his own and our salvation, and may arrange them for the increase of his Apostolate and of our Empire. These we grant him to arrange for himself: Pesaro, Fano, Senigallia, Ancona, Fabriano, Cagli, Jesi and Osimo; so that no one ever dare to cause him or St Peter any disturbance, or to harass him by any device. Whoever presumes to do so shall lose all that he has, and St Peter shall recover what is his.

units.la: 4. Ut hoc autem in æternum ab omnibus conservetur, hoc præceptum manu nostra diu (Deo victura confirmavimus, & nostro sigillo præcepimus insigniri, ut sibi suisque successoribus valebit. Datum Romæ, &c.
units.tr: 4. So that this may be preserved for ever by all, we have confirmed this precept with our hand, to last for God's sake, and have commanded it to be marked with our seal, so that it may be valid for him and his successors. Given at Rome, etc.

units.la: Signum Domini Ottonis in victissimi Romanorum Imperatoris Aug.
units.tr: Sign of Lord Otto, most victorious Emperor of the Romans, Augustus.

units.la: In autographo Bulla est appensa plumbea, in cujus una parte sculptum, O D D O IMPERATOR ROMANORUM.
units.tr: On the autograph a leaden bulla is appended, on one side of which is carved: OTTO IMPERATOR ROMANORUM.

units.la: In altera caput est hominis cum pilis crispis cumq; spatulis & inscriptione, A U R E A R O M A.
units.tr: On the other is the head of a man with curled hair and shoulders, with the inscription: AUREA ROMA.

units.la: HENRICI II. IMP. AUG.
units.tr: HENRY II, AUGUSTUS EMPEROR

units.la: RESPONSUM AD CONSILIARIOS, SPADENTES, UT Herimanno Duci Alemanniæ æmulo suo, & Episcopo Constantiensi, qui Argentinam spoliarant, in Constantiæ direptione recompensaret.
units.tr: A RESPONSE TO HIS COUNCILLORS, THE EUNUCHS, CONCERNING HERIMANN, DUKE OF ALEMANNIA, HIS RIVAL, AND THE BISHOP OF CONSTANCE, WHO HAD PLUNDERED STRASBOURG: THAT THEY SHOULD MAKE RESTITUTION FOR WHAT WAS SEIZED WHEN CONSTANCE WAS SACKED.

units.la: Bsit, ut pro Herimanni insania in illum retorqueatur vindicta, à quo mihi Regni est concessa corona. Fortassis etsi pro Argentina Constantiam vastarem, non mihi damnum minuerem, sed duplicarem. Insuper male comparat Regnum, qui in ejus adeptione animæ postpositimentum. Coronavit me Deus non ad violationes Ecclesiarum, sed ad puniendos violatores
units.tr: Far be it from me that vengeance for Herimann's madness should be turned against him by whom the crown of the kingdom has been granted to me. Perhaps even if I were to lay waste Constance in return for Strasbourg, I would not lessen my loss but double it. Moreover, he makes a poor bargain for a kingdom who has set his soul's salvation second to gaining it. God crowned me not for the violation of churches, but for punishing those who violate them.

units.la: HENRICI II. IMPER. AUG. CONSTITUTIO
units.tr: HENRY II, EMPEROR AUGUSTUS, CONSTITUTION

units.la: De Regalibus beato Petro concessis.
units.tr: Concerning the regalia granted to blessed Peter.

units.la: In nomine Domini Dei omnipotentis, Patris, & Filii, & Spiritus sancti, Amen.
units.tr: In the name of the Lord God almighty, Father, and Son, and Holy Spirit. Amen.

units.la: Ego HENRICUS, Dei gratia Imperator Augustus, spondeo atque promitto per hoc pactum confirmationis nostræ, tibi beato Petro Principi Apostolorum & clavigero regni cælorum, & vicario tuo Donno Benedicto Summo Pontifici & universali Papæ, sicut à prædecessoribus vestris nunc in potestate vestra ac ditione tenuistis & dispositis civitatem Romanam cum Ducatu suburbanis, atque viculis omnibus, & territoriis ejus, montanis, ac maritimis a litoribusac portu- cunctis civitatibus, castellis, oppidis, ac viculis Tusciæ b partibus, id est Portū, Centumcellas, Tu-scia, Bleda, d Marurianū, Surriū, Nepem, Castellū, e Gallicéfe, Orthe, Polimartū, f Ameriā, g Perusiā, cum tribus insulis suis, id est, h Majorē & Minorē, Pulvésim & lacū, Narniā & Urticulū, integritate, eum curbibus, civitatibus, k oppidis, & castellis, quæ piæ recordationis l Dominus Carolus, & l Domin. Ludovicus, & Otto, & itidē Otto filius ejus, prædecessores vestris jamdudū per donationis m pagmam con- nostri beato Petro Apostolo, & prædecessoribus vestris jamdudum per donationis pagnam con-cessit.
units.tr: I, HENRY, by the grace of God Augustus Emperor, promise and pledge by this charter of our confirmation to you, blessed Peter, Prince of the Apostles and keeper of the keys of the kingdom of heaven, and to your vicar, Lord Benedict, Supreme Pontiff and universal Pope: that you shall hold and dispose, in your power and dominion, as your predecessors have held and disposed them, the city of Rome with its duchy, its suburbs, all its villages and territories, mountain and maritime, from the shores and the port; and all the cities, castles, towns and villages of the parts of Tuscany, namely Porto, Centumcellae, Tuscia, Bleda, Maturianum, Surrium, Nepi, Castellum, Gallicum, Orte, Polimartum, Amelia, Perugia, with its three islands, namely Maggiore and Minore, Polvese and the lake, Narni and Orticulum, entire, with their cities, towns and castles, which the pious memory of Lord Charles, and Lord Louis, and Otto, and likewise Otto his son, our predecessors, long ago granted by a deed of donation to blessed Peter the Apostle and to your predecessors.

units.la: a al. lateribus. b al. pertinā-tibus. c al. Caram. d al. Martu-riam. al. Ma-turanum. e al. Galisen-se. f al. Ameliam. g al. Tudertū. k al. Majore & Minore. i omnibus urbibus, k al. civit. pertinentibus, necnon & opp. l al. Donnus ubique, m gratiam. contulerunt, hoc est civitatem Ravennam, & Æmiliam, Bobium, Cesenam, Forum populi, Forum Livii, Faventiam, Imolam, Bononiam, Ferrariam, Comiaclum, Adrianis, atque Gabellum, cum omnibus finibus, territoriis atque insulis terra marique; ad supradictas civitates pertinentibus, Fanum, Senogalliam, Anconam, Ariminum, Pensaurum, Fanum, Senogalliam, Anconam, d Auximum, Humanam, e Esim, Forum Sempronii, montem Feltri, Urbinum, & territorium f Baluensem, g Callem, h Luciolis, & Eugubium, cum omnibus finibus & territoriis ad easdem civitates pertinentibus. Eodem modo territorium Sabinense, sicut a praedictis Imperatoribus antecessoribus beato Petro Apostolo per donationis scriptum concessum est sub integritate, & est in partibus Tuscis Longobardorum, castellum Felicitatis, Urbem Veterem, Balneum Regis, Ferenti castrum, rerbium, Ottochem, Martam, i Bledam, Tuscanam, Sinanam, Populonium, k Roseiles, cum finibus atque viculis, & omnibus territoriis, ac maritimis oppidis, seu finibus omnibus. Irenuq; l Alunis cum insula Corsica in Suriano, deinde in montem Bardonis, deinde in Berceto, exinde in Parma, inde in Regium, exinde in Mantua, atq; in monte Silicis, atq; Provincia Veneriarum, & Istria, necnon & cunctum Spoletanum Ducatum, seu Beneventanum, una cum Ecclesia sanctae Christi propè Papiam juxta Padum 1 v. milliario. Item in partibus Campaniae, m Sora, Arces, Aquinum, Arpinum, Theanum, Capuam, necnon & partimonium, ad n potestatem & ditionem vestram pertinentia, sicut est patrimonium Beneventanum & Neapolitanum, atque patrimonia Calabriae & Siciliae, si Deus adiuvat, Fundi, Terracinae.
units.tr: (Variant readings in the margin: "lateribus" for "litoribus"; "pertinacibus" for "pertinentibus"; "Caram" for "Centumcellas"; "Maturiam" and "Maturanum" for "Marurianum"; "Galisense" for "Gallicense"; "Ameliam" for "Amerianum"; "Tudertum" for "Perusia"; "Majore et Minore" for "Majorem et Minorem"; "omnibus urbibus" and "pertinentibus"; "Dominus" throughout; "gratiam" for "donationis".) They granted, namely the city of Ravenna and Emilia, Bobbio, Cesena, Forum Popili, Forum Livii, Faenza, Imola, Bologna, Ferrara, Comacchio, Adria, and Gabello, with all boundaries, territories and islands by land and sea pertaining to the aforesaid cities; Fano, Sinigaglia, Ancona, Rimini, Pesaro, Fano, Sinigaglia, Ancona, Osimo, Umana, Iesi, Forum Sempronii, Montefeltro, Urbino, the territory of Balva, Cagli, Luceoli, and Gubbio, with all boundaries and territories pertaining to the same cities. Likewise the territory of Sabina, as was granted to blessed Peter the Apostle by the aforesaid emperors, our predecessors, by a deed of donation, entire; and in the Tuscan parts of the Lombards: the castle of Felicitas, Orvieto, Bagno Regio, the castle of Ferento, Viterbo, Ottocchio, Marta, Bleda, Tuscania, Sinna, Populonia, Roselle, with their boundaries and villages, and all their territories and maritime towns, or all their boundaries. And from Aluni, with the island of Corsica, onward to Mount Bardone, then to Berceto, thence to Parma, thence to Reggio, thence to Mantua, and to Monte Selice, and the province of Venetia and Istria; and also the whole Duchy of Spoleto, or Benevento, together with the church of holy Christ near Pavia, one mile from the Po. Likewise in the parts of Campania: Sora, Arce, Aquino, Arpino, Teano, Capua; and the patrimony pertaining to your power and dominion, such as the patrimony of Benevento and Naples, and the patrimonies of Calabria and Sicily, God willing; Fondi, Terracina.

units.la: 2. Super hoc confirmamus vobis q Fuldense monasterium, & Abbaris ejus consecrationem, atque omnia monasteria, curtes & villas, quas in r Ultramontanis partibus sanctus Petrus habere cognoscitur, s absq; Aterna, Vumiteringa, sive Wilmbach, quae a sancti Petri Ecclesia per concessionis paginam Episcopo nostro Babembergensi collatae sunt: pro quibus sapedictae Ecclesiae ditiones transcribimus, concedimus & confirmamus omnem illam terram, t quae inter Narniam Tenementum, vel Spoletum ex regni nostri parte habuimus.
units.tr: 2. Upon this we confirm to you the monastery of Fulda and the consecration of its abbot, and all the monasteries, courts and villas which blessed Peter is known to have in the transalpine parts, except Aterna, Vumiteringa, or Wilmbach, which were conferred by a charter of grant from the church of St Peter upon our bishop of Bamberg. In return for these, we also transfer to the aforesaid church of St Peter, grant and confirm all that land which we have held on the side of our kingdom between Narni, Tenementum, or Spoleto.

units.la: 3. Sub tuitione praeterea sancti Petri, & vestra vestrorumque successorum praetaxarum Episcopum Babembergensem offerimus; unde sub pensionis nostrae debito equum unum album praeditum ex ejusdem loci Episcopo x vos annualiter suscepturos y sancimus.
units.tr: 3. Moreover, we offer the bishop of Bamberg aforesaid under the protection of St Peter and of you and your successors; and accordingly we decree that you shall receive annually from the bishop of that place one white horse with trappings, as a due of our tribute.

units.la: 4. Offerimus insuper, firmamus, & corroboramus tibi beato Petro ac Vicario tuo Domno Benedicto, & successoribus ejus, prout bonae memoriae Papae Joanni, suisque successoribus a praedictis Ottonibus factum est, civitates & oppida cum piscariis suis, Reatem, Amiternum, z Tiberiem, Narsiam, Balvam, & Marsiam, & alibi civitatem Teramnem cum pertinentiis suis.
units.tr: 4. We further offer, confirm and strengthen to you, blessed Peter, and to your vicar, Lord Benedict, and to his successors, just as was done by the aforesaid Ottos for Pope John of good memory and his successors: the cities and towns with their fisheries, Rieti, Amiternum, Tivoli, Narni, Balva, and Marsi, and elsewhere the city of Teramo with its appurtenances.

units.la: 5. Has omnes supradictas provincias, urbes, & civitates, oppida, atque castella, viculos, ac territoria, simulque patrimonia pro statu regni nostri, cunctosque Christianorum populo conservando, sanctae Ecclesiae tuae, beatae Petrae, Vicarioque tuo Benedicto ac successoribus ejus, usque, in finem saeculi modo confirmamus, ut in suo detineant jure, principatu, atque ditione. Simili nemo per hoc nostrae legationis pactum, confirmamus donationes, quas piae recordationis Pipinus Rex, & postea Dominus Carolus excellentissimus Imperator, ac deinceps Ottones piissimi beato Petro Christi Apostolo tanea voluntate coluerunt; necnon & censum, vel pensionem, seu ceteras donationes, quae a b Palatio Regis Longobardorum inferri solebant, sive de Tuscia, sive de Ducatu Spoletino, sicut in supradictis donationibus continetur, & inter sanctae memoriae Hadrianum Papam & Dominum Carolum Imperatorem convenit, quando idem Pontifex eidem c de supradictis Ducatibus est, Tuscano, & Spoletano, suaeque auctoritatis praeceptum confirmavit, eo scilicet modo, ut annis praedictus census ad partem Ecclesiae sancti Petri persolvatur, salva super eosdem Ducatus in omnibus dominatione, & illorum ad nostram partem subjectione. Ceterum, sicut diximus, suprascripta nomina ita ad vestram partem per hoc nostrae confirmationis pactum d corroboravimus, ut in vestro permaneant jure, principatu, atque ditione; & neq; a nobis, neq; a successoribus nostris, quodlibet argumentum sive machinationem, in quacumque parte vestra potestas immunitatur, e vobis inde aliquid subtrahatur.
units.tr: 5. All these aforesaid provinces, cities, towns, castles, villages and territories, and likewise the patrimonies, for the preservation of the state of our kingdom and of the Christian people, we now confirm to your holy Church, to blessed Peter, to your vicar Benedict and to his successors, to the end of the age, so that they may hold them in their right, principality and dominion. Likewise, by this charter of our grant, we confirm the donations which the pious memory of King Pepin, and afterwards Lord Charles, most excellent Emperor, and then the most pious Ottos, gave to blessed Peter, Apostle of Christ, with a ready will; and also the census or tribute and the other donations which used to be paid from the palace of the Lombard kings, whether from Tuscany or from the Duchy of Spoleto, as is contained in the aforesaid donations, and as was agreed between Pope Hadrian of holy memory and Lord Charles, Emperor, when the same Pontiff, by his authority, confirmed to him the mandate concerning the aforesaid duchies of Tuscany and Spoleto; namely in such a way that the said census is paid every year to the part of the Church of St Peter, saving in all things the lordship over those duchies and their subjection to our side. Moreover, as we have said, we have so confirmed the aforesaid names to your side by this charter of our confirmation, that they may remain in your right, principality and dominion; and neither by us nor by our successors shall any pretext or contrivance be brought, in any part where your power extends, by which anything may be withdrawn from you.

units.la: 6. De supradictis vero provinciis, urbibus, civitatibus, oppidis, castris, viculis, territoriis, acpatrimoniis, necnon & pensionibus, atque censibus, sed potius omnia, quae superius leguntur, id est provincias, civitates, urbes, castella, oppida, terras, patrimonia, atque insulas, censusque, & pensiones, ad partem Ecclesiae beati Petri Apostoli, atq; Pontificum in sacratissima Sede illius resedetium, nos nil quantum possumus defensores esse f teneamur, ad hoc ut eam illi ditionem ad utenduam atq; disponendum firmiter valeant obtinere, salva in omnibus potestate nostra posterorum, atq; nostrorum, secundum quod in pacto & constitutione ac promissionis firmitate Eugenii Pontificis successorum; illius continetur, ut omnis Clerus & universi populi Romani nobilitas propter diversas necessitates, & Pontificum irrationabiles erga populum sibi subjectum asperitates retundendas sacramento se obligaret, quarenus futura Pontificum electio, quantum uniuscujusque intellectus fuerit, canonice & juste, ut ille, qui ad hoc g sanctum regimen eligetur, nemine h contradicente consecratus fiat Pontifex, priusquam talem in praesentia Missorum nostrorum vel universae i generalitatis faciat promissionem pro omnium satisfactione, ac fiducia conservatione, qualem Dominus & venerandus spiritualis Pater noster Leo sponte fecisse dignoscitur.
units.tr: 6. Concerning the aforesaid provinces, cities, towns, castles, villages, territories and patrimonies, and likewise the tributes and censuses; but rather all those things which are read above, that is, the provinces, cities, towns, castles, towns, lands, patrimonies and islands, and the censuses and tributes, we are bound to be defenders, as far as we can, for the part of the Church of blessed Peter, the Apostle, and of the Pontiffs who sit in his most holy See; so that they may be able to hold that dominion firmly for their use and disposal, saving in all things the power of us and of our descendants, according to what is contained in the pact, constitution and firm promise of Pope Eugenius, his successor: namely, that all the clergy and the whole nobility of the Roman people should bind themselves by oath, to restrain on account of various necessities and the unreasonable harshness of the Pontiffs toward the people subject to them; so that the future election of the Pontiffs, as far as each one's understanding allows, shall be canonical and just, and that he who is chosen for this holy rule, with no one opposing, shall be consecrated Pontiff; before he makes such a promise in the presence of our envoys, or of the whole assembly, for the satisfaction of all and the security of their preservation, as our Lord and venerable spiritual Father Leo is known to have made of his own accord.

units.la: 7. Præterea alia minora huic operi inserendů prævidimus, videlicet ut in electione Pōtificum neq; libet neq; servus ad hoc venire præsumat, ut illis Romanis, quos ad hanc electionem per b constitutionem sanctorum Patrum c antiqua admisit consuetudo, aliquod faciat impedimentum. Quod si quis contra hanc nostram constitutionem d venire præsumpserit, exilio tradatur.
units.tr: 7. Furthermore, we have foreseen that other lesser matters be inserted into this work: namely, that in the election of Pontiffs no free man or slave shall presume to come forward, so as to create any impediment for those Romans whom ancient custom has admitted to this election by the constitution of the holy Fathers. If anyone presumes to act against this our constitution, let him be handed over to exile.

units.la: 8. Insuper etiam, ut nullus Missorum nostrorum cujuscumq; impeditionis argumentum componere audeat e in præfatam electionem, prohibemus.
units.tr: 8. Furthermore, we forbid anyone among our Missi to dare to devise any pretext for hindering the aforesaid election.

units.la: 9. Nam & hoc omnimodò instituere placuit, ut qui semel sub f spirituali defensione Donni Apostolici sive nostra fuerint suscepti, impetrata juste utantur defensione. Quod si quis in quemquam illorum, qui hoc promeruerunt, violare præsumpserit, sciat se periculum vitæ suæ esse g incursum.
units.tr: 9. For we have also resolved, by all means, that those who have once been received under the spiritual protection of the Apostolic Lord or under our own shall enjoy the protection they have justly obtained. If anyone presumes to violate it against any of those who have earned this, let him know that he has incurred danger to his life.

units.la: 10. Illud etiam confirmamus, ut h Donno Apostolico justam in omnibus servent obedientiam, seu Ducibus & Judicibus suis, ad faciendam justitiam.
units.tr: 10. We further confirm that they shall keep due obedience in all things to the Apostolic Lord, and likewise to their Dukes and Judges, in administering justice.

units.la: 11. Huic enim institutioni hoc necessario annectendum esse perspeximus, ut Missi Donni Apostolici seu nostri semper sint constituti, qui annuatim nobis renuntiare valeant, qualiter singuli Duces ac Judices populo justitiam faciant.
units.tr: 11. For we have seen that this arrangement must necessarily be joined with this provision: that Missi of the Apostolic Lord or of ourselves shall always be appointed, who may be able to report to us each year how the individual Dukes and Judges administer justice to the people.

units.la: 12. Hanc Imperialem constitutionem quomodo observent, qui Missi, decernimus ut primùm cunctos clamores, qui per negligentiam Ducum vel Judicum fuerint inventi, ad noticiam Donni Apostolici deferant, & ipse unum e duobus eligat, aut statim per eosdem i Missos fiant necessitates emendatæ, aut Misso nostro nobis renuntiante per nostros Nuntios à nobis directos emendentur.
units.tr: 12. As to how those who are Missi shall observe this imperial constitution, we decree that they first bring to the notice of the Apostolic Lord all complaints that are found to arise through the negligence of Dukes or Judges, and that he choose one of two courses: either the needs are remedied at once through the same Missi, or they are remedied by our Nuncios sent by us, when our Missus reports to us.

units.la: 13. Hoc ut ab omnibus fidelibus sanctæ Dei Ecclesiæ & vestris firmum esse credatur, propriæ manus signaculo, & nobilium Optimatum nostrorum subscriptionibus hoc pactum confirmationis nostræ roboravimus, & sigilli nostri impressione assignari jussimus. Signum Domini Henrici gloriosissimi k Romanorum Imperatoris Augusti. Signum I Erchandildi Magunxini Archiepiscopi. Signum Heriberti Colonien sis Archiepiscopi. Signum Bobonis Trevirensis Archiepiscopi. Signum Thiederici Metensis Episcopi. Ego Ebcrhardus Bambergensis m Ecclesiæ Episcopus n Romanæ Sedis subditus o subscripsi. Ego p Mazelinus Wirzeburgensis Episcopus subscripsi. Ego Waltetius Spirensis Episcopus subscripsi. Ego q Ruodardus Constantiensis Episcopus subscripsi. Ego r Rodalricus Curiensis Episcopus subscripsi. Ego Adalbertus Basiliensis Episcopus subscripsi. Ego Hemmo s Werdunensis Episcopus subscripsi. Ego Walter Heichstedensis Episcopus subscripsi. Signum t Richardi Fuldensis Abbatis. Signum Arnoldi u Herfendensis Abbatis. Signum Brucardi Abbatis. Signum Gottifridi Ducis. Signum Beringardi Ducis. Signum Thiederici Ducis. Signum Simonis Comitis. Signum x V Velphonis Comitis. Signum Cunonis Comitis. Signum Kunradi Comitis. Signum Ottonis Comitis. Signum y Bobonis Comitis. Signum Frederici Comitis. Signum Bezelini Comitis. Signum Ezonis Comitis Palatini. Signum Frederici Camerarii. Signum z Ezonis Infertotis. Signum a Heuzonis Pincernarii. Signum b Huzis. c Alimunbeteger. Adilmau. Adilbero. Ego V Vizelius d Astrazburgensis Episcopus. Signum Ryodhois Fluvanensis Abbatis.
units.tr: 13. So that this may be believed firm by all the faithful of the holy Church of God and by yours, we have strengthened this compact of our confirmation with the signature of our own hand and the subscriptions of our noble Optimates, and we have ordered it to be assigned with the impression of our seal. The sign of the Lord Henry, most glorious Augustus, Emperor of the Romans. The sign of I Erchandild, Archbishop of Mainz. The sign of Heribert, Archbishop of Cologne. The sign of Bobo, Archbishop of Trier. The sign of Thiederich, Bishop of Metz. I, Eberhard, Bishop of the Church of Bamberg, subject to the Roman See, have subscribed. I, Mazelin, Bishop of Würzburg, have subscribed. I, Walter, Bishop of Speyer, have subscribed. I, Ruodhard, Bishop of Constance, have subscribed. I, Rodalric, Bishop of Chur, have subscribed. I, Adalbert, Bishop of Basel, have subscribed. I, Hemmo, Bishop of Verdun, have subscribed. I, Walter, Bishop of Eichstätt, have subscribed. The sign of Richard, Abbot of Fulda. The sign of Arnold, Abbot of Herveld. The sign of Brucard, Abbot. The sign of Gottfried, Duke. The sign of Berengar, Duke. The sign of Thiederich, Duke. The sign of Simon, Count. The sign of Welf, Count. The sign of Cuno, Count. The sign of Conrad, Count. The sign of Otto, Count. The sign of Bobo, Count. The sign of Frederick, Count. The sign of Bezelin, Count. The sign of Ezo, Count Palatine. The sign of Frederick, Chamberlain. The sign of Ezo of Infertot. The sign of Heuzo, Cupbearer. The sign of Huzi. Alimunbeteger. Adilmau. Adilbero. I, V Vizelius, Bishop of Strasbourg. The sign of Ryodhoi, Abbot of Fulda.

units.la: HENRICI. II. IMPER. AUG.
units.tr: HENRY II, EMPEROR AUGUSTUS

units.la: DECRETA COMITIORVM ALSTETENSIVM.
units.tr: DECREES OF THE DIET OF ALSTEDT

units.la: IMPERATOR Conventum indicit Alstetam: ibique; & cum Principibus aliis, & in primis cum Saxoniae Ducibus deliberat, de Italia vendicanda, cum victi ante annos decem Saraceni, novos ibi motus excitassent.
units.tr: The Emperor summoned a diet to Alstedt, and there, together with the other princes, and above all with the dukes of Saxony, deliberated on reclaiming Italy, since the Saracens, who had been defeated ten years earlier, had again stirred up new disturbances there.

units.la: 2. In illis Comitiis, cum alia multa cum Saxonibus est honorificè locutus, tum illud dixit praecipuè, se post sceptrum Imperii, nihil habere in terris gente Saxonica carius.
units.tr: 2. At that diet, while he spoke very honourably of many things with the Saxons, he said this especially: that after the sceptre of the Empire he had nothing in the lands dearer than the Saxon people.

units.la: 3. Facta deinceps mentio est collocutionis, quae ante biennium super Carum fluvium habita fuerat, inter Imperatorem & Robertum Galliae Regem: in quae constituenda & conservanda pace in Italia fuerat actum. ejus foederis Regem rursus esse admonendum Principibus placuit.
units.tr: 3. Next, mention was made of the conference that had been held two years earlier beside the river Chaer between the Emperor and Robert, King of France, in which it had been agreed to establish and maintain peace in Italy. The princes resolved that the King should again be reminded of that agreement.

units.la: 4. In Saracenos arma decreta, qui urbem Trojam denuò tentaverant.
units.tr: 4. Arms were decreed against the Saracens, who had once more attempted the city of Troia.

units.la: CHUNRADI. II. IMP. AUG.
units.tr: CHUNRADI. II. IMP. AUG.

units.la: RESPONSUM
units.tr: RESPONSUM

units.la: Quod Imperator justitiam petentes audire & judicare rebus relictis omnibus debeat.
units.tr: That the Emperor ought to hear those who seek justice and to judge, setting aside all other business.

units.la: IN processione Regis ad coronationem, tres venerunt ante illum, cum singulis querimoniis, unus erat colonus Ecclesiae Moguntinensis; alter pupillus fuit; & quaedam vidua. Dum Rex eorum causas audire coepisset, quidam de Principibus suis avertebant eum, dicentes, ne consecrationis suae aliquam moram faceret, & mature divina officia audiret; respiciens ad Episcopos, ut Vicarius Christi, Christianissimè respondebat; Si meum est regimini insistere, & id viri constantis est, nequaquam differre, quod aptè fieri valet, rectius videtur mihi facere quod debeo, quàm quid faciendum sit ab alio. Memini vos saepe dixisse, non auditores legis, sed factores justificari. Si autem ad consecrationem, ut dicitis, festinandum est, tanto cautius in opere Dei gressus meos convenit mihi firmare, quatò me arduae dignitati cognosco propinquare. Haec dicens, in eadem statione moratus, ubi primum occurrerant illi calamitosi, passibus immotis legem praefecerat illis.
units.tr: In the procession of the King to his coronation, three persons came before him, each with a complaint: one was a tenant farmer of the Church of Mainz, another was an orphan, and a certain widow. While the King had begun to hear their causes, some of his princes tried to turn him away, saying that he should not delay his consecration, but should hear the divine offices promptly. Turning to the bishops, as the Vicar of Christ, he answered most Christianly: "If it is my duty to attend to government, and it belongs to a steadfast man not to postpone what can properly be done, it seems to me more right to do what I owe than to do what someone else tells me must be done. I remember that you have often said that not the hearers of the law but its doers are justified. But if we must hasten to the consecration, as you say, then all the more carefully ought I to firm up my steps in the work of God, since I recognise that I am drawing near to a high dignity." Saying this, he remained in the same place where the unfortunate people had first met him, and with unmoved steps he gave them a hearing.

units.la: 2. Hinc paululum procedens, venit ante illum quidam, dicens, se expulsum esse patria omni sine culpa, quem Rex per brachium apprehendens, super omnes circumstantes attraxit usque ad solium suum, ibique causam miseri, cuidam Principum suorum diligenter commendavit. Moguntiae in die Coronationis.
units.tr: 2. Proceeding a little further from there, a certain man came before him, saying that he had been driven from his homeland though he was without any fault. The King, taking him by the arm, drew him up past all those standing around to his throne, and there carefully commended the wretched man's cause to one of his princes. At Mainz, on the day of the coronation.

units.la: CHUNRADI. II. IMPER. AUG.
units.tr: CONRAD II, EMPEROR AUGUSTUS

units.la: DECRETUM
units.tr: DECREE

units.la: In Papienses rebellionis reos, quòd Palatium Imperiale destruxerunt.
units.tr: Concerning the Pavians, guilty of rebellion, because they destroyed the Imperial palace.

units.la: ERAT in civitate Papiensi palatium à Theodorico Rege quondam miro opere conditum, ac postea ab Imperatore Ottone III. nimis adornatum. Cognito obitu Imperatoris Heinrici, antecessoris Chuonradi Regis, statim Papienses inconsultò ad imbellem aulam ruentes Regia moenia fregerunt, totumque palatium usque ad imum fundamenti lapidem erucabant, ne quisquam Regum ulterius infra civitatem illam palatium ponere decrevisset. Ex qua audacia diu magna controversia inter Regem & Papienses habita est. Dicebant Papienses; Quem offendimus? Imperatori nostro fidem & honorem usque ad terminum vitae suae servavimus, quo defuncto, cum nullum Regem haberemus, Regis nostri domum destruxisse nō jure accusabimur. E contrario Rex; Scio, inquit, quod domum Regis vestri non destruxistis, cum eo tempore nullum haberetis: sed domum Regalem sedisse non valetis inficiari. Si Rex periit, Regnum remansit: sicut navis remanet, cujus gubernator cadit. Aedes publicae fuerant, non privatae; juris erant alieni, non vestri. Alienarum autem rerum invasores Regi sunt obnoxii. Ergo vos alienae rei invasores fuistis. Igitur Regi obnoxii estis. Actum in Constantia civitate Alemanniae post diem sanctum Pentecostes.
units.tr: There was in the city of Pavia a palace once built with wonderful workmanship by King Theodoric, and afterwards greatly adorned by the Emperor Otto III. When the death of the Emperor Henry, predecessor of King Conrad, became known, the Pavians at once, without consultation, rushed upon the defenceless court, broke down the royal walls, and tore down the whole palace down to its lowest foundation stone, so that none of the kings should decide to build a palace again within that city. From this audacity a long controversy arose between the King and the Pavians. The Pavians said: "Whom have we offended? We kept faith and honour toward our Emperor until the end of his life; when he died, since we had no king, we shall not be rightly accused of destroying the house of our king." On the other side the King said: "I know that you did not destroy the house of your king, since at that time you had none; but you cannot deny that you occupied the royal house. If the king has perished, the kingdom remains, just as a ship remains when its helmsman falls. The buildings were public, not private; they belonged to another, not to you. Now those who invade the property of others are liable to the King. Therefore you were invaders of another's property, and so you are liable to the King." Given at the city of Constance in Alemannia, after the holy day of Pentecost.

units.la: CONRADI. II. SALICI IMP. AUG.
units.tr: CONRAD II, THE SALIAN, EMPEROR AUGUSTUS

units.la: RESCRIPTVM
units.tr: Rescript

units.la: Quòd virtute hostes, & non fraude sint superandi.
units.tr: That enemies are to be overcome by valour, not by fraud.

units.la: MILZKO Polonus, pulso fratre Ottone, Regem se appellat: & Ulricus quoq; Bojemus, occiso fratre suo Jacomaro, nova molitur. Hi ambo jugum Imperii nostri rigida cervice excutere, & sui juris esse conantur. Otto à fratre Polonia pulsus ad Conradum fugit, ab eo; armis restituitur. Milzko externae opis egens in Bojemiam ad Ulricum Regulum aufugit. quem cum Ulricus Conrado Augusto prodere, ab eo; gratiam inire vellet, Imperator rescripsit, solere Germanos virtute cum hostibus, non fraude certare, nihilq; acrius, quàm perfidiam ulcisci, scelerebus non nomini hostium nasci: oportere armatum esse, quem oderint.
units.tr: Milzko the Pole, having driven out his brother Otto, styles himself king, and Ulric the Bohemian, after killing his brother Jaromir, is also plotting new things. Both are trying to throw off with stiff necks the yoke of our Empire and to be free of its authority. Otto, driven out of Poland by his brother, fled to Conrad, and by him was restored with arms. Milzko, lacking foreign help, fled into Bohemia to the petty king Ulric. When Ulric wished to betray him to Emperor Conrad and so win favour from him, the Emperor replied in writing that it is the custom of the Germans to contend with enemies by valour, not by fraud; that nothing is more keenly to be punished than treachery; and that crimes do not arise from the name of enemies. A man whom they hate must be met in arms.

units.la: SENATUS CONSULTUM RO- MANUM DE LEGE REGIA, QVÀ A PAPA SENATV POPVLO Romano jus omne & potestas HENRICO III. Imperatori & in eum collata est: item de electione Romani Pontificis, & investituris Episcoporum, &c.
units.tr: THE SENATUS CONSULTUM OF ROME CONCERNING THE ROYAL LAW, BY WHICH ALL RIGHT AND POWER WERE CONFERRED UPON HENRY III, EMPEROR, AND TRANSFERRED TO HIM BY THE POPE, THE SENATE AND THE PEOPLE OF ROME: likewise concerning the election of the Roman Pontiff, the investiture of bishops, etc.

units.la: NEgari non potest, quòd pater Domini Regis Henrici pizæ memoriæ HENRICUS Imperator, factus est Patricius Romanorum, à quibus accepit in electione super ordinando Pontifice principatum. Hucaccedit, quòd Nicolaus Papa hoc Domino Regi HENRICO privilegium, quod ex paterno jam jure fuisceperat, præbuit, & perb Synodalis insuper Decreti paginam confirmavit.
units.tr: It cannot be denied that the father of our lord King Henry, of blessed memory, the Emperor Henry, was made Patrician of the Romans, and from them he received the principate in the election of the Pope who was to be ordained. Moreover, Pope Nicholas granted this privilege to our lord King Henry, which he had already received by paternal right, and he further confirmed it by the page of a synodal decree.

units.la: fix Defensorem, cujus auctor habetur Petrus Damiani Cardinal Rom. a Ejus nominis Quarto. b c.1.dist.23.
units.tr: ...Defender, whose author is held to be Peter Damian, Cardinal of Rome. a Of that name the Fourth. b c.1 dist.23.

units.la: HENRICI III. IMPER. AUG. CONSTITUTIO
units.tr: Constitution of the Emperor Henry III Augustus

units.la: De justitia Babenbergensium ministerialium.
units.tr: On the justice of the Babenberg ministerials.

units.la: SI quem ex his Dominus suus accusaverit, de quacunq; re, licet illi juramento se cum suis coæqualibus absolvere, exceptis tribus; hoc est, si in vitam Domini sui, aut in Cameram ejus consilium habuisse arguitur, aut in munitiones ejus. Cæteris verò hominibus de quacunq; objectione, absque Advocato cum suis coæqualibus juramento se poterit absolvere. Et cæteris hominibus non plus debent, quàm septem personas; suis verò sociis duodecim.
units.tr: If their lord should accuse one of them of any matter whatever, the accused may clear himself by oath together with his equals, with three exceptions: that is, if he is charged with having plotted against his lord's life, or against his chamber and council, or against his fortifications. In respect of other men, on any objection whatever, a man may clear himself by oath with his equals without an advocate. And for other men they need not give more than seven persons, but for their fellow ministerials twelve.

units.la: 2. Si occisus fuerit, recompensatio ejus, decem libræ sunt, quæ ad alios non pertinent, nisi ad cognatos occisi.
units.tr: 2. If someone is killed, his compensation is ten pounds, which do not go to anyone except the relatives of the dead man.

units.la: 3. Si beneficium ab Episcopo non habuerit, & repræsentaverit se in ejus ministerio, & beneficium non potuerit obtinere, cui vult, militet, non beneficiarius, sed liberè.
units.tr: 3. If he has not received a benefice from the bishop, but has presented himself for his ministry and has been unable to obtain a benefice, he may serve whom he wishes, not as a beneficiary but as a free man.

units.la: 4. Si absq; liberis obierit, & uxorem prægnantem habuerit, expectetur dum pariat. Et, si masculus fuerit, ille habeat beneficium patris. Si non; proximus agnatus defuncti loricam suam, vel equum, quem meliorem habuerit, Domino suo offerat, & beneficium cognati sui accipiat.
units.tr: 4. If he dies without children and leaves a pregnant wife, let it be awaited until she gives birth. And if it is a male, he shall have his father's benefice. If not, the nearest agnate of the deceased shall offer to his lord his coat of mail, or the horse which he had as the better one, and shall receive his kinsman's benefice.

units.la: 5. In expeditionem iturus ex suo sumptu ad Dominum veniat: deinceps ex ejus impensa alatur. Si expeditio in Italia est, Dominus per singulas loricas unum equum det, & tres libras. Si verò alio, duo ex illis tertio dent impensas.
units.tr: 5. One who is about to set out on an expedition shall come to his lord at his own expense; thereafter he shall be maintained at his lord's cost. If the expedition is in Italy, the lord shall give one horse and three pounds for each coat of mail. If it is elsewhere, two of them shall give the expenses to the third.

units.la: 6. Beneficium habentes à Domino suo non constringantur, nisi ad quinq; ministeria, hoc est, utaut dapiferi sint, aut pincernæ, aut cubicularii, aut marschalci, aut venatores.
units.tr: 6. Those holding a benefice from their lord shall not be bound to any service except five offices, namely, whether they are stewards, cupbearers, chamberlains, marshals, or huntsmen.

units.la: HENRICI IV. IMPER. AUG. RESCRIPTA
units.tr: HENRY IV, EMPEROR AUGUSTUS: RESCRIPTS

units.la: I. Pro dimissione & recompensatione haranscare.
units.tr: I. On the release and compensation for the harascara.

units.la: HEINRICUS Dei gratia Rex, Alberto sanctæ Babebergensis Ecclesiæ venerando Pontifici, suo scilicet dilecto a nepoti, gratiam suam & debitum dilectionis donum. Si omnia vestra prospe-ritatis tenore dirigantur, ut justum est, congaudemus: & si quid adversi vobis occurrerit, quod repellat obumbratio, ut decens est, condolemus: & hanc eandem charitatis vicem vos erga nos servaturum, non dubitamus. Quapropter dilectionis vestræ rogamus privilegium; quia quidam militum N... nomine, misericordiam nostram & auxilium petens venit, ut sibi illam harahscaram conventionio, quam vobis jurejurando promisit, nostri amoris & rogatus causa dimittatis; ut ego ex parte mea vobis compensem, b patremq; meum, ut & ipse vobis compenset, instigem.
units.tr: Henry, by the grace of God king, to Albert, the reverend bishop of the holy church of Bamberg, our dear nephew, greeting, his favour and the due gift of affection. If all your affairs proceed with the success they deserve, we rejoice with you; and if any adversity befalls you, which may cast a shadow over you, we sympathise, as is fitting. We do not doubt that you will return the same kindness towards us. Therefore we ask you, out of your affection, to grant us a favour. A certain soldier, N..., has come to us seeking our mercy and help, asking that, for the sake of our love and at our request, you release him from the agreement (the harascara) which he promised you under oath. In return I will, on my part, make you amends, and I will urge my father^b to make you amends as well.

units.la: b Henricus III. Imp.
units.tr: b Henry III, Emperor.

units.la: II. De Comitiis Moguntinis pro dissensionibus Imperii componendis.
units.tr: II. On the Diet of Mainz, to settle the dissensions of the Empire.

units.la: HEINRICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator Augustus, Ruperto Babebergensis Ecclesiæ Episcopo gratiam & omne bonum. Notum est tibi, quanto periculo tota fluctuat Ecclesia; quatuserror in omni surgit Saxonia; quantaq; desolatione nobilis illa Metelis penitus destruitur Ecclesia. Et non solùm ibi, sed & in diversis partibus Ecclesia nostri dividitur Imperii. Igitur consilio nostrorum fidelium statuimus fieri Moguntiæ colloquium in Dominico die ante proximum S. Andreæ festum. Huc Colloquio omnes Regni Principes nostri fideles interfuunt; & præterea omnes, quorum nobis declaratur aut fides, aut consilii providentia. Ad quod venire te quàm intimè rogamus, quia nullus tam ardua negotia Regni & divisio Ecclesiæ, coadunari poterit sine tua maxima sapientia, & egregio consilio & fide, quæ hactenus nobis frequenter in necessitatibus, & in hujusmodi controversiis Regni, prout nos voluimus, & res exaggerat, præstò fuit. Ad quod Colloquium omnes Saxones nostri fideles venient, rogantes summopere, nos in Saxoniam venire, & hos novos errores componere. Mere. Metensès autem è contrario Metim clamant nos transfire, quatinus illic tandem pax & securitas reddatur Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: Henry, by the grace of God Roman Emperor Augustus, to Rupert, bishop of the church of Bamberg, grace and every good. You know well how greatly the whole Church is tossed by danger; how error arises in every part of Saxony, and how that noble church of Metz is utterly destroyed by desolation. And not only there, but in various parts of the Empire the Church is divided. Therefore, by the counsel of our faithful subjects, we have resolved that a conference be held at Mainz on the Sunday before the next feast of St Andrew. All the princes of our realm, our faithful subjects, will attend this conference, and besides them all those whose faith or prudence in counsel has been declared to us. We earnestly ask you to come to it, because no such weighty matters of the realm and the division of the Church can be settled without your great wisdom, your excellent counsel and your loyalty, which have hitherto been at hand for us, as we wished, in our necessities and in controversies of this kind in the realm. All our faithful Saxons will come to this conference, urgently asking that we come into Saxony and settle these new errors. The men of Metz, on the other hand, call out that we should cross over to Metz, so that peace and security may at last be restored to the Church there.

units.la: 2. Nos quoq;, invitante Archiepiscopo, Coloniæ nativitatem Domini celebraturi, summopere desiderauimus hoc Colloquium ante fieri, ut hujusmodi dissensiones Regni prius componentur, quàm nos in remotiora transfiremus loca. Sed idcirco prædictam expeditionem distulimus, quæ communi omnium nostrorum consilio, quæ nobis agenda sint, considerentur.
units.tr: 2. We too, invited by the archbishop, intend to celebrate the Lord's Nativity at Cologne, and we have very much wished that this conference be held beforehand, so that such dissensions of the realm may first be settled before we go to more distant places. But for this reason we have postponed the aforementioned expedition, so that by the common counsel of all our people it may be considered what must be done.

units.la: 3. Ergo rogamus te peream, qua compater nobis effectus es, dilectionem, ne te corporis tui, vel quàlibet alia res impediat, quin ad prætatū Colloquium tempore statuto venias, & illam magnam sapientiam, & solitam fidem tuam, de nostra & Regni utilitate, quæ necessaria sunt, cum disponas.
units.tr: 3. Therefore we ask you, by that love through which you have become our kinsman, that neither the infirmity of your body nor any other matter prevent you from coming to the aforementioned conference at the appointed time, and that you arrange, with that great wisdom and your accustomed loyalty, the things that are necessary for our good and the good of the realm.

units.la: III. De fide Imperio servanda; & de controversia feudi decreto per Imperatorem facto.
units.tr: III. On keeping faith with the Empire; and on the dispute over a fief, decided by the Emperor.

units.la: HEINRICVS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator Augustus, Hartuuico Magdeburgensi Archiepiscopo, gratiam & omne bonum. 1. Laborem tuum & studium circa honorē nostrum maximū esse audivimus: ideoq; dignas tibi gratias, prout justū est, referimus, nunc quidē pauca, multas autē factis, cùm Deo annuente ad te venerimus. Tu tantū, sicut cœpisti, in tantū pro obtinendo nobis Regni honore in his partibus tis solicitus. Nos enim, qui specialē tibi præ cæteris fidē habemus proximē, quando à te discessimus, omnia nostra tuæ fidei commisimus. Quod quia fideliter er gratia hactenus obiervasti, & adhuc te cōservaturū veraciter credimus. Facigitur ut bonus ac discretus dem, quam in te firmam esse credimus, utq; ad finē perducim omnibus. Nos vero in loco nostro te habeimus: & quodcumq; habet perfecta fides, de te nobis fieri cōfidimus. In hujus itaq; fidei monium, iterū tibi nos & omnia nostra committimus, ut ita agas in omnibus, sicut bene tibi conciliat.
units.tr: Henry, by the grace of God Roman Emperor Augustus, to Hartwig, archbishop of Magdeburg, grace and every good. 1. We have heard that your labour and zeal on behalf of our honour are very great. Therefore we return to you the thanks you deserve, as is just: a few now, but many in deeds when, God willing, we come to you. Continue only as you have begun, being so solicitous in these parts to obtain for us the honour of the realm. For we, who place special trust in you before others, when we last left you, committed all our affairs to your faith. Since you have kept this faithfully and with grace up to now, we truly believe that you will keep it still. Act therefore as a good and discreet man, as we believe you to be, and bring to completion what we have entrusted to you. We hold you in our place, and we trust that whatever perfect faith can do will be done by you for us. In witness of this faith, we again commit ourselves and all our affairs to you, so that you may act in all things as is well suited to you.

units.la: 2. Beneficium autē N. Præpositi, fidelis nostri, quod & antea tibi commisimus, iterum tibi mittimus, ut ad utilitatem ejus illud conserves, & illi, qui injustè tenet, ex nostra parte interdicat dominus ejus, qui modo beneficium tibi illicitē usurpavit, nobis, dū querimonia inde esset, te...
units.tr: 2. The benefice of N., provost, our faithful man, which we previously entrusted to you as well, we send to you again, so that you may preserve it for his advantage; and let his lord, who lately usurped the benefice from you unlawfully, be forbidden on our part to hold it wrongfully against him, while there is complaint about it ...

units.la: IV. De hostibus & bannitis Imperii persequendis.
units.tr: IV. On pursuing the enemies and outlaws of the Empire.

units.la: HEINRICVS Dei gratia Imperator Augustus, A. glorioso * Duci & Amico fidele, quidquid amici affectibus poterit esse fidelius. 1. Cum aliquis privatū commodum suū postponit, & in utilitatibus insudat, ea est firma amicitia. Quam amicitiæ benevolentiā te nobis impēdisse gaudemus &, sicut optimo fideli & intimo amico, dignam facere remunerationem intendimus. Nam cum vellet contra Græcos ire, & cum Dux Poloniæ, tuus & amicus & consanguineus, auxilium tuum contra suos peteret propter nos, sicut amicus fidelissimus, remansisti, ut nostris inimicis resisteris, tuū dum pro nihilo cōputans, tantummodò nostram causam promovendo adjuvares. Quid igitur nisi maximas tibi gratias referentes, sicut nostro optimo fideli, votis omnibus exoptemus dari occasionem, qua tibi amantissimē vicissitudinem meritam repēdamus? Et sicut in nos bonum ...
units.tr: Henry, by the grace of God Emperor Augustus, to A., the glorious duke and faithful friend, whatever can be most faithful in the affection of a friend. 1. When someone sets aside his private advantage and toils for the common good, that is firm friendship. We rejoice that you have shown us this benevolence of friendship, and as to a most excellent, faithful and intimate friend, we intend to make you a worthy return. For when we wished to go against the Greeks, and the Duke of Poland, your friend and kinsman, sought your help against his own people on our behalf, you, as a most faithful friend, remained behind to resist our enemies, counting your own concerns as nothing, and simply helping by advancing our cause. What then can we do but, giving you the greatest thanks, as to our best and most faithful man, wish with all our hearts for an opportunity by which we may repay you most lovingly in return, as you have deserved? And just as you have done good to us ...

units.la: * Intelligit Othonē Bavariæ Ducem, quem Imperator proscripsit & Ducatū privarat. * fc. a fratre.
units.tr: * He means Otto, Duke of Bavaria, whom the Emperor proscribed and deprived of his duchy. * Supply: "by a brother."

units.la: 2. Rogamus & te charissime, ut te interveniente frater tuus futura opera emendet, si quid hactenus propter suas necessitates in causa nostra negligēnus egit. Et quia victrici dextera suis angustiis cuperavit, ad nostras injurias, sicut fidelis amicus, respiciat. Nam quia se cū præsidio in illas partes tulit, ubi inimici nostri morantur, & bona eorū sita sunt; ecce locus, ecce occasio, qua & inimicis nocere, & sibi nos poterit amicissimos comparare. Tu ergo, Dilectissime, id modis omnibus vales, fratri tuo persuade, ut * N. non Ducem, sed judiciario ordine abjudicatum persequatur, & omnibus ei adversetur, sicut infestissimo hosti nostro.
units.tr: 2. We also ask you most dearly that, through your intercession, your brother make amends by future deeds for whatever he has hitherto done negligently in our cause because of his own difficulties. And since he has desired, with his victorious right hand, to relieve his own straits, let him, as a faithful friend, have regard to our wrongs. For since he has carried his force into those parts where our enemies are staying and where their goods are situated, behold the place, behold the opportunity by which he may both harm our enemies and make us most friendly to himself. You, therefore, most beloved, can do this in every way: persuade your brother that he pursue * N., not as duke but as one condemned by judicial sentence, and oppose him in every way, as the most hostile enemy of ours.

units.la: 3. Quicumq; autem de familia Salzeburgēsis Archiepiscopi, & aliorum fidelium nostrorum, dicti sunt captivi, rogamus ut causa nostræ dilectionis facias 4 reddi.
units.tr: 3. As for whoever from the household of the archbishop of Salzburg and of our other faithful men are said to have been taken captive, we ask you, for the sake of our affection, to have them returned.

units.la: V. De obedientia urbis Romæ Imperio debita.
units.tr: V. On the obedience owed by the city of Rome to the Empire.

units.la: HEINRICVS Dei gratia Romanorum b Rex, Consulibus, Senatui, populo Romano, majoribus & minoribus, gratiam suam cum bona voluntate. Divina disponente gratia, postquam Regnum patrium nostrum intravimus, Urbem, caput & sedem nostri Imperii pio affectu vi-sere optavimus, eam, more c majorum prædecessorū exaltare, honorare, ditare, ut Dominus fideles, ut pater filios, civis conciues decrevimus. Hujus autem propositum desiderū, non voluntatis, iterum diversa distrubata retardavere Regni negocia. Quibus tandem Dei nobis favente clementia sedatis, consiliis, subjectis, expediti in Italiam venimus, illamq; præ cæteris terris discordem & divisam pro re, ad justitiam & concordiam coegimus. Ad vos ergo properantes, & jam diu deliberatum in ad effectum perducere conantes, ut Legati nostri, jussu nostro, laudaverunt, nosq; invitati sumus ecclesiæ & ab Ecclesia, vobis & à vobis pro faciendā & recipienda justitia, pacificē venimus. Volumus quatenus idoneos Nuncios, veritatē voluntatis provides, & nostri honoris devotos, nobis obviam earis, quorum consilio & nostrorum uinito, ad vos vobis communi & nobis aperuus veniamus.
units.tr: Henry, by the grace of God King of the Romans, to the consuls, senate, and people of Rome, greater and lesser, greeting, with his favour and goodwill. By the disposing grace of God, after we entered our paternal kingdom, we desired with pious affection to visit the City, the head and seat of our Empire, and we resolved to exalt, honour, and enrich it, as our predecessors did, as a lord his faithful, a father his sons, a citizen his fellow citizens. But various and divided affairs of the kingdom delayed this purpose and desire of ours, though not our will. When these were at last settled by the favouring clemency of God, and our counsels and subjects were put in order, we came into Italy. Since it was more discordant and divided than other lands, we compelled it toward justice and concord. Hurrying to you, and trying to bring to completion what we had long deliberated, as our envoys have praised by our command, and invited and summoned by the Church, we came peacefully to you and for you, to carry out and receive justice. We wish that you send us suitable messengers, faithful to the truth of our will and devoted to our honour, to meet us, so that by their counsel and our agreement we may come to you openly, for the common good of you and us.
VI.

units.la: De beneficio vacante per Episcopum non concedendo sine Imperatoris scitu & voluntate.
units.tr: On a vacant benefice not to be conferred by the Bishop without the knowledge and will of the Emperor.

units.la: HEINRICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator Augustus, Ruperto Babebergensi Episcopo gratiam & omne bonum. Quoniam semper nobis fuisti fidelis, quemadmodum debuisti, & honorem nostrum sicut vir sapiens & fidelis egregius retinere & amplificare studuisti; grates tibi quam maximas referimus; & inde procul dubio scias, dignam tibi facere remunerationem intendimus. Tua itaque rogamus fidelitatem confidenter, ut beneficio, quod fuit Oudalrici divitis, nullam promissionem vel concessionem alicui facias, donec nobis loquaris, aut inde nostram sententiam certis literis voluntatem. Si enim hoc attenderis, nos faciemus propter tuam charitatem, quod nos rogasti in tuis basiis. Et tu stude honori nostro, sicut in te confidimus providere.
units.tr: HEINRICH, by the grace of God Augustus Emperor of the Romans, to Rupert, Bishop of Bamberg, grace and every good thing. Since you have always been faithful to us, as you ought to have been, and have sought to keep and enlarge our honour like a wise man and an outstanding faithful servant, we give you the greatest thanks; and you may know without doubt that we intend to make you a worthy return. We therefore confidently ask your loyalty that you make no promise or grant of the benefice that belonged to Ulrich the rich to anyone until you have spoken with us, or have made our judgement and will known to you by a sure letter. For if you observe this, we will do for the sake of your affection what you asked of us in your kisses. And you should take care for our honour, as we trust you will provide.

units.la: VII. De beneficio paterno in filium conferendo.
units.tr: VII. On conferring a paternal benefice on the son.

units.la: HEINRICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator Augustus, Ruperto Babebergensium Episcopo gratiam suam & omne bonum. Novit optime Dilectio tua, quanto tempore quam optima fidelis nobis servierit Oudalricus, & filius ejus G... qui nuper misericordia omnibus bonis, quia immatura morte recessit a saeculo. Urget itaque nos tam humanitatis compassio, quam justitiae necessitudo, ut in parentes ejusdem G... aviae & paternae servitutis memores simus, & orbitatem eorum debitae pietatis suffragio consulamus. Unde te sollicite commonemus, & summis precibus obsecramus, ut filio eius, patris beneficium benigne pro respectu Dei, & nostra interventione concedas, nulla hoc differes cunctatione, nulla excusans vel abnuens ratione. Commendationem autem pueri usque in praesentiam nostram ut differas rogamus, sicut de nobis curas.
units.tr: HEINRICH, by the grace of God Augustus Emperor of the Romans, to Rupert, Bishop of Bamberg, his grace and every good thing. Your Affection knows very well how long and how excellently the faithful Ulrich served us, and his son G..., who lately, to the grief of all good men, departed this life by untimely death. Therefore both the compassion of humanity and the claim of justice urge us to remember the service of his parents, grandparents and forebears, and to provide for their bereavement by the support of due piety. Hence we earnestly remind you and beseech you with the utmost entreaty that you graciously grant the benefice of the father to his son, for the sake of God's regard and through our intercession; do not delay this at all, and do not excuse or refuse it on any ground. We ask, however, that you defer the boy's recommendation until he is in our presence, as you take care of us.

units.la: VIII. De Custodia Ecclesiae, & alio beneficio vacante.
units.tr: VIII. On the Custody of the Church and another vacant benefice.

units.la: HEINRICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator Augustus, Ruperto reverentissimo, & patrino suo in Christo dilectissimo, gratiam suam & plurimam in Christo salutem. Cum praeomnibus maximam habeam in te fiduciam, miror quod totiens te pro una eademque re rogavi, & nihil mihi dignum pro mea spe respondisti; praesertim cum nihil unquam ita sit arduum, quod putaverim abs te denegari. Sed & adhuc iteratas preces ingeminando itentidem Dilectionis tuae dulcedinem exoratam, ut de Custodia Ecclesiae tuae inclinatius mihi aurem praebeas, & eam mihi per praesentium nuncium transmittas.
units.tr: HEINRICH, Emperor Augustus by the grace of God, to Rupert, most reverend, and his most beloved godfather in Christ, his grace and abundant salvation in Christ. Since I place greater trust in you than in anyone, I wonder that I have so often asked you for one and the same matter, and you have answered me nothing worthy of my hope; especially since nothing has ever been so difficult that I thought it could be refused by you. But, again repeating my prayers, I beg the sweetness of your Affection, that you more readily lend your ear to me concerning the Custody of your Church, and send it to me by the bearer of these presents.

units.la: 2. Praeterea quia Comes Oudalricus obiisse dicitur, non aliter te rogo, quam ut revocem tibi memoriam, si quid pro amore & voluntate tua fecerim, ita ut aperte in hac petitione experiar, quantum digas. Necte rogo, nisi talia, quae honori & proficuo tuo erunt profutura. Rogo, inquam, ut beneficia, quae ex te habuit, nulli promittas, necaliquid inde facias, sed totam ipsius rei actionem differas, ad nostram utriusque ad invicem praesentiam.
units.tr: 2. Besides, since Count Ulrich is said to have died, I ask you only to recall to your memory whatever I have done for your love and goodwill, so that in this request I may clearly test how much you value it. Nor do I ask you for anything except such things as will be profitable to your honour and advantage. I ask, I say, that you promise the benefices that he had from you to no one, nor do anything about them, but defer the whole business of the matter until we are both present with each other.

units.la: IX. De Praeposito vel Custode Ecclesiae.
units.tr: IX. On the Provost or Custos of the Church.

units.la: HEINRICUS Dei gratia Imperator Augustus, Ruperto venerabili Episcopo & dilecto compatri, gratiae suae optimam voluntarem. Quia in Custodia Babebergensi per effectum operis nostram voluntate, magnas tibi grates, sicut optimo fideli nostro, referimus. Quod superest, rogamus, tibi praecipimus, ut prohibeas, ne ejusdem Ecclesiae Custos alicujus inde aut calumniam in patiatur; & illos, qui se de illa Custodia beneficiatos asserunt, Episcopali auctoritate constringia de ipsorum manibus excute, & restitue. Nam id Principum nostrorum decreto indultum et confirmatum est, ut nullus Praepositus vel Custos Ecclesiae, potestatem habeat quidquam de bonis Ecclesiae in beneficium alicui praestare: & si factum fuerit, irritum habeti.
units.tr: HEINRICH, by the grace of God Emperor Augustus, to Rupert, venerable Bishop and beloved co-father, his grace and the best goodwill. Since in the Custody of Bamberg, by the actual working of our will, we give you great thanks, as to our excellent faithful servant. For the rest, we ask and command you to see to it that the Custos of that same Church suffers no false accusation arising from it; and those who claim to have been given benefices from that Custody, compel them by episcopal authority, and take them out of their hands and restore it. For this has been granted and confirmed by the decree of our princes, that no Provost or Custos of a Church has the power to bestow anything of the goods of the Church as a benefice on anyone; and if it has been done, let it be held void.

units.la: X. De officio Episcopali.
units.tr: X. On the episcopal office.

units.la: HEINRICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator Augustus, Ottoni Babenbergensis Ecclesiae Episcopo, gratiam, dilectionem & omne bonum. Perfectus amor, cum utriq; domesticus cordis sit, non ad oculum tantum valet, non ad oculum spectat, non pendet ex tempore, per quem absentes longius separantur, tanto arctius mutua pro se solicitudine constringuntur. Nos certe absentis pluorem, quam dum a affuisti, curam gerimus; eodem, quo te proveximus, animo cunctata tibi ... quod adhuc de rebus tuis optata comperimus, te videlicet ab Ecclesia tua honorifice recepit gratia omnibus respondionum habitibus, & actuum temperantia placuisse, & in praestandis beneficiis neve fiant laudabiliter exhibuisse caurelam. Qua de re consulimus, hortamur, & petimus, ut quod facias, ne primitias bonae famae, si manum remiseris, perdas, quia bona inceptio fine fine.
units.tr: HEINRICUS, by the grace of God Roman Emperor Augustus, to Otto, Bishop of the Church of Bamberg: grace, love and every good. Perfect love, since it is native to the heart of both parties, does not depend on the eye, does not look to the eye, and does not depend on time. Absence may separate people farther, but the more distant they are, the more closely they are bound by mutual concern for one another. Indeed, we care for you more now that you are absent than we did when you were present. With the same mind by which we advanced you, we have learned from reports about your affairs that you were honourably received by your Church, that by the graciousness of your bearing and the moderation of your conduct you have pleased everyone, and that in bestowing benefices you have shown a commendable caution. For this reason we advise, exhort and ask you to continue so, lest by slackening your hand you lose the first-fruits of your good reputation, since a good beginning has no end.

units.la: a Fuit enim Cancellarius Imperatoris. speciosi corporis instar est sine capite. Nemo te à delecto Ecclesiasticæ secundum justitiam terrore detorqueat, precio flectat, suadendi fellito melle seducat; quoniam tentatus his omnibus probatus fuerit, facilè omnia propulsabis. Si quid autem grave tuis viribus æstimabis, ad nos tibi culdubio succursuros ex nostri differas occasione præcepti.
units.tr: For he was the Emperor's chancellor. A fair body is like a body without a head. Let no one turn you aside from the choice of the Church that is according to justice by fear, bend you by bribes, or seduce you with the honeyed poison of persuasion. Since you have been tried and proved in all these matters, you will easily ward off everything. But if you judge anything to be too heavy for your strength, you may be sure that we will come to your aid; do not put the matter off on the pretext of our instruction.
XI.

units.la: De Comitiis Imperialibus Spiram indictis pro reformando statu Roman- i Imperii.
units.tr: On the Imperial Diet called at Speyer for the reform of the state of the Roman Empire.

units.la: HEINRICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator Augustus, Ottoni Babenbergensium Episcopo gratiam abundè & omne bonum. Roma nostri Nuncii redierunt, & Dei gratia maxima nobis læta & prospera retulere. Mandant etiam nobis nostri fideles, quod tempus hactenus acceptabile, ut Romanæ Sedi & Reipublicæ consulamus. Quapropter necessario nostros Principes convocamus, ut inde, sicut justum est, eorum consilium & auxilium habeamus. Ad quod plurimum indigemus tuæ fidei præsentia, & tui consilii prudentia; quoniam & te corderenus diligimus de omni honore nostro, prout nobismetipsis, indubitanter confidimus. Confidenter igitur & tuam rogamus dilectionem, ut die Veneris post proximum festum sanctæ Mariæ, venias ad Ramam, & ibi super his tuo & aliorum nostrorum Principum cōsilio ad Dei honorem & Regni, & Ecclesiæ pacis statum tractabimus. Et hilariter facias hoc, sciens quòd te citò dimittemus. Et hoc ter tibi parceremus, nisi tam alti negocii nos urgeret instantia.
units.tr: Henry, by the grace of God Augustus Emperor of the Romans, to Otto, Bishop of Bamberg, grace abundantly and every good thing. Our messengers have returned from Rome and have brought us news, very joyful and prosperous, by the grace of God. Our faithful subjects also tell us that now is the acceptable time to take thought for the Roman See and the commonwealth. Therefore we are of necessity calling our princes together, so that from them, as is right, we may have their counsel and aid. For this we have very great need of the presence of your faithfulness and the wisdom of your counsel, since we love you dearly and trust without doubt in you as in ourselves, in all our honour. We therefore earnestly ask your affection to come to Rome on the Friday after the next feast of St. Mary, and there, with your counsel and that of our other princes, we will deal with these matters for the honour of God, and for the state of the kingdom and the peace of the Church. And do this gladly, knowing that we will send you away quickly. And we would spare you even this trouble, were we not pressed by the urgency of so high a business.

units.la: 2. Præterea mandamus tibi, ut mittas pro Comite N... quem tibi commisimus, & eum repræsentes.
units.tr: 2. Furthermore, we order you to send for Count N..., whom we have entrusted to you, and to present him.
XII.

units.la: De expeditione Imperiali in rebellem Comitem Flandrensium.
units.tr: On the imperial expedition against the rebellious Count of Flanders.

units.la: HEINRICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator Augustus, Ottoni Babenbergensi Episcopo suo fideli chanflimo gratiam & omne bonum. Cum Dei providentia & magnæ pietatis filio de nostro Regno ubiq; pacificato gauderemus, advenerunt nobis nuncii ex parte Godefridi Comitis, & Balduini Comitis, aliorumque fidelium nostrorum Marehiæ Flandrensis, intimantes eos non posse sustinere molestias Roberti Comitis, qui Regnum nostrum invasit, & ad ignominiam omnium, qui in eo sunt, sibi nostrum Cameracensem Episcopatum usurpavit. Unde, quemadmodum res hortabatur, nostros Principes convocatos consuluimus, & ab eis sapienter re notata, consilio eorum consilio nos facturos expeditionem in Flandriam supra tam præsumptuosum hostem, quam miles debet esse, ne diutius de imminutione & dedecore Regni nostri impunè superbiat. Quidem tam manifestum & tam commune Regni nostri dedecus tibi fieri, si tuum honorem pensare debes cordetenus. Ut igitur fidelitér hoc facias & prudenter, rogamus te sub spe remuneration gratissimæ, & per fidelitatem, quam nobis & Regno debes, monemus, ut omni occasione ficta, sicut honor est Regni atq; tuus, ad expeditionem venias; sciens quod in proximo festo Sancti omnium Tungrensi juxta Leodium convenientes, parati super Flandriam equitare.
