Nec mirentur, tum esse adventum nostrum Radisponam, sicut mellexeras, quando nobiscum eras; quia necessitas intervenit, & utiliter ad dedecus Regni firmiter est laudata ab omnibus nostris nostra super hostes in Flandriam.
units.tr: Henry, by the grace of God Emperor Augustus of the Romans, to Otto, Bishop of Bamberg, his faithful and dearest, grace and every blessing. While we rejoiced, by God's providence and by the son of great piety, that our kingdom was everywhere at peace, messengers came to us on behalf of Count Godfrey, Count Baldwin, and others of our faithful men of the March of Flanders. They reported that they could not endure the harassment of Count Robert, who had invaded our kingdom and, to the disgrace of all who are in it, had usurped our bishopric of Cambrai for himself. Whereupon, as the matter demanded, we summoned our princes and consulted them. Having carefully considered the matter, they advised us, and we resolved on their counsel, to make an expedition into Flanders against an enemy so presumptuous, as a soldier ought to do, lest he continue to boast with impunity of the diminution and dishonour of our kingdom. Therefore, since this shame to our kingdom is so manifest and so common, you should weigh it in your heart as touching your own honour. So that you may do this faithfully and prudently, we ask you, in the hope of a most welcome reward, and we admonish you by the fidelity you owe to us and to the kingdom, that, setting aside every pretext, as is for the honour both of the kingdom and of yourself, you come to the expedition, knowing that at the next feast of All Saints we shall gather at Tongeren near Liège, ready to ride against Flanders. Nor let them wonder that our arrival is at Regensburg, as you had planned when you were with us; for necessity has intervened, and it has been firmly approved by all our men as useful for the shame of the kingdom, namely our expedition against the enemies in Flanders.

units.la: XIII.
units.tr: XIII.

units.la: Ad Episcopum Bambergensem, ut in fide perseveret; & beneficium quoddam Ecclesiastico cum in quendam Imperii fidelem conferat.
units.tr: To the Bishop of Bamberg, that he should persevere in the faith; and concerning the granting of a certain ecclesiastical benefice to a certain faithful subject of the Empire.

units.la: Anno Christi 1105. a Propter rebellionem filii Henrici Regis Rom. qui tyrannidem Imperii invaserat. b Preces Imperiales pro beneficio Ecclesiastico.
units.tr: In the year of Christ 1105. a On account of the rebellion of the son of King Henry of the Romans, who had seized the tyranny of the Empire. b Imperial letter concerning an ecclesiastical benefice.

units.la: HEINRICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator, Ottoni Babenbergensi Episcopo, suo & certo fideli, gratiam & omne bonum.
units.tr: HENRY, by the grace of God Emperor of the Romans, to Otto, Bishop of Bamberg, his certain and faithful man, grace and every good.

units.la: 1. Nunc imminente necessitate debet apparere, qui sint fideles nobis, & ipsa evidentia manifestandum est, quantum nos diligant & honorem nostrum. Scias igitur, quod nos nunc venimus cum multis militibus; & adhuc ibidem plures ex speciatus, cupientes cum Dei adjutorio micos nostros invadere, & castrum nostrum Nurenberc, quod obsident, liberare. Quapropter optimo fideli, rogando mandamus, ut ad nos venire feltines cum omnibus, quos habere poteris, tibi confidimus.
units.tr: 1. Now, with necessity pressing upon us, it ought to become clear who are faithful to us, and it must be made manifest by the very evidence how greatly they love us and our honour. Know therefore that we are now coming with many soldiers; and there are yet more of our men in that place, who, desiring with God's help to attack our enemies and to free our castle at Nuremberg, which they are besieging. Wherefore we command you, as our best and faithful man, by this request, to come to us, and to bring with you all whom you are able to bring; we trust in you.

units.la: 2. Insuper etiam diligenter te rogamus, ut in præsenti nostram consideres necessitatem, & qui nobis est necessarius, concedas beneficium, quod à te poscimur, animadvertens, quòd multis præsens periculum compellit multis supplicare, & eorum voluntate facientes ipsos in nostra fide confirmare; & hac ratione constrictos, de his & de aliis multis oporter nos te rogare aliter, quam mus: sed nos, Deo volente, si prosperitas advenerit, te & Ecclesiam tuam, sicut dignum est, respice. De hac re fac, secundum quod tibi dicet N... ex nostri parte.
units.tr: 2. Moreover, we also earnestly ask you to consider our present necessity, and to grant the favour which we demand of you, to him who is necessary to us; bearing in mind that the present danger compels many to make supplication to many, and that by their own will they make them more firmly confirmed in our faith; and being bound by this consideration, we must ask you concerning these and many other matters otherwise than we do; but, God willing, if prosperity comes, we shall have regard for you and your Church, as is fitting. Act in this matter according to what N. shall tell you on our behalf.
XIV.

units.la: Pro fide legitimo Imperio servanda ad versus Tyrannum invasorem.
units.tr: For the legitimate Empire to be kept faithful, against the tyrant invader.

units.la: HEINRICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator Augustus, Ottoni Babenbergensi Episcopo gratiam & omne bonum.
units.tr: HENRY, by the grace of God Roman Emperor Augustus, to Otto, Bishop of Bamberg, grace and every good.

units.la: 1. Scimus, quia legationibus filii nostri frequenter fatigaris, sicut nobis per tuū Nuncii mandasti. Confidimus autem de tuæ bonitatis fide, nec precibus, nec minis, nec persuasionibus, nec blanditiis acquiescas.
units.tr: 1. We know that you are frequently wearied by embassies from our son, as you have sent word to us through your messenger. We trust, however, in the faithfulness of your goodness, that you will yield neither to prayers, nor to threats, nor to persuasions, nor to flattery.

units.la: nostris contra nos inimicis, sed semper fideliter nobiscum permaneas. Quantascunque aduersitates ab inimicis nostris sustineas, nullatenus tamen terreatis, sed certus esto, quòd te non deserimus sive in pace, sive in periculo, & fiduciam habeas in omnipotente Domino, quòd nobiscum patiens liberaberis periculo. Sicut ergò de te confidimus, & per Nuncium tuum tibi mandavimus ad diem & locum, quem condiximus, venire non dubites.
units.tr: against us, our enemies, but always remain faithful to us. Whatever adversities you endure from our enemies, do not be terrified in any way; but be certain that we do not desert you, whether in peace or in danger, and have confidence in the almighty Lord, that you will be delivered from danger along with us, while you are patient. Since we therefore trust in you, and have sent word to you through your messenger to come to the day and place we appointed, do not hesitate.

units.la: 1. Igitur per fidem, quam nobis debes, neque precibus, neque minis aliquatenus terreatis, ut ab illorum nostrum transferatis: & ab omni Ecclesia, atq; per omnes Congregationes tibi commissas, orationes sine intermissione facere ad Deum pro nobis.
units.tr: 2. Therefore, by the faith you owe us, do not be terrified in any way by prayers or threats, so that you do not turn aside from our side to theirs; and from the whole Church, and through all the congregations committed to you, make prayers to God for us without intermission.

units.la: 3. Castrum etiam tuum ita diligenter custodiri facias, ne aliquis ex custodibus ab eo discedat.
units.tr: 3. See also that your castle is guarded so carefully that none of the garrison withdraws from it.

units.la: 4. Nuncium etiam tuum ad consolandos mittas Nurenbergenses.
units.tr: 4. Also send your messenger to comfort the Nurembergers.

units.la: HENRICI IV. IMPERATORIS AUG. RESCRIPTUM
units.tr: HENRY IV, AUGUSTUS EMPEROR, HIS RESCRIPT

units.la: Vt Abbas propter contumaciam Abbatia Imperialis abdicetur.
units.tr: That an abbot be deprived of an imperial abbey on account of his contumacy.

units.la: HEnricus Dei gratia Rex, Udalrico Monacho. Miramur, quo ausu cujusve solatio Abbatiam nostram contra nos retinere voluerit, nec nobis inde serviens, nec patrono nostro Adelberto, cui hanc dedimus, quicquam subjectionis imperdiens. Quapropter volumus, firmiterque tibi sub interminatione propriæ salutis præcipimus, ut aliquam nostra relinquere non differas, nec ulterius aliquid de hac re amittere præsumas. Vuigando quoque Nuncio nostro portandam tradas. Dat. &c.
units.tr: Henry, by the grace of God King, to Udalric the monk. We marvel by what daring, and with whose encouragement, you have chosen to keep our abbey against us, neither serving us in this matter nor showing any submission to our patron Adalbert, to whom we gave it. Therefore we will, and firmly command you under threat of your own salvation, that you not delay in giving up our abbey in any way, nor presume to lose anything further in this matter. Hand it over to be carried by our messenger Wigand as well. Given, etc.

units.la: EJUSDEM MANDATUM
units.tr: THE SAME MANDATE

units.la: A- d Monachos Laureshamenses de obedientia Abbatis depositi nullatenus ulterius exhibenda.
units.tr: To the monks of Lorsch, that they are by no means to render any further obedience to the deposed Abbot.

units.la: Sicut de vestra semper obedientia accepimus, sic & modò probare volumus. Præcipimus quidem Udalricum quondam dictum Abbatem vestrum, quem nos propter inobedientiam & malum exemplum, temerarium judicavimus, nihil vobis debere jubere, nec vos ultrà ei obedire debere. Ergo si nostræ voluntati obsecundatis, in nullo sibi amplius obediatis.
units.tr: As we have always understood of your obedience, so now too we wish to prove it. We do indeed command that Udalric, formerly called your Abbot, whom we have judged rash on account of his disobedience and bad example, is to order you nothing, and that you ought no longer to obey him. Therefore, if you comply with our will, obey him in nothing any more.

units.la: DECRETA COMITIORUM WORMATIENSIUM IN CAUSA HENRICI V. IMPERATORIS, & GREGORII VII P. R. celebratorum Anno Domini M. LXXVI.
units.tr: DECREES OF THE DIET OF WORMS IN THE CASE OF HENRY V, EMPEROR, AND GREGORY VII, SUPREME PONTIFF, HELD IN THE YEAR OF OUR LORD 1076.

units.la: HEnricus, Dei gratia Rex, * gratiam, salutem, dilectionem non omnibus sed paucis eandem. In maximis negotiis, maximis maximorum opus est consiliis, qui & facultatem habeant exterius, & voluntate non careant interius, ut rei, cui bene cupiunt, bene consulere, & velint. Quamcunque cujuslibet profectus nec facultas sine voluntate, nec voluntas sine facultate proficit. Quod utrumque Tu N. fidelissime, ut arbitramur, æqualiter possides: vel, ut verius dicamus, imo tibi maxima non deest facultas, major tamen adhuc maxima facultate, si bene te novimus fidem tuam diligenter notavimus, in nostram & regni utilitatem exuberat voluntas. De præsenti fideliter exhibitis, in futuris crescit spes fidelius exhibendis. Tuæ autem dilectionem commendatam promissione tua gavisi sumus. Affiit ergo in tempore hoc opportuno tua cum fratribus voluntas, quam non modò nostra, verùm etiam omnium Cœpiscoporum fratrumque tuorum totius oppressæ Ecclesiæ exoptat necessitas.
units.tr: Henry, king by the grace of God, to [him], grace, greeting and love, the same not to all but to a few. In the greatest affairs there is need of the greatest counsels, from men who have both the means outwardly and not a lack of will inwardly, so that they both wish and are able to advise well concerning the matter they desire to serve well. Neither ability without will nor will without ability profits any undertaking. You, N., as we believe, most faithfully possess both equally; or, to speak more truly, though you lack no great ability, your will, which is greater still than your great ability, abounds for our advantage and the advantage of the realm, since we have come to know you well and have carefully observed your faithfulness. From what you have faithfully shown in the present, hope grows that you will show even more faithfulness in the future. We have rejoiced that your love was commended to us by your promise. Your will has therefore come together with your brothers at this fitting time, a will which not only our need but also that of all our fellow bishops and your brothers, and of the whole oppressed Church, longs for.

units.la: * al. spes nostra major sit fide tua.
units.tr: * Another reading: our hope may be greater than your faith.

units.la: * Qui sc Gregorium VII. ab electione nominavit. a vide Speculum Saxon. initio. b Luc. 22. c al. carnale. Deo; Regali verò gladio, ad expugnandos & expellédos Christi inimicos exterius, & ad obedientiam Sacerdotii interius, omnem hominem docens forte constringendum, ut ita de alio in alium chrismate tendetetur, dum nec Sacerdotii Regnum, nec Sacerdotium Regni honore privaretur. Hanc Deus dinationem qualiter Hildebrandica confuderit insania, tu ipse nosti, si scire novisti, vel volui nullum ejus judicio licet esse Sacerdotem, nisi qui hoc à fastu suo emendicaverit. Me quoque Deus in Regnum, non autem illum vocavit ad Sacerdotium, quia me de Deo, & non de illo regnum velle vidit, quia ipse me Regem non constituit, Regno privare studuit, minitans Regnum ... que mihi se tollere, quorum neutrum concessit. Haec & ut similia quum saepius in nostram, ut ipsi contumeliam struxerit, non tamen adhuc sufficere credit, qui de die in diem nova & exquisita fusionis genera nobis ingerit, ut in nostris Nuncis noviter argumentum dedit. Nam charta non sufficit, qualiter eosdem nostros Nuncios tractaverit, quam indignis modis affecerit, quod delitere eos incarceraverit, & carceratos nuditate, frigore, fame, siti, ac plagis contrivit, ... mum ad exemplum per medium civitatis circumductos omnibus spectaculum praebere jubet ... eundem cum Decio tyranno insanire, & Sanctos alfare credas & dicas. Unde ne pigeat Christi communi nostrum, scilicet meae & Coepiscoporum tuorum, petitioni satisfacere, utin Hepidotum Vormaciam veniat, & ibi pluta, quorum pauca docet Chartula, cum centum Principibus & quid agendum sit doceas, rogatus per dilectionem Coepiscoporum, oratus per utilitatem ... obligarus per vitae nostrae & Regni totius honorem. Valete.
units.tr: * He who named Gregory VII at his election. a See the Saxon Mirror at the beginning. b Luke 22. c Another reading: carnal. [God]; but the royal sword, to fight down and drive out Christ's enemies outwardly, and to bring about obedience to the priesthood inwardly, teaching that every man is to be bound in this way, so that the chrism passes from one to another, while neither the kingdom of the priesthood is deprived of its honour nor the priesthood of the honour of the kingdom. How Hildebrandine madness has confounded this ordinance of God, you yourself know, if you have learned to know it; and by his judgment no one is allowed to be a priest unless he has begged it from his arrogance. God also called me to the kingdom, not him to the priesthood, because he saw that I desired the kingdom from God and not from him; for he himself did not appoint me king, and he strove to deprive me of the kingdom, threatening that the kingdom ... which he himself to take from me, neither of which he granted. These things, and things like them, he has devised against us many times, to our insult, yet he does not believe them enough; from day to day he heaps upon us new and exquisite kinds of slander, as he has lately given occasion in the case of our envoys. For a letter is not sufficient to describe how he has treated those same envoys, with what unworthy outrages he has afflicted them, how he secretly imprisoned them, and wore them down by nakedness, cold, hunger, thirst and blows ... he orders them to be led through the middle of the city as an example, to offer a spectacle to all ... you would believe that he rages along with the tyrant Decius and that he calls the saints ... Wherefore, do not be reluctant to satisfy the common petition of us, that is, of me and your fellow bishops, that you come to Worms, and there, with a hundred princes, teach and make known what is to be done concerning the many things of which the little letter teaches a few. Be asked through the love of your fellow bishops, be entreated for the common good, be bound by the honour of our life and of the whole realm. Farewell.

units.la: DILECTIS IN CHRISTO FRATRI- BUS ET DOMINIS, ARCHIEPISCOPIS, EPI- SCOPIS, Principibus, Romani Imperii Ducibus, Marchionibus, Comitibus, Majoribus & Minoribus, Clero & Populo, Sanctae Ecclesiae Cultoribus, THEODORICUS VERDUNENSIS EPISCOPUS Dei gratia, id quod est, fraternam dilectionem, debitam servitutem, perpetuam in Domino Salutem.
units.tr: TO THE BELOVED BROTHERS AND LORDS IN CHRIST, THE ARCHBISHOPS AND BISHOPS, PRINCES, DUKES, MARGRAVES, COUNTS OF THE ROMAN EMPIRE, GREATER AND LESSER, CLERGY AND PEOPLE, WORSHIPPERS OF THE HOLY CHURCH, THEODORIC, BISHOP OF VERDUN, BY THE GRACE OF GOD, WHICH IS TO SAY, BROTHERLY LOVE, DUE SERVICE, AND PERPETUAL SALVATION IN THE LORD.

units.la: REGNI nostri perturbatio &, ut verius dicam, nisi Dominus avertat, proxima nimis annis in maximum dolorem nos excitat, in lachrymas vocat, in miserabilem querimoniam Deo & hominibus nos animat. Hildebrandus, qui dicitur caput, jam ex cauda Ecclesiae fundamentum, jam detrimentum est Ecclesiae. Hic dispergit, qui dicebatur congregare: hic Ecclesiam odit, qui dicebatur diligere: jam usque ad omnimodam haeresim infirmat, qui dicebatur Ecclesiam Sanctam confirmare. O inaudita arrogantia hominis, supra omnem Ecclesiam in se gloriantem, omnem maliciam malè agentis, unitatem Ecclesiae sciudentis; quod inauditum est, Regnum & Regem Catholicum destruere praesumentis, impios justificantis, pios injustissime damnantis, Dominum Patrum pervertentis,
units.tr: The disturbance of our kingdom, or, to speak more truly, unless the Lord turn it away, has in these very recent years stirred us to the greatest grief, called us to tears, and moved us to a miserable complaint before God and men. Hildebrand, who is called the head, has now become from the tail of the Church its foundation, and now its ruin. He scatters, though he was said to gather; he hates the Church, though he was said to love it; and now he weakens it to every kind of heresy, though he was said to confirm the Holy Church. O unheard-of arrogance of the man, glorying in himself above the whole Church, a man who does every wickedness in his evil doing, who tears apart the unity of the Church; what is unheard of, who presumes to destroy the kingdom and the Catholic King, who justifies the impious, who most unjustly condemns the pious, who perverts the Fathers of the Lord...

units.la: PATRIBUS NON FRATRIBUS, DO- MINIS NON AMICIS, ENGELBERTUS De- signatus Trevirensis Episcopus Ecclesiae, devotissimas Oratio- nes in Christo.
units.tr: To the Fathers, not brothers; to the lords, not friends: Engelbert, designated Bishop of Trier, to the Church, with most devoted prayers in Christ.

units.la: FERRE sententiam contra Apostolicum, non est tutum; imo insanum & omnino nefas quid audere in illum, qui in vice sancti Petri fungitur legatione ipsius Christi. Iste autem vafrit sedem Apostolicam, qui inaudita clamore effertur, qui prophanis novitatibus studet plo nomine delectatur, quem neque Christianum appellem, quia non habet characterem, cem & charitatem, quam b Christus suis militibus impressit, qua Christus suos notavit: non contra hunc, non insurgere, magnum sanctae matris Ecclesiae est periculum, & plane est contra Dei Ecclesiae, discordiam totius mundi emersisse? Quis, inquam, non videt, per hunc quali significem sanguinem mundi effusum esse? De multis rationibus, qui non sequitur Christum, nequaquam appellare Christianum: ita certe nec Papam, quem video toties & tam manifestum homicidam, Ecce bonus & sanctus Papa, cujus consiliis, cujus instinctu & ductu, membra Christi tot & tam perditis dis sunt dilacerata. En bonus pastor, qui in illos tanta crudelitate grassatur, pro quibus Christus ... ce per endit, quos ipse proprio sanguine redemit. En verus Pontifex, & justus Sacerdos, qui sicut dum illud quod lumuntur in Dominica mensa fit verum corpus & sanguis Christi, ita non poenitentium ea, quae juste tractata sunt, condonat sacramenta. Nihil certe ita est impium & nefarium, nihil detestabile & execrabile, quod ipse curet, dum alios contra Regem armet; dum alios ad bellum, quod ipse omnibus intendit, excitet. Inter has multiplices calamitates & miserias, quas patitur & continet sancta Ecclesia, mihi quoque illata est ab eo tam superba quam violenta injuria. Cum enim electus pari consensu tam Cleri quam plebis ellem electus Episcopus, tamen eo impediente, nullam quam obtendente, fere per biennium consecrationem obtinere non potui, omnibus ejusdem Ecclesiae illis & Suffraganeis intercedentibus, & inusitatam suae Metropoleos viduitatem multum quer... Nihil mihi profuit syncerus introitus, & legitima mea electio apud illum, nihil valuit consuetudo horitas Episcoporum, & studiosa loci intercessio. Ut taceam mea, ut praetermittam privata: quod minus & non purus ejus introitus, quae minatus est, pervenit ad perditissima exempla. Ne plus pe... sancta, quae modo extremum trahit spiritum, periclitetur Ecclesia, ex me dico, quod nullam ... entiam posthac servabo, nec meo judicio amplius sedebit in loco & in vice sancti Petri, quem ipse non sequitur obstupenda abusione novitatis suae, & inaudita decreti.
units.tr: It is not safe to pass sentence against the Apostolic See. Indeed, it is madness and utterly wrong to dare anything against him who, in the place of St Peter, carries out the embassy of Christ himself. But this man, who is borne along with unheard-of clamour, who devotes himself to profane novelties and delights in his own name, whom I cannot call a Christian, since he lacks the character and the charity which Christ stamped upon his soldiers, by which Christ marked his own: is it not a great danger to holy mother Church that we should not rise up against him, and that discord with God's Church should have arisen throughout the whole world? Who, I say, does not see that through him, as it were, the blood of the whole world has been poured out? For many reasons, one who does not follow Christ cannot rightly be called a Christian; so certainly neither can the Pope be called one, whom I see so often and so manifestly to be a murderer. Behold the good and holy Pope, by whose counsels, by whose instigation and leadership, so many and such lost members of Christ have been torn apart! Behold the good shepherd, who rages with such cruelty against those for whom Christ gave himself up, whom he redeemed with his own blood! Behold the true Pontiff and just priest, who, just as that which is taken at the Lord's table becomes the true body and blood of Christ, so grants the sacraments to the unrepentant, which have been justly handled! Certainly nothing is so impious and wicked, nothing so detestable and execrable, that he does not take care to do it, while he arms others against the King and stirs others to the war which he himself directs against everyone. Among these manifold calamities and miseries which holy Church suffers and endures, an injury as proud as it is violent has also been inflicted on me by him. For when I had been elected bishop with the equal consent of both clergy and people, nevertheless, with him obstructing and alleging no reason, I could not obtain consecration for almost two years, although all the suffragans of the same church interceded, and I lamented greatly the unusual widowhood of his metropolis. My sincere entry and my lawful election before him availed me nothing; the custom and authority of bishops and the zealous intercession of the place were of no avail. To say nothing of my own affairs, to pass over private matters: his entry, which was not pure, and what he threatened, has come to the most desperate examples. Lest the holy Church, which now draws its last breath, be further endangered, I say on my own account that I will no longer observe his ..., nor in my judgment will he any longer sit in the place and stead of St Peter, whom he does not follow, through the astonishing abuse of his novelty and his unheard-of decree.

units.la: SENTENTIA EPISCOPORUM IMPERIA- LIUM, DAMNANS HILDEBRANDUM PAPAM.
units.tr: THE SENTENCE OF THE IMPERIAL BISHOPS, CONDEMNING HILDEBRAND THE POPE.

units.la: Sigifridus Moguntinus — Archiepiscopus Udo Treverensis V Vilhelmus Trajectensis, Hermannus Metensis, Henricus Leodiensis, Richardus Verdonensis, Bibo Tullensis, Huzmannu Spirensis, Burcardus Halberstadensis, V Vernherus Strasburgensis, Burckhardus Basiliensis, Otto Constantiensis, Adelbero V Virtzburgensis, Rudbertus Babenbergensis, — Episcopus Otto Ratisponensis, Elingardus Frisingensis, Udalricus Eystettensis, Fridericus Monasteriensis, Eilbertus Mindensis, Hezil Hiltuneshcymensis, Beno Osnaburgensis, Eppo Neapolitanus, Imardus Paderbrunnensis, Thiedo Brandenabrugensis, Burckhardus Lofannensis, Bruno Unensis,
units.tr: Sigifrid of Mainz, Archbishop; Udo of Trier; V. William of Utrecht; Hermann of Metz; Henry of Liège; Richard of Verdun; Bibo of Toul; Huzmann of Speyer; Burchard of Halberstadt; V. Werner of Strasbourg; Burckhard of Basel; Otto of Constance; Adalbero V. of Würzburg; Rudbert of Bamberg; Otto of Regensburg, Bishop; Elingard of Freising; Ulrich of Eichstätt; Frederick of Münster; Eilbert of Minden; Hezil of Hildesheim; Benno of Osnabrück; Eppo of Naumburg; Imard of Paderborn; Thiedo of Brandenburg; Burchard of Lausanne; Bruno of Merseburg,

units.la: HILDEBRANDO fratri &c. Cum primum Ecclesiae gubernacula invasisses, etsi bene nobis tolerare esset, quam illicitam & nefariam te contra jus & fas familiari tibi arrogantia praesumpsisti, dissimulanda tamen, dispensatoria quadam taciturnitate, tam vitiosa introitus tui exordia putarimus, sperantes videlicet ta criminosa principia consequentis regiminis tui probitate & industria emendanda, & aliquatenus obliteranda. Verum nunc, ut lamentabilis universalis Ecclesiae status clamat & deplorat, malis initiis tuis per pejores actionum decretorum, tuorum progressus, infoelici respondes vigore & pertinacia. Cum enim Dominus & Redemptor noster, pacis & charitatis bonum quasi singulare characterem impresserit, cujus rei testimonia exstitunt plura, qua ut epistolari brevitate comprehendi valeant: tu e contrario, dum prophanis studes novitatibus, dum magis amplo quam bono nomine delectaris, dum inaudita elatione distenderis, velut quidam signifer schismatis, omnia membra Ecclesiae secundum Apostolum quieta & tranquilla vita ante haec tua tempora agebant, supra crudelitate, crudelitate, lophria lacessiti; flammaque; discordiae, quas in Rom. Eccl. diris factionibus exciuisti: omnes Ecclesiae Germaniae, Galliae, & Hispaniae furiali demetia sparsisti. Sublata enim, quantum in te fuit, omni ... ab Episcopis, quibus divinitus per gratiam Sp. S. qui maxime in ordinationibus operatur, collata ... omnique rerum Ecclesiasticarum administratione plebeio furori praeatributa, dum nemo ... Episcopus aut Presbyter est, nisi qui hoc indignissima assentatione a fastu suo emedicaverit, omnem.
units.tr: To Brother Hildebrand, etc. When you first seized the government of the Church, although we could well have tolerated it, even though you presumed, with the arrogance natural to you, in a manner unlawful and wicked, against right and law, we nevertheless thought such a faulty beginning of your entry should be passed over in a certain prudent silence, hoping, to be sure, that the criminal beginnings would be amended, and somewhat wiped away, by the uprightness and diligence of your subsequent rule. But now, as the lamentable state of the universal Church cries out and laments, you answer your evil beginnings with ever worse decrees and actions, and your progress with unhappy vigour and obstinacy. For since our Lord and Redeemer has impressed upon peace and charity a kind of singular mark, of which there are many testimonies, too many to be comprehended in the brevity of a letter, you, on the contrary, while you labour after profane novelties, while you delight in a name more grand than good, while you have swollen with unheard-of pride, like some standard-bearer of schism, have, though all the members of the Church, according to the Apostle, lived a quiet and tranquil life before your time, been provoked with cruelty, cruelty, [pride?] ...; and you have stirred up the flames of discord, which you kindled in the Roman Church with dreadful factions; you have scattered a furious madness over all the churches of Germany, Gaul and Spain. For, as far as lay in you, all ... taken away from the bishops, to whom it was conferred by divine grace through the Holy Spirit, who works most of all in ordinations, and all administration of ecclesiastical affairs handed over to the rage of the common people, so that no one ... is a bishop or presbyter unless he has, by this most unworthy flattery, purchased his way out of his pride; every ...

units.la: a. An Verdensis? an Genevensis? omnem Apostolicæ institutionis vigorem, illamque pulcherrimam membrorum Christi distributionem, quam Doctor gentium toties commendat & inculcat, miserabili confusione miscuisti: siccq; haec tua gloriosa decreta (quod sine lachrymis dici non potest) Christi fere nomen periit. Quis autem illud pro indignitate rei non stupeat, quod novam quandam indebitamq; potentiam tibi usurpando arrogas, ut debita universæ fraternitati jura destruas? Asseris enim, cujuscunq; nostrum Parrochialiquod delictum ad te vel sola fama perveniat, ultra jam non habere quemquam nostrum aliquam potestatem vel ligandi vel solvendi, praeter te solum aut eum, quem tu specialiter ad hoc delegeris. Quæ sententia quod omnem insaniam excedat, quis in sacris litteris eruditus non videat?
units.tr: a. Is he from Verdun? Is he from Geneva? You have mixed up, in miserable confusion, all the vigour of Apostolic teaching and that most beautiful distribution of the members of Christ, which the Teacher of the Gentiles so often commends and impresses; and by these your glorious decrees (which cannot be spoken of without tears) the very name of Christ has almost perished. Who, moreover, would not be astonished at the unworthiness of the matter, that you arrogate to yourself a certain new and undue power, so as to destroy the rights owed to the whole brotherhood? For you assert that none of us has any power, whether of binding or of loosing, any longer, in respect of any parish offence which reaches you even by mere rumour, except yourself alone, or him whom you specially appoint for this. Which opinion surpasses all madness: who, learned in the sacred letters, does not see this?

units.la: Quia ergo per hos aliosq; praesumptionem tuarum spiritus Ecclesiam Dei tam graviter perturbatam, diutius tolerare omni malo deterius judicavimus, placuit, ut communi omnium nostrum consilio tibi, quod hactenus tacuimus, innotescat, quamobrem nec modo nec unquam potueris Apostolicæ sedi praeesse: Tu ipse bonæ memoriæ HENRICO Imperatori ipsum corporali sacramento obstrinxisti, quod numquam vivente ipso Imperatore, aut filio ejus Domino nostro glorioso Rege, qui modo summæ rerum praeest, Papatum aut ipse suscipetes, aut aliquam ... quantum in te est, suscipere paterebis, absque assensu & laudamento vel patris, dum viveret, vel dum ipse viveret. Atque hujus sacramenti sunt hodie testes plerique Episcopi, qui hoc tunc & oculis suis viderē & auribus audiere.
units.tr: Therefore, since by these and other presumptuous acts of your spirit the Church of God has been so gravely disturbed, we have judged that we should no longer tolerate it, as it is worse than any evil. It has pleased all of us, by common counsel, that what we have hitherto kept silent be made known to you: wherefore you could neither now nor ever preside over the Apostolic See. You yourself bound yourself by bodily oath to the Emperor Henry, of good memory, that, never while the Emperor himself lived, or while his son, our glorious Lord the King, who now presides over the highest affairs, lived, would you either assume the papacy yourself, or permit anyone ... to assume it, as far as lies in you, without the consent and approval either of the father, while he lived, or of the son himself while he lived. And of this oath the many bishops who then saw it with their own eyes and heard it with their own ears are witnesses today.

units.la: DECRETA COMITIORUM FORCHEIMENSIUM DE LEGE REGIA, ET NE IMPERIUM PROCEDAT SUCCESSIONE, SED ELECTIONE,
units.tr: DECREES OF THE DIET OF FORCHHEIM CONCERNING THE ROYAL LAW, AND THAT THE EMPIRE SHOULD PASS NOT BY SUCCESSION BUT BY ELECTION,

units.la: STATUTA A RVDOLPHO REGE AB ARCHIEPISCOPIS, EP- ISCOPIS, DUCIBUS, COMITIBUS, MAJORIBUS & MINORIBUS ELECTIO IN CONVENTU APUD FORCHEIM, ANNO DOMINI MLXXVII.
units.tr: STATUTES MADE BY KING RUDOLF WITH THE ARCHBISHOPS, BISHOPS, DUKES, COUNTS, GREATER AND LESSER NOBLES CONCERNING THE ELECTION, AT THE ASSEMBLY IN FORCHHEIM, IN THE YEAR OF OUR LORD 1077.

units.la: Saxones & Suevi Forcheim convenerunt, sed & de aliis regionibus Legati aderant, quicquid de Republica commodè definierint, idem laudare suos indicant. Aderat etiam Legatus Apostolicus, qui cuncta, quae de Regno Principes utiliter disponerent, Apostolicæ sublimitatis auctoritate firmaret. Ex multis, quos probitate dignos in electione proposuerunt, tandem RODULFUM Ducem Suevorum Regem sibi Saxones & Suevi concorditer elegerunt.
units.tr: The Saxons and Swabians met at Forchheim, and envoys from other regions were also present. Whatever they usefully decided concerning the commonwealth, they indicated that their people would approve. The Apostolic Legate was also present, who would confirm by the authority of the Apostolic majesty all that the princes wisely arranged concerning the kingdom. From the many whom they proposed as worthy of uprightness for the election, at last the Saxons and Swabians unanimously chose Rudolf, Duke of the Swabians, as king.

units.la: 1. At cum singuli deberent eum Regem laudare, quidam voluerunt aliquas conditiones ponere, ut hac lege eum super se levarent Regem, quatenus sibi de suis injuriis specialiter promitteret justificationem. Otto namque Dux non prius volebat eum sibi Regem constituere, nisi promitteret honorem sibi injuste ablatum restituere.
units.tr: 1. But when all were to acclaim him as king, some wished to lay down certain conditions, so that they would raise him over themselves on this condition: that he would specifically promise them redress for their injuries. For Duke Otto did not want first to make him king over himself unless he promised to restore the honour unjustly taken from him.

units.la: 3. Tamen quaedam sunt ibi cautae speciales aliter exceptae, quas quod injuste viguerant, emendare: scilicet ut Episcopatus non pro pretio nec pro amicitia daretur, sed unicuique Ecclesiae de suis electionem (sicut jubent Canones) permitteret.
units.tr: 3. Nevertheless, there are certain special provisions there, otherwise excepted, which were to correct what had been unjustly in force: namely, that bishoprics should not be given for a price or for friendship, but that he would allow each church to elect its own bishop, as the canons command.

units.la: 4. Hoc etiam ibi consensu communi comprobatum, Romani Pontificis auctoritate est corroboratum, ut Regia potestas nulli per hereditatem, sicut ante fuit consuetudo, cederet, sed filius Regis, etiamsi valde dignus esset, per electionem spontaneam, quam per successionis lineam, Rex potestate, si vero non esset dignus filius, vel si nollet eum populus, quem Regem facere vellet, habeat in potestate populus.
units.tr: 4. This was also approved there by common consent and confirmed by the authority of the Roman Pontiff: that the royal power should not pass to anyone by inheritance, as had been the custom before, but that the king's son, even if he were very worthy, should be chosen by free election rather than by the line of succession. If the son were not worthy, or if the people did not want him, the people should have it in their power to make king whomever they wished.

units.la: 5. Haec omnia legaliter constituta sunt in conventu apud Forcheim, anno Dominicæ incarnationis M LXXVII. anno IV. Venerabilis Papæ Gregorii in hoc nomine Septimi, Indictione XV. Idibus Martii.
units.tr: 5. All these things were legally established at the assembly at Forchheim, in the year of the Lord's incarnation 1077, the fourth year of the venerable Pope Gregory, in this name the Seventh, indiction 15, on the Ides of March.

units.la: Haec ita commemorat Bruno in Histor. Belli Saxonici, pag. 134. & seq. qui quidem Bruno cum Episcopo suo Constantiensi ipsi Conventui interfuit. Hujus Conventus & Decretorum etiam meminit Paulus Bernriedensis in Vita Gregorii Papæ VII. pag. 214. hisce verbis:
units.tr: Bruno recounts these things thus in his History of the Saxon War, p. 134 and following; he indeed was present at this very assembly with his bishop of Constance. Paul of Bernried also mentions this assembly and its decrees in his Life of Pope Gregory VII, p. 214, in these words:

units.la: Facto Conventu apud Forecheim, Legati Romanæ Ecclesiæ (Bernhardus Cardinalis Diaconus, & Bernhardus Abbas Massiliensis, cum Christiano postea Aversanæ Ecclesiæ Episcopo) literas Apostolicas in medium protulerunt: quam parum Dominus Papa de promissione Regis laetatus fuerit, cum adversarii Ecclesiæ plus audaciæ quam terroris ex præsentia Regis acciperet. Ad hoc, ajebant, eum petere, ut novi Regis electionem, de qua audierat, in adventum ejus differrent, si hoc sine periculo fieri posse perpenderent.
units.tr: When the assembly at Forchheim had been held, the legates of the Roman Church (Bernhard, cardinal deacon, and Bernhard, abbot of Marseilles, with Christian, afterwards bishop of the church of Aversa) produced the apostolic letters. The lord Pope was little pleased with the king's promise, since the adversaries of the Church gained more boldness than fear from the king's presence. Besides this, they said, he asked that the election of the new king, of which he had heard, be deferred until his arrival, if they judged this could be done without danger.

units.la: Peractaque igitur Legatione, Archiepiscopi, Episcopi, Duces, Marchiones, Comites, Majores atque Minores, debitam reverentiā Legatis impendentes, per confessum singuli surrexerunt; &, quot cotumelis, & quot periculis jam à Henrico Rege affecti essent, vel se afficiendos fore non dubitarent, Legatis lamentari coeperunt, seque totiens insidias ejus inter ipsa pacis oscula vix evasisse, ut necjuramento ejus deinceps aliquam fidem exhibere possent: hoc quoque; addentes, se tamdiu eum post depositionem tolerasse, non utique ut correctionem ejus, utpote penitus desperatam, exspectarent, sed ut quibusdam occasionem calumniandi auferrent, qui fortasse ei, si non tamdiu exspectaretur, correctionem interclusam fore conquererentur, totaque illa de cum hujusmodi queri monuis transacta, nec meditatem injuriarum sibi illatarum enumerare potuerunt.
units.tr: Therefore, when the legation had been concluded, the archbishops, bishops, dukes, marquises, counts, greater and lesser nobles, showing due reverence to the legates, each rose in turn from his seat. They began to lament to the legates how many insults and how many dangers they had already suffered from King Henry, or did not doubt they would suffer, and how they had barely escaped his snares amid the very kisses of peace, so that they could no longer place any trust in his oath. They added this too: that they had tolerated him so long after his deposition, not indeed to wait for his correction, which they utterly despaired of, but so as to take from certain people the occasion for slander, who perhaps would complain that correction had been cut off if he had not been waited for so long. And when all this business had been carried through in this way, they could not enumerate even half of the injuries done to them.

units.la: In crastinum vero iterum ad hospitia Legatorum convenientes, pro sua necessitate sublevandā, eos consuluerunt, suggerentes eis periculosissimum & irrevocabile schisma in toto Regno futurum, nisi in eodem Conventu, ut deliberaverant, in alicujus novi capitis sublevatione Confœderati illud anticipare festinarent. Legati autem Legationis suæ non immemores, satis compendiosè ad hæc responderunt, sibi quidem optimum videri, si Regis constitutionem juxta eorum Legationem, in adventum Domini Papæ sine periculo differre possent. Cæterum in provisione Regni non tam in eorum consilio, quàm in Principum arbitrio sitam esse dixerunt, qui Rempublicam in manibus tenerent, ac totius Regni damnum sive profectuum optimè prænossent. Itaq; Principes Regni de adventu Papæ incerti, sed de maxima dissensione eventura, & periculo, si differrent, certissimi, accepta licentia à Legatis apud Moguntinum Archiepiscopum convenerunt, & quid eis agendum esset, singulari diligentia invicem tractaverunt; considerantes quidem, se ad nullam dilationem ab Apostolico coactos, sed hoc in eorum arbitrio positum esse; necalicui, nisi sibi ipsis deinceps imputandum fore, si dilatio noceret.
units.tr: On the following day, gathering again at the lodgings of the legates to relieve their distress, they consulted them, suggesting that a most dangerous and irrevocable schism would arise throughout the kingdom unless, in that same assembly, as they had resolved, they hurried to anticipate it by raising up some new head. The legates, however, not forgetful of their mission, replied briefly, saying that it seemed best to them if the king's election could be deferred without danger, according to their legation, until the lord Pope's arrival. But they said that the arrangement of the kingdom lay not so much in their counsel as in the judgment of the princes, who held the commonwealth in their hands and best knew the loss or gain of the whole kingdom. Therefore the princes of the kingdom, uncertain of the Pope's arrival but quite certain that the greatest dissension would come, and danger if they deferred, received leave from the legates and gathered at the Archbishop of Mainz. With singular care they discussed among themselves what should be done, considering that they were not compelled by the Apostolic See to any delay, but that this lay in their own judgment, and that henceforth no one but themselves would be blamed if the delay did harm.

units.la: Insuper se nullius subjectionis exhibendæ Henrico Regi obnoxios, imò per Apostolici banni transgressionem damnandos, ii aliquā subjectione Regi deinceps exhiberent. Nam Papa, priusquam eum mathematizarent, ex parte omnipotentis Dei, & S. Petri, & sua, illi Regnum interdixit, & omnes Christianos juramento, quod *sibi fecissent, vel facturi essent, absolvit; &, ut nullus ei, ut Regi serviret, interdixit, qui posteā ab eo communione tantū, non Regnū, falsa correctionis promissione recuperavir.
units.tr: Moreover, they were bound to no subjection owed to King Henry; rather, they would be condemned by transgression of the Apostolic ban if they should henceforth show him any subjection. For the Pope, before they had put him under the ban, had in the name of almighty God, and of St Peter, and in his own name, forbidden him the kingdom, and had absolved all Christians from the oath they had sworn or were about to swear to him; and he had forbidden anyone to serve him as king. Afterwards Henry recovered from him communion only, not the kingdom, by a false promise of correction.

units.la: Hoc igitur Principes Regui diligentissimè perscrutati, se quidem à Regis Henrici potestate penitus, ut prædictū est, emancipatos, nec se illi plus, quàm illū illis, alicujus fidelitatis vel subjectionis obnoxios, ut liberi homines, Rudolphum Ducē Suevorum suffragaverunt multum renitente, suffragaverunt; vel alterius horæ inducias ad consulendum petentes, Regiā dignitate sublimaverunt, virum sanè in humilitate præcipuum, Regio honori ætate & moribus idoneum; eiqs se debito fidelitatis sacramento subdiderunt. Quique Regnum non ut proprium, sed pro dispositione sibi creditum reputans, omne hæreditarium jus in eo repudiavit, & vel filio suo se hoc adoptaturum fore penitus abnegavit, justissimè arbitrio Principum esse deceneas, ut post mortem ejus liberè, non magis filium ejus, quàm alium egerent, nisi quem ad id culminis ætate & morum gravitate dignum invenissent.
units.tr: The princes of the kingdom, having most diligently examined this, and having been wholly freed, as has been said, from the power of King Henry, and not bound to him by any fidelity or subjection any more than he was bound to them, as free men, with much reluctance chose Rudolf, Duke of the Swabians. They chose him, or, asking a respite of another hour to take counsel, raised him to royal dignity: a man indeed outstanding in humility, and suitable in age and character for royal honour. They bound themselves to him by the oath of due fidelity. He, regarding the kingdom not as his own but as entrusted to him for disposal, renounced every hereditary right in it, and utterly denied that he would adopt this for his son. He declared it most justly the judgment of the princes that after his death they should act freely, not rather for his son than for another, unless they found someone worthy of that height by age and gravity of character.

units.la: Huncigitur Rudolphum tam legitimè electum Archiepiscopi Moguntinus & b Magdeburgensis cum eorum Suffraganeis Legatis Sedis Apostolicæ præsentibus, & Regni Principibus, Regali inunctione consecrarunt. Electus est autem ab Archiepiscopis, Episcopis, Ducibus, Comitibus, Majoribus atque Minoribus, in Conventu apud Forcheim anno Dominicæ incarnationis M LXXVII. anno IV. venerabilis Papæ Gregorii in hoc nomine Septimi, indictione XV. Idibus Martii.
units.tr: Thus Rudolf, so lawfully elected, was consecrated with royal anointing by the Archbishops of Mainz and Magdeburg, together with their suffragans, the legates of the Apostolic See being present, and the princes of the kingdom. He was elected by the archbishops, bishops, dukes, counts, greater and lesser nobles, at the assembly in Forchheim, in the year of the Lord's incarnation 1077, the fourth year of the venerable Pope Gregory, in this name the Seventh, indiction 15, on the Ides of March.

units.la: HENRICI IV. IMPERATORIS AUG. IVRAMENTUM GREGORIO VII. P. R. COR- PORAL TER PRÆSTITUM IN OPP. DO CANUSII.
units.tr: The Oath of Henry IV, Emperor Augustus, Sworn Bodily to Pope Gregory VII at Canossa

units.la: Ego Henricus Rex de murmuratione & dissensione, quā nunc habent contra me Archiepiscopi, & Episcopi, Duces, Comites, ceterique Principes Regni Teutonicorum, & alii, qui eos in eadem dissensionis causa sequuntur, infra terminum, quem Dominus Papa Gregorius constituerit, aut justitiam secundum judicium ejus, aut concordiam secundum consilium ejus, faciam, nisi certum impedimentum mihi vel sibi obstiterit. Quo transacto ad peragendum idem paratus ero.
units.tr: I, King Henry, concerning the murmuring and dissension which now exist against me on the part of the archbishops, bishops, dukes, counts, and the other princes of the kingdom of the Teutons, and others who follow them in this cause of dissension, will make justice according to the judgment of the Lord Pope Gregory, or concord according to his counsel, within the term which the Lord Pope Gregory shall set, unless some certain impediment stands in the way of me or of them. When that term has passed, I shall be ready to carry out the same.

units.la: Item si idem Dominus Papa Gregorius ultra montes, seu ad alias partes terrarum ire voluerit, securus erit ex mei parte, & eorum quos constringere potero, ab omni lesione vitæ aut membriomembrorum ejus, seu captione, tam ipse quàm qui in ejus conducţu & comitatu fuerint, seu qui abillo mittuntur, vel ad eum de quibuscumque terrarum partibus venerint, in eundo & ibi morando seu inde redeundo: neq; aliud aliquid impedimentum habebit ex meo consensu, quod contra honorem suum sit. Et si quis ei fecerit, cum bona fide secundum posse meum illum adjuvabo.
units.tr: Likewise, if the same Lord Pope Gregory wishes to go beyond the mountains, or to other parts of the earth, he shall be safe on my part, and on the part of those whom I can constrain, from every injury to life or limb, or from capture, both he himself and those who are in his escort and retinue, or who are sent by him, or who come to him from whatever parts of the earth, in going, staying there, or returning from there; nor shall he have any other hindrance, with my consent, which would be contrary to his honour. And if anyone does him harm, I will assist him in good faith, according to my power, against that person.

units.la: Actum Canusii, quinto Kal. Februarii, Indictione decima quinta.
units.tr: Done at Canossa, on the fifth day before the Kalends of February, in the fifteenth indiction.

units.la: HENRICI IV. IMPERAT. AUG. ET RUDOLPHI PSEUDO- REGIS ROMANI IVRAMENTA IN CONCILIO ROMANO prastita.
units.tr: The Oaths of Henry IV, Emperor Augustus, and of the Pseudo-King of the Romans Rudolph, Made at the Roman Council

units.la: His itaque piè & feliciter actis, inter multas proclamationes conquesti sunt Legati Regis Rudolphi super Henrico, quòd nulli loco nullique personæ parcens, regionem Transalpinam contereret & conculcaret; neminem debitus honor, vel reverentia, vel dignitas tueretur: & ceu vilia mancipia non modò Sacerdotes, sed etiam Episcopi Archiepiscopique caperentur, vinculisque manciparentur, partimque trucidarentur. Decreverunt ergo quam plures Concilii, in illus tyrannidem gladium Apostolicum debere evaginari: sed distulit Apostolica mansuetudo. Juraverunt igitur Legati Henrici Regis illud, quod in sequentibus scriptum repertitur.
units.tr: When these things had been done devoutly and successfully, amid many outcries the legates of King Rudolph complained against Henry, that sparing no place and no person, he wore down and trampled the Transalpine region; that no one was protected by due honour, reverence or dignity; and that, like worthless slaves, not only priests but even bishops and archbishops were seized, bound in chains, and some of them slaughtered. Therefore several of the council decided that the apostolic sword ought to be unsheathed against this tyranny; but apostolic gentleness deferred it. Accordingly the legates of King Henry swore the oath that is found written in what follows.

units.la: SACRAMENTVM NVNTIORVM HENRICI REGIS.
units.tr: The Oath of the Messengers of King Henry

units.la: Legati Domini mei Regis ad vos venient infra terminum Ascensionis Domini, exceptis legitimis sponsiis, id est morte, vel gravi infirmitate, vel captione, absque dolo, qui Legatos Romanæ Sedis securè ducent & reducent. Et Dominus Rex obediens erit illis in omnibus, secundum justitiam & judicium illorum. Et hæc omnia observabit absque dolo, nisi quantum ex jussione vestra remanserit. Et hæc jure ex præcepto Domini mei Regis Henrici.
units.tr: The legates of my lord the King will come to you within the term of the Lord's Ascension, except for lawful hindrances, that is, death, grave sickness, or capture, without deceit; and they will safely escort and return the legates of the Roman See. And my lord the King will be obedient to them in all things, according to their justice and judgment. And he will observe all these things without deceit, except insofar as it remains by your command. And this is sworn by the command of my lord King Henry.

units.la: ITEM IVSIVRANDVM NVNTIORVM RVDOLPHI RE- GIS, ITIDEM Q. RVDOLPHI, QVOD SEQVITVR.
units.tr: Likewise the Oath of the Messengers of King Rudolph, and Likewise of Rudolph, Which Follows

units.la: Si colloquium ex vestro præcepto constitutum fuerit in partibus Teutonicis, loco & tempore vobis definito ante præsentiam vestram, vel Legatorum vestrorum, Dominus noster Rex Rudolphus vel ipse veniet, vel Episcopos & fideles suos mittet, paratusque erit judicium, quod sancta Romana Ecclesia decreverit, de causa Regni subire, nulloque malo ingenio conventum à vobis sive Legatis vestris constitutum impediet. Et postquam certum, inde vestrum Nuntium videbit de pace in Regno constituenda & confirmanda, studebit ut Legatio vestra provenire ad pacem Regni & concordiam possit. Hæc omnia observabuntur, nisi quantum ex vestra certa licentia remanserit, vel ex impedimento legitimo, scilicet morte, vel gravi infirmitate, vel captione, sine dolo.
units.tr: If a conference is arranged by your command in the German lands, at a place and time fixed by you before your presence or that of your legates, our lord King Rudolph will either come himself or send his bishops and faithful men, and he will be ready to submit to the judgment that the holy Roman Church has decreed concerning the cause of the kingdom, and he will not hinder by any evil contrivance the meeting arranged by you or your legates. And after the matter is settled, he will see to it that your messenger establishes and confirms peace in the kingdom, and he will strive so that your legation may bring about peace and harmony in the kingdom. All these things will be observed, except insofar as it remains by your certain permission, or by a lawful impediment, namely death, grave sickness, or capture, without deceit.

units.la: RUDOLPHI REGIS ROMA- NORUM ET PRINCIPUM IMPERII PROPOSITIO IN SYNODO ROMANA CONTRA HENRICVM IV. Imperatorem.
units.tr: Proposition of King Rudolph of the Romans and the Princes of the Empire in the Roman Synod against Henry IV, Emperor.

units.la: Nos ex Legatione Domini nostri Regis Rudolphi, & Principum ejus, conquerimur Deo & Sancto Petro, vestræque Paternitati, & cuncto huic sanctissimo Concilio, quod ille Henricus, quem vos Apostolica auctoritate depositistis à Regno, ipsum Regnum contra vestrum interdictum tyrannicè invasit, omnia circumquaque ferro, præda, incendio devastavit: Archiepiscopos, Episcopos, de Episcopatibus suis impia crudelitate expulit, & eorum Episcopatus suis sotoribus in beneficia distribuit. Per cujus etiam tyrannidem piæ memoriæ Wcrinharius Magdeburgensis Archiepiscopus occisus est: Adelbertus V Vormaciensis Episcopus adhuc ab eo contra Sedis Apostolicæ præceptum in captione cruciatur. Multa hominum millia ejus factione sunt occisa; quàm plures Ecclesiæ, ablatis reliquiis, incensæ, ac penitus destructæ.
units.tr: We, from the embassy of our lord King Rudolph and of his Princes, complain to God and to Saint Peter, to your Paternity, and to this whole most holy Council, that that Henry, whom you by apostolic authority deposed from the kingdom, has tyrannically invaded the kingdom itself against your interdict, and has laid waste everything round about with sword, plunder and fire. He has driven Archbishops and Bishops from their sees with impious cruelty, and has distributed their bishoprics as benefices to his supporters. Through his tyranny also, Wecelin (Wcrinharius) of Magdeburg, Archbishop of blessed memory, was killed; Adalbert V, Bishop of Worms, is still tortured in captivity by him, contrary to the precept of the Apostolic See. Many thousands of men have been slain by his faction; how many churches, stripped of their relics, have been burned and utterly destroyed.

units.la: 2. Innumerabilia quidem facinora sunt, quæ idem Henricus in Principes nostros perpetravit, eò quod sibi contra Sedis Apostolicæ decretum, ut Regi, obedire noluerunt: & Colloquium, quod vos pro inquirenda justitia, & pace componenda fieri decrevistis, ex culpa Henrici, & sequacorum ejus, remansit.
units.tr: 2. There are countless crimes which the same Henry has committed against our Princes, because they refused to obey him as king, contrary to the decree of the Apostolic See; and the colloquy which you decreed should be held to seek justice and settle the peace did not take place, through the fault of Henry and his followers.

units.la: 3. Quapropter vestram humiliter implorumus clementiam, ut nobis, imò sanctæ Dei Ecclesiæ, decretam sacrilego pervasori Ecclesiarum justitiam faciatis.
units.tr: 3. Therefore we humbly implore your clemency, that you would do justice, decreed for us and indeed for the holy Church of God, against the sacrilegious invader of churches.

units.la: Actum Romæ, anno ab Incarnatione Domini MLXXX. Pontificatus verò Domini Gregorii Papæ Septimi anno VII. Indictione III.
units.tr: Done at Rome, in the year of the Lord's Incarnation 1080, in the seventh year of the pontificate of the lord Pope Gregory VII, third indiction.

units.la: DECRETUM COMITIORUM BRIX- INÆ NORICÆ CELEBRATORUM, CONTRA GREGORIVM VII. PAPAM.
units.tr: Decree of the Diet of Brixen in Noricum, against Pope Gregory VII.

units.la: ANno Domini MLXXX. cùm apud Brixinam Noricam triginta Episcoporum convenius, nec non & Optimarum exercitus non solùm Italiæ sed & Germaniæ, jussu HENRICI Regis congregaretur, factus est omnium consensus adversùs Hildebrandum Papam, cognominatum Gregorium Septimum, quem Pseudomonachum, totiusque vastanitæ pestiferum principem, & præcipuè sanctæ Romanæ Sedis invasorem affirmantes, ab Apostolica Sede depellendum, quamvis absentem, dijudicabant; & VVigbertum Ravennensem Archiepiscopum ipsi subrogandum eligebant.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1080, when thirty bishops had assembled at Brixen in Noricum, and the best men of the army, not only from Italy but also from Germany, were gathered by command of King Henry, the consent of all was given against Hildebrand the Pope, surnamed Gregory VII. They declared that he, whom they called a false monk and the pestilent prince of the whole world, and above all an invader of the holy Roman See, was to be driven from the Apostolic See, though absent, and they chose Wibert, Archbishop of Ravenna, to be substituted in his place.

units.la: Hujus Decreti conclusio hæc est: Quia, inquiunt, illum constat non à Deo electum, sed à seipso in fraude ac pecunia impudentissimè obiectum: qui Ecclesiasticum subvertit ordinem, qui Christianì Imperii perturbavit regnum, qui Regi Catholico ac pacifico corporis & animæ intentat mortem; qui perjurum defendit *Regem; qui inter concordes seminavit discordiam, inter pacificos litcs, inter fratres scandala, inter conjuges divortia, & quicquid quietè inter piè viventes stare videbatur, concussit: nos, au hore Deo, congregati in unum, legatis ac literis freti decem & novem Episcoporum, die sancta præteritæ Pentecostes Moguntiæ congregatorum contra eundem Hildebrandum procacissimum, sacrilegia ac incendia prædicantem, perjuria & homicidia defendentem, Catholicam & Apostolicam fidem de corpore & sanguine Domini in quæstione ponentem, Hæretici Berengarii antiquum discipulum, divinationum ac somniorum cultorem, manifestum necromanticum, Phytonico spiritu laborantem, & idcirco à vera fide exorbitantem, judicamus canonicè deponendum & expellendum: & nisi ab ipsa Sede his auditis descenderit, in perpetuum condemnandum. Facta sunt hæc VII.KAL. Julii, feria v. Indict. iii.
units.tr: The conclusion of this decree is as follows: "Because, they say, it is clear that he was not elected by God, but thrust himself into office by fraud and money, most shamelessly; because he has overturned the ecclesiastical order, disturbed the realm of the Christian Empire, and plotted the death of the Catholic and peaceable King, in body and soul; because he defends a perjurer, has sown discord among those who were at peace, strife among the peaceable, scandals among brothers, divorces among spouses, and has shaken whatever seemed to stand quietly among the godly: we, gathered together by the will of God, relying on letters and messages from nineteen bishops who met at Mainz on the holy day of Pentecost just past, judge that the same Hildebrand, most insolent, who preaches sacrilege and arson, defends perjuries and murders, calls into question the Catholic and Apostolic faith concerning the body and blood of the Lord, is a former disciple of the heretic Berengar, a worshipper of divinations and dreams, a manifest necromancer, afflicted with a Pythonic spirit, and therefore straying from the true faith, is to be canonically deposed and expelled; and unless he steps down from the See itself after hearing these charges, he is to be condemned forever. These things were done on the seventh day before the Kalends of July, a Thursday, in the third indiction."

units.la: HENRICI IV. IMPERATORIS AUG. SENTENTIA CONTRA HILDEBRANDVM PAPAM LATA in Comitiis Brixinensibus.
units.tr: The Sentence of the Emperor Henry IV Augustus against Pope Hildebrand, pronounced at the Diet of Brixen.

units.la: HENRICUS non a usurpative, sed pia Dei ordinatione Rex, Hildebrando non jam Apostolico, sed falso Monacho.
units.tr: Henry, king not by usurpation but by the pious ordinance of God, to Hildebrand, no longer Apostolic but false monk.

units.la: 1. Hanc talem pro confusione tua salutationem promemisti, qui nullum in Ecclesia ordinem præteremisti, quem confusionis non honoris, maledictionis non benedictionis participem fecceris. Ut enim de multis pauca & egregia loquamur: Rectores sanctæ Ecclesiæ, videlicet Archiepiscopos, Episcopos, vel Presbyteros, non modò tangere sicut Christos Domini, non timuisti, quin servos, nescientes quid faciat Dominus eorum, sub pedibus tuis calcasti. In quorum conculcatione tibi favorem ab ore vulgi comparasti, quos omnes nihil scire, te autem solum omnia nosse judicasti. Quæ utique scientia non ad ædificationem, sed ad destructionem uti studuisti: ut pure hoc beatum Gregorium, cujus nomen tibi vendicasti, de te credamus propheràsse, sic dicentem: Ex affluentia subjectorum...
units.tr: 1. You have put forward this greeting of yours as a sign of your confusion, you who have passed over no order in the Church without making it a sharer in confusion and not honour, in curse and not blessing. To speak briefly of many matters, and those notable: the rectors of the holy Church, namely archbishops, bishops, or presbyters, you did not fear to touch as the Lord's anointed; rather, you trampled them under your feet as servants who do not know what their Lord is doing. By trampling them down you bought for yourself the favour of the common people's mouths, while you judged that all of them knew nothing and you alone knew everything. You have striven to use this knowledge not for building up but for tearing down. So that we may believe, with regard to you, the prophecy of that blessed Gregory whose name you claimed for yourself, when he said: "From the abundance of his subjects..."

units.la: 2. Et nos quidem hæc omnia sustinuimus, dum Apostolicæ Sedis honorem conservare studuimus, sed humilitatem nostram timorem fore intellexisti; ideoque in ipsam Regiam potestatem nobis à Deo concessam exurgere non timuisti, quam te à nobis auferre ausus es minari, quasi nos à te regnum acceperimus, quasi in tua & non in Dei manu sit Regnum vel Imperium. Quia Dominus noster Iesus Christus nos ad Regnum, te autem non vocavit ad Sacerdotium. Tu enim his gradibus ascendisti, scilicet astutia & fraude, quodque Monachica professio abominatur, pecunia favorem, favore ferrum, ferro Sedem pacis adisti, & de Sede pacis pacem turbasti, dum subditos in Prælatos armasti, dum Episcopos nostros à Deo vocatos tu non vocatus spernendos docuisti; dum Laicis ministerium eorum super Sacerdotes usurpasti, ut ipsi deponant vel condemnent, qui ipsos de manu Domini per impositionem manuum Episcoporum docendos acceperant.
units.tr: 2. Indeed we have borne all these things while we strove to preserve the honour of the Apostolic See, but you understood that our humility was fear. Therefore you did not fear to rise up against the royal power itself, which God has granted us, and you have dared to threaten to take it from us, as if we had received the kingdom from you, as if the kingdom or empire lay in your hand and not in God's. For our Lord Jesus Christ called us to the kingdom, but He did not call you to the priesthood. For you climbed up by these steps, namely by craft and fraud, and what monastic profession abhors: you reached the See of peace by money, by favour the sword, by the sword the See of peace; and from the See of peace you have disturbed the peace, while you armed subjects against prelates, while you taught that our bishops, called by God, are to be despised by you who were not called; while you usurped for laymen the ministry over priests, so that they might depose and condemn those who had received from the hand of the Lord, through the imposition of the bishops' hands, the right to teach.

units.la: 3. Me quoque (licet indignus inter Christianos sim ad Regnum unctus) tetigisti, quem sanctorum Patrum traditio soli Deo judicandum docuit; nec pro aliquo crimine, nisi à fide (quod absit) exorbitaverimus, deponendum coaslervit. Ipse verò quid verus Papa beatus Petrus clamat? Deum timete, Regem honorificate. Tu autem, quia Deum non times, me contitutum ejus inhonoras. Unde beatus Paulus, ubi Angelo de cœlo, alia si prædicaverit, non pepercit, te quoque in terris alia docentem non excepit. Aitenim: Si quis vel ego, vel Angelus de cœlo, praeter id quod evangelizavimus vobis, evangelizagelizaverit, anathema sit. Tu igitur hoc anathemate, & omnium Episcoporum nostrorum & nostro iudicio damnatus, descende, vendicatam tibi Sedem Apostolicam relinque; alius in solium beati Petri ascendat, qui nulla violentiam religione palliet, sed beati Petri sanam doctrinam doceat.
units.tr: 3. You have also touched me, though I am unworthy among Christians and anointed to the kingdom, whom the tradition of the holy Fathers has taught can be judged by God alone, and who may not be deposed for any crime unless we have strayed from the faith (which God forbid). But what does the true Pope, the blessed Peter, cry out? "Fear God, honour the king." But you, because you do not fear God, dishonour me, His appointee. Hence the blessed Paul, who did not spare the angel from heaven if he should preach otherwise, did not exempt you either, teaching otherwise on earth. For he says: "If anyone, even I or an angel from heaven, should preach to you a gospel other than what we have preached to you, let him be accursed." You, therefore, condemned by this anathema and by the judgment of all our bishops and of ourselves, descend; leave the Apostolic See which you have claimed for yourself. Let another ascend the throne of the blessed Peter, one who will not cloak violence under religion, but will teach the sound doctrine of the blessed Peter.

units.la: Ego Henricus Rex Dei gratia, cum omnibus Episcopis nostris dicimus; Descende, Descende.
units.tr: I, Henry, King by the grace of God, together with all our bishops, say: Descend, descend.

units.la: HENRICI IV. IMPERATORIS AVG. EDICTUM AD CLERVM POPVLVMQVE ROMANVM, ut à Papæ obedientia recedant, ex Comitiis Brixinensibus.
units.tr: Edict of the Emperor Henry IV to the Clergy and People of Rome, that they withdraw from obedience to the Pope, issued from the Assembly at Brixen.

units.la: Henricus Dei gratia Rex, universæ sanctæ Romanæ Ecclesiæ Clero & Populo gratiam & omne bonum.
units.tr: Henry, King by the grace of God, to the whole clergy and people of the holy Roman Church: grace and every blessing.

units.la: Hæc fides firma & inconcussa creditur, quæ semper & eadem & præsenti servatur sententi, nec diuturna ejus, cum debetur, absentia nec longi temporis tædio immutatur. Quam talem nobis servare scimus, & gratias agimus: & ut eadem perseveret, petimus, videlicet ut (sicut facie micis nostris amici, inimicis nostris inimici jugiter existatis. Inter quos scilicet Hildebrandum Monachum notantes, vos in ejus inimicitiam excitamus, quod hunc & Ecclesiæ invasorem & oppressorem & Romanæ Reipubl. vel Regni nostri insidiatorem comprehendimus, ut in subsequenti epistola à nobis directa pernoscere in promptu est.
units.tr: This faith is believed to be firm and unshaken, one that is always kept the same and in the same judgment, and that, when it is owed, is not changed by long absence or by the weariness of a long time. We know that you keep it thus toward us, and we give thanks; and that it may continue the same, we ask that, just as you are always friends to our friends, so you may be enemies to our enemies. Among these enemies we are noting in particular Hildebrand the monk, and we stir you up to enmity against him, because we have seized him as an invader and oppressor of the Church and a plotter against the Roman commonwealth and our kingdom, as will be readily clear from the following letter sent by us.

units.la: HENRICUS DEI GRATIA REX, HILDEBRANDO.
units.tr: HENRY, BY THE GRACE OF GOD KING, TO HILDEBRAND.

units.la: Quum hactenus à te ea, quæ sunt Patris, expectarem, tibique in omnibus magni fidelium strorum indignatione obedirem; recepi à te vicissitudinem, qualem oportebat ab eo, qui regnique nostri perniciosissimus hostis esset. Nam quum primum omnem hæreditariam gnitatem, quæ mihi ab illa Sede Apostolica debebatur, superbo ausu rapuisses; longius inde progressus, regnum Italiæ pessimis artibus alienare tentasti. Neque hoc contentus, in reverendissimos episcopos, qui nobis velut dulcissima membra uniti sunt, manum mittere non timuisti, eoque sinus injuriis acerbissimisque contumeliis contra divina & humana jura (ut ipsi ajunt) exagitasti omnia quum ego quadam patientia dissimularem, tu hoc non patientiam sed ignaviam æstimans ipsum caput insurgere ausus es, mandans quæ nosti, scilicet (ut tuis verbis utar) quod aut tu moriere, aut mihi animam aut regnum tolleres. Hanc inauditam contumaciam ego non verbis sed rebus condam dijudicans, generalem conventum omnium Regni Primatum, ipsis supplicantibus, habui. Quum ea quæ hactenus metu & reverentia tacebantur, in medium deducta fuissent, veris allegationibus illorum, quas ex ipsorum literis audies, palam factum est, te nullatenus in Apostolica sede posse sistere. Quorum sententiæ, quod justa & probabilis coram Deo hominibusque videbatur, ego quoque assentiens omne tibi Papatus jus, quod habere vilius es, abrenuntio, atque ut à sede II. bis, cujus Patriciatus, Deo tribuente, & jurato Romanorum assensu, debetur, descendas edicto.
units.tr: Since hitherto I had looked for from you the things that belong to a father, and had obeyed you in all things, to the great indignation of my faithful subjects, I have received from you a return such as was fitting from one who is the most pernicious enemy of my kingdom. For when first you had with proud audacity snatched away all the hereditary dignity that was owed to me by that Apostolic See, you went further from there and tried by the worst arts to alienate the kingdom of Italy. Not content with this, you did not fear to lay hands on the most reverend bishops, who are united to us like most dear limbs, and so with injuries and most bitter insults, against divine and human law (as they themselves say), you have harassed them all. While I was overlooking this with a certain patience, you, judging it not patience but cowardice, dared to rise up against the head itself, sending the message you know, namely (to use your own words) that either you must die, or you will take away my soul or my kingdom. Judging this unheard-of insolence not by words but by deeds, I held a general assembly of all the princes of the kingdom, at their request. When those things that had hitherto been kept silent out of fear and reverence were brought into the open, by the true accusations of those men, which you will hear from their own letters, it was made plain that you can in no way stand in the Apostolic See. To their judgment, since it seemed just and credible before God and men, I too assent, and I renounce for you every right of the papacy that you may have, and by this edict I command you to descend from the see of Rome, to which the patriciate is owed by God's grant and by the sworn assent of the Romans.

units.la: HVCVSQVE EPISTOLA.
units.tr: HITHERTO THE LETTER.

units.la: 2. Hæc series nostræ epistolæ ad Hildebrandum Monachum. Quam idcirco & vobis mus, ut & vobis nostra voluntas, & nobis, immo Deo & nobis vestra satisfaciat caritas. Exurge in eum fidelissimi, & sit primus in fide primus in ejus damnatione. Non autem, ut languinem datis, dicimus (quippe quum major tibi sit post depositionem pœna, vita quam mors nolit, descendere cogatis, & alium communi omnium Episcoporum & veltro consilio à nobis electum in Apostolicam Sedem recipiatis, qui, quod iste in Ecclesia vulneravit, curare velit & possit.
units.tr: 2. This is the substance of our letter to Hildebrand the monk. We have sent it to you for this reason: that our will may satisfy you, and your charity may satisfy us, or rather God and us. Rise up against him, most faithful ones, and let the first in faith be the first in his condemnation. We do not say this so that you shed blood (since, for him, after deposition, a greater punishment is to live than to die, which he would not want), but so that you compel him to descend, and receive into the Apostolic See another elected by us with the common counsel of all the bishops and of yourselves, one who will be willing and able to heal what this man has wounded in the Church.

units.la: HERMANNI REGIS ROMANO- RUM JURAMENTUM,
units.tr: The Oath of Hermann, King of the Romans,

units.la: Principibus Imperii præstitum in electione.
units.tr: Sworn to the princes of the Empire at his election.

units.la: Ab hac hora & deinceps fidelis ero per rectam fidem, beato Petro Apostolo, ejusque Vicario beato Gregorio, qui nunc in carne vivit; & quodcunque ipse mihi præcepit, sub his verbis, PER VERAM OBEDIENTIAM, fideliter, sicut oportet Christianum, observabo.
units.tr: From this hour onward I will be faithful, in the true faith, to the blessed Peter the Apostle and to his Vicar, the blessed Gregory, who now lives in the flesh; and whatever he commands me under these words, BY TRUE OBEDIENCE, I will faithfully observe, as becomes a Christian.

units.la: 2. De ordinatione vero Ecclesiarum, & de tertiis, vel Censu, quæ Constantinus Imperator vel Carolus sancto Petro dederunt, & de omnibus Ecclesiis, vel prædiis, quæ Apostolicæ Sedi ... quibus viris vel mulieribus aliquo tempore sunt oblata, vel concessa, & in mea sunt vel fuerint potestate. ita conveniam cum Papa, ut periculum schismatis, & perditionem animæ meæ non incurram, & Deo sanctoq; Petro, adjuvante Christo, dignum honorem & utilitatem impendam.
units.tr: 2. Concerning the ordering of the churches, and concerning the tithes or the census which the Emperor Constantine or Charles gave to St Peter, and concerning all the churches or estates which have at any time been offered or granted to the Apostolic See by men or women, and which are or shall be in my power, I will so come to terms with the Pope that I do not incur the danger of schism or the ruin of my soul, and that, with Christ helping, I will render due honour and advantage to God and to St Peter.

units.la: 3. Et eo die, quando illum primitus vidi, fideliter per manus meas miles sancti Petri & illius efficiar.
units.tr: 3. And on the day when I first see him, I will become, through my hands, a faithful soldier of St Peter and of him.

units.la: HENRICI IV. IMPERATORIS AUG. RESCRIPTUM
units.tr: Letter of the Emperor Henry IV

units.la: DE RECEPTIONE CLEMENTIS PAPAE, ET Rejectione Hildebrandi Antipapæ.
units.tr: On the reception of Pope Clement, and the rejection of Hildebrand the antipope.

units.la: EX Henricus Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator Semper Augustus Theodorico * Episcopo dilectionem nulli majorem. In primis te scire volumus, quia nulli melius, quàm tibi, confidimus, nec Episcopum Trajectensem fidei monitorem, sed ad honorem Regni tractandum tibi misisse cooperatorem. Deinde ad singula, quæ mandasti, negotia, singula damus responsa, sed brevissima, quia infinita tibi reservamus ore ad os dicenda.
units.tr: Henry, by the grace of God Emperor of the Romans, ever Augustus, to Theoderic, bishop, love greater than any. First, we wish you to know that we trust no one more than you, and we have sent you the bishop of Utrecht not as a monitor of faith but as a colleague in managing the honour of the kingdom. Then, to each of the matters you commanded, we give a single reply, but a very brief one, since we reserve for you the infinite things to be said face to face.

units.la: 2. Sed quidem hoc, quod in margine epistolæ tuæ de Romano negotio nobis mandasti, in primis tibi dicimus: Romani in die S. Benedicti intravimus. Qualiter à Romanis recepti sumus, qualiter cum Romanis stetimus, qualiter à Romanis recessimus, ab aliis multis te audisse credimus. Tum etiam litteris nostris tibi indicamus, quas te nondum vidisse putamus: sed etiam malumus alio quàm nostro ore te rescisse, quæ nobis Dominus fecit. Incredibile enim videtur, quod verissimum probatur, quod factum est in Roma, ut ita dicam, cum decem hominibus, in nobis operatus est Dominus, quod antecessores nostri si fecissent cum decem militibus, miraculum omnibus esset. Nam cum in Theutonicas partes de acquirenda Roma jam desperantes redire vellemus, ecce Romani nuntiis Legatis, ut Romam intraremus, rogaverunt, seque in omnibus nobis obedituros promiserunt, quod & fecerunt. Summo namque gaudio nos incantes receperunt, summo studio secum manentes adjuverunt, summo triumpho & fide ab eis recedentes prosecuti sunt, in tantum ut in Domino fiducialiter dicamus, quia tota Roma in manu nostra est, excepto illo castello, in quo inclusus est Hildebrand, scilicet in domo Crescentii.
units.tr: 2. But as for what you commanded us in the margin of your letter concerning the Roman affair, we first tell you this: we entered Rome on the day of St Benedict. How we were received by the Romans, how we stood with the Romans, how we withdrew from the Romans, we believe you have heard from many others. We also indicate it to you in our letter, which we think you have not yet seen; but we would rather you learned of what the Lord has done for us from our own mouth. For it seems incredible, yet it is proved most true, that what was done in Rome, so to speak, with ten men, the Lord worked through us; what our predecessors would have done with ten soldiers would have been a miracle to everyone. For when we were about to return to the German lands, despairing of winning Rome, behold, the Romans, through their envoys, asked us to enter Rome, and promised that they would obey us in all things, which they also did. Indeed they received us with the greatest joy, aided us with the greatest zeal while we remained among them, and followed us as we departed with the greatest honour and loyalty; so much so that we can confidently say in the Lord that all Rome is in our hand, except that castle in which Hildebrand is shut up, namely in the house of Crescentius.

units.la: 3. Quem Hildebrandum legali omnium Cardinalium ac totius populi Romani judicio scias rejectum, & elatum Papam nostrum Clementem in Sede Apostolica sublimatum, omnium Romanorum acclamatione, nosque à Papa Clemente ordinatum, & consensu omnium Romanorum consecratum in die sancto Paschæ Imperatorem, totius populi exultatione.
units.tr: 3. You should know that Hildebrand was rejected by the lawful judgement of all the cardinals and of the whole Roman people, and that our Pope Clement was raised up and installed in the Apostolic See by the acclamation of all the Romans; and that we were ordained by Pope Clement and, with the consent of all the Romans, consecrated Emperor on the holy day of Easter, to the exultation of the whole people.
