units.la: 4. His itaque factis benedictione Dei & S. Petri omnium gaudio à Roma recessimus, & quanquam possumus ad has partes propetamus: & in via reditus invenit nos tuus nuncius. Gaudeant, qui velint; doleant, qui velint: nos, Deo propitio, assumus.
units.tr: 4. Thus, with these things done, by the blessing of God and St Peter, we departed from Rome amid the joy of all, and although we are hastening to these parts, on the return journey your messenger found us. Let those who wish rejoice; let those who wish grieve: we, by God's favour, are here.

units.la: 5. Dominus ille quid agat, scire non curamus, sed quod tu monuisti, libenter, ne nobis dampnum accidat, providebimus. De Saxonibus verò, de Salzburgensi Archiepiscopo, de Comite Adelberto, de aliis ad nos redire volentibus, id tibi respondemus, quia consiliis tuis libenter acquiescimus, ut tantummodo pax vera fiat in nostris temporibus, videlicet ut fideles sint, cum ad nos redierint.
units.tr: 5. We do not care to know what that lord is doing, but what you have advised we will gladly provide for, lest any loss befall us. As for the Saxons, the archbishop of Salzburg, Count Adalbert, and others who wish to return to us, we answer you thus: since we gladly accede to your counsels, so that true peace may come about in our times, namely that they be faithful when they have returned to us.

units.la: 6. Tu autem si non gravaris facere quod volumus, Augustam ad nos venire post festum Apostolorum Petri & Pauli rogamus, quia Deo volente in festivitate eorum Ratisponæ erimus. Studeas ergo ad nos venire, ut tuo adventu possis lætificare.
units.tr: 6. If you do not mind doing what we wish, we ask you to come to Augsburg to us after the feast of the Apostles Peter and Paul, since, God willing, we shall be at Regensburg on their feast day. Therefore take care to come to us, so that by your coming you may gladden us.

units.la: 7. Insuper mandat tibi Apostolicus Clemens & Imperator HENRICUS, ut sicut nos diligas, Archiepiscopum Treverensem consecrare properes. Vale.
units.tr: 7. Furthermore, the Apostolic Clement and the Emperor Henry instruct you, that as you love us, you should hasten to consecrate the archbishop of Trier. Farewell.

units.la: HERMANNI REGIS ROM- ANORUM ET PRINCIPUM IMPERII RECESSUS
units.tr: Recess of Hermann, King of the Romans and Princes of the Empire

units.la: COMITIORUM GOSLARIENSIUM, DE ABDICATIONE HENRICI IV. Imperatoris.
units.tr: The Diet of Goslar, concerning the abdication of Henry IV, Emperor.

units.la: HERMANNUS Rex Nativitatem Domini Goslarę celebravit, ad quem Ostiensis Episcopus Apostolici Legatus post Epiphaniam pervenit in Saxoniam, & Colloquio interfuit, quod Saxones contra HEINRICI fautores condixerunt, ut hoc illis probarent, se jure HEINRICUM ut excommunicatum. Quod & facto Colloquio, decimo quinto post Epiphaniam, firmissimè approbaverunt: ea videlicet ratione, quia Romanus Pontifex illum eis à se in Romana Synodo anathematisatum, literis denunciavit.
units.tr: Hermann the King celebrated the Lord's Nativity at Goslar. The Bishop of Ostia, the Apostolic Legate, came into Saxony after the Epiphany and took part in a conference, which the Saxons had arranged against the supporters of Henry, in order to prove to them that they were right in holding Henry to be excommunicated. This they most firmly approved at the conference held on the fifteenth day after the Epiphany, for the reason that the Roman Pontiff had notified them by letter that he had anathematized Henry in the Roman Synod.

units.la: 2. Adversari autem eis objecerunt, quod Papa cum nequiverit excommunicare, eò quòd excommunicari non potuerit vocari, judicari, sive damnari. Ad hæc Saxones responderunt, se judicium Sedis Apostolicæ nec debere retractare, nec posse; hoc cum illo potius tractandum, qui illum damnaverit, cum Saxonibus, quòd damnationi ejus non interfuerunt, qui Sedis Apostolicæ judicio nullam retractationem, sed obedientiam debuerint. Ita ergo soluto Colloquio discessum est ab invicem. A- anno Domini M LXXXV.
units.tr: Moreover, the opponents objected to them that the Pope, since he could not excommunicate him because he could not be called, judged or condemned, had no such power. To this the Saxons replied that they neither ought nor were able to call into question the judgment of the Apostolic See; this matter was rather to be dealt with by him who had condemned Henry, and not by the Saxons, who had not taken part in his condemnation and who owed obedience, not re-examination, to the judgment of the Apostolic See. So the conference was ended and the parties separated from one another. In the year of the Lord 1085.

units.la: DECRETA COMITIORVM QVEDELNBVR GENSIVM DE ANNO MLXXXV.
units.tr: Decrees of the Assembly at Quedlinburg of the Saxons, in the Year 1085.

units.la: HERMANNVS Rex in Quintilineburg Pascha celebravit, ubi & Legatus domini Apostolici ipsa Paschali hebdomada, generalem synodum cum Archiepiscopis, Episcopis & Abbatibus S.Petri fidelibus, solenniter celebravit. Interfuit autem huic Synodo, Gebhardus revera simus Juvavien sis Archiepiscopus, item venerabilis Hartwigus Magdeburgensis Archiepiscopus, cum suis suffraganeis. item suffraganei Moguntinae sedis de Saxonia. Nam V Virceburgensis & V Wormatiensis, Augustensis quoq; & Constantiensis de Alemannia, quia ipsi canonica necessitate impediti, venire non potuerunt, per legationem suam se S.Concilio repraesentaverunt, seq; per omnia dem synodi statutis assensuros, mandaverunt. Rex etiam Hermannus cum suis Principibus Synodo interfuit.
units.tr: King Hermann celebrated Easter at Quedlinburg, where the legate of the Apostolic See, during that same Easter week, solemnly held a general synod with the archbishops, bishops and abbots faithful to St Peter. Taking part in this synod were Gebhard, truly archbishop of Salzburg [Juvavia], and the venerable Hartwig, archbishop of Magdeburg, with his suffragans, as well as the suffragans of the see of Mainz from Saxony. Bishops V of Würzburg and V of Worms, and likewise those of Augsburg and Constance from Alemannia, being prevented by canonical necessity from coming, sent a legation to represent them at the holy council, and instructed it that they would assent to all the decrees of the synod. King Hermann also took part in the synod with his princes.

units.la: 1. Cum ergo omnes juxta ordinem suum consedissent, prolata sunt in medium decreta sanctorum Patrum, de primatu sedis Apostolicae, quod nulli unquam liceat ejus judicium retractare, et ejus judicio judicare. Quod de totius synodi publica professione laudatum & confirmatum est, contra Heinricianos, qui fideles S.Petri constringere voluerunt, ut excommunicationem de Papae Gregorii, super Heinricum cum illis retractare praesumerent.
units.tr: 1. When all had taken their seats according to their rank, the decrees of the holy Fathers concerning the primacy of the Apostolic See were brought forward, namely that no one may ever be permitted to call in question its judgment, or to pass judgment on its judgment. This was praised and confirmed by the public profession of the whole synod, against the Henricians, who wished to bind the faithful of St Peter so that they would presume to call in question with them the excommunication of Henry pronounced by Pope Gregory.

units.la: 3. Quidam autem Babenbergensis clericus nomine Gumbertus, Romani Pontificis primatum detogare volens, in mediam synodum se contulit, asserens, Romanos Pontifices hunc sibi primatum asserpuisse, non aliunde concessum hereditasse, videlicet, ut nullius de eorum judicio judicare debeat, nec illi alicujus judicio subjaceant. Qui cum aperte à tota synodo confutatus esset, praecipue tamen a quodam laico convictus est, per illud Evangelicum: Non est discipulus supra magistrum. Cum enim hoc generaliter in omnibus ecclesiasticis ordinibus observandum deputetur, ne major a minore judicetur, hoc Vicario S.Petri denegare potuit, quem omnes Catholici pro domino & magistro venerantur.
units.tr: 3. Now a certain clergyman of Bamberg named Gumbert, wishing to detract from the primacy of the Roman Pontiff, came forward into the midst of the synod, asserting that the Roman Pontiffs had seized this primacy for themselves and had not inherited it as granted from elsewhere, namely that no one ought to judge of their judgment, nor should they be subject to the judgment of anyone. When he had been openly refuted by the whole synod, he was especially convicted by a certain layman, by that Gospel saying: "The disciple is not above the teacher" [Matt. 10.24]. For since this is to be observed generally in all ecclesiastical orders, that the greater not be judged by the lesser, he could not deny this to the Vicar of St Peter, whom all Catholics revere as lord and master.

units.la: 4. In eadem synodo ordinatio V Vecilonis, Moguntini invasoris, & Sigefridi Augustensis & Norberti Curiensis, imo omnes ordinationes & consecrationes excommunicatorum, penitus judicatae sunt, juxta decretum sanctorum Patrum Innocentii, Leonis primi, Pelagii, atque ejus successoris Gregorii primi.
units.tr: 4. In the same synod the ordination of V Vecilo, the Mainz intruder, and of Sigefrid of Augsburg and Norbert of Chur, indeed all ordinations and consecrations performed by excommunicates, were utterly condemned, in accordance with the decrees of the holy Fathers Innocent, Leo I, Pelagius, and his successor Gregory I.

units.la: 5. Item secta praedicti V Vecilonis ejusq; sociorum, sub anathemate damnata est, quae asserunt, culares suis rebus exspoliatos ecclesiastico non subjacere judicio, nec excommunicari posse, ipsos excessibus: quaeque excommunicatos absque reconciliatione recipi posse, contendit.
units.tr: 5. Likewise the sect of the aforesaid V Vecilo and his associates was condemned under anathema; this sect asserted that laymen stripped of their goods are not subject to ecclesiastical judgment, nor can they be excommunicated for their offences, and it maintained that excommunicates may be received without reconciliation.

units.la: 6. Statutum autem est ibi, ut quicunq; ab Episcopo suo, nec officio nec communione privatus excommunicatus esset, etsi injuste; nullatenus tamen reciperetur ad communionem, nisi absolutus ecclesiastico more. Similiter & pro sacrilegio excommunicatos decrevit sancta synodus non recipiendos, absq; solita reconciliatione, & nisi dudum, quae sacrilege sibi vendicaverant, reddidissent. Eadem synodo, Presbyteris, Diaconibus, Subdiaconibus, perpetua, juxta decretum sanctorum Patrum indicta est continentia.
units.tr: 6. It was also decreed there that whoever had been excommunicated by his bishop, deprived of office and of communion, even if unjustly, should in no way be received back into communion unless absolved in the ecclesiastical manner. Similarly the holy synod decreed that those excommunicated for sacrilege are not to be received without the customary reconciliation, and unless they have first restored what they had claimed for themselves by sacrilege. In the same synod, perpetual continence was enjoined on priests, deacons and subdeacons, in accordance with the decree of the holy Fathers.

units.la: 7. Item statutum est, ne laici pallas altaris & sacra vasa contingant.
units.tr: 7. It was also decreed that laymen shall not touch the altar cloths and the sacred vessels.

units.la: 8. Item, ne laici decimas sibi vindicent in proprietatem, nec etiam in beneficium, nisi concessione legitimorum possessorum.
units.tr: 8. Likewise, that laymen shall not claim tithes for themselves as property, nor even as a benefice, except by grant of the lawful possessors.

units.la: 9. Item, ut vernum jejunium in prima hebdomada Quadragesimae, aestivum in Pentecoste celebretur.
units.tr: 9. Likewise, that the spring fast be observed in the first week of Lent, and the summer fast at Pentecost.

units.la: 10. Item, ne quis Caseum & ova comedat in Quadragesima.
units.tr: 10. Likewise, that no one shall eat cheese and eggs in Lent.

units.la: 11. Item synodali judicio confirmata & laudata est ordinatio domini Gebehardi Constantiensis Episcopi, imo omnia quae praefatus sedis Apostolicae legatus, cum esset Constantiae ordinavit.
units.tr: 11. Likewise, by the judgment of the synod, the ordinance of Lord Gebhard, bishop of Constance, was confirmed and praised, indeed everything that the aforesaid legate of the Apostolic See had ordained while he was at Constance.

units.la: 12. Item, ibi mota est quaestio, de consanguinitate Regis & uxoris suae. Unde & Rex in synodo surrexit, seq; de hac re judicium S.Synodi, per omnia observaturum professus est. Sanctae ut dus hanc causam in praesenti canonice examinari non posse judicavit, eo quod legitimi accusatores non.
units.tr: 12. Likewise, the question was raised there concerning the consanguinity of the King and his wife. Whereupon the King also rose in the synod and professed that he would observe in all things the judgment of the holy synod on this matter. The holy synod judged that this case could not be canonically examined at present, because there were no lawful accusers.

units.la: 13. In fine autem synodi sententia anathematis cum ardentibus candelis promulgata est, in Grudum haereticharchâ, sedis Apostolicae pervasore, & in apostatas S.Petri, Hugone Albanensem, Johannem Porruensem Episcopos Petrum Excancellarium. item in Leomarum Bremensem, Utonem Hildesheimensem, Ottonem Constantiensem, Burchardum Basiliensem, Huzmannum Spirensem, Eberhardum Episcopos. item in V Vecilonem Moguntinum invasorem, Sigefridum Augustensem, Norbertum Curiensem, in hos (inquam) & in omnes eorum complices, inevitabilis sententia anathematis promulgata est. Subscripserunt per se aut per Legatos suos: Hermannus Rex Romanorum. Otto Monachus Cluniacensis, Legatus Gregorii Papae. Gebhardus Salisburgensis, | Archiepiscopi. Hardwicus Maydenburgensis, | Archiepiscopi. Adalberto V Virtzburgensis, | Altmannus Bathavensis, | Bernardus Merseburgensis, | Episcopi. Guntherus Ciricensis, | Bennio Moelianus, | Albernu.
units.tr: 13. At the end of the synod the sentence of anathema was proclaimed, with lighted candles, against Grudus, the heretical archbishop, usurper of the Apostolic See, and against the apostates from St Peter: the bishops Hugh of Albano, John of Porto, Peter the former chancellor; also against Liemar of Bremen, Udo of Hildesheim, Otto of Constance, Burchard of Basel, Huzmann of Speyer and Eberhard, bishops. Likewise against V Vecilo, the Mainz intruder, Sigefrid of Augsburg and Norbert of Chur; against these (I say) and all their accomplices, an inevitable sentence of anathema was proclaimed. They subscribed, either in person or through their legates: Hermann, King of the Romans; Otto, monk of Cluny, legate of Pope Gregory; Gebhard of Salzburg, archbishop; Hartwig of Magdeburg, archbishop; Adalbert of Würzburg, Altmann of Passau, Bernard of Merseburg, bishops; Gunther of Zeitz, Bennio of Meissen, Alberno.

units.la: Albertus Vangionus, Burckhardus Halberstarensis, Hermannus Mediomatricus, Reginardus Mindensis, Wigoldus Augustanus, Gebhardus Constantiensis,Heinricus Bambergensis,
units.tr: Albert of Worms, Burchard of Halberstadt, Hermann of Metz, Reginhard of Minden, Wigold of Augsburg, Gebhard of Constance, Henry of Bamberg.

units.la: Eckbertus Marchuo Saxonum Brunovicensium. Heinricus Craflus, filius Ottonis Ducis Bavariæ. Conradus Comes à Beuchlingen.
units.tr: Eckbert, margrave of the Saxon Brunswickers; Henry Kraft, son of Duke Otto of Bavaria; Conrad, Count of Beuchlingen.

units.la: DECRETA COMITIORUM MOGUNTI- NENSIUM ANNO DOMINI MLXXXV.
units.tr: DECREES OF THE DIET OF MAINZ IN THE YEAR OF OUR LORD 1085.

units.la: MENSE Majo Moguntiæ, ubi constitutum fuerat, Heinricus Imperator, Proceres, Duces, frequentes coeunt. Item Petrus Portuensis Episcopus, duo Flaminès Romani, Legati Clementis Tertii Pontificis Maximi Archiepiscopi hi atque minores Pontifices Galliæ, Germaniæ, Wezilo Moguntinus, Angelbertus Trevirensis, Segivinus Agrippinensis, Luitmarus Bremensis, Theodericus Virdunensis, Heinricus Leodiensis, Conradus Trajectensis, Udalricus Aichstetensis, Meginardus Fruxinensis, Otto Reginoburgensis, Rupertus Bambergensis, Hermannus Spirensis, Otto Constantiensis, Burckhardus Lofaniensis, Sigefridus Augustanus, Gebhardus Pragensis, Uto Hildeshaymensis, Hainricus Badeborniensis, Erpho Monasteriensis, Volckmarus Mindensis, Bibo Tullensis, Burckhardus Basilensis, Otto Argentoratensis,
units.tr: In May at Mainz, where it had been appointed, the Emperor Henry, the nobles and the dukes gathered in large numbers. Likewise present were Peter, bishop of Porto, two Roman flamens, legates of Pope Clement III, the Supreme Pontiff, and these archbishops and lesser bishops of Gaul and Germany: Wezilo of Mainz, Angelbert of Trier, Segivin of Cologne, Luitmar of Bremen, Theoderic of Verdun, Henry of Liège, Conrad of Utrecht, Ulrich of Eichstätt, Meginhard of Fulda, Otto of Regensburg, Rupert of Bamberg, Hermann of Speyer, Otto of Constance, Burchard of Lausanne, Siegfried of Augsburg, Gebhard of Prague, Uto of Hildesheim, Henry of Paderborn, Erpho of Münster, Volkmar of Minden, Bibo of Toul, Burchard of Basel, Otto of Strasbourg.

units.la: Conveniunt. Adsunt Legati aliorum Pontificum Galliæ, Italiæ, Germaniæ. Communi consensu Hildebrandi secta pietati Christianæ repugnans, explosa, exibitata est. Ottonem, qui & Urbanus, superbi Parres, sacrilegii, irreligiositatis accusant, convincunt, in numero impiorum computant. Superque Conciliabuli quatuordecim Episcopos albo Pontificum eradunt, senatu Sacerdotum more perduellionis, perjurii, perfidiæ, homicidii, parricidii, eosdem condemnant. Hermannum Ren, Heribertum Saxonem, Velphonem Bojum, proscribunt, eadem censura devovent. Senatusconsultum penitus tale: Devora capita, quæ numeravimus, velut contagio ab omnibus vitentur Christianis; quidem à nobis secessione fecerunt, non nos ab illis. Ad concionem sacram, quemadmodum profligere, venire derrectant; pietatem Christianam polluunt; concordiam contaminant; ovibus deserris ad Reipublicæ profugiunt; ad bella, incendia, homicidia, parricidia, latrocinia, rapinas non solùm amantur, verum etiam duces sunt. Crebrò benignè vocati, reverti noluerunt; versutos, obscuros, vafros se esse factis produnt, & nos experimentis sentimus. Egregii sanè pastores, quibus tuum credetis. Nemo oves persequitur, nullo viso lupo ramen fugiunt. Quidnam delignas-fortuna ad tempora Domitiani Decii, servaslet?
units.tr: They assembled, and legates of the other pontiffs of Gaul, Italy and Germany were present. By common consent the faction of Hildebrand, which is repugnant to Christian piety, was cast out and banished. They accuse and convict Otto, who is also called Urban, a proud man, of sacrilege and irreligion, and count him among the impious. Moreover, they strike fourteen bishops of the conventicle from the roll of pontiffs, and, after the manner of a senate of priests, condemn the same men of treason, perjury, treachery, homicide and parricide. They proscribe Hermann Ren, Heribert the Saxon and Welf the Bavarian, and devote them to the same censure. The decree runs thus: "The cursed heads whom we have named are to be shunned by all Christians as a contagion. They have separated themselves from us, not we from them. They refuse to come to holy sermons; they pollute Christian piety, they contaminate concord, and, having deserted their sheep, they flee to the civil government. They are not only lovers of war, arson, homicide, parricide, robbery and plunder, but even their leaders. Though often kindly called, they have refused to return. By their deeds they show themselves crafty, shifty and sly, and we have felt it by experience. Truly fine ministers, to whom you would entrust your flock! No one pursues the sheep, yet with no wolf in sight they flee. What would have become of them had fortune preserved them for the times of Domitian and Decius?"

units.la: In eodem Concilio Pragensis dicio, ficur ab Imperatore Ottone Secundo, Benedicto Octavo Pontifice Maximo, consensu D. V Volfigangi Reginoburgensis Episcopi institutura fuerat, certis limitibus cuncta, in quibus Cracovia quoq; comprehendi repetitur. Clemens Papa arq; Heinricus Augustus diploma dederunt.
units.tr: In the same council, the Bohemian territory, as it had been established by Emperor Otto II with the consent of Pope Benedict VIII and with the approval of the lord Wolfgang, bishop of Regensburg, is again declared to be comprised within fixed boundaries, in which Kraków too is included. Pope Clement and Emperor Henry gave a diploma to this effect.

units.la: Wladislaus quoq; Bojemiæ atq; Poloniæ Rex constituius est. Ipsum cum uxore Swatava, Pragæ xvii. Julii, Angelbertus Archiepiscopus Treverorum jussu Cæsaris inauguravit, acclamante Senatu, Equitatu, populoq; Bojemo: Vratislavo pacifico Bojemiæ atq; Poloniæ Regi, à Deo coronato, vita, latus, victoria.
units.tr: Wratislaw was also appointed king of Bohemia and Poland. At Prague, on 17 July, Archbishop Angelbert of Trier, by order of the Emperor, invested him with his wife Svatava, while the senate, the cavalry and the Bohemian people acclaimed: "To Wratislaw, the peaceful king of Bohemia and Poland, crowned by God: life, joy, victory!"

units.la: RECESSUS COMITIORUM ULMENSIUM, CUJUS DECRETA HISCE VERBIS REF- ERT BERTHOLDUS CON- STANTIENSIS in Chronic. Anno MXCIII.
units.tr: Recess of the Diet of Ulm, whose decrees Berthold of Constance sets out in these words in his Chronicle, in the year 1093.

units.la: E B E H A R D U S a Constantiensis Episcopus, & Apostolicæ Sedis Legatus, V Velphonem Bajoariæ permanus in Militem accepit, sicut & proprium fratrem Bertholdum D Alemanniæ jam dudum fecit. Cum quibus & reliquis Alemanniæ Principibus magnum Conventum apud Ulmam habuit.
units.tr: Ebehard, bishop of Constance and legate of the Apostolic See, received Welf into the militia in Bavaria, as he had long before done for his own brother Berthold in Alemannia. Together with these and the other princes of Alemannia he held a great assembly at Ulm.

units.la: 1. In quo Conventu firmissimè laudatum est, ut Constantiensi Episcopo omnimodè secundum statuta Canonum obediretur, & ut Duci Bertholdo & Comitibus secundum Legem Alemannorum obtemperaretur.
units.tr: 1. In this assembly it was firmly resolved that the bishop of Constance be obeyed in all things, according to the statutes of the canons, and that Duke Berthold and the counts be obeyed according to the law of the Alemanni.

units.la: 2. Deinde firmissimam pacem tam Duces quàm Comites, tam majores quàm minores jurare vituros à vii. Calend. Decembris usque in Pascha, & à Pascha in dies annos juraverunt, videlicet Monachis suis conversis & Clericis, Catholico Episcopo subjectis, Ecclesiis & earum arum, & mercatoribus, & omnibus eodem juramento obligatis: excepto c Arnoldo invasore Constantiensis Ecclesiæ, & omnibus ejus fautoribus. Hanc pacem singuli Principes, qui convenerunt, usquequaque per potestatem suam utquequaque virium jurare fecerunt.
units.tr: 2. Next, the dukes as well as the counts, the greater as well as the lesser, swore that they would keep a firm peace, from the seventh day before the Kalends of December until Easter, and from Easter onward year by year, namely for their monks who had been converted and for the clergy subject to the Catholic bishop, for the churches and their (?) and for merchants, and for all others bound by the same oath, excepting Arnold, the invader of the church of Constance, and all his supporters. Each of the princes who had assembled caused this peace to be sworn by all who were under his power, as far as each could manage.

units.la: DECRETUM COMITIORUM CONSTAN- TIENSIUM ANNO DOMINI MXCIV.
units.tr: DECREE OF THE ASSEMBLY OF CONSTANCE IN THE YEAR OF THE LORD 1094.

units.la: E B E H A R D U S Constantiensis Ecclesiæ Episcopus, magnâ Synodum Constantiæ, in Mada majore ante Pascha, cum Abbatibus & Clericis innumerabilibus, & cum prædictis Ducibus, (V Velphone Bajoariæ, & Bertholdo Alemanniæ ac Carinthiæ) & reliquis Alemanniæ Principibus canonicè celebravit, ibique multa, quæ corrigenda erant, correxit.
units.tr: Eberhard, Bishop of the Church of Constance, held a great synod at Constance, in the Mada majore, before Easter, canonically, with countless abbots and clergy and with the aforesaid dukes (Welf of Bavaria, and Berthold of Alemannia and Carinthia) and the other princes of Alemannia. There he corrected many things that needed correcting.

units.la: 2. Ibi etiam incontinentiam Presbyterorum & violentiam Symoniacorum adeò prohibuisset, ut etiam populum ab eorum officio sub banno prohibuisset, si ipsi in tali facinore positi comitem & jus ministrare præsumsissent.
units.tr: 2. There he also so strictly forbade the incontinence of priests and the violence of simonists that he prohibited the people, under the ban, from taking part in their office, if such men, caught in such a crime, presumed to administer the office of the count or the law.

units.la: 3. Statuit etiam ibi juxta statuta sanctorum Patrum, ut jejunium Martii in prima hebdomada Quadragesimæ, & jejunium Junii in hebdomade Pentecostes semper celebretur.
units.tr: 3. There he also decreed, in accordance with the statutes of the holy Fathers, that the fast of March in the first week of Lent and the fast of June in the week of Pentecost should always be observed.

units.la: 4. Item statuit, ut tam in hebdomada Pentecostes, quàm in hebdomada Paschali, dies festivè celebrarentur. Nam usque ad illud tempus Constantiensis Episcopatus more Commercialium non est secutus, videlicet integram septimanam in Pascha, & unum diem tantùm in Pentecoste observando: quamvis utræque septimanæ ejusdem observationis esse debuerint.
units.tr: 4. He likewise decreed that the feast days should be celebrated with solemnity both in the week of Pentecost and in the Easter week. For until that time the bishopric of Constance had followed the custom of the merchants, namely observing the whole week at Easter but only one day at Pentecost, although both weeks ought to be kept in the same way.

units.la: 5. Querimonia Praxidis a Reginæ, quæ dudum ad V Velphonè Ducem Italiæ b matrimonio cessit, ad Constantiensem Synodum pervenit.
units.tr: 5. The complaint of Queen Praxedis, who long ago was given in marriage to Welf, Duke of Italy, came before the synod of Constance.

units.la: 6. In hac Synodo venerabilis Abbas Sigefridus c de Cella sancti Salvatoris super Dunum obedientiarum suum se proclamavit, qui se & bona sua * ad aliud Monasterium libere contulit.
units.tr: 6. In this synod the venerable Abbot Sigefrid of Cella of St. Salvator above the Dunum declared himself an obedientiary, and he freely transferred himself and his goods to another monastery.

units.la: CONRADI REGIS ROMA- NORUM PACTUM CUM ROMANO PONTIFICE.
units.tr: The Compact of King Conrad of the Romans with the Roman Pontiff.

units.la: C O N R A D U S Rex, filius H E I N R I C I IV. Imperatoris, Domino Papæ Urbano, Coronam venienti, obviam progreditur, eique stratoris officium exhibuit, quarto Idus Aprilis.
units.tr: Conrad, King, son of the Emperor Henry IV, goes forward to meet Pope Urban, who was coming to receive the crown, and performed for him the office of stable-groom (leading his horse), on the fourth day before the Ides of April.

units.la: 2. Deinde fecit et fidelitatem juramento, de vita, de membris, & de Papatu Romano.
units.tr: 2. Then he also swore fealty to him, for life, for limb, and concerning the Roman papacy.

units.la: 3. Dominus autem Papa ei filium sanctæ Romanæ Ecclesiæ recepit illum, eique consilium & adjutorium ad obtinendum Regnum, & ad coronam Imperii acquirendam dari, operam pro sibi promittit, salva quidem in illis Ecclesiæ & statutis Apostolicis, maximè de investituris in spiritualibus officiis à laicis non usurpandis.
units.tr: 3. The Lord Pope, on his part, received him as a son of the holy Roman Church, and promised that he would work to have him given counsel and aid for obtaining the kingdom and for acquiring the crown of the Empire, saving indeed in these matters the liberties of the Church and the apostolic statutes, especially concerning investitures in spiritual offices, which laymen are not to usurp.

units.la: {a} Synodus Constantiensis, anno MXCIV. (Ed.)
units.tr: {a} Synod of Constance, in the year 1094. (Ed.)

units.la: DECRETVM COMITIORUM AQUISGR- ANENSIUM, DE DEPOSITIONE CONRADI REGIS Romanorum, Papæ Urbano contra Imperatorem adhærentis; & electione HAINRICI V. Regis, Anno Domi- ni MXCVI.
units.tr: Decree of the Assembly of Aachen, concerning the deposition of Conrad, King of the Romans, who adhered to Pope Urban against the Emperor; and the election of Henry V as King, in the year of our Lord 1096.

units.la: HAINRICUS IV. Cæsar Augustus, ubi filiũ CONRADUM, sibi instinctu Machthyldis Comitissæ & Urbani Papæ rebellantem, ad sanitatem reducere non potuit, VIII. Idus Januarii ad Aquas Granęas, ad Conventus Procerum Imperii agendos concedit. Ibi habito eorum, quicunque, sententiam dicere jus erat, consilio, in Senatuum verba fecit:
units.tr: When the Emperor Henry IV, Augustus Caesar, could not bring his son Conrad, who was rebelling at the instigation of Countess Matilda and Pope Urban, back to his senses, he granted, on 6 January at Aachen, that assemblies of the nobles of the Empire should be held. There, having taken the counsel of those who had the right to give an opinion, he addressed the senators as follows:

units.la: O fidelissimi civium, piissimiq; amicorum Romani Imperii Procerec, Christianæq; familiæ columen, [...] per Deum immortalem, per majestatem Imperii, per salutem & dignitatem vestram, per jurisjurandi religionem, qua nobis & Reip. astricti estis, obtestor, ut positis gratia atq; odio, in commune consulatum & Rempub. capessatis: pietatē, pacem jam pridē, factione atq; perditis paucorum terris depulsam, veteri labore vestrasq; industria reducē stabilitę: sæviorē tempestas rursus fluctibus obtruit. Me in Imperio educatum, quē Deus summus rerum arbiter, & vos Imperatorem rebus humanis imposuit, neq; hostis, sed quod fallum esse, & neminē credere percupiam, filius meus illecebris ... captus, quem genui, participē Regni feci, successorē declaravi, contra jus gentium, adversus ... & sanguinis necessitudinē, contra divinum edictum, immemor beneficiorum, oblitus ... non solum dignitatē, sed & vita privare conatur paremiem; cui vitam, dignitatē, quidquid dehabet, acceptum referat necesse est, extinguere conititur. Dux factio fœmina est: diutius, quām filius placeret, me Deus servat. Vitam, quam natura mihi donat, proles mea mihi invidet. Expectare senis recusat. Quæ sanè nostræ sunt injuriæ, nihil ad vos. Verum nunc vestrum duce fœmina occupavit regnū, vi & armis tenet. Vos in mea injuria despecti estis; vestra beneficia mihi erepta sunt; nō me, sed vos coteminit. Vestra res agitur, audaciam hominū spectate. Non opus est malis Geniis, hominum ex ... plurima mala. Uni animali hominis ambitio honoris, avaritię immensa cupido: nulli rerum major libido, nulli rabies acrior. Quid reliquū est, nisi ut cæteri omnes ab hoc quasi in loco illustri convicto exempla sibi sumant, parricidia passim impunē committant: Si ulla apud vos est memoria CONRADI ... aviq; HAINRICI parentis mei, majorumq; vestrorum, nolite pati, Imperiū vestro sanguine atq; dolore partū, per ecclesias & parricidia tabescere; per amplitudinē, salutemq; vestram, per immortalem majorum gloriam obsecro, auferte procul in ultimas terras ex Germania, victrice gentium, flagitiū hoccę, tenus inaudiū. Defensum tot civilibus prœlis orbē Romanū alterite à vitiis, scelerę immanissimo Rempub. Christianā vindicate, pœnas impietatis scelerati reddant, sentiant sacrilegi impostores, Germanicam virtutē nondum à majoribus degenerasse; vos in portū vestigiis inniti decet, terrori pessimis, bonis patrocinio esse. Quod tum fiet, si uno consensu filium meum minorem natu, majore cedera exhæredato atq; proscripto, Cæsarem declaravimus.
units.tr: O most faithful of citizens, most loyal friends of the Roman Empire, nobles, and pillar of the Christian family: I beseech you by the immortal God, by the majesty of the Empire, by your own safety and dignity, and by the sanctity of the oath by which you are bound to me and to the commonwealth, that, laying aside favour and hatred, you take up the common counsel and the good of the state; and that you restore peace, long since driven from the lands by faction and the ruin of a few, to stability by your old labour and your diligence. A fiercer storm has again overwhelmed us with its waves. I, reared in the Empire, whom the supreme God, the arbiter of human affairs, and you have placed as Emperor over human affairs, am now attacked not by an enemy (which I would most wish to be false, and believe of no one) but by my own son, whom I begot, captured by allurements ... I have made him a sharer in the kingdom and declared him my successor; yet, against the law of nations, against ... and the bond of blood, against the divine command, forgetful of benefits, and oblivious ... he tries to deprive me not only of my dignity but of my life, and he strives to extinguish the one to whom he must owe, as received from me, whatever life and dignity he has. The leader of this faction is a woman: God preserves me longer than my son would wish. The life which nature gives me, my offspring envies me. He refuses to wait for an old man. These wrongs done to me are indeed my own affair, nothing to you. But now he has seized the kingdom with a woman as your leader, and holds it by force and arms. You have been despised in my injury; your benefits have been snatched from me; he has contemned not me but you. It is your cause that is at stake: look upon the audacity of these men. There is no need for evil spirits; man is enough for many evils. In the one creature, man, there is ambition for honour and an immense greed for wealth; in no one is there a greater lust for power, in no one a fiercer madness. What remains, unless all others take example from this man, as if from a conspicuous place, convicted, and commit parricides everywhere with impunity? If there is any memory among you of Conrad ... and of Henry, my grandfather and parent, and of your ancestors, do not allow the Empire, won by your ancestors' blood and toil through so many civil battles, to wither away through church-wrecking and parricide. By your safety and dignity, by the immortal glory of your forefathers, I beg you: drive far away, to the farthest lands beyond Germany, the victor over nations, this crime unheard of until now. Defend the Roman world, defended by so many civil battles; free the commonwealth of Christians from vices and from this most monstrous wickedness. Let the wicked pay the penalty of their impiety, let the sacrilegious impostors feel that German virtue has not yet degenerated from our forefathers. It is fitting for you to rest upon the footsteps of your ancestors, to be a terror to the worst and a protection to the good. This will happen if, by one consent, we declare Caesar my younger son, my elder having been disinherited and proscribed.

units.la: Hæc ubi Augustus dixit, pauci, quibus omnia alia, atq; fides & Respublica, chariora erant, contradicentur. Cæteri omnes indignitate facinoris commoti, æqua postulare Augustum censent, ejusq; pronunciant: ex consilio decreto more majorum, HAINRICUM filium Augusti impuberem adCæsarem consalutant; isq; se nunquam à patre defecturum solenniritu jurat.
units.tr: When Augustus had said this, a few, for whom all other things, and faith and the commonwealth, were dearer, spoke against it. All the others, moved by the outrage of the deed, judged that Augustus's demands were just, and they declared so. By decree of the council, in the manner of their ancestors, they hailed Henry, the emperor's son, not yet of age, as Caesar; and he swore with solemn rite that he would never fall away from his father.

units.la: DECRETA NORTHUSENSIA HENRICO V. IMPERATORE,
units.tr: Decrees of Northausen, under the Emperor Henry V

units.la: Anno Domini M C V. HEINRICUS nominis illius Quintus Rex, Episcopis atq; Clericis Conventu generalem in villa Northusium dictur, quarto Kalendas Junii, ubi super Ecclesiasticæ institutionis depravata disciplina tractaretur, indixit.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1105, Henry, the fifth king of that name, called a general assembly of bishops and clergy, which is said to have been summoned to the village of Northausen on the fourth day before the Kalends of June, where the depraved state of ecclesiastical discipline was to be discussed.

units.la: I. In quo Consilio super sententiis instantibus Patrum decretis primo relictis, quæq; poterant ad pacem facile dabiliter corrigebantur: quædam verò, quæ & graviora videbantur, ad Apostolicam audiri ... rent.
units.tr: I. In this council, the sentences of the Fathers, which were pressing, were first set aside, and those matters which could easily be corrected for the sake of peace were corrected; but certain matters which seemed more serious were referred to the Apostolic See ...

units.la: 2. Simoniaca quippe hæresis Patrum consuetudine condemnata: Nicolaitarum quoq; fornicaria ... ibidem est ab omnibus abdicata.
units.tr: 2. Simony, indeed, a heresy condemned by the custom of the Fathers, and the fornication of the Nicolaitans also ... was there renounced by all.

units.la: 3. Jejunum mensis Martii hebdomada Quadragesimæ; jejunium verò mensis Junii in ipsa hebdomada Pentecostes Romano more celebrandum, à præceptis Præsulibus Apostolica authoritate ... quos.
units.tr: 3. The fast of the month of March in the week of Lent, and the fast of the month of June in the very week of Pentecost, is to be observed in the Roman manner, by the bishops' precepts, with Apostolic authority ... whom.

units.la: 4. Et Pax Dei confirmatur.
units.tr: 4. And the Peace of God is confirmed.

units.la: 5. His verò, qui à Pseudoepiscopis fuerant consecrati, per Catholicam manus impositionem re-... proximo jejunio danda fore promittitur.
units.tr: 5. But those who had been consecrated by the pseudo-bishops are promised that they will be restored through Catholic laying on of hands and that this will be granted at the next fast.

units.la: 6. Hinc hæc Rex HEINRICUS, cum servorū Dei Conventui nō nisi vocatus interesse vellet, (ingens ... Episcopis & Clericis, & Abbatū atq; Monachorū Ecclesiasticā sine unitate turba cōfluxerat) tandem
units.tr: 6. Hence King Henry, who wished to attend the assembly of God's servants only when summoned (a huge and disunited crowd of bishops, clergy, abbots and monks had flowed together), at last

units.la: b fc.Italiæ tandem in abjecto productus habitu, locoq; stans editiori, omnibus juxta Principum decreta, gestaque juta rationabiliter innovavit: si qua vero irrationabilia rogabantur, mira acultra suorum prudenti responsione, & avita magnanimitate confutavit: in omnibus his & sibimet mitio modo vans adolescentiae verecundiam, & Christi sacerdotibus dignam exhibens reverentiam.
units.tr: at last brought forward in humble dress and standing on a higher place, he reasonably renewed all matters according to the decrees of the princes and the deeds done justly. If unreasonable things were demanded, however, he refuted them with a remarkable and more than ordinary prudent reply and with ancestral magnanimity. In all these things he tempered the shame of his youth and showed the reverence due to Christ's priests.

units.la: 7. Inter haec obortis lachrymis, ipsum Regem coeli, cunctamque militiam coeli testabatur, se regnandi cupiditate paternum sibi regimen usurpare: neq; Dominum & patrem suum a Romano depoai Imperio exoptare, imo debitam pertinaciam & inobedientiae ejus semper compassionem [illegible, ~2 letters] bere: siq; sancto Petro suisq; successoribus lege Christiana subjici velit, sive Regno cedere, sive retinere ipsi se subesse promisit. Quod auditum omnis multitudo collaudans, lachrymas simul & preces tam pro patris conversione, quam pro filii prosperitate fundere coepit, voce magna Kyrie eleison[?] dicens. mans.
units.tr: 7. Amid these things, with tears flowing, he called upon the King of heaven and the whole heavenly host to witness that he was not usurping paternal government out of desire to rule. Nor did he wish his lord and father to be deprived of the Roman Empire; rather, he always felt compassion for his due obstinacy and disobedience. If he wished to be subject to St Peter and his successors under Christian law, he promised that he himself would be subject to them, whether he ceded the kingdom or kept it. When this was heard, the whole multitude praised it and began to pour out tears and prayers, both for the father's conversion and for the son's prosperity, crying out loudly, "Kyrie eleison."

units.la: 8. Eadem hora Uto Hildinshcimensis, & Henricus Paderbrunensis, ac Fridericus Halberstadiensis, Praesules vestigiis Metropolitani prostrati, ipsius atq; Regis stantis totiusq; praesentia testimonio, Apostolicae sedi dederunt obedientiae. Quorum etiam commissa Apostolico nihil judicio reservantur, sub officii sui tantum suspensione.
units.tr: 8. At the same hour Uto of Hildesheim, Henry of Paderborn and Frederick of Halberstadt, bishops, prostrated themselves at the feet of the metropolitan, and in the presence of him and of the king, who stood by, and of all, they gave obedience to the Apostolic See. Their charges are also reserved entirely for Apostolic judgment, and they are suspended only from the exercise of their office.

units.la: HENRICI IV. IMP. AUG. RESCRIPTUM
units.tr: THE RESCRIPT OF HENRY IV, AUGUSTUS EMPEROR

units.la: AD FILIUM HENRICUM V. REGEM ROMANORUM, NE patre ejus affectis obediat impia & innaturalia suadentibus.
units.tr: TO HIS SON HENRY V, KING OF THE ROMANS, that he not obey those who urge impious and unnatural things against his father.

units.la: SI interrogem te, Fili dulcissime, traditio hominum an mandatum Dei praestantius, magis dum sit, respondebis, nisi a vero deductus fis, similem esse jumentis, qui coelestia terrenis divina non praeferat. Cur ergo magis audis eos, qui tibi suggerunt, persequere patrem tuum, quod verbum ipsius Dei, honora patrem tuum? Isti te decipiunt non instruunt: isti honori tuo non prodesse sed invident: isti sub specie fidei, perfidiae laqueos nectunt: non aliter pervenire potuerunt ad destructionem honoris tui nisi per destructionem nostri. Fuerit sane, ut peccatis meis exigentibus sententia adversariorum meorum est) abjecerit me Deus, ne regnem; attamen tuum non erat, in animam meam operam dedisse, & Regnum, quod tibi paraveram, mihi praripuisse. Barbara Regum inhumanum facinus damnant ac devovent, ipsi Pagani abhorrent, & qui Deum nesciunt, quod religendis hominibus naturae debeant recognoscunt. Sed quid mirum, si maligna surreptio seduxit & immaturam aetatem decepit, cum etiam senes & fixum animi statum ad malum mala consilia numquam inflectant? Fortuna mea alieni potius, quam tui sceleris est. Nam tu in manibus suas eras, non ille in tuis. Si autem injuriam addideris, non jam excusari poteris, cum & factam criminem scias, & infectam non facere queas.
units.tr: If I were to ask you, most beloved son, whether the tradition of men or the commandment of God is the more excellent and deserving of preference, you would answer, unless you had been led away from the truth, that God's commandment is. You would then be like the beasts, who do not prefer heavenly things to earthly, or divine things to human. Why then do you listen more to those who advise you, "Persecute your father," than to the very word of God, "Honour your father"? They deceive you; they do not instruct you. They do not wish well to your honour but envy it. Under the appearance of loyalty they weave snares of treachery. They could not bring about the ruin of your honour except by bringing about our ruin. Granted, as my sins deserve, and as my adversaries judge, God may have cast me off so that I should not reign. Yet it was not for you to plot against my life and snatch from me the kingdom I had prepared for you. Barbarian kings condemn and curse such an inhuman deed; even pagans abhor it, and those who do not know God acknowledge by nature what they owe to mankind. But what wonder if malicious stealth has led you astray and deceived your immature age, when even old men of settled mind are never turned to evil by evil counsels? My misfortune is the crime of others rather than yours. For you were in their hands, not they in yours. But if you add injury, you can no longer be excused, since you know the crime was committed and cannot undo it.

units.la: 2. Audivi enim, quod Pascha Leodii celebrandum decrevetis: quo in loco fides & pietas episcopi me recepit, cum non esset, qui vel beneficiorum nostrorum recordaretur, vel fortunae convertiturs: cujus profecto beneficiis in me te decet Regia liberalitate respondere, tantoq; certior fide poteris esse, quanto fidelius erga nos probatur egisse. Hic, nisi te forte domo receperit, me festivitate Paschali retinendum decrevit. At dicis, dignum & conveniens esse, ut ea festivitas nosti potius quam dividat: te velle, te cupere, ut ibi tecum agam dies Paschalis laeticiae: quod quid cupere, si non esset, q timerem. Neq; n. non possum timere eos, quos mihi vitam permisisse dum in manibus eorum mors & vita fuisse. Omnia mihi suspecta sunt, omnia timenda sunt, turba, ubi tanto difficilior est periculi cautio, quanto major sceleris occasio. Inde est, q ex medio qui me oderunt, longe recessi, & in extremis Regni tui finibus me cōtraxi, ut vel secessu loci tuti vel si fortuna mea postulaverit extraneam humanitatem expetere, citius Regno tuo cedere. Precor ergo ut causa patris tui Paschalem Curiam alibi disponas, & in domo ejus, qui me hunc gratia recepit, cum non liceat Imperatorem salte hospitem esse linas, ne vel in meum ludibrium tuum opprobrium narretur, quod in solennitate Dominicae Resurrectionis incerta hospitia mea quaerere cogatur. Si feceris, quod postulo, maximas gratias habeo: sin autem, malo villicus extremis Regnis, quam ludibrio haberi in Regnis quondam meis. Ex Leodio.
units.tr: 2. For I have heard that you have decided to hold the Paschal feast at Liège. There the faith and piety of the bishop received me, when there was no one else who remembered our benefits or turned toward my changed fortune. You ought, with royal generosity, to repay his kindness to me, and you may be the more certain of his loyalty the more faithfully he is shown to have acted toward us. Here, unless perhaps he has received you into his own house, he has resolved that I should be kept for the Paschal festival. But you say that it is fitting and proper that this festival should unite us rather than divide us; that you wish and long for me to spend the Paschal days of joy with you there. If you did not desire this, I would be afraid. For I cannot help fearing those who, while my life lay in their hands, allowed me to live. Everything is suspect to me, everything is to be feared, and in a crowd, where caution against danger is all the harder, the greater the opportunity for crime. That is why I have withdrawn far from the midst of those who hate me, and confined myself to the furthest borders of your kingdom, so that, either by the retreat of a safe place, or, should my fortune require me to seek foreign hospitality, I might more readily give way to your kingdom. I beg you, therefore, for your father's sake, to arrange the Paschal court elsewhere, and not in the house of him who has received me here out of kindness, since it is not permitted that the Emperor be even a guest. Otherwise your disgrace would be talked of to my mockery, that at the solemnity of the Lord's Resurrection I am forced to seek an uncertain lodging. If you do what I ask, I shall be most grateful; but if not, I would rather be a steward in the remote realms than be made a laughingstock in the kingdoms that were once mine. From Liège.

units.la: HENRICI V. CAESARIS AUG. EDICTUM
units.tr: HENRY V, EMPEROR AUGUSTUS, EDICT

units.la: DE VINDICANDIS INIVRIIS IN CAESAREAM MAIESTA- TEM ILLATIS.
units.tr: ON AVENGING THE INJURIES INFLICTED ON THE IMPERIAL MAJESTY.

units.la: Henricus Rex Principibus Imperii.
units.tr: Henry, King, to the Princes of the Empire.

units.la: SI per invasionem Regnum occupasset, tamen resistentes potestati nostrae retinuerem, in tum possem. Nunc autem cum in sumpta Regni dignitate vestris parentum praeceptis, aliquis impune in publicam cohortem Regum & Nosarmis vexare. Cum n. Leodium Curia Patherbrunnensis habenda fuerat, ad fluvium Mosam venitlemus, Episcopus Leodiensis & Florentius, de quorum fide & obsequii devotione multum praesumebamus, nobis lateter insidias parabant, & nostros insidiose & ad pugnam imparatos credebant, capiebant, fugabant. Quae & quanta sustinuerunt, tam pudet referre, quam inultum dimittere. Igitur constrictus & eventus asperitatis, Mo ad articulo Coloniam diverti. Quae cum me recipere satis superbe refutaret, apud villam sanctum die Palchae utcunque peregri. Cui nunquam Regiae personae tanta contumelia facta est? Non me petit haec contumelia, vos deperdit estis; illi praesumptores decreta vestra authoritatem suam tantum statuta firma esse volunt; denique in quos totus Regni pondus se reclinet, hoc est ... Regem, quae constituistis, destituere parant, ut nihil eorum, quae vos decrevistis, ratum sit. Infra; Regni regnum mea Regni potius est, quam mea. Nam unius capitis licet summi dejectio, reparabile regnum damnum est: Principum autem conculcatio, ruina Regni est. An haec impune ferremus? & exigno... nostra magis tumebit eorum superbia: Absit, ut qui dicimur inhonorati, dicamur & in- ... sed ... Quia igitur contra tam superbos hostes R.P. viribus utendum est ... nos ... rogando praecipimus, & praecipiedo rogamus: cujus collectioni tempus ... Julias, locum Wirtziburgensem urbem praefinimus.
units.tr: If he had seized the kingdom by invasion, I could still hold down those who resist our power, and I would be able to do so. But now, having taken up the dignity of the kingdom on the advice of your parents, someone is allowed to harass the public court of kings and our princes with impunity. For when the court of Paderborn was to be held at Liège, we came to the river Meuse. Bishop Liège and Florentius, on whose loyalty and devoted obedience we relied greatly, secretly prepared ambushes against us. They believed our men to be treacherously caught and unprepared for battle, and they seized, routed and scattered them. What and how great the things they inflicted upon us are, I am as ashamed to report as I am to let them go unavenged. Therefore, hard pressed and driven by the harshness of events, I turned aside to Cologne. When that city proudly refused to receive me, I somehow made my way to the village of Saint [...] on the day of Easter. Has any royal person ever suffered such an insult? This insult is not aimed at me alone; you are the ones it destroys. Those presumptuous men want your decrees to have authority only so long as their own statutes stand firm. In the end, they are preparing to depose the king on whom the whole weight of the kingdom rests, so that none of the things you have decided may stand. Further on: the kingdom's cause is the cause of the princes rather than mine. For although the fall of one head, however high, is a loss the kingdom can repair, the trampling of the princes is the ruin of the kingdom. Should we bear these things with impunity? [...] their pride will swell all the more against us. Far be it that we, who are called dishonoured, should be called [...]. Since, therefore, we must use our strength against such proud enemies, we [...] by asking and we command by requesting: for whose gathering we appoint the time [...] July, and the place the city of Würzburg.

units.la: HENRICI IV. IMP. AUG. RESCRIPTUM AD FILIUM HENRICUM V. REGEM DE PERFIDIA ET IMPIETATE EJUS IN SE IMPERATOREM PATREM.
units.tr: THE RESCRIPT OF THE EMPEROR HENRY IV AUGUSTUS TO HIS SON HENRY V THE KING, CONCERNING HIS PERFIDY AND IMPIETY TOWARDS HIMSELF, THE EMPEROR AND HIS FATHER.

units.la: Henricus Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator Augustus, Henrico filio suo. Si ea nos debaffectione tractatiles, quae debetes, lubentissimè tecum loqueremur, & paterna tibi mandarevel quia longè alius quàm paternae affectionis & humanitatis circa nos animus tibi fuit, ... cum loquatur, quod ipsa rei manifestissimae veritas habet. Tu enim ipse scis, sicuti... experimento facti tibi conscius es, qualiter data fide & securitate per sonas & honoris no- ... affectione devotionis promisisti nos ducere Moguntiam coram Principibus, & inde nos se- ... reducere quocunque vellemus. Hac fiducia cum tecum amanter & indubitanter ascendere- ... contra datam fidem apud Bingam nos cepisti, ubi nec paternae lacrymae, nec patris moeror, nec tu- ... jua ad pedes tuos aliorumque advolvebamur, te commovit ad misericordiam, quin nos caperes, & ... mortalibus inimicis illudendum & custodiendum traderes, ubi multimodo genere cruci... cerrotis afflicti, compluribus fermè venire usque ad ipsum mortis articulum.
units.tr: Henry, by the grace of God Roman Emperor Augustus, to his son Henry. If we could deal with you according to the affection that you owe, we would most gladly speak with you and give you paternal counsel. But you have shown a spirit quite different from paternal affection and humanity towards us, as the very manifest truth of the matter shows. For you yourself know, and you are conscious of the deed through experience, how, with faith and safety pledged in the persons and honour of [the princes], you promised with devoted affection to lead us to Mainz before the princes, and from there to bring us back wherever we wished. Trusting in this, we ascended with you lovingly and without doubt, but contrary to the pledged faith you seized us at Bingen. There neither a father's tears, nor a father's grief, nor the prostrate pleas of ours and of others at your feet moved you to mercy, but you seized us, and handed us over to be mocked and guarded by mortal enemies, where in many ways, afflicted by torment, we were brought almost to the point of death itself.

units.la: 2. Ante captivitatem abstulisti nobis Episcopatus, & quaecunque de honore Regni potuisti, & praestra, & ipsam familiam: in captivitate verò quicquid residuum erat, ut Lanceani, & Crucem, & Regalia insignia vi & timore mortis, ut ipse bene scis, & omni ferme notum est Christianitati, à extorsisti, relicta vix ipsa vita. Cum hoc tibi de nobis non sufficeret, postea semper ubicunque modis omnibus, quibus potuisti, nos persequi non cessasti, ut vel perderes vel de Regno ex-
units.tr: 2. Before the captivity you took from us the bishoprics and whatever you could of the honour of the kingdom, and the treasure, and even the household itself. In captivity, however, whatever remained, such as the lance, the cross and the royal insignia, you extorted by force and by fear of death, as you well know and as is known to almost all Christendom, leaving us scarcely life itself. Since this was not enough for you concerning us, afterwards, wherever you could and by every means you could, you did not cease to persecute us, so that you might either destroy us or drive us from the kingdom.

units.la: 1. Verùm nos satis mirari non possumus, qua ratione vel occasione tam obstinate facias, cum de Papa & Romana Ecclesia nulla tibi relicta sit occasio. Nos n. Nuncio Domini Papae & RoEcclesiae te praesente parati fuimus & fumus obaedire, & omnem debitam obaedientiam & reverentiam coram & semper exhibere, & consilio Principum, & spiritualis patris nostri Hugonis CluAbbatis, aliorumque Religiosorum virorum de statu Ecclesiae & honore Regni libentissime
units.tr: 1. Truly we cannot sufficiently wonder by what reason or occasion you act so obstinately, since no occasion has been left to you concerning the Pope and the Roman Church. For we were, and still are, ready in your presence to obey the Lord Pope's nuncio and the Roman Church, and always to show all due obedience and reverence, and we most willingly act in accordance with the counsel of the princes, of our spiritual father Hugh, Abbot of Cluny, and of other religious men, concerning the state of the Church and the honour of the kingdom.

units.la: Te ergo rogamus pro honore Regni, & tua & paterna devotione, & per auctoritatem Romani & Romanae Ecclesiae, ut de injuria nobis illata, & de his, quae nobis vi & injuste abstulisti, ju-. Rogamus etiam, ut cum nil rationis tibi sit, quare nos prosequaris, nos & fideles nostros re, mo permittas nos pacificè & quietè vivere, ut integrè & cum tranquillitate possimus dicta agere. Recognosce etiam, & tecum cogita, quia Deus justus judex est, cui communis ... & vindictam: cujus etiam judicia sunt occulta, velut abyssus multa. Quoniam quantucunque ... honore & infortunia gloriaris, & super humiliatè te extollas, forte an de sed sancta sua inter ... misericordia aliud jam definivit, intercedente justitia, quam tu ipse cogites & dispo-... nulla alia vel reverentia vel intercessio nobis valet, opto ut justitiam consequi possimus, ... persecutionis impetus cessaret. Ad hoc idem Romanum Pontificem, & sanctam universalem ... Ecclesiam appellamus.
units.tr: Therefore we ask you, for the honour of the kingdom, and by your own and your father's devotion, and through the authority of the Roman Pontiff and the Roman Church, that you make amends for the injury done to us, and restore those things which you took from us by force and unjustly. We also ask that, since you have no reason to pursue us, you permit us and our faithful men to live peacefully and quietly, so that we may carry out what has been said with integrity and tranquillity. Recognize also, and consider with yourself, that God is a just judge, to whom belong vengeance and retribution, and whose judgments are hidden, like a great deep. For however much you glory in your honour and fortune, and exalt yourself above the humbled, perhaps God's holy mercy has already decided otherwise, justice intervening, than you yourself think and arrange. No other reverence or intercession avails us. I desire that we may obtain justice, and that the assault of this persecution may cease. To this end we appeal to the Roman Pontiff and to the holy universal Church.

units.la: HENRICI IV. IMPER. AUG. PROTESTATIO A- D PRINCIPES IMPERII, Super injusta sua depositione.
units.tr: Protestation of Emperor Henry IV to the Princes of the Empire, concerning his unjust deposition.

units.la: Henricus Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator Augustus, ab Episcopis, Ducibus, Marchionibus, ... Regni Principibus, gratiam & dilectionem, dignantibus eam recapere. ConConquerimur Deo omnipotenti, & Dominæ meæ sanctæ Mariæ, & beato Petro Principi Apostolorum, patrono nostro, & vobis Principibus omnibus, quod injustè & inhumanè & crudeliter cum fili in illa fide, in qua dubitare non debueramus, tractati sumus, & tam honore Regni quàm praedicto omnibus, quæ habebamus, contra divinum & humanum jus, ad infamiam & improperium Regni ta expoliati sumus, ut nihil penitus præter solam vitam nobis relictum sit. Ubi cum fere omnes ex-tis, magna pars vestri visa est dolere & contristari: sed (proh dolor) nihil nobis vestra consulit quin de nobis sibi satisfaceret voluntas inimicorum nostrorum odiosa. Et quia cum consilio & ope tu filii nostri, fide & securitate vitæ & honoris ab eo primum accepta, fiducialiter & desiderantes Hugguntiam in præsentiam Legati Romani & Principum renderamus, ut eorum dispositione aggravem tam de statu Ecclesiæ & honore Regni, quàm de salute animæ nostræ, ipse non est ventus in lun-tate & obedientia nos contra datam fidem capere, & usque ad articulum mortis ferme duces, ausi sumus ita nos illi credere, ut injuriis & contumeliis nos pro voluntate sua, sicut prius, valeat eftare.
units.tr: Henry, by the grace of God Augustus Emperor of the Romans, to the bishops, dukes, marquises, and princes of the kingdom: grace and affection, and may they deign to receive us back. We complain to almighty God, to my Lady the holy Mary, to blessed Peter, Prince of the Apostles, our patron, and to all of you princes, that we have been treated unjustly, inhumanly and cruelly, together with our son, in that faith in which we ought not to have doubted. We have been stripped, contrary to divine and human law, both of the honour of the kingdom and of all that we possessed, to the infamy and disgrace of the kingdom, so that nothing whatever is left to us except life alone. When almost all of you had been gathered, a large part of you seemed to grieve and be saddened; but (alas) your counsel did nothing for us, except that the hostile will of our enemies found satisfaction in us. And because, with the counsel and help of our son, having first received from him faith and security of life and honour, we went confidently to Hugguntia, into the presence of the Roman legate and the princes, desiring to submit ourselves so that by their disposition the affairs both of the state of the Church and the honour of the kingdom, and the salvation of our soul, might be settled; he was not willing to take us in obedience and according to the faith given, and we, nearly to the point of death, dared to trust him, and so he was able, as before, to hold us to his injuries and insults at his pleasure.

units.la: Quapropter multum rogamus vos, & obnixè precamur, ut pro timore Dei, & honore Regni & honestate vestra dignemini studere, quomodo de injuria in manibus vestris nobis illata possimus recuperare justiciam. Nos quoq; pro consilio vestro & aliorum, qui nos odio habent, religiosorum virorum, parati sumus tam filio nostro, si in aliquo eum offendimus, quam in Regno, libenter emendare. Præterea sicut Domino Papæ in præsentia Legati sui & vestri dire parati sumus, ita & nunc parati sumus eis omnem debitam reverentiam & obedientiam corde & devotione præsentialiter exhibere, & tam consilio vestro quàm spiritalis patris nostri, Gonis Cluniacensis Abbatis, ac aliorum religiosorum virorum, deStatu Ecclesiæ & honoris Regni quantum in nobis est, disponere.
units.tr: Therefore we ask you very earnestly and beseech you, for the fear of God, for the honour of the kingdom and for your own honour, to take care how justice may be recovered for the injury done to us in your hands. We too, following your counsel and that of the others, religious men, who hate us, are ready to amend freely whatever we have offended in our son, and in the kingdom. Moreover, just as we declared to the Lord Pope in the presence of his legate and of you, so now we are ready to show them all due reverence and obedience in person, with heart and devotion, and to dispose, as far as lies in us, of the state of the Church and the honour of the kingdom, by your counsel and that of our spiritual father, Hugh, Abbot of Cluny, and of the other religious men.

units.la: Cùm igitur ad hæc omnia parati simus, rogamus vos & obnixè deprecamur, quatenus pro Dei & honore Regni & vestro instanter moneatis filium nostrum, quum secundum prædictam tentiam nulla ei adversum nos relidua sit occasio, amodò desistat nos & fideles nostros persequi, & patè & pacificè vivere permittat, ut supradicta integrè & cum tranquillitate perficiantur. Quod si noluerit, rogamus vos per authoritatem Romanæ Ecclesiæ, cui nos committimus, & honoris Regni, ne super nos & super fideles nostros veniatis: quia manifestum est cum non divinæ legis zelo, Romanæ Ecclesiæ dilectione, sed concupiscentia Regni, patre injustè eo privato, hoc incepit. Apud quem si interpellatio vestra, nullaque alia interventio ad præsens prodesse poterit, appellamus Romanum Pontificem, & sanctam universalem Romanam Sedem & Ecclesiam. Ex Leodio.
units.tr: Since, therefore, we are ready for all these things, we ask and earnestly beseech you that, for the sake of God, the honour of the kingdom and your own, you urgently admonish our son: since, according to the aforesaid sentence, he has no remaining occasion against us, he should now cease to persecute us and our faithful, and allow us to live freely and peacefully, so that the aforesaid things may be carried out fully and in tranquillity. But if he is unwilling, we ask you, by the authority of the Roman Church, to which we commit ourselves, and by the honour of the kingdom, not to come against us and our faithful. For it is manifest that this was begun not from zeal for the divine law nor from love of the Roman Church, but from desire for the kingdom, our father having been unjustly deprived of it. If your intercession with him, and no other intervention, can avail at present, we appeal to the Roman Pontiff, and to the holy universal Roman See and Church. From Liège.

units.la: PRINCIPUM IMPERII RESCRIPTUM AD HEINRICVM QVONDAM IMPERATOREM, Ex Castris apud Coloniam Agrippinam.
units.tr: RESCRIPT OF THE PRINCES OF THE EMPIRE TO HENRY, FORMERLY EMPEROR, FROM THE CAMP NEAR COLOGNE (COLONIA AGRIPPINA).

units.la: POST inveteratam, id est, per annos circiter quadraginta, discissionem Imperii Romani, tam divinas quàm humanas jam penè leges abolevit, & exceptis moribus omnimodis, giis, perjuriis, rapinis, & incendiis, ipsum regnum nostrum non tantùm in solitudinem, jam ad apostasiam Catholicæ fidei, sive in ipsum Paganismum, propemodùm redegit: re-te tandem suam Ecclesiam divina clementia, nos, ejusdem Christi filius, per Spiritum Sanctum in unitatem fidei æquanimes respicimus; ipsum incorrigibile schismatum illorum Heinricum scilicet, dictum Imperatorem nostrum, zelo Dei & Apostolicæ fidei obedidicavimus, Catholicum nobis (licet ipsius de femine natum) Regem elegimus. Cujus regni cipium sui finem esse conspiciens, etiam ipse tanquam voluntarius, sed (ut jam ejus fatentur litermis invitus collaudavit, regalia reddidit, filii curam cum regno nostræ fidei lachrymando fit, de reliquo nullam se regni pompam, sed animæ potius suæ medelam ulterius affectaturum spondit.
units.tr: AFTER the Roman Empire had been torn apart for about forty years, he has almost abolished both divine and human laws. Apart from every kind of misconduct, sacrilege, perjury, plunder and arson, he has reduced our kingdom not only to a wilderness but nearly to apostasy from the Catholic faith, or indeed to paganism itself. But at last, when the divine mercy looked upon its Church, we, the son of the same Christ, through the Holy Spirit, looking on it with an even mind for the unity of faith, have renounced that incorrigible Henry, the schismatic, called our Emperor, out of zeal for God and the Apostolic faith. We have chosen as a Catholic king one who, though born of his seed, is ours. Seeing that the end of his reign was at hand, he himself, as if of his own will, but (as his letters now confess) unwillingly, also gave praise, returned the royal regalia, and, weeping, committed the care of his son and the kingdom to our faith. For the rest, he promised that he would seek no pomp of kingship, but rather the healing of his own soul.

units.la: At nunc ecce pristinis se reddens tergiversationibus, præjudicium se passum per orbem rum conqueritur: Gallorum, Anglorum, Danorum, cæterarumque finitimarum gentium dios cordibus nostris infigere meditatur: super illatis etiam injuriis recuperari sibi justiciam patur: consiliis quoque nostris amodò promptum obedire se pollicetur. Re autem vera solitismentis c ultra hæc Domini dispergere, Christi exercitum exarmare conatur, & (ut in præparatu vineam Domini, quæ jam sero floresce cœpit, tam per se singularem utique ferum denuo scere, quàm per vulpes, illos nimirum, qui sibi adhærent, pestilentes homines, demoliri, ac per legia Sacerdotum Belial anathemati reciduo reddere, imò (quod dictu nephas est) Christum jam rum in Ecclesia sua resurgentem in omnium cordibus crucifigere meditatur.
units.tr: But now, behold, returning to his old evasions, he complains that he has been wronged throughout the world. He plans to fix hatreds of the French, the English, the Danes and the other neighbouring peoples in our hearts. He also seeks to recover justice for the injuries done to him. He promises that he will henceforth obey our counsels readily. In truth, however, by his usual machinations he goes further: he tries to scatter the Lord's flock and disarm Christ's army. As in the Lord's vineyard, which has only lately begun to flourish, he seeks to make it wild again, both by himself, singularly savage, and through foxes, those pestilent men who cling to him, to tear it down; and through the legates of the priests of Belial he seeks to render it once more liable to anathema. Indeed, which is an impiety even to speak of, he plans to crucify Christ, who is already rising again in his Church, in the hearts of all.

units.la: Quapropter placet tam * Regi quàm universis Regni Principibus, imò cuncto exercitu orthodoxo, quo senior idem, nec ulla sibi pateat adversum nos justa querela, quacunque elegantia
units.tr: Therefore it pleases the King, as well as all the princes of the realm, and indeed the whole orthodox army, that the same elder should have no just complaint left open to him against us, and that, by whatever

units.la: * Heinrico V. hujus filio. mate, quicunq; maluerit statione, coram praesenti Senatu, simul & Populo, causam suam agat, justi-tiam suscipiat, justiciam & reddat, quatenus ab ortu schismatis, omnibus seditionum causis, ac si nihil ad rem iam tuent diffinitum, undiq; discussis, tam filio quam patri sua justicia respondeat: Ecclesiae veRegni q; status, non ut ipse more suo proponit, post logas inducias, sed in praesentiarum his controversiis exemptis, vacillare desinat. Ex Castris.
units.tr: (* Henry V, this man's son.) ... route he prefers, he should, in the presence of the present Senate and the people together, bring his cause, accept justice and render it. Let all the causes of sedition from the beginning of the schism be thoroughly discussed on every side, as if nothing remained in dispute, so that he may answer with his justice to the son as well as to the father. And let the state of the Church and of the kingdom cease to waver, not after long delays, as he himself proposes in his usual way, but now, with these controversies settled. From the camp.

units.la: HENRICI IV. IMPERATO- RIS AUGUSTI RESCRIPTUM AD PRINCIPES IMPERII.
units.tr: The Rescript of the Emperor Henry IV Augustus to the Princes of the Empire.

units.la: HENRICUS Dei gratia Imperator Augustus, Archiepiscopis, Episcopis, Ducibus, Comitibus, caeterisq; Regni Principibus, gratiam & dilectionem, dignantibus ea recipere.
units.tr: Henry, by the grace of God Emperor Augustus, to the Archbishops, Bishops, Dukes, Counts and the other Princes of the Kingdom: grace and goodwill, if they deign to receive them.

units.la: 1. Rogamus filium nostrum, & vos multum precari sumus, ut dimisso exercitu ordinaremus, quomodo possemus convenire, ut de injuria nostra & pace componenda ad honorem Regni posset dignè & decenter definiri. Placuit vobis remandare. Unde nobis longè gravior prioti oritur, quod dimissa obsidione Coloniae vultis super nos & fideles nostros sub specie colloquii venire, datis induciis octo dierum: quae numquam dari possunt homini alicujus conditionis, ut scitis, usque ad hanc diem pro legitima definitione alicujus minoris negotii, nedum pro causa, secundum legem divinam vel humanam, vel etiam secundum usum hominum. Oportet enim non habere, si vobis placeret, saltem tales induciis, intra quas possemus convocare, & praecipere ad hanc eandem causam, ut sint vobiscum, Moguntinum, & Trevirensem, & Bremensem Archiepiscopos; Frilingensem, Augustensem, Curiensem, Basiliensem Episcopos; Ducem Maximum cum Duce Theodorico, & Ducem Bohemicum, & Comitem Flandrensem cum Comite Bur-gundiae & alios, qui ad praetatum negocium, ut bene scitis, sunt valde necessarii.
units.tr: 1. We have asked our son, and we have earnestly begged you, that once the army was dismissed you would arrange how we might meet, so that our injury and the restoration of peace might be settled worthily and fittingly to the honour of the Kingdom. You have decided to send back word. Hence a much graver grievance arises for us: you wish, once the siege of Cologne is lifted, to come against us and our faithful followers under the pretext of a conference, with a truce of eight days granted. Such a truce can never be granted to a man of any rank, as you know, up to this day, for the lawful settlement of even a minor matter, much less of a cause that concerns the divine or human law, or even the custom of men. For it is necessary not to have such a truce, if it pleased you, but at least a truce within which we might summon and order, for this same cause, that the Archbishops of Mainz, Trier and Bremen be with you; the Bishops of Freising, Augsburg, Chur and Basel; Duke Maximus with Duke Theodoric, and the Duke of Bohemia, and the Count of Flanders with the Count of Burgundy, and others who, as you well know, are very necessary to the said business.

units.la: 2. Quapropter, sicut prius, rogamus & obnixè precamur, quatenus pro Deo & anima vestra, et pro appellatione Domini Romani Pontificis Paschalis, & Romanae Ecclesiae, & pro honore Regni apud filium nostrum efficere, ut dimisso exercitu cessel nos persequi, & ordinetur quomodo secure & absque omni ambiguitate possimus nos cum caeteris supradictis ad agendum de injuria, & pace in regno componenda, quaeré & pacificè convenire. Quod si nullatenus cessare erit, proclamationem indicere facimus, & semper facimus, Deo, & sanctae Mariae, & beato Petro patrono nostro, & omnibus Sanctis, & omnibus Christianis, & vobis maximè, omni devotione precan-te dignemini cessare eum prosequi ad persecutionem tantae injuriae, & vos eum imitari.
units.tr: 2. Therefore, as before, we ask and earnestly beg that, for God's sake and for your own soul, and for the appeal to the lord Roman Pontiff Paschal and to the Roman Church, and for the honour of the Kingdom, you bring it about with our son that, once the army is dismissed, he cease to pursue us, and that it be arranged how we may meet peacefully and without any doubt, safely, with the others mentioned above, to deal with the injury and with the restoration of peace in the Kingdom. But if he will in no way cease, we are making, and always make, a proclamation to God, and to holy Mary, and to blessed Peter our patron, and to all the Saints, and to all Christians, and above all to you, praying with all devotion that you deign to cease pursuing him in the persecution of so great an injury, and that you imitate him.

units.la: 3. Appellavimus, & tertiò appellamus Dominum Romanum Pontificem Paschalem, & sanctam & universalem Sedem & Romanam Ecclesiam.
units.tr: 3. We have appealed, and for the third time we appeal, to the lord Roman Pontiff Paschal, and to the holy and universal See and the Roman Church.

units.la: 4. Quod si hoc tantum nobis, & ad hoc, ut ipse cessel nos persequi, prodesse non poterit, communis nos omnipotenti Patri & Filio sancto, Spiritui Paracleto, & beatae Mariae perpetuè Virgini beato Petro & Paulo, & sancto Lamperto, omnibusq; Sanctis, ut divina miseratio, omniumque eorum intercessio, humilitatem nostram respicere, nosq; contra tantum tamq; injuriosum impetum defendere dignetur, Amen.
units.tr: 4. But if this alone cannot avail us, and cannot avail to make him cease to pursue us, may the common Father Almighty, and the Holy Son, the Paraclete Spirit, and the blessed Mary, ever Virgin, and blessed Peter and Paul, and Saint Lambert, and all the Saints, deign by divine mercy, and by the intercession of all of them, to regard our humility and to defend us against so great and so injurious an assault. Amen.

units.la: HENRICI V. IMP. AUG. EDICTUM
units.tr: EDICT OF HENRY V, EMPEROR AUGUSTUS

units.la: Contra impia & turbulenta decreta Paschalis Papae & Conciliabuli Triensis.
units.tr: Against the impious and turbulent decrees of Pope Paschal and the Synod of Troyes.

units.la: PASCALIS Papa Augustobonae in Trecasiorum & Galliae Lugdunensis urbe, conciliato sibi Episcoporum favore, ad captandam plebis auram, leges turbulentissimas rogat atq; perCaesarem de creandis Pontificibus ad disquisitionem vocat: ipsum Pontificalibus Comitiis ad plebem transfert; nempe communem omnium 4 Pastorem, communiter omnium capiendum esse statuit; pollui religionem, si quisquam sacris addictus coelestis atq; immortalis, terreno atq; mortali Regi se in clientelam atq; servitutem Sacerdotiorum administrationem ad Pontificem Maximum, armorum ad Caesarem pertinere. Igitur Episcopis jusjurandum exactum, futuros in potestate Romani Pontificis.
units.tr: Pope Paschal, at Augustobona in the city of the Tricasses in Lugdunensis Gaul, having won over the favour of the bishops and seeking to catch the breath of popular applause, proposes most turbulent laws. Through the Emperor he summons the creation of pontiffs to examination. He transfers the pontifical elections to the people, decreeing that the common pastor of all should be chosen in common by all. He says that religion would be polluted if anyone devoted to heavenly and immortal things submitted himself as a client and slave to an earthly and mortal king. The administration of the priesthoods, he says, belongs to the Supreme Pontiff and the arms to the Emperor. Therefore an oath was exacted from the bishops that they would be in the power of the Roman Pontiff.

units.la: HAINRICUS Quintus Caesar Augustus per edicta ita obnunciat: Non licere Gallis curiosis quae nihil ad eos attinent, curare: cuilibet facile esse de alieno largiri. Christiani orbis Imperator a Deo optimo maximo impositum esse; proinde sede veteri more & ritu priscae religionis, supremae Majestatis placitis non defuturum, daturumque jure suo operam, ne quid Reipublicae incumbentis capiat. extare vetustissimam sanctissimorum Patrum legem, tempore CAROLI MAGNI, quia Paschalis, atq; cum eo sententes, per omnium Sacerdotum religiones devoventes proscribuntur. Nullo pacto fas jusq; esse fastuoso Pontifici, levissimis Gallis, magis imperitioribus tot Divos, tot piissimos, Pontifices maximos, minores, Mystas, Monachos, Reges, Imperatores atq; caelites impietatis condemnare, se quoad vita suppetat, non pal-lium, ut instituta à majoribus accepta, per tot annos hactenus observata, fraude & astu paucorum, cum maxime Christianorum morum pernicie, obliterentur: Pontifices, Episcopos, Mystas, Monachos ab Imperatoribus atq; Regibus collocupletatos esse. Ubi his pares opibus facti sunt, more perditorû, qui plura donata fuerint, plura concupiscere; illisq; sordere prima quæq;, ubi majora sperarint, titulo honoris libertatis Ecclesiasticæ fraudulentos homines grassari, illud conari, ut se excluso, paulatim etiam populum, Sacerdotes, Episcopos, alios in ordinem atque servitutem tandem redigant, atq; armis quorum beneficia possident, ne hæc aliquo pacto repeti queant, vertant. Pontifices Romanorum Imperium animo cogitare, Regnum Christiani populi adfectare, non quieturos, donec opprimere, omnibus jugum servitutis, quod ipsi excussere, imponant: Christi cruciamenta declarare, nam sit rabies Sacerdotum: adversus immodicam concupiscentiam, cui se semel animus devoverit, nullum stare terminum: se sane impuberem, imperitum omnium rerum ab illis egregiis Patribus dolo circumventum in patrem charissimum concitatum esse, armaque horum consilio sumpsisse. Nunc genitore oppresso, adversus se conspirasse, neq; modum ambitioni ponere, nisi alios omnes dignitate, honore expolissent, &c, quò ipsis quidquid lubeat, licear, ab singulis jutamentum, se futuros sub rum potestate, quicquid illi dicant, pro legibus habituros, atq; tandem pro Deo adoraturos, existere.
