units.tr: Henry V, Caesar Augustus, announces by edict as follows: it is not permitted for the meddlesome Gauls to concern themselves with what does not pertain to them; it is easy for anyone to be generous with what belongs to another. The Emperor of the Christian world has been set over it by God, most good and most great. Therefore, keeping to the ancient seat, custom and rite of the old religion, he will not fail the pleasure of the supreme majesty, and by his right he will take care that nothing is seized from the commonwealth that falls to him. There exists a most ancient law of the most holy Fathers, from the time of Charlemagne, by which Paschal and those who think with him, cursing through the religious orders of all priests, are proscribed. By no means is it lawful or right for the arrogant Pontiff and the most flimsy Gauls, and those more unskilled than the rest, to condemn as impious so many divine men, so many most pious supreme and lesser pontiffs, mystics, monks, kings, emperors and saints. He, so long as life remains to him, will not allow the institutions received from his ancestors and observed until now for so many years to be obliterated by the fraud and cunning of a few, with the greatest ruin of Christian morals. Popes, bishops, mystics and monks have been enriched by emperors and kings. When they have become equal to these in wealth, they behave like ruined men: having been given more, they desire more, and the first gifts seem sordid to them where they hope for greater. Fraudulent men rage under the title of ecclesiastical liberty and attempt this: that, with him shut out, they may gradually reduce the people, priests, bishops and others to order and servitude, and turn to arms to keep the benefices they possess, lest these in any way be sought back. The Roman Pontiffs have the Empire in their minds and aim at the kingdom of the Christian people; they will not rest until they crush all and impose on all the yoke of servitude which they themselves have thrown off. They make the sufferings of Christ their pretext, for such is the madness of the priests. Against immoderate desire, to which a mind has once devoted itself, no limit stands. He, a youth truly below age and inexperienced in all matters, was circumvented by the guile of those eminent Fathers and roused against his most beloved father, and took up arms on their counsel. Now that his father is oppressed, they have conspired against him, nor do they set any limit to their ambition unless they strip all others of dignity and honour, and so on, so that whatever pleases them may be permitted to them; that they demand an oath from each that he will be under their power, will hold whatever they say as law, and will finally worship them as God.

units.la: HEINRICI V. IMP. AUG. RESCRIPTVM
units.tr: THE RESCRIPT OF HENRY V, EMPEROR AUGUSTUS

units.la: Ad Paschalem Papam, ut Ecclesiastici regalia & feuda sua Imperio ac Cæsari resignent, & decimus contenti in Ecclesia vivant.
units.tr: To Pope Paschal, that churchmen should surrender their regalia and fiefs to the Empire and to Caesar, and live content with tithes in the Church.

units.la: CÆsar Paschali Papæ novissimè rescripsit: quamvis veterem consuetudinem atq; ritum, à tot sanctissimis Patribus per tot annos observatum, jure atq; armis tenere possit, nihil tamen nisi ferre, si a Pontificalibus Comitiis excidat, modò Episcopi, Mystæ, Monachi, prædia stipendia, fiscos, nervos Reipublicæ, arces, civitates, urbes, oppida, vicos Regios, castella, Reipublicæ Cæsari reddant, decimis contenti vivant, Dei & pauperum, populiq; causam, philosophiam interpretando, vota illustrando, crucem Christi præferendo, agant; atq; universis Christianis pauperatem atq; simplicitatem Servatoris nostri, b Comitum ejus æmulando præluceant.
units.tr: Caesar lately wrote back to Pope Paschal. Although he could hold on by right and by arms to the old custom and rite, observed by so many most holy Fathers over so many years, he would bear nothing of it, if it should fall away from the pontifical assemblies, provided only that the bishops, mystics, and monks return to the commonwealth and to Caesar the estates, stipends, treasuries, sinews of the commonwealth, citadels, cities, towns, villages of the crown, and castles; that they live content with tithes, and act for the cause of God, of the poor and of the people, by interpreting philosophy, illuminating vows, and setting the cross of Christ before them; and that they shine before all Christians by imitating the poverty and simplicity of our Saviour and of his companions.

units.la: Convenit itaq; inter Pontificem Maximum atq; Cæsarem, uti Sacerdotes, Flamines, Pontifices Maximi, minores, medioximi, omissis hujuscemodi Reipublicæ (ut Christus magister noster appellat) spinis, victu parabili ac parco contenti, Christi præceptoris nostri, quoad liceat, modestiam, paupertatem sectentur, studio literarum operam navent.
units.tr: It is therefore agreed between the Supreme Pontiff and Caesar that priests, flamens, high priests, the lesser and the middling sort, having laid aside the thorns of such worldly business (as Christ our master calls them), and content with plain and frugal fare, should follow, as far as is permitted, the modesty and poverty of Christ our teacher, and devote their efforts to the study of letters.

units.la: PACTUM HENRICI. V. IMPERATORIS ET PASCHALIS II. PAPÆ
units.tr: The Agreement of Emperor Henry V and Pope Paschal II

units.la: DE PACE ET IVRIBVS IMPERII ET ECCLESIAE.
units.tr: Concerning the Peace and the Rights of the Empire and the Church.

units.la: INter Nuncios Imperatoris, & Petrum Leonis & cæteros Nuncios Pontificis, in Porticu sancti Petri convenit, ut Imperator die Coronationis suæ omne malè usurpatum Ecclesiasticum jus in manus Pontificis, astante Cleto & populo, per scriptum deponeret, cum ipsum Papa de negocis regni faceret, idq; sacramento firmaret, dimitteret Ecclesias libertas cum oblationibus & possessionibus quæ ad Regnum non pertinent, absolveret Papa ab juramentis populos, quæ contra Episcopos compulsi sunt; patrimonia possessionesq; beati Petri restitueret, sicuti à Carolo, Ludovico, Henrico aliisq; Imperatoribus concessa sunt libera, servaretq; ea beato Petro pro juribus; nihil faceret ut Papa Pontificatum amittat, nihilq; ipse patiatur in vita vel in membris, vel capiatur captione, aut per se, aut per suspectam personam, nec ipse, nec fideles ejus, qui pro ipso fidem dederint, id est, Petrum Leonis cum filiis suis, quorum bona nullum patiantur detrimentum, & si quod fecerit, Rex fideliter ipsos adjuvaret. Pro hujusmodi observandis Pontificis prædes dabit Fridericum sororis suæ filium, Engilbertum & Theobaldum Marchiones, Herimannum & Gotfridum Comites, Fridericum Palatinum Comitem Saxonum, Berengarium de Bajoaria, Fridericum Saxonem, Albertum Cancellarium, Cononem Berengarii fratrem, Siceboth Bajoarium, Henricum Carinthiæ Ducem, Bertulfum Bertulfi Ducis filium,
units.tr: Between the envoys of the Emperor and Peter Leonis and the other envoys of the Pope, it was agreed in the portico of St Peter's that on the day of his coronation the Emperor would surrender in writing into the Pope's hands, in the presence of Cletus and the people, all the ecclesiastical rights he had wrongfully seized, and that the Pope would confirm this by oath when he dealt with the affairs of the kingdom. The churches are to be released into freedom, along with the offerings and possessions that do not belong to the kingdom. The Pope is to absolve the people from the oaths they were forced to swear against the bishops. He is to restore the patrimonies and possessions of the blessed Peter, which were granted free by Charles, Louis, Henry and other emperors, and to keep them for the blessed Peter as his rights. The Pope shall do nothing by which he loses the papacy, and he himself shall suffer no harm to life or limb, nor be taken captive, either in person or through a suspect agent. Neither he nor his faithful, who have given their faith for him, namely Peter Leonis with his sons, shall suffer loss of goods; and if any harm is done, the King shall faithfully help them. For the observance of these terms, the Pope's sureties will be Frederick, his sister's son, the Margraves Engelbert and Theobald, the Counts Herimann and Godfrey, Frederick the Count Palatine, the Saxon Berengar of Bavaria, Frederick the Saxon, Albert the Chancellor, Cono, brother of Berengar, Siceboth of Bavaria, Henry Duke of Carinthia, and Bertulf, son of Duke Bertulf.

units.la: Qui jurabit Papæ securitatem de vita, de membris, de Papatu, de captione. Quæ nisi Imperator servaret, ad Romanam Ecclesiam cum suis honoribus teneretur. Obsides pro securitate Pontificis Reddare pollicitus est proxima V. feria, cosq; securè ad insulam mittere in potestatem Papæ,
units.tr: Each of these shall swear to the Pope that he will guarantee his life, his limbs, his papacy and his freedom from capture. If the Emperor did not keep these terms, he would be bound to the Roman Church together with his honours. He promised to return hostages for the Pope's safety on the Thursday following, and to send them safely to the island, into the Pope's power.

units.la: FrideaFridericum Ducem nepotem suum,
units.tr: Frederick, the Duke, his nephew,

units.la: Brunonem Episcopum Spirensem,
units.tr: Bruno, Bishop of Speyer,

units.la: Conradum nepotem Comitis Herimanni, & filium ejus,
units.tr: Conrad, the nephew of Count Herimann, and his son,

units.la: & Henricum Friderici Comitis fratrem.
units.tr: and Henry, brother of Count Frederick.

units.la: Obsides si recepissFet, eos redderet in die Coronationis suae, ponte transmisso: & si forte coronatus non fuisset, aut non transisset, similiter redderet apud Castellum Sancti Angeli. Legatos, quos ad eum Papa dirigerer, dum irent & redirent, securos a se suisque redderet, & si eis scienter aliquid injurium esset, emendaturum fideliter.
units.tr: If he had received the hostages, he would return them on the day of his coronation, after crossing the bridge. And if by chance he were not crowned, or did not cross, he would likewise return them at the Castle of St Angelo. He would also return the legates whom the Pope sent to him safe from himself and his people, both while they went and while they came back; and if anything wrong were knowingly done to them, he would faithfully make amends.

units.la: 1. Quae postquam omnia impleverit Rex, Papa juberet Episcopis adstantibus in die Coronationis ejus, ut regalia Imperatori dimitterent, quae a temporibus Caroli, Ludovici, Henrici, aliorumque predecessorum ad Regnum pertinebant; scripto firmarent sub anathematis poena, auctoritate sua, ne quorum vel praesentium vel absentium, vel successores eorum Regni se intromitterent juribus, neque invaderent civitates, Ducatus, Comitatus, monetas, vectigalia, mercata. Advocationes Imperatorum, centurionum jura, curtesque esset Imperii cum pertinentiis suis, & militaria Imperii castra. Nec Imperatorem, nec Romanum Imperium, super his ulterius inquietaret, & privilegio sub anathemate confirmaret, ne posteri sui ultra inquietare praesumerent. Imperatorem benigne & cum honore suscAperet, & more praedecessorum ipsius Catholicorum Imperatorum, scienter & non sub tecto coronaret, & ad tenendum Imperium officii sui juvaret auxilio. Haec si Papa non impleret, Petrus Leonis cum suis omnibus se ad Imperatorem teneret. Obsides, nisi effugerent, altero post Coronationem die restitueret: si ex ipsius Papae parte remanserit, ut non coronetur, similiter redderet. Haec ita constituta jure jurando firmavit Imperator,
units.tr: 1. When the King had done all these things, the Pope would order the bishops present at his coronation to surrender to the Emperor the regalia which, from the times of Charles, Louis, Henry and the other predecessors, belonged to the kingdom. They were to confirm in writing, under penalty of anathema and by his authority, that neither they, nor their successors, whether present or absent, would intrude upon these rights of the kingdom or seize the cities, duchies, counties, mints, tolls or markets. The advocacies of the emperors, the rights of the centurions, and the courts of the Empire with their appurtenances, and the military camps of the Empire, are to remain his. The Pope shall not further disturb the Emperor or the Roman Empire concerning these matters, and shall confirm by privilege, under anathema, that his successors also shall not presume to disturb them. He shall receive the Emperor kindly and with honour, and, after the manner of his Catholic predecessors, crown him knowingly and not under a roof, and help him with his aid to hold the Empire as his duty requires. If the Pope did not fulfil these terms, Peter Leonis with all his people would side with the Emperor. The hostages, unless they escaped, he would return the day after the coronation; and if the failure to crown him came from the Pope's side, he would likewise return them. The Emperor confirmed these terms by oath,

units.la: Albertus Cancellarius,
units.tr: Albert the Chancellor,

units.la: Herimannus, Fridericus & Gothifridus Comites,
units.tr: Herimann, Frederick and Godfrey, the Counts,

units.la: Fridericus Saxo,
units.tr: Frederick the Saxon,

units.la: Cono Berengarii frater,
units.tr: Cono, brother of Berengar,

units.la: Siceborh de Bavaria,
units.tr: Siceborh of Bavaria,

units.la: Henricus Carinthiae Dux,
units.tr: Henry, Duke of Carinthia,

units.la: Bertulfus Bertulfi Ducis filius.
units.tr: Bertulf, son of Duke Bertulf.

units.la: Hi omnes post Imperatorem eo ordine juraverunt, ut si Imperator haec implere nollet, ipsi cum omnibus suis cum Romana Ecclesia tenerent.
units.tr: All these swore after the Emperor, in that order, that if the Emperor were unwilling to fulfil these terms, they themselves with all their people would side with the Roman Church.

units.la: TRANSACTIO INTER HENRICUM V. IMPERA- TOREM ET PASCHALEM II. PAPAM DE INVESTITURIS ECCLESIASTICORUM.
units.tr: AGREEMENT BETWEEN HENRY V, EMPEROR, AND PASCHAL II, POPE, CONCERNING INVESTITURES OF ECCLESIASTICAL OFFICES.

units.la: IN verbo Pontificis juratum est in agro juxta Pontem Mammeum, qui Romanos Teutonesque dirimebat, hoc videlicet modo: Quod ulterius non inquietaret Imperatorem eiusque Imperium de praesumpto detemerato Ecclesiarum jure, & de injuria sibi suisque irrogata in persona Imperatoris, ac bonis nullum aliquod sibi vel alicui personae non redderet, neque pro hac causa Imperatorem unquam anathemati subderet, eidemque Imperatori privilegio sub anathemate confirmaret, ut episcopos & Abbates liberè electos absque Symonia, idem Imperator anulo & virga investiat, Episcopi vero sic investitus liberè consecrationem ab Archiepiscopo, ad quem pertinuerit, sumat. Si quis populo & Clero eligatur, & non ab Imperatore investiatur, à nemine consecretur, & Archiepiscopi Episcopi libertatem habentem securandi ita amissos ab Imperatore, Regnumque, & Imperium pacum officii sui auxilio illi conservabit.
units.tr: On the word of the Pope it was sworn in a field near the Mammean Bridge, which divided the Romans and the Germans, in this manner: that he would no longer trouble the Emperor and his Empire concerning the presumed and rash right over the churches, nor concerning the injury done to himself and his people in the person of the Emperor and in his goods; that he would not return any of these to himself or to any other person; that for this cause he would never subject the Emperor to anathema; and that he would confirm to the same Emperor by privilege, under anathema, that the Emperor himself should invest bishops and abbots freely elected, without simony, with the ring and the staff. A bishop so invested should receive consecration freely from the archbishop to whom it belongs. If anyone is elected by the people and clergy and is not invested by the Emperor, let him be consecrated by no one; and the archbishops and bishops, having the freedom to secure their offices, shall keep for him, by the help of their office, the kingdom and empire in peace, as they were lost from the Emperor.

units.la: Cum haec sacramento firmasset, Imperator demum, quod eundem Pontificem cum Episcopis, & omnes, qui cum eo vel pro eo capti essent, obsidesque, & securos perduceret in Transtyberinae civitatis, neque ulterius aut caperet aut capi permitteret, juravit his, qui in Apostolicae manerent; & Populo Romano tam per se, quam per suos, pacem servaret, eundemque fideliter juvaret, ut Papatum secure & quiete teneret, patrimonia & possessiones Ecclesiae Romanae restitueret, cetera, quae de jure habere debet, more antecessorum recuperare ac tenere bona fide, & eidem Pontifici fideliter obedirer, salvo honore Imperii & Regni, sicuti Catholici Imperatores Catholicis Romanis Pontificibus solent. Post haec Fridericus Colonienśis Archiepiscopus, Gebehardus Tridentinensis, Episcopi, Burcardus Monasteriensis, Episcopi, Bruno Spirensis, Albertus Cancellarius, Fridericus, Herimannus, Comites, Albertus, Fridericus,
units.tr: When he had confirmed these things by oath, the Emperor at last swore to those who remained in the Apostolic See, and to the Roman people, both personally and through his own men, that he would keep the peace; that he would faithfully help the same Pope so that he might hold the papacy securely and quietly; that he would restore the patrimonies and possessions of the Roman Church and recover and hold in good faith the other things which it ought to have by right, in the manner of his predecessors; and that he would faithfully obey the same Pope, saving the honour of the Empire and the Kingdom, as Catholic Emperors are accustomed to do for Catholic Roman Pontiffs. After this, Frederick, Archbishop of Cologne, Gebhard, Bishop of Trent, Burchard, Bishop of Münster, Bruno, Bishop of Speyer, Albert the Chancellor, Frederick, Herman, Counts, Albert, Frederick,

units.la: Y BerengaBerengarius, Fridericus, Gothfridus, & Guarnerius ac Bonifacius Marchio, in hunc modum juraverunt.
units.tr: and Berengarius, Frederick, Godfrey, and Guarnerius, and Marquess Boniface, swore in this manner.

units.la: HENRICI V. IMPER. AUG. ET PASCHALIS II. PAPÆ CONVENTIONES DE PACE PVBLICA, ET INVESTITVRIS EC- clesiasticorum.
units.tr: Conventions of the Emperor Henry V and Pope Paschal II concerning the public peace and the investiture of ecclesiastics.

units.la: JURAMENTUM IMPERATORIS.
units.tr: The Oath of the Emperor.

units.la: EGo Henricus Imperator liberos dimittam quarta vel quinta feria proxima Dominum Papam Paschalem, & Episcopos, & Cardinales, & omnes captivos & obsides, qui pro eo & eo capti sunt, & liberos secure produci faciam intra portam Transtiberinae civitatis: nec ullo modo capiam, aut capi faciam vel permittam eos, qui in fidelitate Domni Papae Paschalis permanent & populo Romano, & Transtiberinae insulae civitati pacem & securitatem servabo tam per me quam per meos, & in personis & in rebus, qui pacem mihi servaverint.
units.tr: I, the Emperor Henry, will release the lord Pope Paschal, and the bishops, cardinals, and all the captives and hostages who have been taken on his account, on the fourth or fifth day next, and will have them brought out safely and unhindered through the gate of the Transtiberine city. I will not seize them, nor cause or permit them to be seized, who remain in the fidelity of the lord Pope Paschal and of the Roman people; and I will keep peace and security for the city and the Transtiberine island, both by myself and by my men, both in persons and in goods, for those who have kept the peace toward me.

units.la: 2. Patrimonia & possessiones sanctae Romanae Ecclesiae, quae abstuli, restituam; & cuncta, quae habere debet, more antecessorum meorum recuperare & tenere adjuvabo bona fide. Et Domno Papae Paschali obediam, (salvo tamen honore Regni & Imperii) sicut Catholici Imperatores Catholicis Pontificibus Romanis. Haec omnia observabo bona fide, sine fraude & malo ingenio.
units.tr: 2. I will restore the patrimonies and possessions of the holy Roman Church which I have taken away, and I will help in good faith to recover and hold all that it ought to have, in the manner of my predecessors. And I will obey the lord Pope Paschal (saving, however, the honour of the Kingdom and the Empire), as Catholic emperors obeyed Catholic Roman pontiffs. I will observe all these things in good faith, without fraud or evil design.

units.la: Erisi sunt juratores ex parte Imperatoris HENRICI: Fredericus Coloniensis Archiepiscopus, Gebehardus Tridentinensis Episcopus, Bruno Spirensis Episcopus, Bruchardus Monasteriensis Episcopus, Albertus Cancellarius, Herimannus Comes, [al. Dux] Berengarius Comes Sultzbachensis, Fredericus Comes Palatinus, Item Fredericus Comes, Bonifacius Marchio Tusciae, Albertus Comes de Blandriaco, Godefridus Comes Palatinus Rheni, Warnerius Marchio.
units.tr: These were the swearers on the part of the Emperor Henry: Frederick, Archbishop of Cologne; Gebhard, Bishop of Trent; Bruno, Bishop of Speyer; Burchard, Bishop of Münster; Albert, the chancellor; Hermann, Count [another reading: Duke]; Berengar, Count of Sulzbach; Frederick, Count Palatine; likewise Frederick, Count; Boniface, Margrave of Tuscany; Albert, Count of Blandrate; Godfrey, Count Palatine of the Rhine; Warner, Margrave.

units.la: CONCESSIO PAPAE DE INVESTITVRIS Episcopatuum.
units.tr: The Pope's Concession concerning the Investiture of Bishoprics.

units.la: DOmnus Papa Paschalis concedit Domno Imperatori Henrico, & Regno privilegio suo sub anathemate, & confirmabit, & corroborabit, Episcopo vel Abbate electo sine symonia assensu Imperatoris, quod Domnus Imperator eum annulo & virga investiat. Episcopus autem vel Abbas ab Imperatore investitus libere accipiat consecrationem ab Episcopo, ad quem pertinuerit. Si quis vero a Clero & a populo eligatur, nisi ab Imperatore investiatur, & a nemine consecretur, & Archiepiscopi & Episcopi libertatem habeant consecrandi ab Imperatore investitos. Super his etiam Domnus Papa Paschalis non inquietabit Imperatorem Henricum, nec ejus Regnum & Imperium.
units.tr: The lord Pope Paschal grants to the lord Emperor Henry and to the Kingdom, by his privilege, under anathema, and will confirm and strengthen, that when a bishop or abbot has been elected without simony and with the Emperor's assent, the lord Emperor shall invest him with the ring and staff. Moreover, a bishop or abbot invested by the Emperor shall freely receive consecration from the bishop to whom it pertains. But if anyone is chosen by the clergy and people, and is not invested by the Emperor, let him be consecrated by no one; and archbishops and bishops shall have liberty to consecrate those invested by the Emperor. Concerning these matters, the lord Pope Paschal shall not disturb the Emperor Henry, nor his Kingdom and Empire.

units.la: SACRAMENTVM EX PARTE PAPAE.
units.tr: The Oath on the Part of the Pope.

units.la: DOmnus Papa Paschalis non inquietabit Domnum Imperatorem Henricum, nec ejus Regnum, de investitura Episcopatuum & Abbatiarum, neque de injuria sibi illata & in personis & bonis, neque aliquod malum reddet sibi vel alicui personae pro hac causa; & penitus in personam Imperatoris Henrici nunquam anathema ponet, nec remanebit in Domno Papa, quin coronet eum, sicut in Ordine cotinetur, & Regnum & Imperium officii sui auxilio cum tenere adjuvabit pro posse suo. Et haec adimplebit Domnus Papa sine fraude & malo ingenio.
units.tr: The lord Pope Paschal will not disturb the lord Emperor Henry, nor his Kingdom, concerning the investiture of bishoprics and abbacies, nor concerning the injury done to him in persons and goods; nor will he render any evil to him or to any person for this cause; and he will never at all lay anathema upon the person of the Emperor Henry, nor will the lord Pope refrain from crowning him, as is contained in the Order; and he will help him, by the aid of his office, to hold the Kingdom and Empire to the best of his power. And the lord Pope will fulfil these things without fraud or evil design.

units.la: Haec sunt nomina illorum Episcoporum & Cardinalium, qui praecepto Domni Papae Paschalis privilegium & amicitiam sacramento confirmaverunt Domno Imperatori HENRICO: Petrus Portuensis Episcopus, Centius Sabinienfis Episcopus, Robertus Cardinalis Sancti Eusebii, Bonifacius Cardinalis Sancti Martini,
units.tr: These are the names of those bishops and cardinals who, at the command of the lord Pope Paschal, confirmed by oath the privilege and friendship to the lord Emperor Henry: Peter, Bishop of Porto; Centius, Bishop of Sabina; Robert, Cardinal of Saint Eusebius; Boniface, Cardinal of Saint Martin;

units.la: Anastasius Cardinalis Sancti Clementis.
units.tr: Anastasius, Cardinal of Saint Clement.

units.la: Gregorius Cardinalis Apostolorum Petri & Pauli.
units.tr: Gregory, Cardinal of the Apostles Peter and Paul.

units.la: Item Gregorius Cardinalis Sancti Chrysogoni.
units.tr: Likewise Gregory, Cardinal of Saint Chrysogonus.

units.la: Joannes Cardinalis Sanctæ Potentianæ.
units.tr: John, Cardinal of Saint Potentiana.

units.la: Risus Cardinalis Sancti Laurentii.
units.tr: Rizo, Cardinal of Saint Lawrence.

units.la: Rainerus Cardinalis Sanctorum Marcellini & Petri.
units.tr: Rainer, Cardinal of Saints Marcellinus and Peter.

units.la: Vitalis Cardinalis Sanctæ Balbinæ.
units.tr: Vitalis, Cardinal of Saint Balbina.

units.la: Dinzo Cardinalis Sancti Marci.
units.tr: Dinzo, Cardinal of Saint Mark.

units.la: Theobaldus Cardinalis Joannis & Pauli.
units.tr: Theobald, Cardinal of Saints John and Paul.

units.la: Joannes Diaconus Sanctæ Mariæ in Schola Græca.
units.tr: John, Deacon of Saint Mary in the Greek School.

units.la: Leo b Diaconus Sancti Vitalis Martyris.
units.tr: Leo, Deacon of Saint Vitalis the Martyr.

units.la: Abbo c Diaconus Sanctorum Sergii & Bachi.
units.tr: Abbo, Deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus.

units.la: PRIVILEGIVM PASCHALIS PAPÆ, QUOD FECIT IMPERATORI HENRICO, DE INVESTI- TURIS EPISCOPATUUM ET ABBATIARUM.
units.tr: PRIVILEGE OF POPE PASCHAL, WHICH HE GAVE TO THE EMPEROR HENRY, CONCERNING THE INVESTITURE OF BISHOPRICS AND ABBEYS.

units.la: Paschalis Episcopus, servus servorum Dei, carissimo in Christo filio, Henrico Teutonicorum Regi, & per Dei omnipotentis gratiam Romanorum Imperatori Augusto, salutem & Apostolicam benedictionem.
units.tr: Paschal, Bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his most beloved son in Christ, Henry, King of the Teutons, and by the grace of almighty God Augustus Emperor of the Romans, greeting and apostolic blessing.

units.la: 1. Regnum vestrum sanctæ Romanæ Ecclesiæ singulariter cohærere dispositio divina constituit. Prædecessores siquidem vestri probitatis & prudentiæ amplioris gratia Romanæ Urbis coronam & imperium consecuti sunt. Ad cujus videlicet coronæ & imperii dignitatem, tuam quoq; personam, Fili carissime Henrice, per nostri sacerdotii ministerium Majestas divina provexit. Illam igitur dignitatis prærogativam, quam prædecessores nostri vestris prædecessoribus Catholicis Imperatoribus concesserunt, & privilegiorum paginis confirmaverunt, nos quoque tuæ Dilectioni concedimus, & præsentis privilegii pagina confirmamus, ut Regni tui Episcopis & Abbatibus liberè præter violentiam & symoniam electis, investituram virgæ & annuli conferas; post investionem verò canonicè consecrationem accipiant ab Episcopo, ad quem pertinuerit.
units.tr: 1. The divine disposition has established that your kingdom clings in a special way to the holy Roman Church. Your predecessors indeed obtained the crown and empire of the City of Rome by reason of their uprightness and greater prudence. And to the dignity of that crown and empire the divine Majesty has raised your own person, dearest son Henry, through the ministry of our priesthood. We therefore grant to your Dilection that prerogative of dignity which our predecessors granted to your Catholic predecessors, the Emperors, and confirmed by the pages of their privileges; and by the page of this present privilege we confirm it, namely that you may confer the investiture with the staff and ring upon the bishops and abbots of your kingdom who are freely elected, without violence or simony; and after the investiture, they shall receive canonical consecration from the bishop to whom it belongs.

units.la: 2. Si quis autem à Clero, vel à Populo præter assensum tuum electus fuerit, nisi à te investiatur, à nemine consecretur: [exceptis nimirum illis, qui vel in Archiepiscoporum, vel in Romani Pontificis dispositione consistere.]
units.tr: 2. But if anyone is elected by the clergy or the people without your assent, let him not be consecrated by anyone unless he is first invested by you; [excepting, of course, those who stand under the disposition of the Archbishops or of the Roman Pontiff.]

units.la: 3. Sanè Archiepiscopi & Episcopi libertatem habeant à te investitos Episcopos & Abbates canonice consecrandi.
units.tr: 3. Moreover, let the archbishops and bishops have the liberty of canonically consecrating the bishops and abbots invested by you.

units.la: 4. Prædecessores enim vestri Ecclesias Regni sui tantis regalium suorum beneficiis ampliarunt, Regnum ipsum Episcoporum maximè & Abbatum præsidiis oporteat comuniri, & populares dissensiones, quæ in electionibus sæpè contingunt, regali oporteat Majestate compesci. Quamobrem prudentiæ vestræ & potestati cura debet sollicitius imminere, ut & Romanæ Ecclesiæ magnitudo, & cetera salus, tuis (præstante Domino) beneficiis & servitiis consetvetur.
units.tr: 4. For your predecessors enlarged the churches of their kingdom with so many of their royal benefits; it is fitting that the kingdom itself be fortified chiefly by the support of bishops and abbots, and that popular dissensions, which often arise in elections, be curbed by royal majesty. Therefore the care of your prudence and power ought to attend more diligently to this, so that both the greatness of the Roman Church and the general welfare may be preserved, by your benefits and services (the Lord granting it).

units.la: 5. Si quia igitur Ecclesiastica vel Secularis potentia aut persona hanc nostræ concessionis paginam contra eam temerario ausu venire tentaverit, anathematis vinculo, nisi resipuerit, innodetur, honorisque ac dignitatis suæ periculum patiatur. Observantes autem hoc misericordia divina custodiat personam ac majestatem potestatemque tuam ad honorem suum & gloriam feliciter imperare concedat.
units.tr: 5. If therefore any ecclesiastical or secular power or person shall rashly presume to act against this page of our concession, let him be bound with the chain of anathema unless he repents, and let him suffer the peril of his honour and dignity. But may the mercy of God keep those who observe this, and guard your person, majesty and power, and grant that you may reign happily to His honour and glory.

units.la: CONFIRMATIO.
units.tr: CONFIRMATION.

units.la: Hæc sunt verba, quæ dixit Domnus Apostolicus Domno Imperatori Henrico in communione corporis & sanguinis Christi, die Coronationis suæ: Domne Imperator Henrice, corpus Domini natum ex Maria Virgine, passum in cruce pro nobis, sicut sancta Catholica tenet Ecclesia, damus tibi in confirmationem veræ pacis & concordiæ inter me & te, Amen. Anno Verbi incarnati MCXI. hoc confirmatum est in basilica Sancti Petri, xvi. Cal. Martii, regnante in cœlis Domino nostro Jesu Christo cum Patre æterno & Spiritu sancto, Amen.
units.tr: These are the words which the Lord Apostolic spoke to the Lord Emperor Henry in communion of the body and blood of Christ, on the day of his coronation: "Lord Emperor Henry, the body of the Lord, born of the Virgin Mary, suffered on the cross for us, as the holy Catholic Church holds, we give to you in confirmation of true peace and concord between me and you. Amen." In the year of the incarnate Word 1111, this was confirmed in the basilica of St Peter, on the sixteenth day before the calends of March, Our Lord Jesus Christ reigning in heaven with the eternal Father and the Holy Spirit, Amen.

units.la: HENRICI V. IMP. AUG. EDICTUM DE INVESTITVRIS ECCLESIASTICORVM.
units.tr: THE EDICT OF EMPEROR HENRY V CONCERNING THE INVESTITURE OF CHURCHMEN.

units.la: Henricus Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator Augustus, omnibus Christi fidelibus in Ecclesia.
units.tr: Henry, Emperor and Augustus of the Romans by the grace of God, to all the faithful of Christ in the Church.

units.la: 1. Notum esse volumus dilectioni & discretioni vestræ ea, quæ inter nos & Dominum illum lum Paschalem erant, quomodo incepta tractata sint: scilicet de conventione inter me & ipsum de traditione Romanorum in me & meos, ut audita intelligatis, intellecta examinetis, examinata dijudicetis.
units.tr: 1. We wish it to be known to your affection and discernment what was begun and handled between us and that Lord Paschal, namely the agreement between me and him concerning the surrender of the Romans to me and mine, so that, having heard it, you may understand; having understood it, you may examine; and having examined it, you may judge.

units.la: 2. Igitur dum in eo totus essem, ut me ad Ecclesiae utilitatem & ipsius votum, si justum esset, componerem, coepit exaltationem & dilatationem regni super omnes antecessores meos promittere. Studebat tamen subdole, quomodo Regnum & Ecclesiam a statu suo discinderet, tractare. Quod facere aggressus est. Regno quidem jam a Carolo quadringentis & amplius annis, & sub sexaginta trious Apostolicis investituras Episcopatuum, eorundem authoritate & privilegiorum firmitate tenenti, absque omni audientia auferre volebat.
units.tr: 2. Therefore, while I was wholly intent on settling matters for the good of the Church and according to his wish, if it were just, he began to promise an exaltation and enlargement of the kingdom above all my predecessors. Yet he was craftily plotting how to tear the kingdom and the Church away from their proper state, and he set about doing so. He wished to take away without any hearing the investitures of bishoprics, which the kingdom had held since Charles, for more than four hundred years, and under sixty-three apostolic pontiffs, by their authority and the firmness of their privileges.

units.la: 3. Et quum per Nuncios nostros ab eo quaereremus, quid de Nobis fieret, in quo Regnum nostrum constat, quomodo fere omnia antecessores nostri Ecclesiis concesserunt & tradiderunt, sub-junxit: Fratres, Ecclesiae decimas & oblationibus suis contenta sint: Rex vero praedia & regalia, quae a Carolo & Ludevico, Ottone & Henrico Ecclesiis collata sunt, sibi & successoribus suis recipiat & detineat. Ad hoc quum nostri responderent, Nos quidem nolle violentiam Ecclesiis inferre, nec ista subtrahendo rot sacrilegia incurrere, fiducialiter promisit, & faciamus eo pro eo firmavit Dominica Esto mihi, si omnia haec cum justitia & authoritate Ecclesiis auferre, Nobisque & Regno cum justitia & authoritate reddere. Multi itidem firmantibus, si hoc, ut praemissum est, ita complesset, quod tamen nullo modo fieri potest. Eabatime quoque, uti quaerebat, investituras Ecclesiarum resignaturum: sicut in Charta conventionis plenius poterius videre.
units.tr: 3. When we asked him through our envoys what would become of us, on whom our kingdom depends, since almost all our predecessors had granted and handed over these things to the churches, he added: "Brothers, let the churches be content with their tithes and offerings; let the king receive and keep for himself and his successors the estates and regalia which Charles and Louis, Otto and Henry conferred on the churches." When our men replied that we were unwilling to inflict violence on the churches, nor to incur such sacrileges by withdrawing these things, he promised confidently, and confirmed with the Lord's oath, "So help me," that if he could take away all these things from the churches with justice and authority, and restore them to us and the kingdom with justice and authority, he would do so. Many likewise affirmed that if this were accomplished as premised, which in no way can be done. He would also, as he was asked, resign the investitures of the churches, as you may see more fully in the charter of agreement.

units.la: HAEC EST CHARTA CONVENTIONIS EIVS AD ME.
units.tr: THIS IS THE CHARTER OF HIS AGREEMENT WITH ME.

units.la: DOMINUS Papa praecipiet Episcopis praesentibus in die coronationis Regis, ut dimittant regalia Regno, quae ad Regnum pertinebant tempore Caroli, Henrici, & aliorum praedecessorum ejus; & scripto firmabit sub anathemate, ne quis eorum vel praesentium, vel absentium, vel successorum eorum, intromittant se ullo modo, vel invadant eandem regalia, id est civitates, Ducatus, Marchias, Comitatus, monetas, teloneum, mercatum, Advocatias, omnia jura Centuriorum, id est Villicorum, turres & villas, quae Regni erant, cum omnibus pertinentiis suis, militiam & castra. Nec ipse Regem & Regnum super his ulterius inquietabit, sed privilegio suo sub anathemate confirmabit, nec super suos inquietare praesumant: Regem benigne & honorifice suscipiet, & more praedecessorum suorum Catholicorum fideliter non subtracto coronabit, & ad tenendum Regnum cum his omnibus officii sui auxilio adjuvabit.
units.tr: The Lord Pope shall instruct the bishops present on the day of the king's coronation to surrender to the kingdom the regalia which belonged to the kingdom in the time of Charles, Henry and his other predecessors; and he shall confirm in writing under anathema that none of them, whether present, absent or their successors, shall in any way meddle with or invade those same regalia, namely cities, duchies, marches, counties, mints, tolls, markets, advocacies, all the rights of the centuries, that is, of the bailiffs, towers and estates which were of the kingdom, with all their appurtenances, military service and castles. Nor shall he himself further trouble the king and the kingdom about these matters, but shall confirm this by his privilege under anathema; nor shall they presume to trouble their own people about them. He shall receive the king kindly and honourably, and, after the manner of his Catholic predecessors, crown him faithfully and without withholding anything, and shall assist him with all the help of his office in holding the kingdom with all these things.

units.la: Si Dominus Papa haec Regi non adimpleverit; ego Petrus Leonis juro, quod tota potentia mea tenebo ad Dominum Regem. Obsides autem, nisi effugerint, reddemus altero die post coronationem Regis. Si per Papam remanserit, ita coronetur similiter reddendum Dominico die quum Rex ad processionem venerit. Obsides dabo Gratianum filium meum, & filium Vizonis filii, & filium sororis meae, si eum habere potero.
units.tr: If the Lord Pope does not fulfil these things for the king, I, Peter Leo, swear that I will hold with all my power for the Lord King. We will return the hostages, unless they escape, on the second day after the king's coronation. If it is the Pope's fault that it does not happen, the king shall be crowned in the same way, and the hostages shall be returned on the Sunday when the king comes to the procession. I will give as hostages my son Gratian, the son of Vizo the son, and the son of my sister, if I can have him.

units.la: HAEC SVNT SACRAMENTA EX PARTE DOMINI Papa- e:
units.tr: THESE ARE THE OATHS ON THE PART OF THE LORD POPE:

units.la: EGO Petrus Leonis juro vobis, quia Dominus Papa proximo die Dominico adimplebit Regi, quod in Charta conventionis scriptum est.
units.tr: I, Peter Leo, swear to you that the Lord Pope will fulfil for the king, on the next Sunday, what is written in the charter of agreement.

units.la: HAEC SVNT SACRAMENTA EX PARTE REGIS:
units.tr: THESE ARE THE OATHS ON THE PART OF THE KING:

units.la: Ego Comes Hermannus: Ego Comes Gotfridus: Ego Volmarus: Ego Adelbertus,
units.tr: I, Count Hermann; I, Count Godfrey; I, Volmar; I, Adalbert,

units.la: Juro vobis, quia Dominus Rex proxima quarta vel quinta feria ita Principes jurare faciet, & obsides dabit sicut in Charta conventionis scriptum est. Et sic observabunt Domino Papae, eo tenore, si Dominus Papa proximo die Dominico sic adimpleverit Regi per omnia, sicut in Charta conventionis scriptum est.
units.tr: swear to you that the Lord King will make the princes swear on the next fourth or fifth day, and will give hostages, as is written in the charter of agreement. And they will keep faith with the Lord Pope on this condition: that if the Lord Pope thus fulfils everything for the king on the next Sunday, as is written in the charter of agreement.

units.la: 4. Ego vero, ut ostenderem, nullam Ecclesiarum Dei disturbationem ex velle nostro procedere, in cunctorum oculis astantium & auribus hoc Decretum promulgavi:
units.tr: 4. But I, in order to show that no disturbance of God's churches proceeds from my will, promulgated this decree in the sight and hearing of all who stood by:

units.la: Ego Henricus Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator Augustus, affirmando & beato Petro, omnibus Episcopis & Abbatibus, & omnibus Ecclesiis omnia, quae antecessores mei Reges vel etiam Imperatores eis concesserunt vel tradiderunt, & quae illi prosperae aeternae retributionis obtinuerunt, do. Ego peccator pro timore terribilis judicii nullo modo subtrahere recuso.
units.tr: I, Henry, by the grace of God Emperor and Augustus of the Romans, affirming it to blessed Peter, to all bishops and abbots, and to all churches, give all the things which my predecessors, kings or even emperors, granted or handed over to them, and which they obtained for the prosperity of eternal reward. I, a sinner, out of fear of the terrible judgment, by no means refuse to restore them.

units.la: 5. Hoc Decreto a me lecto & subscripto, petii ab eo, ut, sicut in Charta conventionis ejus scriptum est, mihi adimpleret. Quum ergo supradictae postulationi insisterem, scilicet ut cum justitia & dignitate, promissa mihi conventione, fideliter universis in faciem ejus resistentibus, & Decreto suo palam haeresim incidere clamantibus, scilicet Episcopis, Abbatibus, tam suis quam nostris, & omnibus Ecclesiae filiis: hoc, si salva pace Ecclesiae dici potest, privilegium proferre voluit.
units.tr: 5. With this decree read and signed by me, I asked him to fulfil for me what was written in the charter of agreement. As I insisted on this demand, namely that the promised agreement be carried out faithfully and with justice and dignity, all those who resisted him to his face, and loudly cried that by his decree he was falling into heresy, namely bishops and abbots, both his own and ours, and all the sons of the Church, he wished to bring forward this privilege, which, if it can be said with the peace of the Church preserved, ...

units.la: PASCHALIS PAPAE DECRETVM.
units.tr: THE DECREE OF POPE PASCHAL

units.la: PASCHALIS Episcopus, servus servorum Dei, dilecto filio HENRICO Regi, & ejus successoribus Imperatoribus, &c.
units.tr: Paschal, Bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son Henry, King, and to his successors, the Emperors, etc.

units.la: Divina legis institutionibus sanctum est, & sacris canonibus interdictum, ne Sacerdotes curis secularibus occupentur, neve ad Comitatum, misipro damnatu erunt, atque pro aliis, qui injuriam patiuntur, accedant. Unde 1Corinth.6. & Apostolus Paulus inquit: Judicia si habueritis, contemptibiles qui sunt in Ecclesia, illos constituite ad judicandum. Investi Iv vestris autem Regni partibus Episcopi vel Abbates adeo curis secularibus occupantur, ut Comitatum assiduè frequentare, & militiam exercere cogantur: quæ nimirum aut vix aut nullo modo sine rapinis, sacrilegiis, incendiis, aut homicidiis exhibetur. Ministri vero altaris, ministri curiæ facti sunt: quia civitates, Ducatus, Marchionatus, monetas, telonea, & cætera ad Regni servitium pertinentia à Regibus acceperunt. Unde etiam mos Ecclesiæ intolerabilis molevit, ut electi Episcopi nullo modo consecrationem acciperent, nisi prius per manum Regiam investirentur. Aliquando etiam multi Episcopi investi sunt.
units.tr: The institutions of divine law have declared, and the sacred canons have forbidden, that priests should be occupied with secular cares, or be sent to the court as advocates for the condemned, or go on behalf of others who suffer wrong. Hence the Apostle Paul says in 1 Corinthians 6: "If you have judgments concerning things of this life, appoint to judge those who are of no account in the Church." But in your kingdom the bishops and abbots are so occupied with secular cares that they are compelled to attend the court constantly and to perform military service. This can scarcely, if at all, be carried out without robbery, sacrilege, arson, or murder. The ministers of the altar have become ministers of the court, for they have received from the kings cities, duchies, margraviates, mints, tolls, and other things pertaining to the service of the kingdom. Hence there has also arisen the intolerable custom of the Church, that elected bishops could not receive consecration in any way unless they were first invested by the royal hand. Sometimes, too, many bishops have been invested.

units.la: Hinc & aliis plurimis malis, quæ per investituram plerumque contigerant, prædecessores nostri Gregorius Octavus & Urbanus Secundus, felicis memoriæ Pontifices, excitati, collectis frequenter Episcopalibus Conciliis, investituras illas manus Laicæ damnaverunt: & si qui Clericorum per eam tenuissent Ecclesias, deponendos; datores quoque communione privandos percensuerunt, juxta illud Apostolicorum Canonum capitulum, quod se ita habet: Si quis Episcopus secularibus statibus usus Ecclesiam per ipsos obtineat, deponatur, & segregetur, omnesq; qui illi communicant. Quorum vestigia subsequentes & nos eorum sententiam Episcopali Concilio confirmamus.
units.tr: Because of this, and of very many other evils which generally came about through investiture, our predecessors Gregory VIII and Urban II, Popes of happy memory, were roused, and, having frequently convened episcopal councils, condemned those investitures by lay hands. They also determined that any of the clergy who had held churches through it should be deposed, and that the givers should be deprived of communion, according to that chapter of the Apostolic Canons which reads thus: "If any bishop, using secular powers, obtains a church through them, let him be deposed and cut off, and all who communicate with him." Following their footsteps, we too confirm their sentence by an episcopal council.

units.la: Tale itaque, fili charissime Henrice Rex, & nunc per officium nostrum Dei gratia Romanorum Imperatori, & Regi regalia illa dimittenda præcepimus, quæ ad Regnum manifestè pertinebant tempore Caroli, Ludovici, Ottonis, & ceterorum prædecessorum tuorum. Interdicimus etiam & sub anathematis districtione prohibemus, ne quis Episcoporum seu Abbatum, præsentium vel futurorum, eadem regalia invadant, id est civitates, Ducatus, Marchias, Comitatus, monetas, teloneum, mercatum, Advocatias, jura Centurionum, & turres, quæ Regni erant, cum pertinentiis suis, militiam & castra: & nec se deinceps, nisi per gratiam Regis, de ipsis regalibus intromittant. Sed nec posteris nostris liceat, qui post nos in Apostolica Sede successuri erunt, aut Te aut Regnum super hoc inquietare negocio.
units.tr: Accordingly, most beloved son Henry the King, who now by our office, by the grace of God, are Emperor of the Romans and King, we have commanded that those royal rights be relinquished which manifestly belonged to the kingdom in the time of Charles, Louis, Otto, and your other predecessors. We also forbid, and under the penalty of anathema prohibit, that any of the bishops or abbots, present or future, seize those same royal rights, namely cities, duchies, margraviates, counties, mints, tolls, markets, advocacies, the rights of centurions, and towers which belonged to the kingdom, with their appurtenances, military service and castles; and that they henceforth meddle with those royal rights only by the grace of the King. Nor let it be permitted to our successors, who will come after us in the Apostolic See, to disturb you or the kingdom in this matter.

units.la: Porrò Ecclesius cum oblationibus & hereditariis possessionibus, quæ ad Regnum manifestè pertinebant, liberas manere decrevimus, sicut in die coronationis tuæ Omnipotenti Domino in conspectu totius Ecclesiæ promisisti. Oportet enim Episcopos curis secularibus expeditos, curam suorum agere populorum, nec Ecclesiis suis abesse diutius. Ipsi enim, juxta Paulum Apostolum, pervigilant, tanquam rationem pro animabus eorum reddituri.
units.tr: Moreover, we have decreed that the churches, with their offerings and hereditary possessions, which manifestly belonged to the kingdom, remain free, as you promised before Almighty God in the sight of the whole Church on the day of your coronation. For it is right that bishops, freed from secular cares, should attend to the care of their peoples and not be absent from their churches longer than necessary. For they, according to the Apostle Paul, keep watch as those who must give account for their souls.

units.la: 6. De traditione verò in nos vel in nostros, sic seres habet. Vix portas civitatis ingressi sumus, cùm stris in fra muri moenia securè vagantibus, quidam vulnerati, alteri interfecti, omnes verò spoliati aut capti sunt. Ego tamen quasi pro levi causa non motus, bona & tranquilla mente usque ad Ecclesiam beati Petri januas cum processione perveni. Quod sic gestum fuisse, rei veritas multorum astipulatur testimoniis, qui interfuere, protestatur.
units.tr: 6. As for the betrayal against us or ours, the matter stands thus. We had scarcely entered the gates of the city when some of our men, wandering safely within the walls, were wounded, others killed, and all of them stripped or captured. Yet I, not moved as though by a slight cause, with a good and calm mind, came with the procession as far as the gates of the Church of Saint Peter. That this was done so, the truth of the matter is confirmed by the testimony of many who were present and bear witness.

units.la: HENRICI V. IMPER. AUG. EDICTUM
units.tr: EDICT OF HENRY V, EMPEROR AUGUSTUS

units.la: UT ARCHIEPISCOPO PROPTER REBELLIONEM ET perfidiam per Imperatorem damnato, nulla obedientia præstetur.
units.tr: THAT NO OBEDIENCE SHALL BE RENDERED TO THE ARCHBISHOP, WHO HAS BEEN CONDEMNED BY THE EMPEROR FOR REBELLION AND PERFIDY.

units.la: HEINRICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator Augustus, Præpositis & Decanis, & omni congregationi, cunctis etiam Moguntiensis Ecclesiæ civibus, tam majoribus, quàm minoribus sibi fidelibus, gratiam & omne bonum.
units.tr: Henry, by the grace of God Roman Emperor Augustus, to the provosts and deans, to the whole congregation, and also to all the citizens of the Church of Mainz, both greater and lesser, who are faithful to him: grace and every good.

units.la: 1. Confiteantur Domino misericordiæ ejus, & mirabilia ejus filiis hominum. quia non est prudentia, non est sapientia, non est consilium contra Dominum: qui, sancti Spiritus inspirante gratia, convertit corda patrum in filios, & corda filiorum ad patres ipsorum. Unde & nos non cessamus gratias agere pro vobis, cujus gratia & dono amara vestra dulcia facta sunt nobis. Et ideò, licet ineffabilem divinæ pietatis inspirationem luctum nostrum in gaudium, & amaritudinem verteredulcedinem, pro antiqua tamen fidelitate, quam in cordibus vestris divinitus jam incaluisse cognovimus, dilectionem vestram admonere potius, quàm rogare decernimus.
units.tr: 1. "Let them confess to the Lord his mercies, and his wonders to the sons of men; for there is no prudence, no wisdom, no counsel against the Lord" (Ps. 107). By the inspiration of the grace of the Holy Spirit, he turns the hearts of fathers to their sons and the hearts of sons to their fathers. Hence we too do not cease to give thanks for you, by whose grace and gift your bitter things have become sweet to us. And therefore, although the ineffable inspiration of divine piety turns our mourning into joy and bitterness into sweetness, we have decided to admonish your affection rather than to ask anything of you, on account of the old fidelity which we know has already been divinely kindled in your hearts.

units.la: Memores esse debetis in omnibus, qua fide, quo pacto, quibus sacramétis & obsidibus Adelbertum perjurum & traditorem, qui non meritis, sed nomine dicitur Episcopus, fidelitati vestræ strictissima conventione tradiderimus. Et cùm vos omnia bona, promittéretis nobis ab eo, & nihil promisso nihil, nisi bonum, speraremus, ab ipso exspectavimus pacem; & ecce turbatio. Enim Spiram ad nos redintegrata sibi corporis & honoris sui potestate veniens obsides manu ad manum ipse nobis præsentavit, & suis sacramentis vestra firmavit, statimque inde discedens, missis ubique litteris ac nunciis, nos & honorem nostrum impugnavit, ac per totam Saxoniam & Thuringiam, Bavariam & Alemanniam, amicos nostros, tanquam inimicos, contra nos ubique solicitare cœpit; sicque quasi canis, qui revertitur ad vomitum, antiquæ suæ perfidiæ recepit venenum, quasi vipera, quæ virus resumit post coitum, à mari usque ad mare per totum Regnum dissundit & Imperium. Pro his igitur & aliis malis, nobis responsurum, statutis inducis enim ad nos veniemus, & non venit. Sed insuper apponens iniquitatem super iniquitatem, Spiram, quod in cor nostrum altius ascendit, armatâ manu & ereētis militaribus signis violenter invadere voluit; sed frustrato Deo gratias) labore rediens, & congregatis, quos potuit, castrum nostrum Stroumburc funditus destruxit. deinde alia castra nostra contumaciter obsedit. Invasorem Virdunensis Ecclesiæ contra & fas consecrari fecit: Regnum nostrum & Imperium rapinis & homicidiis, cæde & incêdiis, quasi silva sic ubique devastavit, ut nihil jam in diversis ipsius restet erroribus, nisi ut fiant novíssima munus pejora prioribus.
units.tr: You must remember in all things by what faith, in what manner, and with what sacraments and hostages we handed over to your fidelity, under the strictest agreement, Adalbert, the perjurer and traitor, who is called bishop not by merit but by name. Since you promised us every good thing through him, and we hoped for nothing but good from his promise, we looked to him for peace; and behold, turmoil. For coming to us at Speyer, with the power of his body and his honour restored to him, he himself presented the hostages to us hand to hand, and confirmed your pledge with his sacraments; and immediately leaving there, by sending letters and messengers everywhere, he attacked us and our honour, and began to stir up our friends everywhere against us as if they were enemies, through all Saxony and Thuringia, Bavaria and Alemannia. And so, like a dog that returns to its vomit, he took back the poison of his old perfidy; like a viper that takes up its venom again after mating, he spreads it from sea to sea through the whole kingdom and empire. For these and other evils he was to answer to us, and he was to come to us at the appointed truce, and he did not come. Moreover, adding iniquity to iniquity, he wished to attack Speyer violently with an armed hand and raised military standards, which has risen higher in our heart; but he returned from his labour frustrated (thanks be to God), and, having gathered those he could, he utterly destroyed our castle of Strasbourg (Stroumburc). Then he stubbornly besieged our other castles. He caused an intruder into the Church of Verdun to be consecrated contrary to right and law. He laid waste our kingdom and empire with robberies and murders, slaughter and burnings, like a forest, everywhere, so that nothing now remains in his various errors except that the latest deeds should be worse than the earlier ones.

units.la: Y 3. Hæc igitur & alia mala, quorum non est numerus, licet ab Oriente usque in Occidentem in omnes sint omnibus, vobis tamen nota sunt eò melius, quò secretis ejus omnibus præ ceteris vos felicet familiaris fuistis familiarius. Sed & omnes, qui in Regno nostro sunt, sciunt, omnes clamare potuerunt, & tacuerint, lapides clamabunt. Et ideò, dilectissimi nobis tam clerici, quam laici; tam milites, quam cives, qui hæc omnia vidistis & audistis, diligenter apud vos cogitare & recogitare debetis, quanta fidem & dilectionem pro Sacramentis & obsidibus vestris vestra tibi dilectio debeat, qui nec proprium quidem fratrem suum, filiis scilicet fratrum suorum, debitam fidem servavit.
units.tr: 3. These and other evils, whose number is beyond counting, though they are known everywhere from East to West, are nonetheless better known to you, since you were more intimately familiar with all his secrets than anyone else. Moreover, all who are in our kingdom know them; all could cry out, and if they were silent, the stones would cry out. Therefore, most beloved to us, both clergy and laity, soldiers as well as citizens, who have seen and heard all these things, you must think carefully and reflect again on how much faith and affection your fidelity owes to our pledges and hostages, when he did not even keep due faith with his own brother's sons.

units.la: 4. Verùm, quia interalia speciali ter hoc in nostra conventione fuit, ut quando aliquid contra nos moliretur nostræ dignitati, statim determinatis induciis transactis, vestro studio & labore expellere curab urbe: idcirco si veti fidejussores crediti negocii esse desideratis, monemus vos omnes prædem & obl ides, quos dedistis, & Sacramenta, quæ fecistis, quatenus obsidibus vestris consulentes, sacramentis præcaventes, eundem perjurum vestrum ac nostrum, Adelbertum scilicet dictum Episcopum, civitatem nullatenus intrare permittatis, sed quasi scopus ab eo mundatam, cum Duce & Gotfrido Palatino Comite, aliisque fidelibus nostris, diligentissimè servare studeatis. Quod si fecerit is, & hæc omnia diligenter servaverit, præ omnibus, quos in Regno nostro habemus, ex amicis amicissimos vos semper habebimus.
units.tr: 4. But because, among other special terms of this agreement, it was stipulated that whenever he attempted anything against us or our dignity, then, once the appointed truce had passed, you would with your zeal and labour expel him from the city, therefore, if you wish to be the sureties of the business entrusted to you, we admonish you all, regarding the pledges and hostages you gave and the oaths you swore: that, looking after your hostages and guarding against your oaths, you permit that same perjurer of yours and ours, the aforesaid Bishop Adalbert, in no way to enter the city, but that you diligently strive to keep it cleansed of him, as of a target, together with the Duke, Count Palatine Godfrey, and our other faithful. If he does this and keeps all these things diligently, we shall always hold you, of all the friends we have in our kingdom, to be the most friendly.

units.la: 5. Et, si quid unquam peccaveritis in nos, exemplo illius peccatricis mulieris, totum transfibit multum, cui dimissa sunt peccata multa, quoniam dilexit multum. Quid plura? Deus, quiad hoc mundum, ut filios, qui erant dispersi, congregaret in unum, ita dispersos nostros sub jugum redigere coacervando revocet, & revocando coacervet, ut in charitate Christi & disperia congreget, & congregata conservet. In hæc igitur verba Deo vos, & nos Deo & vobis intimè commendamus, optamus ut cùm reversi ad vos fuerimus, meliores vos filios invenire, quàm reliquisse gaudeamus.
units.tr: 5. And if you have ever sinned against us, let it be as with that sinful woman, to whom many sins were forgiven because she loved much; let it all be forgiven. In short, may God, who made the world so that he might gather the scattered sons into one, likewise bring our scattered people back under the yoke, and by gathering and recalling them, gather them in the charity of Christ and in peace, and keep them gathered. We therefore commend you to God in these words, and commend ourselves to God and to you most heartily. We hope that when we have returned to you, we may rejoice to find you better sons than we left you.

units.la: HENRICI V. IMPER. AUG. ET CALLIXTI PAPÆ CONVENTIONES
units.tr: THE CONVENTIONS OF HENRY V, EMPEROR AUGUSTUS, AND POPE CALLISTUS

units.la: DE INVESTITVRIS EPISCOPORVM ET ABBATVM; pacta, accordata & publicata in Comitiis Wormatiensibus.
units.tr: CONCERNING THE INVESTITURE OF BISHOPS AND ABBOTS; agreed, settled and published at the Diet of Worms.

units.la: IN nomine sanctæ & individuæ Trinitatis. Ego Henricus Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator Augustus, pro amore Dei, & sanctæ Romanæ Ecclesiæ, & Domni Papæ Callixti, & pro anima meæ, dimitto Deo & Sanctis ejus Apostolis Petro & Paulo, sanctæque Catholicæ Ecclesiæ, omnem investituram per annulum & baculum, & concedo in omnibus ecclesiis, quæ in Regno vel Imperio meo sunt, canonicam fieri electionem & liberam consecrationem.
units.tr: In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity. I, Henry, by the grace of God Emperor Augustus of the Romans, for the love of God, of the holy Roman Church, of Lord Pope Callistus, and for the good of my soul, release to God, to his holy apostles Peter and Paul, and to the holy Catholic Church, all investiture by ring and staff; and I grant that in all the churches which are in my kingdom or empire a canonical election and free consecration shall take place.

units.la: 2. Possessiones & regalia beati Petri, quæ à principio hujus discordiæ usque ad hodiernam diem vel tempore patris mei, sive etiam meo, ablata sunt, quæ habeo, eidem sanctæ Romanæ Ecclesiæ restituo; quæ autem non habeo, ut restituantur, fideliter curabo.
units.tr: 2. The possessions and regalia of the blessed Peter which were taken away, from the beginning of this discord until the present day, whether in the time of my father or in my own, I restore to the same holy Roman Church, so far as I hold them; and as for those which I do not hold, I will faithfully work for their restoration.

units.la: 3. Possessiones etiam omnium aliarum Ecclesiarum, & Principum, & omnium aliorum tam clericorum quàm Laicorum, quæ in guerra istâ amissæ sunt, consilio Principum & justitiâ, quas habeo, reddam; quas non habeo, ut reddantur, fideliter juvabo.
units.tr: 3. Likewise, the possessions of all other churches, princes, and all others, clerical as well as lay, which were lost in this war, I will restore, by the counsel of the princes and in justice, so far as I hold them; and as for those which I do not hold, I will faithfully help toward their restitution.

units.la: 4. Et do veram pacem Domno Papæ Callixto, sanctæque Romanæ Ecclesiæ, & omnibus partibus ejus sunt, vel fuerunt; & in quibus sancta Romana Ecclesia auxilium postulaverit à me, fideliter juvabo, & de quibus fecerit mihi querimoniam, debitam sibi faciam justitiam.
units.tr: 4. And I grant true peace to Lord Pope Callistus and to the holy Roman Church, and to all those who are or have been on its side; and in whatever matters the holy Roman Church shall seek aid from me, I will faithfully give it aid, and for whatever complaints it makes to me, I will do it due justice.

units.la: Hæc omnia acta sunt consensu & consilio Principum, quorum nomina subscripta sunt: Adelbertus Archiepiscopus Moguntinus. Fridericus Archiepiscopus Coloniensis. H. ...... Ratisponensis Episcopus. Otto Babenbergensis Episcopus. Bruno Spirensis Episcopus. H. ......... Augustensis Episcopus. Godebaldus Trajectensis Episcopus. Uldaricus Constantiensis Episcopus. H. ...... Fuldensis Abbas. Henricus Dux Bavariæ. Fridericus Dux Sueviæ. Bruno Dux Saxoniæ. Dietboldus Marchio Cambiensis à Vochburg. Bonifacius Marchio Tusciæ. Theobaldus Marchio. Gotfridus Palatinus Comes Rheni. Otho Palatinus Comes à Wittelsbach. Engelbertus Marchio Istriæ. Beringarius Comes Habspurgi. Theodoricus Comes Montisbellicardi, & alii complures.
units.tr: All these things were done with the consent and counsel of the princes, whose names are subscribed: Adalbert, Archbishop of Mainz. Frederick, Archbishop of Cologne. H. ..., Bishop of Regensburg. Otto, Bishop of Bamberg. Bruno, Bishop of Speyer. H. ..., Bishop of Augsburg. Godebald, Bishop of Utrecht. Ulrich, Bishop of Constance. H. ..., Abbot of Fulda. Henry, Duke of Bavaria. Frederick, Duke of Swabia. Bruno, Duke of Saxony. Dietbold, Margrave of Cham at Vohburg. Boniface, Margrave of Tuscany. Theobald, Margrave. Godfrey, Count Palatine of the Rhine. Otto, Count Palatine at Wittelsbach. Engelbert, Margrave of Istria. Berengar, Count of Habsburg. Theodoric, Count of Montbéliard, and many others.

units.la: PROFESSIO PAPAE.
units.tr: THE PROFESSION OF THE POPE.

units.la: EGo Callixtus servus servorum Dei, tibi dilecto filio Heinrico Dei gratia Romanorum Imperatori Augusto. Concedo electiones Episcoporum & Abbatum Teutonici Regni, qui ad Regnum pertinent, in praesentia tua fieri absque simonia & aliqua violentia, ut, si qua inter discordia emerserit, Metropolitani & Provincialium consilio vel judicio, saniori parti assensum & auxilium praebeas. Electus autem regalia per sceptrum a te recipiat, & quae ex his jure tibi debet, faciat. Ex aliis vero partibus Imperii, consecratus infra sex menses regalia a te per sceptrum recipiat, & quae ex his jure tibi debet, faciat: exceptis omnibus, quae ad Romanam Ecclesiam pertinere noscuntur. De quibus vero mihi querimoniam feceris, & auxilium postulaveris, secundum officii mei debitum auxilium meum praestabo. Do tibi veram pacem, & omnibus, qui in parte tua sunt vel fuerint tempore hujus discordiae. Data anno MCXXII. nono Calendas Octobris.
units.tr: I, Callistus, servant of the servants of God, to you, my beloved son Henry, by the grace of God Emperor Augustus of the Romans: I grant that the elections of bishops and abbots of the German kingdom, which pertain to the kingdom, shall take place in your presence, without simony and without any violence; so that, if any discord arises among them, you shall give your assent and aid to the wiser part, by the counsel or judgment of the metropolitan and the provincial bishops. The one elected shall receive the regalia from you by the sceptre, and shall perform for you the duties that he owes you by right for them. In the other parts of the Empire, the one consecrated shall receive the regalia from you by the sceptre within six months, and shall perform the duties that he owes you by right for them; excepting all those things which are known to pertain to the Roman Church. As for whatever complaints you make to me and whatever aid you seek, I will render my aid according to the duty of my office. I grant you true peace, and to all who are or have been on your side during this discord. Given in the year 1122, on the ninth day before the Kalends of October.

units.la: FORMVLAE
units.tr: FORMULAS

units.la: JURAMENTORUM FIDELITATIS ET HOMAGII, QUAE A FIDELIBUS IMPERII IN ITA- LIA exigere mandavit Imp. Henricus V. Aug.
units.tr: JURAMENTS OF FIDELITY AND HOMAGE, WHICH EMPEROR HENRY V ORDERED TO BE EXACTED FROM THE FAITHFUL OF THE EMPIRE IN ITALY.

units.la: ADIVRATIO SEV PROMISSIO, QVAE REGIBVS DEBET FIERI.
units.tr: THE OATH OR PROMISE WHICH IS TO BE MADE TO KINGS.

units.la: A Bhac hora inantea fidelis ero N. Imperatori per rectam fidem, secundum meum scire & posse. Non ero in consilio, ut vitam aut membra perdat, Italicum Regnum, & suam rectam potestatem adjutor ei secundum meum scire & posse, ad tenendum & defendendum contra omnes homines, qui sibi tollere voluerint.
units.tr: From this hour forward I will be faithful to N. the Emperor, in right faith, according to my knowledge and ability. I will not be party to any plan by which he would lose life or limb, the Italian Kingdom, or his rightful power; I will help him, according to my knowledge and ability, to hold and defend them against all men who would seek to take them from him.

units.la: ALLOCVTIO EIVS, QVI IVRAVIT.
units.tr: THE ADDRESS OF HIM WHO SWEARS.

units.la: Si quea, quae supra scripta sunt, juratsti, aut juraveris, & per rectam fidem adimpleveris, Senior meus neque per se, neque per subjectam personam tollet tibi vitam, aut membra, nec te capiet propter hoc, quod usque modo contra eum fecisti; nisi inantea sis contra eum, & convictus fueris.
units.tr: If you have sworn, or shall swear, the things written above, and fulfil them in right faith, my Lord shall not take your life or limbs, neither by himself nor through any subordinate person, nor shall he seize you on account of anything you have done against him until now, unless you afterwards act against him and are convicted.

units.la: 1. Praedia & proprietates, quae juste & legaliter habes, non tibi tollet, nisi juste judicio per veram sententiam sit judicatum.
units.tr: 1. He shall not take from you the estates and properties which you hold justly and lawfully, unless it has been adjudged by a true sentence in a just judgment.

units.la: 2. Si beneficium de Regno aut de Ecclesiis non habueris, & legem & justitiam ante Missum mei imperatoris feceris, non te distringet ad curtem venire, nisi tu sponte volueris.
units.tr: 2. If you have not held a benefice of the Kingdom or of the churches, and have done right and justice before the envoy of my Emperor, he shall not compel you to come to the court unless you yourself are willing.

units.la: PRINCIPUM IMPERII EDICTUM
units.tr: THE EDICT OF THE PRINCES OF THE EMPIRE

units.la: DE OBITV IMPERATORIS HENRICI V. AVG. ET NOVA electione facienda.
units.tr: CONCERNING THE DEATH OF THE EMPEROR HENRY V, AUGUSTUS, AND THE NEW ELECTION TO BE HELD.

units.la: Adalbertus Moguntinus, Fridericus Coloniensis, Oudalricus Constantiensis, Per Dei misericordiam Archiepiscopi: Buggo Wormatiensis, Arnolphus Spirensis Oudalricus Fuldensis Abbas: Henricus quoque Dux [Bavariae, Fridericus Dux [Sueviae, Godefridus Palatinus Comes, Beringerus Comes de Sultzbach,
units.tr: Adalbert, Archbishop of Mainz; Frederick, Archbishop of Cologne; Udalric, Archbishop of Constance, by the mercy of God; Bucco of Worms; Arnold of Speyer; Udalric, Abbot of Fulda; Henry, likewise Duke [of Bavaria]; Frederick, Duke [of Swabia]; Godfrey, Count Palatine; Berengar, Count of Sulzbach,

units.la: & usque b professionis Principes, qui exequiis Imperatoris interererant, Venerabili fratri Otroponi [Babebergensi,] hinc fraternas in Christo orationes, inde fidelissimum devotae servitutis.
units.tr: and all the other princes of rank who were present at the emperor's funeral, to the venerable brother Otto [of Bamberg]: from us, brotherly prayers in Christ; from you, the most faithful service of devoted obedience.

units.la: Quam Domnus Imperator viam universae carnis ingressus est, & nos exequias ejus cum jubilatione & reverentia complevimus, ipse ordo rei, & temporis qualitas, exigere videbatur, ut de pace Regni aliquid conferremus, si non abesset praesentiae vestrae consilium, & aliorum Principum, tam negocio utile & pernecessarium quam exspectare quia grave erat & difficile, sedit omnium sententia, si vestrae tantum non displicet concordiae, Curiam in festo B. Bartholomaei apud Magdeburgum celebrare, & ibidem convenientibus Principibus de statu & successore Regni, ac negociis prout Spiritus Sanctus aspiraverit, ordinare. Nullum tamen praejudicium deliberationi & electioni vestrae facientes, nihil nobis singulare ac privatum in hac re usurpamus; quin potius discrete vestrae hoc apprime intimatum esse cupimus, quatenus oppressionis, qua Ecclesia cum universo regno usque modo laboravit, dispositionis divinae providentiam invocetis, ut in substitutione alterius pastoris, sic Ecclesiae suae & Regno provideat, quod tanto servitutis jugo amodo careat, & suis legibus utatur, nos quoque omnes cum subjecta plebe, temporali perfruamur tranquillitate.
units.tr: Since the lord Emperor has gone the way of all flesh, and we have completed his funeral with due lamentation and reverence, the very order of affairs and the character of the time seemed to require that we should take some counsel for the peace of the realm, if the advice of your presence and that of the other princes were not lacking. As this matter is as useful as it is absolutely necessary, and as it was grave and difficult to wait for, the sentiment of all has been this: if it does not displease your harmony, to hold a court at Magdeburg on the feast of St. Bartholomew, and there, with the princes assembled, to ordain concerning the state and the successor of the realm, and the business, as the Holy Spirit shall inspire. Yet we make no prejudice to your deliberation and election, and we claim nothing singular or private for ourselves in this matter. Rather, we very much wish this to be made especially known to your discretion, so that you may invoke the providence of divine disposition, which the Church together with the whole realm has hitherto suffered under such oppression, that in the appointment of another minister, He may provide for His Church and the realm, so that it may henceforth be free of so great a yoke of servitude and use its own laws, and that all of us, together with the subject people, may enjoy temporal tranquillity.

units.la: 2. Contestamur etiam Dilectionem vestram, ut pacem credito nobis coelitus populo, infra praescriptum Curiae terminum, & ultra ad quatuor hebdomades ordinetis, quatenus omnibus tutior sit concursus ac reditus, & ut curialiter, more videlicet antiquorum Principum, cum propria impensa, neminem pauperum laedentes conveniatis.
units.tr: 2. We also call upon your Dilection, that you should keep the peace entrusted to us by heaven for the people, within the prescribed term of the court and further, for four weeks, so that the coming and going may be safer for all, and that you may assemble in a courtly manner, that is, in the manner of the ancient princes, at your own expense, harming none of the poor.

units.la: LOTHARII III. IMPER. AUG. MANDATUM AD EPISCOPUM BAMBERGENSEM, UT AD EC- CLESIAM SUAM REDEAT, SUB POENA CONFISCATIONIS, BONORUM ECCLESIASTICORUM.
units.tr: Mandate of the Emperor Lothair III Augustus to the Bishop of Bamberg, that he return to his church, under penalty of confiscation of the church's goods.

units.la: Lotharius Rex auctoritate sua Ottoni Episcopo, ut clericus a redeat, praecipiendo & petendo mandavit; adeo, ut jurejurando affirmaret, se res Ecclesiasticas in suum redegere velle dominium, nisi quantocyus sponsam suam Ecclesiam Babebergensem diu viduatam pastoris desiderato reditu, consolando recrearet.
units.tr: Lothair the King, by his own authority, commanded and requested Bishop Otto, by way of precept, that he return as a clergyman; so much so that he affirmed on oath that he would bring the ecclesiastical property under his own lordship, unless as quickly as possible he comforted and restored his bride, the Church of Bamberg, long widowed, with the longed-for return of her minister.

units.la: Apostolus itaque Pomeranorum his legationibus b contraire non valens, antequam responsum Archiepiscopi Danorum recuperet, ad sedem suam redire compulsus est.
units.tr: The Apostle of the Pomeranians, therefore, being unable to resist these embassies, was compelled to return to his see before he recovered the reply of the Archbishop of the Danes.

units.la: LOTHARII III. IMPERAT. AUG. PROCESSUS IN EXAMINATIONE ABBATIS CASINENSIS à Fratribus accusati.
units.tr: THE PROCEEDINGS OF THE EMPEROR LOTHAR III AUGUSTUS IN THE EXAMINATION OF THE ABBOT OF MONTE CASSINO, ACCUSED BY THE BRETHREN.

units.la: Imperator direxit Hannonem Abbatem Coenobii Lunaeburgensis, & Petrum Diaconum Monasterium, per eos Fratribus mandans, ne quid incompositum aut indisciplinatum in habitu, in incessu seu locutione praeferrent: venturum se ad Monasterium cum Cardinalibus, Archiepiscopis, Episcopis, Principibus, Ducibus, Religiosisque ex omni Imperio viris. Ac liquidem inventum Rainaldum tanto ordine indignum, confestim eum removeret, atque in B. Benedicti sede idoneum praeponere omni studio quaereret.
units.tr: The Emperor sent Hannon, Abbot of the monastery at Lüneburg, and Peter the Deacon to the monastery, instructing the brethren through them that they should display nothing disorderly or undisciplined in their dress, their bearing or their speech. He himself would come to the monastery with cardinals, archbishops, bishops, princes, dukes and religious men from the whole Empire. And if Rainald were found unworthy of so high an office, he should at once remove him and make every effort to set in the seat of St Benedict a man fit for it.

units.la: 2. Residente itaque Imperatore in Capitulo, cum Imperii Proceribus, confidente quoque Peregrino Aquilegiensi Patriarcha cum Archiepiscopis, Episcopis, Cardinalibus, Abbatibus, jussit introduci Abbatem; multa contra eum proferentes, rebelle hostemque Imperii clamantes. Tunc quidam exurgens in medium dicere coepit, eum posteaquam cum Henrico Duce convenerat, hostem Pontificis atque Imperatoris claruisse. Contradicente illo, jubet Imperator utramque partem Capitulum ingredi, ut cum Patriarcha & Cardinalibus inde consulraret. Tunc Peregrinus Patriarcha, Aimericusque Diaconus Cancellarius, dixerunt, illum tanto Coenobio praeesse non posse, multa causis, quod scilicet a filio Petrileonis Subdiaconus ordinatus esset, sacramentumque Rogerio praebuisset; tum quia contra praecepta Canonum, excommunicati eligere non potuisset. Pr mo quod contra Ecclesiastica instituta Subdiaconum elegissent, proferentes Eugenii Papae decretum ita scribentis: Abbates per monasteria tales eligantur & ordinentur, qui Sacerdotali vel Levitico honore praediti, &c. Sed cum jam Sol ad occasum vergens noctem indiceret terris, Imperatore jubente solutus conventus est.
units.tr: 2. On the next day, the Emperor being seated in the chapter house with the nobles of the Empire, and with Patriarch Peregrine of Aquileia confidently present along with archbishops, bishops, cardinals and abbots, he ordered the Abbot to be brought in. They put forward many charges against him and cried out that he was a rebel and an enemy of the Empire. Then a certain man rose and began to say that after he had come to terms with Duke Henry, he had plainly become an enemy of the Pope and the Emperor. When he denied this, the Emperor ordered both parties to withdraw into the chapter house, so that they might deliberate there with the Patriarch and the cardinals. Then Patriarch Peregrine and Aimeric the Deacon, the chancellor, said that he could not preside over so great a monastery, for many reasons: namely, that he had been ordained subdeacon by the son of Petrileo, and had sworn an oath to Roger; and also because, contrary to the precepts of the canons, an excommunicate man could not have been elected. First, they had chosen a subdeacon contrary to ecclesiastical institutions, citing the decree of Pope Eugenius, which reads: "Abbots are to be chosen and ordained for monasteries from among those who are endowed with the honour of the priesthood or of the Levites," and so on. But since the sun was already sinking towards the west and announcing night to the lands, the assembly was dismissed at the Emperor's command.

units.la: 3. Die altero, Imperatore residente in Capitulo cum Praelatis atque Magnaribus, Electus surgens cum vellet objecta diluere, priusquam verba finiret, surgentes Fratres accusare coeperunt, sicut & prius, dicentes, electionem ejus sediriose non canonice fuisse celebratam.
units.tr: 3. On the second day, with the Emperor seated in the chapter house with the prelates and magnates, the elect rose to answer the charges, but before he could finish his words, the brethren rose again and began to accuse him, as they had before, saying that his election had been carried out in a seditious and uncanonical manner.
