units.la: Imperator his motus surrexit, & manu silentium indicens, multum rari dixit tantam congregationem adeo inordinate loqui, negociaque sua tam indisciplinate tractare. Praecepit itaque, ut rationabiliter negocia sua exequerentur.
units.tr: The Emperor, moved by this, rose, and calling for silence with his hand, said with great wonder that so large an assembly was speaking so disorderly and conducting its affairs so undisciplined. He therefore ordered them to carry on their business in a reasonable manner.

units.la: Quod cum factum esset, Hannon Episcopus Basiliensis dixit: Si quid contra Electum habetis, rationabiliter & non tumultuose proferte. Tunc quidam ex eis illum accusare coeperunt, quod electionem suam munere linguae & manus pemissione redemisset.
units.tr: When this had been done, Hannon, Bishop of Basel, said: "If you have anything against the elect, put it forward reasonably and not tumultuously." Then some of them began to accuse him of having bought his election with a gift of his tongue and the permission of his hand.

units.la: Pandulfus Vesterarius exurgens dixit: Sunt quidem multa, quae adversus Electum proferri possunt, sed illud intolerabile, quod a filio Petrileonis ordinatus est, indignumque valde ducimus, ut in tanta Ecclesia, quae Monasteriorum omnium caput ac mater est, Abbas Subdiaconus sit, qui nec Missarum solemnia celebrare, nec possit a delictis absolvere. Tunc Anselmus Episcopus: Multa (inquit) adversus Electum proferuntur, sed hoc potissimum addponendum illum objicitur, quia teste Domino fundamentum, quod super arenam collocatur, deire non potest. Unde, si placet, sepositis exteris, hoc unum teneamus. Quod cum placuisset, cari Fratribus egredi jussis, Rainaldum cum suis ad se purgandum introduci praecipiunt. Et cum diu moras traherent, mandat Imperator his, qui ad discutiendum convenerant, ut Electo suaderent, se ipsum impoin potestatem Imperatoris ac Pontificis ponere, ut quicquid illi statuerent, hoc ipse absque dilatione sequeretur. Ad hæcille diu cunctarus tandem consensit, seque illis liberè ex toto promisit. Post hæc omnibus ad Imperatorem revertis Basiliensis Episcopus gesta omnia cunctis per ordinem pandit. Demum Imperatore sciscitante, an qui Electo faverant, idem facere vellent? ad omnia eos paratos invenit: sicque secundi diei conventus solutus est. Acta sunt hæc quartà & quintà feria tertiæ hebdomadis, mense Septembrio, secundo post festum S. Crucis die.
units.tr: Pandulf the Chamberlain rose and said: "There are indeed many things that can be brought against the elect, but this is intolerable: that he was ordained by the son of Petrileo; and we think it very wrong that in so great a church, which is the head and mother of all monasteries, the abbot should be a subdeacon, one who can neither celebrate the solemn Masses nor absolve from sins." Then Bishop Anselm said: "Many things (he said) are brought against the elect, but this above all is to be laid against him: that, as the Lord testifies, he cannot stand firm, because he is building on sand, not on rock. Therefore, if it pleases you, let us set aside the others and hold to this one point." When this was agreed, the dear brethren were ordered to leave, and they commanded that Rainald be brought in with his men to clear himself. And when they had delayed for a long time, the Emperor directed those who had gathered to examine the matter to persuade the elect to put himself wholly into the power of the Emperor and the Pope, so that whatever they decided, he would follow without delay. At this he hesitated for a long time, but at last he consented and freely promised them full submission. After this, when all had returned to the Emperor, the Bishop of Basel laid out all that had happened, in order, before everyone. Finally, when the Emperor asked whether those who had favoured the elect wished to do the same, he found them ready for everything; and so the assembly of the second day was dismissed. These things were done on the fourth and fifth days of the third week, in September, on the second day after the feast of the Holy Cross.

units.la: SENATUSCONSULTUM ROMANUM
units.tr: THE ROMAN SENATUS-CONSULTUM

units.la: DE RECVPERANDIS IMPERII ROMANI IVRIBVS PER ELECTVM Imperatorem, ab injusta Papæ usurpatione & tyrannide. EXCELLENTISSIMO ATQUE PRÆCLARO URBIS ET ORBIS TOTIUS DOMINO, CONRADO DEI GRATIA ROMANO- RUM Regi Semper Augusto, S. P. Q. R. Salutem & Romani Imperii fœli- cem & inclytam gubernationem.
units.tr: ON RECOVERING THE RIGHTS OF THE ROMAN EMPIRE THROUGH THE ELECTED EMPEROR, FROM THE UNJUST USURPATION AND TYRANNY OF THE POPE. To the most excellent and illustrious lord of the City and of the whole world, Conrad, by the grace of God Always August King of the Romans, S.P.Q.R. send greetings and wish the Roman Empire a happy and renowned government.

units.la: REGALI excellentiæ per plurima jam scripta, nostra facta & negotia diligenter exposuimus, quo modo in vestra fidelitate permaneamus, ac pro vestra Imperiali corona exaltada & omnimodò augenda quotidiè decerremus. Ad quæ, quia Regalis industria, ut postulavimus, rescribere dignata non fuit, plane tanquam filii & fideles de Domino & patre satis miramur. Nos enim quicquid agimus, pro vestra fidelitate & honore facimus. Et quidem Regnum & Imperium Romanorum, vestro à Deo regimini concessum, exaltare atque amplificare cupientes, in eum statum, quo fuit tempore Constantini & Justiniani, qui totum orbem vigore Senatus & Populi Romani suis tenuere manibus, reducere, Senatu pro his omnibus Dei gratia restituto, & eis, qui vestro Imperio semper rebelles erant, quique tantum honorem Romani Imperii subripuerant, magna ex parte conculcans, quatenus ea, quæ Cæsari & Imperio deberentur, per omnia & in omnibus obtineatis, vehementer atque unanimiter satagimus atque studemus. Et ob hujus rei effectum, bonum principium ac fundamentum fecimus. Nam pacem & justiciam omnibus eam volentibus observanius: fortitudinis, id est, turres & domos potentum Ubis, qui vestro Imperio unà cum Siculo & Papa resistere parant, cepimus; & quasdam in vestra fidelitate retinemus, quasdam verò subvertentes solo coæquavimus.
units.tr: We have already written many times to your royal excellence, setting out diligently our deeds and affairs, and how we remain in your allegiance and strive daily to exalt and in every way to enlarge your imperial crown. Since your royal diligence has not deigned to reply to these letters, as we asked, we marvel greatly, as sons and faithful subjects marvel at a lord and father. For whatever we do, we do for your loyalty and honour. Indeed, desiring to exalt and enlarge the kingdom and empire of the Romans, which God has entrusted to your rule, and to restore it to the condition it had in the time of Constantine and Justinian, who held the whole world in their hands by the power of the Senate and People of Rome, we are striving and labouring earnestly and with one mind, with God's grace restoring the Senate for all these purposes, and, by crushing in large part those who were always rebels against your empire and had stolen the great honour of the Roman Empire, to see that what is owed to Caesar and the Empire is obtained in every respect and in all things. To achieve this we have laid a good beginning and foundation. For we observe peace and justice towards all who wish it. We have seized the strongholds, that is, the towers and houses of the powerful men of the city who prepare to resist your empire together with the Sicilian and the Pope; some we keep in your allegiance, and others, having overthrown them, we have levelled with the ground.

units.la: Sed pro his omnibus, quæ vestræ dilectionis fidelitate facimus, Papa Frangipanes, & filii Petronis, hominas & amici Siculi, excepto Jordano nostro, fidelitate in vestra vexillifero & adjutore, Thomæus quoque & alii plures undique nos impugnant, ne liberè, ut decet, Imperialem Regio capiti valeamus imponere coronam. At nos, quoniam amanti nullus labor gravis est, licet inde pluridamna sustineamus, pro vestro amore & honore gratanter patimur. Scimus namque nosa vobis inde præmium, sicut à patre, acceptuors; vosque in eos, sicut in Imperii hostes, vindictam dabimus.
units.tr: But for all these things which we do in the loyalty of your love, Frangipani the Pope, and the sons of Petro, men and friends of the Sicilian, except our Jordan, the standard-bearer and helper of your fidelity, and Thomaeus too, and many others, attack us on every side, so that we cannot freely place on the royal head the imperial crown, as is fitting. Yet since for one who loves no labour is heavy, we bear many losses for your love and honour, and we bear them gladly. For we know that we shall receive reward from you, as from a father, and we shall take vengeance on them, as on enemies of the Empire.

units.la: I. Cum tanta igitur nostra in vobis fidelitas sit, tantaque pro vobis sustineamus, precamur ne spes nobis deficiat, nec Regia dignitas nos vestros fideles & filios despiciat. Neque si in Regalibus auxilium sinistra de Senatu & nobis flaverit, in eam intendat aut respiciat. Qui enim de nobis vestra solitudini mala suggerunt, de vestra & nostra (quod absit) dissensione lætari volunt, & utrosque sunt) callidè opprimere moliuntur. Sed circa hæc, ne fiant, Regalis prudentia, ut decet, solita & provida: reminiscarúque vestra solertia, quot & quanta mala Papalis Curia, & dicti cives nostri, Imperatoribus, qui fuerunt ante vos, fecerint, & nunc deteriora vobis cum Siculo tentaverunt. Sed nos Christi gratia in vestra fidelitate viriliter eis resistimus, ac plures ex illis Urbe, sicut pessimos hostes Imperii, ut sunt, pepulimus.
units.tr: 1. Since, then, our loyalty to you is so great, and we endure so much for you, we pray that hope may not fail us, nor that royal dignity may despise us, your faithful subjects and sons. Nor, if some wind of advice from the Senate and from us should blow to the left in royal matters, should you turn to it or regard it. For those who suggest evils to you against us wish, in your solitude and in our (God forbid) dissension, to rejoice, and they seek to crush both of us craftily. But in these matters, so that they may not come about, let royal prudence act, as is fitting, as it always does, with foresight; and let your shrewdness call to mind how many and how great evils the Papal Curia and the citizens called ours have inflicted on the Emperors who were before you, and how they have now tried worse things against you with the Sicilian. But by Christ's grace we resist them manfully in your loyalty, and have driven many of them from the City, as the worst enemies of the Empire that they are.

units.la: 3. Appropinquet itaque nobis Imperialis celeriter vigor. Quoniam, quicquid vultis, in Urbe obtineatis, poteritis: & ut breviter ac succinctè loquamur, potenter in Urbe, quæ caput mundi est, ut optatis, habitare, toti Italiæ ac regno Teutonico, omni Clericorum remoto obstaculo, liberius & memoriam omnes ferè antecessores vestri, dominari valebitis. Sine mora ergo precamur, ut veniatis interim de statu vestro, quem semper desideramus salubrem & prosperum, de his Regalibus litteris ac nunciis nos lætificare dignemini. Sumus enim per omnia vestræ voluntati semper obtemperare parati.
units.tr: 3. Let the imperial power therefore approach us quickly. For whatever you wish, you will be able to obtain in the City; and to speak briefly and to the point, you will be able to dwell powerfully in the City, which is the head of the world, as you desire, and to rule over all Italy and the German kingdom more freely, with every obstacle of the clergy removed, as nearly all your predecessors did in the past. Therefore we urgently beg that you come without delay, and that you deign to gladden us with royal letters and messengers concerning your condition, which we always desire to be healthy and prosperous. For we are ready in all things to obey your will.

units.la: 4. Sciatis præterea, quia pontem Mylvium extra Urbem parum longè per tempora multa pro Imperatorum contrario destructum, nos, ut exercitus vester per eum transire queat, ne Petri Leonis per castellum Sancti Angeli vobis nocere possint, ut statuerant cum Papa & Siculo, magno communine restauranus, & in parvo temporis spacio muro fortissimo & silicibus juvante Deo compleblitur. Concordiam autem inter a Siculum & b Papam hujusmodi esse accepimus. Papa concessit Siculo virgam & annulum, dalmaticam & mitram atque sandalia, & ne ullum mittat in terram suam.
units.tr: 4. Furthermore, you should know that the bridge of Milvius outside the City, which for a long time has been destroyed by the opposition of the Emperors, we, so that your army may be able to cross over it, and so that the Petri Leonis may not be able to harm you from the castle of Sant'Angelo, as they had planned with the Pope and the Sicilian, are restoring at great common expense, and with God's help it will be completed in a short space of time as a very strong wall and with stones. We have heard that the agreement between the Sicilian and the Pope is of this kind: the Pope has granted to the Sicilian the rod and ring, the dalmatic and mitre and sandals, and that he will not send any legate into his land unless the Sicilian asks for one. And the Sicilian has given him much money for the loss to you and to the Roman Empire, which by God's grace has been yours.

units.la: a Petrum Leonem antipapam, qui se Anacletum nominari voluit.
units.tr: a Peter Leo, the antipope, who wished to be called Anacletus.

units.la: b Innocentium II. suam Legatum, nisi quem Siculus petierit: & Siculus dedit ei multam pecuniam pro detrimento vestro & Romani Imperii, quod Dei gratia vestrum exstitit. Haec omnia solicitè vestra animadvertat, optime Rex, prudentia. Rex valeat, quicquid cupit obtineat, super hostes Imperium teneat, Roma sedeat, regat orbem, Princeps terrarum ceu fecit Justinianus. Cæsaris accipiat Cæsar, qua sunt sua Præsul, Ut Christus justit, Petro solvente tributum.
units.tr: b Innocent II. ... Let all these things be carefully noted by your prudence, excellent King. May the King prosper; may he obtain whatever he desires; may he hold the empire over his enemies; may Rome be seated and rule the world, a prince of the lands as Justinian did. Let Caesar receive what is Caesar's, and the Prelate what is his, as Christ commanded, Peter paying the tribute.

units.la: Nos de cætero Legatos nostros precamur, ut benignè recipiatis, & quod vobis dixerint, credatis, quia scribere cuncta nequivimus. Sunt enim Nobiles viri, Guido Senator, Jacobus filius Sixti Procuratoris, & Nicolaus eorum socius.
units.tr: We further beg our envoys to be received kindly, and to be believed in what they tell you, since we could not write everything. They are noble men: Guido the Senator, James son of Sixtus the Procurator, and Nicholas, their companion.

units.la: CONRADI III. IMPERAT. AUG. RESCRIPTUM AD JOANNEM COMNENVM IMPERATOREM Constantinopolitanum.
units.tr: Letter of the Emperor Conrad III Augustus to John Comnenus, Emperor of Constantinople.

units.la: CONRADUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator Augustus, Joanni eadem gratia Constantinopolitano Imperatori salutem & dilectionem fraternam, amicitiam, honorem, & gloriam.
units.tr: Conrad, by the grace of God Emperor Augustus of the Romans, to John, by the same grace Emperor of Constantinople, greeting, fraternal affection, friendship, honour, and glory.

units.la: 1. Ut parentes nostri, videlicet Romanorum Imperatores, antecessores nostri, ad antecessores vestros, scilicet regnum & populum Græcorum constituerunt, constituo: & sicut servaverunt, conservabo.
units.tr: 1. As our forefathers, namely the Roman emperors, our predecessors, established for your predecessors, that is, the kingdom and people of the Greeks, so I establish; and as they kept it, so I will keep it.

units.la: 2. Non est gens, regnum, aut populus, qui non noverit, nostræ Romanæ Reipub. vestram novam Romam & dici & fore filiam, ex hujusque radice ramos & fructus ejus processisse. Propter quod hæreditatem, quæ à matre debetur filiæ, constituimus, æternamque volumus; & eò amplius, quod quæ matri debentur, filiam velle cernimus, scilicet ut auctoritas materna præcinat consilio, auxilio; respondeat autem gloria & honore filiastina dilectio.
units.tr: 2. There is no nation, kingdom, or people that does not know that your New Rome is both called and is the daughter of our Roman Commonwealth, and that its branches and fruits have sprung from its root. For this reason we have established and wish to make permanent the inheritance that is owed by a mother to her daughter; and all the more so because we see that a daughter wishes what is owed to a mother, namely that the maternal authority should go before with counsel and aid, while filial affection should answer with glory and honour.

units.la: 3. Sint ergo res utriusque communes, utriusque amicus idem, idem inimicus, sive in terra sive in mari: & cognoscat ac timeat matris virtutem & valentiam, qui nô honoraverit filiam, sive Normannus, sive Siculus, sive quis alter quicunque, ubicunque. Neq; enim obliti sumus, vel ego vel Principes nostri Imperii, quoscunq; hostium nostrorum incursus vel invasiones in Imperium & magnificam Romanam. Sed cùm divina clementia subveniet, retribuemus unicuiq; ipsorum secundum multitudinem ipsorum malitiæ. Videbit ergo & audiet universa regnorum latitudo, quàm facili manu prosternentur latrones, qui insurrexerunt in utriusq; Imperii nostri monarchiam: quia cooperante Deo, si alas excutiemus, hostem modò volitantem capiemus, & cordis ejus evisceribimus audentiam, quæ modò extollitur contra utriusq; Imperii nostri honorem & gloriam. Conservamus igitur quæ justa & amicabilia sunt ad vos, eadem vos ad nos: & tanto studiosius, quanto per conjugium sororis dilectissimæ conjugis nostræ, Imperatricis videlicet nobilissimæ, & filii tui confœderati simus propinquius.
units.tr: 3. Let the affairs of both be common, let both have the same friend and the same enemy, whether on land or at sea; and let whoever does not honour the daughter, whether a Norman, a Sicilian, or any other whatsoever, anywhere, know and fear the virtue and strength of the mother. For neither I nor the princes of our Empire have forgotten the attacks or invasions of our enemies against the Empire and the glorious Roman state. But when the divine mercy comes to our aid, we will repay each of them according to the multitude of their malice. Then the whole breadth of kingdoms will see and hear with what ease the robbers who have risen against the monarchy of our two empires will be cast down; for with God cooperating, if we shake their wings, we will seize the enemy now flying about, and tear out the boldness of his heart, which is now raised against the honour and glory of our two empires. Therefore we keep toward you what is just and friendly, and you toward us likewise; and all the more eagerly, since through the marriage of the most beloved sister of our wife, namely the most noble Empress, and your son, we are more closely allied.

units.la: 4. Verùm quia de nostris hilaritate scire successibus, dilectionis & nobilitatis tuæ credimus experientiam, quid post discessum prudentissimorum Apocrisiariorum tuorum, in generali & solenni curia cum universis Imperii nostri Principibus celebrata, cui eos interesse voluimus, Deo auxiliante actum sit, tibi sicut unico fratri nostro & amico dilectissimo dignum duximus intimare. Noveris igitur, quòd omnes, qui Imperium nostrum offendisse videbantur, cooperante Deo, potenter in nostro Imperiali jure inclinavimus, eosq; in plenitudinem gratiæ nostræ suscipientes, universas Imperii nostri partes abundanti pace ditavimus. Adhoc Francia & Hispania, Anglia, Dania, cæteraq; regna Imperio nostro adjacentia, quotidiana legatione sua, cum debita reverentia & obsequio nos frequentant, ad ea, quæ Imperii nostri mandata sunt, se prompta esse tam obsidibus quàm Sacramentis affirmantes.
units.tr: 4. But since we believe that by your affection and nobility you know by experience to rejoice in our successes, we have judged it fitting to make known to you, as to our one brother and most beloved friend, what has been done, with God's help, after the departure of your most prudent envoys, in the general and solemn assembly held with all the princes of our Empire, at which we wished them to be present. Know therefore that all who seemed to have offended our Empire, with God cooperating, we have powerfully brought under our imperial law, and receiving them into the fullness of our grace, we have enriched all parts of our Empire with abundant peace. Moreover, France, Spain, England, Denmark, and the other kingdoms adjoining our Empire frequent us with their daily embassies, with due reverence and obedience, affirming that they are ready, both by hostages and by oaths, for those things which are commanded by our Empire.

units.la: 5. Nolumus etiam latere discretionis tuæ prudentiam, quòd Dominus Papa, totaque Apulia, Italia, & Longobardia, de die in diem advētum nostrum desiderant: & ut nostra eis Imperiali subveniamus potentia; cum omni devotione expostulant. Hujus rei gratia dilectissimum & præcordialem Imperii nostri Principem Embriconem, venerabilem Herbipolensem Episcopum, amicum tuum, ad exquirendam Domini Papæ voluntatem Romam misimus. Cognita verò ipsius circa nos voluntate, communicato Principum nostrorum consilio, ea quæ ad utriusque Imperii nostri honorem spectat, per carissimos & prudentes Nuncios nostros, Robertum scilicet Principem Capuanum, illustrem utique virum ac nobilem nobisque fidelem, necnon Albertum dilectum Capellanum nostrum & in fide constantem, tuæ significamus nobilitati.
units.tr: 5. We also do not wish to hide from your discretion that the Lord Pope, and all Apulia, Italy, and Lombardy, long from day to day for our coming, and with every devotion they demand that we aid them with our imperial power. For this reason we sent to Rome our most beloved and dear prince of the Empire, Embricho, and the venerable Bishop of Würzburg, your friend, to seek out the will of the Lord Pope. Having learned his will concerning us, and with the counsel of our princes communicated, we make known to your nobility, through our most dear and prudent envoys, Robert, namely Prince of Capua, a man truly illustrious and noble and faithful to us, and also Albert, our beloved chaplain, constant in the faith, those things which pertain to the honour of both our empires.

units.la: 6. Hos igitur tanquam nos audias, & quæ tibi dixerint, sicut decet excellentiam tuam, & sicut de te speramus & credimus, ad effectum perducas, & honestos & idoneos Apocrisiarios tuos unà cum Nunciis nostris sine dilatione ad nos remittas.
units.tr: 6. Therefore hear them as you would hear us, and bring to completion what they have said to you, as befits your excellence, and as we hope and believe of you; and send back to us, without delay, your honest and suitable envoys together with our messengers.

units.la: 7. Præterea de Rutenis, qui ad cótemptū Imperii nostri occisis hominibus nostris, pecuniâ nostrâ sibi usurpaverunt, sicut convenit in causa amici & propinqui tui, & sicut nobis scripsisti, ita facias.
units.tr: 7. Furthermore, concerning the Ruthenians, who, in contempt of our Empire, killed our men and seized our money for themselves, do as is fitting in the case of your friend and relative, and as you have written to us.

units.la: 8. Militibus quoque Imperii nostri, Alemanis scilicet, qui apud te sunt, sicut decet excellentiam tuam, benignus exsistas. 9. Nihilominus etiam te rogamus, ut hominibus Imperii nostri Teutonicis videlicet, qui Constantinopoli morantur, locum, in quem ad honorem Dei Ecclesiam ædificent, concedas, tum respectu divinæ remunerationis, tum & interventu & petitione nostræ dilectionis. Recordari quoq; dettua discretio, quòd nos in literis prioribus, per præfatum Capellanum nostrum tuæ nobilitati præsentatis, hoc idem à te pro Dei amore & honore petivimus: quia si ipse, qui dat salutem Regibus, fuerit in medio nostri, certum est quòd non gaudebunt inimici nostri.
units.tr: 8. Be also kind to the soldiers of our Empire, namely the Germans, who are with you, as befits your excellence. 9. Nevertheless we also ask you to grant to the men of our Empire, namely the Teutons, who dwell at Constantinople, a place in which they may build a church to the honour of God, both out of regard for divine reward and at the intercession and request of our affection. Let your discretion also recall that in our earlier letters, presented to your nobility through the aforesaid chaplain of ours, we asked the same of you for the love and honour of God; for if He who gives salvation to kings is in the midst of us, it is certain that our enemies will not rejoice.

units.la: Datum XVIII. Kal. Aprilis, MCXLII. Ratisponæ, in Christo feliciter, Amen.
units.tr: Given on the 18th day before the Kalends of April, 1142, at Regensburg, in Christ, happily. Amen.

units.la: FRIDERICI I. IMPER. AUG. RESCRIPTUM
units.tr: THE RESCRIPT OF THE EMPEROR FREDERICK I, AUGUSTUS

units.la: DE IVRIBVS IMPERII, ET POTESTATE IN PAPAM, CARDINALES, & cateros Status Ecclesiasticos. EPISTOLA PAPÆ.
units.tr: ON THE RIGHTS OF THE EMPIRE AND THE POWER OVER THE POPE, THE CARDINALS, AND OTHER ECCLESIASTICAL ORDERS. LETTER OF THE POPE.

units.la: HAdrianus Episcopus, servus servorum Dei, Friderico Imperatori salutem & Apostolicam benedictionem. Lex Divina, sicut parentes honorantibus longævitatem promittit, ita maledicentibus patri & matri sententiam mortis intendit. Veritatis autem voce docemur, quia omnis, qui se exaltat, humiliabitur. Quapropter, Dilecte in Domino Fili, super imprudentia tua non mediocriter admiramur, quòd beato Petro & sanctæ Romanæ Ecclesiæ, non quantam debueras, reverentiam exhibere videris. In literis enim ad nos missis nomen tuum nostro præponis: in quo insolentiæ, ne dicam arrogantiæ, notam incurris. Quid dicam de fidelitate beato Petro & nobis à te prostrata & jurata, quomodo eam observes? quum ab hiis, qui Dii sunt, & filii Excelsi omnes, homagium requiris, fidelitatem exigis, & manus eorum sacratas manibus tuis innectis, & manifeste nobis factus contrarius, Cardinalibus à latere nostro directis non solum Ecclesias, sed & Civitates Regni tui claudis. Resipisce ergo, resipisce, tibi consulimus. Quia, dum a nobis consecrationem & coronam meruerum inconcessa captas, ne concessa perdas, Nobilitati tuæ timemus. Vale.
units.tr: Hadrian, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to Frederick the Emperor, greeting and apostolic blessing. The divine law, just as it promises long life to those who honour father and mother, so it threatens death to those who curse father and mother. We are taught by the voice of truth that everyone who exalts himself will be humbled. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, we are not a little astonished at your lack of judgement, in that you seem to show less reverence than you ought to blessed Peter and the holy Roman Church. For in the letters you sent to us you place your name before ours, in which you incur the mark of insolence, not to say arrogance. What shall I say of the fealty, prostrated and sworn to blessed Peter and to us by you? How do you keep it? When you demand homage from those who are gods and all sons of the Most High, you exact fealty, and you bind their consecrated hands in your hands; and, having plainly become hostile to us, you shut not only churches but also the cities of your kingdom against the cardinals sent from our side. Therefore repent, repent; we advise you so. For while you seek from us things not granted, having received consecration and crown, we fear for your nobility, lest you lose what has been granted. Farewell.

units.la: RESCRIPTUM IMPERATORIS.
units.tr: THE RESCRIPT OF THE EMPEROR

units.la: FRidericus Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator Semper Augustus, Hadriano Romanæ Ecclesiæ Pontifici, omnibus illis adhærere, quæ a cœpit Jesus facere & docere.
units.tr: Frederick, by the grace of God Roman Emperor, ever Augustus, to Hadrian, Pontiff of the Roman Church: to adhere to all those things which Jesus began both to do and to teach.

units.la: 1. Lex b justitiæ unicuique, quod suum est, restituit. Non enim parentibus nostris derogabus in hoc Regno nostro debitum exhibemus honorem, à quibus & Regni dignitate suscepimus & coronam. Numquid tempore CONSTANTINI Sylvester regale aliquid habuisse dignoscitur? Sed ejus pietatis concessione libertas data est Ecclesiæ, pax restituta, & quicquid regale Papa vester habere dignoscitur, largitione Principum obtinet. Unde cum Romano Pontifici scribimus jure & ex antiquo nomen nostrum præponimus, & ad justitiæ normam eidem nobis scribenti concedimus. Revolvite Annales, & si lectum neglexistis, quod asserimus, illic invenitur.
units.tr: 1. The law of justice restores to each what is his own. For we do not derogate from our parents, and in this our kingdom we render the honour that is due to them, from whom we have received both the dignity of the kingdom and the crown. At the time of Constantine, is it known that Sylvester possessed anything royal? But by the grant of that piety liberty was given to the Church and peace was restored; and whatever royal thing your Pope is known to have, he obtains by the bounty of princes. Hence when we write to the Roman Pontiff we place our name first, by right and by ancient custom, and we concede to him, writing to us, what accords with the rule of justice. Turn over the Annals, and if you have neglected to read them, you will find there what we assert.

units.la: 1. Ab hiis autem, qui Dii sunt per adoptionem, & regalia nostra tenent, cur homagium & regalia sacramenta non exiganus? cum ille noster & vester institutor, ab homine Rege nihil accipiens, sed bona omnibus conferens, tamen pro se & Petro c censum Cæsari persolvit, & exemplum vobis dedit, ut & vos ita faciatis. Docet itaq; vos, dicens: d Discite à me, quia mitis sum & humilis corde. Aut regalia nostra nobis dimittant, aut si hæc sibi utilia judicaverint, quæ Dei Deo, quæ Cæsaris Cæsari solvant.
units.tr: 1. But from those who are gods by adoption and hold our royal rights, why should we not demand homage and royal oaths? For that founder of yours and ours, receiving nothing from a human king but conferring goods on all, nevertheless paid tribute to Caesar for himself and for Peter, and gave you an example that you should do likewise. Thus he teaches you, saying: "Learn from me, for I am meek and humble in heart." Either let them give back our royal rights to us, or, if they judge these useful to themselves, let them pay what is God's to God and what is Caesar's to Caesar.

units.la: Cardinalibus utiq; vestris clausæ sunt ecclesiæ, & non patent civitates; quia non videmus eos Cardinales, sed Carpinales; non prædicatores, sed prædatores; non pacis corroboratores, sed pecuniæ; non orbis reparatores, sed auri insatiabiles corrasores. Cum autem viderimus eos, quæ Ecclesia, portantes pacem, illuminantes patriam, assistentes causæ humilium in æquitate, stipendiis & commeatu eos sustentare non differemus.
units.tr: Surely your churches are closed to your cardinals, and the cities are not open to them; for we do not see them as Cardinals but as Carpinales (plunderers), not as preachers but as predators, not as strengtheners of peace but of money, not as restorers of the world but as insatiable scrapers-up of gold. But when we see them as the Church's men, bearing peace, illuminating the fatherland, and supporting the cause of the humble with equity, we will not delay to sustain them with stipends and provisions.

units.la: Humilitati autem, quæ est custos virtutum, & manuetudinis vestræ, non minimam notam incurrit, cum hujusmodi quæstiones, religioni non multum conferentes, sæcularibus personis proponi. Provideat itaque Paternitas vestra, ne, dum talia movet, quæ indigna ducimus, offendiculum præbeat his, qui velut ad imbrem serotinum ori vestro aures suas arrigere festinant. Non enim non possumus respondere auditis, cum superbiæ desertabilem bestiam usque ad Sedem Petri repetare videmus, paci Ecclesiæ bene semper providentes. Valete.
units.tr: Your humility, which is the guardian of the virtues, and your gentleness incur no small mark, since such questions, which do little to advance religion, are put before secular persons. Let your Paternity therefore take care that, while raising matters which we deem unworthy, it does not offer a stumbling block to those who hasten to turn their ears to your mouth as to a late rain. For we cannot but answer what we have heard, when we see the detestable beast of pride hunted back as far as the See of Peter, always providing well for the peace of the Church. Farewell.

units.la: FRIDERICI I. IMPER. AUG. EDICTUM
units.tr: THE EDICT OF FREDERICK I, EMPEROR AUGUSTUS

units.la: DE IVRIBVS ET DIGNITATE IMPERII ATQVE ECclesiæ vindicandis à tyrannide Papæ & Cardinalium ejus.
units.tr: CONCERNING THE RIGHTS AND DIGNITY OF THE EMPIRE AND THE CHURCH, TO BE VINDICATED FROM THE TYRANNY OF THE POPE AND HIS CARDINALS.

units.la: CUm divina potentia, à quo omnis potestas in cœlo & in terra, nobis Christo ejus regnum & imperium regendum commiserit, & pacem Ecclesiarum Imperialibus armis conservandam ordina[illegible, ~40 letters]arum, debita solicitudine tractaremus, Apostolicus scripto nobis mandavit, quòd præ oculis habe-remus, quomodo ipse nos in throno Regni coronaverit, & neq; inde pœnituerit eum, [illegible, ~20 letters] enim beneficia nostra Excellentia ab eo suscepisset. Ecce audistis blasphemiam. Recolite litteras, & percutiamini antiquatios vestros, & videte si audium sit hujusmodi verbum in diebus vestris, in diebus antiquis. Sed nec patres nostri annunciaverunt nobis, quòd unquam Regnum alicui Principum ab aliquo Apostolicorum beneficiatum sit, sicut ille vesanæ mentis vir scripsit, se nos inbeneficiasse, pro eo solo, quòd solum unctionem per reverentiam B. Petri ab eo accepimus.
units.tr: Since the divine power, from whom all power in heaven and on earth comes, has entrusted to us his kingdom and empire to rule under Christ, and since we are bound to attend with due care to preserving the peace of the Churches by imperial arms, the Apostolic [Pope] has written to us, bidding us keep before our eyes how he crowned us on the throne of the kingdom, and that he has not repented of it, [...] for he had received our great benefits from him. Behold, you have heard the blasphemy. Read the letter, strike your foreheads, and see whether such a word was ever heard in your days or in the days of old. Our fathers never told us that a kingdom was ever conferred as a benefice on any prince by any of the Apostolics, as that man of deranged mind has written, that he had conferred a benefice on us, solely because we received the anointing from him out of reverence for St. Peter.

units.la: 5. Ecce scandalum, quod, nisi Deus avertat, inficiet totum corpus Ecclesiæ, juxta illud: Necesse est ut veniant scandala. Sed quid sequitur? Vae autem illi, per quem veniunt scandala. Per nos igitur non veniunt, sed per illum, qui se dicit Vicarium Petri, & non est, quia si in viridi ligno hoc facit, quid in arido fiet? Talis toxicatus nos de Mammona iniquitatis suæ appetit, videlicet, quòd nos in Regnum coronavit, & neq; inde pœnituerit eum, si majora beneficia ab eo suscepimus. Videamus igitur si hæc ve-rantur.
units.tr: 5. Behold the scandal, which, unless God averts it, will infect the whole body of the Church, according to that saying: It must needs be that offences come. But what follows? Woe to him through whom the offences come. The offences do not come through us, but through him who calls himself the Vicar of Peter and is not, for if he does this in the green wood, what will be done in the dry? Such a poisoned man seeks from us, out of the mammon of his iniquity, that he crowned us king and has not repented of it, as if we had received greater benefits from him. Let us see, then, whether these things are true.

units.la: 6. Certè nobis coronam per electionem Principum imposuimus: nihil nisi solam unctionem accepimus: & ubi est beneficium, quod ab eo consecuti sumus? Quæ est ergo illa pœnitentia? Ant sunt majora beneficia? An potest esse majus beneficium, quàm Romanum Imperium? Nos ipsi coronam imposuimus, & quomodo tum coronavit, dum coronam Regni nobis ipsi imposuimus. Regnum non ab eo, sed à Deo suscepimus. Videte ergo, qualiter mentitus sit. Sed quia ipse sibi usurpavit, sine consensu nostro; & Viterbium, Cameram Regni, sibi fecit sedem, præponens ... ancillam præferens dominæ.
units.tr: 6. Certainly we placed the crown on ourselves by the election of the princes; we received nothing but the anointing. Where is the benefice which we obtained from him? What, then, is this repentance? Or are the benefits greater? Can there be a greater benefit than the Roman Empire? We ourselves placed the crown on our head, and how did he crown us, when we ourselves placed the crown of the kingdom upon ourselves? We received the kingdom not from him but from God. See, then, how he has lied. But because he has usurped for himself, without our consent, and has made Viterbo, the chamber of the kingdom, his seat, preferring [...] the handmaid preferred to the mistress.

units.la: 7. Ut quia, te teste, nusquam pejus agitur divinum servitium, quàm Romæ, ubi domus Petri facta est spelunca latronum, & habitatio dæmonum: & ubi ille alter Simon hæresiarcha, quærens sua non quæ Jesu Christi, cuncta spiritualia habet venalia: nos judicabimus cum in virga Regni nostri, & ... mus ab eo, quæ nostræ ditionis sunt, urbes & castella, munitiones & oppida, quæ in tota tenet ... & videbimus, quis liberet de manu nostra.
units.tr: 7. Since, as you yourself bear witness, nowhere is divine service worse performed than at Rome, where the house of Peter has become a den of robbers and a habitation of demons, and where that other Simon, the heresiarch, seeking his own and not the things of Jesus Christ, holds all spiritual things for sale: we shall judge [...] with the rod of our kingdom, and [...] the cities and castles, fortresses and towns that are of our dominion, which he holds in all [...]; and we shall see who will deliver them out of our hand.

units.la: 8. Excommunicationem ejus non timebimus, quæ ter tantum apud suos vilipenditur, despicit, neglignurâ. Numquid potest nos excommunicare paries dealbatus? tumens in supercilio Pharum, mortificans animas, quæ non moriuntur, & vivificans quæ non vivitant. Nonne magis secundum B. Gregorium ligandi solvendiq; potestate se privat, qui hanc pro suis voluntatibus, non pro meritis exercet? Quid ejus cis Alpes timemus excommunicationem? dum trans Alpes vulgares parvi pendunt suam excommunicationem. Romæ in sede sua vilipenditur cum sua excommunicatione; & nobis tam gravis est sua indignatio?
units.tr: 8. We shall not fear his excommunication, which is held in contempt, scorned and disregarded only by his own people. Can a whitewashed wall excommunicate us, puffed up in its pride, a lighthouse that kills souls which do not die and gives life to those who are not alive? Does not he rather, according to St. Gregory, deprive himself of the power of binding and loosing, who exercises it for his own will and not for merit? Why should we fear his excommunication on this side of the Alps, when on the far side of the Alps common people think little of it? At Rome, in his own see, his excommunication is despised; and is his indignation so grave to us?

units.la: 9. Ecce qualis subsannatio? Certè vos ipse vidistis & audistis, quàm derisi nos habuerint, vocānos stultos Allemannos, quòd ad præceptū ejus starem us subjecti, quorū dexteras totus orbis ferre posset. Igitur quia vos Primas estis cis Alpes, & cor Regni, & Metropolis illa vestra, Trev· inclyta, quæ inconsutili præpollet tunica Domini, vestro consilio & auxilio summâ & mysteriainconsutilem tunicam Domini, id est, Emath, de manu illius Amorrhæi, videlicet Apostolici, à quo ... Scissa & divisa forte, & in jus Ægyptiorum iterum vendita est, eruemus. Non enim per ostium, sed aliunde ascendit in ovile: fur quippe est & latro.
units.tr: 9. Behold what mockery! Surely you yourselves have seen and heard how they have derided us, calling us foolish Germans because we stood subject to his command, we whose right hands the whole world could bear. Therefore, since you are the primate on this side of the Alps and the heart of the kingdom, and that your famous metropolis of Trier, which excels in the seamless tunic of the Lord, by your counsel and help, with highest mystery, we shall rescue the seamless tunic of the Lord, that is, the Emath of God, from the hand of that Amorite, namely the Apostolic, by whom [...] torn and divided, perhaps, and sold again into the law of the Egyptians. For he does not enter the sheepfold by the door, but climbs in by another way; for he is a thief and a robber.

units.la: 10. Nos in brachio Regni & arcu extento eam eruemus: & vobis, qui idcò secundæ Romæ ut si ille deviaverit, vos conversus confirmetis fratres vestros: quod & vobis in baculo suo Petri dedit, sicut ipse à Domino accepit, ut solus sitis inter omnes post Petrum, sicut ipse post Christum Emath Dei regendam in vice Petri Imperiali authoritate committimus, ut omnes de Regno cis Alpes, non Viterbii ad novam Romam, sed Treverim ad secundam Romam veniant, qui in secundum judicium & justitiam, non nummo cooperante, sicut Romæ, ubi nummus regnat ... quæstiones suas exequantur, dum Deus tantum sit in causa; & ideò Deus merces operis.
units.tr: 10. We shall rescue her with the arm of the kingdom and an outstretched bow; and to you, who for this reason are the second Rome, so that if he has gone astray, you may turn and strengthen your brethren, which he gave to you on his staff of Peter, just as he himself received it from the Lord, so that you alone among all after Peter may be, as he was after Christ, we commit by imperial authority the Emath of God to be governed in the place of Peter, so that all from the kingdom on this side of the Alps may come, not to Viterbo, to the new Rome, but to Trier, to the second Rome, to pursue their causes in a second judgment and justice, with no money cooperating, as at Rome, where money reigns [...], since God alone is in the cause; and therefore God is the reward of the work.

units.la: 11. Nonne & hoc Petrus factis ostendit, dum vobis baculum suum præscius futurorum tradidit adhuc tota dignitas Apostolici ad vos tantum Metropolitanum quasi hæreditario jure devolvitur ... Nonne ideò adhuc Apostolicus sine baculo est, ut vos sitis in baculo ejus? Igitur hæres Petrum, qui se dicit Vicarium Petri, & non est, insurgite, & Suffraganeos vestros, Metensem, & Virdunensem, ut vobis & Regno subscribant, efficite: & vos columna Regni, pro Regno titubat, viriliter state, & stando, quis & quid sitis, factis ostendite, ut per vos ceteri nobis ... ' itant, & filius Belial unanimiter, prout Dominus dederit, resistant. mus filius nester, FRIDERICUS Romanorum Imperator, tale quid egit, quale temporibus antecessorum nostrorum legimus perpetratum. Cum enim nos duos de melioribus fratribus nostris, Bernhardum tit. S. Clementis et Cancellarium nostrum tit. S. Marci Presbyteros Cardinales ad ipsius praesentiam misissemus, ipse cum primum praesentiam pervenerunt, alacriter visus est eos recepisse. Sequenti vero die cum rediissent ad eum, et litteras nostras auribus legerentur, accepta occasione cuiusdam verbi, quod ipsarum literarum series continebat, inligere ritionem ronae beneficium tibi contulimus, in tantam animi commotionem exarsit, ut convicia, quae in nos et Ecclesiam Ecclesiastas dicitur conjecisse, et quam inhoneste ipsosa praesentia sua recedere, ac de terra sua velociter exire copulerit, et re opprobrii et lamentabile su referre. Ea autem ab ipsius praesentia excedentibus, facto edicto, ne aliquis de ad Apostolicam Sedem accedat, per omnes fines ejusdem regni custodes dicitur posuisse, qui eos, qui ad Sedem venire voluerint, violenter debeant revocare.
units.tr: 11. Did not Peter also show this by his deeds, when, knowing the future, he handed his staff to you? The whole dignity of the Apostolic passes to you alone, the metropolitan, as if by hereditary right. Is it not for this reason that the Apostolic is still without a staff, so that you may be in his staff? Therefore, you who are the heir of Peter, and who say you are the Vicar of Peter and are not, rise up, and bring it about that your suffragans, of Metz and Verdun, subscribe to you and to the kingdom; and you, pillar of the kingdom, which totters for the kingdom, stand manfully, and by standing show by your deeds who and what you are, so that through you the others [...] and the son of Belial, with one accord, as the Lord shall grant, may resist. Our son, Frederick, Emperor of the Romans, did such a thing as we read was committed in the times of our predecessors. For when we had sent two of our better brethren, Bernard, titular cardinal of St. Clement, and our Chancellor, titular cardinal of St. Mark, priests, into his presence, he, as soon as they arrived before him, seemed eagerly to receive them. But on the following day, when they had returned to him and our letters were read aloud, an occasion was seized upon from a word which the series of those letters contained, namely, that we had conferred the benefice of the Empire upon you; he burst into such agitation that he hurled insults against us and the Church of the Romans, calling us [...], and drove them dishonourably from his presence and quickly out of his land, and made them return in shame and lamentation. Then, after they had withdrawn from his presence, by a published edict he is said to have posted guards at all the borders of his kingdom, that no one should approach the Apostolic See, and that they should violently turn back those who wished to come to the See.

units.la: Super quo facto licet aliquatulum perturbamur, ex hoc tamen in maiorem consolationem accipimus, quod ad id de vestro et Principum consilio non processit. Unde confidimus enim ut motu, consilio et persuasione vestra facile revocandum. Quocirca, Fratres, quoniam in hoc facto non solum vestra et omnium Ecclesiarum res agi dinoscitur, caritatem vestram monemus et exhortamur in Domino, quatenus vos nati vos muri pro domo Domini, et praefati filium nostrum ad viam rectam quam citius reducere studeatis, mam sollicitudine adhibentes, ut a Reinaldo Cancellario suo, et Palatino Comite, qui magnas blasphemias in Legatos nostros et matre vestram sacrosanctam Romanam Ecclesiam evomere praesumpserunt, tale et tam ex tusa tione faciat exhiberi, ut sicut multorum aures amaritudo sermonis eorum offendit, sic etiam saturatio multos recta debeat revocare. Non acquiescat idem filius noster consilio iniquorum: consideret novissima et antiqua, iam viam incedat, per quam Iustinianus et alii Catholici Imperatores incesserunt. Exemplo siquidem et honorem in terris et felicitatem in caelis sibi poterit cumulare. Vos etiam, sicut ad rectam iter...
units.tr: Although we are somewhat disturbed by this deed, we take it for greater comfort that it did not proceed from your counsel and that of the princes. Hence we trust that by your motion, counsel and persuasion it can easily be recalled. Wherefore, brethren, since in this matter not only your affair and that of all the Churches is seen to be at stake, we admonish and exhort your charity in the Lord, that you, as walls born for the house of the Lord, and as we have said, study to bring our aforesaid son back to the right way as quickly as possible, applying such diligence that his Chancellor Reinald and the Count Palatine, who have presumed to vomit great blasphemies against our legates and against your mother, the holy Roman Church, be made to give such satisfaction and such a full retraction that, just as the bitterness of their words has offended the ears of many, so also their recantation should call many back to the right course. Let our same son not consent to the counsel of the wicked; let him consider the latest and the ancient examples, and walk now in the way by which Justinian and the other Catholic emperors walked. For by this example he will be able to heap up honour on earth and happiness in heaven. You also, as to the right way...

units.la: 4. Haec & alia, utputa de concordia Rogerii & Guilhelmi Siculi, & aliis, quae in Italia facta sunt, convenientibus, quae ad plenum prosequi non audemus, ab ore Domini nostri Imperatoris audivimus.
units.tr: 4. These things, and others (for instance concerning the agreement between Roger and William the Sicilian, and the other matters that were settled in Italy), which we do not dare to pursue fully, we heard from the lips of our Lord the Emperor.

units.la: 5. Absente autem Palatino Comite, & in praeparatione expeditionis in Italiam praemisso, a Cancellario adhuc praesente aliud non audivimus, nisi quod humilitatis erat & pacis, praeter quod pro periculo vitae, quod a populo imminebat, pro vitiis suis allegant, cunctis, qui ibi aderant, Imperii testimonium ei perhibentibus.
units.tr: 5. But with the Count Palatine absent, and sent ahead in preparation for the expedition into Italy, while the Chancellor was still present, we heard nothing else than what belonged to humility and peace; except that they allege, for the danger to his life which was threatening from the people, his faults; all who were there bearing witness to him of the Empire's testimony.

units.la: 6. De caetero sanctitatem vestram suppliciter rogamus & obsecramus, ut nostrae parcatis infirmitati, magnanimitatem filii vestri, sicut bonus pastor, leniatis scriptis veltus scripta priora suavitate dulcorantibus, quatenus & Ecclesia Dei tranquilla devotione laetetur, & Imperium in suae gloriae status glorietur: ipso mediante & adjuvante, qui mediator Dei & hominum factus est, homo Christus Iesus.
units.tr: 6. For the rest, we humbly ask and beseech your holiness, that you spare our weakness, and, like a good shepherd, soften the mind of your son by your writings, sweetening the earlier writings with gentleness, so that the Church of God may rejoice in calm devotion, and the Empire may glory in the state of its glory: with him mediating and helping, who was made the mediator of God and men, the man Christ Jesus.

units.la: HADRIANUS PAPA IMP. FRIDERICO AUG. DE SENTENTIA EPISCOPO- RUM COGITUR INTERPRETARI, QUOMODO IMPERIUM DICATUR & SIT BENEFICIUM PAPAE.
units.tr: HADRIAN, POPE, TO HIS EMPEROR FREDERICK AUGUSTUS, CONCERNING THE SENSE IN WHICH THE EMPIRE IS SAID TO BE A BENEFICE OF THE POPE, AND IS ONE, AS THE BISHOPS' OPINION REQUIRES.

units.la: E Xquo universalis Ecclesiae curam, Deo prout ipsi placuit) disponente, suscepimus, ita in cunctis negotiis magnificentiam tuam honorare curavimus, ut de die in diem animus tuus magis ac magis in amore nostro & veneratione Sedis Apostolicae debuisset accendi. Unde sine grandi admiratione non fermus, quod cum audito ex suggestione quorundam animum tuum aliquantulum concussum fuisse commotorum, duos de melioribus & majoribus fratribus nostris, Rolandum scilicet Cancellarium ut S. Marci & Bernhardum ut S. Clementis Presbyteros Cardinales, qui pro tuae Majestatis honore in Romana Ecclesia solliciti semper extitérunt, pro voluntatis tuae cognitione ad tuam praesentiam destinavimus, aliter quam Imperialem decuerit honorificentiam, sint tractati.
units.tr: Since we have taken up the care of the universal Church, God so disposing it as he pleased, we have taken pains to honour your magnificence in all matters, so that your mind should, from day to day, be kindled more and more with love for us and reverence for the Apostolic See. Hence we cannot bear, without great astonishment, that when we heard, at the suggestion of certain persons, that your mind had been somewhat shaken and disturbed, we sent two of our better and greater brothers, Roland, Chancellor, as cardinal-priest of St Mark, and Bernard, as cardinal-priest of St Clement, who have always been diligent in the Roman Church for the honour of your Majesty, to learn your will in your presence; and they were treated otherwise than the imperial honour would have fitted.

units.la: 2. Occasione siquidem cujusdam verbi, quod est Beneficium, tuus animus (sicut dicitur) est commotus, quod utiq; nedum tanti viri, sed nec cujuslibet minoris animum merito commovisset. Licet enim hoc nomen, quod est Beneficium, apud quosdam in alia significatione, quam ex impositione habeat, sonat: tunc tamen in ea significatione accipiendum fuerat, quam nos ipsi posuimus, & quam in actione sua noluimus retinere. Hoc enim nomen ex bono & facto est editum, & dicitur beneficium apud non feudum, sed bonum factum. In qua significatione in universo sacrae Scripturae corpore invenitur, ubi ex beneficio Dei non tanquam ex feudo, sed velut ex benedictione & bono facto ipsius gubernari dicimur & nutrimur. Et tua quidem magnificentia liquido recognoscit, quod nos ita bene & honorifice Imperialis dignitatis insigne tuo capiti imposuimus, ut bonum factum valeat ab omnibus judicari. Unde quod quidam verbum hoc, & illud scilicet, contulimus tibi insigne Imperialis coronae, a sensu suo longe ad alium retorquere, non ex merito causae, sed de voluntate propria, & illorum suggestione, pacem Regni & Ecclesiae nullatenus diligunt, hoc egerunt. Per hoc enim vocabulum, contulimus, illud intellexerimus, nisi quod superius dictum est, impossumus.
units.tr: 2. Indeed, on account of a certain word, which is beneficium, your mind was (so it is said) disturbed; and this would rightly have disturbed not only so great a man but anyone of lesser rank. For although this word, beneficium, sounds among some people in a sense other than that which it has by its original imposition, yet it should have been taken in the sense which we ourselves gave it, and which we did not wish to alter in our act. For this word is formed from bonum and factum, and beneficium means a good deed, not a fief. In this sense it is found throughout the whole body of Holy Scripture, where we are said to be governed and nourished by the benefit of God, not as by a fief, but as by his blessing and good deed. Your magnificence clearly acknowledges that we placed the insignia of imperial dignity on your head so well and honourably that the good deed can be judged by all. Hence, those who twist this phrase, "we conferred on you the insignia of the imperial crown," far away from its meaning to another sense, not on the merits of the case but from their own will and at their suggestion, who in no way love the peace of the kingdom and the Church, have done this. For by the word conferred we understand nothing other than what was said above, that we placed the crown upon you.

units.la: 3. Sane quod postmodum personas Ecclesiasticas a debita sacrosanctae Romanae Ecclesiae visitare dicitur, revocare iusserit, si ita est, quam incovenienter actu sit, tua, Fili in Christo carissime, veritas, ut credimus, recognoscit. Nam si aliquid apud nos amaritudinis habebas, per nuntios & litteras nobis fuerat intimandum, & nos honori tuo curavissemus, sicut filii carissimi, providere. Sed quoniam ad commonitionem dilecti filii nostri Henrici Bajoariae & Saxoniae Ducis, duos nostris, Henricum tit. S. Nerei & Achillei & Iacinctum tit. S. Mariae in Cosmidin Diaconales, prudentes siquidem & honestos viros, ad tuam prudentiam destinavimus, Celsitudinem monentes & hortantes in Domino, quatenus eos honeste & benigne recipias, & quod ab nostra tuae magnificentiae fuerit intimatum, a sincerite cordis nostri noverit tua Excellentia, ac per hoc cum eisdem filiis nostris, mediante jam dicto filio nostro Duce, ita Celsitudo convenire, ut inter te ac matrem tuam sacrosanctam Romanam Ecclesiam nullius seminarium debeat remanere.
units.tr: 3. As for the report that you afterwards ordered the ecclesiastical persons who were visiting from the sacrosanct Roman Church due to be recalled, if this is so, your truth, most dear son in Christ, recognises, we believe, how improperly it was done. For if you had any bitterness against us, it should have been made known to us through messengers and letters, and we would have taken care to provide for your honour, as for a most dear son. But since, at the admonition of our beloved son Henry, Duke of Bavaria and Saxony, we have sent to your prudence two of our men, Henry, deacon of the title of SS. Nereus and Achilleus, and Hyacinth, deacon of the title of St Mary in Cosmedin, prudent and honest men, admonishing and exhorting Your Highness in the Lord to receive them honourably and kindly, and that what has been made known by us to your magnificence, Your Excellence may know from the sincerity of our heart; and so that Your Highness may come to terms, through the aforementioned Duke, our son, with those same sons of ours, in such a way that no seedbed of discord remains between you and your mother, the sacrosanct Roman Church.

units.la: FORMULA SACRAMENTI FIDELIUM IMPERII.
units.tr: The Formula of the Oath of the Faithful of the Empire.

units.la: E Gq Nijuro quod amodo inantea ero fidelis Domino meo Friderico Romanorum Imperatori contra omnes homines, sicut jure debeo Domino & Imperatori, & adjuvabo cum rei publicae coronam Imperii, & omnem honorem ejus in Italia, nominatim & specialiter civitatem Romam & quicquid in ea juris habere debet, vel in omni virtute Comitatus vel Episcopatus N. Regalia non auferam ibidem, necalibi; & si fuerint ablata, bona fide recuperare & reinere adjuvabo. Neq;
units.tr: I, N., swear that from now on I will be faithful to my lord Frederick, Emperor of the Romans, against all men, as I rightly owe to my lord and Emperor. I will help him to maintain the crown and dignity of the Empire and all his honour in Italy, especially and by name the city of Rome, and whatever right he ought to have there, or in every county or bishopric N. I will not take away his regalia there or elsewhere; and if they have been taken away, I will help to recover and retain them in good faith. Nor

units.la: Anno Christi 1159.
units.tr: In the year of Christ 1159.

units.la: Anno Christi 1158. bo. Neq; in consilio ero neq; in facto, quod vitam, membrum, vel honorem suum perdat, vel male captione teneatur. Omne mandatum ejus, quod ipse mihi fecerit, per se vel epistolam suam, aut Legatum suum, de faciendo justitiam, deliberet observabo, & illud audire vel recipere vel loqui ... lo malo ingenio evitabo. Haec omnia observabo fide bona sine fraude: sic me Deus adiuvet, & sancta quatuor Evangelia.
units.tr: In the year of Christ 1158. Nor will I be party to any counsel or deed by which he loses life, limb or honour, or is taken and held unjustly. I will observe in good faith, without fraud, every command that he gives me, whether by himself, by his letter or by his envoy, concerning the doing of justice, and I will consider it. ... by evil cunning I will avoid hearing, receiving or speaking of it. All these things I will observe in good faith without deceit: so may God help me, and the holy four Gospels.

units.la: FRIDERICI I. IMPERATO- RIS AUGUSTI
units.tr: FREDERICK I, EMPEROR AUGUSTUS

units.la: LEGES CASTRENSES, LATAE APUD BRIXIAM In Conventu Principum Imperii Anno Domini M.C.LVIIII.
units.tr: CAMP LAWS, ENACTED AT BRESCIA in the Assembly of the Princes of the Empire in the year of the Lord 1159.

units.la: 2. Qui aliquem vulneraverit, & hoc se fecisse negaverit, tunc si vulneratus per duos veraces testes, non consanguineos suos, illum convincere poterit, manus ei abscindatur. Quòd si testes deficiunt, & ille juramento se expurgare voluerit, accusator, si vult, poterit juramentum refutare, & illum impetere.
units.tr: 2. Whoever wounds someone and denies having done it: if the wounded man can convict him by two credible witnesses who are not his relatives, the offender's hand shall be cut off. If witnesses are lacking and he wishes to clear himself by oath, the accuser may, if he wishes, refuse the oath and attack him.

units.la: 3. Si quis homicidium fecerit, & a propinquo occisi, vel amico, vel socio, per duos veraces testes non consanguineos occisi convictus fuerit, capitalem sententiam subibit. Verum si testes defecerint, & homicida se juramento expurgare voluerit, amicus propinquus occisi duello cum eo petere.
units.tr: 3. If anyone commits homicide and is convicted, by two credible witnesses who are not kin of the slain man, at the instance of a kinsman, friend, or companion of the slain, he shall undergo the death sentence. But if witnesses fail and the killer wishes to clear himself by oath, the slain man's kinsman and friend may seek a duel with him.

units.la: 4. Si extraneus miles pacifice ad castra accesserit, sedem in palefrido sine scuto & armis, cum laeserit, pacis violator judicabitur. Si autem sedens in dextrario, & habens scutum in collo, lanceam in manu, ad castra accesserit, si quis eum laeserit, pacem non violavit.
units.tr: 4. If a foreign soldier comes peacefully to camp, seated on a palfrey without shield and arms, and someone injures him, the one who injured him shall be judged a violator of the peace. But if he comes to camp seated on a warhorse, with shield on his neck and lance in hand, and someone injures him, he has not violated the peace.

units.la: 5. Miles, qui mercatorem spoliaverit, duplicitèr reddet ablata, & jurabit quòd nescivit illum mercatorem. Si servus, tondebitur, & in maxilla comburetur, vel Dominus suus reddet pro eo poenam.
units.tr: 5. A soldier who has robbed a merchant shall restore the goods twofold and swear that he did not know the man was a merchant. If he is a servant, he shall be shorn and branded on the cheek, or his lord shall pay the penalty for him.

units.la: 6. Quicunq; aliquem spoliare Ecclesiam vel forum viderit, prohibere debet, tamen sine prohibere non poterit, reum accusare debet in curia.
units.tr: 6. Whoever sees someone plundering a church or the market must forbid it; but if he cannot forbid it, he must accuse the offender in court.

units.la: 7. Nemo aliquam mulierem habeat in hospitio. Qui vero habere praesumpserit, auferetur ei omne suum harnascha, & excommunicatus habebitur, & mulieri nasus abscindetur.
units.tr: 7. No one shall keep any woman in his lodging. Whoever presumes to do so shall lose all his baggage, shall be held excommunicate, and the woman's nose shall be cut off.

units.la: 8. Nemo impugnabit castrum, quod à Curia defensionem habet.
units.tr: 8. No one shall attack a castle that has the Court's protection.

units.la: 9. Si servus furtum fecerit, & in furto fuerit deprehensus, si prius fur non erat, non ideo suspenderetur, sed rodebitur, verberabitur, & in maxilla comburetur, & ejicietur de exercitu, nisi Dominus eum damnat cum omni suo harnascha. Si prius fur erat, suspenderetur.
units.tr: 9. If a servant commits theft and is caught in the act, then if he was not a thief before, he shall not be hanged for it but shall be shorn, beaten, branded on the cheek, and expelled from the army, unless his lord condemns him together with all his baggage. If he was a thief before, he shall be hanged.

units.la: 10. Si servus aliquis culpatus non in furto fuerit deprehensus, sequenti die expurgabit se judicio ignito ferri, vel Dominus juramentum pro eo praestabit. Actor vero jurabit, quòd aliam ob causam non interpellat eum de furto, nisi quòd putat culpabilem.
units.tr: 10. If a servant accused of theft was not caught in the act, he shall clear himself on the following day by the ordeal of hot iron, or his lord shall give oath on his behalf. The plaintiff shall swear that he does not charge him with theft for any other reason than that he thinks him guilty.

units.la: 11. Si quis invenerit equum alterius, non tondebit eum, nec ignotum faciet, sed dicet Domino, & tenebit non furtivè, & imponet ei onus suum. Quòd si ille, qui amittit equum in via deprehenderit oneratum, non dejiciet onus illius, sed sequens ad hospitium recipiet equum suum.
units.tr: 11. If anyone finds another's horse, he shall not shear it nor disguise it, but shall tell the owner and keep it openly, not secretly, and shall load it with his own burden. But if the one who lost the horse finds it on the road loaded, he shall not throw down its load, but following it, shall take his horse back to lodging.

units.la: 12. Si quis vero villam vel domum incenderit, tondebitur, & in maxillis comburetur, & verberabitur.
units.tr: 12. If anyone sets fire to a village or a house, he shall be shorn, branded on the cheeks, and beaten.

units.la: 13. Faber non comburet carbones in villa, sed portabit ligna ad hospitium suum, & ibi cesset. Quòd si in villa fecerit, tondebitur, verberabitur, & in maxillis comburetur.
units.tr: 13. A smith shall not burn coals in the village, but shall carry his wood to his lodging and stay there. If he does so in the village, he shall be shorn, beaten, and branded on the cheeks.

units.la: 14. Si quis aliquem laeserit, imponens ei quòd pacem non juraverit, non erit reus violatae pacis nisi ille probare poterit duobus idoneis testibus, quòd pacem juraverit.
units.tr: 14. If someone injures another, charging him with not having sworn the peace, he shall not be guilty of breaking the peace unless he can prove, by two reliable witnesses, that he swore it.

units.la: 15. Nemo recipiet servum, qui sine Domino est. quod si fecerit, reddet in duplo, quicquid abstulerit.
units.tr: 15. No one shall receive a servant who is without his lord. If he does, he shall restore double whatever he has taken.

units.la: 16. Quicunq; foveam invenerit, liberè fruatur ea. Quòd si ablata fuerit ei, non reddet malum pro malo, non ulcisceretur injuriam suam, sed conqueretur Marscalco justiciam acceptuus.
units.tr: 16. Whoever finds a pit may freely enjoy it. If it is taken from him, he shall not repay evil for evil nor avenge his injury, but shall complain to the marshal and accept justice.

units.la: 17. Sed si mercator Teutonicus civitatem mirivit, & cemeniit mercatum, & portas erit datas exercitum, & carrus vendiderit in exercitu, Camerarius auferet ei omne forum suum, & verberabitur, & tondebit, & comburetur in maxilla.
units.tr: 17. But if a German merchant has traded in a town and made a bargain, and has given pledges to the army, and has sold a wagon in the army, the chamberlain shall take all his goods, and he shall be beaten, shorn, and branded on the cheek.

units.la: 18. Nullus Teutonicus habeat socium Latinum, nisi sciat Teutonicum: sed si habuerit, auseretur ei quicquid habet.
units.tr: 18. No German shall have a Latin companion unless he knows German; but if he does, all that he has shall be taken from him.

units.la: 19. Si miles militi convicia dixerit, negare poterit juramento: si non negaverit, componet ei X. libras monetæ, quæ tunc erit in exercitu.
units.tr: 19. If a soldier insults another soldier, he may deny it under oath; if he does not deny it, he shall pay him ten pounds of the money current then in the army.

units.la: 20. Si quis invenerit vasa plena vini, vinum inde extrahat ita caute, ne vasa confringat, vel ligamina incidat vasorum, ne ad damnum exercitus totum vinum effundatur.
units.tr: 20. If anyone finds vessels full of wine, he shall draw the wine out so carefully that he does not break the vessels or cut their bindings, lest all the wine be spilled to the army's loss.

units.la: 21. Si castrum aliquod captum fuerit, bona, quæ intus sunt, auferantur: sed non incendatur, nisi forte hoc Marscalcus faciat.
units.tr: 21. If any castle is taken, the goods within it shall be carried off, but it shall not be burned, unless perhaps the marshal does so.

units.la: 22. Si quis venatus fuerit cum canibus venaticis, feram, quam invenerit, & canibus agitaverit, sine alicujus impedimento habebit.
units.tr: 22. If anyone hunts with hunting dogs, he shall have, without hindrance from anyone, any beast that he finds and drives down with the dogs.

units.la: 23. Si quis per canes leporarios feram fugaverit, non erit necessario sua, sed erit occupantis.
units.tr: 23. If anyone drives a beast out with hounds meant for hares, it shall not necessarily be his, but shall belong to whoever seizes it.

units.la: 24. Si quis lancea vel gladio feram percusserit, & antequam manu levaverit, alter occupaverit, non occupantis erit, sed qui occiderit eam, sine contradictione obtinebit.
units.tr: 24. If someone strikes a beast with a lance or sword, and another seizes it before he has lifted it by hand, it does not belong to the seizer but to the one who killed it, who shall obtain it without contradiction.

units.la: 25. Si quis birsando feram balista vel arcu occiderit, cujus erit.
units.tr: 25. If anyone kills a beast by shooting it with a crossbow or bow, whose it shall be.

units.la: 26. Hanc treugam Archiepiscopi, Episcopi, Abbates, datis pro se dextris firmaverunt, & violatores pacis Pontificalis officii severitate coercendos promiserunt.
units.tr: 26. The archbishops, bishops, and abbots have confirmed this truce by giving their right hands on behalf of themselves, and have promised that violators of the peace shall be restrained with the severity of the pontifical office.

units.la: FRIDERICI I. IMPER. AUG. EDICTUM
units.tr: Edict of Emperor Frederick I Augustus

units.la: De rebellibus Imperii per Italiam in ordinem redigendis: & de honore Germanici Impe- rii tutando & conservando contra Papisequas.
units.tr: On bringing the rebels of the Empire in Italy back to order, and on defending and preserving the honour of the German Empire against the Papists' followers.

units.la: FRIDERICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator & Semper-Augustus, dilecto suo Alberto Erisingensi Episcopo, gratiam suam & omne bonum. Cum coeli stupeant, & totus orbis contremiscat, & cuncta turbari cogitet elementa a facie scelestissimæ perfidiæ, a nece plaiculari malitiæ, abauditu nefandæ traditionis, quam quædam * civitates Longobardiæ, Mediolanum scilicet, Placentia, Cremona, Bergomum, Brixia, Parma, Mantua, & Marchia Veronensis, contra nostram Majestatem, contra Imperii honorem, sine causa, sine aliqua præcedenti culpa commiserunt, super re tam horrida credimus nimirum * fidem tuam condolere, & omnia viscera tua conturbari. Non enim in nostram solummodo redundat rebellio personam, quia jugo dominationis nostræ projecto, Teutonicorum Imperium, quod multo labore, multisque dispendiis, ac plurimorum Principum & Illustrium virorum sanguine emptum, & hactenus conservatum est, refutare & exterminare conantur, dicentes; Nolumus hunc regnare super nos, nec Teutonici amplius dominabuntur nostri. Quia vero, antequam nostris temporibus Imperium destrui patiamur, & in posteros nostros tantæ confusionis & jacturæ dispendia transmittamus, malumus honestam mortem, . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
units.tr: Frederick, by the grace of God Roman Emperor and Ever-August, to his beloved Albert, Bishop of Eichstätt [Erisingensis], his grace and every good. When the heavens are astonished, the whole world trembles, and the elements seem ready to be thrown into confusion at the face of most wicked treachery, at the deadly bloodshed of malice, and at the report of the unspeakable betrayal which certain cities of Lombardy, namely Milan, Piacenza, Cremona, Bergamo, Brescia, Parma, Mantua and the March of Verona, have committed against our Majesty and against the honour of the Empire, without cause and without any previous fault, we believe that your loyalty surely grieves over so dreadful a matter and that all your inmost feelings are disturbed. For this rebellion does not fall only upon our person: having cast off the yoke of our rule, they try to refute and destroy the Teutonic Empire, which has been bought with great labour, many expenses and the blood of many princes and illustrious men, and has been preserved until now, saying: We do not want this man to reign over us, and the Teutons shall no longer rule over us. But since we would rather die an honourable death than allow the Empire to be destroyed in our times and hand on to our descendants the losses and damage of such great confusion, . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .

units.la: FRIDERICI I. IMPERATORIS AUGUSTI CONSTITUTIO
units.tr: THE CONSTITUTION OF FREDERICK I, EMPEROR AUGUSTUS

units.la: De pacts conventionis & conditionibus pacis cum Mediolanensibus factæ.
units.tr: Concerning the pacts of agreement and the conditions of peace made with the Milanese.

units.la: IN nomine Domini nostri JESU CHRISTI. Hæc est conventio, per quam Mediolanenses in gratiam Imperatoris redituri sunt & permansuri.
units.tr: In the name of our Lord JESUS CHRIST. This is the agreement by which the Milanese shall return into the favour of the Emperor and remain there.

units.la: 1. Cumas & Laudam civitates ad honorem Imperii relevari non prohibebunt, & amodo non impugnabunt, nec destruent; & a fodro, & viatico, & ab omnimoda exactione se ibidem per omnem ditionem continebunt, & ultra se non intromittent, ut sint liberæ illæ civitates, sicut Mediolanenses ab ipsis sunt liberi: excepto respectu juris Ecclesiastici, quod habent ad Archiepiscopum & Ecclesiam Mediolanensem.
units.tr: 1. The cities of Cumas and Lodi shall not forbid being raised again to the honour of the Empire, and from now on they shall neither attack nor destroy them; and they shall refrain throughout the whole dominion from fodder, provisions for the road, and every kind of exaction, and shall not interfere further, so that those cities may be free just as the Milanese are free from them; except in respect of the ecclesiastical right which they have to the Archbishop and the Church of Milan.

units.la: 2. Omnes Mediolanenses communiter a minoribus usque ad majores, ab annis *XIV. & supra usque ad annos LXX. fidelitatem Domino Imperatori jurabunt, & sine malo ingenio, & observabunt.
units.tr: 2. All the Milanese, commonly from the lesser to the greater, from the age of fourteen years and upward up to seventy years, shall swear fidelity to the Lord Emperor, and shall keep it without evil intent.

units.la: 3. Palatium Imperiale ad honorem Domini Imperatoris arbitratu bonorum elevabunt, & eum debito honore bona fide observabunt.
units.tr: 3. They shall raise the Imperial palace to the honour of the Lord Emperor at the judgement of good men, and shall observe it in good faith with the due honour.

units.la: 4. Pecuniam pro emendatione injuriarum Domino Imperatori, vel Dominæ Imperatrici, sive Curiæ promissam, statutis temporibus persolvent, hoc est tertiam partem infra x x x. dies, ex quo hæc pactio confirmata fuerit: aliam vero tertiam partem infra octavam beati Martini: tertiam autem reliduam partem infra octavas Epiphaniæ. Hisque, sic persolutis, nullis privatis teneantur promissionibus. Pecuniæ promissæ summa hæc est: novem milia marcarum argenti sive auri vel monetæ ejusdem æstimationis & precii.
units.tr: 4. They shall pay the money promised to the Lord Emperor or the Lady Empress, or to the Court, for making amends for the injuries, at the appointed times: that is, a third part within thirty days from the day this pact is confirmed; another third part within the octave of Saint Martin; and the remaining third part within the octave of Epiphany. And once these have been paid in this way, they shall be bound by no private promises. The sum of the promised money is this: nine thousand marks of silver, or of gold, or of coin of the same value and worth.

units.la: 5. Pro his tantum prætaxatis capitulis bona fide complendis & conservandis, c c c. obsides dabunt Capitaneos, valvassores, populares, quales approbati fuerint à Domino Archiepiscopo Mediolanensi, & Comite Blandratensi, & Marchione Guilhelmo Montisferrati, & tribus Consulibus, si hæc Domino Imperatori placuerint, juramento astrictis ad hanc electionem fideliter faciendam. Obsides vero in partibus Italiæ omnes servantur, præter L. vel pauciores, per interventum Regis Bohemorum Ladeslai & aliorum Principum, ultra montes, si Domino Imperatori placuerit, deferendos. Quibus autem commissi fuerint obsides in Italia, jurent in praesentia Mediolanensium ad haec praedestinatorum, quod praefixo tempore transacto intra octo dies, ex quo requisiti fuerint a Mediolanensibus, eos eis liberè reddant, ut illi securè eos habeant, si praetaxata capitula ab eis observata fuerint. Tres verò Principes Alemaniae dextras dabunt, quod obsides illi, qui ultra montes deferentur, si qui erunt, eodem pacto fideliter reddentur.
units.tr: 5. Only for the faithful completion and observance of the aforesaid chapters, they shall give three hundred hostages: captains, vavassors, and commoners, such as shall be approved by the Lord Archbishop of Milan, the Count of Blandrate, and Marquis William of Montferrat, and three consuls, if these choices please the Lord Emperor, bound by oath to make this election faithfully. The hostages, however, shall all be kept in the parts of Italy, except fifty or fewer, who shall be conveyed across the mountains, if it pleases the Lord Emperor, through the mediation of Ladislaus, King of the Bohemians, and other princes. Those to whom the hostages have been entrusted in Italy shall swear in the presence of the Milanese, who have been designated for this purpose, that after the fixed time has passed, within eight days from the time they are demanded by the Milanese, they will freely return them to them, so that the Milanese may hold them securely, provided the aforesaid chapters have been observed by them. Moreover, the three princes of Germany shall give their right hands that those hostages who are conveyed across the mountains, if there are any, will likewise be faithfully returned under the same pact.

units.la: 6. Consules verò, qui nunc sunt, ex auctoritate & concessione Domini Imperatoris usque ad Kal. Februarii proximè venturas perseverent, & pro Consulatu suo Domino Imperatori jurent. Venturi verò Consules à populo eligantur, & ab ipso Imperatore confirmentur quorum medietas ad ipsum veniat, dum in Longobardia fuerit: alibi autem eo existente, duo ad eum ex Consulibus veniant, & juramento facto officium Consulatus sui à Domino Imperatore recipiant pro se & sociis suis facturis idem juramentum Domino Imperatori coram communi suae civitatis. Si autem Legatus à Domino Imperatore destinatus fuerit in Italiam, eadem coram ipso & per ipsum fiant.
units.tr: 6. The consuls who now hold office shall continue, by the authority and grant of the Lord Emperor, until the first of February next, and shall swear to the Lord Emperor for their consulship. The consuls to come shall be chosen by the people and confirmed by the Emperor himself, half of whom shall come to him while he is in Lombardy; but if he is elsewhere, two of the consuls shall come to him, and having taken the oath, shall receive the office of their consulship from the Lord Emperor, swearing the same oath to the Lord Emperor, for themselves and their colleagues, before the commune of their city. If, however, a legate has been sent by the Lord Emperor into Italy, these things shall be done before him and through him.

units.la: 7. Legati verò Domini Imperatoris in Italiam directi, si civitatem adierint, in Palatio sedeant, & placita ad eos delata ad honorem Imperii diffiniant.
units.tr: 7. The legates of the Lord Emperor directed into Italy, if they enter a city, shall sit in the palace and settle the disputes brought before them for the honour of the Empire.

units.la: 8.
