Antequam castra ab obsidione moveantur, captivi omnes reddantur in potestatem Regis Boemorum, qui & securitatem per se & honestos Principes eis faciat, quod captivos illos Domino Imperatori reddat, si eis Dominus Imperator pacem fecerit cum Cremonensibus, Papiensibus, Novarensibus, Cumanis, Laudensibus, Vercellensibus; non solùm autè Mediolanensibus, verùm etiam confoederatis eorum, Tordonensibus, Cremensibus, & Insulanis: salvo honore Domini Imperatoris, & illibatis amicitiis Mediolanensium, & in suo statu permanentibus. Si verò pax ei cum praedictis civitatibus facta non fuerit, captivi veteres eis reddantur, nec ob id gratia Domini Imperatoris ipsi & amicorum priventur.
units.tr: 8. Before the camps are moved from the siege, all the prisoners shall be handed over into the power of the King of the Bohemians, who shall also give security, through himself and honourable princes, that he will restore those prisoners to the Lord Emperor, if the Lord Emperor makes peace with the Cremonese, the Pavians, the Novarese, the Cumans, the Laudenses, and the Vercellese; and not only with the Milanese, but also with their allies, the Tortonese, the Cremenses, and the Insubrians: saving the honour of the Lord Emperor, and with the friendships of the Milanese unimpaired and remaining in their condition. If, however, peace has not been made with the aforesaid cities, the old prisoners shall be restored to them, and on that account they shall not be deprived of the grace of the Lord Emperor, either themselves or their friends.

units.la: 9. Regalia, veluti monetam, telonium, pedaticum, portus, comitatus, & alia similia, si qua sunt, communi Mediolanensium dimittet, & ultrà se non intromittet: & si quis per violentiam haec obtinere voluerit, & justiciam inde coram Domino Imperatore vel Nuncio ejus facere noluerit, Mediolanenses vindictam de eo pro sua possibilitate sument in persona & possessione, & regalia Domino Imperatori restituent sine fraude & malo ingenio.
units.tr: 9. The Commune of Milan shall give up the regalia, such as the mint, the toll, the pedage, the ports, the counties, and other similar rights, if there are any, and shall not interfere further; and if anyone wishes to seize these by violence, and is unwilling to seek justice for them before the Lord Emperor or his envoy, the Milanese shall take vengeance on him according to their ability, against his person and possessions, and shall restore the regalia to the Lord Emperor without fraud or evil intent.

units.la: 10. Hoc pacto & ordine Dominus Imperator Mediolanenses & Cremenses cum cxx. marcarum emendatione in gratiâ suâ recipiet, & eos & amicos eorum in plena curia publicè à banno absolvet, & captivos eorum omnes, veteres & novos, eis reddet statim postquam obsides Imperatori dederint, & captivos tam veteres quàm novos in manum Regis Boemorum reddiderint.
units.tr: 10. By this pact and arrangement the Lord Emperor shall receive the Milanese and the Cremenses into his favour, with a payment of one hundred and twenty marks, and in full court he shall publicly absolve them and their friends from the ban, and shall restore to them all their prisoners, old and new, immediately after they have given hostages to the Emperor and have handed over all their prisoners, old and new, into the hand of the King of the Bohemians.

units.la: 11. Datis autem obsidibus & captivis, altera die vel tertia exercitus ab obsidione recedet, & Dominus Imperator Mediolanenses & eorum res clementer tractabit.
units.tr: 11. Once the hostages and prisoners have been given, on the second or third day the army shall withdraw from the siege, and the Lord Emperor shall treat the Milanese and their property with clemency.

units.la: 12. Commune Mediolani praefatas conditiones servabit plenariè, bona fide, sine fraude & malo ingenio, quantum non permanserit per justum impedimentum, & per parabolam Friderici Romanorum Imperatoris, vel Nuncii ejus, aut ejus successoris.
units.tr: 12. The Commune of Milan shall fully observe the aforesaid conditions, in good faith, without fraud or evil intent, except insofar as it has not been maintained through a just hindrance, and through the decision of Frederick, Emperor of the Romans, or his envoy, or his successor.

units.la: 13. Collectam praedictae pecuniae liceat modò facere Mediolanensibus ab his, quos in sua societate habere consueverant, praeter Cumanos, Laudenses, & eos qui de Comitatu Sefrensi fidelitatem Domino Imperatori nuper juraverunt.
units.tr: 13. It shall be lawful for the Milanese now to levy the collection of the aforesaid money from those whom they were accustomed to have in their alliance, except the Cumans, the Laudenses, and those of the County of Seprio who have recently sworn fidelity to the Lord Emperor.

units.la: FRIDERICI I. IMPER. AUG. EDICTVM
units.tr: Edict of the Emperor Frederick I, Augustus

units.la: De electione novi Pontificis Romani; & de concordia Germanorum, Francorum & Anglorum.
units.tr: On the election of a new Roman Pontiff, and on the harmony of the Germans, French and English.

units.la: FRIDERICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator & Semper-Augustus, dilecto & fideli suo, Eberhardo Venerabili Saltzburgensi Archiepiscopo, gratiam suam & omne bonum.
units.tr: Frederick, by the grace of God Roman Emperor and ever-Augustus, to his beloved and faithful Eberhard, the venerable Archbishop of Salzburg, his grace and every good.

units.la: 1. Intimamus Dilectionis tuae auribus, quòd Nuncii tui ideò tamdiu detinuimus, ut aliqua nova de negotiis nostris, quae per Legatos nostros Romae tractabantur, per apices nostros tuae charitati pandereinus. Cùm autem essemus in eorum quotidiana exspectatione, & interim Nuncii Papae cum ipsis de verbo pacis & concordiae agerent, divina providentia, quae in sui dispositione nunquam fallitur, ipsum a Papam in nocte beati Egidii de medio tractulit. De cujus obitu literas accepimus: & verò substituenda necessariò esset talis persona, quae ad universorum salutem fidelium, Ecclesiarum Dei statum in unionem pacis reformaret, & ipsum Imperium ac Fideles Imperii honestius tractaret.
units.tr: 1. We make known to your Affection's ears that we have detained your messengers so long so that we might explain to your Charity, by our letters, some news about our affairs that were being negotiated at Rome through our envoys. While we were waiting for them daily, and meanwhile the messengers of the Pope were treating with them concerning a word of peace and concord, divine providence, which never errs in its arrangements, removed the Pope from the midst of us in the night of the blessed Giles. We have received letters about his death. Indeed, a person must necessarily be put in his place who would, for the salvation of all the faithful, reform the state of the Churches of God into a unity of peace, and would deal more honourably with the Empire itself and the faithful of the Empire.

units.la: 2. Pro electione Pontificis faciendâ, jam in Romana Ecclesia partes esse audivimus, & plurimùm inde dolemus. Inde est, quod pro hujus rei novitate tibi nuncianda, Nuncium tuum Dilectionis tuae remittimus, fidelitatis tuae sinceritatem comonentes, intimè hortantes, & quàm maximè rogantes, ut si forte pro aliquo Romanae Sedis electo assensus discretionis tuae requiritus fuerit, non statim, quasi praecipitata ratione, vel nobis incósultis, favorem tuum adhibeas, sed ne Imperium nostris temporibus in se ipsum divisum deploretur, ad unitatem nobiscum studeas operam dare. Idem quoque tuis Suffraganeis & Coepiscopis nunciandum & praecipiendum attentius rogamus.
units.tr: 2. We have heard that, for the making of a election of a Pontiff, parties have already formed in the Roman Church, and we grieve greatly over this. Hence it is that, to announce this new matter to you, we are sending back your messenger, admonishing the sincerity of your loyalty, urging you earnestly and asking you most strongly that, if perhaps your assent should be required for someone elected to the Roman See, you should not at once lend your favour, as if by a hastily made decision, or without consulting us; but that you should take care to work for unity with us, so that the Empire may not be seen torn apart within itself in our times. We also ask that the same be announced and enjoined more carefully to your suffragans and fellow bishops.

units.la: 3. Praeterea Dilectionem tuam volumus non latere, & juxta petitionem Regis Francorum, Venerabile Legatum gitum nostrum Papicensem Episcopum, prudentem ac discretū magnæque sanctitatis virum, à Curia nostra transmisimus, qui duo tanti nominis Regna, Anglorum videlicet ac Francorum, ipsosq; Reges ad hrmam pacem & stabilem amicitiam vice nostra commonear, auctoritate reformet, & supra firmissimum dilectionis & amicitiæ nostræ fundamentum cum omni plenitudine & integritate stabiliat. Noveris etiam, quòd hæc b tria Regna in tantam nostræ voluntatis & dilectionis unitatem inclinata firmabuntur, quòd ex quo primùm stabilita fuerunt, nūquam in tam concordi pace ligata manserunt.
units.tr: 3. Moreover, we want your Affection not to be unaware that, at the request of the King of the French, we have sent from our Court our venerable legate, the Bishop of Pavia, a prudent and discerning man of great holiness, who is to remind and, by his authority, reform on our behalf the two kingdoms of such great name, namely of the English and of the French, and the kings themselves, to a firm peace and stable friendship, and to establish them upon the most firm foundation of our love and friendship with all fullness and integrity. Know also that these three kingdoms, inclined to such a unity of our will and love, will be strengthened, so that since they were first established they have never remained bound together in such a harmonious peace.

units.la: 4. De cætero noster prædictus Legatus hoc verbum electionis de Romano Pontifice in cordibus eorum ita firmabit, ut ipli unà nobiscum unnm inde velint sapi.intŕque, nec in aliquam personam favorem suum tamsubitò ponant, nisi quam nostrum trium unicus laudaverit assensus.
units.tr: 4. For the rest, our aforesaid legate will so fix this word about the election of the Roman Pontiff in their hearts that they will wish to think the same along with us, and will not so quickly place their favour upon any person, unless it be one whom the single assent of us three has approved.

units.la: 5. De his autem omnibus per Alemanniam & c Burgundiam & Aquitaniam apices nostros direximus, universitatem fidelium hoc scire volentes, quòd ad Kathedram tanti regiminis, aliam personam nullatenus recipere intendimus, nisi quam ad honorem Imperii, & quietem & unitatem Ecclesiæ, unanimi & concordi assensu fideles elegerint.
units.tr: 5. We have sent our letters concerning all these matters through Germany, Burgundy and Aquitaine, wishing the whole body of the faithful to know that we intend in no way to receive any other person to the seat of so great a government, except one whom the faithful have chosen with unanimous and harmonious assent, for the honour of the Empire, and for the quiet and unity of the Church.

units.la: 6. Post reditum verò Legatorum nostrorum, quæcunq; de negotiis Imperii & Ecclesiæ nobis attulerint, per majores Nuncios nostros fidelitati tuæ insinuabimus, & ex consilio discretionis tuæ universa tractabimus. Data in obsidione Cremæ, 16. Kal. Octobris.
units.tr: 6. After the return of our envoys, whatever they bring us concerning the affairs of the Empire and the Church, we will report to your loyalty through our greater messengers, and we will deal with the whole matter by the counsel of your discretion. Given at the siege of Crema, the 16th day before the Kalends of October.

units.la: FRIDERICI I. IMPER. AUG. EDICTUM
units.tr: The Edict of Frederick I, Emperor Augustus

units.la: De destruenda rebelli civitate.
units.tr: On the destruction of the rebellious city.

units.la: FRIDERICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator & semper-Augustus, dilecto suo Reimundo Gureensi Episcopo, gratiam suam & omne bonum. Dilectioni tuæ significare dignum duximus, quòd Cremam 6. Kal. Febr. divina nobis auxiliante dextera, devictam funditus destruximus, ita tamen, quòd habitatoribus suis, vitam tantùm supplicitér à nobis postulantibus, in persona propria pepercimus. Quod quia tibi gratum esse indubitanter scimus, mandamus tibi, quàm intimè rogantes, quatenus unà nobiscum omnipotenti Deo grates condignas agas, & ut is, qui salutem dat Regibus, hostium victoriam nobis tribuat, incessanter implores. Præterea te scire volumus, quòd in omnibus gravaminibus & adversitatibus tuis tibi, tanquam dilecto ac fideli nostro, condolemus, & in reditu nostro, vita comite, omnia mala tibi adversantia sedare intendimus. Data in triumpho Cremæ, 6. Kalend. Februarii.
units.tr: Frederick, by the grace of God Emperor of the Romans and ever-August, to his beloved Reimund, Bishop of Gurk, his grace and every blessing. We have thought it worth informing your Affection that Crema, conquered on 6 days before the Kalends of February, with the divine right hand assisting us, we have utterly destroyed; yet in such a way that we spared its inhabitants' lives, which they asked of us humbly and as suppliants, though we did not spare their persons. Since we know without doubt that this is pleasing to you, we charge you, earnestly entreating, that together with us you give fitting thanks to almighty God, and that you unceasingly implore him, who gives salvation to kings, to grant us victory over our enemies. Moreover, we want you to know that in all your troubles and adversities we sympathise with you as with our beloved and faithful servant, and that on our return, with life as our companion, we intend to calm all the evils that beset you. Given in the triumph of Crema, 6 days before the Kalends of February.

units.la: FRIDERICI I. IMPERAT. AUG. EDICTUM
units.tr: Edict of the Emperor Frederick I Augustus

units.la: De indictione Concilii Papiensis ad schisma Papale tollendum.
units.tr: On the summoning of the Council of Pavia to end the Papal schism.

units.la: FRIDERICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator & semper Augustus, Herimanno Brixinensi Episcopo salutem & omne bonum.
units.tr: Frederick, by the grace of God Emperor of the Romans and ever Augustus, to Hermann, Bishop of Brixen, greeting and every blessing.

units.la: 1. Quòd in passione sua Christus duobus gladiis contentus fuit, hoc in Romana Ecclesia & in Imperio credimus miræbili providentia declarasse, cùm per hæc duo rerum capita & principia totus mundus tam in divinis quàm in humanis ordinetur. Cumque unus Deus, unus Papa, unus Imperator sufficiat, & una Ecclesia Dei esse debeat, quod sine dolore dicere non possumus, duos Apostolicos in Romana Ecclesia habere videmur. Defuncto itaque Adriano Papa in Kal. Sept. Cardinales, qui uli-mnæ immobiles esse videbantur, quibus sancta & universalis firmissimè innitereture Ecclesia, non quæ Dei sunt sed sua quærentes, & unitatem Ecclesiæ scindentes, duos Pontifices elegerunt, & ambos consecraverunt. Pro tanta namque & tam perniciosa Ecclesiæ jactura, tota nimirum Italica Ecclesia conturbatur, & dissensionis schismate orto in capite, jam in inferiora membra defluxisset, & totum Ecclesiæ corpus deformasset, nisi nos consilio & auxilio Religiosorum virorum, qui spiritu Dei aguntur, tam impudicæ iniquitati justitiæ rigorem opposuissemus.
units.tr: 1. We believe that in his Passion Christ was content with two swords, and that in the Roman Church and in the Empire he declared this by a wonderful providence, since the whole world, in divine and in human affairs alike, is ordered through these two heads and principles. And since one God, one Pope and one Emperor suffice, and the Church of God ought to be one, which we cannot say without grief, we seem to have two apostolic men in the Roman Church. Accordingly, when Pope Hadrian died on the first of September, the cardinals, who seemed to be the immovable hinges on which the holy and universal Church rests most firmly, seeking not what is God's but their own, and splitting the unity of the Church, elected two pontiffs and consecrated both. For from so great and so ruinous a loss to the Church, the whole Italian Church is indeed thrown into confusion; and the schism, having arisen in the head, would already have flowed down into the lower members and disfigured the whole body of the Church, had we not opposed the rigour of justice to such shameless iniquity, by the counsel and help of religious men who are led by the Spirit of God.

units.la: 2. Ne itaque, in tantæ discordiæ universalis Ecclesia periclitari possit, Romanum Imperium, quod ad remedium tam perniciosi morbi divina Clementia provicit, universorum salutis debet sollicitè providere, & ne tanta mala in Ecclesia Dei præeminent, futuris casibus solerter obviare.
units.tr: 2. Therefore, lest the universal Church should be in danger from so great a discord, the Roman Empire, which divine clemency has provided as a remedy for so pernicious a disease, ought carefully to provide for the salvation of all, and skilfully to meet beforehand the future crises, lest such great evils should prevail in the Church of God.

units.la: 3. Coadunatis itaque, in unum omnibus Episcopis, tam Italicis quàm Teutonicis, caterisque; Principibus ac viris religiosis, qui zelum Dei & Ecclesiæ habere videbantur, quod facto opus esset diligenter investigavimus, ex decretis Romanorum Pontificum & statutis Ecclesiæ veraciter accipientes, quòd exorto schismate in Romana Ecclesia ex duorum Apostolicorum dissensione, ambos vocare, & secundum sententiam & consilium orthodoxorum litem decidere debeàmus.
units.tr: 3. Having therefore gathered together all the bishops, both Italian and German, and the other princes and religious men who seemed to have zeal for God and the Church, we diligently inquired what needed to be done, taking from the decrees of the Roman pontiffs and the statutes of the Church that, when a schism has arisen in the Roman Church from the dissension of two apostolic men, we ought to summon both and settle the dispute according to the judgement and counsel of the orthodox.

units.la: 4. Ex consilio itaque, omnium, qui aderant, Episcoporum, cæterorumque Principum, curiam solennem & generalem conventum omnium Ecclesiasticorum virorum, in octava Epiphaniæ, Papiæ celebrandam indiximus: ad quam ambos, qui se dicunt Romanos Pontifices, vocabimus, omnesque Episcopos Imperii nostri, & aliorum regnorum, Franciæ videlicet, Angliæ, Hispaniæ, atque Ungariæ, ut eorum in præsentia nostra justo declaretur examine, quis illorum regimen universalis Ecclesiæ de jure debeat obtinere.
units.tr: 4. Therefore, by the counsel of all the bishops and other princes who were present, we have appointed a solemn court and general assembly of all churchmen, to be held at Pavia in the octave of the Epiphany; to which we will summon both who call themselves Roman pontiffs, and all the bishops of our Empire and of the other kingdoms, namely of France, England, Spain and Hungary, so that in their presence it may be justly determined by examination which of them ought by right to hold the rule of the universal Church.

units.la: 5. Quia verò ad unitatem Ecclesiæ reformandam sapientia admodùm nobis necessaria est, ut ea nequaquam carere valeamus, dilectionem vestram attentissimè rogamus, & rogando commonemus, quatenus pro fidelitate Ecclesiæ & Imperii ad prædictam curiam omni occasione remota venias, ut in adventu tuo unitas & pax & tranquillitas Ecclesiæ reformetur. Interim autem prædictæ scissuræ in neutram partem assensum vestrum declines, nec tanquam justam & rationabilem aliquatenus recipias. Data Cremæ, x. Kalend. Novembris.
units.tr: 5. Since, indeed, wisdom is most necessary to us for reforming the unity of the Church, so that we may by no means be without it, we most earnestly ask your love, and by asking we admonish, that for the sake of the loyalty owed to the Church and the Empire you come to the aforesaid court with every obstacle removed, so that at your arrival the unity, peace and tranquillity of the Church may be restored. Meanwhile, do not lean your assent toward either side of the aforesaid division, nor in any way accept it as just and reasonable. Given at Cremona, on the tenth of the Kalends of November.

units.la: FRIDERICI. I. IMPERAT. AUG. MANDATUM
units.tr: FRIDERICI. I. IMPERAT. AUG. MANDATUM

units.la: AD PSEVDOPAPAM ET CARDINALES RO- MANOS, ut se sistant in Concilio Papiensi, ubi de justitia electionis novi Papæ cognoscatur.
units.tr: A MANDATE OF THE EMPEROR FREDERICK I AUGUSTUS, TO THE PSEUDO-POPE AND THE ROMAN CARDINALS, that they present themselves at the Council of Pavia, where the justice of the election of a new Pope is to be examined.

units.la: FRIDERICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator & semper Augustus, Rolando Cancellario, cæterisque Cardinalibus, qui eum elegerunt Romanum Pontificem, salutem & omne bonum.
units.tr: FREDERICK, by the grace of God Emperor of the Romans and ever Augustus, to Rolandus the Chancellor and the other Cardinals who elected him Roman Pontiff, greeting and every blessing.

units.la: 1. Quoniam divina præordinante Clementia, Romani Imperii gubernacula suscepimus, oportet ut in omnibus viis nostris ipsius legem custodiamus, cujus munere, cujus voluntate dignitatis nostræ apicem adepti sumus.
units.tr: 1. Since, by the ordaining providence of divine Clemency, we have taken up the government of the Roman Empire, it behooves us to keep its law in all our ways, by whose gift and whose will we have attained the summit of our dignity.

units.la: 2. In hoc itaque sacratissimo proposito constituti, cum omnibus Ecclesiis in Imperio nostro constitutis debeamus patrocinari, sacrosanctæ Romanæ Ecclesiæ tanto propensius debemus providere, quanto ipsius cura & defensio à divina providentia creditur nobis esse commissa specialius.
units.tr: 2. Established therefore in this most sacred purpose, although we ought to protect all the churches established in our Empire, we ought to provide all the more eagerly for the most holy Roman Church, inasmuch as its care and defence are believed to have been committed to us by divine providence in a more special way.

units.la: 3. Ea propter de discordia, quæ in substituendo Romanum Pontificem inter vos suborta est, plurimùm dolemus, timentes ne occasione hujus schismatis Ecclesia Christi sanguine redempta debeat dilacerari, præsertim cùm rebus Ecclesiæ foris titubare videatur, quoniam unitas ipsius scissura domestica interius dilaniatur.
units.tr: 3. Therefore we grieve greatly over the discord which has arisen among you in substituting a Roman Pontiff, fearing lest, on the occasion of this schism, the Church of Christ, redeemed by the blood of Christ, should be torn apart, especially since the affairs of the Church appear to totter abroad, while its unity is rent apart within by domestic division.

units.la: 4. Ut autem huic pesti competens & Deo gratum exhibeamus remedium, Religiosorum virorum consilio generalem curiam & conventum, in octava Epiphaniæ, Papiæ indiximus celebrandam. Ad quam evocavimus totius Imperii nostri & aliorum regnorum, scilicet Angliæ, Franciæ, Ungariæ, Daciæ, Archiepiscopos, Episcopos, Abbates, & viros religiosos ac Deum timentes, quatenus remoto omni seculari judicio hoc tam magnum Ecclesiæ negocium Ecclesiasticarum tantùm personarum sententia itasopiatur, ut & Deo debitus exinde honor deferatur, & Ecclesia Romana suâ integritate & justitiâ non possit à quoquam privari; vel status Urbis, quæ caput Imperii nostri est, inquietari.
units.tr: 4. In order, however, to apply a fitting remedy to this plague, one that is pleasing to God, we have, on the advice of religious men, appointed a general court and assembly to be held at Pavia in the octave of the Epiphany. To it we have summoned the archbishops, bishops, abbots, and religious and God-fearing men of our whole Empire and of the other kingdoms, namely England, France, Hungary and Denmark, so that, with all secular judgment set aside, this so great affair of the Church may be settled by the opinion of ecclesiastical persons alone, that due honour may thereby be rendered to God, and that the Roman Church may not be deprived of its integrity and justice by anyone, nor the state of the City, which is the capital of our Empire, be disturbed.

units.la: 5. Proinde eruditioni vestræ mandamus, & ex parte Dei omnipotentis & totius Ecclesiæ Catholicæ præcipimus, ut ad eandem curiam sive conventum veniatis, Ecclesiasticarum personarum sententiam audituri & recepturi. Testis enim nobis est Deus, quia in hac curia nec amore nec odio alicujus personæ quicquam aliud quærimus, quàm honorem Dei & Ecclesiæ suæ unitatem.
units.tr: 5. Accordingly we command your learning, and on behalf of Almighty God and of the whole Catholic Church we order, that you come to the same court or assembly, to hear and receive the judgment of the ecclesiastical persons. For God is our witness that in this court we seek nothing else, out of love or hatred for any person, than the honour of God and the unity of his Church.

units.la: 6. Quòd si ad tam celebrem Ecclesiæ conventum examinationis causa venire volueritis, Carissimi Principes nostri & Ecclesiæ Catholicæ, Hermannus Verdensis, Daniel Pragensis, patres & Episcopi venerabiles, quos de Palatio nostro ad vos transmisimus, unà cum Comite Palatino, consanguineo nostro, aliisque Legatis nostris, securum vobis conductum præstabunt.
units.tr: 6. But if you are willing to come to so famous an assembly of the Church for the sake of examination, our dearest Princes and of the Catholic Church, Hermann of Verden, Daniel of Prague, venerable fathers and bishops, whom we have sent to you from our Palace, together with the Count Palatine, our kinsman, and our other Legates, will provide you with a safe conduct.

units.la: 7. Si verò justitiam Dei & Ecclesiæ in tam solenni conventu recipere nolueritis, videat Deus & judicet. Nos autem ipsius favente gratia, qui dat salutem Regibus, justitiam Dei, quæ nullum magis quàm Imperatorem Romanum decet, prosequemur.
units.tr: 7. But if you are unwilling to receive the justice of God and of the Church in so solemn an assembly, let God see and judge. We, however, by the favour of his grace, who gives salvation to kings, will pursue the justice of God, which becomes no one more than the Roman Emperor.

units.la: FRIDERICI. I. IMPER. AUG. ET CONCILII GENERALIS PAPIENSIS EDICTA
units.tr: Edicts of Frederick I, Emperor Augustus, and of the General Council of Pavia

units.la: Super depositione Pseudopapæ, & electione novi Papæ.
units.tr: On the deposition of the false pope, and the election of a new pope.

units.la: FRIDERICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator & semper Augustus, dilectissimo suo Eberhardo venerabili Saltzburgensi Archiepiscopo, & Suffraganeis ejus, Alberto Frisingensi Episcopo, Hartmanno Brixinensi, & Romano Gurcensi, totiúsque Provinciæ Saltzburgensi, gratiam suam & omne bonum.
units.tr: Frederick, by the grace of God Emperor of the Romans and always Augustus, to his most beloved Eberhard, venerable Archbishop of Salzburg, and to his suffragans, Albert, Bishop of Freising, Hartmann of Brixen, and Roman of Gurk, and to the whole province of Salzburg, his grace and every blessing.

units.la: 1. Si sacro Concilio Papiæ interfuisseris, omnia, quæ ibidem gesta vel in Romana Ecclesia facta sunt, oculata fide cognoscere poteritis. Ne autem ab his, qui pravis delationibus & mendaciis jam ferè totum orbem respersèrunt, veritas possit obnubilari, vel vestra sinceritas trahi in contrarium, quantò breviùs possumus, seriem totius rei, sine aliqua falsitatis commixtione, mera veritate vobis significare dignum duximus.
units.tr: 1. If you had been present at the holy Council of Pavia, you could have learned with your own eyes everything that was done there and in the Roman Church. So that the truth may not be clouded by those who have now almost filled the whole world with false accusations and lies, or your sincerity be drawn to the opposite side, we have thought it right to set out for you, as briefly as we can, the sequence of the whole affair, with no admixture of falsehood, but pure truth.

units.la: 2. Luce clarius constat, quòd Papa Adriano adhuc vivente, Rolandus Cancellarius & quidam Cardinales, non attendentes illud Dominicum; Sit sermo vester, est est, non non, conspiratione facta cum Vilhelmo Siculo, prius ab eis excommunicato, & cum cæteris hostibus Imperii, Mediolanensibus, Brixiensibus, Placentinis, ne forte per mortem Papæ Adriani tam iniqua factio evanesceret, juramen-
units.tr: 2. It is as clear as daylight that while Pope Adrian was still alive, Roland the Chancellor and certain cardinals, not heeding the Lord's saying, "Let your speech be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay" [Matt. 5:37], conspired with William of Sicily, whom they had previously excommunicated, and with the other enemies of the Empire, the Milanese, the Brescians and the Piacentines, so that if Pope Adrian died, so wicked a faction would not vanish. They swore

units.la: ménalem vicem [illegible, ~4 letters] consti ınxerunt, ut defuncto Papa nullus alius ei substitueretur, nisi qui in ea-confirmatione cum eis convenisset. Hac de causa duodecimo die post electionem Domini Victoris, Papæ, collecti in Sede beati Petri, jam dicti conspiratores egressi ab Urbe ad Civitatem Neronianam venerunt, aquarum viventium, se contulerunt, & idolum sibi Rolandum Cancellarium dicentes, hunc esse Simonem Petrum, qui Apostolicæ dignitatis apicem tam nefaria præsumebat. Quod hæc conspiratio facta fuerit, & ille jam dictus Rolandus per ... non est fictitium, sed religiosus vir ab illo, qui facit manifesta consilia cordis, ... declaratum.
units.tr: a mutual oath and agreed that, when the Pope died, no one else should be set in his place unless he had agreed with them in that confirmation. For this reason, on the twelfth day after the election of Lord Victor as Pope, the aforesaid conspirators, gathered in the See of St Peter, left the City and went to the Neronian city, to the place called Aquae Viventes. There they made an idol of Roland the Chancellor, calling this man Simon Peter, who so wickedly presumed to seize the summit of apostolic dignity. That this conspiracy was formed, and that the aforesaid Roland ... is not fiction, but has been declared by a religious man, one from whom the Lord, who reveals the counsels of the heart, ...

units.la: 3. Dum hæc Romæ agerentur, & nos, quid super tanto scismate agendum esset, vitos religiosos Episcopos videlicet & Episcopos consuluraremus, superveneruut quasi nisi à Deo, Tarentasiensis episcopus, Abbas Claravallensis, Abbas Moremundensis, & alii Abbates numero decem, Mediolanensibus. Qui recepto à nobis verbo, dum Mediolanum pro investigatione ... redirent, acceperunt ab eis tale responsum: Domini Patres, nos tenemur strictius Domino Papæ & Cardinalibus, quòd non debeamus redire ad gratiam Imperatoris sine voluntate, & ipsi e contra sine nostra voluntate nullam pacem facere possunt. Responderunt ... Vos de cetero non tenemini Domino Papæ, quia mortuus est. Et illi statim subjunxerunt: Papa, nos ideò non sumus absoluti; quia nihilominus tenemur Cardinalibus, & ipsi retinuntur. Hæc prædicti Patres Abbates in responsis à Mediolanensibus testificati sunt coram multis viris. Præterea, multa experimenta factæ conspirationis per literas in via deprehensas accepit, sicut nuncius iste plenius vidit & audivit.
units.tr: 3. While these things were being done at Rome, and we were taking counsel about what should be done concerning so great a schism, namely with the religious bishops and the bishops, there came, as if sent by God, the Bishop of Tarentaise, the Abbot of Clairvaux, the Abbot of Moremund, and ten other abbots, to the Milanese. When they had received our word, and were returning to Milan for the investigation of ..., they received from them this answer: "Lord Fathers, we are bound more strictly to the Lord Pope and the cardinals, so that we ought not to return to the Emperor's favour without their consent; and they, on the other hand, cannot make peace without our consent." They replied: "You are no longer bound to the Lord Pope, because he is dead." And they at once added: "Pope, we are not therefore released, because we are nonetheless bound to the cardinals, and they are held back." These aforesaid Fathers and Abbots testified to these answers from the Milanese before many men. Moreover, the messenger saw and heard more fully that many proofs of the conspiracy were received through letters intercepted on the way.

units.la: 4. Sanc ex consilio Orthodoxorum, sicut alia vice meminimus vobis mandasse, generalem conventum Religiosorum Papæ indiximus, ad quem ambos, qui se dixerunt Romanos Pontifices, non ad concilium sæculare, sicut ora mendacii afferunt, sed ad examen Ecclesiæ per duos venerabiles Episcopos Verdensem videlicet & Pragensem, convocavimus. Alter verò, quòd prius eorum haberet conscientiam, Dominus Victor videlicet, judicio Ecclesiæ ultrò se obtulit: altero, videlicet Rolando, contumaciter renitente, & dicente, quia cum ipse omnes deberet judicare, ipse à nullo vellet judicari.
units.tr: 4. Indeed, on the counsel of the orthodox, as we mentioned to you on another occasion, we summoned a general assembly of the religious for the Pope, and to it we summoned both men who called themselves Roman pontiffs, not to a secular council, as the mouths of lies assert, but to the examination of the Church, through two venerable bishops, namely the Bishop of Verden and the Bishop of Prague. The one, Lord Victor, since he had the better conscience of the two, offered himself of his own accord to the judgment of the Church; the other, namely Roland, obstinately resisted, saying that since he ought to judge everyone, he himself would be judged by no one.

units.la: 5. Habito itaque venerabili Concilio, in quo Patriarcha Aquileiensis, & multi Archiepiscopi episcopi religiosi convenerant, per octo continuos dies maxima gravitate, diligentissima examinatione, remota omni laica persona, tractatum est, quis ex duobus summi Pontificatus apicem de jure teneret obtinere.
units.tr: 5. Therefore, a venerable council having been convened, in which the Patriarch of Aquileia and many archbishops, bishops and religious had gathered, the question of which of the two should rightly hold the summit of the supreme pontificate was discussed for eight continuous days with the greatest seriousness and the most diligent examination, every lay person having been removed.

units.la: 6. Post longam itaque deliberationem, quia illa nefandissima conspiratio, Deo & Ecclesiæ admonitus, manifestis indicus non solum probata, verùm in facie totius Ecclesiæ coram positæ revelata in Domino Victore nihil reprehensibile inventum est, nisi quod pauciores numero Cardinales nò à conspiratione illa exortes, cum pro bono pacis inter Regnum & Sacerdotium concilio, electionem & invocata S. Spiritu, Ecclesia Dei Rolandum Cancellarium, conspiratorem & schismaticum discordias & iras & perjuria bona esse evangelizantem, condemnavit, & Dominum Victorem in patrem spiritalem & universalem Pontificem confirmavit. Quæ nos Ecclesia duce secuti approbamus, & universalis Ecclesiæ parte & rectore, cooperante divina Clementia, fore denunciamus.
units.tr: 6. Therefore, after long deliberation, since that most abominable conspiracy, warned by God and the Church, was not only proved by plain indications but revealed before the face of the whole Church, and since nothing blameworthy was found in Lord Victor, except that a few cardinals, who were not free of that conspiracy, had been [wrongly] chosen for the sake of the peace between the kingdom and the priesthood, the Church of God, guided by the Holy Spirit invoked in the election, condemned Roland the Chancellor, conspirator and schismatic, who preached that discords, wrath and perjuries are good, and confirmed Lord Victor as spiritual father and universal Pontiff. Following the Church as our leader, we approve these things, and we declare that, with the cooperation of divine clemency, they will be the part and rule of the universal Church.

units.la: 7. Hoc itaque factum divinis suffultum præludiis, & in Apostolica stabilitate supra petram, ... videlicet, firmiter fundatum, à vestra beatitudine, pro pace totius Ecclesiæ & salute Imperii approbari, & ab omni Ecclesia vestræ sanctitati commissa tenere & conservari rogamus & præcipimus. Data Papiæ, xv. Kalend. Martii.
units.tr: 7. Therefore, this deed, supported by divine preludes and firmly founded on the apostolic stability upon the rock, ..., we ask and command that it be approved by your blessedness for the peace of the whole Church and the safety of the Empire, and that it be held and preserved by every Church committed to your holiness. Given at Pavia, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of March.

units.la: DICTUM GENERALE A SYNODO PRÆSIDENTIBUS PER PARTES MUNDI DIRECTUM.
units.tr: General Decree Sent Through the Regions of the World by the Presidents of the Synod.

units.la: Sedis Apostolicæ turbatio Christianorum animos admodum saucia-vit, nos, qui ad resecanda mata & pacem Ecclesiæ reformandam, Papiæ fuimus congregati, qualitate causæ modumque; cœri Concilii dispensationem universitati veritatis plenarie duximus intimandum: quatenus sententia mera veritate monstrata auditorum animi fallitatem, quam forte conceperant, expellant, & amodò per scripta schismatica non seducantur.
units.tr: The disturbance of the Apostolic See has grievously wounded the hearts of Christians. We, who gathered at Pavia to cut away these evils and to restore the peace of the Church, have judged it right to make fully known to the whole world the nature of the case and the manner of the council's proceedings, so that, with the plain truth set before them, the hearers may drive out whatever falsehood they may have conceived, and no longer be led astray by schismatic writings.

units.la: 1. Cum igitur Orthodoxorum Papiæ congregatorum Universitas in nomine Domini conseper * vii. dies continuos, omni remoto seculari judicio, legitimè & canonicè agitata, ac dilecta, sufficienter & canonice in conspectu Concilii per testes idoneos est comprobatum, Papa Victorem, & nullum alium, in basilica beati Petri à sanctori parte Cardinalium, petitio, & consensu ac desiderio Cleri fuisse electus & solenniter innuntiatum: præsente & non ... Rolando quondam Cancellario, in cathedra B. Petri fuerit collocatus: & quod ibi cum ... & Clero Romano, Te Deum laudamus, gloriose decantatu: & inde ad Palatium cum bandis ... pulsibus insignibus est deductus: & Clerus & populus secundum consuetudinem interrogatum, si placeret? tribus vicibus clara voce respondit, Placet.
units.tr: 1. Therefore, since the assembly of the orthodox gathered at Pavia, in the name of the Lord, for seven continuous days, with all secular judgment set aside, was legitimately and canonically conducted, and it has been sufficiently and canonically proved before the council by suitable witnesses that Pope Victor, and no other, was elected in the basilica of St Peter by the greater part of the Cardinals, at the request, with the consent and desire of the clergy, and was solemnly proclaimed; that, with ... Roland, formerly chancellor, being present and not ..., he was placed in the chair of St Peter; and that there, with ... and the Roman clergy, they sang the Te Deum laudamus in glorious chorus; and thence he was led to the Palace with banners ... and signs; and the clergy and people, according to custom, were asked whether it pleased them, and three times answered in a clear voice, "Placet" ("It pleases us").

units.la: 2. Probatum est etiam, quod Rolandus xii. die post Domini Victoris promotionem ab Urbe apud Civitatem, in qua Nero Imperator quondam ab Urbe profugus latitavit, primò est im-... Probatum est, quòd in secundo die post promotionem Domini Victoris, Rolandus interRectoribus & Clero Romano ac Clericis de sua Cardinalia, si Domino Victori esset obedi-, expresse confessus est, se nunquam fuisse immantatum, & expressè dixit; Hæc & obedire et, quem im-
units.tr: 2. It has also been proved that Roland, on the twelfth day after the promotion of Lord Victor, fled from the City to the town in which the Emperor Nero once hid after fleeing from the City ... It has been proved that on the second day after the promotion of Lord Victor, Roland, in the presence of the rectors, the Roman clergy and the clerics of his own cardinalate, expressly confessed that he had never been ..., and he expressly said: "We are ready to obey him whom you see to be spotless."

units.la: * leg. viii. quem immaculatum esse videtis. Super his capitulis fuerunt testes, & sub stola tactis sacrosanctis Evangeliis juraverunt:
units.tr: * Read "viii." Whom you see to be spotless. Witnesses to these chapters were present, and, with hands on the holy Gospels beneath the stole, they swore:

units.la: Dominus Petrus Christianus, Decanus Basilicæ beati Petri, & in persona sua, & omnium fratrum suorum.
units.tr: Lord Peter Christian, Dean of the basilica of St Peter, both in his own person and in the name of all his brothers.

units.la: Juraverunt etiam venerabiles Archipresbyteri & Rectores Cleri Romani: Blasius & Manerius Presbyteri, Joannes Presbyter Genitilis, Aimeradus Archipresbyter, Berardus Archipresbyter, Joannes Archipresbyter, Benedictus Diaconus, Magister Ptolemaeus Archipresbyter, Magister Gerardus, & Nicolaus, & alii honesti Clerici Romani.
units.tr: The venerable archpriests and rectors of the Roman clergy also swore: Blasius and Manerius, presbyters; John, presbyter of Genitilis; Aimeradus, archpriest; Berardus, archpriest; John, archpriest; Benedictus, deacon; Master Ptolemaeus, archpriest; Master Gerardus, and Nicolaus, and other honourable Roman clerics.

units.la: Præterea Petrus Illustris Urbis Præfectus, Stephanus de Thebaldo, Stephanus Normannus, Gimundus de domo Petri Leonis, Joannes de Stephano, & alii Principes & Nobiles Romani, qui ad vocationem serenissimi Imperatoris venerant, in conspectu Concilii super jam dictis capitulis, ex maxima parte similiter perhibuerunt, & jurare voluerunt. Sed nos, quia religiosorum Presbyterorum testimonium sufficiens & abundantissimum habebamus, duximus laicis in hac parte praetermittendum.
units.tr: Moreover, Peter, Illustrious Prefect of the City; Stephen de Thebaldo; Stephen the Norman; Gimundus of the house of Peter Leo; John de Stephano; and other Roman princes and nobles, who had come at the summons of the most serene Emperor, in the presence of the council gave similar testimony on the aforesaid chapters for the most part, and were willing to swear. But since we had the testimony of the religious presbyters as sufficient and most abundant, we judged it right to set the laymen aside in this matter.

units.la: 4. Deinde venerabiles Episcopi, Hermannus Verdensis, Daniel Pragensis, & Otto Comes, & Magister Heribertus Præpositus, quos Dominus Imperator ex concilio xxii. Episcopi & Cistercienses & Clairavallensis Abbatum, aliorumque religiosorum tunc præsentium, Romam legaverat, ut partes ante Concilii præsentiam Papam evocarent, in conspectu Concilii testimonium perhibuerunt, quod Rolandum Cancellarium & partem ejus trinis edictis per intervalla publice & solenniter, ad præsentiam Ecclesiæ Papæ congregandæ, remoto omni seculari judicio, vocarent, quod Rolandus Cancellarius & sui Cardinales viva voce & ore proprio judicium vel examen Ecclesiæ se nolle recipere manifeste dixerunt. Vidimus etiam scripta Henrici Pisani Cardinalis ad minimum Imperatorem directa, in quibus expresse continebatur, quod nullum vellent Ecclesiæ judicium vel examen. Super hæc omnia idem Henricus, & Otto Cardinalis sancti Nicolai de Tulliano, qui tempore Concilii & ante apud Januam morabantur; & Joannes Anagnus Cardinalis & Joannes Pioznus, sanctæ Romanæ Ecclesiæ Subdiaconi, qui tunc apud Placentiam erant, dies à Concilio sunt expectati, & per literas & nuncios Concilii sunt vocati, & contemptim vocati.
units.tr: 4. Then the venerable bishops Hermann of Verden, Daniel of Prague, and Count Otto, and Master Heribert, provost, whom the Lord Emperor had sent to Rome from the council of twenty-two bishops, and of the Cistercian and Clairvaux abbots and other religious then present, so that they might summon the parties to appear before the Pope in the presence of the council, gave testimony in the presence of the council that they had summoned Roland the Chancellor and his party by three edicts, given at intervals, publicly and solemnly, to appear before the assembly of the Church with the Pope, all secular judgment set aside; and that Roland the Chancellor and his cardinals plainly said, by word of mouth, that they were unwilling to accept the judgment or examination of the Church. We have also seen letters of Cardinal Henry of Pisa addressed to the Emperor, in which it was expressly stated that they wished for no judgment or examination of the Church. Over all these matters, the same Henry, and Cardinal Otto of St Nicholas in Tullianum, who stayed at Genoa during and before the council, and John of Anagni, Cardinal, and John Pioznus, subdeacons of the holy Roman Church, who were then at Piacenza, were awaited for days after the council, and were summoned by letters and messengers of the council; and when summoned, they treated the summons with contempt.

units.la: 5. Ex his igitur omnibus sufficienter instructi, & veritate hinc inde plenarie declarata, reverendo Concilio, ut electio Domini Victoris, qui tanquam agnus mansuetus & innocens Ecclesiæ judicium humiliter suscepturus, approbaretur & confirmaretur, & electio Rolandi pro nihil cassaretur. Et factum est ita. Electione itaque Domini Victoris, remoto omni seculari judicio, Spiritus gratia invocata, confirmata atque recepta, Christianissimus Imperator, post omnes & post omnem Clerum ultimus, consilio & petitione Concilii electionem Domini Victoris probavit & approbavit: & post eum omnes Principes, & innumerabilis hominum multitudo, quae præsens erat, tribus vicibus interrogata, si eis placeret, respondit cum gaudio magna voce, Placet.
units.tr: 5. Having therefore been sufficiently informed by all these things, and the truth having been fully declared on all sides, the council decided that the election of Lord Victor, who, like a gentle and innocent lamb, would humbly submit to the judgment of the Church, should be approved and confirmed, and that the election of Roland should be annulled as void. And so it was done. The election of Lord Victor, with all secular judgment set aside and the grace of the Spirit invoked, was confirmed and received. The most Christian Emperor, last of all after all the bishops and all the clergy, at the advice and request of the council, approved and ratified the election of Lord Victor; and after him all the princes and the countless multitude of men who were present, asked three times whether it pleased them, answered with joy in a loud voice: "Placet" ("It pleases us").

units.la: 6. Sequenti die proxima, id est prima sexta feria Quadragesimæ, Dominus Victor cum processione ab Ecclesia sancti Salvatoris extra civitatem, in qua fuerat ejus hospitium, ad Catholicam religiosè deductus est. Ibi religiosissimus Imperator ante januas Ecclesiæ cum suis pedibus de equo strepam humiliter tenuit, & apprehensum per manum usque ad altare conduxit, des ejus est osculatus: & nos omnes Patriarchæ, Archiepiscopi, Episcopi, & Abbates, & omnes Cipes cum universa ultitudine, quæ præsens erat, pedes Apostolicos sumus osculati.
units.tr: 6. On the following day, that is, the first Friday of Lent, Lord Victor was led in solemn procession from the church of the Holy Saviour outside the city, where he had his lodging, to the Cathedral. There the most devout Emperor, before the doors of the church, dismounted from his horse and humbly held the stirrup with his own hands; then, taking Victor by the hand, he led him up to the altar and kissed his feet. And we all, patriarchs, archbishops, bishops and abbots, and all the princes with the whole multitude present, kissed the apostolic feet.

units.la: 7. Proxima autem die sequenti, id est Sabbato, habito generali Concilio, Dominus nos cum illo, Rolandum Cancellarium (schismaticum, & ejus principales fautores accensos anathematizavimus, & tradidimus eum Satanae in interitum carnis, ut spiritus salvus sit in die Domini.
units.tr: 7. On the next day, that is, Saturday, a general council was held, and we, together with him, anathematized Roland the Chancellor (the schismatic) and his principal ardent supporters, and handed him over to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, so that the spirit may be saved on the day of the Lord.

units.la: 8. Illud etiam discretionis veritas prudentiam volumus non latere, manifeste est, quod Rolandus Cancellarius, & ejus sequaces quidam Cardinales, vivente adhuc Papa Alexandro, no conjuraverunt. Fuit autem tenor conjurationis: quod si eis viventibus Papam Alexandrum contingeret, Cardinalem unum de illis eligerent, qui in eadem conjuratione esset astrictus.
units.tr: 8. We also wish that the truth of discernment and prudence not be hidden: it is clear that Roland the Chancellor and certain of his cardinal followers conspired while Pope Alexander was still alive. The tenor of the conspiracy was this: that if Pope Alexander should die while they were alive, they would elect as pope one cardinal from among themselves who was bound by the same conspiracy.

units.la: 9. De cætero ex parte Dei omnipotentis, & beatorum Apostolorum Petri & Pauli, & omnium sanctorum & virorum Orthodoxorum, qui divino intuitu ad reticendam schismatis contritionem venerunt, universitatem vestram humiliter implorainus & monemus in Christo, ut ea, quæ Ecclesiæ Dei pacem conturbata, ad honorem Creatoris & sponsæ suæ, matris vestræ, sacrosanctæ Romanæ Ecclesiæ tranquillitatem, & ad salutem omnium Christianorum fideliter ordinavit, vos omnes dubios & gravitate removeat, ut frequentes sine ulla dubitatione reneatis: orantes, ut redemptor noster Christus, vestalem Pontificem & Papam nostrum Victorem, de cujus sanctitate & religione omnes gaudeamus. tempora longa conservet, & praestet ei omnimodam tranquillitatem & pacem, ita quòd per Deus omnipotens honoretur, & Ecclesia Romana, omnisque Christiana religio gratum Domini incrementum. Ut autem omnis actio plenius legentibus elucescat, dignum duximus, ut omnium nostrum consensus & nomina subscribantur. Ego Peregrinus Aquileiensis Archiepiscopus cum Suffraganeis meis interfui & consensi. Ego Arnaldus Archiepiscopus Moguntinus cum xiv. Suffraganeis interfui & consensi. Ego Articus Bremensis Archiepiscopus cum meis Suffraganeis consensi. Ego Hellinus Treverensis Archiepiscopus cum meis Suffraganeis consensi. Ego Reinaldus Coloniensis Archiepiscopus cum meis Suffraganeis consensi. Ego Wickmannus Magdeburgensis Archiepiscopus cum meis Suffraganeis consensi. N. Bizuntinus Archiepiscopus per Legatum & Episcopum Basiliensem consensit. N. Arelatensis Archiepiscopus consensit. E. Lugdunensis Archiepiscopus cum suis Suffraganeis consensit. N. Viennensis Archiepiscopus cum suis Suffraganeis consensit. Henricus Rex Anglorum per litteras & Legatos suos consensit. Ludislaus Rex Boëmorum consensit. Waldemarus Rex Danorum consensit. Guido Electus Ravennas Archiepiscopus consensit. N. Episcopus Firminus consensit. N. Episcopus Ferentinus consensit. N. Episcopus Mantuanus consensit. N. Episcopus Pergamensis consensit. N. Episcopus Faventinus consensit.
units.tr: 9. For the rest, in the name of almighty God, and of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul, and of all the saints and orthodox men who came out of divine zeal to put an end to the contrition of the schism, we humbly implore and admonish you all in Christ: that you remove all doubts and scruples from the matters which he has faithfully ordained for the disturbed peace of God's Church, for the honour of the Creator and of his spouse, your mother the holy Roman Church, for her tranquillity, and for the salvation of all Christians, and that you hold them frequently and without any doubt. We pray that our redeemer Christ may preserve our Pontiff and Pope Victor, of whose holiness and religion we all rejoice, for many years, and grant him complete tranquillity and peace, so that through him Almighty God may be honoured, and the Roman Church and all Christian religion may increase in the favour of the Lord. That the whole proceeding may be clearer to the readers, we have thought it fitting that the consent and names of all of us be subscribed. I, Peregrinus, Archbishop of Aquileia, was present with my suffragans and consented. I, Arnold, Archbishop of Mainz, was present with my fourteen suffragans and consented. I, Articus, Archbishop of Bremen, consented with my suffragans. I, Hellinus, Archbishop of Trier, consented with my suffragans. I, Reinald, Archbishop of Cologne, consented with my suffragans. I, Wichmann, Archbishop of Magdeburg, consented with my suffragans. N., Archbishop of Besançon, consented through a legate and the Bishop of Basel. N., Archbishop of Arles, consented. E., Archbishop of Lyon, consented with his suffragans. N., Archbishop of Vienne, consented with his suffragans. Henry, King of the English, consented through his letters and legates. Ladislaus, King of the Bohemians, consented. Waldemar, King of the Danes, consented. Guido, elect of Ravenna, Archbishop, consented. N., Bishop of Fermo, consented. N., Bishop of Ferentino, consented. N., Bishop of Mantua, consented. N., Bishop of Pergamo, consented. N., Bishop of Faenza, consented.

units.la: Abbatum vero & Archipresbyterorum multitudo innumerabilis multorumRegnorum interfuit & consensit.
units.tr: A countless multitude of abbots and archpriests from many kingdoms was present and consented.

units.la: Longobardorum innumerabilis multitudo interfuit & consensit.
units.tr: A countless multitude of Lombards was present and consented.

units.la: Universi fere Principes Romani Imperii, tam Teutonici quàm Italici, tam in Urbe quàm extra Urbem, interfuerunt, & assensum cum ingenti desiderio praebuerunt.
units.tr: Almost all the princes of the Roman Empire, both Teutonic and Italian, both in the City and outside the City, were present and gave their assent with great eagerness.

units.la: FRIDERICI I. IMPER. AUG. MANDATA ET RESCRIPTA.
units.tr: Frederick I, Emperor Augustus: Mandates and Rescripts.

units.la: I. De expeditione Italica adversus Alexandri Papae fautores Imperio Teutonico rebellantes; & de receptione Papae Victoris per Imperatorem confirmati.
units.tr: I. Concerning the Italian expedition against the adherents of Pope Alexander, who rebel against the Teutonic Empire; and concerning the reception of Pope Victor, confirmed by the Emperor.

units.la: FRIDERICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator & Semper-Augustus, dilecto & fideli suo Pilignio Venerabili Aquileiensi Patriarchae, gratiam suam & omne bonum.
units.tr: Frederick, by the grace of God Emperor of the Romans and Ever-August, to his beloved and faithful Pilgrim, the venerable Patriarch of Aquileia, greeting, his grace and every good.

units.la: Litteras a tua Dilectione transmissas accepimus, quarum tenore dispecto, tuae devotionis desiderio satisfacientes, de statu nostro tibi rescribimus & eventu, ut aliter, quam res acciderit, apud te divulgatum fuit, veritatem tu ipse cognoscas & referas.
units.tr: We have received the letter sent by your Affection. Having considered its contents, and wishing to satisfy your devotion, we write back to you about our condition and the outcome, so that you may learn and report the truth yourself, since it has been made known to you otherwise than the matter actually turned out.

units.la: Sumus itaque per gratiam Dei in bono statu, quia salus, & vita, & prosperitas nos & nostra cum comitantur. Quia vero secundum varium eventum belli, diversa diversa referunt, hanc veritatem accipias; Mediolanenses castrum quoddam, nomine Sarkanum, situm juxta Cumas, fortitudine oppederunt, & nos fideles nostros, qui in castro erant, liberare volentes, congregata Longobardorum infinita, ad locum accessimus, eosque, qui nostros obsederunt, ex omni parte dimus, ita quod nullatenus manus nostras evadere poterant, nisi forte ex desperatione, vel ex portis, per nos & per medium exercitum nostrum impetum facerent, & transire fugientes tentarent; & ita contigit. Mane enim in vigilia B. Laurentii, ipsi armati p medios nostros irruperunt, ... Quibus nos cum Teutonicis nostris ducis, adjunctis & aliquibus Longobardis, audacter & viriliter resistentes obviam venimus, parte multi corruentes interierunt. Praeterea vexillum eorum, quod in curru superbe erexerat, ... decimus & destruximus, ibique plus quam xxx. eorum milites, qui ad custodiam solius vexilli fuerant, truncavimus, ipsosque p Dei adjutorii viribus nostris in fugam convertimus, & ad castra redere copulimus, capiuntque cum honore & victoria tenuimus, quavis Longobardi innumerabiles a fuga recessissent, quamvis etiam interfectis aliquibus de nostris magnum damnum recepissemus; ... tanta damna suorum acceperunt, quod nos damna nostra, respectu illorum, nulla reparavimus.
units.tr: By the grace of God we are therefore in good condition, since health, life and prosperity accompany us and ours. Because, however, the outcome of the war varies and reports differ, receive this truth. The Milanese besieged a certain fortress, called Sarkanum, situated near Cumae, in strength. Wishing to free our loyal men who were in the fortress, we gathered an immense force of Lombards, came to the place, and surrounded on every side those who were besieging ours, so that they could in no way escape our hands, except perhaps by desperation, when they made an assault through the gates and through the middle of our army, trying to flee past us. And so it happened. For early on the vigil of St Lawrence, they rushed armed through the midst of our men... We, with our Teutonic men of the duke, joined by some Lombards, resisted boldly and manfully and came to meet them; many fell and died. Moreover, their standard, which they had proudly raised on a chariot, ... we took down and destroyed; there we cut down more than thirty of their soldiers who had been guarding the standard alone, and by the strength of God's help we turned the rest to flight and brought our men back to the camp, and we held them captive with honour and victory, though countless Lombards had escaped by flight, and although we had suffered considerable loss among our own when some were killed; ... they suffered such losses of their own, compared with which we made good none of our losses.

units.la: Corpora suorum occisorum ipsi recolligerent, lxxv. currus ad civitatem Mediolanensium transferret, non aliquis, in quo tres vel quatuor mortui non jacerent. Sic hostibus fugatis, nos ad Cumanam civitatem captivis reversi sumus. Qui aliter de nobis praedicat, scias non esse Evangelium, quod evangelizat.
units.tr: Their own men gathered up the bodies of their dead, and seventy-five carts carried them to the city of the Milanese; there was not one cart in which three or four dead did not lie. Thus, with the enemy put to flight, we returned to the city of Como with captives. Whoever preaches otherwise about us, know that it is not the Gospel that he preaches.

units.la: Quicunque etiam sta u Reverendissimi Papae Victoris minorari & attenuari praedicant, scias omnino quia jam multa Regna Hispaniae, Ungariae, Daciae, Boëmiae, Comes quoque Barholi, & Comes cum tota Provincia & Burgundia, ei obediunt, & de die in diem dilatatur & crescit.
units.tr: Moreover, whoever preaches that the authority of the most reverend Pope Victor is diminished and weakened, know altogether that many kingdoms of Spain, Hungary, Dacia and Bohemia already obey him, and so does the Count of Barcelona, and the Count with the whole Province and Burgundy; and he grows and is extended from day to day.

units.la: Merito debet tua Dilectio, quos Principes Alemanniae expeditione nostra, pmiserunt & jurave-runt, omnatu egarsiorum & variorum communi consilio posituerunt, solis civibus & armis coeteri in ipsa expeditione. Unde qua, licut persona tua grata nobis est, ita & necessaria, mandamus Dilectioni tuae & fidei tuam.
units.tr: Your Affection rightly ought to ... those princes of Germany who promised and swore to our expedition, and who by the common counsel of the wicked and the various ... set themselves against it, while the rest joined this expedition with citizens and arms alone. Wherefore, since your person is as pleasing to us as it is necessary, we command your Affection and your faithfulness.

units.la: b. i.e. cum toto Regno Arelatensi.
units.tr: b. That is, with the whole Kingdom of Arles.

units.la: c. gaarzionum tuam monemus,ut de honore Imperii nostri,sicut alii Principes & fideles nostri,cogites [illegible, ~3 letters] xiv.die post Pascha cum honesta militia ad nos Papiæ venias, certus existens, quod nulli [illegible, ~4 letters] expeditionem remittemus, quamvis multi quaerant absolvi: & quicunq; [illegible, ~3 letters] nebit, contra [illegible, ~2 letters] voluntatem remanebit. Si vero ante hunc terminum nos videre voluerit, gratarum [illegible, ~4 letters] runtamen hoc pro constanti habere debes & tenere, quòd ab expeditione tuam personam [illegible, ~2 letters] do absolvemus.
units.tr: c. We admonish your ... of our Empire, that, like the other princes and our faithful men, you consider the honour of our Empire, and that on the fourteenth day after Easter you come to us at Pavia with honourable soldiery, certain that we shall remit the expedition to no one, although many seek to be released; and whoever will not come will remain against our will. If, however, he wishes to see us before this term, he ought nevertheless to hold and keep this as certain: that we shall absolve your person from the expedition [illegible].
II.

units.la: Super eadem expeditio- ne Italica.
units.tr: Concerning the same Italian expedition.

units.la: FRIDERICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator & Semper-Augustus, Eberhardo Saltzburgensi Archiepiscopo, gratiam suam & omne bonum. Tuam experientiam minimè latere credimus, non pro cumulandis divitiis ad usum nostrum aut filiorum nostrorum, sed solum in eodem ad reformationem & augmentum Imperii, dispendio tam rerum nostrarum, quàm in fidelium instantia, etiam attritione proprii corporis laborassemus incessanter. Nunc verò, quia contumacia diolanentium à primævo pacis inimicorum, & Ecclesiarum temeratorum, bono nostro propinquo instinctu Diaboli, obstare pro viribus nituntur, te unà cum aliis Principibus, cæterisq; Imperii fideles subsidium nostrum evocare decrevimus. Unde dilectioni tuæ mandamus, atq; sub debito praecipimus, quatenus omni occasione postposita, cùm membrum Imperii censeatis, & hoc fideli exutisti, ne Regnum aliquatenus in tempore nostro vacillet, & diminutionem sentiat, littera tua xiv.die post Paschæ Papiæ exercitui nostro accedas. Nam quicunq; nobis in auxilium venire, nos & successores nostros ditare & sublimare diligenter intenderit incunctanter sciat, toti negocio nostro cum victoria brevi (ut arbitramur) Dei nutu imponemus. Si quis autem in temporis aliquatenus subtraxerit, hunc nec nobis nec Imperio nostro fidelem esse censeamus.
units.tr: Frederick, by the grace of God Emperor of the Romans and Ever-August, to Eberhard, Archbishop of Salzburg, greeting, his grace and every good. We believe that your experience is not unknown to you: we have laboured without ceasing, not to heap up riches for our own use or for our sons, but solely for the reform and increase of the Empire, at the cost both of our own resources and of the urgent needs of the faithful, and even at the wearing down of our own body. Now, however, since the obstinacy of the Milanese, enemies of the primal peace and violators of the Churches, by the nearby prompting of the Devil to our harm, strive with all their strength to resist, we have decided to summon you, together with the other princes and the faithful of the Empire, to our aid. Therefore we command your Affection and, under penalty, we enjoin that, with every excuse set aside, since you count yourself a member of the Empire and are of its faithful, you come by your letter to our army at Pavia on the fourteenth day after Easter, so that the Kingdom may not waver in any way in our time and feel any diminution. For whoever intends diligently to come to our aid, and to enrich and exalt us and our successors, let him know without delay that, by God's will, we shall bring the whole business to a swift victory, as we judge. If anyone withdraws himself at all in this time, we shall not count him faithful either to us or to our Empire.
III.

units.la: De Concilio per Imperatorem Cremæ indicto ad tollendum schisma Papale.
units.tr: On the council convened at Cremona by the Emperor to end the papal schism.

units.la: FRIDERICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator Semper-Augustus, fideli suo Ebenhardo venerabili Saltzburgensi Archiepiscopo, gratiam suam & omne bonum.
units.tr: Frederick, by the grace of God Roman Emperor, ever August, to his faithful Eberhard, venerable Archbishop of Salzburg, his grace and every blessing.

units.la: 1. Quanto majori gitate antecessorum nostrorum, Regum & Imperatorum, Ecclesiam Salzburgensem decoratam, finitè cognovimus, eò majori pietate & ampliori dilectione, dignitatem Salzburgensis Ecclesiæ semper fovere studuimus, & omnibus modis promovere. Inde cùm non decet quàm de excellentiori & clarissimo Principe nostro, plurimum speraremus, & in tua sententia, in necessitatibus sanctæ Ecclesiæ Dei & Imperii, non modicam fiduciam habemus, ut tuus Ecclesiæ Dei in pendulo nutaret, ad Papiensem Curiam, ubi tam Ecclesiastici Principes, cum cularibus, pro gloria Dei & honore Imperii promovendo solenniter convenerant, tuam per apicibus nostris & nuncios evocavimus; & quare non veneris, admodum nos admirati sumus.
units.tr: 1. As we have learned how greatly the Church of Salzburg was adorned by the favour of our predecessors, kings and emperors, so with all the more piety and greater affection have we always striven to cherish the dignity of the Church of Salzburg and to advance it in every way. Hence, since we expected much from you, our most excellent and distinguished prince, and have no small confidence in your judgement in the needs of the holy Church of God and of the Empire, we summoned you by our letters and messengers to the Papal court at Pavia, where the ecclesiastical princes, together with the secular ones, had solemnly assembled to promote the glory of God and the honour of the Empire. We were greatly astonished that you did not come.

units.la: 2. Præterea indicto generali Concilio pro necessitatibus Imperii & Ecclesiæ, Dominica Vocem jucunditatis tuam sanctitatem, tuam reverentiam scriptis & nuncus iteratis mus, & attentissime rogavimus, ut diligenter perspectis schismatibus & pressuris, in quibus Ecclesia fluctuans laborabat, tuam laudabilem præsentiam sacro Conventui exhiberes, & de medio tanti mali scandala prudentiæ tuæ consilium opemque necessariam negocio tam arduo negates: sed ne sic tuam personam evocare valuimus.
units.tr: 2. Moreover, after a general council was proclaimed for the needs of the Empire and the Church, we wrote to your holiness and reverence again and again, and sent messengers, and most earnestly asked that, having carefully considered the schisms and troubles by which the Church was wavering and labouring, you would grace the sacred assembly with your laudable presence and bring the counsel and necessary help of your prudence to the removal of so great an evil in so arduous a business. But we have not been able to summon your person in this way.

units.la: 3. Unde quia tua res agitur, paries cum proximus ardet, & quia publica res ista fuit, non (nam de animarum salute agebatur) miramur nos primitus. Mirantur & universi Principes Seculares quàm Ecclesiastici, qui ad excolendam vineam Dei non timuerunt portare pondus æstus, quare te subtraxeris, & magna suspicione te suspectum habent, quòd in tempore turbulento ipsum quasi murum inexpugnabilem pro domo Israël non opposueris. Mandamus itaque omni, monentes & studiosius te rogantes, ut remota omni occasione & dilatione tuam ipsius presentiam in proxima Nativirate sanctæ Dei Genetricis Mariæ nobis & Curiæ nostræ exhibere nunc Cremæ, assumpto tecum fideli nostro Venerabili Episcopo Brixiensi.
units.tr: 3. Therefore, since your own affair is at stake, and it is like a neighbour's wall burning, and since this was a public matter (for the salvation of souls was at issue), we are first of all astonished. All the princes, secular as well as ecclesiastical, also wonder why you have withdrawn, you who did not fear to bear the burden and heat in cultivating the vineyard of God. They hold you under great suspicion, that in a troubled time you have not set yourself up as an impregnable wall for the house of Israel. We therefore command you, admonishing and asking you more earnestly, that, all excuse and delay set aside, you present yourself to us and to our court here at Cremona at the coming Nativity of Holy Mary, Mother of God, bringing with you our faithful venerable Bishop of Brescia.
IV.

units.la: Archiepiscopus ad expeditionem evocatur sub pœna proscriptionis & depositionis.
units.tr: The Archbishop is summoned to the expedition under penalty of proscription and deposition.

units.la: FRIDERICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator Semper-Augustus, Eberhardo Venerabili Salzburgensi Archiepiscopo, gratiam suam & omne bonum.
units.tr: Frederick, by the grace of God Roman Emperor, ever August, to Eberhard, venerable Archbishop of Salzburg, his grace and every blessing.

units.la: 1. Cum facti Imperii nostri dispositio consilio Principum, & maximè Religiosorum, indigeat, cùm toties rogatus à nobis & diligenter invitatus, semel saltem ad festum beatæ Mariæ venire noluerit, de prudentia tua facis mirari non possumus, sed & universis Principibus admodum videtur extraneum.
units.tr: 1. Since the arrangement of the affairs of our Empire needs the counsel of the princes, and especially of the religious, and since you, though asked by us so often and invited with diligence, were unwilling to come even once for the feast of blessed Mary, we cannot wonder at your prudence; indeed it seems quite strange to all the princes.

units.la: 2. Præterea cùm Salzburgensis Ecclesia tanto amplioris servitii debito teneatur Imperio, tanto amplius ab Imperiali munificentia præ cæteris dotata & exaltata, collatis sibi beneficiis gaudere dinoscitur, miramur, & de ratione non videmus, quare in summis Imperii necessitatibus tanto jam tempore tam fortiter, auxiliante Deo, insudavimus & insudamus, tantum servitium debitum defectum perferre debeamus.
units.tr: 2. Moreover, since the Church of Salzburg is bound to the Empire by a debt of service so much the greater, and is known to be endowed and exalted above others by imperial generosity and to enjoy the benefits conferred upon it, we marvel, and cannot see the reason, why in the greatest necessities of the Empire, when we have so long laboured, and still labour, vigorously with God's help, you should allow so great a debt of service to remain unpaid.

units.la: 3. Cum igitur quantumcunq; Religiosi ab ipsa veritate, quæ sunt Cæsaris, Cæsari reddantur [?]num, & una dignitas nisi folium qualicunq; pecunia, sed & personis & annatura laboribus nostris ad-[?] Imperialia scripta tuæ fidelitati tam præcipiendo quam rogando mandamus, quia-[?] pro [?]um Pascha pro magnitudine facultatis & debiti, cum multa nobis succurras, & xv. die [?] Paschæ in campo Veronæ cum reliquis exercitibus te præsentes, teq; ita factorum nunc sla[?] præsentium latoris, Capellani & Nuncii nostri Burensis Colon. fidelis & firma promissi[?]are non differas. Quòd si animum prudentiæ tuæ ab his averteris, & omnino noluerIS ve-[?]ubitanter scire te volumus, quòd nos, favent- & semper nos præcedente Dei clementia, cum filio Principum & Religiosorum ita de Salzburgensi Ecclesia ordinabimus, ut & honor Dei religionis non minuatur, & debitum servitium Imperio de cætero rationabiliter exsolvatur.
units.tr: 3. Therefore, since religious men too must render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and [the duty is owed] not by one dignity alone, nor by money only, but by persons and by labours, we command your fidelity by these imperial writings, both by order and by request, that you not delay to be present with the remaining armies in the field at Verona on the fifteenth day after Easter, bringing with you as much as your means and your debt allow, since you have many resources. Know this, that our chaplain and messenger, the faithful Burensis of Cologne, the bearer of these presents, has been sent to you. If you turn your mind away from these things and are altogether unwilling, we want you to know without doubt that we, with the favour of God's mercy going before us, will so order the Church of Salzburg, with the princes and the religious, that the honour of the religion of God is not diminished and the due service to the Empire is henceforth rendered in reasonable measure.

units.la: V. Super eadem re.
units.tr: V. On the same matter.

units.la: FRIDERICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator & Semper-Augustus, fideli suo A. Venerabili [?]ensi Episcopo, gratiam suam & omne bonum.
units.tr: Frederick, by the grace of God Roman Emperor and ever August, to his faithful A., venerable Bishop of Brescia, his grace and every blessing.

units.la: I. Cum abipla veritate omnis homo, sed & quantumcunq; Religiosus, quæ sunt Cæsaris, Cæsari [?] beatur; & Salzburgensis Ecclesia quàm maximi servitii debito, sacro teneatur Imperio, im-[?] ... ficimus, quare Salzburgensis Archiepiscopus totiès rogatus & vocatus non ad consilium, [?]editionis auxilium venire voluerit, & terminum, quem per proprium Capellanum suum [?] festum B. Mariæ condixerat, tam incuriose neglexerit. Nunc ergò per præsentium latorem, fi-[?] lauum nostrum, Burensem Colon iterum ad expeditionis auxilium cum personis & armaturis [?]vimus, & ut tua diligentia ad id faciendum eum studiose commoneat, solertèr & intensissi[?]us. Quod si pro consuetudine sua venire noluerit, de contemptu & injuria tam tuæ dilectio[?]ur, quam & omnibus Imperii Principibus ibi conqueri necessarium habemus.
units.tr: 1. Since every man, however religious, must render what is Caesar's to Caesar, and the Church of Salzburg is bound to the sacred Empire by the very great debt of service, ... we have been made to see why the Archbishop of Salzburg, though so often asked and summoned, not for counsel but to come to the aid of the expedition, was unwilling to come, and so carelessly neglected the day which he had fixed through his own chaplain for the feast of blessed Mary. Now therefore, through the bearer of these presents, our faithful Burensis of Cologne, we summon him again, with persons and arms, to the aid of the expedition, and we ask that your diligence remind him of this earnestly and most urgently. But if he is unwilling to come, as is his custom, we must complain of the contempt and injury both to your dilection and to all the princes of the Empire there.

units.la: 2. Nosaut, si necesse fuerit, de Salzburgensi Ecclesia ita cum consilio Principum & Religiosorum abimus, q; & honor Dei non diminuetur, & religio Ecclesiæ non subvertetur, si (Deo volen[?] to debitum servitium exsolvetur. Novit Deus, qui corda scrutatur, q; nos virtutem in quolibet [?]nunc, magis autem in eo, cujus propositum in virtutibus decoratur, diligimus & reveremur; &, [?]premis injuriis coacti, ad molestiam cujusquam, non nisi multùm inviti provocamur.
units.tr: 2. Moreover, if it is necessary, we will also deal with the Church of Salzburg, with the counsel of the princes and the religious, in such a way that the honour of God is not diminished and the religion of the Church is not overthrown, provided that (God willing) the due service is paid. God, who searches the hearts, knows that we love and revere virtue wherever it is found, and the more so in one whose purpose is adorned with virtues; and we are provoked, compelled by such injuries, to trouble no one, except very unwillingly.

units.la: 3. De cætero præfatum Capellanum nostrum dilectioni tuæ committimus, ut ex parte nostra di[?]ter audias, & ad ea, quæ eidem dedimus in præceptis, ipsum consilio & conductu adjuves, quatenus [?]o his & pro omnibus fidelibus servitiis tuis & multa dilectione tua, vobis ad promerendum sem-[?]mus attenti.
units.tr: 3. For the rest, we commit our aforesaid chaplain to your dilection, so that you may hear him diligently on our behalf, and help him with counsel and escort in those things which we have given him in commands, so that... for these things and for all your faithful services and your great affection, we are attentive to deserve from you in return.

units.la: VI. Vt Archiepiscopus ad Curiam Imperialem evocatus se in persona Imperatori sistat, nec ulla pecunia absentiam suam redimere possit.
units.tr: VI. That the Archbishop, when summoned to the Imperial Court, must present himself before the Emperor in person, and may not redeem his absence with any sum of money.

units.la: FRIDERICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator Semper-Augustus, Eberhardo Venerabili Salzburgensi Archiepiscopo, gratiam suam & omne bonum. Inter anxias & innumeras tribulationes, [?]exigentibus peccatis hominum, jamdiu universalis laborat Ecclesia, consilium religionis tuæ [?]tempore requisivimus, ut discretio tua, quæ directo tramite ad summum bonum attingere nitis[?]salutis nobis ostenderet, & ab errore minus eruditorum animos declinaret. Non solùm autem [?]iam tuam admodùm necessariam Imperio subtraxisti, verùm nos & omnes Principes & fide-[?]es, secus quàm decet honestatem tuam inunoderatis verbis cum offensione aggravasti. Sanè [?]ionis tuæ Nuncius ad nos venisset, & servitium pecuniæ tuæ pro redemptione expeditionis [?]isset, nos communicato cum Principibus nostris cõfilio, pecuniam tuam cum honore non [?]accipere, quia nostræ consuetudinis non est alicujus pecuniam accipere, & odium etiam inter [?]re. Cùm autem, sicut decet Imperialem Excellentiam, nobis personam tuam exhibueris, [?]gis de tuo adventu gaudere poterimus, & de instante necessitate Imperii & Ecclesiæ, te-[?]cæteris Imperii Principibus tuo consilio salubrius tractare poterimus & ordinare.
units.tr: Frederick, by the grace of God Roman Emperor, ever August, to Eberhard, venerable Archbishop of Salzburg, his grace and every good. Amid anxious and countless tribulations, with the sins of men demanding it, the universal Church has long been suffering. In this time we have sought the counsel of your religion, so that your discretion, which strives by a direct path to reach the highest good, might show us the way of salvation and turn the minds of the less learned away from error. Yet you have not only withdrawn your very necessary presence from the Empire, but you have also burdened us and all the Princes and faithful with immoderate words, to our offence and contrary to what befits your honour. Indeed, if your messenger had come to us and offered money to buy off the expedition, we, having taken counsel with our Princes, would not have accepted your money with honour, since it is not our custom to accept anyone's money, and it would also have stirred hatred. But since, as befits the Imperial Majesty, you have shown yourself to us in person, we may rejoice at your coming, and, concerning the pressing need of Empire and Church, we may be able to deal with and settle matters more beneficially with you and the other Princes of the Empire, by your counsel.
