units.la: VII. Rebellem Imperio Civitatem Mediolanensem lata, & de forma executionis in recipi- endis deditis rebellibus.
units.tr: VII. Concerning the city of Milan, rebellious against the Empire, the sentence pronounced, and the manner of receiving the rebels who surrendered.

units.la: FRIDERICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator & Semper-Augustus, Eberhardo Salzburgensi Archiepiscopo, gratiam suam & omne bonum.
units.tr: Frederick, by the grace of God Roman Emperor and ever August, to Eberhard, Archbishop of Salzburg, his grace and every good.

units.la: 1. Diu ... [?]æstimamus, ut hi, qui tribulationibus nostris & Imperii, personarum servitio & rerum [?]enus fideliter comunicaverunt, à Domino, qui consolatur nos in tribulatione nostra, [?]ia recipiant, & felicissimis eventibus nostris, ac gloriosissimis triumphis, quales nulli [?]notorii concessos esse credimus, grata vicissitudine participent & cógratulentur. Tuæ [?]onem, quæ utrumque honorem nostrum sitibundo pectore anhelare, luce clarius constat, significa[?]us; quia in virtute Dei, per quem Reges regnant, & potentes jacunt justitiam, felicem & glorio[?]a victoriâ cum plenitudine honoris adepti sumus. In Kal. enim Mart. prima videlicet [?]Imperii Mediolanum, submota omni simulatione fraudis, qua in prima deditione [?]um reversi, summa necessitate famis & inediæ coacti ad Curiam nostram apud Laudam [?]dos gladios in cervicibus suis deferentes, & Majestati nostræ reos se esse profitentes,
units.tr: 1. For a long time ... we think that those who have faithfully shared with us, in our tribulations and those of the Empire, in the service of persons and goods, should receive from the Lord, who comforts us in our tribulation, and should share in and rejoice with us, by a welcome turn of fortune, in our most happy events and most glorious triumphs, such as we believe have been granted to no one. Your ... which, as clear as daylight, longs with a thirsty heart for both our honours, we wish to make known: for in the power of God, through whom kings reign and the mighty decree justice, we have obtained a happy and glorious victory with full honour. For on the Kalends of March, that is, the first day of the month, Milan, all pretence of deceit being set aside, by which at the first surrender they had deceived us, and driven by the extreme necessity of hunger and famine, came to our Court at Lodi, bearing naked swords on their necks and confessing themselves guilty before our Majesty,

units.la: A a perfopersonas, res, ipsa, nque civitatem, abiq; omni tenore, & sine aliqua conditione interpositâ, in nostram potestatem cum plena deditione reddidisse.
units.tr: ...persons, goods, and the city itself, without any restriction and with no condition interposed, into our power with full surrender.

units.la: 2. Praeterea iv. Nonas ejusdem mensis, Mediolanenses cum omni militia & suis hominibus, qui de civitate non recesserant, vexilla & universa signa bellica, clavesque civitatis, & Consulatum, ligatique bla noster reliquerunt, refutantes omni genera armorum, omnem potestatem, nisi quam tamen permissione nostrae potestatis obtinere. Juraverunt insuper, quaecunque eos jurare fecimus, fide quam universa mandata nostra, sicut de personis & rebus & de ipsa civitate ordinaremus, bona fide observarent, & de iis omnibus observandis caeteri oblides & meliores & majores de civitate nobis dederunt.
units.tr: 2. Moreover, on the fourth day before the Nones of the same month, the Milanese, together with all their soldiers and their men who had not left the city, left behind their banners and all military standards, the keys of the city and the Consulate, and, bound, they renounced every kind of arms and every power, except what they might hold by our permission. They also swore whatever we made them swear, and promised in good faith that they would observe all our commands, whatever we should ordain concerning persons, goods, and the city itself; and for the observance of all these things, the other hostages and the better and greater men of the city gave themselves to us.

units.la: 3. Ex sententia ergo divina, cujus judicia abyssus multa, qui frangit omnem superbiam, & decreto praelictis hostibus occasio malignandi, & facultas rebellandi praestetur, fossata complanavimus, muros subvertimus, turres omnes destruximus, ipsamque civitatem in ruinam & desolationem redegimus, ad promovenda alia negotia, & ad plenariam Imperii reformationem, exercitum nostrum victrices aquilas feliciter convertemus.
units.tr: 3. Therefore, by the divine sentence, whose judgments are a great abyss, who breaks every pride, and by decree, no opportunity of mischief and no power of rebelling is to be granted to the aforesaid enemies: we have levelled the ditches, overthrown the walls, destroyed all the towers, and reduced the city itself to ruin and desolation. To advance other business and the complete reformation of the Empire, we will turn our army and victorious eagles wherever we shall happily decide.

units.la: 4. De caetero, dilectos & fideles nostros Nuncios O. Veronensem Episcopum, & C. Capritanum nostrum in occursum sibi apud Tridentum transmittimus, qui juxta magnificentiam suam ad Curiam nostram te perducant.
units.tr: 4. Henceforth we send our beloved and faithful envoys, O., Bishop of Verona, and our Captain C., to meet you at Trent, who will escort you to our Court in a manner befitting your dignity.

units.la: VIII. Super eadem re.
units.tr: VIII. On the same matter.

units.la: FRIDERICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator Semper-Augustus, dilecto suo Ronaldo Cremonensi Episcopo, gratiam suam & omne bonum.
units.tr: Frederick, by the grace of God Roman Emperor and ever August, to his beloved Ronald, Bishop of Cremona, his grace and every good.

units.la: 1. Dignum arbitramur, ut ii, qui tribulationibus nostris & Imperii, personarum periculo & pedio hactenus hdeliter communicaverunt, ab eo, qui consolatur nos in omni tribulatione, ne nostra consolationis gaudia recipiant, & felicitatem eventibus nostris, ac gloriosos triumphos quam in ante ceterorum nostrorum concessos esse credimus, grata vicissitudine participent & gloriantur.
units.tr: 1. We think it right that those who have hitherto faithfully shared in our tribulations and those of the Empire, at the peril of persons and goods, should receive from him who comforts us in every tribulation the joys of our consolation, and by a welcome exchange should share in and rejoice in our happy events and glorious triumphs, which we believe have been granted to no others before.

units.la: 2. Tuxigitur Dilectioni, quoniam omnem honorem nostrum sinibundo pectore audierint clarius constat, signficandum duximus, quod in virtute Dei, per quem Reges regnant, & potentes justitiam, felicem & gloriosam de Mediolano victoriam cum omni plenitudine honorum adepti sunt. In Kal. enim Martii, videlicet prima die mensis, hostes Imperii Mediolanenses, summota omni dilatione fraudis, qua in prima deditione nos circumvenerunt, summa necessitate famis & fiducia ad Curiam nostram apud Laudam venerunt, & nudos gladios in cervicibus suis ferentes, & Mediolanenses profitentes, personas, res, ipsamque civitatem, absque omni tenore, & sine conditione interposita, in nostram partem cum plenaria deditione reddiderunt.
units.tr: 2. Therefore, since your Love, which, as is clear as daylight, longs with a thirsty heart for our honour, we thought should be informed that, in the power of God, through whom kings reign and the mighty decree justice, they have obtained a happy and glorious victory from Milan with every fullness of honour. For on the Kalends of March, that is, the first day of the month, the enemies of the Empire, the Milanese, all delay of deceit set aside, by which they had deceived us at the first surrender, came with extreme need of hunger and in trust to our Court at Lodi, and, bearing naked swords on their necks and confessing themselves Milanese, surrendered persons, goods, and the city itself into our power with full surrender, without any restriction and with no condition interposed.

units.la: 3. Ex sententia igitur divina, cujus judicia abyssus multa, qui frangit omne superbum, nec deserto praedictis hostibus occasio malignandi, vel facultas rebellandi praestetur, fossata complanavimus, muros subvertimus, turres omnes destruximus, & totam civitatem in ruinam & desolationem redegimus, ad promovenda alia negotia, & ad plenariam Imperii reformationem exercitum nostrum & Aquilas triumphales, prout voluerimus, convertemus.
units.tr: 3. Therefore, by the divine sentence, whose judgments are a great abyss, who breaks every proud man, and no opportunity of mischief or power of rebelling being granted to the said enemies, we have levelled the ditches, overthrown the walls, destroyed all the towers, and reduced the whole city to ruin and desolation. To advance other business and the complete reformation of the Empire, we will turn our army and triumphal eagles wherever we wish.

units.la: X. De Pace Imperatoris & Regis Francorum.
units.tr: X. On the Peace of the Emperor and the King of the French.

units.la: FRIDERICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator, à Deo Coronatus, Magnus & Pacificus, Victor ac Triumphator, Semper-Augustus, dilecto consanguineo suo Ludovico, gratia Francorum Regi gloriosi, salutem & sinceram dilectionis sinceritatem. Postquam divinitas, per quam Reges regnant, & legum conditores justa decernunt, ad Romani Imperii nos sublimavit, & ex pacis abundantia, quam mundus dare non potest, feliciter regnandi felicia nobis concessit, desiderio desideravimus facere tuâ videre, & familiaritatis tuae perfrui dulcedine. Sed praepedientibus magnis ac multimodis valde dilaceratis Imperii nostri negotiis, quo plurimus, effectui mancipare non potuimus. Quia vero per Legatos tuos, & per epistolam tuam, mulier aeque te optare cognovimus & credimus, non modice gaudemus, sperantes in eo, qui dat ad gibus, quod ex nostra salutifera colloquutione, universo orbi pacis & tranquillitatis non procuret & Ecclesiis Dei emergendi, reparandi, multiplicandi praebeatur incrementum. Sed quod volunt bonae benignum deduxerunt hinc inde nondum complere potuit, nec tua tarditas, nec nostra negligentia imputandum recessit. Nunc autem, quia in praecincta Italicae expeditionis jam fumus, & Imperii nostri ad eandem unanimiter intendunt, quo in loco, quo tempore convenire & contendere possimus, incertum habemus, nisi forte si completa expeditione vita comes fuerit, super hoc ipsis nostris diligentissime ordinabimus. Volumus etiam, ut quod tu de nobis, nos de te semper possimus. Vera enim amicitia nunquam fallit.
units.tr: FREDERICK, by the grace of God Emperor of the Romans, crowned by God, Great and Peaceful, Victor and Triumphator, Ever-August, to his beloved kinsman Louis, illustrious by the grace of God King of the French, greeting and sincere warmth of affection. Since the divine power, through whom kings reign and lawgivers decree what is just, has raised us to the Roman Empire and, from an abundance of peace which the world cannot give, has granted us to reign happily, we have longed with desire to see you face to face and to enjoy the sweetness of your friendship. But since great and manifold affairs of our Empire, greatly torn apart, have stood in the way, we have not been able to bring this about as much as we wished. Because, however, we have learned and believe, through your envoys and your letter, that you desire the same, we rejoice not a little, hoping in him who gives good things that from our salutary conference peace and tranquillity may be procured for the whole world, and an increase may be granted to the Churches of God for rising up, being restored, and multiplying. But what good men on both sides have wished to bring about has not yet been able to be completed; the delay is to be imputed neither to your slowness nor to our negligence. Now, however, since we are on the very point of the Italian expedition, and our Empire is unanimously intent upon it, we are uncertain in what place and at what time we can meet and confer; unless perhaps, if the expedition is completed and life accompanies us, we shall arrange this most diligently. We also wish that you may always be able to rely on us as we can rely on you. For true friendship never deceives.

units.la: XI. De Unitate Imperii & Regni Franciae.
units.tr: XI. On the Unity of the Empire and the Kingdom of France.

units.la: FRIDERICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator & Semper-Augustus, dilecto consanguineo suo Ludovico, Illustri Francorum Regi, salutem & sinceram dilectionis affectum. Legatum Nobilitatis tuae, quia debuimus alacriter ac, sicut expimus, benigne Imperatoris nostri, dantes his, quae sincere tua nobis nuncuata sunt. Placet igitur & sublimitati nostrae, ut inter nos sit consanguineos, & inter cognata Regna nostra, detersa totius rancoris nebula, sincerae dilectionis splendor refulgeat, & foedus amicitiae, quod facit utraque unum, inde indissolubilem semper conservet firmitatem. Sane quae sunc que necessaria sunt ad conservandam inter nos mutuae dilectionis integritatem, dilecto consanguineo nostro fideli tuo Henrico Comiti Trecatum amicè & plenarie ordinavimus, & sicut conditum est, inviolabiliter observare curabimus. Datum Papiae post destructionem Mediolani, II. Kal. Junii.
units.tr: FREDERICK, by the grace of God Emperor of the Romans and Ever-August, to his beloved kinsman Louis, illustrious King of the French, greeting and the sincere affection of love. We have received the envoy of your Nobility, as we ought, eagerly and, as we hope, kindly, and we give assent to those things which your sincerity has announced to us. It therefore pleases also our Highness that between us, as kinsmen, and between our kindred kingdoms, the cloud of all rancour being dispelled, the splendour of sincere love should shine forth, and that the covenant of friendship, which makes the two one, should always preserve from it an indissoluble firmness. Indeed, whatever things are necessary for preserving the integrity of our mutual love, we have arranged fully and in a friendly manner with our beloved kinsman, our faithful Henry, Count of Troyes, and as has been agreed, we shall take care to observe them inviolably. Given at Pavia after the destruction of Milan, the second day before the Kalends of June.
XII.

units.la: De Pseudopapa in Franciam transfugio.
units.tr: On the pseudo-pope's flight into France.

units.la: FRIDERICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator & Semper-Augustus, dilecto amico suo, Venerabili N. Episcopo Suessionensi, & Regis Francorum Cancellario, salutem cum intima & sincera dilectione. In veritate audivimus, quod Rollandus quondam Cancellarius, qui propter fideles nostros ... Romam non habet nec invenit, ubi caput suum reclinet, periculo maris seipsum cum suis ... quibusdam committent, ut tenam Franciae genarum intret, eamque schismaticae pravitatis errore ... ut etiam quomodolibet commodat viginti mille libras, & amplius, unde creditoribus suis debita persolvat; quia sub aliena ... valde graviter ipse laborat. Rogantes itaque tuam dilectionem intimo & pleno affectu monemus, quatinus praedictum Schismaticum, nostrum & totius Imperii atrocem inimicum, nullo modo recipias, nec recipi ab alio permittas, Regique Francorum bona fide consulas, ne ipsum, vel aliquem de suis Pseudocardinalibus vel Nunciis recipiat. Tantum enim ac tale odium inter nostrum Imperium & suum Regnum exinde posset oriri, quod non de facili compescere possemus aut sedare.
units.tr: Frederick, by the grace of God Roman Emperor and ever-August, to his beloved friend, the venerable N., Bishop of Soissons and Chancellor of the King of the Franks, greeting, with heartfelt and sincere affection. We have heard in truth that Rolandus, formerly chancellor, who because of our faithful ... has no Rome and finds no place where he may lay his head, has committed himself and his ... with the danger of the sea to certain people, so that he may enter the territory of France, and ... by the error of schismatic wickedness ... that he may in any way borrow twenty thousand pounds or more, from which to pay his debts to his creditors, since under another's ... he labours very grievously. We therefore, asking your love with sincere and full affection, advise you that you by no means receive the aforesaid schismatic, our and the whole Empire's fierce enemy, nor allow him to be received by anyone else, and that you counsel the King of the Franks in good faith, lest he receive him, or any of his pseudo-cardinals or envoys. For so great and such a hatred could arise from this between our Empire and his kingdom that we could not easily restrain or calm it.

units.la: XIII.
units.tr: XIII.

units.la: De Concilio in Burgundia inter Imperatorem & Regem Franciae, & inter utriusque communes Proceres celebrando pro confirmatione electi Papae.
units.tr: On a council to be held in Burgundy between the Emperor and the King of France, and between the common nobles of each, for the confirmation of the elected Pope.

units.la: FRIDERICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator & Semper-Augustus, dilecto suo ** Archiepiscopo, gratiam suam & omne bonum. Inter innumeras & tumescentes tempestatum procellas, quibus parva navicula B. Petri quassata, & inter pressuras diversas, quibus sancta Dei Ecclesia frequenter afflicta & tribulata est, tandem verus ille Mediator Dei & hominum Jesus Christus, qui Ecclesiam suam unicam sponsam proprio characterer sui pretiosi sanguinis insignivit & redemit, consolationis iam, quam ascendens in caelum fidelibus suis repromisit, inquiens: Non relinquam vos orphanos, ecce vobiscum sum omnibus diebus usque ad consummationem saeculi, evidentibus & manifestis declarat indiciis. Nam enim sicut stella matutina in medio nebulae oriens, solita pietate Ecclesiam suam in tribulatione respexit, & surgens imperavit ventis & mari, & facta est tranquillitas magna. Pro illa siquidem concordia, quae inter Nos & Regem Francorum pro schismate Romanae Ecclesiae jamdiu agitabatur, ... Spiritus Sancti gratia, quae facit habitare unanimes in domo Domini, mediantibus hinc inde Legatis pari voluntate, & unanimi consensu inter nos convenit, quod nos videlicet una cum Archiepiscopis, Episcopis, & Patribus Orthodoxis ac viris Religiosis, Baronibus & universis utriusque Regni civibus, IV. Kal. Septemb. in die videlicet Decollationis Joannis Baptistae, super fluvium Saonam ... Episcopatu Bizantino Concilium generale pariter celebraturi sumus, in quo Rex Francorum dilectus consanguineus noster cum universis Archiepiscopis suis, Episcopis, & cum omnibus Regni sui Principibus, & tota Gallicana Ecclesia Reverendum Patrem nostrum Dominum Papam Victorem, sacramenta & firmissimas securitates praeordinatum est, in Apostolicum & Universalem sanctae Ecclesiae Pontificem recipiet, & debitam ei exhibebit reverentiam. Verum quia hoc negotium tam necessarium, ubi de reconciliatione sanctae Dei Ecclesiae & totius Christianitatis in commune agitur, sine tuae discretionis caeterorumque Principum ac Christi fidelium consummari nec debet nec poterit, exoramus te & monemus in ea fide, quam debes Imperio, Dei Ecclesiae, & animae tuae, quatinus omni occasione summota cum sapientioribus & magis illustratis personis tui Episcopatus apud Bisantium, IV. die ante praedictum terminum familiae Curiae, nobis occurras, ad Concilium nobiscum processurus. Et quia abundans cautela militum tuorum, quos recum adducis, in armis & clypeis sunt muniti. Insuper tentoria deferas, ... domorum rationem necessaria erunt. Ibi enim per gratiam in Dei totum negotium Domini Victoris ad gloriam Dei, & ad pacem, & unitatem sanctae Ecclesiae, & omnimodum honorem ... honcsto fine terminabitur.
units.tr: FREDERICK, by the grace of God Emperor of the Romans and ever-Augustus, to his beloved ** Archbishop, his grace and every good. Amid the countless and swelling storms by which the little boat of St. Peter is battered, and amid the various oppressions by which the holy Church of God is often afflicted and troubled, that true Mediator between God and men, Jesus Christ, who marked and redeemed His Church, His only spouse, with the distinctive seal of His precious blood, now declares by clear and manifest signs the consolation which, ascending into heaven, He promised to His faithful, saying: "I will not leave you orphans; behold, I am with you all days, even to the end of the age." For as the morning star rising in the midst of the cloud, He has looked upon His Church in her tribulation with His accustomed kindness, and rising, He commanded the winds and the sea, and there was a great calm. For that agreement which between Us and the King of the Franks has long been under discussion concerning the schism of the Roman Church, ... by the grace of the Holy Spirit, which makes brothers dwell together in unity in the house of the Lord, through Legates going back and forth with equal will and by unanimous consent it has been agreed between us that we, namely together with the Archbishops, Bishops, Orthodox Fathers and religious men, Barons and all the citizens of both kingdoms, on the fourth day before the Kalends of September, that is, on the day of the Beheading of John the Baptist, will hold a general council together, beside the river Saône ... in the Bishopric of Besançon, in which our beloved cousin the King of the Franks, with all his Archbishops, Bishops, all the Princes of his kingdom and the whole Gallican Church, shall receive the Reverend Father our Lord Pope Victor, previously ordained by sacraments and most firm securities, as Apostolic and Universal Pontiff of the holy Church, and shall pay him due reverence. But since this matter, so necessary, in which the reconciliation of the holy Church of God and of all Christendom is treated in common, neither ought nor can be brought to completion without your discretion and that of the other Princes and faithful of Christ, we beg and admonish you, in that faith which you owe to the Empire, to the Church of God and to your own soul, that, every excuse set aside, you meet us at Besançon, four days before the said date, with the wiser and more illustrious persons of your bishopric and household of the Court, to go with us to the council. And since a sufficient guard of your soldiers, whom you bring with you, are armed with weapons and shields. Moreover, you shall bring tents ... the arrangement of houses will be necessary. For there, by the grace of God, the whole business concerning Lord Victor will be concluded to the glory of God, to the peace and unity of the holy Church, and to every honour ... with an honourable end.
XIV.

units.la: Super eadem re.
units.tr: On the same matter.

units.la: FRIDERICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator & Semper-Augustus, dilecto suo E. Venerabili Lugdunensi Archiepiscopo & Primati Galliarum, gratiam suam & omne bonum. Imperialis nostrae celsitudinis propositum, quod Lugdunensem Ecclesiam ac Civitatem a diutinis laboribus suis ... & in antiquae dignitatis suae statum reformare decrevimus, pro tua fideli erga nos devotione nostro incessanter vigilat, quoad usque (Deo opitulante) debitum sortiatur effectum. Unde ... divinitas, quae piis omnium consiliis interesse, & ea promovere consuevit, congruam nobis ... opportunitatem obtulit, ut partes Burgundiae, immo ipsam Civitatem Lugdunensem in ... Majestatis nostrae persona quantocyus adeamus, ac ruinas ejus in statum sui decorem cooperante Deo erigamus. Comes siquidem Trecensis, quum ad Curiam nostram in legatione Domini Regis Francorum venisset, & Reverendum Patrem nostrum Papam Victorem humili veneratione honoratiser, studiose à nobis postulavit, quatinus ad Colloquium inter nos & eum Regem habendum accederemus; tantumque huic verbo instituit, quoadusque universorum nostrorum Principum colloquium indiximus, iv. Kalend. Septembris, ad Pontem Laone, inter Divionem & Dolam, cum Archiepiscopis, Abbatibus, aliisque Cleri nostri Prioribus illo venturi. Quia ergo tua prudentia in eodem Colloquio nobis plurimum necessaria est, Venerabilitati tuae studiose mandamus injungimus, quatinus ad idem Colloquium omnes Suffraganeos tuos evoces, & cum universis Prioribus, Abbatibus, & Cleri celebritate, omni remota occasione, venias, quia nos ibidem gratia promovente, super Ecclesiae Dei restituenda unitate, & super Domini Papae Victoris cuiusmodi tione finem imponemus. Interea vero consilium non fuit, ut nihilominus (prout dictum erat) tractaremus, quia quaecunque sunt in bellicis rebus agenda seu disponenda, per praesentiam nostram convenienter adimplere curabimus. Dominus quidem Papa nobiscum adest, & oportebit propter Ecclesiam domorum in tentorus habitare.
units.tr: Frederick, by the grace of God Emperor of the Romans and ever Augustus, to his beloved E., venerable Archbishop of Lyons and Primate of the Gauls, his grace and every blessing. Our imperial highness has resolved to restore the Church and city of Lyons from their long labours to the state of their former dignity, and our purpose in this, out of your faithful devotion toward us, keeps watch without ceasing, until by God's help it reaches its due effect. Therefore the divinity, which is accustomed to take part in the godly counsels of all and to advance them, has offered us a fitting opportunity to approach the parts of Burgundy, indeed the city of Lyons itself, in the person of our majesty as quickly as possible, and by God's cooperation to raise its ruins to the state of their proper beauty. For the Count of Troyes, when he had come to our court on an embassy from the lord King of the Franks, and had earnestly and respectfully asked us, with humble reverence toward our reverend father Pope Victor, that we should come to a colloquy between ourselves and that King, pressed this request so hard that, until we had summoned a colloquy of all our princes for the fourth day before the Kalends of September, at Pont-de-Laône, between Dijon and Dole, with the archbishops, abbots and other priors of our clergy coming there. Since therefore your prudence is very much needed by us at this colloquy, we earnestly command and enjoin your venerability that you summon all your suffragans to the same colloquy, and that you come with all the priors, abbots and throng of the clergy, setting aside every excuse, because there, by the gracious help of God, we will put an end both to the restoring of the unity of the Church of God and to the matter of the lord Pope Victor of whatever kind. Meanwhile, it was not our intention that, nevertheless (as was said), we should deal with these matters, since whatever is to be done or arranged in the business of war, we will take care to carry out fittingly through our presence. The lord Pope is indeed with us, and for the sake of the Church it will be necessary to dwell in tents and houses.

units.la: X V. Super eadem re.
units.tr: XV. On the same matter.

units.la: FRIDERICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator, & Semper-Augustus, fideli suo M. Dunelmensi Episcopo, gratiam suam & omne bonum. Quoniam in schismate, quod est in Romana Ecclesia universus orbis in se ipsum divisus est, & tota Christianitas in modica turbatione concutitur, animi compassione sanctae Dei Ecclesiae doloribus condolemus, totius consilii & auxilii propensem curam & sollicitudinem adhibere cupientes, ut totius dissentionis discrimine sublato, Ecclesia Dei, sicut in unitate fidei, ita sub unius Pastoris regimine in unum ovile congregetur. Inde est, ex consilio Principum, cum dilecto consanguineo nostro Ludovico Illustri Regi Francorum iv. Kal. Septembris, in die videlicet Decollationis Sancti Johannis Baptistae, super fluvium Saonam * Consilium. * Concilium celebrare statuimus; in quo, aspirante Spiritu sancto, qui facit unanimes habitare in domo Domini, speramus, ut Ecclesiasticae pacis & unitatis status reformetur, & Dominus Papa Victor apostolicae Sedis gubernacula debeat obtinere. Verum quia hoc negotium tam arduum, tamque salubre, & tam necessarium, ubi de reconciliatione sanctae Ecclesiae, & salute totius Christianitatis in communi agitur, sine tuae discretionis praesentia consummari nec debet, nec potest, exorantes communis te in ea fide, quam debes Imperio & sanctae Dei Ecclesiae, & animae tuae, quatinus omni occasione summota apud Bisantium quarto die ante praedictum terminum familiariter, more Curiae, nobis occurras, ad Concilium nobiscum processurus, &c.
units.tr: Frederick, by the grace of God Emperor of the Romans and ever Augustus, to his faithful M., Bishop of Durham, his grace and every blessing. Since in the schism that exists in the Roman Church the whole world has been divided against itself, and all Christendom is shaken by no small disturbance, we, moved with compassion, grieve with the sorrows of the holy Church of God, desiring to apply a care and concern inclined to every counsel and aid, so that with the danger of all this dissension removed, the Church of God, just as it is joined in unity of faith, may also be gathered into one fold under the rule of one Shepherd. Hence it is that, by the counsel of the princes, we have resolved, together with our beloved kinsman Louis, the illustrious King of the Franks, to hold a council on the fourth day before the Kalends of September, that is, on the day of the Beheading of Saint John the Baptist, beside the river Saône (*Consilium / *Concilium); at which, with the Holy Spirit breathing upon us, who makes those of one mind to dwell in the house of the Lord, we hope that the state of ecclesiastical peace and unity may be restored, and that the lord Pope Victor may obtain the helm of the apostolic See. But since this matter is so arduous, so healthful, so necessary, in which the reconciliation of the holy Church and the salvation of all Christendom is at stake, it neither ought nor can be brought to completion without your discreet presence; therefore we beseech you, by that faith which you owe to the Empire, to the holy Church of God and to your own soul, that, every excuse set aside, you meet us familiarly at Bisantium four days before the said term, after the manner of the court, to go forward with us to the council, etc.
XVI.

units.la: De Concilio generali apud Bisantium celebrando pro recipiendo Victore Papa per Imperatorem confirmato, ab Ecclesiis Gallicanis.
units.tr: On Summoning a General Council at Besançon, to Receive Pope Victor, Confirmed by the Emperor, from the Gallican Churches.

units.la: FRIDERICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator & Semper-Augustus, fideli suo C. Augustanensi Episcopo, gratiam suam & omne bonum.
units.tr: FREDERICK, by the grace of God Roman Emperor and Ever-Augustus, to his faithful C., Bishop of Augsburg, his grace and every good thing.

units.la: 1. Inter varias & tumescentes tempestatum procellas, quibus jam diu navicula beati Petri fluctuata; & inter pressuras diversas, quibus sancta Dei Ecclesia frequenter afflicta & tribulata est, verus ille mediator Dei & hominum Christus Jesus, qui Ecclesiam suam velut unicam sponsam proprio charactere sui pretiosi sanguinis insignivit & redemit, consolationis gratiam, quam ascendens coelum fidelibus suis repromisit, inquiens: Non relinquam vos orphanos: ecce ego vobiscum sum omnibus usque ad consummationem saeculi, evidentibus & manifestis declarat indiciis. Ipse enim, sicut stella matutina in medio nunc oriens, solita pietate Ecclesiam suam in tribulatione respexit, & surgens imperavit ventis & mari, & facta est tranquillitas magna. Pro illa siquidem controversia, quae inter nos & Regem Francorum pro schismate Romanae Ecclesiae jam diu agitatur, aspirante Sancti Spiritus gratia, qui facit unanimes habitare in domo, mediantibus hinc inde Legatis, tandem pari voluntate & unanimi consensu inter nos convenit, quod nos videlicet, una cum Archiepiscopis, Episcopis & Pr. nibus ordinis ac vitae Religiosis, Baronibus, & universis Regni utriusque Principibus, iv. Kal. Septembr. in die Decollationis S. Johannis Baptistae, supra fluvium Saona, in Episcopatu Bisuntino, Concilium generale pariter celebraturi sumus, in quo Rex Francorum, dilectus consanguineus noster, cum nostris Archiepiscopis, Episcopis, & cum omnibus Regni sui Principibus, & tota Gallicana Ecclesia, reverendum Patrem nostrum Dominum Octavianum Papam, sicut per sacram ementa & firmissimas sanctiones praeordinatum est, in Apostolicum Universalem sanctae Dei Ecclesiae Pontificem recipiet, & debitam ei reverentiam exhibebit.
units.tr: 1. Amid the various and swelling storms by which the little ship of blessed Peter has long been tossed, and amid the diverse pressures by which the holy Church of God has often been afflicted and troubled, that true Mediator between God and men, Christ Jesus, who marked and redeemed his Church, as his only bride, with the distinguishing seal of his precious blood, shows by clear and manifest signs the grace of consolation that he promised to his faithful ones when he ascended into heaven, saying: I will not leave you orphans; behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age. For he, like the morning star now rising in the midst, has looked upon his Church in her tribulation with his accustomed mercy, and, rising up, has commanded the winds and the sea, and there was a great calm. Indeed, concerning that controversy which has for a long time been pursued between us and the King of the Franks over the schism of the Roman Church, by the breathing of the grace of the Holy Spirit, who makes those who dwell in one house to be of one mind, and through legates going back and forth on both sides, it has at last been agreed between us with equal will and unanimous consent that we, together with the archbishops, bishops, provosts and the religious of the orders of life, the barons, and all the princes of both kingdoms, shall hold a general council together on the fourth day before the Kalends of September, on the feast of the Beheading of St John the Baptist, beside the river Saône, in the diocese of Besançon. At that council, the King of the Franks, our beloved kinsman, together with our archbishops and bishops, with all the princes of his kingdom, and with the whole Gallican Church, will receive our reverend father, Lord Octavian, as Pope, just as he has been predestined by sacred decrees and most firm sanctions, as the universal Apostolic Pontiff of the holy Church of God, and will show him due reverence.

units.la: 2. Verum quia hoc negocium tam arduum, tamque salubre, & tam necessarium, ubi de reconciliatione sanctae Dei Ecclesiae, & totius salute Christianitatis in communi agitur, sine tuae discretionis praesentia, consummari nec debet nec potest, exoramus te in ea fide, quam Imperio & S. Dei Ecclesiae & animae tuae debes, quatenus omni occasione summota, cum sapientioribus & magis idoneis personis tuae dioecesis apud Bisuntium invadere praedictum terminum familiariter, more Curiae, nobis occurras, ad Concilium nobiscum processurus. Et quia abundans cautela non nocet, Milites tui, quos secum adduces, in armis & ornamentis munitos. Insuper & tentoria defetas, quae propter domorum raritatem necessaria sunt. Ibi enim per Dei totum negocium Domini Victoris Papae ad gloriam Dei, & ad pacem & unitatem sanctae Ecclesiae, & omnimodum honorem Imperii honesto fine terminabitur.
units.tr: 2. But since this matter, so arduous, so salutary, and so necessary, in which the reconciliation of the holy Church of God and the salvation of all Christendom in common are at stake, ought not and cannot be brought to completion without the presence of your discretion, we beg you, by the faith that you owe to the Empire, to the holy Church of God, and to your own soul, that, every hindrance removed, you come to meet us, familiarly and in the manner of the Court, together with the wiser and more suitable persons of your diocese, at Besançon, on the appointed day, to proceed with us to the council. And since excessive caution does no harm, let your soldiers, whom you will bring with you, be equipped with arms and gear. Furthermore, bring tents too, which are necessary because of the scarcity of houses. For there, by God's help, the whole business of Lord Pope Victor will be brought to an honourable end, to the glory of God, to the peace and unity of the holy Church, and to the full honour of the Empire.

units.la: 3. Denique omnibus in Ordine Clericali constitutis scribimus, suadendo & rogando, quatenus ad praefatum Concilium veniant, aut ruentibus rebus suis succurrant.
units.tr: 3. Finally, we write to all who hold office in the clerical order, urging and requesting that they come to the aforesaid council, or else come to the aid of their affairs, which are falling into ruin.

units.la: XVIII.
units.tr: XVIII.

units.la: De exsequendis Decretis Comitiorum Herbipolensium super confirmatione & receptione Pa- schalis Papae, & damnatione Alexandri Pseudopapae.
units.tr: On Carrying Out the Decrees of the Diet of Würzburg concerning the Confirmation and Reception of Pope Paschal, and the Condemnation of the Pseudopope Alexander.

units.la: FRIDERICUS Dei gratia Romanus Imperator & Semper-Augustus, dilecto fideli & consanguineo suo Henrico Comiti Trecarum, gratiam suam & omne bonum.
units.tr: FREDERICK, by the grace of God Roman Emperor and Ever-Augustus, to his beloved faithful kinsman Henry, Count of Troyes, his grace and every good thing.

units.la: 1. Cunctis populis, quos clementiae nostrae regit Imperium, jam dudum innotuisse credimus, qualiter exorta quondam inter Ecclesiae Romanae Cardinales de Apostolatu discordia, in Reges & regna imperii pestifero est diffusa, pro qua ad optabile pacis bonum revocanda, quantos post beatae memoriae Papae Victoris electionem ac confirmationem Catholicam, Papiae, Laudae, Mediolani, Laodicenque in diversis Imperii finibus, in corpore nostro labores tam nos, quam invicti Principes nostri pertulerimus, quantas rerum copias zelo justitiae impenderimus, in extremis quoque mundi partibus jam audiri non dubitamus. Denique beatissimo Papa Victore ad Paradisi gaudia assumpto, & in ejus locum Episcopis Cardinalibus almae Sedis Apostolicae, Domino Paschali viro Christianissimo in praesentia Episcoporum & Religiosorum Lombardiae ac Tusciae, Illustris quoque Praefecti Urbis Romae, Nobilium Romanorum, Catholice substituto, ipsum etiam Dominum Paschale, ex Ecclesiae Principum Imperii judicio atque consilio in Papam & Patrem Catholicum solenniter recepimus, debito honore veneravit semper intendimus. Proinde obstinata Schismaticorum perfidia, morte viri justi, falsis successibus aperta fronte adscribens, Syreneis suis blanditiis fidelium quorundam nostrorum animos adeo molita est de novo immutare, ut nisi morbis novis nova maturius remedia objicerentur, nostrorum non modica videretur ex fiducia nostrae lenitatis seducenda.
units.tr: 1. We believe that it has long been known to all the peoples whom the Empire of our clemency rules how, after the dispute that arose among the Cardinals of the Roman Church concerning the Apostolate, a pestilential division spread among the kings and kingdoms of the Empire; and we do not doubt that it is now heard in the farthest parts of the world how much labour, both we and our unconquered princes endured in our own persons, and how great a supply of resources we expended out of zeal for justice, in order to recall that dispute to the desired good of peace, in the various regions of the Empire, at Pavia, Lodi, Milan and Laon, after the election and Catholic confirmation of Pope Victor of blessed memory. Finally, when that most blessed Pope Victor was taken up into the joys of Paradise, and in his place the bishops and cardinals of the sacred Apostolic See, in the presence of the bishops and religious of Lombardy and Tuscany, and likewise of the illustrious Prefect of the City of Rome and the Roman nobles, as a Catholic substitute, chose the most Christian Lord Paschal, we, by the judgment and counsel of the princes of the Church of the Empire, also solemnly received that same Lord Paschal as Pope and Catholic Father, and we have always intended to honour him with due reverence. Accordingly, the obstinate treachery of the schismatics, openly ascribing the death of a just man to false successes, has so laboured with its siren flatteries that it has begun anew to change the minds of some of our faithful, so that unless new remedies were applied more promptly to these new diseases, a not inconsiderable number of our people would seem likely to be led astray through trust in our mildness.

units.la: 2. Igitur zelo reformandi decoris domus Dei ardentius accensi, cum Regem Francorum, qui nulla nostra culpa praeunte, una cum Rulando Imperii nostri hoste publico, ejusque sequacibus, Imperium nostrum honorem manifeste molitur auferre, post multos nostros ammonitus irrevocabilem persensisse mus, universis Imperii nostri Principibus in sancto Pentecostes Curiam generalem Wirceburc indiximus, quorum coetu celeberrimo ibidem solenniter praesidente, Ecclesiae Dei statum, ac Domini Paschalis Papae negotium, sedulo ac magnifice duximus roborandum. Invocata igitur devotis Spiritus sancti gratia, & universorum qui aderant consilio communicato, ad removendam pro re nostra omnem ambiguitatem ipsi nos manu propria super Sanctorum reliquias juramentum publice praestitimus, quod Rollandum Schismaticum, vel ejus successorem, quem pars ipsius elegerit, pro papam nunquam recipiemus, nec ad eum recipiendum assensum unquam alicui praebebimus. Nullorum fautorum ejus gratiam nostram unquam * rescindemus, nisi ab errore viae suae ad unitatem Ecclesiae suae fuerit conversus. Dominum vero Paschalem Papam manutenebimus semper atque promovebimus, eique tanquam Patri Catholico & universali Pontifici obedientiam, honorem ac reverentiam exhibebimus, & ab ipso ejusque parte (vita comite) nunquam recedemus. Electos quoque, qui sub ejus successore, quem pars ipsius elegerit, consecrationem receperint, honore aut ordinibus suis ejus obedientia privari nunquam permittemus, & hujus absolutionem sacramenti nunquam ademus, nec oblatam recipiemus.
units.tr: 2. Therefore, burning more ardently with zeal to restore the beauty of the house of God, when, after many admonitions from us, we perceived that the King of the Franks, who, without any fault of ours, and with Roland, a public enemy of our Empire, and his followers, openly seeks to take away the honour of our Empire, could not be turned back, we summoned a general court of all the princes of our Empire at Würzburg on the holy feast of Pentecost. With that most crowded assembly presiding there in solemn fashion, we resolved to strengthen with care and dignity the state of the Church of God and the business of Lord Pope Paschal. Therefore, with the grace of the Holy Spirit invoked in devotion, and with the counsel of all who were present having been shared, in order to remove every ambiguity concerning our position, we ourselves, with our own hand upon the relics of the saints, publicly swore an oath that we would never receive Roland the schismatic, or his successor whom his party may choose, as pope, and that we would never give our assent to anyone receiving him. We would never restore the favour of any of his supporters, unless he had been turned from the error of his way to the unity of his Church. But we will always maintain and advance Lord Pope Paschal, and we will show him obedience, honour and reverence as to a Catholic Father and universal Pontiff, and we will never withdraw from him and his party (while life remains). Likewise, we will never permit those elected who have received consecration under his successor, whom his party has chosen, to be deprived of their honour or orders because of their obedience to him, nor will we take away the absolution of this sacrament, nor will we accept what is offered.

units.la: 3. Praeterea noster in Imperio successor, quem Principes universi elegerint, hunc honorem Ecclesiae Dei & Imperio, & hanc partem nostram sub eodem juramento tuebitur semper atque tenebit.
units.tr: 3. Moreover, our successor in the Empire, whom all the princes shall elect, will likewise always defend and maintain this honour of the Church of God and of the Empire, and this our part, under the same oath.

units.la: 4. Idem quoque juramentum Archiepiscopi omnes & Episcopi, atque Electi, qui interfuerunt XL. super sancta Dei Evangelia manu propria, unusquisque sub stola sua praestiterunt, & puverunt. Nihilo minus Principes seculares universi, Dux videlicet Saxoniae, ac Bavarus, Marchio senior, Conradus Palatinus Comes de Rheno, & Ludovicus Landgravius, & reliqui super Sanctorum reliquias publice id ipsum juraverunt. Repente autem Spiritus sanctus mentem adeo fecit unius voluntatis, quod Electi omnes, qui praesentes aderant, primo Reinoldus Coloniensis Electus & Italiae Archicancellarius, deinde caeteri omnes in Sabbatho Quatuor temporum Dei & honorem Imperii, sacros Ordines devotissime susceperunt.
units.tr: 4. All the archbishops and bishops, and the elect who were present, likewise swore and pledged the same oath upon the holy Gospels of God, each with his own hand, under his stole, to the number of forty. Nevertheless, all the secular princes, namely the Duke of Saxony, the Bavarian, the senior Margrave, Conrad, Count Palatine of the Rhine, and Louis, Landgrave, and the rest, publicly swore the same thing upon the relics of the saints. Then suddenly the Holy Spirit made the minds of all the elect who were present so united in one will that, first Reinold, Elect of Cologne and Archchancellor of Italy, and then all the others, most devoutly received the holy orders on the Saturday of the Ember days, for the honour of God and of the Empire.

units.la: 5. Firmiter quoque a nobis & ab universis decretum est, ut quicunque supersunt ordinandi, in Quatuor temporibus similiter exequantur: alioquin dignitatis, ad quam electi sunt, honore, mota dilatione, priventur.
units.tr: 5. We and all others have also firmly decreed that whoever remain to be ordained shall likewise be ordained during the Ember days; otherwise, without further delay, they shall be deprived of the dignity to which they have been elected.

units.la: 6. Adhoc Honorabiles Legati Illustris amici nostri Henrici gloriosi Anglorum Regis, ad nos transmissi, in totius Curiae nostrae praesentia, super Sanctorum reliquias ex parte Regis Angliae nobis juraverunt, quod Rex ipse cum toto Regno suo in parte nostra fideliter stabit, Dominum Paschalem, quem nos tenemus, tenebit: de Rolando autem Schismatico manutenendo de caetero se intromittet.
units.tr: 6. In addition, honourable legates sent to us by our illustrious friend Henry, the glorious King of the English, swore to us in the presence of our whole court, upon the relics of the saints, on behalf of the King of England, that the King himself, with his whole kingdom, would stand faithfully on our side and would hold to Lord Paschal, whom we hold; and that henceforth he would not meddle in maintaining Roland the schismatic.

units.la: 7. Quia vero justitiae, quam hostes Ecclesiae ac nostri, sive superbia, sive ex causae suae diffidentia averunt, nos semper hactenus stare parati, nunc tandem ad insolita sacramenta, ex eorum manifesta
units.tr: 7. Since we have always hitherto been ready to stand by justice, which the enemies of the Church and ours have turned away from, whether through pride or through distrust of their own cause, now at last, if they force us by their manifest and unaccustomed oaths, ...

units.la: * leg. reddemus. nisi festa obstinatione, simus impulsi, à Schismaticorum communione omnis homo, excommunicatus sit. Favorem enim illorum, etsi aliquomodo visus est venialis, in posterum prorsus erit intolerabilis.
units.tr: * [Read: reddemus.] Unless we are driven by their fixed obstinacy, let every man be excommunicated from communion with the schismatics. For their favour, although it seemed in some way a venial matter, will in future be utterly intolerable.

units.la: 8. Ad perfectum vero hujus negotii firmamentum, ex totius Herbipolensis Ciuitatis ... firmissime praecipimus, ut si quis ad sui mandatum Antistitis aut Praesidis Provinciae, vel Domini sacramentum supradictum non praestiterit, si Clericus sit aut Monachus, Ecclesiastico privetur beneficio; si Laicus, allodia & beneficia, quaecunque possidet, nostra ipsi auctoritate à suo Judice vel Domino prorsus admittantur.
units.tr: 8. For the perfect confirmation of this business, ... we most firmly command that if anyone, at the command of his bishop or the governor of the province, or of his lord, has not given the aforesaid oath, then if he is a cleric or monk he shall be deprived of his ecclesiastical benefice; if he is a layman, all the allodial property and benefices which he holds shall, by our own authority, be wholly taken from him by his judge or lord.
XIX.

units.la: De Duce Burgundiae adversus injurias Regis Franciae per Imperium tuendo.
units.tr: On defending the Duke of Burgundy against the injuries of the King of France through the Empire.

units.la: FRIDERICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator, Semper Augustus, dilecto & fideli suo Henrico Comiti Trecatum gratiam suam & omne bonum. Audivimus, unde plurimum gaudemus, dolemus, quod Rex videlicet Franciae in proximo festo sancti Johannis terram Ducis Burgundiae nostri dilecti, & nostri obligati, hostiliter invadere atque destruere proponit. Quod nos nullatenus possumus aut debemus sustinere. Unde tuam dilectionem, cui plenarie confidimus, toto animo exhortamur, & summopere postulamus, quatenus pro nostro amore ipsum Regem ab hoc proposito modis omnibus retrahas & impedias, & ne per te vel per tuos ipsi Duci aliquod damnum vel injuriam proveniat, te ipsum à consilio & auxilio Regis subtrahas, nec Duci noceas. Quod si Rex hac intentione desistere vel supersedere noluerit, scias pro certo, quod non patiemur nec sustinebimus, immo ei resistendo amicum nostrum Ducem cum toto robore Imperii nostri juvare, custodire & defendere. Veruntamen si inter Ducem & matrem ejus aliqua quaestio, quae tendit ad discordiam orta est vel fuerit, nos una cecum ad eandem quaestionem componendam satis ex abundanti paratos esse possumus.
units.tr: FREDERICK, by the grace of God Emperor of the Romans, ever Augustus, to his beloved and faithful Henry, Count of Troyes, his grace and every good. We have heard, and we rejoice and grieve greatly at it, that the King of France proposes to invade and lay waste with hostile force, at the feast of St John next, the land of Duke of Burgundy, our beloved and our liegeman. This we can in no way bear or ought to allow. Therefore we earnestly exhort your affection, in which we place full trust, with all our heart, and we most strongly request that, for love of us, you restrain and hinder the King himself from this purpose by every means, and that no harm or injury come to the Duke through you or your people; that you withdraw yourself from the counsel and aid of the King and do no injury to the Duke. But if the King is unwilling to desist or to delay in this purpose, know for certain that we will not suffer or endure it; rather, by resisting him, we will help, protect and defend our friend the Duke with the whole strength of our Empire. Yet if any dispute which tends toward discord has arisen or shall arise between the Duke and his mother, we are more than ready to settle that same dispute once and for all.
XX.

units.la: De Represaliis contra Regis Franciae subditos in Imperio concedendis, si Imperialis ho- mines in Francia laedantur.
units.tr: On Granting Reprisals against the Subjects of the King of France in the Empire, if Imperial Men Are Harmed in France.

units.la: GLORIOSO & Magnifico Ludovico Regi Francorum, N. Christi Dei gratia Imperialis Aulae Cancellarius, & Legatus Italiae, salutem & servitium suum. Ratio suggerit, & Principum fuerudo depoleat, ut quemadmodum Regni vestri negotiatores per Romanum Imperium pacem & securitate fruuntur, ita vestra vice nostri nullatenus sub vestra jurisdictione laedantur. Quia igitur Mediolanensis Vicecomes quosdam nostros mercatores injuste exspoliavit, & unum ex eis in carcerem & compeditum, petimus & ex parte Augusti Serenissimi vestram Excellentiam commonemus, ut hominem & res detentas reddi faciatis. Alioquin si damna illius modi per vestros negotiatores illata refarcita, aut si novum telonenum ad damnum resarciendum super vestros mercatores fuerit constitutum, vestra discretio non gravetur.
units.tr: To the glorious and magnificent Louis, King of the Franks, N., by the grace of Christ God Chancellor of the Imperial Court and Legate of Italy, greeting and his service. Reason suggests, and the form of princely courtesy demands, that just as the merchants of your kingdom enjoy peace and security throughout the Roman Empire, so our merchants should in turn not be harmed in any way under your jurisdiction. Since the Viscount of Milan has unjustly despoiled some of our merchants, and has thrown one of them into prison and fettered him, we ask, and on behalf of the most serene Emperor we admonish your Excellency, that you cause the man and the goods detained to be restored. Otherwise, if the losses of this kind inflicted by your merchants are made good, or if a new toll has been set up upon your merchants to make good the loss, let your discretion not be burdened.

units.la: FRIDERICI I. IMPER. AUG. LAUDUM.
units.tr: Of Frederick I, Emperor Augustus: Judgments

units.la: Super Ducatu Bavariae & Marchionatu Superioris Austriae.
units.tr: Concerning the Duchy of Bavaria and the Margraviate of Upper Austria.

units.la: FRIDERICUS divina favente clementia Romanorum Imperator Semper-Augustus. Quam rerum commutatio ex ipsa corporali institutione possit firma constitere, vel eaque leguntur vel geruntur, nulla valeant refragatione convelli; ne qua tamen possit esse gestarum dubitatas, nostra debet Imperialis auctoritas praecavere.
units.tr: Frederick, by the favour of divine clemency, Emperor of the Romans, ever Augustus. So that the things that are read or done, however firmly their arrangement may stand on its own material basis, may be overturned by no objection, and so that no doubt may arise about what has been done, our imperial authority ought to take precaution.

units.la: 1. Noverit igitur omnium Christi Imperiique nostri fidelium praesens aetas, & futura posteritas, qualiter nos, ejus cooperante gratia, à quo coelinus pax nulla est hominibus super terram, in nostra Curia Ratisponae, in nativitate sanctae Mariae celebrata, in praesentia multorum Religiosorum & Catholicorum Principum, item & controversiam, quae inter dilectissimum patruum nostrum Heinricum Ducem Austriae, & Karissimum nepotem nostrum Heinricum Ducem Saxoniae, dimissa exstitit super Ducatu Bavariae, & super Marchia à superiori fluminis parte Anasi, terminavimus modo. Quod Dux Austriae resignavit nobis Ducatum Bavariae & dictam Marchiam, quatenus, nos, Qua resignatione facta, mox eundem Ducatum Bavariae in beneficium contulimus Duci Austriae. Dux autem Bavariae resignavit nobis Marchiam Austriae cum omni jure suo, & cum omnibus beneficiis, quae quondam Marchio Liupoldus habebat ad Ducatum Bavariae.
units.tr: 1. Let the present age and future posterity of all the faithful of Christ and of our Empire therefore know that we, by the cooperating grace of him from whom there is no heavenly peace for men upon earth, have now settled, in our Court at Regensburg, celebrated on the Nativity of St. Mary, in the presence of many religious and Catholic princes, the controversy which had been left pending between our most beloved uncle Henry, Duke of Austria, and our dearest nephew Henry, Duke of Saxony, concerning the Duchy of Bavaria and the march beyond the upper part of the river Enns. The Duke of Austria resigned to us the Duchy of Bavaria and the said march; that resignation having been made, we at once conferred the same Duchy of Bavaria as a fief upon the Duke of Austria. The Duke of Bavaria, for his part, resigned to us the march of Austria with all his right, and with all the benefits which the late Margrave Leopold had held in connection with the Duchy of Bavaria.

units.la: 2. Ne autem in hoc facto honor & gloria patrui nostri charissimi aliquatenus minuatur, consilio & judicio Principum, Illustri Uladislao Duce Bohemiae sententiam promulgante, & aliis Principibus approbantibus, Marchiam Austriae in Ducatum commutavimus, & eundem Ducatum cum omni jure, praefato patruo nostro Heinrico, & praenobilissimae uxori suae Theodorae, in beneficium concessimus, percipiunt jure sancientes, ut ipsi & liberi eorum post eos indifferenter filii eundem Ducatum Austriae haereditario jure à Regno teneant & possideant. 5. Si autem prædicta Dux Austriæ, patruus noster, & uxor ejus absque liberis decesserint, liberum habeant eundem Ducatum afficiendi, cui voluerint.
units.tr: 2. So that the honour and glory of our most dear uncle may in no way be diminished by this act, by the counsel and judgment of the princes, with Duke Ladislaus of Bohemia pronouncing the sentence and the other princes approving, we have converted the march of Austria into a duchy, and have granted that same duchy, with all right, as a fief to our aforesaid uncle Henry and to his most noble wife Theodora; decreeing by law that they and their children after them, sons alike, shall hold and possess the same Duchy of Austria from the Kingdom by hereditary right. 5. If, however, the aforesaid Duke of Austria, our uncle, and his wife die without children, they shall have free power to bestow the same duchy on whomsoever they wish.

units.la: 6. Statuimus quoque, ut nulla magna persona in ejusdem Ducatus regimine sine Ducum consensu vel potestate, aliquam justitiam præsumat exercere.
units.tr: 6. We also decree that no great person in the government of that same duchy shall presume to exercise any jurisdiction without the consent or authority of the dukes.

units.la: 7. Dux vero Austriæ de Ducatu suo aliud servitium non debet Imperio, nisi quòd ad Curias, quas Imperator præfixerit in Bavaria, evocatus veniat: nullamque expeditionem debeat, nisi forte quam in Regna vel provincias Austriæ vicinas ordinaverit.
units.tr: 7. The Duke of Austria, moreover, owes the Empire no other service from his duchy, except that he come when summoned to the courts which the Emperor shall appoint in Bavaria; and he owes no expedition, unless perhaps one which he shall order into the kingdoms or provinces neighbouring Austria.

units.la: Ut autem hæc nostra constitutio omni ævo rata & inconvulsa permaneat, præsentem inde paginam conscribi, & sigilli nostri impressione munigiri jussimus, adhibitis testibus idoneis, quorum nomina hæc: Pilgrinus Aquilegiensis Patriarcha. Eberhardus Archiepiscopus Salisburgensis. Otto Episcopus Frisingensis. Conradus Episcopus Brixinensis. Heinricus Episcopus Ratisbonensis, & Tridentinensis. Dominus Welpho Dux Spoletæ. Conradus frater Imperatoris [Dux Sueviæ.] Fridericus filius Regis * Conradi [Dux Sueviæ.] Heinricus Dux Carinthiæ. Marchio Engelbertus de Istria. Marchio Albertus de Baden. [alii habent, de Stachen, sive Staden.] Diepoldus Marchio de Voburg. Otto Comes Palatinus [sc. de Wittelinspach] & frater ejus Fridericus. Gebhardus Comes de Sultzbach. Engelbertus Comes de Hail. Gebhardus Comes de Burckhausen: & alii quam plures.
units.tr: So that this our constitution may remain valid and unshaken for all time, we have ordered that the present document be drawn up and secured with the impression of our seal, with suitable witnesses present, whose names are these: Pilgrim, Patriarch of Aquileia. Eberhard, Archbishop of Salzburg. Otto, Bishop of Freising. Conrad, Bishop of Brixen. Henry, Bishop of Regensburg and of Trent. Lord Welf, Duke of Spoleto. Conrad, brother of the Emperor [Duke of Swabia]. Frederick, son of King Conrad [Duke of Swabia]. Henry, Duke of Carinthia. Margrave Engelbert of Istria. Margrave Albert of Baden [others have of Stachen or Staden]. Diepold, Margrave of Vohburg. Count Palatine Otto [namely of Wittelsbach] and his brother Frederick. Count Gebhard of Sulzbach. Count Engelbert of Hail. Count Gebhard of Burghausen, and very many others.

units.la: Signum Domini FRIDERICI Imperatoris invictissimi.
units.tr: Sign of the lord Frederick, most invincible Emperor.

units.la: Ego Reinaldus Cancellarius vice Arnoldi Moguntinensis Archiepiscopi & Archicancellarii, recognovi: regnante Domino FRIDERICO Rom. Imp. in Christo. Datum Ratisbonæ 15. Cal. Octobr. indictione quarta, anno Dominicæ Incarnationis MCLVI, anno Regni ejus quinto, Imperii secundo.
units.tr: I, Reinald, Chancellor, on behalf of Arnold, Archbishop of Mainz and Archchancellor, have recognised this. In the reign of the lord Frederick, Roman Emperor, in Christ. Given at Regensburg, 15 days before the Kalends of October, in the fourth indiction, in the year of the Lord's Incarnation 1156, in the fifth year of his reign and the second of his Empire.

units.la: PACTUM QVOD PEPIGERVNT ROMANI CVM DO- MINO FRIDERICO IMPERATORE ET Semper Augusto.
units.tr: The Pact Which the Romans Made with the Lord Frederick, Emperor and Ever Augustus.

units.la: IURAVERUNT præsentes, & jurabunt futuri SENATORES & totus POPULUS ROMANUS Domino FRIDERICO Imperatori fidelitatem, & quod juvabunt cum coronam Imperii Romanum retinere, & defendere eum contra omnes homines: & justitias suas tam intra Urbem, quàm extra juvabunt eum retinere, & quod nunquam erunt tam in consilio quàm in facto, ubi Dominus Imperator malâ captione capiatur, vel membrum perdat, vel aliquod detrimentum in persona patiatur: & quod Senatum non nisi per eum vel per Nuncium suum convocabunt, sine fraude & malo ingenio.
units.tr: The present senators and the whole Roman people have sworn, and future senators and people will swear, fidelity to the Lord Emperor Frederick; that they will help him to retain the Roman imperial crown and defend him against all men; and that they will help him to keep his rights both within the City and outside it. They will never be party, either in counsel or in deed, to any plot by which the Lord Emperor may be taken by treachery, lose a limb, or suffer some harm to his person. They will not convene the Senate except through him or his envoy, without deceit or evil design.

units.la: Dominus Imperator confirmabit Senatum perpetuo in eo vigore, in quo nunc est, & augebit ut tenore, ut Senatus per eum ordinetur, & ei subjectus fiat, & faciet inde privilegium cum sigillo, in quo continentur hæc, videlicet confirmatio Senatus, & quod faciet salva omnia jura Populi Romani, quantum ad Imperatorem pertinet, quod ea illis non auferet, & Urbis, & locationis libellos tertii & quarti generis conservabit, & præcipiet in eodem privilegio nulli aufferri Romanis in toto Imperio suo plateaticum, portaticum, aut ripaticum: & si aliquis fort. quis ausu ipsum auferre, incidat in poenam centum librarum auri.
units.tr: The Lord Emperor will confirm the Senate in perpetuity in the authority it now holds, and will enlarge it in such a way that the Senate is appointed through him and made subject to him. He will issue a privilege under seal containing these terms: the confirmation of the Senate, and that he will keep all the rights of the Roman people intact so far as they pertain to the Emperor, and will not take them away from them. He will also preserve the charters of the third and fourth kind concerning the City and its leases, and by the same privilege he will command that no one shall take from the Romans anywhere in his empire the toll on streets, the toll on gates, or the toll on riverbanks. If anyone should perhaps presume to take it, he shall incur a penalty of one hundred pounds of gold.

units.la: Hæc omnia cum subscriptione Principum Curiæ fient.
units.tr: All these things shall be done with the signature of the princes of the Court.

units.la: FRIDERICI I. IMPER. AUG. DECRETVM
units.tr: FRIDERICI I. IMPER. AUG. DECRETVM

units.la: De duobus schismaticis Archiepiscopis Salisburgensibus removendis, & novo absque confirmato & investito recipiendo.
units.tr: On the removal of the two schismatic Archbishops of Salzburg, and the receiving of a new one without confirmation and investiture.

units.la: FRIDERICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator & Semper Augustus, dilectis suis omnibus Ministerialibus Salzburgensis Ecclesiæ, & universo clero & populo ipsius Ecclesiæ, Carinthiam & Marchiam (Stirensem) constitutis, gratiam suam & omne bonum.
units.tr: FREDERICK, by the grace of God Roman Emperor and ever Augustus, to his beloved ministerials of the Church of Salzburg, and to the whole clergy and people of the same Church, dwelling in Carinthia and the March (of Styria), his grace and every good.

units.la: 1. Cùm tuam monemus, ut de honore Imperii nostri, sicut alii Principes & fideles nostri, cogites & dd. xiv. die post Pascha cum honesta militia ad nos Papiæ venias, certus existens, quòd nulli expeditionem remittemus, quamvis multi quæriant absolvi: & quicunque remanebit, contra voluntatem remanebit. Si vero ante hunc terminum nos videre volueris, gratum valde est; tamen hoc pro constanti habere debes & tenere, quòd ab expeditione tuam personam nullo absolvemus.
units.tr: 1. We admonish you to think of the honour of our Empire, as do the other princes and our faithful, and to come to us at Pavia with honourable soldiery on the fourteenth day after Easter. Be assured that we shall remit the expedition to no one, though many seek to be released; whoever stays behind will stay against our will. If indeed you wish to see us before this term, it is very welcome. Yet you ought to hold and keep this as certain: that we shall absolve your person from the expedition to no one.

units.la: II. Super eadem expeditione Italica.
units.tr: II. Concerning the same Italian expedition.

units.la: FRIDERICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator & Semper-Augustus, Eberhardo Salzburgensi Archiepiscopo, gratiam suam & omne bonum. Tuam experientiam minime latere credimus, non pro cumulandis divitiis ad usum nostrum aut filiorum nostrorum, sed solummodo ad reformationem, & augmentum Imperii, dispendio tam rerum nostrarum, quàm in fidelium instantia, etiam attritione proprii corporis laborassemus incessanter. Nunc vero, quia contumaciam Dialanensium à primaevo pacis inimicorum, & Ecclesiarum temeratorum, bono nostro proposito, instinctu Diaboli, obstare pro viribus nituntur, te unà cum aliis Principibus, cæterisque Imperii fidelibus subsidium nostrum evocare decrevimus. Unde dilectioni tuæ mandamus, atque sub debito fidelitatis præcipimus, quatenus omni occasione postposita, cùm membrum Imperii censeatis, & hoc fidelis extitisti, ne Regnum aliquatenus in tempore nostro vacilllet, & diminutionem sentiat, litteræ tuæ xiv. die post Paschæ Papiæ exercitui nostro accedas. Nam quicunque nobis in auxilium venerint, nos & successores nostros ditare & sublimare diligenter intendere in cunctantem sciat, quod toti negotio nostro cum victoria brevi (ut arbitramur) Dei nutu imponemus. Si quis autem temporis aliquatenus subtraxerit, hunc nec nobis nec Imperio nostro fideles esse censeamus.
units.tr: FREDERICK, by the grace of God Roman Emperor and ever Augustus, to Eberhard, Archbishop of Salzburg, his grace and every good. We believe your experience is not unaware that we have laboured incessantly, not to heap up riches for our own use or that of our sons, but only for the reform and increase of the Empire, at the expense of our own resources and in the urgent service of the faithful, even to the wearing down of our own body. Now, because the obstinacy of the Dialanenses, enemies of peace from the beginning and violators of the Churches, by the prompting of the Devil, strive with all their strength to hinder our good purpose, we have decided to call for your aid, together with the other princes and the remaining faithful of the Empire. Therefore we command your affection, and under the bond of fidelity we order, that, every excuse set aside, since you are counted a member of the Empire and have always been faithful, you come with your letters to our army at Pavia on the fourteenth day after Easter, lest the kingdom waver in any way in our time and suffer diminution. For let whoever comes to our aid know that we diligently intend to enrich and exalt him and our successors. Let the one who hesitates know that we shall bring the whole business to a conclusion with victory soon, as we judge, by the will of God. If anyone withdraws himself at all from this time, we judge him faithful neither to us nor to our Empire.

units.la: III. De Concilio per Imperatorem Cremæ indicto ad tollendum schisma Papale.
units.tr: III. On the Council called by the Emperor at Cremona to remove the Papal schism.

units.la: FRIDERICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator Semper-Augustus, fideli suo Ebenerabili Salzburgensi Archiepiscopo, gratiam suam & omne bonum.
units.tr: FREDERICK, by the grace of God Roman Emperor and ever Augustus, to his faithful Venerable Archbishop of Salzburg, his grace and every good.

units.la: 1. Quanto majori largitate antecessorum nostrorum, Regum & Imperatorum, Ecclesia Salzburgensem decoratam, fuisse cognovimus, eò majori pietate & ampliori dilectione, dignitatem Salzburgensis Ecclesiæ semper fovere studuimus, & omnibus modis promovere. Inde cùm nos quam de excellentiori & clarissimo Principe nostro, plurimum sperarèmus, & in tuæ fidelitatis constantia, in necessitatibus sanctæ Ecclesiæ Dei & Imperii, non modicam fiduciam habere eimus, ut Ecclesiæ Dei in pendulo nutaret, ad Papiensem Curiam, ubi tam Ecclesiastici Principes quam seculares, pro gloria Dei & honore Imperii promovendo solenniter convenientes, tuam personam apicibus nostris & nuntiis evocavimus; & quare non veneris, admodum nos admirati sumus.
units.tr: 1. By how much greater the generosity of our predecessors, kings and emperors, we have learned the Church of Salzburg was adorned, by so much greater piety and fuller affection have we always striven to cherish and in every way to promote the dignity of the Church of Salzburg. Therefore, since we hoped very much from your most excellent and illustrious person, and have no small confidence in the constancy of your fidelity in the necessities of the holy Church of God and of the Empire, lest the Church of God hang tottering in the balance, we summoned your person by our letters and messengers to the court at Pavia, where ecclesiastical and secular princes gather solemnly to promote the glory of God and the honour of the Empire. And we have been greatly astonished that you did not come.

units.la: 2. Præterea indicto generali Concilio pro necessitatibus Imperii & Ecclesiæ celebrando Dominica Vocem jucunditatis tuam sanctitatem, tuam reverentiam scriptis & nuntiis iteratò invitamus, & attentissimè rogavimus, ut diligenter perpendis schismatibus & pressuris, in quibus sancta Ecclesia fluctuans laborabat, tuam laudabilem præsentiam sacro Conventui exhiberes, & ad remedium de medio tanti mali scandala prudentiæ tuæ consilium opemque necessariam negotio tam arduo negares: sed ne sic tuam personam evocare valuimus.
units.tr: 2. Moreover, with a general council called to be held for the needs of the Empire and the Church, on the Sunday Vocem jucunditatis, we have again invited your holiness and your reverence by writing and by messengers, and most earnestly asked that you weigh carefully the schisms and distresses in which the holy Church, tossed about, was labouring, and that you would present your praiseworthy presence to the sacred assembly, and not deny the counsel and necessary help of your prudence in so arduous a matter, for the remedy that would remove so great an evil. But we have not been able to summon your person in this way.

units.la: 3. Unde quia tua res agitur, paries cùm proximus ardet, & quia publicares ista fuit, non (nam de animarum salute agebatur) miramur nos primitùs. Mirantur & universi Principes Seculares quàm Ecclesiastici, qui ad excolendam vineam Dei non timuerunt portare pondus æstus, quare te subtraxeris, & magna suspicione te suspectum habent, quòd in tempore tribulationis ipsum quasi murum inexpugnabilem pro domo Israel non opposueris. Mandamus itaque, tuam monentes & studiosius te rogantes, ut remota omni occasione & dilatione tuam ipsius praesentiam in proximam Nativitatem sanctæ Dei Genetricis Mariæ nobis & Curiæ nostræ exhibere non differas Cremæ, assumpto tecum fideli nostro Venerabili Episcopo Brixiensi.
units.tr: 3. Hence, since your own affair is at stake, when the neighbouring wall is burning, and since this was made public (for it concerned the salvation of souls), we first wonder, and not without reason. All the secular princes as well as the ecclesiastical, who did not fear to bear the heat of the day to cultivate the vineyard of God, also wonder why you withdrew, and they hold you under great suspicion that in the time of tribulation you did not set yourself up as an impregnable wall for the house of Israel. We therefore command, admonishing you and asking you more earnestly, that, every excuse and delay set aside, you not delay to present your person to us and to our court at Cremona by the next Nativity of Holy Mary, Mother of God, taking with you our faithful Venerable Bishop of Brescia.

units.la: IV. Archiepiscopus ad expeditionem evocatur sub pœna proscriptionis & depositionis.
units.tr: IV. The Archbishop is summoned to the expedition under penalty of proscription and deposition.

units.la: FRIDERICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator Semper-Augustus, Eberhardo Venerabili Salzburgensi Archiepiscopo, gratiam suam & omne bonum.
units.tr: FREDERICK, by the grace of God Roman Emperor and ever Augustus, to Eberhard, Venerable Archbishop of Salzburg, his grace and every good.

units.la: 1. Cum sacri Imperii nostri dispositio consilio Principum, & maximè Religiosorum, indigeat, cur toties rogatus à nobis & diligenter invitatus, semel saltem ad festum beatæ Mariæ Virginis venire noluerit, de prudentia tua satis mirari non possumus, sed & universis Principibus admodum videtur extraneum.
units.tr: 1. Since the arrangement of our holy Empire needs the counsel of princes, and especially of religious men, we cannot sufficiently wonder at your prudence: why, though asked by us so often and invited diligently, you were unwilling to come even once, at least for the feast of the blessed Virgin Mary. It seems exceedingly strange to all the princes as well.

units.la: 2. Præterea cùm Salzburgensis Ecclesia tanto amplioris servitii debito teneatur Imperio amplius ab Imperiali munificentia ita præ cæteris ditata & exaltata, collatis sibi beneficiis, & gaudere diuscitur, miramur, & de ratione non videmus, quare in summis Imperii necessitatibus tanto jam tempore tam fortiter, auxiliante Deo, insudavimus & insudamus, tantum defectum perferre debeamus.
units.tr: 2. Moreover, since the Church of Salzburg is bound by a much greater debt of service to the Empire, having been adorned and exalted beyond the others by imperial munificence, and has long enjoyed the benefices conferred upon it, we marvel and do not see the reason why, in the Empire's greatest necessities, we have for so long laboured, and still labour strongly with God's help, while you must bear such a lack.

units.la: 3. Cum igitur quantumcunque Religioni ab ipsa veritate, quæ sunt Cæsaris, Cæsari reddere dignitatis non solum qualicunq; pecunia, sed & personis & armatura laboribus nostris adiuvare. Imperialia scripta tuae fidelitati tam praecipiendo quam rogando mandamus, quatenus ad Patchan pro magnitudine facultatis & debiti, cum militia nobis succurras, & xv. die Patchae in campo Veronae cum reliquis exercitibus te praesentes, teq; ita factuum nunc statuto praesentium latoris, Capellani & Nuncii nostri Burensis Colon. fideli & firma promissione care non differas. Quod si animum prudentiae tuae ab his averteris, & omnino noluéris verbum indubitanter scire te volumus, quod nos, favente & semper nos praecedente Dei clementia, consilio Principum & Religiosorum ita de Salzburgensi Ecclesia ordinabimus, ut & honor Dei non minuatur, & debitum servitium Imperio de cetero rationabiliter exsolvatur.
units.tr: 3. Since, therefore, one must render to Caesar what is Caesar's, not only in money of whatever kind but also in persons and arms, to assist our labours, we command your fidelity by imperial writing, both by precept and by request: that you come to our aid with soldiery at Pavia, according to the measure of your means and obligation, and that you be present with the remaining armies on the fifteenth day after Easter in the field at Verona. Do not delay in this, according to the appointed time, with a faithful and firm promise, through the bearer of these letters, our chaplain and messenger of the Burensis of Cologne. But if you turn your mind away from these things and altogether refuse, we want you to know without doubt that we, with God's favour and clemency always going before us, by the counsel of princes and religious men will so ordain concerning the Church of Salzburg that the honour of God is not diminished, and the due service to the Empire is henceforth rightly rendered.

units.la: V. Super eadem re.
units.tr: V. On the same matter.

units.la: FRIDERICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator & Semper-Augustus, fideli suo A. Venerabili Curiensi Episcopo, gratiam suam & omne bonum.
units.tr: FREDERICK, by the grace of God Emperor of the Romans and ever Augustus, to his faithful A., the venerable Bishop of Chur, his grace and every good.

units.la: 1. Cum ab ipsa veritate omnis homo, sed & quantumcunq; Religiosus, quae sunt Caesaris, Caesari reddere jubeatur; & Salzburgensis Ecclesia quàm maximi servitii debito, sacro tenearur Imperio, minime deficimus, quare Salzburgensis Archiepiscopus toties rogatus & vocatus non ad consilium, sed ad expeditionis auxilium venire voluerit, & terminum, quem per proprium Capellanum suum nobiliter feltum B. Mariae condixerat, tam incuratè neglexerit. Nuncaut per praesentium latore, fidelem Capellanum nostrum, Burenf. Colon. iterum ad expeditionis auxilium cum personis & armaturis ipsum arripere vimus, & ut tua diligentia ad id faciendum eum studiose commonear, folerter & intensissimus. Quòd si pro consuetudine sua venire noluerit, de contemptu & injuria tam tuae dilectionis quàm & omnibus Imperii Principibus ibi conqueri necessarium habemus.
units.tr: 1. Since every man, however religious, is commanded by the very truth to render to Caesar what is Caesar's, and since the Church of Salzburg is bound by the greatest debt of service to the sacred Empire, we are by no means lacking in our demands. Therefore, although the Archbishop of Salzburg has been asked and summoned so many times, not to a council but to bring aid for the expedition, and has so carelessly neglected the term which he had agreed through his own chaplain, the nobly born B. of Mary's feast, we have resolved to summon again our faithful chaplain, of Bure, Cologne, with his people and arms, to the aid of the expedition, through the bearer of these presents; and we charge your diligence to remind him of this task earnestly and most urgently. But if he should refuse to come, as is his custom, we shall have to complain of the contempt and injury both to your affection and to all the Princes of the Empire there.

units.la: 2. Nosaut, si necesse fuerit, de Salzburgensi Ecclesia ita cum consilio Principum & Religiosorum ordinabimus, q; & honor Dei non diminuetur, & religio Ecclesiae non subvertetur, si Deo volentario debitum servitium exsolvetur. Novit Deus, qui corda scrutatur, q; nos virtutem in quolibet, magis autem in eo, cujus propositum in virtutibus decoratur, diligimus & reveremur; &, premis injuriis coacti, ad molestiam cujusquam, non nisi multum invito provocamur.
units.tr: 2.
