We, however, if it should be necessary, shall settle the affairs of the Church of Salzburg with the counsel of the Princes and the religious, so that the honour of God is not diminished and the religion of the Church is not overthrown, if the due service is rendered to God willingly. God, who searches the hearts, knows that we love and revere virtue in anyone, but most of all in one whose purpose is adorned with virtues; and, forced by such injuries, we are roused to trouble no one except very unwillingly.

units.la: 3. De caetero praefatum Capellanum nostrum committimus, ut ex parte nostra dicitur audias, & ad ea, quae eidem dedimus in praeceptis, ipsum consilius & conducto adjuves, quatenus ro his & pro omnibus fidelibus servitiis tuis & multa dilectione tua, vobis ad promerendum semper umus attenti.
units.tr: 3. For the rest, we commit our aforesaid chaplain to you, so that you may hear what is said on our behalf, and may assist him with counsel and with aid in those things which we have given him in charge, so that, for this and for all your faithful services and your great affection, you may always be attentive to deserve well of us.

units.la: VI. Ut Archiepiscopus ad Curiam Imperialem evocatus se in persona Imperatoris sistat, nec ulla pecunia absentiam suam redimere possit.
units.tr: VI. That the Archbishop, summoned to the Imperial Court, must present himself in the person of the Emperor, and that no money can redeem his absence.

units.la: FRIDERICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator Semper-Augustus, Eberhardo Venerabili Salzburgensi Archiepiscopo, gratiam suam & omne bonum. Inter anxias & innumeras tribulationes, exigentibus peccatis hominum, jamdiu universalis laborat Ecclesia, consilium religionis tuae impore requisivimus, ut discretio tua, quae directo tramite ad summum bonum attingere nititur, salutis nobis ostenderet, & ab errore minus eruditorum animos declinaret. Non solum autem tuam admodum necessariam Imperio subtraxisti, verum nos & omnes Principes & fideles, secus quàm decet honestatem tuam immoderatis verbis cum offensione aggravasti. Sanè nuncius tuae Nuncius ad nos venisset, & servitium pecuniae tuae pro redemptione expeditionis fuerit, nos communicato cum Principibus nostris consilio, pecuniam tuam cum honore non accipere, quia nostrae consuetudinis non est aliquo pecuniam accipere, & odium etiam inter nos. Cum autem, sicut decet Imperialem Excellentiam, nobis personam tuam exhibueris, regis de tuo adventu gaudere poterimus, & de instante necessitate Imperii & Ecclesiae, cae- teris Imperii Principibus tuo consilio salubrius tractare poterimus & ordinare.
units.tr: FREDERICK, by the grace of God Emperor of the Romans and ever Augustus, to Eberhard, the venerable Archbishop of Salzburg, his grace and every good. Amid anxious and countless tribulations, caused by the sins of men, the universal Church has long been suffering. We have sought the counsel of your religion at this time, so that your discretion, which strives by a direct path to attain the highest good, might show us the way of salvation and turn the minds of the less learned from error. You have not only withdrawn your most necessary service from the Empire, but have also burdened us and all the Princes and faithful with immoderate words, to the offence of all, contrary to what your honour requires. Indeed, if your messenger had come to us and had offered money for redemption from the expedition, we, with the counsel of our Princes, would not have accepted your money with honour, since it is not our custom to accept money for anything, and there would also be hatred between us. But since you have presented yourself to us, as befits the Imperial Majesty, we shall be able to rejoice at your coming, and, concerning the pressing need of the Empire and the Church, we shall be able to treat and settle matters more beneficially with the other Princes of the Empire by your counsel.

units.la: VII. Rebellem Imperio Civitatem Mediolanensem laetam, & de forma executionis in recipi- endis deditis rebellibus.
units.tr: VII. That the city of Milan, rebellious against the Empire, is glad, and concerning the manner of executing the reception of the surrendered rebels.

units.la: FRIDERICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator & Semper-Augustus, Eberhardo Salzburgensi Archiepiscopo, gratiam suam & omne bonum.
units.tr: FREDERICK, by the grace of God Emperor of the Romans and ever Augustus, to Eberhard, Archbishop of Salzburg, his grace and every good.

units.la: Finum aestimamus, ut hi, qui tribulationibus nostris & Imperii, personarum servitio & rerum tenus fideliter communicaverunt, à Domino, qui consolatur nos in tribulatione nostra, gratia recipiant, & felicissimis eventibus nostris, ac gloriosissimis triumphis, quales nulli nostro concessos esse credimus, grata vicissitudine parti cipient & congratulentur. Tuae quoque honorem nostrum sitibundo pectore anhelate, luce clarius constat, significuius quàm in virtute Dei, per quem reges regnant, & potentes sacrum justitiam, felicem & gloriosam victoria cum plenitudine honoris adepti sumus. In Kal. enim Mart. prima videlicet imperii Mediolanum, submoti omni simulatione fraudis, quàm in piam addictione convenit, summa necessitate famis & inedia coacti ad Curiam nostram apud Laudam & nudos gladios in cervicibus suis deferentes, & Majestati nostrae reos se esse profitentes, personas, res, ipsamque civitatem absque omni tenore, & sine aliqua conditione interpolita, in nullo potestatem cum plena deditione reddidere.
units.tr: We think it fitting that those who have faithfully shared with us and the Empire in our tribulations, in service of persons and goods, should receive grace from the Lord, who comforts us in our tribulation, and should share in and rejoice at our most happy events and most glorious triumphs, such as we believe have been granted to no one else. Your heart too thirsts for our honour, as is clearer than light: we have obtained, by the power of God, through whom kings reign and the powerful decree justice, a happy and glorious victory with the fullness of honour. For on the Kalends of March, in the first year of our reign, Milan, having put aside all pretence of deceit, as befits pious submission, and compelled by extreme need of famine and hunger, came to our court at Lodi, carrying naked swords on their necks, and professing themselves guilty before our Majesty, they surrendered persons, goods and the city itself without any reservation and without any interposed condition, with full surrender of power.

units.la: 2. Praeterea IV. Nonas ejusdem mensis, Mediolanenses cum omni militia & vrbis exeuntes, nos redeuntes, vexilla & universa signa bellica, clavicq; civitatis, & Consulatus dignitatis, nost. s. [?] averunt, refutantes omnia genera armorum, omnem potestatem, nisi quam cum permissione nostra possent obtinere. Juraverunt insuper, quaecunque eos jurare fecimus, & universa mandata nostra, sicut de personis & rebus & de ipsa civitate ordinaremus, bona fide observarent, & de his omnibus observandis et c. obsides et meliores & majores dederunt nobis dederunt.
units.tr: 2. Moreover, on the fourth of the Nones of the same month, the Milanese, together with all their soldiers, went out of the city as we returned, and surrendered the banners and all the military standards, the keys of the city and the emblems of the consulship, refusing every kind of arms and all power, except what they might hold with our permission. They further swore to observe faithfully whatever we caused them to swear and all our commands, as we should order concerning persons, goods and the city itself, and they gave us hostages and their better and greater men, for the observance of all these things.

units.la: 3. Ex sententia ergo divina, cujus judicia abyssus multa, qui frangit omnem superbum, nec tero praedictis hostibus occasio malignandi, & facultas rebellandi praestetur, follata complanatis muros subvertimus, turres omnes destruximus, ipsamque civitatem in ruinam & desolationem redegimus, ad promovenda alia negotia, & ad plenariam Imperii reformationem, exercitum nostrum victrices aquilas feliciter convertemus.
units.tr: 3. Therefore, by the divine judgment, whose judgments are a great deep, who breaks every proud man, and so that no occasion of doing harm or power of rebelling is further granted to these enemies, we have overthrown the walls, levelled the towers, and reduced the city itself to ruin and desolation; and, to advance other business and the full reformation of the Empire, we shall turn our army, with its victorious eagles, happily elsewhere.

units.la: 4. De caeteris, dilectos & fideles nostros Nuncios O. Veronensem Episcopum, & C. Capitaneum nostrum in occursum sibi apud Tridentum transmittimus, qui juxta magnificentiam Imperii nostri ad Curiam nostram te perducant.
units.tr: 4. As for the rest, we send our beloved and faithful messengers, O., Bishop of Verona, and C., our captain, to meet you at Trent, who shall lead you to our Court in keeping with the magnificence of our Empire.

units.la: VIII. Super eadem re.
units.tr: VIII. Concerning the same matter.

units.la: FRIDERICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator Semper-Augustus, dilecto suo Romano Episcopo, gratiam suam & omne bonum.
units.tr: FREDERICK, by the grace of God Roman Emperor, ever August, to his beloved Roman Bishop, his grace and every good.

units.la: 1. Divinum aestimamus, ut ii, qui tribulationibus nostris & Imperii, personarum periculo & Ecclesiae, pedio hactenus fideliter communicaverunt, ab eo, qui consolatur nos in omni tribulatione nostra, consolationis gaudia recipiant, & felicissimos eventus nostros ac gloriosissimum triumphum, quem ante ostentat, eorum nostrorum concessisse credimus, grata vicissitudine participent & gloriam.
units.tr: 1. We judge it divine that those who have hitherto faithfully shared with us in our tribulations, in the danger to the persons of the Empire and of the Church, should receive the joys of consolation from him who comforts us in all our tribulation; and we believe that he has granted them our most fortunate successes and the most glorious triumph which he displays before us, so that they may share in them by a welcome reciprocity, and in the glory.

units.la: 2. Tux igitur Dilectioni, quoniam in omnem honorem nostrum sinibundo pectore anhelas clarius constat, significandum duximus, quod in virtute Dei, per quem Reges regnant, & potentes justitiam, felicem & gloriosam de Mediolano victoriam cum omni plenitudine honorum adeptam. In Kalendis Martii, videlicet prima die mensis, hostes Imperii Mediolanenses, summota omni dilatione fraudis, quam in prima deditione nos circumvenerunt, summa necessitate famis & miseriae ad Curiam nostram apud Laudam venerunt, & nudos gladios in cervicibus suis ferentes, & Mariteros se profitentes, personas, res, ipsamque civitatem, absque omni tenore, & sine conditione in pacta, in nostram partem cum plenaria deditione reddiderunt.
units.tr: 2. Therefore, since it is quite clear that you pant with a sincere heart for every honour of ours, we have thought it necessary to signify to your Love that, in the power of God, through whom kings reign and rulers decree justice, we have won a happy and glorious victory over Milan, with every fullness of honours. On the Kalends of March, that is, on the first day of the month, the enemies of the Empire, the Milanese, having put aside all delay of deceit, by which they had deceived us in the first surrender, came to our court at Lodi in the greatest need of hunger and misery, carrying naked swords upon their necks and professing themselves penitents; and they surrendered their persons, goods and the city itself to our side, without any condition or term of agreement, with full surrender.

units.la: 3. Ex sententia igitur divina, cujus judicia abyssus multa, qui frangit omne superbum, nec ro praedictis hostibus occasio malignandi, vel facultas rebellandi praesterur, follata complanatis muros subvertimus, turres omnes destruxumus, & totam civitatem in ruinam & desolationem redegimus, ad promovenda alia negotia, & ad plenariam Imperii reformationem exercitum & Aquilas triumphales, prout volucrimus, convertemus.
units.tr: 3. Therefore, by the divine sentence, whose judgments are a great deep and who breaks every proud thing, and since no opportunity of doing mischief nor power of rebelling is left to the aforesaid enemies, we have levelled their walls to the ground, destroyed all their towers, and reduced the whole city to ruin and desolation; and we shall turn the army and the triumphal eagles to other undertakings, and to the full reformation of the Empire, as we shall see fit.
X.

units.la: De Pace Imperatoris & Regis Francorum.
units.tr: On the Peace of the Emperor and the King of the Franks.

units.la: FRIDERICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator, a Deo Coronatus, Magnus & Pacificus, Victor ac Triumphator, Semper-Augustus, dilecto consanguineo suo Ludovico, gratiam Francorum Regi glorioso, salutem & sinceram dilectionis sinceritatem. Postquam divinae... per quam Reges regnant, & legum conditores justa decernunt, ad Romani Imperii nos sublimavit ... pacis abundantia, quam mundus dare non potest, feliciter regnandi felicia nobis concessit tempora, desiderio desideravimus faciem tuam videre, & familiaritatis tuae perfrui dulcissima alloquia, sed praepedientibus magnis ac multimodis valde dilacerati Imperii nostri negotiis, quae pariter pimus, effectui mancipare non potuimus. Quia vero per Legatos tuos, & per epistolam tuam ... aequo te optare cognovimus & credimus, non modice gaudemus, sperantes in eo, qui dat lucem ... gibus, quod ex nostra salutifera colloquutione, universo orbi pacis & tranquillitatis novum modum & Ecclesiae Dei emergendi, respirandi, multiplicandi praebeatur tempus. Sed quod voluntatis bonae benignum detinebatur hunc inde nondum completum potuit, nec tuae tarditatis, nec nostrae vel impetrandum recessum. Nunc autem, quia in praesentia Italiae expeditionis jam fumus, & Imperii nostri ad eandem unanimiter intendunt, quo in loco, quo tempore convenire & ... possumus, incertum habemus, nisi forte si completa expeditione vita comes fuerit, super hoc ... cipibus nostris diligentissime ordinabimus. Volumus etiam, ut quod tu de nobis, nos de te ... semper possimus. Vera enim amicitia nunquam fallit.
units.tr: FREDERICK, by the grace of God Emperor of the Romans, crowned by God, great and peaceful, victor and triumphant, ever Augustus, to his beloved kinsman Louis, the glorious King of the Franks, greeting and sincere sincerity of affection. Since the divine ... through whom kings reign and makers of laws decree what is just, has raised us to the height of the Roman Empire ... by the abundance of peace, which the world cannot give, has granted us happy times for reigning happily, we have longed with desire to see your face and to enjoy the sweetest conversation of your friendship. But with great and manifold affairs of our greatly torn Empire hindering us, which we equally desire, we have not been able to bring them to effect. Because, however, we have learned and believe from your envoys and from your letter ... that you desire the same, we rejoice not a little, hoping in him who gives light ... that from our salutary conference a new opportunity is offered to the whole world for peace and tranquillity, and for the Church of God to emerge, to breathe and to multiply. But what the kind good will of both of us kept in suspense has not yet been completed, nor can it be obtained by your delay or by our withdrawal. Now, however, since we are already on the expedition into Italy, and our Empire is united in its intention toward it, we are uncertain at what place and at what time we can meet, unless perhaps, if the expedition is completed and life remains with us, we shall arrange this most diligently with our princes ... We also wish that whatever you have said about us, we about you ... we may always be able. For true friendship never deceives.
XI.

units.la: De Unitate Imperii & Regni Franciae.
units.tr: On the Unity of the Empire and the Kingdom of France.

units.la: FRIDERICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator & Semper-Augustus, dilecto consanguineo suo Ludovico, Illustri Francorum Regi, salutem & sinceram dilectionis affectum. Legatum Nobilitatis, quam debemus in alacritate suscepimus, benigne Imperii dei aures ... dantes Ius, quae sincerit ate tua nobis nuntiata sunt. Placet igitur & sublimitati nostrae, ut ... quod. sanguineos, & inter cognata Regna nostra, detersa totius rancoris nebula, sinceræ dilectionis splendor refulgeat; & fœdus amicitiæ, quod facit utraque unum, incolubilem semper conservet vinculum. Sane quæcunque necessaria sunt ad conservandam inter nos mutuæ dilectionis integritatem, dilecto consanguineo nostro fideli tuo Henrico Comiti Trecarum amicè & plenariè ordinavimus, & sicut conditum est, inviolabiliter observare curabimus. Datum Papiæ post destructionem Mediolani, II. Kal. Junii.
units.tr: Frederick, by the grace of God Roman Emperor and ever Augustus, to his beloved kinsman Louis, Illustrious King of the Franks, greeting and sincere affection of love. We have gladly received the envoy of your Nobility, and we kindly lend our ears to what your sincerity has announced to us. It therefore pleases our sublimity that, between our kindred kingdoms, the cloud of all rancour having been wiped away, the splendour of sincere love should shine forth, and that the bond of friendship, which makes the two one, should always keep an indissoluble tie. Indeed, whatever is necessary for preserving the integrity of our mutual love, we have arranged fully and in a friendly manner with our beloved kinsman and faithful man, Henry, Count of Troyes, and we will take care to observe it inviolably as it has been agreed. Given at Pavia, after the destruction of Milan, on the second day before the Kalends of June.
XII.

units.la: De Pseudopapa in Franciam transfugio.
units.tr: Concerning the pseudo-pope's flight into France.

units.la: FRIDERICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator & Semper-Augustus, dilecto amico suo, Venerabili N. Episcopo Suessionensi, & Regis Francorum Cancellario, salutem cum intima & sincera dilectione. In veritate audivimus, quod Rollandus quondam Cancellarius, qui propter fideles nostros Romam non habet nec invenit, ubi caput suum reclinet, periculo maris se ipsum cum suis pauperibus quacibus commisit, ut terram Francorum attingeret, eamque schismaticæ pravitatis errore, manifestus Dei & Ecclesiæ ac Imperii inimicus, commaculet & spoliet; ut etiam quomodocunque colligat viginti mille libras, & amplius, unde creditoribus suis debita persolvat; quia sub alieno ære valde graviter ipse laborat. Rogantes itaque tuam dilectionem intimo & pleno affectu monemus, quatenus prædictum Schismaticum, nostrum & totius Imperii atrocem inimicum, nullo modo recipias, nec recipi ab alio permittas, Regique Francorum bona fide consulas, ne ipsum, vel aliquem de suis Pseudocardinalibus vel Nuncus recipiat. Tantum enim ac tale odium inter nostrum Imperium & suum Regnum exinde poterit oriri, quod non de facili compescere poterimus aut sedare.
units.tr: FREDERICK, by the grace of God Emperor of the Romans and ever Augustus, to his dear friend, the venerable N., Bishop of Soissons and Chancellor of the King of the Franks, greeting with heartfelt and sincere affection. We have heard in truth that Rolandus, once Chancellor, who on account of our faithful subjects has neither Rome nor a place to lay his head, committed himself with his poor companions to the perils of the sea, so that he might reach the land of the Franks and there defile and despoil it with the error of schismatic perversity, being a manifest enemy of God, of the Church and of the Empire; and that he is somehow gathering twenty thousand pounds and more, from which to pay his creditors, since he is labouring very heavily under borrowed money. We therefore urge your affection with heartfelt and full goodwill, that you receive in no way the aforesaid schismatic, our and the whole Empire's fierce enemy, nor permit him to be received by anyone else, and that you give good faith counsel to the King of the Franks, that he not receive him, or any of his pseudo-cardinals or nuncios. For so great and such hatred may arise from this between our Empire and his kingdom that we will not be able to restrain or calm it easily.

units.la: XIII.
units.tr: XIII.

units.la: De Concilio in Burgundia inter Imperatorem & Regem Franciæ, & inter utriusque communes Proceres celebrando pro confirmatione electi Papæ.
units.tr: On the council to be held in Burgundy between the Emperor and the King of France, with the common nobles of both realms, for the confirmation of the elected Pope.

units.la: FRIDERICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator & Semper-Augustus, dilecto suo * * Archiepiscopo, gratiam suam & omne bonum. Inter innumeras & tumescentes tempestatum procellas, quibus navicula B. Petri quassata, & inter pressuras diversas, quibus sancta Dei Ecclesia frequenter afflicta & tribulata est, tandem verus ille Mediator Dei & hominum Jesus Christus, qui Ecclesiam suam unicam sponsam proprio characteræ sui pretiosi sanguinis insignivit & redemit, consolationis etiam, quam ascendens in cœlum fidelibus suis repromisit, inquiens: Non relinquam vos orphanos, ecce vobiscum sum omnibus diebus usque ad consummationem sæculi, evidentibus & manifestis declarat indiciis. Ecce enim sicut stella matutina in medio nebulæ oriens, solita pietate Ecclesiam suam in tribulatione aspexit, & surgens imperavit ventis & mari, & facta est tranquillitas magna. Pro illa siquidem controversia, quæ inter Nos & Regem Francorum pro schismate Romanæ Ecclesiæ jamdiu agitabatur, Gratia Spiritus Sancti, quæ facit habitare unanimes in domo Domini, mediantibus hinc inde legatis dem pari voluntate, & unanimi consensu inter nos convenit, quod nos videlicet una cum Archiepiscopis, Episcopis, & Patribus Orthodoxis ac viris Religiosis, Baronibus & universis utriusque Regni civibus, IV. Kal. Septemb. in die videlicet Decollationis Joannis Baptistæ, super fluvium Saonam Episcopatu Bizantino Concilium generale pariter celebraturi sumus, in quo Rex Francorum dilectus consanguineus noster cum universis Archiepiscopis suis, Episcopis, & cum omnibus Regni sui Principibus, & tota Gallicana Ecclesia Reverendum Patrem nostrum Dominum Papam Victorem, per sacramenta & firmissimas securitates prærodinatum est, in Apostolicum & Universalem Ecclesiæ Pontificem recipiet, & debitam ei exhibebit reverentiam. Verum quia hoc negotium duum, tamque salubre, & jam necessarium, ubi de reconciliatione sanctæ Dei Ecclesiæ, & totius unitatis in commune agitur, sine tuæ discretionis cæterorumque Principum ac Christi fidelium cōsummari nec debet nec potest, exoramus te & monemus in ea fide, quam debes Imperio, Dei Ecclesiæ, & animæ tuæ, quatinus omni occasione sumi nota cum sapientioribus & magis creatis personis tui Episcopatus apud Bisantium, IV. die ante prædictum terminum familiari Curiæ, nobis occurras, ad Concilium nobilium processurus. Et quia abundans cautela, indites tui, quos tecum adduces, in armis & clypeis sint muniti. Insuper tentoria deferas, er domorum raritatem necessaria erunt. Ibi enim per gratiam Dei totum negotium Domictoris ad gloriam Dei, & ad pacem, & unitatem sanctæ Ecclesiæ, & omnimodum honorem honesto fiue terminabitur.
units.tr: FREDERICK, by the grace of God Roman Emperor and ever Augustus, to his beloved * * Archbishop, his grace and every good. Amid the countless and swelling storms by which the little ship of St Peter has been battered, and amid the various oppressions by which the holy Church of God has often been afflicted and troubled, that true Mediator between God and men, Jesus Christ, who marked and redeemed his Church, his only spouse, with the precious character of his own blood, makes clear by manifest and evident signs the comfort he promised to his faithful ones when he ascended into heaven, saying: I will not leave you orphans; behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age. For behold, like the morning star rising in the midst of the cloud, he has looked upon his Church in its tribulation with his accustomed mercy, and, rising, he commanded the winds and the sea, and there was a great calm. Indeed, concerning that dispute which for a long time has been pursued between us and the King of the Franks over the schism of the Roman Church, by the grace of the Holy Spirit, which makes brethren dwell together in unity in the house of the Lord, through envoys passing back and forth on both sides, we have come to agreement with one equal will and unanimous consent: namely, that we, together with the archbishops, bishops, and orthodox Fathers, and religious men, barons, and all the citizens of both realms, shall hold a general council together on the fourth day before the Kalends of September, that is, on the feast of the Beheading of John the Baptist, upon the river Saône in the diocese of Besançon. At that council our beloved cousin the King of the Franks, with all his archbishops and bishops, all the princes of his realm, and the whole Gallican Church, shall receive our reverend father Lord Pope Victor, who has been predestined by oaths and most firm guarantees, as the Apostolic and Universal Pontiff of the Church, and shall show him the reverence due. But since this affair, so holy and so salutary, and now so necessary, in which the reconciliation of the holy Church of God and the whole unity of all is at stake, ought not and cannot be brought to completion without your discretion and that of the other princes and the faithful of Christ, we beseech and admonish you, by the faith that you owe to the Empire, to the Church of God, and to your own soul, that, setting aside every excuse, you meet us with the wiser and more distinguished persons of your diocese at Besançon, four days before the aforesaid date, with our familiar court, so that you may go forward with us to the council of the nobles. And since abundant caution is needed, let your men whom you bring with you be armed with weapons and shields. Furthermore, bring tents, for houses will be scarce and they will be necessary. For there, by the grace of God, the whole affair of Lord Victor will be concluded to the glory of God, to the peace and unity of the holy Church, and to every honourable end.
XIV.

units.la: Super eadem re.
units.tr: On the same matter.

units.la: FRIDERICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator & Semper-Augustus, dilecto suo E. Venerabili Lugdunensi Archiepiscopo & Primati Galliarum, gratiam suam & omne bonum. Imperialis nostræ solicitudinis propositum, quod Lugdunensem Ecclesiam ac Civitatem a diutinis laboribus suis, & in antiquæ dignitatis suæ statum reformare decrevimus, pro tua fidei erga nos devotione, nostro miscellanter vigilat, quoad usque (Deo opitulante) debitum sortiatur effectum. Unde divinitas, quæ piis omnium consiliis interesse, & ea promovere consuevit, congruam nobis opportunitatem obtulit, ut partes Burgundiæ, immo ipsam Civitatem Lugdunensem in Majestatis nostræ personam quantocyus adeamus, ac ruinas ejus in statum sui decorem cooperante Deo erigarus. Comes siquidem Trecensis, quum ad Curiam nostram in legatione Domini Regis Francorum venisset, & Reverendum Patrem nostrum Papam Victorem humili honorasset, studiose a nobis poposcit, quatinus ad Colloquium inter nos & cum Regem habendum accederemus; tantumque huic verbo instiit, quoadusque universorum nostrorum Principum ad Colloquium indiximus, iv. Kalend. Septembris, ad Pontem Laone, inter Divionem & Dijon cum Archiepiscopis, Abbatibus, aliisque Cleri nostri Prioribus illo venturi. Quia ergo tua prudentia in eodem Colloquio nobis plurimum necessaria est, Venerabilitatem tuae studiose monemus, injungimus, quatinus ad idem Colloquium omnes Suffraganeos tuos evocès, & cum universis Prioribus, Abbatibus, & Cleri celebritate, omni remota occasione, venias, quia nos ibidem gratia promovente, super Ecclesiae Dei restituenda unitate, & super Domini Papae Victoris confirmatione finem imponemus. Interea vero consilium non fuit, ut multiam (prout dictum erat) transferemus, quia quaecunque sunt in bellicis rebus agenda seu disponenda, per praesentiam nostram venienter adimplere curabimus. Dominus quidem Papa nobiscum aderit, & oportebit propter Cum domorum in teritoriis habitare.
units.tr: FREDERICK, by the grace of God Emperor of the Romans and ever-Augustus, to his beloved E., venerable Archbishop of Lyon and Primate of the Gauls, his grace and every good. The purpose of our imperial solicitude, which we have decided to restore the Church and city of Lyon from their long labours to the state of their former dignity, watches over this matter mixed with your devotion of faith toward us, until (God helping) it obtains its due effect. Whence the divine power, which is wont to be present at the pious counsels of all and to promote them, has offered us a fitting opportunity to approach quickly the parts of Burgundy, indeed the city of Lyon itself, in the person of our Majesty, and, with God cooperating, to raise its ruins to their proper beauty. The Count of Troyes, when he had come to our court on an embassy from the lord King of the Franks, and had honoured our Reverend Father Pope Victor with humble reverence, earnestly asked us that we should come to a colloquy to be held between ourselves and the King. He pressed this request so hard that we have summoned all our princes to the colloquy on the fourth day before the Kalends of September, at Pont-de-Laône, between Dijon and Dijon, with the archbishops, abbots and other priors of our clergy coming there. Therefore, since your prudence is greatly necessary to us at that colloquy, we earnestly admonish and enjoin your venerability that you summon all your suffragans to the same colloquy, and that you come, with all the priors, abbots and the multitude of the clergy, setting aside every excuse, because there, with grace advancing, we shall bring to an end the matter of restoring the unity of the Church of God and of confirming Lord Pope Victor. Meanwhile, it is not our intention, as was said, to move the army, but whatever has to be done or arranged in military affairs we will take care to carry out in our presence. The lord Pope will indeed be with us, and it will be necessary to dwell in tents, because of the scarcity of houses in the territories.

units.la: XV. Super eadem re.
units.tr: XV. On the same matter.

units.la: FRIDERICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator, & Semper-Augustus, fideli suo M. Duce Thuringiae gratiam suam & omne bonum. Quoniam in schismate, quod est in Romana Ecclesia universus orbis in se ipsum divisus est, & tota Christianitas in modica turbatione concutitur, nos animi compassione sanctae Dei Ecclesiae doloribus condolemus, totius consilii & auxilii propriam curam & sollicitudinem adhibere cupientes, ut totius dissensionis discrimine sublato, Ecclesia Dei, sicut in unitate fidei, ita sub unius Pastoris regimine in unum ovile congregetur. Inde est, quod ex consilio Principum, cum dilecto consanguineo nostro Ludovico Illustri Rege Francorum iv. Kal. Septembris, in die videlicet Decollationis Sancti Johannis Baptistae, super fluvium Sa * Concilium celebrare statuimus: in quo, aspirante Spiritu sancto, qui facit unanimes habitare in domo Domini, speramus, ut Ecclesiasticae pacis & unitatis status reformetur, & Dominus Papa Victor Apostolicae Sedis gubernacula debeat obtinere. Verum quia hoc negotium tam arduum, tamque & tam necessarium, ubi de reconciliatione sanctae Ecclesiae, & salute totius Christianitatis in communi agitur, sine tuae discretionis praesentia consummari nec debet, nec potest, exorantes communiter te in ea fide, quam debes Imperio & sanctae Dei Ecclesiae, & animae tuae, quatinus omni occasione summota apud Bisantium quarto die ante praedictum terminum familiariter, more Curiae, nobis occurras, ad Concilium nobiscum processurus, &c.
units.tr: FREDERICK, by the grace of God Emperor of the Romans and ever-Augustus, to his faithful M., Duke of Thuringia, his grace and every good. Since, in the schism which exists in the Roman Church, the whole world is divided against itself and all Christendom is shaken by no small disturbance, we, moved with compassion of spirit, grieve over the sorrows of the holy Church of God, desiring to apply our own care and concern for all counsel and aid, so that, with the peril of all dissension removed, the Church of God may be gathered into one fold, as in unity of faith, so under the rule of one Shepherd. Hence it is that, by the counsel of the princes, together with our beloved kinsman Louis, the illustrious King of the French, we have resolved to hold a council on the fourth day before the Kalends of September, that is, on the feast of the Beheading of St John the Baptist, upon the river Sa[ône]. In this council, with the Holy Spirit breathing, who makes those dwell together in unity in the house of the Lord, we hope that the state of ecclesiastical peace and unity will be reformed, and that Lord Pope Victor ought to obtain the helm of the Apostolic See. But because this matter, so arduous and so necessary, in which the reconciliation of the holy Church and the salvation of all Christendom are treated in common, ought not and cannot be concluded without the presence of your discretion, we jointly beseech you, in that faith which you owe to the Empire, to the holy Church of God and to your own soul, that, every occasion set aside, you meet us at Besançon on the fourth day before the said term, as is customary at court, to go forth with us to the council, etc.
XVI.

units.la: De Concilio generali apud Bisantium celebrando pro recipiendo Victore Papa per Imperatorem confirmato, ab Ecclesiis Gallicanis.
units.tr: ## On the General Council to be held at Besançon, to receive Pope Victor, confirmed by the Emperor, from the Gallican Churches.

units.la: FRIDERICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator & Semper-Augustus, fideli suo C. Augustae nensi Episcopo gratiam suam & omne bonum.
units.tr: FREDERICK, by the grace of God Roman Emperor and ever Augustus, to his faithful C., Bishop of Augsburg, greeting and every good.

units.la: 1. Inter varias & tumescentes tempestatum procellas, quibus jam diu navicula beati Petri fata; & inrer pressuras diversas, quibus sancta Dei Ecclesia frequenter afflicta & tribulata est, tamen verus ille mediator Dei & hominum Christus Jesus, qui Ecclesiam suam velut unicam sponsam proprio charactere sui pretiosi sanguinis insignivit & redemit, consolationis gratiam, quam ascendens coelum fidelibus suis repromisit, inquiens: Non relinquam vos orphanos: ecce ego vobiscum sum omnibus usque ad consummationem saeculi, evidentibus & manifestis declarat indicis. Ipse enim, sicut stella in medio nunc oriens, solita pietate Ecclesiam suam in tribulatione respexit, & surgens imperavit ventis & mari, & facta est tranquillitas magna. Pro illa siquidem controversia, quae inter nos & Regem Francorum pro schismate Romanae Ecclesiae jam diu agitatur, aspirante Sancti Spiritus gratia, quatenus habitare unanimes in domo, mediantibus hinc inde Legatis, tandem pari voluntate & unanimi consensu inter nos convenit, quod nos videlicet, una cum Archiepiscopis, Episcopis & Pr. tribus orthodoxis ac viris Religiosis, Baronibus, & universis Regni utriusque Principibus, iv. Kal. Septembr. in die Decollationis S. Johannis Baptistae, supra fluvium Saona, in Episcopatu Bisuntino, Concilium generale pariter celebraturi jussimus: in quo Rex Francorum, dilectus consanguineus noster, cum nostris Archiepiscopis, Episcopis, & cum omnibus Regni sui Principibus, & tota Gallicana Ecclesia, Venerandum Patrem nostrum Dominum Octavianum Papam, sicut per sacramenta & firmissimas Vitates praeordinatum est, in Apostolicum Universalem sanctae Dei Ecclesiae Pontificem recipere debitamque reverentiam exhibebit.
units.tr: 1. Amid the many swelling storms by which the little boat of St Peter has long been tossed, and amid the various pressures by which the holy Church of God has often been afflicted and troubled, yet that true Mediator between God and men, Christ Jesus, who marked and redeemed his Church, as his one bride, with the stamp of his precious blood, shows by clear and evident signs the grace of comfort which he promised to his faithful when he ascended into heaven, saying: "I will not leave you orphans; behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age." For he, like a star now rising in the midst, has looked upon his Church in tribulation with his accustomed mercy, and rising he commanded the winds and the sea, and there was a great calm. Indeed, concerning that controversy which has long been pursued between us and the King of the Franks over the schism of the Roman Church, the grace of the Holy Spirit breathing upon us, so that brothers may dwell together in unity, and through envoys passing back and forth, it has at last been agreed between us, with equal will and unanimous consent, that we ourselves, together with the archbishops, bishops, abbots and godly and religious men, barons, and all the princes of both kingdoms, have ordered a general council to be celebrated together on the fourth day before the Kalends of September, the feast of the Beheading of St John the Baptist, beside the river Saône, in the diocese of Besançon; at which the King of the Franks, our beloved kinsman, together with our archbishops, bishops, and all the princes of his kingdom, and the whole Gallican Church, shall receive our venerable father, Lord Octavian the Pope, as Universal Apostolic Pontiff of the holy Church of God, as has been appointed beforehand by sacraments and most firm pledges, and shall render him due reverence.

units.la: 2. Verum quia hoc negotium tam arduum, tamque salubre, & tam necessarium, ubi de reconciliatione sanctae Dei Ecclesiae, & totius salute Christianitatis in communi agitur, sine tuae discretionis praesentia consummari nec debet nec potest, exorantes monemus in ea fide, quam Imperio & S. Dei Ecclesiae & animae tuae debes, quatenus omni occasione summota, cum sapientioribus & magis idoneis personis tuae dioecesis apud Bisuntium iv. praedictum terminum familiariter, more Curiae, nobis occurras, ad Concilium nobiscum processurus. Et quia abundans cautela non nocet, Milites tui, quos secum adducès, in armis & equis multi. Insuper & rentoria deferas, quæ propter domorum raritatem necessaria sunt. Ibi enim per gratiam Dei totum negocium Domini Victoris Papæ ad gloriam Dei, & ad pacem & unitatem sanctæ ecclesiæ, & omnimodum honorem Imperii honesto fine terminabitur.
units.tr: 2. But since this matter, so arduous, so salutary, and so necessary, in which the reconciliation of the holy Church of God and the salvation of all Christendom are at stake, ought not and cannot be brought to completion without the presence of your discretion, we urge and admonish you, in that faith which you owe to the Empire, to the holy Church of God and to your own soul, that, every excuse set aside, you meet us in a friendly manner, as is the custom of the court, at Besançon on the aforesaid day, with the wiser and more suitable persons of your diocese, to proceed with us to the council. And since excessive caution does no harm, bring with you many of your soldiers, armed and mounted. Moreover, bring tents, which are necessary because of the scarcity of houses. For there, by the grace of God, the whole affair of Lord Pope Victor will be brought to an honourable end, to the glory of God, to the peace and unity of the holy Church, and to the full honour of the Empire.

units.la: 3. Denique omnibus in Ordine Clericali constitutis scribimus, suadendo & rogando, quatenus ad præfatum Concilium veniant, aut ruentibus rebus suis succurrant.
units.tr: 3. Finally, we write to all who hold office in the clergy, persuading and asking them to come to the said council, or to come to the aid of their affairs in their collapse.

units.la: XVIII. De exsequendis Decretis Comitiorum Herbipolensium super confirmatione & receptione Paschalis Papæ, & damnatione Alexandri Pseudopapæ.
units.tr: ## XVIII. On carrying out the decrees of the Diet of Würzburg concerning the confirmation and reception of Pope Paschal, and the condemnation of Alexander the pseudo-pope.

units.la: FRIDERICUS Dei gratia Romanus Imperator & Semper-Augustus, dilecto fideli & consanguineo suo Henrico Comiti Trecarum, gratiam suam & omne bonum.
units.tr: FREDERICK, by the grace of God Roman Emperor and ever Augustus, to his beloved faithful kinsman Henry, Count of Troyes, greeting and every good.

units.la: 1. Cunctis populis, quos clementiæ nostræ regit Imperium, jam dudum innotuisse credimus, qualiter exorta quondam inter Ecclesiæ Romanæ Cardinales de Apostolatu discordia, in Reges & Regna impetu pestifero est diffusa, pro qua ad optabile pacis bonum revocanda, quantos post beatæ memoriæ Papæ Victoris electionem ac confirmationem Catholicam, Papiæ, Laudæ, Mediolani, Laodiceæ, atque in diversis Imperii finibus, in corpore nostro labores tam nos, quam invicti Principes nostri pertulerimus, quantas rerum copias zelo justitiæ impenderimus, in extremis quoque mundi partibus jam auditum non dubitamus. Deniq; beatissimo Papa Victore ad Paradisi gaudia assumpto, & in ejus locum ab Episcopis Cardinalibus almæ Sedis Apostolicæ, Domino Paschali viro Christianissimo in præsentia Episcoporum & Religiosorum Lombardiæ ac Tusciæ, Illustris quoq; Præfecti Urbis Romæ, cum multorum Nobilium Romanorum, Catholicè substituto, ipsum etiam Dominum Paschalē, ex Ecclesiæ ac Principum Imperii judicio atq; consilio in Papam & Patrem Catholicum solenniter recepimus, debitoq; honore venerari semper intendimus. Proinde obstinata Schismaticorum perfidia, morte viri justi suis successibus aperta fronte adscribens, Syreneis suis blanditiis fidelium quorundam nostrorum animos adeo molita est de novo immutare, ut nisi morbis novis nova maturius remedia objicerentur, pars nostrorum non modica videretur ex fiducia nostræ lenitatis seducenda.
units.tr: 1. We believe that it has long been known to all the peoples whom the Empire of our clemency governs, how a discord over the Apostolate arose among the Cardinals of the Roman Church and spread like a pestilence through kings and kingdoms. To call back the desired good of peace, we have not doubted that it has also been heard of in the farthest parts of the world, how great were the labours that we and our invincible princes endured in our own person, and how great the resources that we expended out of zeal for justice, after the election and Catholic confirmation of the blessed Pope Victor, at Pavia, Lodi, Milan, Lodi-Lodi... and in various parts of the Empire. Finally, when the blessed Pope Victor was taken up into the joys of Paradise, and in his place, by the bishops and cardinals of the holy Apostolic See, Lord Paschal, a most Christian man, was Catholically set up, in the presence of the bishops and religious men of Lombardy and Tuscany, together with the illustrious Prefect of the City of Rome and many Roman nobles, we solemnly received this same Lord Paschal, by the judgment and counsel of the Church and of the princes of the Empire, as Pope and Catholic Father, and we have always intended to honour him with due reverence. Accordingly, the obstinate perfidy of the schismatics, ascribing the death of that just man to its own successes, with open brow, by its Siren blandishments has so worked upon the minds of some of our people as to change them anew, that unless new remedies were applied to the new diseases more promptly, a no small part of our people would seem likely to be led astray from trust in our gentleness.

units.la: 2. Igitur zelo reformandi decoris domus Dei ardentius accensi, cum Regem Francorum, qui nulla nostra culpa præeunte, unà cum Rulando Imperii nostri hoste publico, ejusq; sequacibus, Impedimentum nostrum honorem manifeste molitur auferre, post multos nostros ammonitus irrevocabilem persensisse mus, universis Imperii nostri Principibus in sancto Pentecostes Curiam generalem Wirceburc indiximus, quorum cœtu celeberrimo ibidem solenniter præsidente, Ecclesiæ Dei statum, ac Domini Paschalis Papæ negotium, serio ac magnifice duximus roborandum. Invocata igitur devotissime Spiritus sancti gratia, & universorum qui aderant consilio communicato, ad removendam pro pace nostra omnem ambiguitatem ipsi nos manu propria super Sanctorum reliquias juramentum publice præstitimus, quod Rollandum Schismaticum, vel ejus successorem, quem pars ipsius elegerit, papam nunquam recipiemus, nec ad eum recipiendum allensum unquam alicui præbebimus. Nullam fautorum ejus gratiam nostram unquam *rescindemus, nisi ab errore viæ suæ ad unitatem Ecclesiæ suæ fuerit conversus. Dominum vero Paschalem Papam manutenebimus semper atq; promovimus, eiq; tanquam Patri Catholico & universali Pontifici obedientiam, honorem ac reverentiam exhibebimus, & ab ipso ejusq; parte (vita comite) nunquam recedemus. Electos quoque, qui sub ejus successore, quem pars ipsius elegerit, consecrationem receperint, honore aut ordinibus suis ejus obedientia privari nunquam permittemus, & hujus absolutionem sacramenti nunquam recipiemus, nec oblatam recipiemus.
units.tr: 2. Therefore, kindled more ardently with zeal to restore the beauty of the house of God, when we perceived that the King of the Franks, who, with no fault of ours going before, together with Rolandus, public enemy of our Empire, and his followers, openly strives to take away our honour, had been warned by us many times and had become irrevocably hardened, we summoned a general court at Würzburg at Pentecost for all the princes of our Empire. With that most crowded assembly presiding solemnly there, we resolved to strengthen earnestly and magnificently the state of the Church of God and the affair of Lord Pope Paschal. Therefore, after invoking most devoutly the grace of the Holy Spirit, and after taking counsel with all who were present, to remove all ambiguity for the sake of our peace, we ourselves, with our own hand, upon the relics of the saints, publicly swore that we would never receive Rolandus the schismatic, or his successor whom his party may choose, as pope, nor would we ever give our consent to anyone's receiving him. We would never remit the favour of any of his supporters, unless he had been converted from the error of his way to the unity of his Church. But we will always maintain and advance Lord Pope Paschal, and will render to him, as to a Catholic Father and universal Pontiff, obedience, honour and reverence, and we will never depart from him or from his party (as long as life lasts). We will also never permit those elected who have received consecration under his successor, whom his party may choose, to be deprived of honour or of their orders by his obedience, and we will never receive absolution from this sacrament, nor will we accept it when offered.

units.la: * leg. reddemus.
units.tr: * read reddemus.

units.la: 3. Præterea noster in Imperio successor, quem Principes universi elegerint, hunc honorem Ecclesiæ Dei & Imperio, & hanc partem nostram sub eodem juramento tuebitur semperatque tenebit.
units.tr: 3. Moreover, our successor in the Empire, whom all the princes shall choose, will defend and always maintain this honour of the Church of God and of the Empire, and this our part, under the same oath.

units.la: 4. Idem quoque juramentum Archiepiscopi omnes & Episcopi, atque Electi, qui interfuerunt XL. super sancta Dei Evangelia manu propria, unusquisque sub stola sua præstiterunt, & juraverunt. Nihilo minus Principes seculares universi, Dux videlicet Saxoniæ, ac Bavarus, Marchio senior, Conradus Palatinus Comes de Rheno, & Ludovicus Landgravius, & reliqui omnes Sanctorum reliquias publice id ipsum juraverunt. Repente autem Spiritus sanctus mentem adeo fecit unius voluntatis, quod Electi omnes, qui præsentes aderant, primo Reinoldus Coloniensis Electus & Italiæ Archicancellarius, deinde cæteri omnes in Sabbatho Quatuor temporum eadem Dei & honorem Imperii, sacros Ordines devotissime susceperunt.
units.tr: 4. All the archbishops, bishops, and elect who were present, about forty, likewise swore the same oath, each with his own hand upon the holy Gospels of God, under his stole. Nevertheless, all the secular princes, namely the Duke of Saxony and the Bavarian, the elder Margrave, Conrad the Count Palatine of the Rhine, and Louis the Landgrave, and all the rest, publicly swore the same upon the relics of the saints. Then suddenly the Holy Spirit made the minds of all so of one will that all the elect who were present, first Reinald, elect of Cologne and Archchancellor of Italy, and then all the others, on the Saturday of the Ember Days, most devoutly received the holy Orders for the same honour of God and of the Empire.

units.la: 5. Firmiter quoque à nobis & ab universis decretum est, ut quicunque supersunt ordinandi, in Quatuor temporibus similiter exequantur: alioquin dignitatis, ad quam electi sunt, honore, nora dilatione, priventur.
units.tr: 5. It has also been firmly decreed by us and by all that whoever remain to be ordained shall likewise be carried out in the Ember Days; otherwise they shall, without further delay, be deprived of the dignity to which they have been elected.

units.la: 6. Adhoc Honorabiles Legati Illustris amici nostri Henrici gloriosi Anglorum Regis, ad nos transmissi, in totius Curiæ nostræ præsentia, super Sanctorum reliquias ex parte Regis Angliæ nobi juraverunt, quod Rex ipse cum toto Regno suo in parte nostra fideliter stabit, Dominam Paschalem, quem nos tenemus, tenebit: de Rolando autem Schismatico manutenendo de cætero se intromittet.
units.tr: 6. Moreover, honourable envoys of our illustrious friend Henry, the glorious King of the English, sent to us, in the presence of our whole court, swore to us on the relics of the saints on behalf of the King of England, that the King himself, with his whole kingdom, will stand faithfully on our side, will hold to Lord Paschal, whom we hold; but as for maintaining Rolandus the schismatic, he will henceforth not concern himself with it.

units.la: 7. Quia verò justitiæ, quam hostes Ecclesiæ ac nostri, sive superbia, sive ex causæ suæ diffidentia erunt, nos semper hactenus stare parati, nunc tandem ad insolita sacramenta, ex eorum ina- nifesta nisi festa obstinatione, timus impulsi, à Schismaticorum communione omnis homo, omnis ... at. Favorem enim illorum, etsi aliquo modo visus est venialis, in posterum prorsus erit irremissibilis.
units.tr: 7. Since, indeed, the justice which the enemies of the Church and of ours, whether through pride or through distrust of their own cause, will (?) ... we, always hitherto ready to stand fast, now at last, driven by fear, turn to unusual sacraments from their unmanifest, not festive, obstinacy; from communion with the Schismatics let every man, every ... Their favour, though in some way it seemed venial, will in future be utterly unpardonable.

units.la: 8. Ad perfectum vero hujus negotii firmamentum, ex totius Herbipolensis Concilii decreto firmissime praecipimus, ut si quis ad sui mandatum Antistitis aut Praelatis Provinciae, vel Domini sacramentum supradictum non praestiterit, si Clericus sit aut Monachus, Ecclesiastico privetur beneficio; si Laicus, allodia & beneficia, quaecunque possidet, nostra ipsi auctoritate à suo Judice vel Domino prorsus adimantur.
units.tr: 8. For the perfect firmness of this business, by the decree of the whole Council of Würzburg we most firmly command that if anyone does not render the aforesaid sacrament (oath) at the command of his Bishop or of the prelates of the province, or to his lord, then, if he is a cleric or a monk, let him be deprived of his ecclesiastical benefice; if he is a layman, let all the allodial lands and benefices he possesses be utterly taken from him by our authority, through his judge or lord.

units.la: XIX. De Duce Burgundiae adversus injurias Regis Franciae per Imperium tuendo.
units.tr: XIX. On defending the Duke of Burgundy by the Empire against the injuries of the King of France.

units.la: FRIDERICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator, Semper Augustus, dilecto & fideli suo Henrico Comiti Trecarum gratiam suam & omne bonum. Audivimus, unde plurimum gravi dolemus, quod Rex videlicet Franciae in proximo festo sancti Johannis terram Ducis Divionensis nostri dilecti, & nostri obligati, hostiliter intrare atque destruere proponit. Quod nos nullatenus possumus aut debemus sinistre. Unde tuam dilectionem, cui plenarie confidimus, toto affectu hortamur, & summopere postulamus, quatenus pro nostro amore ipsum Regem ab hoc proposito modis omnibus retrahas & impedias, & ne per te vel per tuos ipsi Duci aliquod damnum vel gravamen proveniat, te ipsum à consilio & auxilio Regis subtrahas, nec Duci noceas. Quod si Rex ab hac intentione deflectere vel superseder nolverit, scias pro certo, quod non patiemur nec sufferemus, immo eri resistendo amicum nostrum Ducem cum toto robore Imperii nostri privare cum & defensare. Verumtamen si inter Ducem & matrem ejus aliqua quaestio, quae tendit ad discordiam orta est vel fuerit, nos una tecum ad eandem quaestionem componendam facis ex abundanti ... possumus.
units.tr: FREDERICK, by the grace of God Roman Emperor, ever Augustus, to his beloved and faithful Henry, Count of Troyes, grace and every good. We have heard, and we grieve greatly, that the King of France proposes to enter hostilely and lay waste, at the coming feast of St John, the land of our beloved Duke of Dijon, who is also bound to us. This we can and ought in no way regard with indifference. Therefore we exhort your affection, in which we place full trust, with all our warmth, and earnestly request that, for our sake, you restrain and hinder the King from this purpose by every means, and that you withdraw yourself from the King's counsel and aid, and do no harm to the Duke, so that no damage or burden comes to the Duke through you or yours. If the King will not turn aside or delay from this intention, know for certain that we will not suffer or permit it; indeed, we will resist, and with the whole strength of our Empire we will deprive and defend our friend the Duke. Nevertheless, if any dispute which tends to discord has arisen or shall arise between the Duke and his mother, we can, together with you, readily settle the same question ...

units.la: XX. De Represaliis contra Regis Franciae subditos in Imperio concedendis, si Imperialis homines in Francia laedantur.
units.tr: XX. On granting reprisals against the subjects of the King of France within the Empire, should Imperial men be harmed in France.

units.la: GLORIOSO & Magnifico LUDOVICO Regi Francorum, N. Christi Dei gratia Imperialis Cancellarius, & Legatus Italiae, salutem & servitium suum. Ratio suggerit, & Principum consuetudo deposcit, ut quemadmodum Regni vel Imperii negotiatores per Romanum Imperium pacem & securitatem fruuntur, ita vestra vice nostri nullatenus sub vestra juris dictione laedantur. Quia igitur Mauriensis Vicecomes quosdam nostros mercatores injuste exspoliavit, & unum ex eis in captivitate et compeditum, petimus & ex parte Augusti Serenissimi vestram Excellentiam commonemus, ut hominem & res detentas reddi faciatis. Alioquin si damna illius modi per vestros negotiatores illata resarcita, aut si novum teloneum ad damnum resarciendum super vestros mercatores fuerit constitutum, vestra discretio non gravetur.
units.tr: To the glorious and magnificent Louis, King of the Franks, N., by the grace of Christ God Imperial Chancellor and Legate of Italy, greeting and his service. Reason suggests, and the custom of princes requires, that just as the merchants of your kingdom enjoy peace and security throughout the Roman Empire, so in turn our merchants should in no way be harmed under your jurisdiction. Since therefore the Viscount of Maurienne has unjustly plundered some of our merchants, and has held one of them captive and in chains, we ask, and on behalf of the most serene Augustus we admonish your Excellency, to have the man and the detained goods restored. Otherwise, if the losses of that kind inflicted by your merchants are made good, or if a new toll has been imposed upon your merchants to make good the damage, let your discretion not be troubled.

units.la: FRIDERICI I. IMPER. AUG. LAUDUM.
units.tr: The Laudum of Frederick I, Emperor and Augustus.

units.la: Super Ducatu Bavariae & Marchionatu Superioris Austriae.
units.tr: Concerning the Duchy of Bavaria and the March of Upper Austria.

units.la: FRIDERICUS divina favente clementia Romanorum Imperator Semper Augustus. Quamquam rerum commutatio ex ipsa corporali institutione possit firma constitui, vel ea, quae legitur vel geruntur, nulla valeant refragatione convelli, ne qua tamen possit esse gestae rei dubitas, nostra debet Imperialis auctoritas praecavere.
units.tr: Frederick, by the favour of divine mercy, Roman Emperor and ever Augustus. Although a change in the possession of things may be firmly established by the very terms of its grant, and although what has been read or done may not be overturned by any objection, nevertheless, lest any doubt arise about the matter done, our imperial authority ought to take precautions.

units.la: 1. Noverit igitur omnium Christi Imperiique nostri fidelium praesens aetas, & futura qualiter nos, cujus cooperante gratia, à quo caelitus pax missa est hominibus super terram, in nostra Curia Ratisponae, in nativitate sanctae Mariae celebrata, in praesentia multorum Religiosorum & Catholicorum Principum, litem & controversiam, quae inter dilectissimum patrum nostrum Henricum Ducem Austriae, & Karissimum nepotem nostrum Henricum Ducem Saxoniae, diu exstitit super Ducatu Bavariae, & super Marchia à superiori fluminis parte Anasi, terminavimus modo. Quod Dux Austriae resignavit nobis Ducatum Bavariae & dictam Marchiam, quater... Quo resignatione facta, mox eundem Ducatum Bavariae in beneficium contulimus Duci Saxoniae. Dux autem Bavariae resignavit nobis Marchiam Austriae cum omni jure suo, & cum omnibus beneficiis, quae quondam Marchio Leopoldus habebat ad Ducatum Bavariae.
units.tr: 1. Let the present age and future generations of all the faithful of Christ and of our empire know how we, by whose cooperating grace peace was sent from heaven to men upon earth, at our court at Regensburg, celebrated at the Nativity of St Mary, in the presence of many religious and Catholic princes, have now brought to an end the suit and controversy which for a long time existed between our most beloved father Henry, Duke of Austria, and our dearest nephew Henry, Duke of Saxony, concerning the Duchy of Bavaria, and concerning the March beyond the river Anasus (Enns). The Duke of Austria resigned to us the Duchy of Bavaria and the said March, four times... When this resignation was made, we at once bestowed the same Duchy of Bavaria as a benefice on the Duke of Saxony. The Duke of Bavaria, for his part, resigned to us the March of Austria with all his right, and with all the benefices which the late Margrave Leopold had held from the Duchy of Bavaria.

units.la: 2. Ne autem in hoc facto honor & gloria patrui nostri charissimi aliquatenus minuatur, consilio & judicio Principum approbantibus, Illustri Uladislao Duce Bohemiae sententiam promulgante, Marchiam Austriae in Ducatum commutavimus, & eundem Ducatum cum omni jure, praefato patruo nostro Heinrico, & praenobilissimae uxori suae Theodorae, iisque beneficium concessimus, perpetuo jure tenendum, ut ipsi & liberi eorum post eos indifferenter filiae eundem Ducatum Austriae haereditario jure à Regno teneant & possideant.
units.tr: 2. Lest, however, in this matter the honour and glory of our most dear uncle be diminished in any degree, with the counsel and judgment of the princes approving, and with the Illustrious Ladislaus, Duke of Bohemia, pronouncing the sentence, we have exchanged the March of Austria for a duchy, and have granted that same duchy, with all right, to our aforesaid uncle Henry and his most noble wife Theodora, and to their heirs, to be held in perpetuity, so that they and their children after them, sons and daughters alike, may hold and possess the same Duchy of Austria by hereditary right from the Kingdom.

units.la: 3. Stabilem praedictus Dux Austriae, patruus noster, & uxor ejus absq; liberis decesserint, liberam habeant facultatem eundem Ducatum affectandi, cui voluerint.
units.tr: 3. If the aforesaid Duke of Austria, our uncle, and his wife die without children, they shall have the free power to grant the same duchy to whomever they wish.

units.la: 4. Statuimus quoq;, ut nulla magna persona in ejusdem Ducatus regimine sine Ducum consensu vel permissione, aliquam justitiam praesumat exercere.
units.tr: 4. We also decree that no great person in the government of this duchy shall presume to exercise any jurisdiction without the consent or permission of the dukes.

units.la: 5. Dux vero Austriae de Ducatu suo aliud servitium non debet Imperio, nisi quod ad Curias, quas Imperator praenixerit in Bavaria, evocatus venire; nullamq; expeditionem debeat, nisi forte quam Imperator in Regna vel provincias Austriae vicinas ordinaverit.
units.tr: 5. The Duke of Austria, moreover, shall owe the Empire no other service from his duchy, except that he come when summoned to those courts which the Emperor shall appoint in Bavaria; nor shall he owe any military expedition, unless perhaps one which the Emperor shall order into the kingdoms or provinces neighbouring Austria.

units.la: Ceterum ut haec nostra Institutio omni aevo rata & inconvulsa permaneat, praesentem inde paginam conscribi, & sigilli nostri impressione insigniri jussimus, adhibitis testibus idoneis, quorum nomina sunt haec: Pilgrinus Aquilegiensis Patriarcha. Eberhardus Archiepiscopus Salisburgensis. Otto Episcopus Frisingensis. Conradus Episcopus Brixinensis. Henricus Episcopus Ratisbonensis, & Tridentinensis. Dominus Welpho Dux Spoletae. Conradus frater Imperatoris [Dux Sueviae.] Fridericus filius Regis * Conradi [Dux Sueviae.] Henricus Dux Carinthiae. Marchio Engelbertus de Istria. Marchio Albertus de Baden. [alii habent, de Stachen, sive Staden.] Dietpoldus Marchio de Voburg. Otto Comes Palatinus [sc. de Wittelinspach] & frater ejus Fridericus. Gebhardus Comes de Sultzbach. Engelbertus Comes de Hail. Gebhardus Comes de Burckhausen: & alii quam plures.
units.tr: Furthermore, so that this our ordinance may remain valid and unshaken for all time, we have ordered that a present document be written up concerning it and marked with the impression of our seal, with suitable witnesses present, whose names are these: Pilgrim, Patriarch of Aquileia. Eberhard, Archbishop of Salzburg. Otto, Bishop of Freising. Conrad, Bishop of Brixen. Henry, Bishop of Regensburg and of Trent. Lord Welf, Duke of Spoleto. Conrad, brother of the Emperor [Duke of Swabia]. Frederick, son of King Conrad [Duke of Swabia]. Henry, Duke of Carinthia. Margrave Engelbert of Istria. Margrave Albert of Baden [others have "of Stachen, or Staden"]. Dietpold, Margrave of Vohburg. Otto, Count Palatine [namely of Wittelsbach], and his brother Frederick. Gebhard, Count of Sulzbach. Engelbert, Count of Hall. Gebhard, Count of Burghausen; and very many others.

units.la: Signum Domini FRIDERICI Imperatoris invictissimi.
units.tr: Sign of Lord Frederick, the most invincible Emperor.

units.la: Ego Reinaldus Cancellarius vice Arnoldi Moguntinensis Archiepiscopi & Archicancellarii, recognovi: regnante Domino FRIDERICO Rom. Imp. in Christo. Datum Ratisbonae 15. Cal. Octobr. indictione quarta, anno Dominicae Incarnationis MCLVI. anno Regni ejus quinto, Imperii secundo.
units.tr: I, Reinald, Chancellor, in place of Arnold, Archbishop of Mainz and Archchancellor, have witnessed this: in the reign of Lord Frederick, Roman Emperor, in Christ. Given at Regensburg, 15 Kalends of October, in the fourth indiction, in the year of the Lord's Incarnation 1156, in the fifth year of his reign and the second of his empire.

units.la: PACTUM QUOD PEPIGERUNT ROMANI CUM DO- MINO FRIDERICO IMPERATORE ET S- emper Augusto.
units.tr: The Pact which the Romans made with the Lord Frederick, Emperor and ever Augustus.

units.la: JURAVERUNT praesentes, & jurabunt futuri Senatores & totus Populus Romanus Domino Friderico Imperatori fidelitatem, & quod juvabunt eum coronam Imperii Romani retinere, & defendere eum contra omnes homines: & justitias suas tam intra Urbem, quam extra juvabunt eum retinere, & quod numquam erunt tam in consilio quam in facto, ubi Dominus Imperator mala captione capiatur, vel membrum perdat, vel aliquod detrimentum in persona sua patiatur, & quod Senatum non nisi per eum vel per Nuncium suum ordinabunt, sine fraude & malo ingenio.
units.tr: The present Senators and the whole Roman People have sworn, and future Senators will swear, fidelity to the Lord Frederick the Emperor, and that they will help him to retain the crown of the Roman Empire and defend him against all men; and that they will help him to retain his rights both within the City and outside it; and that they will never be, either in counsel or in deed, where the Lord Emperor is caught by a snare, or loses a limb, or suffers any harm to his person; and that they will appoint the Senate only through him or through his envoy, without deceit or evil design.

units.la: 1. Dominus Imperator confirmabit Senatum perpetuo in eo vigore, in quo nunc est, & augebit tenore, ut Senatus per eum ordinetur, & ei subjectus sit, & faciet inde privilegium cum sigillo, in quo contineantur haec, videlicet confirmatio Senatus, & quod faciet salva omnia jura Populi Romani, quantum ad Imperatorem pertinet, quod ea illis non auferet, & Urbis, & locationis libellos tertii & quarti generis conservabit, & praecipiet in eodem privilegio ne auferri Romanis in toto Imperio suo plateatium, portaticum, aut ripaticum: & si aliquis fort qui ipsum fecerit, incidat in poenam centum librarum auri.
units.tr: 1. The Lord Emperor shall confirm the Senate in perpetuity in the vigour it now has, and shall enlarge it by its tenor, so that the Senate is appointed through him and is subject to him; and he shall make thereof a privilege under seal, in which the following shall be contained: namely, the confirmation of the Senate; and that he will preserve all the rights of the Roman People, so far as they pertain to the Emperor, and will not take them away from them; and that he will keep the libelli of the third and fourth kind concerning the City and its leases; and he shall direct in the same privilege that no plateaticum, portaticum, or ripaticum be levied from the Romans in his whole Empire; and if anyone perchance shall do so, he shall incur a penalty of one hundred pounds of gold.

units.la: 2. Haec omnia cum subscriptione Principum Curiae fient.
units.tr: 2. All these things shall be done with the signature of the Princes of the Court.

units.la: FRIDERICI I. IMPER. AUG. DECRETUM
units.tr: DECREE OF EMPEROR FREDERICK I, AUGUSTUS

units.la: De duobus schismaticis Archiepiscopis Salisburgensibus removendis, & novo ab se confirmato & investito recipiendo.
units.tr: On the removal of the two schismatic Archbishops of Salzburg, and the receiving of the new archbishop confirmed and invested by him.

units.la: FRIDERICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator & Semper Augustus, dilectis suis omnibus ac Ministerialibus Salzburgensis Ecclesiae, & universo clero & populo in suis Ecclesiae, in Carinthiam & Marchiam (Stirensem) constitutis, gratiam suam & omne bonum.
units.tr: Frederick, by the grace of God Roman Emperor and ever Augustus, to all his beloved ministerials of the church of Salzburg, and to the whole clergy and people established in his churches in Carinthia and the March (of Styria): his grace and every blessing.
1. Whereas

units.la: 1. Cùm Deo pacis auctori & amatori placuit Romanum Imperium in unam vocare cum Romana Ecclesia, & pacis jocunditate post diutinos labores universam respirare Ecclesiam, habit animum pro Salzburgensis Ecclesiæ statu solicitos esse, & ejus restaurationi diligenter intendere, quoniam per duos sibi invicem oppositos Ecclesia graviter distracta fuerat, nec aliqua spes superesset ut manus, quæ distraxerant, in integrum possent distracta restituere, tam Domno & Papæ, quam tribus ejus Domnis Cardinalibus, nobis quoq; & majoribus Imperii Principibus, visum fuit utrosq; removeri; & alium, per quem facilius reformari posset Ecclesia, substitui. Post multam deliberationem, in gratia & beneplacito Domni Papæ ac nostro, uterq; super hoc verbo se potestate juris, quod in Salzburgensi Ecclesia quisq; videbatur habere, in manus Domni Papæ ac penitus abrenunciavit.
units.tr: 1. When it pleased God, the author and lover of peace, to bring the Roman Empire into unity with the Roman Church, and after long labours to let the whole Church breathe again in the joy of peace, we resolved to be concerned for the condition of the church of Salzburg and to apply ourselves diligently to its restoration. The church had been grievously torn apart by two men opposed to each other, and no hope remained that the hands which had torn it apart could restore what was torn. It seemed good to us, and to the greater princes of the Empire, that both should be removed, both the Domnus and the Pope and his three Domnus cardinals, and that another be put in their place through whom the Church could more easily be reformed. After long deliberation, by the favour and pleasure of the lord Pope and of ourselves, each of them renounced entirely, in this matter, into the hands of the lord Pope whatever power of right each seemed to have in the church of Salzburg.

units.la: 2. Vacante sic Ecclesia Prælatos Salzburgenses & alios, qui cum ipsis aderant, de faciendis electione diligenter convenimus. Sed, licet nobis magna supplicarent instantia, ut ad usque omnium præsentiam differretur electio, tamen Domni Papæ mandato ac nostro, & omnium Principum consilio, quoniam sepe nocet differre paratis, ad electionem accesserunt, & de gremio Ecclesiæ Romanæ, Dominum videlicet Chunradum Guinei nostrum Palatinum, in Ecclesia vestra enutritu, in Pastorem & Episcopū animarū suarum corditer & unanimi voce elegerūt. Quam utiq; electionē Domnus Papa totaq; Curia ratam habuit, confirmavit, nosq; de regalibus ipsum investituus cū ea integritate, qua Archiepiscopus Eberhardus decedens illa tenuisse dinoscitur. Nam generali Principū sententia judicatū est, quidquid vel prædictum ejusdem Ecclesiæ bona in nostra teneremus potestate, vel per quoslibet alios infeudatum, quocunq; modo sub hoc tempore est alienatum, inane prorsus esse debere & irritum.
units.tr: 2. The church being thus vacant, we, together with the prelates of Salzburg and the others who were present with them, carefully met to make an election. Although they begged us with great insistence that the election be deferred until all were present, nevertheless, by the mandate of the lord Pope and of ourselves, and by the counsel of all the princes, since delay often harms those who are ready, they proceeded to the election. From the bosom of the Roman Church, namely the lord Conrad, our Palatine of Guinei, who had been brought up in your church, they unanimously and with one heart chose him as minister and bishop of their souls. The lord Pope and the whole Curia approved and confirmed this election, and we invested him with the regalia, with the same integrity that Archbishop Eberhard, at his death, was known to have held them. For it was judged by the general sentence of the princes that whatever goods of the same church we held in our power, or that had been enfeoffed to anyone else, or alienated in any way during this period, must be utterly empty and void.

units.la: 3. Quamvis ergo Majestas nostra sæpenumero à vobis graviter læsa sit, & acriter ultrà, provocata, tamen divini amoris intuitu, ac beati Ruodberti reverentia, & ex consueta Imperialis mansuetudinis clementia, tam vos quàm Salzburgensem Ecclesiam serena pietate propospicere, & in antiquum statum nostræ auctoritatis munimine revocate. Universitatem igitur diligenter commonitam esse cupimus, ut, quod tam à Domno Papa, quàm à nobis, ad honorem restaurationem Ecclesiæ Salzburgensis in spiritualibus & in temporalibus modo factum est, debita veneratione & alacritate recipiatis, ac ratum teneatis; & Domno Chunrado Archiepiscopo vestro, consanguineo nostro, ea fide & devotione & obedientia & servire studeatis, ut nostræ benignitatis ctum merito super hoc experiri debeatis. Si quis verò, quod non credimus, his, quæ magna cōstitutione ad utilitatem & reformationem Salzburgensis Ecclesiæ nunc ordinata sunt, contrarium sumpserit, & à Domno Papa excommunicationis sententiam recipiet, & nostræ Majestatis indignationem proculdubio sentiet. Datum Venetiæ, v. Idus Augusti, Anno Dominicæ incarnationis MCLXXVII.
units.tr: 3. Although our Majesty has often been gravely wronged by you, and sharply provoked beyond measure, nevertheless, out of regard for divine love, in reverence for the blessed Ruodbert, and from the customary clemency of imperial gentleness, we have resolved to look upon you and the church of Salzburg with calm piety, and to restore it to its former state under the protection of our authority. We therefore wish the whole community to be diligently warned that you receive with due reverence and eagerness, and hold as valid, what has now been done for the honour and restoration of the church of Salzburg, in spiritual and temporal matters, both by the lord Pope and by us. Serve the lord Conrad, your archbishop and our kinsman, with such faith, devotion and obedience that you may deservedly experience in this matter the kindness of our goodwill. If anyone, which we do not believe, takes a position contrary to what has now been ordained by this great constitution for the benefit and reform of the church of Salzburg, and receives sentence of excommunication from the lord Pope, he will without doubt feel the indignation of our Majesty. Given at Venice, on the fifth day before the Ides of August, in the year of the Lord's incarnation 1177.

units.la: FRIDERICI I. IMPER. AUG. RESCRIPTUM AD EMANVELEM PORPHYROGENETVM, IMPERA- TOREM CONSTANTINOPOLITANUM,
units.tr: Rescript of Frederick I, Emperor Augustus, to Manuel Porphyrogenitus, Emperor of Constantinople

units.la: Quod Græcorum Imperator de jure subditus esse debeat Romano Imperio.
units.tr: That the Emperor of the Greeks ought by right to be subject to the Roman Empire.

units.la: FRIDERICUS divina favente clementia, inclytus Triumphator, Romanorum Imperator Dei coronatus, sublimis in Christo, Fidelis, Magnus, Pacificus, Gloriosus Cæsar, Græcorum Imperator, & semper Augustus, salutem & fraterni amoris affectum.
units.tr: Frederick, by the favour of divine clemency, illustrious triumphant Emperor of the Romans, crowned by God, exalted in Christ, faithful, great, peaceful, glorious Caesar, Emperor of the Greeks, and ever Augustus, sends greeting and the affection of brotherly love.

units.la: 1. Sicut ille Rex Regum, à quo omnis potestas, Romanum Imperium caput totius orbis constituit, ita etiam Sedem Romanæ Ecclesiæ omnium Ecclesiarum unicam matrem, dominam, et stramq; ordinavit. quod utiq; duorum numero gladiorum signavit, quos dixit orbi sufficere, thor fidei Christianæ.
units.tr: (1) As that King of kings, from whom all power comes, has established the Roman Empire as the head of the whole world, so he has also ordained the See of the Roman Church as the sole mother and mistress of all churches; and this he indeed marked by the number of two swords, which he said were sufficient for the world, that is, the two pillars of the Christian faith.

units.la: 2. Quapropter tuam prudentiam commonemus, quatinus nobis & Romano Imperio rem debitum recognoscas, & Summo Pontifici, quem nomine Sanctum appellas, debitam obedientiam & honorem.
units.tr: (2) Therefore we admonish your prudence that you acknowledge the due obligation to us and to the Roman Empire, and to the Supreme Pontiff, whom you call holy, the due obedience and honour.

units.la: FRIDERICI I. IMPER. AUG. DECRETUM
units.tr: FREDERICK I, AUGUST EMPEROR, DECREE

units.la: De translatione fori remittenda: & de libera bonorum traditione ad Ecclesias ab Imperatore obtinenda.
units.tr: On the remission of the transfer of a market, and on the free surrender of goods to churches to be obtained from the Emperor.

units.la: IN nomine sanctæ & individuæ Trinitatis. FRIDERICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator Semper-Augustus.
units.tr: In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity. Frederick, by the grace of God Emperor of the Romans, ever August.

units.la: 1. Quæ Imperiali constituuntur auctoritate, literis competit annotari, ne vel transeuntium porum antiquitate in oblivionem devenient, vel pravorum hominum fraudulentis machinationibus indignam sui mutationem incurrant.
units.tr: 1. Those things which are established by imperial authority ought to be committed to writing, so that they do not fall into oblivion through the passage of time, nor suffer unworthy alteration through the fraudulent schemes of wicked men.

units.la: 2. Noverint igitur universi, tam præsentes, quàm posterî futurae ætatis, fideles Imperii quos ctus noster Adilbertus Frisingensis Episcopus, ad Majestatis nostræ præsentiā accedens, humiliter hi conquerendo significavit, quòd Nobilis vir, Henricus de Brunsvvick, quondam Dux Bavariæ & Saxoniæ, forum in Vergen cum ponte, & Ecclesia tua à lóge retroactis temporibus quiete possederat, dilaxerit, & illud in villa Munchen violenter transtulerit. Cujus siquidem rei veritas, etsi nostræ conscientiæ Serenitati, ipse tamen eam septem legitimis testibus, in nostra cóprobavit audientia. Sunt autem Conradus Saltzburgensis Archiepiscopus, Chuno Ratisbonensis Episcopus, Berchtoldus Marchio Istriæ, Gebhardus Comes de Sultzbach, Otto Palatinus major, & frater ejus Otto minor, Fridericus Burggravius.
units.tr: 2. Let all, both present and future generations, know that our faithful subjects, Adalbert, Bishop of Freising, approaching the presence of our Majesty, humbly complained and made known that the noble man Henry of Brunswick, formerly Duke of Bavaria and Saxony, had for a long time disturbed the market at Vergen with its bridge, and your Church had peacefully possessed it in past times, and had violently transferred it to the village of Munich. Although the truth of this matter was known to the serenity of our conscience, he nevertheless proved it before our hearing by seven lawful witnesses. These are: Conrad, Archbishop of Salzburg; Chuno, Bishop of Regensburg; Berthold, Margrave of Istria; Gebhard, Count of Sulzbach; Otto the elder Palatine, and his brother Otto the younger; Frederick, Burgrave.

units.la: 5. Consequenter igitur super eadem causa à Principibus Curiæ nostræ, requisita sententia, judicatum quod præfati Henrici factum temerarium in irritum ducere Imperialis deberet autoritas.
units.tr: 5. Consequently, therefore, the Princes of our Court, when their opinion was sought on the same matter, judged that the authority of the Empire ought to annul the rash deed of the aforesaid Henry.

units.la: 4. Quocirca secundum juris tenorem, translationem prædicti fori in vacuum revocantes, ipsum forum cum ponte memorato, fideli nostro Episcopo Frisingenti, suisque successoribus, restituimus, & privilegio eis & suæ Ecclesiæ in perpetuum confirmamus.
units.tr: 4. Wherefore, in accordance with the tenor of the law, we revoke the transfer of the aforesaid market to nothing, and we restore the same market with the said bridge to our faithful Bishop of Freising and his successors, and confirm it by privilege to them and to their Church forever.

units.la: 5.
