Item ad instantiam prætaxati venerabilis Episcopi postulationem ex indulgentia Imperialis Clementiæ permissimus, & benevolo approbamus assensu, ut prædia quæcunque, sumptibus suis ipse conquisivit, prohibitu suo Ecclesiis vel aliis religiosis locis, seu ad Altaria quaelibet possit contradere, & de eorundem præ aliorum reditibus pro suo arbitrio ordinare.
units.tr: 5. Likewise, at the petition of the aforesaid venerable Bishop, we have by the indulgence of Imperial Clemency permitted and with gracious assent approved that he may, with his own consent, give over to churches or other religious places, or to any altars whatsoever, any estates which he himself has acquired at his own expense, and may dispose of the revenues of the same at his own discretion, in preference to others.

units.la: 6. Erut hæc nostra constitutio in omne ævum rata permaneat & incovulsa, per præsentem paginam memoriam facti conscribi fecimus, & Majestatis nostræ bulla communiri. Testes hujus rei prædicti Conradus Saltzburgensis Archiepiscopus. Chuno Ratisbonensis Episcopus. Berchtoldus Marchio Istriæ. Otto Palatinus Major. | fc.de Scheiren & Witteslpach. Otto Palatinus minor. Gebhardus Comes de Sultzbach. Fridericus 4 Burggravius....... Itemalii testes, qui eidem negotio intererant: Diethpoldus Pataviensis Episcopus. Henricus Curiensis Electus, Geffiodonius Mantuensis Episcopus. Gotefridus Cancellarius Imperialis. Rudolphus Notarius Imperialis. Romanus Præpositus Halberstattensis. Henricus Burggravius..... Siberto Comes de Nuivvenburg. Heinricus Comes de Altendorff. Degenhard Comes de Holenstain. Conrad Burggravius de Nurmberg. Amelbrecht de Lochhofen. Heinricus Marschalch de Papenheim. Burckhardus Camerarius. Atzo Camerarius. Regilo Camerarius. Rudolphus de Waldecke. Heinricus Felix Prior. Adilold de Dombach. Engelram de Achdorff, & frater ejus Heinricus. Rudolphus de Ried. Hartinus Malscadus. Berchtholdus de Reihemhausen. Sibot de Holtzhausen.
units.tr: 6. That this our constitution may remain valid and inviolate for all time, we have caused the memorial of the deed to be written in this present document, and to be strengthened by the bulla of our Majesty. Witnesses of this matter: the aforesaid Conrad, Archbishop of Salzburg; Chuno, Bishop of Regensburg; Berthold, Margrave of Istria; Otto the elder Palatine; Schiren and Wittelsbach; Otto the younger Palatine; Gebhard, Count of Sulzbach; Frederick, Burgrave. Other witnesses who were present at the same business: Diepold, Bishop of Passau; Henry, Elect of Chur; Geoffrey, Bishop of Mantua; Gottfried, Imperial Chancellor; Rudolph, Imperial Notary; Romanus, Provost of Halberstadt; Henry, Burgrave; Siegfried, Count of Neuenburg; Henry, Count of Altendorf; Degenhard, Count of Hohenstein; Conrad, Burgrave of Nuremberg; Amelbrecht of Lochhofen; Henry, Marshal of Papenheim; Burkhard, Chamberlain; Atto, Chamberlain; Regilo, Chamberlain; Rudolph of Waldeck; Henry Felix, Prior; Adelold of Dombach; Engelram of Achdorf, and his brother Henry; Rudolph of Ried; Hartwig Malscad; Berthold of Reichenhausen; Sibot of Holzhausen.

units.la: Ego Gottfridus Imperialis Aulæ Cancellarius vice Domini Christiani Moguntiæ Sedis Archiepiscopi, Germaniæ Archicancellarii, recognovi.
units.tr: I, Gottfried, Chancellor of the Imperial Court, acting for Christian, Archbishop of the See of Mainz, Archchancellor of Germany, have acknowledged this.

units.la: Signum Domini Fridericι Romanorum Imperatoris invictissimi.
units.tr: Seal of the Lord Frederick, most invincible Emperor of the Romans.

units.la: Acta sunt hæc anno ab incarnatione Domini MCLXXX, indictione XIII. Regnante Friderico Romanorum Imperatore gloriosissimo: anno Regni ejus XXIX. Imperii vero XXVI. Datum Ratisbonæ in solenni Curia, III. Idus Julii, feliciter: AMEN.
units.tr: These things were done in the year of the Lord's incarnation 1180, in the thirteenth indiction, Frederick being Emperor of the Romans, most glorious: in the twenty-ninth year of his reign and the twenty-sixth of his empire. Given at Regensburg in the solemn Court, on the third day before the Ides of July, happily. AMEN.

units.la: ISAACI ANGELI IMPERATORIS CONSTANTINOPOLITANI MANDATUM
units.tr: MANDATE OF ISAAC ANGELUS, EMPEROR OF CONSTANTINOPLE

units.la: AD FRIDERICVM IMPERATOREM ROMANORVM, De Superioritate recognoscenda.
units.tr: TO FREDERICK, EMPEROR OF THE ROMANS, On Acknowledging His Superiority.

units.la: Sacratissimus Imperator Constantinopolitanus, mandat tibi Advocato Romanæ Urbis gratiam sum, si dignaris: eam si dedigneris, scire tamé te oportet, Monarchiam Romanæ Urbis penes eum esse, cum superiorem tibi imperitare debere, quod nunc ut cedas oportet, quia te & exercitum terminis suæ ditionis tanquam retibus conclusit.
units.tr: The most sacred Emperor of Constantinople charges you, the Advocate of the City of Rome, to grant him your favour, if you deign to. But if you disdain to, you ought nonetheless to know that the sovereignty of the City of Rome rests with him, since he ought to rule over you as your superior. And now you ought to yield, because he has enclosed you and your army within the bounds of his dominion, as if in nets.

units.la: FRIDERICI I. IMPER. AUG. RESPONSUM
units.tr: FREDERICK I, EMPEROR AUGUSTUS: REPLY

units.la: De superioritate Romani Imperii super Latinos & Graecos, & cunctos orbis populos.
units.tr: On the superiority of the Roman Empire over the Latins and Greeks, and over all the peoples of the world.

units.la: SCIAT ille tuus, quem Sacratissimum Imperatorem vocas, me electione Principum & consecratione universalis Papæ Urbis Romæ, nomen Imperatoris & Romani Imperii dignitatemque suscepisse, ab Imperatoribus, avis scilicet meis & proavis, sanguine Ducem, sanctitatis nomen, sicut arrogans canis, mihi non ascribere, qui me peccatorem agnosco. Pro peccatis vero meis ob defensionem Christianæ gentis irrer hoc aggredior, & nulla prorsus apud eum, sed penes nos, auctore Deo, & in omnibus terris Romani majestas Imperii constitit. Retia, quibus nos conclusos applaudit, tela aranearum essent, facile rumpemus, eoque vilipendimus. Id cani tuo refer, et conspectu nostro lerrimè recedens: quia si Romani offuscaretur gloria Imperii, signum forsitan tu referres, qualis nitas Domini tui exigit.
units.tr: Let that man of yours, whom you call the most sacred Emperor, know that I have received the name of Emperor and the dignity of the Roman Empire by the election of the princes and the consecration of the universal Pope of the city of Rome, and that I have received them from Emperors who were my grandfathers and great-grandfathers by blood. Let him not ascribe to me the name of holiness, like an arrogant dog, since I acknowledge myself a sinner. I undertake this task for the defence of the Christian people, for the sake of my own sins; and the majesty of the Roman Empire rests in no way with him, but with us, by the authority of God, and throughout all lands. The nets with which he boasts of having enclosed us are spiders' webs; we will easily break through them, and so we hold them in contempt. Report this to your dog, and withdraw quickly from our sight. For if the glory of the Roman Empire were dimmed, you might perhaps report a sign of what the dignity of your lord requires.

units.la: FRIDERICI I. IMPER. AUG. RESPONSUM
units.tr: Reply of Frederick I, Emperor Augustus

units.la: In Regem Graecorum, qui in litteris, quas tribus vicibus Domino Imperatori misit, nomen ejus taciuit, nec eum Imperatorem vocavit, pronuntiatum publicè Philippopoli in Imperiali ha- bitu & tribunali, circumstantibus S. Rom. Imperii Principibus, in præsen- tia Legatorum Graecorum.
units.tr: Concerning the King of the Greeks, who in the letters he sent to our Lord the Emperor three times left out his name and did not call him Emperor. Pronounced publicly at Philippopolis, in imperial dress and on the tribunal, with the princes of the Holy Roman Empire standing around, in the presence of the Greek envoys.

units.la: NON possumus satis mirari, & indignum valde gerimus, quòd frater noster nomen nostrum, quod multis Regibus, & Principibus, & Provinciis notum est, quod FRIDERICUS dicitur, in literis suis ponere non consuevit. Antecessor verò ipsius piæ recordationis EMMANUEL, & quando inimici eramus ad invicem nomen nostrum expressè posuit in literis suis, nec in aliquo dignitatibus nostræ Majestatis derogavit. Quod & nos ei versa vice fecimus. Prædecessor quidem bonæ memoriæ KAROLUS victoria felix monarchiam urbis Romæ obtinuit, & plus quam gentis annis sine interruptione ad tempora nostra usque derivata est. Et nos, auctore Deo, & Principum libera electione, celsitudine sacri Romani Imperii fermè xxxvIII annis potestative gloriamur. In urbe enim Roma, quæ Domina & caput orbis dicitur, coronam & Imperium totius Christianitatis ab altari B. Petri Apostolorum Principis accepimus, à Domno Adriano Papa successore Petri unctus oleo exultationis præ participibus nostris, & nomen nostrum celebre & gloriosum in cunctis terris. Hæc idcirco diximus, si forte Dominus vester nomen & dignitatem nostram ignorat. Scriptis, de cætero literas ejus non recipiemus, nisi solennitas nominis & Majestatis nostræ expressè contineatur. Nos enim eum nomine suo appellavimus, & appellamus.
units.tr: We cannot sufficiently wonder at this, and we take it very badly that our brother does not customarily write our name in his letters, the name that is known to many kings, princes and provinces: Frederick. His predecessor, of blessed memory Emmanuel, even when we were enemies towards one another, expressly put our name in his letters, and in nothing did he detract from the dignity of our Majesty. We, in turn, did the same for him. Indeed, our predecessor of good memory, Charles, happy in victory, obtained the monarchy of the city of Rome, and it has passed down to our times without interruption for more than a thousand years. And we, by the favour of God and the free election of the princes, glory in the exalted power of the Holy Roman Empire for nearly 38 years. For in the city of Rome, which is called the Lady and head of the world, we received the crown and the Empire of all Christendom from the altar of the blessed Peter, prince of the Apostles, anointed by Lord Adrian the Pope, successor of Peter, with the oil of gladness above our fellows; and our name is celebrated and glorious in all lands. We have said these things so that, if perhaps your Lord does not know our name and dignity, he may learn it. Henceforth we will not receive his letters in writing unless the solemn form of our name and Majesty is expressly contained in them. For we have addressed him, and do address him, by his own name.

units.la: 2. Dominus vester Sanctum se appellat: mirabilis est sanctitas, quæ sanctos viros, honestos, religiosos, benignè, utpote fideles Nuncios, in osculo pacis exceptos, in quorum ore non est inventum mendacium, nec iniquitas, desubitò consuevit incarcerare, & fame ac nuditate usque ad mortem marcerare. Longè faciat à nobis Deus talem sanctitatem.
units.tr: 2. Your Lord calls himself Holy. Wondrous is that holiness which is accustomed suddenly to imprison holy men, honest, pious and kindly received with the kiss of peace as faithful messengers, in whose mouth no lie or iniquity was found, and to waste them away with hunger and nakedness unto death. May God keep such holiness far from us.

units.la: EIVSDEM IMPERATORIS Responsum Legatis Soldani, & filii ejus, necnon & Admiralis, datum Iconii, commu- nicato consilio Principum.
units.tr: The reply of the same Emperor to the envoys of the Sultan, and of his son, and also of the Admiral, given at Iconium, the counsel of the princes having been shared.

units.la: SOldanus juxta amicitiam diu cum Imperio nostro habitam Legatos suos ad nos misit, & ad terram suam invitavit, & securitatem viæ, & bonum forum, nobis & exercitui nostro pollicebatur. Præterea alii Nuncii ipsius, & filii sui præsentiam nostram Adrianopoli adierunt, uberiora & amplioribus beneficiorum promissa nobis offerentes. Sed, qui nobiscum terram illam ingressi sunt, videntes nobis pro securitate viæ, arcus & tela, gladios & lanceas, & omne genus armorum, & insultationes insolitos clamores exhiberi, & pro bono foro nobis sub specie fidelis amicitiæ pollicito, magnus Melech cum omni fortitudine & virtute gentis suæ in manu hostili nos & exercitum nostrum circumderunt sicut apes, & exarserunt in nos sicut ignis in spinis: & tamen in nomine Domini nostri Jesu Christi, Romanus Imperator & Advocatus specialis terræ Hierosolymitanæ hostium cuneos penetravit securus, & fugato multitudinis vestræ exercitu, tradidit Deus noster civitatem hanc in manus nostras. Sed quia Romanus Imperator, cui collaterales semper esse debent misericordia & veritas, magis parcere, quàm ferire; hanc gratiam Dominis vestris & vobis impertiri decrevimus, ut nostra in super vos, dummodo detis obsides ad arbitrium nostrum, quòd in bona pace, & bono statu terram vestram exire debeam.
units.tr: The Sultan, according to the friendship long held with our Empire, sent his envoys to us and invited us to his land, promising us and our army safety of the road and a fair market. Moreover, other messengers of his and of his son came into our presence at Adrianople, offering us richer and greater benefits. But those who entered that land with us, seeing that for the safety of the road bows and arrows, swords and lances, and every kind of weapon, together with unusual insults and shouting, were displayed to us, and that for a fair market, promised to us under the appearance of faithful friendship, the great king [Melech] with all the strength and valour of his people surrounded us and our army in hostile hand like bees, and blazed against us like fire among thorns; yet in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Roman Emperor and special advocate of the land of Jerusalem penetrated the ranks of the enemy in safety, and, your multitude's army having been put to flight, God delivered this city into our hands. But since the Roman Emperor, to whom mercy and truth should always be companions, is more inclined to spare than to strike, we have decided to grant this grace to your Lords and to you, so that we may go out of your land in good peace and good condition, provided that you give hostages at our discretion.

units.la: HENRICI VI. IMP. AUG. EDICTUM De Indulgentiis Militiae Sacrae Privilegiis.
units.tr: EDICT OF HENRY VI, AUGUSTUS EMPEROR, Concerning the Indulgences and Privileges of the Holy Army.

units.la: Henricus Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator, Rex Siciliae & semper Augustus, dilectis ac fidelibus suis Archiepiscopis, Abbatibus, Ecclesiarum Praelatis, gratiam suam & omne bonum.
units.tr: Henry, by the grace of God Roman Emperor, King of Sicily and ever Augustus, to his beloved and faithful Archbishops, Abbots and Prelates of the Churches, his grace and every blessing.

units.la: 1. Universitati vestrae duximus significandum, quòd per gratiam Dei regno Siciliae nobis subjugato, & in bonum statum reducto, ad honorem ejus, qui brachia sua extendit in crucem pro nobis, memoratus, tecolentes miseriam & angustias, quae Terra promissionis, peccatis exigentibus, feritate Paganorum intolerabiliter opprella sustinet, in solemni Cuna apud Bajum in festo Resurrectionis Domini celebrata pro redemptione ejusdem terrae mille quingentos milites, & totidem sargantos, in expensis nostris à Mattio usque ad annum transmittere decrevimus, & hoc manifeste ipsos pondimus, ut mihi triginta uncias auri; & tantum annonae, quae erad annum sufficiet, datum. Pecuniam vero navesque ascendent, eis dabimus: annonam autem traducì faciemus, & ex illa parte maris, ubi appulerint, eis praesentabimus.
units.tr: 1. We have thought it right to make known to your community that, by the grace of God, the kingdom of Sicily has been brought under our rule and restored to good order. Out of honour to him who stretched out his arms on the cross for us, and remembering the misery and distress which the Land of Promise, because of our sins, suffers under the savage oppression of the Pagans beyond endurance, we have decided to send, at our own expense, one thousand five hundred knights and as many sergeants, from March until the end of the year, to be solemnly celebrated at Bari at the court held on the feast of the Lord's Resurrection, for the redemption of that land. We have decided to give each of them thirty ounces of gold and as much provision as will suffice for a year. We will give them the money and ships, and we will have the provisions carried across and presented to them on that part of the sea where they land.

units.la: 2. Milites itaque & sargantri jurabunt obedire illi, quem Magistrum eis ac Ducem constituemus: & perpetuo itare in servitio Dei.
units.tr: 2. The knights and sergeants shall swear to obey the man whom we appoint as their Master and Leader, and to remain constantly in the service of God.

units.la: 3. Et si aliquem eorum ex hoc mundo migrare contigerit, quidquid de pecunia vel annona ei data reliquerit, nulli assignare poterit, sed pro consilio Magistrorum ac Ducum exercitus alii, qui vivente ejus compleat & pro ipso serviat, assignabitur.
units.tr: 3. And if any of them should happen to depart from this world, whatever money or provisions have been given to him and remain unused, he shall not be able to assign them to anyone; instead, by the counsel of the Masters and Leaders of the army, they shall be assigned to another who, while he lives, may complete the term and serve in his place.

units.la: 4. Mandamus ergo universitati vestrae rogantes, ut hanc voluntatem nostram militibus & hominibus in dioecesi vestra constitutis insinuare curetis: ut si qui eorum ad propulsandas injurias Christo & Christianitati illatas instinctu divino ire voluerint, intra terminum praedictum adire properarent.
units.tr: 4. We therefore ask and charge your community to take care to make known this our will to the knights and men established in your diocese, so that if any of them, moved by divine impulse, wish to go to repel the injuries inflicted on Christ and Christendom, they should hasten to come within the aforesaid time limit.

units.la: Datum apud Tranum, 11. Idus Aprilis.
units.tr: Given at Trani, on the eleventh day before the Ides of April.

units.la: HENRICI VI. IMPER. AUG. CONSTITUTIO IMPERIUM UT PROCEDAT SUCCESSIONE, NON ELECTIONE, & alia quaedam capitula.
units.tr: Constitution of Emperor Henry VI, Augustus, that the Empire should pass by succession, not by election, and certain other chapters.

units.la: Ex Joanne Monacho refertur ab Auctore Magni Chronici Belgici, pag. 205.
units.tr: Reported from John of Monaco by the author of the Great Belgian Chronicle, p. 205.

units.la: Cum Imperator Henricus videns, Regnum Almanniae, & Imperium Romanorum, propter frequentes mutationes Imperatorum, multa mala perpessum, priusquam vota Principum in personam Imperatoris potuissent convenire, ordinavit, ut amplius electio non fieret, sed per solam sanguinis successionem Imperium conferretur, ita, ut qui propinquior Imperatori esset, haereditarie fieret Imperator.
units.tr: When the Emperor Henry saw that the kingdom of Germany and the Roman Empire had suffered many evils because of the frequent changes of emperors, he ordained, before the wishes of the princes could come together upon a person as Emperor, that election should no longer take place; instead, the Empire should be conferred by succession of blood alone, so that whoever was nearer to the Emperor should become Emperor by hereditary right.

units.la: 2. Utrantem Henricus a filio suo Fredericو, quem de Constantia uxore sua habuit, exordium, Regnum Siciliae & Calabriae, & Ducatum Apuliae, & Principatum Capuae, quae ab avis haeres acceperat, Romano Imperio univit, ut perpetuo tenerentur unus Dominus.
units.tr: 2. Beginning with his son Frederick, whom he had by his wife Constance, Henry united with the Roman Empire the kingdom of Sicily and Calabria, the duchy of Apulia, and the principality of Capua, which he had received as heir from his grandfathers, so that they might be held perpetually under one lord.

units.la: Ordinavit etiam, ut mulieres, masculis deficientibus, succederent in haereditatem.
units.tr: He also ordained that women should succeed to the inheritance when males were lacking.

units.la: Et ne Imperator mortuas manus Ecclesiasticarum personarum ultra expoliaret.
units.tr: And that the Emperor should no longer plunder the goods of deceased ecclesiastical persons.

units.la: Constitutioni igitur huic profuturae consenserunt Curia Romana, & Principes LII. qui Imperatores eligere consueverunt, quorum sigilla litteris super hoc confectis sunt appensa.
units.tr: To this constitution, which was to be beneficial, the Roman Curia and the princes, fifty-two in number, who were accustomed to elect emperors, gave their consent, and their seals were appended to the letters drawn up for this purpose.

units.la: PRINCIPUM IMPERII DIPLOMA DE ELECTIONE OTTONIS IV. IMPERATO- RIS Augusti.
units.tr: THE DIPLOMA OF THE PRINCES OF THE EMPIRE CONCERNING THE ELECTION OF THE EMPEROR OTTO IV, AUGUSTUS.

units.la: Sanctissimo Patri ac Domino Innocentio, sacrosanctae Romanae Sedis Summo Pontifici, Principes & Barones Alemanniae, Clerici & Laici, debitam in Christo reverentiam & obsequium.
units.tr: To our most holy Father and Lord Innocent, Supreme Pontiff of the most sacred Roman See, the Princes and Barons of Germany, clergy and laity, offer due reverence and obedience in Christ.

units.la: 1. Cum placuisset ei, qui aufert spiritum Principum, & magnus & terribilis est super Reges terrae, Henricum Imperatorem de medio auferre, necessarium nobis fuit vitam, de substituendo Regis, & colloquium habere. Convenimus ergo saepius, & miserias & oppressiones, quas hactenus sustinuerimus, tecensentes, per universos regni ...... animos nostros erectiores, honori Ecclesiæ Dei, & pacis ac quieti subjectorum expeduet, deliberantes, nunc inlium quasi finaliter eligere putabamus. Verum quia non est prudentia, non est potentia, nisi per Deum, placent ei, qui Abrahæ filium immolare volenti victimam providit, & Dominus fratribus juniorem de posteriorantes accepit, atq; Matthiam ex discipulorum numero ad sortem electus elegit. Serenissimum Dominum nostrum OTTONEM, quondam Henrici Ducis Saxoniæ, ad regimen Romani Imperii de tenui peregrinationis suæ ex inopinato offerre nobis, itaq; Sancti Spiritus gratia, prædictum Dominum Ottonem, Christianæ fidei cultorem devotum, atq; sanctæ Romanæ Ecclesiæ Advocatum & defensorem fidelissimum, & judiciariæ potestatis servatorem justissimum, de longa & antiqua Regum prosapia ex utraq; linea specialiter editum, manu Regni factigii juste & rationabiliter elegimus; & sicut debuimus, ipsius electioni consensimus, ipsumq; in Augustorum sede à Carolo Magno apud Aquisgranum huic dignitati deputatam, & corona, & regni diademate per manum Domini Adolphi Coloniensis Archiepiscopi ea, cuit, solemniter & licenter coronavimus.
units.tr: 1. Since it pleased Him who takes away the spirit of princes, and who is great and terrible above the kings of the earth, to remove Emperor Henry from the midst, it was necessary for us to take thought for the life of the realm and to choose a king, and to confer together. We therefore met often, reviewing the miseries and oppressions we had hitherto endured, and deliberating how our spirits, throughout the whole realm, might be raised up more firmly, for the honour of the Church of God and for the peace and quiet of the subjects. We thought we might now at last choose one as it were finally. But since there is no wisdom and no power except through God, it pleases Him who provided a victim when Abraham was willing to sacrifice his son, and who took the younger son over the firstborn, and who by lot chose Matthias from the number of the disciples, that the most serene Lord our Otto, son of the late Duke Henry of Saxony, should, unexpectedly and from the distant pilgrimage of his exile, be offered to us for the government of the Roman Empire. Therefore, by the grace of the Holy Spirit, we have justly and reasonably chosen the aforesaid Lord Otto, a devoted worshipper of the Christian faith, a most faithful advocate and defender of the holy Roman Church, and a most just guardian of judicial power, specially born of the long and ancient line of kings on both sides, with the hand of the realm's chief officers. As we ought, we have consented to his election, and we have solemnly and lawfully crowned him, in the seat of the Emperors that Charles the Great appointed for this dignity at Aachen, with the crown and the diadem of the kingdom, by the hand of Lord Adolf, Archbishop of Cologne.

units.la: 2. Nos autem Principes, qui jam dictum Dominum in Regem elegimus, feudam nostram Imperio tenemus, à manu ipsius recipientes, hominium sibi fecimus, & fidelitatem juravimus. Tanta igitur dignitatis munus excellentissimus Princeps divinæ potius gratiæ, quàm suis meritis, bens, primitias hujus honoris afferens Domino, propria voluntate juramento firmavit, sanctæ Romanæ Ecclesiæ, deinde omnia Ecclesiarum jura bona fide servare & manu tenere subjectos Imperii, exheredatos maximè & à suis possessionibus violenter ejectos, in sua posse juvare & conservare. Pravam illam consuetudinem insuper, quam Imperatores resi in occupandis rebus mobilibus vel se moventibus decedentium Episcoporum vel Principum hucusque servaverunt, penitus extirpans, nos Ecclesiasticos Principes ex hac indulgentia Regali benevolentia liberos dimisit, & decedentium bona suis successoribus servari statuit.
units.tr: 2. Moreover, we princes, who have chosen the aforesaid Lord as king, hold our fiefs of the Empire, receiving them from his hand, and have done homage to him and sworn fidelity. Therefore the most excellent Prince, bringing to the Lord the first fruits of this honour, a gift of so great dignity, acknowledging that it comes rather from divine grace than from his own merits, has confirmed by oath, of his own free will, that he will preserve in good faith the holy Roman Church, and then all the rights of the churches, and will hold them and maintain them in his hand; and that he will aid and preserve in their possessions the subjects of the Empire, especially those disinherited and violently driven from their possessions. Moreover, he has utterly rooted out that wicked custom which the Emperors until now have observed, of seizing the movable goods, or goods that move themselves, of bishops or princes who die; and, by this royal kindness, he has allowed us ecclesiastical princes to be free, and has decreed that the goods of the deceased be kept for their successors.

units.la: 3. Paternitati ergo vestræ dignum supplicare duximus, quatenus fidem & devotionem nostri Regis attendentes; merita quoque Illustrissimi patris sui Henrici Ducis Saxoniæ, obsequio sanctæ Romanæ Ecclesiæ numquam recessit, memoriter tenentes, paci & quieti vestræ, intuitu Dei & nostri obsequii, providentes, ipsius electionem & consecrationem confirmare, & Imperiali coronatione armare, paterna pietate dignemini. Sanctitatem insuper vestram obnixè rogamus, quatenus Principes & Barones, à tam rationabili electione discordes, Ecclesiastica censura ad concordiam revocetis, & ab illicita fidelitate partis advers sancti Petri resolutos, ad præstandam Regi Domino nostro fidelitatem & subjectionem, ad vestra compellatis. Ut autem à Domino Rege nostro jura Romanæ Ecclesiæ, ut pretiosa integra & illibata serventur, nos in bona fide spondemus, & pro Domino Rege nostro ... inus.
units.tr: 3. We have therefore thought it fitting to beseech your Paternity that, bearing in mind the faith and devotion of our King, and remembering the merits of his most illustrious father, Henry Duke of Saxony, who never withdrew from obedience to the holy Roman Church, you would deign, with fatherly kindness, to provide for your own peace and quiet, for the sake of God and of our obedience, by confirming his election and consecration, and by arming him with the imperial coronation. Furthermore, we earnestly ask your Holiness that you would, by ecclesiastical censure, recall to concord those princes and barons who are at odds over so reasonable an election, and that you would compel them, released from the unlawful fidelity to the party adverse to St. Peter, to render fidelity and subjection to our Lord King. And that the rights of the Roman Church may be preserved whole and unimpaired by our Lord King, we pledge ourselves in good faith, and for our Lord King ...

units.la: f. Corbejen-sis. Ego Adolphus Coloniensis Archiepiscopus elegi & subscripsi. Ego Berardus Paderbornensis Episcopus elegi & subscripsi. Ego Thietmarus Mindensis Episcopus elegi & subscripsi. Ego Witichindus * Condejensis Abbas elegi & subscripsi. Ego Gerardus Tudensis Abbas elegi & subscripsi. Ego Eribertus Werdensis Abbas elegi & subscripsi. Ego Henricus Dux Lotharingiæ, qui & Brabantiæ, Marchio Romani Imperii, elegi & subscripsi. Ego Henricus Comes de Kuke consensi & subscripsi.
units.tr: Corbejensis. I, Adolf, Archbishop of Cologne, have elected and subscribed. I, Berard, Bishop of Paderborn, have elected and subscribed. I, Thietmar, Bishop of Minden, have elected and subscribed. I, Witikind, Abbot of Corvey, have elected and subscribed. I, Gerard, Abbot of Tuda, have elected and subscribed. I, Eribert, Abbot of Werden, have elected and subscribed. I, Henry, Duke of Lotharingia, who is also of Brabant, Margrave of the Roman Empire, have elected and subscribed. I, Henry, Count of Kuke, have consented and subscribed.

units.la: OTHONIS IV. IMP. AUG. DECRETVM
units.tr: DECREE OF OTTO IV, EMPEROR AUGUSTUS

units.la: De bonis Ecclesiasticis in necessitatem publicam erogandis; de personarum Ecclesiasticarum reformatione; & de bello Papæ ac Regi Francorum inferendo. Factum in Comitiis Valentianis Anno Domini MCCXII.
units.tr: Concerning the church goods to be devoted to public necessity; concerning the reform of ecclesiastical persons; and concerning war to be waged on the Pope and the King of the Franks. Enacted at the Diet of Valenciennes in the year of the Lord MCCXII.

units.la: SI Rex Francorum non esset, tuti à quolibet hoste in toto mundo haberi possemus, & totum gladiis nostris supponere. Sed hucusque contra nos favorem impendente, & Clerus semper quasi propriam habente, Papa Romanus nostra præsumit anathemate ferire, atq; nostros Procères hodie nostra absolvere. Quum dum Sicamonti Regi se amicum præstat, audet is vires in Imperium extendere, qui semper gratiam flatus est in genus nostrum, & ipsum Regem Johannem largus opes & denaria nobis plurit, exhæredare præsumit. Contra hunc igitur solum totæ concitatæ insurgere, hic primus conciliatur & domitur oportet, qui solus impedit nostros proventus, & bis opponit, & in omni hoste, qui se contra nos levat, ipse quoq; hostis fit. Quo superato, & domitis aliquos vincere facile poterimus, Regnumq; Francorum jugo Imperii nostri supponere, & ad vobis patuit.
units.tr: If there were no King of the Franks, we could be held safe from every enemy in the whole world and bring everything under our swords. But hitherto the Roman Pope, lending favour to our enemies and always holding the Clergy as if it were his own, presumes to strike us with anathema, and today presumes to absolve our nobles from their allegiance to us. While he shows himself a friend to King Sicamont, he dares to extend his forces against the Empire, and he presumes to disinherit King John, who has always been generous to our house and has often supplied us with money and wealth. Therefore it is against this one man alone that all should rise together; he must first be won over and subdued, since he alone hinders our revenues and opposes us at every turn, and, being the enemy of every man who rises against us, is himself our enemy. Once he is overcome, and others subdued, we shall easily be able to conquer them too, and to place the Kingdom of the Franks under the yoke of our Empire, as has been made clear to you.

units.la: 2. Clerum autem & Monachos, quos Rex Francorum Philippus sic exaltat, amat, protegit, & de vigore conde dignitate, aut deponamus, aut deportemus oportet, sic tamen ut pauci maneant, quibus satis sit arcta facultas, & qui oblata tantummodo supe vivant, villas autem & decimas majores non recipiat, illiq; habeant, quibus Respublica curae est, qui pugnando faciunt populos & Clerum ... quaerere. Illo quippe die, quo nos Papa Romanus primum Imperiali diademate infigne reddidit, hanc promulgavimus legem, & in scriptis redactam per totum orbem firmiter servari jussimus: ut decimas tantum & oblata munera possideant, villas autem & praedia nobis relinquant, ut hinc populus vivat, & Milites habeant stipendia sua.
units.tr: 2. As for the Clergy and the Monks, whom King Philip of the Franks so exalts, loves and protects, and in whose strength and dignity he so rests, we must either depose them or cast them down, yet in such a way that only a few remain, for whom a narrow livelihood is enough, and who live only on the offerings made to them; but they shall not receive the large estates and tithes, and those who care for the commonwealth, who by fighting provide for the peoples and the Clergy ... are to have them. For on that day on which the Roman Pope first made us distinguished by the imperial diadem, we proclaimed this law, and we ordered it committed to writing and firmly observed throughout the whole world: that they should possess only the tithes and the offerings, but leave the estates and landed properties to us, so that the people may live from them and our soldiers may have their pay.

units.la: 3. Nunc quia mihi Clerus in ista lege non paret, nunquid non debemus gravare manus, & illi decimas cum villis licenter auferre? Nunquid nō possumus legē superaddere legi? KAROLUS Tunitus, etiamsi noluit illis villas tollere, quia tamen decimas ipsis tulit, nobis non licebit ... villas cum decimis auferre? Qui possumus leges condere & jura novare, qui soli tenemus tolerare Imperium, non licebit nobis Clerum hac lege ligare, ut primitiis rebusq; oblatis contenti, ... hæc iam culta novalia, & villas tot delitiis opibusq; fluctes, impiger Miles habebit, quam generaliter fructus consumere natum, quod otia ducit, quodq; sub tecto marcet, & umbra, qui ... quorum omnis labor in hoc est, ut Baccho Veneriq; vacent, quibus crapula obesis ... ventresq; abdomine onerat? Unde nos, quamprimum Papa nobis in dicta lege rebelles, ... in Halconis, Aquampendentem, Bitral, Radichofonem, Arduam, Sancti Quirici castrum, ... Biccum, vicosq; innumeros & plurima castella, quibus dives Roma circumvallatur, ... ipsi conpuimus, quae fortiter potenteq; armis adhuc ipso nolente tenemus, diuq; tenebimus, quamvis nobis Imperium supplantare laboret, & jus nostrum praesumat Friderico Regi ... committere.
units.tr: 3. Now, since the Clergy does not obey me in this law, must we not lay our hands upon them and freely take away from them the tithes together with the estates? Can we not add law to law? KAROLUS TUNITUS: even though he did not wish to take away their estates, yet because he took the tithes from them, shall it not be lawful for us to take away the estates together with the tithes? We who can make laws and devise rights, we who alone hold the Empire to be borne, shall it not be lawful for us to bind the Clergy by this law, so that, content with the first fruits and the offerings, they ... the fields now cultivated and the estates flowing with so many delights and riches shall be held by the tireless soldier, who was born to consume the produce generally, who lives in idleness, and who withers under roof and shade, whose whole labour is that they should be free for Bacchus and Venus, whose bellies are burdened with gluttony and swollen with paunch? Whence we, as soon as the Pope, rebellious to us in the said law, ... in Halconis, Aquapendente, Bitral, Radicofani, Ardea, the castle of San Quirico, ... Bicco, and countless villages and very many castles with which rich Rome is encircled, ... we have ourselves seized, which we hold by force of arms, even against his will, and shall long hold, although he labours to supplant us in the Empire and presumes to commit our right to King Frederick ...

units.la: 4. Tunc Proceres uno ore concorditer legem confirmantes, bellum fore promittunt, omnesque ... jurant, observaturos se quicquid Imperator dixerat. Otho Romanorum Imperator semper Augustus subscripsit. Johannes Rex Angliae, Franciae & Hiberniae per Guillermum Comitem Salesberiensem subscripsit. Henricus Dux Lotharingiae & Brabantiae, Marchio Romani Imperii, subscripsit. Otho Comes Palatinus Burgundiae subscripsit. Ferrandus Comes Flandriae & Henoniae subscripsit. Reginaldus Comes Boloniae subscripsit. Willelmus Comes Hollandiae subscripsit. N. Comes de Limburg subscripsit. N. Comes Barrensis subscripsit. Herveus Comes Nivernensis subscripsit. Petrus Comes Altisiodorensis subscripsit. Henricus Comes de Kuke subscripsit. Hugo Baro de Boves subscripsit.
units.tr: 4. Then the nobles, confirming the law with one voice and in agreement, promise that there shall be war, and all ... swear that they will observe whatever the Emperor had said. Otto, Emperor of the Romans, ever Augustus, subscribed. John, King of England, France and Ireland, subscribed through William, Earl of Salisbury. Henry, Duke of Lorraine and Brabant, Marquis of the Roman Empire, subscribed. Otto, Count Palatine of Burgundy, subscribed. Ferdinand, Count of Flanders and Hainaut, subscribed. Reginald, Count of Boulogne, subscribed. William, Count of Holland, subscribed. N., Count of Limburg, subscribed. N., Count of Bar, subscribed. Hervé, Count of Nevers, subscribed. Peter, Count of Auxerre, subscribed. Henry, Count of Cuijk, subscribed. Hugh, Baron of Boves, subscribed.

units.la: Et multi alii tam Proceres, quam Comites de Alemannia, de Henonia, de Brabantia, & de Flandria, subscripserunt. Actum in oppido Valenciense in Comitatu Henoniae, anno ab Incarnatione Domini MCCXV, anno Imperii Domini Othonis invictissimi Imperatoris XV.
units.tr: And many others, both nobles and counts, from Germany, from Hainaut, from Brabant and from Flanders, subscribed. Enacted in the town of Valenciennes in the county of Hainaut, in the year from the Incarnation of the Lord MCCXV, in the fifteenth year of the reign of our most invincible Lord Otto, Emperor.

units.la: FRIDERICI II. ROMANO- RUM REGIS AUREA BULLA, DE LIBERTATE ECCLESIASTICA.
units.tr: The Golden Bull of Frederick II, King of the Romans, concerning ecclesiastical liberty.

units.la: Fridericus divina favente Clementia Romanorum Rex & Semper Augustus & Rex Siciliae. Regnum nostrum tunc stabiliri confidimus, cum Altissimum, de cujus munera, quae bona recepimus, honoramus. Tanto enim Domino, qui bona tribuit nobis, ad debitas operis & devotionis astringimur, quanto ipsum misericordem in nobis & misericordiam ... tabilem experimur. Cognoscentes igitur gratiam, quæ data est nobis ab ipso [?] quæ præ oculis immensa & innumera beneficia vestra, Domine & reverentissime Pater, ctor & benefactor noster, Domine * Innocenti, Dei gratia Summæ Pontificis, cujus beneficium, operam, & tutelam aliri sumus, protecti panter & promoti, civitatem nostram mater noster felicis memoriæ Constantia Imperatrix & Siciliæ Regina quasi utero nos jactavit, vobis, beatissime Pater, & omnibus successoribus vestris Catholicis, queque Romanæ Ecclesiæ speciali matri nostræ, omnem obedientiam, honorificentiam, atque semper humili corde ac devoto spiritu impendimus, quam prædecessores nostri Reges & Imperatores Catholici vestris antecessoribus impendisse noscuntur, nihil exinde volentes diminui, sed augeti, ut major devotio emitescat.
units.tr: Frederick, by the favour of divine clemency, Roman King, ever Augustus, and King of Sicily. We trust that our kingdom is then established when we honour the Most High, from whose gifts we have received the good things we have. For we are bound to the due works and devotion by as much as we find Him merciful and steadfast toward us. Therefore, knowing the grace given to us by Him [?], and the immense and countless benefits of yours before our eyes, Lord and most reverend Father, our author and benefactor, Lord Innocent, by the grace of God Supreme Pontiff, by whose benefit, work and protection we have been sheltered and promoted, our mother of happy memory, the Empress Constance and Queen of Sicily, bore us as from her womb. To you, most blessed Father, and to all your Catholic successors, and to the Roman Church, our special mother, we render all obedience and honour, always with a humble heart and devoted spirit, which our predecessors, the Catholic kings and emperors, are known to have rendered to your predecessors. We wish nothing of this to be diminished, but increased, so that greater devotion may shine forth.

units.la: 2. Illum igitur volentes abolere abusum, quem quidam prædecessorum nostrorum dignoscuntur, decretum in electionibus Prælatorum: concedimus & sancimus, ut electiones torum liberè & canonicè fiant, quatenus ille præficiatur Ecclesiæ viduatæ, quem totum vel major & famor partis ipsius duxerit eligendum, dummodo nihil defit et de canonicis.
units.tr: 2. Wishing therefore to abolish that abuse which some of our predecessors are known to have practised in the elections of prelates, we grant and sanction that the elections of prelates be made freely and canonically, so that he be set over the widowed Church whom the whole, or the greater and sounder part of it, shall have chosen to elect, provided nothing be lacking from the canons.

units.la: 3. Appellationes autem in negotiis & causis Ecclesiasticis ad Sedem Apostolicam eorum persecutionem sive processum nullus impedire præsumat.
units.tr: 3. Moreover, appeals in ecclesiastical business and causes to the Apostolic See, nobody shall presume to hinder their prosecution or proceeding.

units.la: 4. Illum quoque dimittimus & refutamus abusum, quem in occupandis bonis Prælatorum, aut etiam Ecclesiarum vacantium nostri confuevernt antecessores motu propriæ voluntatis. Omnia nos spiritualia vobis & aliis Ecclesiarum Prælatis relinquimus, ut quæ sunt Cæsaris Cæsari, & quæ Dei Deo recta distributione reddantur.
units.tr: 4. We also dismiss and reject the abuse which our predecessors were accustomed to practise of their own accord, in seizing the goods of prelates or of vacant churches. We leave all spiritual things to you and the other prelates of the churches, so that what belongs to Caesar is rendered to Caesar, and what belongs to God is rendered to God by right distribution.

units.la: 5. Super eradicando autem Hæreticæ pravitatis errores, auxilium dabimus & operam.
units.tr: 5. Concerning the eradication of the errors of heretical wickedness, we will give aid and effort.

units.la: 6. Possessiones etiam, quas Ecclesia Romana recuperavit, ab antecessoribus suis, busliber alis detentas, liberas & quietas sibi dimittimus, & ipsam ad eas obtinendas mittimus adjuvare. Quas vero nondum recuperavit, ad recuperandum erimus pro viribus: & quæcunque, ad manus nostras devenerint, fine difficultate ac mora eas restituemus. Has pertinet tota terra, quæ est à Radicofano usque Ceperanum, Marchia Anconitana, Ducatus Spoletanus, terra Comitissæ Mathildis, Comitatus Bertinotis, Exarchatus Ravennæ, Pentapolis, Trebaria, cum adjacentibus terris, & omnibus aliis ad Romanam Ecclesiam pertinentibus jurisdictione, distractu, & honore suo.
units.tr: 6. The possessions also which the Roman Church has recovered, held by its predecessors or by others, we leave to it free and quiet, and we send to help it obtain them. Those which it has not yet recovered we will strive to recover to the best of our powers, and whatever comes into our hands we will restore without difficulty or delay. To these belong the whole land from Radicofani to Ceperano, the March of Ancona, the Duchy of Spoleto, the land of Countess Matilda, the County of Bertinoro, the Exarchate of Ravenna, Pentapolis, Trevaria, with the adjacent lands, and all others pertaining to the Roman Church in jurisdiction, revenue and honour.

units.la: 7. Verumtamen cùm ad recipiendum coronam Imperii, vel pro necessitatibus Apostolicæ Sedis vocati venerimus, de mandato Summi Pontificis recipiemus procurationem ab ipsis. Omnia igitur supradicta, & quæcunque alia pertinent ad Romanam Ecclesiam, luntate & conscientia, consilio & consensu Principum Imperii liberè illi dimittimus, restituimus; necnon ad omnem scrupulum removendum, prout melius valet & efficacius concedimus, conferimus, donamus, ut sublata omnis contentionis & dissensionis materia, & plena concordia in perpetuum inter Ecclesiam & Imperium perseverent.
units.tr: 7. However, when we have come to receive the crown of the Empire, or have been summoned for the needs of the Apostolic See, we will receive provision from them at the command of the Supreme Pontiff. Therefore all the above, and whatever else pertains to the Roman Church, by our will and conscience, with the counsel and consent of the princes of the Empire, we freely release and restore to it. And so that every scruple may be removed, we grant, confer and give, as best and most effectively we may, so that, all matter of contention and dissension being removed, full concord may remain for ever between the Church and the Empire.

units.la: 8. Adjutores etiam erimus ad retinendum & ad defendendum Ecclesiæ Romanæ civitatem, cum omnibus ad ipsum spectantibus, tam citra Pharum quam ultra, necnon Corsicam, Sardiniam, ac cetera jura, quæ ad eam pertinere noscuntur, tanquam devotus filius & Catholicus. ceps.
units.tr: 8. We will also be helpers in retaining and defending the city of the Roman Church with all things belonging to it, as much this side of the Pharos as beyond it, and also Corsica, Sardinia, and the other rights which are known to pertain to it, as a devoted and Catholic son.

units.la: 9. Ut autem hæc omnia memorato sanctissimo Patri nostro Domino Innocentio, Romanæ Ecclesiæ Summo Pontifici, ejusque successoribus per nos & nostros successores Reges & Imperatores observentur, firma & inconvulsa semper permaneant; præsens privilegium scriptum Majestatis nostræ aurea bulla jussimus communiri. Testes autem sunt hi: Sigefridus Moguntinus Archiepiscopus, Sedis Apostolicæ Legatus. Eberhardus Salisburgensis Archiepiscopus. Conradus Ratisponensis Episcopus. Otto Wirzburgensis Episcopus. Manegoldus Patavienlis Episcopus. Engelardus * Zilensis Episcopus. Giadiacus Bohemorum Rex. Ludovicus Dux Bavariæ. Leopoldus Dux Austriæ & Styriæ. Hermannus Lanthgravius Turingiæ. Comes Albertus de Eberstein. Comes Adolphus de Sonneberch. Comes Burchardus de Mannesvelde. Berardus Bers. Comes Ludovicus de Wirtemberg. Gebehardus * Bufclavius Magdeburgensis. Henricus de Stahenvverch. Vultetus de Langenberg. Henricus de Calandina Marefcalcus Imperii.
units.tr: 9. That all these things may be observed by us and by our successors, kings and emperors, toward our said most holy Father, Lord Innocent, Supreme Pontiff of the Roman Church, and toward his successors, and may remain always firm and unshaken, we have ordered the present written privilege to be confirmed with the golden bulla of our Majesty. The witnesses are these: Siegfried, Archbishop of Mainz, Legate of the Apostolic See; Eberhard, Archbishop of Salzburg; Conrad, Bishop of Regensburg; Otto, Bishop of Würzburg; Manegold, Bishop of Passau; Engelhard, Bishop of Zeitz; Ladislaus, King of the Bohemians; Louis, Duke of Bavaria; Leopold, Duke of Austria and Styria; Hermann, Landgrave of Thuringia; Count Albert of Eberstein; Count Adolf of Sonneberg; Count Burchard of Mannsfeld; Berard Bers; Count Louis of Württemberg; Gebehard Bufclavius of Magdeburg; Henry of Stahenwerch; Vultetus of Langenberg; Henry of Calandina, Marshal of the Empire.

units.la: * Citicensis.
units.tr: Of Zeitz.

units.la: * Burgravius. Walterus de Sepf Pincerna Imperii, & alii quam plures.
units.tr: Burgrave. Walter de Sepf, Cupbearer of the Empire, and very many others.

units.la: Signum Domini Friderici Secundi Romanorum Regis invictissimi, & Regis Siciliæ. Ego Conradus Dei gratia & Apostolicæ Sedis Metensis & Spirensis Episcopus, Imperialis Aulæ Cancellarius, vice Domini Sigefridi Moguntini Archiepiscopi, & Apostolicæ Sedis Legati, actoque Germaniæ Archicancellarii recognovi.
units.tr: The sign of Lord Frederick II, most invincible King of the Romans and King of Sicily. I, Conrad, by the grace of God and of the Apostolic See Bishop of Metz and Speyer, Chancellor of the Imperial Court, in place of Lord Siegfried, Archbishop of Mainz and Legate of the Apostolic See, and acting as Archchancellor of Germany, have recognised this.

units.la: Acta sunt hæc Anno Domini nostri Jesu Christi millesimo ducentesimo decimo tertio, indictione prima, regnante Domino Friderico Secundo Romanorum Rege gloriosissimo, & Rege Siciliæ, anno regni ejus, Romani primo, regni vero ejus Siciliæ decimo sexto. Datum apud Egram per manus Bertholdi de Nise, Regalis Aulæ Protonotarii, quarto Idus Julii.
units.tr: These things were done in the year of our Lord Jesus Christ 1213, in the first indiction, in the reign of Lord Frederick II, most glorious King of the Romans and King of Sicily, in the first year of his Roman reign and the sixteenth of his reign in Sicily. Given at Eger by the hand of Berthold of Nise, Protonotary of the Royal Court, on the fourth of the Ides of July.

units.la: Post annos sex huic per omnia simIlem Auream Bullam dedisse reperitur Honorio Papæ Tertio, totidem verbis conceptam, quæ Romæ exstat in Castello S. Angeli, & in Bibliotheca Vaticana.
units.tr: It is found that six years later he gave to Pope Honorius III a golden bull altogether similar to this one, conceived in the same words, which survives in Rome in the Castle of St Angelo and in the Vatican Library.

units.la: FRIDERICI II. IMPER. AUG. RECESSUS SIVE CONSTITUTIONES COMITIORUM FRANCOFVRDIANORVM de Anno MCCXIX.
units.tr: FRIDERICI II. IMPER. AUG. RECESSUS SIVE CONSTITUTIONES COMITIORUM FRANCOFVRDIANORVM de Anno MCCXIX.

units.la: Ex Alberico refert Auctor Magni Chronici Belgici, pag. 221.
units.tr: The author of the Great Belgian Chronicle reports this from Albericus, p. 221.

units.la: Ex Fridericus Curiam apud Franckfordiam quatuordecim diebus habuit, ubi pluribus adunatis Principibus, multa de statu & utilitate Regni tractata sunt: injusta telonea, injustæ monetæ, bella civilia, nisi de consensu & consilio Regis & Principum, & omnes injustitiæ sub pœna vitæ, à Regibus & Principibus interdictæ sunt.
units.tr: Frederick held a court at Frankfurt for fourteen days, where, with many princes assembled, much was discussed concerning the state and welfare of the realm: unjust tolls, unjust coinage, and civil wars, unless by the consent and counsel of the King and the Princes, and all injustices, were forbidden by kings and princes under penalty of life.

units.la: 1. Ibique congregato exercitu Italiam intrare Imperator disposuit, ut benedictioni Imperiali interesset.
units.tr: 1. There, having gathered an army, the Emperor resolved to enter Italy, so that he might be present at the imperial benediction.

units.la: FRIDERICI II. IMPER. AUG. CONSTITUTIO De juribus ac privilegiis Civitatis Norimbergensis.
units.tr: FREDERICK II, AUGUSTUS EMPEROR: CONSTITUTION On the rights and privileges of the City of Nuremberg.

units.la: IN nomine sanctæ & individuæ Trinitatis. Fridericus Secundus divina favente Clementia Romanorum Rex & Semper-Augustus, & Rex Siciliæ. Cum ex debito Regiæ eminentiæ omnium Imperii fidelium jura piè debeamus & velimus favore tueri atque gubernare ex abundanti Serenitatis nostræ benevolentia eorum intendimus jura non solummodo roborare, verum quoque Regali autoritate potentia, quorum continua obsequia nobis ex suis meritis grata admodum sunt & accepta.
units.tr: IN the name of the holy and undivided Trinity. Frederick the Second, by the favour of divine clemency King of the Romans, ever Augustus, and King of Sicily. Since by the duty of our royal eminence we ought and wish to protect and govern with devotion the rights of all the faithful of the Empire, we intend, out of the abundant goodwill of our Serenity, not only to strengthen their rights but also to support them with royal authority and power, since their continual services to us are, on account of their merits, most pleasing and acceptable.

units.la: 1. Ad evidentiam igitur specialis gratiæ ac dilectionis, quam gerimus ad charissimam civitatem nostram Nurembergensem, antiqua jura à Divis prædecessoribus ac progenitoribus nostris, iuclitis Romanorum Imperatoribus & Regibus Semper Augustis eidem loco tradita, non solummodo confirmamus. Imo si quid habere videntur defectum, cum locus ille nec habeat vineta neque navigia, imo in montuoso sit situs fundo, de mera benignitate supplemus.
units.tr: 1. To make manifest, therefore, the special favour and affection which we bear towards our most dear city of Nuremberg, we not only confirm the ancient rights handed down to that place by our divine predecessors and progenitors, the renowned Roman Emperors and Kings, ever Augustus. Moreover, if anything seems to be lacking, since that place has neither vineyards nor ships, and indeed lies on a mountainous site, we supply it out of pure kindness.

units.la: 2. Statuentes & profuturis temporibus incommutabiliter observari sancientes, quòd quilibet civis loci illius nullum habere debeat Advocatum, præterquam nos & successores nostros Romanorum Reges & Imperatores.
units.tr: 2. We decree, and by this ordinance ordain that it be unchangeably observed in future times, that no citizen of that place shall have any advocate except us and our successors, the Roman Kings and Emperors.

units.la: 3. Item quicunque civis antedictæ civitatis fecerit se alicujus muntman, tam civis ille, quàm qui eum receperit, gratiam nostram demeruit, & in utroque pax non violatur.
units.tr: 3. Likewise, whatever citizen of the aforesaid city makes himself a muntman of anyone, both that citizen and whoever receives him have forfeited our favour, and the peace is not violated in either case.

units.la: 4. Item nemo aliquem civem loci illius duello impetere debet in toto Romano Imperio.
units.tr: 4. Likewise, no one shall challenge any citizen of that place to a duel anywhere in the whole Roman Empire.

units.la: 5. Item quicunque alicui civi Norimbergensi aliqua bona sua sive prædia, sive feuda obligaverit vel pignoraverit, quocunque illa bona obligata devolventur, sive ad dominos sive ad hæredes, civis qui à fuerunt obligata, in quieta permaneat possessione, quoniamque à successore redimantur.
units.tr: 5. Likewise, whoever has pledged or mortgaged to any Nuremberg citizen any of his goods, whether lands or fiefs, whoever the mortgaged goods pass to, whether to lords or to heirs, the citizen to whom they were pledged shall remain in quiet possession, until they are redeemed by a successor.

units.la: 6. Item quicunque aliquem Norimbergensem bonis suis, sive prædiis, sive feudis quocunque modo beneficiaverit; si forte Dominus feudi aliquo tempore illi feudum negaverit, vel si aliquis ipsum per hoc impetierit, & civis cum suis concivibus testimonio legitimo comprobaverit se esse investitum, in quieta permaneat possessione.
units.tr: 6. Likewise, whoever has enfeoffed any Nuremberger in any way with his goods, whether lands or fiefs: if at some time the lord of the fief should deny him the fief, or if anyone should attack him on that account, and the citizen proves by lawful testimony, together with his fellow citizens, that he has been invested, he shall remain in quiet possession.

units.la: 7. Item nullus Dominus aliquem Norimbergensem compellere debet ad jus, quod appellatur Landrecht.
units.tr: 7. Likewise, no lord shall compel any Nuremberger to the law called the Landrecht.

units.la: 8. Item quicunq; Dominus aut creditor alicui Norimbergensi accommodata reddere renuerit, tunc civis illius aut mercator vel suus vogtman, erit pignus Norimbergensibus.
units.tr: 8. Likewise, whatever lord or creditor refuses to repay what he has borrowed from any Nuremberg citizen, then that citizen's merchant or his vogtman shall be a pledge for the Nurembergers.

units.la: 9. Nullus Norimbergensis sit alicujus hominis episcopi de jure, nec unus mercator pro alio.
units.tr: 9. No Nuremberger shall by right be the man of any bishop, nor shall one merchant answer for another.

units.la: 10. Item quicquid aliquis Norimbergensis ibidem deliquit, pro quo delicto puniendus esset in corpore aut rebus, si satisfecerit Sculteto nostro, nulli amplius respondere debet de hoc delicto, & ad nostram percipiet.
units.tr: 10. Whatever offence any Nuremberger has committed there, for which he would have to be punished in body or goods, if he has made satisfaction to our bailiff, he shall owe no further answer to anyone for this offence, and the fine shall go to our treasury.

units.la: 11. Adhæc civibus sæpedicti talis gratia pro jure ab omnibus prædecessoribus nostris Romanorum Regibus tradita & indulta dinoscitur, quam nos quoq; approbamus, ut si Dominus eorum ab ipsis fleutam exigit, non particulatim sed in communi quilibet pro posse suo persolvere debeat.
units.tr: 11. Moreover, it is known that this favour, granted and conceded as a right to the aforesaid citizens by all our predecessors, the Roman Kings, we also approve: that if their lord demands from them the fleuta, it shall not be paid by individuals separately but by everyone together, each according to his ability.

units.la: 12. Item in nundinis a Werde, civis Norimbergensis cum denariis Norimbergensibus recambiet & emet aurum & argentum, & nemo prohibebit.
units.tr: 12. Likewise, at the fairs of Werd, a Nuremberg citizen may exchange and buy gold and silver with Nuremberg coin, and no one shall forbid it.

units.la: 13. Similiter in nundinis Nordlingensibus cum denariis Nurembergensibus ement & emt aurum & argentum; & Magister monetæ Nurembergensis illuc ibit, si voluerit, & denarios monetæ ibi formabit.
units.tr: 13. Likewise, at the fairs of Nördlingen, they may buy and sell gold and silver with Nuremberg coin; and the Master of the Nuremberg mint shall go there, if he wishes, and mint coins there.

units.la: 14. Nullus Norimbergensis in celebratione Curiæ Regalis ibidem de aliquibus rebus vel theloneum.
units.tr: 14. No Nuremberger shall pay any toll on any goods there during the holding of the royal court.

units.la: 15. In b Ascha Nurembergenses non magis solvent thelonei de rebus suis, quam naturæ visua.
units.tr: 15. At Asch the Nurembergers shall pay no more toll on their goods than they would for their natural sight.

units.la: 16. De Ratispona usq; Pataviam nullum solvent theloneum.
units.tr: 16. From Regensburg as far as Passau they shall pay no toll at all.

units.la: 17. In civitate Wourmacenti, in festo Joannis Baptistæ, si unus Norimbergensis dabit libram unam piperis & duas chirothecas, anno illo nihil aliud solvent vel amplius Norimbergenses.
units.tr: 17. In the city of Worms, on the feast of John the Baptist, if a Nuremberger gives one pound of pepper and two pairs of gloves, the Nurembergers shall pay nothing else or anything more in that year.

units.la: 18. In civitate Spirensi nihil solvent Nurembergenses: e converso Spirenses nihil solvent Nuremberg.
units.tr: 18. In the city of Speyer the Nurembergers shall pay nothing; and conversely, the Speyerers shall pay nothing at Nuremberg.

units.la: 19. Utigitur hæc nostræ renovationis largitas & confirmationis sanctio perpetuum recipiatur, atq; in posterum inviolabiliter observetur, hoc scriptum inde fieri jussimus, sigillo Regiæ Maiestatis communitum, sancientes, & interminatione gratiæ nostræ districtius, necnon sub perpetua pœna personarum præcipientes, ne ulla omnino persona alta vel humilis, secularis sive ecclesiastica, ullo unquam tempore ei contradicere præsumat, vel aliquo aulo temerario contravenire. Testes: Eberhardus Salzburgensis Archiepiscopus. Otto Freilingensis Episcopus. Henricus Eystetensis Episcopus. Seyfridus Augustanus Episcopus. Aquensis Præpositus. Ludovicus Comes Palatini Rheni & Dux Bavariæ. Leupuldus Dux Austriæ & Styriæ. Bernhardus Dux Carinthiæ. Comes Egeus Junior de Utach. Henricus Nobilis de Nyfe. Comes Conradus Burggravius de Nuremberg, Marchio de Baden. Anshelmus de Justingen, Marschalcus Imperii. Philippus de Bonnl, & alii plures.
units.tr: 19. So that this gift of our renewal and this sanction of confirmation may be received in perpetuity and inviolably observed in future, we have ordered this writing to be made, sealed with the seal of Your Royal Majesty, decreeing and commanding most strictly, under threat of our grace and under perpetual penalty of persons, that no person whatsoever, high or low, secular or ecclesiastical, shall ever presume at any time to contradict it or to contravene it by any rash act. Witnesses: Eberhard, Archbishop of Salzburg. Otto, Bishop of Freising. Henry, Bishop of Eichstätt. Seyfried, Bishop of Augsburg. The Provost of Aachen. Louis, Count Palatine of the Rhine and Duke of Bavaria. Leopold, Duke of Austria and Styria. Bernhard, Duke of Carinthia. Count Egeno the Younger of Urach. Henry, noble of Nyffe. Count Conrad, Burgrave of Nuremberg, Margrave of Baden. Anselm of Justingen, Marshal of the Empire. Philip of Bonn, and many others.

units.la: Ego Conradus Metensis & Spirensis Episcopus, Imperialis Aulæ Cancellarius, vice Domini Sanctæ Moguntinensis Sedis Archiepiscopi ac totius Germaniæ Archicancellarii, recognovi. Datum anno incarnationis Domini millesimo ducentesimo decimo nono: regnante piissimo Domino Friderico II. divina favente clementia Romanorum Rege Semper Augusto, & glorioso Siciliæ, anno Romani Regni ipsius septimo, Siciliæ vero vicesimo secundo, feliciter. Datum apud Nuremberg, anno suprascripto, v 1. Idus Novembris, v 11. Indictione.
units.tr: I, Conrad, Bishop of Metz and Speyer, Chancellor of the Imperial Court, on behalf of the Lord Archbishop of the holy see of Mainz and Archchancellor of all Germany, have acknowledged this. Given in the year of the incarnation of the Lord 1219, the most pious Lord Frederick II, by the favour of divine clemency King of the Romans, ever Augustus, and glorious King of Sicily, reigning; in the seventh year of his reign over the Romans, and in the twenty-second of his reign over Sicily, happily. Given at Nuremberg, in the year above written, on the 1st (v. 1.) day before the Ides of November, in the 11th indiction.

units.la: FRIDERICI II. IMPER. AUG. EDICTUM
units.tr: EDICT OF EMPEROR FREDERICK II, AUGUST

units.la: De cassandis statutis adversus libertatem Ecclesiæ editis.
units.tr: On the annulling of statutes issued against the liberty of the Church.

units.la: NOs Fridericus Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator & Semper Augustus, hac edicto irritamus, & præcipimus irritari omnia statuta & consuetudines, quæ civitates, vel loca, Consules, vel quæcumq; aliæ personæ contra libertatem Ecclesiæ, vel personas ecclesiasticas edere, vel servare tentaverint adversus Canonicas vel Imperiales sanctiones. Et ea de Clericis infra duos menses post hujusmodi publicationem edicti penitus aboleri, &c. Datum Ronc die Coronationis, &c.
units.tr: We, Frederick, by the grace of God Roman Emperor and ever Augustus, by this edict annul, and command to be annulled, all statutes and customs which cities or places, consuls, or any other persons whatsoever, have attempted to issue or maintain against the liberty of the Church or ecclesiastical persons, contrary to canonical or imperial sanctions. And these concerning clergy are to be utterly abolished within two months after the publication of this edict, etc. Given at Ronc on the day of the Coronation, etc.

units.la: FRIDERICI II. IMPER. AUG. CONSTITUTIO
units.tr: FRIDERICI II. IMPER. AUG. CONSTITUTIO

units.la: Pro Ecclesiastica libertate.
units.tr: Concerning ecclesiastical liberty.

units.la: FRidericus Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator Semper Augustus, & Rex Siciliæ, Potestatibus, Consulibus, ac Comitibus universorum Comitatuum, & Castrorum Italiæ.
units.tr: Frederick, by the grace of God Emperor of the Romans, ever Augustus, and King of Sicily, to the magistrates, consuls, and counts of all the counties and fortified towns of Italy.

units.la: Cum divæ memoriæ Imperatores Romani sacrosanctam Ecclesiam multiplici libertate donarint, nos disponente Deo, a quo est omnis potestas, ad fastigium culminis Imperialis electi, pie ab illis, & a sanctissimæ Sedis Præsulibus pro statu Ecclesiarum & Ecclesiasticorum vigore edita, conservare volumus inconcussa; & illis contraria, sicut ad nos spectare dignoscitur antiqua. Cum igitur ad aures Celsitudinis nostræ pervenerit, nonnullos vestrûm cupidine cæca seductos quædam detestanda ediderint statuta, præjudicantia Ecclesiasticæ libertati, ac divino & humano juri obviantia manifeste, nos ea tanquam de radice pravitatis hæreticæ provenientia, auctoritate præsentium cassamus sub pœna mille marcharum, districtius inhibentes, ne quis vestrûm illis de cetero hærere præsumat, aut eorum prætextu Ecclesias & Ecclesiasticos viros contra sanctiones canonicas & legitimas molestare. Quinimmò ea de nostris Capitularibus seu breviariis condemnata penitus abolentes, Ecclesias & Ecclesiasticas personas permittatis indulta sibi libertate gaudere, si vultis pœnam effugere prænotatam, & indignationem Regiam evitare.
units.tr: Since the Roman Emperors of blessed memory have endowed the most holy Church with manifold liberty, we, by the disposition of God, from whom all power comes, raised to the summit of the imperial dignity, wish to keep inviolate what was piously enacted by them and by the Presidents of the most holy See for the welfare of the churches and of churchmen, and, as is rightly known to belong to us, to keep ancient laws contrary to them. Since it has therefore come to the ears of Your Highness that some of you, led astray by blind greed, have issued certain detestable statutes, which clearly prejudice ecclesiastical liberty and plainly oppose divine and human law, we, regarding them as springing from the root of heretical wickedness, by the authority of these present letters quash them under a penalty of a thousand marks, and we sternly forbid any of you to presume henceforth to cling to them, or under their pretext to harass churches and churchmen contrary to canonical and lawful sanctions. Moreover, by completely abolishing those things condemned in our Capitularies or breviaries, you shall permit the churches and ecclesiastical persons to enjoy the liberty granted to them, if you wish to escape the aforesaid penalty and avoid the displeasure of the King.

units.la: Datum in castris apud sanctum Leonem, anno Domini millesimo, ducentesimo, vigesimo, Indictione octava, Kalendis Octobris.
units.tr: Given in camp at Saint Leo, in the year of the Lord one thousand two hundred and twenty, eighth indiction, on the Kalends of October.

units.la: FRIDERICI II. IMPER. AUG. CONSTITUTIONES
units.tr: THE CONSTITUTIONS OF THE EMPEROR FREDERICK II AUGUSTUS

units.la: CONTRA HAERETICOS.
units.tr: AGAINST THE HERETICS.

units.la: FRidericus Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator, Semper Augustus, dilectis Principibus, cunctisque populis, quos Clementiæ nostræ regit imperium, salutem & gratiam.
units.tr: Frederick, by the grace of God Emperor of the Romans, ever Augustus, to our beloved princes and all peoples whom the rule of our Clemency governs: greeting and grace.

units.la: 1. Commissi nobis cœlitùs cura regiminis, & Imperiale, cui dante Domino præsidemus, fastigium dignitatis, materialem, quo divisim à Sacerdotio fungimur, gladium adversus hostes fidei & in exterminium Hæreticæ pravitatis exigunt exerendum, ut vipereos perfidiæ filios contra Deum & Ecclesiam insultantes, tanquam materni uteri corrosores, in judicio & justitia persequamur, maleficos vivere non passuri: per quorum {a}sententiam seductem mundus inficitur, & gregi fidelium per {a}alios scientiam morbidas gravior infligitur corruptela.
units.tr: 1. The care of government committed to us from heaven, and the height of imperial dignity over which, by the Lord's gift, we preside, and the material sword, which we wield separately from the priesthood, demand to be drawn against the enemies of the faith and for the extermination of heretical depravity. Thus we shall pursue, in judgment and justice, the viper-like sons of perfidy who insult God and the Church, as corrupters of their mother's womb, since we do not intend to allow evildoers to live. Through their teaching the world is infected, and a more serious and deadly corruption of knowledge is inflicted by them on the flock of the faithful.

units.la: 2. Statuimus itaque, sancientes, ut Hæretici, quocumque nomine censeantur, ubicumque per Imperium damnati fuerint ab Ecclesia, & seculari Judici assignati, animadversione debita puniantur. Si qui verò de prædictis, postquam fuerint deprehensi, territi metu mortis redire voluerint ad fidei unitatem, juxta canonicas sanctiones ad agendam pœnitentiam in perpetuum carcerem detrudantur.
units.tr: 2. We therefore decree and ordain that heretics, under whatever name they are known, wherever in the Empire they have been condemned by the Church and handed over to the secular judge, shall be punished with due penalty. But if any of the aforesaid, after they have been caught, struck with fear of death, wish to return to unity of the faith, they shall be consigned to perpetual prison to perform penance, in accordance with the canonical sanctions.

units.la: 3. Præterea quicumque Hæretici reperti fuerint in civitatibus, oppidis, seu aliis locis Imperii, per inquisitores ab Apostolica Sede datos, & alios Orthodoxæ fidei zelatores, ii, qui jurisdictionem ibidem habuerint, ad inquisitorum & aliorum Catholicorum vitorum insinuationem eos capere teneantur, & eos captos arctius custodite, donec per censuram Ecclesiasticam damnatos, damnabili morte pereant, qui fidei sacramenta & gloriam æternæ vitæ damnabant.
units.tr: 3. Moreover, whatever heretics are found in cities, towns or other places of the Empire, through inquisitors sent from the Apostolic See and other zealots of the orthodox faith, those who have jurisdiction there shall be bound to seize them at the instigation of the inquisitors and other Catholic men, and to hold them captive under close guard, until, condemned by ecclesiastical censure, they perish by a damnable death, since they have condemned the sacraments of the faith and the glory of eternal life.

units.la: 4. Simili quoque pœna plecti censemus omnes, quos ad fovendum Hæreticorum errores callidi hostis suscitat advocatos, vel parat illicitos defensores, maximè cùm idem facinus, quos inquinat, quod nisi monitione præmissa destiterint, & eorum vitæ duxerint consulendum.
units.tr: 4. We likewise judge that all who are summoned by the crafty enemy to foster the errors of heretics, or who prepare themselves as unlawful defenders, shall be punished with the same penalty, especially since the same crime defiles them, unless, after a warning has been given, they desist and take thought for their souls.

units.la: 5. Eos præterea, qui convicti in uno loco de hæresi ad alia loca se transferunt, ut cautius possint vindicare virus Hæreticæ pravitatis, debitam censemus subire vindictam: ut super hoc per viros ab eadem errore conversos ad fidem, necnon & per alios, qui eos de hæresi convicerunt, quod & in hoc nobis concedimus licitè faciendum, evidens testimonium habeatur.
units.tr: 5. Furthermore, we decree that those who, convicted of heresy in one place, move to other places, so that they may more cautiously spread the poison of heretical depravity, shall undergo due vengeance; so that in this matter clear evidence may be had through men converted from the same error to the faith, and also through others who convicted them of heresy, which we also grant may lawfully be done in this matter.

units.la: 6. Item morus sententiæ ducimus addicendos, si quos Hæreticorum ad judicium tractos, in extremo vitæ periculo hæresim abjurantes, postmodùm de falso juramento constitutit & de fide mentiti convincì, ac eos cõtigerit ejusdem morbi spontaneam incurrere recidivam, ut sibi damnabiliùs iniquitas sit mentita, & pœnam debitam mendacium non evadat.
units.tr: 6. We also decree that those who, having been brought to judgment as heretics, abjure heresy at the extreme peril of life, and afterwards are convicted of false oath and of lying about their faith, and who happen to fall back spontaneously into the same disease, shall be condemned to death, so that their iniquity in lying may be more heavily condemned, and the lie may not escape the punishment it deserves.

units.la: 7. Omne insuper proclamationis & appellationis beneficium ab Hæreticis, receptatoribus, & fautoribus eorundem, penitus amovemus, volentes ut de finibus Imperii, in quibus semper debet exire fides, Hæreticæ labis genimina modis omnibus deleantur.
units.tr: 7. Moreover, we entirely remove from heretics, their harbourers and their supporters every benefit of appeal and of protest, wishing that within the bounds of the Empire, where faith must always flourish, the offspring of the heretical stain be wiped out by every means.

units.la: 8. Cæterùm quia, quanto majora divinæ nutu miserationis accepimus, & altiore locum præ filiis obtinemus, tanto devotiora debemus obsequia gratitudinis conferentes, si quando igitur in minimis cõtemptores nostri culminis excandescat auctoritas, si reos læsæ majestatis in personis & liberorum suorum exhæredatione damnamus; multo fortius justiusque contra Dei blasphemas nomus, & Catholicæ fidei detractores provocamur, eorundem Hæreticorum, receptatorum, fautorum, & advocatorum suorum, ac eorundem hæredes & posteros nisi; ad secundam progeniem, cunctis temporalibus, publicis officiis, & honoribus Imperiali auctoritate privantes, ut in paterni criminis continuo mœrore tabescant, verè scientes, quòd Deus zelotes est, & peccata patrum potenter ulciscens, nec quidè à nostræ miserocordiæ finibus duximus excludendum; ut si qui hæresis non sequaces latentem patrum per fidiam revelarint, quacumque reatus illorum animadversione plectantur, præditæ punitioni non subjaceat innocentia filiorum.
units.tr: 8. Furthermore, since we have received from the will of divine mercy greater gifts, and occupy a higher place than our sons, we ought to render correspondingly more devoted services of gratitude. Therefore, if at any time the authority of our summit grows angry against those who despise it even in small matters, and we condemn those guilty of high treason to the loss of their persons and of their children's inheritance, then much more strongly and justly are we roused against the blasphemers of God and the detractors of the Catholic faith. Their heretics, harbourers, supporters and advocates, and their heirs and descendants as far as the second generation, we deprive by imperial authority of all temporal public offices and honours, so that they may waste away in constant grief for their fathers' crime. We truly know that God is a jealous God, who powerfully avenges the sins of the fathers; nor have we thought it right to exclude such persons from the bounds of our mercy: so that if any who do not follow heresy reveal the hidden treachery of their fathers, whatever their guilt, they shall be punished by a penalty that is not inflicted on the innocence of the sons.

units.la: {a} al. scientiam
units.tr: {a} another reading: scientiam

units.la: 9. Adhæc notum fieri volumus, Fratres Prædicatores & Minores, pro fidei negotio in partibus Imperii contra Hæreticos deputatos: cæteros quoq;, qui ad Hæreticos judicandos accesserint, nisi ab Imperio fuerint proscripti, eundo, morando, & redeúndo sub nostri Imperii speciali defensione receptos, & quos apud omnes sub ope accrecõmendatione fidelium Imperii esse volumus inoffensis, universitati vestræ mādantes, quatenus quocumq; & apud quemcumque vestrum pervenerint, benigne recipiatis eosdem, & personas eorum ab incursu Hæreticorum eis insidiantium conservantes indemnes.
units.tr: 9. Moreover, we wish it to be made known that the Brothers Preachers and Minorites, appointed for the business of the faith against heretics in the regions of the Empire, as well as others who have come to judge heretics, unless they have been outlawed by the Empire, while going, staying and returning, are received under our special protection of the Empire, and we wish them to be secure and unharmed under the aid and recommendation of the faithful everywhere in the Empire. We command your community that, wherever and to whomever of you they come, you receive them kindly and keep their persons unhurt from the attack of the heretics who lie in wait for them.

units.la: Exod. 34. Jerem. 32. indemnes,omne consilium, ducatum, & auxilium impendatis, pro tam acceptis coram Deo negoti exequendis. Hæreticos verò,quos & ipsi vobis ostenderint, in jurisdictione vestra singuli capiantur, diligenti custodia detinete,donec post Ecclesiasticæ damnationis judicium pœnam subeant, quæ tenetur: sciturí, quòd in ipsius executione negotii gratum Deo & laudabile nobis obsequium impendetis, si ad expellendam de partibus nostri Imperii novam & insolitam Hæreticæ pravitatis infamiam operam & operam unà cum eisdem Fratribus præstiteritis efficacem. Et si quis exinde foret negligens vel remissus ac etiam inutilis,coram Deo, & in conspectu nostro poterit merito culpabilis apparere. Datum * Paduæ x x i i.Februarii,x i i.Indictione.
units.tr: Exod. 34. Jerem. 32. unharmed, you shall give every counsel, guidance and help in carrying out so acceptable a business before God. Those heretics whom they themselves point out to you shall each be seized within your jurisdiction and held under careful custody until, after the judgment of ecclesiastical condemnation, they undergo the penalty that is owed. Know that in carrying out this business you will render to God a pleasing service and to us a praiseworthy obedience, if you give effective help, together with the same Brothers, toward driving out of the regions of our Empire the new and unaccustomed infamy of heretical depravity. And if anyone is negligent or remiss in this, or even useless, he may rightly appear guilty before God and in our sight. Given at Padua, on the 22nd of February, in the 12th indiction.

units.la: CONSTITUTIO II.
units.tr: CONSTITUTION II.

units.la: FRIDERICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator Semper Augustus, Hierusalem & Siciliæ Rex, dilectis Principibus suis, Venerabilibus Archiepiscopis & Episcopis, aliisque Prælatis Ecclesiarum, Ducibus, Marchionibus, Comitibus, Baronibus, Potestatibus, Scultetis, Burgravius, Advocatis, Judicibus, Ministerialibus, Officialibus, & omnibus per totum Imperium constitutis, præsentes literas inspecturis, fidelibus suis, gratiam suam & omne bonum.
units.tr: FREDERICK, by the grace of God Roman Emperor, ever Augustus, King of Jerusalem and Sicily, to his beloved princes, the venerable archbishops and bishops, and the other prelates of the churches, dukes, margraves, counts, barons, potentates, schultheiss, burgraves, advocates, judges, ministerials, officials, and all established throughout the whole Empire, who shall see these present letters, to his faithful subjects, his grace and every good.

units.la: 1. Inconsuetilem tunicam Dei nostri dissuere conantur Hæretici, & vocabuli vicio sævientes, quod significationè divisionis denuntiat, in ipsius indivisibilis fidei unitate nitintur inducere sectam, & oves à Petri custodia, cui pascendæ à pastore bono sunt creditæ, segregare.
