Hi sunt lupi intrinsecus, eo usque mansuetudine prætendentes ovium, quousque ovile possint subintrare minicum, quod post ipsorum interitum desiderant demoliri: hi sunt angeli pessimi, hi pavidi, sunt filii à patre nequitiæ & fraudis auctore ad simplices animas destinandi colubri, qui colubri ciphant: hi serpentes, qui latenter videntur inserpere, & sub mellis dulcedine virus evomere, cibum se simulent ministrare, à cauda feriunt, & mortis poculum velut quoddam dirissimum immiscent. Horum sectæ veteribus, vel nec in publicum prodeant, non sunt notatæ nominibus, vel (quod est forte nephandius) non contentæ.ut velut ab Arrio Arriani, vel à Nestorio Nestoriani aut à similibus similes nuncupentur: sed in exemplum Martyrum, qui pro fide Catholica martyrium subierunt, Patarenos se nominant, velut expolitos passioni.
units.tr: 1. The heretics try to tear the seamless tunic of our God, and, raging with the vice of a word that signifies division, they strive to introduce a sect into the unity of that indivisible faith and to separate the sheep from the custody of Peter, to whom they were entrusted by the good Shepherd to feed. They are wolves within, feigning the gentleness of sheep only until they can slip into the fold, which they desire to tear down once its keepers have perished. They are wicked angels, they are cowards, they are serpents sent by the father of wickedness and the author of deceit to destroy simple souls, serpents that hiss. They are snakes that seem to creep in unseen and spit their poison beneath the sweetness of honey; they pretend to serve food, but they strike from the tail and mix in the cup of death as if it were some most deadly drug. Their sects, like those of old, do not come forth openly and are not marked by names, or (which is perhaps more abominable) they are not content to be named after their leaders, as the Arians were from Arius or the Nestorians from Nestorius, or others like them from similar men. Instead, in imitation of the martyrs who underwent martyrdom for the Catholic faith, they call themselves Patarenes, as if they were polished for suffering.

units.la: {a} al.concepta. {b} ms.Filium.
units.tr: {a} Another reading: "concepta." {b} Manuscript: "Filium."

units.la: CONSTITUTIO III.
units.tr: CONSTITUTION III.

units.la: FRIDERICUS Dei gratia Imperator Semper-Augustus, &c. Patarenorum complices & receptatores, seu quocumque modo fautores, qui, ut alios à pœna possint eximere, de se velut improvidi non formidant, publicatis omnibus bonis eorum relegandos in perpetuum esse censemus, & ipsorum ad honores aliquos nullatenus admittantur. Si tamen aliquis fautorum huiusmodi detexerit aliquam Patarenum, de cuius perfidia manifestè probarur & liquet, in fidei præmium, quam agnovit favore piissimæ de Imperiali clementia restitutionis beneficium in integrum consequatur.
units.tr: FREDERICK, by the grace of God Emperor, ever Augustus, etc. We decree that the accomplices and harbourers of the Patarines, and all who in any way favour them, who, so that they may save others from punishment, do not fear for themselves as though they were careless of their own safety, shall have all their goods confiscated and be exiled for ever, and shall in no way be admitted to any honours. If, however, any such favourer has disclosed some Patarine whose treachery is plainly proven and evident, he shall, as the reward of his faith in acknowledging it, obtain by the favour of the most pious imperial clemency the benefit of full restitution.

units.la: INCIPIVNT CAPITVLA CONSTITVTIONIS CONTRA Patarenos edita per Dominum Fredericum Illustrem virum, Romanorum Imperatorem semper Augustum, Hierusalem & Siciliæ Regem.
units.tr: THE CHAPTERS OF THE CONSTITUTION AGAINST THE PATARINES, issued by Lord Frederick, illustrious man, Emperor of the Romans, ever Augustus, King of Jerusalem and Sicily.

units.la: 1. Patarenos, Speroniftas, Leoniftas, Arnaldiftas, Circumcisos, Passaginos, Josephinos, Cathari, Albanenses, Francischos, Bennatoles, Comiftas, Waldenses, Burgaros, Commimellos, Minus & Orcholenos, cum illis de Aqua nigra, Pauperes de Lugduno, & omnes Hæreticos utriusque sexus quocunque nomine censeantur, perpetua damnamus infamia, diffidamus atque bannimus, contemnentes ut bona talium confiscentur, nec ad eos ulterius revertantur, ita quòd filii eorum ad successionem pervenire non possint, cùm * longè sit gravius æternam quàm temporalem offendere majestatem. Qui autem inventi fuerint sola suspicione notabiles, nisi ad mandatum Ecclesiæ, juxta consideratio-nem suspicionis qualitatemque personæ, propriam innocentiam congrua purgatione monstraverint, eaque infames & banniti ab omnibus habeantur, ita quòd si sic banniti per annum permanserint, extunc eos sicut Hæreticos condemnamus.
units.tr: 1. We condemn to perpetual infamy, outlaw and proscribe the Patarines, Speronists, Leonists, Arnaldists, Circumcised, Passagians, Josephists, Cathari, Albanenses, Franciscans, Bennatoles, Comists, Waldenses, Burgari, Commimelli, Minus and Orcholeni, together with those of Aqua Nigra, the Poor of Lyons, and all heretics of either sex, by whatever name they are called. We decree that their goods be confiscated and never revert to them again, so that their sons cannot succeed to them, since it is far more serious to offend the eternal majesty than the temporal one. Those who are found notable by mere suspicion, unless at the command of the Church, according to the consideration of the suspicion and the quality of the person, have shown their own innocence by a suitable purgation, shall be regarded as infamous and outlawed by all; and if they remain thus outlawed for a year, then we condemn them as heretics.

units.la: 2. Statuimus etiam hoc edicto in perpetuum valituro, ut † Potestates & Consules seu Rectores, quibuscunque fungantur officiis, pro defensione fidei præstent publicè juramentum, quòd de terris f ditioni subjectis, universos Hæreticos ab Ecclesia denotatos, bona fide pro viribus exterminare studebunt, ita quòd a modò, quandocunque quis fuerit in perpetuam Potestatem vel temporalem assumptus, hoc teneatur juramento firmare capitulum: alioquin neque pro Potestatibus, neque pro Consulibus seu consimilibus habeantur, eorumque sententias extunc decernimus inutiles & nullas. Si verò Dominus temporalis, requisitus & monitus ab Ecclesia, terram suam purgare neglexerit ab Hæretica pravitate, post annum à tempore monitionis elapsum terram ipsius exponimus Catholicis cupandam, qui eam exterminatis Hæreticis absque ulla contradictione possideant, & in fidei puritate conservent, salvo jure Domini temporalis, dummodò super his nullum præstet obstaculum, neque aliquod impedimentum opponat, eadem nihilominus lege servata contra eos, qui * non habent Dominos temporales Principales.
units.tr: 2. We also enact, by this edict to remain in force for ever, that the Potestates, Consuls, or Rectors, whatever offices they hold, shall publicly swear an oath in defence of the faith, that they will zealously and in good faith strive to exterminate from the lands subject to their authority all heretics denounced by the Church. From now on, whenever anyone is raised to a perpetual or temporal power, he shall be bound to confirm this chapter by oath; otherwise he shall not be regarded as Potestas, nor as Consul or the like, and we decree their sentences thereafter to be void and null. If, however, a temporal lord, when required and warned by the Church, neglects to cleanse his land of heretical depravity, then, after a year has elapsed from the time of the warning, we expose his land to be occupied by Catholics, who, once the heretics are driven out without any opposition, shall possess it and keep it in purity of faith, saving the right of the temporal lord, provided he offers no obstacle in these matters and raises no impediment; the same law shall nonetheless be observed against those who do not have temporal lords as their principals.

units.la: 3. Credentes præterea, receptatores, defensores, & fautores Hæreticorum bannimus, statuentes, ut si, postquam quilibet talium fuerit fidelium excommunicatione notatus, satisfacere contempserit infra annum, extunc ipso jure sit factus infamis, & ad publica officia seu consilia, vel ad tractatus quosque eligendos hujusmodi, nec ad testimonium admittatur. Sit etiam intestabilis, ut nec testamenti factionem habeat, nec ad hereditatis alicujus successionem accedat. Nullus ei præterea super quocunque negocio, sed ipse aliis respondere cogatur. Quòd si Judex extiterit, ejus sententia nullam habeat roboris firmitatem, nec causæ aliquæ ad ejus notitiam perferantur. Si fuerit Advocatus, ejus a. al. audiencium nullatenus admittatur. Si Tabellio autem fuerit, instrumenta confecta per manum ipsius penitus sint momenti.
units.tr: 3. Furthermore, we outlaw those who believe in, harbour, defend and favour heretics, decreeing that if any such believer, having been marked by excommunication, scorns to make satisfaction within a year, he shall by that very law become infamous, and shall not be admitted to public offices or councils, nor be chosen for such negotiations, nor be admitted as a witness. He shall also be intestable, so that he has no power to make a will, nor may he succeed to any inheritance. Moreover, no one shall be answerable to him in any matter, but he himself shall be compelled to answer to others. If he is a judge, his sentence shall have no force of strength whatever, and no cases shall be brought to his notice. If he is an advocate, he shall not be admitted to the hearing of any other causes. If he is a notary, instruments drawn up by his hand shall be wholly without validity.

units.la: 4. Adjicimus insuper, quod Hæreticus per Hæreticum convinci possit: & quod domus Patarenorum, receptatorum, defensorum, & fautorum, sive ubi docuerint, sive ubi alius manus imposuerint, * Abestnegativa in mt. Hæreticus per Hæreticum convinci poterit. nullo tempore reparandæ. Datum Paduæ, xxii. Febr. xiii. Indictione.
units.tr: 4. We add further that a heretic may be convicted by a heretic; and that the houses of Patarines, harbourers, defenders and favourers, whether they have taught in them or whether others have laid hands on them, shall never be restored. [Marginal note: "negativa" is absent in the margin text.] A heretic can be convicted by a heretic. Given at Padua, 22 February, in the thirteenth indiction.

units.la: FRIDERICI II. IMP. AUG. DECRETUM
units.tr: DECREE OF EMPEROR FREDERICK II, AUGUSTUS

units.la: Proscriptionis Comitum Habspurgensium propter vim Ecclesiæ Beronensi illatam.
units.tr: Proscription of the Counts of Habsburg for the violence done to the Church of Beronensis.

units.la: FRIDERICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator Semper-Augustus, & Rex Siciliæ, universis Principibus Alamanniæ, tam ecclesiasticis quàm secularibus, & aliis Imperii fidelibus, ad quos literæ istæ pervenerint, gratiam suam & omne bonum. Universitati vestræ renore præsentium volumus esse notum, quod veniens ad præsentiam nostram Dietricus Beronensis Ecclesiæ Præpositus, filius Hofter, sua Celsitudini nostræ conquestione monstravit, qualiter Wernherus & Hartmannus Comites de Kiburg, eidem Ecclesiæ suæ damna enormia irrogantes, eum & alios Canonicos suæ eadem Ecclesia Domino famulantes, de gremio ipsius Ecclesiæ turpiter ejecerunt, quòd ipse, nec aliquis Canonicorum, sex jam annis elapsis, ad serviendum Deo ibidem audeat. Et licet per Constantiensem videlicet Diocesanum Episcopum excommunicationis sententia contra eos propter hoc fuerit promulgata, & terra eorum suppositia interdicto, ipsi nihilominus in contemptum Dei & Ecclesiæ adversus ipsum, & Ecclesiam suam in nullo satisfacere procurarunt, in eadem contumacia contumaciter permanserunt, sic quòd eadem excommunicationis sententia per Summum Pontificem extitit confirmata. Propter quod PræPræpositus in præsentia Venerabilium Cicensis, Tridentini & Brixinensis Episcoporum, & alioquàm plurium tam Imperii quàm * Regni Magnatum, Excellentiæ nostræ humiliter supplicav-erunt quod ad Imperiale spectat officium, exinde prosequi dignaremur. Nos igitur protervam prærumComitum contumaciam attendentes, ad petitionem quoque prædicti Constantiensis Dioc. Episcopi, cujus censuram ecclesiasticam, Dei timore postposito, dicti Comites per triennium, ferritut, contemnentes, ab infestatione ipsius Ecclesiæ non desistunt, cùm absonum sit Imperio tam enormes Ecclesiis Dei violentias irrogati, quas ex collata nobis plenitudine potestatis demodis omnibus & fovere tenemur, præsentibus prædictis Principibus & ceteris tam Imperii Regni Magistratibus, prædictos Comites excommunicationis sententiam contemnentes, sententiliter proscriptos denunciamus, mandantes ipsos de cetero velut proscriptos ab omnibus evitari. Rursus Heinrico Romanorum Regi filio nostro per literas nostras dedimus in mandatis, ut ipsos Comites pro prædictis memoratis excessibus proscriptos denunciet, & ab ipsa proscriptione decernimus non solvendos, nisi prædicto Præposito condignè satisfaciant & Ecclesiæ luæ, sicut debent. Data in Campania, apud Montem S. Joannis, die xxiii. Februarii, xi. Indict.
units.tr: FREDERICK, by the grace of God Emperor of the Romans, ever Augustus, and King of Sicily, to all the princes of Alamannia, both ecclesiastical and secular, and to the other faithful of the Empire to whom this letter may come, greeting and every good thing. By the tenor of these presents we wish it to be known to all of you that Dietrich, provost of the Church of Beromünster, son of Hofter, came into our presence and complained to our Highness how Werner and Hartmann, Counts of Kyburg, inflicting enormous losses on his church, shamefully expelled him and the other canons serving the Lord in that same church from its bosom, so that for six years now neither he nor any of the canons dares to serve God there. And although a sentence of excommunication was pronounced against them for this by the bishop of Constance, the diocesan, and their lands were placed under interdict, they nonetheless, in contempt of God and the Church, made no effort to make amends to him or to his church, and remained stubbornly in that obstinacy, so that the same sentence of excommunication was confirmed by the Supreme Pontiff. On this account the provost, in the presence of the venerable bishops of Chur, Trent and Brixen, and of many other magnates of both the Empire and the kingdom, humbly petitioned our Excellency that we would deign to pursue the matter in accordance with the imperial office. We therefore, observing the shameless obstinacy of the Counts, and also at the petition of the aforesaid bishop of Constance, whose ecclesiastical censure these Counts have for three years borne, putting the fear of God aside and despising it, and who do not cease from harassing that Church, since it is unseemly for the Empire that such enormous violences be inflicted on the Churches of God, which by the fullness of power conferred on us we are bound in every way to cherish, with the aforesaid princes and the other magistrates of the Empire and kingdom present, we declare the aforesaid Counts, who despise the sentence of excommunication, to be proscribed by sentence, and we order that from now on they be shunned by all as proscribed persons. Moreover, by our letters we have instructed Henry, King of the Romans, our son, to declare the same Counts proscribed for the aforesaid excesses; and we decree that they are not to be released from this proscription unless they make adequate satisfaction to the aforesaid provost and to his Church, as they ought. Given in Campania, at Mont Saint-Jean, on the 23rd day of February, in the eleventh indiction.

units.la: FRIDERICI II. IMP. AUG. PRAECEPTUM
units.tr: THE PRECEPT OF FREDERICK II, EMPEROR AUGUSTUS

units.la: De Pataviensi Decano, Papæ adversus Imperium adhærente, capiendo & plectendo.
units.tr: Concerning the Dean of Passau, who adhered to the Pope against the Empire, to be seized and punished.

units.la: IMP. FRIDERICUS Augustus, Ottoni Bojorum Duci & Palatino Comiti Rheni, gratiam suam omne bonum. Certior factus sum literis Eberhardi Archiepiscopi Juvavensis, atque Friderici Ducis Austriæ, a Albertum quendam Sacerdotulum, authoritate Gregorii, qui dicitur Papa, in nos con-cia jactare eumque in viis, oppidis, castellis suis habitare. Quàm id impium sit, tute existimare possumus, qui maledicit Principi suo. Te atque tuum avum ex infimo loco, ego & avus meus ad fastigium summum eveximus; hujusmodi criminis læsæ Majestatis obnoxius exigatur. Data in Ilidione Faventiæ, quarto Nonas Octobris.
units.tr: Frederick, Emperor Augustus, to Otto, Duke of the Bavarians and Count Palatine of the Rhine, his grace and every good thing. I have been informed by letters from Eberhard, Archbishop of Salzburg, and from Frederick, Duke of Austria, that a certain priest named Albert, by the authority of Gregory, who is called Pope, is spreading inflammatory sermons against us, and that he lives in the roads, towns and castles of the duke. We can easily judge for ourselves how impious this is, since he curses his own prince. You and your grandfather were raised by me and my grandfather from the lowest rank to the highest summit. Let such a man be held liable for the crime of lese-majesty. Given at Ilidione near Faenza, on the fourth of the Nones of October.

units.la: FRIDERICI II. IMPER. AUG. EDICTUM
units.tr: EDICT OF FREDERICK II, EMPEROR AUGUSTUS

units.la: De Papæ Romani tyrannide & Antichristianismo, adversus conjurationem Principum Imperii in Comitiis Bud: Jinis congregatorum.
units.tr: On the tyranny and Antichristianism of the Roman Pope, against the conspiracy of the princes of the Empire assembled at the Diet of Buda.

units.la: FRIDERICUS Augustus ubi rescivit, plerosque conjuratorum Principum apud * Budam, ut condictum erat, Comitia Cæsarea habere, Principibus cunctis, maximè Ottoni Bojorum Regulo, Præfectoque prætorio Rheni, literas mittit. Illarum literarum hæc sententia fuit:
units.tr: When Frederick Augustus learned that most of the conspiring princes were holding an imperial diet at Buda, as had been agreed, he sent letters to all the princes, especially to Otto, petty king of the Bavarians and prefect of the praetorium of the Rhine. The sense of those letters was this:

units.la: Pleraque crimina sibi objecta à Romano Pontifice negando diluit, alia in illum retorquet, confutat. Pontifices Romanos auctos divitiis & dignitate à se atque cæteris Imperatoribus, æmulos pertinacissimos omnium Regum atque Principum, neque pati ultra ferre posse. Manibus pedibusque noctes diesque id eos conari, ut non tam se, quam SS. Romano Imperio, tanquam capite oppresso cæteris membris omnibus servitutem imponant, affectare eos dominationem atque divinitatem, ut ab omnibus haud aliter, immò magis, quam Deus timeatur. Nam multos Antichristos inclusos manentes illis, nec ullos alios, quemadmodum opera ostendunt, exitio Christianæ religionis esse quidem optimè sentire de Christo atque ejus religione prædicat, nihilque magis cupere, quàm tempore Respublica Christiana pristinam majestatem, simplicitatem & pacem recuperet. Quæ nequaquam poterit, nisi spinæ eradicentur, hoc est, ambitio, superbia, fastus, luxus Sacerdotum Romanorum, subtractis opibus atque divitiis extirpentur radicitus. Copiaterum sapientissimos quosque corrumpere solet in rebus divinis non solum Romanum Episcopum, sed unumquemque Sacerdotem sibi patrem fore, modò rebus prophanis sibi cöinissis abstineat, proponit. Imperium Christianum, ipse caput constitutus sit à Deo, non armis, non vi opprimi posse; sed luxuria, cupiditate, quæ omnium malorum est, enervari, adulterari, corrumpi. Quod ne fiat, se obviam iturum, se summo pro commisso sibi à Deo negotio, potestate conjuncta divinitus traditò contrà enisurum, ut ovili parem, populo Pontificem, mundo parentem, demacta persona lupi, Tyranni, atq; Domini, cestum eundem abdicata Regnotum, humanarum litium cura, piophanorum negotiorum administratione quibus illi interdictum sit, ad æmulanda pauperis Christi, cujus Vicarium se jactitat, vestigia cogat amplius neque passurum, ut Christianæ plebi lupus ovina pelle tectus diutius imponat. Opus vel maximum pietatis esse atq; charitatis, gratissimum immortali Deo, opes & aurum, ornamenta malorum Sacerdotibus auferre. Namq; hæc (inquit) perniciem esse religionis, adeò ut homo ille, qui dicitur papa, divitiis nimiùm auctus, maximo pietatis Christianæ detrimento, omnia sibi licere, more Tyrannorum pessimorum putet, rationem actuum nemini, quasi sit Deus, reddere velit. Id quod soli Deo convenit, usurpet; se errare, ullàve mendacii religione altingi non posse, credi sibi impudentissimè si... imperii. imprimis ... [illegible, ~20 letters] Fraudes, dolos, commenta, fucum taceri, a sibi ut vicino enim intus & in cute non- ... ellet. Vt ... de quicumque rem Christianam salvam esse velint, faveant, adiuvent, & causam Christi ... Imperatoris ... omnium denique Christianorum agenti, bene precetur. Datum in obsidione Ascu- ... vicesimo die, Indictione tertia decima.
units.tr: He answers most of the crimes charged against him by the Roman Pontiff by denying them, turns others back upon the Pontiff, and refutes them. The Roman Pontiffs, enriched with wealth and dignity by him and by other emperors, are the most stubborn rivals of all kings and princes, and can bear it no longer. Night and day, with hands and feet, they strive to impose servitude on the Holy Roman Empire, as though its head were crushed and all the other members with it; they aim at lordship and divinity, so that by all men God is feared no otherwise, indeed more, than they are feared. For he declares that many Antichrists, dwelling within those walls, and no others, as their works show, are the ruin of the Christian religion, though they hold quite correct views about Christ and his religion. He says he desires nothing more than that in time the Christian commonwealth recover its former majesty, simplicity and peace. This cannot be done unless the thorns are uprooted, that is, the ambition, pride, haughtiness and luxury of the Roman priests, and their wealth and riches are taken away and destroyed root and branch. For the abundance of riches is wont to corrupt even the wisest men in divine matters; and he proposes that not only the Roman bishop but every priest would become a father to them, provided he abstains from the secular affairs committed to him. The Christian empire, of which he himself has been constituted head by God, cannot be crushed by arms or force, but is weakened, adulterated and corrupted by luxury and greed, which is the root of all evils. To prevent this, he says, he will come forward and, with the power joined to the charge committed to him by God, strive against it with the utmost effort, so that the Pontiff, who should be a equal to the flock, a parent to the people and the world, having laid aside the mask of the wolf, the tyrant and the lord, and having abdicated this kingdom and the care of human disputes and the administration of profane affairs, from which he has been forbidden, is forced to imitate the footsteps of the poor Christ, whose vicar he boasts himself to be. He will no longer allow a wolf clothed in sheep's skin to prey longer upon the Christian people. It is the greatest work of piety and charity, and most pleasing to the immortal God, to take away wealth, gold and ornaments from evil priests. For these things (he says) are the ruin of religion, so that the man who is called pope, puffed up with excessive riches, to the greatest detriment of Christian piety, thinks that everything is permitted to him in the manner of the worst tyrants, and wishes to render an account of his actions to no one, as if he were God. He claims for himself what belongs to God alone; he says he cannot err or be caught in the bond of any lie, and he is brazenly believed... [illegible]. Frauds, tricks, inventions and deceptions are kept silent... [illegible]. Let all who wish Christian affairs to be safe favour and help, and let them pray well for the cause of Christ, the Emperor, and finally for all Christians. Given at the siege of Ascu... on the twentieth day, in the thirteenth indiction.

units.la: [illegible, ~30 letters] ... Bohemiae Regem, ad quem & alium adjecit a Legatu perferendam, quae sequitur.
units.tr: [illegible] ... King of Bohemia, to whom he also added another letter, to be delivered by a legate, which follows.

units.la: De conjuratorum Comitiis pro electione novi Imperatoris indictis, sic scribit Aventinus lib. 7. Annal. sol. 536. Privas Imperatoris, licet & in libris Pontificalibus legimus, & diplomata ostendunt, FRIDERICUS ille Secundus tanta immunitate Sacerdotum genus condonavit, quā mox adversum ... fuerunt Romanenses. Matthaeo igitur Dominicano (ut nihil hoc genus hominum, sicut vulgo dici ... non audet potissimum consultore, dum Imperator Germanis rebus intentus, devicta Austria ... Romani Flamines cum Jacobo Tempolo Duce Venetiarum, quem in Dominium Croatiae ... atque Dalmatiae, quartae partis & dimidii totius Romani Imperii, in epistola cohortatoria ad eum ... nuncupant: cum Mediolanensibus, Bononiensibus, Brixiensibus, Civibus, Episcopis, item caeteris Lombardis, quibus utilius bellum quam pax videbatur, dato his Gregorio à Montelongo Duce, ... conspirant, occasionem rebellionis faciendae praestolantur. Et ne Germania suppetias ferre posset, bona concordiae pellere, discordiae mala serere, in Germania orbeque Romano decernunt.
units.tr: Concerning the diet of the conspirators called for the election of a new emperor, Aventinus writes thus in book 7 of his Annals, page 536: We read in the pontifical books, and the documents show, that the Emperor Frederick II granted such immunity to the priestly class that soon afterwards the Romans turned against... Therefore Matthew the Dominican (since this kind of men does not dare... as is commonly said... while the Emperor, intent upon German affairs, having conquered Austria...), the Roman Flamines, together with Jacob Tempolo, Duke of Venice, whom in a letter of exhortation to him they name lord of Croatia and Dalmatia, and of a fourth part and a half of the whole Roman Empire... conspire with the Milanese, Bolognese, Brescians, citizens, bishops, and likewise the other Lombards, to whom war seemed more useful than peace, Gregory of Montelongo being given as leader to them, and wait for an opportunity to make a rebellion. And so that Germany could not bring aid, they decree to drive out the good of concord and sow the evils of discord in Germany and the Roman world.

units.la: Principes, Equites, avaritissimum quemque & maxime honorum, pecuniae studiosum, decimis, Ecclesiasticis opibus eisdem distributis, adversus Pontifices concitare constituunt. Hocque consilium magis Gregorium tentare voluisse, quam quod aequum aut justum censeret, aut denique ex animi sententia voto successurum speraret, ejus epistolae indicant. Quippe conquerentes etiam Nuncio suo, Episcopos, quos hic devoverat, ipse nihilo secius benigne datis ad eosdem literis, dissimulata devotione fratres suos venerabiles appellat. Nec Legatum tanto tempore, efflagitantibus conscius, virum gravem, aut Senatorem quempiam mittere voluit; maxima ex parte ipse Suevorum conatus frustratus est, complorante Alberto, multitudine hujus negotii tragico modo. Posteaquam ergo Italiae plenique cives, Episcopi, Dynastae conjurarunt, vulturii Romanenses (res ante cum b filio Augusti tentata non processit) alia via dimicant. Fridericus Austriacus proscriptus ab Angusto, pulsus patria, exutus urbibus, vicis, castellis, Neostadii in confinio Austriae, finire circumsidebatur. Is primus haud gravarim, spe recuperandi perdita, socius accessit. Eadem tempestate Conradus Tullolius Frisingensis Episcopus ob limites, uti cum Ottone Regnlo Bojorum, Praefecto praetorio Rhem, discepтabat, in suaque ditione omnes non partis a sacris arcebat, clanculque templis, nemine nisi suis admissis, rem divinam fieri praecipiebat.
units.tr: The princes, knights, and every most greedy man, eager for honours and money, they resolve to stir up against the pontiffs by distributing among them the tithes and ecclesiastical wealth. Their letters show that Gregory wished to test this plan more than that he judged it fair or just, or hoped that it would succeed according to his own mind. Indeed, complaining also to his nuncio about the bishops whom he had there cursed, he nevertheless, with letters kindly given to the same men, calls them his venerable brothers, concealing his devotion. Nor did he, though he was aware of the long-standing demands, wish to send a legate, a grave man or any senator; for the most part he himself frustrated the efforts of the Swabians, while Albert lamented the great tragic turn of this affair. Therefore, after the Italian cities and many citizens, bishops and dynasts conspired, the Roman vultures (a matter previously attempted with the son of Augustus did not proceed) fight by another way. Frederick of Austria, outlawed by Augustus, driven from his homeland, stripped of towns, villages and castles, was besieged at Neustadt on the border of Austria. He, without much hesitation, having lost hope of recovering, joined them first as an ally. At the same time Conrad Tulluel, bishop of Freising, because of boundaries, as he was disputing with Otto, petty king of the Bavarians, prefect of the praetorium of the Rhine, kept all people in his dominion who were not on his side away from the sacraments, and ordered divine service to be celebrated secretly in the churches, with none admitted except his own followers.

units.la: Moguntinus quoque, Archiepiscopus itidem Ottoni ob praereptum sibi Laureacum, vetustissimum Moravorum contubernium, diras atque inferias dixerat. Pontifex Romanus, invitis hisce Episcopis, Moravico atque Frisingensi, atque inconsultis, Ottonem ad se provocantem solvit, fama simul dissipat, Ludovicum patrem Ottonis, Principem in orbe Romano pietate, sapientia, armis, eloquentia, opinione virtute nulli secundum, crudeliter sceleræ Imperatoris Friderici I. ... specie amicitiae, cui familia ... Germaniae Regulos obtinebat, credulus his & ob superiora beneficia operam suam pollicetur; ... tam, quam ... promittit. Ultro arces, urbes, castella, quò conjurati tuto se reciperent, atque summa rerum consultarent, aperit. Wenzeslaum quoque Regem Bojemiae cognatum sui in partes ... Hinc ante ... primas sibi partes conjurationis in Germania sumpsere, sociosque Belum IV. ... Ugrorum affinitate; Haimricum Ducem Poloniae, filium D. Hedwigae, sanguine Ottoni con- ... adscitscunt. Mater hujus ex Bojaria ab Andechs oriunda erat, ille filium suum Elisabeth Haunoldus ... Ottonis desponderat; & Laodomia mater Ottonis Bojema erat. Filium deinde Cumbrosum ... Imperii allicuunt. Ottocarum Regis Bojemiae filium, Friderici Austriaci, qui liberis careret, neptis ... cur, hocque, connubio viam sibi ad Austriam, Styriamque, Bojemiam aperiebant. Homines invicem ... ndo sacramentis religione fidem altringunt. Ipsi potentia Friderici Augusti atque opes ... erant. Praeterea Pontificum dignitatem atque vires molestę ferebant animo, hocnovo au- ... ri eorum divitiis inhabitant. Ubi se pares viribus Imperatoris fore exstitimarunt, Budevisii ... Bojemiae convenire; filium Regis Danorum rebus imponere statuunt a Pontifice Romano ... ut eodem Legatos forces, graves, sapientes mittat, qui hisce Comitis Caesareis interint.
units.tr: The Archbishop of Mainz likewise, for the same reason as Otto, because Laureacum, the most ancient seat of the Moravians, had been snatched from him, had pronounced curses and funeral rites upon him. The Roman Pontiff, against the wishes of these bishops, of Moravia and Freising, and without consulting them, absolves Otto, who was calling him to account, and at the same time spreads a rumour about Ludwig, Otto's father, a prince in the Roman world second to none in piety, wisdom, arms, eloquence and reputation for virtue, who was cruelly... of the Emperor Frederick I... under the appearance of friendship, to which the family... held the petty kings of Germany. Credulous, and because of his earlier favours, he offers his services to them; ... he promises as much as... Of his own accord he opens citadels, towns and castles, where the conspirators might withdraw safely and consult about the highest affairs. They also won over Wenceslaus, King of Bohemia, a kinsman of theirs, to their side... Hence they took for themselves the first place in the conspiracy in Germany, and associated as allies Béla IV... by kinship with the Hungarians; Henry, Duke of Poland, son of Lady Hedwig, of blood related to Otto... Her mother was from Bavaria, descended from the Andechs; he had betrothed his son to Elizabeth Haunold, Otto's ... and Laodomia, Otto's mother, was of Bohemia. Then they lure Cumbrosus into the Empire. Ottokar, son of the King of Bohemia, Frederick of Austria, who was without children, their granddaughter... by this marriage they opened for themselves the way to Austria, Styria and Bohemia. The men bound one another with oaths and the sanction of religion. They themselves were relying on the power and resources of Frederick Augustus... Moreover, they were troubled in spirit by the dignity and power of the pontiffs, and they settled in their wealth. When they believed themselves equal in strength to the Emperor, they resolved to meet at Buda in Bohemia and to appoint the son of the King of Denmark to the government; and that the Roman Pontiff should send to the same place grave, wise and eminent legates, who would take part in this Imperial diet.

units.la: FRIDERICI II. IMPER. AUG. MANDATA
units.tr: Mandates of the Emperor Frederick II, August

units.la: Imperator cum superiori Epistola Legatos, Convētu in Bojaria indicto, ad Wentzeslaum Re- ... proficisci juber, qui illum officii admonant, beneficia à majoribus Imperatoribus in gentem ... collata commemorent. Duces Bojemiae ab avo patruoque Imperatoribus Regio diade- ... mitos esse, quorum tertius sit V Ventzeslaus; spectandam esse audaciam Romanorum Flami- ... nium fallacia seductus, se atque Rempublicam discordiae malis perditum erat: Pontificem ... insidiari nationi orbis reginae. Ideo dare illum operam, ut ejus valentissimas gentes, Bo- ... Tyrones, Venedos, Sclavos, Danos, Cimbros, Ugros, committere quovis queat modo. Cives ... Monachos adversus Mystas, hos in Episcopos ab eodem cocitari. Praesules Pontificibus, ... illis cultu, mitra, pedo, lituo; Pontificio aequari; prophanos, avaritissimum quemque; atque pecuniae maxime
units.tr: With his earlier letter, the Emperor orders legates to set out for Wenceslaus, to go to the assembly summoned in Bavaria. They are to admonish him of his duty and recall the benefits conferred on the nation by the earlier Emperors. The dukes of Bohemia were crowned with the royal diadem by their grandfather and uncle, the Emperors, and the third of them is Wenceslaus V. They are to be warned that the audacity of the Romans must be watched, and that he, seduced by the deceit of the flatterers, has been ruined together with his realm by the evils of discord. The Pontiff plots against the nation, the queen of the world. He therefore takes pains to set against one another its most powerful peoples, the Bohemians, Tyrolese, Wends, Slavs, Danes, Cimbri and Hungarians, by whatever means he can. Monks are stirred up against the laity, and these in turn against the bishops. Prelates are made equal to the Pontiffs in dress, mitre, staff and crozier. The profane are all the most greedy, and above all for money.

units.la: b. Conrado IV. Regae Romanor.

units.la: Anno Christi 1227. Aventi. lib. 7. Annal. Bojor. sol 542. * sc. Germanicae.
units.tr: In the year of Christ 1227. Aventinus, Annals of Bavaria, book 7, p. 542. * That is, German.

units.la: a. sc. Pontificem Rom. Papa per discordiam civilem & bella intestina quaerit Imperium Fracicum sive Germanicae destruere. maxime studiosum, decimis distributis, contra Sacerdotes bene sentientes sollicitari. Quod sint Ro-manenses illi, opera eorum ostendere. Christum mundo pacem dedisse; illos bella civilia propinare, Princes, Regulos, Tetrarchas, eisdem fallis Christis cohortantibus, invicem sævire, & velut membra in gusto capiti suo repugnare, atque divinæ majestati resistere; Gregorium ix. captum Imperii co-nundine, ut solus regnet, omnia perturbare atque commiscere, cuncta tumultu complere, ut sursum sum universa ferantur. Jam pridem eos, qui Babyloniæ, hoc est, Romæ templo Dei incubent, di-vinam affectare, & astutè id dissimulare; solaque Germanicas vires ab his timeri, quas ut spectaculobi paria componant, Vulpeculas illas conari: ut Germania illa victrix terrarum, ejus bellicosissimi populi, Venedi, Sclavi, Ugri, Dani, Teutones, suis viribus, mutuis vulneribus corruant, sunimopere studere. Ita exangues atque defessos prædæ effœminatis illis, libidini atque servituti primarii factis proculdubio obnoxios fore. Aliter non orbem terrarum, neque cunctas gentes conglobat, utstillimus Germaniæ gentibus quicquam officere posse. Omnes homines naturâ proclives ad malia omnia mala exempla ex bonis initiis orta esse. Ubi semel Romanus Sacerdos gladium nactus exneminem licentiæ ejus atque furori finem aut modum statuere ausurum, neque illum cessatum, nec omnes, juxta bonos ac malos, in servitutem redigat. Ac nos tandem fero eventu rerum, nostris edocti sapere cogamur.
units.tr: a. That is, the Roman Pontiff. The Pope, through civil discord and internal wars, seeks to destroy the Frankish or German Empire, and he is most eager to stir up, by distributing tithes, those priests who are well disposed against it. What those Romans are is shown by their works. Christ gave peace to the world; they offer civil wars to it. They urge princes, petty kings and tetrarchs, by the same false Christs, to rage against one another and, like limbs in revolt against their head, to resist the divine majesty. Gregory IX, having seized the Empire as merchandise, so that he alone may reign, throws everything into confusion and disorder, fills all things with tumult, so that all things are carried upwards. For some time now those who sit in the temple of God at Babylon, that is, at Rome, have aspired to divinity and cunningly concealed it. They fear the German forces alone, and the little foxes strive to set them against one another as a spectacle, so that that victorious nation of the lands, its most warlike peoples, the Wends, Slavs, Hungarians, Danes and Teutons, may fall by their own strength and mutual wounds. Thus, exhausted and worn out, they will undoubtedly be made subject as prey to those effeminate men, the chief makers of lust and servitude. Otherwise he does not gather the world's lands or all the nations, so that he could hinder anything for the most noble nations of Germany. All men are by nature prone to every evil, and all evil examples have arisen from good beginnings. Once the Roman priest has got the sword, no one will dare to set an end or limit to his licence and fury, nor will he cease, nor will he reduce all, good and bad alike, to servitude. At last, taught by the harsh outcome of events, we are compelled to be wise.

units.la: Hæcubi dicta sunt à Legatis, Rex Bojemus commutato animo, alioqui Pontificis Maximus natus, quòd Legatum & petentibus non miserat, suspectos habens, cœpta improbat, se in potes-tatem gusti atque Cæsaris fore respondet, atque fœdus novis sacramentis, datis obsidibus, Egræ con-firmatum redintegrandum decernit. Idem cæteri Principes censent. Ortonem Bojum, qui aberdiscordiæ auctorem, contra Rempublicam fecisse, crimine perfidiæ, proditæ Majestatis, populistiani, accersendum esse b statuunt.
units.tr: When these things had been spoken by the legates, the King of Bohemia changed his mind. Born otherwise as a supporter of the Pontiff, he was suspicious because he had not sent legates to those who asked. He disapproves of the undertakings, answers that he will be in the power of the Emperor, and decides that the covenant, confirmed at Eger with new sacraments and with hostages given, is to be renewed. The other princes give the same opinion. They decide that Otto the Bavarian, who had been the author of the discord against the commonwealth, is to be summoned on the charge of treachery, of betrayed majesty, and of stirring up the people.

units.la: a. sc. Principibus ad Comitia Budissina conventuris.
units.tr: a. That is, to the princes about to meet at the Assembly of Bautzen.

units.la: b. sc. in Comitiis Egranis.
units.tr: b. That is, at the Assembly of Eger.

units.la: FRIDERICI II. IMPER. AUG. PRAECEPTUM
units.tr: FREDERICK II, EMPEROR AUGUSTUS, PRECEPT

units.la: De metallifodinis in Comitatu Palatino Rheni.
units.tr: On the metal mines in the Palatinate of the Rhine.

units.la: Fridericus Secundus Dei gratia Romanorum Rex semper-Augustus, & Rex Siciliæ. Dignum est & consentaneum rationi, ut hi, qui ad exaltationem nostram votis fidelibus & intiis præclaris aspirant, à munificentiâ nostrâ ampliora beneficia consequantur. Hac itaque conderatione inducti, universis Imperii fidelibus, tam præsentibus quàm futuris, notum facimus, quinos attendentes sinceram fidem & devotionem, nec non & obsequia, quæ dilectus consanguineus noster Ludovicus Dux Bavariæ Palatinus Comes Reni, Majestati nostræ frequenter exhibuit, & intea poterit exhibere, ex vera scientia & de mera liberalitate nostra donavimus sibi & hæredibus suis in rectum feudum concessimus, omne genus metalli tam in auro & argento, quàm in aliis, quæ in terris patrimonii & feudi sui fuerit repertum, cum omni jure & utilitate exinde proveniente, & nos & Imperium percipere deberemus. Statuimus igitur & auctoritate Regia distinctè præcipimus, nulla unquam persona, alta vel humilis, ecclesiastica vel secularis, contra hanc nostram concessionem venire præsumat; quod qui præsumpserit, offensam nostram & gravem indignationem incurret, pœna temeritatis suæ centum libras auri componat, quarum medietas Cameræ nostræ, altera vero iis injuriam persolvatur. Ad hanc autem nostræ donationis & concessionis memoriam perpetuo legium inde scribi, & sigillo Magnificentiæ nostræ jussimus communiri. Hujus rei testes sunt: Cunradus Ratisponensis Episcopus. Otto Frisingensis Episcopus. Otto Dux a Moraviæ, Palatinus Comes Burgundiæ. Comes Cunradus de b Sofburch. Genehardus Landgravius de Lukenberg. Diepoldus frater ejus. Anshelmus Marescalcus de c Finstingen. Ramungus de Svvabach. Albertus d Lupus. Albertus Rindesmul, & alii quàm plures.
units.tr: Frederick the Second, by the grace of God Roman King, ever-August, and King of Sicily. It is worthy and consistent with reason that those who strive by faithful vows and distinguished deeds toward our exaltation should obtain greater benefits from our munificence. Moved therefore by this consideration, we make known to all the faithful of the Empire, both present and future, that, considering the sincere faith and devotion, and also the services, which our beloved kinsman Louis, Duke of Bavaria, Palatine Count of the Rhine, has frequently shown and will in future be able to show to our Majesty, we have, from certain knowledge and from our pure generosity, given to him and his heirs, and granted in direct fief, every kind of metal, whether gold, silver, or other, that has been or may be found in the lands of his patrimony and fief, with all right and profit arising from it, which we and the Empire ought to receive. We therefore decree and, by royal authority, expressly command that no person, high or low, ecclesiastical or secular, presume to act contrary to this our grant. Whoever presumes to do so shall incur our displeasure and grave indignation, and shall pay as a penalty for his rashness one hundred pounds of gold, of which half shall go to our Treasury and the other half to the one wronged. To preserve the memory of this our donation and grant forever, we have ordered that a charter be written and confirmed with the seal of our Magnificence. The witnesses of this matter are: Conrad, Bishop of Regensburg; Otto, Bishop of Freising; Otto, Duke of Moravia, Palatine Count of Burgundy; Count Conrad of Sofburch; Genehard, Landgrave of Lukenberg; Diepold, his brother; Anshelm, Marshal of Finstingen; Ramung of Schwabach; Albert Lupus; Albert Rindesmul, and many others.

units.la: Ego Cunradus Metensis Episcopus & Spirensis, Imperialis Aulæ Cancellarius, vice Domini Sifridi Moguntinensis Sedis Archiepiscopi & totius Germaniæ Archicancellariæ, recognovi. Acta hæc anno Dominicæ Incarnationis MCCXCIX. Indict. VIII. regnante Domino nostro Friderico Dei gratia Illustrissimo Romanorum Rege semper-Augusto, & Rege Siciliæ; anno Regni ejus in Germania septimo, & in Sicilia vicesimo secundo, feliciter.
units.tr: I, Conrad, Bishop of Metz and of Speyer, Chancellor of the Imperial Court, acting for the Lord Siegfried, Archbishop of the See of Mainz and Archchancellor of all Germany, have recognized this. These acts were done in the year of the Lord's Incarnation 1299, indiction VIII, in the reign of our Lord Frederick, by the grace of God most illustrious Roman King, ever-August, and King of Sicily; in the seventh year of his reign in Germany and the twenty-second in Sicily, happily.

units.la: FRIDERICI II. IMPER. AUG. CONSTITUTIO
units.tr: Constitution of Emperor Frederick II, Ever Augustus

units.la: De Metallifodinarum privilegio Dominis Plauensibus concesso.
units.tr: On the privilege of mining granted to the Lords of Plauen.

units.la: Fridericus II. Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator, semper-Augustus, Hierusalem et Siciliæ Rex, Dilectis ac Nobilibus sibi Heinrico seniori, Regni nostri Advocato, & exceCapitaneo, Domino de Plauen, & Heinrico Juniori, strenuo militi ejus filio salutem in perpetuum.
units.tr: Frederick II, by the grace of God Emperor of the Romans, ever Augustus, King of Jerusalem and Sicily, to his beloved and noble Heinrich the Elder, Advocate and Captain of our kingdom, Lord of Plauen, and to Heinrich the Younger, his valiant knight and son, greeting in perpetuity.

units.la: Consideratā devotione vestrā quam geritis circa Deum, propter quem non tantum laborum & periculorum, verum etiam proprii sanguinis effusione & prodigi mortibus vos indifferenter exposuistis ad profligandum & evacuandum gentilitatis errorem, tum maximè cum circa Ratisbonam civitatem, sanctæ Mariæ & magnis Ecclesiæ inimicos ex campo expulsis & occidistis, ad laudem Dei & sacri Imperii, vestræque stirpis ad honorem, propter quam vestram strenuitatem, multa commenda nobis & Ecclesiæ evenerunt. Comperta igitur fidelitate singulorum & omnium vestrorum progenitorum ex nobilissima prosapia veteranorum Romanorum orundorum, quam in obsequiis nobis & Imperii indefessam invenimus & probatam. Operaeque pretium judicamus vestris expensis & laboribus Imperiali nostra munificentia subvenire. Propterea vobis Heinricis seniori & juniori de Plauen & eorum heredibus facultatem concedimus, & potestatem quaerere & fodere aurum & argentum, aliaque omnia metalla in debeatis & possitis. Et si quæ in præsenti vel in posterum aurifodinæ vel argenti ad cujuscunque generis commoda, vel utilitates in territorio districti Dominationis vestræ inveneritis, hæc vobis & hæredibus cedant cum proventu omnimodo. Nobis necalicui ulli aliquid inde reteneri debere. Insuper indulgentes vobis & hæredibus vestris masculis, ut debeatis & possitis aureos Grossos & Denarios monetare, quæ ab omnibus Christi fidelibus, ut bona moneta tanquam nova accepta debet esse & rara. Donamus etiam oppida Aschk & Selb cum omnibus eorum requisitis, quamdiu per amborum vestram vitam de nostro beneplacito & consensu ea possideatis, & deinceps tempore sui possitis. Et si quando contingat, nos ex hac vita decedere præ omnibus aliis hæredibus nostris oppignoran debent. Ad evidentiam autem & perpetuitatem omnium promissorum præsentem paginam nostri sigilli appensione munitam vobis decernimus indulgendam. Datum ad portam Naoburgensem Carinthia, Anno ab incarnationis Domini 1232. 10. Mai indictione quinta.
units.tr: Having considered your devotion toward God, for whose sake you have exposed yourselves without reserve not only to labours and dangers but even to the shedding of your own blood and to death, in order to crush and root out the error of the heathen; and especially since you drove out of the field and slew the enemies of holy Mary and of the great Church near the city of Regensburg, to the praise of God and of the Holy Empire and to the honour of your own line. On account of this your valour, many good things have come to us and to the Church. Having therefore found the fidelity of each and all of your ancestors, who sprang from the most noble stock of the old Romans, tireless and proven in service to us and to the Empire, we judge it worthwhile to aid your expenses and labours with our imperial generosity. Accordingly we grant to you, Heinrich the Elder and Heinrich the Younger of Plauen, and to your heirs, the faculty and power to seek and dig gold and silver and all other metals wherever you may and can. And if, now or in the future, you find any gold or silver mines, or any sources of profit or advantage of whatever kind, within the territory of your lordship, these shall pass to you and your heirs together with all their yield. Nothing from this shall be reserved to us or to anyone else. Furthermore, we indulge you and your male heirs that you may and can coin gold groschen and pennies, which, as good and new coin, shall be accepted by all faithful of Christ and be rare. We also give the towns of Aschk and Selb with all their revenues, to be held by you for as long as you both live, with our consent and pleasure, and afterward for the time of your heirs. And if it should happen that we depart this life, they shall be pledged to you before all our other heirs. For the evidence and permanence of all these promises, we decree that this present document, secured with the appending of our seal, be granted to you. Given at the Naumburg gate in Carinthia, in the year of the Lord's incarnation 1232, 10 May, fifth indiction.

units.la: Ad mandatum Cæsareæ Majestatis.
units.tr: By command of His Imperial Majesty.

units.la: *Uladislaus Rex Bohemiæ.
units.tr: Vladislaus, King of Bohemia.

units.la: & Albertus de Cefskovitz Archicamerarius Cæs. Majest.
units.tr: And Albert of Cefskovitz, Archchamberlain of His Imperial Majesty.

units.la: HENRICI VII. CÆSARIS RESCRIPTUM
units.tr: THE RESCRIPT OF THE EMPEROR HENRY VII

units.la: Protillis, qui apud Liberas Civitates Imperii Monasteriis vel Collegiis obligati essent, ne à Civitatum magistratibus ad exactionum, quæ aut Imperii nomine, aut Reipublicæ causa, bellive fieri solent, onera præstanda cogantur.
units.tr: Concerning prelates who were bound to monasteries or colleges within the free cities of the Empire, that they should not be compelled by the magistrates of those cities to bear the burdens of the exactions which are usually made either in the name of the Empire, or for the public good, or on account of war.

units.la: HEnricus Dei gratia Romanorum Rex & Semper-Augustus, Officiatis & Procuratoribus, cererisque fidelibus suis in Ulren constitutis, gratiam suam & omne bonum. Mandamus vobis, quatenus monasterium de Vettingen, quod sub nostram protectionem recipimus, auctoritate nostra omnibus defensetis; nec in possessiones seu in homines ejusdem Monasterii exactiones aliquas faciatis. In locis verò, quæ nostræ armentæ Advocatiæ, de quibus nobis servicia fieri consueverunt, volumus quod honestè atque modestè eos tractetis, nec pejoris eos conditionis faciatis temporibus a fundatoris sui fuerunt. Siquidem sub nostra dominatione amplioris eos volumus quæ securitate gaudere. Datum apud Ezelingen, Nonas Junii, Indictione vi. Regni X.
units.tr: Henry, by the grace of God King of the Romans and ever Augustus, to his officials and procurators, and to his other faithful subjects established at Ulm, his grace and every blessing. We command you that you defend the monastery of Vettingen, which we receive under our protection, against all persons with our authority, and that you make no exactions of any kind upon the possessions or the men of the same monastery. But in those places which are our own advocacies, from which services are customarily rendered to us, we wish you to treat them honourably and modestly, and not to make their condition worse than it was in the times of their founder. For we wish them under our lordship to enjoy greater security. Given at Esslingen, on the Nones of June, in the sixth indiction, the tenth year of our reign.

units.la: EJUSDEM CÆSARIS
units.tr: EJUSDEM CÆSARIS

units.la: Aliud rescriptum, eadem ex causa.
units.tr: Another rescript of the same, for the same reason.

units.la: HEnricus Dei gratia Romanorum Rex, & Semper-Augustus, fidelibus suis & Ministro, & versis hominibus Uraniæ gratiam suam & omne bonum. Cum ex conjuncta benevolentia nostrum Ordinem sincerius diligamus, jura & libertates Fratrum ejus volumus inviolabiliter. Mandamus vobis sub pœna gratiæ nostræ districtè præcipientes, quatenus ab hominibus de Vettingen, in valle Uraniæ constitutis, nullam prorsus exactionem, vel precariam requisitionem. Quoniam nolumus ut fiat aliqua ratione, sed volumus ut gaudeant omni libertate, qua ab Ordine & Fratribus Cisterciensis sunt gavisi. Indubitanter sciturus, quod quicunque vestrum insurgente mandatum nostrum præsumpserit in hac parte, in rebus eum pronde & in corpore puniemus, quia dictum Claustrum sub nostram protectionem & Imperii recepimus speciale. Datum apud Hagenovve, vi. Kalend. Mai, Indictione vii. Regni xi.
units.tr: Henry, by the grace of God King of the Romans and ever-Augustus, to his faithful subjects, both the minister and the people of Uri, his grace and every good. Since we love your Order sincerely out of close goodwill, we wish the rights and liberties of its brethren to be kept inviolate. We command you under penalty of our favour, strictly ordering that you impose no exaction whatever, nor any request for forced service, upon the men of Vettingen, settled in the valley of Uri. For we do not wish this to happen in any way, but we wish them to enjoy all the freedom which the Order and the brethren of Cistercium have enjoyed. Let you know without doubt that whoever of you presumes to act against our command in this matter, we shall punish in goods and in person, because we have received the said cloister specially under our protection and that of the Empire. Given at Hagenau, on the sixth day before the Kalends of May, in the seventh indiction, the eleventh year of our reign.

units.la: a. sc. Henrici Comitis de Rapotechtsuiler, qui monasterium Vettingense fundavit.
units.tr: a. That is, of Count Henry of Rapperswil, who founded the monastery of Wettingen.

units.la: HENRICI VII. CÆSARIS DECRETUM
units.tr: THE DECREE OF EMPEROR HENRY VII

units.la: De argentifodinis, & de custodia ferarum, vulgariter VVildban, legitimo Domino suo addicendis.
units.tr: Concerning the silver mines and the guarding of the wild animals, commonly called Wildban, to be assigned to their lawful lord.

units.la: HEINRICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Rex & Semper-Augustus, universis Imperii fidelibus, quibus praesens littera fuerit ostensa, gratiam suam & omnem benevolentiam.
units.tr: HENRY, by the grace of God King of the Romans and ever-Augustus, to all the faithful of the Empire to whom this letter shall be shown, his grace and all goodwill.

units.la: 1. Ut ad nostros successores perveniant firmiter ea, quae coram nobis aguntur, in testimonio commendamus, ne tractu temporis a labili hominum memoria evanescant. Noverint igitur praesentes, & recognoscant futuri, quod dilectus Princeps noster Heinricus Basiliensis Episcopus, in solennia Curia apud Francofurtum, coram nobis & Principibus, ubi praesentes erant et advocatis suis, Hermannus Marchio de Baden, & Egino Comes de Friburg, contendentes de argentifodinis, & custodiis sylvarum per Brigaugeam, quod vulgariter VVildbaun dicitur, obtinuit & evicit privilegium suum, ipsas argentifodinas & custodias sibi & Ecclesiae suae attinere; & ipsum Egin- Comitem de Friburg eisdem ab ipso & Ecclesia sua legitime infeodatum.
units.tr: 1. So that what is done before us may firmly reach our successors, we commend it to record, lest it fade from the fragile memory of men over time. Let those present know, and let those to come recognise, that our beloved Prince Henry, Bishop of Basel, at the solemn court held at Frankfurt, before us and the princes who were present, and with his advocates, Hermann, Margrave of Baden, and Count Egino of Freiburg, who were contending over the silver mines and the guarding of the forests across the Breisgau, which is commonly called Wildbann, obtained and won his privilege: that the silver mines and the guardianships belong to himself and to his Church; and that Count Egino of Freiburg was lawfully enfeoffed with them by him and his Church.

units.la: 2. Nos itaque considerantes ipsius Principis devotionem, & quod sufficienter probaverat praelibata suae Ecclesiae attinere, memoratum Eginonem per suam approbatam dementiam Consilii nostri misimus in possessionem bonorum praescriptorum; & eadem ipsi Comiti redibus suis Regia autoritate confirmamus. Mandantes, & sub interminatione gratiae nostrae firmiter praecipimus, ut nulla sit persona, alta vel humilis, ecclesiastica & mundana, quae antefatum Comitem in memoratis argentifodinis & custodiis ferarum impedire audeat vel gravare: & qui secus egerit, gratia nostra sit exclusus.
units.tr: 2. We therefore, considering the devotion of this same Prince, and that he had sufficiently proved that the aforesaid things belong to his Church, sent the said Count Egino, by our approved clemency and the counsel of our court, into possession of the aforementioned goods; and by royal authority we confirm the same to the Count and his heirs. We command, and under threat of loss of our favour we firmly order, that no person, high or low, ecclesiastical or secular, shall dare to hinder or burden the aforesaid Count in the said silver mines and the guarding of the wild animals; and whoever shall act otherwise shall be excluded from our favour.

units.la: 3. Ad hujus etiam fidei evidentiam praesens privilegium ipsi Comiti, sigillo nostro communitum fecimus assignari. Testes sunt hujusmodi: Siffridus Moguntinensis, Thiretericus Treverensis, Egibertus Halberstatensis, Evigillus Numburgensis, Siffridus Ratisbonensis — Archiepiscopi, Episcopi. Conradus Abbas Sancti Galli. Albertus Saxoniae, Otto Moraviae — Duces. Heinricus de Burgovv, Eberhardus & Otto fratres de Eberstain, Cunradus Burggravius de Nurmberg, Heinricus & Albertus fratres de Neiffen, Comes VVoltframus de Veringen, Heinricus & Hermannus fratres de VValdinberg, Gerlacus de Buttingen, Heinricus de Eberstal, Albertus de Tolvvach, Rudolphus Hagge, Eberhardus Dapifer de VValdpurg, Cunradus Pincerna de VVinterstetin, Eberhardus de Monte — Comites.
units.tr: 3. As further evidence of this faith, we have caused this present privilege, strengthened with our seal, to be assigned to the Count. The witnesses are these: Siegfried of Mainz, Theoderic of Trier, Egbert of Halberstadt, Eberhard of Naumburg, Siegfried of Regensburg, archbishops and bishops; Conrad, Abbot of St. Gall; Albert of Saxony, Otto of Moravia, dukes; Henry of Burgau, Eberhard and Otto, brothers of Eberstein, Conrad, Burgrave of Nuremberg, Henry and Albert, brothers of Neuffen, Count Wolfram of Veringen, Henry and Hermann, brothers of Waldenburg, Gerlach of Büttingen, Henry of Eberstein, Albert of Tollwach, Rudolf Hagge, Eberhard, Steward of Waldburg, Conrad, Cupbearer of Winterstetten, Eberhard of Montfort, counts.

units.la: & alii quam plures. Actum apud Francofurtum, anno Domini MCCXXXIV, quinto Calendarum Martii, indictione septima.
units.tr: And very many others. Done at Frankfurt, in the year of the Lord 1234, on the fifth day before the Kalends of March, in the seventh indiction.

units.la: FRIDERICI II. IMPER. AUG. DECRETVM in Regem Romanorum ab Imperatore deficientem ad Papam Romanum.
units.tr: Decree of Frederick II, Emperor Augustus, against the King of the Romans who revolted from the Emperor to the Roman Pontiff.

units.la: ANNO Domini MCCXXIX. Imperator FRIDERICUS contra HENRICUM filium Regis Romanorum, qui se in Syriam occupato, Regnum Alemaniae sibi occupare tentaverat, citatus Moguntiae coegit: eumque majestatis laesae, sive quod partes Pontificis tueri videretur, publico judicio damnatum, cum duobus libris capi jussit, & apud Marturanum Calabriae oppidum, tenuissimo victu ad mortem usque addixit.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1229, the Emperor Frederick, having cited Henry, son of the King of the Romans, who had tried to seize the kingdom of Germany for himself while Frederick was occupied in Syria, compelled him to appear at Mainz. Henry was condemned in a public trial for treason, whether because he seemed to be upholding the cause of the Pontiff, and was taken away with two books and ordered to be held, and at Martirano, a town in Calabria, was condemned to death by the most meagre diet.

units.la: FRIDERICI II. IMPER. AUG. LEX DE SARRACENIS.
units.tr: The Law of Emperor Frederick II, Augustus, concerning the Saracens.

units.la: SARRACENOS, qui utilem nobis operam adversus hostes nostros praebuerunt, salvos ubique in Imperio & Regnis nostris esse volumus.
units.tr: We wish the Saracens, who have given us useful service against our enemies, to be safe everywhere in our Empire and kingdoms.

units.la: 1. Et quae
units.tr: 1. And what

units.la: 1. Et quia digni sunt habiti Imperiali honore, volumus ut magistratibus per Italiam & Siciliam praefecti quiete & pacifice teneant.
units.tr: 1. And since they have been judged worthy of imperial honour, we wish those set in charge of offices throughout Italy and Sicily to hold them quietly and peaceably.

units.la: 2. Et Christiani, qui se Sarracenis illis opponunt, impune occidantur. Caesarum autem Sarracenorum quaestio, si reus captus non esset, in vicinae regionis populos habeatur, qui aeris summa, ac totidem capitum supplicio mulctabuntur.
units.tr: 2. And Christians who oppose those Saracens may be killed with impunity. But if the slayers of the Saracens are not captured, the inquiry is to be directed against the people of the neighbouring region, who shall be punished by a fine of money and an equal number of executions, one for each head.

units.la: ROBERTI COMITIS ATREBATENSIS A PAPA ET CARDINALIBUS ROMANIS in Imperatorem Electi
units.tr: ROBERT, COUNT OF ARTOIS, ELECTED EMPEROR: FROM THE POPE AND THE ROMAN CARDINALS

units.la: RESPONSUM De depositione FRIDERICI II. Imperatoris injustè per Papam facta, & renunciatione suæ electionis.
units.tr: RESPONSE concerning the unjust deposition of Emperor Frederick II by the Pope, and the renunciation of his election.

units.la: DOMINUS{a} Papa scripsit Regi Francorum, solennes eidem Nuncios destinando, significans eidem, ut juberet epistolam suam coram ipso & toto Baronagio Franciæ solenniter & memoriter legi & intelligi. Cujus summa & tenor talis fuisse perhibetur. Noverit dilectus filius Ecclesiæ spiritualis, Illustris{b} Rex. & totum Francorum Baronagium, nos deliberatione & contractu diligenti omnium{c} Fratrum nostrorum condemnasse, & à culmine Imperiali abjudicasse FREDERICUM dictum Imperatorem, & ROBERTUM Comitem, fratrem Regis Francorum, loco ipsius elegisse tuendum, quem etiam omnibus nisibus Ecclesia non tantum Romana, sed universalis, duxit non segniter adjuvandum, & efficaciter promovendum. Nullo igitur modo tantam sponte oblatam dignitatem apertis brachiis suscipere pigritemini, ad quam opes & operam abundanter effundenius consequendam. Scelera enim prædicti FREDERICI multiplicia, sicut jam novit mundus, eundem irrevocabiliter condemnarunt.
units.tr: The Lord{a} Pope wrote to the King of the Franks, sending solemn envoys to him and instructing him to have his letter read and understood solemnly and carefully before himself and the whole baronage of France. Its substance and tenor are reported to have been as follows. Let the beloved son of the spiritual Church, the illustrious King{b} and the whole baronage of the French know that we, after deliberation and careful agreement of all our brothers{c}, have condemned Frederick, called Emperor, and removed him from the imperial summit, and have chosen in his place to be defended Robert, Count, brother of the King of the French, whom the Church, not only Roman but universal, has resolved to aid without delay and to promote effectively with every effort. Therefore by no means be slow to embrace with open arms so great a dignity freely offered, to obtain which we will pour out our resources and labour abundantly. For the manifold crimes of the aforesaid Frederick, as the world now knows, have condemned him irrevocably.

units.la: Ad quod, inito consilio, circumspecta prudentia Francorum respondit: Quo spiritu vel ausu terrarum Papa tantum Principem, quo non est major, imò nec par inter Christianos, non convicto vel confessum de objectis sibi criminibus, exhaeredavit, & ab apice Imperiali præcipitavit? Qui si meritis exigentibus deponendus esset, non nisi per generale Concilium cassandus judicaretur? De transgressionibus suis non est hostibus suis fides adhibenda, quorum Papa dignoscitur esse capitalis. Nobis nunc infans, imò bonus fuit vicinus, nec quid sinistri vidimus de eo in fidelitate seculari, vel fide Catholica. Scimus autem, quod Domino nostro Jesu Christo fideliter militavit, marinis & bellicis se peregrinis confidenter opponés. Tantum religionis in Papa non invenimus. Imò qui cum debuit promovere & Deo militantem protexisse, eum conatus est abientem confundere, & nequiter supplantare. Volumus nos metipsos in tanta pericula præcipitare, ut ipsum FREDERICUM tam potentem impunitus, quem tot Regna contra nos juvabunt, & causa justa præstabit adminiculum. Quid ad Romanos de prodiga sanguinis nostri effusione, dum modò suæ iræ satisfaceremus? Si eum per nos & devicerint, omnes Principes mundi conculcabit, sumens cornua jactantiæ & superbiam, quoniam FREDERICUM magnum Imperatorem continent. Sed nec in vacuum Papæ le mandaremus suscepisse, licet magis constet hoc ob odium Imperatoris, quàm nostri dilectionem ab Romana derivasse, mittemus Nuncios prudentes ex nobis ad Imperatorem, qui quomodo Catholica sentiat, diligenter inquirant, nos super hoc certificaturos. Et si nil nisi sanum invenerint festandus est? Sin autem, & ipsum, imò etiam ipsum Papam, si malè de Deo sentiunt, vel quorumlibet mortalium usque ad internecionem persequemur. Quæ cum audicrunt Nuncii Papales, recesserunt.
units.tr: To this, after taking counsel, the French answered with circumspect prudence: By what spirit or daring has the Pope disinherited and hurled from the imperial summit a prince than whom there is none greater, indeed not even an equal among Christians, without his being convicted or confessing the crimes charged against him? If he were to be deposed for his deserts, would it not be judged that he could be annulled only by a general council? Faith is not to be given to the transgressions alleged by his enemies, of whom the Pope is known to be the chief. To us he was never hostile, indeed he was a good neighbour, and we have seen nothing amiss in him either in secular fidelity or in the Catholic faith. We know that he has fought faithfully for our Lord Jesus Christ, confidently opposing himself to foreign sea-and-war enemies. In the Pope we find no such religion. Indeed, when he ought to have promoted and protected one fighting for God, he has tried to bring him down as he departs and to supplant him wickedly. Do we wish to throw ourselves into such great dangers, to oppose Frederick, so powerful, with impunity, when so many kingdoms will help against us and a just cause will supply the support? What of the Romans, and of our blood lavishly poured out, provided only we satisfy their anger? If they were to conquer him through us, he will trample all the princes of the world, taking up the horns of boasting and pride, since they hold Frederick, the great Emperor. But we would not have it said that the Pope undertook this in vain, although it is clearer that this arose from hatred of the Emperor than from love of us on the part of Rome. We will send prudent envoys from our own number to the Emperor, who will diligently inquire how he thinks in Catholic matters, and will certify us about this. And if they find nothing but what is sound, is he to be favoured? But if otherwise, and if they find that he thinks ill of God, we will pursue him, and even the Pope himself, and any mortals whatever, to destruction. When the papal envoys heard these things, they withdrew.

units.la: Adierunt igitur Dominum Imperatorem Francorum Nuncii solennes, ipsi mandata, quæ à Domino Papa receperunt, seriatim nunciaturi. Quod cum audisset Dominus Imperator, de immanitate factus respondit, se esse virum Catholicum, Christianum, sanè de omnibus Orthodoxæ fidei sententiam, & addit: Non placeat Domino meo Jesu Christo, ut unquam recedam à vestigiis patrum & antecessorum, sequens vestigia perditorum. Judicet autem Dominus inter me & ipsum, qui nescit per orbem tam nequiter diffamavit. Et tendens manus in cœlum, lacrymans, singultando exclamavit: Deus ultionum Dominus reddat ei retributionem. Deinde ad Nuncios ait: Amici mei & vicini charissimi, verè, quicquid dicat inimicus meus sanguinis nec & honoris subversor, credo sicut alius Christianus; & si bellum mihi indicit, non nisi unum, si me defendam ab insurgentibus in me. Spero enim, quod non nisi innocentium, me potenter liberabit. Novit enim Deus, quod Papa in favorem rebellium, præcipuè Mediolanensium hæreticorum, contra me levat calcaneum, & insurgitiracundus. Sed vobis totus in gratiarum actiones assurgo, quod voluistis ante assensum pronunciationem meam de praesenti causa certificari. Ad haec Nuncii: Nolit Deus, ut unquam asceniam nostrum, ut aliquem Christianum sine manifesta causa impugnemus. Necnon pulsat ambitus, dicimus enim Dominum nostrum Regem Galliae, quem linea Regis sanguinis provexit ad sceptra eorum regenda, excellentiorem esse aliquo Imperatore, quem sola electio provehit voluntatis, cit Domino Comiti ROBERTO fratrem esse tanti Regis. Et his dictis cum dilectione & gaudio imperiali recesserunt. Et sic in hoc proposito conatus Papalis irritus evasit.
units.tr: The solemn envoys therefore approached the lord Emperor of the Franks, to announce in order to him the commands they had received from the lord Pope. When the lord Emperor had heard this, he was greatly moved and replied that he was a Catholic, Christian man, and indeed held the opinion of the orthodox faith on all points, and he added: May it not please my Lord Jesus Christ that I ever depart from the footsteps of the fathers and my predecessors, following the footsteps of the lost. But let the Lord judge between me and him, who knows how wickedly he has defamed me throughout the world. And stretching his hands to heaven, weeping and sobbing, he cried out: May the Lord, the God of vengeances, render him his recompense. Then he said to the envoys: My friends and dearest neighbours, truly, whatever my enemy, the subverter of my blood and honour, may say, I believe as another Christian does; and if he declares war on me, it is only against one, if I defend myself against those who rise up against me. For I hope that God, who is the defender of the innocent, will powerfully set me free. For God knows that the Pope, in favour of the rebels, especially the Milanese heretics, lifts his heel against me and rises up in wrath. But I rise to thank you all, because you wished to be informed of the present cause before I gave my assent and pronounced my judgement. To this the envoys said: God forbid that we should ever make our purpose to attack any Christian without a manifest cause. And the court is also shaken, for we say that our lord King of France, whom the line of royal blood has raised to rule their sceptres, is more excellent than any Emperor, whom the sole election of the will raises up; and that the lord Count Robert is the brother of so great a King. With these words they withdrew with imperial affection and joy. And so in this undertaking the papal attempt turned out fruitless.

units.la: FRIDERICI II. IMP. AUG. CONSTITUTIO
units.tr: CONSTITUTION OF FREDERICK II, EMPEROR AUGUSTUS

units.la: De juribus ac privilegiis Ducatus Austriae; CONFIRMATORIA SENTENTIAE FRIDERI- CI I. Imperatoris super controverso Ducatu Bavariae in Comitus Ra- tisponensibus publicatae.
units.tr: On the rights and privileges of the Duchy of Austria; confirming the sentence of Frederick I, Emperor, on the disputed Duchy of Bavaria, published at the Diet of Regensburg.

units.la: IN NOMINE SANCTAE ET INDIVIDUAE Trinitatis, Amen.
units.tr: IN THE NAME OF THE HOLY AND UNDIVIDED TRINITY, AMEN.

units.la: FRIDERICUS Secundus divina favente Clementia Romanorum Imperator semper Augustus, Hierusalem & Siciliae Rex.
units.tr: Frederick the Second, by the favour of divine clemency Emperor of the Romans, ever Augustus, King of Jerusalem and Sicily.

units.la: Justis Principum nostrorum petitionibus condescendere cogimur: quas nisi favorabiliter audiremus, oba idire quod juste petitur, per injuriam male audiremus. Ea propter per praesens privilegium noverit tam praesens aetas, quam successura posteritas, quod noster excellentissimus Princeps Fridericus Dux Austriae & Styriae, ac Dominus Carniolae, dilectus Princeps ac consanguineus, quoddam privilegium Divi Augusti Imperatoris quondam FRIDERICI, avi nostri felicis memoriae recolendae, Heinrico quondam Duci Austriae proavo suo dudum indultum, nostro culmini presentavit, supplicans attentius, ut ei illud innovare, & omnia, quae continentur in eo, confirmare dignaremur. cujus tenor per omnia talis est.
units.tr: We are compelled to yield to the just petitions of our princes; if we did not hear them favourably, we would be wrongly spoken ill of for refusing what is justly asked. Therefore, by this present privilege, let both the present age and future posterity know that our most excellent prince Frederick, Duke of Austria and Styria and lord of Carniola, our beloved prince and kinsman, presented to our majesty a certain privilege of the divine Emperor Augustus Frederick, our grandfather of happy memory, formerly granted to Henry, former Duke of Austria, his great-grandfather. He asked us earnestly that we would deign to renew it and confirm everything contained in it. Its tenor, in every respect, is as follows.

units.la: IN NOMINE SANCTAE ET INDIVIDUAE Trinitatis, Amen.
units.tr: IN THE NAME OF THE HOLY AND UNDIVIDED TRINITY, AMEN.

units.la: FRIDERICUS divina favente Clementia Romanorum Imperator Semper Augustus.
units.tr: Frederick, by the favour of divine clemency Emperor of the Romans, ever Augustus.

units.la: 1. Quanquam rerum commutatio ex ipsa corporali institutione possit firma consistere, nec ea, quae legitime geruntur, ulla valeant refragatione convelli, ne qua tamen res possit esse dubietas, Imperialis debet intervenire auctoritas.
units.tr: 1. Although a change of possessions, established by bodily institution itself, may stand firm, and what has been lawfully done may not be overturned by any objection, nevertheless, lest any matter remain in doubt, imperial authority ought to intervene.

units.la: 2. Noverit igitur omnium Christi Imperiique nostri fidelium praesens aetas, & futuras, qualiter nos, ejus cooperante gratia, a quo coelitus pax missa est hominibus super terram, generali nostra Curia Ratisponae, in nativitate sanctae Mariae celebrata, in praesentia multorum Principum & Catholicorum Principum, litem & controversiam, quae inter nostrum patruum cum Ducem Austriae, & inter neporem nostrum charissimum Heinricum Ducem Saxoniae, orta exstitit super Ducatu Bavariae, & super Marchia a superiori fluminis parte Anasi, termina hoc modo: quod Dux Austriae resignavit nobis Ducatum Bavariae & dictam Marchiam, quam tenebat. Qua resignatione facta, mox eundem Ducatum Bavariae in beneficium contulimus Duci Austriae. Praedictus vero Dux Saxoniae cessit & renunciavit omni juri & actioni, quas habebat ad Marchiam cum omnibus suis juribus & beneficiis.
units.tr: 2. Let the present age and future generations of all the faithful of Christ and of our Empire know that we, with the cooperating grace of him from whom peace was sent from heaven to men upon earth, at our general diet held at Regensburg, celebrated at the Nativity of St Mary, in the presence of many princes and Catholic princes, settled the dispute and controversy which had arisen between our uncle the Duke of Austria and our most beloved nephew Henry, Duke of Saxony, concerning the Duchy of Bavaria and the march on the upper side of the river Enns, in this manner: the Duke of Austria resigned to us the Duchy of Bavaria and the said march which he held. This resignation made, we at once conferred the same Duchy of Bavaria as a benefice on the Duke of Austria. The aforesaid Duke of Saxony yielded and renounced all right and claim which he had to the march, with all its rights and benefits.

units.la: 3. Ne autem in hoc facto honor & gloria patrui nostri charissimi aliquatenus minuatur, de consilio & judicio Principum, illustri Uladislao Duce Boemiae sententiam pronuntiante quam caeteri Principes approbant, Marchionatum Austriae & dictam Marchiam supra dictum, commutavimus in Ducatum, eundemque Ducatum cum subscriptis juribus, privilegiis & gratiis omnibus liberalitate Caesarea contulimus Heinrico praedicto patruo nostro charissimo, praenobili juxta uxori Theodorae, & liberis eorundem, ob singularem favorem, quo ergo dictum patruum nostrum Heinricum Austriae Ducem, ejus conthoralem praenobilem Theodoram & eorum successores, necnon ergo terram Austriae, quae clypeus & corfacri Romani Imperii noscitur, afficimur, de consilio & assensu Principum Imperii, dictis conjugibus, eorum successoribus in Ducatu, necnon praetactae terrae Austriae subnotatas constitutiones, concessiones, indultas auctoritate Imperiali in jura plena & perpetua redactas, donavimus liberaliter vigore praesentium, & donamus.
units.tr: 3. Lest in this matter the honour and glory of our most beloved uncle be in any way diminished, by the counsel and judgment of the princes, with the illustrious Wladislaus, Duke of Bohemia, pronouncing a sentence which the other princes approve, we have exchanged the margraviate of Austria and the said march above mentioned into a duchy. That same duchy, with all the rights, privileges and graces written below, we have bestowed by imperial liberality on the aforesaid Henry, our most beloved uncle, and on his most noble wife Theodora and their children, out of the singular favour with which we regard our said uncle Henry, Duke of Austria, his most noble consort Theodora and their successors, and also the land of Austria, which is known to be the heart of the Holy Roman Empire. With the counsel and assent of the princes of the Empire, we have freely given, by virtue of these present letters and by imperial authority, to the said spouses and their successors in the duchy, and to the aforesaid land of Austria, the constitutions, concessions and indults noted below, brought into full and perpetual right, and we do give them.

units.la: 3. Primò quidem, quòd Dux Austriae quibusvis subsidiis & servitiis non tenetur debet obnoxius sacro Romano Imperio, nec cuiquam alteri, nisi ea de sui arbitrii libertate fecerit: excepto duntaxat, quòd Imperio servire tenebitur in Hungariam duodecim viris armatis per mensmunum sub expensis propriis, in ejus rei evidentiam, ut Princeps Imperii agnoscatur.
units.tr: 3.
