First, indeed, the Duke of Austria is not bound, nor ought he to be obliged, to the holy Roman Empire or to anyone else for any subsidies or services, unless he has done so of his own free choice; except only that he shall be bound to serve the Empire in Hungary with twelve armed men for one month at his own expense, as evidence of this, so that he is recognized as a prince of the Empire.

units.la: 4. Nec pro conducendis feudis requirere seu accedere debet Imperium extra metas Austriæ, nam in terra Austriæ sibi debétur sua feuda conferri per Imperium & locari. Quod si sibi denegare, ab Imperio requirat, exigat literatoriè trina vice, quo facto, justè poßi debit sua feuda, sine offensa Imperii, ac si ea corporaliter conduxisset.
units.tr: 4. Nor ought the Empire to demand or come beyond the boundaries of Austria in order to confer fiefs; for in the land of Austria his fiefs are owed to him to be conferred and granted by the Empire. But if the Empire denies them when he asks, let him demand them by letter three times; which done, he may justly possess his fiefs without offence to the Empire, as if he had received them in person.

units.la: 5. Dux etiam Austriæ non tenetur aliquam Curiam accedere, edictam per Imperium, seu cumvis alium, nisi ultrò de sua fecerit voluntate.
units.tr: 5. The Duke of Austria is also not bound to attend any court summoned by the Empire or by anyone else, unless he does so of his own accord.

units.la: 6. Imperium quoque nullum feudum habere debet Austriæ in Ducatu. Si verò Princeps aliquis vel alterius status persona, nobilis vel ignobilis, cujuscunque conditionis existat, haberet in dicto Ducatu possessiones ab ipso jure feudali dependentes, has nulli locet seu conferat, nisi eas prius consentiat Duce Austriæ memorato: cujus contrarium si fecerit, eadem feuda ad Ducem Austriæ devoluta liberè sibi extunc jure proprietatis & directi dominii pertinebunt, Principibus Ecclesiasticis & Monasteriis exceptis duntaxat in hoc casu.
units.tr: 6. Nor ought the Empire to hold any fief in the Duchy of Austria. But if any prince, or a person of any other estate, noble or ignoble, of whatever condition, should have possessions in the said duchy dependent by feudal right, he shall let or confer these to no one unless he first obtains the consent of the aforesaid Duke of Austria. If he does the contrary, those same fiefs, fallen back to the Duke of Austria, shall from then on pertain freely to him by right of ownership and direct lordship; except only, in this case, ecclesiastical princes and monasteries.

units.la: 7. Cuncta etiam secularia judicia, bannum sylvestrium & ferinarum, piscinæ & nemora in Ducatu Austriæ, debent jure feudali à Duce Austriæ dependere.
units.tr: 7. Likewise all secular courts, the ban of forests and wild beasts, fishponds and woods in the Duchy of Austria ought to depend on the Duke of Austria by feudal right.

units.la: 8. Etiam debet Dux Austriæ de nullis oppositionibus vel objectis quibuscunque, nec coram Imperio nec aliis quibuslibet, cuiquam respondere, nisi id sua propria & spontanea voluerit facere libertate. Sed si voluerit unum locare, poterit de vasallis seu homologiis, & coram illo secundum terminos præfixos parere potest & debet justitiæ complemento.
units.tr: 8. Also the Duke of Austria ought to answer no objections or charges whatever, neither before the Empire nor before any others, unless he wishes to do so of his own free and spontaneous will. But if he wishes to appoint a deputy, he may do so from among his vassals or homagers, and before that person, according to the fixed terms, he may and must appear to complete justice.

units.la: 9. Insuper potest idem Dux Austriæ, cùm impugnatus fuerit ab aliquo de duello, per unum ineum non in enormitatis macula detentum vices suas prorsus supplere. & * illum ipse eadem seu Princeps vel alius quisquam pro alicujus nota infamiæ non potest impetere, nec debet impugnari.
units.tr: 9. Moreover, the same Duke of Austria, when challenged to a duel by anyone, may fully supply his place through one of his own men who is not held in the stain of infamy; and neither he himself, nor another prince, nor anyone else may attack him on account of any mark of infamy, nor ought he to be impugned.

units.la: 10. Præterea quicquid Dux Austriæ in terris suis seu districtibus seu fecerit vel statuerit, hoc Imperium nec alia potentia modis seu viis quibuscunque debet alio quoquo modo in posterum commutare.
units.tr: 10. Furthermore, whatever the Duke of Austria has done or decreed in his lands or districts, neither the Empire nor any other power ought in future to change in any way or by any means.

units.la: 11. Et si, quod Deus avertat, Dux Austriæ sine hærede filio decesserit, idem Ducatus ad seniorem filium, quam reliquerit, devolvatur.
units.tr: 11. And if, which God forbid, the Duke of Austria should die without a son as heir, the same duchy shall devolve to the eldest son whom he leaves.

units.la: 12. Inter Duces Austriæ qui senior fuerit, dominium habeat dictæ terræ. Ad cujus etiam seniorem filium jure hæreditario deducatur: ita tamen, quod ab ejusdem sanguinis stipite non recedat, nec Ducatus Austriæ ullo unquam tempore divisionis alicujus recipiat sectionem.
units.tr: 12. Among the Dukes of Austria, whoever is the senior shall have the lordship of the said land, and it shall pass by hereditary right to his eldest son; yet so that it does not depart from the stock of the same blood, and the Duchy of Austria at no time receive any division or partition.

units.la: 13. Si quis in dicto Ducatu residens, vel in eo possessiones habens, fecerit contra Ducem Austriæ occultè vel publicè, est dicto Duci in rebus & corpore sine gratia condemnatus.
units.tr: 13. If anyone residing in the said duchy, or holding possessions in it, acts against the Duke of Austria, secretly or openly, he is condemned by that Duke in goods and person, without grace.

units.la: 14. Imperium dict o Duci Austriæ contra omnes suos injuriatores debet auxiliari & succurrere quod justiciam assequatur.
units.tr: 14. The Empire ought to aid and succour the said Duke of Austria against all his injurers, so that he may obtain justice.

units.la: 15. Dux Austriæ Principali indutus veste, supposito pileo Ducali, circundato ferro pinnito, habens in manibus, equo insidens, & insuper more aliorum Principum Imperii, conducere ab Imperio feuda sua debet.
units.tr: 15. The Duke of Austria, clothed in princely garb, with a ducal cap set on his head and encircled with a pinnacled iron band, holding (the insignia) in his hands, seated on horseback, and moreover in the manner of the other princes of the Empire, ought to receive his fiefs from the Empire.

units.la: 16. Dicti Ducis institutionibus & destitutionibus in Ducatu Austriæ suo est parendum.
units.tr: 16. Obedience is to be given to the appointments and removals of the said Duke in the Duchy of Austria.

units.la: 17. Et poterit in terris suis omnibus tenere Judæos, & usurarios publicos, quos vulgus vocat Stefchin, sine Imperii molestia & offensa.
units.tr: 17. And he may hold, in all his lands, Jews and public usurers, whom the common people call Stefchin, without molestation and offence to the Empire.

units.la: 18. Si quibus vis Imperii Curiis publicis Dux Austriæ præsens fuerit, unus de Palatinis Archiducensendus: & nihilo minus in consessu & incessu ad latus dextrum Imperii, post Electores obtineat primum locum.
units.tr: 18. If the Duke of Austria is present at any public diets of the Empire, one of the Palatines shall be designated Archduke; and nevertheless, in seating and in procession, he shall hold the first place at the right side of the Empire, after the Electors.

units.la: 19. Dux Austriæ donandi & deputandi terras suas cuicunque voluerit, habere debet potestatem, si (quod absit) sine hæredibus liberis decederet: nec in hoc per Imperium debet aliquali modo impediri.
units.tr: 19. The Duke of Austria shall have the power to give and assign his lands to whomever he wishes, should he (which God forbid) die without free heirs; nor in this ought he to be impeded in any way by the Empire.

units.la: 20. Præfatus quoque Ducatus Austriæ habere debet omnia & singula jura, privilegia, & indulta, sicut cæteri Principatus Imperii dinoscuntur.
units.tr: 20. The aforesaid Duchy of Austria shall also have all and each of the rights, privileges and grants by which the other principalities of the Empire are known to be endowed.

units.la: 21. Volumus etiam, ut si districtus & ditiones dicti Ducatus ampliati fuerint ex hæreditatibus, donationibus, emptionibus, deputationibus, vel quibusvis aliis devolutionum successionibus, præfata jura, privilegia, & indulta, ad augmentum dicti dominii Austriæ plenariè redundent.
units.tr: 21. We also will that if the districts and domains of the said Duchy are enlarged by inheritances, gifts, purchases, grants, or any other successions by devolution, the aforesaid rights, privileges and grants shall fully flow back to the increase of the said dominion of Austria.

units.la: 22. Et ut hæc nostra Imperialis constitutio omni ævo firma & inconvulsa permaneat, præsentes literas conscribi, & sigilli nostri impressione fecimus insigniri, adhibitis idoneis testibus, quorum nomina hæc sunt: Pilegrinus Patriarcha Aquileiensis. Eberhardus Archiepiscopus Salisburgensis.
units.tr: 22. And so that this our Imperial constitution may remain firm and unshaken for all time, we have had the present letters written out and marked with the impression of our seal, with suitable witnesses present, whose names are these: Pilgrim, Patriarch of Aquileia; Eberhard, Archbishop of Salzburg.

units.la: Ortho Otho Frisingensis Episcopus. Chunradus Bathavensis Episcopus. Eberhardus Babenbergensis Episcopus. Hartmannus Brixinensis Episcopus. ⁂ Hartwvicus Ratisponensis & Tridentinensis Episcopus. Dominus Welffo Dux Spoletæ. Chunradus frater Imperatoris. Fridericus Palatinus Rheni, filius Regis Chunradi. Heinricus Dux Charinthiæ. Marchio Engelbertus de Histria. Marchio Albertus de Stadenn. Marchio ƀ Deopaldus de Vochburg. ᶜ Hermannus Palatinus Comes de Rheno. Otho Comes Palatinus, & Frater ejus Fridericus de Schiernn. & Witelspach. Eberhardus Comes de Sultzbach. Rudolfus Comes de Svveinsheut. ᵈ Albertus Comes Hallensis. Eberhardus Comes de Purchaufen. N. Comes de Putina. N. Comes de Peilstain. & quàm plures &c. signum Domini Friderici Imp. invictissimi.
units.tr: Otto, Bishop of Freising; Conrad, Bishop of Passau; Eberhard, Bishop of Bamberg; Hartmann, Bishop of Brixen; Hartwig, Bishop of Regensburg and Trent; Lord Welf, Duke of Spoleto; Conrad, brother of the Emperor; Frederick, Count Palatine of the Rhine, son of King Conrad; Henry, Duke of Carinthia; Margrave Engelbert of Istria; Margrave Albert of Stade; Margrave Diepold of Vohburg; Hermann, Count Palatine of the Rhine; Otto, Count Palatine, and his brother Frederick of Scheyern and Wittelsbach; Eberhard, Count of Sulzbach; Rudolf, Count of Schweinfurt; Albert, Count of Hallermund; Eberhard, Count of Burghausen; N., Count of Pütten; N., Count of Peilstein; and very many others, etc. Sign of Lord Frederick, the most unconquered Emperor.

units.la: Ego Reynaldus Cancellarius vice Arnoldi Moguntinensis Archiepiscopi & Archicancellarii recognovi, regnante Domino Friderico Romanorum Imperatore Augusto, in Christo. Datum Ratisponæ, quintodecimo Kalend. Octobris, indictione quarta, anno Dominicæ incarnationis M.C. c LVI. feliciter, Amen. Anno regni ejus f quinto, Imperii secundo.
units.tr: I, Reginald, chancellor, acting for Arnold, Archbishop of Mainz and Archchancellor, have acknowledged this, Lord Frederick being reigning Emperor of the Romans, Augustus, in Christ. Given at Regensburg, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of October, in the fourth indiction, in the year of the Lord's Incarnation 1156, happily. Amen. In the fifth year of his reign, the second of his Empire.

units.la: 23. Nos itaque qui fidem & obsequia nostrorum Principum non patimur irremunerata, attendentes fidem puram & devotionem synceram, quam prædictus Princeps ad Majestatis personam & sacrum Imperium habet, pro gratis quoque servitiis, quæ nobis & Imperio exhibuit hactenus fideliter & devote, & quæ exhibere poterit ut inantea gratiora, ipsius supplicationibus benigne favorabiliter inclinati, supra scriptum privilegium D. Augusti avi nostri prædicti huic nostro privilegio verbo ad verbum inserti iussimus, omnia, quæ continentur in eo, de Imperialis præeminentiæ gratia confirmantes. Igitur competit etiam nostro Imperiali Imperio, illustri Principi nostro dilecto Friderico, speciali gratia gratiando.
units.tr: 23. We therefore, who do not allow the faith and services of our Princes to go unrewarded, considering the pure faith and sincere devotion which the aforesaid Prince bears toward the person of Majesty and the holy Empire, and also the pleasing services which he has faithfully and devotedly rendered to us and the Empire until now, and which he may render in future with even greater pleasure, being kindly and favourably inclined to his entreaties, have ordered the aforesaid privilege of our grandfather, the Lord Augustus, to be inserted word for word into this our privilege, confirming by the grace of imperial preeminence all that is contained in it. Hence it is also fitting that our Imperial Empire should grant this by special favour to our illustrious and beloved Prince Frederick.

units.la: 24. Quapropter concedimus ei, & damus eidem illustri Principi Duci Austriæ hæc subscripta ad habendum pro jure plenario, ut nullus suorum feudalium, aut suarum terrarum inhabitantium vel possidentium, nulli alteri aliquid juris obediat, excepto etiam sibi recipiendo nostro prædilecto Frederico Principi Duci Austriæ, ac suas vices supplentibus, sive potestatem habentibus.
units.tr: 24. Wherefore we grant to him, and give to the same illustrious Prince, Duke of Austria, the following, to hold as full right: that none of his vassals, nor any inhabitant or possessor of his lands, shall owe obedience to any other person in any right, except that they shall receive as their lord our most beloved Frederick, Prince and Duke of Austria, and those who supply his place or hold his power.

units.la: 25. Concedimus etiam nostro illustri Principi Duci Austriæ crucem nostri diadematis supra cipali pileo suffcrendam.
units.tr: 25. We also grant to our illustrious Prince, Duke of Austria, that the cross of our diadem be carried above his principal cap.

units.la: 26. Volumus etiam, ut dictus Dux Austriæ omnia sua feudalia sive jura liberaliter suscipiat datitione sine omni.
units.tr: 26. We also will that the said Duke of Austria receive all his feudal holdings and rights freely, by grant, without any charge.

units.la: 27. Igitur jura omnia præscripta illustris Dux Austriæ rite & liberaliter tenere debeat, in-bus suis terris, quas jam possidet, & in futurum possidebit.
units.tr: 27. Therefore the illustrious Duke of Austria ought to hold all the aforesaid rights duly and freely, in his lands which he now possesses and will possess in future.

units.la: 28. Statuimus igitur & Imperiali sancimus edicto, quatenus nullus Rex, nullus Marchio, nullus Princeps, nullus Comes, nullus Prælatus, nulla denique persona alia vel humilis, Ecclesiastica vel Mundana, contra præsentis innovationis & confirmationis nostræ tenorem venire præsumat. Quod qui præsumpserit, indignationem nostri culminis & poenam mille librarum auri se noverit incursurum, quarum medietas Camerae, reliqua vero parti passæ injuriam applicetur.
units.tr: 28. We therefore decree and sanction by Imperial edict that no king, no margrave, no prince, no count, no prelate, and finally no other person, however humble, ecclesiastical or secular, presume to act contrary to the tenor of this our present renewal and confirmation. Whoever presumes to do so shall know that he will incur the indignation of our supreme majesty and a penalty of a thousand pounds of gold, of which half shall go to the Treasury and the rest to the party who has suffered the injury.

units.la: 29. Ad hujus igitur innovationis & confirmationis nostræ futuram memoriam & robur tuò valituram, præsens privilegium fieri, & Bulla Aurea typario nostræ Majestatis impressa, jussimus communiri. Hujus testes sunt: Conradus Frisingensis Episcopus. Henricus Bambergensis Electus. Fridericus filius Illustris Regis Castellæ, [Senator Romani Imperij.] Rudolphus Nobilis Comes de Habspurg. Rodomerus Comes de Helffenstain. Albertus de Nifen, & alii quàm plures, &c.
units.tr: 29. For the future memory and strength of this our renewal and confirmation, which shall hold good for all time, we have ordered this present privilege to be made and secured with the Golden Bull impressed with the stamp of our Majesty. Its witnesses are: Conrad, Bishop of Freising; Henry, Bishop-elect of Bamberg; Frederick, son of the illustrious King of Castile, [Senator of the Roman Empire]; Rudolf, noble Count of Habsburg; Rodemar, Count of Helfenstein; Albert of Niefen; and very many others, etc.

units.la: Signum Domini Friderici Secundi Romanorum Imperatoris invictissimi.
units.tr: Sign of Lord Frederick II, most unconquered Emperor of the Romans.

units.la: Acta sunt hæc anno Dominicæ Incarnationis M. C C. X L V. Mense Junio, tertia indictione imperante Domino nostro Friderico gloriosissimo Romanorum Imperatore semper Augusto, Hierusalem & Siciliæ Rege: Romani Imperii ejus anno vigesimo quinto, Regni Hierusalem vigesimo. moprimo, Regni verò Siciliæ quadragesimo septimo. Datum Veronæ, anno, mense, & indictione prædictis.
units.tr: These things were done in the year of the Lord's Incarnation 1245, in June, in the third indiction, the most glorious Lord Frederick, ever Augustus, Emperor of the Romans, being King of Jerusalem and Sicily; in the twenty-fifth year of his Roman Empire, the twentieth of his Kingdom of Jerusalem, the first (as printed) of his reign, and the forty-seventh of his Kingdom of Sicily. Given at Verona, in the year, month and indiction aforesaid.

units.la: FRIDERICI II. IMPER. AUG. FORMULA
units.tr: FREDERICK II, EMPEROR AUGUSTUS: FORMULA

units.la: De jure ac privilegio Regis in Imperio.
units.tr: On the law and privilege of the King in the Empire.

units.la: FREDERICUS Duci Austriæ & Styriæ, suo dilecto Principi & Comiti Carniolæ, gratiam suam & omne bonum. De fulgore throni Cæsarei, velut ex Sole radij, sic cæteræ prodeunt dignitates, ut primæ lucis integritas minorati luminis non sentiat detrimenta; tantoq; magis Imperiale sceptrum extollitur, tanto cura regiminis à sollicitudinibus relevatur, quanto tribunal ipsius dignioris in circuitu circumspicit a contribules regiones. Hac igitur consideratione commoniti, qui cœlesti providentia Romani Imperij moderamur habenas, solij nostri decus tam veterum dignitatum ornatibus confovemus, quam novis honoribus ampliamus.
units.tr: Frederick to the Duke of Austria and Styria, his beloved Prince and Count of Carniola, greetings and every good. Just as rays proceed from the sun, so the other dignities issue from the brilliance of the imperial throne, and the full light of the first ray suffers no sense of loss from the lessening of the lesser light. The more the imperial sceptre is exalted, the more the burden of government is lightened of its cares, the wider its tribunal looks out over the surrounding regions that share its honour. Mindful of this, we who by heavenly providence hold the reins of the Roman Empire adorn the glory of our throne with the honours of the ancient dignities and enlarge it with new ones.

units.la: 2. Tuis igitur Devotissime Princeps noster, supplicationibus favorabiliter inclinati, nec minus ad exaltationem honoris sacri Imperij nostri respectum habentes, de infrascriptorum Principum nostrorum consilio, videlicet Conradi Ratisponensis Episcopi, † Henrici Wormaciensis Episcopi, Henrici Bambergensis Electi, & O...... * Brixiensis Electi: F..... Abbatis Campidonensis: G.... Abbatis b Cluniacensis: Ottonis Ducis c Moraviæ, &B ..... Ducis Bavariæ;
units.tr: 2. Therefore, our most devoted Prince, we have graciously inclined to your supplications, and, having regard also to the exaltation of the honour of our holy Empire, with the counsel of the Princes, our associates named below, namely Conrad, Bishop of Regensburg; Henry, Bishop of Worms; Henry, Elect of Bamberg; O..., Elect of Brixen; F..., Abbot of Kempten; G..., Abbot of Cluny; Otto, Duke of Moravia; and B..., Duke of Bavaria:

units.la: Ducatus Austriæ & Styriæ cum pertinentiis suis & terminis, quos hactenus habuerunt, ad nomen & honorem Regni transferentes, te hactenus prædictorum Ducatuum Ducem, de potestatis nostræ plenitudine & magnificentia Principali, promovemus in Regem, eisdem libertatibus & immunitatibus & juribus prædictum Regnum tuum præsentis epigrammatis auctoritate dotantes, quæ Regiam decent dignitatem: ut tamen ex honore, quem tibi libenter addicimus, nihil honoris vel juris nostri Diadematis aut Imperij subtrahatur: quin immo sicut hactenus tanquam Dux, Princeps & fidelis noster exteras, sic in posterum Regis decoratus honore, tu & successores tui legitimi, Principes fideles & devoti nobis & successoribus nostris in imperio perpetuò persistatis.
units.tr: transferring the Duchy of Austria and the Duchy of Styria, with their appurtenances and boundaries which they have held hitherto, to the name and honour of a Kingdom, we, from the fullness of our power and princely magnificence, promote you, who until now have been Duke of these Duchies, to the rank of King. By the authority of this present privilege we endow your Kingdom with those liberties, immunities and rights which befit royal dignity; yet so that nothing of the honour or right of our Diadem or Empire is withdrawn from the honour which we gladly confer upon you. Rather, just as hitherto you have remained our foreign Duke, Prince and faithful subject, so in future, adorned with the honour of a King, you and your lawful successors shall remain forever faithful and devoted Princes to us and to our successors in the Empire.

units.la: 3. Nihilque; propterea juri vel honori Imperij in prædictis Regno & terris tuis omninò depereat vel decrescat, quæ hactenus habuit in eisdem, eo specialiter & nominatim expresso, quòd successores tui non per electionem Prælatorum, Ducum, Comitum aut quorumlibet Nobilium eligantur in Regem, sed semper major natu seu senior ex generatione tua, ex te & successoribus tuis legitimè descendentes, in ipso Regno succedant. Nullusq; ex eis coronam aut consecrationem in prædicto Regno tuo de manu * cuiusquam accipiat, sed à nobis & successoribus tantùm in Curia nostra, vel ab his, * innuit Papam. qui speciale mandatum à nobis super hoc habeant, coronationis & consecrationis munus & decus pro tempore consequentur. Alij verò hæredes minores natu non habeant aliud, nisi quod ex Regis gratia poterunt obtinere.
units.tr: 3. Nor shall anything of the right or honour of the Empire be lost or diminished in the aforesaid Kingdom and your lands, whatever it has held in them hitherto, with this especially and expressly stated: that your successors shall not be chosen as King by election of Prelates, Dukes, Counts or any Nobles, but always the eldest or senior by birth of your line, descending lawfully from you and your successors, shall succeed in the Kingdom itself. Let none of them receive the crown or consecration in your aforesaid Kingdom from the hand of anyone, but let them obtain the office and honour of coronation and consecration in due time only from us and our successors at our Court, or from those who hold a special mandate from us in this matter. [Marginal note: he hints at the Pope.] The other younger heirs shall have nothing except what they can obtain by the King's favour.

units.la: 4. Illud etiam juri Regio & honori coniungimus, ut si quis Comes, Nobilis, vel ministerialis, aut Miles de Regno tuo contra te & successores tuos, & terram tuam forsitan excesserit, & pro suo excessu castrum vel munitiones suas ab excedente eo per te vel per nuntios tuos peti contingerit, ipseque negaverit, assignare ipsum, ex jure Regiæ dignitatis per sententiam Curiæ tuæ bannire & forbannire valeas, ipsumque extra legem facere, omni juris suffragio, prout est moris Imperii, carituruin.
units.tr: 4. We further join to the royal right and honour this: that if any Count, Noble, ministerial or Knight from your Kingdom should offend against you and your successors and perhaps against your land, and if, on account of his offence, you or your messengers should demand that he surrender his castle or fortifications, and he refuses, then, by the right of royal dignity and by sentence of your Court, you may proclaim and outlaw him, and make him an outlaw, stripped of every right of legal protection, as is the custom of the Empire.

units.la: 5. Cæterum, ut pacem & justiciam, quæ sunt Regnorum omnium fundamenta, possis in prædicto Regno tuo constantius confovere, præsentium tibi auctoritate concedimus, ut si quis in prædicto regno manifestus extiterit malefactor, tuo videlicet aut Curiæ tuæ justo judicio condemnetur. Cumque aliquis de prædicto Regno renuerit, foverit vel defenderit eundem, & requisitus tuo judicio noluerit assignare, eadem pœna puniri debeat receptator; eademque defensor, qua malefactor ipse, punitur deberet.
units.tr: 5. Moreover, so that you may more steadfastly cherish peace and justice, which are the foundations of all kingdoms, in your aforesaid Kingdom, we grant by the authority of these presents that if anyone in the aforesaid Kingdom shall be a manifest evildoer, he shall be condemned by your just judgment or that of your Court. And when anyone of the aforesaid Kingdom refuses to surrender, shelters or defends such a man, and when required by your judgment he refuses to hand him over, the harbourer shall be punished with the same penalty, and the defender shall be punished with the same penalty as the evildoer himself would have been.

units.la: 6. Ad decus præterea Regni tui, præsentis privilegii auctoritate promittimus, ut de provincia Carniolæ Ducatum facias, immediatè tibi, & per te nobis & successoribus nostris & Imperio respondeat: & ut in Ducatu ipso cognatum tuum, fidelem nostrum, in Ducem valeas promovere, plenam tibi concedimus potestatem.
units.tr: 6. Furthermore, for the honour of your Kingdom, we promise by the authority of this present privilege that you may make the province of Carniola a Duchy, which shall answer directly to you, and through you to us, our successors and the Empire; and, so that in that Duchy you may promote your kinsman, our faithful subject, to the rank of Duke, we grant you full power.

units.la: Ad cujus rei memoriam & robur perpetuò valituram, præsens privilegium fieri, & Bulla nostra aurea, typario nostræ Majestatis impressa, jussimus communiri.
units.tr: In memory of this matter and to be valid forever, we have ordered this present privilege to be made and strengthened by our golden Bull, impressed with the seal of our Majesty.

units.la: FRIDERICI II. IMPER. AVG. DIPLOMA
units.tr: FREDERICK II, EMPEROR AUGUSTUS, DIPLOMA

units.la: De usurpatione Papæ Romani in jurisdictione & auctoritate seculari: & quòd Papa non possit instituere aut deßituere Imperatorem, Reges ac Principes.
units.tr: Concerning the usurpation by the Roman Pope of jurisdiction and authority in secular matters, and that the Pope cannot institute or depose an Emperor, Kings and Princes.

units.la: FRIDERICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator semper-Augustus, Hierusalem & Siciliæ Rex, Universis præsentes literas inspecturis per Regnum Franciæ constitutis, dilectis sibi, salutem, & omne bonum.
units.tr: Frederick, by the grace of God Roman Emperor, ever-August, King of Jerusalem and Sicily, to all who shall inspect these present letters, established in the Kingdom of France, to his beloved ones, greeting and every blessing.

units.la: 1. Cùm per aliquos retroactos Romanæ sedis Antistites, & præsentem, nos & alios Reges, Principes orbis, & Nobiles, Regna, Principatus, honores quos libet, & Jurisdictionem habentes, gravatos merito censeamus, ex eo quod ipsi contra Deum, & Justitiam, posse sibi jurisdictioné & auctoritatem usurpant instituendi & destituendi, seu removendi ab Imperio, Regnis, Principatibus, & honoribus suis Imperatores, Reges, & Principes, seu quoscunq; Magnates, temporalem auctoritatem in eos temporaliter exercendo, absolvendo etiam à sacramentis, quibus Dominis suis vasalli tenentur, contra dominos, excommunicationis tantummodo sententia promulgata.
units.tr: 1. Since we judge that we, and other kings, princes of the world, and nobles, and those who hold kingdoms, principalities, honours of whatever kind, and jurisdiction, have been rightly aggrieved by some of the past and present bishops of the Roman see, in that they, against God and justice, usurp for themselves the jurisdiction and authority to institute, depose, or remove from their empire, kingdoms, principalities and honours, emperors, kings and princes, or any magnates whatever, exercising temporal authority over them in temporal matters, and also absolving vassals from the oaths by which they are bound to their lords, by promulgating against lords a mere sentence of excommunication.

units.la: 2. Quodq; quæstione sive dissensione, inter dominos & vasallos, seu inter duos Nobiles & vicinos invicem contendentes, prout assolet, emergente, prædicti summi Pontifices ad petitionem unius partis tantummodo partes suas temporaliter interponunt, volendo ipsos invitos in se compromittere, vel aliter ad concordiam coërcere, & alligando se fidelibus contra dominos, aut uni de partibus supradictis, quòd non prius pacem cum aliis faciant quàm alligaros sibi ponant in pace, recipiendo similiter promissionem de non faciendo pacem cum dominis à vasallis.
units.tr: 2. Likewise, when a question or dispute arises between lords and vassals, or between two nobles and neighbours contending with one another, as is customary, the aforesaid supreme Pontiffs interpose their temporal authority only at the petition of one party, wishing to bind the parties against their will to themselves, or otherwise to constrain them to concord; and they bind the faithful against their lords, or against one of the aforesaid parties, so that they may not make peace with others until they have placed those bound to them in peace; and likewise they receive a promise from vassals not to make peace with their lords.

units.la: 3. Item in eo quod prædicti summi Pontifices, in præjudicium jurisdictionis, & honoris Regum, & Principum prædictorum, ad petitionem Clericorum, seu Laicorum, cognitionem causarum de rebus temporalibus, possessionibus feodalibus, seu burgensalicis, in Ecclesiastico foro tractandas recipiunt, & committunt.
units.tr: 3. Again, in that the aforesaid supreme Pontiffs, to the prejudice of the jurisdiction and honour of the aforesaid kings and princes, at the petition of clerics or laymen, receive and commit to the ecclesiastical forum causes concerning temporal matters, feudal or burgage possessions, to be tried there.

units.la: 4. Ecce quod nos ad prædictam injuriam documentis evidentibus ostendendam, & ipsam à nobis in eis rationabiliter removendam, Magistrum Petrum de Vinea, magnæ Curiæ nostræ Judicem, & G. de Ocra Clericum, dilectos fideles nostros, ad Ludovicum Illustrem Regem Francorum, carissimum amicum nostrum providimus destinandos, affectuosè rogantes, ac ob tuitionem & conservationem jurium nostrorum, & Imperii, Regum aliorum, & Principum, seu quorumcunque Nobilium, efficaciter requirentes eundem, ut cògregatis coram se Laicis Paribus regni sui, aliisque Nobilibus tanto negotio opportunis, per se cum eis super omnibus prædictis & singulis audiat jura nostra.
units.tr: 4. Behold, to demonstrate this injury by manifest documents and to remove it reasonably from us, we have provided for sending Master Peter de Vinea, judge of our great court, and G. de Ocra, clerk, our beloved faithful servants, to Louis the Illustrious, King of the Franks, our most dear friend; we earnestly ask him, and for the protection and preservation of our rights, of the Empire, and of other kings, princes, or whatever nobles, we effectively request that he, having gathered before himself the lay peers of his kingdom and other nobles suited to so great a matter, hear our rights in all the aforesaid points and each of them, dealing with them himself.

units.la: 5. Cæterùm si ipse prædicta non duxerit assumenda, cùm nos, qui auctore Domino Romani Imperii, Regnorum Hierusalem & Siciliæ moderamur habenas, tam enormem injuriam, & tam infortunem usurpationem diebus nostris tolerare nolimus, Regem eundem justa precum intercessione rogamus, quatenus nobis causam nostram, suam, & aliorum Principum, viriliter prosequentibus se contrarium non opponat; nec de Regno suos aliquos Laicos, seu Clericos, temporaliter nobis opponi permittat; nullumque præsenti summo Pontifici, seu successoribus suis, contra nos, discrimine præsenti durante, in Regno, vel de Regno suo præsidium seu receptaculum tribuat, aut tribui patiatur.
units.tr: 5. Moreover, if he should not think fit to take up the aforesaid matters, since we, who by the Lord's authority govern the reins of the Roman Empire and of the kingdoms of Jerusalem and Sicily, are unwilling to tolerate in our days so enormous an injury and so unjust a usurpation, we ask the same King, by the just intercession of our prayers, that he not oppose us while we vigorously pursue our cause, and that of the other princes; nor permit any of his lay or clerical subjects to be temporally set against us; and that, while the present crisis lasts, he grant or allow to be granted to the present supreme Pontiff, or his successors, against us, no protection or refuge in or from his kingdom.

units.la: 6. Porro si forsitan Rex prædictus unà cum Paribus & Nobilibus Regni sui, prout tantum Regem & Regnum decet, partes suas interponendas viderit in prædictis, summumque Pontificem sive per justitiæ debitum, vel modo quolibet, ad istud induxerit ut velit prædicta gravamina nobis, & aliis Christianis Primatibus inrogata, & id specialiter, quod contra nos nuper in Lugdunensi Concilio statuit, quatenus de facto processit, cum prorsus de jure non valeat, revocare.
units.tr: 6. Furthermore, if perchance the aforesaid King, together with the peers and nobles of his kingdom, as befits a king and kingdom, sees fit to interpose their authority in the aforesaid matters, and induces the supreme Pontiff, either by the due demands of justice or in whatever way, to be willing to revoke the aforesaid grievances inflicted upon us and other Christian princes, and especially that which he lately enacted against us at the Council of Lyons, insofar as it proceeded in fact, since it is wholly without validity in law.

units.la: 7. Nos ob honorem & reverentiam Dei & Redemptoris nostri, nec non ob amorem, quem ad Regem & Regnum Franciæ præcæteris singularem habemus, causam, quæ inter nos, & Summum Pontificem vertitur supradictum, quatenus contingit eandem, in manibus ponimus Regis ejusdem; parati omnia, quæcunque per nos idem Rex de Consilio Parium, Nobiliumque suorum vilis & diligenter auditis nostris & Imperii juribus, Ecclesiæ viderit emendanda, corrigere, & in statum debitum integrè reformare, ac deinde pace per hoc inter nos, & Ecclesiam procedente, & reliquis Longobardorum, prout tenentur & debent, vel ad mandatum nostrum & Imperii redeuntibus, vel prorsus ab Ecclesiæ defensione seclusis; promptos nos offerimus, & paratos, vel prædicto Rege ad defensionem Christianitatis & statum pacificum conservandum in Cismarinis partibus remanente, vel unà cum eo, si hoc melius viderit eligendum, ad Transmarinas partes per nos, aut Conradum Carissimum filium nostrum Romanorum in Regem electum, & Regni Hierosolimitani heredem, omne prospero transfretare, ad hoc nos obligantes specialiter & expressim: quòd vel cum Rege Franciæ sive sine eo terram totam Hierosolimitanam, & quicquid unquam à diebus antiquis Regno Hierosolimitano pertinuit, ad proprietatem & ditionem regni ipsius, & Christianitatis cultum; nostris, Imperii, & regnorum nostrorum viribus, laboribus, & sumptibus curabimus revocare. Nihilominus tamen, si forte (quod absit) discrimen præsentis discordiæ inter nos, Ecclesiam, & Lombardos durare contigerit, prædicto Regi ac omnibus Crucesignatis, cum eo quatenus praesentium negotiorum & temporum qualitas patitur, & tempestas, praesidia nostra, terra mariq;, tam in navibus, quam victualibus, promptis affectibus osserimus per praesentes; superq; omnibus & singulis supradictis, quae praesentium series continet literarum, auctoritatem & mandatum plenum praedictis Magistro Petro de Vinea, & G. de Ocra duximus conferendum, ratum habentes, & firmum, quicquid per eosdem in his pro parte nostri culminis extiterit ordinatum.
units.tr: 7. For the honour and reverence of God and our Redeemer, and also out of the love which we bear especially to the King and kingdom of France above all others, we place the cause that lies between us and the aforesaid supreme Pontiff, so far as it pertains to it, in the hands of the same King; ready to correct and to restore wholly to its due state whatever the same King, with the counsel of his peers and nobles, shall judge to be amended in the Church, after our and the Empire's rights have been heard carefully and diligently; and then, with peace thereby proceeding between us and the Church, and with the remaining Lombards returning, as they are bound and ought, either to our command and that of the Empire, or altogether excluded from the defence of the Church; we offer ourselves ready and prepared, either to remain in the Cismarine parts with the aforesaid King for the defence of Christendom and the keeping of a peaceful state, or, if he thinks it the better course to be chosen, to cross with him over to the Transmarine parts, we ourselves or Conrad, our most dear son, elected King of the Romans and heir of the Kingdom of Jerusalem, crossing prosperously by sea; binding ourselves specially and expressly to this: that, either with the King of France or without him, we will by the strength, labours and expense of our Empire and kingdoms take care to recover the whole land of Jerusalem, and whatever from ancient days has belonged to the Kingdom of Jerusalem, to the ownership and dominion of that kingdom and the worship of Christendom. Nevertheless, if perchance (which God forbid) the peril of the present discord between us, the Church and the Lombards should continue, we offer through these presents, with ready good will, our forces by land and sea, both in ships and in provisions, to the aforesaid King and to all who have taken the cross with him, insofar as the quality and times of present affairs, and the storm, permit; and over all and each of the aforesaid matters contained in the series of these present letters, we have resolved to confer full authority and mandate on the aforesaid Master Peter de Vinea and G. de Ocra, holding ratified and firm whatever shall have been ordained by them on our behalf in these matters.

units.la: Datum Cremonae vicesimo secundo Septembris, quartae indictionis.
units.tr: Given at Cremona, on the twenty-second day of September, in the fourth indiction.

units.la: PROCESSVS IN WILHELMI REGIS RO- MANORUM INAUGURATIONE AQUISGRANENSI OBSERVATUS, ANNO MCCXLIX.
units.tr: The Proceedings Observed at the Inauguration of King William of the Romans at Aachen, in the Year 1249.

units.la: ANno Dominicae Nativitatis MCCXLIX. Wilhelmus Comes Hollandiae, apud villam Wornich in Regem Romanorum a Principibus electus, Aquisgrani ad Kalendas Novembres, in festo Omnium Sanctorum, per duos Episcopos Mindensem & Monasteriensem, benedicendum Archiepiscopo Coloniensi in templo praesentatum; duo alii Episcopi Trajectensis & Leodiensis, in modum Diaconi dalmatica induerunt, quem praefatus Conradus Archiepiscopus cum magna solennitate in Regem Romanorum unxit & coronavit.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord's Nativity 1249, William, Count of Holland, who had been elected King of the Romans by the Princes at the village of Wornich, was presented at Aachen on the Kalends of November, on the feast of All Saints, in the church, to be blessed by the two bishops of Minden and Münster, for the Archbishop of Cologne. Two other bishops, those of Utrecht and Liège, dressed him in a dalmatic in the manner of a deacon. The aforementioned Archbishop Conrad then anointed and crowned him King of the Romans with great solemnity.

units.la: 2. Consecratione autem peracta, idem Archiepiscopus locavit eum in sedem Regni, dicens: Super thronum sedis gloriosae sedeas, & judicium & justitiam in terra facias.
units.tr: 2. After the consecration was completed, the same Archbishop seated him on the throne of the realm, saying: May you sit upon the throne of the glorious seat, and execute judgment and justice on the earth.

units.la: 3. Christianus Archiepiscopus Moguntinus cum oleo sanctificato dexteram ejus foris inunxit, dicens: Consecrare te diguetur omnipotens Deus in Regem Romanorum, qui David per manum Samuelis Prophetae unxit super populum Hebraeorum.
units.tr: 3. Christian, Archbishop of Mainz, anointed his right hand on the outside with holy oil, saying: May almighty God deign to consecrate you King of the Romans, whom he anointed over the people of the Hebrews through the hand of the prophet Samuel, as David was anointed.

units.la: 4. Arnoldus Archiepiscopus Treverorum manus super caput ejus imposuit, dicens: Descendat in te spiritus sapientiae, intelligentiae, consilii, replerisq; spiritu timoris Domini.
units.tr: 4. Arnold, Archbishop of Trier, laid his hands upon his head, saying: May the spirit of wisdom, understanding and counsel descend upon you, and may you be filled with the spirit of the fear of the Lord.

units.la: 5. Ludovicus Comes Palatinus Rheni, Archidapifer Regni globum aureum in manus illius posuit, dicens: Accipe globum sphaericum, ut omnes terrae nationes Romano Imperio subjicias, & Augustus gloriosus appellari valeas.
units.tr: 5. Louis, Count Palatine of the Rhine, Arch-steward of the realm, placed a golden globe in his hands, saying: Receive the spherical globe, so that you may subject all the nations of the earth to the Roman Empire, and may be able to be called glorious Augustus.

units.la: 6. Marchio Brandenburgensis, Camerarius Regis, annulum in manum tradidit, dicens: Accipe signaculum Monarchiae, ut Romanum Imperium in suo vigore conserves, & invicta virtute ab omni Barbarorum incursione defendas.
units.tr: 6. The Margrave of Brandenburg, the King's Chamberlain, handed him a ring upon his hand, saying: Receive the seal of sovereignty, so that you may preserve the Roman Empire in its strength, and defend it with unconquered valour from every incursion of the barbarians.

units.la: 7. Dux Saxoniae, Regis Ensifer, gladium ei dedit, dicens: Accipe sceptrum Regium, ut rebelles severa correptione potenter affligas, omnesq; benevolos in tranquilla pace gubernes.
units.tr: 7. The Duke of Saxony, the King's Sword-bearer, gave him a sword, saying: Receive the royal sceptre, so that you may powerfully crush rebels with stern correction, and govern all who are loyal in peaceful tranquillity.

units.la: 8. Rex autem Bohemiae, Pincerna Imperii, de consensu Archiepiscopi Coloniensis, coronam argenteam capiti Regis imposuit, dicens: Accipe diadema splendidum, ut sis virtuosis actibus adeo coruscus in terra, quatenus mercaris coronam aeternae felicitatis habere in caelis; Amen.
units.tr: 8. The King of Bohemia, Cupbearer of the Empire, with the consent of the Archbishop of Cologne, placed a silver crown upon the King's head, saying: Receive the splendid diadem, so that you may shine upon the earth with virtuous deeds, and so that you may deserve to have the crown of eternal happiness in heaven. Amen.

units.la: 9. Posthaec omnes inferiorum partium Principes & Nobiles obedientiam ei praestiterunt.
units.tr: 9. After this, all the Princes and Nobles of the lower regions paid him their obedience.

units.la: FRIDERICI II. IMPER. AUG. ORDINATIO TESTAMENTARIA.
units.tr: Testamentary Ordinance of Frederick II, Emperor Augustus

units.la: EGo Fridericus in primis relinquo pro anima mea, centiesmille uncias auri pro Terrasancta sanctae Romanae Ecclesiae recuperanda, expendenda & exponenda ad voluntatem filii mei Conradi.
units.tr: I, Frederick, first of all bequeath for my soul one hundred thousand ounces of gold, to be spent and laid out for the recovery of the Holy Land for the holy Roman Church, at the will of my son Conrad.

units.la: 1. Item volo, quod omnia male ablata restituantur.
units.tr: 1. Likewise, I will that everything unjustly taken away be restored.

units.la: 2. Item, omnes captivos de Imperio & Regno relinquo liberos, exceptis proditoribus tantum.
units.tr: 2. Likewise, I bequeath freedom to all captives of the Empire and the Kingdom, with the exception of traitors only.

units.la: 4. Item, relinquo totam terram Ecclesiae liberam, & volo quod jura Ecclesiae restituantur.
units.tr: 4. Likewise, I bequeath the whole land free to the Church, and I will that the rights of the Church be restored.

units.la: 5. Item, meum haeredem relinquo, Conradum in Imperio Romano, & Regno Siciliae.
units.tr: 5. Likewise, I appoint as my heir Conrad, in the Roman Empire and the Kingdom of Sicily.

units.la: 6. Item, relinquo filio meo Henrico Regnum Hierosolymitanum, & decem millia unciarum, secundum voluntatem Conradi filii mei.
units.tr: 6. Likewise, I bequeath to my son Henry the Kingdom of Jerusalem and ten thousand ounces, according to the will of my son Conrad.

units.la: 7. Item, nepoti meo filio scilicet filii mei Henrici, relinquo Ducatum Austriae, & decem millia unciarum auri.
units.tr: 7. Likewise, to my grandson, namely the son of my son Henry, I bequeath the Duchy of Austria and ten thousand ounces of gold.

units.la: 8. Item, Manfredum filium meum relinquo Ballivum Conradi in Imperium, a Papia & citra, & Regno Siciliae, usque ad LXX annuos, excepto quando Conradus erit praesens.
units.tr: 8. Likewise, I bequeath my son Manfred as bailiff for Conrad in the Empire on this side of Pavia, and in the Kingdom of Sicily, for seventy years at most, except when Conrad is present.

units.la: 9. Item, sepulturam meam eligo apud Panormum, ubi jacuit Rex Wilhelmus ..........
units.tr: 9. Likewise, I choose my burial place at Palermo, where King William lies ..........

units.la: ALPHONSI IMP. AUG. RESCRIPTUM
units.tr: The Rescript of the Emperor Alfonso Augustus

units.la: Anno Christi 1253.
units.tr: In the year of Christ 1253.

units.la: DE OFFICIO BONI REGIS.
units.tr: CONCERNING THE DUTY OF A GOOD KING.

units.la: ALPHONSUS Dei gratia Electus Romanorum Rex, & Rex Castellæ, Legionis, Galleciæ, Toleti, Murciæ, Cordubæ & Jehenni, Henrico Illustri Regi Anglorum S. Cùm audissemus de moribus tuis, condoluimus in spiritu benignitatis & discretionis. Ideo hortamur te amicè, ut exemplo bonorum Regum ac Principum, quorum titulus ab antiquo talis est: Eris agnus domesticus & suis commilitonibus, & leo externus & rebellibus; talia sequaris, necnon amplius tuorum oppressor, & alienorum receptor & alimentator. Vale.
units.tr: ALFONSO, by the grace of God elected King of the Romans and King of Castile, Leon, Galicia, Toledo, Murcia, Cordoba and Jaén, to Henry the Illustrious, King of the English, greeting. Since we have heard of your conduct, we have grieved for you in a spirit of kindness and discretion. We therefore urge you in friendly fashion to follow the example of good kings and princes, whose motto has long been: You shall be a gentle lamb to your fellow soldiers, and a lion to rebels abroad; and moreover, do not be an oppressor of your own people, but a receiver and sustainer of foreigners. Farewell.

units.la: RICHARDI IMP. AUG. CONSTITUTIO
units.tr: The Constitution of the Emperor Richard Augustus

units.la: Ne bona ad Ecclesiam devoluta à consuetis tributis eximantur: & de aliis capitulis.
units.tr: That goods fallen to the Church are not exempted from the customary taxes; and concerning other chapters.

units.la: RICHARDUS Dei gratia Romanorum Rex Semper-Augustus, Consulibus & Civibus de N. &c.
units.tr: RICHARD, by the grace of God King of the Romans, ever Augustus, to the Consuls and Citizens of N., etc.

units.la: 1. Specialiter duximus indulgendum, ne aliquis civium filiam vel neptem sive consanguineam in uxorem alieni tradere per nos absq; suo pleno consensu aliquatenus compellatur.
units.tr: 1. We have especially resolved to grant that no citizen's daughter, granddaughter or kinswoman be compelled in any way by us to be given in marriage to another man without her full consent.

units.la: 2. Insuper quod nullus civium per nos vel per aliquē alium nostro nomine pro aliqua pecunia extorquenda singulariter ab ipso aliquatenus capiatur.
units.tr: 2. Furthermore, that no citizen be singled out and seized in any way by us, or by anyone else in our name, to extort money from him.

units.la: 3. Ad hæc statuimus & mandamus, ut omnia bona & prædia, quæ hactenus cum civibus precariam Imperio persolvebant, quomodocunq; ad loca religiosorum vel personas alias Ecclesiasticas vel mundanas prædicta bona devolvi & transferri contingat, bona ipsa ad solvendam precariam, sicut antè, nihilominus teneantur.
units.tr: 3. In addition, we establish and command that all goods and estates which hitherto paid the precarious tax to the Empire together with the citizens, however it may come about that those same goods are transferred and passed over to religious houses or to other persons, whether ecclesiastical or secular, those same goods shall nonetheless remain bound to pay the precarious tax, as before.

units.la: Datum Moguntiæ V III. die Septembris, Indict. xv. anno Domini MCCLVII. Regni verò nostri anno primo.
units.tr: Given at Mainz, on the 5th day of September, in the 15th indiction, in the year of the Lord 1257, and in the first year of our reign.

units.la: RICHARDI IMPER. AUG. EDICTUM
units.tr: Edict of Richard, Emperor Augustus

units.la: DE VIARVM CVSTODIA ET SECVRITATE.
units.tr: CONCERNING THE GUARDING AND SAFETY OF THE ROADS.

units.la: BREVE Domini Regis, eo tamen absente, emanavit ad omnes Duces, Comites & Præfectos, in quorum Ducatibus, Comitatibus & Ballivis solebant viatoribus imminere pericula, ut omnes passus periculosos, tam in viis, concavis, & boscis, & haijs, quàm aliis pacis Regiæ perturbationibus faciant videri, & in continenti aut per Dominos locorum aut per semetipsos emendari.
units.tr: The King's writ, though the King himself was absent, was issued to all the Dukes, Counts and Governors in whose duchies, counties and bailiwicks travellers were wont to be threatened with dangers, directing that all dangerous passes, both on the roads, in hollow ways and woods and hedged places, and in other disturbances of the king's peace, be made known, and be put right at once, either by the lords of the places or by themselves.

units.la: RICHARDI IMPER. AUG. EDICTUM
units.tr: RICHARD, EMPEROR AUGUSTUS: EDICT

units.la: Quo Civitas Imperialis Tigurina ab iniqua proscriptione eximitur, & Imperio asseritur.
units.tr: In which the Imperial City of Zurich is freed from an unjust outlawry and secured to the Empire.

units.la: RICHARDUS Dei gratia Romanorum Rex Semper-Augustus, universis Romani Imperii fidelibus gratiam suam & omne bonum. Sane fideli relatione pervenit ad nostræ Serenitatis audi-tum, quod CONRADINUS, olim CONRADI Regis filius, qui se Ducem Sueviæ nomine, ea non contentus injuria, quòd in vanum sibi gloriam alienam usurpat, insuper & cives nostros Tuccenses, in nostro & Imperii gremio speciali collocatos, necad Ducatum eundem, sed ad Imperium, prout stabilivit antiquitas, & modernitas adprobavit, immediatè spectantes, tanquam subesse memorato Ducatui, proscriptionis de facto (cùm nullo penitus jure posset) sententiam promulgavit. Nos cautelam eisdem civibus (ne aliquid in simplicium oculis eos infamiæ nubilum decoloret, prædictam proscriptionis sententiam, utpote omni robore vacuam, authoritate Regia, ex plenitudine potestatis nostræ denunciamus omnino carere viribus, & decernimus esse nullam. Datæ Hagenoa, x x. die Novembris, Indict. v. anno Domini MCCLXII. Regni nostri v I.
units.tr: RICHARD, by the grace of God King of the Romans, ever Augustus, to all the faithful of the Roman Empire, his favour and every blessing. Indeed, by trustworthy report it has come to the hearing of our Serenity that CONRAD, formerly son of King Conrad, who calls himself Duke of Swabia, is not content with this wrong, that he vainly usurps another's glory; moreover, he has pronounced, de facto (though he could by no right do so), a sentence of outlawry against our citizens of Zurich, who are placed in a special way in our bosom and that of the Empire, and who belong immediately to the Empire, not to that Duchy, as antiquity established and modern practice has approved, as though they were subject to the said Duchy. To secure these citizens, lest anything cloud their reputation with the eyes of simple people as infamy, we, by royal authority and from the fullness of our power, declare the aforesaid sentence of outlawry, as utterly void of force, to be without any strength whatever, and we decree it to be null. Given at Hagenau, on the 20th day of November, indiction 5, in the year of the Lord 1262, in the sixth year of our reign.

units.la: RICHARDI IMPER. AUG. RESCRIPTUM
units.tr: Rescript of Richard, Emperor Augustus

units.la: Anno Christi 1264.
units.tr: In the year of Christ 1264.

units.la: AD DIFFIDATORES REGIS ANGLIAE.
units.tr: TO THE DEFIANTS OF THE KING OF ENGLAND.

units.la: RICHARDUS Dei gratia Romanorum Rex, Semper Augustus, & EADVVARDUS Illustris Regis Angliæ primogenitus, cæteriq; Barones omnes & Nobiles, prædicto Regi Angliæ constanter sincere sinceræ fidei & devotionis operibus adhærentes, Simoni de Montefort, Gilberto de Clara, cæterisq; universis & singulis perfidiæ suæ complicibus.
units.tr: RICHARD, by the grace of God King of the Romans, ever Augustus, and EDWARD, firstborn son of the Illustrious King of England, and all the other barons and nobles, adhering constantly and sincerely to the king of England by the works of a sincere faith and devotion, to Simon de Montfort, Gilbert de Clare, and all the rest, each and every one, accomplices of your treachery.

units.la: 1. Ex literis vestris, quas Illustri Regi Angliæ, fratri, patri, & Domino nostro charissimo transmisistis, accepimus nos diffidatos à vobis, quamvis hujusmodi verbalis diffidatio satisfuit ante nobis realiter vestra hostili in rerum nostrarum incendiis, & bonorum nostrorum depopulationibus, persequutione jam probata. Nos igitur vos scire volumus, vos à nobis universis & singulis, tanquam hostes publicos, ab hostibus diffidatos. Qui deinceps personarum vestrarum & rerum dispendiis, ubicunq; nobis ad hoc facultas affuerit, totis viribus insistemus.
units.tr: 1. From your letters, which you sent to the Illustrious King of England, our brother, father and dearest lord, we have learned that you have defied us. Although such a verbal defiance was in fact already superseded by your hostile persecution, now proven by the burning of our property and the plundering of our goods. We therefore want you to know that you are, by us all and each of us, declared public enemies, defied as enemies. Henceforth we shall press on with all our strength, wherever the opportunity arises for us, to the loss of your persons and property.

units.la: 2. De hoc autem, quod falsò nobis imponitis, quòd nec fidele nec bonum consilium Regi Domino vestro damus, nequaquam verum dicitis. Et si vos, Domine Simon de Montefort, vel Gilberte de Clara, velitis hoc idem in Curia Domini Regis asserere, parati sumus secure veniendi ad dictam Curiam procurare conductum, & nostræ super hoc innocentiæ veritatem, & vestrum, sicut perfidorum proditorum, mendacium declarare per alium nobilitate & genere vobis parem. Omnes autem nos contenti sumus prædictorum Dominorum sigillis, videlicet Romanorum Regis, & Domini EADVVARDI. Datum apud Lewes, 12. die Maij, anno Domini 1264.
units.tr: 2. As for what you falsely charge us with, that we give neither faithful nor good counsel to the King, your lord, you are by no means telling the truth. And if you, Lord Simon de Montfort, or you, Gilbert de Clare, wish to assert the same thing in the court of the Lord King, we are ready to secure a safe-conduct for you to come to the said court, and to make the truth of our innocence and the lie of yours, as of faithless traitors, clear through another man equal to you in nobility and birth. Moreover, we are all content with the seals of the aforesaid lords, namely of the King of the Romans and of Lord Edward. Given at Lewes, 12 May, in the year of the Lord 1264.

units.la: CONRADI V. REGIS RO- MANORUM, &c. EDICTUM
units.tr: EDICT OF CONRAD V, KING OF THE ROMANS, etc.

units.la: De Injuriis sibi per Pontifices Romanos illatis.
units.tr: On the injuries inflicted on him by the Roman Pontiffs.

units.la: CONRADUS * Secundus Dei gratia Jerusalem & Siciliæ Rex, ac Dux Svveviæ universis sacri Principibus Imperii.
units.tr: CONRAD the Second, by the grace of God King of Jerusalem and Sicily, and Duke of Swabia, to all the holy Princes of the Empire.

units.la: 1. Ex habundantia cordis os loquitur, & injuriæ nobis illatæ violentia referat hostium labiorum, quam nequivimus nullatenus patientiæ silentio præterire; salva tamen in omnibus Ecclesiæ Catholicæ, quam culto sacro & debita reverentia toto corde & corpore veneramur, quod ad nostram cautelam ulterius insidias, versutias, astus, fallusq; altius formidantes coram Deo, qui corda scrutatur omnium, coram vobis & Christianis publicè protestantes.
units.tr: 1. Out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks, and the violence of the injury done to us forces words from hostile lips, which we could in no way pass over in the silence of patience. Yet, saving in all things the Catholic Church, which we venerate with holy worship and due reverence with our whole heart and body, we publicly protest, before God, who searches the hearts of all, and before you and all Christians, that for our own safety we fear further snares, wiles, tricks and deceits.

units.la: 2. Cum enim magnificus Rex Conradus, divæ memoriæ pater noster, testamento solemniter condito, quodam tempore mortis suæ, nos tenellum infantulum in cunabulis vagientem, nondum nutricis uberibus ablactatum, in manibus sanctæ matris Ecclesiæ reliquisset, sperans quòd nos benigné suscipe-ret, & in brachiis caritatis tractaret suscepturn, & tractatum favorabiliter honoribus proveret. Sed audire, qualiter ille Summus Pontifex, qui erat dictus Innocentius, nocuit innocenti-um repente plus quàm decuerit Papam, ut ardétibus desideriis æstuabat, quod à patre nostro in paternum manserat, & pro nobis pacificè tenebatur, hereditarium regnum nostrum, quod dudum antiqui progenitores nostri propriis affectum sanguinibus cum multis quæsivere laboribus, quæsitum diutius, & possessum variis decoraverunt ornatibus, & diversis decoribus ornaverunt, invasit personabiliter cum exercitu numeroso, & sub prætextu licito, quod se nostrum in eo bajulum prædebat, totum suo dominio vindicavit confestim. verumtamen apprehensa possessione prævium intentionis nephandæ propositum manifestans, & dicti regni tamquam in ejus Regem in se præcisè ferens potestatem, paulatim nomen ibidem delere nostrum, extinguere fidem nostram, & jura Regis suffocare perpetuò satagebat: adeò quod de nobis non sinebat ibi fieri mentionem: & nostras munificè distribuere cœpit in suos consanguineos & nepotes, velut qui corrigias partitur amplas eorum alienum. Ecce qualem in nobis, proh dolor, in nobis exercuit pietatem: Ecce tutelæ nostræ tutelæ decenter officio satisfecit. O sæva patris acerbitas, quæ filium sine fraude filium suis curis expositum sine cura postposuit, qui filium innoxium, sed potius obnoxium ... ionis pœna perpetua condemnavit.
units.tr: 2. For when the magnificent King Conrad, our father of divine memory, had solemnly made his testament at a certain time of his death, he left us, a tender little infant crying in the cradle, not yet weaned from the nurse's breast, in the hands of holy mother Church. He hoped that she would receive us kindly, treat us in the arms of charity, and, once she had received us, would favourably provide for us with honours. But hear how that Supreme Pontiff, who was called Innocent, harmed the innocent suddenly, more than a Pope ought. Burning with eager desires, he violently seized, with a numerous army and under a plausible pretext, namely that he claimed to be our bailiff in it, our hereditary kingdom, which had passed from our father to his son and was held peacefully for us. Our ancient forebears had acquired it for their own blood with many labours, had long held it and adorned it with various ornaments and decorations, and at once he claimed the whole of it for his own dominion. Having taken possession, and revealing the prior purpose of his wicked intention, and claiming for himself the power over the kingdom as its king, he laboured gradually to blot out our name there, to extinguish our faith, and to suppress the rights of the King for ever, so that mention of us was not allowed there. He began to distribute our possessions generously to his kinsmen and nephews, like one who divides wide straps of another's leather. Behold what kindness, alas, he showed toward us! Behold how fittingly he discharged the duty of our guardianship! O cruel bitterness of a father, who set aside without care a son entrusted to his cares without fault, who condemned the innocent son, but rather one liable to ... to perpetual punishment.

units.la: 3. Postmodùm verò cum ille patruus noster Manfredus Tarentinus Princeps, qui forte fide bona nobis à principio laborabat, sufferre diutius rantam nequiciam nequivisset, potérer resumsit denuo causam nostram, & sub specie fidelitatis nostræ & sub nostro titulo bajulatus, post multos belli ... post dnos conflictus, post altercationes innumeras, ipsum regnum non propter eorum injuriam directorum ab Ecclesia manibus violenter eripuit, & illud aliquamdiu sub fide nostra reservavit. Quitandem succedentibus prosperis, quæ frequenter hominum animos solent ad insolentias alterare oblitus fuit sanguinis, oblitus Domini naturalis, fide (sed si fidem habuerat) in perfidiam permutata recipi ocavit ad se negocium dicti regni. Mentitus est regnicolis mortem nostram, & sophisticans in eos Dominum, Pseudoregem se fecit, ibi nobis ex hujusmodi fraudulentia supplantatis. Et ibi fuit error pejor priore. Nam graviorem se fecit in eo nobis adversitas præterita reditura. Oh dolor, oh neptai, oh miseria pupillorum, quibus inde prius offensio oritur, unde defensio sperabatur! O cæca cupido dominii temporalis, quà sacra Pontificis, & consanguinei lenitas ad iniquam fallaciam seducuntur!
units.tr: 3. Afterwards, however, when that uncle of ours, Manfred, Prince of Taranto, who perhaps at first had laboured for us in good faith, could no longer endure such wickedness, he took up our cause again. Under the appearance of our loyalty and under our title of bailiwick, after many wars ... after many conflicts and countless disputes, he violently snatched the kingdom itself from the hands of the Church, not on account of the injury of those who had been directed there, and kept it for some time under our faith. But at length, with success following, which often alters men's minds toward insolence, he forgot his blood and forgot his natural lord, and changing faith (if indeed he had any faith) into perfidy, he began to take the affair of the said kingdom to himself. He lied to the subjects of the kingdom about our death, and deceiving them with the pretence of a lord, he made himself a pseudo-king, we having been supplanted there by such fraud. And there was an error worse than the former, for the past adversity was to return to us with greater weight. Oh grief, oh pity, oh misery of the orphans, from whom offence arises where defence was hoped for! O blind desire for temporal dominion, by which the holy gentleness of a Pontiff and of a kinsman is seduced into wicked deceit!

units.la: Papæ fallacia & fraudulentia propter dominium temporale.
units.tr: The deceit and fraud of the Pope on account of temporal dominion.

units.la: 4. Excessu prædicto taliter ab eodem Manfredo temerè perpetrato, licet bonæ memoriæ Dominus minus Alexander, qui jam in sede Apostolica praesidebat, contra illum graviter indignatus, non quod à nobis subtraxerat, sed quod ab eis extorserat regnum nostrum, in ejus confusionem vehementer tendere videbatur. Unde ad nos super habendo tractatu venerabilem direxit Episcopum Verulansem: nihilominus tamen eodem praesente nobiscum, ad suggestionem forte suorum fratrum degenerantium contrariam voluntatem, per nuncios & litteras Reges & Principes alios ad ejusdemni nostri commercium similiter invitabat, aut quia non erat datum à Deo desuper aut praedestinatum à fatis, ut per eos nancisceremur gratias & honores.
units.tr: 4. With the aforesaid excess so rashly committed by the same Manfred, the late lord Alexander, who then presided in the apostolic see, was gravely angered against him. It was not that he had withdrawn the kingdom from us, but that he had extorted it from them, and he seemed strongly inclined to bring about his confusion. Therefore he sent to us the venerable Bishop of Veroli to discuss the matter. Nevertheless, while the same man was still with us, at the perhaps degenerate suggestion of his brothers, he invited kings and other princes, by messengers and letters, to a similar dealing with us, or perhaps because it was not given from above by God, nor predestined by the fates, that through them we should obtain grace and honours.

units.la: 5. Quod quidem apparet & pet effectum operum patuit subsequenter in Domino U[?] qui nobis exstitit inurbanus, ad Pontificatus officium elevato. Nam dum inter eum & ipsum [?]pem de pace diutius ageretur, ventumque foret ad punctum finaliter, quo firmanda concordia [?]batur, pro facto secundum ipsius formam, idem Apostolicus aequus pater ad jus nostrum ipsi [?]do & ipsius heredibus concedebat, & etiam cofirmabat, utroque stipulabatur eidem, quod contra regni defensionem sibi juxta posse suum Ecclesia non deesset: ut ob id ligata gemmina [?]delium bajulorum nostrorum, qua nos ad ejusdem regni solium resurgere non possemus. Ha[?] non sufficiebat eisdem bajulis pupillum exheredasse solummodo, nisi conjuran-tunt invicem, [?] perpetuo deprimerent nos heredem! Cum autem tractatus ipse, sicut Domino placuit, cadert [?]plenus, & dictus Apostolicus in excidium Principis exarderet, non personam nostram, cui regn[?]tionabiliter debebant, quae ad illius regimen magis accommoda, magis apta, magisque sufficie[?]tillet, unde sopita quievisset pace tranquilla, populus Christianus gavisus extitisset; at velut [?]venit mittere pacem, sed gladium declararetur in scandalis, ex quibus effusio sanguinis sequer[?] hominem extraneum & de regno praedicto penitus alienum, Karolum scilicet, in nostrum prap[?]cium, ad nostrum impediendum negocium invocavit ipsum consiliis & auxiliis contra illum.
units.tr: 5. This indeed appeared, and was afterwards made plain by the effect of their deeds, in the Lord U[?], who proved unfriendly to us once he was raised to the office of the Pontificate. For while peace between him and [?] was being negotiated at length, and the matter came to the point at which concord was to be confirmed, the same apostolic and fair father granted and also confirmed to himself and his heirs our right to the kingdom, on the terms stipulated that the Church would not fail him in the defence of the kingdom, as far as he was able. Thus the gem was bound ... of our faithful bailiffs, so that we could not rise again to the throne of that kingdom. Was it not enough for those bailiffs to have disinherited the ward alone, unless they conspired together to press down the heir for ever? But when that agreement, as it pleased the Lord, fell through, and the said apostolic man blazed up for the ruin of the Prince, he did not regard our person, to whom they ought to have been..., who would have been more fit and more suited to govern that kingdom, by whose rule the people might have rested in quiet peace and the Christian people rejoiced. But as one who did not come to send peace, but a sword, he was declared to be in scandals, from which the shedding of blood would follow. He called in a stranger and wholly alien to the said kingdom, namely Charles, to our prejudice and to the hindrance of our business, and summoned him against us with counsel and aid.

units.la: 6. Post cujus felicem obitum ille successor ejus sanctissimus pater noster Clemens non dementiam, sed inclementiam potius operatus in nobis, constituit in regno praedicto nostrum Carolium ante Regem, qui demum per omne nephas regnum ipsum obtinuit, ut nobis incognitus [?]exstitit. Sed audite pro Deo invidiam per Deum & homines detestandam. Non Sarracenos Lucas, contra quos Dominus Papa crucem sumendam fecerat praedicari, & in quorum excidium gener[?]ductae fuerant & adauctae, salvos illaesos servavit, & Christianos miseros non solum exhaustos[?] occidit innumeros, & afflixit mille generibus tormentorum. Aperite oculos & videte, qualiter [?]cie recti mundum decipiunt & claudunt Presbyteri. Videte, si eis interim in ipso regno sit cre[?]Heu heu quantis injuriis, quantis fraudibus, quantisque doloribus hereditas nostra converta[?] nos, & regnum nostrum transiit ad indebitum possessorem!
units.tr: 6. After his happy death, that successor of his, our most holy father Clement, acting not with clemency but rather with cruelty toward us, set up our Charles, unknown to us, as king in the aforesaid kingdom. He at last obtained that kingdom by every kind of wickedness. But hear, for God's sake, the envy that is to be detested by God and men! He did not spare the Saracens, against whom the lord Pope had caused the cross to be preached, and for whose destruction they had been led forth and increased; but he killed countless wretched Christians, not only exhausting them, but afflicting them with a thousand kinds of torment. Open your eyes and see how the elders deceive the world and shut it in by the appearance of righteousness. See whether in that kingdom there is any ... Alas, alas, by how many injuries, how many frauds and how many sorrows has our inheritance been turned, and our kingdom passed to an unlawful possessor!

units.la: 7. Postquam autem in ipsum Manfredum irruit ira Dei propter commissum in nos peccatum, ut firmiter opinamur; fuitque per ipsum Karolum superatus & etiam intereemptus, regno perdito [?]& sibi cum sua persona perdita culpa fui: dum nos inter saepem Imperii lateremus, quasi jacentes[?] militer attoniti & abscondite sub obscuro, factis seu dictis neminem offendentes, tanquam pup[?] vere desperatus & ab omnibus inhonorus, idem Pontifex generalis timatus est ad instar sohcis[?]soris, ubi nos in Germania viventes invenit, ferens abhominabilem vitam nostram, & verens[?]altius aliquo modo levaremus, velut qui quaerit manopilum & sioponodum, ut habeat nocendi[?]teriam, & occasionem inveniat malignandi: pro eo quod nostris in litteris regni nostri Sicil[?]scribebatur, intendebat (ut audivimus, licet non credamus) contra nos puerum juvenem in[?] lem de pharetra sagittam emittere, & excommunicationis sententiam fulminare, non reputan[?]satis, quod contra Deum & omnem justitiam ablatum fuerit nobis regnum illud Siciliae, nisi [?]ter tolleremur a terra. Ha Deus, quomodo sic universi Pontifices in nostri juris injuriam juravere[?] Ha Deus, si hoc in virido, quid in arido fiet nobis? Si hoc in tanta pueritia passi sumus, quid [?]antiquitate praestolamur?
units.tr: 7. But after the wrath of God rushed upon that same Manfred on account of the sin committed against us, as we firmly believe, and he was overcome and also killed by that Charles, and the kingdom was lost to him, with his own person lost through his guilt, we lay hidden within the hedge of the Empire, like those lying stunned in battle and concealed in darkness, offending no one by deed or word, as one despaired of and dishonoured by all. That same Pontiff, the general ... of the sickle-bearer, found us living in Germany, bearing our abominable life, and fearing lest we should in any way raise ourselves higher. Like one who seeks a weapon and a ..., so that he may have an instrument of harm and find an occasion of malice, because in our letters it was written concerning the kingdom of Sicily, he intended (as we have heard, though we do not believe it) to shoot a young boy against us with an arrow from his quiver and to thunder forth the sentence of excommunication. He did not think it enough that the kingdom of Sicily had been taken from us against God and all justice, unless we were also removed from the earth. Ah God, how did all the Pontiffs swear so to the injury of our right! Ah God, if this is done in green wood, what will be done in dry? If we have suffered this in such boyhood, what do we await in old age?

units.la: 8. Adhuc etiam idem Pater a persecutionum instantia non desistens, sed omnem viam [?]dum excogitans, quibus nos posset perpetuo conculcare; si dici verum liceret, ad illicita n[?]& falcem mittens in nostram messem, praefatum Karolum per Italiam universam Romanum [?]rium Imperii statuit in nostram injuriam manifestam, ut commodius vires nostras reprimeret, [?]cessum nostrum ad ipsum regnum facilius impediret. Sed ad id in potestate deficit auctoritas[?] in auctoritate potestas inane pro certo redditur nomen & officium ingratum. Quid [?]mali fecimus, o sancta mater Ecclesia, quod nostrum devotum filium, olim pupillum tuae [?]commissum per tuos Rectores sic asperè novercaris? In quo umquam te offendimus, [?]rande Pater, quod ita conversus in vitricum multimodè nos persequeris, & injustè forte vas[?] tibi reputas & gravamen injuriamque, quod vivimus super terram? Cum, sciat Deus, nos alia ne[?]mus.
units.tr: 8. Still, the same Father, not ceasing his persecution and devising every means by which he could trample us down forever, sent (if it is lawful to say so) even his sickle into our harvest. He set up the aforesaid Charles throughout all Italy as Roman vicar of the Empire, to our manifest injury, so that he might more conveniently check our forces and more easily hinder our return to the kingdom itself. But in this way authority falls short of power, and power is left without authority: the name and office become empty and thankless. What evil have we done, O holy mother Church, that you so harshly play the stepmother to your devoted son, once a ward committed to your care by your Rectors? In what have we ever offended you, O great Father, that you have turned into a stepfather and pursue us in so many ways, and perhaps wrongly count it an injury and a grievance that we live upon the earth? God knows that we desire nothing else.

units.la: 9. Denique cum vivere nequiremus ulterius contra tot molestias & pressuras, & ignorar[?] quid facere deberemus, ille decorus Deus, qui non reliquit in se sperantes, ecce suam aperi[?] viam, sed in misericordia: quia nostri fideles tam de Imperio quam de Regno, zelo eximiae fidei[?] accensi tot & tantas injurias in nobis sustinere ulterius nequeuntes, in nostrum adjutorium unanimiter[?]ter surrexerunt, exponentes pro nobis non solum bona, sed animas & personas, & nos ad recupe[?] nem nostrorum jurium magnifice suscitarunt. Qui apertis thesauris suis pretiosa nobis munera ob[?] lerunt, aurum sicut Regi magno pro stipendio gentis nostrae nobis affluentiam monstrantes. Nunc cognito quod erat omnino necessarium, munivimus & armavimus justitiam causæ nostræ, ut illud magnificum genus nostrum, quod jam longis & antiquis temporibus imperavit, nostra non degeneraret in persona, & injuriose taliter ipsum pelsundari non contingat, sed alta potentia nostræ dominationis, si Deus annuerit, nostris temporibus relevetur: non ut adversus ipsum Pontificem generalem, contrarium aliquid cogitemus intendere, quem patrem nostrum reputamus & Dominum, (& utinam esset nos filium & devotum relatione debita recognoscere ut deberet) sed in eundem Karolum, inimicum nostrum nostrorumque, jurium detentorem, & contra eum volumus omnino mactialibus schadulis ledere pro nostra justitia, & de nostris juribus in gladiis disputare. Deus autem respiciens è cœlo felicitatem fovet, abhominetur superbiam, & ferens de sancto throno suo sententiam judicet æquitatem.
units.tr: 9. At last, since we could no longer endure so many troubles and pressures and did not know what we ought to do, that noble God, who has not forsaken those who hope in him, has opened his way, see, but in mercy. For our faithful subjects, both of the Empire and of the Kingdom, kindled with the zeal of outstanding loyalty and unable any longer to bear so many great injuries to us, rose up unanimously to our aid, risking for us not only their goods but their souls and persons, and magnificently raised us up to recover our rights. Opening their treasuries, they offered us precious gifts, showing us gold as to a great king, as pay for our people. Now, having recognized what was altogether necessary, we have fortified and armed the justice of our cause, so that that magnificent family of ours, which has ruled from long and ancient times, should not degenerate in our person, nor should it happen that it be injuriously overthrown in this way; rather, by the high power of our dominion, God willing, it shall be raised up in our times. We do not intend to act against the Pope himself, whom we regard as our father and lord (and would that he would acknowledge us, as he ought, as a son and a devoted one, with due regard). Rather, against that Charles, our enemy and the enemy of our people, the holder of our rights, we wish altogether to harm him with warlike manifestos for our justice, and to dispute about our rights with the sword. But God, looking down from heaven, cherishes felicity, abhors pride, and, pronouncing sentence from his holy throne, judges with equity.

units.la: 10. Vestram igitur dilectionem precamur attente, quantum possumus, & hortamur, quatenus super hiis causæ nostræ, quam vobis nudam claramque describimus, cognita veritate penes conscientias vestras habeatis nostram innocentiam excusatam, & ad falsam suggestionem forsitan aliquorum de nobis contractum non credatis, imo nobis in hac justissima causa date celeris auxilium, consilium, & favorem: eundem Summum Pontificem per vestras litteras speciales exorando, ut nobis in jure nostro faveat, & erga nos se gerens benigne rancorem mitigando intuitu vestro temperet motus suos, & conceptam erga nos iram suæ indignationis dignetur vobis intercedentibus exarmare.
units.tr: 10. We therefore earnestly beseech and exhort your love, as much as we can, that concerning these matters of our cause, which we set out to you plainly and clearly, you hold the truth in your consciences and regard our innocence as vindicated. Do not believe that anything wrongly held against us has arisen from the false suggestion, perhaps, of some persons. Rather, give us speedy help, counsel, and favor in this most just cause, by earnestly entreating the same Supreme Pontiff through your special letters, that he may favor us in our right, and, dealing kindly with us, may temper his movements by allaying his rancor out of regard for you, and may deign, through your intercession, to disarm the anger he has conceived against us in his indignation.

units.la: RUDOLPHI I. IMP. AUG. EDICTUM
units.tr: EDICT OF THE EMPEROR RUDOLPH I, AUGUSTUS
