units.la: De diplomatibus & instrumentis lingua Germanica concipiendis.
units.tr: On diplomas and instruments to be drawn up in the German language.

units.la: OMNIA mandata, edicta, privilegia, pacta dotalia, contractus, & id genus alia scripta & instrumenta, in Theutonica lingua, & non, ut antea, in Latina, concipiantur.
units.tr: All mandates, edicts, privileges, marriage-settlement agreements, contracts, and other writings and instruments of this kind shall be drawn up in the Teutonic language, and not, as before, in Latin.

units.la: RUDOLPHI I. IMPER. AUG. RESPONSUM
units.tr: RUDOLPH I, EMPEROR OF THE AUGUSTAN EMPIRE: HIS RESPONSE

units.la: De Coronatione Imperii Romana, quod sine ea electus a Principibus verus Imperator & sit & nomi- nari debeat; redditum Principibus, qui eum ad instantiam Romani Pontificis sæpe admo- nebant, quatenus pro corona Imperii Romam proficisceretur.
units.tr: On the Coronation of the Roman Empire: that without it an emperor elected by the princes is and ought to be called a true emperor; the response given to the princes who often urged him, at the instance of the Roman Pontiff, to set out for Rome to receive the crown of the Empire.

units.la: MULTOS Alemannorum Reges Italia consumpsit: non ibo Romam. Rex sum, IMPERATOR sum, nec minus pro utilitate Reipublicæ hoc facturum confido, quam si Romæ suissem coronatus.
units.tr: Italy has consumed many kings of the Germans: I will not go to Rome. I am king, I am emperor, and I am confident that I will act no less for the good of the Commonwealth in this than if I had been crowned at Rome.

units.la: RUDOLPHI I. IMPER. AUG. DECRETUM
units.tr: RUDOLPH I, EMPEROR AND AUGUSTUS, DECREE

units.la: De jure eligendi Imperatorem inter Regem Bohemiæ & Ducem Bava- riæ controversio.
units.tr: On the dispute between the King of Bohemia and the Duke of Bavaria concerning the right to elect the Emperor.

units.la: RUDOLFUS Dei gratia Romanorum Rex Semper Augustus, universis præsentia inspecturis in perpetuum declaramus, quod præsidentibus nobis Curiæ apud Augustam Idibus Maii solemniter celebratæ, & conlatentis ibidem in præsentia nostra Illustrium Principum Ottockar Bohemiæ Nuncis, & Henrici Ducis Bavariæ Procuratoribus, subortaque inter eos quæstione possessione juris eligendi Romanum Regem per Procuratores dicti Ducis Henrici & Ludovicum Comitem Palatinum Rheni Ducem Bavariæ, filium nostrum charissimum, fuit ratione Ducatus Bavariæ hoc eis competere ex antiquo. Idemque nostrum Ludovicus, cunctisque Principibus, Prælatis, Baronibus, Militibus, & universo populo, qui eidem debant, exitit publice protestatus, quod prædictus Dux Henricus fraterque ipsius, olim electi Richardi Romanorum Regis, nostri prædecessoris, unà cum ipso præsentialiter Principibus Coëlectoribus interfuit, & in eum uterque direxit legaliter votum suum, eumque Romanum Regem unà cum aliis Comprincipibus jus in hoc habentibus eligendo.
units.tr: Rudolph, by the grace of God Roman King and Ever Augustus, to all who shall see the present document, we declare for all time that, while we presided at the Diet solemnly held at Augsburg on the Ides of May, and while there were present in our presence the envoys of the Illustrious Prince Ottokar of Bohemia and the proxies of Duke Henry of Bavaria, a question arose between them concerning the possession of the right to elect the Roman King. Our beloved son Ludwig, Count Palatine of the Rhine and Duke of Bavaria, claimed through the proxies of the said Duke Henry that this right belonged to them by ancient custom by reason of the Duchy of Bavaria. Our son Ludwig likewise publicly protested, in the presence of all the Princes, Prelates, Barons, Knights and the whole people who owed him allegiance, that the aforesaid Duke Henry and his brother, formerly the elected Roman King Richard, our predecessor, were personally present with him at the election of the Electoral Princes, and that each of them had lawfully directed his vote in favour of him, electing him as Roman King together with the other co-princes who had the right in this matter.

units.la: 2. Deinde vero electionis tempore apud Franchaniurte de nobis ab omnibus Principibus jus eligendi habentibus concorditer celebratæ, per Nuncios & Procuratores ejusdem Ducis Henrici, & Henricum Præpositum Oetingensem & Fridericum Rectorem Ecclesiæ de Landshuet, ipsius propter impedimenta legitima legitime excusantes, præsente Venerabili Berchtoldo Babenbergensi Episcopo, Procuratore prædicti Regis Bohemiæ, & contradicente quidem ipsis Procuratoribus contradictione à Principibus Electoribus omnibus tam Ecclesiasticis quam Secularibus, non in dictum Ludovicum Comitem Palatinum Rheni nostrum filium, unà cum aliis Principibus qui in nos direxerat sua vota, prout jam dicti Procuratores in mandatis receperant, concorditer compromissum, qui committum hujusmodi in se recipies, suo & dicti Henrici Ducis fratris sui, ac c. ac omnium aliorum Principum jus in electione habentium auctoritate & nomine, in Romanum Regem solempniter nos elegit, vocibus eorundem fratrum Ducum Bavariæ, Comitum Palatinorum Rheni, ratione Ducatus pro una in Septem Principum jus in electione Regis Romani habentium mero computatis; prout etiam in prædicta Curia Augustensi vivæ nostræ vocis eloquio, utriusque rum, in præsentia Nunciorum prefati Regis Bohemiæ, videlicet Venerabili Wernhardo Seckoviensi Episcopo, Magistro Henrico Præposito Werdensi, N. Commendatore Domus Theutonicæ in Austriam, & Wolfingo Magistro Hospitali S. Johannis de Maurperge, a omnium ibidem præsentium Principum, Prælatorum ac Baronum recognovimus, & recognoscimus manifeste. In hujus testimonium, & perennem memoriam prædictorum, præsentes eis literas donavimus, nostro Regali sigillo, necnon subscriptorum testium sigillis munitas. Qui sunt Hartmannus Augustensis Hiltprandus Eistetensis, Episcopus. Henricus Tridentinus. N. de Sancto Gallo, Abbates. N. de Augea Rudolfus Cancellarius noster. Ex Laicis vero filius noster Ludovicus Comes Palatinus Rheni, Dux Bavariæ. Philippus Dux Karinthiæ. Meinhardus Comes Tyrolensis. Fridericus Burgravius de Nurnberg. Heinricus Marchio de Burgaue. Ulricus de Helfenstain, Ludovicus de Oeungen Albertus & Burchardus de Hochenberg Henricus de Furstenberg, Comites. Tybaldus de Pirreto & Ludovicus de Honburg Henricus & Berchtoldus de Niffen Albertus de Pruckberch Hermannus de Hæginberch Volkmarus de Chemnaten, Barones. & Marquartus filius suus Winhardus de Roibach Henricus de Prisingen,
units.tr: 2. Afterwards, indeed, at the time of our election, which was unanimously held by all the Princes who have the right of election at Frankfurt, the proxies and envoys of the same Duke Henry, namely Henry, Provost of Oetting, and Frederick, Rector of the Church of Landshut, lawfully excused themselves on account of their lawful hindrances; in the presence of the venerable Berthold, Bishop of Bamberg, proxy of the aforesaid King of Bohemia, and with the proxies themselves indeed objecting, the Electoral Princes, both ecclesiastical and secular, all together and in agreement, not on the said Count Palatine Ludwig, our son, together with the other Princes who had directed their votes to us, as the aforesaid proxies had received in their instructions, but by compromise, agreed to elect us solemnly as Roman King, the one who undertook such a commission on himself, by his own authority and that of his brother Duke Henry and of all the other Princes who have the right in the election, the votes of the brothers, the Dukes of Bavaria and Counts Palatine of the Rhine, being counted as one vote for the Duchy among the seven Princes who have the right in the election of the Roman King. Likewise, in the aforesaid Diet at Augsburg, by the living utterance of our own voice, in the presence of the envoys of the said King of Bohemia, namely the venerable Wernhard, Bishop of Seckau, Master Henry, Provost of Werden, N., Commander of the German House in Austria, and Wolfing, Master of the Hospital of St. John at Maurberg, we have acknowledged and do clearly acknowledge this before all the Princes, Prelates and Barons present there. In testimony and everlasting memory of these matters, we have given them the present letters, fortified with our royal seal and also with the seals of the witnesses subscribed below. These are: Hartmann, Bishop of Augsburg; Hiltprand, Bishop of Eichstätt; Henry, Abbot of Trent; N., Abbot of St. Gall; N., Abbot of Reichenau; Rudolph, our Chancellor. Among the laymen, our son Ludwig, Count Palatine of the Rhine, Duke of Bavaria; Philip, Duke of Carinthia; Meinhard, Count of Tyrol; Frederick, Burgrave of Nuremberg; Henry, Margrave of Burgau; Ulrich of Helfenstein, Ludwig of Oettingen, Albert and Burchard of Hohenberg, Henry of Fürstenberg, Counts; Tybald of Pirrat and Ludwig of Hohenburg, Henry and Berthold of Nissen, Albert of Pruckberg, Hermann of Hegenberg, Volkmar of Kemnaten, Barons; and Marquard, his son, Winhard of Roibach, Henry of Prisingen,

units.la: & alii quamplures. Actum & datum Augustæ, Anno Dominicæ Incarnationis millesimo ducentesimo septuagesimo quinto; Regni vero nostri anno secundo.
units.tr: and many others. Done and given at Augsburg, in the year of the Lord's Incarnation one thousand two hundred and seventy-five, and in the second year of our reign.

units.la: PRINCIPUM ELECTO- RUM S. ROMANI IMPERII DIPLOMA
units.tr: THE DIPLOMA OF THE PRINCES ELECTORS OF THE HOLY ROMAN EMPIRE

units.la: Quo ratificantur donationes Pontifici Romano factæ à RODULPHO IMPERATORE.
units.tr: By which the donations made to the Roman Pontiff by King Rudolph are ratified.

units.la: LUDOVICUS Dei gratia Comes Palatinus Rheni, Dux Bavariæ; JOANNES & ADALBERTUS Duces Saxoniæ; OTTO Marchio Brandeburgensis, universis præsentem paginam inspecturis salutem in Auctore salutis.
units.tr: Ludwig, by the grace of God Count Palatine of the Rhine, Duke of Bavaria; John and Albert, Dukes of Saxony; Otto, Margrave of Brandenburg, to all who shall inspect this present page, greeting in the Author of salvation.

units.la: 1. Complectens abolim sibi Romana mater Ecclesia, quadam quasi germana charitatis maniam, illam eo terrenæ dignitatis nomine decoravit, quod est super omne nomen temporalium præsidentium super terram, plantans in ea Principes tanquam arbores præelectas, & ringatu gratia singulari, illud eis dedit incrementum tam mirandæ potentiæ, ut ipsius Ecclesiæ auxilio suffulti, velut germen electum per ipsorum electionem illum, qui frena Romani Imperii geminarent. Hic est illud luminare minus in firmamento militantis Ecclesiæ per luminare majus Christi Vicarium illustratum. Hic est, qui materialem gladium ad ipsius nutum excutere & converti, ut ejus præsidio pastorum pastor adjutus, oves sibi creditas spirituali gladio protegendo munitat, temporali refrænet & corrigat ad vindictam malefactorum, laudem vero bonorum.
units.tr: 1. The Roman mother Church, having once, out of a kind of sisterly love, honoured the Empire with the title of earthly dignity, which is above every name of temporal rulers on earth, and planting princes in it as chosen trees, has by singular grace given them such wonderful growth of power that, supported by the help of the Church itself, they, as a chosen shoot, should through their election govern the reins of the Roman Empire. This is that lesser light in the firmament of the militant Church, illumined by the greater light, Christ's Vicar. This is he who, at her nod, is to draw the material sword and turn it, so that the shepherd of shepherds, aided by his protection, may fortify the sheep entrusted to him by protecting them with the spiritual sword, and may restrain and correct with the temporal sword, for the punishment of evildoers and the praise of the good.

units.la: 2. Ut igitur omnis materia dissensionis & scandali, seu etiâ rancoris occasio inter ipsam Ecclesiam & Imperium auferantur, & duo gladii in domo Domini constituti debito fœdere copulati ipsos exerceant, in utilem reformationem regiminis universi, & nos in actu voluntatis & operis animamur filii devotionis & pacis, quitam Ecclesiam quàm Imperium confovere tenemur: per Dominum nostrum RODULPHUM Dei gratia Romanorum Regem semper Augustum patrem & Dominum nostrum Nicolao Papæ Tertio, ejusdemque successoribus, & ipsi Romanæ Ecclesiæ. recognitum, confirmatum, ratificatum, innovatum, denuò donatum, declaratum sive concessum, aut ratificatum, & actum seu factum est per privilegia vel quæcumque alia scripta quorumcunque renorum per recognitionibus, ratificationibus, approbationibus, innovationibus, confirmationibus, donationibus, concessionibus, & factis seu gestis tam aliorum Imperatorum & Regum Romanorū, Prædecessorum Regis ejusdem, quàm ipsius Regis super fidelitate, obedientia, honorificentia per Romanos Imperatores & Reges Romanis Pontificibus & ipsi Ecclesiæ impedendis, ac possessionibus, honoribus & juribus ejusdem Ecclesiæ, & nominatim super totam terram, quæ est à Radicofano usque Ceperarum, Marchia Anconitana, Ducatu Spoletano, terra Comitissæ Mathildis, Civitate Ravennæ, & Æmilia, Bobio, Cesena, Foropopuli, Forolivii, Faventia, Imola, Bononia, Ferraria, Comacio, Adrianis, atque Gabello, Arimino, Urbino, Monteferetro, territorio Balnensi, Comitatu Bretinorum, Exarchatu Ravennæ, Pentapoli, Massa Trabaria cum adjacentibus terris suis, & omnibus aliis ad prædictam Ecclesiam pertinentibus, cum omnibus finibus, territoriis, atque insulis in terra marique, provinciis, civitatibus, territoriis ad prædicta quoquo modo spectantibus, nec non super civitate Romana, & regno Siciliæ, cum omnibus ad eam spectantibus tam citra Pharum quàm ultra, Corsica quoque atque Sardinia, & ceteris terris ac juribus ad ipsam Ecclesiam pertinentibus, nos nomine Principatus in omnibus & per omnia approbamus & ratificamus, ac iisdem omnibus & singulis & quibuscumque aliis super iisdem per eundem Regem quoquo modo factis, & in posterum faciendis voluntatem nostram, assensum, atq; consensum, unanimiter atque concorditer exhibemus & promittimus, quòd contra promissa vel aliquod promissorum nullo unquam tempore veniemus; sed ea omnia & singula pro posse nostro procurabimus inviolabiliter observari. Et ut hæc nostra voluntas, approbatio, ratificatio, assensus, consensus, atque promissio à nobis eisdem Romanis Pontificibus & Ecclesiæ in perpetuum observentur, hoc præsens scriptum inde fieri fecimus, nostrorumque sigillorum munimine roboratum.
units.tr: 2. Therefore, so that every matter of dissension and scandal, or even any occasion of ill-will, between the Church itself and the Empire may be removed, and the two swords set in the house of the Lord, joined together by due covenant, may exercise their office for the useful reform of the whole government, and we, moved in will and deed as sons of devotion and peace, are bound to cherish the Church no less than the Empire: by our lord Rudolph, by the grace of God King of the Romans, ever August, our father and lord, granted to Pope Nicholas III and his successors, and to the Roman Church itself, recognised, confirmed, ratified, renewed, again given, declared or conceded, or ratified, and done or made by privileges or whatever other writings of whatever kind, by recognitions, ratifications, approvals, renewals, confirmations, donations, concessions, and deeds and acts, both of other Emperors and Kings of the Romans, predecessors of the same King, and of the King himself, concerning the fidelity, obedience and honour to be rendered by the Roman Emperors and Kings to the Roman Pontiffs and the Church itself, and the possessions, honours and rights of the same Church; and specifically over all the land from Radicofani to Ceperano, the March of Ancona, the Duchy of Spoleto, the land of Countess Matilda, the City of Ravenna and Aemilia, Bobbio, Cesena, Forpopoli, Forlì, Faenza, Imola, Bologna, Ferrara, Comacchio, Adria and Gavello, Rimini, Urbino, Montefeltro, the territory of Balneum, the County of Bertinoro, the Exarchate of Ravenna, the Pentapolis, Massa Trabaria with its adjoining lands, and all others pertaining to the aforesaid Church, with all its boundaries, territories and islands by land and sea, provinces, cities, and territories belonging in any way to the aforesaid; and likewise over the city of Rome and the kingdom of Sicily with all things pertaining to it, both on this side of the Pharos and beyond, Corsica too and Sardinia, and the other lands and rights pertaining to the Church itself; we, in the name of the Principality, approve and ratify in all things and in every respect, and to all these and each and all others made in any way by the same King concerning them, and to be made in future, we unanimously and harmoniously express our will, assent and consent, and promise that we will at no time act against the promises or any of them, but will by our best endeavour see that all and each of them are inviolably observed. And so that this our will, approval, ratification, assent, consent and promise may be observed by us toward the same Roman Pontiffs and the Church for ever, we have caused this present writing to be made, and strengthened by the protection of our seals.

units.la: Actum & datum anno Domini millesimo, ducentesimo, septuagesimo nono, decimoquarto Kal. Aprilis, Indictione septima, regnante prædicto Domino nostro Rodulpho Romanorum Rege gloriosissimo, regni ejus anno sexto.
units.tr: Done and given in the year of the Lord 1279, on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of April, in the seventh indiction, in the reign of the aforesaid our lord Rudolph, most glorious King of the Romans, in the sixth year of his reign.

units.la: RUDOLPHI I. IMPER. AUG. DECRETUM
units.tr: RUDOLPH I, EMPEROR AUGUSTUS, DECREE

units.la: I- N ACTIONE EMPTI ET VENDITI CASTRI BECKELHEIMEN- SIS, vertente inter Archiepiscopum Moguntinum & Comites Sponhei- menses.
units.tr: Concerning the sale and purchase of the castle of Beckelheim, the dispute between the Archbishop of Mainz and the Counts of Sponheim.

units.la: RUDOLPHUS Dei gratia Rex Romanorum Semper-Augustus, notum facimus universis ac singulis has literas lecturis aut legi audituris; Quòd nos omnem discordiam, litem & contentionem, quæ fuerunt inter dilectos Principes nostros, Wernherum Archiepiscopum Moguntinum, Ecclesiam suam, Henricum fratrem Comitis de Sponheim, cum omnibus amicis & auxiliariis earum, partibus ex altera, complanavimus, concordavimus & pacificavimus integraliter, perfectè ac perpetuum, super omnibus factis commissis & perpetratis, in toto tempore illo, quo discordia inter eos coepit & duravit, in hunc modum.
units.tr: RUDOLPH, by the grace of God King of the Romans, ever Augustus, makes known to all and each who shall read these letters or hear them read: that we have settled, reconciled and fully and perpetually pacified every discord, quarrel and contention which existed between our beloved princes, Werner, Archbishop of Mainz, and his Church, on the one side, and Henry, brother of Count of Sponheim, with all their friends and helpers, on the other, concerning all deeds committed and perpetrated during the whole time in which the discord between them began and lasted, in the following manner.

units.la: I. In primis castro Beckelnheim, castrensibus hominibus & bonis, quæ præfatus Archiepiscopus habet, sicut habetur in literis divisionis inter Comitem Johannem & Henricum fratrem ejus factæ, renunciavit prædictus Comes Johannes, cum uxore & fratre suo Everhardo, pro se & cunctis hæredibus suis, coram nobis in perpetuum: debebatque meo judicio, sub quo dicta bona constare noscuntur, omnia & singula, quæ ordo juris cum Warandia expostulat. Comes Henricus sua tertia parte debet esse contentus, quemadmodum hucusque tenuit eandem; & Archiepiscopus cum Ecclesia Moguntina in duabus partibus, quas ei vendidit Henricus frater Comitis Johannis, sine aliqua molestatione in possessione quieta permanebit.
units.tr: I. First, the aforesaid Count John, together with his wife and his brother Everhard, renounced for himself and all his heirs, before us, forever, the castle of Beckelheim, its castle people and the goods which the aforesaid Archbishop holds, as set out in the deed of division made between Count John and his brother Henry. And he must, in my judgment, under whom the said goods are known to lie, make good all and each thing which the order of law requires of a warrantor. Count Henry shall be content with his third part, as he has held it hitherto; and the Archbishop, with the Church of Mainz, shall remain in quiet possession, without any disturbance, of the two parts which Henry, brother of Count John, sold to him.

units.la: II. Captivi omnes facto jurejurando pacis, ut moris est, liberi dimissi sunt.
units.tr: II. All prisoners, having sworn an oath of peace, as is customary, were dismissed free.

units.la: III. Omnia præscripta Johannes & Henricus Comites de Sponheim, se firmiter observaturos, super Sancta Dei Evangelia juraverunt. Quòd hi hanc concordiæ & pacis nostram compositionem ad injuriam Archiepiscopi & Ecclesiæ Moguntinæ præfati Comites violare præsumpserint, tunc nos una cum Civitatibus Regni, Francfordia, Fridburg, Wetzlaria, Geilenhausen, Oppenheim, Wesalia, Hopardia, & ipse nobiscum adversus eos, sæpedicto Archiepiscopo & Ecclesiæ ejus auxilium ferente, assistentiam faciemus. Contra hæc auxilium ferre præfatis Comitibus Johanni & Henrico nòn debebunt Fridericus Comes de Liningen, neque filius ejus, neque Everhardus Comes de Katzenelnbogen, neque Emicho Comes de Liningen, seu aliquis eorum, adversus Archiepiscopum & Ecclesiam Moguntinam.
units.tr: III. John and Henry, Counts of Sponheim, swore upon the holy Gospels of God that they would firmly observe everything written above. If these counts should presume to violate this our settlement of concord and peace to the injury of the Archbishop and the Church of Mainz, then we, together with the cities of the realm, Frankfurt, Friedberg, Wetzlar, Gelnhausen, Oppenheim, Wesel and Hoppard, and he with us, will give assistance against them, bringing aid to the aforesaid Archbishop and his Church. Friedrich, Count of Leiningen, nor his son, nor Everhard, Count of Katzenelnbogen, nor Emich, Count of Leiningen, or any of them, shall be bound to bring aid to the aforesaid Counts John and Henry against the Archbishop and the Church of Mainz.

units.la: IV. Hanc autem concordiæ & pacis compositionem de consensu & bona voluntate præfatorum, Archiepiscopi Moguntini, & Comitum Johannis & Henrici de Sponheim fecimus, & ad instantiam eorum sigillum nostrum Regium, unà cum sigillis eorum, & Friderici Comitis de Liningen, & Everhardi Comitis de Katzenelnbogen, his literis fecimus appendi. Actum Moguntiæ, anno Domini MCCLXXXI. in profesto S.Luciæ.
units.tr: IV. We have made this settlement of concord and peace with the consent and good will of the aforesaid Werner, Archbishop of Mainz, and of Counts John and Henry of Sponheim, and at their request we have had our royal seal appended to these letters, together with their seals and those of Friedrich, Count of Leiningen, and Everhard, Count of Katzenelnbogen. Done at Mainz, in the year of the Lord 1281, on the eve of St. Lucy.

units.la: RUDOLPHI I. IMPER. AUG. DECRETUM
units.tr: RUDOLPH I, EMPEROR AND AUGUSTUS, DECREE

units.la: DE DISTINCTIS BVRGGRAVII ET SENATVS POPVLIQVE CIVITATIS juribus,eorumq; concordia & integritate.
units.tr: CONCERNING THE SEPARATE RIGHTS OF THE BURGRAVE AND OF THE SENATE AND PEOPLE OF THE CITY, AND THEIR CONCORD AND INTEGRITY.

units.la: NOs Rudolphus Dei gratia Romanorum Rex Semper-Augustus, ad universorum sacri Imperii Romani fidelium, tam praesentium quàm futurorum, notitiam tenore praesentium volumus pervenire, quòd nos inter nostros fideles Milites Castrenses & Cives de Fridberg ordinationem, concordiam & securitatem fecimus cum consensu & voluntate partis utriusque in hunc modum.
units.tr: WE, Rudolph, by the grace of God Roman King and ever Augustus, wish by the tenor of these presents to make known to all the faithful of the holy Roman Empire, both present and future, that we have made an arrangement, concord and security between our faithful knights of the castle and the citizens of Friedberg, in the following manner, with the consent and will of both parties.

units.la: 1. Quod Cives Castrum in Fridberg nunquam destruent, nec Castrenses de Castro expellent, nec Castrum capient, nec recipient, nec retinebunt, nec talia volentibus facere consilium, auxilium seu favorem praestabunt.
units.tr: 1. The citizens shall never destroy the castle at Friedberg, nor expel the garrison from the castle, nor seize, receive or retain the castle; nor shall they give counsel, aid or favour to those who wish to do such things.

units.la: 2. Milites etiam civitatem Fridberg nunquam destruent, nec de civitate ipsos cives expellent, nec capient, nec recipient, nec insultum communiter in civitatem facient, nec talia volentibus facere consilium, auxilium seu favorem praestabunt.
units.tr: 2. Likewise, the knights shall never destroy the city of Friedberg, nor expel the citizens from the city, nor seize or receive it, nor make a joint assault upon the city; nor shall they give counsel, aid or favour to those who wish to do such things.

units.la: 3. Et si Milites Castrenses contra Cives vel Civitatem praedictam aliquid fecerint praedictorum, tunc ipso facto omnibus libertatibus, & tam feudis Castrensibus, quàm aliis, & omnibus honoribus & juribus, quae vel quos ab Imperio tenuerunt, perpetuò carebunt: & in se elegerunt Domini Papae excommunicationem & nostram proscriptionem faciendam, quando Cives hoc duxerint requirendum. Et si Cives contra Castrenses Milites vel Castrum aliquid fecerint praedictorum, tunc ipso facto omnibus libertatibus, feudis & omnibus honoribus & juribus, quae vel quos ab Imperio tenuerunt, perpetuò carebunt: & in se elegerunt Domini Papae excommunicationem, & nostram proscriptionem faciendam, quando Milites Castrenses hoc duxerint requirendum.
units.tr: 3. And if the knights of the castle do anything of the aforesaid kind against the citizens or the aforesaid city, then by that very act they shall lose for ever all liberties, both the castle fiefs and the others, and all the honours and rights which they held from the Empire; and they have chosen for themselves that excommunication by the Lord Pope and our proscription shall be pronounced, whenever the citizens think fit to demand it. And if the citizens do anything of the aforesaid kind against the knights or the castle, then by that very act they shall lose for ever all liberties, fiefs and all honours and rights which they held from the Empire; and they have chosen for themselves that excommunication by the Lord Pope and our proscription shall be pronounced, whenever the castle knights think fit to demand it.

units.la: 4. Adjectum vel etiam, quòd si inter praedictos Milites & Cives, vel eorum familiam aliquae vel contentiones seu pugnae surrexerint, hoc judicari debet secundum quod in ipsa Civitate ante actis temporibus est consuetum.
units.tr: 4. It is further added that if any quarrels or fights should arise between the aforesaid knights and citizens, or their households, this shall be judged according to the custom long observed in the city itself.

units.la: 5. Promiserunt insuper ex utraque parte, quòd postquam nos viam universae carnis ingressi suerimus, ipsi Castrenses Milites nullum ad Castrum praedictum intromittent, per quem ipsi Cives vel rum Civitas laedi valeat vel offendi: hoc etiam ipsi Cives Militibus facient e converso, donec novus Rex creatus fuerit, cui tam Castrenses quàm Cives faciant, ut tenentur.
units.tr: 5. Moreover, both parties have promised that, after we have gone the way of all flesh, the knights of the castle shall admit no one into the aforesaid castle through whom the citizens or their city might be harmed or injured; and the citizens shall likewise do the same to the knights in return, until a new King is created, to whom both the castle knights and the citizens shall render the obedience they owe.

units.la: 6. Et nos tam Cives quàm Castrenses Milites, ut praedicta per nos inviolabiliter observentur, cum sigillo Serenissimi Domini nostri praedicti Regis, sigilla nostra duximus praesentibus appendenda. Et nos Rudolphus Romanorum Rex sigillo nostro praesentem paginam fecimus communiri. Datum Moguntiae Idus Julij, Indictione xiii. Anno Domini MCCLXXXV. Regni nostri anno xi.
units.tr: 6. And we, both the citizens and the castle knights, so that the aforesaid provisions may be inviolably observed by us, have caused our seals to be appended to these presents, together with the seal of our most serene Lord, the aforesaid King. And we, Rudolph, Roman King, have caused this document to be strengthened with our seal. Given at Mainz, on the Ides of July, in the thirteenth indiction, in the year of the Lord 1285, the eleventh year of our reign.

units.la: RUDOLPHI I. IMPER. AUG. RESCRIPTUM
units.tr: RUDOLPH I, EMPEROR AUGUSTUS: RESCRIPT

units.la: VT DE CIVIBVS IMPERII NEMO SERVILIS CONDITIONIS, TAN- quam in homines liberos, judicare possit.
units.tr: That no one of servile condition may sit in judgement over the citizens of the Empire, as over free men.

units.la: RUDOLPHUS Dei gratia Romanorum Rex Semper-Augustus, prudentibus viris, universis hominibus vallis in Suitz, liberae condicionis existentibus, dilectis suis fidelibus gratiam suam & omne bonum. Inconveniens nostra reputat Serenitas, quòd aliquis servilis condicionis pro Judice vobis detur. Propter quod auctoritate Regia volumus, ut nulli hominum, qui servilis dicionis extiterit, de vobis de cetero judicia liceat aliqualiter exercere, praesentium testimonio tarum, quas nostrae Majestatis sigillo jussimus muniri. Datum in Baden, anno Domini millesimo ducentesimo nonagesimo primo, Regni verò decimo octavo.
units.tr: RUDOLPH, by the grace of God Roman King, ever Augustus, to the prudent men, to all the men of the valley of Schwyz, who are of free condition, his beloved faithful subjects, his grace and every good. Our Serenity considers it improper that anyone of servile condition should be given to you as judge. For this reason we will, by royal authority, that from now on no one of servile lordship may in any way exercise judgements over you; as testimony of which we have ordered these present letters to be fortified with the seal of our Majesty. Given at Baden, in the year of the Lord one thousand two hundred and ninety-one, and in the eighteenth year of our reign.

units.la: RUDOLPHI I. IMPER. AUG. CONSTITUTIO
units.tr: Constitution of Emperor Rudolph I, Augustus

units.la: NE CIVES IMPERIALES EXTRA CIVITATEM AD DVELLVM & extraneaa judicia provocentur.
units.tr: That imperial citizens are not to be summoned outside their city to a duel or to foreign courts.

units.la: RUDOLPHUS Dei gratia Romanorum Rex Semper-Augustus, prudentibus viris, Consulibus & Civibus universis de N. dilectis suis fidelibus gratiam suam & omne bonum.
units.tr: Rudolph, by the grace of God Roman King and ever-Augustus, to the prudent men, the Consuls and all the Citizens of N., his beloved and faithful subjects, grace and every good thing.

units.la: 1. Nullus vos vel vestrum aliquem modo duellico seu per viam duelli extra civitatem Fridberg citare possit, vel debeat evocare.
units.tr: 1. No one may cite you, or any of you, by a duel or by the way of a duel outside the city of Friedberg, nor ought he to summon you there.

units.la: 2. Volumus etiam, quòd nullus vos vel vestrum aliquem pro ullis bonis vel debitis extra dictam civitatem Fridberg citare possit aliqualiter vel vocare, nisi prius in civitate Fridberg sibi fuerit justitia denegata.
units.tr: 2. We also will that no one may in any way cite or summon you, or any of you, outside the said city of Friedberg for any goods or debts, unless justice has first been denied to him in the city of Friedberg.

units.la: Datum apud Franckford, 3. Kalend. Junii, Indictione iv. Anno Domini MCCLXXXXI. Regni vero nostri anno xviii.
units.tr: Given at Frankfurt, on the 3rd day before the Kalends of June, in the fourth indiction, in the year of the Lord 1291, and in the eighteenth year of our reign.

units.la: ADOLPHI IMPER. AUG. CONSTITUTIO DE INSVLIS RHENI, ET DIVERSIS ALIIS Capitulis.
units.tr: Constitution of the Emperor Adolf Augustus concerning the islands of the Rhine, and various other chapters.

units.la: NOs Adolphus Dei gratia Romanorum Rex Semper-Augustus, recognoscimus per praesentes, quòd nobis anno Domini millesimo ducentesimo nonagesimo tertio, in die beatorum Tiburtii & Valeriani Martyrum, in generali Curia apud Nuremberg pro tribunali sedéubus, ad requisitionem spectabilis viri, Reinaldi Comitis Gelrensis, per communem Principum sententiam est obtentum.
units.tr: We, Adolf, by the grace of God Roman King, ever Augustus, acknowledge by these presents that, in the year of the Lord 1293, on the day of the blessed martyrs Tiburtius and Valerian, it was obtained before us in a general court sitting as tribunal at Nuremberg, at the request of the distinguished man Reinald, Count of Gelre, by the common judgment of the Princes.

units.la: 1. Quòd si insula nata est in Rheno vel alio flumine, in Comitatu alicujus Comitis, qui in ipso flumine recipit teolonia & conductus, habetq; Comitatum eundem, teolonia & conductum ab Imperio in flumine praedicto; eadem insula potius spectat ad Imperium & ad ipsum Comitem, quàm ad alium Dominum, cujus districtus protenditur ad ripam fluminis praelibati.
units.tr: 1. First, if an island arises in the Rhine or another river, within the county of some count who receives tolls and conducts in that same river and holds that county, tolls and conducts from the Empire in the aforesaid river; that island belongs rather to the Empire and to that count himself than to another lord whose district extends to the bank of the aforementioned river.

units.la: 2. Secundò ad ejusdem Comitis instantiam est obtentum; quòd nulli licitum est munitionem erigere de novo in Comitatu alicujus Comitis, nisi petita ejus licentia & obtenta. Si autem Comes alicui, aedificanti munitionem, praestitit patientiam, quousque aedificarerur munitio, & passus est dominum ejus tamdiu pacificè possidere, donec secundum terrae consuetudinem praescriberentur alia bona contra Comitè, vel aliū quemcunq; quod postea nō potest impetiā Comite super edificio praelibato.
units.tr: 2. Secondly, it was obtained at the same count's instance that it is lawful for no one to erect a new fortification within the county of a count unless he has asked for and obtained the count's permission. But if the count has allowed someone building a fortification to proceed patiently until the fortification was completed, and has suffered its owner to possess it peacefully for so long that, according to the custom of the land, other goods were prescribed against the count or anyone else, he cannot afterwards contest the aforesaid building against the count.

units.la: 3. Tertiò fuit obtentum; si inter aliquos discordantes super homicidio aliqua compositio intercedat, & à parte, quae injuriam intulit, parti laesae satisfactio impendatur, & compositio fiat pro consanguineis omnibus partis passae injuriam; postmodum verò pars injuriam passa proponat, quòd nō pro omnibus de parte eadem compositio intervenit, sed quibusdam nominatim exceptis; alia parte dicente è contrario, quòd pro omnibus consanguineis laesae partis compositio facta extitit, & satisfactio subsecuta: partis hoc affirmantis probatio cum duobus testibus (ita quod manus affirmantis sit tertia) potius sit admittenda, quàm partis contrarium asserentis.
units.tr: 3. Thirdly, it was obtained: if some composition is made between parties in discord over a homicide, and satisfaction is paid by the party that inflicted the injury to the injured party, and the composition is made on behalf of all the kinsmen of the injured party; afterwards, if the injured party alleges that the composition did not cover all of that party but certain persons were expressly excepted, while the other party maintains on the contrary that the composition was made and satisfaction followed for all the kinsmen of the injured party: the proof offered by the party affirming this should rather be admitted, with two witnesses (so that the affirming party's own hand makes a third), than the proof of the party asserting the contrary.

units.la: 4. Quartò fuit quaesitum pro ipso Comite; si alicujus Domini familia in oppido, cujus dominium spectat ad ipsum, malè tractatur verbis vel factis, utrum Dominus loci vel Scabini ipsius debeant factum hujusmodi judicare? Et obtentum fuit communi sententia, quòd potius spectat ad Dominum judicium hujusmodi, quàm ad Scabinos praedictos: nisi forsan ipsi cives per libertatem concessam ab ipso Domino vel à suis praedecessoribus, contrarium doceant.
units.tr: 4. Fourthly, a question was raised on behalf of the count himself: if the household of some lord is ill-treated in words or deeds in a town whose lordship belongs to the count, do the lord of the place or its magistrates (Scabini) ought to judge such an act? And it was held by common judgment that the judgment of such matters belongs rather to the lord than to the aforesaid magistrates, unless perhaps the citizens themselves show otherwise by a liberty granted by that lord or by his predecessors.

units.la: 5. Quintò sententialiter est obtentum; quòd si aliquis obsidet castrum in terminis Regni Romani, nisi prius obtinuerit in figura judicii, quòd licitè facere illud posset; Nos obsidenti debeamus dare auctoritate Regia in mandatis, ut obsidionem suam dissolvat, & prosequatur suam justitiam coram nobis.
units.tr: 5. Fifthly, it was decided by judgment: if anyone besieges a castle within the bounds of the Roman Kingdom, unless he has first obtained, in the form of a judicial finding, that he may lawfully do so, we ought to give the besieger a command by royal authority to dissolve his siege and pursue his right before us.

units.la: 6. Sextò sententiatum extitit coram nobis; quòd si debitor dicat, se creditori debitum persolvisse, creditor verò neget; ipsius debitoris, & non creditoris, est super hoc probatio admittenda. Datum anno Domini, die & loco praedictis; Regni verò nostri anno secundo.
units.tr: 6. Sixthly, it was pronounced before us: if a debtor says that he has paid the debt to the creditor, and the creditor denies it, the proof on this point must be admitted from the debtor, and not from the creditor. Given in the year of the Lord, on the day and at the place aforesaid; in the second year of our reign.

units.la: ADOLPHI IMPERAT. AUG. CONSTITUTIO NE BONA AD ECCLESIAM DEVOLVTA A CONSVETIS tributis eximantur.
units.tr: The Constitution of Emperor Adolph, that goods transferred to the Church shall not be exempted from their customary taxes.

units.la: NOs Adolphus Dei gratia Romanorū Rex Semper-Augustus, Cōsulibus & civibus de N. Praecipimus & Regali sancimus edicto, ut omnia bona infra a districtum Civitatis constituta, quocunq; nomine censeantur, quae sturam seu precariam persolvere consueverunt, ad quorumcunq; religiosorum seu aliorum cujuscunq; conditionis manus, quocunq; alienationis titulo, transferantur, more solito sturam seu precariam in perpetuum contribuant & persolvant, quemadmodum ab Excellentissimo Principe, inclyto quondam Rudolpho Romanorum Rege, nostro praedecessore, id ipsum sancitum extitit edictum. Datum in Frideberg, 1. Nonar. Augusti, Indictione 6. Anno Domini MCCXCIII. Regni verò nostri anno secundo.
units.tr: We, Adolph, by the grace of God King of the Romans, ever Augustus, direct and by royal edict decree to our consuls and citizens of N., that all goods situated within the district of the city, whatever name they are assessed under, which have been accustomed to pay the sturam or precaria, shall, when transferred into the hands of any religious persons or of others of whatever condition, under whatever title of alienation, continue to pay and render the sturam or precaria in perpetuity in the usual manner, just as the same edict was decreed by the most excellent prince, of renowned memory, Rudolph, King of the Romans, our predecessor. Given at Frideberg, on the 1st of the Nones of August, in the sixth indiction, in the year of the Lord 1293, and in the second year of our reign.

units.la: S. ROMANI IMPERII ARCHI- PRINCIPUM ELECTORUM SENTENTIA EXAVCTORATIONIS ET DEPOSITIONIS DN. ADOL- PHI Romanorum Regis: & de jure Electoris Palatini.
units.tr: The Sentence of the Electors of the Holy Roman Empire, Concerning the Deposition and Removal of Lord Adolf, King of the Romans, and on the Right of the Count Palatine as Elector.

units.la: MOGUNTINUS Pontifex, Saxoniae atq; Brandeburgii Praesides, Legati Regis Bojemiae, Regulum Saxonum arbitrium honorarium (quippe Rudolphus Praefectus praetorio Rheni, Rectorque Bojariae, cujus munus est veluti de querimoniis adversus Caesare delatis cognosce-re, re, jusque dicere, sententiâ pronunciare, venire recusarat) capiunt, tribunali imponunt, ADOLPHUM homicidii, stupri in virginem, sodomiæ, negligentiæ, perjurii, quòd à Francis Occidentalibus intercepta non repetetur, accusant. Deinde Senatusconsulto eum in ordinem redigunt, à fastigio deturbant, Rempublicam oibam capite esse decernunt. Postremò ne Imperium sine capite, sicut corpus sine anima contabesceat, ALBERTUM suis suffragiis rebus imponunt, Cæsarem designant, nuncupant, nonis Kalendis Julius declarant.
units.tr: The Archbishop of Mainz, the governors of Saxony and Brandenburg, and the envoys of the King of Bohemia take Rudolf the Saxon as honorary arbiter, since Rudolf, Count Palatine of the Rhine and steward of the court, and ruler of Bavaria, whose office it is, as it were, to hear complaints brought against the Emperor, to administer justice and pronounce sentence, had refused to attend. They seat him on the tribunal and accuse Adolf of homicide, of the rape of a virgin, of sodomy, of negligence, and of perjury, because he did not seek to recover what had been seized by the Western Franks. Then, by a decree of the Senate, they reduce him to the ranks, cast him down from the summit, and decree that the Commonwealth is to be without a head. Finally, lest the Empire waste away without a head, as a body without a soul, they set Albert over the state by their votes, designate him as Emperor, proclaim him, and declare it on the Nones of July.

units.la: ALBERTI I. IMP. AUG. CONSTITUTIO NE BONA AD ECCLESIAM DEVOLVTA A CONSVETIS tributis eximantur.
units.tr: Constitution of Albert I, Emperor Augustus, that goods devolved to the Church shall be exempt from the customary taxes.

units.la: NOs ALBERTUS Dei gratia Romanorum Rex Semper-Augustus, ad universorum notitiam deducimus per præsentes, quòd volumus, præcipimus & mandamus, quatenus omnia bona infra districtum Civitatis Imperialis constituta, quocunque nomine censeantur, ad quascunque manus devoluta, & quocunque titulo alienata, sive ad religiosos, sive ad alios, quæ ftt uram seu precariam persolvere consueverunt, eandem stcuram seu precariam in præsenti persolvant parter & in futuro. Datum apud Franckinfurt, xv. Kalend. Martii, Indictione xii, anno Domini MCCXCIX. Regni vero nostri anno primo.
units.tr: We, Albert, by the grace of God King of the Romans, ever Augustus, make known to all by these present letters that we wish, command and order that all goods situated within the district of the Imperial City, under whatever name they are assessed, which have passed into whatever hands and have been alienated by whatever title, whether to religious or to others, and which have been accustomed to pay the usual tax or quit-rent, shall likewise pay the same tax or quit-rent now and in future. Given at Frankfurt, 15 days before the Kalends of March, in the twelfth indiction, in the year of the Lord 1299, and in the first year of our reign.

units.la: S. ROMANI IMPERII AR- CHIPRINCIPUM ELECTORUM SENTENTIA IN ALBERTVM I. REGEM ROMAN. PROPTER EIUS excessus in injustitia & tyrannide: & de jure Electoris Palatini.
units.tr: The Sentence of the Electors of the Holy Roman Empire against King Albert I of the Romans, on account of his excesses in injustice and tyranny, and concerning the right of the Elector Palatine.

units.la: ANNO MCCC. circa festum Beati Michaëlis, Dux Rudolphus & Comes Palatinus Rheni præfarus, ab Electoribus Imperii, Moguntinensi, Coloniensi & Treverensi Archiepiscopis vocatus fuit ad Rhenum, contra Regem ALBERTUM. Unde iidem Principes contra ipsum ALBERTUM conspiraverunt, eligentes ipsum Rudolphum pro judice: & asserentes, ad Comitem Palatinum pertinere, quod sit officium Palatinæ dignitatis ex quadam consuetudine, de causis cognoscere, quæ ipsi Regi moverentur. Quare contra Regem proposuerunt, quòd Dominus suum propium, scilicet Regem ADOLPHUM, occidisset: ideò Rex esse non posset, & ad depositionem ipsius cogitabant.
units.tr: In the year 1300, around the feast of Blessed Michael, Duke Rudolph, the aforesaid Count Palatine of the Rhine, was summoned to the Rhine by the Electors of the Empire, the Archbishops of Mainz, Cologne and Trier, against King Albert. These same princes then conspired against Albert himself, choosing Rudolph as judge and asserting that it belonged to the Count Palatine, by a certain custom attached to the office of the Palatine dignity, to hear the causes brought against the King. Accordingly they charged the King that he had killed his own lord, namely King Adolph, and therefore could not be king; and they were planning his deposition.

units.la: ALBERTI I. IMPER. AUG. CONSTITUTIO QVA CONFIRMANTVR ET RATIFICANTVR PRIVILEGIA OMNIA per alios prædecessores Imperatores Ecclesiæ Romanæ concessa.
units.tr: The Constitution of Emperor Albert I Augustus, by which all the privileges granted to the Roman Church by his predecessor emperors are confirmed and ratified.

units.la: SANCTISSIMO in Christo Patri & Domino nostro, Domino Bonifacio, divina providentia sacrosanctæ Romanæ ac universalis Ecclesiæ Summo Pontifici, ALBERTUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator Semper-Augustus, devota pedum oscula beatorum.
units.tr: To the most holy Father in Christ and our Lord, Lord Boniface, by divine providence Supreme Pontiff of the most sacred Roman and universal Church, Albert, by the grace of God Roman Emperor, ever Augustus, offers devout kisses of the blessed feet.

units.la: Profiteor, Beatissime Pater, me bonorum omnium largitori, ac vobis & sanctæ Ecclesiæ tuæ pro innumeris misericordiis & immensis beneficiis obligatum. Profiteor quòd desideri mei recepi desideratum effectum, & differri non audeo, quòd & plus, quàm desiderasse teneram, adinvenimus, mirans sic in præteritis esse provisum, quod de iis, quæ circa talia in futuro peti poterant, ipsos miserationis habetur. Assurgens itaque Deo & sanctitati vestræ, ac eidem Ecclesiæ matri meæ ad gratiarum devotissimas & humillimas actiones, totum me devoveo, totum me offero, & expono ad gratificationis debitum per omnia, in quantum humanæ imbecillitatis condicio patitur, exolvendum. Ad hæc licet prius, antequam circa negotium electionis de me ad Romanum Regnum & Imperium celebrarætaliæ, quæ in hac parte incumbebant, esset per sanctitatis vestræ beneficentiam mei status essentia solidata, fecerim infrascriptas, & super his meas beatitudini vestræ litteras duxerim destinandas, ac in soliditate hujusmodi procuratores mei ad hoc specialiter constituti, & in vestra præsentia renovaverint: ecce nunc tamen, ut gratus reddar, & ipsa in majori firmitate procedant, illa duxi prænumerabus innovanda.
units.tr: Most Blessed Father, I acknowledge that I am bound to the giver of all good things, and to you and to your holy Church, for countless mercies and immense benefits. I confess that I have received the desired outcome of my wishes, and I dare not delay, since I have found more than I had dared to hope for, marvelling that such provision has been made in the past that the Church's mercy is held to cover whatever might be asked in such matters in future. Therefore, raising my thanks to God, to your holiness and to the same Church, my mother, in the most devoted and humble acts of gratitude, I devote myself wholly, offer myself wholly, and expose myself, so far as the condition of human frailty allows, to discharge in every way the debt of gratitude. Moreover, although before the business of my election to the Roman Kingdom and Empire was carried out, and while my status was being firmly established by your holiness's kindness, I made the undertakings below and sent my letters on these matters to your beatitude, and my procurators, specially appointed for this purpose, renewed them in your presence to give them firmer standing: now, nevertheless, so that I may be seen as grateful, and so that these undertakings may proceed with greater firmness, I have thought fit to renew them, as set out above.

units.la: Recognoscens igitur, quòd Romanum Imperium per Sedem Apostolicam de Græcis translatum est in personam magnifici Caroli in Germanos, & quòd jus eligendi Romanorum Regem, in Imperatorem postmodum promovendum, certis Principibus Ecclesiasticis & Sæcularibus est ab eadem Sede concessum, à qua Reges & Imperatores, qui fuerunt & erunt pro tempore, recipiunt temporalis gladii potestatem ad vindictam malefactorum, laude verò honorum pia devotione & sincero corde profiteor, quòd Romanorum Reges in Imperatores postmodum promovendi per Sedem eandem ad hoc potissimè & specialiter assumantur, ut sint S. Romanæ Ecclesiæ Advocati, Catholicæ fidei ac ejusdem Ecclesiæ scipuli defensores.
units.tr: Acknowledging, therefore, that the Roman Empire was transferred by the Apostolic See from the Greeks to the person of the illustrious Charles among the Germans, and that the right to elect a Roman King, to be afterwards advanced to the Empire, has been granted by the same See to certain ecclesiastical and secular Princes, from which See the kings and emperors who have been and will be in turn receive the power of the temporal sword for the punishment of evildoers, I profess, with pious devotion and sincere heart, and in praise of the good, that the Roman Kings who are afterwards to be promoted to the Empire are chosen by the same See chiefly and especially for this purpose: that they may be Advocates of the holy Roman Church and defenders of the Catholic faith and of the same Church's disciples.

units.la: Cætera Catera desiderantur, quae exstant Romae in Castello S. Angeli, quorum haec est summa.
units.tr: The rest is lacking. What survives is in Rome, in the Castle of St Angelo; its substance is this.

units.la: SUPERIORIBUS subjicit juramentum fidelitatis solitis formulis exhiberi consuetum. Addit his confirmationem juramenti pariter fidelitatis exhibiti à patre suo Rodulpho, & alia omnia ab aliis omnibus Imperatoribus praestita. Confirmat itidem privilegia ab eodem Rodulpho & aliis Imperatoribus eidem Ecclesiae Romanae concessa. Ratificat, quae statuta & jurata fuerant per Ludovicum Imperatorem Paschali Papae, & per Ottonem Joanni Pontifici. Et post reverentiam Patri exhibitam, & filialem amorem insinuatum, Ecclesiae juta defendit, primatum & libertatem ejusdem Ecclesiae profitetur defensurum adversus quoscumque ejusdem perturbatores, adversus quos bella movere, si opus sit, pollicetur, spondens suum cum exercitu in Italiam adventum, si placeat. Datum habetur apud Noremberg, anno Domini M.CCC.III. Indictione prima, decimosexto Kalend. Augusti: Regni vero anno quinto.
units.tr: He appends the oath of fidelity, customarily tendered in the usual formulas. To these he adds a confirmation of the oath of fidelity likewise tendered by his father Rudolf, and of all the other things rendered by all the other emperors. He likewise confirms the privileges granted to the same Roman Church by the same Rudolf and other emperors. He ratifies what had been enacted and sworn by Emperor Louis to Pope Paschal, and by Otto to Pope John. And after expressing reverence to his father and showing filial love, he defends the rights of the Church, and professes that he will defend the primacy and liberty of the same Church against any of its disturbers, promising to wage war against them if need be, pledging his coming into Italy with his army, if it be pleasing. It is dated at Nuremberg, in the year of the Lord 1303, first indiction, the sixteenth day before the Kalends of August, and in the fifth year of his reign.

units.la: ALBERTI I. IMPER. AUG. DECRETUM
units.tr: ALBERT I, EMPEROR AUGUSTUS, DECREE

units.la: DE ABSOLVTIONE REGIS BOHEMIAE A BANNO Imperiali.
units.tr: CONCERNING THE ABSOLUTION OF THE KING OF BOHEMIA FROM THE IMPERIAL BAN.

units.la: NOs Albertus Dei gratia Romanorum Rex Semper Augustus, ad universorum notitiam tenore praesentium volumus pervenire. Quòd super discordia, quae inter nos ex una parte, & illustrem quondam Wenceslaum Bohemiae Poloniaeque Regem ex altera, vertebatur, dum vixit, ad * cum ejus filio Illustri Wenceslao Bohemiae Poloniaeq; Rege, avunculo & Principe nostro charissimo, concordiae, quam cum eo cunctis diebus vitae nostrae servare bona fide promittimus, devenimus unionem.
units.tr: We, Albert, by the grace of God Roman King, ever Augustus, wish by the tenor of these presents to make known to all that, concerning the discord which was in progress between us on the one part and the illustrious late Wenceslaus, King of Bohemia and Poland, on the other, while he lived, we have come to a union with his son, the illustrious Wenceslaus, King of Bohemia and Poland, our uncle and most dear prince, in a concord which we promise to keep in good faith all the days of our life.

units.la: 1. Primò quòd omnis excessus, si quos ipsius avunculi nostri Bohemiae & Poloniae Regis genitor praedictus in nos vel Imperium quocunque modo commisit, propter quos in ipsum genitorem suum nostra legalis sententia lata, vel bannum promulgata fuissent, quae eius se extenderent ad heredes praedictum Venceslaum Bohemiae & Poloniae Regem avunculum nostrum, praedicti quondam Wenceslai Bohemiae & Poloniae Regis filium heredem & successorem, ac heredes suos, ab ipsis excessibus suis & bannis absolvimus, & in perpetuum auctoritate Regia reddimus & esse volumus omnimodè absolutos.
units.tr: 1. First, that every offence, if any, which the aforesaid father of our uncle, the King of Bohemia and Poland, committed against us or the Empire in any way, on account of which our legal sentence had been pronounced or a ban promulgated against his father himself, and which extended to his heirs, we absolve from their offences and bans the aforesaid Wenceslaus, King of Bohemia and Poland, our uncle, son, heir and successor of the late Wenceslaus, King of Bohemia and Poland, and his heirs; and by royal authority we restore them and wish them to be completely absolved for ever.

units.la: 2. Promittimus praeterea in Regia fide praedictum Wenceslaum Bohemiae & Poloniae Regem, avunculum nostrum, heredes & successores suos Bohemiae & Poloniae Reges in ipsis Bohemiê & Poloniae Regnis, & omnibus aliis Principatibus & terris ac juribus, & omnib' aliis, quae ad ipsum Wenceslaum Bohemiae & Poloniae Regem, avunculum nostrum, ex successione paterna vel quocumque alio titulo pervenerunt, nec de jure nec de facto, toto vitae nostrae tempore aliquatenus impedire, etiamsi aliquod jus, quod vulgariter dicitur Anspruch / nobis vel Imperio in eis competeret, vel dicteremus competere, vel nobis aut Imperio aliqua competere videretur. Sed ipse Wenceslaus Bohemiae & Poloniae Rex, avunculus noster, heredes ac successores sui Bohemiae & Poloniae Reges, praedicta Regna, Principatus, terras ac omnia supradicta cum pleno dominio, & omnibus Regnorum, Principatuum & terrarum ipsarum titulis, honoribus, juribus, jurisdictionibus, utilitatibus in terra & supra terram, in Regnis, Principatibus ac omnibus praedictis & ex eis provenientibus, feudalia jure tenent, propria verò & hereditaria jure proprietatis & hereditario debent obtinere in perpetuum, & ea quiete & pacificè possidere.
units.tr: 2. We further promise in royal faith that we will not, by right or in fact, in any way impede during the whole of our life the aforesaid Wenceslaus, King of Bohemia and Poland, our uncle, or his heirs and successors as kings of Bohemia and Poland, in the said kingdoms of Bohemia and Poland, and in all other principalities, lands and rights, and all other things which have come to that Wenceslaus, King of Bohemia and Poland, our uncle, by paternal succession or by any other title; even if any right, commonly called an Anspruch, belonged or we should say belongs to us or to the Empire in them, or seemed to belong to us or the Empire in any way. But the same Wenceslaus, King of Bohemia and Poland, our uncle, and his heirs and successors, kings of Bohemia and Poland, shall hold the aforesaid kingdoms, principalities, lands and all the aforesaid things with full dominion, and with all the titles, honours, rights, jurisdictions and advantages of the kingdoms, principalities and lands, on the land and above it, and whatever arises from them, by feudal right; but they ought to hold them by proper and hereditary right of ownership for ever, and to possess them quietly and peacefully.

units.la: 3. Illustres praeterea, Ottonem & Stephanum Duces Bavariae; Ottonem, Hermannum, Joannem & Valdemarum Marchiones de Brandenburg, qui in guerra & discordia praedicta, quae inter nos & praedictum quondam Wenceslaum Bohemiae & Poloniae Regem vertebatur, ipsius Regis Bohemiae fautores & adjutores fuerint; insuper omnes alios, qui notabiliter & actualiter adjutores vel fautores praedicti Regis Bohemiae & Poloniae contra nos in eadem discordia sunt vocati & inventi, sive sint banniti, sive proscripti vel ablitigati per nos vel per alios, praedictae concordiae & unioni includimus, & inclusos esse volumus praesentium tenore, & eos omnibus bonis in praedicta concordia, propter praestitum contra nos praedicto Regi Bohemiae adjutorum vel favorem eis ablatis, & honoribus & juribus eorum restituimus, & esse volumus, plenè & integrè restitutos; nec quod eis ex hoc in ipsis bonis & eorum juribus & honoribus ulla diminutio vel laesio aut praejudicium aliquod generetur.
units.tr: 3. Moreover, we include in the aforesaid concord and union the illustrious Otto and Stephen, Dukes of Bavaria; Otto, Hermann, John and Waldemar, Margraves of Brandenburg, who in the aforesaid war and discord, which was in progress between us and the aforesaid late Wenceslaus, King of Bohemia and Poland, were supporters and helpers of the said King of Bohemia; and besides, all others who have been notably and actually found and named as helpers or supporters of the aforesaid King of Bohemia and Poland against us in that discord, whether they have been banned, proscribed or outlawed by us or by others. By the tenor of these presents we include them in the aforesaid concord and union, and wish them to be included; and to those whose goods were taken from them in the aforesaid concord on account of the aid or favour given against us to the said King of Bohemia, we restore their goods, honours and rights, and wish them to be fully and entirely restored; and let no diminution, injury or prejudice of any kind arise to them from this, in their goods, rights or honours.

units.la: 4. Promittimus insuper super terris, hominibus, bonis & juribus terrae Uratislaviensis stare dictis & ordinationi Spectabilium virorum, Berroldi Comitis de Hennenberg & Burckhardi Burggravii de Magdeburg per nos & praedictum Wenceslaum Bohemiae & Poloniae Regem, avunculum nostrum, ad hoc concorditer electorum.
units.tr: 4. We further promise to abide by the decision and ordinance concerning the lands, men, goods and rights of the land of Breslau, made by the honourable men Berthold, Count of Henneberg, and Burkhard, Burgrave of Magdeburg, who were chosen in agreement by us and by the aforesaid Wenceslaus, King of Bohemia and Poland, our uncle, for this purpose.

units.la: 5. De munitionibus autem, si quas ipsius Wenceslai Bohemiae & Poloniae Regis, avunculi nostri, Progenitores in terra Egrensi, quam cum suis pertinentiis ipse V Venceslaus Bohemiae & Poloniae Rex, avunculus noster, ea integritate, quâ ipsa terra genitori suo per felicis memoriae ADOLPHUM Romanorum Regem, praecessorem nostrum, * olim fuit, compromisit nobis restituere, sua pecunia compacomparaverunt, inter nos & ipsum Wenceslaum Bohemiæ & Poloniæ Regem, avunculi nostrum, taliter est ordinatum, ut eædem munitiones discussioni juris subjaceant: utrum videlicet ad nos, vel ad ipsum Wenceslaum Bohemiæ & Poloniæ Regem, avunculum nostrum, debeant pertinere, nisi ipsias idem Wenceslaus Bohemiæ & Poloniæ Rex, avunculus noster, à nobis in feudum voluerit obtinere. In cujus rei testimonium præsentes exinde conscribi, & Majestatis nostræ sigillo jussimus communiri literas. Datum apud Nurmberg, xv. Calend. Septemb. Indict. III. Anno Domini MCCCV. Regni verò nostri anno VIII.
units.tr: 5. As for the fortresses, however, which the ancestors of that Wenceslaus, King of Bohemia and Poland, our uncle, bought with their own money in the land of Eger, which that Wenceslaus, our uncle, promised to restore to us in the same condition in which the land itself was once granted to his father by Adolf, King of the Romans of happy memory, our predecessor: it has been ordained between us and the same Wenceslaus, King of Bohemia and Poland, our uncle, that these fortresses shall be subject to a legal inquiry, namely whether they ought to belong to us or to the same Wenceslaus, King of Bohemia and Poland, our uncle, unless the same Wenceslaus, our uncle, wishes to hold them from us in fief. In witness whereof we have ordered these letters to be written and secured with the seal of our Majesty. Given at Nuremberg, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of September, in the third indiction, in the year of the Lord 1305, and in the eighth year of our reign.

units.la: ALBERTI I. IMPER. AUG.
units.tr: ALBERTUS I, EMPEROR AUGUSTUS

units.la: MANDATUM DE VINDICANDIS IMPERII provinciis.
units.tr: THE MANDATE CONCERNING THE RECOVERY OF THE PROVINCES OF THE EMPIRE

units.la: REx per literas mandat Comitibus Turingicis; ne a injusto Principi faverent plus, quàm ipsorum dignitas postularet: ipsos non ignorare, quòd eas provincias Adolfus Rex emerit: esse jam expertos, quanto sanguine constiterit pertinax ille favor: satius esse retinere fortunas, & vivere in libertate, quàm novo facuore fortunam incertam tentare. Sese enim non posse desistere, quin vendicet ea, quæ sint Imperii. Addit ad extremum minas, nisi resipiscant, & In poenam majestatem observent, cum adjecta poena ultionis in contumaces.
units.tr: The King, by letter, orders the Counts of Thuringia not to favour the unjust Prince more than their own dignity requires. He says that they are not unaware that King Adolf bought those provinces; they have already learned by experience at how great a cost of blood that stubborn favour was purchased. It is better to keep their fortunes and live in freedom than to try an uncertain fortune with a new faction. For he cannot cease to claim those things which belong to the Empire. He adds at the end threats: unless they come to their senses and observe the majesty due to him, they will be punished, with the penalty of vengeance attached for the obstinate.

units.la: HENRICI VII. IMP. AUG.
units.tr: HENRICI VII. IMP. AUG.

units.la: RESPONSVM, QVOD CIVIVM IMPERIALIVM DOMINVS EST solus Imperator, & non magistratus municipalis.
units.tr: RESPONSE, THAT THE EMPEROR ALONE IS LORD OF THE IMPERIAL CITIZENS, AND NOT A MUNICIPAL MAGISTRATE.

units.la: VENIENTIBUS Nunciis Argentinensibus ad Regem, ac proponentibus, se per Dominos suos Argentinenses, pro gratia Regis & privilegiorum innovatione transmissos: nec Spiræ nec Argentinæ ab ipso responsum habebant. Ascendentes autem versus Columbariam ad Regem, edocti à quodam Secretario Regis, dixerunt ei; Cives vestri Argentinenses hoc petunt. Quos Rex, dicens se ante non intellexisse, quorum fuissent Nuncii, cum Dominos Argentinenses nominassent, favorabiliter exaudivit.
units.tr: When the envoys of Strasbourg came to the King and set forth that they had been sent by their lords of Strasbourg to seek the King's favour and the renewal of their privileges, they had no answer from him, neither at Speyer nor at Strasbourg. But when they went up to the King at Columbaria, they were informed by a certain secretary of the King, and told him: "Your citizens of Strasbourg ask this." The King, saying that he had not previously understood whose envoys they were, since they had named the lords of Strasbourg, heard them kindly.

units.la: HENRICI VII. IMPER. AUG.
units.tr: Henry VII, Emperor Augustus

units.la: RESCRIPTUM NE CIVITATVM IMPERIALIVM INCOLAE AD EXTRANEA judicia pertrahantur.
units.tr: A rescript that inhabitants of the imperial cities are not to be dragged before foreign courts.

units.la: HENRICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Rex Semper-Augustus, universis hominibus vallis in Ure, fidelibus suis dilectis, gratiam suam & omne bonum. Vestris inquietudinibus obviare, commoditatibusque prospicere favorabiliter cupientes, dum tamen de vobis querulantibus justitiæ debitum non negetur, vobis per præsentes concedimus gratiosè, quòd ad nullius secularis judicis tribunal, nostræ Majestatis consistorio duntaxat excepto, super quibuscumque causis seu negotiis, extra terminos vallis prædictæ pertrahi debeatis, dummodo coram a Advocato nostro provinciali intra fines ejusdem vallis parati sitis stare juri, & facere quod dictaverit ordo juris. Datum Constantiæ, anno Domini millesimo trecentesimo octavo, III. Nonas Junii, Indictione VII. Regni verò nostri anno primo.
units.tr: Henry, by the grace of God King of the Romans, ever Augustus, to all the men of the valley of the Ure, his faithful and beloved subjects, greeting and every good thing. Wishing graciously to meet your troubles and provide for your conveniences, provided that justice owed to you as complainants is not denied, we grant you by these presents, graciously, that you are not to be dragged before the tribunal of any secular judge, except the consistory of our Majesty alone, on any causes or business whatsoever, outside the boundaries of the aforesaid valley, provided that you are ready to stand before our provincial Advocate within the bounds of the same valley, and to do what the order of law shall direct. Given at Constance, in the year of the Lord one thousand three hundred and eight, on the third day before the nones of June, in the seventh indiction, and in the first year of our reign.

units.la: HENRICI VII. IMPER. AUG.
units.tr: HENRY VII, EMPEROR AUGUSTUS

units.la: FORMULA DE OFFICIO FORESTARII.
units.tr: FORM CONCERNING THE OFFICE OF FORESTER

units.la: NOS HENRICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Rex Semper-Augustus. Ad universorum Sacri Romani Imperii fidelium noritiam cupimus pervenire, quod nos officium forestii nostri in Nurembergcontulimus Ottoni Forstmeister, fideli nostro dilecto, genero providi viri Conradi dicti Eselerr Scultaeti nostri Nurembergensis, ac omnibus suis hæredibus taliumfeudorum capacibus, cum novalibus suis ad ipsum ex successione progenitorum suorum hucusque devolutis, à nobis & ab Imperio deinceps in feudum possidendum. Ita quod ipse Otto præfatus, una cum servisibi ad regimen ejusdem officii necessariis, sylvam prænotatam foveat, & in omni loco impignoret, ubi eandem sylvam succisam indebite viderit aut nocive. Nulli etiam sine sui demonstratione pro structura aliqua sylvam succidere liceat antedictam: nec coram aliquo Judicum, nisi coram Buticlario nostro apud Nurembergh, qui tunc pro tempore fuerit, justitiam observabit. In cujus rei testimonium hanc literam sibi fieri volumus, sigillo nostræ Majestatis strictius roboraram. Datum in Nuremberg, quarto Idus Julii, anno Domini millesimo trecentesimo nono; Regni verò nostri anno primo.
units.tr: We, Henry, by the grace of God King of the Romans, ever Augustus, wish to make known to the faithful of the whole Holy Roman Empire that we have conferred the office of our forest in Nuremberg upon Otto Forstmeister, our beloved faithful man, son-in-law of the prudent man Conrad, called Eselerr, our Schultheiss of Nuremberg, and upon all his heirs capable of holding fiefs, together with the new clearings that have hitherto passed to him by succession from his forebears, to be held by him in fief from us and from the Empire henceforth. On this condition: that the aforesaid Otto, together with the servants necessary to him for managing the same office, shall guard the aforementioned forest and shall lay a pledge upon anyone in any place where he sees the said forest unlawfully or harmfully cut. Likewise, no one shall be permitted to cut down the aforesaid forest for any construction without his demonstration of need; nor shall he observe justice before any judge except before our Butler at Nuremberg, whoever shall then be in office. In witness of this matter we wish this letter to be made out for him and more firmly strengthened with the seal of our Majesty. Given at Nuremberg, on the fourth day before the Ides of July, in the year of the Lord 1309, and in the first year of our reign.

units.la: HENRICI VII. IMP. AUG. RESCRIPTUM
units.tr: Rescript of Henry VII, Emperor Augustus

units.la: DE REARBORANDA SYLVA IMPERIALI IN AGROS EXCISA.
units.tr: CONCERNING THE REPLANTING OF THE IMPERIAL FOREST CUT DOWN INTO FIELDS.

units.la: HENRICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Rex Semper-Augustus, Prudentibus viris, Sculteto, Consulibus & Civibus in Nuremberg, fidelibus suis dilectis, gratiam suam & omne bonum. Dignum judicat nostra Serenitas, & congruum arbitratur, quòd ea, quæ nostrum & Imperii honorem ac profectum vestrasque commoditates & utilitates respiciunt, affectu benevolo & effectu debito prosequamur. Quapropter vestris consiliis & petitionibus favorabiliter annuentes, fidelitati vestræ districtè committimus & mandamus, sub obtentu nostri favoris vobis nihilominus injungentes, quatenus sylvam nostram & Imperii, sitam propè Nurembergex utraque parte ripæ, quæ dicitur Pegnitz, à quinquaginta annis citrà per incendium vel alio modo quocunque destructam seu vastatam, ac postmodum in agros à quibuscunque redactam, in arbores & in sylvam, sicut solebat esse primitus, auctoritate nostra Regia redigatis. Nos quoque ad hoc, si necesse fuerit, opem & operam dabimus efficacem, præsentium testimonio literarum: sigilli nostri Regii robore signatarum. Datum Spiræ, VII. Calend. Septembr. Anno Domini millesimo trecentesimo nono; Regni verò nostri anno primo.
units.tr: HENRY, by the grace of God Roman King, Ever-August, to the prudent men, the Schultheiss, Consuls and Citizens of Nuremberg, his faithful and beloved subjects, grace and every good thing. Our Serenity judges it worthy and considers it fitting that we should pursue with kindly feeling and due effect those matters which concern the honour and advancement of us and the Empire, and your convenience and advantage. Wherefore, graciously assenting to your counsels and petitions, we firmly commit and command to your fidelity, and nevertheless enjoin upon you under the pretext of our favour, that you restore by our royal authority to trees and to forest, as it was originally wont to be, our forest and that of the Empire, situated near Nuremberg on either bank of the river called Pegnitz, which for fifty years past has been destroyed or laid waste by fire or in any other way whatsoever, and afterwards turned into fields by whomsoever. We too, if it should be necessary, will give effective aid and effort to this, by the testimony of these present letters sealed with the strength of our royal seal. Given at Speyer, on the seventh day before the Kalends of September, in the year of the Lord one thousand three hundred and nine; and in the first year of our reign.

units.la: HENRICI VII. IMPER. AUG. EDICTUM
units.tr: Edict of Henry VII, Emperor Augustus

units.la: QVO COMMVNITAS, QVAE SE A DOMINI SUI POTESTATE justo modo in libertatem vindicavit, in protectionem Imperii suscipitur, & libera Civitas Imperialis efficitur.
units.tr: By which the community, which has justly freed itself from the power of its lord, is taken under the protection of the Empire and becomes a free Imperial City.

units.la: NOS Henricus Dei gratia Romanorum Rex Semper-Augustus, ad universorum noticiam volumus pervenire, quòd nos hominibus habitantibus in valle Suitz, qui se de Nobili viro Eberhardo quondam Comite de Habsburg redemerunt, & per pecuniam, absolutionem & literas testimoniales super eo obtinuerunt, & exhibere potuerunt, ut proponunt, quòd nobis & sacro Romano Imperio pertinent, & pertinere debent de jure, hanc gratiam duximus faciendam, quòd eosdem homines liberamus, prout alii in eadem valle ac circumpositis vallibus existere dignoscuntur, præsentium testimonio literarum, nostræ Majestatis sigilli robore signatarum. Datum Turego, III. Nonas Maii, anno Domini MCCCX. Regni verò nostri anno secundo.
units.tr: We, Henry, by the grace of God Roman King, ever Augustus, wish it to come to the notice of all men that, whereas the men dwelling in the valley of Schwyz, who redeemed themselves from the noble lord Eberhard, once Count of Habsburg, and obtained and were able to show, as they allege, by payment, release and written testimony concerning this, that they belong and ought by right to belong to us and the holy Roman Empire, we have resolved to grant this favour: that we free these men, just as the others dwelling in this valley and in the neighbouring valleys are known to be free. This is given by the testimony of the present letters, strengthened by the seal of our Majesty. Given at Zurich, on the third of the Nones of May, in the year of the Lord 1310, and in the second year of our reign.

units.la: HENRICI VII. IMPER. AUG. MANDATUM
units.tr: HENRY VII, EMPEROR AUGUSTUS, MANDATE

units.la: AD FORRESTARIOS ET ZEIDLARIOS, DE FVRRENTIS VASTATIS aut abalienatis restaurandis.
units.tr: TO THE FORESTERS AND CHARCOAL-BURNERS, CONCERNING THE RESTORATION OF THE WOODS DEVASTATED OR ALIENATED.

units.la: HENRICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Rex Semper-Augustus, strenuis ac providis viris, dicto Hörauf, Conrado Stromer, Ottoni *, cæterisque Forestariis ac Zeidlaris nemoris nostri & Imperii apud Nuremberg, ab utraque parte fluvii dicti Pegnitz constitutis, fidelibus suis dilectis gratiam suam & omne bonum.
units.tr: HENRY, by the grace of God Roman King and ever Augustus, to the vigorous and provident men, Hörauf (called so), Conrad Stromer, Otto *, and the other Foresters and Charcoal-burners of our forest and of the Empire at Nuremberg, situated on either side of the river called Pegnitz, to his faithful and beloved subjects, his grace and every good.

units.la: Officii nostri requirit debitum, ut bona Imperii distracta illicitè vel destructa, ad jus & proprietatem ejusdem Imperii ac utilitatem & commodum nobis subjectorum & Reipublicæ revocemus. Considerantes igitur, quòd nemus nostrum ac Reipub. præjudicium vastatum, & in agros sive novalia à multis retroactis temporibus est redactum: unde fidelitati vestræ, sub Regii favoris obtentu, ac perditione jurium & officiorum vestrorum vobis in ipso nemore competentium districtè præcipiendo mandamus, quatenus infra hinc & festum Omnium Sanctorum proximum certa die collecta vestra coram Sculteto & Consulibus in Nurembergomnes simul & semel exhibeatis præsentiam corporalem, ac manibus vestris sacrosanctis tactis Reliquiis juramentum publicum faciatis, quod dictum nemus à quinquaginta annis citrà destructum, ut prædictum, modis quibuscunq; ac in agros redactum, in statum pristinum, hoc est, in sylvam & arbores, auctoritate Regia redigatis, ac redigi procuretis, non sinentes, quòd aliqui extranei, jus in ipso nemore non habentes, per venditionem aut vias alias capiant vel recipiant aliquem usumfructum, prudentum virorum Civium nostrorum in Nuremberg super præmissis, si necesse fuerit, consilium & auxilium invocantes. Datum in Haimbach, quarto Cal. Septemb. Regni nostri anno secundo.
units.tr: The duty of our office requires that the goods of the Empire, unlawfully sold off or destroyed, be recalled to the right and property of the same Empire, and to the use and advantage of us, its subjects, and of the Commonwealth. Considering therefore that our forest, to the prejudice of the Commonwealth, has been devastated and, for many years past, turned into fields and fallow land, we therefore, by the authority of royal favour, and under penalty of forfeiting your rights and offices which you hold in that same forest, strictly command your fidelity that, before the coming feast of All Saints, on a day appointed, you all together and at once present yourselves in person before the Schultheiss and the Councillors at Nuremberg, and, touching the sacred relics with your consecrated hands, make a public oath that the said forest, destroyed these fifty years past as aforesaid and turned into fields by whatever means, you will restore to its former state, that is, to woodland and trees, by royal authority, and will see that it is so restored, not permitting any outsiders, who have no right in that forest, to take or receive by sale or any other means any usufruct; calling upon the counsel and aid of the prudent men of our citizens of Nuremberg in these matters, if need be. Given at Haimbach, on the fourth day before the Calends of September, in the second year of our reign.

units.la: HENRICI VII. IMPER. AUG. MANDATUM
units.tr: HENRY VII, EMPEROR AUGUSTUS: MANDATE

units.la: DE RESTAVRANDA SYLVA IMPERIALI IN AGROS DESTRVCTA.
units.tr: CONCERNING THE RESTORATION OF THE IMPERIAL FOREST, DESTROYED INTO FIELDS.

units.la: HENRICUS Dei gratia Romanorum Rex Semper-Augustus, Strenuis ac providis viris, Vito Hœrauff, Conrado Stromer, Ottoni, cæterisq; Forestariis ac Zeidlariis nemoris nostri & Imperii perii apud Nuremberg, ab utraque parte fluvii Pegnitz constitutis, fidelibus suis dilectis, gratiam suam & omne bonum. Officii nostri requirit debitum, ut bona Imperii, distracta illicite vel destructa, ad jus & proprietatem ejusdem Imperii, ac utilitatem & commodum nobis subjectorum & Reipublicæ revocemus. Considerantes igitur, quòd nemus nostrum & præfati Imperii apud Nurembergperincendia & extirpationes, in nostrum ac Reipubl. præjudicium, vastatum & in agros sive novalia a multis retroactis temporibus est redactum. Unde fidelitati vestræ, sub Regii favoris obtentu, ac perdiione jurium & officiorum vestrorum, vobis in ipso nemore competentium, districte præcipiendo mandamus, quatenus infra hinc & festum omnium Sanctorum proximum certa die collecta, vestram coram Sculteto & Consulibus in Nuremberg omnes simul & semel exhibeatis præsentiam corporalem, ac manibus vestris, sacrosanctis tactis reliquiis, juramentum publicum faciatis, quòd dictum nemus à quinquaginta annis citrà destructum, ut prædictum, modis quibuscunq; ac in agros redactum, in statum pristinum, hoc est, in sylvam & in arbores, auctoritate Regia redigatis, ac redigi procuretis, non sinentes quod aliqui extranei, jus in ipso nemore non habentes, per venditionem aut vias alias capiant vel recipiant aliquem usumfructum; prudentum virorum Civium nostrorum in Nuremberg super præmissis, si necesse fuerit, consilium & auxilium invocantes. Datum in Haimbach, quarto Calend. Septembr. Regni nostri anno secundo.
units.tr: HENRY, by the grace of God King of the Romans, ever Augustus, to the vigorous and prudent men Veit Hörauff, Konrad Stromer, Otto, and the other foresters and woodsmen of our forest and of the Empire at Nuremberg, stationed on both banks of the river Pegnitz, our faithful and beloved subjects, grace and every good.
