Non enim de præfatis corrigendis seu regulandis per poenam in hoc sæculo transgressoribus inferendam, divina lex aliquid ordinavit aut statuit: neque coactivus judex secundum ipsam contra quenquam in hoc sæculo transgressorem, per se, neque per aliquem successorem, sive Episcopum, sive Presbyterum, aut spiritualem Ministrum, conjunctim vel divisim, mandavit aut voluit coactivum judicium exerceri. Nec ex hiis potest proprie inferri, quod humanæ legi subjaceat lex divina, vel legislator ipsius, sed ut potius econtrario. Nam legislator humanus præcipit fiendum, quod statutum est per divinum legislatorem, aut legem divinam. Neque similiter per ipsius judicem coactivum, Christum videlicet, sed potius econtrario. Verumtamen juste præcipit, quod præcipere potest legislator divinus, & ipsius authoritate judex sive principans coactivus legis humanæ, in istis prædictis & reliquis sæcularibus, nihil illicitum agere circa spiritualia seu de ipsis, nec circa ipsa temporalia vel de ipsis: ac mandat Ministris licita ac sibi debita officia de talibus, ac circa talia exercere, ipsosque rationabiliter in hoc sæculo per poenam arcere personalem atque realem, si transgressi fuerint humanæ legis præcepta, legis divinæ præceptis non repugnantia. Nam ex officio sibi commisso secundum legis divinæ ac humanæ præcepta tenet Episcopos seu Presbyteros ad docendum, prædicandum, & spiritualia Christi fidelibus ministrandum, ut Baptismum, & reliqua similia fidelibus exhibendum. Propter hoc enim ipsis ministrantur carnalia sive corporalia per Christi fideles. Unde Christus: Dignus est enim operarius cibo suo. Et Apostolus 1. Corinth. 9. Si nos vobis spiritualia seminamus, non est magnum, si vestra carnalia (id est, temporalia) metamus. Propter quod quam operarii suscipientes, aut qui susceperunt mercedem, obligati sunt & tenentur, ac arceri poenam in hoc sæculo, ac per coactivum humanum judicem, ad docenda spiritualia, & modo debito & tempore ministranda.
units.tr: 13. In this way, concerning marriage and the other spiritual matters, insofar as they, or the acts of men concerning them and in relation to them, are referred under certain conditions to human laws made about them, a lawgiver may legislate, and it is fitting, indeed necessary, that a coercive secular judge should pass judgment. Thus, as regards a marriage to be contracted or already contracted, many things occur which, through human acts, may be done or omitted lawfully or unlawfully. These must indeed be regulated by the human lawgiver, or by a coercive judge acting under his authority, who restrains transgressors by punishment. Suppose, for example, that after sentence has been passed on a divorce to be made between two spouses, one spouse refuses to leave the other and tries to keep the other by force, or to handle the other's person or goods, as he handled them during the marriage or before the divorce was granted by sentence. Such a person ought to be punished and compelled, in this world, by a real or personal penalty, and by a coercive judge, as one who does not observe the judgment or sentence. For before the divorce a husband was permitted to do certain things to his wife, against her will and to her person and goods, which are not permitted to him after the divorce. For example, he might rebuke and reproach his wife, now separated from him in marriage, and subject her to insulting words; he might demand the marital debt from her; or he might treat her bodily in some other way, by touching her immodestly, or by beating her, or by disposing of her dowry goods and other property without her consent, and things like that. From such acts many serious and dangerous scandals would arise after the divorce, if it were granted. For the sake of removing or forbidding all these things, and for the sake of common and evident utility, indeed necessity, it belongs to the human lawgiver, and he ought, must and can, to legislate, to judge and to compel concerning such things to be done or omitted. That is, he may summon the litigants to appear in court, likewise summon witnesses to speak the truth, restrain transgressors from appearing by punishment, and, finally, pronounce a definitive sentence whether or not the divorce is to be granted. Yet in this he must conform to the divine law, and by his sentence he must command nothing that contradicts its precepts and prohibitions. Moreover, after sentence has been passed, he may compel each of the contending or litigating parties to hold and observe the judgment, inflicting punishment in this world on whoever transgresses the sentence. For the divine law has ordained or established nothing about correcting or regulating these matters by punishment inflicted in this world on transgressors, nor has it commanded or willed that a coercive judge, either himself or through any successor, whether bishop, presbyter, or spiritual minister, jointly or separately, should exercise coercive judgment against anyone in this world who transgresses. Nor can it properly be inferred from these matters that the divine law, or its lawgiver, is subject to human law; rather the reverse. For the human lawgiver commands that to be done which has been established by the divine lawgiver or the divine law. Nor, similarly, is the human coercive judge subject to the divine, namely Christ; rather the reverse. Yet the divine lawgiver rightly commands what he can command, and by his authority the judge or coercive ruler of human law commands, in these matters and in the others of a secular nature, that nothing unlawful be done concerning spiritual matters or about them, nor concerning temporal matters or about them; and he orders the ministers to perform lawful and proper duties concerning and about such matters, and rationally to restrain them in this world by personal and real punishment if they have transgressed the precepts of human law which do not contradict the precepts of divine law. For by the office entrusted to them, according to the precepts of divine and human law, bishops or presbyters are bound to teach, to preach, and to minister spiritual things to the faithful of Christ, such as baptism and other similar things to be given to the faithful. For it is for this reason that carnal or bodily things are ministered to them by the faithful of Christ. Hence Christ says: [Dignus est enim operarius cibo suo] "For the labourer is worthy of his food." And the Apostle, 1 Corinthians 9: [Si nos vobis spiritualia seminamus, non est magnum, si vestra carnalia (that is, temporal things) metamus] "If we have sown spiritual things among you, it is no great thing if we reap your carnal things." Therefore the labourers who receive, or have received, wages are bound and obliged, and in this world are to be restrained by penalty, through the human coercive judge, to teach spiritual things and to minister them at the due time and in the proper manner.

units.la: 14. Ex prædictis igitur evidenter appàret, judicium coactivum sive sententiam proferre, ac exequi per coactivam potestatem, super divortio matrimoniali fieri requisito, ad Romani Principis sive nostram authoritatem, vel eorum quibus per nos concessa fuerit talis authoritas sive potestas, solummodo pertinere. Propter quod ad divortium matrimonii consummandum inter Johannem & Margaretam prædictos.
units.tr: 14. From what has been said it is therefore plainly evident that to pronounce a coercive judgment or sentence, and to execute it by coercive power, concerning a divorce that has been sought, belongs only to the authority of us, the Roman Prince, or of those to whom such authority or power has been granted by us. Accordingly, the divorce of the marriage between the aforesaid John and Margaret is to be carried into effect by us.

units.la: 15. Nos Ludovicus Quartus Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator Augustus, pro tribunali judice sedentes, in causa sive lite divortii seu separationis matrimonii, quæ vertebatur inter Illustres personas, Johannem Regis Bohemiæ filium, requisitum parte ex una, & Margaretham Ducissam Karinthiæ & Tyrolis Comitissam, ex altera parte, tanquam actricem, ac requirentem à dicto Johanne jam vocato conjuge suo de matrimonio separari; Visis & intellectis tam per nos, quàm præfatos Doctores juribus, rationibus, probationibus & testimoniis Margaretæ præfatæ, necnon contumacia jam dicti Johannis, dicimus, diffinimus & determinamus, præfatam Margaretam separari debere seu posse de matrimonio à sæpedicto Johanne, eque converso, cum eisdem vel ipsorum alteriud videbitur expedire. Ipsam quoque Margaretam hoc requirentem instanter, ut supra, separamus, absolvimur, & separatam esse judicamus in matrimonio à jam dicto Johanne per hanc nostram sententiam diffinitivam separantes: ita videlicet, quod de cætero præfatus Johannes supra dictæ Margaretæ in nullo matrimonij debito teneatur, neque similiter præfata Margareta supradicto Johanni: sed liberum sit utrique de corpore proprio sive persona, & omnibus bonis propriis, juribus acrebus tam mobilibus quam immobilibus, facere vel disponere, & quod libet ordinare pro suæ propriæ libero voluntatis.
units.tr: 15. We, Ludwig the Fourth, by the grace of God Roman Emperor, Augustus, sitting as judge on the tribunal, in the cause or suit of divorce or separation of marriage which was being contested between the illustrious persons, John, son of the King of Bohemia, the petitioned party on the one side, and Margaret, Duchess of Carinthia and Countess of Tyrol, on the other side, as plaintiff and as one seeking to be separated in marriage from the said John, now summoned as her spouse; having seen and considered, both by us and by the aforesaid doctors, the laws, arguments, proofs and testimonies of the aforesaid Margaret, and also the contumacy of the said John, we say, define and determine that the aforesaid Margaret ought to be, or can be, separated in marriage from the aforesaid John, and conversely, with whichever of them, or with another, it shall seem expedient. We also, at the instant request of Margaret, as above, separate, absolve and judge her to be separated in marriage from the said John by this our definitive sentence. So that henceforth the aforesaid John shall owe no marital debt to the aforesaid Margaret, nor, likewise, shall the aforesaid Margaret owe it to the aforesaid John; but each shall be free to deal with and dispose of their own body or person and all their own goods, both movable and immovable, and acquired rights, and to order whatever they like by their own free will.

units.la: CAROLI IV. IMPER. AUGUSTI
units.tr: CHARLES IV, EMPEROR AUGUSTUS

units.la: CONFIRMATIO
units.tr: CONFIRMATION

units.la: DE ELECTIONE REGIS BOHEMIAE.
units.tr: CONCERNING THE ELECTION OF THE KING OF BOHEMIA.

units.la: Carolus Dei gratia Romanorum Rex, ad perpetuam rei memoriam. Innata cordi nostro benignitas circa fidelium & devotorum nostrorum honores & commoda continuis vigiliis, votis ipsorum annuentes iugiter nos inducit, quoties postulantium vox est justa. In hoc enim liberalitatis nostræ non errat intentio, sed Regalis sceptri fastigium exrolli salubriter arbitrarur. Sanè ad nostræ Celsitudinis præsentiam venerunt Archiepiscopus Pragensis; Olmucensis, & Vratislaviensis ac Luthomensis Episcopi; necnon Illustres Johannes Carinthiæ Comesque Tyrolis & Goritiæ, germanus noster charissimus, ac Nicolaus Opaviæ & Ranborum Duces, cæterique Prælati, Duces, Principes, Barones, Proceres, & Nobiles Regni nostri Boemiæ, & pertinentiarum ejusdem, præsentiam accedentes, nobis humiliter supplicarunt, ut quasdam literas Friderici Divi Romanorum Imperatoris, prædecessoris nostri, nobis per ipsos exhibitas, quarum renor & series sequitur in hæc verba:
units.tr: Charles, by the grace of God Roman King, to the perpetual memory of the matter. The kindness innate in our heart, concerning the honours and advantages of our faithful and devoted subjects, continually moves us, by daily vigils, to grant their wishes whenever the request of those who ask is just. For in this our generosity does not err in its intention, but judges that it helpfully raises up the dignity of the royal sceptre. Indeed, there came into our presence the Archbishop of Prague, the Bishops of Olmütz, Breslau and Leitomischl, and the illustrious John, Duke of Carinthia and Count of Tyrol and Gorizia, our most beloved brother, and Nicholas, Dukes of Opava and Ratibor, as well as the other prelates, dukes, princes, barons, nobles and lords of our Kingdom of Bohemia and its dependencies. Approaching our presence, they humbly besought us to confirm by royal authority certain letters of Frederick, the divine Roman Emperor, our predecessor, which they had presented to us, the tenor and sequence of which follow in these words:

units.la: Fridericus divina favente clementia Romanorum Imperator Electus & semper Augustus, &c. confirmare autoritate Regia dignaremur. Nos itaque præfatorum Prælatorum, Ducum, Principum, Baronum, Procerum & Nobilium, quos honoris & felicis status Romani Regni, & sacri Imperii fideles & sollicitos præ cæteris novimus delatores, ipsumque Regnum Boemiæ Romani Regni fore membrum nobilius, supplicationibus benignè inclinati, præfatas literas & omnia ac singula contenta in eisdem ratificamus, laudamus, approbamus, confirmamus & de novo ex certa scientia de nostræ Romanæ Regiæ plenitudine potestatis, præfatis Regni Prælatis, Ducibus, Principibus, Baronibus, Procerbus & Nobilibus, ac Universitati Regni ipsius, & pertinentiarum ejusdem ad usum & opus Regum Boemiæ in perpetuum damus tenore præsentium, conferimus & donamus, omnem diminutionem & defectum, si quis in præmissis fuerit, de uberiori dono Majestatis Romanæ Regiæ & plenitudine potestatis reparamus omnimodò & supplentes.
units.tr: Frederick, by the favour of divine clemency, Emperor of the Romans, elect and always Augustus, etc. We would deign to confirm by royal authority... Therefore, inclining graciously to the petitions of the aforesaid prelates, dukes, princes, barons, lords and nobles, whom we know to be, beyond the others, faithful and solicitous promoters of the honour and happy state of the Roman Kingdom and the Holy Empire, and recognising that the Kingdom of Bohemia is a most noble member of the Roman Kingdom, we ratify, praise, approve and confirm the aforesaid letters and all and each of the things contained in them. And anew, from certain knowledge and from the fullness of our Roman royal power, by the tenor of these present letters we give, confer and grant to the aforesaid prelates, dukes, princes, barons, lords and nobles of the said Kingdom, and to the whole community of that Kingdom and its dependencies, for the use and benefit of the Kings of Bohemia, in perpetuity. Whatever diminution or defect there may be in the foregoing, we repair and wholly supply from the more abundant gift of the Majesty of the Roman King and the fullness of power.

units.la: 2. Verum cum contra ea contenta literis nonnulli calumniari aut interpretari sinistrè, seu in sensum reprobum declarare; imò verius obscurare forsitan niterentur, ad tollendum de medio omne dubium vel obscurum, quibus dictarum series aspergitur literarum. Ut Regni Bohemiæ præfati ipsius incolarum status in syncera Imperii dilectione perseveret concordia & unitatem in vinculo pacis conservet: ac incolæ dicti Regni his, quæ dissentiæ causa & materia esse possent, remporibus profuturis, & animarum ac corporum inde nascituris periculis, rerumque dispendiis proventuris, solerti præventione, antequam oriantur, tam prudenter quam salubriter præcilis, manifesti terram hereditent, & in pacis multitudine delectentur electionem Regis Boëmiæ in casu duntaxat & eventu, quibus degenealogia, progenie vel femine aut prosapia Regali Boemiæ masculus vel femella superstes legitimus, quod Deus avertat, nullus fuerit oriundus, vel per quemcunque alium modum vacare contigerit, dictum Regnum ad Prælatos, Duces Principes, Barones, & Nobiles, & communitatem Regni Prælati, & pertinentiarum ejusdem: habitaque cum nonnullis Romanorum Regis, futuri Imperatoris, Electoribus, & aliis Principibus, qui tunc temporis nostræ Celsitudinis præsentiæ assistebant, deliberatione matura, ipsorumque sano digesto consilio, volumus, decernimus, pronuntiamus, interpretamur, & præsentis scripti patrocinio declaramus, rite, juste in perpetuum possidere ipsius Regis Boëmiæ electionem in casu & eventu prædictis, & non aliis, præfatis Prælatis, Ducibus, Principibus, Baronibus, Nobilibus & Communitati dicti Regni & pertinentiarum ejusdem, de nostræ Romanæ plenitudine potestatis, ac ex certa scientia, damus, concedimus, conferimus & donamus, dictamque electionem meliorem, salubriorem & firmiorem, quo potest, modo fieri confirmamus & transferimus in eosdem: volentes etiam ut quicunque in Regem Boemiæ electus fuerit, ad nos & successores nostros Romanorum Reges & Imperatores accedat, suaæ à nobis modo debito & solito regalia accepturus: non obstantibus legibus, consuetudinibus, usibus, observantiis, juribus municipalibus vel communibus, statutis & edictis, factis & editis in contrarium quibuscumque. quas & quæ, quantum ad hoc, ac si forent nominatim & de verbo ad verbum scripta præsentibus & inserta, revocamus, cassamus, irritamus, annihilamus, & de dictæ Romanæ Regiæ plenitudine potestatis decrevimus firmitatis fore nullius penitus vel momenti.
units.tr: 2. But since some might attempt to calumniate the contents of those letters, to interpret them unfavourably, to declare them in a reprobate sense, or indeed perhaps to obscure them, in order to remove from the midst every doubt or obscurity with which the sequence of the said letters is clouded: so that the state of the aforesaid inhabitants of the Kingdom of Bohemia may persevere in sincere love of the Empire, and that the concord and unity of the inhabitants of the said Kingdom may be preserved in the bond of peace, we, by a timely and salutary foresight, before they arise, wisely and beneficially cut off those things which could be the cause and matter of dissension, and the dangers to souls and bodies and the losses of goods which would arise from them in future times; so that they may inherit the land in clear right and delight in the abundance of peace. We have decided, after mature deliberation and with the sound counsel of some electors of the Roman King, future Emperor, and other princes who at that time attended our presence, that the election of the King of Bohemia shall belong to the prelates, dukes, princes, barons, nobles and community of the said Kingdom and its dependencies, in the case and event only in which, from the lineage, progeny, seed or stock of the Bohemian royal house, no male or female legitimate survivor is born (which God forbid), or in which the throne becomes vacant by any other means. We will, decree, pronounce, interpret and declare by the patronage of these present writings, that they may rightly and justly possess the election of the King of Bohemia in perpetuity, in the aforesaid case and event and in no other. From the fullness of our Roman power and from certain knowledge, we give, concede, confer and grant this election to the aforesaid prelates, dukes, princes, barons, nobles and community of the said Kingdom and its dependencies, and we confirm and transfer the said election into them in the best, most salutary and firmest manner possible. We also will that whoever shall be elected King of Bohemia shall come to us and our successors, Roman Kings and Emperors, to receive the royal regalia from us in the due and accustomed manner. Notwithstanding any laws, customs, usages, observances, municipal or common rights, statutes and edicts, made and issued to the contrary, which, so far as this matter is concerned, we revoke, quash, annul and nullify, just as if they were written here by name and word for word; and by the fullness of the said Roman royal power we have decreed that they shall be of no force or weight whatever.

units.la: 3. Insuper ad universorum & singulorum notitiam cupimus pervenire, quòd prædictæ literæ Bullæ Aureæ cum Majestatis præfati Friderici Romanorum Imperatoris Electi, qua ipse Rex Siciliæ Dux Apuliæ, & Princeps Capuæ ante coronationem Regni Romanorum solemniter utebatur, plenarie informati: & sicut gloriosæ memoriæ Henricus avus noster, quondam Romanorum Imperator, sigillo Comitatus Luxemburgensis, & ceteri Divi Romanorum Imperatores Electi prædecessores nostri, suorum titulorum: nosque etiam Marchionatus Moraviæ sigillo autentico ante ipsorum & nostræ coronationis solemnitatem usi fuimus. In cujus Bullæ Aureæ circumferentia ferentia aperte Majestatis scripta sunt verba ista: FRIDERICUS DEI GRATIA SICILIÆ REX, DUX APULIÆ ET PRINCEPS CAPUÆ. Etab illa parte, ubi est impressio castri, XPS VINCIT, XPS REGNAT, XPS IMPERAT, existunt sane & integre, omni carentes vitio.
units.tr: 3. Furthermore, we wish it to come to the notice of all and each that the aforesaid letters, the Golden Bull, were fully examined with the seal of the aforesaid Frederick, Roman Emperor elect, which he himself, as King of Sicily, Duke of Apulia and Prince of Capua, solemnly used before his coronation as King of the Romans; and as Henry, our grandfather of glorious memory, formerly Roman Emperor, used the seal of the County of Luxemburg, and the other divine Roman Emperors elect, our predecessors, used their titles; and we too used the authentic seal of the Margraviate of Moravia before the solemnity of their coronation and of ours. On the circumference of this Golden Bull the following words of the Majesty are openly written: FREDERICK, BY THE GRACE OF GOD KING OF SICILY, DUKE OF APULIA AND PRINCE OF CAPUA. And on that side where the impression of the castle is, there stand, indeed whole and free from every defect: CHRIST CONQUERS, CHRIST REIGNS, CHRIST COMMANDS.

units.la: 4. Nulli ergo omnino liceat hanc nostræ laudationis, ratificationis, approbationis, confirmationis, donationis, reparationis, supplementi, interpretationis, declarationis, revocationis, cassationis, irritationis, & annihilationis paginam infringere, vel ei ausu temerario in aliquo contraire. Contrarium facientes, si qui fuerint, quod absit, ultra indignationem nostræ Celsitudinis Romanæ, quam ob hoc se noverint graviter incursuros, mille marcas auri puri nostro & Romani Regni fisco componant: ipsarum videlicet mediratem nostræ & successorum nostrorum Romanorum Regum & Imperatorum Curiæ seu Cameræ; & reliquam passis injuriam, irremissibiliter applicandam.
units.tr: 4. Therefore let no one at all be permitted to infringe this page of our praise, ratification, approval, confirmation, gift, repair, supplement, interpretation, declaration, revocation, quashing, annulment and abolition, or to act in any rash way contrary to it in any respect. Should any, which God forbid, act contrary, let them know that they will incur, besides the grave indignation of our Roman Majesty, a fine of a thousand marks of pure gold, to be paid to the treasury of ours and of the Roman Kingdom: one half to the court or chamber of us and of our successors, Roman Kings and Emperors, and the remainder to be applied without remission to the party injured.

units.la: 5. In quorum omnium testimonium & ad certitudinem plenio-rem præsentes fieri jussimus, & nostræ majestatis sigilli appensione muniri. Hujus rei testes sunt: Gerlacus Archiepiscopus Moguntinensis, sacri Imperii per Germaniam Archicancellarius. Rudolphus Senior Saxoniæ Dux, sacri Imperii Marescalcus. Rudolphus Junior Saxoniæ | Duces. & Fridericus de Teck Joannes Burggravius Nurmbergensis. Ulricus Landgravius de Lutemberg. Fridericus de Orlemund, | Comites. Ulrich de Helfenstein, | & Rudolphus de Wertheim Petrus de Herfii, Crafto de Hohenloh Gottfridus de Bruneck, | Romani Regni Præfati Principes & Barones. Eberhardus & Fridericus de Valse, Eglof de Friburg, & Burckhardus de Erlbach,
units.tr: 5. In testimony of all these things, and for fuller certainty, we have ordered these present letters to be made and secured by the appending of the seal of our Majesty. The witnesses of this matter are: Gerlach, Archbishop of Mainz, Archchancellor of the Holy Empire throughout Germany; Rudolf the Elder, Duke of Saxony, Marshal of the Holy Empire; Rudolf the Younger, Dukes of Saxony; and Frederick of Teck, John Burgrave of Nuremberg, Ulrich, Landgrave of Lüttemberg; Frederick of Orlamünde, Ulrich of Helfenstein and Rudolf of Wertheim, Counts; Peter of Herfi, Crafft of Hohenlohe, Gottfried of Bruneck, Princes and Barons of the Roman Kingdom; Eberhard and Frederick of Walsee, Eglof of Freiburg, and Burkhard of Erlbach.

units.la: Datum Pragæ, Anno Domini MCCCXLVIII. Indictione prima, VII. Idus Aprilis: Regnorum nostrorum anno II.
units.tr: Given at Prague, in the year of the Lord 1348, in the first indiction, on the seventh day before the Ides of April, in the second year of our reigns.

units.la: CAROLI IV. IMPER. AUG. RESCRIPTUM DE PRIMARIIS PRECIBVS.
units.tr: CHARLES IV, EMPEROR AUGUSTUS: A RESCRIPT CONCERNING PRIMARY PRAYERS (PRECES PRIMARIAE).

units.la: Anno Christi 1353.
units.tr: In the year of Christ 1353.

units.la: KAROLUS Dei gratia Romanorum Rex semper Augustus & Bohemiæ Rex, honorabilibus Præpositio & Conventui Canonicorum Regularium monasterii in Revengersburch Ordinis Sancti Augustini Moguntinæ diœcesios, devotis nostris dilectis gratiam Regiam & omne bonum. Assumpti divinitus, quamvis insufficientibus meritis, ad culmen regiæ dignitatis, libenter personas Ecclesiasticas promovemus, ipsisque gratiam à Deo collatam gratiosius impartimur. Cum itaque nobis tam de jure quam antiqua & approbata consuetudine, à divis Romanorum Imperatoribus & Regibus prædecessoribus nostris hactenus observata, competat, quod ex coronationis nostræ solemniis ad Romanorum regnum, quæ in nobis nuru divino dudum sunt completa, in quolibet monasterio in Imperio constituto unam tantum personam virtute primariarum precum nostrarum ad beneficium Ecclesiasticum facere possimus promoveri. Hinc est quod pro dilecto nobis Perro Conradi de Dylle presbytero devoto nostro dilecto vobis primarias dirigimus preces nostras, devotioni vestræ attento studio inquirimus, & hortamur, vobis nihilominus per regalia sceptra mandates, quatenus præfato Petro aut ipsius procuratori ac nomine & vice ipsius de beneficio Ecclesiastico cum cura vel sine cura, quod vacat ad præsens, vel quod primum vacaverit, ad vestram præsentationem, collationem, seu quamvis aliam dispositionem spectans, in quacunque diœcesi aut Moguntina aut Treverensi, aut aliis quibuscunque diœcesibus hujusmodi beneficium constitutum fuerit, auctoritate & virtute primariarum precum nostrarum providere debeatis, quavis contradictione cessante, dummodo vobis pro alia persona prius non direxerimus preces nostras: jus nostrum & dictam consuetudinem in præmissis nobis taliter servatum, prout jura, gratias & liberalitates vobis & dicto vestro monasterio à divis Romanorum Impp. & regibus prædecessoribus nostris datas & concessas nos delectet non minuere sed augere; præsentium sub nostro majestatis sigillo testimonio literarum. Datum Spyræ, Anno Domini MCCCL. tertio, Indictione sexta, 6. Kal. Decemb. Regnorum nostrorum anno octavo.
units.tr: Karl, by the grace of God Roman King, ever Augustus, and King of Bohemia, to the honourable Provost and Convent of the Regular Canons of the monastery at Revengersburch, of the Order of St Augustine, in the diocese of Mainz, our devoted and beloved subjects: royal favour and every blessing. Raised by God, though with insufficient merits, to the summit of royal dignity, we gladly advance ecclesiastical persons and more graciously bestow upon them the grace given by God. Since, therefore, we are entitled both by law and by ancient and approved custom, hitherto observed by the divine Roman Emperors and Kings our predecessors, to make one person, by virtue of our primary prayers, eligible for an ecclesiastical benefice in each monastery within the Empire, upon the solemnities of our coronation to the Roman kingdom, which by divine will have long since been fulfilled in us, hence it is that we send our primary prayers to you on behalf of our beloved Peter Conradi de Dylle, a priest and our devoted beloved one. With earnest care we seek and exhort your devotion, and we further command you by the royal sceptre that, to the aforesaid Peter, or to his proxy acting in his name and place, you must provide, by the authority and virtue of our primary prayers, a benefice with or without cure of souls which is vacant at present or which shall first fall vacant, belonging to your presentation, collation, or any other disposition, in whatever diocese, whether Mainz or Trier or any other diocese, such benefice may be situated; any opposition ceasing, provided we have not previously sent our prayers on behalf of another person. In these matters, our right and the said custom, thus preserved for us, we are pleased to augment rather than diminish, just as we are pleased to maintain the rights, graces and liberalities granted and conceded to you and to your said monastery by the divine Roman Emperors and kings our predecessors. In witness whereof we have given these letters under our majesty's seal. Given at Speyer, in the year of the Lord 1350, in the third year, in the sixth indiction, on the 6th day before the Kalends of December, in the eighth year of our reign.

units.la: CAROLI IV. IMP. AUG. FORMULA CONCESSAE SEDIS LIBERAE, ET FRYGRAVIATVS.
units.tr: Formula of Emperor Charles IV Augustus: the grant of a free seat and Frygraviatus

units.la: Anno Christi 1354.
units.tr: In the year of Christ 1354.

units.la: CAROLUS Dei gratia Romanorum Rex Semper-Augustus, & Bohemiæ Rex, ad perpetuam rei memoriam. Etsi Regiæ dignitatis circumspecta benignitas universos & singulos fideles suos, quos Romanum ambit Imperium, pio favore persequitur: ad illorum tamen statum & cómo-da proda promovenda, specialiùs & ferventiùs aspirare tenetur, quos pro exaltandis sacri Imperii honoribus, fide & opere repererit continua solicitudine, assiduisque laboribus indefessos. Attendentes itaque multa grata servitia & accepta, quae Venerabilis Theodoricus Mindensis Ecclesiae Episcopus, Princeps Consiliarius & devotus noster dilectus, nobis & sacro Imperio fructuosè & fideliter hactenus exhibuit, exhibet in praesenti, & exhibiturum speramus fructuosiùs in futurum, volentesque sibi intuitu praemissorum gratiam facere specialem, ei in persona & successoribus suis, ac ipsi Ecclesiae Mindensi duas liberas sedes, quae proprie & vulgariter Vemeding nuncupantur, unam videlicet ante villam Halcri prope Lubek, & aliam ante villam Walnen prope Mindam, de liberalitate Regia & certa nostra scientia damus, concedimus & donamus; statuentes, decernentes auctoritate praesentium, & volentes, ut dictus Episcopus successores sui, ac ipsa Mindensis Ecclesia, dictas duas sedes cum universis & singulis iurisdictionibus, honoribus, praerogativis, iuribus, gratiis, utilitatibus, commodis & libertatibus tenere, habere ac ipsis gaudere debeant, quibus caeteri consimiles sedes habentes, sicut Ducatus Ascaniae & Westfaliae gaudent, iure vel consuetudine seu quomodolibet potiuntur. Mandamus igitur universis & singulis Principibus tam spiritualibus quàm secularibus, Baronibus, Nobilibus, Universitatibus, caeterisque nostris & sacri Imperii fidelibus cujuscunque dignitatis, conditionis vel status existant, praesentibus & futuris, firmiter & districtè, quatenus praedictum Theodoricum Episcopum, successores suos, & ipsam Ecclesiam Mindensem, in hac nostra donationis & collationis gratia, non impediant, nec ab aliis impediri permittant, verùm eos in ea manuteneant, protegant, favorabiliter & conservent. Contrarium facientes poenam banni Regii & centum marcharum auri se noverint irremissibiliter incursuros, quarum medietatem Regiae Camerae sive Fisco, residuum verò Venerabilium Episcoporum dictae Mindensis Ecclesiae, qui pro tempore fuerint, utilitati & usibus volumus applicari, praesentium sub nostrae Majestatis sigillo testimonio literarum. Datum Franckfordiae, Anno Domini MCCCLIV. Indictione septima, xviii. Kalend. Februarii, Regnorum nostrorum anno octavo.
units.tr: CHARLES, by the grace of God King of the Romans, ever Augustus, and King of Bohemia, to everlasting remembrance of the matter. Although the watchful kindness of royal dignity pursues all and each of its faithful subjects, whom the Roman Empire embraces, with loyal favour, it is nevertheless bound to strive more especially and more fervently for the advancement of the status and advantages of those whom it finds, by constant care and tireless labours, untiring in the exaltation of the honours of the holy Empire, in faith and in work. Therefore, considering the many pleasing and welcome services which the Venerable Theodoric, Bishop of the Church of Minden, our Counsellor-Prince and devoted beloved one, has hitherto faithfully and fruitfully rendered to us and to the holy Empire, renders at present, and which we hope he will render more fruitfully in future; and wishing to grant him a special grace in view of these matters, we give, grant and bestow upon him, in his person and in his successors, and upon the Church of Minden itself, two free seats, which are properly and commonly called Vemeding: namely one before the village of Halcri near Lübeck, and another before the village of Walnen near Minden, by royal generosity and our certain knowledge. By the authority of these presents we decree, ordain and will that the said Bishop, his successors, and the Church of Minden itself, should hold and have these two seats with all and each of their jurisdictions, honours, prerogatives, rights, graces, advantages, conveniences and liberties, and should enjoy them, just as the other seats of the like kind enjoy them, as the Duchies of Anhalt and Westphalia enjoy and possess them by right, custom, or in any other way. We therefore command all and each of the Princes, both spiritual and secular, Barons, Nobles, communities, and our other faithful subjects of the Holy Empire, present and future, of whatever dignity, condition or status they may be, firmly and strictly, that they do not hinder the aforesaid Bishop Theodoric, his successors, and the Church of Minden itself, in this our gift and grant of grace, nor permit them to be hindered by others, but rather that they uphold, protect, favour and preserve them in it. Those acting to the contrary shall know that they will incur without remission the penalty of the Royal ban and one hundred marks of gold, half of which we will to be applied to the Royal Treasury or Fisc, and the remainder to the uses and advantage of the Venerable Bishops of the said Church of Minden who shall be in office at the time. In witness of these presents under the seal of our Majesty. Given at Frankfurt, in the year of the Lord 1354, in the seventh indiction, on the eighteenth day before the Kalends of February, in the eighth year of our reign.

units.la: RECOGNITIO QUOD IMPERATRICI IMPONITUR DIADEMA in Aquisgrano.
units.tr: Recognition that the diadem was placed on the Empress at Aachen.

units.la: UNIVERSIS sacri Imperii Romani fidelibus & subditis, Wilhelmus Dei gratia sanctae Coloniensis Ecclesiae Archiepiscopus, sacri Imperii per Italiam Archicancellarius, salutem. Sacris nuper literalibus Serenissimi ac invictissimi Domini CAROLI, Dei gratia Romanorum Semper Augusti & Bohemiae Regis receptis affatibus, quibus nobis idem Dominus noster demandare curavit, prout etiam nobis apud ipsius Regiam Majestatem personaliter constitutis duxit viva voce oraculo committendum, quatenus Serenissimam Dominam nostram Annam ipsius consortem Romanorum Reginam augurare, iungere, consecrare, Regniq; diadema eidem imponere curaremus: Nos in ipsius Dominae nostrae comitatu ac obsequio, ut decebat, Aquisgranum perreximus, ac ibidem in Ecclesia Beatae Mariae Aquensis, in qua ex more Divi Romanorum Reges & Reginae inungi, consecrari & coronari consueverunt, infra Missarum solennia, cum ea, qua decuit, solennitate per nos officiosè celebrata, eandem Serenissimam Dominam nostram in Romanorum Reginam cum ceremoniis & solennitatibus debitis & consuetis propensiùs & observatis, inunximus & consecravimus, ipsamque in solio Regiae Majestatis collocantes, in Reverendorum Patrum & Dominorum, Episcoporum, Abbatum, & aliorum Praelatorum, necnon Procerum, Comitum, Nobilium, Baronum, Regni fidelium, populíque innumeri multitudinis praesentia, eidem Dominae nostrae sacri Romani Regni imposuimus diadema. In quorum testimonium hanc paginam conscribi, nostrique majoris sigilli appensione fecimus communiri. Datum & actum in Ecclesia Beatae Mariae Virginis Aquensis, Leodiensis dioecesis, Anno Domini MCCCLIV. Dominic. Septuagesima, quae fuit mensis Februarii die nona.
units.tr: To all the faithful and subjects of the Holy Roman Empire, Wilhelm, by the grace of God Archbishop of the Holy Church of Cologne, Archchancellor of the Holy Empire through Italy, greeting. Having lately received the sacred letters and spoken instructions of the most serene and invincible lord, Lord CHARLES, by the grace of God ever August King of the Romans and of Bohemia, by which our said lord took care to entrust us with a charge, and also, when we were personally present before his Royal Majesty, he deigned to commit to us by a living voice, namely that we should anoint, join in marriage, consecrate, and place the diadem of the kingdom upon the most serene Lady Anne, his consort, our Lady, as Queen of the Romans: we, in attendance upon and in service to the same our Lady, as was fitting, proceeded to Aachen, and there, in the church of the Blessed Mary of Aachen, in which the Divine Kings and Queens of the Romans have customarily been anointed, consecrated and crowned according to custom, during the solemn Masses, with that solemnity which was fitting, celebrated by us dutifully, we anointed and consecrated the same most serene Lady, our Lady, as Queen of the Romans, with the due and customary ceremonies and solemnities, more fully and observed; and, setting her upon the throne of his Royal Majesty, in the presence of the Reverend Fathers and Lords, the Bishops, Abbots and other Prelates, as well as the Nobles, Counts, Noblemen, Barons, the faithful of the Kingdom, and an innumerable multitude of people, we placed the diadem of the Holy Roman Kingdom upon the same our Lady. In testimony of which we have caused this page to be written and fortified by the appending of our greater seal. Given and done in the church of the Blessed Virgin Mary of Aachen, diocese of Liège, in the year of the Lord 1354, on Dominica Septuagesima, which was the ninth day of the month of February.

units.la: CAROLI IV. IMPER. AUG. CONSTITUTIO
units.tr: CONSTITUTION OF THE EMPEROR CHARLES IV, AUGUSTUS

units.la: DE OFFICIO ARCHICANCELLARII IMPERATRICIS IN CORO- NATIONE EJUS & ALIAS OBSERVANDO.
units.tr: CONCERNING THE OFFICE OF THE ARCHCHANCELLOR IN HIS CORONATION OF THE EMPRESS AND OTHER MATTERS TO BE OBSERVED.

units.la: DECERNIMUS, & hoc Imperiali sancimus edicto: quod tu, & omnes tui successores Abbates Fuldenses, dum & quotiens Imperatricem sive Reginam Romanam coronari, aut in veste Imperiali seu Regia sedere vel stare contigerit, tu & dicti successores tui coronam suam, quotiens more vel ordine poscente, à capite ipsius deponi debuerit, & deponendi eandem ac tenendi, & etiam reponendi, quotiens necesse fuerit, fungi debeatis officio, ut ex hoc dictum Cancellariatus officium, necnon insignis Fuldensis Ecclesia, tanquam nobile membrum Imperii, propensiùs honoretur.
units.tr: We decree, and by this imperial edict we sanction, that you and all your successors, the Abbots of Fulda, shall, whenever and as often as the Empress or Queen of the Romans happens to be crowned, or to sit or stand in imperial or royal robes, perform the office of removing her crown from her head, as often as custom or order requires it to be removed, and of holding it, and also of replacing it, as often as it is necessary; so that by this means the office of the Chancellery, and the distinguished Church of Fulda, as a noble member of the Empire, may be honoured the more.

units.la: CAROLI IV. IMPER. AUG. CONFIRMATIO CONSTITUTIONIS Ludovicianæ.
units.tr: Confirmation of the Constitution of Ludwig by Charles IV, Emperor Augustus

units.la: DE IVRE ET SVCCESSIONE ELECTORVM PAL- ATINORVM.
units.tr: Concerning the right and succession of the Palatine Electors

units.la: CAROLUS Dei gratia Romanorum Rex Semper-Augustus, & Bohemiæ Rex; notum facimus universis, quòd constitutus in nostra præsentia Illustris Rupertus senior Comes Palatinus Rheni, sacri Imperii Archidapifer & Dux Bavariæ, sororius & Princeps noster dilectus, nobis quasdam literas claræ memoriæ Illustris Johannis quondam Bohemiæ Regis, genitoris nostri dilecti, curavit ostendere, ut de tenore ipsarum dignaremur testimonium perhibere. Quarum tenor sequitur in hæc verba.
units.tr: We, Charles, by the grace of God King of the Romans, ever Augustus, and King of Bohemia, make known to all that the illustrious Rupert the Elder, Count Palatine of the Rhine, Archdapifer of the Holy Empire and Duke of Bavaria, our brother-in-law and beloved Prince, appeared before us and was pleased to show us certain letters of the illustrious John, of blessed memory, formerly King of Bohemia, our beloved father, so that we might deign to bear witness to their tenor. The tenor of these follows in these words.

units.la: Nos JOHANNES Dei gratia Bohemiæ Rex ac Lucenburgensis Comes, notum esse volumus tenore præsentium universis, nos vidisse & plenè perlegisse literas Serenissimi Principis, Domini LUDOVICI Romanorum Imperatoris, & Domini Ludovici Marchionis Brandenburgensis, continentes ordinationem & tractatum de Comitibus Palatinis Rheni, quis ipsorum jus seu vocem electionis in Romano Imperio seu Rege Romanorum quamprimùm eligendo habere merito deberet. Ex quibus siquidem literis prædictis liquidè apparet, Excellenti Principi Domino Rudolfo Comiti Palatino Rheni ac Duci Bavariæ, quamprimùm opportunitas ad hoc se offerret, ut Romanorum Rex eligi deberet, competere jus & vocem in electione duntaxat, & nulli alteri personæ. Eo igitur per dictum Dominum Rudolfum supplicatum nobis extitit, ut ordinationi prænotatæ in prædictis literis contentæ nostrum præbere vellemus consensum benevolum & assensum. Nos itaque, tanquam is ad quem hoc de jure, sicut ad Principem & Elector Imperii, spectare dinoscitur, supplicationibus prædicti Domini Ducis annuere cupientes, præfatam ordinationem factam per literas prædictas ratificamus, & nostrum ei præbemus consensum, assertionem & assensum expressum, recognoscentes ipsum in prima electione futuri Regis Romanorum eligendi faciendâ habere vocem eligendi, tanquam Principem & nostrum in ipsa electione Coelectorem, harum nostrarum testimonio literarum. Datum Franckfurt, quinta feria proxima ante diem Palmarum, Anno Domini MCCCXXXIX.
units.tr: We, John, by the grace of God King of Bohemia and Count of Luxemburg, wish it to be known by the tenor of these presents to all that we have seen and fully read the letters of the most serene Prince, the Lord Ludwig, Emperor of the Romans, and of the Lord Ludwig, Margrave of Brandenburg, containing the ordinance and agreement concerning the Counts Palatine of the Rhine, and who of them ought rightly to have the right or vote of election in the Roman Empire or in electing the King of the Romans as soon as it should be held. From the said letters it indeed plainly appears that the most excellent Prince, the Lord Rudolf, Count Palatine of the Rhine and Duke of Bavaria, should have the right and vote in the election alone, and no other person, whenever the opportunity should offer itself for the King of the Romans to be elected. Therefore, at the petition of the said Lord Rudolf, it was made known to us that we would be pleased to give our benevolent consent and assent to the ordinance noted above, contained in the said letters. We, therefore, as the one to whom this right, as to a Prince and Elector of the Empire, is known to belong, desiring to grant the supplications of the aforesaid Lord Duke, do ratify the aforesaid ordinance made by the said letters, and give him our consent, assertion and express assent, acknowledging him to have the vote of electing in the first election of the future King of the Romans to be made, as a Prince and our fellow Elector in that election, by the testimony of these our letters. Given at Frankfurt, on the Thursday next before Palm Sunday, in the year of the Lord 1339.

units.la: Nos igitur ad universorum noticiam volumus pervenire, quòd easdem literas sub proprijs figuris & elementis, & sub sigillo majori consueto dicti genitoris nostri in vera figura sigillatas vidimus, & de veritate & integritate ipsarum testimonium perhibemus, præsentium sub nostro sigillo testimonio literarum. Datum in Keyserspergh, Anno Domini MCCCLIV. xi Kalend. Junii, Regnorum nostrorum anno octavo.
units.tr: We therefore wish it to come to the notice of all that we have seen the same letters, sealed with their proper figures and characters, and with the customary greater seal of our said father, in their true figure, and we bear witness to their truth and integrity, by the testimony of these presents under our seal. Given at Kaiserspergh, in the year of the Lord 1354, on the eleventh day before the Kalends of June, in the eighth year of our reign.

units.la: CAROLI IV. IMPER. AUG. MANDATUM
units.tr: CHARLES IV, EMPEROR AUGUSTUS: MANDATE

units.la: DE IVRE ET SVCCESSIONE ELECTORVM PALATINORVM.
units.tr: CONCERNING THE RIGHT AND SUCCESSION OF THE PALATINE ELECTORS.

units.la: KAROLUS Dei gratia Romanorum Rex Semper-Augustus, & Bohemiæ Rex, Rudolpho Saxoniæ Duci, &c. Princeps & avuncule dilecte, literas felicis recordationis Illustris Johannis olim Bohemiæ Regis, genitoris nostri carissimi, vero suo sigillo pendenti sigillatas vidimus, expresse continentes, quòd felicis recordationis Illustris Rudolffus, olim Comes Palatinus Rheni & Dux Bavariæ, Princeps & socer noster dilectus, ratione dicti Comitatus sacri Imperii esset Elector, & eo justitia suadente rationabiliter declaravimus, Illustrem Ruperetum antiquiorem Comitem Palatinum Rheni & Ducem Bavariæ, sororium & Principem nostrum dilectum, dicti olim Rudolffi socerum nostri germanum, verum Imperii Principem Electorem fore, & unà cum aliis sacri Imperii Principibus Electoribus veram eligendi vocem Romanorum Regem in Imperatorem promovendum habere, prout in literis nostro sub appresso sigillo sigillata præmissa singula lucidius contineri videbis. Et quia prælibata rationem sapiunt, dilectionem nam atteneto studio requirimus, exhortamur, ut super eadem materia literas tuo sub sigillo sigillatas præfato Ruperto Principi nostro juxta formulam notulæ, quam tibi præsentibus mittimus interclusam, in qua nil aliud continetur, quàm in nostra litera est expressum, eo dumtaxat excepto, quòd nos sub certis modo & forma, & tua dilectio sub aliis, loquimur, prout convenit, velis exhibere. Datum Oppenheim, anno Domini MCCCLIV. feria tertia proxima post Ascensionem Domini nostri: Regnorum nostrorum octavo.
units.tr: Charles, by the grace of God King of the Romans, ever Augustus, and King of Bohemia, to Rudolf, Duke of Saxony, etc., our prince and dear uncle: We have seen the letters of the illustrious John, of happy memory, formerly King of Bohemia, our most beloved father, sealed with his true seal hanging from them, which expressly state that the illustrious Rudolf, of happy memory, formerly Count Palatine of the Rhine and Duke of Bavaria, our beloved prince and father-in-law, was by reason of the said County of the Holy Empire an Elector; and that we, as justice required, reasonably declared that the illustrious Rupert the Elder, Count Palatine of the Rhine and Duke of Bavaria, our beloved brother-in-law and prince, the German brother of the said Rudolf our father-in-law, is the true Elector of the Empire, and, together with the other Electors, Princes of the Holy Empire, has the true right of voting in the election of the Roman King to be promoted to Emperor; as you will see the aforesaid particulars set out more clearly in our letters sealed with our seal attached. And since the aforesaid matters are reasonable, we request and exhort your affection, with diligent zeal, that you be willing to present letters sealed with your seal on this same matter to the aforesaid Prince Rupert, our prince, according to the form of the note which we send you enclosed with these presents. In that note nothing else is contained than what is expressed in our letter, except only that we speak under certain conditions and in a certain manner, and your affection speaks under others, as is fitting. Given at Oppenheim, in the year of the Lord 1354, on the Tuesday next after the Ascension of our Lord, in the eighth year of our reign.

units.la: CAROLI IV. IMPER. AUG. CONSTITUTIO
units.tr: CAROLI IV. IMPER. AUG. CONSTITUTIO

units.la: DE INCORPORATIONE DVCATVVM POLONIAE ET SILESIAE, & Marchionatus Lusatiae, quòd perpetuò Regno Bohemiæ sint indivisibiliter counita.
units.tr: CONCERNING THE INCORPORATION OF THE DUCHIES OF POLAND AND SILESIA, AND OF THE MARGRAVIATE OF LUSATIA, SO THAT THEY ARE PERPETUALLY AND INDIVISIBLY UNITED WITH THE KINGDOM OF BOHEMIA.

units.la: IN nomine Domini Sanctæ & individuæ Trinitatis. CAROLUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator Semper-Augustus, &c. ad perpetuam rei memoriam. Insignes laudabilis famæ titulos moderni temporis meretur gloriosa posteritas, si quod prædecessorum Illustrium circumspecta prudentia instauravit provisio, vigilanti cura prosequitur, & gratæ solicitudinis munit officio, ut fructuosi(?) ris solertia perenni successorum commendentur memoriæ, & ex perfectione bonorum operum, quæ ex relucenti speculo vetustatis surgat de felicibus mortuis felix memoria rediviva.
units.tr: In the name of the Lord, of the holy and undivided Trinity. Charles, by the grace of God Roman Emperor, ever August, etc., to the perpetual memory of the matter. Glorious posterity deserves the distinguished titles of praiseworthy fame of the present age, if it carefully pursues with watchful concern what the prudent foresight of illustrious predecessors established, and performs the office of grateful solicitude, so that the diligence of the more fruitful may be commended to the everlasting memory of successors, and so that, from the perfection of good works which rises from the shining mirror of antiquity, the happy memory of the fortunate dead may be revived.

units.la: 1. Sanè licet pridem recolendæ memoriæ Divus F R I D E R I C U S Romanorum Imperator Augustus, prædecessor noster, de singulari suæ benignitatis munere, claræ recordationis Illustri Wenceslao quondam Boemiæ Duci, qui Regnum Bohemiæ ante coronationem suam regebat, & suis hæredibus Bohemiæ Regibus censum de terra Poloniæ, quem antecessores ejus Ducès Bohemiæ à Polonia multis temporibus accipere consueverant, quemque Poloniæ & Silesiæ Duces sacro Imperio vere tenebantur, ut prout in literis Imperatoris prætati evidenter exprimitur, liberaliter duxerit concedum. Ipsi quoque Duces Poloniæ & Silesiæ eundem censum Illustribus progenitoribus, & prædictis nostris Bohemiæ Regibus, in signum subjectionis debitæ, & in recognitionem sui superioris dominii rite persolverint multis temporibus retroactis: tamen ad abundantius cautelæ præsidium, transeuntis poris dicti Duces suorum hæredum & successorum nomine atque vice, Principatus terras ac dominia sua, à clarae memoriae Illustri Joanne quondam Bohemiae Rege, genitore nostro carissimo deluso & à Corona Regni Bohemiæ præstiterunt solemnitatis, obedientiæ, homagii, subjectionis & fidelitatis debitæ juramenta corporalia.
units.tr: 1. Indeed, although the late Divine Frederick, Roman Emperor Augustus, our predecessor, of worthy memory, by the singular gift of his kindness, had graciously granted to the illustrious Wenceslaus, of famous memory, formerly Duke of Bohemia, who ruled the Kingdom of Bohemia before his coronation, and to his heirs, the kings of Bohemia, the tribute from the land of Poland, which the dukes of Bohemia had customarily received from Poland for many times past, and which the dukes of Poland and Silesia were truly bound to render to the Holy Empire, as is clearly stated in the letters of the aforesaid Emperor; likewise, the same dukes of Poland and Silesia had duly paid this tribute to the illustrious forefathers and to our aforementioned kings of Bohemia, as a sign of due subjection and in acknowledgement of their superior lordship, over many past times. Nevertheless, for the greater safeguard of caution, the said dukes, passing over in the name and place of their heirs and successors, had given to the illustrious John, of famous memory, formerly King of Bohemia, our dearest father, and to the Crown of the Kingdom of Bohemia, the solemn corporal oaths of obedience, homage, subjection and due fidelity for their principalities, lands and dominions.

units.la: 2. Et licet insignis Ducatus Vratislaviensis & Silesiæ, cum suis omnibus pertinentiis, ad utilem & immediatum Dominum Illustrem quondam Bohemiæ Regem, progenitorem nostrum, & Coronam Regni Bohemiæ spectaverit ab antiquo, sicut hoc literæ recolendæ memoriæ Domini Rudolphi Romanorum Regis, prædecessoris nostri, ostendunt. In quarum prima quandam ordinationem inter Illustrem Ottocarum quondam Bohemiæ Regem, proavum nostrum carissimum ex una, & Henricum Ducem Vratislaviensem parte ex altera: videlicet quòd dictus Ottocarus Rex eidem Henrico Vratislaviensi & Silesiæ Duci, in casu, si Ducem præmori contingerit, in præmissò Ducatu Vratislaviensi & Silesiæ, terris, & omnibus dominiis suis debeiet succedere, per le facta madeit, & ipsarum dicto Henrico Duci jam sublato de medio, prædictum Regem Ottocarum, heredes & successores suos, Reges Bohemiæ, de Ducatu Vratislaviensi & Silesiæ, terris & dominiis prædictis, quam actu vacantibus, propter multa grata servitia, quæ Illustres Bohemiæ Reges sacro Romano Imperio fecerant, solenniter investivit, lucidiùs attestantur: tamen Illustris quondam Johannes Boemiæ Rex, genitor noster prædictus, cum Henrico septimo & ultimo Vratislaviæ & Silesiæ Duce, nostro, dum uterque ipsorum vitam ageret in humanis, quandam ordinationem iniit & tractavit; videlicet quòd dictus Dux Henricus terram & districtum Glacensem cum vasallagiis, feudis, dominiis & aliis omnibus pertinentiis suis, de consensu dicti genitoris nostri, ad vitæ duntaxat tempora habere deberet, ut tamen eo moriente, Ducatus sui, puta Vratislaviensis & Silesiæ, ad prædictum Glacensem dominium, ad usum & possessionem genitoris nostri, hæredum & successorum ipsius Regum, & Coronæ Regni Bohemiæ, sine difficultate qualibet revenirent. Sicque hoc processu rerum ad finem devenit intentum. Eoque dictus genitor noster, dum viveret, moriente Duce prædicto, Ducatum Vratislaviensem & terram Glacensem prædictam tenuit & possedit, & nos utrumque de præsenti, velut Bohemiæ Rex, in possessione renentes, utrobilibet dominamur.
units.tr: 2. And although the distinguished Duchy of Breslau and Silesia, with all its appurtenances, has from of old belonged to the useful and immediate lordship of the illustrious late King of Bohemia, our forefather, and to the Crown of the Kingdom of Bohemia, as the letters of our predecessor, the king of the Romans, of worthy memory, Lord Rudolf, show. In the first of these, a certain arrangement is recorded between the illustrious Ottokar, formerly King of Bohemia, our dearest great-grandfather, on the one part, and Duke Henry of Breslau on the other: namely, that the said King Ottokar should succeed to the aforesaid Duchy of Breslau and Silesia, with its lands and all its dominions, to the same Duke Henry of Breslau, in the event that the Duke should die before him; and that, the said Henry having been removed from the midst, the aforesaid King Ottokar, his heirs and successors, Kings of Bohemia, were solemnly invested with the Duchy of Breslau and Silesia, with the lands and dominions aforesaid, which were then vacant, on account of many pleasing services which the illustrious Kings of Bohemia had rendered to the Holy Roman Empire. Yet the illustrious late John, King of Bohemia, our aforesaid father, with Henry the seventh and last Duke of Breslau and Silesia, our kinsman, while each of them was living among men, made and concluded a certain arrangement: namely, that the said Duke Henry should hold the land and district of Glogau, with its vassalages, fiefs, dominions and all other appurtenances, with the consent of our said father, only for the duration of his life; but that, when he died, his duchy, that is Breslau and Silesia, should revert without any difficulty to the aforesaid lordship of Glogau, to the use and possession of our father, of his heirs and successors, the Kings, and of the Crown of the Kingdom of Bohemia. And thus, by this course of events, the matter reached its intended end. Hence our said father, while he lived, after the aforesaid Duke died, held and possessed the Duchy of Breslau and the aforesaid land of Glogau; and we now hold both in possession, as King of Bohemia, and rule in each of them.

units.la: 3. Et quamvis Marchia Budisinensis & Görlicensis, quæ cum ceteris civitatibus, oppidis & pertinentiis suis ad Regnum & Coronam Bohemiæ ab antiquo pertinuerunt, per Illustrem Ottocarum quondam Regem Bohemiæ, proavum nostrum, in personas quondam Illustrium Brandenburgensium Marchionum, ex certis causis & rationibus alienata fuerit: aliquando tamen Marchionibus prædictis, absque sexus masculini hæredibus, decedentibus ex hac vita, Nobiles, Milites, Clientes, cives, universique incolæ Marchiæ Budisinensis & Gorlicensis prædictæ, animadversione debita cognoscentes, qualiter ad Coronam & Regnum Bohemiæ, tanquam ad immediatum & naturalem Dominum, ad subjectionem & obedientiam Illustris Joannis quondam Bohemiæ Regis genitoris nostri, tanquam ad ordinarium, legitimum & naturalem dominum suum, & ad Coronam Regni Bohemiæ, de cujus gremio jamdudum constiterant, ut præfertur, deliberatione non improvida redierunt.
units.tr: 3. And although the Margraviate of Bautzen and Görlitz, which together with the other cities, towns and appurtenances had belonged from of old to the Kingdom and Crown of Bohemia, was alienated by the illustrious Ottokar, formerly King of Bohemia, our great-grandfather, to the persons of the illustrious former Margraves of Brandenburg, for certain causes and reasons; nevertheless, sometimes, when the said Margraves departed this life without heirs of the male sex, the nobles, knights, vassals, citizens, and all the inhabitants of the aforesaid Margraviate of Bautzen and Görlitz, recognising with due attention how they had belonged to the Crown and Kingdom of Bohemia as to their immediate and natural lord, and how they had been placed under the subjection and obedience of the illustrious John, formerly King of Bohemia, our father, as to their ordinary, lawful and natural lord, and to the Crown of the Kingdom of Bohemia, from whose bosom, as has been said, they had long since come, returned to it by a not unwise deliberation.

units.la: 4. Nos igitur indefessam solicitudinis operam, & diligentiam exquisitam, quam saepedicti proavus, pater, ac progenitores nostri carissimi, quondam Bohemiæ Reges, ad obtinendum subjectionis vasallagium, & obedientiam Illustrium Silesiæ & Poloniæ Ducum, videlicet Lignicensis, Brigensis, Munsterbergensis, Olsnensis, Glogoviensis, Saganensis, Opuliensis, Falckenbergensis, Strelicensis, Teschinensis, Tolsnensis, Buthuniensis, Stenaviensis, Ofuetiensis: Principatus Massoviae, & Ducatus in Plotzka, Principum & fidelium nostrorum; Principatus seu Ducatus Vratislaviensis & Silesiæ necnon civitates, videlicet Vratislavia, Novumforum, Franckenstain, Stinaviam, Goravv, & medium partem Glogoviæ & pertinentiarum ipsius: & etiam Budisinensem & Gorlicensem Marchiam, ut præfertur, non absque magnis impensis & infinitis laboribus habuerunt, in nostræ Majestatis aciem continuò revolventes, ut virtutum ipsorum frequentia, & solicitudo laborum, præteriti sub felice nostro regimine solidetur, sicut dudum de plenitudine Romanæ Regiæ potestatis statuendum duximus, & nunc ex certa scientia statuimus de nostræ Imperialis plenitudine potestatis, quòd omnes supradictæ sententiæ, & Clementiæ Imperialis & Regalium literarum, quas ad probationum dictarum intentionum adduximus, semper & ubique in judicio & extra, & in singulis actibus publicis & privatis, quotiens tenorem præsentium legi & publicari contigerit, ejusdem efficaciæ, vigoris & auctoritatis exstitisse. existant, ac si in signis propriis originalia viderentur; & præcipuè cum eadem originalia per nos ac nõnullos sacri Imperii Principes, Barones, Proceres, auscultata & examinata fuerunt diligenter; & demum communicato super omnibus præmissis nonnullorum sacri Imperii Principum, Baronū & Nobilium consilio speciali, prædictis omnibus de verbo ad verbum, prout superius exprimitur, intellectis, & inexamine deliberatè & provide discussis adductis, ne ex interpretatione sinistra quorumlibet, nostris heredibus & successorum nostrorum Regum Bohemiæ, & Coronæ Regni ejusdem, juribus, hominibus & statui valeat in posterum derogari: auctoritate Imperiali dictos Silesiæ, Poloniæ, & cæteros prædictos Duces, nostros Principes & vasallos, cum Principatibus, feudis & vasallagiis ipsorum præsertim cum à Corona Regni præfati immediatè dependeant: dictum quoq; Ducatum Uratislaviensem, cum civitate Uratislavia, Noviforensi, Franckenstain, Stinaviensi, Gorensi, Glogoviensi, & cæteris oppidis ibidem: necnon Marchiam Budisinensem & Gorlicensem, cum vasallis, vasallagis, feudis, feudatariis, utilitatibus, fructibus, obventionibus, jurisdictionibus, judiciis, honoribus, juribus, consuetudinibus, & omnibus dictorum Ducatuum & Marchiæ pertinentiis, velut utile & immediatum dominium nostrum, & Regni Bohemiæ præfati, eidem Regno, & ejus felici Coronæ, in perpetuum adjungimus, incorporamus, invišceramus, adscribimus, adproprianus, & indivisibiliter conjungimus, conunimus.
units.tr: 4. We therefore, bringing to mind continually the tireless labour of care and the diligent effort which our most dear great-grandfather, father and forefathers, formerly Kings of Bohemia, expended in obtaining the vassalage of subjection and the obedience of the illustrious Dukes of Silesia and Poland, namely of Liegnitz, Brieg, Münsterberg, Oels, Glogau, Sagan, Oppeln, Falkenberg, Strehlen, Teschen, Tost, Beuthen, Steinau, and Ohlau; of the Principality of Masovia, and the Duchy of Płock, our princes and faithful men; and the Principality or Duchy of Breslau and Silesia, as well as the cities, namely Breslau, Neumarkt, Frankenstein, Steinau, Glogau, and the half part of Glogau and its appurtenances; and also the Margraviate of Bautzen and Görlitz, as has been said, which they obtained not without great expense and endless labours; and we have repeatedly considered in the sight of our Majesty that, through the frequent exercise of their virtues and their diligent labours, what was achieved under our happy rule should be confirmed. As we formerly decided, from the fullness of the Roman royal power, and now, from certain knowledge and by the fullness of our imperial power, we establish that all the aforesaid sentences, and the letters of imperial and royal clemency which we have adduced as proof of the said intentions, shall have, and have had, always and everywhere, in judgement and outside it, and in all public and private acts, whenever the tenor of these present letters shall be read and published, the same efficacy, force and authority, as if the originals were seen under their own seals; and especially since these same originals were carefully heard and examined by us and by several Princes, Barons and Nobles of the Holy Empire; and finally, after a special council of several Princes, Barons and Nobles of the Holy Empire had been held on all the aforesaid matters, all the aforesaid documents, understood word for word as set out above, and adduced and deliberately and prudently discussed in examination, so that by a malicious interpretation of anyone the rights, men and estate of our heirs and successors, the Kings of Bohemia, and of the Crown of the same Kingdom, may not in future be diminished: by imperial authority we join, incorporate, embowel, ascribe, appropriate and indivisibly conjoin and unite to the aforesaid Kingdom of Bohemia and its happy Crown, in perpetuity, the said Dukes of Silesia and Poland, and our other aforesaid princes and vassals, together with their principalities, fiefs and vassalages, especially since they depend immediately on the Crown of the said Kingdom; also the said Duchy of Breslau, with the city of Breslau, Neumarkt, Frankenstein, Steinau, Glogau, and the other towns there; and likewise the Margraviate of Bautzen and Görlitz, with its vassals, vassalages, fiefs, feudatories, revenues, fruits, incomes, jurisdictions, judgements, honours, rights, customs, and all the appurtenances of the said Duchies and Margraviate, as our useful and immediate dominion and that of the aforesaid Kingdom of Bohemia.

units.la: 5. Speciali etiam ex nomine interpretamur, pronuntiamus, diffinimus, protestamur, & dicinius, ac de certa nostra scientia declaramus, quòd præfati Duces Silesiæ & Poloniæ, heredes & successores ipsorum, in perpetuum, quotiens Ducatus eosdem aut alterum ex eis vacare contigerit, ipsos vel ipsum à nobis, heredibus & successoribus nostris Boemiæ Regibus, & Coronæ Regni ejusdem, homagii, obedientiæ, fidelitatis & subjectionis debitæ teneantur ac debeant præstare & facere corporalia juramenta, suppléntes omnem defectum, si quis in literis vel privilegiis dictorum Imperatorum & Regum Romanorum memoriæ recolendæ, aut etiam in ordinatione seu tractatu dicti genitoris nostri, quem cum præfato Henrico septimo & ultimo Uratislaviensi & Silesiæ Duce habuisse dignoscitur, seu in reditu Nobilium, Militum, clientum, civium, & incolarū Budisinensis & Görlicensis Marchiæ, quò ad Regnum Boemiæ, ut præmittitur, ex causis legitimis redierunt, vel in præsentibus nostris literis verborum defectus, interpretatione dubia, sententiarum obscuritate, vel alia quavis occasione, compertus fuerit, de certa nostra scientia, ac de prædicta Imperialis plenitudine potestatis, non obstantibus legibus, consuetudinibus, usibus, observantiis, juribus municipalibus vel communibus, statutis seu edictis, publicis, vel privatis, factis & editis in contrarium, quibuscumque; quas & quæ, quantum ad hæc, ac si nominatim de verbo ad verbum præsentibus inscripta & inserta consisterent, etiamsi de his jure vel consuetudine deberet fieri mentio specialis, revocamus, cassamus, irritamus, annihilamus, & de prædictæ Imperialis potestatis plenitudine decrevimus firmitatis esse nullius penitus & momenti.
units.tr: 5. By a special title we also interpret, pronounce, define, protest and declare, and from our certain knowledge we make clear, that the aforesaid Dukes of Silesia and Poland, and their heirs and successors, in perpetuity, whenever it happens that those Duchies, or one of them, becomes vacant, are bound and obliged to render to us, our heirs and successors, Kings of Bohemia, and to the Crown of the same Kingdom, the solemn corporal oaths of homage, obedience, fidelity and due subjection; supplying every defect if any is found, whether in the letters or privileges of the Emperors and Kings of the Romans of worthy memory, or in the arrangement or agreement which our said father is known to have made with the aforesaid Henry the seventh and last Duke of Breslau and Silesia, or in the return of the nobles, knights, vassals, citizens and inhabitants of the Margraviate of Bautzen and Görlitz, who, as has been stated, returned for lawful causes to the Kingdom of Bohemia; or in the words of these our present letters, in a doubtful interpretation, an obscurity of meaning, or any other occasion whatever; by our certain knowledge and by the aforesaid fullness of imperial power, notwithstanding any laws, customs, usages, observances, municipal or common rights, statutes or edicts, public or private, made and issued to the contrary, whatever they may be; which, as far as these matters are concerned, we revoke, quash, invalidate, and annul, just as if they were set out by name, word for word, and inserted in these present letters, even if special mention of them ought to be made by law or custom; and by the fullness of the aforesaid imperial power we have decreed that they shall be of no force or validity whatever.

units.la: 6. Nulli ergò hominum liceat hàc nostræ adjunctionis, appropriationis, conjunctionis, incorporationis, invisceracionis, adscriptionis, interpretationis, pronuntiationis, diffinitionis, protestationis, declarationis, discreti defectus suppletionis, revocationis, cassationis, irritationis & annihilationis paginam infringere. Contrarii vero facientes, si qui fuerint, quod absit, ultra indignationem nostræ Celsitudinis, quam ob hoc se noverint incursuros, mille marcas auri puri nostro & Romani Regni fisco componant: ipsatum videlicet mediatatem nostræ seu successorum nostrorū Curiæ seu Camerę, reliquam passis injuriam irremissibiliter applicandam.
units.tr: 6. Therefore let no one of mankind be permitted to infringe this page of our adjunction, appropriation, conjunction, incorporation, invisceration, ascription, interpretation, pronouncement, definition, protestation, declaration, supplying of a lack of discretion, revocation, cassation, annulment and annihilation. If any who act contrary to it, which God forbid, shall be found, then, beyond the indignation of our Highness, which they may know they will incur for this, they shall pay a fine of a thousand marks of pure gold to the treasury of ourselves and of the Roman Kingdom: half of it to our Court or Chamber, or that of our successors, and the remainder to be applied without remission to the party injured.

units.la: Signum Serenissimi Principis ac Domini, Domini KAROLI Quarti Ro- manorum Imperatoris, Semper-Augusti.
units.tr: Seal of the Most Serene Prince and Lord, Lord Charles IV, Roman Emperor, Ever Augustus.

units.la: Testes hujus sunt:
units.tr: The witnesses to this are:

units.la: Venerabilis Ernestus Pragensis Archiepiscopus.
units.tr: The venerable Ernest, Archbishop of Prague.

units.la: Illustris Rudolphus Senior Dux Saxoniæ, sacri Imperii Archimarschallus, avunculus noster. [Pretzlaus Uratislaviensis, Cancellarius Aulæ nostræ, ] Episcopi. Johannes Olmicensis, ac Venerabiles Johannes Lurhoniensis, Theodoricus Mindensis, [Henricus Lumudensis, Illustres [Rudolphus Junior Saxoniæ ] Duces. & Joannes Opaviæ Spectabiles [Burghardus Magister Curiæ nostræ, Burggravius Magdeburgensis, ] Comites. & Albertus de * Anchral. [Johannes de Rosenberg, Johannes de Sternberg, Ztrincko de Hasenberg, & Nobiles Gonflaus de Schvvanberg, Butzcko de Constat, Dionysius de Romnitz, [& Ulricus de Visa:
units.tr: The illustrious Rudolf the Elder, Duke of Saxony, Archmarshal of the Holy Empire, our uncle. [Pretzlaus of Breslau, Chancellor of our Court,] bishops. John of Olmütz, and the venerable John of Lauban, Theodoric of Minden, [Henry of Lebus,] the illustrious [Rudolf the Younger of Saxony] dukes, and John of Opava, the distinguished [Burchard, Master of our Court, Burgrave of Magdeburg,] counts, and Albert of Anhalt [...] John of Rosenberg, John of Sternberg, Ztrincko of Hasenburg, and the nobles Gonflaus of Schwanberg, Butzko of Kostelec, Dionysius of Romnitz, [and Ulrich of Vitza:

units.la: & alii quàm plures nostri fideles, præsentium sub Bulla Aurea. Datum Pragæ, Anno Domini 1355. Indictione octava, 7. Idus Octobr.
units.tr: and many other of our faithful, present under the Golden Bull. Given at Prague, in the year of the Lord 1355, the eighth indiction, on the 7th of the Ides of October.

units.la: * f. Anhalt
units.tr: * perhaps Anhalt

units.la: INFRA SCRIPTÆ LITERÆ SUNT OBTENTÆ A PRINCIPIBUS ELECTORI- BUS IN SOLENNI CURIA IMPERIALI IN NUREMBERG.
units.tr: The letters written below were obtained from the Electoral Princes in the solemn Imperial Diet at Nuremberg.

units.la: GERLACVS ARCHIEPISCOPVS MOGVNTINENSIS, TANQVAM Princeps Elector, confirmat incorporationem & declarationem Domini CAROLI Imper. factam super Ducatibus Poloniæ & Silesiæ, & Marchionatu utriusque Lusatiæ.
units.tr: Gerlach, Archbishop of Mainz, as Prince Elector, confirms the incorporation and declaration made by Lord Charles, Emperor, concerning the Duchies of Poland and Silesia and the Margraviate of both Lusatias.

units.la: NOS Gerlacus Dei gratia sanctæ Mogunrinensis Sedis Archiepiscopus, & Sacri Imperii per Germaniam Archicancellarius, ad perpetuam rei memoriam. Serenissimus ac invictissimus Princeps & Dominus, Dominus CAROLUS divina favente clementia Romanorum Imperator Semper-Augustus & Boëmiæ Rex, Dominus noster gratiosus, provida sua circumspectione adeo ertens, qualiter insignes & laudabiles famæ titulos moderni temporis meretur gloriosa posteritas, ad prædecessorum Illustrium circumspecta pridem instauravit provisio, vigilanti cura prosequitur, ac gratæ solicitudinis munit officio, ut fructuosi laboris solertia, perenni successorum commendetur memoriæ, & ex consequentia bonorum operum quasi ex relucenti speculo vetustaris resurgat de felicibus mortuis felix memoria, rediviva.
units.tr: We, Gerlach, by the grace of God Archbishop of the holy see of Mainz and Archchancellor of the Holy Empire throughout Germany, to the perpetual memory of the matter. The most serene and invincible Prince and Lord, Lord Charles, by the favouring clemency of God Roman Emperor, ever august, and King of Bohemia, our gracious Lord, through his provident circumspection, pursues with watchful care what the earlier wise provisions of illustrious predecessors had begun, and discharges the office of pleasing solicitude, so that the diligence of fruitful labour may be commended to the perpetual memory of successors, and that from the consequence of good works, as from a shining mirror, the happy memory of the fortunate dead may rise again, revived from antiquity.

units.la: 1. Licet pridem recolendæ Serenissimus Princeps, Dominus FRIDERICUS Rom.Imp.Semper Augustus, prædecessor præfati Domini nostri Imperatoris, de singulari benignitate claræ recordationis, Illustri Principi Domino Wenceslao quondam Boemiæ Duci, qui Regnum Boemiæ ante coronationem suam regebat, & suis heredibus Regibus Boemiæ, censum de terra Poloniæ, quem antecessores ejus Duces Boemiæ a Polonia multis temporibus accipere consueverunt, quamquam Poloniæ & Silesiæ Duces sacro Imperio solvere tenebantur, prout in literis Domini Friderici Imp. præfatis evidenter exprimitur, liberaliter duxerit erogandum. ipsi quoque Duces Poloniæ & Silesiæ eundem censum Illustribus progenitoribus & prædecessoribus prædicti Domini nostri Imperatoris in Regno Boemiæ, eisdem Regni Boemiæ Regibus in signum subjectionis, & in recognitionem superioris dominii rite persolverit multis temporibus retroactis: tamen ad abundantius cautelæ prævidium, tractu temporis dicti Duces, suo, heredum & successorum suorum nomine ac vice, Primatus, terras ac dominia a claræ memoriæ Illustri Principe, Domino Joanne quondam Boemiæ Regi, genitore dicti Domini nostri Imperatoris, dum viveret, & demum ab eodem Domino nostro Imperatore CAROLO, tanquam Boemiæ Regi, præfato ipsius genitore defuncto, & a Corona Regni Boemiæ, in feudum cum solemnitate debita susceperunt, dictoque Domino Imperatori, ac ipsius genitori, dum viveret, tanquam Boemiæ Regibus, & Coronæ Regni Boemiæ, præstiterunt solemniter obedientiæ, homagii, subjectionis & fidelitatis debitæ corporalia juramenta.
units.tr: 1. Although formerly the most serene Prince, Lord Frederick, Roman Emperor ever august, predecessor of the aforesaid Lord our Emperor, of blessed memory and by singular kindness, generously granted to the illustrious Prince Lord Wenceslas, once Duke of Bohemia, who ruled the Kingdom of Bohemia before his coronation, and to his heirs, the Kings of Bohemia, the tribute from the land of Poland, which their predecessors, the Dukes of Bohemia, had customarily received from Poland for many times, although the Dukes of Poland and Silesia were bound to pay it to the Holy Empire, as is clearly expressed in the aforesaid letters of Lord Emperor Frederick; likewise the Dukes of Poland and Silesia themselves duly paid the same tribute for many past times to the illustrious progenitors and predecessors of the aforesaid Lord our Emperor, the Kings of Bohemia, in sign of subjection and in acknowledgement of superior lordship. Yet, for the greater security of caution, in course of time the said Dukes, in their own name and in the name and place of their heirs and successors, received in solemn form, as a fief from the Crown of the Kingdom of Bohemia, the principalities, lands and dominions from the illustrious Prince, Lord John, of blessed memory, once King of Bohemia, father of the said Lord our Emperor, while he lived, and finally from the same Lord our Emperor Charles, as King of Bohemia, after the death of the aforesaid his father; and they solemnly rendered to the said Lord Emperor, and to his father while he lived, as Kings of Bohemia and to the Crown of the Kingdom of Bohemia, the bodily oaths of obedience, homage, subjection and due fidelity.

units.la: 3. Et licet insignis Ducatus Uratislaviæ & Schlesiæ, cum suis omnibus pertinentiis, ad utile & immediatum dominium Illustrium quondam Boemiæ Regum, progenitorum & prædecessorum antedicti Domini nostri Imperatoris & Coronam Regni Boemiæ spectaverit ab antiquo, sicut hoc tetæ recolendæ memoriæ Serenissimi Principis Domini RUDOLPHI quondam Romanorum Regis, prædecessoris dicti Domini nostri Imperatoris, in quarum prima quandam Ordinationem inter Illustrem Principem Dominum Ottocarum quondam Boemiæ Regem, proavum ipsius domini nostri Imperatoris ex una, & Dominum Henricum Ducem Uratislaviensem parte ex altera, videlicet quod dictus Rex Ottocarus eidem domino Henrico Uratislaviensi & Silesiæ Duci, in casu, si Ducem prædictum contingeret, in prædictum Ducatu Uratislaviensi & Schlesiæ terris, & omnibus dominiis suis, succedere, pro se factum adiserit. Et in secunda ipsarum dicto Domino Henrico Duce jam sublato de medio, prædictum Regem Ottocarum, heredes & successores ipsius, Boemiæ Reges, de Ducatu Uratislaviensi & Silesiæ terris & dominiis prædictis, tanquam actu vacantibus, propter multa grata officia, quæ Illustres Boemiæ Reges sacro Romano Imperio fecerant, solemniter invenit, lucidius attestantur. Cum Illustris quondam Joannes Boemiæ Rex, genitor dicti Domini nostri Imperatoris præfatus, cum Illustri Domino Henrico VII. & ultimo Uratislaviensi & Schlesiæ Duce, sororio ipsius Domini nostri Imperatoris, dum uterque ipsorum viram ageret in humanis, quandam Ordinationem iniit & tractavit, videlicet quod dictus Dux Henricus terram & districtum Glacensem, cum vasallagiis, feudis, dominiis & omnibus pertinentiis suis, de consensu genitoris dicti Domini nostri Imperatoris, ad vitæ suæ duntaxat tempora habere deberet, ut tamen eo moriente Ducatus sui, Uratislaviensis & Schlesiæ, ad prædictum dominium Glacense, ad usum & possessionem dicti genitoris Domini nostri Imperatoris, heredum & successorum ipsius, Regum Boemiæ, & Coronæ Regni ejusdem sine difficultate qualibet revenirent, sicut hoc processu dierum ad finem pervenit intentum: eo quod prædictus Rex Joannes, præfati Domini nostri Imperatoris genitor, dum viverer, moriente Duce prædicto, & Ducatum Uratislaviensem & terram Glacensem præfatam tenuit & possedit, & ipse Dominus Imperator de præsenti, veluti Boemiæ Rex, possessionem tenens utrobique dominatur.
units.tr: 3.
