And although the famous Duchy of Breslau and Silesia, with all its appurtenances, has from of old belonged to the useful and immediate dominion of the illustrious former Kings of Bohemia, the ancestors and predecessors of the aforesaid Lord our Emperor, and to the Crown of the Kingdom of Bohemia, as the documents of the most serene Prince, Lord Rudolph, of blessed memory, once Roman King, predecessor of the said Lord our Emperor, more clearly attest, in the first of which is an ordinance between the illustrious Prince, Lord Ottokar, once King of Bohemia, great-grandfather of the Lord our Emperor, on the one side, and Lord Henry, Duke of Breslau, on the other side, namely that the said King Ottokar, for himself, had agreed that, if the said Duke Henry should die, he would succeed in the aforesaid Duchy of Breslau and the lands of Silesia and all his dominions; and in the second, after the said Duke Henry had been taken from the midst, the aforesaid King Ottokar, his heirs and successors, the Kings of Bohemia, were solemnly found to hold the Duchy of Breslau and the lands and dominions of Silesia as actually vacant, on account of the many pleasing services which the illustrious Kings of Bohemia had rendered to the Holy Roman Empire. Since the illustrious former John, King of Bohemia, father of the said Lord our Emperor, mentioned above, and the illustrious Lord Henry VII, the last Duke of Breslau and Silesia, brother-in-law of the said Lord our Emperor, while both of them were living among men, entered into and negotiated a certain ordinance, namely that the said Duke Henry should hold the land and district of Glatz, with its vassalages, fiefs, dominions and all appurtenances, with the consent of the father of the said Lord our Emperor, only for the duration of his life; but that, upon his death, his Duchies of Breslau and Silesia should return without any difficulty to the aforesaid dominion of Glatz, to the use and possession of the said father of the Lord our Emperor, of his heirs and successors, the Kings of Bohemia, and of the Crown of the same Kingdom; which intention, in the course of days, came to its end, because the aforesaid King John, father of the aforesaid Lord our Emperor, while he lived, after the death of the said Duke, held and possessed the Duchy of Breslau and the aforesaid land of Glatz, and the Lord Emperor himself, now holding possession as King of Bohemia, rules over both.

units.la: 4. Et quamvis Marchia Budisinensis & Gorlicensis, quae cum caeteris civitatibus, oppidis & pertinentiis suis ad Regnum & Coronam Boemiae ab antiquo pertinuerunt, per Illustrem Dominum Ottocarum quondam Boemiae Regem, proavum dicti Domini nostri, in personas Illustrium Principum & Dominorum quondam Brandenburgensium Marchionum, ex certis & rationabilibus causis, alienatae fuerant; aliquando tamen Dominis Marchionibus praedictis, absque heredibus sexus masculini decedentibus ab hac vita, Nobiles, Milites, Clientes, Cives, & universi incolae Marchiae Budisinensis & Gorlicensis praefatae, animadversione debita cognoscentes, qualiter ad Regnum & Coronam Boemiae, tanquam ad immediatum & naturale dominium dudum pertinuerant, ad subjectionem & obedientiam dicti Illustris Domini Johannis quondam Boemiae Regis, genitoris antecedicti Domini nostri Imperatoris, tanquam ad ordinarium, legitimum & naturalem Dominum suum, & ad Coronam Regni Boemiae, de cujus gremio dudum constiterant, ut praescribitur, deliberatione non improvida redierunt.
units.tr: 4. And although the Margraviate of Bautzen and Görlitz, which together with the other cities, towns and appurtenances had from of old belonged to the Kingdom and Crown of Bohemia, had been alienated by the illustrious Lord Ottokar, once King of Bohemia, great-grandfather of our said Lord, into the hands of the illustrious Princes and Lords, the former Margraves of Brandenburg, for certain and reasonable causes; nevertheless, sometimes, when the said Lords Margraves died from this life without heirs of the male sex, the nobles, knights, vassals, citizens and all the inhabitants of the aforesaid Margraviate of Bautzen and Görlitz, recognising with due attention how they had formerly belonged to the Kingdom and Crown of Bohemia as to their immediate and natural dominion, returned, by no improvident deliberation, to the subjection and obedience of the said illustrious Lord John, once King of Bohemia, father of the aforesaid Lord our Emperor, as to their ordinary, lawful and natural lord, and to the Crown of the Kingdom of Bohemia, from whose bosom, as has been said, they had long stood.

units.la: 5. Supradictus itaque Dominus noster Carolus Imp. exquisitam diligentiam & sollicitudinem, quam saepedicti proavus, pater & progenitores sui quondam Boemiae Reges, ad obtinendum subjectionem, vasallagium & obedientiam Illustrium Principum Dominorum Silesiae & Poloniae Ducum, videlicet Lignicensis, Brigensis, Munsterbergensis, Olsnensis, Glogoviensis, Saganensis, Oppoliensis, Falckenbergensis, Strelicensis, Teschensis, Gozlensis, Butinensis, Stinaviensis & Ofuiicensis: Principatus Massoviae, & Ducatus in Plotzk, Principi & fideli ejusdem Domini Imperatoris, tanquam Regis Boemiae: Principatus seu Ducatus Vratislaviensem & Silesiae: necnon civitates, videlicet Vratislaviam, Novumforum, Franckestein, Stinaviam, Sorovv, Glogovia, Nambslaviam, & pertinentia ipsarum: & etiam Budisinensem & Gorlicensem Marchiam, ut praefertur, non absque magnis impensis, & infinitis laboribus habuerunt, in sua mentis acie, intima meditatione revolvetes, ut virtutis ipsorum frequentia, & sicut dudum cum plenitudine Romanae Regiae potestatis statuendum duxerat, ita & nunc ex certa scientia statuit, & de suae Imperialis plenitudine potestatis, quod omnes supradictae sententiae & clausulae Imperialium & Regalium litterarum, quas ad probationem dictarum intentionum adduxit, semper & ubique, in judicio & extra, & in singulis actibus publicis & privatis, quotiens tenore praescrito legi sive publicari contigerit, ejusdem efficaciae, vigoris, & auctoritatis existant, ac si in figuris propriis originalia viderentur: ea praecipue, cum eadem originalia per eundem Dominum Imperatorem, nos ac nonnullos sacri Romani Imperii Dominos, Principes, Barones, Procersince; auscultata & examinata fuerint diligenter: ac demum communicato per eundem dictum Dominum nostrum Imperatorem super omnibus praemissis, nostro & nonnullorum sacri Imperii Principum, Baronum & Nobilium consilio speciali, praedictis omnibus de verbo ad verbum, prout superius exprimitur, & in examen deliberatae & provisae disclusionis adductis, ne ex interpretatione sinistra quorumlibet praedicti Domini nostri Imperatoris, tanquam Regis Boemiae, heredum & successorum suorum, Regum Boemiae, & Coronae Regni ejusdem, juribus, honoribus & statu valeat in posterum derogari, ipse Dominus Imperator auctoritate Imperiali dictos Silesiae & Poloniae & ceteros praedictos Duces, ipsius tamen Regis Boemiae Principes & vasallos, cum Principatibus, feudis & vasallagiis ipsorum, praesertim cum a Corona Regni immediate dependeant: dictu quoq; Ducatu Vratislaviensem, cum civitate Vratislavia, Noviforensi: civitates Franckenbergensem, Stinaviensem, Gotensem, Glogoviensem, & caeteras oppidas ibidem: necnon Marchiam Budisinensem & Gorlicensem, cum vasallis, vasallagiis, feudis, feudatariis, utilitatibus, fructibus, obventionibus, jurisdictionibus, judiciis, honoribus, juribus, consuetudinibus, & omnibus dictorum Ducatuum & Marchiae pertinentiis, velutile & immediatum dominium suum, & Regni Boemiae praefati, eidem Regno & ejus felici Coronae, in perpetuum, nostro & aliorum Dominorum Principum Electorum accedente consensu, adjunxit, incorporavit, invisceravit, adscripsit, appropriavit, indivisibiliter & inseparabiliter comunivit.
units.tr: 5. Therefore the above-mentioned Lord our Charles, Emperor, with the exquisite diligence and solicitude which his oft-mentioned great-grandfather, father and forefathers, once Kings of Bohemia, had shown in obtaining the subjection, vassalage and obedience of the illustrious Princes and Lords, the Dukes of Silesia and Poland, namely of Liegnitz, Brieg, Münsterberg, Oels, Glogau, Sagan, Oppeln, Falkenberg, Strehlen, Teschen, Gozlen, Bytom, Stinau and Ofuiicz; the Principality of Masovia and the Duchy of Płock, as princes and faithful subjects of the same Lord Emperor as King of Bohemia; the Principality or Duchy of Breslau and Silesia; and likewise the cities, namely Breslau, Neumarkt, Frankenstein, Steinau, Schweidnitz, Glogau, Namslau, and their appurtenances; and also the Margraviate of Bautzen and Görlitz, as stated above, which they obtained not without great expense and infinite labours, revolving in the keen intention of his mind with deep meditation, so that by the frequent exercise of their virtue, and as he had long ago decided with the fullness of the Roman royal power, so now also he decides from certain knowledge, and by the fullness of his Imperial power, that all the aforesaid sentences and clauses of the Imperial and royal letters, which he has adduced as proof of the said intentions, shall always and everywhere, in judgment and out of it, and in all public and private acts, whenever they happen to be read or published in the prescribed tenor, have the same efficacy, force and authority as if they were seen in their own forms as originals; especially since these same originals have been diligently heard and examined by the same Lord Emperor, by us, and by several Lords, Princes, Barons and Nobles of the Holy Roman Empire; and finally, when all the foregoing matters had been communicated by the said Lord our Emperor, with the special counsel of ourselves and of several Princes, Barons and Nobles of the Holy Empire, and had been brought, word for word, as expressed above, into the examination of a deliberate and provident disclosure, lest by any evil interpretation of anyone the rights, honours and state of the aforesaid Lord our Emperor, as King of Bohemia, of his heirs and successors, the Kings of Bohemia, and of the Crown of the same Kingdom, might be derogated from in future, the same Lord Emperor, by Imperial authority, joined, incorporated, invested, ascribed, appropriated and indivisibly and inseparably united to the said Kingdom of Bohemia and its happy Crown, in perpetuity, with the consent of ourselves and the other Lord Electoral Princes, the said Dukes of Silesia and Poland and the other aforesaid Dukes, being princes and vassals of the same King of Bohemia, together with their principalities, fiefs and vassalages, especially since they depend immediately on the Crown of the Kingdom; also the said Duchy of Breslau, with the city of Breslau and Neumarkt, the cities of Frankenstein, Steinau, Schweidnitz, Glogau and the other towns there, and likewise the Margraviate of Bautzen and Görlitz, with vassals, vassalages, fiefs, feudatories, utilities, fruits, revenues, jurisdictions, judgments, honours, rights, customs and all the appurtenances of the said Duchies and Margraviate, as their useful and immediate dominion and that of the aforesaid Kingdom of Bohemia.

units.la: 6. Specialiter etiam & ex nomine praedictus Dominus noster Imperator interpretatus est, diffinitionem tiavit, protestatus est, & dixit, ac de certa scientia sua declaravit, quod praefati Duces Silesiae & Poloniae heredes & successores eorum in perpetuum, quotiens Ducatus eosdem, aut alterum ex eis vacare contigerit, ipsos vel ipsum a praefato Domino nostro Imperatore, tanquam a Rege Boëmiae, ac heredibus & successoribus suis Boemiae Regibus, & a Corona Regni Boemiae praefati, absque renitentia seu dilatione in feudum tenere recipere, dicto Domino Imperatori, tanquam Regi Boemiae, heredibus & successoribus suis Boemiae Regibus, & Coronae Regni ejusdem, homagii, obedientiae, fidelitatis & subjectionis debitae teneantur & debeant praestare & facere corporalia juramenta. Supplevit etiam praefatus Dominus noster Imperator omne defectum, si quis in litteris & privilegiis, aut etiam ordinatione testamenti dicti genitoris, quae cum praefato Domino Henrico VII. & ultimo Vratislaviensi & Silesiae Duce habuisse dignoscitur; seu in reditu Nobilium, Clientum, Militum, Civium, incolarum Budisinensis & Gorlicensis Marchiae, qui ad Coronam Regni Boemiae, ut praemittitur, ex causis legitimis redierunt; vel in consiliis, tenore, litteris suis, verborum defectu, interpretatione dubia, lententiarum obscuritate, vel qua vis occasione compertus fuerit, de certa sua scientia, ac de praedicta Imperialis plenitudine potestatis, non obstantibus legibus, consuetudinibus, usibus, observantiis, juribus municipalibus vel constitutionibus, statutis seu edictis, publicis vel privatis, factis & editis in contrarium quibuscunque; quas & quantum ad haec, ac si nominatum de verbo ad verbum suis litteris inscripta & inserta consisterent, in de his jure vel consuetudine deberet fieri mentio specialis, revocavit, cassavit, irritavit, annihilavit, & de dicta Imperatoriae potestatis plenitudine decrevit firmiter, fore nullius penitus momenti.
units.tr: 6. Especially, and by name, our aforesaid Lord the Emperor has interpreted, defined, declared, and said, and by his certain knowledge has made clear, that the aforesaid Dukes of Silesia and Poland, their heirs and successors forever, whenever those duchies, or either of them, shall happen to become vacant, are to receive them, or him, in fief from our aforesaid Lord the Emperor as King of Bohemia, and from his heirs and successors as Kings of Bohemia, and from the Crown of the aforesaid Kingdom of Bohemia, without reluctance or delay; and that they are bound and obliged to render to the said Lord Emperor, as King of Bohemia, to his heirs and successors as Kings of Bohemia, and to the Crown of the same Kingdom, the homage, obedience, fidelity and subjection owed, and to make the corporal oaths. Our aforesaid Lord the Emperor has also supplied every defect, if any should be found, in the letters and privileges, or even in the ordinance of the will of the said father, which is known to have been held with the aforesaid Lord Henry VII and the last Duke of Wrocław and Silesia; or in the return of the nobles, clients, soldiers, citizens and inhabitants of the March of Budissin and Görlitz, who, as has been said, returned to the Crown of the Kingdom of Bohemia for lawful causes; or in the counsels, tenor, letters, lack of words, doubtful interpretation, obscurity of sentences, or by whatever occasion it may be discovered; and by his certain knowledge and the aforesaid plenitude of imperial power, notwithstanding any laws, customs, usages, observances, municipal rights or constitutions, statutes or edicts, public or private, made and issued to the contrary whatsoever (which, as far as these matters are concerned, are to be considered as if they were named word for word and inscribed and inserted in his letters, and in which no special mention would need to be made by law or custom), he has revoked, quashed, annulled, and abolished them, and by the said plenitude of imperial power has firmly decreed that they shall be of no force whatever.

units.la: 7. Inhibuit etiam praefatus Dominus noster Imperator Carolus, quod nulli hominum liceat Imperialis indulti super praemissa editi paginam infringere, seu ei quovis ausu temerario contraire. Et voluit auctoritate sua contrafacientes quoslibet poenam mille marcarum puri auri incurrere, & earum medietatem fisco Romani Imperii, residuam vero Regni Boemiae & successorum suorum Cameris irremissibiliter applicari, sicut in originalibus literis dicti Domini nostri Imperatoris, quas sub Bulla Aurea, typario suae Majestatis desuper erogasse dignoscitur, plenius & distinctius est expressum.
units.tr: 7. Our aforesaid Lord the Emperor Charles has also forbidden that anyone whatsoever be permitted to infringe the page of the imperial indult issued concerning the above matters, or to act contrary to it by any rash daring. And by his authority he wished that all who act against it incur a penalty of a thousand marks of pure gold, half of which is to be applied without remission to the fisc of the Roman Empire, and the rest to the Chambers of the Kingdom of Bohemia and of his successors; as is set out more fully and distinctly in the original letters of the said Lord our Emperor, which are known to have been issued under the Golden Bull, with his Majesty's seal impressed upon them.

units.la: 8. Nos igitur, qui supra, Gerlacus Sedis Moguntinensis Archiepiscopus, ex eisdem rationabilibus & evidentibus causis, quibus antedictus Serenissimus Princeps, Dominus noster Imperator CAROLUS, circumspecta sua providentia motus dignoscitur, & ex omnibus praedictis, tanquam ex movis legitimis, sacri Romani Imperii statum & augmentum prospicientibus, propensius animati, supradictis adjunctioni, incorporationi, invisceratione, adscriptioni, adpropriationi, communioni, interpretationi, pronunciationi, diffinitioni, protestationi, declarationi, decreto, defectuum suppletioni, revocationi, cassationi, irritationi, annihilationi, poenarum adjectioni, & omnibus aliis, quae expressim aut sunt expressata superius, velut Archiepiscopus Moguntinensis, sacri Romani Imperii per Germaniam Archicancellarius, & Princeps Elector, animo deliberato, & sano procedente consilio, nostro benevolum consensum & assensum praesentibus adhibemus; ac supra dicta omnia, & eorum quemlibet, singulaque, in omnibus suis tenoribus, sententiis, punctis & clausulis de verbo ad verbum, prout praevidenter expressa, ex officii nostri debito, laudamus, approbamus, & de certa nostra scientia confirmamus plenissime perpetuis temporibus valitura, praesentium sub nostro sigillo testimoniorum. Datum in Nurnberg, anno Domini MCCCLV. in die beatae Luciae Virginis.
units.tr: 8. We therefore, the undersigned, Gerlach, Archbishop of the See of Mainz, moved by the same reasonable and evident causes by which the aforesaid Most Serene Prince, our Lord the Emperor Charles, is known to have been moved by his circumspect providence, and being more inclined, from all the aforesaid things, as from lawful motives looking to the state and increase of the Holy Roman Empire, by sound and deliberate counsel, as Archbishop of Mainz, Archchancellor of the Holy Roman Empire through Germany, and Prince Elector, we give our benevolent consent and assent by these presents to the aforesaid adjunction, incorporation, insertion, ascription, appropriation, communion, interpretation, pronouncement, definition, protestation, declaration, decree, supplying of defects, revocation, quashing, invalidation, annulment, addition of penalties, and all the other things which have been expressed or stated above; and we praise, approve, and by our certain knowledge fully confirm, from the duty of our office, all the aforesaid things, and each and every one of them, singly, in all their tenors, sentences, points and clauses, word for word, as they have been carefully expressed, to be valid in perpetuity; witness our seal appended to these presents. Given at Nuremberg, in the year of the Lord 1355, on the day of the blessed Virgin Lucy.

units.la: CONFIRMATIO STATUTI CAROLI IMPER.
units.tr: CONFIRMATION OF THE STATUTE OF CHARLES IMPERIAL

units.la: QUOD LICEAT PERSONAE NULLAE EXTRA RE- GNUM BOHEMIAE citari; & quod Rex tenere debeat aurifodi- nas, & alterius monetae.
units.tr: That no person may be summoned outside the Kingdom of Bohemia, and that the King ought to hold gold mines and mints of other coinage.

units.la: NOS Gerlacus Dei gratia sanctae Moguntinensis Sedis Archiepiscopus, sacri Romani Imperii per Germaniam Archicancellarius, omnibus in perpetuum. Cum per recoledae memoriae Divos Romanorum Imperatores & Reges, Illustribus quondam Regibus Boemiae clarae memoriae, ac claro Regno Boemiae & ejusdem Regni coronae olim concessum fuerit & indultum sit, quod in eodem Regno a tempore, cujus contraria hodie non extat memoria, consuetudine laudabili conservata, diuturnitate temporum, & praescripta moribus utentium, sine contradictionis aut interpretationis obstaculo introductum, quod nullus Princeps, Baro, Nobilis, Miles, Cliens, Burgensis, nulla denique persona ejusdem Regni, & pertinentiarum ejus ubicunque existentium, cujuscunque status, dignitatis, praeminentiae vel conditionis existat, ad cujuscunque actoris instantiam, extra Regnum ipsum ad quodcunque tribunal seu alterius jus, praeterquam Regis Boemiae Regalis Curiae suae judicium citari poterit, seu mahi vel vocari debeat, perpetuis inantea temporibus sive possit. Cumque Serenissimus & invictissimus Princeps & Dominus, Dominus CAROLUS IV. divina favente clementia Romanorum Imperator semper Augustus & Boemiae Rex Illustris, Dominus noster gratiosus, privilegium, consuetudine & indultum hujus Imperiali auctoritate, & de plenitudine Imperialis potestatis, innovans & confirmans, duxerit statuendum, ut si quispiam praedictorum, puta Princeps, Baro, Nobilis, Miles, cliens, civis, burgensis seu rusticus, aealia quaecunque persona, ad cujuscunque tribunal extra Regnum praedictum Boemiae quaecunque causa, criminali, civili, & mixta, seu super quocunque negotio citatus fuerit, quocunque tempore, vel citata coparere, vel in judicio respondere non teneatur: sique adversus hujusmodi non comparentes, vel non comparentes, a quocunque judice extraneo extra Regni Boemiae constituto, judicialiter procedi, processus fieri, seu sententias interlocutorias, vel diffinitivas, una vel plures, in quibuscunque praemissis causis sive negotiis quovis modo ferri vel promulgari contigerit, eadem auctoritate & potestate omnes, praecepta, processus & sententias hujusmodi, necnon executiones & omnia ex eis, vel aliquo eorum quovis modo secuta irritaverit penitus & cassaverit: adjiciendo expresse & auctoritate simili decernendo, ut quemadmodum in praedicto Regno Boemiae, a tempore, cujus contrarii non habetur memoria, juge- riter observatum existit, ita nulli Principi, Baroni, Nobili, Militi, Clienti, civi, burgensi, seu rustico, nulli denique personae seu incolae Regni Boemiae, expediti, cujuscunque status, praeminentiae, dignitatis vel conditionis existat vel existat, a quibuscunque processibus, sententiis interlocutoriis vel definitivis, sive praeceptis Regis Boemiae, aut Judicis Curiae suae, necnon executionibus eorundem contra se in Regali judicio seu coram Regis, Regni & Curiae praedictorum Judicibus, factis, latis seu habitis, vel ferendis inanter seu fiendis, ad quodcunque aliud judicium liceat appellare: provocationes quoque, seu appellationes, iis quas contra hoc interponi contigent, eo ipso juribus non subsistere, & appellantes ipsos poenam perditionis causarum ipso facto statuens incurrisse.
units.tr: We, Gerlach, by the grace of God Archbishop of the holy See of Mainz, Archchancellor of the Holy Roman Empire throughout Germany, to all, in perpetuity. Whereas by the Divine Emperors and Kings of the Romans of blessed memory, it was granted and indulged to the illustrious former Kings of Bohemia, of clear memory, and to the famous Kingdom of Bohemia and the crown of the same Kingdom, that in the same Kingdom, from a time of which no contrary memory now exists, a laudable custom has been preserved, introduced by the lapse of time and established by the practice of those using it, without obstruction of objection or interpretation, that no prince, baron, noble, knight, client, citizen, burgher, in short no person of the same Kingdom and its dependencies, wherever existing, of whatever rank, dignity, pre-eminence or condition he may be, may be or ought to be summoned, cited or called, at the instance of any plaintiff, outside the Kingdom itself to any tribunal or to the jurisdiction of another, except before the judgment of the King of Bohemia and his Royal Court, for all future time. And whereas the Most Serene and Invincible Prince and Lord, Lord Charles IV, by the favouring mercy of God Emperor of the Romans, ever Augustus, and Illustrious King of Bohemia, our gracious Lord, renewing and confirming by his imperial authority and from the fullness of imperial power this privilege, custom and indult, has decreed that if any of the aforesaid persons, namely prince, baron, noble, knight, client, citizen, burgher or peasant, or any other person whatever, is cited to any tribunal outside the aforesaid Kingdom of Bohemia, in any cause, criminal, civil or mixed, or concerning any business whatever, at whatever time, he is not bound to appear when cited or to answer in judgment; and if proceedings are taken against such non-appearing persons by any foreign judge established outside the Kingdom of Bohemia, or processes are made, or interlocutory or definitive sentences, one or several, are in any way delivered or promulgated in any of the aforesaid causes or business, he has, by the same authority and power, utterly annulled and quashed all such precepts, processes and sentences, as well as the executions and everything that has followed from them or any of them in any way; expressly adding and decreeing by like authority that, just as in the aforesaid Kingdom of Bohemia, from a time of which no contrary memory is held, it has been continually observed, so no prince, baron, noble, knight, client, citizen, burgher or peasant, and in short no person or inhabitant of the Kingdom of Bohemia, of whatever rank, pre-eminence, dignity or condition he may be, shall be permitted to appeal from any processes, interlocutory or definitive sentences, or precepts of the King of Bohemia or of the judge of his Court, nor from executions of the same against himself, made, delivered or held in the royal court or before the judges of the King, Kingdom and Court aforesaid, or those to be delivered or made in future, to any other tribunal whatever; and that challenges or appeals, which may be lodged against these, are by that very fact without legal force, and that the appellants themselves incur by the fact the penalty of losing their causes.

units.la: 1. Necnon auctoritate Imperiali, & de certa sua scientia declaravit, quod ipse & omnes successores sui Boemiae Reges, universas auri & argentifodinas, atque minerias stanni, cupri, ferri, plumbi, & alteriuscunque metalli gravis, aceum salis, tam inventas, quam inveniendas in posterum quibuscunque temporibus in Regno suo Boemiae praedicto, ac terris, dominiis, territoriis & districtibus eidem Regno subjectis, & omnibus pertinentiis suis, tenere juste possint & potuerint ut in perpetuum, & legitime possidere: necnon Judaeos justo titulo habuisse & habere; & telonia a praeterito instituta seu indicta percipere, & nova rationabiliter instituere posse & potuisse: necnon monetas auri & argenti in omni loco & parte Regni sui Boemiæ prædicti, & subditarum eidem terrarum & pertinentiis ubique, si heredes aut successores sui Boemiæ Reges decreverint, ipsisque placuerit inde facere & mandare, sub omnibus modis & forma, in prædicto Regno Boemiæ circa talia consuetis usq; ad hæc tempora laudabiliter observari, &c.
units.tr: 1. Moreover, by imperial authority and from his own certain knowledge, he declared that he himself and all his successors as Kings of Bohemia may justly hold and have been able to hold, and lawfully and permanently possess, all gold and silver mines, and mines of tin, copper, iron, lead and any other heavy metal, and salt works, whether already discovered or to be discovered in the future at any times, in his aforesaid Kingdom of Bohemia, and in the lands, lordships, territories and districts subject to the same Kingdom, and all their dependencies; and that they have had and have justly had Jews, and have been able to collect tolls instituted or imposed from of old, and reasonably to establish new ones; and also that they may and could order, and that it has pleased them, and their heirs or successors as Kings of Bohemia, to make and command coins of gold and silver in every place and part of his aforesaid Kingdom of Bohemia, and in the lands subject to it and their dependencies everywhere, in all the ways and forms customary in the aforesaid Kingdom of Bohemia in such matters, which have been laudably observed up to the present time, etc.

units.la: 3. Quòd virtute Imperialis edicti, & consuetudine diutius introducta, liceat Boemiæ Regibus perpetuo tempore à quibuscunque Principibus, Magnatibus, Comitibus ac personis aliis quibuscunque, terras, castra, possessiones, prædia sive bona, emere, comparare, & in donum vel donationem ex quacunq; causa, aut in obligationem recipere, sub talium castrorum, terrarum, possessionum, prædiorum, seu bonorum conditione consueta, ut videlicet propria recipiantur & comparentur ut propria, libera aut libera, & ea quæ dependent in feudum similiter emantur in feudum, seu donata ac comparata taliter teneantur: ita tamen quòd ipsi Reges Boemiæ de his, quæ hoc modo comparaverint vel receperint, & Regno Boemiæ applicanda duxerint, ad consueta & debita jura de talibus sacro explenda & reddenda Imperio perpetuò sint adstricti, sicut in forma prædicti Domini nostri Imperatoris, quas desuper nostro & aliorum Principum Electorum consilio edidisse dignoscitur, plenius est expressum.
units.tr: 3. That by virtue of the imperial edict and a custom long established, it is permitted to the Kings of Bohemia, in perpetuity, to buy and acquire from any princes, magnates, counts or any other persons whatever lands, castles, possessions, estates or goods, and to receive them in gift or donation for any cause, or in pledge, under the usual condition of such castles, lands, possessions, estates or goods; namely that they are received and acquired as allodial, free or freehold, and those which depend as fiefs are likewise bought as fiefs, or, given or acquired, are held in that way; provided, however, that the Kings of Bohemia are bound in perpetuity, concerning those things which they have acquired or received in this way and have decided to be applied to the Kingdom of Bohemia, to perform and render to the Empire the customary and due rights pertaining to such things, as is more fully expressed in the form of our aforesaid Lord Emperor, which he is known to have issued thereon with the counsel of ourselves and the other Electoral Princes.

units.la: 4. Nos igitur præmissa omnia, & eorum quodlibet, sicut in solennibus Curiis Nurnbergæ celebratis in commune consilium nobiscum, & cum cæteris Principibus Electoribus nostris habitum, per ipsum Dominum nostrum Imperatorem deducta, multoq; studio ventilata, & rationabilia facta fuerint judicata, recognoscimus de nostro consilio & pleno processisse consensu; ratificantes, ac singula & omnia rata habentes & grata, benevolum nostrum eis adhibemus consensum ex certa scientia, pariter & assensum. In cujus rei testimonium præsentes literas fieri, & nostri sigilli appensione fecimus communiri. Datum in Nurnberg, anno 1356. in crastino Epiphaniæ ejusdem.
units.tr: 4. We therefore recognise that all the aforesaid matters, and each of them, as they were brought forward by our Lord the Emperor in the solemn Diets celebrated at Nuremberg, and as were debated with great care and judged reasonable, were carried out in common counsel with us and with the other Electoral Princes, and with our full consent; ratifying, and holding each and all as valid and acceptable, we give our benevolent consent and assent, from certain knowledge, likewise. In witness of which we have caused these present letters to be made and strengthened by the appending of our seal. Given at Nuremberg, in the year 1356, on the day after the Epiphany of the same.

units.la: CAROLI IV. IMPER. AUG. DECRETUM
units.tr: CHARLES IV, EMPEROR AUGUSTUS, DECREE

units.la: De jure & successione Electorum Palatinorum.
units.tr: On the right and succession of the Electors Palatine.

units.la: NOS KAROLUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator semper Augustus & Bohemiæ Rex, recognoscimus publicè per præsentes, & notificamus cunctis ipsam intuentibus seu legi audientibus, quòd nos cum omnibus Principibus Electoribus, Ecclesiasticis & sæcularibus, & ipsi nobiscum, voluntate communi & unanimiter, in Imperiali nostra Curia Nurenbergæ deliberavimus & concordavimus, & cum jure & sententia invenimus; invenimus, declaramus & pronunciamus pro jure, tanquam Rex Bohemiæ, sacri Imperii Romani Archipincerna & Coëlector præfatorum Principum; Ex quo magnificus Rupertus senior Comes Palatinus Rheni, sacri Romani Imperii Archidapifer, Dux Bavariæ, est in possessione vocis & electionis, in electione Romanorum Regis futuri Imperatoris, & etiam in possessione & dominio seu usu habet Principatum Palatinatus, Archidapiferiam, terras, vasallagia, cum omnibus pertinentiis, super quibus electio & vox Comitatus Palatini Rheni fundata est, sicut hoc nobis & omnibus Principibus præfatis & cuilibet liquidum est & notum, sine hæsitatione quacunq; quòd merito dictus Rupertus admittendus est, & nos ipsum de jure admisimus, & admittere volumus & debemus, ad quaslibet causas & ad omnia facta, quæ nos & antefati nostri Coelectores tractabimus vel faciemus pro honore & utilitate sacri Romani Imperii, & ejus fidelium subditorum, omnimodè sicut de jure & de honesta laudabili consuetudine Comes Palatinus Rheni, Archidapifer sacri Imperii, & Princeps Elector, merito admitti debet.
units.tr: We, Charles, by the grace of God Roman Emperor, ever Augustus, and King of Bohemia, publicly acknowledge by these presents, and make known to all who see or hear them read, that we, with all the Electoral Princes, ecclesiastical and secular, and they with us, by common will and unanimously, have deliberated and agreed in our Imperial Court at Nuremberg, and have found and judged in accordance with law and sentence; we find, declare and pronounce as law, as King of Bohemia, Arch-cupbearer of the Holy Roman Empire and co-elector of the aforesaid Princes, that since the illustrious Rupert the Elder, Count Palatine of the Rhine, Arch-steward of the Holy Roman Empire, Duke of Bavaria, is in possession of the vote and election in the election of the future Roman King and Emperor, and also holds in possession, dominion or use the Principality of the Palatinate, the Arch-stewardship, lands and fiefs, with all their appurtenances, on which the election and vote of the County Palatine of the Rhine is founded, as is clear and known to us and to all the aforesaid Princes, without any doubt whatever, that the said Rupert rightly ought to be admitted; and we have by law admitted him, and wish and ought to admit him, to whatever causes and to all acts which we and our aforesaid fellow electors shall treat or perform for the honour and advantage of the Holy Roman Empire and its faithful subjects, in every way, just as by law and by honourable and laudable custom the Count Palatine of the Rhine, Arch-steward of the Holy Empire and Elector Prince, ought rightly to be admitted.

units.la: 2. Etiam invenimus & pronunciamus tanquam jus & pro jure, si ita contingeret, quod aliquis alius cum Ducem Rupertum pro eisdem electione & voce electionis Romani Regis futuri Imperii petere vellet, quòd hujusmodi impetitionem facere non posset nec deberet, nisi priùs impetraret Principatum & terras prænarrati Palatinatus, Archidapiferiam seu officiū Dapiferiæ, vasallagia quidquid ad hujusmodi Palatinatum pertinet, & eam obtineat, sicut juris est. Quia nos cum jure & per sententiam invenimus, quòd electio & vox super Principatum, & super terras Palatinatus, & super Archidapiferiam taliter fundatæ sunt, quòd unum sine alio persistere non potest: sed oportet ea simul in omni impetitione tam in damno, quam in lucro inseparabiliter permanere. Harum testimonio literarum, nostro Imperiali sigillo sigillatarum. Datum Nurnbergiæ, anno Domini MCCCLVI. quinta feria post Epiphaniam Domini; Regnorum nostrorum anno decimo, Imperii verò primo.
units.tr: 2. Likewise we find and pronounce, as a right and by right, that if it should so happen that anyone else, seeking the same election and vote in the election of the future Roman King of the Empire, were to seek to challenge Duke Rupert, such a challenge could not and ought not to be made unless he first obtained the Principality and lands of the aforesaid Palatinate, the Arch-stewardship or office of steward, the fiefs, and whatever pertains to such Palatinate, and held them, as is right. For we have found by law and by sentence that the election and vote concerning the Principality, the lands of the Palatinate and the Arch-stewardship are so founded that one cannot exist without the other, but that they must remain inseparably together in every challenge, both in loss and in gain. In witness whereof these letters, sealed with our Imperial seal, are given at Nuremberg, in the year of the Lord 1356, on the fifth day after the Epiphany of the Lord; in the tenth year of our kingdoms, but the first of our Empire.

units.la: Simili per omnia tenore literas suas ediderunt Electores. Nos Gerlacus D.g. Archiepiscopus Moguntinus. Beymundus D.g. Archiepiscopus Trevirensis. Wilhelmus D.g. Archiepiscopus Coloniensis. Rudolphus D.g. Dux Saxoniæ Junior, &c. Ludovicus, qui nuncupatur Romanus, Marchio Brandenburgensis.
units.tr: The Electors issued their letters in exactly the same terms. We: Gerlach, by God's grace Archbishop of Mainz; Boemund, by God's grace Archbishop of Trier; Wilhelm, by God's grace Archbishop of Cologne; Rudolf, by God's grace Duke of Saxony the Younger, etc.; Ludwig, who is called the Roman, Margrave of Brandenburg.

units.la: CONSTITVTIONES KAROLI IV. IMPER. AVG. AUREA BULLA.
units.tr: The Constitutions of Charles IV, Emperor Augustus: the Golden Bull.

units.la: In nomine sanctæ & individuæ Trinitatis feliciter, Amen.
units.tr: In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, happily. Amen.

units.la: Carolus Quartus divina fauente clementia, Romanorum Imperator, semper Augustus, & Bohemiæ Rex, ad perpetuam rei memoriam.
units.tr: Charles IV, by the favour of divine clemency, Emperor of the Romans, ever Augustus, and King of Bohemia, to the perpetual memory of the matter.

units.la: OMNE regnum in seipso divisum desolabitur. nam Principes ejus facti sunt socii furum, ob quod Dominus misit in medio eorum spiritum vertiginis, ut palpent in meridie, sicut in tenebris, & candelabra eorum movit de loco suo, ut cæci sint, & duces cœcorum; & qui ambulant in tenebris, offendunt, & cæci mente scelera perpetrant, quæ in divisione contingunt. Dic Superbia, quomodo in Lucifero regnalles, si divisionem auxiliatricem non habuisses? Dic Sathan invide, quomodo Adam de Paradyso ejecisses, nisi eum ab obedientia divisisses? Dic Luxuria, quomodo Trojam destruxisses, nisi Helenam à viro suo divisisses? Dic Ira, quomodo Romanam Rempublicam destruxisses, nisi in divisione Pompejum & Julium sævientibus gladiis, ad intestina prælia concitasses? Tu quoque Invidia, Christianum Imperium à Deo, ad instar sanctæ & individuæ Trinitatis, fide, spe, & charitate, virtutibus Theologicis roboratum, cujus fundamentum super Christianissimo regno feliciter liberatur, antiquo veneno, quod velut serpens in palmites Imperiales, & membra ejus propinquiora, scelere vomuisti, ut concussis columnis totum ædificium ruinæ subjiceres, divisionem inter septem Electores Sacri Imperii, per quos, velut septem candelabra lucentia in unitate spiritus septiformis, sacrum illuminari debet Imperium, multotiens posuisti.
units.tr: EVERY kingdom divided against itself shall be laid waste. For its princes have become companions of thieves, and therefore the Lord has sent into the midst of them a spirit of giddiness, so that they grope at noon as in darkness, and he has moved their candlesticks from their place, so that they are blind, and leaders of the blind; and those who walk in darkness stumble, and, blind in mind, commit the crimes that arise from division. Tell me, Pride, how would you have reigned over Lucifer, had you not had division to help you? Tell me, envious Satan, how would you have cast Adam out of Paradise, had you not separated him from obedience? Tell me, Lust, how would you have destroyed Troy, had you not separated Helen from her husband? Tell me, Wrath, how would you have destroyed the Roman Republic, had you not stirred up internal battles by setting Pompey and Julius against one another with raging swords? And you too, Envy, have many times set division among the seven Electors of the Holy Empire, through whom, like seven shining candlesticks in the unity of the sevenfold Spirit, the Holy Empire ought to be enlightened, and you have done this so that, as the pillars were shaken, you might bring the whole building down into ruin; you who, like a serpent, have spat out the ancient poison of your crime upon the Imperial vines and their nearest members, so that the Christian Empire, fortified by the theological virtues of faith, hope and charity, after the likeness of the holy and undivided Trinity, whose foundation is happily set upon the most Christian kingdom, might be overthrown.

units.la: 2. Sane cum ex officio, quo Cæsarea dignitate potimur, futuris divisionum & dissensionum periculis inter Electores ipsos, de quorum numero, ut Rex Bohemiæ, esse dignoscimur, ratione duplici, tam ex Imperio, quam electionis jure, quo fungimur, occurrere teneamur: infrascriptas leges, ad unitatem inter Electores fovendam, & electionem unanimem inducendam, ac detestandæ divisioni prædictæ, variisq; periculis ex ea sequentibus, aditum præcludédum, in solemni Curia nostra Nurenbergensi, assidentibus nobis omnibus Principibus Electoribus, Ecclesiasticis & Secularibus, ac aliorum Principum, Comitum, Baronum, Procerum, Nobilium, & Civitatum multitudine numerosa, in solio Majestatis Cæsareæ, Imperialibus infulis, insigniis, & diademate decorati, matura deliberatione previa, de Imperialis potestatis plenitudine edidimus, statuimus, & duximus sanciendas, sub Anno Domini Millesimo, Trecentesimo, Quinquagesimo sexto, indictione nona, quarto Idus Januarii, Regnorum nostrorum anno decimo, Imperii verò 4 secundo.
units.tr: 2. Indeed, since by the office which we hold in the Imperial dignity we are bound to meet, on a twofold ground, both from the Empire and from the right of election which we exercise, the future dangers of division and dissension among the Electors themselves, of whose number we are known to be, as King of Bohemia, one; we have, in our solemn Diet at Nuremberg, with all the Electors, ecclesiastical and secular, sitting with us, and a numerous multitude of other princes, counts, barons, nobles, and cities, seated on the throne of Imperial Majesty and adorned with the Imperial mitre, insignia and diadem, after mature deliberation, and from the fullness of Imperial power, decreed, established and resolved to sanction the laws set out below, in order to foster unity among the Electors and to bring about a unanimous election, and to close the door to the detestable division just mentioned and to the various dangers that follow from it. This was done in the year of the Lord one thousand three hundred and fifty-six, in the ninth indiction, on the fourth day before the Ides of January, in the tenth year of our kingdoms and the second of our Empire.

units.la: CAP. I. QVALIS ESSE DEBEAT CONDVCTVS ELECTO- RVM, & à quibus.
units.tr: CHAP. I. WHAT KIND OF SAFE-CONDUCT THE ELECTORS OUGHT TO HAVE, AND FROM WHOM.

units.la: DECERNIMUS, & præsenti edicto Imperiali perpetuò valituro sancimus, ex certa scientia, & de Imperialis plenitudine potestatis, ut quotiescunq; & quandocunq; futuris temporibus necessitas, sive casus, electionis Regis Romanorum in Imperatorem promovendi emerserit, & Principes Electores ad electionem hujusmodi, juxta antiquam laudabilem consuetudinem, habuerint proficisci; unusquisq; Princeps Elector, si & quando super hoc fuerit requisitus, quoslibet Principes Collectores suos, vel ipsorum nuncios, quos ad electionem ipsam transmiserint, per terras, territoria, & loca sua, & etiam ultra, sicut longius poterit, conducere teneatur, & eis absq; dolo conductum versus civitatem, in qua talis electio fuerit celebranda, & ab illa etiam redeundo; sub pœna perjurii ac perditionis (pro illa duntaxat vice) suæ vocis, quà in electione hujusmodi fuerat habiturus, quas quidem pœnas eos, vel eum, qui in præstando memorato conductu rebelles seu rebellem, negligentes seu negligentem se præbuerint, eo ipso decernimus incidisse.
units.tr: We decree, and by this present Imperial edict, which shall remain in force forever, we sanction, from certain knowledge and from the fullness of Imperial power, that whenever and as often as in future times the need or occasion arises to elect a King of the Romans to be promoted to the Emperor, and the Electors have, according to the old and praiseworthy custom, to set out for such an election, each Elector, if and when he is requested to do so, shall be bound to conduct, through his lands, territories and places, and even beyond them as far as he can, any fellow Electors or their envoys whom they have sent to that election, and to conduct them without deceit to the city where such an election is to be held, and back again from it; under penalty of perjury and of the loss of his vote in that election (for that occasion only), which he would otherwise have had. We decree that by this very fact those who show themselves rebellious or negligent in granting this safe-conduct, or any of them, incur these penalties.

units.la: 2. Statuimus insuper, & mandamus universis aliis Principibus, feuda à Sacro Imperio Romano tenentibus, quocunq; nomine censeantur, necnon Comitibus, Baronibus, Militibus, Clientibus, Nobilibus & Ignobilibus, Civibus & Communitatibus castrorum, civitatum & locorum Sacri Imperii universis, ut eodem tempore, dum videlicet Regis Romanorum in Imperatorem promovendi electio celebranda occurrerit, unumquemque Principem Electorem ab ipsis, vel eorum aliquo, conductum hujusmodi postulantem, vel ejusdem nuncios, quos ad electionem ipsam direxerit, ut præfatur, per territoria sua, & alias, quanto possunt remotius, absq; dolo, modo prædicto conducant. Si qui vero huic nostræ constitutioni contrarie præsumpserint, subscriptas eo ipso pœnas incurrant. Omnes quidem Principes & Comites, Barones, Nobiles, Milites, & Clientes, ac universi contrarium facientes, reatum perjurii, & privationem omnium feudorum, quæ à S. Romano Imperio, & à quibuscunque aliis obtinent, & etiam omnium possessionum suarum à quocunque habitarum, incurrant. Omnes quoque cives, & communitates contra prænissa facere præsumentes, similiter sint perjuri, & nihilominus universis suis juribus, libertatibus, privilegiis, & gratiis, à sacro obtentis Imperio, sint omnino privati, & cum personis, & bonis suis omnibus bannū & proscriptionem Imperiale incurrant; atq; eosdem quos ipso facto ex nunc, prout ex tunc, omni jure privamus. Deinceps, cuilibet hominum auctoritate propria, & sine judicio, seu invocatione Magistratus cujusliber, impune licebit eos invadere; nulla mq; poenam propter hoc invadens ipsos, debebit ab Imperio, seu quovis alio formidare, praesertim cum contra Rempublicam ac Sacri Statum Imperii ac dignitatem, ac etiam contra honorem proprium & salutem, tantae rei temerarii neglectores, tanquam rebelles, inobedientes & perfidi, infideliter & perverse agere convincantur.
units.tr: 2. We further establish and command all other princes holding fiefs from the Holy Roman Empire, by whatever name they are called, and likewise counts, barons, knights, vassals, nobles and commoners, citizens and communities of the castles, cities and places of the Holy Empire, all of them, that at the same time, namely when the election of a King of the Romans to be promoted to Emperor is to be held, they shall, through their territories and elsewhere, as far as they can, without deceit and in the manner described, conduct every Elector who asks for such a safe-conduct from them or from any one of them, or his envoys whom he has sent to that election, as stated above. If anyone presumes to act contrary to this our constitution, let him incur the penalties written here by this very fact. All princes and counts, barons, nobles, knights and vassals, and all who act contrary to this, shall incur the guilt of perjury and the loss of all fiefs which they hold from the Holy Roman Empire or from any others, and also of all their possessions, from whomever they hold them. Likewise all citizens and communities who presume to act against the aforesaid shall similarly be perjured, and, besides this, they shall be wholly deprived of all their rights, liberties, privileges and graces obtained from the Holy Empire, and shall incur the Imperial ban and proscription, with their persons and all their goods; and these same persons we deprive, by this very fact, from now on as from then, of every right. Henceforth it shall be lawful for anyone, on his own authority and without judgment or the invocation of any magistrate whatsoever, to attack them with impunity; and the one attacking them shall fear no penalty on this account from the Empire or from anyone else, especially since those who are careless of so great a matter are proved to act faithlessly and perversely, as rebels, disobedient and treacherous, against the Republic, the holy state and dignity of the Empire, and also against their own honour and safety.

units.la: 3. Decernentes insuper, & mandantes, ut omnium civitatum cives, & communia jam dictis Principibus Electoribus, & eorum cuilibet hoc poscenti, eorumq; nunciis, victualia in communi pretio atq; currus, pro suis, seu nunciorum praedictorum, hominumq; suorum necessitatibus, dum ad praedictam civitatem causa celebrandae electionis praedictae accesserint, & etiam dum discesserint ab eadem, vendere seu vendi facere teneantur; nullam in praemissis frandem quomodolibet adhibendo: aliquin contrarium facientes, poenas illas volumus ipso facto incurrere, quas in praecedentibus contra cives & communitates duximus promulgandas.
units.tr: 3. We further decree and command that the citizens and communities of all cities shall be bound to sell or cause to be sold provisions at the common price, and carriages, for the needs of the aforesaid Electors, to any of them who asks for them, and to their envoys, and to their men, when they come to the aforesaid city for the purpose of holding the aforesaid election, and also when they depart from it; using no fraud in these matters in any way. We wish that those who act contrary incur, by this very fact, those penalties which we have ordered to be promulgated above against citizens and communities.

units.la: 4. Quisquis insuper ex Principibus, Comitibus, Baronibus, Militibus, Clientibus, Nobilibus seu ignobilibus, Civibus seu Communitatibus civitatum, Principi Electori, ad Electionem de Rege Romanorum celebrandam eunti, vel ab ipsa denuo redeunti, hostiles custodias tendere, seu insidias parare praesumpserit, aut ipsos, vel eorum aliquem in sua, vel suorum personis, aut rebus, invadere vel turbare, seu ipsorum, vel alicujus eorum nuncios antedictos, sive conductum petierint, sive etiam non duxerint exigendum; huncunà cum universis malitiae suae complicibus, ipso facto supradictas poenas decernimus incurrisse; ita videlicet, quòd quaevis persona poenâ incidat, sive poenas, quas juxta praemissa pro qualitate personarum duximus infligendas.
units.tr: 4. Furthermore, whoever among princes, counts, barons, knights, vassals, nobles or commoners, citizens or communities of cities, presumes to lay hostile ambushes or set traps for an Elector going to the election of a King of the Romans, or returning again from it, or presumes to attack or disturb them, or any one of them, in their persons or property, or the aforesaid envoys of them or of any one of them, whether they have asked for a safe-conduct or have not thought it necessary to demand one: such a person, together with all accomplices in his wickedness, we decree has by this very fact incurred the penalties stated above; so that any person whatever shall be liable to the penalty, or to the penalties which we have ordered to be inflicted according to the rank of the persons, in accordance with what has been set out.

units.la: 5. Si vero aliquis Princeps Elector, cum aliquo suo Coelectore inimicitias gereret, & inter eos quaecunque contentio, controversia seu dissensio verteretur; hiis nequaquam obstantibus, alter alterum, vel alterius nuncios ad electionem hujusmodi destinandos, praemisso modo conducere sit astrictus sub poena perjurii, ac perditionis (ea vice dumtaxat) suae vocis in electione, ut superius est expressum.
units.tr: 5. If indeed any Elector had enmity with a fellow Elector, and any quarrel, controversy or dissension arose between them, nonetheless, notwithstanding these things, each of them is bound to furnish a safe-conduct to the other, or to the other's envoys to be sent to such an election, in the manner described, under penalty of perjury and of the loss of his vote in the election (for that occasion only), as is expressed above.

units.la: 6. Si qui vero alii Principes, Comites, Barones, Milites, Clientes, Nobiles & Ignobiles, cives vel communia civitatum, cum aliquo Principe Electore, vel pluribus ex eisdem, adversam gererent voluntatem, seu quaevis discordia inter ipsos ad invicem, vel guerra, sive dissensio verteretur, nihilominus omni contradictione & dolo cessantibus, Principi Electori, vel Principibus, seu ejus vel ipsorum nunciis ad electionem hujusmodi destinandis, & redeuntibus ab eadem, talem debeant praestare conductum, prout singuli poenas jam dictas, per nos videlicet in se latas, voluerint evitare; quas eos, qui secus se egerint incurrisse decernimus eo ipso.
units.tr: 6. If, however, any other princes, counts, barons, knights, vassals, nobles or commoners, citizens or communities of cities, bore a hostile will toward some Elector, or several of them, or if any discord, war or dissension arose between them, nevertheless, with all opposition and deceit set aside, they must furnish such a safe-conduct to the Elector or Electors, or to their envoys to be sent to such an election and returning from it, as each of them wishes to avoid the penalties already mentioned, which we have laid down against those who act otherwise; and we decree that those who act otherwise incur them by this very fact.

units.la: 7. Ad praemissorum autem omnium firmitatem, & certitudinem ampliorem, jubemus & volumus, ut universi Principes Electores, & caeteri Principes, nec non Comites, Barones, Nobiles, Civitates, seu ipsarum communitates, praemissa omnia litteris & juramentis suis firmare, & ad ea bona fide, ac sine dolo implenda efficaciter se debeant obligare. Quicunque veto litteras hujusmodi dare renuerit, poenas illas ipso facto incidat, quas pro personarum conditione, per praemissa singulis duximus infligendas.
units.tr: 7. To make all the foregoing firmer and more certain, we command and will that all the Electors, the other princes, and likewise the counts, barons, nobles, cities, and their communities shall confirm all the foregoing by their letters and oaths, and shall bind themselves effectively to fulfil them in good faith and without deceit. Whoever refuses to give such letters shall incur ipso facto those penalties which we have decided, by the above provisions, to impose on individuals according to their rank.

units.la: 8. Si quis autem Princeps Elector, aliusve Princeps, cujuscumque conditionis, aut status, seudum vel feuda à Sacro tenens Imperio, aut Comes, Baro, vel Nobilis, seu successores talium vel haeredes, supra & infra scriptas Imperiales nostras constitutiones & leges adimplere noluerit, aut eis contraire praesumpserit; siquidem talis Princeps, Elector exiterit, ex tunc caeteri sui Coelectores à suo ipsum deinceps excludant consortio, ipsque voce electionis, & aliorum Principum Electorum loco, dignitate careat atque jure; necinvestiatur de feudis, quae à Sacro Imperio visus fuerit obtinere, alius veto Princeps, aut vir Nobilis, ut praefertur, in has nostras leges committens, similiter non investiatur feudis, quae à Sacro Imperio, vel alias obtinet à quocunque; & nihilominus omnes praemissas poenas, suam concernentes personam, incidar eo ipso.
units.tr: 8. If any Elector, or other prince of whatever rank or status, holding a fief or fiefs from the Holy Empire, or any count, baron, or noble, or their successors or heirs, is unwilling to fulfil the above and below written Imperial constitutions and laws, or presumes to act against them, then, if such a person is an Elector, his fellow Electors shall thenceforth exclude him from their company, and he shall lose his voice in the election and his dignity and right, in place of the other Electors. Nor shall he be invested with the fiefs which he is found to hold from the Holy Empire. Likewise, if another prince, or noble man, as stated, offends against these our laws, he shall not be invested with the fiefs which he holds from the Holy Empire or from anyone else; and nevertheless he shall incur, ipso facto, all the penalties mentioned above, so far as they concern his person.

units.la: 9. Quamvis autem universos Principes, Comites, Barones, Nobiles, Milites, Clientes, Civitates quoq; & Communitates illarum, ad praestandum cuilibet Principi Electori, vel ejus nunciis, praefatum conductum, ut praedicitur, indistincte velimus, & decreverimus obligari; nihilominus eorum cuilibet singulares conductus & conductores, pro regionum & locorum adjacentia, cuilibet magis, aptos duximus designandos, ut statim per sequentia plenius apparebit.
units.tr: 9. Although we have willed and decreed that all princes, counts, barons, nobles, knights, vassals, and likewise cities and their communities, be indiscriminately bound to provide the aforesaid safe-conduct to any Elector or his envoys, as has been said, nevertheless we have thought fit to appoint for each of them particular safe-conducts and guarantors, according to the neighbourhood of regions and places, as will appear more fully in what follows.

units.la: 10. Primò namq; Regem Bohemiae, Sacri Imperii Archipincernam, conducent Archiepiscopus Moguntinensis, Bambergensis & Herbipolensis Episcopi; Burggravii Nurembergenses; item illi de Hoenloe, de Wertheim, illi de Bruneck, & de Hanouu; item civitates, Nuremberg, Rotenburg, & Windesheim.
units.tr: 10. First, the Archbishop of Mainz, and the Bishops of Bamberg and Würzburg, shall escort the King of Bohemia, Archcupbearer of the Holy Empire; the Burgraves of Nuremberg; likewise those of Hohenlohe, of Wertheim, those of Bruneck, and of Hanau; likewise the cities of Nuremberg, Rothenburg, and Windsheim.

units.la: 11. Deinde Archiepiscopum Colonienfem, Sacri Imperii per Italiam Archicancellarium, conducent & conducere tenebuntur Moguntinensis & Trevirensis Archiepiscopi; Comes Palatinus Rheni, Landgravius Hassiae; item de Katzenelnbogen, de Nassouu, de Dietze, Comites; item de Isenburg, de Wesserburg, de Runckel, de Limpurg & Falckenstein; item civitates Wetzlar, Geylnhausen & Fridberg.
units.tr: 11. Next, the Archbishop of Cologne, Archchancellor of the Holy Empire through Italy, shall be escorted, and the Archbishops of Mainz and Trier are bound to escort him: the Count Palatine of the Rhine, the Landgrave of Hesse; likewise the counts of Katzenelnbogen, of Nassau, of Diez; likewise those of Isenburg, of Westerburg, of Runkel, of Limburg, and of Falkenstein; likewise the cities of Wetzlar, Gelnhausen, and Friedberg.

units.la: 12. Item Archiepiscopum Trevirensem, Sacri Imperii per Galliam, & Regnum Arelatense Archicancellarium, conducent Archiepiscopus Moguntinensis, Comes Palatinus Rheni; item de Spanheim, de Veldentz Comites; item Die Raugraven, Wildegraven, de Nassoup, de Isenburg, de Westerburg, de Runckel, de Limburg, de Dietz, de Katzenelnbogen, de Eppenstein, de Falckenstein; item civitas Moguntinensis.
units.tr: 12. Likewise, the Archbishop of Trier, Archchancellor of the Holy Empire through Gaul and the Kingdom of Arles, shall be escorted by the Archbishop of Mainz and the Count Palatine of the Rhine; likewise the counts of Spanheim and Veldenz; likewise the Rhinegraves, the Wildgraves, those of Nassau, of Isenburg, of Westerburg, of Runkel, of Limburg, of Diez, of Katzenelnbogen, of Eppstein, and of Falkenstein; likewise the city of Mainz.

units.la: 13. Deinde Comitem Palatinum Rheni, Sacri Imperii Archidapiferum, conducere debebit Archiepiscopus Moguntinensis.
units.tr: 13. Next, the Count Palatine of the Rhine, Archsteward of the Holy Empire, shall be escorted by the Archbishop of Mainz.

units.la: 14. Ducem vero Saxoniæ, Sacri Imperii Archimareschallum, tenebitur conducere Rex Bohemiæ, Moguntinensis, & Magdeburgensis Archiepiscopi; item Bambergensis, & Herbipolensis Episcopi; Marchio Misnensis, Langravius Hassiæ; item Fuldensis, & Hersfeldensis Abbates; Burggravii Nurenbergenses; item illi de Hohenloe, de Wertheim, de Bruneck, de Hanovv, de Falckenstein, item civitates Erffordia, Mülhausen, Nuremberg, Rotenburg, & Windesheim.
units.tr: 14. The Duke of Saxony, Archmarshal of the Holy Empire, shall be bound to be escorted by the King of Bohemia and the Archbishops of Mainz and Magdeburg; likewise by the Bishops of Bamberg and Würzburg; the Margrave of Meissen and the Landgrave of Hesse; likewise the Abbots of Fulda and Hersfeld; the Burgraves of Nuremberg; likewise those of Hohenlohe, of Wertheim, of Bruneck, of Hanau, and of Falkenstein; likewise the cities of Erfurt, Mühlhausen, Nuremberg, Rothenburg, and Windsheim.

units.la: 15. Et hi omnes proxime nominati, Marchionem Brandenburgensem, Sacri Imperii Archicamerarium, similiter conducere tenebuntur.
units.tr: 15. All those just named shall likewise be bound to escort the Margrave of Brandenburg, Archchamberlain of the Holy Empire.

units.la: 16. Volumus autem & expresse statuimus, ut unusquisque Princeps Elector, qui talem voluerit habere conductum, his, a quibus ipsum postulare decreverit, hoc ipsum adeo tempestive, viamque qua fuerit transiturus, insinuet, & talem conductum exposcat, ut illi, qui ad conductum hujusmodi impendendum deputati, & qui taliter fuerint requisiti, ad hoc oportune se valeant & commode praparare.
units.tr: 16. We will also and expressly ordain that every Elector who wishes to have such a safe-conduct shall notify those from whom he has decided to request it, and shall ask for it in good time, stating the route by which he intends to travel, so that those who are appointed to provide such a conduct, and who have been asked in this way, may be able to prepare themselves for it properly and conveniently.

units.la: 17. Præmissas vero constitutiones, circa materiam conductus editas, ita sane debere declaramus intelligi, ut unusquisq; superius nominatus, vel forsan non expressus, a quo in casu præmisso conductum requiri contigerit, ad præstandum ipsum per suas dumtaxat terras & territoria, ac etiam ultra, quanto poterit remotius, absq; dolo, sub poenis contentis superius, sit astrictus.
units.tr: 17. We declare that the foregoing constitutions issued concerning the matter of safe-conduct are to be understood in such a way that each of the persons named above, or perhaps not named, from whom a safe-conduct happens to be requested in the case set out, is bound to provide it, without deceit and under the penalties contained above, not only through his own lands and territories but also beyond them, as far as the escort can go.

units.la: 18. Præterea statuimus, ac etiam ordinamus, ut Archiepiscopus Moguntinensis, qui fuerit pro tempore, singulis Principibus Coelectoribus suis, Ecclesiasticis & Secularibus, electionem eandem, per suos nuncios, patentibus debeat litteris intimare. in quibus quidem litteris talis dies & terminus exprimatur, infra quem eædem litteræ ad singulos eosdem Principes verisimiliter pollint pervenire.
units.tr: 18. Furthermore, we also decree and ordain that the Archbishop of Mainz who is in office at the time shall, through his envoys, notify each of his fellow Electors, ecclesiastical and secular, of this election by open letters. In these letters a day and a term shall be stated, within which the same letters may reasonably be expected to reach each of these princes.

units.la: 19. Hujusmodi vero litteræ continebunt, ut a die in litteris ipsis expressa, infra tres menses continuos, omnes & singuli Principes Electores, Frankenford super Moganum esse debeant constitui, vel suos Legales ad eundem terminum, atq; locum nuncios destinare, cum plena & omnimoda potestate, suisq; patentibus litteris, majori cujuslibet eorum sigillo signatis, ad eligendum Romanorum Regem in Cæsarem promovendum.
units.tr: 19. Such letters shall state that, within three continuous months from the day expressed in the letters, all and each of the Electors must be present at Frankfurt on the Main, or must send their lawful envoys to that day and place, with full and unlimited power, and with their open letters sealed with their greater seal, to elect the King of the Romans to be promoted to Emperor.

units.la: 20. Qualiter autem, & sub qua forma, tales litteræ confici debeant, & quæ in eis solemnitas debeat immutabiliter observari, & in qua forma & modo Principes Electores nuncios suos, ad electionem hujusmodi destinandos, ad potestatem, mandatum, seu procuratoria ordinate debuerint, ad finem præsentis libri conscriptum invenitur clarius expressum; & eandem formam illic traditam, mandamus, & de Imperialis potestatis plenitudine usquequaque decernimus observari.
units.tr: 20. How, and in what form, such letters ought to be drawn up, what solemnity must be unchangeably observed in them, and in what form and manner the Electors ought properly to give their envoys, sent to this election, power, mandate, or procuratorial authority, is found more clearly set out at the end of this present book. We command that the form given there be observed, and by the fullness of Imperial power we decree that it be observed in every respect.

units.la: 21. Cum autem ad hoc perventum fuerit, quod de Imperatoris, vel Regis Romanorum obitu in diocesi Moguntinensi constiterit, ex tunc infra unum mensem a die notitiæ obitus hujusmodi continuè numerandum, singulis Principibus Electoribus obitum ipsum & intimationem, de quibus praemittitur, per Archiepiscopum Moguntinensem jubemus, & decernimus, suis patentibus litteris declarari. quod si idem Archiepiscopus in executione, & intimatione hujusmodi, negligens aut remissus fortassis existeret, extunc iidem Principes motu proprio etiam non vocati, pro fidei suæ virtute, quasacrum prosequi tenentur Imperium, post hoc infra tres menses, sicut in constitutione proxime posita supra cōtinetur, in civitate Frankenford sæpe dicta conveniant, electuri Regem Romanorum in Cæsarem promovendum.
units.tr: 21. When it has come to pass that the death of the Emperor or King of the Romans has been established in the diocese of Mainz, then, within one month continuously counted from the day on which the news of such death is received, we command and decree that the Archbishop of Mainz declare the death and the notice of which we have spoken to each of the Electors by his open letters. But if the same Archbishop should perhaps be negligent or remiss in carrying out and giving such notice, then the same princes, even if not summoned, shall of their own accord, by the strength of their faith, which they are bound to pursue as the Holy Empire, assemble within three months after this, as is contained in the constitution placed just above, in the aforesaid city of Frankfurt, to elect the King of the Romans to be promoted to Emperor.

units.la: 22. Debet autem unusquisq; Princeps Elector, vel sui nuncii, prædictam civitatem Frankenford cum ducentis equitaturis tantummodo, præfatæ electionis tempore, introire; in quorum numero quinquaginta tantum armatos, vel pauciores, secum introducere poterit, sed non plures.
units.tr: 22. Each Elector, or his envoys, must enter the aforesaid city of Frankfurt at the time of the said election with only two hundred horsemen; of these he may bring with him fifty armed men, or fewer, but not more.

units.la: 23. Princeps vero Elector, ad electionem hujusmodi vocatus & requisitus, & ad ipsam non veniens, vel legales nuncios cum litteris patentibus, sigillo suo majori sigillatis, plenamq; & liberam ac omnimodam potestatem continentibus, ad eligendum Romanorum Regem, futurum Imperatorem non dirigens; aut veniens, aut hujusmodi nuncios forte transmittens, si postea Princeps ipse, aut prædicti nuncii, à prædicto electionis loco recederent, Rege Romanorum futuro Cæsare non electo, nec ad præmissa procuratore legitimo substituto solemniter & relicto, electionis vocem seu jure, quod incidem electione habuit, & tali modo deseruit, careat ea vice.
units.tr: 23. If an Elector, summoned and requested to this election, neither comes to it, nor sends lawful envoys with open letters sealed with his greater seal and containing full and free and unlimited power to elect the King of the Romans, who is to be Emperor; or if, having come, or perhaps having sent such envoys, he or the said envoys withdraw from the said place of election before the King of the Romans, who is to be Caesar, has been elected, and without a lawful proxy being solemnly appointed and left for the aforesaid matters, then he shall lose, for that occasion, his voice in the election, or the right which he had in the election, and which he has thus forfeited.

units.la: 24. Injungimus autem civibus de Frankenford, & mandamus, ut ipsi universos Principes Electores in genere, & quemlibet eorum, ab invasione alterius, si quid inter eos advertitatis emergeret, & etiam ab omni homine, cum omnibus eorum hominibus, quos ipsi, & eorum quilibet, in præfato ducentorum equorum suorum numero, ad præfatam duxerint civitatem, in virtute juramenti, quod super hoc ipsos ad Sancta præstare statuimus, fideli studio & solerti diligentia protegant, & defendant; alioquin perjurii reatum incurrant, & nihilominus omnia jura sua, libertates, privilegia, gratias & indulta, quæ à sacro obtinere noscuntur Imperio, omnino amittant; bannumque Imperiale cum personis, & bonis suis omnibus incidant eo ipso; & liceat extunc omni homini auctoritate propropria, ac fine judicio, cives eosdem, quos eo casu exnunc, prout extunc, omni jure privamus, tamquam proditores, infideles, & rebelles Imperii, impunè invadere, ita quod invadentes hujusmodi, poenam quamcumque à Sacro Imperio, vel quovis alio, nequaquam debeant formidare.
units.tr: 24. We enjoin and command the citizens of Frankfurt to protect and defend, with faithful zeal and careful diligence, all the Electors in general and each one of them, from the attack of another, should any dispute arise between them, and also from every man, together with all their men whom they, or any of them, bring into the said city within the number of their two hundred horses, by virtue of the oath which we decree they shall swear on the holy things concerning this matter. Otherwise they shall incur the guilt of perjury, and, besides, shall wholly lose all their rights, liberties, privileges, favours, and indults which they are known to hold from the Sacred Empire; and they shall incur the Imperial ban, with their persons and all their goods, ipso facto. And from then on it shall be lawful for any man, on his own authority and without judgment, to attack with impunity those citizens whom, in that case, we now deprive, as we then deprive them, of every right, as traitors, faithless men, and rebels against the Empire; so that those who attack them shall have no fear of any penalty whatever from the Holy Empire or from anyone else.

units.la: 25. Cives insuper antedicti de Franckenford, per omne rempus illud, quo super electione saepe dicta tractari, & agi contigerit, neminem in praefatam civitatem cujuscumque dignitatis, conditionis vel status extiterit, intromittant, vel intrare quovis modo permittant; Principibus Electoribus, eorum nuncis, & Procuratoribus antedictis dumtaxat exceptis, quorum quilibet cum ducentis equis debebit, ut praedicitur, intromitti.
units.tr: 25. Furthermore, the aforesaid citizens of Frankfurt shall not admit, nor permit to enter by any means, anyone of whatever dignity, condition or rank into the said city during the whole time in which the election often mentioned happens to be discussed and conducted; except only the Electoral Princes, their envoys and the aforesaid proctors, each of whom, as has been said, shall be admitted with two hundred horses.

units.la: 26. Si verò post ipsorum Principum Electorum introitum, seu in ipsorum praesentia, in praefata civitate aliquem reperiri contigerit, illius exitum cives ipsi debebunt absque mora, & cum effectu, protinus ordinare, sub omnibus poenis contra ipsos superius promulgatis, ac etiam in virtute juramenti, quod cives ipsi de Franckenford super eo, virtute praesentis constitutionis, praestare debebunt ad Sancta, ut in praecedentibus est expressum.
units.tr: 26. But if, after the entry of the Electoral Princes themselves, or in their presence, someone should happen to be found in the said city, the citizens themselves shall be bound to arrange his departure at once, without delay and effectively, under all the penalties promulgated above against them, and also under the sanction of the oath which the citizens of Frankfurt must swear concerning this matter by virtue of the present constitution, upon the holy things, as has been expressed in the preceding sections.

units.la: CAPUT II.
units.tr: CHAPTER II.

units.la: DE ELECTIONE ROMANI REGIS.
units.tr: ON THE ELECTION OF THE ROMAN KING.

units.la: Postquam autem saepe dicti Electores seu nuncii, civitatem Frankenford ingressi fuerint, statim subsequenti die, diluculò in Ecclesia Sancti Bartholomaei Apostoli, ibidem in omnium ipsorum praesentia Missam de sancto Spiritu faciant decantari ad finem, ut ipse sanctus Spiritus corda ipsorum illustret, & eorum sensibus lumen suae virtutis infundat, quatenus ipsi suo fulti praesidio, hominem justum, bonum, & utilem eligere valeant in Regem Romanorum, futurumque Caesarem, ac pro salute populi Christiani.
units.tr: After the Electors, or their envoys, have entered the city of Frankfurt, then on the following day, at dawn, in the Church of St Bartholomew the Apostle, they shall have a Mass of the Holy Spirit sung there in the presence of all of them, so that the Holy Spirit himself may illuminate their hearts and pour the light of his power into their minds, that, supported by his protection, they may be able to choose a just, good and useful man as King of the Romans, and future Emperor, and for the welfare of the Christian people.

units.la: 2. Peracta quoque Missa hujusmodi, omnes illi Electores, seu nuncii accedant ad altare, in quo Missa eadem extitit celebrata, ubi Principes Electores Ecclesiastici coram Evangelio Beati Joannis: In principio erat verbum, quod illi ante ipsos poni debebit, manus suas pectori cum reverentia superponant: Seculares vero Principes Electores, dictum Evangelium corporaliter manibus suis tangant; qui omnes, cum tota ipsorum familia, tunc ibi debebunt inermes assistere. Ac Archiepiscopus Moguntinensis formam juramenti eis dabit, & unà cum ipsis, & ipsi, vel absentium nuncii, unà cum eo juramentum praestabunt vulgariter in hunc modum.
units.tr: 2. When this Mass has also been completed, all those Electors, or envoys, shall go to the altar at which the Mass was celebrated. There the ecclesiastical Electors shall lay their hands reverently on their breasts before the Gospel of St John, "In the beginning was the Word", which shall be placed before them. The secular Electors shall touch the said Gospel bodily with their hands. All of them, with their whole household, shall then be bound to attend there unarmed. The Archbishop of Mainz shall give them the form of the oath, and together with him, they and the envoys of those absent shall take the oath in the vernacular in this manner.

units.la: 3. Ego N. Archiepiscopus Moguntinensis, Sacri Imperii per Germaniam Archicancellarius, ac Princeps Elector, juro ad haec sancta Dei Evangelia hic praesentialiter coram me posita, quod ego per fidem, qua Deo, & Sacro Romano Imperio sum astrictus, secundum omnem discretionem & intellectum meum, cum Dei adjutorio eligere volo temporale caput populo Christiano, id est, Regem Romanorum in Caesarem promovendum, qui ad hoc existat idoneus, in quantum discretio & sensus mei me dirigunt, & secundum fidem praedictam; vocemque meam, & votum, seu electionem praefatam, dabo absque omni pacto, stipendio, pretio, vel promisso, seu quocumque modo talia valeant appellari; sic me Deus adjuvet, & omnes Sancti.
units.tr: 3. "I, N., Archbishop of Mainz, Archchancellor of the Holy Empire throughout Germany, and Prince Elector, swear by these holy Gospels of God placed here before me, that by the faith by which I am bound to God and the Holy Roman Empire, I will, according to all my discernment and understanding, with God's help, elect as temporal head of the Christian people, that is, as King of the Romans to be promoted to Emperor, the man who is fit for this, insofar as my discernment and judgment direct me and in accordance with the aforesaid faith; and I will give my voice, my vote, or the aforesaid election, without any pact, stipend, price, or promise, or whatever other name such things may bear. So God help me, and all the Saints."

units.la: 4. Praestito denique per Electores seu nuncios, in forma & modo praedictis, hujusmodi juramento, ad electionem procedant, necamodò de jam dicta civitate Frankenford separentur, nisi prius major pars ipsorum temporale caput mundo elegerit, seu populo Christiano, Regem videlicet Romanorum in Caesarem promovendum.
units.tr: 4. Finally, when the Electors, or their envoys, have taken this oath in the aforesaid form and manner, they shall proceed to the election, and they shall not thereafter be separated from the aforesaid city of Frankfurt until the greater part of them has chosen the temporal head for the world, or for the Christian people, namely the King of the Romans to be promoted to Emperor.

units.la: 5. Quod si facere dilulerint infra triginta dies, à die praestiti juramenti praefati continuò numerandos, extunc transactis eisdem triginta diebus, amodò panem manducet & aquam bibant, & nullatenus civitatem exeant antedictam, nisi prius per ipsos, vel majorem partem ipsorum, Rectorem seu temporale caput fidelium electum fuerit, ut praefertur.
units.tr: 5. But if they put this off for thirty days, counted continuously from the day of the aforesaid oath, then, once those thirty days have passed, they shall eat bread and drink water from then on, and by no means leave the said city, unless first a ruler or temporal head of the faithful has been elected by them, or by the greater part of them, as stated.

units.la: 6. Postquam autem in eodem loco ipsi, vel pars eorum major numero elegerit, talis electio pro nndebabari & reputari debebit, ac si foret ab ipsis omnibus, nemine discrepante, concorditer celebrata.
units.tr: 6. Once they, or the greater part of them in number, have elected in that same place, such an election shall be held and regarded as if it had been celebrated by all of them together, with no one dissenting.

units.la: 7. Sique per tempus aliquod morari, abesse, & tardare contigeret aliquem de Electoribus, seu nuncis antedictis, dum tamen veniret, antequam praedicta esset electio celebrata, hunc ad electionem ipsam in eo statu admitti debere decernimus, in quo ipsa adventus sui tempore consistebat.
units.tr: 7. And if it should happen that any of the aforesaid Electors, or envoys, is delayed, absent, or late for some time, yet comes before the election has been completed, we decree that he must be admitted to the election in the state in which it stood at the time of his arrival.

units.la: 8.
