Et quia de antiqua, approbata, & laudabili consuetudine, tam inconvulse, quam immutabiliter quod subscribitur, semper extitit hactenus observatum; ideoque & nos constituimus, & de Imperialis decernimus plenitudine potestatis, quod is, qui modo praemissò in Regem fuerit Romanorum electus, peracta statim electione hujusmodi, priusquam in aliquibus causis aliis, sive negotiis, virtute Sacri Imperii administret, universis & singulis Principibus Electoribus, Ecclesiasticis & Secularibus, qui propinquiora sacri Imperii membra esse noscuntur, omnia ipsorum privilegia, litteras, jura, libertates, concessiones, antiquas consuetudines, & etiam dignitates, & quidquid ipsi ab Imperio usque in diem electionis suae obtinuerunt & possederunt, absque dilatione & contradictione confirmare & approbare debeat, per suas literas & sigilla; ipsisque praemissa omnia innovare, postquam Imperialibus fuerit infulis coronatus.
units.tr: 8. And because, from ancient, approved and praiseworthy custom, what is written below has always been observed hitherto, as inviolably as unchangeably, therefore we also establish, and by the fullness of imperial power decree, that he who has been elected King of the Romans in the manner set out above shall, immediately after such election, and before he administers anything in other causes or affairs by virtue of the Holy Empire, confirm and approve, without delay or contradiction, by his letters and seals, all the privileges, letters, rights, liberties, grants, ancient customs, and also dignities of each of the Electoral Princes, ecclesiastical and secular, who are known to be the nearer members of the Holy Empire, together with whatever they have obtained and possessed from the Empire up to the day of his election; and after he has been crowned with the imperial insignia, he shall renew all the aforesaid things.

units.la: 9. Confirmationem autem hujusmodi, electus ipse cuilibet Principi Electori in specie, primò, suo Regali faciet nomine; & deinde sub Imperiali titulo innovabit; & in his ipsos Principes omnes in genere, & quemlibet eorum in specie nullatenus impedire, sed potius absque dolo gratiosè tenebitur promovere.
units.tr: 9. The elected man himself shall make this confirmation to each Prince Elector individually, first in his royal name, and then he shall renew it under the imperial title. In these matters he shall by no means hinder those Princes in general, or each of them in particular, but rather shall be bound to promote them graciously and without deceit.

units.la: 10. In casu denique, quo tres Principes Electores præsentes, seu absentium nuncii, quartum ex se, seu eorum consortio, videlicet Principem Electorem præsentem, vel absentem, in Regem Romanorum elegerint, vocem illius electi, si præsens adfuerit, aut nunciorum ipsius, si cum abesse contingeret, plenum vigorem habere, & eligentium augere numerum, partemque majorem decernimus constituere, ad instar cæterorum Principum Electorum.
units.tr: 10. Finally, in the case where three Electors present, or the envoys of those absent, elect a fourth from among themselves or from their company, namely an Elector Prince, present or absent, as King of the Romans, we decree that the vote of that chosen man, if he is present, or of his envoys if he happens to be absent, shall have full force, shall increase the number of electors, and shall constitute the greater part, on a par with the other Electoral Princes.

units.la: CAP. III.
units.tr: CAP. III.

units.la: DE SESSIONE a TREVERENSIS, COLONIEN- SIS & Moguntinensis Archiepiscoporum.
units.tr: Concerning the seating of the Archbishops of Trier, Cologne and Mainz.

units.la: In nomine sanctæ & individuæ Trinitatis feliciter, Amen.
units.tr: In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, happily. Amen.

units.la: Carolus Quartus divina favente clementia, Romanorum Imperator, semper-Augustus, & Bohemiæ Rex, ad perpetuam rei memoriam.
units.tr: Charles the Fourth, by the favour of divine clemency, Roman Emperor, ever Augustus, and King of Bohemia, to the perpetual memory of the matter.

units.la: Decor, & gloria Sacrosancti Romani Imperii, & honor Cæsareus, & Reipublicæ grata compendia, venerabilium & illustrium Principum Electorum concordi voluntate foventur, qui velut columnæ proceres sacrum ædificium circumspectæ prudentiæ solerti pietate sustentant, quorum præsidio dextra Imperialis potentiæ roboratur; & quando mutui favoris amplioři benignitate stringuntur, tanto uberioris pacis & tranquillitatis commoda feliciter profluunt populo Christiano. Utigitur inter venerabiles Moguntinensem, Coloniensem, necnon Treverensem Archiepiscopos, Sacri Imperii Principes Electores, omnium litium, & suspectuum mala, quæ & qui de prioritate seu dignitate sessionum suarum in curiis Imperialibus, & Regalibus, suborni valerent, in posterum perpetuis inantea temporibus amputentur, & ipsi in cordis & animorum quieta conditione manentes, de opportunitatibus Sacri Imperii concordi favore, & virtuosæ dilectionis studio convenientius meditari valeant, pro consolatione populi Christiani, habita deliberatione cum omnibus Principibus Electoribus, tam Ecclesiasticis quam Secularibus, & de ipsorum consilio decernimus, & de Imperatoriæ potestatis plenitudine, hac edictali lege perpetuo valitura, sancimus, quod supradicti venerabiles Archiepiscopi, Treverensis videlicet, ex opposito & liniari directione versus Imperatoris faciem; Moguntinensis vero in suis dioecesi & provincia, & extra provinciam suam in toto Archicancellariatu suo Germanico, provincia Coloniensi dumtaxat excepta; & demum Coloniensis in suis dioecesi & provincia, & extra provinciam suam in tota Italia & Gallia, in dextero latere Romanorum Cæsaris, sedere possint, valeant, & debeant in omnibus publicis actibus Imperialibus, puta judiciis, collationibus feudorum, & in refectionibus mensarum, ac etiam in consiliis, & in omnibus aliis agendis, propter quæ contingit seu continget eos pro honore seu utilitate Imperiali tractandis mutuo convenire & hunc modum sessionis sub omni eo ordine, sicut expressatur superius, ad prædictorum Coloniensis, Treverensis, & Moguntinensis Archiepiscoporum successores, perpetuò extendi volumus, ut nullo umquam tempore super his quævis dubietas generetur.
units.tr: The grace and glory of the Most Holy Roman Empire, the honour of Caesar and the welcome advantages of the commonwealth are fostered by the united will of the venerable and illustrious Electoral Princes, who, like pillars, support the sacred edifice with wise circumspection and diligent devotion, and by whose protection the right hand of imperial power is strengthened; and when they are bound together by the fuller kindness of mutual favour, so much the richer blessings of peace and tranquillity flow happily to the Christian people. Therefore, having taken counsel with all the Electoral Princes, both ecclesiastical and secular, for the consolation of the Christian people, we decree and, by the fullness of imperial power, enact by this edictal law, to remain in force forever, that the aforesaid venerable Archbishops, namely of Trier, facing the Emperor's face opposite and in a straight line, and of Mainz in his diocese and province, and beyond his province throughout his German archchancellorship, except the province of Cologne alone; and finally of Cologne in his diocese and province, and beyond his province throughout all Italy and Gaul, on the right side of the Roman Caesar, may and shall sit, and in all public imperial acts, that is, in judgments, the conferring of fiefs, and at the table during meals, and also in councils and in all other business, on account of which it happens or will happen that they must meet together to deal with matters touching imperial honour or advantage; and we wish this manner of seating, under every order just expressed above, to be extended in perpetuity to the successors of the aforesaid Archbishops of Cologne, Trier and Mainz, so that at no time whatever may any doubt arise concerning these matters.

units.la: CAP IV.
units.tr: CHAPTER IV.

units.la: DE PRINCIPIBUS ELECTORIBUS IN communi.
units.tr: CONCERNING THE PRINCE-ELECTORS IN GENERAL.

units.la: Statuimus insuper, ut quotiescunque Imperialem curiam ex nunc inantea celebrari contigerit, in qualibet sessione, videlicet tam in consilio, quam in mensa, & locis aliis quibuscunque, ubi Imperatorem, vel Regem Romanorum cum Principibus Electoribus sedere contigerit, a dextro latere Imperatoris vel Regis Romanorum immediate post Archiepiscopum Moguntinensem, vel Coloniensem, illum videlicet, quem tunc temporis pro qualitate locorum, & varietate provinciarum, juxta privilegii sui tenorem, dicto lateri dextro Imperatoris assidere contigerit: Rex Bohemiæ (cum sit Princeps coronatus & unctus) primum; & post eum continuò Comes Palatinus Rheni, secundum sedendi loca debeant obtinere; ad sinistram vero partem immediate post illum, quem ex prædictis Archiepiscopis in latere sinistro sedere contigerit, primum locum Dux Saxoniæ, & post eum Marchio Brandeburgensis alterum obtinebit.
units.tr: We further decree that whenever the Imperial court shall be held from now on, at every session, namely in the council, at the table, and in all other places whatsoever where the Emperor or the King of the Romans shall sit with the Prince-Electors, the King of Bohemia (since he is a crowned and anointed prince) shall obtain the first place, and immediately after him the Count Palatine of the Rhine the second, on the right-hand side of the Emperor or King of the Romans, immediately after whichever of the aforesaid Archbishops of Mainz or Cologne shall happen to sit on that right side, according to the tenor of his privilege and the circumstances of places and the variety of provinces at that time. On the left side, immediately after the one of the aforesaid Archbishops who shall happen to sit on the left side, the Duke of Saxony shall hold the first place, and after him the Margrave of Brandenburg shall hold the second.

units.la: 2. Cæterum, quotiens & quando deinceps Sacrum vacare continget Imperium, extunc Moguntinensis Archiepiscopus potestatem habebit (sicut potestatem habuisse dignoscitur ab antiquo) cæteros Principes antedictos, suos in dicta electione consortes, litteratorie convocandi.
units.tr: 2. Moreover, whenever and as often as the Holy Empire shall in future become vacant, the Archbishop of Mainz shall then have the power (as he is known to have had from of old) of summoning by letter the other aforesaid Princes, his partners in that election.

units.la: 3. Quibus omnibus, seu his, qui potuerint, & voluerint interesse, in electionis termino in vicem congregatis, dictus Archiepiscopus Moguntinensis, & non alter, eorundem Coelectorum suorum vota singulariter habebit inquirere, ordine subsequenti.
units.tr: 3. When all of these, or those who are able and willing to be present, have gathered together at the appointed time of the election, the said Archbishop of Mainz, and no other, shall have the right to ask the individual votes of his fellow electors, in the following order.

units.la: 4. Primò quidem interrogabit à Treverensi Archiepiscopo, cui primam vocem competere declaramus, sicut invenimus hactenus competiisse; secundò, à Coloniensi Archiepiscopo, cui competit dignitas ɑgnitas, nec non officium Romanorum Regi primum diadema Regium imponendi; tertiò, à Rege Bohemiæ, qui inter Electores Laicos ex Regiæ dignitatis fastigio, jure & merito obtinebit primatiam; quartò, à Comite Palatino Rheni; quintò, à Duce Saxoniæ; sextò, à Marchione Brandenburgensi. horum omnium vota, præmisso jam ordine, dictus Archiepiscopus Moguntinensis perquiret. quo facto, dicti Principes, sui consortes, ipsum vice versa requirent, ut & ipse intentionem suam exprimat, & ipsis apertiat votum suum.
units.tr: 4. First he shall ask the Archbishop of Trier, to whom we declare that the first voice belongs, as we have found it has belonged hitherto; second, the Archbishop of Cologne, who holds the dignity of chancellor and the office of placing the first royal crown on the King of the Romans; third, the King of Bohemia, who among the lay electors, from the height of royal dignity, rightly and deservedly holds the primacy; fourth, the Count Palatine of the Rhine; fifth, the Duke of Saxony; sixth, the Margrave of Brandenburg. Having first observed this order, the said Archbishop of Mainz shall ask the votes of all of these. When this is done, the said Princes, his fellow electors, shall in turn ask him to declare his own intention and disclose his vote to them.

units.la: 5. Præterea, in celebratione Imperialis curiæ, Marchio Brandenburgensis aquam lavandis Imperatoris, vel Regis Romanorum, manibus ministrabit; primum vero poluin Rex Bohemiæ; quem tamen sub Regali corona juxta privilegiorum Regni sui continentiam, nisi libera voluntate voluerit, non tenebitur ministrare. Comes etiam Palatinus Rheni cibum afferre tenebitur. Dux Saxoniæ Marescallatus officium exercebit, ut solitum est fieri ab antiquo.
units.tr: 5. Furthermore, at the celebration of the Imperial court, the Margrave of Brandenburg shall pour water for the hands of the Emperor or King of the Romans; the King of Bohemia shall offer the first basin, though he shall not be bound to serve it, under the royal crown, according to the contents of the privileges of his kingdom, unless he is willing of his own free will. The Count Palatine of the Rhine shall be bound to bring the food. The Duke of Saxony shall exercise the office of marshal, as has been customary from of old.

units.la: CAP. V. DE IVRE COMITIS PALATINI RHENI, ET etiam Saxoniæ Ducis.
units.tr: CHAPTER V. CONCERNING THE RIGHT OF THE COUNT PALATINE OF THE RHINE, AND ALSO OF THE DUKE OF SAXONY.

units.la: QUOTIENS insuper, ut præmittitur, Sacrum vacare contingeret Imperium, Illustris Comes Palatinus Rheni, Sacri Imperii Archidapifer, ad manus futuri Regis Romanorum in partibus Rheni, & Suevîæ, & in jure Franconico, ratione Principatus, seu Comitatus Palatini privilegio, eiusdem debet Provisor ipsius Imperii, cum potestate judicia exercendi, ad beneficia Ecclesiastica præsentandi, recolligendi redditus & proventus, & investiendi de feudis, juramenta fidelitatis vice & nomine Sacri Imperii recipiendi; quæ tamen per Regem Romanorum postea electum, suo tempore omnia innovari, & de novo sibi ipsa juramenta præstari debebunt: feudis Principum dûtaxat exceptis, & illis quæ Vanlehen vulgariter appellantur, quorum investituram, & collationem soli Imperatori, vel Regi Romanorum, specialiter reservamus. Ipse tamen Comes Palatinus omne genus alienationis seu obligationis rerum Imperialium, hujusmodi provisionis tempore, expresse sibi noverit interdictum.
units.tr: Whenever, as has been said above, the Holy Empire happens to be vacant, the Illustrious Count Palatine of the Rhine, Arch-steward of the Holy Empire, is to be the provisor of the same Empire, by the privilege of his principality or county palatine, in the parts of the Rhine and Swabia and in the Franconian law, until the king of the Romans is chosen. He has power to exercise jurisdiction, to present to ecclesiastical benefices, to collect revenues and income, to invest with fiefs, and to receive oaths of fidelity in the place and name of the Holy Empire. These matters, however, shall all be renewed at the proper time by the king of the Romans afterwards elected, and new oaths shall be sworn to him. The exceptions are the fiefs of the princes and those commonly called Vanlehen, whose investiture and conferral we specially reserve to the emperor alone, or to the king of the Romans. The Count Palatine himself is to know that every kind of alienation or pledging of imperial property is expressly forbidden to him during the time of this provision.

units.la: 2. Et eodem jure provisionis, Illustrem Ducé Saxoniæ, Sacri Imperii Archimarescallum, frui volumus in illis locis, ubi Saxonica jura servantur, sub omnibus modis & conditionibus licut superius est expressum.
units.tr: 2. By the same right of provision, we wish the Illustrious Duke of Saxony, Arch-marshal of the Holy Empire, to enjoy the same in those places where Saxon law is observed, under all the modes and conditions expressed above.

units.la: 3. Et quamvis Imperator, sive Rex Romanorum, super causis, pro quibus impetitus fuerit, habeat (sicut ex consuetudine introductum dicitur) coram Comite Palatino Rheni, Sacri Imperii Archidapifero, Electore Principe, respondere; illud tamen judicium Comes ipse Palatinus nō alibi, præterquam in Imperiali curia, ubi Imperator, seu Romanorum Rex præsens extiterit, potenit exercere.
units.tr: 3. And although the emperor, or the king of the Romans, when impleaded in causes for which he has been summoned, has (as it is said to be introduced by custom) the right to answer before the Count Palatine of the Rhine, Arch-steward of the Holy Empire, and Elector Prince, nevertheless the Count Palatine himself may exercise that jurisdiction nowhere else than in the imperial court, where the emperor or the king of the Romans is present.

units.la: CAP. VI. DE COMPARATIONE PRINCIPVM ELECTO- RVM ad alios Principes communes.
units.tr: CHAPTER VI. ON THE COMPARISON OF THE ELECTORAL PRINCES WITH OTHER COMMON PRINCES.

units.la: DECERNIMUS, ut in celebratione Imperialis curiæ, quotienscunque illâ deinceps perpetuò celebrari contigerit, antedicti Principes Electores, Ecclesiastici & Seculares, juxta præscriptum ordinem atque modum, à dextris & sinistris immutabiliter teneant loca sua; eisque, vel eorum alicui, in quibuscunque actibus ad curiā ipsam spectantibus eundo, sedendo, vel stando, nullus Princeps alius, cujuscunque status, dignitatis, præeminentiæ, vel conditionis existat, ullatenus præferatur; enter expresso, quod nominatim Rex Bohemiæ in celebratione curiarum hujusmodi, in omnibus singulis actibus antedictis, quemcunque Regem alium, quacunque etiam singulari dignitatis prerogativa fulgentem, quem quovis casu seu causa venire, vel adesse forte contingeret, immutabiliter ac ecclē.
units.tr: We decree that, whenever the Imperial Diet shall in future be held continuously, the aforesaid Electoral Princes, both ecclesiastical and secular, shall keep their places immutably at the right and left hands, according to the prescribed order and manner; and that, in any acts pertaining to the Diet, whether walking, sitting or standing, no other prince, of whatever rank, dignity, pre-eminence or condition he may be, shall in any way be placed before them or any one of them. It is expressly provided that the King of Bohemia, in the holding of such Diets, in all and each of the aforesaid acts, shall immutably and...

units.la: CAP. VII. DE SVCCESSIONE PRINCIPVM Electorum.
units.tr: CHAPTER VII. ON THE SUCCESSION OF THE PRINCIPAL ELECTORS.

units.la: In nomine sanctæ & individuæ Trinitatis feliciter, Amen.
units.tr: In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, happily. Amen.

units.la: Carolus Quartus divina favente clementia, Romanorum Imperator, semper-Augustus, & Bohemiæ Rex, ad perpetuam rei memoriam.
units.tr: Charles IV, by the favour of divine clemency, Emperor of the Romans, ever Augustus, and King of Bohemia, to the perpetual memory of the matter.

units.la: INTER folicitudines illas innumeras, quibus pro felici statu Sacri Imperii, cui auctore Domino fenter præsidemus, cor nostrum quotidie fatigatur, ad hoc præcipue meditatio nostra dirigitur, qualiter desiderata & salubris semper unio inter Sacri Imperii Principes Electores jugiter vigeat, & cordacorum in sincerae charitatis concordia conservetur, quorum providentia suo tempore orbi humanæ, tanto celeriùs, iantoque facilius subvenietur, quanto inter eos nullus error surrepserit, & puorfuerit charitas custodita, obscuritate succisa, & jure cujuslibet dilucidè declarato. Sane generaliter longe lateq; est publicum, & quasi per totum orbem notorié manifestum, Illustres, Regem Bohemiæ, nec non Comitem Palatinum Rhen, Ducem Saxoniæ, & Marchionem Brandenburgensem, Regni & Principatuum suorum, in electione Regis Romanorum in Cæsarem promovendi, omnibus Principibus Ecclesiasticis suis Coëlectoribus, jus, vocem, & locum habere, & unà cum ipsis esse, & esse veros & legitimos Sacri Imperii Principes Electores.
units.tr: AMONG those countless anxieties by which our heart is wearied daily for the happy state of the Holy Empire, over which, with the Lord as author, we preside, our thought is chiefly directed to this: that the desired and always wholesome union among the Princes Electors of the Holy Empire may flourish continually, and that concord of hearts may be preserved in sincere charity. By their providence the human world will be helped at its proper time, and all the more quickly and easily, the less any error has crept in among them, and the more charity has been kept, obscurity being cut away and the law of each one having been made clear. Indeed, it is widely and far and wide public, and almost notoriously manifest throughout the whole world, that the Illustrious Kings of Bohemia, and likewise the Count Palatine of the Rhine, the Duke of Saxony, and the Margrave of Brandenburg, of their kingdom and principalities, have the right, the voice, and the place in the election of the King of the Romans to be promoted as Caesar, together with all the Ecclesiastical Princes, their fellow electors, and that they are true and lawful Princes Electors of the Holy Empire.

units.la: 1. Ne inter eorundem Principum secularium Electorum filios, super jure, voce, & potestate præfata, futuris temporibus, scandalorum & dissensionum posset materia suscitari, & sic bonum commune periculosis dilationibus impediri, futuris auctore Deo cupientes periculis salubriter obviam.
units.tr: 1. Lest, in future times, matter for scandals and dissensions should arise among the sons of the same secular Princes Electors concerning the aforesaid right, voice, and power, and so the common good be hindered by dangerous delays, we desire, with God as author, to meet future perils healthfully.

units.la: 3. Statuimus & Imperiali auctoritate, præsenti lege perpetuis temporibus valitura, ut postquam iidem Principes Electores Seculares, & eorum quilibet, esse desierit, jus, vox, & testas electionis hujusmodi ad filium suum primogenitum, legitimum, laicum; illo verò non extante ad ejusdem primogeniti primogenitum, similiter laicum, libere & sine contradictione, cujus potestas devolvatur.
units.tr: 3. We enact, by imperial authority, by this present law to remain valid in perpetual times, that when the same secular Princes Electors, or any one of them, shall have ceased to be, the right, voice, and power of election of this kind pass to their eldest legitimate lay son; and if he is not living, to the eldest legitimate lay son of that firstborn, freely and without contradiction, in whom their power devolves.

units.la: 4. Si vero primogenitus hujusmodi absque hæredibus masculis, legitimis, laicis, ab hac nigrarer, virtute præsentis Imperialis edicti, jus, vox, & potestas electionis prædictæ, ad seniorem fratrem laicum per veram paternalem lineam descendentem, & deinceps ad illius primogenitum devolvatur.
units.tr: 4. But if such a firstborn departs from this light without legitimate male lay heirs, then by virtue of this present imperial edict the right, voice, and power of the aforesaid election pass to the elder lay brother descending through the true paternal line, and thereafter to his firstborn.

units.la: 5. Et talis successio in primogenitis, & hæredibus Principum earundem, in jure, voce, & potestate præmissis, perpetuis temporibus observetur.
units.tr: 5. And such succession among the firstborns and heirs of the same Princes, in the right, voice, and power set out above, shall be observed in perpetual times.

units.la: 6. Ea tamen conditione & modo, ut si Principem Electorem, seu ejus primogenitum, filium seniorem laicum, mori, & hæredes masculos, legitimos, laicos, defectum ætatis patiente, quæ contigerit, tunc frater senior ejusdem primogeniti, tutor eorum & administrator existat, senior ex eis legitimam ætatem attigerit, quam in Principe Electore decem & octo annos complere ceuseri volumus, & statuimus perpetuò haberi; quam dum attigerit, jus, vocem, & potestatem omnia ab ipsis dependentia, tutor ipse sibi totaliter cum officio teneatur protinus assignare.
units.tr: 6. Yet on this condition and in this manner: if the Prince Elector, or his firstborn, or his elder lay son, should die, and his legitimate male lay heirs, while still under age, should have the defect of years, then the elder brother of that firstborn shall be their guardian and administrator until the elder of them reaches legitimate age, which we wish to be counted, and decree to be held forever, as eighteen years for a Prince Elector. As soon as he has reached it, the guardian himself is bound at once to assign to him wholly, together with the office, all the right, voice, and power dependent on them.

units.la: 7. Si vero aliquem ex hujusmodi Principatibus ipsorum Imperio Sacro vacare contigerit, tunc Imperator, seu Rex Romanorum, qui pro tempore fuerit, de ipso providere debebit & potest, tanquam dere ad se & Imperium legitime devoluta.
units.tr: 7. If, however, any of these principalities should happen to fall vacant to the Holy Empire, then the Emperor, or the King of the Romans who is in office at the time, ought and may provide for it, as a matter lawfully fallen to himself and to the Empire.

units.la: 8. Salvis tamen semper privilegiis, juribus, & consuetudinibus Regni nostri Bohemiæ super electione Regis in casu vacationis per regnicolas, qui jus habent eligendi Regem Bohemiæ, facienjuxta continentiam eorundem privilegiorum, & observatam consuetudinem diuturnam, à divis Romanorum Imperatoribus, sive Regibus, obtentorum, quibus ex hujusmodi sanctione Imperiali nullo præjudicari volumus; imò, ipsa decernimus nunc & perpetuis futuris temporibus in omni suo tenore & forma, indubiam tenere roboris firmitatem.
units.tr: 8. Always saving, however, the privileges, rights, and customs of our Kingdom of Bohemia concerning the election of the King, in the case of a vacancy, by the inhabitants of the kingdom who have the right to elect the King of Bohemia, acting according to the tenor of those same privileges and the long-observed custom obtained from the divine Roman Emperors or Kings; by this imperial sanction we do not wish them to be prejudiced in any way. Rather, we now decree, and for all future perpetual times, that in their whole tenor and form they shall hold indubitable strength and firmness.

units.la: CAP. VIII.
units.tr: CHAPTER VIII.

units.la: DE REGIS BOHEMIAE ET REGNICOLARVM ejus immunitate.
units.tr: CONCERNING THE IMMUNITY OF THE KING OF BOHEMIA AND OF HIS SUBJECTS.

units.la: CUm per divos Romanorum Imperatores, & Reges, prædecessores nostros, illustribus Bohemiæ Regibus, progenitoribus & prædecessoribus nostris, nec non Regno Bohemiæ, ejusque Regni coronæ, olim concessum fuerit gratiosius & indultum, sitque in Regno eodem tempore cujus contrarii hodie non exstitit memoria, consuetudine laudabili, inconvulsè servata, turnitate temporum, & præscripta moribus utentium, sine contradictionis aut interruptionis culo introductum, quod nullus Princeps, Baro, Nobilis, Miles, Cliens, Civis, Burgensis, seu Rusticus, nulla denique persona ejusdem regni, & pertinentiarum ejusdem ubicumque existentium, cujusque status, dignitatis, præeminentiæ, vel conditionis existat, ad cujuscumque actoris instantiam, extra Regnum ipsum ad quodcumque tribunal, seu alterius, præterquam Regis Bohemiæ, & Judicum Regalis curiæ suæ judicium citari potuerit, sive trahi, nec vocari debeat perpetuis inantea temporibus possit. Ideoque privilegium, consuetudinem, & indultum hujusmodi, auctoritate Imperiali, & de Imperii potestatis plenitudine, ex certa scientia innovantes, & etiam confirmantes, hac præsenti nostra constitutione Imperiali perpetuis temporibus valitura statuimus, ut si contra privilegium, consuetudinem vel indultum præfatum quispiam prædictorum, puta Princeps, Baro, Nobilis, Miles, Cliens, Civis, Burgensis, seu Rusticus, aut alia quæcumque persona præmissa, ad cujuscumque tribunal extra Regnum prædictum Bohemiæ, in quacumque causa, criminali, civili, vel mixta, seu super quocumque negotio citatus fuerit, quocumque tempore, vel citata, comparere, vel in judicio respondere minime teneatur. Quòd si adversus hujusmodi non comparentes, vel non comparentem, à quocumque Judice, cujuscumque auctoritatis exstitat, extra Regnum ipsum Bohemiæ constituto, judicialiter processus fieri, seu sententias interlocutorias vel definitivas, unam vel plures, in quibuscumque nominatis causis sive negotiis, quovis modo fieri vel promulgari contingeret, auctoritate præmissa de plenitudine insuper antedictæ Imperatoriæ potestatis, citationes, præcepta, processus, & sententias hujusmodi, necnon executiones, & omnia quæ ex eis, vel aliquo eorum, quomodolibet sequi, attentari possent vel fieri, irritamus penitus & cassamus.
units.tr: Since the divine Roman Emperors and Kings, our predecessors, long ago granted and indulged to the illustrious Kings of Bohemia, our forebears and predecessors, and also to the Kingdom of Bohemia and the crown of that kingdom, a more gracious indulgence; and since it has been introduced in that kingdom, from a time whose contrary no one remembers today, by a laudable custom inviolably observed, by the lapse of time and by a prescription of the practice of those who use it, without any challenge or interruption, that no prince, baron, noble, knight, client, citizen, burgher or peasant, and in short no person of that kingdom and its dependencies, wherever they may be, of whatever status, dignity, pre-eminence or condition, may be cited or summoned, at the suit of any plaintiff, outside the kingdom itself, to any tribunal other than that of the King of Bohemia and the judges of his royal court, nor ought to be summoned for all future time: therefore we, by imperial authority and from the fullness of imperial power, from certain knowledge, renewing and also confirming this privilege, custom and indulgence, decree by this our present imperial constitution, to remain valid in perpetuity, that if any of the aforesaid persons, namely prince, baron, noble, knight, client, citizen, burgher or peasant, or any other person mentioned above, is cited before any tribunal outside the said Kingdom of Bohemia, in any cause, criminal, civil or mixed, or concerning any business whatsoever, at whatever time, he is not bound to appear or to answer in court, or, having been cited, to appear. But if, against such non-appearing persons or person, any judge of whatever authority, sitting outside the Kingdom of Bohemia, should happen to conduct judicial proceedings, or to make or promulgate in any way one or more interlocutory or definitive sentences in whatever named causes or business, we, by the authority aforesaid and moreover by the fullness of the aforesaid imperial power, utterly annul and quash such citations, precepts, processes and sentences, as well as the executions and all that could follow from them, or from any of them, or be attempted or done in any way.

units.la: 2. Addi2. Adjicientes expresse, & edicto Imperiali perpetuò valituro, eadem auctoritate, & de præmissæ potestatis plenitudine decernentes, ut quemadmodum in prædicto Regno Bohemiæ, à tempore, cujus contrarii non habetur memoria, junctim observatum existit, ita nulli prorsus Principi, Baroni, Nobili, Militi, Clienti, Civi, Burgensi, seu Rustico, nulli denique personæ, seu incolæ Regni Bohemiæ sæpe dicti, cujuscumque status, præeminentiæ, dignitatis, vel conditionis existant, vel existat, à quibuscumque processibus, sententiis interlocutoriis vel diffinitivis, sive præceptis Regis Bohemiæ, aut quorumlibet suorum judicum, nec non executionibus eorundem, contra se in Regali judicio, seu coram Regis, Regni, seu prædictorum Judicum tribunalibus factis aut latis, habitis vel ferendis mantea seu fideiussis, liceat ad quodcumque aliud judicium appellare. Provocationes quoque seu appellationes huiusmodi, si quas contra hoc interponi contigerit, eo ipso viribus non subsistant, & appellantes ipsi pœnam perditionis causarum ipso facto se noverint incurrisse.
units.tr: 2. Adding expressly, and by this imperial edict to remain valid forever, decreeing by the same authority and the fullness of the aforesaid power, that just as in the aforesaid Kingdom of Bohemia it has been observed continuously from a time whose contrary is not remembered, so no prince, baron, noble, knight, client, citizen, burgher or peasant, and no person or inhabitant of the oft-named Kingdom of Bohemia, of whatever status, pre-eminence, dignity or condition they are or may be, shall be permitted to appeal to any other tribunal from any processes, interlocutory or definitive sentences, or precepts of the King of Bohemia or of any of his judges, nor from the executions of the same, made or pronounced against them in the royal court, or before the tribunals of the King, the kingdom or the aforesaid judges, whether already given or yet to be given, under pledge or surety. Likewise, any provocations or appeals of this kind, if any should be lodged against this, shall by that very fact have no force, and the appellants themselves shall know that by that very fact they have incurred the penalty of forfeiting their causes.

units.la: CAP. IX.
units.tr: CAP. IX.

units.la: DE AVRI, ARGENTI, ET ALIARVM specierum mineris.
units.tr: Concerning the mines of gold, silver and other kinds of metal

units.la: PRÆSENTI constitutione in perpetuum valitura statuimus, ac de certa scientia declaramus, quòd successores nostri Bohemiæ Reges, nec non universi & singULI Principes Electores, Ecclesiastici & Seculares, qui perpetuò fuerint, universas auri & argenti fodinas, atque mineras stanni, cupri, ferri, plumbi, & alterius cujuscumque generis metalli, ac etiam salis, tam inventas quàm etiam inveniendas in posterum quibuscumque temporibus, in Regno prædicto, ac terris & pertinentiis eidem Regno subjectis, nec non supradicti Principes in Principatibus, terris, dominiis, & pertinentiis suis, tenere justè possint & legitimè possidere, cum omnibus juribus (nullo prorsus excepto) prout possunt seu consueverunt talia possideri; nec non Judæos habere; theolonea in præterito statuta & indicta percipere; quodque progenitores nostri, Reges Bohemiæ felicis memoriæ, ipsique Principes Electores, ac progenitores & prædecessores eorum, legitimè potuerint usque in præsens, sicut hoc antiqua, laudabili, & approbata consuetudine, diuturnique ac longissimi temporis cursu præscripta noscitur observatum.
units.tr: By this constitution, to be valid in perpetuity, we decree and declare of certain knowledge that the successors of ours as Kings of Bohemia, as well as all and each of the Princes Electors, ecclesiastical and secular, who shall exist at any time, may justly hold and lawfully possess all the gold and silver mines, and the mines of tin, copper, iron, lead and any other kind of metal, and also of salt, both those already discovered and those to be discovered hereafter at whatever time, in the aforesaid Kingdom and in the lands and appurtenances subject to the same Kingdom; and likewise the aforesaid Princes in their principalities, lands, dominions and appurtenances; and that they may have Jews; and collect the tolls established and imposed in the past; and that our forebears, the Kings of Bohemia of happy memory, and the Princes Electors themselves, and their forebears and predecessors, have been able lawfully to do so until now, as is known to have been observed by ancient, praiseworthy and approved custom, and prescribed by the long course of a very lengthy period of time.

units.la: CAP. X.
units.tr: CAP. X.

units.la: DE MONETIS.
units.tr: ON COINAGE.

units.la: STATUIMUS præterea, ut Regi Bohemiæ, successori nostro, qui fuerit pro tempore, sicut constat ab antiquo Illustris memoriæ Bohemiæ Regibus, nostris prædecessoribus, licuisse, & in possessione pacifica continua ipsos fuisse juris sub sequentis, videlicet monetas auri & argenti, in omni loco & parte Regni sui, & subditarum ei terrarum & pertinentiarum omnium, ubi Rex ipse decreverit, ubique placuerit, cudi facere, & mandare, sub omni modo & forma, in Regno ipso Bohemiæ, in his ad hæc utique tempora observatis, quodque futuris perpetuò Bohemiæ Regibus, hac nostra Imperiali constitutione & gratia perpetuò valituris, à quibuscumque Principibus, Magnatibus, Comitibus, ac aliis, quascumque terras, castra, possessiones, prædia, sive bona, liceat emere, comparare, seu donum vel donationem, ex quacumque causa, aut in obligationem recipere, sub talium terrarum, locorum, possessionum, prædiorum, seu bonorum conditione consueta, ut videlicet propria recipiant vel comparentur ut propria, libera velut libeta, & ea quæ dependent in feudum, similiter emanant feudum, seu comparata taliter teneantur; ita tamen, quòd ipsi Reges Bohemiæ, de iis, quæ hoc modo comparaverint vel receperint, & Regno Bohemiæ duxerint applicanda, ad pristina ac consueta talibus sacro explenda & reddenda Imperio sint astricti.
units.tr: We further ordain that the King of Bohemia, our successor, whoever he may be at the time, shall be entitled, as has been established from of old to the Kings of Bohemia of illustrious memory, our predecessors, and as they have continuously and peacefully possessed the right, to have gold and silver coins struck and minted in every place and part of his kingdom and of all the lands and appurtenances subject to him, wherever the King himself shall decide and wherever it shall please him, in every manner and form, within the Kingdom of Bohemia itself, as has been observed in these times up to the present; and that future Kings of Bohemia, by this our Imperial constitution and grace which shall remain in force forever, may receive, buy, or acquire by gift or donation, for any cause whatever, or take in pledge from any Princes, magnates, counts, or others, any lands, castles, possessions, estates, or goods whatever, on the customary terms of such lands, places, possessions, estates, or goods, so that they may receive or acquire them as their own, free as allodial property, and that those which depend on a fief are likewise held as fiefs, or acquired in such a way; provided, however, that the Kings of Bohemia are bound, with regard to what they shall have acquired or received in this way and have decided to apply to the Kingdom of Bohemia, to render and pay the customary dues owed to the Empire for such things, as before.

units.la: Præsentem nihilominus constitutionem & gratiam, virtute præsentis legis nostræ Imperiales, versos Principes Electores, tam Ecclesiasticos quam Seculares, successores & legitimos hæredes, plene extendi volumus, sub omnibus modis & conditionibus, ut præfertur.
units.tr: We desire that the present constitution and grace, by virtue of this our Imperial law, be fully extended to the Electoral Princes, both ecclesiastical and secular, their successors and lawful heirs, under all the modes and conditions stated above.

units.la: CAP. XI.
units.tr: CAP. XI.

units.la: DE IMMVNITATE PRINCIPVM ELECTORVM.
units.tr: ON THE IMMUNITY OF THE ELECTORAL PRINCES

units.la: STATUIMUS etiam, ut nulli Comites, Barones, Nobiles, Feudales, Vasalli, Castrenses, Milites, Clientes, Cives, Burgenses, nullæ quoque personæ, Coloniensi, Moguntinensi & Treverensi, Ecclesiis subjecti vel subjectæ, cujuscumque status, conditionis, vel dignitatis existant, ad cujuscumque actoris instantiam extra territorium, & terminos aclimites earundem Ecclesiarum, & pertinentiarum suarum, ad quodcumque aliud tribunal, seu cujuscumque alterius, præterquàm Archiepiscopi Moguntinensis, Treverensis, & Coloniensis, & Judicum suorum judicium citari poterint vel trahi seu vocari debeant perpetuis inantea temporibus sive possint, sicut in ... inveniemus temporibus observatum.
units.tr: We further decree that no counts, barons, nobles, feudal tenants, vassals, castle-dwellers, knights, clients, citizens, burghers, nor any persons whatsoever who are subject to the Churches of Cologne, Mainz and Trier, of whatever rank, condition or dignity they be, may at the suit of any plaintiff be cited, drawn or summoned outside the territory and boundaries of these Churches and their dependencies, before any other tribunal or court than the judgment of the Archbishops of Mainz, Trier and Cologne and of their judges, now and in perpetual times to come, as has been observed in ... times past.

units.la: 2. Quod si contra præsens edictum nostrum, prædictos Ecclesiarum Trevetensis, Moguntinensis, seu Coloniensis subditos, vel eorum aliquem seu aliquos, ad cujuscumque instantiam, seu ad cumq; tribunal, pro quacumq; causa criminali, civili, vel mixta, seu quocumq; negotio, extra territorium, limites seu terminos dictarum Ecclesiarum, vel alicujus earum citati contingeret, comparere vel respondere minime teneantur; & citatio, & processus, & sententiæ interlocutoriæ vel diffinitivæ contra non venientes à talibus judicibus extraneis latæ vel factæ, fiendæ vel ferendæ, necnon præceptorum, & præmissorum executiones, & omnia quæ ex eis, vel aliquo eorum quomodolibet sequi, attentari possent vel fieri, irrita decernimus eo ipso.
units.tr: 2. If, contrary to this our present edict, it should happen that any of the subjects of the aforesaid Churches of Trier, Mainz or Cologne, or any one or more of them, be cited outside the territory, limits or boundaries of the said Churches or of any of them, at the suit of anyone whomsoever, or before any tribunal, for any criminal, civil or mixed cause, or any other business, they are by no means bound to appear or to answer; and we declare by this very fact null and void the citation, the proceedings, and the interlocutory and final sentences issued or to be issued or pronounced against non-appearing persons by such foreign judges, as well as the executions of these and of the aforesaid matters, and everything that could be attempted or done in any way to follow from them or any of them.

units.la: 3. Adjicientes expressè, quòd nulli Comiti, Baroni, Nobili, Feudali, Vasallo, Castrensi, Militi, Clienti, Civi, Rustico, nulli demum personæ Ecclesiis hujusmodi subjectæ, seu ejus incolæ, cujusque status, dignitatis, vel conditionis existant, à processibus, sententiis interlocutoriis & diffinitivis, sive præceptis Archiepiscoporum & Ecclesiarum hujusmodi, vel suorum Officiatorum temporum aut executionibus eorundem contra se in Archiepiscopali, seu Officiatorum prædictorum judicio citis aut latis, habitis vel ferendis inanteà seu fiendis, ad quodcumque tribunal aliud liceat appellare, quamdiu in Archiepiscoporum prædictorum, & suorum judicio querulantibus non fuerit justitia negata: appellationes contra hoc factas non recipi statuimus, cassaque & irritas nunciamus.
units.tr: 3. We expressly add that no count, baron, noble, feudal tenant, vassal, castle-dweller, knight, client, citizen, peasant, nor finally any person subject to such Churches or resident in them, of whatever rank, dignity or condition, may appeal to any other tribunal from the proceedings, interlocutory and final sentences, or commands of the Archbishops and Churches of this kind, or of their officials, or from the execution of the same against themselves, cited or pronounced in the court of the said Archbishops or of their officials, whether already held or to be held or pronounced in future, so long as justice has not been denied to complainants in the judgment of the aforesaid Archbishops and their officials. We decree that appeals made against this are not to be received, and we declare them quashed and void.

units.la: 4. In defectum vero justitiæ, prædictis omnibus ad Imperialem dumtaxat curiam & tribunal seu Judicis immediatè in Imperiali curia pro tempore Præsidentis audientiam; & etiam eo casu nondum quemvis alium judicem, sive ordinarium, sive etiam delegatum, his, quibus denegata fuerit justitia, liceat appellare. Quicquid vero contra præmissa factum fuerit, sit irritum eo ipso.
units.tr: 4. But in default of justice, in all the aforesaid matters, it shall be permitted to those to whom justice has been denied to appeal only to the Imperial court and tribunal, or to the judge who at the time presides in the Imperial court and gives the hearing directly; and even in that case not to any other judge, whether ordinary or even delegated. Whatever shall have been done contrary to the foregoing shall be void by this very fact.

units.la: 5. Eandem constitutionem virtute præsentis legis nostræ Imperialis, ad Illustres Comites Palatinos Rheni, Ducem Saxoniæ & Marchionem Brandenburgensem, Principes Electores sive laicos, successores, hæredes, & subditos eorum, plenè extendi volumus, sub omnibus modis & conditionibus, ut præfertur.
units.tr: 5. We wish this same constitution, by virtue of this our present Imperial law, to be fully extended to the Illustrious Counts Palatine of the Rhine, the Duke of Saxony and the Margrave of Brandenburg, the Electoral Princes who are laymen, their successors, heirs and subjects, under all the modes and conditions aforesaid.

units.la: CAP. XII.
units.tr: CAP. XII.

units.la: DE CONGREGATIONE PRINCIPVM ELECTORVM.
units.tr: ON THE ASSEMBLY OF THE ELECTORS OF THE PRINCES

units.la: In nomine sanctæ & individuæ Trinitatis feliciter, Amen.
units.tr: In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, happily. Amen.

units.la: Carolus Quartus divina favente clementia, Romanorum Imperator, semper-Augustus, & Bohemiæ Rex, ad perpetuam rei memoriam.
units.tr: Charles IV, by the favour of divine clemency, Emperor of the Romans, ever Augustus, and King of Bohemia, to the perpetual memory of the matter.

units.la: INTER illas multiplices Reipublicæ curas, quibus assiduè mens nostra distrahitur, multa consideratione necessarium fore prospexit nostra sublimitas, ut Sacri Imperii Principes Electores, ad tractandum de ipsius Imperii orbisque salute, frequentius solito congregentur, qui solidæ bases Imperii, & columnæ immobiles, quemadmodum per longinquas ad invicem terrarum consistuntque distantias, ita de incumbentibus regionum sibi cognitarum defectibus referre simul & conferre noverunt, sanisque providentiæ suæ consiliis non ignorant accommodatis talium reformationibus salubriter operam dare.
units.tr: AMONG those manifold cares of the Commonwealth by which our mind is constantly distracted, our Majesty has foreseen that it will be necessary, after much consideration, that the Electors, Princes of the Holy Empire, should gather more often than usual to treat of the welfare of the Empire and of the world; they who are the solid foundations and immovable pillars of the Empire, and who, although they are separated from one another by long distances of lands, know how to report to and confer with one another concerning the defects of the regions known to them, and, not being ignorant of what is fitting for the sound counsels of their foresight, to labour usefully towards such reforms.

units.la: 2. Hinc est, quod in solemni curia nostra in Nuremberg, cum Venerabilibus Ecclesiasticis & Illustribus secularibus Principibus Electoribus, & multis aliis Principibus & Proceribus, per nostram Celsitudinem celebrata, habita cum eisdem Principibus Electoribus deliberatione, & de ipsorum consilio, pro bono & salute communi, cum dictis Principibus Electoribus, tam Ecclesiasticis quam secularibus, duximus ordinandum, quòd iidem Principes Electores de cætero per singulos annos mel, transactis à festo Paschæ Resurrectionis Dominicæ quatuor septimanis continuè numerandis, aliqua civitatum Sacri Imperii personaliter congregentur, & ad idem tempus proxime affuturum anno præsenti, colloquium seu curia, & congregatio hujusmodi, in civitate nostra Imperiali Metensi per nos & eosdem Principes celebretur; ac tunc, & deinceps, die quolibet congregationis hujusmodi locus per nos, quo sequenti anno conveniant, ipsorum consilio statuatur, hac nostra ordinatione, ad nostrum & ipsorum dumtaxat beneplacitum duratura. qua durante, ipsos sub nostro Imperiali conductu recipimus, ad dictam curiam accedendo, stando, ac etiam recedendo.
units.tr: 2. Hence it is that, in our solemn court at Nuremberg, celebrated by our Highness with the Venerable Ecclesiastical and Illustrious secular Electors, and many other Princes and Nobles, and after deliberation held with the same Electors and by their counsel, we have decided, for the common good and welfare, with the said Electors, both ecclesiastical and secular, that the same Electors shall from now on meet in person each year, in some city of the Holy Empire, in the month of May, beginning four weeks after the Feast of the Lord's Resurrection (Easter); and that a colloquy or court and assembly of this kind shall be held at our Imperial city of Metz, by us and the same Electors, at the same time in the coming year. Then, and thereafter, the place to which they are to come in the following year shall be fixed on each day of such an assembly by us, with their counsel; this our ordinance to remain in force only at our pleasure and theirs. While it remains in force, we receive them under our Imperial safe-conduct, in going to the said court, in staying there, and also in leaving.

units.la: 3. Præterea, ne tractatus communis salutis & pacis, per tractum & moram solatu, seu exspectativam frequentationem convivii retardetur, ut aliquando fieri est consuetum, concordi voluntate maximus ordinandum, ut deinceps curia seu congregatione præfata durante, generales omnium Principum celebrare alicui non liceat invitatas; particulares verò, quæ agendorum expeditionem non impediant, cum moderamine sint permissæ.
units.tr: 3. Moreover, so that the discussion of the common welfare and peace is not delayed by protracted delay and idleness, or by the expectation of frequent banquets, as has sometimes been the custom, we have by unanimous will decreed that, while the aforesaid court or assembly lasts, it shall not be permitted to hold general invited banquets of all the Princes; but private gatherings, which do not hinder the dispatch of business, are allowed in moderation.

units.la: CAP. XIII.
units.tr: CAP. XIII.

units.la: DE REVOCATIONE PRIVILEGIORVM.
units.tr: ON THE REVOCATION OF PRIVILEGES.

units.la: PRÆTEREA statuimus, & hoc Imperiali perpetuo sancimus edicto, quòd universa privilegia & litteræ, quibuscunque personis, cujuscunque status, præeminentiæ, vel dignitatis existant, civitatum, oppidorum, & quorumlibet locorum universitatibus, super quibuscumque juribus, gratiis, immunitatibus, consuetudinibus, seu rebus aliis, etiam proprio motu, seu alias à nobis, vel prædecessoribus nostris, sub quibuscumque coloendæ memoriæ divis Romanorum Imperatoribus, & Regibus, prædecessoribus nostris, sub quibuscumque verborum tenoribus concessa & concessæ, seu à nobis vel successoribus nostris Romanorum Imperatoribus & Regibus, inantea futuris temporibus concedenda seu concedendæ, non debeant aut possint libertatibus, jurisdictionibus, juribus, & honoribus, seu dominiis Principum Electorum Sacri Imperij, Ecclesiasticorum & Secularium, aut alicujus ipsorum in aliquo penitus derogare; etiamsi in talibus privilegijs & litteris quarumlibet personarum cujuscunque præeminentiæ, dignitatis, aut status exstiterint, ut præfertur, seu universitatum hujusmodi expresse cautum sit, vel fuerit in favorem, quòd revocabilia seu revocabiles esse non debeant, nisi de ipsis, & toto in eis comprehenso tenore in tali revocatione fieret de verbo ad verbum seriatim mentio specialis. hujusmodi namque privilegia & literas, si & inquantum libertatibus, jurisdictionibus, juribus, honoribus, seu dominiis dictorum Principum Electorum, aut alicujus ipsorum derogare, vel obviare censentur in aliquo, quo ad hoc revocamus ex certa scientia & callamus, revocataque & revocatas intelligi, reputari, & haberi decernimus de plenitudine Imperatoriæ potestatis.
units.tr: Furthermore, we decree, and by this perpetual Imperial edict we sanction, that all privileges and letters, granted or to be granted by us, or by our predecessors, the Roman Emperors and Kings of blessed memory, or by our successors, the Roman Emperors and Kings in future times, to whatever persons, of whatever rank, pre-eminence or dignity they may be, to the communities of cities, towns and any places whatever, concerning any rights, favours, immunities, customs or other matters, even granted of their own accord or otherwise, and in whatever terms they were or are expressed, shall not and may not in any way derogate from the liberties, jurisdictions, rights, honours or dominions of the Electors of the Holy Empire, ecclesiastical and secular, or of any of them. Even if in such privileges and letters, granted to any persons of whatever pre-eminence, dignity or status, as has been said, or to such communities, it has been expressly provided, or shall have been provided in favour, that they ought not to be revocable, unless a specific mention of them, and of their whole tenor contained in them, word for word and in order, were made in such revocation. For such privileges and letters, if and insofar as they are judged to derogate from, or to obstruct, in any respect the liberties, jurisdictions, rights, honours or dominions of the said Electors, or of any of them, we revoke them to that extent of our certain knowledge and deliberate purpose, and we decree, from the fullness of Imperial power, that they are to be understood, regarded and held as revoked.

units.la: CAP. XIV. DE HIS, QVIBVS VT INDIGNIS AVFERVNTVR bona feudalia.
units.tr: CHAPTER XIV. CONCERNING THOSE WHO ARE DEPRIVED OF FIEF PROPERTY AS UNWORTHY.

units.la: IN plerisque partibus vasalli, & feudatarij dominorum, feuda seu beneficia, quæ à dominis ipsis obtinent, intempestivè, verbaliter & in fraude renunciant, seu resignant eadem; & facta resignatione hujusmodi, dominos ipsos malitiosè diffidant, suasque inimicitias eis denunciant, damna eis subsequenter gravia inferendo: & beneficia seu feuda sic relicta prætextu guerræ seu inimicitiæ iterum invadunt, & occupant, & detinent occupata. ea propter præsenti constitutione in perpetuum valituras sancimus, quòd talis resignatio, seu renunciatio haberi debeat pro non facta, nisi liberè & realiter facta fuerit per eosdem, ita quòd possessio beneficiorum & feudorum hujusmodi, dominis ipsis corporaliter & realiter assignetur, in tantum, quòd nullo umquam tempore diffidantes ipsi in bonis, feudis, seu beneficiis resignatis, dominos ipsos perturbent per se, vel alios, aut molestent, nec ad hoc, consilium præstent, auxilium, vel favorem. contrarium faciens, seu dominos suos in beneficiis & feudis resignatis, vel non resignatis invadens quomodolibet vel perturbans, vel damna in ipsis inferens, seu consilium, auxilium præstans talia facientibus, vel favorem, feuda & beneficia hujusmodi eo ipso amittat, infamis existat, & banno Imperiali subjaceat, & nullus ad feuda vel beneficia hujusmodi parcat ei de cætero, quocunque tempore aditus, vel regressus, nec de novo concedi sibi valeant ullo modo; & facta eis contra hoc illorum concessio, seu investitura sequuta, viribus non subsistat. postremò, omnes pœnas prædictas illos vel illum, qui prædicta relignatione non facta, contra dominos suos fraudulenter agentes, vel agens, scienter eos invaserint, vel invaserit, diffidatione quacumque prævia vel obmissa, vigore præsentis sanctionis incurrere decernimus ipso facto.
units.tr: In many parts of the Empire, vassals and feudatories renounce or resign the fiefs or benefices they hold from their lords, at an improper time, by mere words and by fraud. Once such a resignation has been made, they maliciously defy their lords, declare enmity against them, and afterwards inflict serious losses upon them. Under the pretext of war or enmity, they then seize again the benefices and fiefs thus abandoned, and hold on to what they have seized. Therefore, by this constitution, which is to remain valid in perpetuity, we decree that such a resignation or renunciation shall be regarded as not having been made, unless it has been made freely and in fact by those concerned, so that possession of such benefices and fiefs is handed over to the lords themselves bodily and in fact. Thus, the defiant vassals shall never at any time disturb or harass their lords, either personally or through others, in the goods, fiefs or benefices that have been resigned, nor shall they give counsel, aid or favour for this purpose. Whoever acts contrary to this, or in any way invades or disturbs his lords in the benefices and fiefs, whether resigned or not, or inflicts losses on them, or gives counsel, aid or favour to those who do such things, shall by that very fact lose those fiefs and benefices, shall be infamous, and shall be subject to the Imperial ban. No one shall thereafter grant him any fief or benefice of this kind, by way of inheritance or reversion, in any manner whatever; and any grant or investiture made to them contrary to this shall be of no force. Finally, we decree that all the penalties mentioned above shall by this present sanction be incurred by ipso facto those persons who, without such a resignation having been made, act fraudulently against their lords, or who knowingly invade them, whether or not a prior or omitted defiance has been issued.

units.la: CAP. XV. DE CONSPIRATORIBVS.
units.tr: CAP. XV. CONCERNING CONSPIRATORS.

units.la: DEtestandas præterea, & sacris legibus reprobatas conspirationes & conventiculas, seu colligationes illicitas, in civitatibus & extra, vel inter civitatem & civitatem, inter personam & personam, seu inter personam & civitatem, prætextu patentelæ, seu receptionis in cives, vel alterius cujuscumque coloris conjurationes; insuper & confœderationes & pacta, nec non & consuetudinem circa hujusmodi introductam, quam censemus potius corruptelam, reprobamus, damnamus, & ex certa scientia damnamus: quas civitates, seu personæ, cujuscumque dignitatis, seu conditionis, aut status, sive inter se, vel cum aliis, absque auctoritate dominorum, quorum subditi vel ministeriales sunt, seu in quorum districtu sunt, eisdem dominis nominatim non exceptis, fecerint hactenus, & facere præsumpserint in posterum, sicut per sacras divorum Augustorum, prædecessorum nostrorum, leges, prohibitas non ambigitur & cassatas; illis confœderationibus & legis dumtaxat exceptis, quas Principes, & Civitates, ac generali pace provinciarum atque terrarum inter se firmasse noscuntur. illas enim nostræ decisioni specialiter reservantes, in suo decernimus vigore manere, donec de his aliud duxerimus ordinandum.
units.tr: Furthermore, we denounce and, by the sacred laws, reject as reprobate the conspiracies and little assemblies, or unlawful alliances, whether within cities or outside them, or between one city and another, between one person and another, or between a person and a city, under the pretext of a pact of citizenship or admission to the burghers' rights, or under any other colour whatsoever; likewise we reject and condemn, and from certain knowledge condemn, the confederations and agreements, and also the custom introduced concerning such things, which we judge rather to be a corruption. Those cities or persons, of whatever dignity, condition or status, who have hitherto made, and who presume to make in future, such alliances either among themselves or with others, without the authority of the lords whose subjects or ministerials they are, or in whose district they lie, the lords not being excepted by name, are beyond doubt forbidden and annulled by the sacred laws of our predecessors, the divine Augusti. The only exceptions are those confederations and laws which Princes and Cities are known to have established among themselves for the general peace of the provinces and lands. For we specially reserve those to our own decision, and we decree that they remain in force by their own authority until we shall have ordained otherwise concerning them.

units.la: 1. Personam singularem, quæ de cætero contra tenorem præsentis constitutionis, & nostræ legis quæ super hoc edita, confœderationes, colligationes, conspirationes, & pacta hujusmodi inire præsumpserit, ultra pœnam legis ejusdem, noram infamiæ, & pœnam decem librarum auri; civitatem vero, vel universitatem in hanc legem nostram similiter committentem, cenum librarum auri, nec non amissionis & privationis libertatum, & privilegiorum Imperialium, pœnas incurrere decernimus ipso, mediatæ pœnæ hujusmodi pecuniariæ fisco Imperiali; reliqua verò domino districtus, in cuius præjudicium factæ fuerint, applicanda.
units.tr: 1. A single person who henceforth, contrary to the tenor of the present constitution and of our law issued on this matter, presumes to enter into such confederations, leagues, conspiracies and pacts shall incur, beyond the penalty of that same law, the mark of infamy and a fine of ten pounds of gold. A city or corporate body likewise offending against this our law shall incur a fine of one hundred pounds of gold, together with the loss and deprivation of its liberties and Imperial privileges. We decree that these penalties fall upon them by the very fact, with half of the monetary penalty to go to the Imperial treasury and the remainder to be applied to the lord of the district to whose prejudice the acts were done.

units.la: CAP. XVI. DE PFALBVRGERIIS.
units.tr: Chapter XVI. Concerning the Pfahlburgers.

units.la: CÆterum, quia nonnulli cives & subditi Principum, Baronum, & aliorum hominum, sicut frequens ad nos querela perduxit, jugum originariæ subjectionis quærentes abjicere, imò ausu temerario merario contemnentes, in aliarum civitatum cives recipi se procurant, & frequenter in praeiudicium procurarunt; & nihilominus in priorum dominorum, quos tali fraude praesumpserunt, velut munt deferere, terris, civitatibus, oppidis, & villis corporaliter residentes, civitatum ad quas modo se transferunt, libertatibus gaudere, & ab eis defensari contendunt, qui in partibus Alamanniae Pfalburgensi consueverunt vulgariter appellari. quoniam autem patrocinari non debent alicui dolo, de Imperatoriae potestatis plenitudine, omnium Principum Electorum, Ecclesiasticorum & Saecularium accedente consilio, ex certa scientia statuimus, & praesenti lege perpetuo valitura sancimus, quod praedicti cives & subditi, eis, quib. subsunt, taliter illudentes, in omnibus terris, locis, & civitatibus Sacri Imperii a praesenti die in posterum, civitatum in quarum cives tali fraude recipi lerant, vel hactenus procurarunt, iurib. & libertatibus in nullo potiantur, nisi ad hujusmodi civitates corporaliter & realiter transeuntes, ibique larem fovetes, continue & vere ac non ficte residentes, debita onera & municipalia subeant munera in eisdem. Si qui vero contra praesentis legis tenorem recepti sint, vel fuerint in futurum, illorum receptio omni careat firmitate, & cujusCUMque dignitatis, conditionis, aut status existant, in nullo casu penitus, sive causa, ad quas recipi se procurant, juri. vel libertatibus gaudeant quomodolibet, vel fruantur, stantibus quibuscumque juribus, privilegiis, vel consuetudinibus observatis, quantocumque tempore, & obtentis; quas & quae, in quantum praesenti nostrae legi obveniant, praesentibus ex certa revocamus de praedictae Imperialis plenitudine potestatis, omnique carere decernimus mitatis.
units.tr: Moreover, since, as frequent complaints have brought to us, some citizens and subjects of princes, barons and other lords seek to throw off the yoke of their original subjection, and, with rash daring, scorn it altogether. They have themselves received as citizens of other cities, and have often done so to the prejudice of others. Nevertheless, while still residing bodily on the lands, in the cities, towns and villages of their former lords, whom they have deceitfully presumed to desert as if they were deserting them, they contend that they enjoy the liberties of the cities to which they now transfer themselves and are defended by them. In the regions of Germany these people are customarily called Pfahlburgers. Since no one ought to be shielded by fraud, we, from the fullness of imperial power, with the advice of all the Electors, ecclesiastical and secular princes, have decided on sure knowledge and by this law, which is to remain valid forever, decree that the aforesaid citizens and subjects who mock those to whom they are subject in this way, in all lands, places and cities of the Holy Empire, from the present day onward, shall enjoy no rights or liberties in those cities into which they have procured reception by such fraud, or have so procured up to now. They shall bear the due burdens and municipal duties in those cities only if they transfer bodily and in fact to those cities, and there keep their hearth, residing continually and truly, not feignedly. If any persons have been or shall in future be received contrary to the terms of this law, their reception shall lack all validity, and, whatever their dignity, condition or status, they shall in no case and for no cause, for which they procure reception, enjoy or make use of any right or liberty whatsoever. Any rights, privileges or customs that have been observed, however long they have lasted and however they were obtained, insofar as they conflict with this our law, we by this present act revoke from the same fullness of imperial power, and we decree that they shall be wholly void.

units.la: 2. Circa praemissa omnia Principum, Dominorum, & aliorum hominum, quos taliter contigit, vel continget in posterum, iuribus circa personas, & bona subditorum quorumcumque ipsos saepe dicto modo deferentium, semper salvis. Ihos nihilominus, qui saepe dictos cives, & alienos recipere, contra praesentis nostrae legis dispositionem, praesumpserint, vel recipere in praesumpserunt, si eos omnino non dimiserint infra mensem post intimationem praesentium eis centum marcas auri puri pro transgressione hujusmodi totiens, quotiens deinceps factum fuerit, decernentes; quarum medietas Imperiali fisco nostro, reliqua vero dominis illorum, quorum fuerunt, irremissibiliter applicetur.
units.tr: 2. In all the matters above, the rights of princes, lords and other persons, touching the persons and goods of their subjects, whoever they be who have been, or shall in future be, thus affected by the aforesaid practice, remain always intact. Nevertheless, those who have presumed, or shall presume, to receive the aforesaid citizens and aliens contrary to the provisions of this our law, if they do not wholly dismiss them within a month after notice of these presents is given to them, we decree shall pay one hundred marks of pure gold for each such transgression, as often as it shall be committed hereafter. Half of this sum shall go irrevocably to our imperial treasury, and the remainder to the lords to whom those persons belonged.

units.la: CAP. XVII. DE DIFFIDATIONIBVS.
units.tr: CAP. XVII. CONCERNING DIFFIDATIONS.

units.la: EOs, qui de caetero adversus aliquos iustam diffidationis causam se habere fingentes, ipsos in locis, ubi domicilia non obtinent, aut ea communiter non inhabitant, intempestive diffidant, declaramus damna quaecumque per incendia, spolia, vel rapinas diffidatis ipsis, cum honore suo inferre non posse.
units.tr: We declare that those who, pretending to have a just cause of diffidation against certain persons, unseasonably diffidate them in places where they do not hold a domicile or do not commonly reside, cannot inflict any damages whatever by fire, plunder or robbery upon the persons so diffidated, with their honour intact.

units.la: 2. Et quia patrocinari non debent alicui fraus & dolus, praesenti constitutione in perpetuum valitura sancimus, diffidationes hujusmodi quibuscumque dominis aut personis, cum quibus fuerunt in societate, familiaritate, vel honesta quavis amicitia conversati, sic factas vel fiendas in posterum, non valere, neque licere praetextu diffidationis cujuslibet quempiam invadere per incendia, spolia, vel rapinas, nisi diffidatio per tres dies naturales ipsi diffidando personaliter, vel in loco, quo habitare consuevit, publice fuerit intimata, possitque de intimatione hujusmodi, per testes idoneos, fides plena. Quisquis secus quempiam diffidare vel invadere modo praemisso praesumpserit, ipso incurrat, ac si nulla diffidatio facta esset; quem etiam tamquam proditorem, per quemcumque Judices poenis legalibus statuimus castigari.
units.tr: 2. And since fraud and deceit ought not to be defended by anyone, we decree by this constitution, which is to remain valid in perpetuity, that diffidations of this kind, made or to be made in future against any lords or persons with whom the diffidator has been in association, familiarity, or any honest friendship, are not valid, and it is not lawful, under the pretext of any diffidation, to attack anyone by fire, plunder or robbery, unless the diffidation has been announced publicly over three natural days, either to the diffidated person himself in person or in the place where he is accustomed to live, and unless full faith can be given to such announcement through suitable witnesses. Whoever shall presume to diffidate or attack anyone otherwise than in the manner set out above, let him incur the penalty as if no diffidation had been made at all; and we decree that he be punished by whatever judges with the legal penalties as a traitor.

units.la: 3. Prohibemus etiam & damnamus universas & singulas guerras, & lites injustas, quoq; injusta incendia, spolia, rapinas, indebita & inconsueta theolonea & conductus, & extorsiones pro ipsis conductibus extorqueri consuetas, sub poenis, quibus sacrae leges praemissa, & eorum libet, sanciunt puniend a.
units.tr: 3. We also prohibit and condemn all wars and unjust lawsuits, likewise unjust fires, plunder and robbery, undue and unaccustomed tolls and escorts, and the extortions customarily exacted for those escorts, under the penalties which the sacred laws decree for the aforesaid offences and for whichever of them is to be punished.

units.la: CAP. XVIII. LITTERA INTIMATIONIS.
units.tr: CHAPTER XVIII. LETTER OF INTIMATION.

units.la: VObis Illustri & magnifico Principi Domino & c. Marchioni Brandeburgensi, Sacri Imperii Archicamerario, Coelectori, & amico nostro charissimo. Electionem Romanorum Regis ex rationabilibus causis imminet facienda, praesentibus intimamus; vosque ex officio ad electionem praefatam rite vocamus, quatenus a die tali, &c. infra tres menses computandos, per vos, seu nuncios aut procuratores vestros, unum vel plures, sufficiens mandatum habentes, ad locum debitum, juxta formam sacrarum legum super hoc editarum, venire curetis, decreturi, tractaturi, & concordaturi cum aliis Conprincipibus & Coelectoribus vestris & nostris, de electione futuri Regis Romanorum in Imperatorem postmodum favente Domino promovendi, eandem manifesti usque ad plenam consummationem electionis hujusmodi, & alias facturi, & procuraturi prout in sacris legibus super hoc deliberate editis inveniatur expressum; aliis, non obstante vestra, seu vestrorum absentia, in praemissis una cum aliis Conprincipibus & Coelectoribus vestris & nostris, prout legum ipsarum sanxerit auctoritas, finaliter procedemus.
units.tr: To you, the illustrious and magnificent Prince, Lord, etc., Margrave of Brandenburg, Archchamberlain of the Holy Empire, Co-elector, and our most dear friend: We hereby notify you that, for reasonable causes, the election of a King of the Romans is about to be held; and we formally summon you to the aforesaid election, so that, from the day of such-and-such, etc., within three months to be counted, you take care to come, either in person or through your envoys or proxies, one or more, holding sufficient authority, to the due place, according to the form of the sacred laws issued on this matter; there to decide, deliberate, and agree with the other princes and co-electors, both yours and ours, concerning the election of the future King of the Romans, who, by the favour of the Lord, is afterwards to be promoted to Emperor; and to make and carry out the same declarations until the full conclusion of such an election, and to do other things as is expressly found in the sacred laws deliberately issued on this matter. Otherwise, your absence or that of your representatives notwithstanding, we shall proceed to a final decision in the aforesaid matters, together with the other princes and co-electors, both yours and ours, as the authority of those laws shall have prescribed.

units.la: CAP. XIX.
units.tr: CAP. XIX.

units.la: FORMA PROCVRATORII, MITTENDI PER cum principem Electorem, qui nuncios suos ad electionem faciendam duxerit destinandos.
units.tr: FORM OF A PROCURATORY, TO BE SENT BY a prince Elector who has decided to send his messengers to make the election.

units.la: NOs talis, Dei gratia, &c. Sacri Imperii &c. notum facimus tenore præsentium universis: quòd cum electio Romanorum Regis ex rationabilibus causis imminet facienda, nos de honore & statu Sacri Imperii solicitudine debita intendere cupientes, ne tam gravibus dispendiis periculosè subjaceat, de fide & circumspectionis industria dilectorum nobis &c. fidelium nostrorum obtinentes utique præsumptionis indubiæ fiduciam singularem, ipsos & quemlibet eorum in solidum, ita quòd non sit melior conditio occupantis, sed quod per unum inceptum fuerit, per alium finiri valeat, & licitè terminari, omni jure, modo & forma, quibus melius & efficacius possumus, seu valemus, nostros veros & legitimos Procuratores, & nuncios speciales facimus, constituimus, & ordinamus, ad tractandum ubilibet unà cum aliis Conprincipibus, & Coëlectoribus nostris, tam Ecclesiasticis quàm Secularibus, & cum ipsis concordandum, conveniendum, & concludendum de persona quacunq; habili acidonea, in Regem Romanorum eligenda; ac ipsis tractatibus super electione talis personæ habendis, pro nobis, loco & nomine nostris interessendum, tractandum, & deliberandum, nec non vice & nomine nostris eandem personam nominandum, & in ipsam consentiendum, ac etiam in Regem Romanorum promovendum, ad Sacrum Imperium eligendum, ac in animam nostram præstandum quodcumque juramentum, quod necessarium debitum, seu consuetum fuerit; circa præmissa, & quodlibet præmissorum, alium, vel alios procuratores in solidum substituendum & revocandum, omnia & singula faciendum, quæ in præmissis, & circa præmissa etiam usque ad consummationem tractatuum, nominationis, deliberationis, & electionis hujusmodi, de præsenti faciendæ necessaria, aut utilia fuerint, seu etiam quomodolibet oportuna, etiamsi præmissa, vel eorum quodlibet, mandatum exigant speciale; etiamsi majora vel magis singularia fuerint supradictis, & quæ nosmetipsi facere possemus, si hujusmodi tractatuum, deliberationis, nominationis & electionis futuræ negotiis, præsentes & personaliter adessemus, gratum & ratum habentes, & habere volentes, & nos perpetuò habituros firmiter promittentes, quicquid per antedictos Procuratores, seu nuncios nostros, necnon substiruros, aut substituendos, ab ipsis seu eorum altero, in præmissis seu præmissorum quolibet, actum, gestum, seu factum fuerit, aut quomodolibet ordinatum.
units.tr: We, such-and-such, by the grace of God, etc., of the Holy Empire, etc., make known by the tenor of these presents to all: that since the election of a King of the Romans is about to be held for reasonable causes, and since we desire to attend with due care to the honour and state of the Holy Empire, lest it be exposed dangerously to such grave losses, and since we place a singular and undoubted confidence in the faith and careful diligence of our beloved and faithful ones, etc., we make, constitute and ordain them, and each of them, jointly and severally, so that the condition of the one who first enters upon the business is no better, but what has been begun by one may be finished and lawfully concluded by another, by every right, manner and form by which we best and most effectually can or may, our true and lawful procurators and special messengers, to treat anywhere together with our other co-princes and co-electors, both ecclesiastical and secular, and to agree, convene and conclude with them concerning any suitable and fit person to be elected King of the Romans; and to be present, treat and deliberate in our place and on our behalf in the negotiations concerning the choice of such a person; and likewise to name that same person in our place and name, to consent to him, to promote him to the King of the Romans, to elect him to the Holy Empire, and to take in our soul whatever oath shall be required, due or customary; and concerning the foregoing, and each of them, to substitute and revoke another or others as procurators jointly and severally; to do all and each of the things which in the foregoing matters, and concerning them, even up to the completion of the negotiations, nomination, deliberation and election of this kind to be carried out at present, shall be necessary or useful, or in any way fitting, even if the foregoing or any of them demand a special mandate, even if they be greater or more particular than the above, and which we ourselves could do if we were present in person at the business of such negotiations, deliberation, nomination and future election; holding and wishing to hold as pleasing and ratified, and firmly promising that we shall hold forever, whatever shall be done, enacted or in any way ordained in the foregoing or any part of them by the aforesaid procurators or our messengers, or by our substitutes or those to be substituted, or by either of them.

units.la: CAP. XX.
units.tr: CAP. XX.

units.la: DE VNIONE PRINCIPATVVM ELECTORVM, & Iurium eis connexorum.
units.tr: ON THE UNION OF THE ELECTORAL PRINCIPALITIES, AND OF THE RIGHTS CONNECTED WITH THEM.

units.la: In nomine sanctæ & individuæ Trinitatis feliciter, Amen.
units.tr: In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, happily. Amen.

units.la: Carolus Quartus divina favente clementia, Romanorum Imperator, semper-Augustus, & Bohemiæ Rex, ad perpetuam rei memoriam.
units.tr: Charles IV, by the favour of divine clemency, Roman Emperor, ever Augustus, and King of Bohemia, to the perpetual memory of the matter.
