units.la: Quia universi & singuli Principatus, quorum virtute Seculares Principes Electores, jus & vocem in electione Regis Romanorum, in Cæsarem promovendi, obtinere noscuntur, cum jure hujusmodi, nec non officiis, dignitatibus, & juribus aliis, eis, & cuilibet eorum annexis, & dependentibus ab eisdem, adeò conjuncti, & inseparabiliter sint uniti, quòd jus, vox, officium, & dignitas quoque jura, ad quemlibet Principatuum eorundem spectantia, cadere non possint in alium, qui Principatum ipsum cum terra, vasallagiis, feudis, & dominio, ac ejus pertinentiis uniuersis possidere; præsenti edicto Imperiali perpetuò valituro sancimus, unumquemque Principatuum prædictorum, cum jure & voce electionis, ac officio, cæterisque omnibus dignitatibus, juribus & pertinentiis ad ipsum spectantibus, ita perseverare, & esse debere unitum perpetuis temporibus indivisibiliter & conjunctum, quòd possessor Principatus cujuslibet, etiam juris, vocis, officii, & dignitatis, & pertinentiarum omnium ad illum spectantium, quieta debeat & libera possessione gaudere, ac Princeps Elector ab omnibus reputari, ipseque, & nemo alius, per cæteros Principes Electores, ad electionem, & omnes actus alios pro Sacri Imperii honore, vel oportunitate gerendos, omni tempore assumi, sine contradictione qualibet, & admitti; nec aliquid præmissorum ab altero, cum sint & esse debeant inseparabilia, dividi, vel ullo tempore debeat separari, aut in judicio, vel extra divisim repeti valeat, aut evinci, vel etiam per sententiam separari; nec aliquis unum sine alio impetens audiatur. quod si per errorem, vel aliis auditus quis fuerit, aut processus, judicium, sententia, vel aliquid hujusmodi contra præsentem dispositionem nostram emanaverit, seu quomodolibet attemptari contigerit, hoc totum, & omnia ex his, & quolibet eorum sequentia, co ipso viribus non subsistant.
units.tr: Since all and each of the principalities, by virtue of which the secular princes are known to hold the electoral right and vote in choosing the King of the Romans, to be promoted to Caesar, together with the right of this kind, as well as the offices, dignities and other rights annexed to them and to each of them and dependent upon them, are so closely joined and inseparably united that the right, the vote, the office and the dignity, and likewise the rights pertaining to any one of those principalities, cannot pass to another who holds that principality together with its land, vassalages, fiefs, and dominion, and all its appurtenances; by this imperial edict, which is to remain valid in perpetuity, we decree that each of the aforesaid principalities, with the right and vote of election, the office, and all other dignities, rights and appurtenances belonging to it, shall so continue and ought to be united and conjoined in perpetual times, indivisibly, that the possessor of any principality, together with the right, vote, office and dignity, and all appurtenances belonging to it, shall enjoy quiet and free possession, and that the prince elector shall be regarded by all, and he himself, and no other, shall at all times be taken up and admitted by the other princes electors, without any contradiction, to the election and to all other acts to be performed for the honour or advantage of the Holy Empire; and that none of the aforesaid things shall be divided from another, since they are and ought to be inseparable, nor at any time be separated, nor be sought or evicted in court or outside it separately, nor be separated even by sentence; and no one who attacks one without the other shall be heard. But if through error, or for any other reason, a hearing, a process, a judgment, a sentence, or anything of this kind has issued against this our present disposition, or happens to be attempted in any way, let all of this, and everything that follows from any of these, by that very fact have no force.

units.la: CAP. XXI.
units.tr: CAP. XXI.

units.la: DE ORDINE PROCESSIONIS INTER ARCHIEPISCOPOS.
units.tr: OF THE ORDER OF PROCESSION AMONG THE ARCHBISHOPS.

units.la: QUoniam autem superius in principio constitutionum nostrarum praesentium, circa ordinem electionis Ecclesiasticorum Principum Electorum in consilio, & in mensa, & alias quotiens Imperialem curiam celebrarent, seu Principes Electores deinceps cum Imperatore vel Rege Romanorum congregari contigerit, sufficienter duximus providendum, super qua priscis audivimus temporibus pluries dissceptatum; expedire credimus etiam processionis & deambulationis inter eosdem diffinire.
units.tr: Since we have sufficiently provided above, at the beginning of these present constitutions, for the order of election of the ecclesiastical Electoral Princes, and for their order at the council table, at the banquet, and whenever they assemble at the Imperial court, or whenever the Electoral Princes happen to be gathered with the Emperor or the King of the Romans in future, a matter which we have heard was often disputed in earlier times, we believe it also expedient to settle the order of procession and of walking among the same.

units.la: 2. Quapropter hoc perpetuo Imperiali edicto decernimus, ut quotiescumque in congregatione Imperatoris, vel Regis Romanorum, & Principum praedictorum, Imperatore vel Rege ipsis ambulante, insignia ante faciem suam portari contigerit, Archiepiscopus Trevirensis in directa metrali linea ante Imperatorem vel Regem transeat, illique soli medii inter eos ambulent, quos Imperialia vel Regalia contingent insignia deportare.
units.tr: 2. Therefore by this perpetual Imperial edict we decree that whenever, in an assembly of the Emperor or King of the Romans and the aforesaid Princes, insignia happen to be carried before the face of the Emperor or King while he is walking, the Archbishop of Trier shall pass in a straight line measured before the Emperor or King, and only those who are to carry the Imperial or Royal insignia shall walk in the middle between them.

units.la: 3. Cum autem Imperator, vel Rex, absque insigniis eisdem incesserit, extunc idem Archiepiscopus Imperatorem, vel Regem praefato modo praecedat, ita quod nemo penitus inter eos medius habeatur; aliis duobus Archiepiscopis Electoribus, loca sua juxta distinctionem provinciarum circa sessionem superius declaratam, etiam circa processionem perpetuo servaturis.
units.tr: 3. But when the Emperor or King walks without the insignia, then the same Archbishop shall go before the Emperor or King in the aforesaid manner, so that no one at all is placed between them; the other two Archbishop Electors shall also keep their places in procession permanently, according to the division of provinces declared above concerning the seating.

units.la: CAP. XXII.
units.tr: CAP. XXII.

units.la: DE ORDINE PROCESSIONIS PRINCIPUM ELECTO- RUM, & per quos insignia deportentur.
units.tr: CONCERNING THE ORDER OF PROCESSION OF THE PRINCE-ELECTORS, AND BY WHOM THE INSIGNIA ARE CARRIED.

units.la: AD declarandum autem in Imperatoris, vel Regis Romanorum deambulantis praesentia, processionis ordinem Principum Electorum, de quo supra fecimus mentionem, statuimus, ut quotiescumque in celebratione Imperialis curiae Principes Electores cum Imperatore, seu Rege Romanorum, in quibuscumque actibus vel solemnitatibus processionaliter ambulare contigerit, & Imperialia vel Regalia debuerint insignia deportari, Dux Saxoniae Imperialem vel Regalem ensem deferens, Imperatorem seu Regem immediate praecedat, & inter illum, & Archiepiscopum Trevirensem medius habeatur; Comes vero Palatinus, pomum Imperiale portans, à latere dextro; & Marchio Brandenburgensis sceptrum deferens, à sinistro latere ipsius Ducis Saxoniae lineariter gradiantur; Rex autem Bohemiae Imperatorem seu Regem ipsum immediate, nullo interveniente, sequatur.
units.tr: To declare the order of procession of the Prince-Electors, of which we have made mention above, in the presence of the Emperor or the King of the Romans when he walks in procession, we decree that whenever in the celebration of the Imperial court the Prince-Electors happen to walk in procession with the Emperor or the King of the Romans, in whatever acts or solemnities, and the Imperial or Royal insignia ought to be carried, the Duke of Saxony, bearing the Imperial or Royal sword, shall walk immediately before the Emperor or King, with the Archbishop of Trier kept in the middle between him and the Emperor; the Count Palatine, carrying the Imperial orb, shall walk in a line on the right side, and the Margrave of Brandenburg, bearing the sceptre, on the left side of the same Duke of Saxony; while the King of Bohemia shall follow immediately behind the Emperor or King himself, with no one intervening.

units.la: CAP. XXIII.
units.tr: CAP. XXIII.

units.la: DE BENEDICTIONIBVS ARCHIEPISCOPORVM IN praesentia Imperatoris.
units.tr: ON THE BLESSINGS OF THE ARCHBISHOPS IN THE PRESENCE OF THE EMPEROR.

units.la: QUotiens insuper in Imperatoris, vel Regis Romanorum praesentia, Missarum solemnia celebrari, ac Moguntinensem, Trevirensem, & Coloniensem Archiepiscopos, vel duos ex eis adesse contigerit, in confessione, quae ante missam dici consuevit, ac in porrectione Evangeliorum, & Pacis post Agnus Dei portanda, nec non & in benedictionibus post finita Missarum solemnia, ac etiam ante mensam faciendis, & in gratiis post cibum acceptum agendis, is inter eos ordo servetur, prout de ipsorum consilio duximus ordinandum, quod prima die haec omnia & singula, a primo; secunda die, a secundo; tertia vero, a tertio peragantur.
units.tr: Furthermore, whenever the solemn Masses are celebrated in the presence of the Emperor or the King of the Romans, and it happens that the Archbishops of Mainz, Trier and Cologne, or two of them, are present, the following order shall be observed among them in the confession which is customarily said before Mass, in the presentation of the Gospels, and in the Peace to be carried after the Agnus Dei, and likewise in the blessings given after the solemn Masses are finished, and also in those given before the meal, and in the thanksgivings to be offered after food has been taken. This order, which we have decided to ordain on their advice, is that on the first day all these things, each and every one, are to be performed by the first; on the second day, by the second; and on the third day, by the third.

units.la: 2. Primum autem, seu secundum, vel tertium hoc casu, secundum quod prius vel posterius quisque liber eorum consecratus exstitit, debere intelligi declaramus, & ut se invicem honore condigno & decenti praeveniant, & exemplum aliis praebeant invicem honorandi, is, quem circa praemissa ordo tegerit, ad hanc alterum convenienti & charitativa inclinatione invitet, & tunc demum ad praemissa procedat, seu quodlibet praemissorum.
units.tr: 2. We declare, moreover, that the first, the second, or the third in this case is to be understood according to which of them was consecrated earlier or later. And so that they may mutually anticipate one another with fitting and due honour, and set an example to others of honouring one another, he whom the order described above assigns to these matters shall invite the other to this, with a suitable and charitable bow, and only then proceed to the aforesaid acts, or to any one of them.

units.la: CAP. XXIV.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXIV.

units.la: INFRA SCRIPTAE LEGES PROMVLGATAE SVNT IN Curia Metensi per Dominum Carolum IV. Romanorum Imperatorem, & Bohemiae Regem Augustum, Anno Domini M. CCC. LVI. in die Natalis Christi, assistentibus sibi omnibus Sacri Romani Imperii Electoribus, praesentibus dominis, Venerabili in Christo Patre Domino Theodorico Episcopo Albanensi, Sancta Romana Ecclesia Cardinali, ac Carolo Regis Francia primogenito, Normandiae Duce Illustri, ac Delphino Viennensi.
units.tr: THE FOLLOWING LAWS WERE PROMULGATED AT METZ, in the court of Lord Charles IV, Emperor of the Romans and August King of Bohemia, in the year of the Lord 1356, on the day of Christ's Nativity, all the Electors of the Holy Roman Empire assisting him; present were the lords: the Venerable Father in Christ, Lord Dietrich, Bishop of Albano, Cardinal of the Holy Roman Church, and Charles, firstborn son of the King of France, Illustrious Duke of Normandy, and the Dauphin of Vienne.

units.la: SI quis cum Principibus, Militibus, vel privatis, seu quibuscumque personis, plebeis etiam, scelestam factionem, aut factionis ipsius inierit sacramentum, vel dederit, de nece Venerabilium & Illustrium Principum nostrorum, & Sacri Romani Imperii, tam Ecclesiasticorum quam Secularium, Principum Electorum, seu alterius eorundem (nam & ipsi pars corporis nostri sunt. Eadem enim severitate voluntatem sceleris, qua effectum puniri jura voluerunt): ipse quidem, utpote majestatis reus, gladio feriatur, bonis ejus omnibus fisco nostro addictis: filii vero ejus, quibus vitam Imperiali speciali liter lenitate concedimus (paterno enim deberent perire supplicio, in quibus paternum, hoc est, hæreditarii criminis metuuntur exempla) à materna vel avita, omnium etiam proximorum hęreditate, & successione habeantur alieni, ex testamentis aliorum nihil capiant, sint perpetuo egentes & pauperes, infamia eos paterna semper comitetur, ad nullum umquam honorem, ad nulla prorsus sacramenta perveniant, sint postremo tales, ut his perpetua egestate sordentibus sit & mors solatium, & vita supplicium. Denique jubemus eos esse notabiles sine venia, qui pro talibus umquam apud nos intervenire temptaverint.
units.tr: If anyone, whether with princes, soldiers, private persons, or any other persons, even of the common people, shall enter into or give an oath to a wicked faction, or to any such faction, concerning the death of our Venerable and Illustrious Princes and of the Holy Roman Empire, both ecclesiastical and secular, the Electors or any other of them (for they too are part of our body; for we wish the intention of a crime to be punished with the same severity as its effect), he himself, as guilty of treason, shall be struck down with the sword, and all his goods shall be forfeited to our treasury. His sons, to whom we grant life by a special kindness of the Empire (for they would have to perish with their father's punishment, in whom the examples of a paternal, that is, hereditary, crime are feared), shall be regarded as strangers to the inheritance and succession of their mother's and grandfather's estates, and of all their relatives; they shall take nothing from the wills of others; they shall be perpetually needy and poor; infamy shall always accompany them from their father; they shall attain to no office and to no sacraments whatever; and finally they shall be such that, sunk in perpetual want, death is their comfort and life their punishment. Lastly, we order that those be marked without pardon who have ever attempted to intercede with us for such persons.

units.la: 2. Ad filias sane ipsorum, quotlibet numero fuerint, Falcidiam tantum ex bonis matris, sive testata, sive intestata decesserit, volumus pervenire, ut habeant mediocrem potius filiæ alimoniam, quàm integrum emolumentum aut nomen hęredis consequantur. minor enim circa eas debet esse sententia, quas pro infirmitate sexus minus ausuras esse confidimus.
units.tr: 2. Indeed, to their daughters, however many there be, we wish only the Falcidian portion of the mother's goods to pass, whether she dies testate or intestate, so that they may have a modest maintenance as daughters rather than obtain the full advantage or the name of heir. For our judgment concerning them ought to be milder, since we trust that, on account of the weakness of their sex, they will dare less.

units.la: 3. Emancipationes quoque, quæ à prædictis sive in filios, post legem duntaxat latam, sive in filias fuerint collatæ, non valeant. dotes, donationes quorumlibet, postremò item alienationes, quas ex eo tempore qualibet fraude, vel jure factas esse constiterit, quo primò memorati de ineunda factione, ac societate cogitaverint, nullius statuimus esse momenti. Uxores sine prædictorum recuperata dote, si in ea conditione fuerint, ut, quæ à viris titulo donationis acceperunt, seu accipiunt, filiis debeant reservare, tempore quo usufructus absumitur; omnia ea fisco nostro se reliQuras esse cognoscant, quæ juxta legem filiis debebantur; Falcidia etiam ex his rebus, filiabus tantum, non etiam filiis deputetur.
units.tr: 3. Likewise, emancipations which have been granted by the aforesaid persons, either to sons after the law alone was proclaimed, or to daughters, shall not be valid. Dowries, donations of any persons whatever, and finally likewise alienations, which shall be found to have been made by any fraud or right from the time when the aforementioned men first thought of entering into the faction and conspiracy, we declare to be of no force. Wives, unless the dowry has been recovered, if they are in such a condition that what they have received or receive from their husbands by title of donation ought to be reserved for their sons at the time when the usufruct is used up, shall all know that everything which by law was owed to the sons is to be left to our treasury; the Falcidian portion from these goods shall be assigned to daughters only, not to sons.

units.la: 4. Idem, quod de prædictis, eorumque filiis cavimus, etiam de satellitibus, consciìs, ac ministris, filisque eorum simili severitate censemus. Sane si quis ex his in exordio initæ factionis, studio veræ laudis accensus, ipse prodiderit factionem, & præmio à nobis & honore donabitur. Is verò, qui usus fuerit factione, si vel sero, tamen incognita adhuc consiliorum arcana patefecerit, absolutione *tantum, ac venia dignus habebitur.
units.tr: 4. What we have provided concerning the aforesaid persons and their sons, we likewise decree, with similar severity, concerning attendants, accomplices, and ministers, and their sons. Indeed, if any of these, kindled by zeal for true praise, at the beginning of the begun faction, reveals the faction himself, he shall be rewarded by us with a prize and with honour. But he who has taken part in the faction, if even late, yet while the secrets of the plans are still unknown, shall reveal them, shall be held worthy of absolution and pardon only.

units.la: 5. Statuimus insuper, ut si quid contra prædictos Principes Electores, Ecclesiasticos vel Secularies, commissum dicatur, etiam post mortem rei, id crimen instaurari posse.
units.tr: 5. We further decree that if anything is said to have been committed against the aforesaid Princes Electors, ecclesiastical or secular, this crime can be renewed even after the death of the accused.

units.la: 6. In hoc item crimine, quod ad læsam in Principibus Electoribus suis Majestatem pertinet, etjam in caput domini, servi torquentur.
units.tr: 6. In this crime also, which pertains to injured majesty in their Electoral Princes, servants are tortured even against the head of their master.

units.la: 7. Volumus insuper, & præsenti Imperiali sancimus edicto, ut etiam post mortem nocentium hoc crimen inchoari possit, ut convicto mortuo, memoria ejus damnetur, & bona successoribus ejus eripiantur. nam ex quo scelcratissimum quis ceperit consilium, exinde quodammodo sua mente punitus est.
units.tr: 7. We wish moreover, and by this present Imperial edict we decree, that this crime may be begun even after the death of the guilty, so that, the dead man being convicted, his memory is condemned and his goods are snatched from his successors; for from the moment someone has conceived the most wicked plan, he is in a certain manner already punished in his own mind.

units.la: 8. Porrò, ex quo quis tale crimen contraxit, neque alienare, neque manumittere eum posse, nec ei solvere jure debitorem, decernimus.
units.tr: 8. Furthermore, from the moment someone has incurred such a crime, we decree that he can neither alienate nor manumit, nor lawfully pay his debts to another.

units.la: 9. In hac causa in caput domini servos torqueri statuimus, id est, propter causam factionis damnandæ contra Principes Electores, Ecclesiasticos & Seculares, ut præmittitur.
units.tr: 9. In this cause we decree that servants are to be tortured against the head of their master, that is, on account of the cause of the faction to be condemned against the Electoral Princes, ecclesiastical and secular, as has been premised.

units.la: 10. Et si decesserit quis, propter incertam personam successoris bona servantur, si in a casu hujusmodi fuisse mortuus arguatur.
units.tr: 10. And if anyone dies, his goods are kept on account of the uncertain person of the successor, if he is proved to have died in a case of this kind.

units.la: CAP. XXV.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXV.

units.la: DE INTEGRITATE PRINCIPATVVM ELECTORVM.
units.tr: ON THE INTEGRITY OF THE ELECTORAL PRINCIPALITIES.

units.la: SI cæteros Principatus congruit in sua integritate servari, ut corroboretur justitia, & subjecti fidelitas pace gaudeant & quiete, multo magis magnifici Principatus, dominia, honores, & jura Electorum Principum debent illæsa servari. nam ubi majus incumbit periculum, majus debet remedium adhiberi, ne columnis ruentibus, basis totius ædificii collidatur.
units.tr: If it is fitting that the other principalities be preserved in their integrity, so that justice may be strengthened and subjects may enjoy the peace and quiet of their loyalty, much more should the great principalities, dominions, honours and rights of the Electoral Princes be preserved unharmed. For where the greater danger lies, the greater remedy must be applied, lest with the pillars falling, the base of the whole building be crushed.

units.la: 2. Decernimus igitur, & hoc perpetuis temporibus valituro Imperiali sancimus edicto, quòd exnunc inantea perpetuis futuris temporibus, insignes & magnifici Principatus, videlicet Regnum Bohemiæ, Comitatus Palatinus Rheni, Ducatus Saxoniæ, & Marchionatus Brandenburgensis, terræ, distinctus, homagia, vassallagia, & alia quævis ad ipsa spectantia, scindi, dividi, seu quavis conditione dimembrari non debeant, sed ut potiùs in sua perfecta integritate perpetua maneant, primogenitus filius succedat in eis, sibique soli jus ac dominium competat, nisi forte mente captus, fatuus, seu alterius famosi & notabilis defectus existeret, propter quem non deberet, seu posset hominibus principari. in quo casu, inhibita sibi successione, secundogenitum, si fuerit in ea progenie, seu alium seniorem fratrem, vel consanguineum laicum, qui paterno stipiti in descendenti recta linea proximior fuerit, volumus successurum; qui tamen apud alios fratres, & sorores, se clementem & pium exhibebit continuò, juxta datam sibi à Deo gratiam, & juxta suum beneplacitum, & ipsius patrimonii facultates; divisione, scissione, seu dimembratione Principatus, & pertinentiarum ejus, sibi omnibus modis interdicta.
units.tr: 2. We therefore decree, and by this Imperial edict, which is to hold good in perpetuity, we enact that from now on, for all future times, the distinguished and magnificent principalities, namely the Kingdom of Bohemia, the Palatine County of the Rhine, the Duchy of Saxony and the Margraviate of Brandenburg, together with their lands, districts, homages, vassalages and all other things pertaining to them, shall not be cut up, divided, or dismembered in any way, but shall rather remain in their full and perpetual integrity. The firstborn son shall succeed to them, and the right and dominion shall belong to him alone, unless perhaps he be mentally incapacitated, foolish, or afflicted with some other notorious and conspicuous defect on account of which he ought not, or could not, rule over men. In that case, with succession barred to him, we wish the second-born, if there be one in that line, or another elder brother, or a lay blood relative who is nearer to the paternal stock in the direct descending line, to succeed. Yet he shall continually show himself merciful and pious towards the other brothers and sisters, according to the grace given him by God, according to his own good pleasure, and according to the resources of the patrimony itself. Division, splitting, or dismemberment of the principality and its appurtenances is forbidden to him in every way.

units.la: Hh 3 CAP. suo Regali faciet nomine: & deinde sub Imperiali titulo innovabit; & in his ipsos Principes omnes in genere, & quemlibet eorum in specie nullatenus impedire, sed potius absque dolo gratiose tenebitur promovere.
units.tr: ...shall do so in his royal name; and afterwards he shall renew it under the imperial title. In these matters he shall be bound not to hinder the Princes themselves, all in general and each one in particular, in any way, but rather shall be bound to promote them graciously and without deceit.

units.la: 10. In casu denique, quo tres Principes Electores praesentes, seu absentium nuncii, quartum ex se, seu eorum consortio, videlicet Principem Electorem praesentem, vel absentem, in Regem Romanorum elegerint, vocem illius electi, si praesens adfuerit, aut nunciorum ipsius, si eum abesse contingeret, plenum vigorem habere, & eligentium augere numerum, partemque majorem decernimus constituere, ad instar caeterorum Principum Electorum.
units.tr: 10. Finally, in the case in which three Electoral Princes who are present, or the messengers of those who are absent, elect as King of the Romans a fourth from among themselves or from their company, namely an Electoral Prince present or absent, we decree that the vote of that person chosen, if he is present, or of his messengers, if it happens that he is absent, shall have full force; that it shall increase the number of electors; and we decree that it shall constitute the greater part, in the same way as the other Electoral Princes.

units.la: CAP. III.
units.tr: CAP. III.

units.la: DE SESSIONE a TREVERENSIS, COLONIEN- SIS & Moguntinensis Archiepiscoporum.
units.tr: Concerning the seating of the Archbishops of Trier, Cologne and Mainz.

units.la: In nomine sanctae & individuae Trinitatis feliciter, Amen.
units.tr: In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, happily, Amen.

units.la: Carolus Quartus divina favente clementia, Romanorum Imperator, semper-Augustus, & Bohemiae Rex, ad perpetuam rei memoriam.
units.tr: Charles the Fourth, by the favour of divine clemency, Roman Emperor, ever Augustus, and King of Bohemia, to the perpetual memory of the matter.

units.la: DECOR, & gloria Sacrosancti Romani Imperii, & honor Caesareus, & Reipublicae grata compendia, venerabilium & illustrium Principum Electorum concordi voluntate foventur; qui velut columnae proceres sacrum aedificium circumspectae prudentiae solerti pietate sustentant; quorum praesidio dextra Imperialis potentiae roboratur, & quando mutui favoris amplioris benignitate stringuntur, tanto uberioris pacis & tranquillitatis commoda feliciter profluunt populo Christiano. Utigitur inter venerabiles Moguntinensem, Coloniensem, necnon Treverensem Archiepiscopos, Sacri Imperii Principes Electores, omnium litium, & suspectuum mala, quae & qui de priori tate seu dignitate sessionum suarum in curiis Imperialibus, & Regalibus, suborin valerent, in posterum perpetuis inantea temporibus amputentur, & ipsi in cordis & animorum quieta conditione manentes, de opportunitatibus Sacri Imperii concordi favore, & virtuosae dilectionis studio convenientes meditari valeant, pro consolatione populi Christiani, habita deliberatione cum omnibus Principibus Electoribus, tam Ecclesiasticis quam Secularibus, & de ipsorum consilio decernimus, & de Imperatoriae potestatis plenitudine, hac edictali lege perpetuo valitura, sancimus, quod supradicti venerabiles Archiepiscopi, Treverensis videlicet, ex opposito & liniari directione versus Imperatoris faciem; Moguntinensis vero in suis dioecesi & provincia, & extra provinciam suam in toto Archicancellariatu suo Germanico, provincia Coloniensi dumtaxat excepta; & demum Coloniensis in suis dioecesi & provincia, & extra provinciam suam in tota Italia & Gallia, in dextero latere Romanorum Caesaris, sedere possint, valeant, & debeant in omnibus publicis actibus Imperialibus, puta judiciis, collationibus feudorum, & in refectionibus mensarum, ac etiam in consiliis, & in omnibus aliis agendis, propter quae contingit seu continget eos pro honore seu utilitate Imperiali tractandis mutuo convenire & hunc modum sessionis sub omni eo ordine, sicut expressatur superius, ad praedictorum Coloniensis, Treverensis, & Moguntinensis Archiepiscoporum successores, perpetuo extendi volumus, ut nullo umquam tempore super his quaevis dubietas generetur.
units.tr: The dignity and glory of the Holy Roman Empire, the honour of Caesar, and the advantages of the commonwealth are cherished by the united will of the venerable and illustrious Electoral Princes, who, like pillars, support the sacred edifice by the diligent piety of prudent judgment; by whose protection the right hand of Imperial power is strengthened, and when they are bound together by the kindness of a greater mutual favour, the benefits of a much richer peace and tranquillity flow happily to the Christian people. Therefore, so that among the venerable Archbishops of Mainz, Cologne and likewise Trier, Electoral Princes of the Holy Empire, all the evils of lawsuits and suspicions, which might arise from disputes about the priority or dignity of their seats at the Imperial and royal courts, may be cut off for all future time, and so that they themselves, remaining in a calm state of heart and mind, may be able to meet and deliberate on the affairs of the Holy Empire with united goodwill and a zeal for virtuous affection, for the comfort of the Christian people, having taken counsel with all the Electoral Princes, both ecclesiastical and secular, and by their advice, we decree, and by the fullness of Imperial power we sanction by this edictal law, to remain in force forever, that the aforesaid venerable Archbishops—namely, that of Trier, sitting opposite and in a straight line facing the face of the Emperor; that of Mainz indeed in his diocese and province, and outside his province throughout his German archchancellorship, except the province of Cologne alone; and finally that of Cologne in his diocese and province, and outside his province throughout all Italy and Gaul, on the right side of the Roman Emperor—may and must sit, and in all public Imperial acts, namely judgments, grants of fiefs, and at the banquet tables, as well as in councils and in all other business, for which it happens or will happen that they must meet together to treat matters for Imperial honour or advantage; and we wish this manner of seating, in all the order just expressed above, to extend perpetually to the successors of the aforesaid Archbishops of Cologne, Trier and Mainz, so that at no time whatever may any doubt arise on these points.

units.la: CAP. IV.
units.tr: CHAPTER IV.

units.la: DE PRINCIPIBUS ELECTORIBUS IN communi.
units.tr: CONCERNING THE PRINCE-ELECTORS IN GENERAL.

units.la: STATUIMUS insuper, ut quotiescunque Imperialem curiam ex nunc inantea celebrari contigerit, in qualibet sessione, videlicet tam in consilio, quam in mensa, & locis aliis quibuscunque, ubi Imperatorem, vel Regem Romanorum cum Principibus Electoribus sedere contigerit, a dextro latere Imperatoris vel Regis Romanorum immediate post Archiepiscopum Moguntinensem, vel Coloniensem, illum videlicet, quem tunc temporis pro qualitate locorum, & varietate provinciarum, juxta privilegii sui tenorem, dicto lateri dextro Imperatoris assidere contigerit: Rex Bohemiae (cum sit Princeps coronatus & unctus) primum; & post eum continuo Comes Palatinus Rheni secundum sedendi loca debeant obtinere; ad sinistram vero partem immediate post illum, quem ex praedictis Archiepiscopis in latere sinistro sedere contigerit, primum locum Dux Saxoniae, & post eum Marchio Brandeburgensis alterum obrinebit.
units.tr: We further decree that whenever the Imperial Court shall henceforth be held, at every session, that is, both in council and at table, and in all other places whatsoever where the Emperor or the King of the Romans shall sit with the Prince-Electors, the King of Bohemia (since he is a crowned and anointed Prince) shall obtain the first place of sitting, and immediately after him the Count Palatine of the Rhine the second, on the right side of the Emperor or King of the Romans, immediately after whichever of the aforesaid Archbishops of Mainz or Cologne shall happen to sit at the right side of the Emperor, according to the nature of the places and the variety of the provinces and the terms of his privilege. On the left side, immediately after the one of the aforesaid Archbishops who happens to sit on the left side, the Duke of Saxony shall obtain the first place, and after him the Margrave of Brandenburg the second.

units.la: 1. Caeterum, quotiens & quando deinceps Sacrum vacare continget Imperium, extunc Moguntinensis Archiepiscopus potestatem habebit (sicut potestatem habuisse dignoscitur ab antiquo) caeteros Principes antedictos, suos in dicta electione consortes, litteratorie convocandi.
units.tr: 1. Moreover, as often and whenever hereafter the Holy Empire shall become vacant, the Archbishop of Mainz shall then have the power (as he is known to have had it from of old) of summoning by letter the other aforesaid Princes, his partners in that election.

units.la: 3. Quibus omnibus, seu his, qui potuerint, & voluerint interesse, in electionis termino invicem congregatis, dictus Archiepiscopus Moguntinensis, & non alter, eorundem Coelectorum suorum vota singulariter habebit inquirere, ordine subsequenti.
units.tr: 3. When all of these, or those who are able and willing to be present, have gathered together at the time of the election, the said Archbishop of Mainz, and no other, shall have the power of asking for the votes of his co-electors individually, in the following order.

units.la: 4. Primo quidem interrogabit a Treverensi Archiepiscopo, cui primam vocem competere declaramus, sicut invenimus hactenus competiisse; secundo, a Coloniensi Archiepiscopo, cui competit dignitas, nec non officium Romanorum Regi primum diadema Regium imponendi; tertiò, à Rege Bohemiæ, qui inter Electores Laicos ex Regiæ dignitatis fastigio, jure & merito obtinebit primatiam; quartò, à Comite Palatino Rheni; quintò, à Duce Saxoniæ; sextò, à Marchione Brandenburgensi. horum omnium vota, præmisso jam ordine, dictus Archiepiscopus Moguntinensis perquiret. quo facto, dicti Principes, sui consortes, ipsum vice versa requirent, ut & ipse intentionem suam expromat, & ipsis aperiat votum suum.
units.tr: 4. First, he shall ask the Archbishop of Trier, to whom we declare that the first voice belongs, as we have found it has belonged hitherto; second, the Archbishop of Cologne, to whom belongs the dignity and also the office of placing the first royal crown upon the King of the Romans; third, the King of Bohemia, who among the lay Electors by the eminence of royal dignity shall rightly and deservedly hold the primacy; fourth, the Count Palatine of the Rhine; fifth, the Duke of Saxony; sixth, the Margrave of Brandenburg. The said Archbishop of Mainz shall seek the votes of all these in the order already stated. When this is done, the said Princes, his partners, shall in turn request him to declare his own intention and disclose his vote to them.

units.la: 5. Præterea, in celebratione Imperialis curiæ, Marchio Brandenburgensis aquam lavandis Imperatoris, vel Regis Romanorum, manibus ministrabit; primum vero potum Rex Bohemiæ; quem tamen sub Regali corona juxta privilegiorum Regni sui continentiam, nisi libera voluntate voluerit, non tenebitur ministrare. Comes etiam Palatinus Rheni cibum afferre tenebitur. Dux Saxoniæ Marescballatus officium exercebit, ut solitum est fieri ab antiquo.
units.tr: 5. Furthermore, at the celebration of the Imperial Court, the Margrave of Brandenburg shall supply water for washing the hands of the Emperor or King of the Romans; and the King of Bohemia shall give the first drink, which, however, he shall not be bound to serve, unless he wishes to do so of his own free will, under the royal crown, in accordance with the contents of the privileges of his kingdom. The Count Palatine of the Rhine shall be bound to bring the food. The Duke of Saxony shall exercise the office of Marshal, as has been the custom from of old.

units.la: CAPUT V. De Iure Comitis Palatini Rheni, et etiam Saxoniæ Ducis.
units.tr: CHAPTER V. On the Right of the Count Palatine of the Rhine, and also of the Duke of Saxony.

units.la: Quotiens insuper, ut præmittitur, Sacrum vacare contingit Imperium, Illustris Comes Palatinus Rheni, Sacri Imperii Archidapifer, ad manus faturi Regis Romanorum in partibus Rheni, & Sueviæ, & in jure Franconico, ratione Principatus, seu Comitatus Palatini privilegio, etiam debet Provisor ipsius Imperii, cum potestate judicia exercendi, ad beneficia Ecclesiastica præsentandi, recolligendi redditus & proventus, & investiendi de feudis, juramenta fidelitatis vice & nomine Sacri Imperii recipiendi; quæ tamen per Regem Romanorum postea electum, suo tempore omnia innovari, & de novo sibi ipsi juramenta præstari debebunt: feudis Principum dūtaxat exceptis, & illis quæ Vanlehen vulgariter appellantur, quorum investituram, & collationem soli Imperatori, vel Regi Romanorum, specialiter reservamus. Ipse tamen Comes Palatinus omne genus alienationis seu obligationis rerum Imperialium, hujusmodi provisionis tempore, expresse sibi noverit interdictam.
units.tr: Whenever, moreover, as has been premised, the Holy Empire happens to be vacant, the Illustrious Count Palatine of the Rhine, Archdapifer of the Holy Empire, who is to attend the table of the King of the Romans in the regions of the Rhine and Swabia and under Franconian law, by reason of his principality or county palatine and by privilege, must also be Provisor of the same Empire, with power to exercise judgments, to present to ecclesiastical benefices, to collect rents and revenues, and to invest with fiefs, and to receive oaths of fealty in the place and name of the Holy Empire. All of these, however, shall have to be renewed in their proper time by the King of the Romans afterwards elected, and new oaths sworn to him, except the fiefs of princes only, and those which are commonly called Vanlehen, whose investiture and conferral we specially reserve to the Emperor alone, or to the King of the Romans. The Count Palatine himself, however, shall be expressly aware that every kind of alienation or pledging of imperial property is forbidden to him during this provision.

units.la: 2. Et eodem jure provisionis, Illustrem Ducem Saxoniæ, Sacri Imperii Archimarescballum, frui volumus in illis locis, ubi Saxonica jura servantur, sub omnibus modis & conditionibus licut superius est expressum.
units.tr: 2. And by the same right of provision, we wish the Illustrious Duke of Saxony, Archmarshal of the Holy Empire, to enjoy it in those places where Saxon law is observed, under all the modes and conditions expressed above.

units.la: 3. Et quamvis Imperator, sive Rex Romanorum, super causis, pro quibus impetitus fuerit, habeat (sicut ex consuetudine introductum dicitur) coram Comite Palatino Rheni, Sacri Imperii Archidapifero, Electore Principe, respondere; illud tamen judicium Comes ipse Palatinus nō alibi, præterquam in Imperiali curia, ubi Imperator, seu Romanorum Rex præsens extiterit, poterit exercere.
units.tr: 3. And although the Emperor, or the King of the Romans, may (as is said to have been introduced by custom) answer before the Count Palatine of the Rhine, Archdapifer of the Holy Empire, an Elector Prince, concerning the causes for which he has been impleaded, nevertheless the Count Palatine himself may exercise that judgment nowhere else than in the Imperial court, where the Emperor or the King of the Romans is present.

units.la: CAPUT VI. De Comparatione Principum Electo- rum ad alios Principes communes.
units.tr: CHAPTER VI. On the Comparison of the Electoral Princes with Other Common Princes.

units.la: Decernimus, ut in celebratione Imperialis curiæ, quotienscunque illā deinceps perpetuò celebrari contigerit, antedicti Principes Electores, Ecclesiastici & Seculares, juxta præscriptū ordinem atque modum, à dextris & sinistris immutabiliter teneant loca sua; eisque, vel eorum alteri, in quibuscunque actibus ad curiā ipsam spectantibus eundo, sedendo, vel stando, nullus Principalius, cujuscunque status, dignitatis, præeminentiæ, vel conditionis existat, ullatenus præferatur; expressè, quod nominatim Rex Bohemiæ in celebratione curiarum hujusmodi, in omnibus singulis actibus antedictis, quemcunque Regem alium, quacunque etiam singulari dignitatis prærogativa fulgentem, quovis casu seu causa venire, vel adesse forte contingeret, immutabiliter antecedat.
units.tr: We decree that at the holding of the Imperial Diet, whenever it shall happen to be held continually from now on, the aforesaid Electoral Princes, both ecclesiastical and secular, shall hold their places unchangeably at the right and left, according to the prescribed order and manner; and that no Prince, of whatever rank, dignity, pre-eminence or condition he may be, shall in any way be placed before them or either of them, in any acts pertaining to the Diet, whether walking, sitting or standing. Expressly, the King of Bohemia, in the holding of such Diets, shall unchangeably precede in all and each of the aforesaid acts any other King whatever, even one shining with some singular prerogative of dignity, should he happen to come or be present for any reason or cause.

units.la: CAPUT VII. De Successione Principum Electorum.
units.tr: CHAPTER VII. On the Succession of the Electoral Princes.

units.la: In nomine sanctæ & individuæ Trinitatis feliciter, Amen.
units.tr: In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, happily. Amen.

units.la: Carolus Quartus divina favente clementia, Romanorum Imperator, semper-Augustus, & Bohemiæ Rex, ad perpetuam rei memoriam.
units.tr: Charles IV, by the favour of divine clemency, Roman Emperor, ever August, and King of Bohemia, to the perpetual memory of the matter.

units.la: Inter solicitudines illas innumeras, quibus pro felici statu Sacri Imperii, cui auctore Domino feliciter præsidemus, cor nostrum quotidie fatigatur, ad hoc præcipue meditatio nostra dirigitur, qualiter desiderata & salubris semper unio inter Sacri Imperii Principes Electores jugiter vigeat, & corda eorum in sincerae charitatis concordia conservantur, quorum providentia suo tempore orbi fluctuanti, tanto celerius, tantoque facilius subveniretur, quanto inter eos nullus error surrepserit, & pumer fuerit charitas custodita, obscuritate suscisa, & jure cujuslibet dilucidè declarato. Sane generaliter longe lateque est publicum, & quasi per totum orbem notorie manifestum, Illustres, Regem Bohemiæ, nec non Comitem Palatinum Rheni, Ducem Saxoniæ, & Marchionem Brandenburgensem, vt Regni & Principatuum suorum, in electione Regis Romanorum in Cæsarem promovendi, cæteris Principibus Ecclesiasticis suis Coelectoribus, jus, vocem, & locum habere, & unà cum ipsis esse veros & legitimos Sacri Imperii Principes Electores.
units.tr: Among those countless anxieties by which our heart is daily wearied for the happy state of the Holy Empire, over which, with the Lord as author, we preside happily, our thought is directed chiefly to this: how the desired and always wholesome unity among the Electoral Princes of the Holy Empire may continually flourish, and how their hearts may be preserved in the concord of sincere charity. Through their foresight the wavering world would be helped all the sooner and all the more easily, the more no error has crept in between them, and charity has been kept whole, obscurity removed, and the right of anyone clearly declared. Indeed, it is public far and wide throughout the whole world, and almost notoriously manifest everywhere, that the illustrious King of Bohemia, as well as the Count Palatine of the Rhine, the Duke of Saxony and the Margrave of Brandenburg, have, for the election of a King of the Romans to be promoted to Caesar, in the name of their kingdoms and principalities, the right, the voice and the place alongside the other ecclesiastical Princes, their co-electors, and that together with them they are the true and lawful Electoral Princes of the Holy Empire.

units.la: 2. Ne inter eorundem Principum seculariū Electorum filios, super jure, voce, & potestate prædicta, futuris temporibus, scandalorum & dissensionum possit materia suscitari, & sic bonum commune periculosis dilationibus impediri, futuris auctore Deo cupientes periculis salubriter obviam.
units.tr: 2. So that in future times no matter for scandals and dissensions may be stirred up among the sons of these same secular Electoral Princes concerning the aforesaid right, voice and power, and so the common good be hindered by dangerous delays, we desire, with God as author, to meet future perils wholesomely.

units.la: 3. Statuimus & Imperiali auctoritate, præsenti lege perpetuis temporibus valitura, decernimus, ut postquam iidem Principes Electores Seculares, & eorum quilibet, esse desierit, jus, vox, & potestas electionis hujusmodi ad filium suum primogenitum, legitimum, laicum; illo vero non existente, ad ejusdem primogeniti primogenitum, similiter laicum, libere & sine contradictione, cujus pertinet devolvatur.
units.tr: 3. We decree, and by imperial authority, by this present law which shall hold force for perpetual times, we ordain that after these same secular Electoral Princes, or any one of them, shall have ceased to live, the right, voice and power of such election shall devolve freely and without contradiction upon his firstborn legitimate lay son; and if he does not exist, upon the firstborn, likewise lay, of that same firstborn, to whom it belongs.

units.la: 4. Si vero primogenitus hujusmodi absque hæredibus masculis, legitimis, laicis, ab hac luce migraret, virtute præsentis Imperialis edicti, jus, vox, & potestas electionis prædictæ, ad seniorem fratrem laicum per veram paternalem lineam descendentem, & deinceps ad illius primogenitum laicum devolvatur.
units.tr: 4. If, however, such a firstborn should depart from this light without legitimate lay male heirs, then by virtue of the present imperial edict, the right, voice and power of the aforesaid election shall devolve upon the elder lay brother descended in the true paternal line, and thereafter upon that brother's firstborn lay son.

units.la: 5. Et talis successio in primogenitis, & hæredibus Principum eorundem, in jure, voce, & potestate præmissis, perpetuis temporibus observetur.
units.tr: 5. And such succession among the firstborn and heirs of these same Princes, in the aforesaid right, voice and power, shall be observed in perpetual times.

units.la: 6. Ea tamen conditione & modo, ut si Principem Electorem, seu ejus primogenitum seniorem laicum, mori, & hæredes masculos, legitimos, laicos, defectum ætatis patientes, quere contigerit, tunc frater senior ejusdem primogeniti, tutor eorum & administrator existat, & senior ex eis legitimam ætatem attigerit, quam in Principe Elector decem & octo annos complere censeri volumus, & statuimus perpetuò haberi; quam dum attigerit, jus, vocem, & potestatem, omnia ab ipsis dependentia, tutor ipse sibi totaliter cum officio teneatur protinus assignare.
units.tr: 6. On this condition and in this manner, however: if it should happen that the Electoral Prince, or his elder lay firstborn, dies and his legitimate lay male heirs are left under age, then the elder brother of that firstborn shall be their guardian and administrator; and when the elder of them has reached legitimate age, which we wish to be considered, and decree to be held forever, as eighteen years for an Electoral Prince, the guardian himself shall be bound at once to assign to him wholly, together with the office, all the right, voice and power dependent upon them.

units.la: 7. Si vero aliquem ex hujusmodi Principibus ipsorum Imperio Sacro vacare contingeret, tunc Imperator, seu Rex Romanorum, qui pro tempore fuerit, de ipso providere debebit & potest, tamquam de re ad se & Imperium legitime devoluta.
units.tr: 7. If, however, any of these Princes should happen to fall vacant from the Holy Empire, then the Emperor, or the King of the Romans who shall be in office at the time, ought and may provide concerning it, as concerning a matter legitimately devolved upon himself and the Empire.

units.la: 8. Salvis tamen semper privilegiis, juribus, & consuetudinibus Regni nostri Bohemiæ super electione Regis in casu vacationis per regnicolas, qui jus habent eligendi Regem Bohemiæ, juxta continentiam eorundem privilegiorum, & observatam consuetudinem diuturnam, à diversis Romanorum Imperatoribus, sive Regibus, obtentorum, quibus ex hujusmodi sanctione Imperiali nullo præjudicari volumus; imò, ipsa decernimus nunc & perpetuis futuris temporibus in omni suo tenore & forma, indubiam tenere roboris firmitatem.
units.tr: 8. Saving always the privileges, rights and customs of our Kingdom of Bohemia concerning the election of a King in the case of a vacancy by the inhabitants of the kingdom, who have the right to elect the King of Bohemia, according to the content of those same privileges and the long-observed custom, obtained from various Emperors or Kings of the Romans; by this imperial sanction we wish them in no way prejudiced; indeed, we decree that they now and for all future time keep, in their whole tenor and form, an undoubted firmness of strength.

units.la: CAP. VIII.
units.tr: CHAPTER VIII.

units.la: DE REGIS BOHEMIAE ET REGNICOLARVM ejus immunitate.
units.tr: CONCERNING THE IMMUNITY OF THE KING OF BOHEMIA AND OF HIS SUBJECTS.

units.la: CUm per divos Romanorum Imperatores, & Reges, prædecessores nostros, illustribus Bohemiæ Regibus, progenitoribus & prædecessoribus nostris, necnon Regno Bohemiæ, ejusque Regni coronæ, olim concessum fuerit gratiosius & indultum, siquè in Regno eodem tempore cujus contrarin hodie non existit memoria, consuetudine laudabili, inconvulsa servata, diuturnitate temporum, & præscripta moribus utentium, sine contradictionis aut interruptionis culo introductum, quod nullus Princeps, Baro, Nobilis, Miles, Cliens, Civis, Burgensis, seu Rusticus, nulla denique persona ejusdem regni, & pertinentiarum ejusdem ubicumque existentium, cujuscumque status, dignitatis, præeminentiæ, vel conditionis existat, ad cujuscumque actoris instantiam, extra Regnum ipsum ad quodcumque tribunal, seu alterius, præterquam Regis Bohemiæ, & Judicium Regalis curiæ suæ judicium citari potuerit, sive trahi, nec vocari debeat perpetuis inantea temporibus possit. ideoque privilegium, consuetudinem, & indultum hujusmodi, auctoritate Imperiali, & de Imperii potestatis plenitudine, ex certa scientia innovantes, & etiam confirmantes, hac præsenti nostra constitutione Imperiali perpetuis temporibus valitura statuimus, ut si contra privilegium, consuetudinem vel indultum prænotatum quispiam prædictorum, puta Princeps, Baro, Nobilis, Miles, Cliens, Civis, Burgensis, seu Rusticus, aut alia quæcumque persona prætermissa, ad cujuscumque tribunal extra Regnum prædictum Bohemiæ, in quacumque causa, criminali, civili, vel mixta, seu super quocumque negotio citatus fuerit, quocumque tempore, vel citata, comparere, vel in judicio respondere minime teneatur. quòd si adversus hujusmodi non comparentes, vel non comparentem, à quocumque judice, cujuscumque auctoritatis existat, extra Regnum ipsum Bohemiæ constituto, judicialiter procedi, seu sententias interlocutorias vel definitivas, unam vel plures, in quibuscumque nominatis causis sive negotiis, quovis modo fieri vel promulgari contingeret, auctoritate præmissa, de plenitudine insuper antedictæ Imperatoriæ potestatis, citationes, præcepta, processus, & sententias hujusmodi, necnon executiones, & omnia quæ ex eis, vel aliquo eorum, quomodolibet sequi, attentari, ptari possent vel fieri, irritamus penitus & cassamus.
units.tr: Since the deified Roman Emperors and Kings, our predecessors, long ago granted and indulged to the illustrious Kings of Bohemia, our forefathers and predecessors, and to the Kingdom of Bohemia and the crown of that kingdom, a favour and privilege, and since it was introduced in that kingdom at a time whose contrary no one now remembers, kept by a laudable custom that has never been shaken, established by the length of time and prescribed by the habits of those who use it, without any challenge or interruption, that no prince, baron, noble, knight, client, citizen, burgher or peasant, indeed no person of that kingdom and its dependencies, wherever they may be, of whatever rank, dignity, pre-eminence or condition, may be cited, summoned or called at the suit of any plaintiff outside the kingdom itself, before any tribunal or court other than that of the King of Bohemia and the judgment of his royal court, for all future time: therefore, by Imperial authority and from the fullness of Imperial power, with certain knowledge, renewing and also confirming this privilege, custom and indult, we decree by this present Imperial constitution, to remain valid in perpetuity, that if any of the aforesaid persons, namely a prince, baron, noble, knight, client, citizen, burgher or peasant, or any other person not mentioned, is cited at any time, in any cause, criminal, civil or mixed, or upon any business whatever, before any tribunal outside the said Kingdom of Bohemia, contrary to this privilege, custom or indult, he is not bound to appear or to answer in court. And if any judge, of whatever authority, sitting outside the said Kingdom of Bohemia, should proceed judicially against such a person who does not appear, or against a person not appearing, or should happen to make or pronounce in any way one or more interlocutory or definitive sentences in any named causes or business, then by the authority aforesaid, and moreover by the fullness of the aforesaid Imperial power, we utterly annul and quash those citations, orders, processes and sentences, as well as the executions, and everything that could or might be attempted or done in consequence of them, or of any of them, in any way.

units.la: 2. Adiect 2. Adjicientes expresse, & edicto Imperiali perpetuò valituro, eadem auctoritate, & de praemissæ potestatis plenitudine decernentes, ut quemadmodum in prædicto Regno Bohemiæ, à tempore, cuius contrarii non haberur memoria, jugiter observatum existit, ita nulli prorsus Principi, Baroni, Nobili, Militi, Clienti, Civi, Burgensi, seu Rustico, nulli demum personæ, seu incolæ Regni Bohemiæ supra dicti, cujuscumque status, prærominentiæ, dignitatis, vel conditionis existant, vel existat, à quibuscumque processibus, sententiis interlocutoriis vel diffinitivis, sive præceptis Regis Bohemiæ, aut quorumlibet suorum judicum, nec non executionibus eorundem, contra se in Regali judicio, seu coram Regis, Regni, seu prædictorum Judicum tribunalibus factis aut latis, habitis vel ferendis manenteque seu fixis, liceat ad quodcumque aliud judicium appellare. provocationes quoque seu appellationes huiusmodi, si quas contra hoc interponi contigerit, eo ipso viribus non subsistant, & appellantes ipsi poenam perditionis causarum ipso facto se noverint incurrisse.
units.tr: 2. Adding expressly, and by this Imperial edict, which is to remain valid in perpetuity, decreeing by the same authority and from the fullness of the aforesaid power, that just as it has been continuously observed in the said Kingdom of Bohemia from a time whose contrary is not remembered, so no prince, baron, noble, knight, client, citizen, burgher or peasant, and finally no person or inhabitant of the aforesaid Kingdom of Bohemia, of whatever rank, pre-eminence, dignity or condition they are or may be, shall be permitted to appeal to any other tribunal against any proceedings, interlocutory or definitive sentences, or orders of the King of Bohemia, or of any of his judges, or against executions of the same, made or pronounced against them in the royal court, or before the tribunals of the King, the kingdom, or the aforesaid judges, whether already made or pronounced, or still to be held, or remaining and fixed. Likewise, any appeals or provocations of this kind, if any should happen to be lodged against this, shall by that very fact have no force, and the appellants shall know that they have by the same fact incurred the penalty of losing their cases.

units.la: CAP. IX.
units.tr: Chapter IX.

units.la: DE AVRI, ARGENTI, ET ALIARVM specierum mineris.
units.tr: Concerning gold, silver, and the mines of other kinds of metal.

units.la: PRÆSENTI constitutione in perpetuum valitura statuimus, ac de certa scientia declaramus, quòd successores nostri Bohemiæ Reges, nec non universi & singuli Principes Electores, Ecclesiastici & Seculares, qui perpetuò fuerint, universas auri & argenti fodinas, atque mineras stanni, cupri, ferri, plumbi, & alterius cujuscumque generis metalli, ac etiam salis, tam inventas quàm etiam inveniendas in posterum quibuscumque temporibus, in Regno prædicto, ac terris & pertinentiis eidem Regno subiectis, nec non supradicti Principes in Principatibus, terris, dominiis, & pertinentiis suis, tenere juste possint et legitimè possidere, cum omnibus juribus (nullo prorsus excepto) prout possunt seu consueverunt talia possideri; nec non Judæos habere; theloneam præterito statuta & indicta percipere; quodque progenitores nostri, Reges Bohemiæ felicis memoriæ, ipsiique Principes Electores, ac progenitores & prædecessores eorum, legitimè potuerint usque in præsens, sicut hoc antiqua, laudabili, & approbata consuetudine, diuturnoque ac longissimi temporis curriu præscripta noscitur observatum.
units.tr: By this constitution, to be valid in perpetuity, we decree and, from certain knowledge, declare that our successors as kings of Bohemia, and all and each of the Electors, ecclesiastical and secular, who shall ever exist, may justly hold and lawfully possess all the gold and silver mines and the mines of tin, copper, iron, lead, and of every other kind of metal, and also of salt, both those already discovered and those to be discovered at any time in future, in the aforesaid kingdom and in the lands and dependencies subject to that kingdom; and likewise the aforesaid Princes in their principalities, lands, domains and dependencies; and may have Jews; and may levy tolls, and moreover the customary and imposed dues; and that our forebears, the kings of Bohemia of happy memory, and those same Electors, together with their forebears and predecessors, have been able to do these things lawfully up to the present, as this is known to have been observed by ancient, praiseworthy and approved custom, and sanctioned by the long course of a very lengthy time.

units.la: CAP. X.
units.tr: CHAPTER X.

units.la: DE MONETIS.
units.tr: CONCERNING COINAGE.

units.la: STATUIMUS præterea, ut Regi Bohemiæ, successori nostro, qui fuerit pro tempore, sicut constat ab antiquo Illustris memoriæ Bohemiæ Regibus, nostris prædecessoribus, licuisse, & in possessione pacifica continua ipsos fuisse juris sub sequentibus, videlicet monetas auri & argenti, in omni loco & parte Regni sui, & subditarum ei terrarum & pertinentiarum omnium, ubi Rex ipse decreverit, ubique placuerit, cudi facere, & mandare, sub omni modo & forma, in Regno ipso Bohemiæ, in his ad hæc utique tempora observatis, quòdque futuris perpetuò Bohemiæ Regibus, hac nostra Imperiali constitutione & gratia perpetuò valituris, à quibuscumque Principibus, Magnatibus, Comitibus, ac aliis, quaecumque terras, castra, possessiones, prædia, sive bona, liceat emere, comparare, seu donum vel donationem, ex quacumque causa, aut in obligationem recipere, sub talium terrarum, castrorum, possessionum, prædiorum, seu bonorum conditione consueta, ut videlicet propria recipiunt vel comparentur ut propria, libera velut libera, & ea quæ dependent in feudum, similiter emanfeudum, seu comparata taliter teneantur; ita tamen, quòd ipsi Reges Bohemiæ, de iis, quæ hoc comparaverint vel receperint, & Regno Bohemiæ duxerint applicanda, ad pristina ac consueta talibus sacro explenda & reddenda Imperio sint astricti.
units.tr: We further decree that the King of Bohemia, our successor who shall be for the time being, as it is established from of old that the illustrious kings of Bohemia, our predecessors, were permitted, and had been in continuous peaceful possession, of the following right: to have gold and silver coins struck and minted, in every place and part of his kingdom and of all the lands and appurtenances subject to him, wherever the King himself shall decide and wherever it shall please him, in any manner and form, within the Kingdom of Bohemia itself, as observed in these times up to the present; and that future kings of Bohemia, by this our Imperial constitution and grace which shall remain in force forever, may be permitted to buy, acquire, or receive as a gift or donation, for whatever cause, or to take in pledge, from any princes, magnates, counts, or others, whatever lands, castles, possessions, estates, or goods, under the customary condition of such lands, castles, possessions, estates, or goods: namely, that they are received or acquired as their own, free as free property, and that those which depend upon them as fiefs are likewise held as fiefs, or as acquired in the same way; provided, however, that the Kings of Bohemia themselves are bound to apply and restore to the sacred uses and to the Empire, in the customary manner, whatever they shall have acquired or received in this way and have decided to apply to the Kingdom of Bohemia.

units.la: 2. Præsentem nihilominus constitutionem & gratiam, virtute præsentis legis nostræ Imperiales universos Principes Electores, tam Ecclesiasticos quam Seculares, successores & legitimos hæredes ... plene extendi volumus, sub omnibus modis & conditionibus, ut præfertur.
units.tr: 2. We wish that the present constitution and grace, by virtue of this our present Imperial law, be fully extended to all the Electors-Prince, both ecclesiastical and secular, their successors and lawful heirs ... under all the modes and conditions, as stated above.

units.la: CAP. XI.
units.tr: CHAPTER XI.

units.la: DE IMMVNITATE PRINCIPVM ELECTORVM.
units.tr: ON THE IMMUNITY OF THE ELECTORAL PRINCES.

units.la: STATUIMUS etiam, ut nulli Comites, Barones, Nobiles, Feudales, Vasalli, Castrenses, Milites, Clientes, Cives, Burgenses, nullæ quoque personæ, Coloniensi, Moguntinensi & Treverensi, Ecclesiis subjecti vel subjectæ, cujuscumque status, conditionis, vel dignitatis existant, ad cujuscumque actoris instantiam extra terri torium, & terminos a limites earundem Ecclesiarum, & pertinentiarum suarum, ad quodcumque aliud tribunal, seu cujuscumque alterius, præterquàm Archiepiscopum Moguntinensis, Treverensis, & Coloniensis, & Judicum suorum judicium citari poterint potibus retroactis, vel trahi seu vocari debeant perpetuis inantea temporibus sive possint, sicut in praeteritis temporibus observatum.
units.tr: We also decree that no counts, barons, nobles, feudal tenants, vassals, castle-dwellers, knights, clients, citizens or burghers, and no persons at all, of whatever estate, condition or dignity, who are subject to the churches of Cologne, Mainz and Trier, whether men or women, may be cited outside the territory and boundaries of these churches and their dependencies, at the suit of any plaintiff, before any tribunal other than that of the archbishops of Mainz, Trier and Cologne and their judges. Nor shall they be dragged or summoned in this way, either in past times or in perpetuity henceforth, or be able to be, as has been observed in past times.

units.la: 1. Quod si contra praesiens edictum nostrum, prædictos Ecclesiarum Trevetensis, Moguntinensis, seu Coloniensis subditos, vel eorum aliquem seu aliquos, ad cujuscumque instantiam, seu ad cujuscumq; tribunal, pro quacumq; causa criminali, civili, vel mixta, seu quocumq; negotio, extra territorium, limites seu terminos dictarum Ecclesiarum, vel alicujus earum citari contingeret, comparere vel respondere minimè teneantur; & citatio, & processus, & sententiæ interlocutoriæ vel diffinitivæ contra non venientes à talibus judicibus extraneis latæ vel factæ, fiendæ vel ferendæ, necnon praecepta, & præmissorum executiones, & omnia quæ ex eis, vel aliquo eorum quomodolibet sequi, attentari poterunt vel fieri, irrita decernimus eo ipso.
units.tr: 1. But if, contrary to this present edict of ours, the subjects of the churches of Trier, Mainz or Cologne, or any one or more of them, should be cited, at the suit of anyone and before any tribunal whatever, for any criminal, civil or mixed cause, or any business at all, outside the territory, limits or boundaries of the said churches or of any of them, they are not bound to appear or to answer. We decree that the citation, the proceedings, and the interlocutory and final sentences issued or made against those who do not appear by such foreign judges, whether already made, to be made or to be pronounced, as well as the orders and executions of these, and everything that may be attempted or done as a consequence of them in any way, are void by that very fact.

units.la: 3. Adjicientes expresse, quòd nulli Comiti, Baroni, Nobili, Feudali, Vasallo, Castrensi, Militi, Clienti, Civi, Rustico, nulli demum personæ Ecclesiis hujusmodi subjectæ, seu ejus incolæ, cujuscunque status, dignitatis, vel conditionis existant, à processibus, sententiis interlocutoriis & diffinitivis sive præceptis Archiepiscoporum & Ecclesiarum hujusmodi, vel suorum Officiatorum temporalium aut executionibus earundem contra se in Archiepiscopali, seu Officiatorum prædictorum judicio citatis aut latis, habitis vel ferendis inantea seu fiendis, ad quodcunque tribunal aliud licet appellare, quamdiu in Archiepiscoporum prædictorum, & suorum judicio querulantibus non fuerit justitia denegata: appellationes contra hoc factas non recipi statuimus, cassalsque & irritas nuncriamus.
units.tr: 3. We add expressly that no count, baron, noble, feudal tenant, vassal, castellan, knight, client, citizen, peasant, and finally no person subject to such churches or their inhabitants, of whatever status, dignity or condition, may appeal to any other tribunal from the proceedings, interlocutory and final sentences, or orders of such archbishops and churches or of their secular officials, or from the executions of these, whether cited or pronounced against them in the court of the archbishops or of the aforesaid officials, whether held, to be held or to be made in future, for as long as justice has not been denied to those complaining before the aforesaid archbishops and their court. We decree that appeals made against this are not to be received, and we declare them quashed and void.

units.la: 4. In defectum vero justitiæ, prædictis omnibus ad Imperialem dumtaxat curiam & tribunal seu Judicis immediatè in Imperiali curia pro tempore Præsidentis audientiam; & etiam eo casu nemo ad quemvis alium judicem, sive ordinarium, sive etiam delegatum, his, quibus denegata fuerit justitia, recurrere appellare. Quicquid vero contra præmissa factum fuerit, sit irritum eo ipso.
units.tr: 4. But in default of justice, all the aforesaid matters are to be referred solely to the imperial court and to the tribunal or hearing of the judge who is at the time President of the imperial court. And even in that case no one, to whom justice has been denied, may have recourse or appeal to any other judge, whether ordinary or delegated. Whatever is done contrary to the above shall be void by that very fact.

units.la: 5. Eandem constitutionem virtute præsentis legis nostræ Imperialis, ad Illustres Comites Palatinum Rheni, Ducem Saxoniæ & Marchionem Brandenburgensem, Principes Electores sive laicos, successores, hæredes, & subditos eorum, plenè extendi volumus, sub omnibus conditionibus, ut præfertur.
units.tr: 5. By virtue of this our imperial law, we wish this same constitution to be fully extended to the illustrious Counts Palatine of the Rhine, the Duke of Saxony and the Margrave of Brandenburg, the lay prince-electors, and to their successors, heirs and subjects, under all the conditions stated above.

units.la: CAP. XII.
units.tr: CAP. XII.

units.la: DE CONGREGATIONE PRINCIPVM ELECTORVM.
units.tr: CONCERNING THE CONGREGATION OF THE PRINCE-ELECTORS.

units.la: In nomine sanctæ & individuæ Trinitatis feliciter, Amen.
units.tr: In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, happily, Amen.

units.la: Carolus Quartus divina favente clementia, Romanorum Imperator, semper-Augustus, & Bohemiæ Rex, ad perpetuam rei memoriam.
units.tr: Charles IV, by the favour of divine clemency, Roman Emperor, ever Augustus, and King of Bohemia, to the perpetual memory of the matter.

units.la: INTER illas multiplices Reipublicæ curas, quibus assiduè mens nostra distrahitur, multa consideratione necessarium fore prospexit nostra sublimitas, ut Sacri Imperii Principes Electores, ad tractandum de ipsius Imperii orbisque salute, frequentius solito congregentur, qui solidæ bases Imperii, & columnæ immobiles, quemadmodum per longinquas ad invicem terrarum constitutas distantias, ita de incumbentibus regionum sibi cognitarum defectibus referre simul & conferre noverunt, animisque providentiæ suæ consiliis non ignorant accommodatis talium reformationibus salubriter operam dare.
units.tr: AMID those manifold cares of the Commonwealth by which our mind is constantly distracted, our Majesty has foreseen that it will be necessary, after much consideration, for the Princes-Electors of the Holy Empire to gather more often than usual to deal with the safety of the Empire and of the world. They are the solid foundations and immovable pillars of the Empire, and, since they are set at great distances from one another, they know how to report to and confer with one another on the defects that afflict the regions known to them, and, with minds well adapted to the counsels of their foresight, they know how to apply themselves usefully to such reforms.

units.la: 2. Hinc est, quod in solemni curia nostra in Nuremberg, cum Venerabilibus Ecclesiasticis & Illustribus secularibus Principibus Electoribus, & multis aliis Principibus & Proceribus, per nos Celsitudinem celebrata, habita cum eisdem Principibus Electoribus deliberatione, & de ipsorum consilio, pro bono & salute communi, cum dictis Principibus Electoribus, tam Ecclesiasticis quam secularibus, duximus ordinandum, quòd iidem Principes Electores de cetero per singulos annos in mel, transactis à festo Paschæ Resurrectionis Dominicæ quatuor septimanis continuè numerandis, aliqua civitatum Sacri Imperii personaliter congregentur, & ad idem tempus proxime affuturum anno præsenti, colloquium seu curia, & congregatio hujusmodi, in civitate nostra Imperiali Metensi per nos & eosdem Principes celebretur; ac tunc, & deinceps, die quolibet congregationis hujusmodi locus per nos, quo sequenti anno conveniant, ipsorum consilio statuatur, hac nostra ordinatione, ad nostrum & ipsorum dumtaxat beneplacitum duratura. qua durante, ipsos sub nostro Imperiali conductu recipimus, ad dictam curiam accedendo, stando, ac etiam recedendo.
units.tr: 2. Hence it is that, in our solemn court at Nuremberg, celebrated by us in person with the venerable ecclesiastical and illustrious secular Princes-Electors and many other Princes and nobles, after deliberation held with the same Princes-Electors and by their counsel, we have judged it right to ordain, for the common good and safety, together with the said Princes-Electors, both ecclesiastical and secular, that the same Princes-Electors shall henceforth gather in person each year in some city of the Empire in the month of May, beginning four weeks after the feast of the Lord's Resurrection; and that the colloquy or court and gathering of this kind, due to be held in the coming year in our Imperial city of Metz, shall be celebrated by us and the same Princes; and that then and thereafter, on each day of such a gathering, the place where they are to meet in the following year shall be fixed by us with their counsel. This our ordinance is to last only at our pleasure and theirs. While it lasts, we receive them under our Imperial safe-conduct, both in coming to the said court, in staying there, and in leaving.

units.la: 3. Præterea, ne tractatus communis salutis & pacis, per tractum & moram solatu, seu excessivam frequentationem conviviorum retardetur, ut aliquando fieri est consuetum, concordi voluntate maximus ordinandum, ut deinceps curia seu congregatione præfata durante, generales omnium Principum celebrate alicui non liceat invitatas; particulares verò, quæ agendorum expeditionem non impediant, cum moderamine sint permissæ.
units.tr: 3. Furthermore, lest the business of the common safety and peace be delayed by the protraction and delay of leisure, or by the excessive frequenting of banquets, as has sometimes been the custom, we have with one accord most fittingly ordained that, while the aforesaid court or gathering lasts, general invitations of all the Princes shall not be permitted to be held; but private ones, which do not hinder the despatch of business, shall be allowed in moderation.

units.la: CAP. XIII.
units.tr: CAP. XIII.

units.la: DE REVOCATIONE PRIVILEGIORVM.
units.tr: ON THE REVOCATION OF PRIVILEGES.

units.la: PRÆTEREA statuimus, & hoc Imperiali perpetuo sancimus edicto, quòd universa privilegia, litteræ, quibuscunque personis, cujuscunque status, præeminentiæ, vel dignitatis existant, civitatum, oppidorum, & quorumlibet locorum universitatibus, super quibuscunque junctis gratiis, immunitatibus, consuetudinibus, seu rebus aliis, etiam proprio motu, seu alias à nobis, vel à colendæ memoriæ divis Romanorum Imperatoribus, & Regibus, prædecessoribus nostris, sub quibuscumbuscumque verborum tenoribus concessa & concessæ, seu à nobis vel successoribus nostris Romanorum Imperatoribus & Regibus, inantea futuris temporibus concedenda seu concedendæ,non debeant aut possint libertatibus, jurisdictionibus, juribus, & honoribus, seu dominiis Principum Electorum Sacri Imperij, Ecclesiasticorum & Secularium, aut alicujus ipsorum in aliquo penitus derogare; etiam si in talibus privilegijs & litteris quarumlibet personarum cujuscunque præeminentiæ, dignitatis, aut status exiterint,ut præfertur,seu universitatum hujusmodi expresse cautum sit, vel fuerit in suturum, quòd revocabilia seu revocabiles esse non debeant, nisi de ipsis, & toto in eis comprehenso tenore in tali revocatione fieret de verbo ad verbum seriatim mentio specialis. hujusmodi namque privilegia & litteras, si & inquantum libertatibus, jurisdictionibus, juribus ,honoribus, seu dominus dictorum Principum Electorum, aut alicujus ipsorum derogare, vel obviare censentur in aliquo, quo ad hoc revocamus ex certa scientia & cassamus,revocaque & revocatas intelligi,reputari , & haberi decernimus de plenitudine Imperatoriæ potestatis.
units.tr: Furthermore, we decree, and by this perpetual Imperial edict we sanction, that all privileges and letters, granted or to be granted, whether by us or by the Roman Emperors and Kings our predecessors of revered memory, or by us or our successors the Roman Emperors and Kings in future times, to whatever persons of whatever rank, pre-eminence or dignity they may be, and to the corporate bodies of cities, towns and any other places, concerning whatever joined graces, immunities, customs or other matters, whether granted of our own accord or otherwise, and under whatever wording they are or shall be expressed, ought not, and may not, in any respect derogate from the liberties, jurisdictions, rights, honours or dominions of the Electors of the Holy Empire, whether ecclesiastical or secular, or of any of them. Even if it has been expressly provided, or shall be provided in future, in such privileges and letters of any persons whatever, of whatever pre-eminence, dignity or rank, as stated above, or of such corporate bodies, that they ought not to be revocable or are not to be revoked, unless specific mention were made in such revocation, word for word and item by item, of the very tenor contained in them, nonetheless, insofar as such privileges and letters are judged to derogate from or obstruct the liberties, jurisdictions, rights, honours or dominions of the said Electors, or of any of them, in any respect, we revoke them for this purpose from certain knowledge and annul them, and by the fullness of Imperial power we decree that they are to be understood, regarded and held as revoked.

units.la: CAP. XIV.
units.tr: CHAP. XIV.

units.la: DE HIS, QVIBVS VT INDIGNIS AVFERVNTVR bona feudalia.
units.tr: CONCERNING THOSE WHO ARE DEPRIVED OF FEUDAL GOODS AS UNWORTHY.

units.la: IN plerisque partibus vasalli,& feudatarij dominorum, feuda seu beneficia, quæ à dominis ipsis obtinent,inempestivè, verbaliter & in fraude renunciant, seu resignât eadé;& facta resignatione hujusmodi, dominos ipsos malitiosè diffidant ,suasque inimicitias eis denunciant,damna eis subsequèter gravia inferendo:& beneficia seu feuda sic relicta prætextu guerræ seu inimicitiæ iterum invadùr, & occupant,& detinent occupata,ea propter præsenti constitutione in perpetuum valituria sancimus, quòd talis resignatio,seu renunciatio haberi debeat pro non facta, nisi liberè & realiter facta fuerit per eoldem, ita quòd possessio beneficiorum & feudorum hujusmodi, dominis ipsis corporaliter & realiter assignetur, in tantum, quòd nullo umquam tempore diffidantes ipsi in bonis, feudis,seu beneficiis resignatis, dominos ipsos perturbent per se, vel alios,aut molestent, nec ad hoc,consilium præstent, auxilium, vel favorem. contrarium faciens, seu dominos suos in beneficiis & feudis resignatis,vel non resignatis invadens quomodolibet vel perturbans, vel damna in ipsis inferens, seu consilium , auxilium præstans talia facientibus, vel favorem,feuda & beneficia hujusmodi eo ipso amittat, infamis existat,& banno Imperiali subjaceat,& nullus ad feuda vel beneficia hujusmodi pateat ei de cætero,quocunque tempore aditus, vel regressus,nec de novo concedi sibi valeant ullo modo;& facta eis contra hoc illorum concessio, seu investitura sequuta, viribus non subsistat. postremò, omnes pœnas prædictas illos vel illum, qui prædicta resignatione non facta, contra dominos suos fraudulenter agentes, vel agens, sciens eos invaserint, vel invaserit, diffidatione quacunque prævia vel obmissa, vigore præsentis sanctionis incurrere decernimus ipso facto.
units.tr: In most regions, vassals and feudatories resign the fiefs or benefices they hold from their lords at the wrong time, merely by word of mouth, and fraudulently. Once such a resignation has been made, they maliciously renounce their fealty to those lords, declare enmity against them, and afterwards inflict serious losses on them. The benefices or fiefs thus given up are then invaded and occupied again under the pretext of war or enmity, and the occupied property is kept. For this reason, by the present constitution, which is to remain valid in perpetuity, we decree that such a resignation or renunciation shall be held as not made, unless it has been made freely and in fact by those same vassals, so that possession of such benefices and fiefs is handed back to the lords bodily and in fact. Moreover, the vassals who have renounced their fealty shall never at any time disturb or molest their lords, in person or through others, in the goods, fiefs or benefices resigned, nor shall they give counsel, aid or favour for doing so.
