Whoever acts contrary to this, or invades or in any way disturbs his lords in fiefs and benefices, whether resigned or not, or inflicts damage on them, or gives counsel or aid or favour to those who do such things, shall by that very fact lose the fiefs and benefices, become infamous, and be subject to the Imperial ban. No access or return to such fiefs or benefices shall ever again be open to him, and they cannot be granted to him anew in any way; and any grant or investiture made to him contrary to this shall have no force. Lastly, we decree that all the penalties mentioned above are incurred by force of the present sanction, ipso facto, by those who, without having made such a resignation, act fraudulently against their lords, or who knowingly invade them, whether with prior defiance or without any defiance at all.

units.la: CAP. XV.
units.tr: CHAPTER XV.

units.la: DE CONSPIRATORIBVS.
units.tr: ON CONSPIRATORS.

units.la: DEtestandas præteteà, & sacris legibus reprobatas conspirationes & conventiculas, seu colligationes illicitas,in civitatibus & extra, vel inter civitatē & civitatē, inter personā & personam,seu inter personam & civitatē, prætextu parentelæ, seu receptionis in cives, vel alterius cujuscumque coloris conjurationes; insuper & confœderationes & pacta, nec non & consuetudinem circa hujusmodi introductam,quam censemus potius corruptelam,reprobamus,damnamus, & ex certa scien-tia damus: quas civitates, seu personæ, cujuscumq; dignitatis,seu conditionis, aut status, sive inter se, vel cum aliis, absq; auctoritate dominorum,quorum subditi vel ministeriales sunt,seu in quorum districtu sunt ,eisdem dominis nominatim non exceptis, fecerint hactenus, & facere præsumpserint in scilicet sicut per sacras divorum Augustorum, præde cessorum nostrorum, leges, prohibitas non ambigitè cassaras; illis confœderationibus & legis dumiaxat exceptis, quas Principes, & Civitates, ac generali pace provinciarum atque terrarum inter se firmasse noscuntur. illas enim nostræ declaratiōnis specialiter reservantes, in suo decernimus vigore manere, donec de his aliud duxerimus ordinandum.
units.tr: Furthermore, we detest and reject, as already condemned by the sacred laws, all conspiracies, secret meetings, and unlawful leagues, whether within cities or outside them, or between city and city, between person and person, or between person and city, under the pretext of kinship, of admission to citizenship, or of any other kind whatever. Likewise we reject and condemn all confederations and pacts, and the custom introduced concerning such things, which we judge to be rather a corruption; and of our certain knowledge we declare them void. Any cities or persons, of whatever dignity, condition or rank, who have hitherto made such arrangements, either among themselves or with others, without the authority of the lords whose subjects or ministerials they are, or in whose district they lie, those lords not being specifically excepted, and who have presumed to make them, are hereby declared, as the prohibitions of the sacred laws of the deified Augusti, our predecessors, have plainly annulled. The only exceptions are those confederations and leagues which princes and cities are known to have concluded among themselves for the general peace of the provinces and lands. These we expressly reserve by this our declaration, and we decree that they shall remain in force by their own validity until we order otherwise concerning them.

units.la: 2. Personam singularem, quæ de cetero contra tenorem præsentis constitutionis,& nostræ leges antiquæ super hoc editæ,confœderationes, colligationes, conspirationes, & pacta hujusmodi inire præsumpserit ,ultra pœnam legis ejusdem, notam infamiæ, & pœnam decem librarum auri; civitatem vero, vel universitatem in hanc legem nostram similiter committentem, centum librarum auri, nec non anussionis & privationis libertatum,& privilegiorum Imperialium,pœnas incurrere decernimus corpore, mediatate pœ æ hujusmodi pecuniariæ fisco Imperiali; reliqua verò domino districtus,in cujus judicium facæ fuerint, applicanda.
units.tr: 2. Any single person who in future presumes, contrary to the terms of the present constitution and of our older laws issued on this matter, to enter into confederations, alliances, conspiracies, and pacts of this kind shall incur, over and above the penalty of that law, the mark of infamy and a fine of ten pounds of gold. A city or corporate body which likewise offends against this our law we decree shall incur a fine of one hundred pounds of gold, together with the loss of its liberties and Imperial privileges. Half of such monetary penalties shall go to the Imperial treasury, and the rest to the lord of the district in whose court the offence was committed.

units.la: CAP. XVI.
units.tr: CHAPTER XVI.

units.la: DE PFALBVRGERIIS.
units.tr: Concerning the Pfalburgers.

units.la: CÆterum ,quia nonnulli cives & subditi Principum, Baronum, & aliorum hominum, sicut frequens ad nos querela perduxit ,jugum originariæ subjectionis quærentes abjicere ,imò assu ie- H h
units.tr: Furthermore, since frequent complaint has reached us that some citizens and subjects of princes, barons and other lords, seeking to throw off the yoke of their original subjection, and even scorning their oath of allegiance, arrange to be received as citizens of other cities, and do so more often than the aforesaid,

units.la: meratio metario contemnentes, in aliarum civitatum cives recipi se procurant, & frequentius ut prædicti procurarunt; & nihilominus in priorum dominorum, quos tali fraude præsumpserunt, vel ut prædicti munt deferere, terris, civitatibus, oppidis, & villis corporaliter residentes, civitatum, ad quas modo se transtulerunt, libertatibus gaudere, & ab eis defensari contendunt, qui in partibus Alsatiæ Pfalburgensis confuevetunt vulgariter appellari. quoniam autem patrocinari non debent alicui dolo, de Imperatoriæ potestatis plenitudine, omnium Principum Electorum, Ecclesiasticorum & Secularium accedente consilio, ex certa scientia statuimus, & præsenti lege perpetuo valitura, quod prædicti cives & subditi, eis, quib. subsunt, taliter illudentes, in omnibus terris, locis & vinciis Sacri Imperii à præsenti die in posterum, civitatum, in quarum cives tali fraude recipi se permittunt, vel hactenus procurarunt, iurib. & libertatibus in nullo potiantur, nisi ad hujusmodi corporaliter & realiter transeuntes, ibique larem fovetes, continuè & verè ac non fictè residentes, debita onera & municipalia subeant munera in eisdem. Si qui vero contra præsentis legis tenorem recepti sint, vel fuerint in futurum, illorum receptio omni careat firmitate; & cujuscunque dignitatis, conditionis, aut status existant, in nullo casu penitus, sive causa, ad quas recipi se procurant, iurib. vel libertatibus gaudeant quomodolibet, vel fruantur, stantibus quibuscunque iuribus, privilegiis, vel consuetudinibus observatis, quantocumque tempore, & obtentis; quas & quæ, in quantum præsenti nostræ legi obveniant, præsentibus ex causa revocamus de prædictæ Imperialis plenitudine potestatis, omnique carere decernimus robore firmitatis.
units.tr: and yet, while still physically residing in the lands, cities, towns and villages of their former lords, whom they have presumed to desert by such fraud, they contend that they enjoy the liberties of the cities to which they have now transferred and are defended by them (those who in the parts of Alsace are commonly called Pfalburgers). Since no one ought to be defended in fraud, we have decided, by the fullness of imperial power and with the consent of all the Electors, ecclesiastical and secular, from certain knowledge and by this law, which shall remain in force forever, that these citizens and subjects, deceiving those to whom they are subject in this way, shall not enjoy any rights or liberties in any lands, places or provinces of the Holy Empire from this day forward, in any city in whose citizenship they permit themselves to be received by such fraud or have hitherto sought to be received, unless they move there bodily and in fact, establish their household there, and reside there continuously and truly, not feignedly, and bear the customary burdens and municipal duties in the same. If any have been received contrary to the terms of this law, or shall be received in future, their reception shall be wholly without force; and whatever their dignity, condition or status, in no case at all shall they in any way enjoy or make use of the rights or liberties to which they seek admission, whatever rights, privileges or customs have been observed and obtained, for however long a time; these, insofar as they conflict with this our law, we revoke for cause by the said fullness of imperial power, and decree that they shall be wholly without force of validity.

units.la: 2. Circa præmissa omnia Principum, Dominorum, & aliorum hominum, quos tales contingit, vel contingent in posterum, iuribus circa personas, & bona subditorum quorumcumque, ipsos sæpe dicto modo deferentium, semper salvis. Hos nihilominus, qui sæpe dictos cives, & alienos recipere, contra præsentis nostræ legis dispositionem, præsumpserint, vel recipere in præsumpserunt, si eos omnino non dimiserint infra mensem post intimationem præsentium eis centum marcas auri puri pro transgressione hujusmodi totiens, quotiens deinceps factum fuerit, decernentes; quarum medietas Imperiali fisco nostro, reliqua vero dominis illorum, qui fuerint, irremissibiliter applicetur.
units.tr: 2. In all the matters set out above, the rights of princes, lords and other persons, which pertain or shall in future pertain to them, over the persons and goods of any subjects who have fled in the manner mentioned above, always remain intact. Nevertheless, if any who have presumed to receive the aforesaid citizens and aliens, or have presumed to receive them, contrary to the provisions of this our present law, do not wholly dismiss them within a month after notice of these present letters, we decree that they shall pay one hundred marks of pure gold for each such transgression, as often as it occurs from then on. Half of this shall go irrevocably to our imperial treasury, and the other half to the lords of those persons concerned.

units.la: CAP. XVII.
units.tr: CAP. XVII.

units.la: DE DIFFIDATIONIBVS.
units.tr: ON DIFFIDATIONS.

units.la: EOs, qui de cætero adversus aliquos iustam diffidationis causam se habere fingentes, ipsos in locis, ubi domicilia non obtinent, aut ea communiter non inhabitant, intempestive diffidant, declaramus damna quæcumque per incendia, spolia, vel rapinas diffidatis ipsis, cum honore suo inferre non posse.
units.tr: We declare that those who from now on, pretending to have a just cause of diffidation against certain persons, untimely diffidate them in places where they do not hold a domicile, or do not commonly dwell, cannot inflict any damage whatever by fires, plunder or robbery upon the persons so diffidated, with their honour intact.

units.la: 2. Et quia patrocinari non debent alicui fraus & dolus, præsenti constitutione in perpetuum valitura sancimus, diffidationes hujusmodi quibuscumque dominis aut personis, cum quibus *aliquo fuerunt in societate, familiaritate, vel honesta quavis amicitia conversati, sic factas vel hendas inposterum, non valere, nec licere prætextu diffidationis cujuslibet quempiam invadi per incendia, spolia, vel rapinas, nisi diffidatio per tres dies naturales ipsi diffidando personaliter, vel in loco, quo habitare consuevit, publice fuerit intimata, postque de intimatione hujusmodi, per testes idoneos fide plena fides. Quisquis secus quempiam diffidare vel invadere modo præmisso præsumpserit, ipso facto in eo ipso incurrat, ac si nulla diffidatio facta esset; quem etiam tamquam prodito rem, per quoscunque Judices pœnis legalibus statuimus castigari.
units.tr: 2. And since fraud and deceit ought not to be protected by anyone, we decree by this constitution, which is to remain in force for ever, that diffidations of this kind, made or issued henceforth against any lords or persons with whom the diffidator has at any time associated in fellowship, familiarity, or any honest friendship, are not valid; and that it is not lawful, under the pretext of any diffidation whatever, to attack anyone by fires, plunder or robbery, unless the diffidation has been announced to him, personally by the diffidator, or publicly in the place where he is accustomed to live, over three natural days, and afterwards full faith is given, through suitable witnesses, to the announcement of this kind. Whoever presumes to diffidate or attack anyone otherwise than in the manner stated above shall, by that very act, incur the penalty as if no diffidation had been made at all; and we decree that such a person, as one who has betrayed the affair, be punished with legal penalties by whatever judges.

units.la: *Leg. alioqui.
units.tr: *Leg. alioqui.

units.la: 3. Prohibemus etiam & damnamus universas & singulas guerras, & lites injustas, queq; injusta incendia, spolia, rapinas, indebita & inconsueta theolonea & conductus, & pro ipsis conductibus extorqueri consuetas, sub poenis, quibus sacræ leges præmissa, & cuiuscunque generis, sanciunt punienda.
units.tr: 3. We also prohibit and condemn all and each of the wars and unjust suits, likewise unjust fires, plunder, robberies, undue and unaccustomed tolls and safe-conducts, and the payments customarily extorted for those safe-conducts, under the penalties which the sacred laws decree for the aforesaid offences and offences of every kind.

units.la: CAP. XVIII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XVIII.

units.la: LITTERA INTIMATIONIS.
units.tr: LETTER OF NOTIFICATION.

units.la: VObis Illustri & magnifico Principi Domino &c. Marchioni Brandeburgensi, Sacri Imperii Archicamerario, Coëlectori, & amico nostro charissimo. Electionem Romanorum Regis ex rationabilibus causis imminet facienda, præsentibus intimanus; vosque ex officio vestro bito ad electionem præfatam rite vocamus, quatenus à die tali, &c. infratres menses computandos, per vos, seu nuncios aut procuratores vestros, unum vel plures, sufficiens mandatum, ad locum debitum, juxta formam sacrarum legum super hoc editarum, venire curetis, deliberaturi, tractaturi, & concordaturi cum aliis Conprincipibus & Coëlectoribus vestris & nostris, de electione futuri Regis Romanorum in Imperatorem postmodum favente Domino promovendi, eandem manuri usque ad plenam consummationem electionis hujusmodi, & aliàs factum, & prout in sacris legibus super hoc deliberatè editis invenitur expressum; aliàs, non obstante vestra seu vestrorum absentia, in præmissis una cum aliis Coprincipibus & Coëlectoribus vestris & nostris, prout legum ipsarum sanxerit auctoritas, finaliter procedemus.
units.tr: To you, the illustrious and magnificent Prince, Lord etc., Margrave of Brandenburg, Archchamberlain of the Holy Empire, Co-elector, and our most dear friend: We hereby notify you that the election of a King of the Romans is about to be held for reasonable causes; and by virtue of your office we duly summon you to the aforesaid election, so that, from the day such-and-such, etc., within the next months, you take care to send, in person or through your messengers or proxies, one or more sufficient mandates to the proper place, according to the form of the sacred laws issued on this matter, to deliberate, treat, and agree with the other co-princes and co-electors, both yours and ours, concerning the election of the future King of the Romans, who, God willing, is to be afterwards promoted to Emperor; and to continue this same business until the full completion of such an election, and otherwise to do what is set out in the sacred laws deliberately issued on this matter; otherwise, notwithstanding your absence or that of your people, we shall proceed finally in the aforesaid matters, together with the other co-princes and co-electors, both yours and ours, as the authority of those laws shall have prescribed.

units.la: CAP. XIX.
units.tr: CHAPTER XIX.

units.la: FORMA PROCVRATORII, MITTENDI PER cum principem Electorem, qui nuncios suos ad electionem facien- dam duxerit deslinandos.
units.tr: FORM OF A PROXY, TO BE SENT BY A PRINCE ELECTOR WHO HAS RESOLVED TO DISPATCH HIS MESSENGERS TO CONDUCT THE ELECTION.

units.la: NOs talis, Dei gratia, &c. Sacri Imperii &c. notum facimus tenore praesentium universis: quòd cum electio Romanorum Regis ex rationabilibus causis imminet facienda, nos de honore & statu Sacri Imperii solicitudine debita intendere cupientes, ne tam gravibus dispendiis periculosè subjaceat, de fide & circumspectionis industria dilectorum nobis &c. fidelium nostrorum obtinentes utique praesumptionis indubiae fiduciam singularem, ipsos & quemlibet eorum in solidum, ita quòd non sit melior conditio occupantis, sed quod per unum inceptum fuerit, per alium finiri valeat, & licitè terminari, omni jure, modo & forma, quibus melius & efficacius possumus, seu valemus, nostros veros & legitimos Procuratores, & nuncios speciales facimus, constituimus, & ordinamus, ad tractandum ubilibet unà cum aliis Conprincipibus, & Coëlectoribus nostris, tam Ecclesiasticis quàm Saecularibus, & cum ipsis concordandum, conveniendum, & concludendum de persona quacumq; habili ac idonea, in Regem Romanorum eligenda; ac ipsis tractatibus super electione talis personae habendis, pro nobis, loco & nomine nostris interesse ndum, tractandum, & deliberandum, nec non vice & nomine nostris eandem personam nominandum, & in ipsam consentiendum, ac etiam in Regem Romanorum promovendum, ad Sacrum Imperium eligendum, ac in animam nostram praestandum quodcumque juramentum, quod necessarium debitum, seu consuetum fuerit; circa praemissa, & quodlibet praemissorum, alium, vel alios procuratores in solidum substituendum & revocandum, omnia & singula faciendum, quae in praemissis, & circa praemissa etiam usque ad consummationem tractatuum, nominationis, deliberationis, & electionis hujusmodi, de praesenti faciendae necessaria, aut utilia fuerint, seu etiam quomodolibet oportuna, etiamsi praemissa, vel eorum quodlibet, mandatum exigant speciale; etiamsi majora vel magis singularia fuerint supradictis, & quae nosmetipsi facere possemus, si hujusmodi tractatuum, deliberationis, nominationis & electionis futurae negotiis, praesentes & personaliter adesse mus, gratum & ratum habentes, & habere volentes, & nos perpetuò habituros firmiter promittentes, quicquid per antedictos Procuratores, seu nuncios nostros, necnon subsitutos, aut subsitiuendos, ab ipsis seu eorum altero, in praemissis seu praemissorum quolibet, actum, gestum, seu factum fuerit, aut quomodolibet ordinatum.
units.tr: WE, such-and-such, by the grace of God, etc., of the Holy Empire, etc., make known by the tenor of these presents to all: that since the election of a King of the Romans is about to be held for reasonable causes, we, desiring to attend with due care to the honour and condition of the Holy Empire, lest it be exposed to such grave losses in peril, and placing in our beloved and faithful ones, etc., a singular confidence founded on their fidelity and the diligence of their circumspection, do make, constitute and ordain them, and each of them, jointly and severally, so that the condition of the first occupant is not the better, but what has been begun by one may be finished and lawfully concluded by another, by every right, manner and form by which we best and most effectually can or may, our true and lawful proctors and special messengers; to treat anywhere together with our other fellow princes and fellow electors, both ecclesiastical and secular, and to agree, come to terms and conclude with them concerning whatever fit and suitable person is to be elected King of the Romans; and, in the negotiations concerning the choice of such a person, to be present on our behalf, in our place and in our name, and to deal and deliberate; likewise, in our name and stead, to nominate that same person, to consent to him, and to promote him to be elected King of the Romans and to the Holy Empire, and to take in our soul whatever oath shall be required, due or customary; and concerning the foregoing, and any part of them, to substitute and revoke other proctor or proctors jointly and severally; to do all and singular things which in the foregoing matters, and concerning them, even until the completion of such negotiations, nomination, deliberation and election, shall be necessary, useful, or in any way fitting to be done at present, even if the foregoing, or any part of them, call for a special mandate, and even if they be greater or more particular than those stated above, and which we ourselves could do, were we present in person at these negotiations, deliberation, nomination and the future election; holding and wishing to hold as pleasing and ratified, and firmly promising that we shall hold for ever, whatever shall have been done, transacted, or in any way ordained in the foregoing matters or any part of them by the said proctors or our messengers, as well as by the substitutes or those to be substituted, or by either of them.

units.la: CAP. XX.
units.tr: CHAPTER XX.

units.la: DE VNIONE PRINCIPATVVM ELECTORVM, & Iurium eis connexorum.
units.tr: ON THE UNION OF THE ELECTORAL PRINCIPALITIES, AND OF THE RIGHTS ATTACHED TO THEM.

units.la: In nomine sanctae & individuae Trinitatis feliciter, Amen.
units.tr: In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, happily. Amen.

units.la: Carolus Quartus divina favente clementia, Romanorum Imperator, semper-Augustus, & Bohemiae Rex, ad perpetuam rei memoriam.
units.tr: Charles IV, by the favour of divine clemency, Emperor of the Romans, ever Augustus, and King of Bohemia, for the perpetual memory of the matter.

units.la: CUM universi & singuli Principatus, quorum virtute Seculares Principes Electores, jus & vocem in electione Regis Romanorum, in Caesarem promovendi, obtinere noscuntur, cum jure hujusmodi, nec non officiis, dignitatibus, & juribus aliis, eis, & cuilibet eorum annexis, & dependentibus ab eisdem, adeò conjuncti, & inseparabiliter sint uniti, quòd jus, vox, officium, & dignitas quoque jura, ad quemlibet Principatuum eorundem spectantia, cadere non possint in alium, quam illum, qui Principatum ipsum cum terra, vasallagiis, feudis, & dominio, ac ejus pertinentiis universis, dignoscitur possidere; praesenti edicto Imperiali perpetuò valituro sancimus, unumquemque Principatuum praedictorum, cum jure & voce electionis, ac officio, caeterisque omnibus dignitatibus, juribus & pertinentiis ad ipsum spectantibus, ita perseverare, & esse debere unitum perpetuis temporibus indivisibiliter & conjunctum, quòd possessor Principatus cujuslibet, etiam juris, vocis, officii, & dignitatis, & pertinentiarum omnium ad illum spectantium, quieta debeat & libera possessione gaudere, ac Princeps Elector ab omnibus reputari, ipseque, & nemo alius, per caeteros Principes Electores, ad electionem, & omnes actus alios pro Sacri Imperii honore, vel oportunitate gerendos, omni tempore assumi, sine contradictione qualibet, & admitti; nec aliquid praemissorum ab altero, cum sint & esse debeant inseparabilia, dividi, vel ullo tempore debeat separari, aut in judicio, vel extra divisim tepe valeat, aut evinci, vel etiam per sententiam separari; nec aliquis unum sine alio impetens audiatur. quod si per errorem, vel aliàs auditus quis fuerit, aut processus, judicium, sententia, vel aliquid hujusmodi contra praesentem dispositionem nostram emanaverit, seu quomodolibet attemptari contigerit, hoc totum, & omnia ex his, & quolibet eorum sequentia, eo ipso viribus non subsistant.
units.tr: SINCE all and each of the principalities by whose power the secular princes are known to hold the electoral office, the right and the voice in electing the King of the Romans to be promoted to Emperor, together with that right and the other offices, dignities and rights attached to each of them and dependent on them, are so joined and inseparably united that the right, the voice, the office and the dignity, as well as the rights belonging to each of those principalities, cannot fall to anyone other than him who is known to possess that principality with its land, vassals, fiefs and lordship, and all its appurtenances: by this present imperial edict, which shall remain in force forever, we decree that each of the aforesaid principalities, with the right and voice of election, the office, and all the other dignities, rights and appurtenances belonging to it, shall so continue and must be united and joined indivisibly in perpetual times, that the possessor of any principality shall enjoy quiet and free possession also of the right, voice, office and dignity, and of all appurtenances belonging to it, and that he shall be regarded by all as an elector prince, and that he himself, and no one else, shall at all times be taken up and admitted by the other electoral princes, without any contradiction, to the election and all other acts to be performed for the honour or advantage of the Holy Empire; and that none of these things be divided from another, since they are and must be inseparable, nor at any time be separated, nor may they be divided or evicted apart in court or outside it, nor may they be separated even by sentence; nor shall anyone be heard who attacks one without the other. But if through error, or otherwise, anyone has been heard, or any proceeding, judgment or sentence, or anything of this kind, has issued against this our present disposition, or has happened to be attempted in any way, let all of this, and all that follows from these or any of them, by that very fact have no force.

units.la: Hh 2 CAP. & Illustrium Principum nostrorum,& Sacri Romani Imperii,tam Ecclesiasticorum quamSecularium Principum Electorum,seu alterius eorundem(nam& ipsi pars corporis nostri sunt.Eadem enim severitate voluntatem sceleris, qua effectum puniri jura voluerunt) : ipse quidem, utpote majestatis reus, gladio feriatur,bonis ejus omnibus fisco nostro addictis: filii vero ejus, quibus vitam Imperiali speciali liter lenitate concedimus(paterno enim deberent perire supplicio,in quibus paterni, hoc est, hæreditarii criminis metuuntur exempla)à materna vel avita,omnium etiam proximorum hereditate,& successione habeantur alieni,ex testamentis aliorum nihil capiant, sint perpetuo egentes & pauperes, insamia eos paterna semper comitetur, ad nullum umquam honorem, ad nulla prorsus sacramenta pervenianti, sint postremò tales,ut his perpetua egestate sordentibus sit & mors solatium,& vita supplicium. Denique jubemus eos esse notabiles sine venia, qui pro talibus umquam apud nos intervenire tempraverint.
units.tr: ...of our illustrious princes and of the Holy Roman Empire, both ecclesiastical and secular electoral princes, or of any other of them (for they too are part of our body; for the laws wished the intention of a crime to be punished with the same severity as its execution): he indeed, as guilty of majesty, shall be struck down by the sword, all his goods being forfeited to our treasury; but his sons, whose lives we grant by special imperial leniency (for they would have to perish by the father's punishment, since the examples of paternal, that is hereditary, crime are feared), shall be regarded as strangers to the inheritance of the mother or grandfather and of all their near relatives, and to succession; they shall receive nothing from the wills of others; they shall be perpetually needy and poor; infamy shall always accompany them from their father; they shall attain to no honour and to no sacraments at all; finally, let them be such that, with this perpetual want defiling them, death shall be their consolation and life their punishment. Lastly, we order that those who have ever attempted to intercede before us for such persons be marked without pardon.

units.la: 2. Ad filias sane ipsorum, quotlibet numero fuerint, Falcidiam tantùm ex bonis matris, sive testata,sive intestata decesserit,volumus pervenire,ut habeant mediocrem potius filiæ alimoniam,quàm integrum emolumentum aut nomen hæredis consequantur. mitior enim circa eas debet esse sententia,quas pro infirmitate sexus minus ausuras esse confidimus.
units.tr: 2. To the daughters of these men, however many in number, we wish only the Falcidian portion from the goods of the mother to pass, whether she dies testate or intestate, so that they may have a moderate maintenance as daughters rather than obtain the full advantage or the name of heir. For the sentence ought to be milder toward those whom, because of the weakness of their sex, we trust will dare less.

units.la: 3. Emancipationes quoque,quæ à prædictis sive in filios,post legem duntaxat latam, sive in filias fuerint collatæ, non valeant. dotes, donationes quorumlibet, postremò item alienationes, quas ex eo tempore qualibet fraude,vel jure factas esse constiterit,quo primò memorati de ineunda factione,ac societate cogitaverint, nullius statuimus esse momenti. Uxores sane prædictorum recuperata dote,si in ea conditione fuerint,ut,quæ à viris titulo donationis acceperunt, seu accipiunt, filiis debeant reservare,tempore quo usufructus absumitur; omnia ea fisco nostro se reliQuras esse cognoscant, quæ juxta legem filiis debebantur ; Falcidia etiam ex his rebus, filiabus tantum, non etiam filiis deputetur.
units.tr: 3. Emancipations too, which have been granted by the aforesaid men to their sons after the law alone was passed, or to their daughters, shall not be valid. Dowries, gifts of any persons, and likewise, finally, alienations which shall be found to have been made by any fraud or right from the time when the aforementioned men first thought of entering into the conspiracy and association, we declare to be of no force. Indeed, the wives of the aforesaid men, having recovered their dowry, if they are under the condition that what they have received or receive from their husbands by title of gift they must reserve for the sons, at the time when the usufruct is consumed, shall know that all those things which by law were owed to the sons are forfeit to our treasury; the Falcidian portion from these things shall be assigned to the daughters only, not to the sons.

units.la: 4. Idem, quod de prædictis, eorumque filiis cavimus, etiam de satellitibus, consciis, ac ministris, filiisque eorum simili severitate censemus. Sane si quis ex his in exordio initæ factionis, studio veræ laudis accensus, ipse prodiderit factionem, & præmio à nobis & honore donabitur. Is verò,qui usus fuerit factione , si vel serò,tamen incognita adhuc consiliorum arcana patefecerit , absolutione *tantum,ac venia dignus habebitur.
units.tr: 4. What we have provided concerning the aforesaid men and their sons, we likewise judge with similar severity concerning their attendants, accomplices and ministers, and their sons. Indeed, if anyone of these, at the beginning of the conspiracy, kindled by zeal for true praise, himself reveals the conspiracy, he shall be rewarded by us with a prize and honour. But he who has taken part in the conspiracy, if even late, yet reveals the secrets of the plans not yet known, shall be held worthy only of absolution and pardon.

units.la: 5. Statuimus insuper,ut si quid contra prædictos Principes Electores,Ecclesiasticos vel Seculares,commissum dicatur,etiam post mortem rei,id crimen instaurari posse.
units.tr: 5. We further decree that if anything is said to have been committed against the aforesaid electoral princes, ecclesiastical or secular, that crime can be renewed even after the death of the accused.

units.la: 6. In hoc item crimine,quod ad læsam in Principibus Electoribus suis Majestatem pertinet,etiam in caput domini,servi torquentur.
units.tr: 6. In this crime also, which pertains to the majesty offended in their electoral princes, slaves are tortured even against the head of their master.

units.la: 7. Volumus insuper,& præsenti Imperiali sancimus edicto, ut etiam post mortem nocentium hoc crimen inchoari possit , ut convicto mortuo , memoria ejus damnetur, & bona successoribus ejus eripiantur. nam ex quo sceleratissimum quis ceperit consilium, exinde quodammodo sua mente punitus est.
units.tr: 7. We wish moreover, and by this present imperial edict we decree, that this crime may be begun even after the death of the guilty, so that, if he is convicted when dead, his memory be condemned and his goods be taken from his successors. For from the time someone has conceived a most wicked plan, he has in a sense been punished by his own mind.

units.la: 8. Porrò, ex quo quis tale crimen contraxit, neque alienare, neque manumittere eum posse, nec ei solvere jure debitorem,decernimus.
units.tr: 8. Furthermore, from the time someone has contracted such a crime, we decree that he can neither alienate nor manumit, nor may a debtor lawfully pay him.

units.la: 9. In hac causa in caput domini servos torqueri statuimus, id est, propter causam factionis damnandæ contra Principes Electores, Ecclesiasticos & Seculares,ut præmittitur.
units.tr: 9. In this matter we decree that slaves be tortured against the head of their master, that is, on account of the cause of the conspiracy to be condemned against the electoral princes, ecclesiastical and secular, as has been set out above.

units.la: 10. Et si decesserit quis,propter incertam personam successoris bona servantur,si in a casu hujusmodi fuisse mortuus arguatur.
units.tr: 10. And if anyone dies, his goods are kept on account of the uncertain person of the successor, if he is shown to have died in such a case.

units.la: CAP. XXV.
units.tr: CAP. XXV.

units.la: DE INTEGRITATE PRINCIPATVVM ELECTORVM.
units.tr: ON THE INTEGRITY OF THE ELECTORAL PRINCIPALITIES.

units.la: Sicut cæteros Principatus congruit in sua integritate servari, ut corroboretur justitia, & subjecti fidelitate pace gaudeant & quiete, multo magis magnifici Principatus, dominia, honores, & jura Electorum Principum debent illæsa servari.nam ubi majus incumbit periculum, majus debet remedium adhiberi, ne columnis ruentibus,basis totius ædificii collidatur.
units.tr: Just as it is fitting that the other principalities be preserved in their integrity, so that justice may be strengthened, and the subjects may rejoice in fidelity, peace and quiet, much more ought the magnificent principalities, the dominions, honours and rights of the Electoral Princes be preserved unimpaired. For where the greater danger lies, the greater remedy must be applied, lest, when the pillars fall, the foundation of the whole building be crushed.

units.la: 2. Decernimus igitur, & hoc perpetuis temporibus valituro Imperiali sancimus edicto, quòd exnunc inanted perpetuis futuris temporibus , insignes & magnifici Principatus , videlicet Regnum Bohemiæ,Comitatus Palatinus Rheni,Ducatus Saxoniæ,& Marchionatus Brandenburgensis,terræ, districtus, homagia, vassallagia, & alia quævis ad ipsa spectantia, scindi, dividi, seu quavis conditione dimembrari non debeant,sed ut potiùs in sua perfecta integritate perpetua maneant,primogenitus filius succedat in eis,sibique soli jus ac dominium competat,nisi forte mente captus, fatuus, seu alterius famosi & notabilis defectus existeret , propter quem non deberet, seu posset hominibus principari. in quo casu , inhibita sibi successione, secundogenitum , si fuerit in ea progenie, seu alium seniorem fratrem,vel consanguineum laicum,qui paterno stipiti in descendenti recta linea proximior fuerit,volumus successuruṁ; qui tamen apud alios fratres, & sorores, se clementem & pium exhibebit continuò, juxta datam sibi à Deo gratiam,& juxta suum beneplacitum, & ipsius patrimonii facultates; divisione, scissione, seu dimembratione Principatus, & pertinentiatum ejus, sibi omnibus modis interdicta.
units.tr: 2. We therefore decree, and by this Imperial edict, which is to remain valid for all time, we sanction that from now on, and for all future times, the distinguished and magnificent principalities, namely the Kingdom of Bohemia, the Palatine County of the Rhine, the Duchy of Saxony, and the Margraviate of Brandenburg, together with the lands, districts, homages, vassalages and all other things whatsoever pertaining to them, ought not to be cut up, divided, or dismembered in any way; but rather they are to remain perpetually in their full integrity. The firstborn son shall succeed to them, and the right and dominion shall belong to him alone, unless perhaps he should be found mentally incapacitated, foolish, or afflicted with some other notorious and conspicuous defect on account of which he ought not, or could not, rule over men. In that case, his succession being barred, we will that the second-born son, if there be one in that line, or another elder brother, or a lay blood relative who is nearer to the paternal stock in the direct line of descent, shall succeed; who nevertheless shall continually show himself merciful and pious toward his other brothers and sisters, according to the grace given him by God, and according to his good pleasure and the resources of the patrimony itself; all division, severance, or dismemberment of the principality and its appurtenances being forbidden to him in every way.

units.la: C A P. XXVI.
units.tr: Chapter 26.

units.la: De Curia Imperiali & sessione.
units.tr: Of the Imperial Court and the sitting.

units.la: DE, qua solemnis Curia Imperialis vel Regia fuerit celebranda, veniant circa horam primam Principes Electores, Ecclesiastici & Seculares, ad domum habitationis Imperialis, sive Regalis, & ibi Imperator vel Rex ipse omnibus insignibus Imperialibus induetur, & ascensis equis, omnes vadant cum Imperatore, vel Rege, ad locum sessionis aptatae, & illic quilibet eorum in ordine & modo supra in lege, de ordine processionis ipsorum Principum Electorum, plenius diffinito.
units.tr: Concerning the manner in which the solemn Imperial or Royal Court is to be held: about the first hour, the Electors, both ecclesiastical and secular, shall come to the house of the Imperial or Royal residence, and there the Emperor or King himself shall be vested with all the Imperial insignia. Then, having mounted their horses, all shall go with the Emperor or King to the prepared place of sitting, and there each of them shall take his place in the order and manner more fully defined above in the law concerning the order of procession of the Electors themselves.

units.la: 2. Porrabiretiam Archicancellarius, in cujus Archicancellariatu haec fuerint, super baculo genteo, omnia sigilla & typaria Imperialia, & Regalia.
units.tr: 2. Moreover, the Archchancellor, in whose archchancellorship these matters fall, shall carry on a staff of gentian wood all the seals and Imperial and Royal signets.

units.la: 3. Seculares vero Principes Electores sceptrum, pomum, & ensem, secundum quod superius explicitur, deportabunt.
units.tr: 3. The secular Electors, however, shall carry the sceptre, the orb and the sword, as is explained above.

units.la: 4. Portabuntur etiam immediate ante Archiepiscopum Trevirensem suo loco transeuntem, primo, Aquisgranensis; secundo, Mediolanensis corona; & hoc ante Imperatorem duntaxat, qui jam est Imperialibus infulis decoratus; quas gestabunt aliqui Principes inferiores, ad hoc per Imperatorem juxta placitum deputandi.
units.tr: 4. The crown of Aachen and the Milanese crown shall also be carried immediately before the Archbishop of Trier as he passes into his place, first the Aachen crown, second the Milanese crown; and this only before the Emperor, who is already adorned with the Imperial regalia. These shall be borne by certain inferior Princes, who are to be appointed for this purpose by the Emperor at his pleasure.

units.la: 5. Imperatrix etiam, vel Regina Romanorum, suis Augustalibus amicta insignis, post Regem vel Imperatorem Romanorum, & etiam post Regem Bohemiae, qui Imperatorem immediate subsequitur, competentis spacii intervallo, suis associata Proceribus, suisque comitata virginibus, ad locum sessionis procedat. *
units.tr: 5. The Empress or Queen of the Romans also, arrayed in her Augustal robes and distinguished, shall proceed to the place of sitting after the King or Emperor of the Romans, and also after the King of Bohemia, who immediately follows the Emperor, at a suitable interval of space, accompanied by her chief nobles and attended by her maidens.

units.la: * Hic finiunt Decreta Comitiorum Metensium.
units.tr: * Here end the Decrees of the Diet of Metz.

units.la: C A P. XXVII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXVII.

units.la: DE OFFICIIS PRINCIPVM ELECTORVM IN solemnibus Curiis Imperatorum, vel Regum Romanorum.
units.tr: CONCERNING THE DUTIES OF THE ELECTORAL PRINCES AT THE SOLEMN DIETS OF THE EMPERORS OR KINGS OF THE ROMANS.

units.la: STATUIMUS, ut quandocumque Imperator vel Rex Romanorum solemnes curias suas celebraverit, in quibus Principes Electores sua deservire, seu exercere debent officia, subscriptus in hunc ordo servetur.
units.tr: We decree that whenever the Emperor or King of the Romans holds his solemn diets, at which the Electoral Princes ought to perform their duties or offices, the following order shall be observed.

units.la: 1. Primo enim, Imperatore, vel Rege ipso, in sede Regia, sive solio Imperiali sedente, Dux Saxoniae officium suum agat hoc modo. ponerur enim ante aedificium sessionis Imperialis vel Regiae, acervus avenae, tantae altitudinis, quod pertingat usque ad pectus vel antelam equi, super quo sedebit ipse Dux, & habebit in manu baculum argenteum, & mensuram argenteam, quae simul faciant in pondere duodecim marcas argenti; & sedens super equo, primo mensuram eandem de avena plenam accipiet, & famulo primitus venienti ministrabit eandem. quo facto, figendo baculum in avenam recedet, & Vicemarescallus ejus, puta de Pappenheim, accedens, vel eo absente Marescallus curiae, ulterius avenam ipsam distribuat.
units.tr: 1. First, with the Emperor or King himself seated in the royal chair, or on the imperial throne, the Duke of Saxony shall perform his office in this way. A heap of oats shall be placed before the building of the imperial or royal session, of such height that it reaches to the breast or breastplate of a horse. The Duke himself shall sit upon a horse, holding in his hand a silver staff and a silver measure, which together weigh twelve marks of silver. Seated on the horse, he shall first take the same measure full of oats and give it to the servant who first comes forward. Having done this, he shall withdraw, fixing the staff in the oats. Then his deputy marshal, namely of Pappenheim, or, if he is absent, the marshal of the court, shall come forward and distribute the oats further.

units.la: 2. Ingresso vero Imperatore, vel Rege ad mensam, Principes Electores Ecclesiastici, videlicet Archiepiscopi, stanresante mensam cum caeteris Praelatis, benedicent eandem, secundum ordinem, qui circa haec eis in superioribus est praescriptus. & benedictione completa, iidem Archiepiscopi omnes, si adsint; alioquin duo, vel unus, sigilla & typaria Imperialia, sive Regalia a Cancellario curiae recipient; eoque in cujus Archicancellariatu curiam ipsam celebrari contingeret, in medio procedente, & aliis duobus ex alterutro latere sibi junctis, sigilla & typaria ipsa, omnes quidem baculum, in quo suspensa fuerint, manibus contingentes, ea portabunt, & ante Imperatorem, vel Regem reverenter ponenrin mensa. Imperator vero, sive Rex eadem ipsis statim restituet; & in cujus Archicancellariatu hoc fuerit, ut praefertur, is majus sigillum collo appensum, usque ad finem mensae gestabit, & deinceps donec ad hospitium suum perveniat, ab Imperiali, sive Regali curia equitando. baculus vero, de quo praemittitur, tlfe debebit argenteus, duodecim marcas argenti habens in pondere, cuius tam argenti quam precii partem tertiam unusquisque Archiepiscoporum ipsorum persolvet, & baculus ipse pronus una cum sigillis & typariis, debet Cancellario Imperialis curiae assignari, in usus suos bene placitos convertendus. Postquam autem is, quem ordo tetigerit, portando sigillum majus ab Imperiali curia ad hospitium suum redierit, ut praefertur, statim sigillum ipsum per aliquem de suis familiaribus praedicto Imperialis curiae Cancellario remittet super equo, quem juxta propriae dignitatis decentiam & amorem, quem ad Cancellarium curiae gesserit, ipsi Cancellario tenebitur elargiri.
units.tr: 2. When the Emperor or King has come to the table, the Ecclesiastical Electoral Princes, namely the Archbishops, shall stand at the table with the other prelates and bless it, in the order prescribed above for such matters. When the blessing is finished, all the Archbishops, if they are present, or otherwise two or one of them, shall receive from the Chancellor of the court the imperial or royal seals and signets. The Archbishop in whose archchancellorship the court happens to be held shall carry them, walking in the middle, with two others joined to him on either side. All of them shall touch with their hands the staff on which the seals have been hung, carry them, and reverently place them on the table before the Emperor or King. The Emperor or King shall immediately return them to the same men. And the one in whose archchancellorship this takes place, as stated, shall wear the greater seal hung from his neck until the end of the table, and afterwards, until he reaches his lodging, riding away from the imperial or royal court. The staff mentioned above must be of silver, weighing twelve marks of silver. A third part of this silver, and of its value, shall be paid by each of the Archbishops, and the staff itself, together with the seals and signets, shall be handed over to the Chancellor of the imperial court, to be converted to his own well-pleasing uses. Once the man whom the order has reached has returned, as stated, from the imperial court to his lodging, carrying the greater seal, he shall immediately send the seal, by one of his household, to the aforesaid Chancellor of the imperial court, on a horse, which he shall be bound to give to the Chancellor as a gift, in keeping with the decency of his own dignity and the goodwill he has shown to the Chancellor of the court.

units.la: 3. Deinde Marchio Brandenburgensis Archicamerarius accedat super equo, habens argenteas pelves cum aqua in manibus, ponderis duodecim marcarum argenti, & pulchrum manutergium; & descendens ab equo, dabit aquam Domino Imperatori, vel Regi Romanorum manibus abluendis.
units.tr: 3. Then the Margrave of Brandenburg, Archchamberlain, shall approach on horseback, carrying in his hands silver basins with water, weighing twelve marks of silver, and a fine towel. Dismounting from his horse, he shall give water to the Lord Emperor or King of the Romans to wash his hands.

units.la: 4. Comes Palatinus Rheni inrrabit similiter super equo, habens in manibus quatuor scutellas argenteas cibis impletas, quarum quaelibet tres marcas habeat in starera, & descendens ab equo, portabit & ponet ante Imperatorem, vel Regem in mensa.
units.tr: 4. The Count Palatine of the Rhine shall likewise ride in on horseback, holding in his hands four silver dishes filled with food, each of which shall weigh three marks by the balance. Dismounting from his horse, he shall carry them and set them before the Emperor or King on the table.

units.la: 5. Post hoc Rex Bohemiae Archipincerna, veniat similiter super equo, portans in manibus cuppam seu scyphum argenteum, ponderis duodecim marcarum, coopertum, vino & aqua permixtum impletum; & descendens de equo, scyphum ipsum Imperatori, vel Regi Romanorum porriger ad bibendum. 6. Sicut autem hactenus obseruatum fuisse comperimus, ita statuimus, ut peractis per Principes Electores Seculares, praedictis eorum officiis, ille de Falckenstein Subcamerarius, equū & pelves Marchionis Brandenburgensis, pro se recipiat: Magister coquinę de Nortemberg, equum & scutellas Comitis Palatini: Vicepincerna de Limburg, equum & scyphum Regis Bohemiæ: Vicemarescallus de Pappenheim, equum, baculum & mensuram praedictam Ducis Saxoniæ; si tamen ipsi in tali Imperiali seu Regali curia praesentes existant, & eorum quilibet in officio suo ministret; si vero ipsi, vel eorum aliqui a praefata curia se duxerint absentandos, extūc Imperialis vel Regalis curiæ quotidiani ministri vice absentium, puta quilibet in loco ejus absentis, cui in vocabulo seu in officio communicat, sicut gerit officium, sic collatin praemissis & fructum.
units.tr: 5. After this, the King of Bohemia, Archbutler, shall likewise come on horseback, carrying in his hands a cup or silver bowl of twelve marks' weight, covered and filled with wine mixed with water. Dismounting from his horse, he shall offer the bowl to the Emperor or King of the Romans to drink. 6. Moreover, as we have found was observed until now, we decree that, when the aforesaid offices of the Secular Electoral Princes have been performed, the following shall receive for themselves the fees and horses: the Subchamberlain, von Falckenstein, shall take the horse and basins of the Margrave of Brandenburg; the Master of the Kitchen, of Nortemberg, the horse and dishes of the Count Palatine; the Deputy Butler, of Limburg, the horse and cup of the King of Bohemia; the Deputy Marshal, of Pappenheim, the horse, staff and aforesaid measure of the Duke of Saxony. This applies if they are present at such an imperial or royal court and each of them performs his office. But if they, or any of them, have chosen to be absent from the said court, then the daily servants of the imperial or royal court shall take the place of the absent men, each in the place of the absent man whose name or office he shares, and, just as he performs the office, so shall he receive the aforesaid duties and fruits.

units.la: CAP. XXVIII.
units.tr: CAP. XXVIII.

units.la: DE MENSIS IMPERIALIBVS ET Electoralibus.
units.tr: Concerning the Imperial and Electoral Tables.

units.la: IMperialis insuper mensa vel Regia sic debet aptari, ut ultra alias aulæ tabulas, sive mensas, in altitudine sex pedum sit altius elevata, in qua praeter Imperatorem duntaxat, vel Regem Romanorum, die solemnis curiæ nemo penitus collocetur.
units.tr: The Imperial table, or the royal table, shall moreover be so arranged that it is raised higher, by six feet in height, than the other tables or benches of the court; and at it, apart from the Emperor alone, or the King of the Romans, no one at all shall be seated on the day of a solemn court.

units.la: 2. Sedes vero & mensa Imperatricis sive Reginæ parabitur à latere in aula; ita quod ipsa mensa tribus pedibus Imperiali sive Regali mensa sit bassior, & totidem pedibus eminentior supra sedes Principum Electorum. qui Principes suas inter se una eademque altitudine sedes habebunt, & mensas.
units.tr: 2. The seat and table of the Empress or Queen shall be prepared at the side in the hall, so that her table is three feet lower than the Imperial or royal table, and three feet higher than the seats of the Electoral Princes. These Princes shall have their seats and tables, all at one and the same height, among themselves.

units.la: 3. Infra sessionem Imperialem mensæ pro septem Principibus Electoribus, Ecclesiasticis & Secularibus, praeparentur, tres videlicet à dextris, & tres aliæ à sinistris, & septima directe versus faciem Imperatoris vel Regis, sicut superius in capitulo de sessionibus, & ordine Principum Electorum per nos est clarius definitum; ita etiam, quòd nullus alius cujuscunq; dignitatis, vel status existat, sedeat inter ipsos, vel ad mensas eorum.
units.tr: 3. Below the Imperial session, tables shall be prepared for the seven Electoral Princes, both ecclesiastical and secular: namely three on the right and three on the left, and the seventh directly facing the face of the Emperor or King, as we have more clearly defined above in the chapter on the sessions and the order of the Electoral Princes. Likewise, no other person of whatever dignity or rank shall sit between them or at their tables.

units.la: 4. Non liceat autem alicui praedictorum Secularium Principum Electorum, peracto officii sui debito, se locare ad mensam sibi paratam, donec alicui suorum Conprincipum Electorum ejus officium restat agendum; sed cum aliquis eorum, vel aliqui ministerium suum expleverint, ad praeparatas sibi mensas transeant, & juxta illas stando expectent, donec caeteri ministeria sua expleverint supradicta, & tunc demum omnes & singuli pariter ad mensas suas sibi positas se locabunt.
units.tr: 4. Moreover, once his duty of office has been discharged, it shall not be lawful for any of the aforesaid secular Electoral Princes to take his place at the table prepared for him, so long as the office still remains to be performed by one of his fellow Electoral Princes. Rather, when one or some of them have completed their ministry, they shall go over to the tables prepared for them and, standing beside them, wait until the others have completed the aforesaid ministries; and only then shall all and each of them together take their places at the tables set for them.

units.la: 5. Invenimus etiam ex clarissimis relatibus, & traditionibus antiquorum, illud à tempore, cujus contrarii jam non habetur memoria, per eos, qui nos praecesserūt, feliciter esse jugiter observatum, ut Regis Romanorum futuri Imperatoris, in civitate Franckenford celebraretur electio, & prima coronatio Aquisgrani, & in oppido Nuremberg prima sua Regalis curia haberetur. Quapropter certis ex causis etiam futuris praemissa servari debere temporibus declaramus, nisi praemissis omnibus, seu eorum alicui, impedimentum legitimum obviaret.
units.tr: 5. We have also found, from the most clear reports and the traditions of the ancients, that from a time whose contrary is no longer remembered, it has been happily and continually observed by those who went before us that the election of the future King of the Romans and Emperor be held in the city of Frankfurt, his first coronation at Aachen, and his first royal court be held in the town of Nuremberg. Wherefore we declare that, for certain causes, the aforesaid things ought to be observed in future times as well, unless a lawful hindrance should stand in the way of all of them, or of any one of them.

units.la: 6. Quandocumque insuper aliquis Princeps Elector Ecclesiasticus, vel etiam Secularis, justo impedimento detentus, ad Imperialem curiam vocatus, venire non valens, nuncium vel procuratorem cujuscunque status, vel dignitatis transmiserit, missus ipse (licet loco mittentis juxta datum sibi ab comandatum, admitti debeat) in mensa tamen vel sede, quæ illi, qui ipsum transmittit, deputata fuerit, non sedebit.
units.tr: 6. Moreover, whenever any Electoral Prince, ecclesiastical or secular, detained by a just impediment and summoned to the Imperial court, is unable to come and sends a messenger or proxy of whatever rank or dignity, that person (although he ought to be admitted in place of the one sending him, according to the mandate given to him) shall not sit at the table or seat assigned to the one who sends him.

units.la: 7. Praeterea consummatis his, quæ in Imperiali qualibet curia, vel Regali fuerint pro tempore celebranda, recipiet Magister curiæ pro se totum ædificium, sive ligneum apparatum Imperialis, sive Regalis sessionis, ubi sederit Imperator, vel Rex Romanorum, cum Principibus Electoribus, ad celebrandas solemnes cutias, vel feuda, sicut praemittitur, Principibus conferenda.
units.tr: 7. Furthermore, when those things which are to be celebrated at the time in any Imperial or royal court have been completed, the Master of the Court shall take for himself the whole building, or wooden structure, of the Imperial or royal session where the Emperor or King of the Romans sat with the Electoral Princes, for the celebrating of solemn courts or the conferring of fiefs upon the Princes, as has been set out above.

units.la: CAP. XXIX.
units.tr: CAP. XXIX.

units.la: DE IVRIBVS OFFICIALIVM, DVM PRINCIPES FEVDA sua ab Imperatore vel Rege Romanorum recipiunt.
units.tr: ON THE RIGHTS OF THE OFFICIALS WHEN THE PRINCES RECEIVE THEIR FIEFS FROM THE EMPEROR OR THE KING OF THE ROMANS.

units.la: DEcernimus hoc Imperiali edicto, ut Principes Electores Ecclesiastici, vel etiam Seculares, dum feuda seu regalia ab Imperatore vel Rege recipiunt, ad dandum vel solvendum aliquid nulli penitus sint astricti. nam pecunia, quæ tali praetextu persolvitur, Officiatis debetur. cum ergo ipsi Principes Electores, cunctis Imperialis curiæ praesint officiis, suos etiam habentes in hujusmodi officiis substitutos, datos ad hoc à Romanis Principibus & dotatos, videretur absurdum, quòd substituti Officiales, à suis superioribus quocunque quæsito colore exenia postularent; nisi forte ipsi Principes Electores sponte & liberaliter his aliquid largirentur.
units.tr: By this Imperial edict we decree that the Princes Electors, whether ecclesiastical or secular, when they receive fiefs or regalia from the Emperor or the King, are in no way bound to give or pay anything to anyone. For the money that is paid under such a pretext is owed to the officials. Since the Princes Electors themselves preside over all the offices of the Imperial court, and have their own substitutes in such offices, appointed and endowed for this purpose by the Roman princes, it would seem absurd that substitute officials should demand gifts from their superiors under any pretext whatever; unless, perhaps, the Princes Electors themselves freely and generously bestow something on them.

units.la: 2. Porro, cæteri Principes Imperii, Ecclesiastici vel Seculares, dum praedicto modo eorum aliquis feuda sua ab Imperatore Romanorum, vel à Rege, suscipit, dabit Officialibus Imperialis, sive Regalis curiæ, sexaginta tres marcas argenti, cum uno fertone; nisi eorum aliquis privilegio seu indulto Imperiali vel Regali tueri se posset, & probare se solutū vel exemptum à talibus, aut etiam aliquibus cunq; , quæ solvi in susceptione feudorum hujusmodi consuevissent. Prædictarum insuper sexaginta trium marcarum, & fertonis divisionem facit Magister curiæ Imperialis seu Regalis, hoc modo; Primò enim decem marcas pro semetipso reservans, dabit Cancellario Imperialis, sive Regalis curiæ decem marcas; magistris, notariis, & dictatoribus, tres marcas; & sigillatori pro cera, & pergameno unum fertonem; ita videlicet, quòd Cancellarius, & Notarii, Principi recipienti feudum, nomine ad aliud, quam ad dandum sibi testimonialem recepti feudi, seu simplicis investiturae litteram alterius. Item dabit Magister curiæ Pincernæ de Limburg, de præfata pecunia decem marcas; Magistro Coquinæ de Nortemberg, decem marcas; similiter Vicemarescallo de Pappenheim, decem marcas; & Camerario de Falckenstein, decem marcas. Tali tamen conditione, si ipsi & eorum quilibet in hujusmodi curiis solemnibus præsentialiter adsint in suis officiis ministrando; si vero ipsi, vel aliqui eorum absentes fuerint, extunc Officiales Imperialis sive Regalis curiæ, qui talibus præfuni ossiciis, eorum, quorum supplent absentiam, singuli singulorum, sicut vicem, nomenq; & laborem sustinebunt, sic lucrum & commoda reportabunt.
units.tr: 2. Furthermore, when any of the other Princes of the Empire, ecclesiastical or secular, receives his fiefs in the aforesaid manner from the Emperor of the Romans or from the King, he shall give to the officials of the Imperial or Royal court sixty-three marks of silver with one ferto; unless he can protect himself by an Imperial or Royal privilege or indult, and prove that he has been paid or exempted from such charges, or from any other payments that were customarily made on the receipt of such fiefs. Moreover, the Master of the Imperial or Royal court makes the division of the aforesaid sixty-three marks and the ferto in this way: first, keeping ten marks for himself, he shall give ten marks to the Chancellor of the Imperial or Royal court; three marks to the masters, notaries and drafters; and one ferto to the sealer for wax and parchment; so that the Chancellor and the notaries shall receive nothing else from the Prince receiving the fief, except for giving him a testimonial of the fief received or a letter of simple investiture. Likewise, the Master of the court shall give ten marks of the said money to the Cupbearer of Limburg; ten marks to the Master of the Kitchen of Nortemberg; likewise ten marks to the Deputy Marshal of Pappenheim; and ten marks to the Chamberlain of Falckenstein. Yet on this condition: that they, and each of them, be personally present at such solemn courts, performing the duties of their offices; but if they, or any of them, are absent, then the officials of the Imperial or Royal court who preside over these offices shall each take the place, name and labour of those whose absence they supply, and shall receive the gain and advantages in the same way.

units.la: 3. Dum autem Princeps aliquis equo, vel alteri bestiæ insidens, feuda sua ab Imperatore recipit vel Rege, equus ille, seu bestia, cujuscumq; speciei sit, debetur superiori Marescallo, id est, Duci Saxoniæ, si præsens adfuerit; alioquin illi de Pappenheim, ejus Vicemarescallo; aut illo absente, Imperialis, sive Regalis curiæ Marescallo.
units.tr: 3. When any Prince, sitting on a horse or other beast, receives his fiefs from the Emperor or the King, that horse or beast, of whatever kind it be, is owed to the chief Marshal, that is, the Duke of Saxony, if he is present; otherwise to the Pappenheimer, his Deputy Marshal; or, if he too is absent, to the Marshal of the Imperial or Royal court.

units.la: CAP. XXXI. DE INSTITVTIONE PRINCIPVM ELECTO- RVM in linguis.
units.tr: ## CHAPTER XXXI. ON THE TRAINING OF THE ELECTORAL PRINCES IN LANGUAGES.

units.la: CVM Sacri Romani Celsitudo Imperii, diversarum nationum moribus, vita, & idiomate distinctarum, leges habeat & gubernacula moderari, dignum est, & cunctorum sapientum judicio censetur expediens, quòd Electores Principes ipsius Imperii columnæ & latera, diversorum idiomatum & linguarum differentiis instruantur; ut plures intelligant, & à pluribus intelligantur, qui plurimorum necessitatibus relevandis Cæsareæ Sublimitati assistunt, in partem sollicitudinis constituti.
units.tr: Since the Holy Roman Empire, whose majesty rules over nations distinguished by different customs, ways of life and idioms, has laws and governance to administer, it is fitting, and by the judgment of all wise men deemed expedient, that the Electoral Princes, the pillars and supports of the Empire itself, be instructed in the differences of the various idioms and languages, so that they may understand more people and be understood by more, since they stand by Caesar's lofty majesty in relieving the needs of many and are placed in a share of its concerns.

units.la: 2. Quapropter statuimus, ut Illustrium Principum, puta Regis Bohemiæ, Comitis Palatini Rheni, Ducis Saxoniæ, & Marchionis Brandenburgensis, Electorum filii, vel hæredes & successores, cum verisimiliter Theutonicum idioma sibi naturaliter inditum scire præsumantur, & ab infantia didicisse, incipiendo à septimo ætatis suæ anno, in , , ac linguis instruitur; ita quòd infra quartumdecimum ætatis annum existant in talibus juxta datam sibi à Deo gratiam eruditi; cum illud non solum utile, imo ex causis præmissis summè necessarium habeatur; eò quòd linguæ ut plurimum ad usum, & necessitatem Sacri Imperii frequentari sint solitæ, & in his plusquam dua ipsius Imperii negotia ventilentur.
units.tr: 2. Therefore we decree that the sons, or heirs and successors, of the illustrious princes who are Electors, namely the King of Bohemia, the Count Palatine of the Rhine, the Duke of Saxony and the Margrave of Brandenburg, be instructed in the German language, which is presumed to be naturally implanted in them and learned from infancy, and that from the seventh year of their age they be instructed in ... and in languages; so that by their fourteenth year they be educated in these things according to the grace God has given them. This is held not only to be useful but, for the reasons stated above, most necessary, because the languages have customarily been used mostly for the needs and business of the Holy Empire, and more than two of the Empire's affairs are discussed in them.

units.la: 3. Hunc autem proficiendi modum in præmissis ponimus observandum, ut relinquatur optioni parentum, ut filios, si quos habuerint, seu proximos, quos in Principatibus sibi credunt venturos, ad loca dirigant, in quibus de hujusmodi possint linguagiis edoceri, vel in propriis domibus pædagogos, instructores, & pueros consocios in his peritos eis adjungant, quorum conversatione pariter & doctrina in linguis ipsis valeant erudiri. Ipsi Galli trium linguarum idioma, scil. Italicum, Gallicum & Hispanicum, vocant Romanum, unde fluxerunt.
units.tr: 3. We direct that the manner of learning these things be left to the choice of parents, who may either send their sons, or nearest relatives whom they believe will come into the principalities, to places where they can be taught these languages, or attach to them in their own homes tutors, instructors and boys skilled in these languages as companions, through whose company and teaching they may be instructed in the languages. The French themselves call the idiom of the three languages, namely Italian, French and Spanish, Roman, from which they sprang.

units.la: CAROLI IV. IMPER. AUG. CONSTITUTIO DE FORESTARIIS ET ZEIDLARIIS.
units.tr: CONSTITUTION OF CHARLES IV, EMPEROR AUGUSTUS, CONCERNING THE FORESTERS AND BEEKEEPERS.

units.la: IN nomine sanctæ & individuæ Trinitatis feliciter, Amen. Carolus Quartus divina favente clementia Romanorum Imperator semper Augustus, & Boëmiæ Rex, ad perpetuam rei memoriam. Accedentes Majestatis nostræ præsentiam dilecti fideles nostri cives civitatis nostræ Nurnbergensis sua nobis conquestione monstrarunt, qualiter literæ & privilegia ipsorum, quas & quæ a nostra Celsitudine, necnon à recolendæ memoriæ Divis Imperatoribus & Regibus Romanorum, prædecessoribus nostris super sylvis & nemoribus ad civitatem Nurnbergensem spectantibus, pro earum reformatione obtinent, & obtinuisse noscuntur, per forestarios, custodes, & alios officiales eorundem nemorum, & per nonnullas alias personas, in certis clausulis & articulis earundem litterarum temere violantur, necipsis observantur & attenduntur eo modo, prout merito & de jure forent observandæ, in eorundem civium & civitatis, ac nostrum & Imperii præjudicium, & dispendium non modicum & jacturam; eidem Majestati nostræ humiliter & devotè supplicantes, quatenus super præmissis maissis gratiose ipsis consulere, ac de salubri & opportuno remedio providere, literisq; ipsorum super eisdem sylvis in urbe Romana, tempore Coronationis nostræ in Imperatorē, per eos à nobis impetratis, & sub sigillo cereo nostræ Majestatis obtentis, sub Imperiali typario & Bulla aurea confirmare, innovare & approbare dignaremur. Quarum tenor per omnia sequitur in hæc verba:
units.tr: In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, happily, Amen. Charles IV, by the favour of divine clemency Roman Emperor, always Augustus, and King of Bohemia, to the perpetual memory of the matter. Our beloved and faithful citizens of our city of Nuremberg, coming into the presence of our Majesty, showed us by their complaint that their letters and privileges, which they hold and are known to have held from our Highness, and also from the Emperors and Kings of the Romans of blessed memory, our predecessors, concerning the forests and groves belonging to the city of Nuremberg, for their reform, are rashly violated by the foresters, the wardens, and other officials of those groves, and by certain other persons, in certain clauses and articles of those letters; and that they are not observed or heeded in the manner in which they ought rightly and lawfully to be observed, to the no small prejudice, loss and damage of those citizens and of the city, and of us and the Empire. Humbly and devoutly beseeching our Majesty that, concerning the aforesaid matters, we would graciously consult them and provide a wholesome and fitting remedy, and deign to confirm, renew and approve their letters concerning those forests, obtained from us by them in the city of Rome at the time of our coronation as Emperor, and secured under our wax seal, under the Imperial seal and golden bull. The tenor of these, in all things, follows in these words:

units.la: Nos C A R O L U S Quartus divina favente clementia Romanorum Imperator semper Augustus, & Boëmiæ Rex. Notum facimus universis præsentes literas inspecturis, quòd respicientes & confidentes defectus & dampna, qui & quæ nobis & Imperio quotidiè proveniunt in nostris & Imperii sylvis & nemoribus prope Nurmberg litis. Et quia dampna cadè ex notoria informatione cognoscimus, auctoritate nostra Imperiali, in loco ubi primò Romæ in Monasterio S. Petri in Imperatorem coronati fuimus, infra Missarum solemnia donamus & confirmamus civibus de Consilio civitatis Nurembergensis, fidelibus nostris dilectis, omnibusq; eorū successoribus, pro custodia & salvamento earundem sylvarum, infrascripta jura, constitutiones & statuta pro juribus perpetuis habendis.
units.tr: We, Charles IV, by the favour of divine clemency Roman Emperor, always Augustus, and King of Bohemia, make known to all who shall inspect the present letters that, considering and being aware of the defects and damages which daily arise for us and the Empire in our forests and groves near Nuremberg, and because we know the damages from reliable information, by our Imperial authority, in the place where we were first crowned Emperor at Rome in the Monastery of St Peter, during the solemn Masses, we grant and confirm to the citizens of the council of the city of Nuremberg, our beloved and faithful subjects, and to all their successors, for the protection and preservation of those forests, the following rights, constitutions and statutes, to be held as perpetual rights.

units.la: 1. Inprimis, q omnes Officiales, Forestarii & Mellicidæ, qui Zeidlaru vulgariter nücupantur, super utrisq; sylvis utrobiq; & ex utraq; parte fluvii Pegnitz, quādo ex parte Consulū civitatis Nurebergensis requiruntur, singulis annis semel tenentur venire ad Consilium civitatis Nurembergensis, & ad Sanctos jurare, cōstanter observare & tenere, quicquid prædicti Cives de Consilio civitatis Nurebergensis deliberaverint, pro Imperio & civitate ipsorū, quod utile fit eisdē sylvis: & debent etiā accusare & nunciare per dictum eorum juramentum, quicquid prædictis sylvis poterit esse nocivum & damnosum.
units.tr: 1. First, that all officials, foresters and beekeepers, who are commonly called Zeidlaru, in both forests on either side and on both banks of the river Pegnitz, are bound, whenever they are summoned on the part of the council of the citizens of Nuremberg, once a year to come before the council of the city of Nuremberg and to swear on the saints that they will constantly observe and maintain whatever the aforesaid citizens of the council of the city of Nuremberg decide for the Empire and their city, as useful to those forests; and they are also to report and denounce, by the said oath, whatever may be harmful and damaging to the aforesaid forests.

units.la: 2. Quilibet etiam Forestarius super manso suo forestali, qui vulgariter forstbub nuncupatur, tenebitur residere, & non plus. Et idem Forestarius, dum in eodem manso suo forestali resederit, debet impignorare ibidem, & nusquam aliunde: & quicumq; aliunde impignoraret, quàm in manso forestali, super quo residet, illud pro spolio reputari debet & censeri.
units.tr: 2. Likewise, every forester is bound to reside on his forester's holding, which is commonly called forstbub, and not elsewhere. And the same forester, while he resides on his forester's holding, ought to take pledges there and nowhere else; and whoever takes a pledge elsewhere than on the forester's holding where he resides, that pledge ought to be reckoned and regarded as plunder.

units.la: 3. Prædicti etiam Officiales forestarii, aliiq; servitores ipsorū, nulli tenentur vendere aliqua ligna de ambabus sylvis, nec alicui dare licentiam ducendi ligna de eisdem sylvis, exceptis illis, qui antiquitùs de eisdem sylvis utebantur, & qui jus in hoc habere noscuntur.
units.tr: 3. The aforesaid forester officials and their servants are bound not to sell any wood from either forest, nor to give anyone permission to carry wood from those forests, except those who have from ancient times used those forests and are known to have a right in this matter.

units.la: 4. Supremi etiam Forestarii in propriis eorum personis in civitate Nurembergensi residere tenebuntur. Si verò vellent extra ipsam civitatem residere, extunc nullum jus in prædictis sylvis, neq; super Forestarios habere debebunt, donec eos in prædicta civitate contigerit residere.
units.tr: 4. The chief foresters are also bound to reside in their own persons in the city of Nuremberg. But if they wished to reside outside that city, then they shall have no right in the aforesaid forests, nor over the foresters, until it happens that they reside in the aforesaid city.

units.la: 5. Nullus etiam Officialium seu Forestariorum dictarum sylvarum mansos suos aut jura eorum, quæ in eisdem sylvis obtinent, ullo modo Nobilibus aut militibus vendere debebunt, quoniam illud Imperio & dictæ civitati in eisdem sylvis esset nocivum & damnosum.
units.tr: 5. Neither shall any of the officials or foresters of the said forests sell their holdings or their rights, which they hold in those same forests, in any way to nobles or knights, since that would be harmful and damaging to the Empire and to the said city in those forests.

units.la: 6. Volumus etiā, qualitercumq; quolibet anno prædictæ sylvæ per præsatos cives dispositæ fuerint & ordinatæ, quòd eandē ordinationem & statuta præfati Officiales, Forestarii & Mellicidæ earundem sylvarum, vel quicunq; ad easdem sylvas pertinet, easdem constitutiones constanter & firmiter debeant observare. Et si ipsi illud transgrederentur, & nollent esse obedientes, in quibuscunq; acticulis priùs scriptis & expressis, vel quæ adhuc pro utilitate sylvarū ordinaretur, & super eo statueretur, hoc fieret: extunc Judex & Cives prædictæ civitatis Nurebergensis possunt & debebunt eosdē transgressores & inobedientes corrigere, in rebus & personis, prout ipsis videbitur prædictos deliquisse.
units.tr: 6. We also will that, in whatever manner the aforesaid forests are arranged and ordained each year by the said citizens, the aforesaid officials, foresters and beekeepers of those forests, or whoever pertains to those forests, shall constantly and firmly observe the same ordinances and statutes. And if they should transgress this and refuse to obey, whether in any articles previously written and set out, or in whatever shall yet be ordained for the benefit of the forests and decreed on that matter, then the judge and the citizens of the aforesaid city of Nuremberg may and shall correct those transgressors and disobedient persons, in their goods and persons, as it shall seem to them that the aforesaid persons have offended.

units.la: 7. Castrū etiam Brun nuncupatū, & in dictis sylvis situm, & quod ad nos & Imperium spectat & pertinet, prædictis civibus Nurembergensibus committimus omni eo modo & intentione, & cum omnibus juribus, sicut nos castrum nostrum & turrim supra Nuremberg situm ipsis duximus committendum, ut sit ipsis civibus cum eisdem parendum & intendendum, prout in literis, quas eis super hoc dedimus, continetur expressum.
units.tr: 7. Also the castle called Brun, situated in the said forests, and which belongs and pertains to us and the Empire, we entrust to the aforesaid citizens of Nuremberg, in every manner and intention, and with all rights, just as we have decided to entrust to them our castle and tower situated above Nuremberg, so that the same citizens shall obey and attend to it, as is expressly set out in the letters which we have given them on this matter.

units.la: 8. Et sicut antedictis civibus nostris Nurembergensibus supradicta jura, statuta, & constitutiones priūs tanquā Romanorum Rex, & sub sigillo nostro Regali scriptis nostris cōcessimus & cōfirmavimus: sic auctoritate Imperiali & ex certa nostra scientia iplis eadē jura & statuta innovamus & confirmamus, præsentium, sub nostræ Imperialis Majestatis sigillo, testimonio literarum. Datum Romæ, anno Domini millesimo trecentesimo quinquagesimo quinto, in sancto die Paschæ, sicut in Imperatorem coronati, Regnorum nostrorum anno nono, Imperii verò primo.
units.tr: 8. And just as we previously granted and confirmed the aforesaid rights, statutes and constitutions to our aforesaid citizens of Nuremberg, as Roman King, and written under our royal seal, so now, by Imperial authority and from our certain knowledge, we renew and confirm the same rights and statutes to them, by the testimony of these present letters under the seal of our Imperial Majesty. Given at Rome, in the year of the Lord 1355, on the holy day of Easter, in the year of our coronation as Emperor, in the ninth year of our reign, and the first of the Empire.

units.la: 9. Nos itaq; cōsiderātes gravia & irrecuperabilia damna, quæ nobis & sacro Imperio ac prædictæ civitati Nurembergensi, ex prædictorū nemorū devastatione provenerunt, ac quotidie & incessanter proveniunt & emergunt: volentesq; pro ipsorū reformatione, melioratione & augmēto oportuna adhibere remedia, prædictorumq; civiū Nurembergensiū justis & rationabilibus, ut ipsorum privilegia illibata remaneant, & in omnibus eorū articulis contentis in eisdē incōcusse inviolabiliterq; eis observēntur, gratiosius annuentes, matura deliberatione Principum & Procerum, aliorumq; nostrorum fidelium prǣhabita, de Imperialis mansuetudinis nostræ magnificētia suprascriptas literas & privilegia, ac omnia & singula in eisdē contenta in omnibus eorum clausulis, punctis & articulis, prout de verbo verbum tenor ipsarum præsentibus inseritur & exprimitur, & de plenitudine Imperatoriæ Majestatis, ac de certa nostra scientia, virtute præsentiū approbamus, innovamus, ratificamus, & præsentibus confirmamus: volentes ac decernentes expressè, ut prædictæ literæ, & omnia contenta in iisdē, perpetuis temporibus inviolabilis roboris & efficacię obtineant firmitatem, quodq; ab omnibus inconrulse & inviolabiliter debeant observari; adjicientes expressè, ut si Magistri forestæ, Forestarii aut Mellicidæ Zeidlaru vulgariter nücupati, aliiq; Officiales & Custodes nemorū, contra prædictā nostrā confirmationem quicquam facerent & attentarent, prædictisq; civibus eorum literas & contenta in eisdem eisdem transgredeertur, vel non observarent, quod extunc ipsi & omnes transgressores ab eorum officiis & utilitatibus, quæ & quas in dictis nemoribus habuerunt, cadant & sint penitus destituti.
units.tr: 9.
