We therefore, considering the grave and irreparable damages which have arisen for us, for the holy Empire and for the said city of Nuremberg, from the devastation of the said groves, and which arise and emerge daily and without cease, and wishing to apply fitting remedies for their reform, improvement and increase, and graciously assenting to the just and reasonable requests of the said citizens of Nuremberg, so that their privileges may remain unimpaired and be observed by all in all the articles contained in them, without disturbance and inviolably, after mature deliberation with the princes and nobles and our other faithful subjects, by the magnificence of our Imperial clemency, and out of the fullness of Imperial Majesty and from our certain knowledge, by virtue of the present letters, we approve, renew, ratify and by these presents confirm the aforesaid letters and privileges, and all and each of the things contained in them, in all their clauses, points and articles, as the tenor of the same is inserted and expressed word for word in these presents; willing and expressly decreeing that the aforesaid letters, and all things contained in them, shall have the firm force and efficacy of an inviolable validity for all perpetual times, and that they shall be observed by all without disturbance and inviolably. We add expressly that if the masters of the forest, the foresters or the beekeepers, commonly called Zeidlaru, or other officials and wardens of the groves, should do or attempt anything contrary to this our confirmation, or should transgress or fail to observe the said letters and the contents of them towards the said citizens, then they themselves and all transgressors shall fall from and be utterly deprived of their offices and the benefits which they have had in the said groves.

units.la: 10. Volumus insuper, & sub gratiæ nostræ obtentu districtè mandamus, ut quicquid de prædictis sylvis defertis & devastatis, quæ vulgariter furrent nuncupantur, supradicti Magistri forestæ, Forestarii vel Mellicidæ, aut alii Officiales prædictorum nemorum, ultra numerum ducentorum quæ morgen vulgariter dicuntur, tenent aut occupant; quod illud, & tota excrescentia illorum nemorum in Imperio ac dictæ Civitati pro reformatione ipsorum nemorum absq; contradictione quaelibet, habere jacere dimittant, & ulterius de eadem relidua excrescentia ultra prædictum numerum nemoris non intromittant. Volumus namque ac nostræ intentionis existit, ut prædicta excrescentia devastarum nemorum, quæ furreut dicuntur, ad usus dictorum nemorum redeant & applicentur, & suis temporibus in nemora crescant & redigantur.
units.tr: 10. We will moreover, and under the favour of our grace strictly command, that whatever of the aforesaid deserted and devastated forests, which are commonly called furren, the aforesaid masters of the forest, foresters or beekeepers, or other officials of the aforesaid groves, hold or occupy beyond the number of two hundred which are commonly called morgen, they shall let that, and the whole growth of those groves, go to the Empire and to the said city for the reform of those groves, without any contradiction whatever, and shall not further intrude upon the remaining growth beyond the aforesaid number of the grove. For we will, and it is our intention, that the aforesaid growth of the devastated groves, which are called furreut, shall return and be applied to the uses of the said groves, and in their proper time grow and be brought back into the groves.

units.la: 11. Quicquid insuper prætati Magistri forestæ, Forestarii aut Mellicidæ, aut alii Officiales jam dictis ducentis jugeribus, aut alias agris, pascuis, pratis, vel juribus, antiquitus ad prædicta nemora spectantibus, vendiderunt, aut in hereditatem converterunt, vel quovis alio modo a nemore ipsius proprietate ipsius alienarunt: illud totum taliter venditum, vel in hereditatem conversum, vel modolibet alienatum, absq; dilatione ulteriori qualibet, ad Imperium & ad proprietatem & usum ctorum nemorum liberè reducere & recuperare debebunt & tenentur. Quod si non facerent, prætati cives nostri Nurembergenses, vice & auctoritate nostra & Imperii, de hujusmodi juribus venditis vel alienatis, aut in agros seu hereditatem conversis, si liberè intromittant, & proprietatem & usum nemorum ipsorum illicò reducere tenebuntur.
units.tr: 11. Moreover, whatever the aforesaid masters of the forest, foresters, or Mellicidae, or other officials have sold, or converted into inherited property, or otherwise alienated from the ownership of the woods, whether of the said two hundred acres or of fields, pastures, meadows, or rights formerly belonging to the said woods, all that so sold, converted into inheritance, or alienated in any way, they shall be bound and obliged to recover and restore freely to the Empire and to the ownership and use of the said woods, without any further delay. If they should fail to do so, our aforesaid citizens of Nuremberg, in our place and by the authority of ourselves and the Empire, shall be bound to take back at once, freely, the ownership and use of the woods, if they intervene concerning such rights that have been sold or alienated, or converted into fields or inheritance.

units.la: 12. Volumus insuper & decernimus districtè, gratiæ nostræ sub obtentu præcipientes, ut nominati Magistri forestæ, Forestarii, Mellicidæ, vel alii Officiales prædictorum nemorum, habent & habere noscuntur jura ipsorum, quæ nobis & Imperio in prædictis sylvis & nemoribus habent & habere noscuntur omnino hominum vel personæ, cujuscunq; status, dignitatis, conditionis, seu præeminentiæ existant, vel quocunque nomine nuncupatur, vendere, impignorare, obligare, permutare, vel donare ratione debeant aut præsumant. Et quicunque eorum contra hoc quovis modo faceret vel attentaret, vel per quemcunq; modum attemptare præsumeret: ille ab omnibus officiis & juribus, quæ in dictis nemoribus habebat, vel habere poterat, cadat & eisdem privarus sit & perpetuò destitutus: prætatiq; cives nostri Nurembergenses extunc de hujusmodi juribus & officiis, tanquam ad nos & Imperium devolutis, auctoritate nostra & Imperii se intromittere tenebuntur.
units.tr: 12. Furthermore, we will and firmly decree, under penalty of forfeiting our favour, that the named masters of the forest, foresters, Mellicidae, or other officials of the said woods, who have, or are known to have, rights in the said forests and woods which are due to us and the Empire, shall not, on any pretext, sell, pledge, mortgage, exchange, or give them away, whatever the man or person of whatever status, dignity, condition, or rank, or by whatever name they are called. And whoever of them does or attempts this in any way, or presumes to attempt it by any means, shall fall from and be deprived and permanently stripped of all offices and rights which he had or could have had in the said woods; and our aforesaid citizens of Nuremberg shall then be bound to intervene, by our authority and that of the Empire, concerning such rights and offices, as having devolved to us and the Empire.

units.la: 13. Nulli igitur omnino hominum liceat contra præsentis nostræ confirmationis & innovationis gratiam & indultum, ac omnia suprascripta & eorū quodlibet facere vel venire, vel aliquo temerario quoquo modo attemptare. Si quis verò contra præmissa, vel aliquod præmissorum fecerit vel attemptare præsumpserit, gravem indignationis nostræ aculeum, & ultra pœnas superius specificatas, pœnas alias gravissimas ad arbitrium proprium infligendas se noverit inevitabiliter incursurum.
units.tr: 13. Let no one at all of mankind therefore be permitted to act against the grace and indulgence of this our present confirmation and renewal, or to do or bring about any of the things written above, or in any rash way to attempt them. But if anyone shall act against the foregoing, or presume to attempt any part of them, he shall know that he will inevitably incur the severe sting of our indignation, and, beyond the penalties specified above, other most severe penalties to be inflicted at our own discretion.

units.la: Signum Serenissimi Principis & Domini, Domini CAROLI Quarti, Romanorum Imperatoris invictissimi, & gloriosissimi Boëmiæ Regis.
units.tr: Seal of the Most Serene Prince and Lord, Lord Charles the Fourth, most invincible Emperor of the Romans and most glorious King of Bohemia.

units.la: Testes hujus rei sunt: Johannes Olomucensis, Johannes Argentinensis, Venerabiles Theodoricus Mindensis, Ecclesiarum Episcopi. Gerhardus Spirensis, & Albertus Syverinensis
units.tr: Witnesses to this matter are: John, Bishop of Olomouc; John, Bishop of Strasbourg; the venerable Theodoric, Bishop of Minden; Gerhard, Bishop of Speyer; and Albert, Bishop of Schwerin.

units.la: Et Henricus Abbas Fuldensis, Serenissimæ Annæ Romanorum Imperatricis Archiaccellarius. Bolko Svvidnicensis, Illustres & Przymislaus Thetschinensis Duces. Burchardus Burggravius Magdeburgensis, Magister Curiæ, Spectabiles Comes de Retz. Czenko de Lyppa, supremus Marescallus, & Camerarius Regni Boëmiæ, Ac Nobiles Sdenko de Sternberg, Judex Curiæ, Busko de Wlhartitz, Magistri Camerae. & Hasko de Sverertiz
units.tr: And Henry, Abbot of Fulda, Archchancellor of the most serene Anna, Empress of the Romans; Bolko, Duke of Schweidnitz, and Przemysl, Duke of Teschen, illustrious dukes; Burchard, Burgrave of Magdeburg, Master of the Court; the distinguished Count of Retz; Czenko of Lipa, Supreme Marshal and Chamberlain of the Kingdom of Bohemia; and the noblemen Sdenko of Sternberg, Judge of the Court; Busko of Wlhartitz, Masters of the Chamber; and Hasko of Svertiz.

units.la: Et alii quàm plures, nostri & sacri Imperii Principes, Nobiles & fideles, præsentium auctoritate typario Imperialis Majestatis nostræ impressa testimonio literarum. Datum Pragæ, anno Domini millesimo trecentesimo quinquagesimo octavo, Indictione undecima, sexto Calend. Novembris, Regnorum nostrorum anno decimo tertio, Imperii vero quarto.
units.tr: And many other princes, nobles and faithful men of our holy Empire, by the authority of these present letters, impressed with the seal of our Imperial Majesty as testimony. Given at Prague, in the year of the Lord one thousand three hundred and fifty-eight, in the eleventh indiction, on the sixth day before the Calends of November, in the thirteenth year of our kingdoms, and the fourth of the Empire.

units.la: Ego Johannes Dei gratia Luthomuschlensis Episcopus, sacræ Imperialis Aulæ Cancellarius, ac Rex.
units.tr: I, John, by the grace of God Bishop of Olomouc, Chancellor of the sacred Imperial Court, and King.

units.la: Reverendi in Christo Domini, Gerlaci Moguntini Archiepiscopi, sacri Imperii per Germaniam Archicancellarii, recognovi.
units.tr: I, Gerlach, Archbishop of Mainz in Christ the Lord, Archchancellor of the holy Empire through Germany, have attested it.

units.la: CAROLI IV. IMPER. AUG. FORMULA
units.tr: FORMULA OF EMPEROR CHARLES IV, AUGUSTUS

units.la: De juribus ac privilegiis Principum Imperii.
units.tr: On the rights and privileges of the Princes of the Empire.

units.la: In nomine sanctæ & individuæ Trinitatis feliciter, Amen. Carolus IV. divina favente clementia Romanorum Imperator Semper-Augustus, & Boëmiæ Rex, ad perpetuam rei memoriam. Quamvis rationabili fide dignorum testimonio dudum informata sit nostra Serenitas, qualiter Spectabiles Nurmbergenses Burggravii ab antiquo tempore nobilitate sua Illustribus Principibus pariter fuerint & fuerint, & adhuc in omnibus & singulis nobilitate Principum potiantur: quia tamen non prædecessores eorum, hujusmodi libertates & honores in aliqua parte sic neglexisse noscuntur, ut prosequuti non sint tali diligentia, quod in hominum communi permanerent notitia, sicut dignitas & honor officii Burggraviatus hujusmodi meriro requirebat. Quapropter attendentes, quod Burggraviatus Nurmbergensis, sacri Imperii nobile membrum existit, ad hoc intentio nostra ratione dirigitur, quod idem Burggravii, hæredes & successores eorum, penes hujusmodi honores, gratias & dignitates adjutorio Imperialis clementiæ rite permaneant in futurum. Et ob hoc, animo deliberato Principum, Comitum, Baronum & Procerum sacri Imperii accedente consilio, de certa scientia, & de Imperialis potestatis plenitudine sententiamus, declaramus & dicimus:
units.tr: In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, happily, Amen. Charles IV, by the favour of divine clemency Roman Emperor, ever Augustus, and King of Bohemia, to the perpetual memory of the matter. Although Our Serenity was long ago informed, by the reasonable testimony of trustworthy men, that the Illustrious Burgraves of Nuremberg have from ancient times been, and still are, equal in nobility to the Illustrious Princes, and enjoy in all and each respect the nobility of Princes; nevertheless, since their predecessors are known to have so neglected these liberties and honours in some part that they did not pursue them with such diligence as would keep them in the common knowledge of men, as the dignity and honour of the office of Burgrave of this kind required. Wherefore, considering that the Burgraviate of Nuremberg is a noble member of the holy Empire, Our intention is directed, for this reason, that the same Burgraves, their heirs and successors, may by the aid of Imperial clemency rightly retain these honours, favours and dignities in future. And therefore, with the deliberate mind of the Princes, Counts, Barons and Nobles of the holy Empire giving their counsel, from certain knowledge and from the fullness of Imperial power, We decide, declare and state:

units.la: 2. Quod Spectabilis Fridericus Burggravius Nurmbergensis, hæredes & successores sui Burggravii Nurmbergenses in perpetuum Illustrium Principum sacri Romani Imperii juribus, dignitatibus, libertatibus & honoribus gaudere & potiri debeat, in Judicibus & in omnibus aliis casibus & negotiis, quæcunque sint, aut quibus valeant speciali nominibus appellari.
units.tr: 2. That the Honourable Frederick, Burgrave of Nuremberg, and his heirs and successors, the Burgraves of Nuremberg, ought to enjoy and possess in perpetuity the rights, dignities, liberties and honours of the Illustrious Princes of the holy Roman Empire, in judgments and in all other cases and affairs, whatever they may be, or by whatever special names they may be called.

units.la: 3. Et nominatim quod potestatem habeant cum Imperii sacri Principibus adinvenire, diffinire et dare juris sententias super omnibus causis & negotiis, sive corpus, res conspiciant vel honores: & hoc in Imperiali Curia vel alibi, ubicunque contingat Principes præsidere judiciis, vel loco Scabinorum.
units.tr: 3. And specifically, that they have power, together with the Princes of the holy Empire, to find, define and give judicial sentences concerning all causes and affairs, whether they concern the person, property or honours; and this in the Imperial Court or elsewhere, wherever it happens that Princes preside over judgments or in place of the Scabins.

units.la: 4. Quodq; ipsi Illustrium Principum jure potiantur & gaudeant, si ad actus duelli appellati vel provocati fuerint, seu ipsimet alios ad actus consimiles duellaniter provocarent, qui Illustrium Principum dignitate vel honore quomodolibet potirentur.
units.tr: 4. Moreover, they shall enjoy and possess the rights of the Illustrious Princes, if they are summoned or challenged to acts of duel, or if they themselves challenge others to similar acts of duel, who in any way hold the dignity or honour of the Illustrious Princes.

units.la: 5. Sententiamus, declaramus & dicimus etiam, quod præfatorum & successorum suorum homines in perpetuum, puta Milites, Clientes, Judices, cives & rustici, quilibet in suo statu, omnibus juribus, gratiis & prærogativis frui & potiri debeant, in rebus, honore, bonis, & omnibus aliis casibus & negotiis suis, quibus homines aliorum Illustrium Principum Imperii potiuntur; & gaudeant, quemadmodum ipsi Principes & homines eorum, hujusmodi libertates usque ad hæc tempora continuasse noscuntur, antiqua consuetudine vel de jure.
units.tr: 5. We also decide, declare and state that the men of the aforesaid Burgraves and their successors, namely soldiers, clients, judges, citizens and countrymen, each in his own station, ought in perpetuity to enjoy and possess all rights, favours and prerogatives in their property, honour, goods and all other cases and affairs, which the men of the other Illustrious Princes of the Empire possess and enjoy, just as the Princes themselves and their men are known to have maintained these liberties down to the present time, by ancient custom or by right.

units.la: 6. Sententiamus, declaramus & dicimus etiam, quod antedictorum Burggraviorum Nurmbergensium, hæredum & successorum suorum homines in perpetuum, videlicet Milites, Clientes, Judices, cives, rustici, & omnes servitores ac subsidies eorum, & omnia bona & homines ipsorum, coram alio judicio, nisi coram ipsis Burggraviis Nurmbergensibus, & eorum Judicibus, citari possint valeant; neq; obligati sint alibi comparere aut respondere cuiquam de objectis. Si vero adversus nostræ declarationis Edictum, ad aliqua alienja judicia citarentur, extunc decernimus citationem, sententias & omnia inde sequentia, carere viribus & nullius esse roboris aut momenti.
units.tr: 6. We also decide, declare and state that the men of the aforesaid Burgraves of Nuremberg, their heirs and successors, namely soldiers, clients, judges, citizens, countrymen, and all their servants and assistants, and all the goods and men of these, may in perpetuity be cited before no other court than before the said Burgraves of Nuremberg and their judges; nor are they bound to appear or answer to anyone elsewhere concerning the matters brought against them. But if, against the edict of this our declaration, they should be summoned to any foreign courts, then We decree that the summons, the sentences and everything following from them shall lack force and be of no validity or weight.

units.la: 7. Nolentes etiam ex hoc dictis Burggraviis, hæredibus & successoribus eorum in perpetuum, ominibus ipsorum conjunctim vel divisim, aliquod præjudicium generari, nisi forsitan anredictis ipsorum judicis notorie justiciam consequi non valeant: tunc & in eo casu actoribus ad Imperialem provocare Curiam, & ibi querela depolita recipere quod est.
units.tr: 7. We also do not wish any prejudice to arise from this to the said Burgraves, their heirs and successors in perpetuity, or to all of them jointly or severally, unless perhaps, in the judgment of the said Burgraves, they cannot obtain justice; then, and in that case only, the plaintiffs may appeal to the Imperial Court and there lodge their complaint and receive what is just.

units.la: 8. Considerantes etiam & in nostræ mentis acie solicitè revolventes, grata, fidelia & dudum servitia, quæ nobis & sacro Imperio præfati Burggravii Nurmbergenses, progenitores & successores eorum hactenus fecisse noscuntur, & facere debebunt & poterunt præstantius in futuro, hæredibus & successoribus eorum in perpetuum de speciali gratia, ac de certa nostra scientia contulimus, concedimus & conferimus in verum ac perpetuum feudum, omnes aurum, argentum, ferri, plumbi, stanni, ac omnium minerarum montana & fodinas, quæ in ipsorum territorio inventæ sunt hactenus, seu repertæ fuerunt in futurum, conditione tali, quod ipsi eosdem in utilitatem & commodum suum proprium convertere & applicare possint & sibi placitum voluntatis; quodq; ipsi hæredes & successores eorum in perpetuum, minerasque & omnia ab eis dependentia, sicut ad nostram Majestatem & sacrum Imperium noscuntur, cum omnibus juribus & utilitatibus, in verum & perpetuum feudum omni modo tenere & possidere debeant, impedimento quolibet procul moto.
units.tr: 8. Also considering, and carefully turning over in the eye of Our mind, the pleasing, faithful and long-standing services which the aforesaid Burgraves of Nuremberg, their ancestors and successors, are known to have rendered to Us and to the holy Empire until now, and which they will be bound and able to render more excellently in future, we have, from special grace and from certain knowledge, conferred, granted and bestowed upon their heirs and successors in perpetuity, as true and perpetual fief, all gold, silver, iron, lead and tin, and the mountains and mines of all metals, which have been found in their territory up to now, or shall be found in future; on condition that they may turn and apply these to their own use and advantage and as they please; and that they and their heirs and successors in perpetuity must hold and possess the mines and all things dependent upon them, as they are known to belong to Our Majesty and the holy Empire, with all rights and profits, in true and perpetual fief in every way, any impediment whatever being removed far away.

units.la: 9. Si, nos vel prædecessores nostri Divi Romanorum Imperatores vel Reges, aliquibus forte Principum Principibus, Comitibus, Baronibus liberis, Ministerialibus, Militibus, Clientibus, Civitatibus, Oppidis, Monasteriis, seu quibuslibet aliis, aliquas tales gratias, jura, & libertates dedisse minus hactenus daremus in posterum, quibus antedicti Burggravii Nurmbergensis, haeredes & successores necnon ipsorum dominia, & judicia provincialia in Nurmberg, debilitata forent aut laesa, vel debilitari possent in posterum; decernimus, quòd eadem donatio seu donationes ... praesentis nostrae declarationis indultum, nullam vim habeant, seu possint habere aliquale ... turum.
units.tr: 9. If We or our predecessors, the Divine Roman Emperors or Kings, have hitherto given, or in future should give, to any Princes, Counts, free Barons, ministerials, soldiers, clients, cities, towns, monasteries, or to any others, such favours, rights and liberties by which the aforesaid Burgrave of Nuremberg, his heirs and successors, and their lordships and provincial courts in Nuremberg, would be weakened or harmed, or could in future be weakened: We decree that the same gift or gifts ... by the indult of this our present declaration, shall have no force, nor be able to have any force ...

units.la: 10. Revocantes donationes hujusmodi de Imperialis potestatis plenitudine, si & in quantum praefatis Burggraviis, haeredibus & successoribus eorum censentur aliquod praejudicium generare, non obstantibus legibus & statutis Imperialibus publicis, communibus, municipalibus seu privatis, necnon usibus, ordinationibus & observantiis quibuscunque, scriptis vel non scriptis; & speciale expresse non obstante lege Imperiali seu statuto, quam vel quod pridem in civitate nostra Metensi consilio Principum fecimus, & conscribi atq; sigillari mandavimus, videlicet quòd nulli liceat ... tanorum vel minerae prorsus habere dominium, nisi duntaxat Principibus Electoribus, sicut legis ac statuti conditio plenius declaravit: & non obstantibus quibusve consuetudinibus ... cunq; modis introductae noscantur; decernentes, quòd haec omnia & eorum quodlibet, non obstant antedictis Burggraviis, in praefatis ipsorum dominiis, privilegiis, libertatibus, gratiis, & in quibus expressata sunt superius, aliquem errorem inducere, seu damnum, impedimentum, aut prejudicium generare, supplentes etiam omnem defectum, si quis in praesentibus nostris literis deprehendatur obscuritate verborum aut sententiarum aut solennitatis obmissae, vel quovis alio modo reperiatur, de Imperialis plenitudine potestatis.
units.tr: 10. Revoking such gifts by the fullness of Imperial power, if and insofar as they are judged to cause any prejudice to the aforesaid Burgraves, their heirs and successors; notwithstanding Imperial laws and public statutes, common, municipal or private, and likewise any customs, ordinances and observances of whatever kind, written or unwritten; and especially notwithstanding an Imperial law or statute which We lately made in Our city of Metz, with the counsel of the Princes, and ordered to be written down and sealed, namely that it is not lawful for anyone to hold any dominion over the mountains or mines at all, except only the Princes Electors, as the condition of the law and statute declared more fully; and notwithstanding any customs, of whatever kind they are known to have been introduced; decreeing that all these things, and each of them, shall not induce any error, nor cause any damage, impediment or prejudice, to the aforesaid Burgraves in their said lordships, privileges, liberties and favours, and in those things which have been expressed above; supplying also every defect, if anything in these Our present letters is found to be obscure in words or sentences, or to have omitted a formality, or is found defective in any other way, by the fullness of Imperial power.

units.la: 11. Nulli ergo hominum liceat hanc nostrae diffinitionis, declarationis, decreti, iahibitionis defectuum supplentionis paginam infringere, seu ei quovis ausu temerario contraire, sub poena marcarum auri purissimi, quam ab eo seu eis, qui contrafecerint, toties, quoties contrafactum fuerit, irremissibiliter exigi volumus: & ejus medietatem nostri Imperialis aerarii sive fisci: residuam vero partem injuriam passorum usibus decernimus applicandam. Qua poena soluta, vel non, semper in intentionis exsistu, quòd praefatae libertates, privilegia, litterae & gratiae, sub omnibus modis ... boad verbum, prout expressantur superius, absque impedimento quolibet, in suo robore permaneant.
units.tr: 11. Therefore let it be lawful for no man to infringe this page of Our definition, declaration, decree and supplying of defects, or to contravene it in any rash daring; under penalty of pure gold marks, which We wish to be exacted without remission from him or them who act against it, as often as it is contravened: one half to Our Imperial treasury or fisc, and the remaining part We decree to be applied to the uses of the injured party. Whether this penalty is paid or not, it is always Our intention that the aforesaid liberties, privileges, letters and favours shall remain in their force, in every way, word for word as they are expressed above, without any impediment whatever.

units.la: verent.
units.tr: ...should.

units.la: Signum Serenissimi Principis & Domini, Domini CAROLI IV. Rom. Imp. invictissimi & gloriosi. Boëmiae Reg s.
units.tr: Sign of the Most Serene Prince and Lord, Lord CHARLES IV, Roman Emperor, most invincible and glorious. King of Bohemia.

units.la: Testes hujus rei sunt: Venerabilis Gerlacus Moguntinensis Archiepiscopus, sacri Imperii per Alemaniam Archicancellarius [Rupertus senior Comes Palatinus Rheni, sacri Imperii Archidapifer,] | Principes Electores, &c. Illustres [Ludovicus Romanus Marchio Brandenburgensis & Lusatiae, sacri Imperii Archicamerarius]

units.la: Sub Bulla aureata typario Imperialis nostrae Majestatis impressa testimonio litterarum. Datum Nurmberg, anno Domini MCCCLXIII. Indictione quintadecima, XVI. Calend. Aprilis: Regnorum nostrorum anno XVII. Imperii vero VIII.
units.tr: Under the golden Bull, impressed with the seal of our Imperial Majesty, as witness of this letter. Given at Nuremberg, in the year of the Lord 1363, in the fifteenth indiction, on the sixteenth day before the Calends of April; in the seventeenth year of our kingdoms and the eighth of our empire.

units.la: Ego Johannes Dei gratia Luthomuschensis Episcopus, Sacrae Imperialis Aulae Cancellarius Reverendi in Christo Patris, Domini Gerlaci Moguntinensis Archiepiscopi, sacri Imperii per Germaniam Archicancellarii, recognovi.

units.tr: On the right and succession of the electors of Saxony.

units.la: IN nomine sanctae & individuae Trinitatis feliciter, Amen. CAROLUS Quartus divina favente clementia Romanorum Imperator, semper Augustus & Bohemiae Rex, ad perpetuam rei memoriam. quamvis sublimitas Caesareae dignitatis, in quam conditor orbis Nos sua pietatis clementia feliciter collocavit, jugiter mentem nostram sollicitet, ut cura pervigili, & laborum studiis nostrorum & Imperii sicut fidelium amputemus incommoda, eisque desideratae pacis amoenitatem, cubiter procuremus: ferventiori tamen affectu cor nostrum accenditur penes ea, quae sacri [illegible, ~20 letters]c ǵes Electores, quadam singularitate concernunt; eos præcipuè, quos Nobilitas, multiplicia virtutum insignia, & præclara fidei devotio, laudabilius recommen-
units.tr: In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, happily. Amen. We, Charles IV, by the favour of divine clemency Emperor of the Romans, ever Augustus and King of Bohemia, to the perpetual memory of the matter. Although the loftiness of the Caesarean dignity, into which the Creator of the world has happily placed Us by the clemency of His goodness, constantly troubles our mind, so that by watchful care and labours devoted to study we may cut away the troubles of Our empire and of the faithful, and procure for them the pleasantness of the peace they desire; yet our heart is kindled with a more fervent affection concerning those matters which concern the sacred [illegible] electors with a certain singularity, especially those whom nobility, the manifold marks of virtue, and the distinguished devotion of faith recommend more praiseworthily...

units.la: Sane sicut alias à Principibus, Comitibus, Baronibus, Nobilibus, Proceribus, ac multis aliis Imperii sacri fidelibus, informationem certissimam, ac luce testimonia clariora accepit Cælitudo, qualiter felicis memoriæ, Illustris Albertus, quondam Saxoniæ Dux, avus illustris Wenceslai, moderni Ducis Saxoniæ, facti Romani Imperii Archimarescballi, Principis Electoris, Lunæburgensis Ducis, avunculi nostri charissimi, velut Archimarescballus ejusdem Imperii Princeps Elector, voluntate, consensu, & votis aliorum suorum Collectorum Principum unanimiter accedentibus, claræ memoriæ serenissimos quondam Rudolphum, Adolphum, Albertum, ejusdem Rudolphi filium, Ducem Austriæ, Romanos Reges, prædecessores nostros, consequenter ordinata, rite & rationabiliter, juxta debitam Sacri Romani Imperii observantiam, in Romanos Reges elegit, ad Imperatoriam Celsitudinem promovendos; & post obitum Alberti, Romanorum Regis, dum aliquandiu nonnullis erroribus Sacrum Imperium fluctua[?] colendæ memoriæ Rudolphus, quondam Saxoniæ Dux, dicti Ducis Alberti filius, & moderni Wenceslai, Saxoniæ & Lunæburgensis Ducis, pater, cclebris recordationis serenissimum principem Henricum, avum nostrum dilectum, cum suis Collectoribus, in Romanorum Regem elegisse: qui etiam avus noster post electionem, eandem adeptus fuit feliciter Cæsaree dignitatem. Cumque manifestissimum exstiterit, & longè, latè per orbem terrarum lucidissime divulgatum, necunquam potuit in dubium revocari, quomodo etiam dictus Rudolphus quondam Saxoniæ Dux, moderni V Wenceslai, Ducis Saxoniæ & Lunæburgensis, pater, felicibus nostris temporibus, cum cæteris suis Collectoribus Sacri Imperii nos in Romanorum Regem elegit solenniter etiam post eandem Electionem, auspice Deo, in Romanorum Imperatorem tunc pro-
units.tr: Certainly, as Our Highness has received from princes, counts, barons, nobles, magnates and many other faithful of the Holy Empire most certain information and testimony clearer than light, how the illustrious Albert, of happy memory, once Duke of Saxony, grandfather of the illustrious Wenceslaus, the present Duke of Saxony, made Archmarshal of the Roman Empire, Prince Elector, Duke of Lüneburg, our dearest uncle, as Archmarshal of the same Empire and Prince Elector, with the will, consent and votes of his fellow electors agreeing unanimously, duly and reasonably, according to the due observance of the Holy Roman Empire, elected in order the most serene princes of illustrious memory, Rudolph, Adolph, Albert son of the same Rudolph, Duke of Austria, our predecessors as Roman kings, to be promoted to the imperial majesty; and after the death of Albert, Roman king, while for some time the Holy Empire was tossed about by certain errors, Rudolph of revered memory, once Duke of Saxony, son of the said Duke Albert and father of the present Wenceslaus, Duke of Saxony and Lüneburg, with his fellow electors, chose the most serene prince Henry, our beloved grandfather, of celebrated memory, as Roman king; and our grandfather, after the election, happily obtained the same imperial dignity. And since it is most manifest, and has been widely and brightly published throughout the world, it could never be called into doubt how the said Rudolph, once Duke of Saxony, father of the present Wenceslaus V, Duke of Saxony and Lüneburg, in our happy times, with his other fellow electors of the Holy Empire, solemnly elected us as Roman king, and also after the same election, under God's guidance, was then promoted as Roman emperor...

units.la: Quodque prædicti, Albertus avus, & Rudolphus pater, dicti V Wenceslai, quondam Saxoniæ Ducis, diuturna temporum præscriptione inconcussa habuerunt, & possederunt legitimè, prout etiam ipse V Wenceslaus in præsentiarum ad instar illorum, ex successione paterna & hæreditaria, dignoscitur justo titulo possidere jus, vocem, dignitatem, & potestatem eligendi Romanum Regem in Imperatorem promovendum, sano tam Ecclesiasticorum, quam Secularium Principum Sacri Imperii Electorum a consensu, & consilio accedente, non improvide, neque per errorem, sed animo deliberato aliorum etiam plurimorum Ecclesiasticorum, & Secularium Principum, Baronum, Nobilium, & nostrorum, & Imperii sacri fidelium, maturo communicato consilio, cupientes, autore Deo juris obviare periculis, & materiam omnium succidere dubiorum, de certa nostra scientia, & plenitudine potestatis Cæsareæ, in his scriptis pronunciamus, decernimus, statuimus, declaramus, & Imperiali perpetuò valituro sancimus edicto, quòd jus, vox, dignitas, & potestas eligendi Regem in Imperatorem promovendum, eidem V Wenceslao, moderno Duci Saxoniæ, Imperii sacri Archimarescallo, ac Principi Electori, hæredibus, & successoribus suis legitimè duntaxat, ab eo descendentibus, quoties casus hujusmodi electionis emerserit, in perpetuum competere, sicut & ritè sibi tanquam Duci Saxoniæ, ac Imperii sacri Archimarescallo, manifestè, ac ipsè velut Saxoniæ Dux, Sacri Romani Imperii Archimarescallus, verus & legitimus Princeps Elector, & post obitum ejus, hæredes & successores sui legitimi, modo & forma subscriptis Principatum, & Comitatum Palatinum Saxoniæ, ac Archimarescalliam Imperii sacri bus & singulis eorum tertiis, dominiis, proprietatibus, c vasallagiis, libertatibus, honoribus mentis, in quibuscunque rebus consistant, & quibuscunque speciali bus possint vocabulis, necnon jus, vocem, dignitatem, & potestatem eligendi Romanorum Regem, in Imperatorem promovendum, sine impedimento quolibet debeat obtinere.
units.tr: And that the aforesaid Albert the grandfather and Rudolph the father of the said Wenceslaus V, once Duke of Saxony, held and lawfully possessed, unshaken through a long prescription of time, and that Wenceslaus V himself at present, after their example, is known to hold by just title, by paternal and hereditary succession, the right, voice, dignity and power of electing the Roman king to be promoted to the emperorship, with the sound consent and counsel of both the ecclesiastical and secular princes who are electors of the Holy Empire, and with the consent and counsel of many other ecclesiastical and secular princes, barons, nobles, and our and the Holy Empire's faithful; not rashly nor through error, but with deliberate mind and after mature consultation, desiring, with God as author, to meet the dangers of law and to cut off the root of all doubts, from our certain knowledge and the fullness of Caesarean power, we pronounce, decree, establish and declare in these writings, and sanction by an imperial edict to be valid forever, that the right, voice, dignity and power of electing the king to be promoted to the emperorship shall belong in perpetuity to the same Wenceslaus V, present Duke of Saxony, Archmarshal of the Holy Empire and Prince Elector, and to his heirs and successors lawfully descended from him alone, whenever a case of such an election arises; just as he himself, as Duke of Saxony and Archmarshal of the Holy Empire, rightly and manifestly holds the principality and County Palatine of Saxony and the Archmarshalship of the Holy Empire, as true and lawful Prince Elector; and after his death his lawful heirs and successors, in the manner and form written below, shall hold them, together with all and each of their [...] lordships, estates, property, fiefs, liberties and honours, whatever they consist of and by whatever special names they may be called; and likewise the right, voice, dignity and power of electing the Roman king to be promoted to the emperorship shall be obtained without any impediment.

units.la: Et ne inter hæredes & successores ipsius, co defuncto, super jure hujusmodi, futuris temporibus orationum, quæstionum, seu litium quævis materia oriatur, decernimus, statuimus, & præsenti sancimus edicto, in perpetuum valituro, quòd post dicti V Wenceslai Saxoniæ moderni Lunæburgensium Ducis obitum, primogenitus ejus filius; & post primogeniti obitum, ejusdem primogeniti senior filius ex ordine geniturae, & sic deinceps à seniore filio descendentes, ex ordine geniturae, per seniorem: Si vero primogenitus Ducis V Wenceslai prædicti decesserit, masculini sexus, legitimus hæredibus non relictis, extunc secundogenitus filius V Wenceslai Ducis post obitum ejus, secundogeniti filius senior, Laicus; & si secundogenitus sine hæredibus legitimus masculini sexus, Laicis, decesserit, tertiogenitus dicti V Wenceslai, & senior ejus filius Laicus, post ipsius; & deinceps per talem modum, directa linea geniturae descendentes ab eo, Laici duntaxat, jus, vocem, dignitatem, & potestatem eligendi Romanorum Regem, promovendum in Imperatorem, & officium Marescballiæ, cum omnibus & singulis suis dominiis, honoribus, juribus, privilegiis, dignitatibus, & pertinentiis, perpetuis temporibus obtinebunt per successionem hereditariam & paternalem, ut præmittitur, ex ordine genituræ.
units.tr: And so that no matter of dispute, question or lawsuit concerning such a right may arise in future times among his heirs and successors after his death, we decree, establish, and sanction by this present edict, valid forever, that after the death of the said Wenceslaus V, present Duke of Saxony and Lüneburg, his firstborn son shall succeed; and after the death of the firstborn, the elder son of that firstborn according to the order of birth, and so on, the descendants of the elder son in order of birth, always through the elder. If, however, the firstborn of the aforesaid Duke Wenceslaus shall die, of the male sex, leaving no lawful heirs, then the second-born son of Duke Wenceslaus shall succeed after his death, namely the elder son of the second-born, a layman; and if the second-born dies without lawful male heirs, laymen, then the third-born of the said Wenceslaus, and his elder son, a layman, after him; and thereafter in such manner, the descendants from him in direct line of birth, laymen only, shall obtain in perpetual times, by hereditary and paternal succession, as premised, in order of birth, the right, voice, dignity and power of electing the Roman king to be promoted to the emperorship, and the office of Marshal, with all and each of their lordships, honours, rights, privileges, dignities and appurtenances.

units.la: §. 5. Si vero præfatum Wenceslaum, modernum Saxoniæ, & Lunæburgensium Ducem legitimis, masculini sexus hæredibus, Laicis, de lumbis ejus directa lineâ genituræ contingeret, extunc Principatus, & Comitatus Palatinus Saxoniæ, nec non Archimarescballiæ Imperii, ac jus, vox, dignitas, & potestas eligendi Romanorum Regem, in Imperatorem promovendum, ad illustrem Albertum, filium Ottonis, quondam Ducis Saxoniæ, Ducem Saxoniæ & Lunæburgensium modernum, patruum dicti Wenceslai, Ducis Saxoniæ & Lunæburgensium legitimos ejus hæredes, masculini sexus, Laicos duntaxat; ita videlicet, quòd post ejusdem Alberti primogenitus ejus filius, & post primogeniti ejus obitum, ejusdem primogenitus senior filius, ordine genituræ, & sic deinceps a seniore filio descendentes, ex ordine genituræ, semper vero primogenitus Ducis Alberti prædicti decesserit, masculini sexus, Laicis duntaxat, hæredibus relictis extunc secundogenitus filius Alberti Ducis prædicti, & post obitum ejus, secundogenitus senior, Laicus: Et si secundogenitus sine hæredibus legitimis, masculini sexus, Laicus, decesserit, Tertiogenitus dicti Alberti, & senior ejus filius Laicus, post mortem ipsius, & deinde eodem modo directa linea genituræ, descendentes ab eo, Laici duntaxat, jus, vocem, dignitatem eligendi Romanorum Regem, promovendum in Imperatorem, & officium Archimarescballiæ, cum omnibus & singulis suis dominiis, honoribus, juribus, privilegiis, dignitatibus, & pertinentiis, perpetuis temporibus obtinebunt per successionem hereditariam & paternalem, ut præmittitur, ex ordine genituræ.
units.tr: § 5. If, indeed, it should happen that Wenceslaus, the present Duke of Saxony and Lüneburg, has lawful male heirs, laymen, from his loins in direct line of birth, then the principality and County Palatine of Saxony, as well as the Archmarshalship of the Empire, and the right, voice, dignity and power of electing the Roman king to be promoted to the emperorship, shall pass to the illustrious Albert, son of Otto, once Duke of Saxony, present Duke of Saxony and Lüneburg, paternal uncle of the said Wenceslaus, Duke of Saxony and Lüneburg, and to his lawful male heirs, laymen only; in such a way that after the firstborn son of the same Albert, and after the death of the firstborn, the elder son of that firstborn, in order of birth, and so on, descendants from the elder son in order of birth; and always, if the firstborn of the aforesaid Duke Albert shall die, of the male sex, laymen only, leaving heirs, then the second-born son of the aforesaid Duke Albert, and after his death the elder second-born, a layman; and if the second-born dies without lawful male heirs, a layman, then the third-born of the said Albert, and his elder son, a layman, after his death; and then in the same way, in direct line of birth, the descendants from him, laymen only, shall obtain in perpetual times, by hereditary and paternal succession, as premised, in order of birth, the right, voice, dignity and power of electing the Roman king to be promoted to the emperorship, and the office of Archmarshal, with all and each of their lordships, honours, rights, privileges, dignities and appurtenances.

units.la: 6. Quibus omnibus non extantibus, ad proximiorem hæredem, secundum lineam primogenitum, duntaxat Laicum, seniorem Ducem Saxoniæ, pro tempore, ac ejus hæredes secundum superius expressarum, in perpetuum legitimè devolventur.
units.tr: 6. When none of all these is extant, the succession shall lawfully devolve in perpetuity upon the nearer heir, in the line, the firstborn, laymen only, namely the senior Duke of Saxony for the time being, and his heirs, according to the orders expressed above.

units.la: 7. Et talis successio & devolutio, ne in his committantur errores, futuris temporibus, habet, ut præmittitur, in omnibus & singulis præscriptis, sine innovatione, perpetuò observari, inviolabiliter; taliter videlicet, quod si aliquem ex eis, modo præmisso, ab hac luce migrare contingeret, qui masculini sexus hæredes legitimos, Laicos, post se relinqueret, debitæ paterætatis, extunc senior frater, nepos, aut consanguineus proximior, in linea genitura, & a fratre non existerit, ejusdem defuncti, Laicus duntaxat, dicti pupilli & juvenis, ad quem devolventur, de jure tutor esse debeat, & curator, tàm diu, donec debitam pertingat ætatem. Cui etiam juveni, quàm cito ætatem debitam pertingenti, vocem, jus, dignitatem, & potestatem, prædictæ Electionis, ac omnia & singula ab ipsis dependentia, idem Tutor sine difficultate, & tenetur qualibet tenebitur, & debebit protinus assignare. Ætatem autem debitam, in hoc casu, videlicet Romanorum Regem, in Imperatorem promovendum, decem & octo annorum esse volumus, & habere. In principatibus autem, Ducatibus, & dominiis aliis temporalibus gubernandis, ætatem observandam decernimus, prout à Divis Romanis Imperatoribus, & Regibus, nostris prædecessoribus, est sancitum.
units.tr: 7. And such succession and devolution, so that no errors may be committed in these matters in future times, shall, as premised, be observed perpetually and inviolably in all and each of the things prescribed, without innovation; namely, that if any of them, in the manner premised, should happen to depart from this light, leaving behind lawful male heirs, laymen, who are not yet of due age, then the elder brother, nephew, or nearest blood relation in the line of birth, not a brother of the same deceased, a layman only, to whom the ward and youth devolves, shall by right be his guardian and curator, for as long as he has not reached due age. And this same guardian shall, without difficulty, assign at once to that youth, as soon as he reaches due age, the voice, right, dignity and power of the aforesaid election, and all and each of the things dependent upon them; and he is and shall be bound to do so. We wish and decree that the due age in this case, namely for the Roman king to be promoted to the emperorship, is and shall be eighteen years. For governing principalities, duchies and other temporal lordships, we decree that the age to be observed is that sanctioned by the divine Roman emperors and kings, our predecessors.

units.la: 8. Porrò ne super jure, voce, dignitate, & potestate Electionis hujusmodi, nec non Ducatu, Principatu, & officio Archimarescballiæ prædictis, ullo unquam tempore contingat dubitari, vel attentari valeant novitates, de Imperatoriæ plenitudine potestatis, & de omnibus scientiis, omnia & singula præmissa, prout in suis clausulis, membris, articulis, atque superius designantur, authorisamus, approbamus, ratificamus, & tenore præcedentium, nostra scientia confirmamus. Insuper Wenceslao, & Alberto, modernis Ducibus Lunæburgensium prædictis, nec non eorum hæredibus, & legitimis successoribus, quondam primùs donavimus, sic hujusmodi donationem iterum innovantes, damus, concedimus, & donamus authoritate Imperiali prædicta, Ducatum & Principatum Lunæburgensem, cujus, authore Deo, possessionem jam obtinent, cum omnibus & singulis eorum terris, castris, oppidis, fortalitiis, dominiis, proprietatibus, {b}vasallagiis, junctibus, usibus, utilitatibus, fructibus, reditibus, proventibus, emolumentis, libertatibus, cibus, armentiis, appendiciis, & pertinentiis universis, in quibuscunque consistant, quæ sint specialibus, & exquisitis vocabulis designari, nihil prorsus exclusò, prout Ducatus, & Principatus Lunæburgen. prædictus in suis terminis, finibus, limitibus, & granitiis circumferentialiter quàm est distinctus, non obstantibus legibus, juribus communibus, municipalibus, & consuetudinibus, privilegiis, vel statutis quibuslibet, in contrarium editis, & servatis, cæterum talia, de quibus speciales & expressa præcedentibus esset mentio faciendæ, quibus omnibus singulis, in quantum præmissis, aut alicui eorum possent quolibet obviare, de dictæ plenitudine Imperatoriæ potestatis penitùs & omnimodò derogamus, supplentes de præfatæ Imperatoriæ plenitudine potestatis omnem defectum, si quis in præmissis, aut eorum aliquo, ex verborum sententiarum obscuritate, sive nimiam omissionem, seu alio quovis modo hunc & inanea tepeant admissus.
units.tr: 8. Furthermore, so that no doubt or novelty ever arises at any time concerning the right, voice, dignity and power of such an election, as well as the Duchy, Principality and office of Archmarshal mentioned above, we, from the fullness of imperial power and with full knowledge of all the matters, approve, ratify and confirm by the tenor of the foregoing all and each of the things premised, as they are set out in their clauses, sections, articles and above. Moreover, to Wenceslaus and Albert, the present Dukes of Lüneburg mentioned above, and to their heirs and lawful successors, we once before gave this grant; now renewing this grant again, by the imperial authority aforesaid we give, grant and bestow the Duchy and Principality of Lüneburg, whose possession, God willing, they already hold, with all and each of its lands, castles, towns, fortresses, lordships, properties, vassalages, connections, uses, advantages, fruits, revenues, proceeds, emoluments, liberties, food, herds, appendages and all their pertinences, wherever they lie, which cannot be designated by special and exact words, nothing at all being excluded, just as the aforesaid Duchy and Principality of Lüneburg is distinguished within its boundaries, limits, borders and marches all around; notwithstanding any laws, common or municipal rights, customs, privileges or statutes issued or observed to the contrary, and such other things, of which special and express mention ought to have been made above, all of which, in so far as they might in any way stand in the way of the premises or any of them, we entirely and in every way derogate from by the fullness of the said imperial power; supplying, from the same fullness of imperial power, every defect, if anything in the premises or any part of them has been admitted in error through obscurity of words or meanings, or through excessive omission, or in any other way.

units.la: a al. Pater.
units.tr: a Another reading: Pater.

units.la: b al. vasallitus.
units.tr: b Another reading: vasallitus.

units.la: 9. Nulli ergo penitus hominum liceat, hanc nostræ pronuntiationis, decreti, statuti, declarationis, sanctionis, authorisationis, approbationis, ratificationis, & confirmationis paginam infringere, aut ei ausu temerario quolibet contraire, sub pœna mille marcarum auri purissimi, quas ab eo, qui contrafecerit, totics, quoties fuerit contrafactum, irremissibiliter exigi volumus, & earum medietatem Imperialis nostræ Cameræ fisco, residuam vero partem injuriam passorum usibus applicari.
units.tr: 9. Therefore let no one at all be permitted to infringe this page of our pronouncement, decree, statute, declaration, sanction, authorisation, approval, ratification and confirmation, or to act rashly against it in any way, under penalty of one thousand marks of the purest gold, which we wish to be exacted without remission from whoever acts against it, as often as it is contravened, and of which one half is to be applied to the treasury of our Imperial Chamber and the remainder to the use of the injured party.

units.la: Signum Serenissimi Principis & Domini, Domini CAROLI QUARTI, Romani Imperatoris, & gloriosissimi Bohemiæ Regis.
units.tr: Seal of the Most Serene Prince and Lord, Lord Charles IV, Roman Emperor and most glorious King of Bohemia.

units.la: Testes hujus rei sunt Venerabiles: Ludovicus Archiepiscopus Moguntinensis, Sacri Imperii per Germaniam; Fridericus Colonien-sis Archiepiscopus, Sacri Imperii per Italiam; Cuno Trevirensis Archiepiscopus, Sacri Imperii per Galliam & Regnum Arelatense. Archicancellarii. Illustres: Rupertus Senior, Comes Palatinus Rheni, Sacri Imperii Archidapifer, Dux Bavariæ; Sigismundus Marchio Brandeburgensis, Sacri Imperii Archicamerarius. Principes Electores. Venerabiles: Joannes Archiepiscopus Pragensis, Apostolicæ Sedis Legatus; Theodorus Metensis, & Ecchardus Wormatiensis. Ecclesiarum Episcopi. Spectabiles: Eberhardus de Wirtenbergk, Theodoricus de Catzenelnbogen, & Heinricus de Sponheim. Comites. Nobiles: Petrus de Wartenbergk, dictus de Coft, Imperialis Curiæ nostræ Magister. Thimo de Colditz, Cameræ nostræ Magister.
units.tr: Witnesses to this matter are the Venerable: Ludwig, Archbishop of Mainz, Archchancellor of the Holy Empire through Germany; Frederick, Archbishop of Cologne, Archchancellor of the Holy Empire through Italy; Cuno, Archbishop of Trier, Archchancellor of the Holy Empire through Gaul and the Kingdom of Arles. The Illustrious: Rupert the Elder, Count Palatine of the Rhine, Archsteward of the Holy Empire, Duke of Bavaria; Sigismund, Margrave of Brandenburg, Archchamberlain of the Holy Empire, Electoral Princes. The Venerable: John, Archbishop of Prague, Legate of the Apostolic See; Theodoric of Metz, and Eckhard of Worms, Bishops of churches. The Distinguished: Eberhard of Württemberg, Theodoric of Katzenelnbogen, and Henry of Sponheim, Counts. The Noble: Peter of Wartenberg, called of Kolb, Master of our Imperial Court; Thimo of Colditz, Master of our Chamber.

units.la: Et alii quam plures nostri & Imperii Sacri Principes, Nobiles & Fideles. Pronunciatum sub Bulla aurea, tipario nostræ Majestatis impressa, testimonio literarum. Datum Franckenford 4 super Mogano, anno Domini millesimo trecentesimo septuagesimo sexto, Indictione quarta decima, quarto Idus Junii: Regnorum nostrorum anno tricesimo, Imperii vero vicesimo secundo.
units.tr: And very many other princes, nobles and faithful of ours and of the Holy Empire. Pronounced under the golden bulla, impressed with the seal of our Majesty, as testimony of the letters. Given at Frankfurt, on the fourth day after Mogan, in the year of the Lord 1376, the fourteenth indiction, on the fourth day before the Ides of June; in the thirtieth year of our reigns, and the twenty-second of our empire.

units.la: Et nos Ludovicus Dei gratia Moguntinensis Ecclesiæ Archiepiscopus, Sacri Romani Imperii per Germaniam Archicancellarius, recognovimus.
units.tr: And we, Ludwig, by the grace of God Archbishop of the Church of Mainz, Archchancellor of the Holy Roman Empire through Germany, have acknowledged it.

units.la: WENZESLAI IMP. AUG. CONSTITUTIO
units.tr: The Constitution of the Emperor Augustus Wenceslaus

units.la: De primariis precibus.
units.tr: On the primary prayers.

units.la: WENCESLAUS Dei gratia Romanorum Rex semper Augustus & Bohemiæ Rex, Illustri Ruperto seniori Comiti Palatino Rheni, sacri Imperii Archidapifero, Bavariæ Duci, Principi & consanguineo nostro charissimo, gratiam nostram & omne bonum. Etsi ad quoslibet Romani Imperii fideles munificentiæ nostræ gratiam libenter extendimus, ad illos tamen præcipue quibus sanguinis identitatem cognoscimus, & fidei puram constantiam invenimus. Igitur nos & inviolabilem fidei firmitatem & devotionis affectum, quos ad nostram personam & sacrum Romanum regnum & Imperium habere dinoscitis, favorabiliter attendentes, & de speciali celsitudine nostræ benevolentia concedendum duximus & concedimus per præsentes, quod tu omnes preces ratione nostræ coronationis in Romanorum Regem, hodie videlicet die sexta mensis Aquisgrani divina favente clementia solenniter suscepta, per civitatem & diœcesim Spirensem Wormaciensem, tam de jure, quam ab antiqua consuetudine divis Romanorum regibus nostris ecclesiis & nobis competentem, porrigere valeas & debeas in singulis tam Kathedralibus quam Collegiatis & conventualibus Ecclesiis & monasteriis utriusque; sex tam secularium quam regularium personarum; nec non ad prælatos & alias personas Ecclesiasticas quascunque: etiamsi Pontificali vel præfulgeant dignitate, in dictis civitatibus & diœcesibus, sicuti easdem preces per nos porrigere possemus: jus & potestatem porrigendi hujusmodi preces nobis competentes in tuam personam omni modo, forma & jure, quibus melius fieri poterit, plenarie transferendo. Et si divina nobis suffragante ad apicem Imperialis culminis fuerimus sublimati, volumus & tibi favorabiliter concedimus e præsentium, quod tu preces primarias, ratione suscepti Imperialis coronationis nobis compertes, etiam porrigere valeas & debeas, in singulis Ecclesiis Cathedralibus & Collegiatis & Monasteriis, & apud Prælatos & quascunque alias personas Ecclesiasticas, seculares & regulares dictarum civitatum & diœcesium omni modo, forma & jure, sicut de Primariis precibus ratione regiæ coronationis. tionis nostræ supereius est expressum. Mandantes sub obtentu nostræ gratiæ, nec non sub pœnæ privationis omnium & singulorum privilegiorum, iurium & gratiarum & libertatum, quæ & quas Romanorum Imperatoribus & Regibus prædecessoribus nostris obtinere dinoscuntur, distrin&ē præcipientes omnibus & singulis Episcopis, Prælatis, Capitulis, Conventibus & personis Ecclesiarum & Monasteriorum Præfatorum, & aliis quibuscunque prædictarum civitatum & diœces. ad quorum notificatum & præbendarum dignitatum, personatuum & officiorum seu beneficiorum collatio, sentatio seu receptio pertinet, & quorum iatione dictarum primariarum precum intercessit, vel esse poterit quomodolibet in futurum, quatenus dictas primarias preces per te ipsis porrigendas promptitudine admittant, sicut tenentur, ac si per nos eis forent exhibitæ seu porrectæ. Dantes & concedentes tibi præsentibus plenariam potestatem, ut rebelles tibi in præmissis, si qui sunt vel erunt, admittendum & exaudiendum dictas preces, auctoritate regali & etiam Imperiali compellere & hercete per te & alios valeas: quemadmodum nos facere possemus, & prout Romanorum Imperatores & Reges in talibus casibus cohercere & compellere poterant & etiam consueverunt. Necessces hujusmodi in dictis Ecclesiis & diœcesibus in præjudicium dictæ concessionis per nos tibi pro aliquo porrigemus: Et si propter importunitatem petentium vel alio quovis modo per nostrum factum fuerit, nostras preces primarias pro aliquo nostris litteris porrigendo, volumus quod tales statuti tanquam per subreptionem obtentæ invalidæ sint, nec aliquam obtineant roboris firmitatem. Sentium sub regiæ Majestatis nostræ sigilli testimonio litterarum. Datum Aquisgrani Anno Domini M.CCC.LXXVI. in octava beatorum Petri & Pauli Apostolorum, regnorum nostrorum Hungariæ, Bohemiæ XIII. Romani vero Primo.
units.tr: Wenceslaus, by the grace of God King of the Romans, ever Augustus, and King of Bohemia, to the illustrious Rupert the Elder, Count Palatine of the Rhine, Archdapifer of the Holy Empire, Duke of Bavaria, our most dear prince and kinsman, greeting, our grace, and every blessing. Although we gladly extend the favour of our bounty to all the faithful of the Roman Empire, we extend it especially to those whom we know to be of our blood and whom we find constant in their loyalty. Therefore, looking with favour upon the unbroken firmness of your faith and the devotion you bear to our person, to the Holy Roman Kingdom and to the Empire, we have judged it fitting, out of the special height of our goodwill, to grant and do grant by these presents that you may and ought to present the prayers that belong to us by reason of our coronation as King of the Romans, which was solemnly received today, that is, on the sixth day of the month, at Aachen by the favour of divine clemency, and that belong to our divine Roman kings by right and by ancient custom, in the city and diocese of Speyer and Worms, to all the cathedral, collegiate, conventual churches and monasteries of either sex, both of secular and of regular persons, and likewise to prelates and to all other ecclesiastical persons, even those who shine with pontifical dignity, in the said cities and dioceses, just as we ourselves could present these prayers. We fully transfer to you the right and power of presenting such prayers, which belong to us, in every way, form and right by which it can best be done. And if, by the help of God, we are raised to the summit of the imperial dignity, we likewise will and graciously grant to you by these presents that you may and ought to present the primary prayers which belong to us by reason of our imperial coronation, in every cathedral, collegiate and monastic church, and before prelates and all other ecclesiastical persons, secular and regular, of the said cities and dioceses, in every way, form and right, just as has been stated above concerning the primary prayers by reason of our royal coronation. We command, under the penalty of our favour and under pain of the loss of all and each of the privileges, rights, graces and liberties which the Roman emperors and kings, our predecessors, are known to have obtained, and we strictly order all and each of the bishops, prelates, chapters, convents and persons of the aforesaid churches and monasteries, and all others of the said cities and dioceses, to whose notice and to whose collation of prebends, dignities, personages and offices or benefices, presentation or reception belongs, and in whose case the said primary prayers have been or may in future in any way be interposed, that they admit the said primary prayers to be presented by you in person with readiness, as they are bound to do, just as if they had been exhibited or presented to them by us. By these presents we give and grant to you full power to compel, by royal and also imperial authority, and to restrain by yourself and others, any rebels to you in the foregoing matters, if there are or shall be any, so that they admit and hear the said prayers, just as we ourselves could do, and as the Roman emperors and kings were able and were accustomed to restrain and compel in such cases. Should any such burdens be imposed by us upon the said churches and dioceses to the prejudice of the said grant made to you, or should it happen through our act, whether by the importunity of petitioners or in any other way, that we present our primary prayers for anyone by our letters, we will that such statutes, as obtained by subreption, be invalid and possess no force or firmness. Given under the witness of the seal of our royal majesty. Given at Aachen in the year of the Lord 1376, on the octave of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul, in the thirteenth year of our reign in Hungary and Bohemia, and the first of our reign as King of the Romans.

units.la: CONFIRMATIO FRIDERICI ET CAROLI- NÆ CONSTITUTIONIS IN FAVO- REM ECCLESIASTICÆ LIBERTATIS PER BONIFA- CIUM IX. PAPAM FACTA.
units.tr: Confirmation of the Constitution of Frederick and Charles, made by Pope Boniface IX in favour of ecclesiastical liberty.

units.la: BONIFACIUS Episcopus, servus servorum Dei, dilectis filiis beatæ Mariæ Effordiensi, & sancti Martini Hingelstadensi, Maguntinensi diocesi, ac beatæ Mariæ ad gradus Maguntinensis, Ecclesiarum Decanis, salutem, &c. Justis & honestis supplicum votis libenter annuimus, illaq; prosequimur favoribus opportunis.
units.tr: Boniface, Bishop, servant of the servants of God, to our beloved sons the deans of the churches of Blessed Mary at Erfurt and of St Martin at Hingelstadt, in the diocese of Mainz, and of Blessed Mary ad gradus at Mainz, greeting, etc. We gladly grant the just and honest prayers of suppliants and support them with fitting favours.

units.la: Dudum siquidem felicis recordationis Honorius Papa Tertius, prædecessor noster, attente considerans, Quod clarę memoriæ Friderieus Imperator Romanorum, semper Augustus, ad laudem Romanæ Ecclesiæ, & sacri decus Imperii, cupiens, ut expurgatis quorundam erroribus, iniquis statutis penitus destitutis, de cætero Ecclesia & Ecclesiasticæ personæ plena vigeant quiete, & secura libertate gauderent.
units.tr: For some time past indeed, Pope Honorius III, our predecessor of happy memory, carefully considering that Frederick, Emperor of the Romans, ever august, of illustrious memory, desiring for the praise of the Roman Church and the honour of the holy Empire that, with the errors of certain men purged away and unjust statutes utterly set aside, the Church and ecclesiastical persons should henceforth flourish in full peace and rejoice in secure liberty.

units.la: Ac pie & juste attendens, quod quorundam pervertsorum iniquitas adeò abundaret, ut non dubitarent contra Ecclesiasticam disciplinam & sacros Canones statuta sua consugere adversus Ecclesiasticas personas & Ecclesiasticam libertatem edita, tali lege hujusmodi statuta iniqua irritaverat & præceperat irrita nunciari.
units.tr: And piously and justly considering that the iniquity of certain perverse men so abounded that they did not hesitate to set their statutes against ecclesiastical discipline and the sacred canons, issued against ecclesiastical persons and ecclesiastical liberty, he had by such a law annulled those unjust statutes and ordered them to be declared void.

units.la: Et omnia statuta & consuetudines, quæ civitates & loca, potestates vel consules aut quicunq; aliæ personæ, contra libertatem Ecclesiæ vel personas Ecclesiasticas hujusmodi edere, aut attemptare temptarent. Contra Canonicas vel Imperiales sanctiones de ipsorum capitularibus, infra duos menses post ipsius legis publicationem penitus aboleri facerent, & si de cætero talia attemptarent, ipso jure decrevit esse nulla, & eos sua jurisdictione privatos.
units.tr: And all statutes and customs which cities and places, magistrates, consuls, or any other persons should issue, or attempt to issue, against the liberty of the Church or ecclesiastical persons, contrary to canonical or imperial sanctions, in their bylaws, he decreed should be utterly abolished within two months after the publication of that law; and if they should henceforth attempt such things, he decreed by law that they were null, and deprived those persons of their jurisdiction.

units.la: Nec non locum, ubi talia deinceps præsumpta fuissent, Banno mille marcarum auri Fisco Imperiali præceperat subjacere.
units.tr: Moreover, the place where such things were thereafter presumed to have been done, he had ordered to be subject to a ban of a thousand marks of gold to the imperial treasury.

units.la: Potestates vero, consules statutarii & scriptores statutorum prædictorum. Nec non consiliarii locorum ipsorum, qui secundum statuta & consuetudines memoratas judicarent, eo tunc essent ipso jure infames, quorum sententias & actus legitimos statuerint aliqualiter non fe nere.
units.tr: The magistrates, the statutory consuls and the writers of the aforesaid statutes, as well as the councillors of those places who judged according to the said statutes and customs, were then by law to be infamous, and their sentences and lawful acts, whatever they had determined, should in no way stand.

units.la: Quodq; si per annum præfatarum constitutionum inventi forent contemptores, bona eorum per totum suum Imperium mandavit impune ab omnibus occupari. Salvis nihilominus aliis parte Contra tales, in eisdem generalibus conciliis promulgatis.
units.tr: And if within a year of the aforesaid constitutions there were found any contemners, he ordered that their goods be seized with impunity by all throughout his whole empire; saving nevertheless the other penalties against such persons, promulgated in those same general councils.

units.la: Et insuper voluit idem tunc Imperator, quod nulla communitas, vel persona publica, vel privata collectas seu exactiones angarias vel per angarias Ecclesiis vel aliis piis locis aut Ecclesiasticis personis hujusmodi imponere, seu invadere Ecclesiastica bona præsumant.
units.tr: And moreover the same Emperor then willed that no community, public or private person, should presume to impose levies, exactions, or forced services upon churches, other pious places, or ecclesiastical persons, or to seize ecclesiastical goods.

units.la: Quod si secus faceret & requisita ab Ecclesia vel Imperio hujusmodi emendare contemptus, triplum refunderet. Et nihilominus Banno Imperiali subjaceret, quod sine satisfactione debita nullatenus remitteretur.
units.tr: But if anyone did otherwise, and having been required by the Church or the Empire, contemptuously refused to make amends, he should repay threefold, and moreover be subject to the imperial ban, which should in no way be lifted without due satisfaction.

units.la: Statuerat insuper quod quicunque communitas vel persona per annum in Excommunicatione propter libertatem Ecclesiæ violatam perfisterer ipso jure, similiter dicto Banno Imperiali subjaceret, à quo nullatenus extraheretur nisi prius ab Ecclesia beneficio absolutionis obtento.
units.tr: He had further decreed that any community or person who persisted for a year in excommunication on account of the violation of ecclesiastical liberty should likewise by law be subject to the said imperial ban, from which he should in no way be released unless he had first obtained absolution from the Church.

units.la: Et insuper ordinaverat, ut nullus Ecclesiasticam personam in criminali quæstione vel civili, ad judicium seculare trahere præsumat, contra easdem canonicas sanctiones & constitutiones Imperiales, quod si secus faceret, actor à suo jure caderet, & judicatum non teneret, & judex foret extunc judicandi auctoritate privatus.
units.tr: And moreover he had ordained that no one should presume to drag an ecclesiastical person before a secular court, in a criminal or civil matter, contrary to the same canonical sanctions and imperial constitutions; and if anyone did otherwise, the plaintiff would lose his right and the judgment would not stand, and the judge would thereupon be deprived of his authority to judge.

units.la: Quodq; judices temporales, qui clericis & personis Ecclesiasticis justitiam denegare præsumerent, tertio requisiti suam jurisdictionem amitterent, prout in dicta Imperiali constitutione plenius continetur.
units.tr: And that temporal judges who presumed to deny justice to clerics and ecclesiastical persons, when thrice required, would lose their jurisdiction, as is more fully set out in the said imperial constitution.

units.la: Dictus inquam prædecessor constitutionem ipsam, etiam de consilio fratrum ipsorum, sanctæ Romanæ Ecclesiæ Cardinalium, qui tunc erant, authoritate Apostolica approbans & confirmans, ip- sam mandavit inviolabiliter observari. nec non statutarios & scriptores, ac violatores prædictos excommunicatos eadem authoritate nunciari.
units.tr: I say that the said predecessor, approving and confirming that constitution by apostolic authority, also with the counsel of his brothers, the cardinals of the holy Roman Church who were then in office, commanded it to be inviolably observed; and by the same authority he declared the statutory writers and the aforesaid violators excommunicate.

units.la: Et deinde ad audiétiam divæ memoriæ Karoli Quarti, etiam Romani Imperatoris semper Augusti deducto, quod nonnullæ seculares personæ in potestate & officiis publicis constitutæ, videlicet Duces, Marchiones, Comites, Barones, & alii domini temporales, necnon consules Civitatum, villarum & oppidorum, & locorum rectores in diversis provinciis ejusdem Imperii constituti, Dei timore postposito, statuta singularia & iniquas ordinationes motu proprio & de facto contra ipsas personas Ecclesiasticas & Ecclesiarum libertates, ac eorum privilegia condiderant, illisq; de facto, & publice utebantur, contra canonicas & legitimas sanctiones.
units.tr: And then, when it was brought to the hearing of Charles IV of divine memory, also Emperor of the Romans, ever august, that certain secular persons placed in power and public office, namely dukes, marquises, counts, barons and other temporal lords, as well as consuls of cities, towns and boroughs, and rectors of places established in various provinces of the same Empire, having set aside the fear of God, had of their own motion and in fact enacted particular statutes and unjust ordinances against those ecclesiastical persons, the liberties of the Churches and their privileges, and openly and in fact made use of them, contrary to canonical and lawful sanctions.

units.la: Utpote, quod nulla bona temporalia in potestatem Ecclesiasticam transferrentur.
units.tr: Namely, that no temporal goods should be transferred into ecclesiastical hands.

units.la: Et ne clerici in sacris ordinibus constituti ad agendum & testificandum in civilibus, & maximè in piis causis aliquatenus admitterentur.
units.tr: And that clerics in holy orders should in no way be admitted to act as witnesses in civil matters, and especially in pious causes.

units.la: Quodq; excommunicati laici & publicè denunciati in Civili foro minimè repellerentur.
units.tr: And that laymen excommunicated and publicly denounced should not be repelled from the civil court.

units.la: Etinsuper prædicti Domini temporales, consules, & rectores per secularem potestatem res & bona clericorum occuparent, arrestarent, & oblationes Christi fidelium minuerent, atque restringerent.
units.tr: And moreover, the said temporal lords, consuls and rectors seized and detained by secular power the property and goods of clerics, and diminished and restricted the offerings of Christ's faithful.

units.la: Exactiones & tallitas indebitas de bonis & reditibus Ecclesiarum exigerent & extorquerent, possessiones Ecclesiarum & personarum earundem devastarent incendiis & rapinis.
units.tr: They exacted and extorted undue levies and tallages from the goods and revenues of the Churches, and laid waste the possessions of the Churches and of their persons with fires and plunder.

units.la: Contractus inter clericos & laicos factus legitime ad libros civitatum, villarum & locorum prædictorum inscribere & sigillare recusarent.
units.tr: They refused to enter in and seal in the registers of the aforesaid cities, towns and places contracts lawfully made between clerics and laymen.

units.la: Donataq; & legata ad fabricas & Ecclesiarum structuras contra prælatorum voluntatem & aliorum quorum intererat, contra justitiam tenere & usurpare præsumerent in fraudem & odium clerí- corum.
units.tr: They presumed unjustly to hold and usurp gifts and bequests made for the fabric and building of churches, against the will of the prelates and of others concerned, to the fraud and hatred of the clergy.

units.la: De bonis etiam & rebus eorundem clericorum, quæ non causa negotiationum, sed propriis eorundem usibus per eorum terras ducebant, sed duci faciebant Theloneum exigere & recipere non verebantur.
units.tr: Nor did they hesitate to exact and receive tolls on the goods and property of these same clerics which they carried, or had carried, through their lands, not for trade but for their own use.

units.la: Et confugientes ad Ecclesias & earum Cæmiteria inde extrahere, contra Canonicas & Imperiales sanctiones hujusmodi præsumpserant & præsumebant, idem Karolus tanquam Imperator Christianissimusque Princeps volens in præmissis providere remedio salutari etiam de Principum, Ducum, Comitum, Baronum, fideliumque aliorum Sacri Imperii consilio & authoritate Imperialiquazcunq; statuta & consuetudines prædictas tanquam per Canonicas, & civiles sanctiones expresse reprobata cassavit, irritavit, & annullavit, ac cassa, & irrita nulliusq; esse roboris penitus voluit vel mo- menti.
units.tr: And they had presumed, and continued to presume, contrary to canonical and imperial sanctions, to drag out of the churches and their cemeteries those who had taken refuge there. Charles, as Emperor and most Christian prince, wishing to provide a salutary remedy in these matters, also with the counsel and imperial authority of princes, dukes, counts, barons and other faithful of the Holy Empire, quashed, annulled and voided whatever statutes and customs aforesaid, as expressly condemned by canonical and civil sanctions, and willed them to be quashed, void, and of no force or effect whatever.

units.la: Præcipiens sub indignatione Imperialis Banni, universis & singulis principibus, ac Dominis temporalibus, consulibus, potestatibus, & aliis in officiis publicis constitutis, quatinus extunc ipsorum statuta & ordinationes, quæ in præjudicium Ecclesiasticæ libertatis edita fuerant, omnino revocarent, & de luce tollerent, quodque secundum ea non judicarent amplius, nec sententias dictarent, eisdemin judicio aut extra judicium quomodolibet pro se & contra Ecclesiasticam libertatem potirentur.
units.tr: Under the displeasure of the imperial ban, he commanded all princes and temporal lords, consuls, magistrates and others constituted in public office, that from then on they should wholly revoke and remove from view their statutes and ordinances issued to the prejudice of ecclesiastical liberty, and should no longer judge according to them, nor pronounce sentences by them, nor in any way avail themselves of them, whether in court or out of court, against ecclesiastical liberty.

units.la: Pronunciavit insuper, & eadem Imperiali decrevit auctoritate, quod quicunque laicus, cujuscunque status vel conditionis exlisteret, ausu sacrilego & propriæ temeritatis audacia sacerdotem vel clericum secularem vel religiosum diffidaret, proscriberet, captivaret, spoliaret, occideret, mutilaret, aut in carcere detineret, aut hujusmodi maleficia perpetrantes scienter acceptaret, vel favoremillis præstaret præter pænas à sacris Canonibus & legalibus sanctionibus eis infliétas, eo ipso redderetur infamis, ac omni honore privatus. Nec ad placita vel consilia nobilium admitteretur quovis modo. Hortans insuper & requirens in Domino prælatos, in illis partibus constitutos, ut legem Imperialem hujusmodi per eorum Ecclesias & synodos publicarent, ne transgressores hujusmodi per simulatam ignorantiam suas valerent malitias excusare, prout in edita tali lege prædicta plenius continetur.
units.tr: He further pronounced, and by the same imperial authority decreed, that any layman, of whatever rank or condition he might be, who with sacrilegious daring and the audacity of his own rashness should defy, outlaw, capture, despoil, kill, maim, or imprison a priest or clergyman, secular or religious, or knowingly receive or favour those committing such crimes, beyond the penalties inflicted on them by the sacred canons and legal sanctions, would by that very fact be rendered infamous and deprived of all honour. Nor should he be admitted in any way to the pleas or councils of nobles. Further, he exhorted and required the prelates constituted in those parts, in the Lord, to publish this imperial law through their churches and synods, so that transgressors might not be able to excuse their malice by feigned ignorance, as is more fully contained in the law published above.

units.la: Cum autem sunt exhibita nobis nuper pro parte dilectorum filiorum Præpositi, Decani & Capituli, ac clericorum perpetuorum beneficiorum in Ecclesia sancti Petri Figlatiensis Moguntinensis diœcesis, & Prælatorum tam sècularium quàm regularium, ac Cleri, consistentium infra limites PræPræposituræ ejusdem Ecclesiæ, petitio continebat, adeò quorundam laicorum, & dominorum temporalium in oppido Figlarienli dictæ diocesis infra eosdem limites ac etiam Figlarienfi loco vicinis malitia inoleverit, quod hujusmodi Imperiales sanctiones transgredi non verentur, & ecclesiasticas libertates violare præsumuntur pro parte præpositi, Decani, Capituli, prælatorum & clericorum dictorum nobis fuit humiliter supplicatum, ut eis providere super præmissis de opportuno remedio dignaremur.
units.tr: Now, since there was recently presented to us on behalf of our beloved sons, the provost, dean and chapter, and the perpetual clergy of the benefices in the church of St Peter at Figlatiensis in the diocese of Mainz, and of the prelates both secular and regular, and of the clergy, residing within the bounds of the provostry of that church, a petition stated that the malice of certain laymen and temporal lords in the town of Figlatium in the said diocese, within the same bounds, and also in places near Figlatium, had grown to such an extent that they do not hesitate to transgress these imperial sanctions and presume to violate ecclesiastical liberties; and it was humbly besought of us on behalf of the provost, dean, chapter, prelates and clergy that we would deign to provide an appropriate remedy for these matters.
