units.la: Nos igitur vestigiis præfati prædecessoris nostri inhærentes, hujusmodi supplicationibus discretioni nostræ per Apostolica scripta mandamus, quatenus vos vel duo vel unus vestrum vos vel alium seu alios constitutiones prædictas in dicto oppido & in aliis locis circumvicinis auctoritate nostra faciatis inviolabiliter observari; transgressores verò ac violatores, & contemptores, sacrilegos prædictos, necnon contradictores quoslibet & rebelles, per censuram Ecclesiasticam appellatione postposita compescendo, invocato ad hoc, si fuerit opus, auxilio Brachii secularis, non obstante si aliquibus communiter vel divisim à sede Apostolica sit indultum, quod interdici, suspendi, vel excommunicari non possint, per literas Apostolicas non faciendo plenam & expressam ac de verbo ad verbum de indulto hujusmodi mentionem. Datum, &c.
units.tr: Therefore we, following in the footsteps of our aforesaid predecessor, by these Apostolic letters command your discretion that, in response to such supplications, you, or two of you, or one of you, by yourselves or through another or others, cause the aforesaid constitutions to be inviolably observed in the said town and in the other neighbouring places, by our authority; and that you restrain by ecclesiastical censure, without any right of appeal, the transgressors, violators and despisers, the aforesaid sacrilegious persons, and likewise all contradictors and rebels whatsoever, invoking, if need be, the aid of the secular arm; notwithstanding any indult granted to them, whether collectively or individually, by the Apostolic See, that they cannot be interdicted, suspended or excommunicated, without making full and express mention of such indult, word for word, in these Apostolic letters. Given, etc.

units.la: WENZESLAI IMP. AUG. RESCRIPTUM
units.tr: THE RESCRIPT OF THE EMPEROR WENCESLAUS AUGUSTUS

units.la: De impedimentis, cur de schismate inter Bonifacium IX. & Bened: Elum Papas cognoscendo & tollendo nondum institutis sit tractatio.
units.tr: On the obstacles that have so far prevented the question of resolving and ending the schism between the Popes Boniface IX and Benedict XIII from being taken up.

units.la: WENCESLAUS Dei gratia Romanorum Rex Semper-Augustus, & Rex Bohemiæ ac Poloniæ, &c. Serenissimo Principi, Domino * Karulo Regi Francorum Illustri, consanguineo carissimo, salutem & fraternæ dilectionis mutuum incrementum.
units.tr: WENCESLAUS, by the grace of God King of the Romans, ever August, and King of Bohemia and Poland, etc., to the most serene Prince, Lord Charles, illustrious King of the Franks, our most beloved kinsman: greetings and an increase of mutual fraternal affection.

units.la: 1. Serenissime Princeps, consanguinee carissime. Venientibus ad nos proximè honorabilibus Ambasiatoribus vestris, in facto sanctæ matris Ecclesiæ hucusq; miserabiliter laniatæ, deliberavimus ad Serenitatem nostram, Serenissimos Principes & Dominos, Sigismundû Regem Ungariæ, fratrem nostrum carissimum, ac Wladislaum Regem Poloniæ, Marchiones Moraviæ b patruos nostros carissimos, ac Duces c Poloniæ, nostro regno Bohemiæ subjectos, aliosq; nostros Imperii sacri regnique Bohemiæ Principes Ecclesiasticos & Seculares, Prælatos & Nobiles advocare. Verùm dictorum Regum imminens necessitas, & occupatio grandis natalium sedium, eorum adventum ad nos, quamquâ nobis invitis, protraxit. Verumtamen cum eisdem Regibus & Principibus tali summus intentione concordes, quòd ulteriori mora postposita apud nos in civitate nostra Uratislavia, intra festum Natalis Domini debebunt finaliter convenire. Quibus, auspice Deo, nobiscum convenientibus, ipsorumq; consilio, in facto sanctæ matris Ecclesiæ, & signanter super via cessionis, sicut expedit, communicato: Serenitati vestræ in hujusmodi facto per Ambasiatores nostros solennes finale responsum volumus destinare. Præsertim cum etiam à Domino nostro Apostolico, Domino * Bonifacio, de intentione & desiderio vestro nondum obtinemus responsum.
units.tr: 1. Most serene Prince, our dearest kinsman. When your honourable ambassadors came to us recently, we resolved to summon to our serenity the most serene princes and lords, Sigismund, King of Hungary, our most beloved brother, and Wladislaus, King of Poland, the Margraves of Moravia, our dearest uncles, and the Dukes of Poland subject to our kingdom of Bohemia, together with the other ecclesiastical and secular princes, prelates and nobles of our holy Empire and of the kingdom of Bohemia. But the pressing needs of the said kings and the great pressure of their own affairs at home have delayed their coming to us, though against our wishes. Nevertheless, the kings and princes are of one mind with us in this matter, so that, without further delay, they are to meet with us finally in our city of Breslau before the feast of the Lord's Nativity. When, God willing, they have assembled with us, and when their counsel has been shared on the affair of our holy mother the Church, and especially on the way of resignation, as is fitting, we wish to send to your serenity a full and final reply on this matter through our solemn ambassadors. Especially since we have not yet received any answer from our Lord and Apostolic, Lord Boniface, concerning your intention and desire.

units.la: 2. Ideoq; ëandem Serenitatem vestram studiosius exoramus, quatenus vestra dilectio Serenitati nostræ Regiæ non imputet, quòd hucusq; vobis absq; dictorum Regum & Principû, quorum in hac parte res agitur, quorumq; consilia vitare non possumus, ne videantur esse coiemti; d quod quoq; omnes tangit, debet ab omnibus approbari; & e quod à pluribus quaeritur, facilius invenitur; responsum non voluimus exhibere, singularis in eo vobis amoris gaudium ostensuri. Sienim à dictis Regibus, quorum hucusq; adventum, confecti tædio, præstolati sumus, responsum & consilium participassemus, dulcem dilectioni vestræ respósum debitum dedisse mus. Datum in Burgelins, die sexta decima mensis Octobris, Anno, &c. M. CCC. XCVIII.
units.tr: 2. Therefore we earnestly beg your serenity that your affection will not impute to our royal serenity that until now we have not wished to give you an answer, though we cannot avoid the counsel of the said kings and princes, whose business this is in this matter. We do this so that they should not seem to have been excluded, and so that you may have the joy of our singular affection toward you. For what concerns all must be approved by all, and what is sought from many is more easily found. Had we shared the answer and counsel of the said kings, whose arrival we have awaited with wearied impatience, we would long since have given your dear affection the due reply. Given at Burgelins, on the sixteenth day of the month of October, in the year, etc., 1398.

units.la: WENZESLAI IMPERATORIS AUGUSTI, ET CAROLI VI. FRANCORUM REGIS DECRETUM
units.tr: DECREE OF THE EMPEROR WENCESLAUS AUGUSTUS AND OF CHARLES VI, KING OF THE FRANKS

units.la: DE EXTIRPATIONE SCHISMATIS INTER DVOS PAPAS.
units.tr: ON THE EXTIRPATION OF THE SCHISM BETWEEN TWO POPES.

units.la: Hoc refertur in Magno Chronico Belgico Monachi Nuliensis, pag. 228.
units.tr: This is reported in the Great Belgian Chronicle of the monk of Nuli, p. 228.

units.la: REX WENCELAUS ad instigationem universitatis generalis sui Studii Pragensis, anno Domini MCCCXCVIII. ex Bohemia ad civitatem Remensem venit, ubi CAROLUS VI. tunc Francorum Rex cum suo germano Ludovico Duce Aurelianensi, huisque & dicti WENZELAI patruis Joanne Biturienfi & Philippo Burgundiæ Ducibus, certo prævio tractatu convenerant ad consultandum de extirpatione schismatis tunc inter Benedictum XIII. & Bonifacium tunc vigentis, ubi conclusum fuit inter cætera, ad id consequendum securissimam & brevissimam esse viam, ut utrumque de Papatu contendentes juri suo cedant sive renuncient, & per utrumque Collegium novus Papa cligatui. Sic igitur WENZELAVS Cæsar de consilio Regis & Principum Franciæ prædictorum misit Legatos suos ad Bonifacium prædictum, & simul Avenionem ad Papam Benedictum, Reverendum Patrem Dominum Petrum de Aliaco Episcopum Cameracensem, qui ab eodem Wenzelao regalia receperat, & M. Nicolaum protho notarium, ut nomine suo peterent, quo juri suo de Papatu cederent.
units.tr: King Wenceslaus, at the instigation of the general university of his Study at Prague, came from Bohemia to the city of Reims in the year of the Lord 1398. There Charles VI, then King of the Franks, had met with his brother Louis, Duke of Orléans, and with the uncles of the said Wenceslaus, John, Duke of Berry, and Philip, Duke of Burgundy, after a certain preliminary negotiation, to consult on the extirpation of the schism then existing between Benedict XIII and Boniface, who was then reigning. There it was concluded, among other things, that the safest and shortest way to achieve this was for each of the two contending for the papacy to yield or renounce his right, and for a new pope to be elected by both colleges. Thus Wenceslaus Caesar, by the counsel of the King and of the aforesaid princes of France, sent his legates to the aforesaid Boniface, and at the same time to Avignon to Pope Benedict: the Reverend Father Lord Peter of Ailly, bishop of Cambrai, who had received the regalia from Wenceslaus himself, and Master Nicholas, chief notary, to ask in his name whether they would yield their right to the papacy.

units.la: PRINCIPUM ELECTO- RUM SACRI ROMANI IMPERII SENTENTIA EXAVTHORATIONIS ET PRIVATIONIS Domini VVencelai Romanorum Regis, Lata & pronunciata Anno Domini M. CCCC.
units.tr: SENTENCE OF THE PRINCES ELECTORS OF THE HOLY ROMAN EMPIRE CONCERNING THE DEPOSITION AND DEPRIVATION OF the Lord Wenceslaus, King of the Romans, passed and pronounced in the year of the Lord 1400.

units.la: IN nomine Domini, Amen. Nos Joannes Dei gratia sanctæ Moguntinensis Ecclesiæ Archiepiscopus, sacri Romani Imperij per Germaniam Archicancellarius, notum facimus universis, præsentibus & futuris.
units.tr: In the name of the Lord, Amen. We, John, by the grace of God Archbishop of the holy Church of Mainz, Archchancellor of the holy Roman Empire throughout Germany, make known to all, present and future, that:

units.la: 1. Quam varia, multiplicia & gravia cùm incommoda tùm dissidia multis abhinc annis, in sacram Ecclesiam invecta sint, etiamnum durantia, atque in dies uberius pullulantia, in sacri Romani Imperij, quod Ecclesiæ Dei & orbi Christiano præsidio esse debebat, gravissimam convulsionem, imminutionem, & dissipationem: id omne ut scribi nequit, sic mala in dies ingruentia, manifeste satis docent atque comprobant. Eamque ob rem sacri Romani Imperii Domini Electores, intervenientibus sacræ Ecclesiæ, Principum, Dynastarum, civitatum, Provinciarum, & subditorum sacri Imperij, prudentem moderatorem expetentium, ardentibus precibus, Illustrissimum Principem Dominum Wenceslaum Bohemiæ Regem, tum sua tum amicorum opera, literis denique, jampridem persæpè & sæpiùs admonuere, eique diligenter ob oculos posuere, privatim ac publicè indecentes ac detestabiles ejus in imperando mores & actiones, nec non ejusmodi Ecclesiæ orbisque Christiani defectus, incommoda atque dissidia, gravissimas item membrorum sacri Imperii avulsiones diminutionesque, contra nominis sui dignitatem damnosè factas, hactenus permissas; nempe quòd pacem in Ecclesia non promoverit, quanquam id summa orbis Christiani necessitas, necnon ipsius ceu Advocati & defensoris Ecclesiæ munus effl agitaret, & ad id faciendum sæpius rogatus, requisitus & admonitus esset: ipso nihilominus Imperium membris aliquot perniciosè mutilante, & mutilum reddi permittente. In quorum numero sunt Mediolanum & Provincia Longobardiæ, quæ juris sacri Romani Imperij fuerant, redeuntibus inde ad Imperium amplissimis emolumentis. In qua ditione Mediolanensis, veluti minister, sacri Imperii partibus fungebatur: cum is, contrà quam eius sublimitatem & dignitatem decebat, accepta pecunia Mediolani Ducem & Comitem Papiensem creavit. Complures insuper urbes terrasque, tam in Germania quàm Italia, ad Imperium pertinentes, quarum quædam ad idem redierant, alienavit: parum pensi habens, ut eas sacro Imperio retineret.
units.tr: 1. How many and how various, manifold and grave, both calamities and dissensions have been brought into the holy Church over many years past, still lasting and sprouting more richly every day, have caused the gravest convulsion, diminution and dissipation of the holy Roman Empire, which ought to have been a bulwark for the Church of God and the Christian world. All this cannot be written out, yet the evils crowding in daily clearly show and prove it. For this reason, the Lord Electors of the holy Roman Empire, with the intervention of the holy Church, of the Princes, lords, cities, provinces and subjects of the holy Empire seeking a prudent ruler, with ardent prayers, have many times over, and more often over long years past, admonished the most illustrious Prince, the Lord Wenceslaus, King of Bohemia, both through their own efforts and those of friends, and finally by letters. They have set before his eyes, privately and publicly, his unseemly and detestable manners and actions in ruling, as well as the defects, calamities and dissensions of the Church and the Christian world of this kind, and the very grave severances and diminutions of the members of the holy Empire, damagingly made against the dignity of his name and hitherto permitted. Namely, that he has not promoted peace in the Church, although the greatest necessity of the Christian world and the office of his own role as advocate and defender of the Church demanded it, and although he was often asked, required and admonished to do so. Yet he has let the Empire be perniciously mutilated in several of its members, and has permitted it to be mutilated. Among these are Milan and the Province of Lombardy, which had been under the right of the holy Roman Empire, with very ample profits returning to the Empire from there. In that lordship the Milanese ruler, as a minister, performed the duties of the parts of the holy Empire; but when he, contrary to what his eminence and dignity required, took money and created a Duke and Count of Pavia. Moreover he alienated many cities and lands, in Germany as well as in Italy, belonging to the Empire, some of which had returned to it, caring little whether he kept them for the holy Empire.

units.la: 2. Præterea membranas perplures nudas rasasque, suæ tamen Majestatis sigillo munitas, amicis pecunia vendidit, in quibus cùm illis tùm aliis, in quorum manus istiusmodi membranæ venerunt, sub Regio sigillo, quæ scribere vellent, licuit. Qua exre, ob sacri Romani Imperij jurium & emolumentorum damnosam imminutionem & dissipationem, graves querelæ subortæ sunt.
units.tr: 2. Moreover, he sold to friends, for money, very many blank and erased parchments, nonetheless bearing his Majesty's seal. On these it was permitted both to those and to others into whose hands such parchments came to write whatever they wished under the royal seal. From this, grave complaints have arisen over the damaging diminution and dissipation of the rights and profits of the holy Roman Empire.

units.la: 3. Controversias porro bellaque, quæ (proh dolor) Germaniam, aliasque sacri Imperij terras, misere afflixerunt & perfunderunt, atque etiamnum perfundunt, nil unquam curæ habuit. Hinc prædationes, incendia, & latrocinia orta, adeo funestis vel hodie incrementis, ut nulli neque Clericis, laici neque agricolæ neque mercatores, neque viri neque mulieres, sive terra sive mari, tuti versentur: ipsa, cœnobia, & domus sacræ, quas sacrum Imperium manu afferete atque tueri decebat, rapinis & incendiis, & ad interitum redigantur. Eò res abiit, ut quivis contra juris & æquitatem, alium pro arbitrio tractarit, ac etiamnum tractet, absque ulla sacræ, præteaque diu, Imperialis auctoritatis reformatione: sicut & locus conveniendi quempiam, ubi nomine Imperii juris defensio & patrocinium suscipiatur plane ignoretur.
units.tr: 3. Furthermore, the controversies and wars which (alas) have miserably afflicted and overwhelmed Germany and the other lands of the holy Empire, and still overwhelm them, he never cared about at all. Hence plundering, arson and robbery have arisen, with such deadly increase even today that no one lives safely, neither clergy nor laity, neither farmers nor merchants, neither men nor women, whether by land or by sea. The monasteries and holy houses themselves, which the holy Empire ought to have taken in hand and protected, are being reduced to ruin by rapine and fire. Matters have gone so far that anyone has treated, and still treats, another against law and equity at his own pleasure, without any correction by holy and, moreover, long-established imperial authority. Just as the place where one might summon someone, where in the name of the Empire the defence and patronage of the law is taken up, is utterly unknown.

units.la: 4. Denique, quod horrendum & immane dictu, cùm propria, tum aliorum facinorosorum, quos secum habet, manu reverendos factorum Anrilites, Sacerdotes, & spirituales personas, alios item plures honestæ notæ homines, contra juris normam, secus quam Romanorum Regem decebat necidedit, aquis submersit, igne cremavit, miserabiliter atrucinitate peremit.
units.tr: 4. Finally, what is horrible and monstrous to tell: by his own hand and that of other criminals whom he keeps with him, he has had reverend prelates, priests and spiritual persons, and several other men of honourable standing, killed contrary to the norm of law and in a manner unbefitting the King of the Romans. He has drowned them in water, burned them in fire, and destroyed them with miserable cruelty.

units.la: 5. Quæ quidem memorata, aliaque multa gravia facinora atque damna adeò divulgata sunt & palam nota, ut excusari vel celari nullatenus queant. Nos igitur, ut præscripsimus, sæpius eum perquam studiosè oravinius, admonuimus, & requisivimus, ut indecenti hac vitæ ratione repudiata, id ubi studii & laboris sumeret, quo sactæ Ecclesiæ, opem ejus veluti Romanorum Regis & Advocati multoties implorantis, pacem & tranquillitatem; sacro autem Imperio pristinum honorem, terras, ditiones, emolumenta denique sua recuperaret, in subsidium & consolationem orbis Christiani hoc nomine graviter debilitati atque oppressi.
units.tr: 5. These matters mentioned, and many other grave crimes and losses, are so widely spread and openly known that they cannot in any way be excused or concealed. We therefore, as we have written, have very earnestly begged, admonished and required him many times that, having put aside this unseemly manner of life, he would apply such zeal and labour as would restore peace and tranquillity to the Church, which often implores his help as King of the Romans and advocate; and to the holy Empire, its former honour, lands, lordships and finally its revenues, for the relief and consolation of the Christian world, grievously weakened and oppressed on this account.

units.la: 6. Etsi verò prædicto Domino Wenceslao, hos aliosque graviores defectus, ipsum tanquam Romanorum Regem Imperiumque concernentes, clarissimè explicuerimus, ac scriptis exhibuerimus: auditis tamen illius responsis, reiteratisque seriis nostris exhortationibus, communicato quinetiam cum Sedi Romanæ negotio, nunquam adhuc deprehendimus eum, sicut Romanorum Regem decet, mores coposuisse, scilicet ad Ecclesiæ pacem, orbi Christiano summè necessariam, sacro item Imperio dignitates, terras ac ditiones suas recuperandas, & fructuosè conservandas. id quod per universas Imperij Provincias est notissimum.
units.tr: 6. Yet although we have set out most clearly to the said Lord Wenceslaus these and other more serious defects concerning him as King of the Romans and the Empire, and have shown them in writing, nonetheless, having heard his replies and our earnest exhortations repeated, and even after the matter was discussed with the Roman See, we have never found him to have amended his manners as the King of the Romans should. Namely, toward peace in the Church, which is most necessary to the Christian world, and toward recovering and profitably preserving for the holy Empire its dignities, lands and lordships. This is most notorious throughout all the provinces of the Empire.

units.la: 7. Quoniam igitur commemoratos plurimasque alios defectus, sacram Ecclesiam & Imperium gravi cum damno gemitu̇q; tangentes, ob instantes prædictorum preces, maximè verò sacramenti ratione, quo nos, ceu sacri Imperij proximè superiora membra, eidem obstringimur nec reticere nec sustinere diutius potuimus. Idcirco ex officio debito cogitandum annitendumque nobis fuit, ut sacro Imperio, cujus vecordi & negligenti administratione in commoda illæc irrepserunt, in orbis Christiani præsidium & consolationem, rectius & salubrius provideretur. Et sanè ut is parendo nobis tam gratam præstitisset, sic eum sufficienter & serio vocavimus atque citavimus, adeò ut ei significavemus, nisi loco & die definitis præsto esset, fore ut cum exhibitarum nobis precum tum juramenti nostri respectu, ejusmodi cōsilia capere & inire cogeremur, quibus sacrum Imperium melius constitueretur, literis id nostris clarissimè attestantibus. Ea propter loco & tempore præscriptis, unà cum Coelectoribus nostris sufficienter oratis, cæteris item sacri Imperij Principibus & Urbibus, comparamus de die in diem expectantes, num præfatus Dominus Wenceslaus comparituros esset, morbis prædictis remedium adhibiturus, ac sacri Romani Imperij tebus rectius deinceps consulturus. At is nec comparere, nec quemquam procuratorio nomine ad nos destinare dignatus est. Quare cum tot præguminum & perniciosorum defectuum causa, eum crebrius privatim & benignè; inde verò, cum nil prosiceremus, coram Principibus, Optimatibus & Urbibus Imperij, in diversis conventibus non sine magnis gravibusque expensis absque tamen ullo fructu, admonuerimus & redarguerimus: ideò commemorata omnia ad sacram Sedem Romanam detulimus. Cæterum cùm nec rem cuncta hæc quicquid pensi habuerit, nil aliud inde conjicere potuimus, quàm eum & Ecclesiæ & Christiani orbis, in primis autem sacri Imperij curam depositisse. Idcirco malum hoc, toti Christianæ Reipub. exitiale, multò diutius ferendum & tolerandum censentes, animo bene confirmato, post multos varios- que tractatus consultationesque, tum inter nos ipsos tùm etiam cum aliis Principibus & Optimatibus sacri Imperij, serio habitas, pro Ecclesiæ salute, Christiani orbis consolatione, sacri Imperij honore & utilitate, præfatum Dominum Wenceslaum, tanquam negligentem & destructorem Imperij, eoque indignum, à sacro Romano Imperio, omnique ejus dignitate hoc tempore penitus removendum esse duximus.
units.tr: 7. Since, therefore, we could no longer pass over or endure the aforementioned and many other defects, which touch the holy Church and the Empire with grave loss and groaning, on account of the urgent prayers of those mentioned, and above all by reason of the oath by which we, as the members of the holy Empire nearest below it, are bound to it, it was our duty to consider and strive how the holy Empire, through whose rash and negligent administration these evils crept in, might be more rightly and beneficially provided for as a protection and consolation of the Christian world. And indeed, so that he might render obedience to us, we summoned and cited him sufficiently and seriously, signifying to him that, unless he were present at the appointed place and day, we would be compelled, both by the prayers presented to us and by respect for our oath, to take and adopt such counsels as would better establish the holy Empire, our letters clearly attesting this. Therefore, at the prescribed place and time, together with our fellow Electors who had likewise been sufficiently summoned, and the other Princes and cities of the holy Empire, we assembled, expecting from day to day whether the said Lord Wenceslaus would appear to apply a remedy to the aforesaid ills and to consult better thereafter for the affairs of the holy Roman Empire. But he has not deigned either to appear or to send anyone to us as a proxy. Wherefore, since we had admonished and rebuked him more often, privately and kindly, for the sake of so many former and pernicious defects, and then, achieving nothing, before the Princes, nobles and cities of the Empire at various assemblies, not without great and grave expense yet without any fruit, we have therefore referred all the aforementioned matters to the holy Roman See. Moreover, since none of this made him any more concerned, we could infer from it nothing other than that he had laid aside care for the Church, the Christian world, and above all the holy Empire. Therefore, judging that this evil, ruinous to the whole Christian commonwealth, must be borne and endured much longer, our minds being well confirmed, after many varied discussions and consultations held seriously, both among ourselves and also with other Princes and nobles of the holy Empire, for the salvation of the Church, the consolation of the Christian world, and the honour and benefit of the holy Empire, we have judged that the said Lord Wenceslaus, as a negligent destroyer of the Empire and therefore unworthy, must at this time be wholly removed from the holy Roman Empire and all its dignity.

units.la: 8. Nos itaque Joannes Archiepiscopus, nomine prædictorum Dominorum sacri Romani Imperij Coelectorum, nostroque, tum commemoratis tùm pluribus aliis insignibus defectibus causisque moti, hac nostra sententia, quam præsenti scripto damus atque ferimus, prædictum Dominum Wenceslaum, ceu inutilem, negligentem, dissipatorem, & indignum sacri Romani Imperij defensorem, eodem Romano Imperio, omnique ejus gradu, dignitate ac ditione ad idem pertinente, privamus & submovemus: cunctis Principibus, Optimatibus, Equitibus, Ingenuis, Urbibus, Provinciis, & subditis sacri Romani Imperij denunciantes, eos ab omni homagio & juramento, personæ Wenceslai nomine Imperij præstito prorsus esse liberos: requirentes atque monentes eos sub jurisjurandi fide, qui sacro Imperio adstricti tenentur, ne prædicto Domino Wenceslao, tanquam Romanorum Regi, deinceps obediant & obsequantur, neque illi jus ullum, obsequium, censum, reditum aut ullam aliam obventionem, quocunque nomine tandem appellanda veniat, ceu Romanorum Regi, pendant, exhibeant, aut exhiberi permittant: sed ejusmodi debita utili & idoneo Romanorum Regi, divino favente numine deinceps sufficiendo, allervent.
units.tr: 8. We, therefore, John the Archbishop, in the name of the aforesaid Lord Electors of the holy Roman Empire, and moved by the aforementioned and many other notable defects and causes, and by our own, by this our sentence, which we give and pronounce by this present writing, deprive and remove the said Lord Wenceslaus, as a useless, negligent, wasteful and unworthy defender of the holy Roman Empire, from the same Roman Empire and from every rank, dignity and lordship pertaining to it. We declare to all Princes, nobles, knights, freemen, cities, provinces and subjects of the holy Roman Empire that they are wholly free from every homage and oath sworn in the name of the Empire to the person of Wenceslaus. We require and admonish them, under the faith of their oath, those who are bound to the holy Empire, that they no longer obey or submit to the said Lord Wenceslaus as King of the Romans, nor pay or render to him, as King of the Romans, any right, service, tax, revenue or any other income, by whatever name it may come to be called, nor permit these to be rendered; but that they should assign such dues to a useful and fit King of the Romans, who, by the favour of the divine will, shall be chosen henceforth.

units.la: 9. In quorum omnium fidem & testimonium, nos Joannes Archiepiscopus Moguntinensis præsens instrumentum, per subscriptos Notarios, hac forma patenti, confici, & majus nostrum sigillum appendi curavimus.
units.tr: 9. In witness and confirmation of all these things, we, John, Archbishop of Mainz, have had the present instrument drawn up in this public form by the undersigned notaries, and have had our greater seal appended.

units.la: 10. Lecta & renunciata fuit sententia præmissa per nos Joannē Archiepiscopum Moguntinensem, nostro & Dominorum Coelectorum nostrorum antememoratorum nomine, sub castro Lonstein ad Rhenum, Treverensis dioecesis, Brubachium versus progressi, è publico folio in tribunalis usum recto, Dominis Coelectoribus nostris ibidem judicio assidentibus, anno Dominicæ incarnationis millesimo quadringentesimo, indictione octava, feria sexta, die vigesima mensis Augusti, paulum ante Nonarum tempus: Pontificatus sanctissimi in Christo patris ac Domini, Domini Bonifacii Noni, divina providentia Papæ, anno undecimo: præsentibus Illustrissimis Principibus ac Dominis,
units.tr: 10. The foregoing sentence was read out and proclaimed by us, John, Archbishop of Mainz, in our own name and in the name of our aforementioned fellow electors, below the castle of Lonstein on the Rhine, in the diocese of Trier, as we advanced toward Braubach, from a public platform set up for the use of the tribunal, our fellow electors sitting in judgment there, in the year of the Lord's incarnation 1400, in the eighth indiction, on Friday, the twentieth day of August, a little before the time of the Nones; in the eleventh year of the pontificate of the most holy father in Christ and lord, Lord Boniface IX, by divine providence Pope; the following most illustrious princes and lords being present:

units.la: Joanne, Illustrissimi Principis ac Domini Ruperti Ducis Bavariæ & Comitis Palatini ad Rhenum filio: Friderico Burggravio Norimbergensi: Nobili Philippo, Domino in Nassau & Sarbrucke, Comitibus Emichone de Liningen, Joanne de Zigenhaim, Cunrado Burggravio, Canonico nostro Moguntinensi Bernhardo à Westenburg, Joanne à Limburg, Baronibus: Reinhardo de Hanovve
units.tr: John, son of the most illustrious prince and lord Rupert, Duke of Bavaria and Count Palatine on the Rhine; Frederick, Burgrave of Nuremberg; the noble Philip, lord in Nassau and Saarbrücken; the counts Emich of Leiningen, John of Ziegenhain, Conrad Burgrave; our canon of Mainz Bernhard of Westerburg; John of Limburg, barons; Reinhard of Hanau.

units.la: Domino Nicolao Brovvin sacræ Paginæ, ] Joanne à V Vitenburg, & | Nicolao Burgman, Decretorum } Doctoribus. Domino Hermanno Præposito S. Gereo- | nis Colonien sis, Legum ]
units.tr: Lord Nicholas Brewin, Doctor of Sacred Scripture; John of Wittenberg, and Nicholas Burgmann, Doctors of Decrees. Lord Hermann, Provost of St. Gereon's in Cologne, Doctor of Laws.

units.la: Item, strenuo Equite Sigfrido de Lindovve, Vicedomino nostro in Ringaugia; Joanne Boisen à V Valdeck, Burggravio nostro in Beckelnheim: Et fidelibus, Henrico Rulmanno à Dadenberg, Gerardo ab Emenberg, Domino in Lantscron, Friderico de Sachsenheim, Kulmanno à Coneren, Joanne de Dalburg, Rudolfo de Zeisskon, necnon pluribus aliis Dominis, Equitibus, & Ingenuis, spiritualibus & secularibus, magno numero admodum, ad suprascripta vocatis atque rogatis.
units.tr: Likewise, the valiant knight Siegfried of Lindau, our Vice-Domain in the Rheingau; John Boos of Waldeck, our Burgrave in BECKELNHEIM; and the faithful Henry Rulmann of Dadenberg, Gerard of Emmerich, lord in Landskron, Frederick of Sachsenheim, Kulmann of Cronberg, John of Dalberg, Rudolf of Zeiskam, and also many other lords, knights, and freemen, both spiritual and secular, in very great number, summoned and requested to the above matters.

units.la: II. Et ego Nicolaus Berchtoldi Fridbergensis, Clericus Moguntinensis dioecesis, Pontificia & Imperiali auctoritate Notarius publicus, ac prædicti Clementissimi Domini mei, Domini Joannis Archiepiscopi Moguntinensis, scriba juratus, quoniam tum temporis, cum judicialis isthæc, quam præscriptimus, sententia lata & renunciata fuit, una cum subscriptis publicis tabellionibus, testibusque commemoratis, præsens interfui, eaque omnia fieri vidi atque audivi: ideo jubente atque petente prædicto Moguntinensi, Domino meo Clementissimo, publicum hoc instrumentum bona fide perscriptum, in publicam redegi formam, illudque consueto mei notariatus signo ac nomine, appenso etiam prædicti Moguntinensis, Domini mei Clementissimi, majore sigillo, in fidem & testimonium prædictorum omnium, subsignavi atque munivi.
units.tr: II. And I, Nicholas Berchtold of Friedberg, clerk of the diocese of Mainz, public notary by papal and imperial authority, and sworn scribe of the aforesaid most clement lord of mine, John, Archbishop of Mainz: since at that time, when this judicial sentence which we have set out above was pronounced and proclaimed, I was present together with the subscribing public notaries and the witnesses named, and saw and heard all these things done, therefore, at the command and request of the aforesaid Archbishop of Mainz, my most clement lord, I have reduced this public instrument, faithfully written out, into public form, and have signed and attested it with the customary sign and name of my notarial office, the greater seal of the aforesaid Archbishop of Mainz, my most clement lord, also being appended, in witness and confirmation of all the foregoing.

units.la: Nomina Notariorum sunt:
units.tr: The names of the notaries are:

units.la: Nicolaus Berchtoli Fridbergensis. Joannes Meier junior Gasterveldensis. Conradus à Leiborn, Clericus Paderbornensis dioecesis. Henricus Stalberg Rotenbergensis. Tilmannus à Honberg. Conradus Coler Zustensis, Coloniensis dioecesis.
units.tr: Nicholas Berchtold of Friedberg. John Meier junior of Gasterfeld. Conrad of Leiborn, clerk of the diocese of Paderborn. Henry Stalberg of Rotenberg. Tilman of Honberg. Conrad Coler of Zusten, of the diocese of Cologne.

units.la: RUPERTI IMP. AUG. CONSTITUTIO
units.tr: The Constitution of King Ruprecht, Augustus

units.la: De Vicariatu Imperii Germanici in absentia Imperatoris.
units.tr: On the vicariate of the German Empire during the Emperor's absence.

units.la: RUPERTUS Dei gratia Romanorum Rex semper Augustus, universis nostri & sacri Imperii fidelibus, ad quos præsentes pervenerint, gratiam nostram & omne bonum.
units.tr: RUPERT, by the grace of God King of the Romans, ever Augustus, to all the faithful of our Holy Empire to whom these present letters come, our grace and every good.

units.la: I. Regiam decet Majestatem illis præcipuè exquisitis intendere laboribus, illis etiam jugi pervigilis mentis vacare considerationibus, per quæ & Sac. Romanorum Imperium nostris præsentibus temporibus optata suscipiat incrementa, res ipsa publica debitis foveatur subsidiis, & divorum more prædecessorum Regiæ Majestatis gladius cunctos vibrantibus terreat aciebus persecutores, & per legitimos tramites calumniantium iniquitates expellat, atque refectis vepribus sub similitantes Imperio desiderata pace fruantur.
units.tr: I. It becomes the royal majesty to give attention to those labours which are above all to be sought, and to devote itself to constant and watchful consideration of mind, by which the Holy Roman Empire may in our present times receive the increases it desires, the commonwealth itself may be cherished with due aid, and, after the manner of the deified predecessors of royal majesty, the sword may terrify all persecutors who brandish their battle lines, may drive out by lawful paths the iniquities of slanderers, and, with the brambles cleared away, may let those who live under the Empire enjoy the peace they desire.

units.la: II. Sanè cum disponente Altissimo pro corona Imperiali diadematis suscipienda ad præsens Italiæ finitus ingressuri, & ut S. Rom. Imperii status, salubris tranquillitas & Respubl. interim in Germania, Gallia & regno Arelatensi, in absentia nostri copiosius atque fructuosius procuretur, de Illustri Magnifici Principis Ludovici Comitis Palatini Rheni & Bavariæ Ducis, filii nostri charissimi, galitatis & gratæ circumspectionis industria præsumptionem & fiduciam utique habentes, indubitatò præcipuè etiam advertentes à divis Romanis Imperatoribus & Regibus prædecessoribus nostris extitisse observatum, ac etiam de jure Comitatus Palatinatus Rheni fuisse & esse, quod cum Romanus Imperator vel Rex ultra montes Italiam ingressus fuerit, in ipsius absentia vicariatum Imperii in Germania, Gallia & Regno Arelatensi ad Comitem Palatinum Rheni pertinuisse & pertinere, eundem dilectum filium nostrum Ludovicum, animo deliberato non per errorem aut improvidè, sed sano & maturo Electorum & aliorum Principum, Comitum & Nobilium nostrorum & Imperii fidelium freti consilio & consensu, de certa nostra scientia & Regiâ plenitudine potestatis per S. Rom. Imperii in Germania, Gallia & Regno Arelatensi provincias, principatus, dominia, districtus, civitates, oppida, castra, villas, & eorundem pertinentias, qualitercunque nominatis omnibus, jure, via & modo quibus melius & efficacius possumus & debemus, facimus, constituimus & ordinamus, notrum & S. Rom. Imperii in Germania, Gallia & Regno Arelatensi vicarium generalem.
units.tr: II. Indeed, since by the disposition of the Most High we are about to enter Italy to receive the diadem of the imperial crown, and so that the state of the Holy Roman Empire, its wholesome tranquillity and the commonwealth may in the meantime be cared for more abundantly and fruitfully in Germany, Gaul and the kingdom of Arles during our absence; trusting in the zeal and the careful prudence of the illustrious and magnificent prince Ludwig, Count Palatine of the Rhine and Duke of Bavaria, our most dear son; and especially attending to the fact that it was observed by the divine Roman emperors and kings, our predecessors, and that it is and has been the right of the County Palatine of the Rhine that, when a Roman emperor or king has entered Italy beyond the mountains, the imperial vicariate in Germany, Gaul and the kingdom of Arles has belonged and belongs to the Count Palatine of the Rhine during his absence; we, not by error or without foresight, but with deliberate mind, relying on the sound and mature counsel and consent of our electors and other princes, counts, nobles and faithful of the Empire, of our certain knowledge and royal fullness of power, appoint, constitute and ordain the same our beloved son Ludwig as our general vicar and that of the Holy Roman Empire in Germany, Gaul and the kingdom of Arles, over the provinces, principalities, lordships, districts, cities, towns, castles, villages and their appurtenances, however named, in all of them, by whatever right, way and mode we best and most effectively can and ought.

units.la: III. Dantes ex nunc & tenore præsentium concedentes eidem plenâ, liberâ & omnimodâ auctoritate, temporalè & generalè jurisdictione, & gladii nutu & providentia Altissimi nobis concraditi potestate, merum & mixtum imperium, ac etiam administrationem & jurisdictionem omnimodam, contentiosam & voluntariam, vice & auctoritate atque nomine nostris in praefati S. Imperij provinciis, pro patribus, dominiis, districtibus, civitatibus, oppidis, castris, villis & eorundem pertinentiis qualiscunque etiam nominatis, per se vel per alium seu alios exercendi, animadvertendi, exequendi in facinorosos & delinquentes & reos homines, eosque & rebelles quoscunque puniendi, relegandi, deportandi, ultimo supplicio addicendi & depingendi, & alias coercendi ratione praevia & modica justitia, prout criminis qualitas exegerit, & delicti ac culpae rebellium & excessus. Et ut etiam apud eum per se ac suum seu suos commissarios, & ad hoc per eum deputandos merum & mixtum imperium, administratio & jurisdictio hujusmodi contentiosa sive voluntaria in loca & homines, cujuscunque status, praeeminentiae vel conditionis existant, infra terminos & limites supradictos consistentes vel consistentia (salva tamen semper sacrosancta Ecclesiastica libertate) libere exerceantur, secundum quod jus seu ratio persuadent.
units.tr: III. Giving now, and by the tenor of these presents granting, to the same full, free and unlimited authority, temporal and general jurisdiction, and, by the nod and providence of the Most High committed to us, the power of the sword: mere and mixed imperium, and also administration and jurisdiction of every kind, contentious and voluntary, in our place and with our authority and name, in the aforesaid provinces of the Holy Empire, over lordships, districts, cities, towns, castles, villages and their appurtenances, however named, to be exercised by himself or through another or others: to take cognisance of, execute and punish criminals, offenders and guilty men, and any rebels whatsoever; to banish, deport, condemn to capital punishment, [to disfigure?] and otherwise restrain them, after a prior and moderate trial, as the nature of the crime requires, and the quality of the offence, guilt and excess of rebels. And that, before him, by himself and by his commissioners and those deputed by him for this purpose, mere and mixed imperium, administration and jurisdiction of this kind, contentious or voluntary, may be freely exercised over places and persons, of whatever status, pre-eminence or condition they be, situated or lying within the boundaries and limits above (always saving, however, the most sacred ecclesiastical liberty), as right or reason persuades.

units.la: 4. Concedentes nihilominus eidem & illi seu illis, quibus hoc commiserit, & in ipsum vel illos jure plenario transferentes auctoritatem, potestatem & licentiam generalem, ne suis quisquam liceat stipendiis, collectas & datias, consueta onera realia & personalia & mixta, quocumque nomine censeantur, nobis & nostro Imperio debitas seu debita, debendas seu debenda, nec no omnes census, reditus, jura, proventus, emolumenta, oblationes, conductus, telonea & pedagia principatuum, dominiorum, monasteriorum, civitatum, terrarum, territoriorum, districtuum, oppidorum, collectorum, villarum & locorum ad nos ratione Imperij, & ipsum sacrum Romanum Imperium in Germania, Gallia & Regno Arelatensi, de jure consuetudine aut alias pertinentes & pertinentia, exigendi, levandi & recipiendi, & ad usus suos pro defensione sacri Imperii & pro ipso Imperio ac evidenti expediente necessitate supportandi & applicandi: poenas & multas ratione praevia imponendi, levandi, & ex causis rationabilibus augmentandi, minuendi, remittendi in judicio & extra: Judices Camerae nostrae servos acceptandi & defendendi: bona damnatorum, rebellium & reorum justitia exigente confiscandi & publicandi: officiales quoscunque & praesertim nostri Imperialis judicii (sine eorum juris praejudicio, ipsis in suis officiis competentis, & usque ad praefens in eisdem habiti & quaesiti) instituendi & destituendi: necnon de omnibus criminibus ordinariis & extraordinariis, enormibus, levibus, publicis & privatis cognoscendi, puniendi, & executionem faciendi tam secundum jura municipalia quam communia seu legis cognitionem: & decisionem hujusmodi committendi, in integrum restituendi, bannum imperiale pronuntiandi, absolutionem concedendi: infamia tam juris quam facti notatos publicandi, eamque juris infamiam tollendi & super eam dispensandi: de causis principalibus & appellationum ad nos & sacrum Imperium interpositarum seu interponendarum, quibuslibet tanquam nostr & Imperii sacri Vicarius generalis cognoscendi, examinandi, & definiendi, & alia, quae causarum merita requirunt, exercendi & exequendi: ferias & nundinas instituendi, imponendi, collocandi & concedendi: rebelles S. Rom. Imperii persequendi & puniendi, privandi, & exuendi feudis, gratiis, libertatibus, immunitatibus, indultis, juribus quibuscunque temporalibus: infames & inhabiles reddendi, pronuntiandi, declarandi: atque destitutos, privatos vel exutos per se vel alium seu alios, etiam per judicium dictum Stillgericht, aut alia quaecunque judicia damnatos & extra jus (ut moris est, sententialiter constitutos & depositos ad honores, status, officia, jura pristina in integrum libere restituendi: Decreta, statuta ac provisiones in praedictis omnibus & quolibet faciendi, de novo, corrigendi & in totum tollendi, semel, pluries, & totiens quoties oportunum fuerit & ordo dictaverit tionis.
units.tr: 4. We also grant to the same, and to him or them to whom he commits this, and transfer to him or them by full right, authority, power and general licence that no one shall be allowed, from his stipends, to levy and collect the taxes and tributes, the customary real, personal and mixed burdens, under whatever name they are reckoned, which are or shall be owed to us and our Empire; likewise all the census, revenues, rights, proceeds, emoluments, offerings, tolls, customs and duties of principalities, lordships, monasteries, cities, lands, territories, districts, towns, collections, villages and places which belong to us by reason of the Empire, and to the Holy Roman Empire itself in Germany, Gaul and the kingdom of Arles, by law, custom or otherwise; to demand, levy and receive them, and to use and apply them for their own purposes, for the defence of the Holy Empire and for the Empire itself, and for evident necessity; to impose, levy and, for reasonable causes, increase, diminish or remit penalties and fines, in court and out of court; to accept and defend the servants of our Chamber; to confiscate and publish the goods of the condemned, rebels and guilty, as justice requires; to institute and dismiss officials of every kind, and especially of our Imperial court (without prejudice to their right, which belongs to them in their offices, and to what they have held and acquired in them until now); to take cognisance of, punish and execute all crimes, ordinary and extraordinary, grave, slight, public and private, according to municipal law as well as common law or the knowledge of the law, and to commit the decision of these; to restore to integrity, to pronounce the imperial ban, to grant absolution; to publish those marked with infamy, both of law and of fact, and to remove that infamy of law and dispense from it; concerning principal causes and appeals made or to be made to us and the Holy Empire, to take cognisance of, examine and determine them as our and the Holy Empire's general vicar, and to exercise and carry out whatever else the merits of the causes require; to institute, impose, fix and grant fairs and markets; to pursue and punish rebels of the Holy Roman Empire, to deprive and strip them of fiefs, favours, liberties, immunities, indults and all temporal rights; to render, pronounce and declare men infamous and incapable; and to restore freely to their former honours, estates, offices and rights in full, those deposed, deprived or stripped, by himself or another or others, even those condemned by the court called the Stillgericht or any other courts and placed outside the law (as is customary, sentenced and deposed); to make, enact, correct anew and wholly abolish decrees, statutes and provisions in all and each of the aforesaid matters, once, several times, and as often as it shall be expedient and the order of the matter dictates.

units.la: 5. Omnia & singula feuda sacri Imperii vacantia vel cum vacaverint, committendi & conferendi, ac de aliis infeudandi & investigandi (exceptis duntaxat feudis insignis Archiepiscoporum, Ducum & Marchionum, & quae cum vexillis seu gladiis recipi consueverunt, & de quib. Officialium Imperialis curiae de more servitur) & ab illis sic recipientibus feuda, dum & quoties se casus obtulerit, homagii, fidelitatis, obedientiae & devotionis debita juramenta nostro & sacri Imperii nomine & vice postulandi & recipiendi: ad Canonicatus & praebendas ac dignitates, etiamsi curatae ac electivae & majores post Pontificales in Metropolitanis & Cathedralibus ac principalibus in Collegiis existant, patronatus, Ecclesias parochiales & beneficia & officia Ecclesiastica seu temporalia, dum & quoties vacaverint, personas aptas & idoneas praesentandi, & eas ad ea conferendi: Dotes, dotalicia, sponsalitia, largitates ac donationes propter nuptias admittendi & confirmandi: mente captis, furiosis, & aliis personis, quae sui juris non existunt, curatores, orphanis, pupillis & viduis tutores & defensores praetendi, actutores & defensores minus legitime datos confirmandi, devolutiones fiscales quorumcunque dominiorum, praediorum & argrorum aut hereditatum, seu etiam rerum mobilium, dummodo ratio illud exegerit, nostri & Imperii nomine exigendi, tenutam & possessionem talium accipiendi.
units.tr: 5. To commit and confer all and each of the fiefs of the Holy Empire that are vacant or shall become vacant, and to invest others with them and to grant investiture (excepting only the fiefs of the archbishops, dukes and margraves, and those which are customarily received with banners or swords, and for which the service of the officials of the imperial court is customary); and, whenever and as often as the case arises, to demand and receive, in the name and place of ourselves and the Holy Empire, the due oaths of homage, fealty, obedience and devotion from those receiving fiefs in this way; to present suitable and fit persons to canonries, prebends and dignities, even if they are cure-bearing and elective and, after the pontifical ones, the greatest in metropolitan and cathedral churches and principal colleges, to patronages, parish churches, benefices and ecclesiastical or secular offices, whenever and as often as they fall vacant, and to confer them on those persons; to admit and confirm dowries, marriage portions, dower gifts, largesses and gifts made on account of marriage; to appoint curators for the mentally incapacitated, the insane and other persons who are not their own masters, and tutors and defenders for orphans, wards and widows; to confirm tutors and defenders given less than lawfully; to exact, in the name of ourselves and the Empire, the fiscal forfeitures of any lordships, estates, lands or inheritances, or even of movable goods, whenever reason requires it; and to take possession and seisin of such things.

units.la: 6. Dantes etiam & Regia concedentes auctoritate & de certa scientia, nostro ac sacri Imperii Romani Vicario generali supradicto potestatem plenissimam, Notarios publicos & tabelliones auctoritate & potestate plenariis creandi, faciendi, & de tabellionatus officio instituendi, seu vestiendi (ut moris est) per pennam & calamarium: receptoab ipsis prius & eorum quolibet pro nobis ac sacro Imperio debitae fidelitatis solito juramento: hoc ipsum etiam eadem auctoritate concedendi & committendi, eosque eorum exigentibus demeritis privandi & destituendi: ac naturales manseres, spurios, bastardos, & quolibet de damnato sive illicito coitu procreatos, viventibus seu mortuis eorum parentibus rite legitimandi: etiamsi forent filii Illustrium Principum, Ducum, Comitum Carinthiæ, Tirolis & Bavariæ & Baronum, & eos natalibus & omnibus legitimis juribus restituendi, omnemque generaliter tuendi, ac natalium defectum abolendi: ad omnia & singula jura successionum etiam ab intestato, ad omnium & agnatorum, honores, dignitates, officia, & ad singulos actus legitimos admittendi & admissi mandandi (sine tamen legitimorum haeredum praejudicio) ac si essent de legitimo matrimonio procreati.
units.tr: 6. Granting and conceding also, by royal authority and of certain knowledge, to our above-mentioned general Vicar of the Holy Roman Empire, the fullest power to create and make public notaries and notaries of record with full authority and power, and to institute them in the office of notary, or to invest them (as is customary) with pen and inkstand; to receive from them, and from each of them, before admission, the customary oath of due fidelity to us and to the Holy Empire; likewise to grant and commit this same power by the same authority, and to deprive and dismiss them when their demerits require it; and to legitimate, according to law, natural children, spurious children, bastards, and whoever is born of a condemned or unlawful union, whether their parents are living or dead; even if they should be sons of illustrious princes, dukes, counts of Carinthia, Tyrol and Bavaria, and barons; and to restore them to their birth and all lawful rights, to protect them in every way, and to abolish any defect of birth; and to admit them to all rights of succession, including intestate succession, to the honours, dignities and offices of all and of their agnates, and to admit and order them to be admitted to each and every lawful act (without prejudice, however, to lawful heirs), just as if they had been born of lawful marriage.

units.la: 7. Et generaliter omnia & singula liberè faciendi & exercendi, quae ad verum sacri Imperii Vicarium generalem pertinent: etiamsi qua ex eis jure & consuetudine speciali exegerint mandatum, sive majora fuerint supra & infra expressis, & quae ad nos & factum Imperium faciendi & agendi decernere dinoscuntur de jure, consuetudine, seu plenitudine Regiae potestatis: non obstantibus quibuscunque literis datis vel dandis, legibus, constitutionibus, consuetudinibus, statutis & juribus municipalibus & localibus, generalibus & specialibus contrariis, quacunque firmitate roboratis. Quibus omnibus & singulis, in quantum praetentibus obviare seu eis derogare possunt, ac si talia specifice in sui capitulis & punctis de verbo ad verbum hic forent inserta & nominatim expressa, de nostra certa scientia & de plenitudine Regiae potestatis specialiter derogamus, ac viribus carere decernimus & decrevimus.
units.tr: 7. And generally to do and exercise freely all and each of the things that pertain to the true general Vicar of the Holy Roman Empire, even if by law and special custom they have required a mandate, and whether they are greater or less than the matters expressed above, and which by law, custom, or the fullness of royal power are known to belong to us and to the Empire to do and to act upon. Notwithstanding any letters given or to be given, laws, constitutions, customs, statutes, and municipal and local rights, general and special, contrary to these, however firmly they may be confirmed. To all of which and each of which, insofar as they can oppose or derogate from what is pretended, as if such things were specifically inserted here word for word in their chapters and points and expressly named, we specially derogate by our certain knowledge and by the fullness of royal power, and we decree and have decreed that they shall be void.

units.la: 8. Mandantes nihilominus firmiter & districtè praecipientes universis & singulis Ecclesiasticis et Secularibus Principibus, etiam si Pontificali praefulgeant dignitate, Marchionibus, Comitibus, Baronibus, Nobilibus, ministerialibus, militibus, Clientibus, Vasallis, Civitatibus, Oppidis, & eorum universitatibus, locorum rectoribus & eorum communitatibus, castris, villis, subditis, terrigenis, incolis, habitatoribus, castellanis, custodibus, officialibus, & hominibus quibuscunque, cujuscunque etiam praeeminentiae, dignitatis, status, gradus seu conditionis existant, praesentibus & futuris, quatenus praedictum Ducem Ludovicum filium nostrum carissimum, nostrum & Imperii Vicarium generalem taliter, ut praedicitur, à nobis constitutum, & personam nostram figurantem: benignè & absque difficultate liberè recipiant, & sibi ac officialibus suis, quos constituet loco sui, omnibus & singulis nostro & Imperii nomine fideliter & effectualiter tanquam nobis in omnibus obedient, pareant & intendant efficaciter & cum effectu, ut exinde eorum sincera devotio per operum efficaciam elucescat. Sub poenis praefatum nostrum & Imperii Vicarium constituendis, infligendis, nec non sub poenis nostrae indignationis gravissimae, & mille marcharum auri purissimi: quas ab ipsis, qui secus attentare praesumpserint, ausu temerario, toties quoties contra factum fuerit, irrevocabiliter per ipsum seu subs-tituendos ab eodem exigi volumus, suisque usibus prout sibi videbitur applicari. Harum sub nostrae Regiae Majestatis sigilli appensione testimonio literarum. Datum Augspurg tertia feria post Festum Nativitatis Beatae Mariae Virginis gloriosae, Anno Domini M.CCCC.I. Regni vero nostri anno secundo.
units.tr: 8. We nevertheless firmly and strictly command all and each of the ecclesiastical and secular princes, even if they shine with pontifical dignity, marquises, counts, barons, nobles, ministerials, knights, clients, vassals, cities, towns and their communities, rulers of places and their communes, castles, villages, subjects, natives, inhabitants, dwellers, castellans, guardians, officials, and whomsoever men, of whatever pre-eminence, dignity, rank, grade or condition they may be, present and future, that they receive graciously and without difficulty, freely, the aforesaid Duke Louis, our most beloved son, constituted by us as our and the Empire's general Vicar in the manner stated, and representing our person; and that they obey, submit to and attend faithfully and effectively, in our name and that of the Empire, to him and to his officials whom he shall appoint in his place, as to us in all things, efficaciously and with effect, so that their sincere devotion may thereby shine forth through the efficacy of their deeds. Under the penalties to be imposed and inflicted on the aforesaid our Vicar, and also under the penalties of our most grave displeasure and a thousand marks of purest gold, which we wish to be irrevocably exacted by him, or by those substituted by him, from those who presume to attempt otherwise, with rash daring, as often as it is done against this, and to be applied to his uses as he shall see fit. In witness whereof we have had this letter sealed with the seal of our royal Majesty. Given at Augsburg, on the Tuesday after the Feast of the Nativity of the glorious Virgin Mary, in the year of our Lord 1401, and in the second year of our reign.

units.la: Ad mandatum Domini Regis
units.tr: By command of the Lord King.

units.la: Johannes Weinheim.
units.tr: Johannes Weinheim.

units.la: LADISLAI TYRANNI ROMANORUM RESCRIPTUM
units.tr: THE RESCRIPT OF LADISLAUS, TYRANT OF THE ROMANS

units.la: De facto unionis inter schismaticos Papas, ad Dominum Gregorium XII. sue partis Papam.
units.tr: On the fact of the union between the schismatic Popes, addressed to Lord Gregory XII, Pope of his party.

units.la: BEATISSIME Pater, decet quempiam obedientia filium vel natura, commoti patris monitiones, & dignas increpationes, quae nequeunt nisi ab effectu & charitatis zelo procedere, pacienter & aequo animo tolerare. Nuper siquidem vestrae Beatitudinis literas solita reverentia debitaque devotione recipiens, animadverti nonnihil irati in eis, ac objurgationis & indignationis affecti, hoc responsum humile praesentibus praebeo moderandum, corrigendumque, si meretur, paulatim entia & virtute.
units.tr: Most blessed Father, it becomes a son, whether by duty or by nature, to bear calmly and with an even mind the admonitions and the fitting rebukes of a father who is moved, which can only proceed from genuine affection and zeal for charity. Having lately received your Blessedness's letter with my accustomed reverence and due devotion, I noticed that you were somewhat angry in it, and moved to reproach and indignation. I therefore offer this humble reply, to be moderated and corrected, if it deserves it, little by little, in its substance and force.

units.la: 1. Credo equidem & certus sum, imo certissimus & mihi conscius, Deo teste, me semper sanctam Ecclesiam, & ejus Antistites Apostolicosque Pastores, & ipsam Beatitudinem vestram praecipuè debui, potuique, & sci vi, filiali reverentia veneratum, veneratumque esse, dum hac mortali vita, ut exinde fruar aeterna. Sed ista tam mordaci & intempestiva commemoratione & expressione, profectò memores beneficii impensi tam pure, tam liberè, tanto denique sumptu, & (ut Bullae Apostolicae verbis utar) profluvio expensis, ad refellendum confutandumque pro mea causa nequeo proferri, noloque (etsi reminisci & recensere pigeat) conticere: Fateor enim, nec unquam inficiatur aliquali matris Ecclesiae adjutum praesidio, illis primordiis obstitisse, quibus Urbani XI. inhumana veritas res omnes orbis ita commiscuit, & praecipuè Regni hujus in tantum attrivit, ut ingenium adhuc, & utinam non ulteriùs permanserit reliquiae illius ruinae supersint, nec sum aut ero ejus imperium oblituisque, unde ad instar magni census pecuniam, & maximi exercitus paucos illos pugiles militare computo. Manet, manuisque & manebit mente repositum, quamvis nec illud porrectum fuerit, quod sui non mediocri foenere & talione mercatus. Sed quid ea tempestate id panxillo ad rantas opes totaque formidabiles copias & terribiles classes, quibus Antipapa abundat larue, tam saepe numero maximo copiarum communis hostis a Andegavensis fultus, & praeterutus, adjumenti ferre potuit, vel vigoris ? attamen ad futuri incrementi finem, aliquam principio tulit opem. Ipsum quippe hostem, cum factione sua in potestatem Regni intrare nitentem, & divina humanaque vastantem, & in hunc disponentem, Clementemque, & deinde Benedicti nomen & sedem pro Apostolica vocentem, armisque me terrentem, judice Deo, & justitia annuente, ut in Domino gloter, ut singuli gloriari, apud Tarentum non solum Regno, sed Italiæ populi & fugavi. Quæ vero non citò fierent, intermedio illo tempore per quosdam Romanos Pontifices jam vita perfunctos, ea scandalorum obstacula, seditiones procuratæ fuerunt, tam inter Regni Proceres, quam ves, non absque eorundem Pontificum & magno incommodo, sileat honestus arbiter, si quid juvat aut opus est hinc inde jamdudum memoria reprehendi & corrigi, quæ recentia & pene in manibus sita excusaturus assurgi: salva semper Apostolicæ Sedis & Ecclesiæ vestræ grata & benedictione paterna.
units.tr: 1. I believe, indeed, and I am certain, nay most certain and conscious to myself, with God as witness, that I have always venerated, and have been bound and able to venerate, with filial reverence, the holy Church, her bishops and apostolic pastors, and above all your own Blessedness, for as long as I live in this mortal life, so that I may afterwards enjoy eternal life. But I cannot be brought forward to refute and confute my cause with such a biting and untimely recollection and mention of the benefit I bestowed so purely, so freely, and at such great expense (to use the words of the Apostolic Bull, "with an outpouring of expenses"). Nor, although it irks me to recall and review it, do I wish to keep silent. For I confess, and no one can deny, that I was helped by some support of Mother Church at those beginnings, when the inhuman truth of Urban XI so confused all the affairs of the world and wore down especially this kingdom to such a degree that its spirit still remains, and would that it had not remained any longer; remnants of that ruin survive. Nor am I, or will I be, forgetful of its command, from which I reckon those few fighters as an army of great size, as a great sum of money. It remains, and will remain, stored in my mind, although that help was not extended except as it was bought with interest and retaliation of no small kind. But what could that little help, in such a time, bring to the vast resources, the whole formidable forces and terrible fleets with which the Antipope abounds, so often supported by the greatest forces of the common enemy, the Angevin, and passed over? Nevertheless, to the end of future growth, it brought some aid at the beginning. For it was I who put to flight, at Taranto, not only the Kingdom but the peoples of Italy, the enemy himself, who strove to enter the power of the Kingdom with his faction, laying waste things divine and human, and who arranged this, calling Clement, and afterwards the name and seat of Benedict, Apostolic, and terrifying me with arms, God being judge and justice assenting, so that, as all may glory in the Lord, each of them may rejoice. But those things which were not quickly done, in that intervening time, through certain Roman Pontiffs now dead, the obstacles of scandals and the seditions that were stirred up, both among the nobles of the Kingdom and among others, were not without great inconvenience to those same Pontiffs. Let an honest arbiter keep silent, if it helps or is necessary that these things, long since reproved and corrected on all sides, be recalled, which I shall come forward to excuse, as they are recent and almost in hand; always saving the favour and paternal blessing of the Apostolic See and of your Church.

units.la: 3. Scio enim & in certum fiumeque teneo, quod Ludovicus de Meloratis offensus is subditis tunc infestus, a Marchiæ Rectoratu mea instantia & prece quietula fuit amotus, in lo voro meo parva mihi Apostolica fuit lara literula, sive breve, dictans, id absque fomite turi mox scandali magnique periculi non posse tunc fieri, sed confestim optimum remedium. Quod quale fuerit? præter alias incursiones & belli strages, duas terras in Aprijs nostrorum cepit, quin potius subito occupavit. Sed per idem postea tempus suasu motuque Pauli de Ll tracti in meliorem fortunam jam sodalitij pœnitentis, & in illius statu & fortunæ mutatione fastiditi, solura ut authoritate confictâ inter illos illa societate fraterna ab eo fuit officio & pendio revocatus. Ego igitur ut pluribus meorum caverem incommodis, inquietum illum & ad artes & res quasdam pronum, imò jam tunc paratum & expeditum, licet eo modo ne quò deterius laberetur, ad stipendia mea recepi, à quo demum & Esculi civitatem non ptu, stipendio & mearum commutatione terrarum, ne pejore loco res tenderet, hac interim primum, ut eam pro Ecclesia conservarem, & illi in tempore restituerem, alia ne in postea quo sinistro successu incommoda mihi & meis ex vicinitate sentirem, quod Beatitudini vestræ intimatum non displicuisse, nec ægre latum fuisse, recolo mihi per Oratorem Fratrem Dominum dictum.
units.tr: 3. For I know, and hold it as certain and fixed, that Ludovico de Meloratis, offended and then hostile to his subjects, was removed from the rectorship of the March at my instance and quiet entreaty. In my service I received a short Apostolic letter, or brief, saying that at that time this could not be done without the spark of a fresh scandal and great danger, but at once the best remedy. What sort of remedy was it? Apart from other incursions and slaughters of war, he seized, or rather suddenly occupied, two lands in Apulia belonging to our side. But afterwards, at the persuasion and urging of Paolo de Ll..., having been drawn into a better fortune of the penitent fellowship, and despised in his state and change of fortune, he was recalled from that office and salary by an invented authority, that fraternal fellowship being thus cut off. I therefore, so that I might guard against many inconveniences to my people, took him, restless and prone to certain arts and affairs, indeed already then prepared and ready, into my pay, though in such a way that things should not slide to a worse state. From him, at last, I also took the city of Ascoli, by payment and by exchange of my lands, lest the affair should tend to a worse place. Meanwhile I first held it so that I might keep it for the Church and restore it to her in due time, lest afterwards by some unlucky outcome I should suffer inconvenience from its proximity to me and mine. I recall that this was made known to your Blessedness through the envoy, Brother Lord named above, and that it was not displeasing nor grievously taken.

units.la: 4. Sed nunc ejus Beatitudinis verbis arguor, me hostilia contra Urbem ex ea fecisse & quòd ad locum electum, ad inveteratum jam (proh dolor) schismatica tollendum, numquam ipsa Beatitudo vestra accedere intendebat: quod ego dictum aut commissum ex me profusus. Profiteor namque, & abstirquod unquam à veritate recedam; scripsi, consului cum fide & humiliter supplicavi, sicut & alii mundi Proceres & Magnates fidi devotique vobis & vestro, & no-stro, & cunctorum fidelium coetui, ut comperi, jam fecerunt, ut locus, eligendus ad tanti spem tuturique boni mysterium, omni prorsus suspicione careret, nec electus Saonæ locus adeo tutus & congruus videbatur. Movebat siquidem zelo vestro, & ut ardua tantaque res, tamque cunctis Christicolis cessaria ac frugi, recte & absque quovis impostoris redivivo carerer scrupulo, sed auxiliante eo, res agitur, foret in perpetuum duratura. Nam & licet mea, ut id rite quovis loco fiat, multum interest rum tamen referr, imò nihil, quocunque terrarum angulo vel recessu bonum agatur, dum modo fiat, ad quod vellem concurrere vobiscum unâ, & sæpe obtuli, & denuò offero, semperque me paratum, & pro viribus adjuturum. Sed proh Deum, vestram sanctam, atque hominum quamobrem tantopere terminor ex re, quâ Beatitudo vestra tot argumentis & rationibus missam mihi Bullam reprobavit, aut etiam Saonæ locus mihi debet esse suspectus, non ratione soli, in domus incliti Francorum Regis, quæ sublimis domus & prosapiæ caput est stabile ceps, (erfi aliquando fuisse dicitur aliquid simultatis, id vestri vel vestrorum similium est) non denique urbis Januæ, in cujus litore vel riparia situs est, quam mihi vinculo vetustis & amicitiæ fidam & charissimam repuro velut meam. His ergo & aliis, quæ nunc relinquo, verborum prolixitas tædiosa, quandoquidem vestræ Beatitudini est complacitum, & proro teneo, atque est, persuadeo, consulo, supplico, oro acobtestor, ne ad causam, præoptatque rei consummationem & perfectionem celerimam, nonsolùm ad Saonam locum pactum, & licitum, ut omnes veré norunt, sed etiam, si libet, Parisius, refertam sapientia urbem proficisci.
units.tr: 4. But now I am accused, in the words of your Blessedness, of having made hostile moves against the City from that quarter, and that your Blessedness never intended to go to the place chosen for the removal, now (alas) long established as schismatic. I profess, and I swear before God that I shall never depart from the truth, that whatever was said or done was not of my own doing. For I have written, advised in good faith, and humbly supplicated, as other nobles and magnates of the world, faithful and devoted to you and to yours, to ours, and to the assembly of all the faithful, have, as I have learned, already done, that the place to be chosen for the hope of so great a work and a future good should be entirely free of all suspicion, and that the place chosen, Savona, did not seem so safe and suitable. For this moved me, out of zeal for you, and so that so arduous and great a matter, so necessary and fruitful for all Christians, might proceed rightly and without any scruple of a returning impostor, and, with that one helping, might endure forever. For although it matters much to me that it be done rightly in any place, it matters nothing in what corner or recess of the lands the good is accomplished, provided only it is done, to which I would wish to contribute with you together, and I have often offered, and offer again, and I am always ready to help with my strength. But, God help us, I am troubled on account of which matter your Blessedness has rejected with so many arguments and reasons the Bull sent to me, or why the place Savona must be suspect to me: not for reason of the soil, nor of the house of the illustrious King of the French, which is a lofty house and the head of its lineage (if at any time some enmity is said to have existed, that is the affair of you or those like you), nor finally of the city of Genoa, on whose shore or bank it lies, which I hold as faithful and very dear to me, as my own, bound by ancient friendship. Therefore, with these and other things which I now leave aside, the tedious length of my words, since it has pleased your Blessedness, and I hold and am, I persuade, advise, supplicate, pray and beseech, that for the sake of the matter, and the most speedy completion and perfection of the affair, you proceed not only to Savona, a place agreed upon and lawful, as all truly know, but also, if it pleases you, to Paris, a city full of wisdom.

units.la: 5. Neque sperno, imò acceptissima mihi est oblatio per vestram Beatitudinem facta, ut temporum & locorum cautam meam, ut justissima vestra est Beatitudo ipsa, sicut pridem mihi spondit, ut pro possessoribus concludatur, habeat unà cum aliis Dominis sacri Collegii in præcommissam recommissam, an non quadret dare veniam, si fiat audacissimè fretus divini præsidij vestri numinis juris & justæ causæ, hoc Regnum ad me pertinens, tam ex successione divæ memoriæ Caroli Regis primi, cujus unicus sum successor & hæres, quàm ex concessione almæ matris Ecclesiæ, ita mecum delium ope & amore, si opus erit, armis & viribus, quibus illud adeptus sum, bene tuebor, ut non que cæde, non absque finali exitio vim inferre volentium, aut quod absit, aberitque Deo tutore orum & mea, in pollestione domini vivus remanceam, aut extinctus. Postremo citatus & monitus emptorie à vestra Beatitudine. Id randem faciam, quod obedientiæ filij veto patri, & matri ex debito facere obligantur. Et licet pridie ante Bullæ Apostolicæ receptionem, meos peritos resad vestram Beatitudinem transmiserim, quos confestim supplico expediri, non dimpostos tamen mittam, me & meam innocentiam excusaturos, atque singula, ad quæ teneor, perac-
units.tr: 5. Nor do I scorn it; indeed the offer made through your Blessedness is most acceptable to me, as to the caution of my times and places, since your Blessedness is most just, as you once promised me, so that a decision may be reached on behalf of the possessors, and you may have, together with the other Lords of the sacred College, the matter once committed and recommitted. Is it not fitting to pardon me if I act with the greatest boldness, relying on the divine protection of your power, on the right and on the just cause, this Kingdom belonging to me, both by the succession of the divine memory of King Charles the First, of whom I am the sole successor and heir, and by the grant of kind Mother Church? So, with the help and love of my faithful men, and, if need be, with arms and forces, by which I obtained it, I will well defend it, so that, with God as guardian of my own people and of me, I may remain living or dead in possession of my lordship, not without final destruction to those who wish to inflict violence. Lastly, I have been summoned and admonished peremptorily by your Blessedness. At length I will do what sons are bound to do out of duty to a father and mother in obedience. And although, the day before the reception of the Apostolic Bull, I sent my experts back to your Blessedness, whom I now beg to be dispatched at once, nevertheless I will not send them without excuse; they will excuse me and my innocence, and will carry out each single thing that I am bound to do.

units.la: 6. Ibid. 6. Sed quæso, Sanctissime Pater, compescite hos animi vestri motus, ab aliis forsitan inter nos dissidium procurantibus concitatos, & placidum pii Patris in filium spiritum reassumatis, otans denique cum Propheta; Domine ne in furore tuo arguas me, &c. Altissimus Beatitudinem vestram bene dirigat, diuturnumque gubernet. Datæ Neapoli, 12. die Octobris, anno Domini M. CCCC. VII.
units.tr: 6. Ibid. 6. But I beg you, most holy Father, to restrain these movements of your mind, which others, perhaps, who are setting us at odds, have stirred up, and to take back the gentle spirit of a loving father toward his son. Finally, I pray with the Prophet: Lord, rebuke me not in thine anger, etc. May the Most High guide your Blessedness well and keep you long. Given at Naples, 12 October, in the year of the Lord 1407.

units.la: LADISLAI TYRANNI ROM. MANDATUM
units.tr: LADISLAUS THE TYRANT'S MANDATE TO THE ROMANS

units.la: DE VNIONE SCHISMATICORVM PAPARVM TRACTANDA.
units.tr: CONCERNING THE UNION OF THE SCHISMATIC POPES, TO BE TREATED

units.la: LADISLAUS Romanorum, Hungariæ, Hierusalem, Siciliæ, Apuliæ, Dalmatiæ, Croatiæ, Ramiæ, Serviæ, Galiciæ, Lodomitiæ, Comaniæ, Bulgariæ Rex, necnon Provinciæ & Fortalquerii ac Pedemontium Comes, Florentinis salutem. Magnifici Domini, amici charissimi, significatum est nobis ab Ambasiatoribus nostris Lucæ morantibus apud Dominum nostrum Papam, & ab aliis ipsarum fide dignis, quod pro schismate tollendo & unione in sancta Dei Ecclesia reformanda, tam eidem Domino nostro Papæ, quam alteri parti terras vestras & loca liberè obtulistis. Quamobrem videtur, quod idem Dominus noster ad prædicta perficienda elegerit civitatem Pisarum: de qua quidem electione plurimum contentamur. Nam scimus, & pro certo tenemus, quod si dicta unio in dicta civitate Pisarum, aut alia terra fieret, quod propter antiquam & charam amicitiam, quæ inter nos voisque semper fuit, & erit, agenda & excipienda nostra pro rerum agendarum conclusione taliter disponetur & omninò fient, ac si in terris nostris fieret unio ante dicta; & licet sæpe tentaverimus ab eodem Domino nostro posse certificari, quomodo succedente dicta unione de statu nostro possemus esse securi, & remanere in secura proprietate dicti c Regni nostri, sicut Domini Cardinales, Archiepiscopi, Episcopi, & alii usque ad infimos Clericos, qui possident, debent in eorum dignitatibus, & beneficiis, ut fertur publicè, remanere, nūquam id obtinere potuimus, nec per literas supplicatorias, nec per nostros Oratores ad dictum Dominum nostrum sæpius destinatos, & ob eam causam nostris Ambasiatoribus literis & precibus in nullo proficientibus ad tantam rem, & ne ex negligentu prætermittatur, decrevimus ad quemcunque locum, ubi unio ipsa fiet, personaliter proficisci, ubi favores à vobis habere credimus nostris præcipuis benevolis & amicis. Cumque parati & expediti sumus, atque in itinere constituti, rogamus Magnificentiam vestram attentè, quatenus nobis intimare placeat, si unio ipsa Pisis, vel alibi in terris vestris fieri debeat, an non, & si ibi eam fieri forte contingat, hortamur, ut pro nobis & societate nostra victualia & alia necessaria tam ibi, quàm in aliis terris vestris in ipso itinere situatis, mandare placeat præparari ad sufficientiam oportunam, ac ut inveniantur pretio competenti: nec minùs in loco statuto, vel statuendo, aliqua conveniens & decens mansio præparetur, ac de omnibus per latorem præsentium, quem ad hoc specialiter transmittimus, nos placeat avisare & reddere certiores, offerentes nos ad quælibet vobis grata. Datum Romæ sub parvo nostro sigillo, die 111. Maii, prima Indictione.
units.tr: LADISLAUS, King of the Romans, Hungary, Jerusalem, Sicily, Apulia, Dalmatia, Croatia, Rama, Serbia, Galicia, Lodomeria, Cumania and Bulgaria, also Count of Provence and Forcalquier and of Piedmont, to the Florentines, greetings. Magnificent lords, dearest friends: our ambassadors, who are staying at Lucca with our lord the Pope, and others worthy of trust, have informed us that, to end the schism and to reform the union of the holy Church of God, you have freely offered your lands and places both to the same our lord the Pope and to the other party. Wherefore it seems that the same our lord has chosen the city of Pisa for carrying out these matters, and we are greatly pleased with this choice. For we know and firmly hold that if the said union were to take place in the said city of Pisa or in another land, then, on account of the ancient and dear friendship which has always existed and will exist between us and you, our role in the arrangement and conclusion of the business to be done will be so disposed, and everything will be carried out entirely, as if the aforesaid union were taking place in our own lands.
