And although we have often tried to be assured by the same our lord how, once the said union has been effected, we might be secure concerning our state and remain in secure possession of our said kingdom, just as the lord Cardinals, Archbishops, Bishops and others down to the lowest clerics, who hold property, are publicly reported to be entitled to remain in their dignities and benefices, we have never been able to obtain this, neither by letters of supplication nor through our ambassadors, who have been sent to the said lord our often, and, since our ambassadors have achieved nothing by letters and entreaties, and so that so great a matter may not be neglected through carelessness, we have resolved to set out in person for whatever place the union itself shall take place, where we believe we shall have the favour of you, our chief well-wishers and friends. And since we are ready and prepared and already on the road, we earnestly ask your Magnificence to be pleased to let us know whether the union itself is to take place at Pisa or elsewhere in your lands, or not; and if it should perchance happen to take place there, we urge you to be pleased to order that provisions and other necessities be prepared for us and our company, both there and in your other lands lying along the route itself, in sufficient quantity and at a fair price; and likewise that in the place fixed, or to be fixed, some suitable and decent lodging be made ready, and that we be pleased to be informed and made certain of all these things by the bearer of these presents, whom we send specially for this purpose, offering ourselves for whatever is pleasing to you. Given at Rome under our small seal, on the 3rd day of May, in the first indiction.

units.la: Quia similiter venient per mare pro nostra societate nonnullæ galeæ & navigia alia, ideo placeat modo simili emenda competenti pretio victualia facere præparari. Datum, ut supra.
units.tr: Since likewise several galleys and other ships will come by sea for our company, we ask that, in the same way, provisions be prepared and bought at a fair price. Given as above.

units.la: Et quoniam credimus Dominum nostrum cognoscere viam talem unionis, unionem pacificam omnibus Christi fidelibus non perducere, sed pejorem scissuram priore, Nos, prout interest, velut Rex vel saltem ut persona sacra ad tanti boni perfectionem intendimus personaliter interesse, tam etiam pro bono publico, quàm privato, ad quod ultimum non attenderent omnes potiùs, quàm ad primum. Ethoc per vestras literas & nuntios speciales, unum post alium, & alium post unum subitò intimetis, pro pecunia omittatis, quin eis satisfaciemus in promptu, ita quod sumus avisati. Nam avisatum intendimus perdere, nec in verbis quomodolibet detineri. Datum, ut supra.
units.tr: And since we believe that our lord knows that such a way of union will not bring about a peaceful union for all the faithful of Christ, but a worse split than the former, we, as is fitting, both as King and at least as a sacred person, intend to be present in person to bring about the completion of so great a good, as much for the public good as for the private, to which last all men would pay more heed than to the first. And you are to make this known to us at once, by your letters and special messengers, one after another and another after one, and do not hold back for money, since we will satisfy them promptly, so that we are informed. For we intend that a notice be lost, and that we be detained by words in no way whatever. Given as above.

units.la: RUPERTI IMP. AUG. EDICTUM
units.tr: THE EDICT OF EMPEROR RUPERT AUGUSTUS

units.la: Pro confirmatione Gregorii XII. Papæ, & infirmatione Alexandri V. à Concilio Pisano electi.
units.tr: For the confirmation of Pope Gregory XII and the invalidation of Alexander V, elected by the Council of Pisa.

units.la: FLAMINES Romani à duobus electis in schismate Pontificibus deficiunt, Pisæ conventus aguntt, utrinque dirasinfetiaque dicunt, atque dignitatem abrogant, Alexandrum Quintum ovili Romano imponunt. RUPERTUS Cæsar, qui rebus Gregorii XII. favebat, per Fdictum obstinat, irrita hujusce modi comitia neque libera, Duodecimum verum pastorem decernit esse Christiani gregis, Alexandrum veluti suppositium rejicit.
units.tr: The Roman prelates abandon the two rival Popes elected in the schism. They hold assemblies at Pisa, pronounce dire and hostile curses on both sides, and strip them of their dignity. They set Alexander V over the Roman fold. Emperor Rupert, who favoured the cause of Gregory XII, declares by edict that such assemblies are void and not free. He decrees that Gregory XII, the Twelfth, is the true shepherd of the Christian flock, and he rejects Alexander as a supposititious pastor.
Kk

units.la: RUPERTI IMPER. AUG. FORMULA
units.tr: RUPERT, EMPEROR AUGUST, FORMULA

units.la: Concessa Sedis libera, & Frygraviatus.
units.tr: Grant of a free seat, and of the Frygraviate.

units.la: RUPERTUS Dei gratia Romanorum Rex semper-Augustus: Notum facimus tenore praesentium universis, quòd ad supplicem petitionis mitantiam Alrigeniti Principis Hermanni Landgravii Hassiae, Svvageri nostri dilecti, Hennen Salentin fidelem nostrum dilectum Frygravium seu Comitem Liberum in sede Fryheholenor vulgariter nuncupata, sita in dominio Zuls constituimus, ipsumque de dicta sede Frygraviatus tenore praesentium investimus, dantes sibi liberam ibidem de caetero judicandi, & omnia exercendi, quae ad Frygraviatus hujusmodi spectare noscuntur de consuetudine seu de jure. Quapropter universis & singulis Praelatis, Ecclesiasticis & Secularibus, Comitibus, Baronibus, Nobilibus, Ministerialibus, Militibus, Civibus, Civitatum communitatibus, & signanter Frygraviis seu Comitibus Liberis sub poena privationis Frygraviatuum officiorum, firmiter inhibemus, ne dictum Hennen in ejusmodi Frygraviatu impediant aliqualiter vel molestent, sicut nostram indignationem Regiam voluerint evitare, poenam sub Regiae Majestatis nostrae sigillo testimonio literarum. Datum Marpurg, Anno Domini M. CCCC. X. die quarta Martii, Regni vero nostri anno decimo.
units.tr: RUPERT, by the grace of God King of the Romans, ever August: We make known by the tenor of these presents to all, that at the humble petition of our beloved kinsman Hermann, Landgrave of Hesse, the illustrious Prince, we appoint our faithful and beloved Hennen Salentin as Frygrave, or Free Count, in the seat commonly called Fryheholenor, situated in the lordship of Zuls, and we invest him, by the tenor of these presents, with the said seat of the Frygraviate, granting him free power there henceforth to judge and to exercise all those rights which are known to pertain to such a Frygraviate by custom or by law. Wherefore we strictly forbid all and singular prelates, ecclesiastical and secular, counts, barons, nobles, ministerials, knights, citizens, the communities of cities, and especially the Frygraves or Free Counts, under penalty of the loss of their Frygraviate offices, that they in any way hinder or molest the said Hennen in such a Frygraviate, as they wish to avoid our royal indignation and the penalty under the seal of His Royal Majesty, our testimony in this letter. Given at Marburg, in the year of our Lord 1410, on the fourth day of March, in the tenth year of our reign.

units.la: Ad mandatum Domini Regis
units.tr: By command of the Lord King.

units.la: Johannes Weinheim.
units.tr: Johannes Weinheim.

units.la: SIGISMUNDI IMPERA- TORIS AUGUSTI MANDATUM
units.tr: THE MANDATE OF THE EMPEROR SIGISMUND

units.la: AD REGEM FRANCIAE, UT VENIAT AD Concilium Constantiense, pro tollendo schismate Paparum, & refor- manda Ecclesia indictum.
units.tr: TO THE KING OF FRANCE, CALLING HIM TO COME TO THE COUNCIL OF CONSTANCE, CONVENED TO END THE SCHISM OF THE POPES AND TO REFORM THE CHURCH.

units.la: SIGISMUNDUS Dei gratia Romanorum Rex semper-Augustus, &c. Serenissimo Principi Carolo Regi Francorum Illustri, Consanguineo nostro carissimo, & fideli dilecto, &c.
units.tr: SIGISMUND, by the grace of God Roman King, ever Augustus, etc., to the most serene Prince Charles, illustrious King of the Franks, our most dear kinsman and beloved faithful friend, etc.

units.la: 1. Rex pacificus pia miseratione disposuit, ne homo creaturarum dignissima, quem de limo terrae formatum ad imaginem & similitudinem suam fecit, per abusum liberi arbitrii labctetur, & labendo à cognitione sui recederet creatoris, dum par in parem imperium non haberet, Praeesse operi superesse voluit, quorum ducatu vita cujuslibet regeretur, ac ipsorum motibus & praeceptis inferiores ceteri obedirent. Sicque statuit duo luminaria super terram, majus videlicet atque minus, ipsis universalis ecclesiae consisteret firmamentum, in quibus Pontificalis auctoritas & Regalis potestas designantur: una videlicet, quae spiritualia; & altera, quae corporalia regerentur. Ad subsistentium machinae spiritualis, beatum Petrum Apostolorum Principem, & in beato Petro Pontificum successores, summus Pontifex in aeternum unigenitus Dei filius Jesus Christus, qui doctrinam hujus tribuit generi salutatem, magistros esse voluit & pastores: ad corporalis vero compaginis firmitatem, cujus facilis est profecto distinctio. Reges & Principes Rex Regum & Dominus Dominantium idem ipse praesse voluit Jesus Christus, ut illi quidem in executione Pontificalis officii spiritualibus vacando negociis proficerent ad salutem: & hii salubriter in excellentia Regiae dignitatis corporalibus gubernando malicus hominum obviarent: sicque machina fieret utriusque subjecti stabilior, ut haberet quodlibet proprium servatorem. Debitum profecto * caritatis, quae a non quae sua sunt quaerit, rum expositum, ut non solum is, qui contemplationis speculam ascendit, sed oportunitate suadente onus onera supportans magis necessarius inveniatur: quia licet ille sit lecurior, hic tamen est utilior & aliis commodum afferens & profectum. Licet enim b Maria sedentis secus pedes Domini, Marthae ministerio praeferatur, & quòd sit status ille tutior, utpote à saeculari strepitu segregatus; attamen potest utilior judicari esse, quòd sibi prodest & aliis, tribulationes sustinens & pressuras, quas virtutes suscipiunt incrementum: quoniam, sicut ait Apostolus, c tribulatio patientiam operatur, patientia probationem, probatio spem, spes autem non confundit. Et plerumque contingit, quòd virtus in infirmitate perficitur.
units.tr: 1. The peaceful King, in his pious compassion, arranged that man, the most worthy of creatures, whom he formed from the clay of the earth in his own image and likeness, should not stumble through the abuse of free will and, stumbling, fall away from the knowledge of his Creator. Since there was no equal to rule over an equal, he willed that some should be set over the work, to lead it, and that by their leading the life of each would be governed, and the rest would obey their movements and commands. So he established two great lights upon the earth, the greater and the lesser, on which the firmament of the universal Church rests, and by which the Pontifical authority and the Royal power are designated: the one, namely, to govern spiritual things, and the other to govern bodily things. For the support of the spiritual machine, he willed that the blessed Peter, Prince of the Apostles, and in blessed Peter the successors of the Pontiffs, should be teachers and shepherds: Jesus Christ, the only-begotten Son of God, the eternal supreme Pontiff, who gave the teaching of salvation to the human race. For the firmness of the bodily framework, whose distinction is indeed easy, the same Jesus Christ, King of kings and Lord of lords, willed to set over kings and princes, so that the former, by devoting themselves to spiritual affairs in the execution of the Pontifical office, might advance to salvation, and the latter, by governing bodily things wholesomely in the excellence of royal dignity, might oppose the wickedness of men; and thus the machine would be the more stable in each of its parts, so that each would have its own proper preserver. Indeed the debt of charity, which does not seek its own, is set out so that not only he who climbs to the watchtower of contemplation, but he who, bearing burdens, supports the burdens of others as opportunity urges, may be found more necessary. For although the former is the safer, the latter is the more useful, bringing benefit and progress to others. For although Mary, sitting at the Lord's feet, is preferred to Martha's service, and that state is safer as being withdrawn from worldly noise, yet it may be judged more useful that one profits both oneself and others by enduring tribulations and pressures, which the virtues take up for their increase; since, as the Apostle says, tribulation works patience, patience proof, proof hope, and hope does not disappoint. And it often happens that virtue is made perfect in weakness.

units.la: * 1. Cor. 13. a. Roman. 16. Philipp. 2. b. Luc. 10. c. Roman. 5.
units.tr: * 1 Cor. 13. a. Rom. 16. Phil. 2. b. Luke 10. c. Rom. 5.

units.la: 2. Sed quia diebus istis novissimis, in quibus superexcrescente malitia in immensum refrigescit caritas, in plerisque proprius appetitus, qui d niti semper in veterum consuevit, adeò debacchatur homine, quodam dato quasi libello repudii libertas arbitrii, qua bonum malumve discernitur, extra terminos honestatis, multum oneris multumque sollicitudinis nobis incumbit, ut animarum corporumque pericula caveantur. Nisi enim malicus hominum congruis obstaculis obviam descensus est profecto labilis ad excessus, & dum per lubricum iter discriminis abusivè descendatur.
units.tr: 2. But because in these latest days, in which, as wickedness grows beyond measure, charity grows cold, in most men their own appetite, which has always been accustomed to strive against the ancients, so rages within a person that, as if a bill of divorce had been given, the freedom of the will by which good and evil are discerned is pushed beyond the bounds of decency; much burden and much anxiety fall upon us, so that the dangers to souls and bodies may be guarded against. For unless the wickedness of men is met with fitting obstacles, the descent to excesses is surely slippery, and while one goes down the treacherous road of danger in a headlong way...

units.la: d. Ovidius lib. 3. Amor. Bellis / proh dolor relevatio vix haberur. Inter profecto curas varias nostris processibus influentes, quotidiana nos excitat, qualiter generali bono statui totius populi Christiani multipliciter modis, nostris temporibus proficere valeamus, ut cum in die illa novissima, die scilicet magni & tremendi Judicis, ducuflio venerit, plenam possimus ipsius Dei superfavente clementia commissis nobis talentis, duplicata Domino importando, reddere rationem. Maximo etiam desiderio jamdudum tenebamur, ut diebus nostris videre possemus unicam Christi sponsam, catholicam Ecclesiam, feliciter reformatam: postea vero cum ad Imperialia gubernacula fuissemus impti, id quod erat nobis in desiderio, transfivir in praeceptum, cum teneamur sanctam matrem Ecclesiam per Imperiale officium tueri, cujus etiam Canones sanctorum Patrum nos appellant Advocatos & defensores.
units.tr: d. Ovid, Amores, book 3: "In wars, alas, scarcely any relief is found." Among the various cares flowing into our affairs, we are daily roused to consider how, in our times, we may be able to advance the general good of the whole Christian people in many ways, so that when that last day comes, the day of the great and terrible Judge, we may, by the favour of God's own mercy, render account to the Lord, presenting the talents committed to us doubled. We were also held for a long time by the greatest desire that in our days we might see the one spouse of Christ, the Catholic Church, happily reformed. Afterwards, when we had been raised to the imperial helm, what had been our desire became a command, since we are bound to protect our holy mother the Church through the imperial office, and whom the Canons of the holy Fathers also call us advocates and defenders.

units.la: 3. Considerantes veritatem, qualiter & quomodo salubriter id peragere valeamus, cum Ecclesiasticis & Secularibus, Ducibus, Comitibus, Baronibus, & Proceribus, aliisque quoque dignitatibus & peritis nostri & Imperii sacri fidelibus, prout tantae rei instantia exigebat, accurato frequenti tractatu praehabito: interea contingit nos intellexisse, quomodo sanctissimus Dominus Johannes Papa XXIII. venerabile Concilium * indixisset. Summo itaque * mf. indux. cura vimus, ne quid negligentiae posset in hoc nobis apud Deum & homines imputari. Et ob fct. hoc per litteras & nuncios instituimus apud eundem Dominum nostrum Papam pro edicatione generalis Concilii, loco alibi & tempore congruo deputandis. Qui nostris votis annuens misit ad reverendissimos in Christo Patres, Dominos ad titulum sanctae Caeciliae Presbyterum & * sanctorum Cosmae & Damiani Diaconum, sanctae Romanae Ecclesiae Cardinales, Apostolicae Sedis Legatos, & Nobilem M . . . traditam eidem in praedictis plena potestatem. Ipsis vero ad nos pervenientibus multa nobiscum habita super his consilia tandem nos cum eisdem pro loco Concilii elegimus tem Constantiensem Provinciae Moguntinensis. Quem locum nos eisdem nominavimus, tutum, & communem omnibus nationibus ad Concilium venturis: & in quo, favente, curabimus personaliter interesse, & omni modo posse secundum nostrum Imperiale tueri omnes cujuscumque status ad Concilium venturos in plena libertate: ita quod o-mnes poltpofito poterunt ad Concilium venire, ibi stare, & recedere pro sua voluntate. Et innos cum praedictis Legatis & nuncios ad initiandum praefatum Concilium assignavimus tempus annuum, incipiendo die prima mensis Novembris nunc instantis.
units.tr: 3. Considering the truth, how and in what way we might be able to accomplish this wholesomely, we held beforehand a careful and frequent deliberation, as the urgency of so great a matter required, with ecclesiastics and laymen, dukes, counts, barons and nobles, and others of dignity and skill, faithful to us and to our Holy Empire. Meanwhile it came to our understanding that the most holy Lord John XXIII, Pope, had called a venerable Council. Therefore, with the highest care, we took thought that nothing of negligence could be imputed to us before God and men. For this reason we undertook, by letters and messengers, with the same Lord our Pope, that a general Council be proclaimed, to be appointed in a suitable place and at a suitable time elsewhere. He, assenting to our wishes, sent to the most reverend Fathers in Christ, the Lords, the Cardinal Priest of the title of Saint Cecilia and the Deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, cardinals of the holy Roman Church and Legates of the Apostolic See, and a noble M..., to whom full power in the aforesaid matters was handed over. When these came to us, after many counsels held with us on these matters, we at last chose with them, as the place for the Council, Constance in the Province of Mainz. This place we named to them as safe and common to all nations coming to the Council, and in which, God willing, we shall ourselves be present in person, and shall, in every way possible and according to our imperial office, protect all persons of whatever rank coming to the Council in full liberty, so that all, laying aside fear, may come to the Council, remain there, and depart as they wish. And we have appointed, together with the aforesaid Legates and messengers, a year's time for opening the said Council, beginning on the first day of the present month of November.

units.la: 4. Expedit quippe, ut universi & singuli solicitudine non pigri, fervente spiritu Domino ferentes, in * vinea Domini Sabaoth, in qua ex denario diurno & labore convenimus, inrefragabiliter * Matth.10. extirpandis vitiorum spinis & peccatorum tribulis, quae superficiem ejus obumbrasse videntur: necnon plantandis virtutum germinibus, in quibus Dominus delectatur, totis affectibus in-tendendo illustrare. Illustrem itaque Serenitatem vestram ex Imperiali officio ad tam suave & dulcis-Rex Franciae vocatur ad Concilium. simum convivium fraternae vel caritativae invitamus & * * requirimus & hortamur in Domino, ut pro religione Catholica, quam Deo debetis, ad cujus divinae religionis exaltationem & statum institutum est praemissum Concilium, velitis in praefato Concilio, tempore praescripto, si commode poteritis, vos; vel si commoditas personalis non patietur, saltem per vestros solemnes Ambassiatores interesse, atque cum effectu diligenter & curare, ut Praelati, Doctores, & Magistri, & viri Ecclesiastici, & laici & seculares, qui sunt in vestro regno & territorio, veniant ad hujusmodi Concilium tempore constituto.
units.tr: 4. It is indeed fitting that all and each, not slothful in care, bearing with fervent spirit in the Lord, labour in the vineyard of the Lord of Sabaoth, in which we gather for the daily denarius and toil; and with all our affections we should strive to illustrate it by uprooting the thorns of vices and the thistles of sins, which seem to have overshadowed its surface, and by planting the seeds of virtues, in which the Lord delights. Therefore we invite Your Serenity, illustrious by imperial office, to this sweet and most pleasant fraternal and charitable feast, and we require and exhort you in the Lord that, for the Catholic religion, which you owe to God, and for whose exaltation and establishment the aforesaid Council has been instituted, you be willing to take part in the said Council at the prescribed time, in person if you can conveniently do so, or, if personal convenience does not allow it, at least through your solemn ambassadors; and that you diligently and effectively see to it that prelates, teachers and masters, ecclesiastics, and laymen and secular persons who are in your kingdom and territory come to such a Council at the appointed time. Matth. 10.

units.la: 5. Ubi dum tantorum Regum, Praesulum, & Principum, quos unitas fidei Orthodoxae connectit honorabili congregatione Concilium ipsum & Comitiva suffultum, ac in cujus nomine, cuius vult spirat, collecta Ecclesia reparationem, ordinationem, reformationem & stabilitatem Johan. 3. sanctae matris & universalis Ecclesiae, ac pacem & quietem populi Christiani, sicut casti consilii Altissimus infusionem suae gratiae amministrabit. . . . . Illa communi consilio etiam a. mf. primado veneficii antiqua & antiquata peste dilidi, quo universalis Ecclesiae unitatem Orien-ministrabit. tiorum dissensio damnabiliter secuit, ut in domum Domini individuam sponsae unicae, orthodoxae b collectionis & intemeratae fidei puritate, (Utinam nostris temporibus caeli-b. vel collationis. c. fort. foli-latur haec gratia, per providam reintegrationem reducatur, & lucis coelestis illuminatione c detur. in revelationem gentium, inveniatur provisio & ejusdem approbatione Concilii rocujus salutiferam executionem vitus Altissimi fugatis erroribus, roborata fide, ad tramites reductis errantibus, reintegrata ejusdem fidei unitate, extirpatis vitiis, virtutibusque; plantis excellibus, moribus reformatis, repressis oppressionibus, libertate solida stabilitate mu-ratis depperditis, & ejusdem Ecclesiae statu prosperoque recuperato occupata restituat, vastata & restaurata conservet, viamque aperiat idem ipse qui novit, & facultatem tribuat ipse qui in praemissis juxta intensum animum nostrum deliderium sibi ministrari salubriter, quod ejusdem universalis sponsus Ecclesiae ipsam dilectam suam purgatam maculis, ornatam nulibus, ac speciosam, unam semper habeat cum unico sponso vero, & formosam, quam macula sua virtutum bonus pastor, qui animam suam pro suis posuit ovibus, non habentem maculam neque rugam, in veritate deaurato circundata varietate introducat ad sui nominis laudem & gloriam, animarum profectum, robur fidei, sanctae matris & universalis Ecclesiae exaltationem ac pacem plebis Christianae, &c.
units.tr: 5. Where, while the Council itself is supported by the honourable gathering of so great Kings, Prelates and Princes, whom the unity of the Orthodox faith binds together, and in whose name the gathered Church breathes where it wills, the Most High will bestow, by the infusion of his grace, the reform, ordering, restoration and stability of the holy mother and universal Church, and the peace and quiet of the Christian people, as the wise counsel of the Most High shall administer. [Johan. 3.] By common counsel, let that ancient and outdated plague of poison, by which the dissension of the Eastern peoples damnably cut the unity of the universal Church, be driven out, so that into the house of the Lord, the undivided one of the single spouse, in the purity of orthodox collation and undefiled faith (Would that in our times this grace might be granted from heaven, be led back by provident reintegration, and be given in the illumination of heavenly light, for a revelation to the Gentiles), a provision may be found, and by the approval of the same Council, whose saving execution the Most High may bring about: errors put to flight, faith strengthened, the erring led back to the right paths, the unity of the same faith restored, vices rooted out, excellent virtues planted, morals reformed, oppressions repressed, liberty and solid stability restored, the lost recovered, and the state and prosperity of the same Church regained, the devastated restored and the restored preserved; and may He who knows the way open it, and He who, according to our intense desire in the aforesaid matters, grants the means, bestow them wholesomely on us, so that the same Bridegroom of the universal Church may have his beloved spouse, cleansed of her stains, adorned without wrinkles and beautiful, always one with the one true Bridegroom, and fair, whom the good shepherd, who laid down his life for his sheep, leads without spot or wrinkle, encircled in truth by golden variety, to the praise and glory of his name, the profit of souls, the strengthening of faith, the exaltation of the holy mother and universal Church, and the peace of the Christian people, etc.

units.la: b. vel collationis. c. fort. foliatur.
units.tr: b. or of collation. c. perhaps: be foliated.

units.la: CONFIRMATIO FRIDERICI ET CAROLINAE CON- STITUTIONIS in favorem Ecclesiasticae libertatis, per Johannem XXIII. Papam facta.
units.tr: The confirmation of the constitution of Frederick and Charles in favour of ecclesiastical liberty, made by Pope John XXIII.

units.la: IOHANNES Episcopus servus servorum Dei, Venerabilibus fratribus Olomucensi & Lubucensi ac Misnensi, Episcopis, salutem, & apostolicam benedictionem. Justis & honestis votis libenter annuimus, illaque favoribus prosequimur opportunis.
units.tr: John, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to our venerable brothers, the bishops of Olomouc, Lubeck and Meissen, greeting and apostolic blessing. We willingly grant just and honest wishes, and we support them with fitting favours.

units.la: Dudum siquidem Honorius papa Tertius praedecessor noster attente considerans, quod memoriae Friedericus secundus Romanorum Imperator semper-Augustus, ad laudem Romanae Ecclesiae & sacri decus imperii, cupiens ut expurgatis quorundam eorioribus, & iniquis statutis, quae in perniciem statuti, de caetero Ecclesiae & Ecclesiasticae personae plena quiete vigerent, & secura libertate frui deberent, ac pie & juste attendens, quod quorundam perversorum iniquitates adeo abundarent, non dubitarent, contra ecclesiasticam disciplinam & sacros Canones statuta condingere, ad ecclesiasticas personas & ecclesiasticam libertatem edita tali lege, hujusmodi statuta iniqua praecepisset irrita nunciari, ac omnia statuta & consuetudines, quae civitates, & loca, potestates aut quaecunque aliae personae, contra libertatem Ecclesiae vel personas ecclesiasticas edere vel tentarent, contra Canonicas vel imperiales sanctiones, de ipsorum capitularibus, mensibus, post ipsius legis publicationem, penitus abolere facerent. Et si de caetero similia attentarent, ipso jure decreverat esse nulla. Ereosque jurisdictione privandos: necnon locum, ubi praesumpta fuissent banno mille marcarum auri praeceperat subjacere. Potestas vero, cives, talliarios & scriptores statutorum praedictorum, necnon Consiliarios locorum ipsorum, & qui statuta, & consuetudines memorata judicarent, extunc essent ipso jure infames, quorum actus legitimos statuerat aliquatenus non tenere. Quodque, si per annum praefatae Constitutionis fuissent contemptores, bona eorum, per totum suum imperium mandavit impune abripi, capi, salvis nihilominus aliis poenis, contra tales in Concilio generali promulgatis. Et insuper idem Imperator, quod nulla communitas, vel persona publica seu privata collectas, sive exactiones, angarias, vel per angarias Ecclesiis vel aliis piis locis aut Ecclesiasticis personis imponerent, aut ab re ecclesiastica bona praesumerent, quod si secus facerent, triplum restituerent, & inhibuit, imperiali subjacerent, ab sq; satisfactione debita nullatenus temitteretur. Statuerat quoque communitas, vel persona per annum in excommunicatione propter libertate Ecclesiae persisteret, ipso jure Imperiali Banno subjaceret, a quo nullatenus extraheretur, nisi prius ab Ecclesia beneficio absolutionis obtento. Et insuper ordinaverat, quod nullus Ecclesiasticam personam in criminali quaestione vel civili trahere ad judicium saeculare praesumeret contra canonicas sanctiones, constitutiones imperiales, quod si secus faceret, actor a jure suo caderet, judicari non teneretur, etiam forer extunc judicandi auctoritate privatus. Quodque, judices temporales, qui clericis vel ecclesiasticis personis justitiam denegare praesumerent, tertio e quilibet suam jurisdictionem amitterent, proinde imperiali constitutione plenius cohibetur. Dictusque quam praedecessor constitutionem ipsam filio etiam fratrum suorum sanctae Romanae Ecclesiae Cardinalium apostolica authoritate & confirmans, ipsam mandavit inviolabiliter observari. Necnon Statutarios, scriptores & victoriosos praedictos, excommunicatos auctoritate apostolica praedicta publice nunciari.
units.tr: Some time ago our predecessor Pope Honorius III, carefully considering that Frederick II, Emperor of the Romans, ever august, of blessed memory, desiring the praise of the Roman Church and the honour of the holy empire, wished that, once certain harsh and unjust statutes, which were to the ruin of the state, had been purged away, the Church and ecclesiastical persons should thereafter flourish in full quiet and enjoy secure liberty. Piously and justly attending to the fact that the iniquities of certain wicked men so abounded that they did not hesitate to enact statutes against ecclesiastical discipline and the sacred canons, he had, by a law issued for ecclesiastical persons and ecclesiastical liberty, ordered such unjust statutes to be declared void. He had also caused all statutes and customs which cities, places, magistrates or any other persons should issue or attempt against the liberty of the Church or against ecclesiastical persons, contrary to canonical or imperial sanctions, to be utterly abolished from their statute books within months of the publication of that law. If they should attempt similar things in future, he had decreed them null by law itself, and their authors deprived of jurisdiction; and he had ordered the place where such things were presumed to be subject to a ban of a thousand marks of gold. The magistracy, the citizens, tax-collectors and writers of the said statutes, as well as the councillors of those places and those who judged under the said statutes and customs, should then be infamous by law itself, and he decreed that their legitimate acts should in some way not be held valid. And if they should be contemners of the said constitution for a year, he ordered their goods to be seized with impunity throughout his whole empire, other penalties promulgated against such persons by a general council remaining in force. Moreover, the same Emperor forbade any community or public or private person to impose levies, exactions or forced labour (angariae) on churches, other pious places or ecclesiastical persons, or to presume to take goods from ecclesiastical property; if they did otherwise, they should restore three times the amount and be subject to the imperial ban, and not be released without due satisfaction. He also decreed that any community or person who persisted for a year in excommunication on account of the liberty of the Church should be subject by law itself to the imperial ban, from which they should in no way be released unless they first obtained absolution from the Church. He further ordered that no one should presume to drag an ecclesiastical person into a criminal or civil case before a secular court, contrary to canonical sanctions and imperial constitutions; if anyone did so, the plaintiff should lose his right and the person sued should not be obliged to answer, and even the judge should then be deprived of judicial authority. And that temporal judges who presumed to deny justice to clerics or ecclesiastical persons should lose their jurisdiction on the third offence; this is more fully restrained by the imperial constitution. His predecessor, confirming that constitution by apostolic authority, along with the cardinals of the holy Roman Church, ordered it to be observed inviolably. He also publicly declared the aforesaid statute-makers, writers and violators excommunicate by the same apostolic authority.

units.la: Et deinde ad audientiam divae memoriae Karoli IV. etiam Romani imperatoris sententi, deducto quod nonnulli seculares in potestatibus & officiis publicis constituti, videlicet Duces, Milites, Barones & alii domini temporales, necnon consules civitatum, oppidorum, villarum Rectores in nonnullis provinciis constituti Dei timore postposito statuta singularia ordinationes, motu proprio de facto, contra personas Ecclesiasticas, Ecclesiarum libertates & privilegia condiderant, eisque de facto & publice insistere praesumpserant, contra Canonicas sanctiones, utpote quod nulla bona temporalia in potestatem Ecclesiasticam transferre. Clerici in sacris constituti ad agendum & testificandum in civilibus, & maxime in pius causis admitterentur; quodque excommunicati laici & publice denunciati in civili foro minime recipi rentur. Et insuper cum praedicti domini temporales, Consules & Rectores per seculares pro ecclesiastica & bona clericorum occuparent, & arrestarent, ac oblationes Christi fidelium diminuerent & tollerent, exactiones & tallias indebitas de bonis & redditibus Ecclesiarum exigerent, & ab eorum possessiones Ecclesiarum & personarum earundem devastarent incendis & rapinis, contra clericos & laicos factos legitimos, ad libros civitatum, villarum & locorum praedictorum sigillare recusarent; donata & legata ad fabricas & Ecclesiarum structuras contra praelatorum tatem & aliorum quorumcunque interetur, contra justitiam usurpare praesumerent, & odium clericorum de bonis etiam & rebus clericorum, quae non causa quotationis sed occasionis fibus propriis, per eorum terras ducebant seu ducentes faciebant, theloneum exigere & inciperent banturs; & confugientes ad Ecclesias & eorum Cemiteria inde extrahere, contra sanctiones praesumebant.
units.tr: Then, when it came to the hearing of Charles IV, also Roman emperor, of blessed memory, it was reported that several secular men, placed in powers and public offices, namely dukes, knights, barons and other temporal lords, and also the consuls of cities and towns, and the rectors of villages set up in some provinces, having put aside the fear of God, had of their own motion issued singular statutes and ordinances against ecclesiastical persons and the liberties and privileges of the churches, and had presumed to enforce them openly and in fact, against canonical sanctions. For example: that no temporal goods be transferred into ecclesiastical hands; that clerics in holy orders be admitted to act and to testify in civil matters, and especially in pious causes; and that excommunicated laymen and those publicly denounced be in no way received in civil courts. Moreover, since the aforesaid temporal lords, consuls and rectors occupied and seized ecclesiastical and clerical goods through secular agents, diminished and took away the offerings of Christ's faithful, exacted undue tolls and levies from the goods and revenues of churches, and laid waste the possessions of the churches and their clergy with fire and plunder; and since they refused to seal legitimate documents for clerics and laymen in the registers of the said cities, villages and places; and since they presumed to usurp against justice goods given and bequeathed for the fabric and structures of churches, against the will of the prelates and of anyone else, and began to exact toll on the goods and property of clerics which were carried or caused to be carried through their lands, not for the sake of trade but merely on the occasion of their own journeys; and since they presumed against the sanctions to drag out of churches and their cemeteries fugitives who had taken refuge there.

units.la: Idē Karolus imperator tanquam Christianissimus princeps, volens in similibus providere, retinere tari, etiam de principum, ducum, Comitum, & Baronum fidelium; aliorum sicut imperatoris Italicorum. ate imperiali quæcunque statuta & consuetudines prædicta tanquam per Canonicas & civiles sanctiones expresse reprobata, C. tilovia in ravit, & annullavit, ac cassa & irrita, nulliusque esse roboris penitus voluit vel momenti : Præcipiens sub indignatione imperialis Banni, universis & singulis principibus & temporalibus dominis, consulibus, potestatibus & aliis in officiis publicis constitutis, quatenus extunc ipsorum statuta & ordinationes, quæ sunt in præjudicium Ecclesiasticæ libertatis editæ, omnino revocarent, & de luce tollerent, quodque secundum ea non judicarent amplius, nec sententias dictarent, aut eisdem in judicio vel extra judicium, quomodolibet pro se & contra Ecclesiasticam libertatem potirentur. Pronunciavit insuper & eadem imperiali decrevit auctoritate, quod quicunque laicus cujuscunque status vel conditionis existat, ausu sacrilego, & proprie temeritatis audacia sacerdotem vel Clericum secularem vel religiosum diffidaret, proicriberet, diffamaret, captivaret, spoliaret, occideret, mutilaret, aut in carcere detineret, ac hujusmodi maleficia perpetrantes scienter receptaret vel favorem eis præstaret, præter pœnas à sacris Canonibus & legalibus sanctionibus eis inflictas, eo ipso redderetur infamis & omni honore privatus, nec ad placita vel consilia nobilium admitteretur quovis modo. Hortans insuper & in domino requirens prælatos in illis partibus constitutos, ut legem imperialem hujusmodi per ipsorum Ecclesias & Synodos publicarent, ne transgressores hujusmodi per simulatam ignorantiam suas valerent malitias excusare, prout in edita tali lege prædicta plenius continetur.
units.tr: The same Emperor Charles, as a most Christian prince, wishing to provide in similar cases, and retaining the faithful princes, dukes, counts and barons, and others as the emperor of the Italians, by imperial authority revoked and annulled all the aforesaid statutes and customs, as expressly condemned by canonical and civil sanctions; he wished them quashed, null and void, and of no force or validity whatever. Under the displeasure of the imperial ban he commanded all and each of the princes and temporal lords, consuls, magistrates and others established in public offices that they should forthwith wholly revoke their statutes and ordinances issued to the prejudice of ecclesiastical liberty and bring them to nothing, and that they should no longer judge according to them, nor pronounce sentences by them, nor take advantage of them in any way, in judgment or outside judgment, for themselves and against ecclesiastical liberty. He further declared, and by the same imperial authority decreed, that any layman of whatever state or condition who, with sacrilegious daring and the audacity of his own rashness, should defy, outlaw, defame, imprison, despoil, kill or maim a priest or a secular or religious cleric, or detain him in prison, and who knowingly harboured or gave favour to those committing such crimes, should, besides the penalties inflicted on them by the sacred canons and legal sanctions, be by that very fact rendered infamous and deprived of all honour, and not be admitted in any way to the pleas or councils of the nobles. Moreover, he exhorted and in the Lord required the prelates established in those parts to publish this imperial law through their churches and synods, so that transgressors might not be able to excuse their malice by feigned ignorance, as is more fully contained in the law issued.

units.la: Cum autem sicut exhibita nobis nuper pro parte Venerabilis fratris nostri Episcopi Wratislaviensis & dilectorum filiorum Cleri, Civitatis & diocesis Wratislaviensis, petitio continebat, adeo perversorum quorundam laicorum in Civitate & diocesi Wratislaviensi & aliis locis circumvicinis habitantium malicia inoleverit, quod hujusmodi imperiales constitutiones transgredi non verentur, & Ecclesiasticas libertates violare præsumunt, pro parte eorundem Episcopi & Cleri nobis fuit humiliter supplicatum, ut providere eis super præmissis oportuno remedio dignaremur. Nos igitur vestigiis discipræde cessoris nostri inhærentes, hujusmodi supplicationibus inclinati fraternitati vestræ per Apostolica scripta mandamus, quatenus vos duo aut unus vestrum per vos vel alium seu alios constitutiones prædictas in præfatis civitate & diocesi Wratislaviensi & aliis locis circumvicinis auctoritate nostra faciatis inviolabiliter observari. Nec non statutarios, scriptores & violatores prædictos excommunicatos, publice nunciari, & ab omnibus aliis arctius evitari, Apostolica auctoritate faciatis tranigressores ac violatores, & contemptores ac sacrilegos prædictos, nec non contradictores quoslibet & rebelles per censuram ecclesiasticam appellatione postposita compescendo, invocato ad hoc etiam, si opus fuerit, auxilio brachii secularis non obstante si aliquibus communiter vel divisim à sede apostolica fit indultum, quod interdici, suspendi, vel excommunicari non possint, per literas apostolicas, non faciendo plenam & expressam, ac de verbo ad verbum de indulto hujusmodi mentionem. Datum Romæ apud sanctum Petrum 13. Calendas Martij, pontificatus nostri Anno tertio.
units.tr: But since, as the petition recently presented to us on behalf of our venerable brother, the Bishop of Breslau, and our beloved sons, the clergy of the city and diocese of Breslau, set out, the malice of certain wicked laymen living in the city and diocese of Breslau and in other neighbouring places has so grown that they do not fear to transgress such imperial constitutions and presume to violate ecclesiastical liberties, it was humbly begged on behalf of the same bishop and clergy that we would deign to provide an appropriate remedy for these matters. We therefore, following in the footsteps of our predecessor and inclined to such supplications, mandate to your brotherhood by apostolic letters that you two, or one of you, by yourselves or through another or others, cause the aforesaid constitutions to be inviolably observed by our authority in the aforesaid city and diocese of Breslau and in other neighbouring places; and that you cause the aforesaid statute-makers, writers and violators to be publicly declared excommunicate and to be more strictly avoided by all others, by apostolic authority; and that you cause the aforesaid transgressors, violators, contemners and sacrilegious persons, and any opponents and rebels, to be restrained by ecclesiastical censure, appeal being disregarded, calling also, if need be, for the help of the secular arm, notwithstanding any indult granted by the apostolic see to anyone, individually or collectively, that they cannot be interdicted, suspended or excommunicated, unless by apostolic letters making full and express mention, word for word, of such indult. Given at Rome, at St Peter's, on the 13th day before the Kalends of March, in the third year of our pontificate.

units.la: SIGISMUNDI IMP. AUG. EDICTUM DE SALVO CONDVCTV IOANNIS HVSSI.
units.tr: SIGISMUND, EMPEROR AUGUSTUS: EDICT CONCERNING SAFE-CONDUCT FOR JOHN HUSS.

units.la: Sigismundus Dei gratia Romanorum Rex Semper Augustus, & Hungariæ, Dalmatiæ, Croatiæ, &c. Rex, Universis & singulis Principibus Ecclesiasticis & Secularibus, Ducibus & Marchionibus, Comitibus, Baronibus, Nobilibus, Proceribus, Militaribus, Militibus, Clientibus, Capitaneis, Potestatibus, Gubernatoribus, Præsidibus, Publicanis, Officialibus, quibuscunque Civitatum, Oppidorum, Villarum & locorum Communitatibus, ac Rectoribus eorundem, ceterisq; nostris & sacri imperii subditis & fidelibus, ad quos præsentes litere pervenerint, gratiam Regiam & omne bonum. Venerabiles, Illustres, Nobiles & fideles dilecti: Honorabilem Magistrum Joannem Huss, sacræ Theologiæ Baccalaureum, & Artium Magistrum, præsentium ostensorem, de Regno Bohemiæ ad generale in civitate Constantiensi celebrandum in proximo, transeuntem, quem etiam in & sacri Imperii protectionem recepimus & tutelam, vobis omnibus & vestrum cuilibet plemmendamus affectu, desiderantes quatenus ipsum cum ad vos pervenerit, grate suscipere, faciliter tractare, atque in his, quæ ad celeritatem & securitatem itineris ipsius pertinent, tam per quam per aquam, promotivam sibi velitis & debeatis ostendere voluntatem, necnon ipsum equis & aliis rebus suis singulis, per quoscunque passus, portus, pontes, terras, dominia, jurisdictiones, civitates, oppida, castra, villas, & quæ liber alia loca vestra, line ulla solutione tributi, telonio, auxilio quovis solutionis onere, omnique protsus impedimento remoto, transire, stare, morari & redire libere permittatis, sibiq; & suis, cum opus fuerit, de securo & salvo velitis & debeatis providere statu, ad honorem & reverentiam nostræ Majestatis. Datum Spiræ, anno Domini M CCCC XIV. Octobr. XVIII. Regnorum nostrorum, Hungariæ, &c. anno XXXIII. Romanorum vero V.
units.tr: Sigismund, by the grace of God King of the Romans, ever Augustus, and King of Hungary, Dalmatia, Croatia, etc., to all and singular ecclesiastical and secular princes, dukes and marquises, counts, barons, nobles, lords, military men, soldiers, vassals, captains, potentates, governors, presidents, tax-collectors, officials, and to the communities of whatever cities, towns, villages and places, and their rulers, and to our other subjects and faithful of the holy Empire, to whom these present letters shall come: greeting in royal favour and every good. Venerable, illustrious, noble and faithful beloved ones: we have received under the protection and guardianship of the holy Empire the honourable Master John Huss, Bachelor of Sacred Theology and Master of Arts, the bearer of these presents, who is passing from the kingdom of Bohemia to the general council to be held shortly in the city of Constance, and we commend him with affection to all of you and to each of you, desiring that when he comes to you, you receive him graciously, treat him kindly, and show him your willing favour in those matters which pertain to the speed and safety of his journey, both by land and by water; and that you allow him, with his horses and all his other belongings, to pass through, stay, linger and return freely, through whatever passes, harbours, bridges, lands, dominions, jurisdictions, cities, towns, castles, villages, and whatever other places are yours, without any payment of tribute, toll, aid or any burden of payment, all hindrance being wholly removed; and that you provide for him and his, when need arises, with a secure and safe condition, in honour and reverence of our Majesty. Given at Speyer, in the year of the Lord 1414, on the 18th of October, in the 33rd year of our kingdoms of Hungary, etc., and the 5th of our reign as King of the Romans.

units.la: Ad mandatum Domini Regis
units.tr: By command of the Lord King.

units.la: Michael de Pacest, Canonicus Wratislaviensis.
units.tr: Michael de Pacest, Canon of Breslau.

units.la: SIGISMUNDI, IMPERATO- RIS AUGUSTI SACRA DIRECTA AD CONCILIUM CONSTANTIENSE.
units.tr: SIGISMUND, AUGUSTUS EMPEROR: LETTER DIRECTED TO THE COUNCIL OF CONSTANCE.

units.la: SACROSANCTAE CONSTANTIENSI SYN- ODO in Spiritu sancto congregata.
units.tr: TO THE MOST HOLY SYNOD OF CONSTANCE, GATHERED IN THE HOLY SPIRIT.

units.la: SUMMA equidem Sapientia rationis suæ lege multiplici, creaturæ sŭæ conditæ jura suaviter disponens, quemadmodum eminens cœlum syderibus ornat, ut vicibus alternatis mundum illustrent, & eorum officiosa diversitas in numero discordet, sed subjectam terrarum latitudinem vernanti rerum universitate depingat: ita humanos actus & in pacis pulchritudine & justitiæ celebritate providit regulariter, ut alter alteri non injurietur, exemplis de superioribus derivatur ad inferiora. Verùm humani generis inimicus, pacis inpatiens, amator litium, discordiæ seminator, salus hominum invidens, inter Serenissimos Principes Francorum & Angliæ Reges, fratres nostros carissimos, contentionis materiam (quod dolenter referimus) suscitavit. Quod etiam vestræ notorium sanctitati, ut molestam admodum & novam etiam sacrosanctam matrem Ecclesiam ex hac experientia dispendiosam sentiret perniciem. Sentit utique, sentit sancta mater Ecclesia tam populi Christiani sibi commissi quàm suam gravem de hujusmodi contentione jacturam. Exeo namque quàm dire, quàm graviter materna ejus viscera quatiantur, quòd ipsa tam raros filios, tam inclitos Principes in suo sentiens utero collidentes. Prudenter advertit Christianæ militiæ potentiam in Christi blasphemos, & inimicos nominis Christi, potenter & magnificè, more solito, exercendam, in opprobrium & grande domesticorum fidei detrimentum talibus contentionibus explicari.
units.tr: INDEED Wisdom, by her manifold law of reason, sweetly ordering the rights of the creature she has made, just as the lofty heaven adorns itself with stars so that in alternating turns they give light to the world, and their dutiful diversity differs in number while it depicts the wide expanse of the lands below with the flourishing variety of all things: so she has likewise regularly provided for human actions, both in the beauty of peace and in the celebration of justice, so that one may not wrong another, and what is found in the higher things is passed down by example to the lower. But the enemy of the human race, impatient of peace, lover of strife, sower of discord, envious of the salvation of men, has stirred up, as we report with grief, a matter of contention between the most serene Kings of France and England, our dearest brothers. This is also well known to your holiness, so that holy mother Church might feel, from this experience, a very troublesome and, for her, novel and costly ruin. Holy mother Church indeed feels, and feels keenly, the grave loss both of the Christian people committed to her and of her own, from such contention. For she perceives how dreadfully and how grievously her maternal bowels are shaken, since she feels her own womb clashing with so few sons, such renowned princes. She wisely observes that the power of Christian warfare, which is to be exercised as usual, powerfully and magnificently, against the blasphemers of Christ and the enemies of the name of Christ, is being spent in such contentions, to the reproach and great detriment of the faithful at home.

units.la: 2. Hæc igitur & alia incommoda dissensionis hujusmodi ex fervore caritatis intrinsicæ, & sincero pensanies affectu, vigilamus attentius, attentioneque solita vigiliter intendimus, multaque sollicitudine pervigiles laboramus discriminibus tantis occurrere, ipsosque Reges inclitos à discordiarum dispendiis pollicetenus præservare, ac glutino solidæ caritatis & concordiæ unite. Quam etiam tractatus, qui super hoc inter ipsos habentur & deducuntur, promittere probabiliter videntur, ut & regnis ipsis & subditis quietis optatæ jocunditas proveniat, perversotum exterminetur malitia, animarum pericula vitentur, Ecclesia sancta in unitate capitis affuturi, eorundem Regum præcipuè & cetororum Katholicorum Principum munita unanimi præsidio & concordi voto, à fluctibus perfecta, ejectaque scissura, largiente altissimo, destructis adversitatibus & erroribus universis respiret, & suorum jurium gaudeat & vitium integritate resumpta. Profectò ad id jugiter nostra suspirat intentio: ad id plenis desideriis anxiamur, non proponentes à cœptis desistere, quin circa negotium hujusmodi sub spe illius, qui facit concordiam in sublimibus, qui ventis imperat & mari, & ad ejus nutum stat spiritus procellarum; pacis consilia cogitantes, in quantum ab alto permittitur prosequi, pacis semitas intendimus studiosè. Nimirum id etiam propensiùs desiderat Christianitatis, maximè hiis diebus, nuseranda conditio: quam etiam intrinsica pluisquàm civilia bella, & inhumaniter efferarum immanitates gentium, & infidelium feritates nationum, affligunt incessanter.
units.tr: 2. Therefore, from the fervour of inner love and a sincere weighing of feeling, we watch more attentively against these and the other evils of such dissension, and with our customary attention we apply ourselves keenly, and with much anxious care we labour vigilantly to meet such great dangers, and to preserve the illustrious kings themselves from the losses of discord, and to unite them with the glue of solid love and concord. The negotiations which are being held and conducted between them on this matter seem reasonably to promise this as well: that for the kingdoms themselves and their subjects the pleasant joy of the desired quiet may come, the malice of the wicked may be exterminated, the dangers to souls may be avoided, and the holy Church, abiding in the unity of her head, may, by the grace of the Most High, be brought to completion and freed from the waves, the schism cast out, all adversities and errors destroyed, and may breathe again, fortified especially by the unanimous protection and harmonious vote of those same kings and of the other Catholic princes, and may rejoice in her rights and regain her integrity. Certainly our intention sighs continually for this; we are anxious with full desire for it. Not proposing to desist from what we have begun, but trusting in Him who makes concord in the heights, who commands the winds and the sea, and at whose nod the spirit of storms stands, we turn our minds to counsels of peace and, so far as it is permitted from on high to pursue them, we earnestly seek the paths of peace. Indeed the condition of Christendom, especially in these days, desires this all the more eagerly, a condition which both internal wars, more than civil, and the inhumanly savage cruelties of fierce peoples, and the ferocity of unbelieving nations, afflict without ceasing.

units.la: 3. Quæsumus igitur, Patres sanctissimi, filiali devotione & reverentia, quatenus cùm sciant, quòd probario fidei patientiam, quæ vincit maliciam, operatur; patientia autem opus perfectum habet, nostrorum processuum causam, ordinem, ac rectam & puram prætendentes attentionem, vestro prudenti consilio & spiritu quieto discutientes: & procul dubio animus rectæ rationis dictamine dijudicans in illis inveniet, unde rectum prosequendo judicium, omni super præmissæ objectionis & turbationis remota materia, quiescet, nec via querelæ patebit. Supplicantes devotè, ut quemadmodum nuper per reverendissimum in Christo patrem Dominum N. Archiepiscopum Girezinensem, amicum nostrum carissimum, & venerabilem Symonem Episcopum Tragurien-sem, Principem & procuratorem nostrum devotum, fidelem ac dilectum, sanctitati vestræ intimavimus, de conclusione negociorum arduorum & aliorum quorumcunque usque ad nostrum adventum superseder dignemini, gratissimam in eo complacentiam, immò gratiam facientes.
units.tr: 3. We therefore ask, most holy Fathers, with filial devotion and reverence, that since they know that the testing of faith produces patience, which conquers malice, and that patience has a perfect work, they would examine, by your prudent counsel and calm spirit, the cause, the order, and the right and pure attention of our proceedings. Without doubt, a mind judging by the dictate of right reason will find in them the means by which, pursuing a right judgment and with every matter of the aforesaid objection and disturbance set aside, it will come to rest, and no path of complaint will remain open. We devoutly beg that, just as we recently made known to your holiness, through the most reverend father in Christ, the Lord N., Archbishop of Gniezno, our dearest friend, and the venerable Simon, Bishop of Trogir, our devoted, faithful and beloved Prince and procurator, you would deign to defer the conclusion of arduous affairs and of any others whatsoever until our arrival, thereby showing us a most welcome pleasure, indeed a grace.

units.la: 4. Retardatio nempe adventus Illustris Principis, Wilhelmi Ducis Bavariæ Comitisque Hanoniæ, Holandiæ, &c. consanguinei nostri carissimi, propter ventorum contrarietatem, effecit ram tantam in Anglia nobis pausandi, qui jam nudiusquartus advenientes speramus breviter unà eodem in tractatibus pacis fine dato bonam facere conclusionem, & per semitas ejusdem Ducis vellis Constantiam directo tramite continuabimus gressus festinanter; quoniam jam nostros & comitivae nostræ equos abhinc remisimus ultra mare, ut ad terram ejusdem Ducis deducantur. Datum in Wytmonter prope civitatem Londoniarum in Anglia, secunda die Junii, regnorum nostrorum, Ungariæ, &c. anno XXX. Romanorum electionis sexto, coronationis verò secundo.
units.tr: 4. The delay in the arrival of the illustrious Prince, William, Duke of Bavaria, Count of Hainaut, Holland, etc., our dearest kinsman, owing to contrary winds, has caused us to pause for so long in England. Having arrived four days ago, we hope to bring matters to a good conclusion briefly, the peace negotiations being brought to an end at the same time; and we shall hasten our steps by the roads of the same Duke, continuing by the direct route to Constance, since we have already sent our horses and those of our retinue back across the sea, to be conducted to the land of the same Duke. Given at Whitmonter, near the city of London in England, on the second day of June, in the thirtieth year of our kingdoms of Hungary, etc., the sixth year of our election as King of the Romans, and the second of our coronation.

units.la: Sacrosanctæ matris & universalis Ecclesiæ Advocatus & filius devotus, SIGISMUNDUS Dei gratia Romanorum & Ungarorum &c. Rex semper-Augustus.
units.tr: Advocate and devoted son of the most holy mother and universal Church, SIGISMUND, by the grace of God King of the Romans, of the Hungarians, etc., ever Augustus.

units.la: RESPONSIO CONCILII CON- STANTIENSIS
units.tr: Response of the Council of Constance

units.la: ACROSANCTA Constantiensis, &c. Regi Romanorum, &c. salutem & Dei omnipotentis benedictionem.
units.tr: The Sacrosanct Council of Constance, etc., to the King of the Romans, etc., greeting and the blessing of Almighty God.

units.la: Si quantam tuæ Serenitatis litteræ pridem nobis direcęe lætitiam attulerint, qualem animis nostris dulcedinem præbuerint, exprimere curaremus, non solùm non liceret, sed si fas esset, in longum nimis protenderetur oratio. At nos cum familiari sermone usuri sumus, dicendi fericem obmittimus. Indicasti quidé ipsem optimam componendæ pacis inter clarissimos Ecclesiæ filios Narolum Franciæ & Henricum Angliæ Reges illustres, illorumq; inclita regna. Quæ pax nō solum eis, sed cuncto Christiano cœtui summa quietem pollicetur, & Ecclesiæ Dei sanctissimæ peroportuna censenda est. Numquid illorum Regum clarissimorum potentiam vidimus, quam & Barbari etiam plurimumq; formidant? Numquid illorum ingentium regnorum Christiana religio suo robore consistit, & magis ac magis dilatabitur, dum ingentia bella sopientur? Si veterū repetas historias, passim futura auspicia considerare licebit, quibus ut primum eorundem Regum Illustrium dissentiones in amicitiam convertentur. Intelligere possumus, fidem Catholicam proinde maxima debere suscipere incrementa: Denique Ecclesiam sanctam & sacrum Imperium suis juribus posse consistere. Verumtamen unum singulari gaudio nostris desideriis præesse dinoscatis, Excellentissime Princeps, ut tua hæc opera pro totius orbis salute procedant. Nam non solum erit tuum nomen etiam apud posteros continuè gloriosum, sed penitus admirabile. Quis enim unquam, ut vetera recensemus, tanta sollercia ac disciplina pro singulorum quiete laboravit? Multi quidem armis, multi reliquis factionibus, quò suum imperium extendrent, insudarunt: tu verò Princeps Clementissime, id pro tuo Imperio deligis, ut alii legitimè & quietè imperare valeant prorsus invigilas. Itaq; si te suprema dignitate decoratū aspicimus, non minus Regali disciplina imbutū, & apud omnes summa devotione veneratioñeq; receptū intelligimus. Deum etiā supplices oramus, elevatisq; ad eum manibus exoramus, ut de tam salubertima pace & ab omnibus pariter concupita Celsitudo tua hominem amplissimum: nos vero suavissimæ spei, quam in capacitate tuis mediantibus studiis habemus, intentum feliciter consequamur.
units.tr: If we were to set out how great the joy was that your Serene Majesty's letter lately brought us, and what sweetness it gave our minds, we would not only be unable to do so, but, were it lawful, the speech would stretch out far too long. Since we shall speak in a familiar manner, we pass over the eloquence of rhetoric. You have indeed pointed out the excellent prospect of composing peace between the most illustrious sons of the Church, the famous kings Charles of France and Henry of England, and their renowned kingdoms. This peace promises the highest quiet not only to them but to the whole Christian body, and is to be judged most opportune for the most holy Church of God. Have we not seen the power of those most famous kings, which even barbarians greatly fear? Does not the Christian religion stand firm by the strength of those mighty kingdoms, and will it not be spread more and more while great wars are laid to rest? If you look back into old histories, you may consider on every side the favourable omens of the future, by which, as soon as the disagreements of those same illustrious kings are turned into friendship, we may understand that the Catholic faith must receive the greatest increase, and finally that the holy Church and the sacred Empire can stand secure in their rights. Yet you should know that one thing is especially pleasing to our desires, most excellent Prince: that your works may go forward for the salvation of the whole world. For your name will not only remain continually glorious even among posterity, but will be wonderfully admired. For who, to recall the old times, has ever laboured with such skill and discipline for the quiet of individuals? Many indeed have toiled with arms, many with other factions, to extend their empire; but you, most merciful Prince, have chosen this for your empire, that others may be able to rule lawfully and quietly, and you watch over it with complete care. Therefore, if we look upon you as adorned with the supreme dignity, and understand you to be imbued no less with royal discipline and received by all with the highest devotion and reverence, we also pray to God as suppliants and, with hands raised to him, beseech that your Highness may happily attain, from this most wholesome peace, so much desired by all alike, the most ample good, and that we may achieve the most sweet hope which we have in your capacity through your diligent efforts.

units.la: Ceterum, Gloriosissime Princeps, si ab hujusmodi concordiæ tractatu ab intimis tui regressum desideriis temperavimus, insidet tamen semper cordibus nostris revisendæ tuæ Serenitatis inexplicabilis affectatio, quò tandem pro universalis Ecclesiæ unitate atq; reformatione, quæ instar, perficere valeamus, utq; etiam sacrum istud Concilium solidius conservetur. Proinde quantum nostræ exhortationes apud tuam màiuetudinem valituræ sunt, obsecramus ut peractis (& o utinam feliciter, ut speramus) cum illis inclitis Regibus tractatibus, quantocius eadem Serenitas revertatur. Nec enim facile dictu est, quanta tua præsentia commoda, qualémve jocunditatem omnibus afferet, quantumq; ex ea hostibus & pacis detractoribus timoris emerget. Et ut paucis agamus, cùm venerit tua inclita Celsitudo, cuncta prosperè, cuncta quietè succedent. Præcipuè autem videtis, Katholice Princeps, ne dum te abesse contingerit, in arduis rebus aliud agamus. Nos, qua tuis maximè desideriis annuere cupientes, prout & hactenus gestum est, ita in futurum curabimus, ne quid grave & magnum decernatur ac fiat: intenti semper, quantum licebit, singula tuæ Celsitudinis vota cum omni studio manstuetudineq; tractare. Datum Constantiæ, VII. Kalend. Julii.
units.tr: Moreover, most glorious Prince, although we have restrained ourselves from the desire, deep in our hearts, to return from such a treaty of concord, there nevertheless remains always in our hearts an inexpressible longing to see your Serene Majesty again, so that at last we may be able to bring about the unity and reformation of the universal Church, which we desire, and so that this holy Council may also be preserved more firmly. Therefore, as far as our exhortations will have weight with your gentleness, we beg that, once the negotiations with those illustrious kings are concluded (and oh, that they may be concluded happily, as we hope), your Serenity may return as quickly as possible. For it is not easy to say how great the advantages of your presence are, what joy it will bring to all, and how much fear will arise in enemies and detractors of peace from it. And to be brief: when your illustrious Highness has come, everything will succeed prosperously and quietly. Above all, Catholic Prince, you see that while you are absent we must not do anything else in matters of difficulty. We, eager to comply with your greatest desires, as has also been done hitherto, will likewise take care in future that nothing grave and great be decreed or done, always intent, as far as it is permitted, on handling each of your Highness's wishes with all zeal and gentleness. Given at Constance, the seventh day before the Kalends of July.

units.la: SIGISMUNDI IMP. AUG. ET COMMUNIUM S. IMPERII ORDINUM
units.tr: SIGISMUND, EMPEROR AND AUGUSTUS, AND THE ORDERS OF THE HOLY ROMAN EMPIRE

units.la: AVISAMENTA
units.tr: ADVICES

units.la: Super materia Apostolicarum reservationum, & collatione beneficiorum hactenus per Summos Pontifices & Ordinarios Collatores practicanda: per Deputatos Provinciarum Nationis Germanicæ concepta in Concilio Constantiensi, & postea per Deputatos ejusdem Nationis audita.
units.tr: Concerning the matter of apostolic reservations and the conferral of benefices hitherto to be exercised by the supreme Pontiffs and the ordinary collators: drafted by the deputies of the provinces of the German nation at the Council of Constance, and afterwards heard by the deputies of the same nation.

units.la: CAPITULUM I.
units.tr: CHAPTER I.

units.la: IN primis ad tollenda illa scandala, quæ hactenus ex diminutione divini cultus Simoniacæ extorsionis pecuniarum, ambitione & cupiditate proventuum Ecclesiasticorum beneficialium, & possessionum eorum desolatione acciderunt in Ecclesia Dei, &c. Pro illorum scandalorum materia recensanda videtur, quòd per hoc sacrum generale Concilium tolli, auferri, & revocari debeant reservationes omnium & singulorum beneficiorum Ecclesiasticorum, tam majorum quàm minorum, quæ laltem in corpore juris non clauduntur: ut sunt videlicet illæ, quæ introductæ sunt in existentia ad regimen, aut per quascumque regulas Cancellariæ, &c. quòd hujusmodi reservationes futuris temporibus nullatenus per quemcumque Summum Pontificem fiant sine declaratione, authoritate, consensu, & approbatione Concilii generalis.
units.tr: FIRST, in order to remove those scandals which hitherto have arisen in the Church of God from the diminishing of divine worship, from simoniacal extortion of money, from the ambition and greed for ecclesiastical benefice revenues, and from the desolation of their possessions, etc. For the listing of the matter of those scandals it seems that this holy general Council should decree that the reservations of all and each of the ecclesiastical benefices, both greater and lesser, which at least are not contained in the body of law, be removed, abolished and revoked: namely those which have been introduced in the curia for governance, or by any rules of the Chancery, etc. That such reservations shall in future times in no way be made by any supreme Pontiff without the declaration, authority, consent and approval of a general Council.

units.la: CAPIT. II.
units.tr: CHAPTER II.

units.la: Item tollatur hæc nimis exorbitans abusio, quam sibi Domini Cardinales velut pro lege servare nantur, videlicet quod bona Ecclesiastica quæcumq; per Cardinales obtenta, si illa vacare contingat, quod aliis quàm Cardinalibus conferre non debeant. Quod atiq; magnum incoveniens esset in Ecclesia sancta Dei: quia introduceret præcisè acceptationem personarum, quâ supremus Monarcha in Ecclesia triumphante non admittit. Item, quia id officium dominorum Cardinalium est, Summo Pontifici, cui universalis solicitudo Ecclesiæ Dei commissa est, secundum suas partes assistere, & in aged vel consilium dare. cujus occasione verisimiliter contingeret, ipsos non nisi in curia Romana decedere, & eorum decessu sua beneficia non nisi ibidem vacare. Idcirco ne beneficia dictorum Dominorum Cardinalium, per ipsos jam obtenta, in cutia perpetuarentur, in magnum detrimentum illorum beneficiorum & suarum possessionum, & (quod pejus est) divini cultus, & Christi fidelium animarum, illa ad sua remedia & Dei laudem frequentandam instituentium: statuat hoc generale Concilium, quòd Domini Cardinales, habentes Ecclesiastica beneficia, de facto illa obtineant, si salte velint, quamdiu vivant: ipsis decedentibus vacare censeantur ipsis Ordinariis Collatoribus, non obstante c. licet statutum, & cap. præsenti, De præbendis, lib. 6. sicut si ipsi ex Romana curia decessissent.
units.tr: Likewise let this exorbitant abuse be removed, which the lord Cardinals hold as if it were a law, namely that any ecclesiastical goods obtained by Cardinals, should they happen to fall vacant, ought not to be conferred on anyone other than Cardinals. This would be a great inconvenience in the holy Church of God, since it would introduce precisely the acceptance of persons, which the supreme Monarch does not admit in the Church triumphant. Also, because it is the office of the lord Cardinals to assist the supreme Pontiff, to whom the universal care of the Church of God is committed, in his duties and to give counsel in his affairs; from which it would probably happen that they died only in the Roman curia, and at their death their benefices became vacant only there. Therefore, lest the benefices of the said lord Cardinals, already obtained by them, be perpetuated in the curia, to the great detriment of those benefices and their possessions, and (what is worse) of divine worship and the souls of Christ's faithful, who established those benefices for their own remedy and for the frequent praise of God: let this general Council decree that the lord Cardinals who hold ecclesiastical benefices may de facto retain them, if at least they wish, as long as they live; and at their death let them be considered vacant to the ordinary collators themselves, notwithstanding the chapter licet as stated, and the chapter praesenti, De praebendis, book 6, just as if they had died in the Roman curia.

units.la: 2. Et præfatorum Dominorum Cardinalium numero reducto, secundum quod in aliis vatoriis articulis est avisatum, nulli Cardinalium tunc inantea aliquod beneficium Ecclesiastum majus aut minus, detur vel assignetur, cui in propria persona præesse, aut ipsum regere non valeat, ipsis sicut pro communitate totius laborent Ecclesiæ, ita ipsis secundum decentiam statuş eorum omnibus fructibus cameræ Apostolicæ, aut de regnis aut provinciis Christianitatis distinctis provinciae, sic quod quilibet annuatim pro decetia sui status servandi, cum debita moderatione & superfluorum amputatione, habeat III. vel IV. milia florenorum: secundum quod huic sacro Concilio profitem lubri remedio contra fastus, pompæ, ambitionis, cupiditatis, & voluptatis morbos, qui à talibus Apostolorum Christi successoribus debent esse longè remoti) visum fuerit expedire.
units.tr: 2. And with the number of the said lord Cardinals reduced, as has been advised in other articles, let no benefice, greater or lesser, ecclesiastical, be given or assigned thereafter to any Cardinal, over which he is not able to preside or govern in person; so that they labour for the common good of the whole Church, and so that, according to the decency of their status, they receive from all the fruits of the Apostolic Chamber, or from the kingdoms or provinces of distinct Christendom, such that each annually, for maintaining the decency of his status with due moderation and the cutting off of superfluities, has three or four thousand florins; as this holy Council shall judge expedient, as a salutary remedy against the diseases of pride, pomp, ambition, greed and pleasure, which ought to be far removed from such successors of the Apostles of Christ.

units.la: CAPIT. III.
units.tr: CHAPTER III.

units.la: Item statuatur & ordinetur, quòd in omnibus beneficiis electivis, sive sint Patriarchatus, Archiepiscopatus, Abbatiæ, Præposituræ, Primiceriatus, Prioratus, Archidiaconatus, Archipresbyteratus, Decanatus, aut alia electiva beneficia inferiora, serventur jura de electione & apostolatione in corpore juris contenta, cum omnibus eorum capitulis, prout polita & ab antiquo per sanctos Patres practicata sunt. quæ etiam beneficia electiva sub quacumq; expectativa gratia cadere non debeant: licet tamen, quod illæ electiones, quoties occurrerint faciendæ, postquam factæ sunt, per immediatos superiores secundum formam juris examinentur, & canonicè factæ confirmentur: & quòd nullo modo liceat Summo Pontifici quicquam in contrarium attentare, præterquàm in electis sibi immediatè subjectis, de quibus habebit prohibere; vel nisi contingat in præmissis quicquam contra formam juris factam aut esse quomodolibet attentatum, quo sicut ad id tenetur, ita sibi liceat taliter acta vel attentata retractando sive in melius ordinando reformare, cum potestate corrigendi vel puniendi transgressores.
units.tr: Likewise let it be enacted and ordained that in all elective benefices, whether they be patriarchates, archbishoprics, abbacies, provostships, primacies, priorates, archdeaconries, archpresbyterates, deaneries, or other lesser elective benefices, the rights of election and confirmation contained in the body of law be observed, with all their chapters, as they have been polished and practised from of old by the holy Fathers. Likewise these elective benefices ought not to fall under any expectative grace; yet it is permitted that those elections, whenever they must be made, after they have been made, be examined by the immediate superiors according to the form of law, and confirmed canonically; and that in no way is it lawful for the supreme Pontiff to attempt anything to the contrary, except in the elected persons immediately subject to him, concerning whom he will have the power to prohibit; or unless it happens that something has been done or attempted in any way against the form of law in the aforesaid matters, in which case, as he is bound to it, so it be lawful for him, by retracting such acts or attempts, or by ordering them for the better, to reform them, with power to correct or punish the transgressors.

units.la: CAPIT. IV.
units.tr: CHAPTER IV.

units.la: Item quia seclusis beneficiis electivis, de quibus in proximo capite mentio facta est, reliqua beneficia Ecclesiastica, quæ saltem non sunt de jure patronatus Laicorum, sunt adhuc in duplici differentia. Nam quædam sunt minora, ut quæ taxam decem marcarum argenti puri non excedunt, alia quæ communi æstimatione hujusmodi taxam excedunt.
units.tr: Likewise, since, setting aside the elective benefices of which mention was made in the immediately preceding chapter, the remaining ecclesiastical benefices, which at least are not of lay patronage, are still of a twofold difference. For some are lesser, such as those which do not exceed the tax of ten marks of pure silver; others, which by common estimation exceed such a tax.

units.la: CAPIT. V.
units.tr: CHAPTER V.

units.la: Item quædam minora beneficia sunt, quæ continuam personalem residentiam, & continuum divini officii requirunt: sic, ut quasi manualia celebrantur. Idcircò ut secundum valorem beneficiorum fiat moderatio talis, ut magis idoneis & bene meritis majora, & minùs bene meritis minora beneficia, secundum æqualem justitiæ distributivæ regulam, quod melius fieri poterit, conferantur, statuat & ordinet hoc sacrum Concilium, quod sub gratiis Apostolicis in forma speciali concessis nullo tenus omnia cadere debeant beneficia memoria, quæ videlicet taxam decem marcarum argenti non excedunt, vel continuum requirunt exercitium divini officii; ut sunt Vicariæ, Capellaniæ, Altaria, & Præmissariæ, tam Cathedralium quàm Collegiatarum Parochialium; Ecclesiarum, Monasteriorum, & Conventuum ac Hospitalium: & ex adverso sub gratiis in forma pauperum concessis non dant beneficia majora, quæ taxam videlicet decem marcarum argenti puri excedent. Et si quæ gratiarum secus factæ reperiantur, careat impetrans commodo literarum Apostolicarum per conficiendarum: & acceptiones & provisiones, super talibus confectis literis factæ, tanquam factæ, & ipso jure nullæ.
units.tr: Likewise, there are certain lesser benefices which require continuous personal residence and the continuous performance of divine office, so that they are celebrated almost as daily services. Therefore, so that the benefices may be moderated according to their value, and so that greater benefices are conferred on the more suitable and well-deserving, and lesser ones on the less deserving, according to the equal rule of distributive justice, as can best be done, this holy Council decrees and ordains that benefices under apostolic graces granted in special form must by no means fall to those graces, namely those mentioned above which do not exceed a tax of ten marks of pure silver or which require the continuous exercise of divine office: such as vicarages, chaplaincies, altars and prebends, of cathedral as well as collegiate churches; parish churches, monasteries, convents and hospitals. And conversely, under graces granted in the form for the poor, they shall not grant greater benefices, that is, those exceeding a tax of ten marks of pure silver. And if any graces made otherwise are found, let the applicant lose the benefit of the apostolic letters to be drawn up; and the acceptances and provisions made on the basis of such letters are, as if they had never been made, null by law.

units.la: CAPIT. VI.
units.tr: CHAPTER VI.

units.la: Item disponat & ordinet hoc sacrum Concilium, quòd Summus Pontifex futuris temporibus quemcunque Ordinatium Collatorem gravare non habeat, neque debeat, nisi per unicam Apostolicam expectativam in forma speciali ad beneficia majora, quæ taxam decem marcarum argenti ut præmittitur, excedent: & similiter non nisi per unicam Apostolicam expectativam in forma pauperum ad beneficia minora, ut præmittitur.
