Et ad cavendum multitudinem per variam importunitatem. tem quandoque imperantium, ut singulis gratiis expectativis, secundum dispositionem juris communis antiqui, ponatur haec clausula: Si pro alio sub tali forma vel gratiae speciali, vel in forma pauperum, sit ipso jure nulla. Sicsimiliter de vacante parte & consequenti, necnon omnia inde secuta nullius sunt roboris vel momenti. Caveatur autem in omnibus, quòd executores Apostolici, secundum tenorem litterarum Apostolicarum, non admittent ullos ad obtinenda Ecclesiastica beneficia habiles & idoneos, nisi qui distincte examinentur de facto reperiuntur.
units.tr: Likewise, this holy Council decrees and ordains that in future the Supreme Pontiff shall not have, nor ought, to burden any ordinary collator, except by a single apostolic expectative in special form for greater benefices, which, as stated above, exceed ten marks of silver; and likewise only by a single apostolic expectative in the form for the poor for lesser benefices, as stated above. And to guard against a multitude of expectatives arising from the varied importunity of those who sometimes command, so that to each expectative grace, according to the disposition of the ancient common law, this clause is to be added: If for another under such form or special grace, or in the form for the poor, it is by law null. Likewise concerning the vacant portion and the consequent, and all things that follow from them are of no force or validity. But let it be provided in all cases that apostolic executors, according to the tenor of the apostolic letters, shall not admit to obtaining ecclesiastical benefices anyone who is not distinctly examined and actually found able and fit.

units.la: CAPIT. VII.
units.tr: CHAPTER VII.

units.la: CAPIT. VIII.
units.tr: CHAPTER VIII.

units.la: Quod in hoc sacro Constantiensi Concilio non solùm Episcopi & Principales infulati Abbates habere debeant voces judicativas & diffinitivas, sed Episcoporum & Abbatum, necnon Capitulorum, & universitatum studiorum Procuratores, Monasteriorum & Conventuum Praeceptores, Generales, Ministri Provinciales, & Priores, Magistri, Doctores, & devotorum Christi fidelium Ordinum, ex subsequentibus videtur apparere, &c.
units.tr: That in this holy Council of Constance not only bishops and principal abbots wearing the mitre ought to have judicial and deciding voices, but also the procurators of bishops and abbots, as well as of chapters and universities of study, the preceptors of monasteries and convents, the generals, provincial ministers and priors, the masters and doctors of the orders of devout Christian faithful, appears from what follows, etc.

units.la: SIGISMUNDI IMP. AUG. LAUDUM
units.tr: The Award of Emperor Sigismund Augustus

units.la: Sigismundus Dei gratia Romanorum Rex Semper-Augustus; Hungariae, Dalmatiae & Croatiae Rex, &c. omnibus & singulis notum facimus, & praesentibus literis testificamur.
units.tr: Sigismund, by the grace of God Roman King, ever Augustus, King of Hungary, Dalmatia and Croatia, etc., make known to all and each, and bear witness by these present letters.

units.la: Quamvis Regia dignitas, in quam nos divina omnipotentia & mera gratia collocavit, Regium animum continuò sollicitat atq; urget, ut scilicet omnes nostras curas & cogitationes, tumultus incommoda, turbas & bella ab omnibus nostris & Imperii subditis & fidelibus avertere, pacem ac quietem procurandam conferamus: tanto tamen cor nostrum magis accenditur, sollicitum est, eas dissensiones ac bella, quae inter praecipua nostra & Imperii membra, et nonnullos alios, potentes Principes, exoriuntur, componere atque extinguere, quanto in-& Imperio, atque adeò publicae salutis majora incommoda & detrimenta existere possint.
units.tr: Although the royal dignity, into which divine omnipotence and pure grace have placed us, constantly stirs and urges our royal mind, so that we should bring about peace and quiet by turning all our cares and thoughts, the troubles, disturbances, tumults, and wars away from all our subjects and faithful of the Empire, our heart is nonetheless all the more kindled and anxious to settle and extinguish those dissensions and wars which arise between our chief members of the Empire and some other powerful princes, the greater the inconveniences and losses that may arise for the Empire and so for the public welfare.

units.la: Quum ergò bello illo, quod inter Archiepiscopum Coloniensem, facti Romani Imperii per Archicancellarium, dilectum nostrum cognatum & Principem Electorem, ejusq; Episcopatus, civitatem ac Cives Coloniensis, nostros & Imperii dilectos fideles, ab una; & Illustrissimum Principem Adolphum Ducem Montensem, Comitem Ravensbergi, &c. dilectum nostrum cognatum & Princi-
units.tr: Since, therefore, in that war which has arisen on the one side between the Archbishop of Cologne, made Elector of the Roman Empire by the Archchancellor, our beloved kinsman and Prince Elector, together with his bishopric, city and citizens of Cologne, our and the Empire's beloved faithful, and on the other side the most illustrious Prince Adolf, Duke of Berg, Count of Ravensberg, etc., our beloved kinsman and Prince

units.la: Calparo Ens. Principem, ab altera parte, ex ortu & geltum eit, publica utilitas longo tempore impedita, regnorum statu, & plurimi utriusq; partis subditi tam corpore quàm fortunis plurimum læsi, atq; ad inopiam redacti sint: Regius noster animus, luisce malis mederi cupiens, ita commotus est, ut Caesar atq; Aquisgranum coràm, ad dissidium & bellù hoc componendù, nos contulerimus. Postquam ab utraq; parte hujus caussæ cognitio nobis permissa fuit, quemadmodùm ea quoq; jure ad nos pertinet; multa quidè, de quibus contendebatur, capita, cōmunicato cum aliquot nostris & Imperii Principibus, Consiliariis, Comitibus, Nobilibus & alijs fidelibus, cōsilio declaravimus, atq; inter utramq; partem per sententiam nostram concilavimus, ut videre est ex litteris nostris Regijs, quas supra dictus fieri, & utriq; parti dari jussimus.
units.tr: Calparo Ens. Prince, on the other part, the public good has long been hindered, the state of the realms and very many subjects of both parties have been greatly harmed in body and fortune and reduced to want. Our royal mind, wishing to remedy these evils, was so moved that we ourselves went to Aachen, in person, to settle this discord and war. After the cause was submitted to us by both parties, as it also belongs to us by right, we declared our opinion on many of the points in dispute, having taken counsel with some of our Princes of the Empire, counts, nobles, councillors, and other faithful men, and we reconciled the parties by our sentence, as may be seen from our royal letters, which we ordered to be drawn up and given to each party.

units.la: 3. Quia tamen duo illa puncta, nimirùm de novo teloneo sive vectigali impolito, necnon à præfato Duce Adolpho belli tempore excitatis operibus ac munimentis, tam plenarie ac declarari non potuerunt: dubiorum istorum capitum cognitione ac decisionem, de utriusq; partis sensu ac voluntate, Nobis Imperii Conventum in urbe Constantiensi habentibus, reseravimus etiam in prædictis Regiæ nostræ Majestatis litteris, capitis istorum mentio fit, his verbis: Aduprædictus Adolphus negatur ullis jus habere, nova vectigalia tam terrà quàm aquà, tam Urbe quàm Episcopatu & subditis imponendi, vi earum litterarum, quas dictus Adolphus, ejusq; prædecessores ex decreto confignarunt, quòd renovare tentatur; respondit prædictus Dux Monteufis, patrem suum jus hoc vectigalium à Romanis Imperatoribus, Regibus, nostro a Patre & b Fratre, necnon alio quodam Romanorum Rege, c cognato nostro & fratre, atq; infeperat Romanorum Rege, qui interea fuerit, atq; adeò à sacro Romano Imperio cum feudi investitura accepisse, idq; litteras repoffe, quibus nemo excipiatur aut immunis pronunciatur; quæ porrò ad ipsum à patre perveneriunt; nec cuiquam ipsius vectigalia impedire aut deteriora facere in eo jure, quo feuda Imperialia minuere fas non est. Super hoc partes utraq; compromisit & consensit, ut ejus decisio secundùm jus penes nos manear, atq; diernum diem & testu Purificationis B. Virginis, ab utraq; parte Legati ad nos Constantiam, ubi rum erimus, mittantur, qui ex veris documentis & litteris totius rei veritatem clarè nos edoutq; nos intra hodiernum diem & festum S. Georgii sententiam definitivam pronunciemus.
units.tr: 3. Because, however, those two points, namely the new toll imposed without permission, and the works and fortifications raised by the aforesaid Duke Adolf during the war, could not be fully declared, we reserved the examination and decision of these doubtful points, with the sense and will of both parties, for us holding the assembly of the Empire in the city of Constance. Mention of these points is made in the aforesaid royal letters of our Majesty, in these words: The aforesaid Adolf is denied any right to impose new tolls, both by land and by water, both in city and in bishopric and on subjects, by virtue of those letters which Adolf and his predecessors deposited by decree, which he is trying to renew. The aforesaid Duke of Berg replied that his father had received this right of tolls from the Roman emperors and kings, our father and brother, and from another Roman king, our kinsman and brother, and from whoever was then Roman king, and so had received it from the Holy Roman Empire with the investiture of a fief, and that he had letters to this effect, in which no one is excepted or declared exempt, and which had come to him from his father; nor may he be hindered or have his tolls made worse in that right, by which imperial fiefs may not lawfully be diminished. On this matter both parties compromised and agreed that the decision should rest with us according to law, and that on the day after the feast of the Purification of the Blessed Virgin, envoys from each party should be sent to us at Constance, where we shall be, who shall make the whole truth of the matter clear to us from true documents and letters, and that we shall pronounce a definitive sentence before the day after the feast of St. George.

units.la: 4. Ad alterum verò controversiæ caput, quo prædicto Duci mandatur, ut nova opera & tiones tam Mulhemianas quàm Monhemianas, bello hoc durante excitatas, funditùs demolitio dem Dux respondit, Mulhemü & Monhemum ex antiqua & paterna hereditate ad se pervenerunt, utrumq; locum à parentibus & majoribus suis inclusum, munitum & immunitate donatum, dominio situm esse: ac proinde sperare atq; existimare, quod ibi exstructum atq; ædificatum à se exstructum atq; ædificatum esse, neq; ad cujusquam pertinere damnum aut injuriam eoq; ad ejus demolitionem minimè teneri, sed potiùs æquum esse, ut patrimonii sui jus integrum sibi relinquatur. nihilominus idem Dux consensit, ut dictæ illæ substructiones & munitiones, nostras in ... gnentur, ea conditione, ut parsutraq; amicos sive Legatos suos proximis Calendis Februarii autorciter ad nos mittat, cum plenis & omnibus eò pertinentibus documentis & testimoniis; utq; nos festù S. Georgii litem hanc sive controversiam sententiâ nostrâ ex jure terminemus. Quòd in neutra partium ad deignatum illum diem Legatos suos miserit, ut nobis intra præscriptum terminum tiam ex jure ferre liceat: at si intra constitutum illud tempus id non fiat, Nos quidem in fæpedicis potestatem munitiones illas & substructiones restituamus ac resignemus.
units.tr: 4. As to the second point of the controversy, in which the aforesaid Duke is ordered to demolish utterly the new works and fortifications, both at Mulheim and at Monheim, raised during this war, the Duke replied that Mulheim and Monheim came to him from his ancient and paternal inheritance, each place having been enclosed, fortified and granted immunity by his parents and ancestors, and situated in his dominion. He therefore hopes and thinks that what has been built and erected there by him, has been built without damage or injury to anyone, and that he is therefore not bound to demolish it; rather it is fair that the right of his patrimony be left whole to him. Nevertheless the same Duke consented that those said substructions and fortifications should be ..., on condition that each party send their friends or envoys to us by the coming first of February, with full and all the documents and testimonies pertaining to the matter, and that we should settle this suit or controversy by our sentence, according to law, before the feast of St. George. If neither party sends its envoys to us on the appointed day, it shall be lawful for us to pronounce a sentence according to law within the prescribed term; but if this is not done within the set time, we shall restore and hand back those fortifications and substructions to the aforesaid party.

units.la: 5. Postea quam ergò intra præfixum illum terminū partis utriusq; Legati sive Deputati ad Constantiam venerunt, sententiam nostram super duabus illis controversiis sive capitibus ac nos, assumtis in consilium:
units.tr: 5. After, therefore, the envoys or deputies of both parties came to Constance within the fixed term, we, having taken counsel, gave our sentence on these two controversies or points:

units.la: Reverendissimo Archiepiscopo Strigoniensi, sanctæ Romanæ Apostolicæ Sedis Legato, cellario nostro,
units.tr: The Most Reverend Archbishop of Gran, Legate of the holy Roman Apostolic See, our Chancellor,

units.la: itemq; Joanne Archiepiscopo Rigensi, Andrea Colotiensi, Georgio Pallaviensi, Georgio Tridentino, & Simone Traguriensi, Rudolpho Duce Saxoniæ & Luneburgi, Sacri Roma-
units.tr: likewise John, Archbishop of Riga, Andrew of Kolocsa, George of Pallavia, George of Trent, and Simon of Trogir, Rudolf, Duke of Saxony and Lüneburg, of the Holy Roman

units.la: Nec non Illustrissimis Principibus Friderico Marchione Brandenburgico, Burggravio Norimbergensi, Sacri Rom. Imp. Archicamerario ut & Ernesto, Gulielmo, Henrico & Othone, Comitibus Palatinis ad Rhenum, Ducibus Alberto Duce Saxoniæ & Luneburgi; Friderico Marchione Misniæ & Landgravio Thuringiæ; & Bernardo Marchione Badensi. Rudolpho Marchione in Hachenberg, Domino in Roetelen & Sulenberg, Ludovico Comite Oringensi, Gunthero Comite Schwartzenburgio, Domino in Reims, nostræ Aulæ Præfecto Juridico,
units.tr: and also the most illustrious Princes Frederick, Margrave of Brandenburg, Burgrave of Nuremberg, Archchamberlain of the Holy Roman Empire, and Ernest, William, Henry and Otto, Counts Palatine on the Rhine, Dukes Albert, Duke of Saxony and Lüneburg; Frederick, Margrave of Meissen and Landgrave of Thuringia; and Bernard, Margrave of Baden, Rudolf, Margrave in Hachberg, Lord in Rötteln and Sulzberg, Louis, Count of Öttingen, Günther, Count of Schwarzburg, Lord in Reuss, our court judicial officer,

units.la: Præterea Nobili Eberhardo Comite Nellenburgensi, Conrado Comite Freiburgensi, Domino in Welschennevenburg, Joanne Comite Lupfensi, Landgravio in Stulingen, &c. Acrandem Alberto ab Honlach.
units.tr: Besides the noble Eberhard, Count of Nellenburg, Conrad, Count of Freiburg, Lord in Welschneufchatel, John, Count of Lupfen, Landgrave in Stühlingen, etc., and finally Albert von Hohenlohe.

units.la: multisq; aliis Nobilibus & Jurisconsultis sive Doctoribus, utramq; partem & ab eis producta instrumenta, testimonia, contradictiones, responsiones, & quidquid ad causam hanc spectat, plenè audivimus, & varia Cæsarea ac Regia diplomata, res judicatas, aliasq; litteras ad vectigalium jus pertinentes, & ab antiquis temporibus hucusq; concessas, diligenter inspeximus ac trutinavimus: animo præmeditato, & maturo præfatorum tam Ecclesiasticæ quàm Sæcularis dignitatis Principū, Comitum, Nobilium & Doctorum, nostrorum fidelium, consilio, Deum & justitiam unicè præ oculis habentes, ex jure hanc sententiam pronunciavimus.
units.tr: and many other nobles and jurists or doctors, we fully heard both parties, and the instruments, testimonies, objections, replies produced by them, and whatever pertains to this cause. We diligently examined and weighed the various imperial and royal diplomas, decided cases, and other letters concerning the right of tolls, granted from ancient times down to now. With a deliberate mind and the mature counsel of the aforesaid Princes of both ecclesiastical and secular dignity, counts, nobles and doctors, our faithful, keeping God and justice alone before our eyes, we pronounced this sentence according to law.

units.la: 6. Primùm, ut quantū ad vectigalia, prædictus Dux Adolphus eas literas, quas tam ipse, quàm ipsius pater & mater Reverendo in Christo patri Coloniensi Archiepiscopo ejusq; Ecclesiæ & subditis, ut & Civibus Coloniensibus concesserunt, ut & jura super ea re pronunciata & facta, & à sæpe nominato Duce Adolpho per juramentum confirmata, prout ea sonant, & tam ex illis quàm ex aliis literis & diplomatis doceri possunt, integra servet, uti frui permittat.
units.tr: 6. First, as regards the tolls, the aforesaid Duke Adolf shall keep whole and allow the enjoyment of those letters which he himself, and his father and mother, granted to the Reverend Father in Christ, the Archbishop of Cologne, his church and subjects, and also to the citizens of Cologne, as well as the rights pronounced and made in that matter, and confirmed by oath by the often-named Duke Adolf, as they sound, and which can be shown from those and other letters and diplomas.

units.la: 7. De secundo articulo, nimirum de novis illis operibus & munitionibus, similiter matura habita cum prædictis nostris Principibus, Comitibus, Nobilibus & fidelibus, deliberatione, eodem etiam Adolpho non ignorate nec invito, ex illa, qua ex compromisso in eundem Adolphum uti nobis licet, potestate, decrevimus ac decidimus, hocq; ipso jubemus, ut omnia ista nova opera & munitiones, tam ab Adolpho Duce Mulhemi & Monhemi ex illa, quàm ipso Archiepiscopo ex altera parte ad Wisselingam, Tuitiū, & Rilam constructa ædificia ac propugnacula, funditus sine ulla mora aut recusatione dejiciantur. Quem in finē certos homines ablegare volumus, qui videant, nobisq; fide faciant, demolitione hanc nulla mora interposita, nulloq; excepto, opere ipso plenè completam ac perfectam esse.
units.tr: 7. Concerning the second article, namely the new works and fortifications: after mature deliberation likewise held with our aforesaid princes, counts, nobles and loyal subjects, and with Adolf himself not unaware of it nor unwilling, by that power which we may use under the compromise placed upon the same Adolf, we have decided and determined, and by this very act we order, that all these new works and fortifications, both those built by Adolf, Duke of Mülheim and Monheim, on the one side, and those built by the Archbishop himself on the other side at Wissel, Tüdden and Rijl, be torn down to the foundations without any delay or refusal. To this end we wish to send certain men who shall see to it and assure us that the demolition has been fully and completely carried out, without any delay and without exception.

units.la: 8. Ut verò hæc sententia nostra tanto firmior habeatur, semperq; maneat, ex plenitudine Regiæ potestatis, utriq; parti, & earum singulis, hoc ipso secundò mandamus, ut sententiæ huic nostræ & rei judicatæ utrimq; stent & satisfaciant, mandatumque hoc nostrum inviolabiliter servent atque exsequantur, nisi nostram & Imperii indignationem incurrere velint. In cujus rei fidem diploma hoc Regiæ nostræ Majestatis sigillo muniri curavimus. Actum Constantiæ, anno millesimo quadringentesimo decimo septimo, die Jovis ante festum S. Georgii; nostri Regni Hungarici, &c. tricesimo primo, Romani verò septimo.
units.tr: 8. So that this our judgment may be held all the firmer and always remain in force, we order both parties, and each of them, by the fullness of royal power, a second time by this very act, that they abide by and comply with this our sentence and the adjudicated matter on both sides, and that they observe and carry out this our command inviolably, unless they wish to incur our displeasure and that of the Empire. In witness of which we have caused this document to be confirmed with the seal of our Royal Majesty. Given at Constance, in the year one thousand four hundred and seventeen, on the Thursday before the feast of St. George; in the thirty-first year of our Kingdom of Hungary, etc., and the seventh of the Roman [kingdom].

units.la: MANDATVM INHIBITORIVM AC DEMOLITORIVM.
units.tr: MANDATE OF INHIBITION AND DEMOLITION.

units.la: NOs Sigismundus Dei gratia Romanorum Rex Semper-Augustus; necnon Hungariæ, Dalmatiæ & Croatiæ Rex, &c. Honorabilibus, Cōsulibus, Senatoribus & universis Civibus Civitatis Coloniensis, nostris & Imperii dilectis fidelibus, significamus, quum non ita pridem latā sententiā decretum à nobis & pronunciatum sit, nova illa opera & propugnacula Mulhemi & Monhemi excitata, sine ulla mora aut impedimento penitus funditus; dejici atq; tolli oportere; eum in finem Strenuum virum, Georgium à Zedelniz, ministrum nostrū & fidelem dilectum, harū litterarum latorem, nobis ablegatū, eiq; in mandatis esse datum, ut actui istiusinterfit, ac omnia ista nova opera ac substructiones, sive muri, aggeres, sepimenta, ac quodcumq; tale fuerint, nullo penitus excepto, superiori belle de novo excitata, diruī, ac funditus complanari curet. Quòd si forte ab iis, qui prædicta propugnacula ac substructiones hactenus nostro nomine tenuerunt ac custodierunt, sumptus aliqui facti, & dictis propugnaculis atq; structuris impositi fuerint: nos verò id in primis satagamus, ut nostræ & Imperii oriones, viæ atq; itinera illis in partibus, quæ ab ejusmodi propugnaculis imminent, periculis & damnis liberentur: eaq; propugnacula vobis admodum vicina sint: petimus à vobis serò, ut deven olihanc re & consilio juveris ac promoveatis, atq; etiam sumtus, si qui facti sunt, persolvaris, quæ admodum vos facturos Nobis certò spondemus. In quo nobis quidem rem gratam facieti, ac vicissim Civitati Regiam nostram gratiam & favorem pollicemur. Datum Constantiæ, xv. die Maij, Regnorum, Hungarici quidem, &c. tricesimo primo, Romani verò anno septimo.
units.tr: We, Sigismund, by the grace of God Roman King, ever Augustus, and also King of Hungary, Dalmatia and Croatia, etc., signify to the honorable consuls, senators and all the citizens of the city of Cologne, our dear and faithful subjects of the Empire, that, since a sentence was not long ago pronounced and declared by us that those new works and bulwarks raised at Mulheim and Monheim must be thrown down and removed utterly and without any delay or hindrance, for this purpose we have sent to you the bearer of these letters, the energetic man Georg von Zedelnitz, our minister and dear faithful servant, and he has been given in his instructions that he is to take part in the business and see to it that all those new works and foundations, whether walls, embankments, fences, or whatever else of that kind there may be, raised anew since the previous war, be torn down and levelled to the ground, leaving nothing out at all. But if any expenses have perhaps been incurred by those who have hitherto held and guarded the aforesaid bulwarks and foundations in our name, and sums have been laid out on the said bulwarks and structures, we, for our part, take especial care that the roads, ways and routes of ours and of the Empire in those regions, which hang over such bulwarks, be freed from dangers and losses. Since those bulwarks are very near to you, we ask you, in turn, to assist and promote this matter by your help and counsel, and also to pay the expenses, if any have been incurred, which we firmly promise you will do. In doing this you will certainly do us a pleasure, and in return we promise the city our royal grace and favour. Given at Constance, on the 15th day of May, in the thirty-first year of our Hungarian reign, etc., and in the seventh year of our Roman reign.

units.la: SIGISMUNDI IMP. AUG. CONSTITUTIO
units.tr: THE CONSTITUTION OF THE EMPEROR SIGISMUND AUGUSTUS

units.la: De Officio Vicarii generalis: & de jure primogenitura.
units.tr: Concerning the office of the Vicar General, and concerning the right of primogeniture.

units.la: SIGISMUNDUS Dei gratia Romanorum Rex Semper Augustus, ac Hungariæ, Dalmatiæ, Croatiæ, &c. Rex, Nobili Brunorio de la Scala filio quondam Nobilis Gulielmi de la Scala, nostro & Imperii Sacri Veronæ & Vincentiæ Vicario generali & fideli dilecto, gratiam Regum & omne bonum.
units.tr: SIGISMUND, by the grace of God Roman King, ever Augustus, and King of Hungary, Dalmatia, Croatia, etc., to the noble Brunoro della Scala, son of the late noble Guglielmo della Scala, our faithful and beloved Vicar General of the Holy Empire at Verona and Vicenza: grace of kings and every good.

units.la: 1. Nobilis fidelis dilecte, licet æterni providentia Principis in terra sine certa causa propriaq; ratione disponat, sintq; adeò incomprehensibilia judicia & investigabiles viæ ejus, ut imperfecta humanæ naturæ conditio non solum in causis operum perscrutandis deficiat, sed in ipsis causarum operationibus vix sufficiat admirari; scimus autem quod universæ viæ ejus misericordia & veritas sunt, & quod homines Cooperatores ejusdem ab Apostolo denuncupantur. Nos etiam, quos cælestis altitudo Consilii ad hoc prætulit in Regalis apicem dignitatis, ut oportuna singulis auxilia pro tempore dispemus,illos,quibus prælle non minus quam prodesse proponimus, nostros Cooperatores cupivenire.
units.tr: 1. Noble, faithful and beloved, although the providence of the eternal Prince disposes things on earth without a fixed cause and reason of its own, and his judgments are so incomprehensible and his ways so unsearchable that the imperfect condition of human nature not only fails to examine the causes of his works but can scarcely wonder at the very workings of those causes; yet we know that all his ways are mercy and truth, and that men are called his co-workers by the Apostle. We too, whom the heavenly height of counsel has raised to the summit of royal dignity so that we may distribute suitable help to each as time requires, desire to have as our co-workers those whom we intend to preside over no less than to benefit.

units.la: 2. Sanè considerantes attentius & infra claustra pectoris nostri sedulò revolventes, quod nefanda hostis antiqui nequitia, qui semper quærit ut noceat; semper in circuitu ambulat, ut offendat plerisq; locis Italiæ & Vicinis eiidem discordiarum Zizaniam seminavit, ingessit lites, commovit dala, odia suscitavit grandia; utiq; desiderio ducimur ingenti, ac modis plurimis excitamur, ut hujusmodi molestiis quamplurimum votis nostris efficacibus & oportunis remediis obviētur, ac ipsis benigna Regiæ Clementiæ provisione proveniente deformata inibi propriam reformatiōnem recipiant, ac prava & noxia procul penitus profligentur.
units.tr: 2. Indeed, considering more attentively and turning over carefully within the recesses of our heart that the nefarious wickedness of the ancient enemy, who always seeks to harm, always walks about seeking whom he may offend, has sown the tares of discord in many places in Italy and its neighbouring regions, stirred up strife, roused quarrels and kindled great hatreds; we are moved by a great desire and are stirred in many ways that such troubles may be met as far as possible by our effective and timely remedies, and that, through the gracious provision of our royal clemency, these regions may receive their own reformation and that wicked and harmful practices may be wholly driven out.

units.la: 3. Attendentes igitur intemeratæ fidei constantiam firmam, ac multiplicia devotionis & fidelitatis insignia, quibus nobiles progenitores tui Domus de la Scala Divos Romanorum Imperatores & Reges, ac ipsum Sacrum Romanum Imperium dignis quod studuerint honoribus venerari. Illum quoque fervidum tuæ mentis ardorem, quod ad nostros & Imperii sacri promovendos honores indefessis laboribus attentius inclinaris, & quod gratiarum datór altissimus personam tuam industriæ nere, providentiæ dono, discretionis virtute, circumspectionis gratia, & aliarum titulis virtutum multiplicitèr decoravit. Quodq; de tuis laudabilibus meritis à tuis progenitoribus radicitus emanatis, duciam obtinere possumus indubiam; & quod nobis obligasti, & juramenti vinculo adstrinxisti, ac heredes tuos legitimos semper inantea perenniter & fideliter in omni obedientia, subjectum, & reverentia nostra & successorum nostrorum in Imperio exhibere, ac in eisdem jugiter perseverare. Quod de omnibus & singulis juribus, servitiis, datiis, donariis, cæsibus, oneribus & solutionibus tam quam de consuetudine seu pacto nobis & sacro Romano Imperio, cum omni promptitudine dignoscaris, actualiter respondere locis congruis, & temporibus oportunis. Et quod omnia & singula in obligatione per te nobis tradita attendens observabis inconcusse, & nullo unquam tempore contravenies, aut contrafacies verbo vel facto per te vel per alium seu alios directè vel indirectè, publicè vel occultè:
units.tr: 3. Therefore, considering the steadfast constancy of your unblemished faith and the manifold tokens of devotion and fidelity by which your noble ancestors of the house of della Scala have honoured with due marks of respect the illustrious Roman Emperors and Kings and the Holy Roman Empire itself; also that fervent ardour of your mind by which you incline more earnestly, with tireless labours, to advance our honours and those of the Holy Empire; and that the Most High giver of graces has richly adorned your person with the gifts of diligence, the gift of foresight, the virtue of discretion, the grace of circumspection and the titles of other virtues; and considering that we may firmly rely on your praiseworthy merits, which have sprung from the roots of your ancestors; and that you have bound yourself to us by the bond of an oath, and have promised that your legitimate heirs will forever hereafter perpetually and faithfully show obedience, subjection and reverence to us and to our successors in the Empire, and will continue steadfast in these things; that you will promptly and fully discharge, in suitable places and at proper times, all rights, services, dues, gifts, taxes, burdens and payments, whether by custom or by agreement, owed to us and to the Holy Roman Empire; and that you will observe unshaken all and each of the obligations you have given us, and will never at any time act against them, by word or deed, by yourself or through another or others, directly or indirectly, openly or secretly:

units.la: 4. Te animo deliberato, de Principum Magnatum, Comitum, Baronum & Procerum nostrorum consilio, Imperialis quoq; plenitudine potestatis, ac de certa nostra scientia ad Vicariatum prædictarum civitatum Veronæ & Vincentiæ, ipsarumq; Territoriorum, districtuum ac pertinentiarum, sicut præfati progenitores tui juste tenuerunt, & possiderunt, eundem restituimus: ac ut evellas & destruas, dissipes & disperdas, ædifices & plantes in eisdem civitatibus ac earum Territoriis, districtibus & pertinentiis ordinavimus, fecimus & creavimus, & de novo constituimus per præsentes nostrum & sacri Romani Imperii Vicarium generalem.
units.tr: 4. We, with deliberate intent, on the counsel of our princes, magnates, counts, barons and nobles, and by the fullness of imperial power and from our certain knowledge, restore to you the Vicariate of the aforesaid cities of Verona and Vicenza, together with their territories, districts and dependencies, just as your aforesaid ancestors justly held and possessed it. And we have ordained, made and created, and by these presents newly appoint, you as our and the Holy Roman Empire's Vicar General, so that you may uproot and tear down, scatter and destroy, build and plant in the same cities and their territories, districts and dependencies.

units.la: 5. Dantes exnunc & concedentes tibi & legitimis heredibus tuis masculis de lumbis tuis descendentibus, plenam, liberam & omnimodam auctoritatem & jurisdictionem generalem & specialem, ac gladii potestatem, merum & mixtum Imperium vice ac auctoritate atq; nomine nostris in præfatis civitatibus, territoriorum, districtuum & pertinentiarum ipsarum limitibus, circumferentis & finibus earum per vos vel alium seu alios, cui vel quibus hoc commiseritis exercendum, animadvertendum in facinorosos & reos, coërtionem quamlibet ratione prævia, & mediante justitia exequendum.
units.tr: 5. Giving and granting now to you and to your legitimate male heirs descended from your loins, full, free and unrestricted authority and jurisdiction, general and special, and the power of the sword, mere and mixed imperium, in our place, by our authority and in our name, within the cities, territories, districts and dependencies, and within their boundaries, circuits and limits, to be exercised by you or by another or others to whom you commit it, to take action against criminals and offenders, and to enforce any coercion whatever, on a reasoned basis and through justice.

units.la: 6. Et ut etiam apud vos seu vestros Commissarios merum & mixtum Imperium, jurisdictiove cōtentiosa, sive voluntaria in præfatis civitatibus, territoriis, districtibus & pertinentiis ipsarum subditis, incolis & hominibus ibidem, cujuscunq; status, præeminentiæ vel conditionis existant, semper in omnibus Sacrosancta Ecclesiastica libertate, de rebus, contractibus vel quasi contractibus, ultimis voluntatibus, maleficiis, criminibus & delictis vel quasi commissis, & perpetratis, in subditos, incolas & homines prædictos, et per eos seu etiam per alios in dictis civitatibus, territoriis & pertinentiis suis perpetratis, (seu etiam perpetrandis, exerceatur liberè, secundū quod jus & ratio persuadet.
units.tr: 6. And so that mere and mixed imperium, and contentious and voluntary jurisdiction, may also be exercised by you or your commissaries in the aforesaid cities, territories, districts and dependencies over their subjects, inhabitants and men there, of whatever rank, pre-eminence or condition they may be, always in all matters preserving sacrosanct ecclesiastical liberty, concerning things, contracts or quasi-contracts, last wills, misdeeds, crimes and offences, or quasi-offences, committed or perpetrated against the said subjects, inhabitants and men, and by them or also by others within your said cities, territories and dependencies (or also to be perpetrated), let it be exercised freely, as right and reason persuade.

units.la: 7. Concedentes nihilominus tibi ac heredibus tuis, ac illi vel illis, cui seu quibus comiserint, auctoritatem, potestatem, jurisdictionem omnimodam, & licentiam generalem, collectas & Datia consueta, onera, realia & personalia ac mixta, nec non omnes census, reditus, jura, proventus, emolumenta, subventiones, conductus, telonia & pedagia prædictarum civitatum, territorium & pertinentiarum ad nos & sacrum Romanum Imperium pertinentes, exigendi & recipiendi poenas & multas ratione prævia imponendi, levandi, & ex causis rationabilibus augmentandi, minuendi, remittendi, in judicio & extra: Judæos Camerae nostrae servos acceptandi, defendendi & tuendi, jura Cæsarea, collectas, subventiones & steuras ab ipsis (prout hoc honor Imperii & necessitas, stulaverit) exigendi in judicio & extra: In causarum cognitione, ipsum solum DEUM habendo præ oculis, ac de plano & summariè sine strepitu & figura judicii, sola veritate inspecta procedendum, terminandum, sententias exequendum; fugitivos inquirendū & puniendum; maleficos, furesque, sicarios & robatores stratarum laqueandum, judicandum, ac piratas maris submergendum juxta Canonum, legum & jurium communium sacratissimas sanctiones, prout secundū ritum & consuetudinem, municipalia jura & statuta persuaserint; ac proditores decapitandū, suspendendi ac eos & eorum quemlibet, dum & quoties se casus obtulerit, condemnandum, puniendum, mem-bra truncanduni, fustibus cædendum, & in facie bullandum, de patria ad tempus, vel perpetuò relegandum, carcerandum, & igne cremandum, mutilandum & debilitandum; bona talium publicandum, infiscandum; officialēs institutendum, & de omnibus crimimbus ordinariis, & extraordinariis, eorum ribus, levibus, publicis & privatis cognoscendum, puniendum & executionem faciendum tam secundum jura communia quam municipalia decidendum, cognitionem & decisionem hujusmodi committendum, in integrum restituendum, absolutionem quamlibet in judicio vel extra exercendum, infamiam tam juris quam facti irrogandum, abolendum & disponendum: De causis principalibus & appellationibus quibuslibet tanquam judices super his à nobis specialiter deputati, cognoscendum, examinandum, diffiniendum; Decretum primum & secundum interponendum, jura declarandum & ornamenta quæ causarum merita requirunt exercendum & requirendum: Ita tamen, quod à tua & officialium tuorum sententia vel sententiis ad audientiam nostri culminis possit liberè totiens, quotiens opportunum fuerit, provocari. Monetas sub vero pondere & caractere aureas & argenteas instituedum: ecias imponendum, & tollendum; Rebelles sacri Imperii persequendum & puniendum; Decreta, statuta & provisiones in prædictis omnibus & quolibet prædictorum faciendu, de novo corrigendum, pariter tollenduni, semel ac pluries & totiens quotiens oportunum fuerit, & ordo tractaverit, & diceverit. Rationes, dotes & dotalitia ac donationes propter nuptias admittendum, approbandum & confirmandum; menre captis curatores, & orphanis, pupillis & viduis tutores præficiendum: devotiones fiscales quarumcunq; hereditatum seu eriam rerum mobilium & immobilium, dum ratio & jus illud exegerint, nostro Regio nomine exigendum, tenutam & possessionem talium capiendù: & generaliter omnia & singula, quæ ad veros & legitimos sacri Romani Imperii in suprādictis civitatibus & pertinentus Vicarios pertinent, ut præmittitur, libere & absq; impedimento quolibet faciendum; et si qua ex eis jure vel consuetudine exigerent mandatum magis speciale.
units.tr: 7. Granting likewise to you and your heirs, and to him or them to whom they shall commit it, full authority, power, jurisdiction and general licence: to exact and receive the customary levies and taxes, both real and personal and mixed burdens, and all the censuses, revenues, rights, proceeds, emoluments, subsidies, tolls, customs duties and road tolls of the aforesaid cities, territories and dependencies belonging to us and to the Holy Roman Empire; to impose, levy, and for reasonable causes increase, diminish or remit penalties and fines on a reasoned basis, both in court and out of court; to accept, defend and protect Jews as servants of our Chamber; to exact the imperial rights, levies, subsidies and taxes from them (as the honour of the Empire and necessity shall demand), both in court and out of court; in hearing causes, keeping God alone before one's eyes, to proceed, to conclude, and to execute sentences summarily and plainly, without noise or the formality of a trial, looking only to the truth; to seek out and punish fugitives; to hang criminals, thieves, assassins and highwaymen, and to drown pirates at sea, in accordance with the most sacred sanctions of the canons, laws and common rights, as local custom, municipal rights and statutes shall persuade; to behead and hang traitors, and to condemn and punish each and every one of them whenever the occasion arises, to cut off limbs, to beat with rods, to brand on the face, to banish from the homeland for a time or for ever, to imprison, to burn with fire, to maim and to cripple; to confiscate and forfeit the goods of such persons; to appoint officials, and to hear, punish and carry out sentences for all ordinary and extraordinary crimes, both grave and light, public and private, and to decide them according to common as well as municipal law; to commit the hearing and decision of such matters; to grant full restitution; to exercise and pronounce any absolution in court or out of court; to inflict, abolish and regulate infamy, whether of law or of fact; to hear and determine principal causes and appeals of every kind, as judges specially deputed by us for these matters; to interpose first and second decrees, to declare rights, and to exercise and grant the honours that the merits of causes require: provided, however, that from your sentence or the sentences of your officials it may be freely appealed to the hearing of our supreme court, as often as it shall be expedient. To establish gold and silver coinage of true weight and stamp; to impose and remove taxes; to pursue and punish rebels of the Holy Empire; to make, correct anew, and likewise abolish decrees, statutes and provisions in all the aforesaid matters and in any of them, as often and as many times as shall be expedient and as the matter shall have been considered and decided; to admit, approve and confirm accounts, dowries, dower settlements and gifts on account of marriage; to appoint curators for the insane and guardians for orphans, wards and widows; to exact, in our royal name, the fiscal dues of any inheritances, or of movable and immovable goods, whenever reason and law require it; to take hold and possession of such goods; and generally to do freely and without any hindrance all and each of the things which, as set out above, pertain to the true and lawful Vicars of the Holy Roman Empire in the aforesaid cities and dependencies; and if any of these things by law or custom should require a more special mandate.

units.la: 8. Quapropter fidelitatibus vestris * * & districtè præcipiendo mandamus, quatenus ad statum pacificum civitatum, territoriorum, districtuum & pertinentiarum prædictarum ac recuperationem nostrorum & Imperii sacri jurium, in præmissis omnibus & singulis fidem vestram, & sollicitudinem, iucurgiam nostram charam gratamq; diligitis, sic efficaciter licq; prompto studio impendatis, ut in nobis sollicitudinis vestræ testimonio electionis nostræ judicium cömendetur, dum tales & tanto negocio duximus proponendum, ex quorum fide & justitia serenitatis nostræ salubre propositum de observatione jurium Imperii civitatum & pertinentiarum prædictarum singulariter exprimatur.
units.tr: 8. Therefore we firmly and strictly command your fidelities that, for the peaceful state of the aforesaid cities, territories, districts and dependencies, and for the recovery of our rights and those of the holy Empire, you apply your loyalty and diligence in all and each of the aforesaid matters, you who hold our care dear and welcome, and that you do so effectively and with prompt zeal, so that our choice may be commended for the proof of your concern. We have thought fit to entrust such a matter to such men, from whose fidelity and justice the salutary purpose of our serenity, concerning the observance of the rights of the Empire in the aforesaid cities and dependencies, may be clearly made known.

units.la: 9. Præsentium sub nostri Regalis Sigilli appéfione testimonio literarum. Datum Budæ Anno Domini Millesimo quadringentesimo duodecimo, vigesima secunda die Januarii; Regnorum nostrorum, Anno Hungariæ, vigesimo quinto, Romanorum vero secundo.
units.tr: 9. In witness whereof, we have given these letters under the appending of our royal seal. Given at Buda in the year of the Lord 1412, on the twenty-second day of January; in the twenty-fifth year of our reign in Hungary, and the second of our reign as King of the Romans.

units.la: 10. Itaq; accedens noštræ Majestatis præsentiâ præfatus Brunorius nobis exposuit, Quod quia ipse usq; modo caruillet & hodiè careret uxore & prole masculina legitima, & omnis caro esset itura viam suam, & nihil stabile sub Sole perfisteret, supplicavitq; nobis quatenus providere dignaremur, in casu quo ipsum fine prole legitima masculina ab hac luce migrare contingeret, Quod extunc Vicariatus prædictarum terrarum ac civitatum à domo illa de la Scala non maneret amotus.
units.tr: 10. Accordingly, the aforesaid Brunorius, coming into the presence of our Majesty, set forth to us that, since he has hitherto lacked, and today still lacks, a legitimate wife and male offspring, and since all flesh must go its way and nothing stable remains under the sun, he begged us to deign to provide that, should he happen to depart this life without legitimate male offspring, the vicariate of the aforesaid lands and cities should not then be removed from the house of della Scala.

units.la: 11. Nos verò considerantes petitionem hujusmodi honestam, maximè inducti meritis progenitorum suorum, qui officio illius Vicariatus longissimis annorum curriculis glorioso regimine præfuerunt. Accetiam pensatis fidelissimis servitiis nobis & Imperio sacro à primordio concessionis prædicti Vicariatus, omni constantia & intemerata devotione die noctuq; per ipsum Brunorium continua exhibitis, quibus nostræ gratiæ munificentiam sibi quodam debito vendicavit, volentes annuere votis & petitionibus suis, ac ipsum ad ulteriora nostra, & Imperii sacri servitia incirare.
units.tr: 11. We, however, considering such a petition honourable, were moved above all by the merits of his forebears, who presided over the office of that vicariate in a glorious rule over very long years. We also weighed the most faithful services, constantly rendered to us and to the holy Empire from the first grant of the aforesaid vicariate, with unwavering and inviolable devotion, day and night, by the same Brunorius, by which he has earned for himself, as by a certain debt, the generosity of our grace. Wishing to grant his prayers and petitions, and to stir him up to further services to us and the holy Empire...

units.la: 12. Primò præinsertum privilegium nostrum auctoritate Cæsarea confirmanus & innovamus, in omnibus suis clausulis & continentiis approbamus. Et randem ipsum privilegium animo deliberato sano principum, Comitum & fidelium nostrorum accedente consilio, & de nostra certa scientia, ore præsentiū, & de plenitudine Imperatoriæ potestatis amplíamus, & in personas Magnificorum Bignami & Pauli de la Scala frarrum præfati Brunorii, nostrorū & Imperii sacri fidelium dilectorum dimus, ipsisq; Fregnano & Paulo, ac heredibus eorum masculis legitimis, de lumbis suis descendentibus, hujusmodi Vicariatum prædictarum terrarum & Civitatum & pertinentiarum earundem tum præfatus Brunorius sine filiis legitimis masculis ab hac luce, quod absit, decederet, & non aliorum conferentes, decernentesq; & hoc Imperiali statuentes edicto, quod ipsi Fregnanus & Paulus, ac eorum heredes legitimi masculi, ipso Brunorio, ut præmittitur, absq; filiis legitimis masculis decedente hujusmodi Vicariatum prætatarum terrarum gaudeant, & fruantur omni honore, jure & potestate in privilegio præinserto concepti, quos eis tenore præsentium concedimus obstaculo procul amoto: Reservato tamen nobis & successoribus nostris Romanis Imperatoribus & Regibus, ac Romano Imperio debita fidelitatis juramento & obedientiæ, tempore suo pacando, quibus eos & heredes eorum, ut præmittitur, semper astrictos esse volumus.
units.tr: 12. First, we confirm and renew the privilege inserted above by imperial authority, and approve it in all its clauses and contents. Furthermore, with deliberate intent, with the sound counsel of our princes, counts and faithful ones, from our certain knowledge and by the fullness of imperial power, we extend it, and we grant it to the magnificent Bignamus and Paulus de la Scala, brothers of the aforesaid Brunorius, our beloved and faithful men and those of the holy Empire, and to Fregnanus and Paulus, and to their legitimate male heirs descended from their loins: this vicariate of the aforesaid lands, cities and dependencies, conferring it on them if the aforesaid Brunorius should depart this life without legitimate male sons, which God forbid, and not on others. And we decree and establish by this imperial edict that Fregnanus and Paulus and their legitimate male heirs, upon the aforesaid Brunorius dying without legitimate male sons, as stated above, shall enjoy this vicariate of the aforesaid lands with all the honour, right and power contained in the inserted privilege, which we grant them by the tenor of these presents, the obstacle being removed. Reserved, however, to us and to our successors, the Roman emperors and kings, and to the Roman Empire, is the due oath of fidelity and obedience, to be rendered in its proper time, to which we wish them and their heirs always bound, as stated.

units.la: 13. Cæterum ad declarationem futuratum successionum, utq; de ordine ipsarum à posteris ambiguitas auferatur & tollatur omnis materia quæstionis, confusionisq; omnis possibilis dubietas extrapetur, detur autem potius clarus & determinatus succedendi in prædictis Vicariatu, ac omnibus supra concessis stylus & ordo. Hoc præsenti nostro Imperiali edicto in perpetuum valituro statuimus, dicimus & sancimus; Quod primogenitus præfati Brunorii masculus ex legitimo & vero matrimonio natus in Vicariatu præfato, & cæteris omnibus & singulis supra concessis & indultis sibi accedat.
units.tr: 13. Moreover, so that the succession may be declared for the future, and so that uncertainty about their order may be removed from posterity, every matter of dispute taken away, and every possible doubt of confusion cut off, let there rather be given a clear and determined manner and order of succeeding in the aforesaid vicariate and in all the grants made above. By this our present imperial edict, to remain valid in perpetuity, we establish, declare and sanction that the first-born male of the aforesaid Brunorius, born of a lawful and true marriage, shall succeed to the aforesaid vicariate and to all and each of the grants made above.

units.la: 14. Et quod dicto primogenito suo decedente, etiam ipso vivente, filius primogenitus masculus legitimo matrimonio ortus dicti primogeniti præferatur aliis quibuscunq; in successione Vicariatus.
units.tr: 14. And that, when this first-born dies, even while he himself is still living, the first-born male son of that first-born, born of a lawful marriage, shall be preferred to all others in the succession to the vicariate.

units.la: L l riatus præscripti, & aliorum superius concessorum, quod quoad prædictam successionem in singulis primogeniturę masculis ex legitimo matrimonio descendentibus observari volumus.
units.tr: ...of the prescribed vicariate and of the others granted above, which, as regards the aforesaid succession, we wish to be observed in each of the first-born males descended from lawful marriage.

units.la: 15. Deficientibus verò, ut supra, primogenitis & primogenitorum primogenitis, tunc etiam genitus masculus ex legitimo matrimonio ex ipso Brunorio ortus, sive ipse primogenitus ab ipso secundogenito ordinatè & secundum rectam lineam masculinam, prout de successione supra praedictum est, succedat; & sic in omnibus observetur.
units.tr: 15. If, as above, the first-born and the first-born's first-born are lacking, then the male born of lawful marriage from Brunorius himself shall succeed, whether this first-born succeeds the second-born in order and according to the direct male line, as has been said above concerning succession; and so let it be observed in all things.

units.la: 16. Illud idè intelligendo suis tertio & quartogenitis, & sic deinceps intelligendo, etiam quod illi primogeniti succedentes ad regimen Vicariatus praefati sint habiles & idonei, sani mente & corpore: Alioquin repertis illis primogenitis, & his qui ordine suprascripto successuri sunt, in defectionis aut mentis & aliis defectibus legitimis & justis, successio in proximiorem post eos, sanum & indefectuosum, ut praemittitur, ordine suprascripto transferatur.
units.tr: 16. It is understood that this applies similarly to their third- and fourth-born, and so on in succession, provided that those first-born who succeed to the government of the aforesaid vicariate are fit and capable, sound in mind and body. Otherwise, if those first-born, and those who are to succeed in the order written above, are found lacking through insanity or other lawful and just defects, the succession shall pass, in the order written above, to the nearest after them who is sound and without defect, as stated.

units.la: 17. Deficiente autem praefato Brunorio (quod absit) sine prole & successore, hujusmodi Vicariatus ad fratres suos praefata concessione nostra devoluta, volumus ut Fregnanus & Paulus tunc indifferenter & simpliciter ac aequaliter in Vicariatu ipso succedant. Et ille eis & heredibus ac ceteris pertinear pari modo, nisi alter praefatorum fratrum, videlicet Fregnanus sive Paulus, prole legitima procreata masculina decesserit, tunc filii fratris superstitis succedant eo modo & forma, quibus de praefato Brunorio est praemissum.
units.tr: 17. But if the aforesaid Brunorius dies (which God forbid) without offspring or heir, this vicariate, by our aforesaid grant, shall devolve upon his brothers. We wish that Fregnanus and Paulus then succeed to the vicariate equally, without distinction and simply; and it shall pertain to them, their heirs and the others in the same way, unless one of the aforesaid brothers, namely Fregnanus or Paulus, dies having begotten legitimate male offspring. In that case the sons of the surviving brother shall succeed in the manner and form stated above concerning the aforesaid Brunorius.

units.la: 18. Ad perpetuam autem conservationem charitatis & zeli praefatae domus de la Scala, dimus praefato Brunorio & impartimur, quod ipse valeat relinquere cuilibet ex aliis filiis suis legitimis post primogenitum, tantum de fortalitiis & bonis, quae annuatim ad reditus duorum millium florenorum se extendant, cum hoctamen, quod tales filii teneantur illa recognoscere per investituram primogenito.
units.tr: 18. For the perpetual preservation of the charity and zeal of the aforesaid house of della Scala, we grant and impart to the aforesaid Brunorius that he may leave to each of his other legitimate sons after the first-born as much of the fortresses and goods as extend to an annual income of two thousand florins, on the condition that such sons be bound to acknowledge those holdings by investiture from the first-born.

units.la: 19. Et sic quilibet Vicarius de la Scala ceteris ejus filiis de tantis bonis tantorum reddituum dum videre providere valeat, ita tamen, quod semper a primogenito recognoscantur, ut supra.
units.tr: 19. And so each Vicar of della Scala may be able to see to and provide for his other sons from such goods and such revenues, provided that they are always acknowledged by the first-born, as above.

units.la: 20. Quibus quidem sic relictis decernimus ipsos omnes ac singulos suprascriptos & verum ab eis esse tacitos & contentos, ipsis super ceteris, quae ad hereditatem illam contingerent, perpetuum silentium imponentes, praesentium sub nostrae Imperialis Majestatis sigillo Testimonio. Datum Ratisponae, Anno Domini millesimo quadringentesimo trigesimo quarto: die October octavo, Romani vicesimo quinto, Bohemiae quintodecimo, Imperii vero secundo.
units.tr: 20. Having thus left these things, we decree that all and each of the aforesaid are to hold themselves content with them, and we impose on them perpetual silence concerning the other matters which might pertain to that inheritance, by the testimony of these presents under the seal of our Imperial Majesty. Given at Regensburg in the year of the Lord 1434, on the eighth day of October, in the twenty-fifth year of our reign as King of the Romans, the fifteenth as King of Bohemia, and the second of our reign as Emperor.

units.la: SIGISMUNDI REGIS ET IMPERATORIS BULLA
units.tr: SIGISMUND, KING AND EMPEROR: THE BULL

units.la: De jure & successione Electorum Palatinorum.
units.tr: On the right and succession of the Palatine Electors.

units.la: SIGISMUNDUS Dei gratia Romanorum Imperator semper Augustus, ac Ungariae, Bohemiae, Dalmatiae, Croatiae, &c. Rex; ad perpetuam rei memoriam.
units.tr: SIGISMUND, by the grace of God Roman Emperor, ever Augustus, and King of Hungary, Bohemia, Dalmatia, Croatia, etc.; to all for perpetual remembrance.

units.la: 1. Quanquam Imperialis sublimitas dignitatis, in qua conditor orbis nos suę pietatis clementia feliciter collocavit, jugiter mentem nostram sollicitet, ut cura pervigili & laborum studiis accuratis nostrorum & Imperii sacri fidelium ampurtemus incommoda, eisque desiderate pacis amoenitatem uberiter procuremus: ferventiori tamen affectu cor nostrum accenditur penes ea, quae sacri decoris, & Illustres ipsius Principes Electores, per quos coepit, & in quibus consistit nostrae gloriae magnitudo, qui & in partem sollicitudinis nobiscum sunt vocati, quadam singularitate concernunt; cuipiam, quos generis nobilitas, multiplicia virtutum insignia & praeclara fidei devotio laudabiliter commendant.
units.tr: 1. Although the imperial sublimity of the dignity in which the Creator of the world, by the clemency of his goodness, has happily placed us constantly troubles our mind, so that with vigilant care and diligent labours we may remedy the troubles of our subjects and of the faithful of the Holy Empire, and richly secure for them the pleasantness of a desired peace; yet our heart is kindled with a more fervent affection concerning those things which, in a certain special way, concern the holy dignity and the illustrious Princes Electors themselves, through whom it began and in whom consists the greatness of our glory, and who have been called to share the burden of care with us, and who are praiseworthily commended by the nobility of their birth, the manifold distinctions of their virtues, and their outstanding devotion to the faith.

units.la: 2. Sane cum aliàs per literas omnium Principum Electorum, & nominatim divae recordationis Serenissimi Principis & Domini, Domini Caroli Quarti Romanorum Imperatoris & Bohemiae Regis, genitoris nostri carissimi, velut Regis Bohemiae; venerabilium Gerlaci Moguntini per Almaniam, Boëmundi Trevirensis per Galliam & regnum Arelatense, Wilhelmi Coloniensis per Italiam, sacri Romani Imperii Archicancellariorum Archiepiscoporum; Rudolphi Ducis Saxoniae, sacri Imperii Archimarschalli; & Ludovici dicti Romer, quondam Imperatoris Ludovici filii, Marchionis Brandenburgensis, sacri Imperii Archicamerarii: ac etiam à Principibus, Comitibus, Baronibus, Nobilibus, Proceribus, ac multis aliis nostris & Imperii sacri fidelibus informationem certissimam & lucidam monia clariora, nostra suscepit Imperialis Cellitudo, qualiter felicis memoriae Illustris Ruperti senior, quondam Comes Palatinus Rheni, sacri Romani Imperii Archidapifer, & Bavariae Ducis, avunculi nostri carissimi; & post praedictum Rupertum senio ... procedunt, Rege Regum & Domino dominantiū, *coronam Imperialem suscepimus: Quodq; prædicti, Rupertus præsenior patruus, ac Rupertus pater dicti Ludovici quondam Comitis Palatini Rheni, diuturna temporum præscriptione inconcusse habuerunt & possederunt legitimè, prout eti-am ipse Ludovicus in præsentiarum ad instar illorum ex successione paterna & hereditaria dignoscitur justo titulo possidere jus, vocem, dignitatem, & potestatem eligendi Romanorum Regem in Imperatorem promovendum: quemadmodum in nostris literis declarationis statuti ac ordinationis sub Regali Romanorum titulo desuper editis ac promulgatis plenius continentur: Et quod longinquitate ut sæpe fit temporis, quòd res clara præsentibus redditur per oblivionem obscura futuris, prudentum cautela providit, ea quæ adduntur, scripturæ testimonio commendari, ut amplioris autoritatis robore posteritati innotescant: Habet interdum nostræ provisionis industria, ut illa in novatione confirmet, & autoritate fulciat innovata.
units.tr: 2. Indeed, since on other occasions our Imperial Highness has received, through letters of all the Princes Electors, and especially of the most serene Prince and Lord, Lord Charles IV, Roman Emperor and King of Bohemia, our dearest father, as King of Bohemia; of the venerable Gerlach of Mainz throughout Germany, Baldwin of Trier through Gaul and the kingdom of Arles, and Wilhelm of Cologne through Italy, archchancellors of the Holy Roman Empire and archbishops; of Rudolf, Duke of Saxony, archmarshal of the Holy Empire; and of Ludwig, called Romer, son of the late Emperor Ludwig, Margrave of Brandenburg, archchamberlain of the Holy Empire; and also from princes, counts, barons, nobles, magnates and many other of our faithful and of the Holy Empire, most certain and clear information concerning all matters, namely how the late Rupert the Elder, of happy memory, Illustrious Count Palatine of the Rhine, archsteward of the Holy Roman Empire and Duke of Bavaria, our dearest uncle, and after the aforesaid Rupert the Elder ... proceed, the King of kings and Lord of lords [willing it], we have received the imperial crown. And that the aforesaid Rupert the Elder, paternal uncle, and Rupert, father of the said Ludwig, late Count Palatine of the Rhine, held and possessed lawfully and without dispute through a long prescription of time, just as Ludwig himself is now recognised to possess by just title, in the manner of those, by paternal and hereditary succession, the right, voice, dignity and power of electing the Roman King to be promoted to Emperor; as is more fully contained in our letters of declaration, statute and ordinance issued and promulgated on this matter under the title of Roman King. And since, as often happens with the lapse of time, what is clear to the present becomes obscure to the future through forgetfulness, the prudent caution of the wise has provided that what is added be commended to the testimony of writing, so that it may become known to posterity with the strength of greater authority. It sometimes belongs to the diligence of our providence to confirm in renewal and to support with authority what has been renewed.

units.la: 3. Unde sane tam Ecclesiasticorum quam Secularium Principum sacri Romani Imperii Electorum consilio & consensu accedente, non improvidè neque per errorem, sed animo deliberato, aliorū etiam Principum plurimorū Ecclesiasticorum & Secularium, Baronū, Nobilium, & Procerum, nostrorum ac Imperii sacri fidelium, maturè communicato consilio, cupientes autore Domino suturis obviare periculis, & materiam omnium succidere dubiorum; de certa nostra scientia & de plenitudine Imperialis potestatis, in his scriptis pronunciamus, decernimus, statuimus, declaramus, & etiam hoc Imperiali perpetuo valituro sancimus edicto: quòd jus, vox, dignitas, & potestas eligendi Romanorum Regem in Imperatorem promovendum eidem Ludovico Comiti Palatino Rheni, tanquam Imperii sacri Archidapifero ac Principi Electori, hæredibus & successoribus suis legitimis, laicis duntaxat, ab eo descendentibus, quoties casus hujusmodi electionis emerserit in perpetuum debeat competere; sicut & ritè sibi tanquam Comiti Palatino Rheni, ac sacri Romani Imperii Archidapifero competit manifestè; ac ipse velut Comes Palatinus Rheni ejusdem Romani Imperii Archidapifer, verus & legitimus Princeps Elector & post obitum ejus hæredes & successores sui legitimi, modo & forma submissis Principatum & Comitatum Palatinum ac Archidapiferiam dicti Imperii sacri, de quibus ipsum die * nostræ coronationis in Aquisgrano solenniter infeudavimus & investivimus, ac tenore præsentium infeudatum & investitum profitemur: cum omnibus & singulis eorum tertis, dominiis, proprietatibus, vasallagiis, libertatibus, honoribus, & pertinentiis, in quibuscunq; rebus consistant, & quibuscunq; specialibus possint vocabulis designari, necnon jus, vocem, dignitatem, & potestatem eligendi Romanorum Regem in Imperatorem promovendum, sine impedimento quolibet debeant obtinere.
units.tr: 3. Therefore, with the counsel and consent of both the Ecclesiastical and the Secular Princes, the Electors of the Holy Roman Empire, not rashly nor through error but with deliberate mind, and after mature consultation with many other Princes, both Ecclesiastical and Secular, barons, nobles and magnates, our faithful subjects and those of the Holy Empire, desiring, with the Lord as author, to meet future dangers and to cut off the matter of all doubts, we pronounce, decree, establish and declare by certain knowledge and from the fullness of imperial power in these writings, and also sanction by this imperial edict, to remain in force forever: that the right, voice, dignity and power of electing the Roman King to be promoted to Emperor shall belong in perpetuity to the same Ludwig, Count Palatine of the Rhine, as Archsteward of the Holy Empire and Prince Elector, and to his lawful heirs and successors, laymen only, descended from him, whenever a case of such an election arises; just as it clearly belongs by right to him as Count Palatine of the Rhine and Archsteward of the Holy Roman Empire; and he himself, as Count Palatine of the Rhine and Archsteward of the same Roman Empire, the true and lawful Prince Elector, and after his death his lawful heirs and successors, in the manner and form set out, we have solemnly enfeoffed and invested, and by the tenor of these presents we declare him enfeoffed and invested with the Principality and County Palatine and the Archstewardship of the said Holy Empire, which we bestowed upon him in Aachen on the day of our coronation; together with all and each of their dependencies, lordships, properties, vassalages, liberties, honours and appurtenances, wherever they consist and by whatever special names they may be designated, and likewise the right, voice, dignity and power of electing the Roman King to be promoted to Emperor, which they shall obtain without any impediment.

units.la: 4. Et ne inter hæredes & successores ipsius, eo defuncto super hujusmodi jure futuris temporibus dubitationum, quæstionum, seu litium quævis materia oriatur; decernimus, statuimus, & præsenti Imperiali sancimus edicto in perpetuum valituro, (prout hoc idem per præfatum Dominum Carolum Quartum Romanorum Imperatorem, genitorem nostrum carissimum, omnium ac singulorum Principum Electorum, & multorum sacri Romani Imperii Principum, Comitum, Nobilium, ac fidelium consilio & unanimi consensu accedente, lege & Imperiali edicto in Aurea Bulla publicè sancitum esse dignoscitur,) quod post obitum dicti Ludovici Comitis Palatini Rheni & Bavariæ Ducis, primogenitus ejus filius, & post primogeniti obitum ejusdem primogeniti senior filius ex ordine genituræ, & sic deinceps à seniori filio descendentes ex ordine genituræ semper senior; si verò primogenitus præfati Ludovici decesserit masculini sexus, laicis duntaxat, legitimis hæredibus non relictis, extunc secundogenitus filius Ludovici Ducis prædicti, & post obitum ejus secundogeniti filius senior laicus: & si secundogenitus sine hæredibus legitimis masculini sexus, laicis duntaxat, decesserit, tertiogenitus dicti Ludovici, & senior ejus filius laicus post mortem ipsius; & deinceps per talem modū directa linea genituræ descendentes ab eo, laici duntaxat, jus, vocem, dignitatem, & potestatem eligendi Romanorum Regem promovēdum in Imperatorem & officiū Archidapiferi, cum omnibus & singulis dominiis, honoribus, juribus, privilegiis, dignitatibus & pertinentiis, in perpetuis temporibus obtinebunt per successionem hæreditariam & paternalem (ut præmittitur) ex ordine genituræ.
units.tr: 4. And so that no matter of doubts, questions or lawsuits concerning this right may arise in future times among his heirs and successors after his death, we decree, establish and sanction by this imperial edict, to remain in force forever (as this same thing is known to have been publicly sanctioned by law and imperial edict in the Golden Bull, with the counsel and unanimous consent of all and each of the Princes Electors and of many Princes, Counts, Nobles and faithful of the Holy Roman Empire, by the aforesaid Lord Charles IV, Roman Emperor, our dearest father): that after the death of the said Ludwig, Count Palatine of the Rhine and Duke of Bavaria, his firstborn son, and after the death of that firstborn, the senior son in order of birth of the same firstborn, and so on, always the senior in order of birth among those descending from the senior son; but if the firstborn of the aforesaid Ludwig shall die leaving no male lawful heirs who are laymen, then the second-born son of the aforesaid Duke Ludwig, and after his death the senior lay son of the second-born; and if the second-born shall die without male lawful heirs who are laymen, then the third-born of the said Ludwig, and his senior lay son after his death; and thereafter, in this manner, those descending from him in the direct line of birth, laymen only, shall obtain the right, voice, dignity and power of electing the Roman King to be promoted to Emperor, and the office of Archsteward, with all and each of the lordships, honours, rights, privileges, dignities and appurtenances, in perpetual times, by hereditary and paternal succession (as is premised) in the order of birth.

units.la: 5. Si verò præfatum Ludovicum modernum Comitem Palatinum Rheni & Bavariæ Ducem sine legitimis masculini sexus hæredibus laicis, de lumbis ejus directa linea genituræ descendentibus, non contigerit; extunc Principatus & Comitatus Palatinus Rheni, necnon Archidapiferia sacri Imperii, & jus, vox, dignitas, & potestas eligendi Romanorum Regem in Imperatorem promovendum, ad seniorem fratrē præfati Ludovici per veram paternalem lineam descendentem, & ad legitimos ejus hæredes masculini sexus, laicos duntaxat, devolvantur: ita videlicet, quod post obitum ejusdem fratris senioris primogenitus ejus filius, & post primogeniti obitum ejusdē primogeniti senior ex ordine genituræ, & sic deinceps ex seniore filio descendētes ex ordine genituræ semper senior: si verò primogenitus senioris fratris (ut præfertur) decesserit, masculini sexus, laicis duntaxat, heredibus nō relictis; extunc secundogenitus prædicti fratris senioris, & post obitum ejus secundogeniti filius senior laicus; & si secundogenitus sine heredibus legitimis masculini sexus laicis decesserit, tertiogenitus dicti fratris senior ejus filius laicus post mortem ipsius; & deinceps per talem modū directa linea genituræ descendentes ab eo, laici duntaxat, jus, vocem, dignitatem, & potestate eligendi Romanorum Regem in Imperatorem promovendū, & officium Archidapiferi cum omnibus & singulis dominiis, honoribus, juribus, privilegiis, dignitatibus, & pertinentiis, perpetuis temporibus obtinebunt per successionem hæreditariam & paternalem (ut præmittitur) ex ordine genituræ.
units.tr: 5. But if it shall not happen that the aforesaid Ludwig, the present Count Palatine of the Rhine and Duke of Bavaria, has male lay heirs descended from his loins in the direct line of birth, then the Principality and County Palatine of the Rhine, and likewise the Archstewardship of the Holy Empire, and the right, voice, dignity and power of electing the Roman King to be promoted to Emperor, shall devolve upon the senior brother of the aforesaid Ludwig, descended by the true paternal line, and upon his lawful male lay heirs only; so that after the death of the same senior brother, his firstborn son, and after the death of that firstborn, the senior in order of birth of the same firstborn, and so on, always the senior in order of birth among those descending from the senior son; but if the firstborn of the senior brother (as has been said) shall die leaving no male lay heirs, then the second-born of the said senior brother, and after his death the senior lay son of the second-born; and if the second-born shall die without male lawful lay heirs, then the third-born of the said senior brother, his senior lay son after his death; and thereafter, in this manner, those descending from him in the direct line of birth, laymen only, shall obtain the right, voice, dignity and power of electing the Roman King to be promoted to Emperor, and the office of Archsteward, with all and each of the lordships, honours, rights, privileges, dignities and appurtenances, in perpetual times, by hereditary and paternal succession (as is premised) in the order of birth.

units.la: {*} Nam pro prædicta forma Imperatoris Caroli IV. Literis. -6. Quibus omnibus non extantibus ad proximiorem hæredem secundum lineam patrem duntaxat laicum, seniorem Comitem Palatinum Rheni pro tempore, ac ejus hæredes secundum eundem modum superius expressatum, in perpetuum legitime devolventur.
units.tr: {*} For according to the aforesaid form of the letters of Emperor Charles IV. -6. If none of these survive, the succession and devolution shall pass lawfully and in perpetuity to the nearest heir in the line, the father being only lay, namely the senior Count Palatine of the Rhine for the time being, and his heirs in the same manner as set out above.

units.la: 7. Et talis successio & devolutio, ne in his committantur errores futuris temporibus, debet præmittitur) in omnibus præscriptis & singulis sine innovatione perpetuo inviolabiliter observari, taliter videlicet; quod si aliquem ex eis præmisso ab hac luce migrare contigerit, qui mascuhni heredes legitimos laicos post se relinquat debitæ patientes ætatis defectum; extunc senior frater, nepos & consanguineus proximior in linea genituræ, si frater non extiterit ejusdem defuncti, laicus duntaxat, dicti pupilli & juvenis, ad quem præscripta devolventur, de jure tutor esse debeat & tamdiu, donec debitam pertingat ætatem: Cui etiam juveni, quam citò ad ætatem debitam pervenerit, jus, vocem, dignitatem, & potestatem prædictæ electionis, ac omnia & singula ab eis dependentia, idem tutor sine difficultate & renitentia qualibet tenebitur & debebit protinus assignare. Ætas autem debitam in hoc casu, eligendi videlicet Romanorum Regem in Imperatorem promovendum, anno octavo annorum censeri volumus & haberi. In principatibus autem, Ducatibus, & dominiis temporalibus gubernandis, ætatem observandam decernimus, prout à Divis Romanorum Imperatoribus & Regibus nostris prædecessoribus est sancitum.
units.tr: 7. Such succession and devolution, so that errors may not be committed in future times, shall be observed inviolably and without innovation in all and each of the things prescribed above (as has been said), in this manner: if any one of those named above should happen to depart from this life, leaving legitimate male heirs who are lay and who lack the age required, then the senior brother, nephew, or nearest kinsman in the line of descent (if the deceased has no brother), who is lay only, shall by right be the guardian of the said minor and young man, to whom the aforesaid succession and devolution pass, and shall remain so until he reaches the required age. The same guardian shall also be bound and obliged, without difficulty or any resistance, to hand over immediately to that young man, as soon as he reaches the due age, the right, voice, dignity and power of the aforesaid election, and all and each of the things dependent on them. We wish and decree that the age in this case, namely for electing the Roman King to be promoted to Emperor, is to be counted and held as the eighth year of age. For governing principalities, duchies and temporal domains, we decree that the age is to be observed as has been sanctioned by the divine Roman Emperors and Kings, our predecessors.

units.la: 8. Porrò ne super jure, voce, dignitate, & potestate Electionis hujusmodi, necnon Principatibus & officio Archidapiferiæ & aliis prædictis ullo unquam tempore contingat scandala suscitari, vel attentari valeant novitates; de Imperiali plenitudine potestatis, & de certa nostra scientia, omnia & singula præmissa, prout in suis clausulis, membris, articulis, atque punctis superius designantur, auctorizamus: necnon omnia & singula privilegia, donationes & concessiones quaslibet per Divos Romanorum Reges & Imperatores, prædecessores nostros, & Nos, dicti Ludovici progenitoribus Comitibus Palatinis Rheni, & sibi quomodolibet factas, datas, & concessas, auctorizamus, approbamus, ratificamus, & tenore præsentium de certa scientia confirmamus; supplentes de præfatæ Imperialis plenitudine potestatis omnem defectum, si quis in præmissis aut eorum aliquo ex verborum defectu, sententiarum obscuritate, solennitatis omissione, seu alio quovis modo nunc & inantea reperiretur admissus.
units.tr: 8. Furthermore, so that at no time hereafter scandals may arise or attempts at innovation be made concerning the right, voice, dignity and power of such election, and likewise concerning the principalities, the office of Archdapifer, and the other matters mentioned above, we, from the fullness of imperial power and of our certain knowledge, authorize all and each of the things set out above, as they are designated in their clauses, members, articles and points; and we likewise authorize, approve, ratify, and by the tenor of these presents confirm from certain knowledge all and each of the privileges, donations and concessions of any kind granted, given and conceded by the divine Roman Kings and Emperors, our predecessors, and by us, to the aforesaid Lewis, the Counts Palatine of the Rhine, his ancestors, and to him in any way; supplying, from the fullness of the aforesaid imperial power, every defect, if any is found in the aforesaid matters, or in any part of them, whether through a defect of words, obscurity of sentences, omission of solemnity, or in any other way, now or henceforth.

units.la: 9. Nulli ergo penitus hominum liceat hanc nostræ pronunciationis, decreti, statuti, declarationis, sanctionis, innovationis, & investituræ, auctorizationis, approbationis, ratificationis, confirmationis, & defectum supplectionis paginam infringere, aut ei ausu temerario quomodolibet contraire; sub pœna mille marcarum auri purissimi, quas ab eo, qui contrafecerit, totiens, quotiens contrafactum fuerit, irremissibiliter exigi volumus, & earum medietatem Imperialis nostræ Cameræ fisco, reliquam verò partem injuriam passorum usibus applicari. † † præsentium sub Bulla Aurea typario nostræ Majestatis impressa testimonio literarum.
units.tr: 9. Let it therefore be entirely unlawful for any man to infringe this page of our pronouncement, decree, statute, declaration, sanction, innovation and investiture, authorization, approval, ratification, confirmation, and supplying of defects, or to contravene it in any way with rash daring; under penalty of one thousand marks of the purest gold, which we wish to be exacted without remission from whoever acts against it, as often as it is contravened, and of which one half is to be applied to the fiscus of our Imperial Chamber and the remaining part to the use of those who have been injured. In witness whereof, these presents are sealed with the Golden Bull impressed with the seal of our Majesty.

units.la: 10. Datum Basileæ anno Domini millesimo quadringentesimo tricesimo quarto, die octava mensis Martii, Regnorum nostrorum anno Ungariæ quadragesimo septimo, Romanorum vigesimo quarto, Bohemiæ quarto decimo, Imperii verò primo.
units.tr: 10. Given at Basel in the year of the Lord one thousand four hundred and thirty-four, on the eighth day of the month of March, in the forty-seventh year of our reign in Hungary, the twenty-fourth of our reign as Roman King, the fourteenth of our reign in Bohemia, and the first of our Empire.

units.la: Alterum exemplar sequentia habet ad hunc modum: Testes hujus rei sunt, Venerabiles, Werinherus Treverensis sacri Imperii per Galliam & regnum Arelatense, Archicancellarii, Archiepiscopi. Theodoricus Coloniensis per Italiam, Illustres, Rudolphus Dux Saxoniæ & Luneburgensis, sacri Imperii Archimarscalcus; Reinaldus Dux Juliacensis & Geldriæ; Fridericus Burggravius Noribergensis. Georgius Patavensis, Johannes Herbipolensis, & Rabanus Spirensis — Episcopi. Adolphus de Clivis, Emerich de Leiningen, Fridericus de Veldentz, Johannes de Catzenelbogen, Johannes de Werthem, & Thomas de Rineck — Comites & fideles.
