units.tr: The other copy has the following in this form: The witnesses of this matter are the Venerable Werner of Trier, Archchancellor of the holy Empire through Gaul and the kingdom of Arles, Archbishop; Theodoric of Cologne, through Italy, the Illustrious Rudolph, Duke of Saxony and Lüneburg, Archmarshal of the holy Empire; Reinald, Duke of Jülich and Guelders; Frederick, Burgrave of Nuremberg; George of Passau, John of Würzburg, and Raban of Speyer, bishops; Adolf of Cleves, Emerich of Leiningen, Frederick of Veldenz, John of Katzenelnbogen, John of Wertheim, and Thomas of Rineck, counts and faithful men.

units.la: Præsentium sub nostræ Majestatis Sigilli testimonio literarum. Datum Aquisgrani anno Domini MCCCCXIV. ipsa die coronationis nostræ, quæ fuit octava Novembris, Regnorum nostrorum anno Hungariæ vigesimo octavo, Romanorum verò Electionis quinto.
units.tr: In witness whereof these presents are sealed with the seal of our Majesty. Given at Aachen in the year of the Lord 1414, on the very day of our coronation, which was the eighth of November, in the twenty-eighth year of our reign in Hungary, and the fifth of our election as Roman King.

units.la: ALBERTI II. IMP. AUGU- STI, ET CAROLI VII. REGIS FRANCORUM PRAGMATICAE SANCTIONIS CAPITVLA.
units.tr: ALBERT II, EMPEROR AUGUSTUS, AND CHARLES VII, KING OF THE FRANKS: CHAPTERS OF THE PRAGMATIC SANCTION.

units.la: CAPIT. I.
units.tr: CHAPTER I.

units.la: ROmanus Pontifex quoq; decennio generalem Synodum loco, quem volet, posthac congregato. Si negligens erit, potestas esto Patribus id designandi.
units.tr: The Roman Pontiff shall also convene a general Synod every ten years, at whatever place he wishes. If he is negligent, the Fathers shall have the power to appoint it.

units.la: 2. Convocati Concilii locum, nisi necessum erit, Pontifex non mutato.
units.tr: 2. The Pontiff shall not change the place of a convened council unless it is necessary.

units.la: CAPIT. II.
units.tr: CHAPTER II.

units.la: BAsiliensis concionis authoritas, & ipsius constantia Decretorum perpetua esto, quae nemo unquam, nec ipse Romanus Pontifex, tollere, infirmare, aut transferre praesumito.
units.tr: The authority of the Council of Basel and the perpetual validity of its decrees shall stand. No one, not even the Roman Pontiff himself, shall presume to annul, weaken or transfer them.

units.la: CAPIT. III.
units.tr: CHAPTER III.

units.la: ROmanus Pontifex majores ecclesias, Metropoles scilicet atq; Episcopales Collegiatasq;, aut eas, quibus Abbates praficiuntur, & Ecclesiasticas dignitates, quae per electionem sibi deligere Rectorem consueverunt, nemini reservato: praeter eas, quae jure scripto vel Romani Principatus causa sibi permittuntur.
units.tr: The Roman Pontiff shall reserve to no one the major churches, namely the metropolitan, episcopal and collegiate churches, or those over which abbots are set, and the ecclesiastical dignities which have customarily chosen their rector by election, except those which are permitted to him by written law or by the cause of the Roman principate.

units.la: 2. Huic decreto non contravenito. si intercedet causa praeter legem faciendi, id Apostolicis rescriptis exprimito.
units.tr: 2. He shall not contravene this decree. If some cause beyond the law should intervene for acting otherwise, he shall state it in apostolic rescripts.

units.la: 3. Idq;, dum ad Pontificatum quippiam assumetur, se servaturum jurato.
units.tr: 3. And while he is being raised to the pontificate, he shall swear that he will observe this.

units.la: CAPIT. IV.
units.tr: CHAPTER IV.

units.la: ECclesia pastore destituta, ii, penes quos est eligendi potestas, die & loco definito conveniunto: peccatorum suorum confessionem agunto, & eucharistiam sumunto. Mox confidentes, praemisso jurejurando, non negligenter, non dolose, non timide, eum, qui gerendae dignitati sit idoneus, eligunto.
units.tr: When a church is left without a minister, those in whom the power of election lies shall assemble on a fixed day and at a fixed place. They shall make confession of their sins and partake of the Eucharist. Then, having first taken an oath, they shall elect, not negligently, not deceitfully, not timidly, the one who is fit to hold the office.

units.la: 2. Principibus fas non esto pro quopiam commendando molestus precibus, aut violenta comminatione, premere aut cogere electores.
units.tr: 2. It shall not be lawful for princes, by troublesome entreaties on behalf of someone's recommendation, or by violent threats, to press or compel the electors.

units.la: CAPIT. V.
units.tr: CHAPTER V.

units.la: ELectionis formam, & electi merita, confirmatores Praelati inquirunto.
units.tr: The confirming prelates shall inquire into the form of the election and the merits of the person elected.

units.la: 2. Scribae, Notarii, moderatum salarium accipiunto.
units.tr: 2. Scribes and notaries shall receive a moderate salary.

units.la: CAPIT. VI.
units.tr: CHAPTER VI.

units.la: ROmanus Pontifex, quem sanctitatis normam prae se ferre oportet, huic sanctioni nequaquam derogato. Si contremnet, & inde scandalum exurgat, ad subsequens universale Concilium deferatur.
units.tr: The Roman Pontiff, who ought to display the standard of holiness, shall in no way derogate from this sanction. If he despises it and scandal arises thence, the matter shall be referred to the next universal council.

units.la: CAPIT. VII.
units.tr: CHAPTER VII.

units.la: ELectiones tametsi pro canonum authoritate legitimae esse videbuntur, si inde aut ecclesia aut patria vel Respublica turbari formidabitur, eum hujusmodi electio ad Romanum Pontificem forte referatur, & ea diligenter examinata nulla dici merebitur, alteram electionem iis, quorum refert, indicito.
units.tr: Elections, although they may seem lawful by the authority of the canons, if it is feared that the church, the country or the commonwealth will be thrown into disorder by them, and such an election is perhaps referred to the Roman Pontiff and, after being carefully examined, deserves to be called null, he shall appoint another election for those whom it concerns.

units.la: 2. Electum vero confirmari aut benedici ab alio, quam ab eo, qui sine medio Electo superior, est, fas non esto.
units.tr: 2. It shall not be lawful for the elect to be confirmed or blessed by anyone other than the one who is superior to the elect without intermediary.

units.la: 3. Si in Pontificis Curia praesens electus erit, a Pontifice benedictionem, si volet, recipito: juramentum posteà suo superiori praestato. Secus qui faciet, centum aureorum multa eum castigato.
units.tr: 3. If the elect is present at the Pontiff's court, he may receive the blessing from the Pontiff if he wishes; afterwards he shall take the oath to his superior. Whoever does otherwise shall be punished with a fine of one hundred gold pieces.

units.la: CAPIT. VIII.
units.tr: CHAPTER VIII.

units.la: UNiversali Synodo, ejusq; definitionibus & decretis, omnis Catholicus, etiam Romanus Pontifex, eatenus obedito, quatenus fides & schismatum explodenda seditio postulat.
units.tr: Every Catholic, even the Roman Pontiff, shall obey a universal synod and its definitions and decrees, so far as faith and the suppression of the sedition of schism require.

units.la: CAPIT. IX.
units.tr: CHAPTER IX.

units.la: QUae Synodus sancto Spiritu autore vocata consedit, eam, sicuti Constantiane Contionis Patres diffiniere, a Christo Deo authoritatem protinus obtinere credito.
units.tr: You shall believe that a synod which has been called and convened with the Holy Spirit as its author obtains authority at once from Christ God, as the Fathers of the Council of Constance defined.

units.la: CAPIT. X.
units.tr: CHAPTER X.

units.la: ECclesiis Dei eos Sacerdotes & pastores praficito, qui doctrina sint & vita illustres, ut creditum sibi populum sollicite instituant, & Deo obedientem gratumq; reddant.
units.tr: Set over the churches of God those priests and ministers who are distinguished in teaching and in life, so that they may diligently instruct the people entrusted to them and make them obedient and pleasing to God.

units.la: CAPIT. XI.
units.tr: CHAPTER XI.

units.la: EXpectativis praeterea gratiis, unde plurima oriri mala constat, locum esse non finito.
units.tr: Let there be no place for expectative graces, from which, as is well known, very many evils arise.

units.la: CAPIT. XII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XII.

units.la: BEneficia, vivo eorum Rectore, nemini reservato. Cum autem administratore vacabunt, eorum, quibus conferte oportebit, mores & merita, graduati ne sint an secus, cognoscito.
units.tr: Benefices shall be reserved to no one while their rector is alive. When they fall vacant under an administrator, the morals and merits of those to whom they are to be conferred shall be examined, and whether they are graduates or not.

units.la: CAPIT. XIII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XIII.

units.la: DEcretum de Theologo, per quasq; Metropoles praebendando, ad Episcopales quoq; Ecclesias extendito, ut in illis praebenda Theologo conferatur, qui in aliqua generali Academia decennem literis operam navavit.
units.tr: The decree concerning the theologian, by which a prebend is provided through the metropolitan churches, shall be extended also to the episcopal churches, so that in those a prebend is conferred on a theologian who has devoted ten years of study to letters in some general academy.

units.la: 2. Beneficio donatus verbum Dei prædicato: & per quasq; hebdomadas semel atq; itci ü literas audire volentibus explanato. Negligenti quotidiana Ecclesiæ stipendia sustrahito.
units.tr: 2. The one endowed with the benefice shall preach the Word of God, and shall explain it once or twice a week, as often as the weeks allow, to those who wish to hear. From the one who is negligent, the daily stipends of the church shall be withheld.

units.la: CAPVT. XIV.
units.tr: CHAPTER XIV.

units.la: POrrò de iis, qui gradu alicujus disciplinæ provecti sunt, hunc ordinem servato.
units.tr: Moreover, concerning those who have advanced to the rank of some academic degree, observe the following order.

units.la: 2. Primum post hanc sanctionem vacuum possessore beneficium Doctori vel Licentiato vel Baccalario conferto.
units.tr: 2. First, after this decree, a benefice that has become vacant through the death of its holder shall be conferred upon a Doctor, a Licentiate, or a Bachelor.

units.la: 3. Duo deinceps, quæ Rectore carebunt, bene merentibus Clericis concedito.
units.tr: 3. Next, the two benefices which fall vacant thereafter shall be granted to deserving clerics.

units.la: 4. Quod his duobus successivum erit, illud Graduatus obtineto.
units.tr: 4. Whatever benefice shall be the next in succession after these two, a Graduate shall obtain.

units.la: 5. Igitur Scholastici gradu insignes sua nomina beneficiorum collatoribus, dum Quadragesima agitur, scripta quotannis tradunto.
units.tr: 5. Therefore, scholars distinguished by a degree shall hand in their names to the collators of benefices each year, while Lent is being observed.

units.la: 6. Beneficiorum præter hoc decretum collatio facta, inanis esto.
units.tr: 6. Any collation of benefices made contrary to this decree shall be void.

units.la: CAPVT. XV.
units.tr: CHAPTER XV.

units.la: ELocis, quæ ab Urbe quatuor dierum itinere distant, in jus vocandi Romam, nisi in majoribus causis, fas non esto.
units.tr: Those who live in places that are four days' journey from the City shall not be summoned to Rome to answer in law, except in greater causes.

units.la: CAPVT. XVI.
units.tr: CHAPTER XVI.

units.la: QVi damno aut injuria gravabitur, eum, qui proximus est superior, appellato, si tale est damnum, quod per ejus sententiam restitui possit. Alioquin si ad Romanam Ecclesiam judex per exceptionem pertinebit, causam definiendam ad eum, qui ejusdem regionis est, judicem (si metus abest) Pontifex committito.
units.tr: Whoever is burdened by loss or injury, let him appeal to the nearest superior, if the loss is of such a kind that it can be made good by that superior's judgment. Otherwise, if the case would come before the Roman Church by way of exception, let the Pontiff commit the decision of the case to a judge of the same region (provided there is no fear).

units.la: CAPVT. XVII.
units.tr: Chapter 17.

units.la: A Gravamine, aut interlocutione judicis secundò non provocato. Eum, qui frustra atq; inaniter tela latam sententiam appellat, quindecim florenis, præter cæteras litis impensas, mulctato.
units.tr: On a grievance, or an interlocutory decree of a judge, not appealed a second time. He who appeals in vain and to no purpose from a sentence once given, and is interdicted from appealing, shall be fined fifteen florins, besides the other costs of the suit.

units.la: CAPVT. XVIII.
units.tr: Chapter 18.

units.la: TRiennem alicujus beneficii & quietum possessorem non turbato, nisi hostilitate, metu, vel gravi impedimento tardatus eris, ne per triennium impetere potueris possidentem.
units.tr: If you have been prevented from disturbing the peaceful possessor of some benefice for three years, except by hostility, fear or serious hindrance, you may not sue the possessor within those three years.

units.la: CAPVT. XIX.
units.tr: CHAPTER XIX.

units.la: CArdinales viginti quattuor tantùm, divinâ & humanâ scientiâ eruditos, annorum triginta, boni nominis & generis legitimi, qui Reipublicæ Christianæ consulere possint, Pontifex de suorum fratrum consilio præficito.
units.tr: Let the Pope, with the advice of his brothers, appoint only twenty-four cardinals, learned in divine and human knowledge, aged thirty years, of good reputation and legitimate birth, who are able to look after the Christian Commonwealth.

units.la: CAPVT. XX.
units.tr: CHAPTER XX.

units.la: DE dignitatibus & beneficiis ecclesiasticis quibusvis, collatis aut conferendis, nihil prorsus, scilicet neq; annatam, neq; fructuum primitias, neq; (ut vulgò dicitur) deportum Pontifex exigito.
units.tr: Concerning ecclesiastical dignities and benefices of every kind, whether already conferred or yet to be conferred, the Pope shall demand absolutely nothing: neither annates, nor first fruits of the revenues, nor (as it is commonly called) the deport.

units.la: 2. Notariis & Scribis mercedem, qui beneficium recipit, solvito.
units.tr: 2. The fee of the notaries and scribes shall be paid by the one who receives the benefice.

units.la: 3. Hujus decreti prævaricatori pœnam symoniacis debitam infligito.
units.tr: 3. Upon any transgressor of this decree, the punishment due to simoniacs shall be inflicted.

units.la: 4. Nihil præterea juris aut tituli in beneficiis contra hanc prohibitionem impetratis sibi acquisitum intelligat.
units.tr: 4. Let him understand that no right or title whatever, acquired in benefices obtained contrary to this prohibition, shall accrue to him.

units.la: CAPVT. XXI.
units.tr: Chapter 21.

units.la: CLerici, qui ecclesiatum & divini cultus obsequiis deputantur, rem omnem divinam & Dei laudes sancte, distincte & graviter celebranto.
units.tr: Clerics who are appointed to the services of the churches and of divine worship shall celebrate every divine rite and the praises of God holily, distinctly and gravely.

units.la: 2. Ad Jesu nomen caput reverenter demittunto.
units.tr: 2. At the name of Jesus they shall bow the head reverently.

units.la: 3. Decanos & reliquos per ecclesias Præfectos hujus statuti prævaricatores castigato.
units.tr: 3. Deans and the other prefects over the churches shall punish those who transgress this statute.

units.la: CAPVT. XXII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXII.

units.la: COnsuetudinem, qua inductum est, eum, qui in aliqua horarum choro affuerit, omnium distributionum participem esse, tollito: idq; ad Decanos & Præpositos, qui suarum prætextu dignitatum rei divinæ non assunt, extendito.
units.tr: Abolish the custom, by which it has been introduced that whoever has been present in any choir of the canonical hours shares in all the distributions; and extend this to the deans and provosts who, on the pretext of their dignities, are not present at the divine service.

units.la: CAPVT. XXIII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXIII.

units.la: QVos noveris, dum res divina agitur, per ecclesiam, aut juxta illam deambulare, aut confabulari, totius diei, quo hoc fecerint, distributionibus privato.
units.tr: Those whom you find walking about through the church, or beside it, or chatting while the divine service is being conducted, deprive of the distributions for the whole day on which they did this.

units.la: 2. Iterum verò in hoc ipso delinquentes, unius mensis stipendiis mulctato.
units.tr: 2. But if they offend again in this same way, fine them the stipends of one month.

units.la: CAPVT. XXIV.
units.tr: Chapter 24.

units.la: TAbulam, ubi designentur ii, qui definitis hebdomadibus sua officia exequi debebunt, in choro appendito. Negligenti totius diei stipem denegato.
units.tr: Let a table be hung up in the choir, on which are shown those who are to perform their duties in the appointed weeks. Let the one who is negligent be denied the stipend for the whole day.

units.la: CAPVT. XXV.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXV.

units.la: FIdei Symbolum non truncato, sed ad verbum absolutè decantato.
units.tr: The Creed of faith to be sung entire, not truncated, but absolutely word for word.

units.la: CAPVT. XXVI.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXVI.

units.la: CAmoenas vulgi in ecclesia canere Laicos prohibeto.
units.tr: Forbid the laity to sing the vulgar songs in church.

units.la: CAPVT. XXVII.
units.tr: Chapter 27.

units.la: REm divinam, quam Missam appellamus, sine ministro nunquam celebrato. Dum eam facis, vocem exaltato, quæ à circumstantibus exaudiri possit. Secus agentem corripito.
units.tr: Never celebrate the divine rite, which we call the Mass, without a minister. When you perform it, raise your voice so that it can be heard by those standing around. Rebuke anyone who acts otherwise.

units.la: CAPVT. XXVIII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXVIII.

units.la: CAnonicos, qui se creditoribus obnoxios ita constituunt, ut si statuto die debito se non absolverint, junt, interdicto rei divinæ cohibeantur, à stipendiis ecclesiæ toto trimestri abstinento: nec quicquam inde, quamdiu divinis abstinebunt, percipiunto.
units.tr: Canons who so arrange their affairs with creditors that, if they have not settled their debts on the appointed day, [they are to be restrained from divine service by interdict], and are to abstain from the stipends of the church for the whole quarter. Nor are they to receive anything from them for as long as they abstain from divine offices.

units.la: CAPIT. XXIX.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXIX.

units.la: Solennibus diebus, dum major Missa fieri debet, Capitulum non cogito; per integram alioquin hebdomadam transgressores quotidiana stipe privato.
units.tr: On solemn days, when the High Mass ought to be celebrated, do not convene the chapter. Otherwise, deprive the offenders of their daily allowance for the whole week.

units.la: CAPIT. XXX.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXX.

units.la: Spectacula, ludos, comessationes, choreas, nundinationes, ludibria, & larvatas personas incedere, ab ecclesia & sacris locis arceto. Contemptorem Clerum trimestri proventu abstinere jubeto: reliquos censura ecclesiastica cohibeto.
units.tr: Keep out of the church and sacred places shows, games, revelries, dances, fairs, mockeries, and people going about in masks. Order the clergy who despise this to abstain from their revenue for a quarter; restrain the rest by ecclesiastical censure.

units.la: CAPIT. XXXI.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXXI.

units.la: Clerico cujusvis status, concubinam foventi, à secunda hujus sanctionis promulgatione non resipiscenti, beneficiorum suorum perceptione menses tres interdicito, & eos fructus in Ecclesiarum, unde percipiuntur, utilitatem impendito.
units.tr: To any cleric of whatever rank who keeps a concubine and does not repent after the second promulgation of this decree, forbid the receipt of his benefices for three months, and let those revenues be spent on the benefit of the churches from which they are drawn.

units.la: 1. Hanc autem constitutionem in Synodis & Capitulis promulgari quotannis imperato.
units.tr: 1. Order that this constitution be promulgated in synods and chapters every year.

units.la: 3. Nec minus Laicos admoneto, nullam, praeter legitimam uxorem, turpi copula contingere.
units.tr: 3. Likewise, admonish laymen that none of them is to have intercourse with anyone except a lawful wife.

units.la: CAPIT. XXXII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXXII.

units.la: Excommunicatos ante latam sententiam & revera denunciatam non vitato, nisi tam notoria excommunicatio erit, quae non valeat ignorari.
units.tr: Do not shun those excommunicated before the sentence has been pronounced and really announced, unless the excommunication is so notorious that it cannot be ignored.

units.la: CAPIT. XXXIII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXXIII.

units.la: Nulli omnino genti, Communitati vel loco sacris interdicito, nisi per semet, aut per privatos, aut Officiales, id est, per suos Magistratus, culpam admisit. Iniquum liquidem est, ob uniuscujusque privati hominis delictum ferire insontes.
units.tr: Do not impose an interdict on any people, community, or place at all from sacred things, unless the fault has been committed by themselves, or by private persons, or by officials, that is, by their own magistrates. For it is plainly unjust to strike the innocent on account of the crime of any private individual.

units.la: CAPIT. XXXIV.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXXIV.

units.la: Nullius literis, quibus quempiam beneficio aut suo jure se abdicasse narratur, nisi testibus aut fideli documento id factum esse constet, credito.
units.tr: Do not believe anyone's letter by which someone is said to have renounced a benefice or his own right, unless it is established that this was done by witnesses or by a trustworthy document.

units.la: Haec Legum Capitula Patres Concilii apud Basileam legitimè congregati, communi omnium sententiâ ritè digesta, sanxerunt; eademque ab ALBERTO II. Imperatore Romanorum, Electoribus Imperii, & CAROLO VII. Rege Francorum admitti, missis ejus rei causa Oratoribus in Hungariam, Moguntiam, & Galliam, petierunt. Et Imperator quidem atque Electores ea in Comitiis Moguntiae celebratis sub praesitito inter se juramento acceptate & conservare promiserunt. CAROLUS etiam Rex Francorum, indicto apud Bituriges Concilio Pragmaticam, quam vocant, Sanctionem tulit: eamque in Parlamenti Senatu promulgari mandavit, Anno Domini M CCCC XXXVIII. Nonis Julii.
units.tr: The Fathers of the Council of Basel, lawfully assembled, with the common consent of all, duly drew up and enacted these chapters of law. They asked that the same be admitted by Albert II, Emperor of the Romans, the Electors of the Empire, and Charles VII, King of the French, sending envoys for this purpose to Hungary, Mainz, and France. And the Emperor indeed, and the Electors, at the Diet celebrated at Mainz, promised to accept and observe them, having sworn an oath among themselves beforehand. King Charles of the French also, having summoned a council at Bourges, enacted what they call the Pragmatic Sanction, and ordered it to be promulgated in the Senate of Parliament, in the year of the Lord 1438, on the Nones of July.

units.la: FRIDERICI III. IMP. AUG. AVISAMENTA
units.tr: Frederick III, Emperor Augustus: Advices

units.la: Quae tempore Basiliensis Concilii à Statibus Imperii Moguntiae in publi- co Conventu fuere deliberata.
units.tr: What was deliberated by the Estates of the Empire at the public assembly at Mainz during the time of the Council of Basel.

units.la: CAPIT. I.
units.tr: CHAPTER I.

units.la: ANNO millesimo quadringentesimo quadragesimo, Moguntiae in materia declarationis animorum super facto dissensionis in Ecclesia Dei exortae, per Dominos Electores faciendā, & de cautione faciendā Nationi Germanicae, de sublatione gravaminum ejusdem Nationis, fuit avisatum in dieta inibi tenta circa festum Purificationis Mariae Virginis, quod cuicunque parti adhaerendum esset, ante omnia providere deberet, ne authoritas Conciliorum generalium infirmetur, & Gravamina, quae dudum praefatae Nationi fuerunt illata, tollantur è medio, & contra ea caveatur in futurum.
units.tr: In the year 1440, at Mainz, it was advised at the diet held there around the feast of the Purification of the Virgin Mary, concerning the declaration of minds, to be made by the lords Electors, on the matter of the division that has arisen in the Church of God, and concerning the security to be given to the German Nation and the removal of the grievances of that same Nation, that whichever party one is to adhere to, one must first of all provide that the authority of the general Councils is not weakened, that the grievances long since inflicted on the aforesaid Nation are removed, and that safeguards are taken against them in the future.

units.la: CAPIT. II.
units.tr: CHAPTER II.

units.la: IN primis, quia Basileae hucusque non est nominatus aliquis locus pro futuro Concilio celebrando, juxta formam constitutionis frequens, ita quod jam [non] pendeat terminus alicujus Concilii; expedit, quòd ille, cui facienda est haec adhaesio, omnes & singulas constitutiones olim in Constantiensi Concilio super authoritate, honore, & reverentia sacrorum generalium Conciliorum promulgatas approbet, recipiat, & providear; & mox in eisdem literis Bullaris, conficiendis super praemissis promittat seu polliceatur, se Oecumenicum vel saltem generale Concilium indicere velle, quantocyus id fieri poterit, in loco rebus gerendis accommodo, ubi personaliter, si poterit; alioquin si nequeat, per Legatos Apostolicos plena potestate fulcitos, Concilium ipsum prosequatur cum effectu. Promittit insuper, operam se daturum, quòd in hujusmodi celebrando Concilio per Nationes procedatur, sicut in prioribus Conciliis reperitur observatum. 2. Et præmissa omnia videntur honestè & justè peti posse. Nam per hoc vetitas prodibit in lucem; & illi, qui ex alia parte, seu sub alia obedientia remanebunt, poterunt aptissimè nobis confoliditi. Papa etiam cui adhærebitur, ex hoc authoritatem suam & Apostolicæ Sedis augebit & confirmabit, quando videbitur ab omnibus synceritas sua in factis Ecclesiæ Dei.
units.tr: First, since up to now no place has been named at Basel for the future Council to be held, in accordance with the customary form, so that the term of some Council no longer hangs in doubt, it is expedient that he to whom this adherence is to be made should approve, accept and provide for all and each of the constitutions once promulgated at the Council of Constance concerning the authority, honour and reverence of the sacred general Councils; and immediately in the Bull letters to be drawn up on these matters he should promise or pledge that he will wish to summon an Ecumenical, or at least a general, Council, as quickly as it can be done, in a place suitable for conducting affairs, where he himself will be present if he can; otherwise, if he cannot, he should pursue the Council effectively through Apostolic Legates endowed with full power. He further promises that he will take care that in celebrating such a Council proceedings are conducted by nations, as is observed in earlier Councils. 2. All the foregoing seems to be justly and honourably sought. For through this the truth will come to light; and those who remain on the other side, or under the other obedience, will be able to be most aptly reconciled to us. The Pope to whom one adheres will also, by this, increase and confirm his authority and that of the Apostolic See, when his sincerity in the affairs of the Church of God is seen by all.

units.la: CAPIT. III.
units.tr: CHAPTER III.

units.la: ITem de præsenti non potest de loco vel de tempore specificè tractari, neque poterit hoc alicujus arbitrio committi, nec alü fortassis indignentur, quali non fit habita ratio commoditatis eorum, quantum ad situm vel aliam aptitudinem loci. & ideò non poterit negotium, quo ad hoc, modis specificari.
units.tr: Likewise, for the present, nothing can be treated specifically concerning place or time, nor can this be committed to anyone's discretion; others perhaps would be indignant, since account would not be taken of their convenience as regards the site or other suitability of the place. And therefore the business cannot be specified in this respect in any way.

units.la: CAPIT. IV.
units.tr: CHAPTER IV.

units.la: DEinde quo ad relevamen gravaminum, avisatum est, quòd cùm dicta Natio plus cæteris nationibus ab Ecclesia Romana sit honoranda, propter auxilia, quæ Ecclesiæ Romanæ multiplicater præstitit, ac propter Imperium Romanum, cujus vis & potestas in eo consistit, quòd Ecclesia Romanam multis dotibus exornavit; ut illi, cui facienda est adhæsio, eidem Nationi in retributionem meritorum suorum pro se & successoribus sanctaque Sede Apostolica, de consensu Cardinalium, propria etiam manuum suarum subscriptione subsequente constituat, ordinet, & in singulare privilegium concedat, per se & successores suos perpetuis temporibus inconcusè servandum, &c. ut inserius seriatim annotatur.
units.tr: Next, as regards the relief of grievances, it has been advised that, since the said Nation is to be honoured above the other nations by the Roman Church, on account of the aid which it has repeatedly given to the Roman Church, and on account of the Roman Empire, whose strength and power consist in this, that it has adorned the Roman Church with many gifts, he to whom adherence is to be made should, in return for the merits of that Nation, establish, ordain and grant to the same Nation, for himself and his successors and the Holy Apostolic See, with the consent of the Cardinals and with his own hand subscribing, a singular privilege, to be observed unshaken by himself and his successors in perpetual times, etc., as is noted below in order.

units.la: CAPIT. V.
units.tr: CHAPTER V.

units.la: IN primis siquidem cassef, annullet, & irriter omnes & singulas reservationes, tam generales quàm speciales sive particulares Ecclesiarum Metropolitanorum, Cathedralium, Collegiatarum, Monasteriorum, dignitatum & beneficiorum Ecclesiasticorum quorumcumque, quibus pro electione provideri consuevit, sive per extravagantes Ad regimen, & Execrabilis, aut per regulas Cancellariæ, seu quascunque alias constitutiones aut ordinationes introductæ sint, reservationibus in Corpore juris clausis duntaxat exceptis. Et quòd hujusmodi beneficia in corpore juris clausa Romanus Pontisex infra unius mensis spacium, ab ipsius vacationis noticia computandum, conferre teneatur: deinde is, cui collatio facta fuerit, eam infra tres menses continuos ordinariè teneatur insinuare. Si verò collatio vel insinuatio amplius retardetur. Ordinarii perinde habeant disponere, acsi nulla reservatio præcessisset.
units.tr: First, then, he shall quash, annul and render void all and each of the reservations, whether general or special or particular, of the Metropolitan, Cathedral and Collegiate churches, monasteries, dignities and ecclesiastical benefices of whatever kind, which were customarily provided for by election, whether they have been introduced by the extravagants Ad regimen and Execrabilis, or by the rules of the Chancery, or by any other constitutions or ordinances, excepting only the reservations enclosed in the Corpus Juris. And that the Roman Pontiff is bound to confer such benefices enclosed in the Corpus Juris within the space of one month, to be reckoned from the notice of their vacancy; then he to whom the collation has been made is ordinarily bound to insinuate it within three continuous months. But if the collation or insinuation is delayed any further, the Ordinaries shall have authority to dispose just as if no reservation had preceded.

units.la: 2. Beneficiis autem & dignitatibus electivis in corpore juris non reservatis, juxta dispositionem juris communis debitè provideatur, postulationibus etiam in dispositione juris communis manentibus.
units.tr: 2. But for benefices and dignities that are elective and not reserved in the Corpus Juris, provision shall be duly made according to the disposition of the common law, with postulations also remaining under the disposition of the common law.

units.la: CAPIT. VI.
units.tr: CHAPTER VI.

units.la: ITem si Episcopus aut Abbas fuerit eligendus, conveniant eligentes, auditurì missam Spiritus Sancti: & confessi & contriti, susceptaeucharistia, ad eligendum ingrediantur. Et primò jurabunt in manibus Præsidentis Capituli, & rursus Præsidens in manibus immediatè sequentis, sub hac forma: Ego N. juro & promitto omnipotenti Deo, & tali Sancto vel Sanctæ, sub cujus vocabulo dedicata est ecclesia, eum eligere, quem credo futurum Ecclesiæ in spiritualibus & temporalibus utiliorem; & non illi vocem dare, quam verisimiliter scivero promissione aut datione alicujus rei temporalis, seu prece per se vel alium interposita, aut alia quacunque intercunque directè vel indirectè pro se electionem procurare.
units.tr: Likewise, if a Bishop or Abbot is to be elected, let the electors assemble, having heard the Mass of the Holy Spirit; and, confessed and contrite, having received the Eucharist, let them enter for the election. And first they shall swear into the hands of the President of the Chapter, and in turn the President into the hands of the one immediately following, in this form: I, N., swear and promise to almighty God, and to such Saint, under whose name the church is dedicated, that I will elect him whom I believe will be more useful to the Church in spiritual and temporal matters; and that I will not give my vote to one whom I shall probably know to be procuring the election for himself, directly or indirectly, by promise or gift of any temporal thing, or by prayer put forward by himself or another, or by any other means whatever.

units.la: 2. Item juramentum præstet, confiteaturque & communicet, qui constituit procuratorem ad eligendum certam personam: necnon & procurator constitui potest, quòd etiam juramentum præstetur ab iis, in quos continget superelectione futuri * Episcopi vel Abbatis fieri compromissum: qui etiam confiteri & communicare teneantur. Quod si prædicta non fecerint, pro illa vice eligendi sunt ipso jure potestate privati.
units.tr: 2. Likewise, he who appoints a proxy to elect a certain person shall swear, confess and communicate; and a proxy may also be appointed, so that the oath is likewise taken by those on whom a compromise for the election of the future * Bishop or Abbot may fall; they too are bound to confess and communicate. But if they have not done the aforesaid, they are on that occasion deprived, by the law itself, of the power to elect.

units.la: 3. In inferioribus verò dignitatibus eligentes, ad confessionem & communionem nullatenus sint astricti, sed in aliis formam superiùs traditam observare teneantur.
units.tr: 3. In the lower dignities, however, the electors are in no way bound to confession and communion, but are bound to observe the form set out above in other respects.

units.la: 4. Finita autem electione, decretum electionis immediatè superiori, ad quem jus pertinet confirmandi, præsentetur, qui in electionis negocio procedat, formam electionis, & electi merita, omnesque circumstantias diligenter examinaturus, ita ut si electio confirmanda sit vel infirmanda, judicialiter confirmetur vel infirmetur.
units.tr: 4. When the election is finished, the decree of election is to be presented to the immediately superior person, to whom the right of confirmation belongs, who shall proceed in the business of the election, diligently examining the form of the election, the merits of the elected and all the circumstances, so that if the election is to be confirmed or annulled, it is confirmed or annulled judicially.

units.la: 5. Confirmatores autem ratione confirmationis nihil exigere, sed neque etiam sponte oblata recipere ratione confirmationis, sub nomine subventionis, subsidii, gratitudinis, aut alio quoisco quisito colore, prætextu consuetudinis, privilegii, superioritatis, aut reverentiæ, aut alia quavis ratione præsumant.
units.tr: 5. Moreover, confirmers shall demand nothing on account of confirmation, nor presume to receive, on account of confirmation, anything even voluntarily offered, under the name of help, subsidy, gratitude, or under any other pretext whatever, on the pretext of custom, privilege, superiority or reverence, or on any other ground.

units.la: 6. Notariis autem cæterisque ministris emolumentum moderatum taxetur, laborum & operarum habito respectu, non autem Prælaturæ valore.
units.tr: 6. For notaries and other officials, a moderate fee shall be fixed, with regard to their labours and services, not with regard to the value of the prelacy.

units.la: 7. Confirmationes aliter factæ sint ipso jure nullæ, & confirmantes ipsi confirmandi potestate sint ea vice privati.
units.tr: 7. Confirmations made otherwise are null and void by law, and those confirming have, for that occasion, no more power than private persons.

units.la: 8. Electiones autem & confirmationes (ut præmittitur) factæ, neque per Papam aut Sedem Apostol.
units.tr: 8. Elections and confirmations made (as has been set out above) neither by the Pope or the Apostolic See

units.la: Epitom. Pragm.Sanct. cap.1. §.6.
units.tr: Epitom. Pragm. Sanct. cap. 1. §. 6.

units.la: * al.Archiepiscopi. Apo stolicam, seu illius aut alia quavis authoritate infringi valeant, seu quomodolibet impediri, nisi forte in perturbationem Ecclesiæ aut privatæ seu publicæ utilitatis electio aliqua vergere timeatur. Quo casu Summus Pontifex, cum ad ipsum confirmatio delata fuerit, si talem urgentissimam causam sibi esse agnoverit, ea prius mature discussa, & parte plenè defensa, accedendo ratione Ecclesiæ Cardinalium vel majoris partis subscriptione, causam hujusmodi veram sufficientemque fore attestantur, tali electione rejecta, ad Capitulum vel Conventum remittat, ut infra competens tempus, juxta loci distantiam, ad aliam, ex qua talia evenire non formidentur, electionem procedant.
units.tr: * Other reading: Archbishops. Apostolic, or be invalidated by that authority or by any other authority whatever, or be impeded in any way, unless perhaps some election is feared to tend toward the disturbance of the Church or to the private or public harm. In that case, when the confirmation has been referred to the Supreme Pontiff, if he has acknowledged that there is such a very urgent cause, the matter having first been maturely examined and the party fully heard, they attest, with the signature of the Cardinals of the Church or of the greater part of them, that the cause of this kind is true and sufficient; the Pontiff, having rejected such an election, shall send the matter back to the chapter or convent, so that within a competent time, according to the distance of the place, they may proceed to another election, from which such things are not to be feared.

units.la: 9. Omni autem casu, quo electio per mediatum Superiorem fuerit confirmanda, remittatur consecrandus aut benedicendus ad suum Superiorem immediatum, nec præsens fuerit in Romana Curia. Quo casu post benedictionem aut consecrationem similiter remittatur, immediato Superiori debitum juramentum præstiturus.
units.tr: 9. In every case in which an election is to be confirmed by a mediate superior, the person to be consecrated or blessed shall be sent back to his immediate superior, provided he is not present in the Roman Curia. In that case, after the blessing or consecration, he shall likewise be sent back, there to take the due oath to his immediate superior.

units.la: CAPIT. VII.
units.tr: CHAPTER VII.

units.la: Rursus avifatum est, quòd cùm ex ineffrenato gratiarum expectativarum Concursu, & antelatione praerogativis à principio vocationis beneficiorum sub gratiis hujusmodi cadentium scri non potest, & ex hoc Ordinarius, subtractionem ministerii sui molestè ferentibus, intrusionis datur occasio, ex quo lites innumeræ suscitantur: avifatum, inquam, est, quòd ille, cui adhæsio sit facienda, omnes gratiis expectativas ac reservationes particulares de beneficiis vacaturis in nostra Natione tellat, & de cætero non concedat, nisi pro toto tempore Pontificatus sui in qualibet collatione, in qua decem fuerint beneficia, de uno; ubi quinquaginta, de duobus duntaxat habeat disponere: in quibus dispositionibus indigena alienigenæ præferatur.
units.tr: It has further been announced that, because of the unbridled rush of expectative graces, and the priority of privileges (which, from the beginning of a benefice's vacancy, cannot be put in writing for those falling under such graces), the Ordinary is given an occasion for intrusion, to the annoyance of those who resent the withdrawal of his ministry, and from this countless lawsuits arise. It is announced, I say, that he to whom adhesion is to be given shall remove all expectative graces and particular reservations of benefices due to become vacant in our Nation, and shall not grant them henceforth, except for the whole time of his pontificate: in each collation in which there are ten benefices, he may dispose of one; where there are fifty, of two only. In these dispositions a native shall be preferred to a foreigner.

units.la: CAPIT. VIII.
units.tr: CHAPTER VIII.

units.la: Item ut nullum beneficium nostræ Nationis exteris personis commendetur, aut de ipso pensio concedatur, sine assensu Ordinarii.
units.tr: Likewise, no benefice of our Nation shall be committed to foreign persons, nor shall a pension be granted from it, without the consent of the Ordinary.

units.la: CAPIT. IX.
units.tr: CHAPTER IX.

units.la: Item ut quæstio de una præbenda in qualibet Ecclesia Metropolitana Theologo assignanda, etiam ad Cathedrales Ecclesias nostræ Nationis extendatur, ut collationes præbendarum hujusmodi teneantur Canonicatu, & præbendam Magistro, Licentiato aut Baccalaureo formato in Theologia, qui per decennium in Universitate privilegiata studuerit, & onus residentiæ ac lectura & prædicationis subire voluerit: quique bis vel semel ad minus per singulas hebdomadas, cessante legitimo impedimento, legat. Quod si neglexerit, arbitratu Capituli in subtractione distributionum totius hebdomadæ puniatur: & si residentiam deseruerit, de alio providearur. Nil tamen perdat, si absens fuerit à divinis.
units.tr: Likewise, the rule concerning one prebend, to be assigned to a theologian in each Metropolitan Church, shall be extended also to the cathedral churches of our Nation, so that the collations of such prebends shall be bound to a canonry, and the prebend shall be given to a Master, Licentiate or Bachelor formed in Theology, who has studied for ten years in a privileged University, and who is willing to undertake the burden of residence, reading and preaching, and who reads twice, or at least once, each week, unless a lawful impediment intervenes. If he neglects this, he shall be punished, at the discretion of the Chapter, by withholding the distributions of the whole week; and if he deserts his residence, another shall be provided. Yet he shall lose nothing if he is absent from the divine services.

units.la: 1. Porrò post collatam, ut præfertur, hujusmodi præbendam, duæ immediatè vacantes libere conferantur: tertia verò postea vacans, & deinceps semper post duas liberè collatas tertia conferatur Magistro aut Licentiato seu Baccalaureo formato in Theologia, qui per decennium in aliqua Universitate privilegiata studuerit; Doctori seu Licentiato in altero Jurium seu Medicina, qui per septem annos: vel in utroque aut altero Jurium Baccalaureo, qui per triennium, si Nobilis ex utroque parente, & ex antiquo genere; aliàs autem per quinquennium, in aliqua Universitate privilegiata studium suum fecerit: qui de gradibus, tempore, & nobilitate supradictis fidem facere tenentur Collatori per legitima documenta.
units.tr: 1. Moreover, after such a prebend has been conferred as stated above, the next two that fall vacant shall be conferred freely. The third that falls vacant afterwards, and thereafter always the third after two freely conferred, shall be given to a Master, Licentiate or Bachelor formed in Theology, who has studied for ten years in some privileged University; to a Doctor or Licentiate in the other law or in Medicine, who has studied for seven years; or to a Bachelor in both or one of the laws, who has studied for three years if he is noble on both sides of his parentage and of ancient stock, otherwise for five years, in some privileged University. These persons are bound to prove to the Collator, by lawful documents, their degrees, time of study and nobility as stated above.

units.la: 3. Hoc etiam in dignitatibus non electivis, personatibus, administrationibus, & officiis distributionum Ecclesiarum observetur.
units.tr: 3. This shall also be observed in non-elective dignities, personages, administrations and offices of the distributions of the Churches.

units.la: 4. Et qui duas præbendas Cathedrales obtinuerit, aut aliàs unum vel plura beneficia in quo vel altero residente ab illo vel ab utroque in omnibus obventionibus ducentorum florenorum Camerae valorem habere valeat, inter personas prædictas non numeretur.
units.tr: 4. And he who holds two cathedral prebends, or otherwise one or more benefices in which he is resident, from one or both of which he may have an income in all revenues of the value of two hundred florins of the Chamber, shall not be counted among the aforesaid persons.

units.la: 5. Item in Ecclesiis Parochialibus oppidorum muratorum instituantur personæ, quæ ad minus per tres annos in Theologia, vel altero Jurium, Magister in artibus, in aliqua Universitate contiguè studentes, si poterint inveniri.
units.tr: 5. Likewise, in the parish churches of walled towns, persons shall be appointed who, if they can be found, have been studying continuously for at least three years in Theology or in one of the laws, or are Masters of Arts, in some University.

units.la: 6. Item ut quolibet anno in Quadragesima qualificati sua nomina Collatoribus supradictis exhibeant: alioquin dispositio aliter facta non irritetur.
units.tr: 6. Likewise, each year in Lent the qualified persons shall present their names to the aforesaid Collators; otherwise a disposition made otherwise shall not be annulled.

units.la: 7. Sin autem tales reperti fuerint, dispositio per quæcunque, etiamsi Cardinalatus, Patriarchalis, Pontificalis, aut alterius cujuscunque dignitatis, aliter, quàm præmittitur, facta, eo ipso irrita sit & inanis: collatio verò, seu provisio, seu quævis alia dispositio ad superiorem proximum devolvatur, qui personæ tali habeat providere. Quod si non fecerit, ad alium superiorem proximum gradatim usque ad Summum Pontificem devolvatur.
units.tr: 7. But if such persons are found, any disposition made otherwise than stated above, by whomsoever it is made, even if of a Cardinal, Patriarch, Pontiff, or any other dignity whatever, shall for that very reason be void and null. The collation, or provision, or any other disposition, shall devolve to the next superior, who is to provide for such a person. If he does not do so, it shall devolve step by step to the next superior, up to the Supreme Pontiff.

units.la: 8. In Ecclesiis autem, in quibus Illustres, aut Militares, seu certo modo genituræ procreati duntaxat recipi consuevetunt, quod supra de literatis aut studiosis personis est expressum, ita intelligatur, si personæ, modo præmisso qualificatæ, inter hujusmodi Nobiles seu Generosos reperiri possunt, qui etiam nomina sua Collatoribus habeant exhibere. Quo cessante, provisio aliter facta irritetur.
units.tr: 8. In those churches, however, in which only the illustrious, or the military, or those born of a certain lineage are customarily received, what has been expressed above concerning learned or studious persons shall be understood thus: if persons qualified in the manner stated above can be found among such nobles or gentlemen, they shall also be required to present their names to the Collators. If this does not happen, a provision made otherwise shall be annulled.

units.la: CAPIT. X.
units.tr: CHAPTER X.

units.la: Item ne Romanus Pontifex, aut quivis alius Ecclesiasticus vel Secularis, pro confirmatione, electione, admissione, postulatione, aut collatione, provisione, praesentatione, seu qualibet alia dispositione circa Ecclesiastica beneficia, secularia vel regularia, & pertinentia ad ea, nec non ordinibus, benedictione, ac pallio, de caetero quicquam ante vel post exigat, ratione literarum pro ipsorum labore competentium salario solvendum.
units.tr: Likewise, the Roman Pontiff, or any other ecclesiastic or secular person, shall not henceforth demand or receive anything, before or after, for confirmation, election, admission, postulation, collation, provision, presentation, or any other disposition concerning ecclesiastical benefices, secular or regular, and pertaining to them, nor for orders, blessing, or the pallium, by way of a fee for letters, as a salary due for their labour.

units.la: 2. Si quis autem exigendo, dando, vel promittendo contrarie praesumpserit, Simoniae poenam ipso facto incurrat, & in beneficio taliter obtento nullum jus nec titulum acquirat. Obligationes quoque, promissiones, censuras & mandata, & quicquid contra judicium hujusmodi statuunt, quacunque etiam Apostolica authoritate contigerit attentari, nullius sint roboris vel momenti.
units.tr: 2. If anyone presumes to act contrary to this by demanding, giving, or promising, he shall incur the penalty of simony by the very fact, and shall acquire no right or title in a benefice so obtained. Likewise, obligations, promises, censures and mandates, and whatever is decreed contrary to such a judgment, shall be of no force or validity, even if attempted by apostolic authority.

units.la: 3. Caveatur, ne illa, quae tempore receptionis beneficiandorum pro fabrica, ornamentis Ecclesiae, vel divini cultus decore dare consueverunt, in principio receptionis per hoc aboleantur: dummodo non ad personarum, sed Ecclesiarum utilitatem convertantur.
units.tr: 3. Care shall be taken that those payments which, at the time of receiving beneficiaries, are customarily given for the building fabric, the furnishings of the Church, or the decoration of divine worship, are not abolished at the outset by this: provided they are applied to the benefit of the churches and not of individuals.

units.la: CAPIT. XI.
units.tr: Chapter 11.

units.la: Item quod is, cui fiat adhaesio, nullam impositionem vel exactionem faciat in natione nostra, pro confirmatione provisionis sibi olim in Concilio Basiliensi promissae, nisi in alio generali Concilio de expresso consensu nationis.
units.tr: Likewise, that the one to whom adherence is given shall not impose or exact anything in our nation, for the confirmation of a provision once promised to him at the Council of Basel, unless at another general council and with the express consent of the nation.

units.la: CAPIT. XII.
units.tr: Chapter 12.

units.la: Item quod in partibus nostrae Nationis, quae ultra quatuor dietas a curia distant, omnes causae, majoribus necnon electionum Ecclesiarum Sedi Apostolicae immediate subjectarum exceptis, in partibus terminentur.
units.tr: Likewise, that in the parts of our nation which lie more than four diets distant from the court, all causes be settled in those parts, except the greater causes and the causes concerning elections of churches immediately subject to the Apostolic See.

units.la: CAPIT. XIII.
units.tr: CAPUT XIII.

units.la: Item ne gravati per saltum, etiam ad Romanum Pontificem, omisso medio, sed ad immediatum Superiorem duntaxat, nec a gravamine in quacunque instantia ante diffinitivam appellent, nisi gravamen ipsum in diffinitiva reparari nequiret. tunc enim ad Superiorem immediatum semel tantum liceat appellare. Quae appellatio si frivola fuerit, appellans appellato ultra expensas in quindecim florenis auri de camera condemnetur. {*}
units.tr: Likewise, those who are aggrieved shall not appeal by skipping over the intermediate instance, even to the Roman Pontiff, but only to the immediate superior; nor shall they appeal from a grievance in any instance before the final judgment, unless the grievance itself could not be repaired in the final judgment. For then an appeal may be made to the immediate superior only once. If that appeal is frivolous, the appellant shall be condemned to pay the costs of the appellee and, in addition, fifteen gold florins to the chamber.

units.la: CAPIT. XIV.
units.tr: Chapter XIV.

units.la: Item ne possessores non violenti sed colorato titulo beneficia proximo triennio hactenus possidentes, vel qui in futurum possidebunt, neque in petitorio neque in possessorio etiam ratione juris noviter quaesiti molestentur, nisi actor legitime impeditus, & de hoc protestatus juxta Concilium Wiennense duxerit intimandum.
units.tr: Likewise, that possessors who do not hold by violence but under a colourable title, and who have held benefices during the last three years, or who shall hold them in future, are not to be molested, either in a petitory or in a possessory action, not even on the ground of a newly sought right, unless the claimant, lawfully hindered and having protested about this, has decided to intimate it in accordance with the Council of Vienne.

units.la: 2. Lis autem mota intelligatur, si ad citationem, executionem, jurisque sui in judicio exhibitionem, & terminorum omnium observationem fuerit concessum.
units.tr: 2. A suit, moreover, is to be understood as begun if a citation, an execution, and the exhibition of one's right in court, together with the observance of all the terms, have been granted.

units.la: 3. Ordinarii autem inquirant, & quem beneficium injuste possidete perspexerint * pridem & alteri legitime provideant, vel ipsi possessori, si voluerit, nisi sit intrusus violenter vel aliasdignus.
units.tr: 3. The ordinaries, moreover, are to inquire, and whoever they find to hold a benefit unjustly, they are to provide for another lawfully, long since, or to the possessor himself, if he wishes, unless he has been intruded violently or is otherwise unworthy.

units.la: CAPIT. XV.
units.tr: CAPUT XV.

units.la: Quia vero protestationibus Dominorum Electorum, &c. durantibus, plures electiones & provisiones factae, plurima beneficia authoritate ordinaria collata, sententiae interlocutoriae diffinitive prolatae, pluraque alia gesta sunt, super quibus possunt ad Papam vel Concilium recurrere, obstantibus protestationibus: ne igitur confidentia protestationum decipiamur, caveatur, quod ille, cui fiat adhaesio, gesta hujusmodi confirmet ex certa scientia, ac si de verbo ad verbum expressa essent: ita quod nullus super hujusmodi beneficiis aut aliis gestis sive actis in Romana curia vel extra molestetur, etiamsi lis super eis alibi penderet quam coram Ordinariis, etiamsi aliquid alterius quaesitum diceretur; quibus talibus (scilicet jus habere praetendentibus) silentium perpetuum imponatur: & ipsorum possessorum tituli, sive juris sint sive facti, quos durante protestatione authoritate ordinaria acquisiverunt, confirmet, & authoritate Apostolica approbet; ipsisque possessoribus seu detentoribus, in quantum opus, de illis de novo provideat.
units.tr: Because, however, during the protests of the lord electors, etc., several elections and provisions have been made, very many benefices have been conferred by ordinary authority, interlocutory sentences have been pronounced as definitive, and many other acts have been done, about which recourse may be had to the Pope or to a Council, notwithstanding the protests; therefore, lest we be deceived by confidence in the protests, let it be provided that the one to whom adhesion is made shall confirm such acts from certain knowledge, as if they had been expressed word for word; so that no one shall be molested concerning such benefices or other acts or deeds, whether in the Roman curia or elsewhere, even if the suit about them is pending elsewhere than before the Ordinaries, and even if something is said to be sought by another; and perpetual silence shall be imposed on those who claim to have a right (to such things); and the titles of the possessors themselves, whether of right or of fact, which they acquired during the protest by ordinary authority, he shall confirm and approve by apostolic authority; and he shall provide anew for those same possessors or holders, insofar as needed, concerning those things.

units.la: CAPIT. XVI.
units.tr: CHAPTER XVI.

units.la: Lites vero coram ordinariis Judicibus pendentes, apud quos juxta formam protestationis licuit litigare, coram illis tantummodo prosequatur & terminetur.
units.tr: Lawsuits, however, pending before the ordinary judges, before whom it was permitted to litigate according to the form of the protest, shall be pursued and concluded before them alone.

units.la: 2. Sententiae vero sub authoritate Papali vel a Consiliariis durante protestatione collatae nondum executae, non exequantur; sed acta & quicquid ad hoc unaquaeque partium habeat allegare coram Ordinario perducatur, quae summarie, simpliciter & de plano, sola facti veritate inspecta, procedens, negotium ipsum unica sententia valeat terminari.
units.tr: 2. Sentences, however, passed under papal authority or by councillors during the protest, but not yet executed, shall not be executed; instead, the records and whatever each party has to allege in this regard shall be brought before the Ordinary, who, proceeding summarily, simply and de plano, looking only to the truth of the fact, may bring the matter to a conclusion by a single sentence.

units.la: CAPIT. XVII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XVII.

units.la: Item de causis durante protestatione motus, & adhuc movendis, pendentibus, quas advocet Papa, similiter in eodem statu committat Ordinariis similī modo terminandis. Et quod ibi cognitum fuerit, Papa ratificet, & authoritate Apostolica ex certa scientia confirmet. Contrà facientibus, ac etiam a. f. ca. quì a eorum authoritate ordinaria beneficia b possidentibus sunt assecuti, impetere praesumpserint, seu b. f. possidentes quomodolibet molestare, perpetuum silentium imponat.
units.tr: Likewise, concerning causes set in motion during the protest and still to be moved, which the Pope may call to himself, he shall similarly commit them, in the same state, to the Ordinaries, to be concluded in the same manner. And whatever has been decided there, the Pope shall ratify and confirm by apostolic authority from certain knowledge. Against those who act contrary to this, and who have presumed to attack, or in any way to molest, possessors of benefices obtained by authority of the ordinary, he shall impose perpetual silence.

units.la: CAPIT. XVIII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XVIII.

units.la: Insuper omnia & singula, quae dicta protestatione durante in praejudicium, gravamen, sive laesionem patitidictionis, juris, vel possessionis Metropolitanorum, dioecesium, dominiorum, terrarum, Praelatorum, Collegiorum, personarum, seu rerum quarumcunque eorum, qui hujusmodi protestationi obedirent, obediverunt, quomodolibet vergentia, Apostolica vel alia quavis authoritate impetrata, seu quomodolibet concessa, vel in posterum concedenda, aut in judicio vel extrajudicialiter quomodolibet obtenta seu obtinenda, callet, irritet, & annullet, & pro infectis penitus habeat: acilli vel illis, qui aliter impetratis, concessis vel obtentis, concedendis vel obtinendis quomodolibet uterentur, eisdem ipsis & eorum jus ex illis quaesitum foret, de Apostolicae potestatis plenitudine ex certa scientia perpetuum silentium imponat.
units.tr: Furthermore, all and each of the things which, during the said protest, have been obtained or granted in any way, or which may be granted or obtained in future, whether in court or out of court, by apostolic or any other authority, and which tend in any way to the prejudice, grievance or injury of the jurisdiction, right or possession of metropolitans, dioceses, lordships, lands, prelates, colleges, persons or things of any of those who obeyed or obey such protest, he shall quash, annul and make void, and hold as wholly null; and upon those who use such grants, obtained, granted or to be obtained or granted otherwise, and upon those by whom the right acquired from them has been held, he shall impose perpetual silence, by the fullness of apostolic power and from certain knowledge.

units.la: CAPIT. XIX.
units.tr: CHAPTER XIX.

units.la: Ut autem praemissa firmiter observentur, polliceatur Papa pro se & successoribus suis, se omnia praemissa & singula inviolabiliter observaturum, & contra ea vel ipsorum aliquod in toto vel in parte nullo unquam tempore innovaturum, decernendo c initurum, &c. Pro firmiori subsistentia committat Romano Regi & Principibus Electoribus, & aliis, quos secum duxerint assumendos, super eorum observantia Pragmaticam sanctionem conficiendi, ac poenis & censuris vallandi & corroborandi potestatem.
units.tr: So that the foregoing may be firmly observed, the Pope shall promise, for himself and his successors, that he will inviolably observe all and each of the foregoing, and will never at any time innovate against them or any part of them, in whole or in part, decreeing that he will proceed, etc. For greater firmness, he shall commit to the Roman King and the Electoral Princes, and to others whom they may choose to associate, the power of drawing up a Pragmatic Sanction concerning their observance, and of fortifying and strengthening it with penalties and censures.

units.la: CAPIT. XX.
units.tr: CHAPTER XX.

units.la: Item committet universis Archiepiscopis nostrae Nationis, quòd si umquam per eum vel successores, aut eorum seu alia quavis authoritate, per oblivionem fortassis vel inadvertentiam d lapsos, vel importunitatem dicentium, aut aliàs qualitercunque in praejudicium vel laesionem eorum, quicquam statui seu concedi contingat, quòd quivis eorum Archiepiscoporum & Episcoporum id cassèt, &c. & poenas, si quae forte desuper quacunque authoritate prolatae forent, seu proferri contingeret, relaxandi, & omnia in pristinum statum producendi, concedat eis & cuilibet eorum plenam potestatem: & ut praemissa, & omnia postquàm sic statuta fuerint, conservent, manutenant, & defendant, contradictiones per censuram Ecclesiasticam appellatione postposita compescendi, totiens quotiens ipsis visum fuerit, invocato etiam ad hoc, si opus sit, auxilio brachii secularis &c.
units.tr: Likewise he shall commit to all the Archbishops of our Nation that, if at any time, through him or his successors, or by any other authority, through perhaps oversight or inadvertence, or the importunity of those who speak, or otherwise in any way, anything should happen to be established or granted to the prejudice or injury of them, each of the Archbishops and Bishops shall annul it, etc., and shall relax the penalties, if any should perhaps have been pronounced or should come to be pronounced upon this by any authority whatever, and shall bring all things back to their former state; he shall grant to them and to each of them full power to keep, maintain and defend the foregoing and all things once so established, and to suppress contradictions by ecclesiastical censure, without regard to appeal, as often as it shall seem fit to them, calling in also, if need be, the aid of the secular arm, etc.

units.la: CONCLUSIO.
units.tr: CONCLUSION.

units.la: Super praemissis aviśamentis concordent, Serenissimus Dominus Romanorum Rex, Illustrissimi Domini Principes Electores, invicem velle assistere, & alterutrum se defendere contra omnem hominem, eos vel alterum eorum conjunctim vel divisim, occasione praemissorum molestare, invadere, seu quomodolibet perturbare conantem.
units.tr: Concerning the foregoing resolutions, the most Serene Lord, the Roman King, and the most Illustrious Lords, the Electoral Princes, agree to assist one another and to defend each other against every man who attempts to molest, attack or in any way disturb them, or either of them, jointly or severally, on account of the foregoing.

units.la: FRIDERICI III. IMP. AUG. MANDATUM
units.tr: THE MANDATE OF FREDERICK III, AUGUSTUS EMPEROR

units.la: Ad Regem * Franciae, ut veniat ad Comitia Moguntina pro tollendo schismate & con- firmatione Decretorum Concilii Basiliensis indicta.
units.tr: To the King of France, summoning him to come to the Diet of Mainz for the removal of the schism and the confirmation of the decrees of the Council of Basel.

units.la: FRIDERICUS, Romanorum Rex semper-Augustus, Austriae, Stiriae, Carinthiae, & Carniolae Dux, Comes Tirolis, &c. Serenissimo Principi, Carolo Regi Francorum, Fratri & Consanguineo nostro Charissimo Salutem, & fraternae dilectionis affectum.
units.tr: FREDERICK, Roman King, ever Augustus, Duke of Austria, Styria, Carinthia and Carniola, Count of Tyrol, etc., to the most serene Prince Charles, King of the Franks, our brother and most beloved kinsman, greeting and the affection of brotherly love.

units.la: I. Dum ad sacri Imperii fastigia divino vocati munere, tantae moli gravissimae gubernationis nostros in Dei nomine, ne suae videremur ordinationi resistere, sincero corde submisimus. Nam numera mala, quibus undique orbis terrarum concutitur, hoc maximè, quo cerramen agitur, nostro sancta scindatur Ecclesia, animum nostrum eò premit ardentiùsque sollicitat, quòd eidem Ecclesiae matri nostrae, filiali dilectionis amore & nobili advocationis officio, fortius constringimur obligati, ut illi laeva nunc jacula patienti, pro viribus nobis distributis ab alto, diligenter succurramus, atque ad concurrendum in hoc tam necessario ac salutari opere Reges & Principes Christiano nomine gaudentes pura synceritate hortentur. Nihil verò ad id aequè pacis conspicimus, quàm si Catholici simul convenimus Reges & Principes Ecclesiae & Saeculares, ut sentiant quicunque dissidentes unam esse vocem omnium. Tunc cum sperandum, quòd nemo usquam illam irridebit, aur spernet; nemo non reverebitur, neque non [illegible, ~3 letters]
units.tr: I. Since I have been called by divine office to the heights of the Holy Empire, and to the very heavy burden of so grave a government, I have submitted with a sincere heart in the name of God, lest I seem to resist His ordinance. For the many evils by which the whole world is shaken, and above all this schism by which our holy Church is torn, weigh upon our mind and urge it the more ardently, because we are bound more strongly, by the filial love of affection and the noble office of advocacy, to that same Church, our mother, so that we may diligently come to her aid, now that she suffers these grievous blows, with the strength distributed to us from on high, and so that the kings and princes who rejoice in the Christian name may be urged with pure sincerity to join in this so necessary and salutary work. Indeed we see nothing more conducive to peace than that Catholics, both ecclesiastical and secular kings and princes, should meet together, so that all who dissent may perceive that there is one voice of all. Then we may hope that no one anywhere will mock or despise it; no one will fail to revere it, nor not [illegible, about three letters]

units.la: 1. Unde Venerabilium & Illustrium virorum, & Sacri Imperii Principum Electorum bus, qui pridem decretum electionis de nostra persona ad culmen Imperii celebratæ, conseftro attulerant; aliis quoque Prælatis, Principibus, Comitibus, Baronibus, Proceribus, & vir fularibus, nostris fidelibus & dilectis, deliberatè consulentibus, conventionem seu dietam nem pro communi constituimus omnium salute in civitate Moguntina, rebus gerendis plucausis accommoda, in diem festum Purificationis gloriosæ Virginis Mariæ proximè futu-erit fecunda mensis Februarii. Ad quam dextera Dei nobis assistente propria intendimus naliter nos transferre, Charissimam fraternitatem vestram puro cordis affectu rogantes, Orthodoxorum progenitorum vestrorum imitantes vestigia pro laude Dei, pro consolatione fiæ suæ sanctæ, ac totius populi Christiani salute, ad conventionem seu dietam hujusmodi vestros oratores de vestræ fraternæ dilectionis proposito, viis quoque & modis, quibus ab tibus calamitatibus sancta possit respirare Ecclesia, distinctè instructos, & ad tractandum, dum, cooperanduim, & concludendum in his plena vestra potestate fulcitos, illic destinare autem fraternitas vestra convocationem & dietam eandem accedere posset & vellet propria, id profectò ingentem gloriam & rebus gerendis fructum uberiorem afferret.
units.tr: 1. Wherefore, by the counsel of the venerable and illustrious men, and of the Electors of the Holy Roman Empire, who had earlier brought to us the decree of the election of our person to the summit of the Empire; and also of other prelates, princes, counts, barons, nobles and vassals, our faithful and beloved, after deliberate counsel, we have appointed a convention or diet for the common salvation of all, in the city of Mainz, suited to the transacting of many matters, to be held on the feast of the Purification of the glorious Virgin Mary, which will fall in the second month, February. To which, with the right hand of God assisting us, we intend to transfer ourselves in person, earnestly asking your brotherly love, imitating the footsteps of your orthodox forefathers, for the praise of God, for the consolation of His holy Church and for the salvation of the whole Christian people, to send your envoys to this convention or diet, clearly instructed in the purpose of your brotherly love, and in the ways and means by which the holy Church may at last breathe free from such calamities, and furnished with full power to treat, to co-operate and to conclude in these matters. Should your brotherhood also wish to come in person to this convocation and diet, it would surely bring immense glory and a richer fruit to the business at hand.

units.la: 3. Hortamur denique Fraternitatem vestram, advertere velle mente fideli, quæ fit nostra hortatio, quantaque Ecclesiæ subsit necessitas, & quàm periculosum effet nostrum silentium re libeat, quod expetimus, propter salutem populi ac decus vestrum, respicientes ad illam, cui fa agitur, qui de cœlo descendit, ut moriturus homo crucem ascenderet, in quo militans Ecclesia, quatenus in eâ suborta tollantur dissidia, & à gravioribus periculis eruatur. Datum Viennæ, Anno Domini M. CCCCXL. die XXI. mensis Maij: Regni nostri anno primo.
units.tr: 3. Finally, we exhort your brotherhood to consider with a faithful mind what our exhortation is, how great the need of the Church is, and how dangerous our silence would be. We desire this for the salvation of the people and for your honour, looking to Him for whose sake this is done, who came down from heaven so that man, destined to die, might ascend the cross; so that the militant Church may be relieved of the dissensions that have arisen within her, and rescued from more serious dangers. Given at Vienna, in the year of the Lord 1440, on the twenty-first day of the month of May, in the first year of our reign.

units.la: Ad mandatum Domini Regis
units.tr: By order of the Lord King

units.la: Conradus Præpositus Viennenfis, Cancellarius.
units.tr: Conrad, Provost of Vienna, Chancellor.

units.la: CONCORDATA NATIONIS GERMANICÆ CUM SANCTA SEDE APOSTOLICA, PRO IPSIVS ECCLESIAE VNIONE, AC PACE & tranquillitate inter eandem & Nationem prædictam perpetuò confoven- dis, inita, conclusa, & accepta, cum GREGORII PAPAE XIII. DECLARATIONE.
units.tr: THE CONCORDAT OF THE GERMAN NATION WITH THE HOLY APOSTOLIC SEE, concluded, agreed and accepted for the union of the Church itself and for the peace and tranquillity to be perpetually maintained between the same Church and the aforesaid nation, together with the declaration of Pope Gregory XIII.

units.la: NICOLAVS Episcopus servus servorum Dei, ad perpetuam rei memoriam. Ad sacram Padem, divina dispositione sublimati, singulis, quæ pro universalis ecclesiæ unione, ac tranquillitate, profutura conspicimus, Apostolicæ providentiæ sollicitudinem libedimus, & ad felicem illorum profecutionem & consummationem, operam & operam impenficaces. Nuper siquidem charissimus in Christo filius noster, FEDERICUS Romanorum Rex, filius, & nonnulli alii dilecti filii, ecclesiastici, & seculares Principes inclytæ nationis Germana; ac dilectus filius noster, Joannes sancti Angeli Diaconus Cardinal.in partibus illis Apodis de latere Legatus, per nos ad dictas partes missus sufficienti desuperà nobis, & fede Apostolica authoritate fultus, ex alia partibus, Romanæ Ecclesiæ & dictæ nationis nomine, pro ipsius Ecclesiæ unione, pace, & tranquillitate, inter Ecclesiam, & nationem prædictam, perpetuo solidandis & convandis, diversa rationabilia & utilia, ordinationes & statuta, à partibus ipsis hinc inde approbata, conclusa, acceptata & concordata, fecerunt ac ediderunt, nobisq; humiliter supplicant ut illis pro firmiori eorum subsistentia, robur Apostolicæ firmitatis adjicere, necnon auctoritatem, & decretum interponere dignaremur. Nos itaq; qui statuta, ordinationes, & concordata dicta, per nonnullos ex venerabilibus fratribus nostris sanctæ Romanæ Ecclesiæ Cardinalibus, gnorum maturitatis, auctoritatis, & literaturæ viros diligenter examinari & discuti fecimus, ct tionabilia & salubria tam Ecclesiæ quàm nationi præfatae fore comperimus; de dictorum, & venerabilium fratrum nostrorum prædictæ Ecclesiæ Cardinalium, consilio & assensu, Apostolicæ auctoritate, & ex certa scientia approbamus, ratificamus, laudamus, & acceptamus, & præsentis scripti patrocinio communimus, juxta mo-dum & formam subsequentes.
units.tr: NICHOLAS, Bishop, servant of the servants of God, for the perpetual remembrance of the matter. Raised by divine disposition to the holy See, we devote the solicitude of apostolic providence to each thing which we see will be useful for the union and tranquillity of the universal Church, and we bring our effort and work to its happy pursuit and completion. Recently indeed our most beloved son in Christ, FREDERICK, King of the Romans, and certain other beloved sons, ecclesiastical and secular princes of the famous German nation, and our beloved son John, Cardinal Deacon of St Angelo, legate a latere in those parts, sent by us to the said parts, supported by sufficient authority from us and from the apostolic See, on the one side, and on the other in the name of the Roman Church and of the said nation, have made, drawn up and issued various reasonable and useful ordinances and statutes, approved, concluded, accepted and agreed upon by the parties on both sides, for the union, peace and tranquillity of the same Church and of the aforesaid nation, to be solidified and confirmed in perpetuity; and they have humbly begged us to deign to add to them the strength of apostolic firmness for their firmer standing, and to interpose our authority and decree. We therefore, who have caused the said statutes, ordinances and agreements to be carefully examined and discussed by some of our venerable brothers, the Cardinals of the holy Roman Church, men of proven maturity, authority and learning, and have found them reasonable and salutary both for the aforesaid Church and for the nation; by the counsel and assent of our said venerable brothers, the Cardinals of the said Church, by apostolic authority and from certain knowledge, we approve, ratify, praise and accept them, and we confirm them by the patronage of this present writing, in the manner and form that follow.

units.la: 1. Placet nobis sup-provisione Ecclesiarum & beneficiorum ecclesiasticorum quorum-que, juris scripti reservatione, & Executabilu,ac Ad regimen,constitutionum,modificatis ut sequitur regem. regimen Ecclesiae generalis, quanquam immerito, superna dispositione vocati, gerimus in nostris desideriis, ut debemus, quod per nostrae diligentiae studium, ad quacumlibet Ecclesiarum & monasteriorum regimina, & alia beneficia Ecclesiastica, juxta divinum beneplacitum, & nostrae intentionis affectum, viri assumantur idonei, qui praesint & prosint committendis eis ecclesiis, monasteriis, & beneficiis praelibatis. Praemissorum itaque consideratione inducti, & suadentibus nobis aliis rationalibus causis non nullorum praedecessorum nostrorum Roman. Pont. vestigiis inhaerentes, omnes Patriarchales, Archiepiscopales, & Episcopales Ecclesias, & etiam monasteria, prioratus, dignitates, personatus, & officia, necnon canonicatus, praebendas, & ecclesias, caeteraque beneficia ecclesiastica cum cura, vel sine cura, saecularia, & regularia, quaecunque, & qualiacunque fuerint, etiamsi ad illa personae consueverint, seu debuerint per electionem, seu quemvis alium modum assumi, nunc apud sedem apostolicam quocunque modo vacantia, & in posterum vacatura: necnon per depositionem, vel privationem, seu translationem per nos, seu auctoritate nostra factas, & inantea faciendas ubilibet: necnon ad quae aliqui in concordia vel discordia electi sive postulati fuerint, quorum electio cassata, seu postulatio repulsa vel per eos facta renunciatio, & admissa auctoritate nostra extiterit, seu quorum electorum, vel postulatorum, & inantea eligendorum seu postulandorum electionem cassari, seu postulationem repelli aut renunciationem admitti per nos, aut auctoritate nostra contingeret apud sedem praedictam, vel alibi ubicunque, & etiam per obitum Cardinalium ejusdem Ecclesiae Romanae, aut officialium dictae sedis quamdiu ipsa officia actualiter tenebunt (videlicet Vicecancellarii, Camerarii, septem Notariorum Auditoris, literarum contradictarum, & apostolici palatii causarum Auditorum, Correctorum, centum, & unius Scriptorum literarum apostolicarum, & viginti quatuor Poenitentiariae praelatae sedis, & viginti quinque Abbreviatorum, necnon verorum Commensalium nostrorum, & aliorum viginti quatuor Capellanorum sedis ejusdem in epitaphio descriptorum) & etiam quorumcunque Legatorum, seu collectorum, in terris Romanae Ecclesiae Rectorum, ac Thesaurariorum, deputatorum seu minorum hactenus, vel deputandorum aut mittendorum in posterum, nunc vacantia, & inantea vacatura ubicunque dictos Legatos, vel Collectores, seu Rectores, & Thesaurarios antequam ad Romanam curiam redierint seu venerint, rebus eximi contingerit ab humanis, necnon quorumlibet pro quibuscunque negotiis ad Romanam curiam venientium, seu etiam recedentium ab eadem, si in locis a dicta curia ultra duas dietas legales non distantibus iam forsan obierint, vel eos inantea ab hac luce transire contigerit, & etiam simili modo quorumcunque cuiusalium peregrinationis, infirmitatis, seu recreationis, vel alia quacunque causa ad quaevis loca recedentium, si eos antequam ad dictam curiam redierint in locis ultra duas dietas ab eadem curia, ut promittitur, non remotis (dummodo eorum proprium domicilium non existat ibidem) jam forsan decesserint, vel in posterum eos contigerit de medio submoveri, etiam nunc per obitum hujusmodi vacantia, vel in posterum vacatura: Rursus monasteria, prioratus, dignitates, personatus, administrationes, officia, canonicatus, praebendas, & ecclesias, caeteraque beneficia ecclesiastica saecularia & regularia, cum cura, vel sine cura, quaecunque & qualiacunque fuerint, etiam si ad illa personae consueverint seu debuerint per electionem, seu quemvis alium modum assumi, quae promoti per nos seu auctoritate nostra ad Patriarchalium, Archiepiscopalium, & Episcopalium ecclesiarum, necnon monasteriorum regimina obtinebant tempore promotionum de ipsis factarum nunc quocunque modo vacantia, aut in posterum vacatura, necnon etiam per executionem pacificam quorumcunque prioratuum, personatuum, officiorum, canonicatuum, praebendarum, ecclesiarum, aut beneficiorum aliorum per nos, seu auctoritate nostrarum literarum immediate collatorum, seu conferendorum in posterum, praeter
