quam si virtute gratiae expectativae affectatio fiet, nunc vacantia & inantea vacatura, plena super praemissis omnibus, & singulis cum fratribus nostris collatione praehabita, & matura deliberatione secuta, ordinationi, dispositioni, ac provisioni nostrae, de ipsorum fratrum consilio, auctoritate apostolica reservamus, Decernentes ex nunc irritum & inane, si secus super praemissis & quolibet eorum, per quoscunque, quavis auctoritate, scienter vel ignoranter, contigerit attentari.
units.tr: 1. It pleases us, in the provision of churches and of ecclesiastical benefices of whatever kind, to reserve to ourselves, saving the written law and the executory [rights], and with the regime of the Church in general modified as follows; although we have been called, though unworthily, by heavenly disposition, we desire, as we ought, that through the diligence of our care, to the government of whatever churches and monasteries and other ecclesiastical benefices, according to the divine good pleasure and the inclination of our intention, suitable men be chosen, who may preside over and profit the churches, monasteries and benefices named above, to be committed to them. Moved by these considerations, and persuaded by other reasonable causes, adhering to the footsteps of some of our predecessors, the Roman Pontiffs, we reserve by apostolic authority, to our ordinance, disposition and provision, with the counsel of our brothers, and after full prior consultation with our brothers and mature deliberation, all Patriarchal, Archiepiscopal and Episcopal churches, and also monasteries, priories, dignities, personages and offices, as well as canonries, prebends and churches, and other ecclesiastical benefices with or without cure, secular and regular, of whatever kind and quality they may be, even if persons have customarily or ought to be taken to them by election or any other mode; which are now vacant in any manner at the apostolic See, or will be vacant in future; likewise by deposition, or deprivation, or translation made by us or by our authority, and to be made hereafter anywhere; likewise to those to which anyone has been elected or nominated in discord or in concord, whose election has been quashed, or whose nomination has been rejected, or whose resignation made by them has been admitted by our authority; or whose elections or nominations, of those elected or nominated hereafter, may be quashed, or nominations rejected, or resignations admitted, by us or by our authority, at the said See or elsewhere anywhere; and likewise by the death of the Cardinals of the same Roman Church, or of the officials of the said See, for as long as they actually hold those offices (namely the Vice-Chancellor, the Chamberlain, the seven Notaries, the Auditors of the Contradicted Letters and of the causes of the Apostolic Palace, the Correctors, the hundred and one Scribes of the apostolic letters, the twenty-four Penitentiaries of the said See, the twenty-five Abbreviators, and also our true Commensals, and the other twenty-four Chaplains of the same See, described in the epitaph); and likewise of any Legates or collectors, or Rectors and Treasurers in the lands of the Roman Church, deputed or lesser hitherto, or to be deputed or sent in future, now vacant and to be vacant hereafter anywhere, should it happen that the said Legates, or Collectors, or Rectors and Treasurers have been removed from human affairs before they have returned or come to the Roman court; likewise of any persons coming to the Roman court for any business whatever, or even departing from it, if, in places not more than two legal days' journey from the said court, they may perhaps already have died, or should it happen that they pass from this light hereafter; and likewise, in the same way, of any persons departing for any place for pilgrimage, sickness, recreation, or any other cause whatever, if they have perhaps already died before they returned to the said court, in places not, as is promised, more than two days distant from the same court (provided that their proper domicile is not there), or if it should happen that they are removed from the midst hereafter; now vacant by such death or to be vacant hereafter. Again, monasteries, priories, dignities, personages, administrations, offices, canonries, prebends and churches, and other ecclesiastical benefices, secular and regular, with or without cure, of whatever kind and quality they may be, even if persons have customarily or ought to be taken to them by election or any other mode; which those promoted by us or by our authority to the government of Patriarchal, Archiepiscopal and Episcopal churches, and of monasteries, held at the time of their promotion, and which are now vacant in any manner, or will be vacant in future; and likewise by peaceful execution of any priories, personages, offices, canonries, prebends, churches or other benefices immediately conferred, or to be conferred hereafter, by us or by the authority of our letters, except if an expectative grace is claimed by virtue of it, now vacant and to be vacant hereafter; with full prior consultation with our brothers on all and each of the foregoing matters, and after mature deliberation, we reserve them to our ordinance, disposition and provision, by the counsel of the same brothers, by apostolic authority. We decree from now on that it is null and void if anything is attempted contrary to the foregoing or to any part of them, by anyone, by whatever authority, knowingly or unknowingly.

units.la: 1. Item placet nobis, quod in Metropolitanis & cathedralibus etiam immediate non subiectis ecclesiis, & monasteriis immediate subiectis sedi apostolicae, fiant electiones canonicae quae ad dictam sedem deferantur, quas etiam ad tempus constit. fe. rec. Nicolai Papae III. quae incipit, Cupientes; expectabimus: & elapso dicto tempore si non praesentatae, vel si praesentatae, minus canonicae fuerint, providebimus; & si canonicae fuerint, eas confirmabimus, nisi ex rationabili, & evidenti causa, ac de dictorum fratrum consilio, de dignioris & utiliori persona duxerimus providendum: proviso quod confirmati praedicti, & per eos provisi, Metropolitanis suis, & aliis praestenr debita juramenta, & alia, ad quae de jure tenentur, etiam in monasteriis dictae sedi immediate non subiectis, & aliis regularibus beneficiis, super quibus pro confirmatione, vel provisione ad dictam sedem non consuevit haberi recursus, electi, seu illi quibus providendum est, pro confirmatione & provisione hujusmodi ad curiam Romanam venire non tenebuntur: ipsaque regularia beneficia sub expectativis gratiis non cadant. Ubi autem pro monasteriis ad dictam curiam venire seu mittere consueverint, non aliter confirmabimus vel providebimus, quam superius de cathedralibus ecclesiis est expressum. Et de monasteriis monialium non disponemus, nisi sint exempta, & tunc per commissionem ad partes.
units.tr: 1. Likewise it pleases us that in metropolitan and cathedral churches, even those not immediately subject, and in monasteries immediately subject to the apostolic See, canonical elections be made and be referred to the said See; these we shall await for the time laid down also in the constitution of blessed memory of Pope Nicholas III which begins "Cupientes"; and if after the said time they have not been presented, or if presented they are less canonical, we shall provide; and if they are canonical we shall confirm them, unless for a reasonable and evident cause, and by the counsel of the said brothers, we judge that a more worthy and useful person should be provided: provided that those confirmed and provided as aforesaid shall give the due oaths to their Metropolitans and the others, and the other things to which they are bound by law, also in monasteries not immediately subject to the said See, and in other regular benefices, for the confirmation or provision of which recourse is not customarily had to the said See; and the elected, or those to whom provision is to be made, shall not be bound to come to the Roman court for such confirmation and provision; and those regular benefices shall not fall under expectative graces. Where, however, for monasteries they have customarily come or sent to the said court, we shall not confirm or provide otherwise than has been expressed above concerning cathedral churches. And we shall not dispose of convents of nuns unless they are exempt, and then by commission to the parts.

units.la: 3. De caeteris vero dignitatibus & beneficiis quibuscunque, saecularibus, & regularibus vacaturis, ultra reservationes praedictas (majoribus dignitatibus post Pontificales, in cathedralibus, & principalibus in collegiatis Ecclesiis exceptis; de quibus jure ordinario providetur per illos inferiores, ad quos alias aliâs pertinet.) placet etiam nobis, quod per quamcunque aliam reservationem, gratiam, expectationem, aut quamvis aliam dispositionem, sub quacunque verborum forma per nos vel auctoritate nostra factam vel faciendam, non impediamus nos, quo minus de illis cum vacabunt de Februarii, Aprilis, Junij, Augusti, Octobris, & Decembris mensibus, libere disponatur per illos, ad quos eorum collatio, provisio, praesentatio, electio, seu quaevis alia dispositio pertinebat: reservatione, aliave dispositione, auctoritate nostra factis vel faciendis, non obstantibus quibuscunque. Quoties vero aliquo vacante beneficio in Januarii, Martii, Maii, Junii, Septembris, & Novembris mensibus liter dispositioni dictae sedis reservatis non appaturerint infra tres menses a die notae vacationis beneficii, quod alicui de illo Apostolica auctoritate provisum fuerit, ex nunc & non antea ordinarius, publicari, & omnes qui ea gaudere voluerint, tempus congruum habeant eam acceptandi, tunc ad dictam sedem, a Kalendis Junii proxime futuris ipsa currere incipiet, & durabit deinceps, nisi a turo Concilio de consensu dictae nationis aliter fuerit ordinatum.
units.tr: 3. Concerning all other dignities and benefices whatsoever, secular and regular, falling vacant beyond the aforesaid reservations (except the greater dignities after the pontifical ones in cathedral churches and the principal dignities in collegiate churches, which are conferred by ordinary law by those lower authorities to whom they otherwise pertain), it also pleases us that we shall not hinder, by any other reservation, grace, expectative, or any other disposition whatever, made or to be made by us or by our authority, in whatever form of words, that such benefices, when they fall vacant in the months of February, April, June, August, October and December, be freely disposed of by those to whom their collation, provision, presentation, election, or any other disposition pertains. This is to hold notwithstanding any reservation or other disposition, made or to be made by our authority. Whenever, however, a benefice falls vacant in the months of January, March, May, June, September and November, and the reserved disposition of the said see does not appear within three months from the day on which the vacancy of the benefice became known, and provision of it has been made by apostolic authority to someone, then from now on and not before, the ordinary shall publish it, and all who wish to enjoy it shall have a suitable time to accept it. Then the annates to the said see shall begin to run from the Kalends of June next, and shall continue thereafter, unless the future Council, with the consent of the said nation, orders otherwise.

units.la: 4. Placet similiter nobis quod circa provisionem dictae sedis ordinandam modus annatarum modo cur at. De Ecclesiis cathedralibus omnibus & monasteriis, virorum duntaxat vacantibus, solvantur de fructibus primi anni a die vacationis, summae pecuniarum in libris Camerae taxatae, quae communia servitia nuncupantur, & si quae excessive taxatae sint, quod providetur, in gravatis regionibus secundum qualitatem rerum, temporum, & regionum, ne nimium graventur ad quod petentibus dabimus commissionem in partibus, qui diligenter inquirant taxent. Taxae autem praedictae pro media parte infra annum a die habitae possessionis pacificae vel majoris partis, solvantur, & pro alia media parte infra annum sequentem, & si infra annum pluries vacaverint, semel tantum solvantur: nec debitum hujusmodi in successorem in ecclesia monasterio transeat. De caeteris vero dignitatibus, personatibus, officiis, & beneficiis secularibus regula bus quibuscunque, quae auctoritate dictae sedis conferentur, vel de quibus provideBitur, pe teriquam vigore gratiarum expectativarum, aut causa permutationis) solvantur annatae seu fructus juxta taxam solitam a tempore possessionis intra annum, et debitum hujusmod, similiter in successorem in beneficio non transeat. Sed de beneficiis quae valorem viginti quatuor florenorum auri de camera non excedunt, nihil solvatur: duretque haec observantia deinceps, nisi eam similiter in futuro concilio de ipsius nationis consensu contingat immutari.
units.tr: 4. It likewise pleases us that, concerning the arrangement of the said see's provision, the manner of annates now in use be observed. From all cathedral churches and monasteries of men alone, when they fall vacant, the sums of money assessed in the books of the Camera, called common services, shall be paid from the fruits of the first year counted from the day of the vacancy. If any have been assessed excessively, this shall be provided for in burdened regions, according to the quality of the affairs, times and regions, so that they are not too heavily burdened; for this purpose we shall grant a commission in the regions to those who petition, who shall carefully inquire and assess. The aforesaid taxes shall be paid, one half within a year from the day of peaceful possession, or of the greater part of it, and the other half within the following year; and if vacancies occur several times within a year, they shall be paid only once. Nor shall such a debt pass to the successor in the church or monastery. Concerning the other dignities, personages, offices and secular benefices of any rules whatever, which are conferred or provided by the authority of the said see, except by virtue of expectative graces or by reason of exchange, the annates or fruits shall be paid according to the usual assessment, within a year from the time of possession; and such a debt likewise shall not pass to the successor in the benefice. But nothing shall be paid for benefices that do not exceed the value of twenty-four gold florins of the camera. This observance shall continue henceforth, unless it likewise happens to be changed at a future council with the consent of the same nation.

units.la: 5. In aliis autem quae per fe.re. Eugenium Papam IIII. etiam praedecessorem nostrum pro dicta natione usque ad tempus futuri generalis concilii permissa, concessa, indulta, & decreta, ac per nos confirmata fuerint, in quantum illa concordiae praesenti non obvient, ista vice nihil volumus esse immutatum: & per hoc, quod in concordatis hujusmodi, sive quibusvis aliis eorum occasione conficiendis literis, propter compendiosiorem descriptionem, Alamania specialiter appellatur, natio ipsa censeri non debet a Germanica natione distincta, seu quomodolibet separata.
units.tr: 5. As to the other matters which were permitted, granted, indulged and decreed for the said nation by Eugene IV of happy memory, our predecessor, until the time of a future general council, and which have been confirmed by us, insofar as they do not conflict with the present concordat, we wish nothing to be changed on this occasion. And by the fact that in such concordats, or in any letters to be drawn up on their account, Germany is named specifically for the sake of a more concise description, that nation is not to be regarded as distinct from or in any way separated from the German nation.

units.la: 6. Et praeterea quia difficile foret praesentes literas ad singula, in quibus de eis forsitan fides faciendae fuerit, loca deferri, eadem Apost. auctoritate decernimus, quod ipsorum transumpto Metropolitanorum dictae nationis sigillo munito, tanquam praesentibus, si exhiberentur, literis plena fides adhibeatur, & perinde sterur ac si dictae praesentes literae forent exhibitae, vel ostensae: & insuper quoq; irritum & inane, si secus super his a quoquam quavis auctoritate scienter, vel ignoranter, contigerit attentari.
units.tr: 6. Moreover, since it would be difficult to carry the present letters to each place where faith in them may perhaps have to be given, we decree by the same apostolic authority that a transcript of them, made by the metropolitans of the said nation and furnished with their seal, shall be accorded full faith just as the present letters would be if they were produced or shown; and, in addition, that anything attempted to the contrary in these matters by anyone, whether knowingly or ignorantly, and by whatever authority, shall be void and null.

units.la: Nulli ergo omnino hominum liceat hanc paginam nostrae approbationis, ratificationis, acceptationis, commutationis, reservationis, constitutionis & voluntatis, infringere, vel ei ausu temerario contraire. Si quis autem hoc attentare praesumpserit, indignationem omnipotentis Dei, & beatorum Petri & Pauli Apostolorum ejus, se noverit incursurum.
units.tr: Therefore let no one at all among men be permitted to infringe this page of our approval, ratification, acceptance, exchange, reservation, constitution and will, or to contravene it with rash daring. If anyone presumes to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of his blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

units.la: Datum Romae apud Sanctum Petrum, anno Incarnationis Dominicae, millesimo, quadringentesimo, quadragesimo septimo, Kalend. Aprilis, Pontif. nostri anno secundo.
units.tr: Given at Rome, at St Peter's, in the year of the Lord's Incarnation 1447, on the Kalends of April, in the second year of our pontificate.

units.la: DECLARATIO CONSTITUTIONIS A NICOLAO V. EDITAE CIRCA COLLA- TIONES BENEFICIORUM VACANTIUM IN MENSIBUS SE- DI APOSTOLICAE RESERVATIS: juxta formam Concordatorum cum Natione Germanica.
units.tr: DECLARATION OF THE CONSTITUTION ISSUED BY NICHOLAS V CONCERNING THE CONFERRING OF VACANT BENEFICES IN THE MONTHS RESERVED TO THE APOSTOLIC SEE: according to the form of the Concordats with the German Nation.

units.la: Gregorius Episcopus servus servorum Dei, ad futuram rei memoriam. Quae in Ecclesiarum Dei incommoda inferunt, nostra nos expeditanimadversione removere. Cum itaque pei literas fel. record. Nicolai Papae V. nationi Germanicae pro illius virtute, & concordia cum Sede Apostolica inter alia concedatur, ut quoties aliquo vacante beneficio Ecclesiastico, in mensibus Januarii, Martii, Maii, Iulii, Septembris, & Novembris, in quibus vacantium Germaniae beneficiorum Ecclesiasticorum dispositio dictae Sedi specialiter reservata est, non apparuerit intra tres menses a die notae vacationis, in loco beneficii, quod alicui de illo Apostolica auctoritate provisum fuerit, extinctis & non antea ordinarius, vel aliusad quem illius dispositio pertinet, de illo disponere possit, & saepe numero contingat, ut antequam inquisitio, quam plerunque etiam in concursu plurium, sive in partibus,
units.tr: Gregory, Bishop, servant of the servants of God, for the future memory of the matter. We are accustomed to remove by our careful attention those things which bring inconveniences upon the Churches of God. Since therefore, by the letters of Nicholas V of happy memory, it was granted to the German nation, among other things, in recognition of its virtue and its concord with the Apostolic See, that whenever any ecclesiastical benefice falls vacant in the months of January, March, May, July, September and November, in which the disposition of the vacant ecclesiastical benefices of Germany is specially reserved to the said See, and it does not appear within three months from the day of the known vacancy, in the place of the benefice, that someone has been provided by Apostolic authority, then the benefice being extinguished and not before, the ordinary or another to whom its disposition belongs may dispose of it; and it often happens that before the inquiry, which is usually made even in the concourse of several persons, or in the regions,

units.la: Nicol. V. statuit Ordinarios posse disponere de beneficiis vacantibus in mensib. Sedi Apost. reservatis, nisi fuerit a dicta Sede provisum, ut sup. in ejus constit. pratribus, sive apud dictam Sedem fieri oportet in vitam, mores, & doctrinam eorum, quibus de dictis beneficiis per Sedem eandem providendum est, compleri possit, aut antequam de ipsis provisionibus, seu de mandatis, quae ad inquisitiones, & provisiones huiusmodi faciendas ab eadem Sede impetrantur, vel Motu proprio procedunt literae Apostolicae conficiantur, vel etiam antequam mandata ipsa a Judicibus, ad quos directa sunt, recipiantur, vel recepta expediantur, interdum quoque literis Apostolicis expeditis, & gratia purificata, seu mandatis praedictis receptis, & inquisitione completa, antequam omnimoda executio perficiatur, propter diversa impedimenta, quae frequenter succedunt, tempus trium mensium, ex quo vacatio beneficii in loco ipsius nota est, expiret, ac proinde ordinarii locorum, aut alii ad quos talium beneficiorum dispositio, cessantibus Apostolicis reservationibus, pertinet, ab ipso tempore praedicto, licet priusquam illud laberetur, provisionis sive alterius dispositionis de illis a dicta Sede jam gratia facta fuerit (quod ipsum ad tribuendum, & quaerendum jus satis superque esse certa juris interpretatione frequenter declaratum est) illa tamen conferre contendant: Quo de causa multis Religione, & pietate insignibus, quando ij post ostensum virtutis, & doctrinae suae specimen, atque inde immensos labores, & lumprus beneficiis potiri debent, alii praeoccupatores obtentu ordinariae collationis huiusmodi contra adversantur: Nos indignum rati, quod temporis mora, quam ad perscrutandum accuratius talium probitatem, inductriam, & alia requisita intercedere pro utilitate Ecclesiae necesse est, locum injuriis aperiat, attendentesque verba praedicta (in loco beneficii cum verbis (nota vacationis) quae protinus antecedunt, conjungi & ad illa duntaxat referri, ac voluntatem concedentis, sensumque concessionis, & literarum praedictarum sic esse, ut dispositio beneficii intra tres menses a die notae vacationis a Sede praedicta fieri, deque gratia facta alicubi apparere debeat, quemadmodum re interutriusque juris interpretes jampridem controversa summa ratione judicatum apparet: vix enim est, ut itineribus non modo infestis, aut prohibitis, quod fere semper aliquo contingit, sed etiam expeditis, quis ex tam longinquis regionibus ad dictam Sedem profectus, & inea ad expediendum negotium, vel paulisper moratus, in eadem se recipere tanta temporis angustia possit. Quocirca aequitate, & justitia suadentibus, praesentium auctoritate declaramus concessionem Nicolai Papae, & literas praedictas locum omnino non habere, quod ordinarii, aut alii collatores praedicti, post lapsum trium mensium ex die notae vacationis in loco beneficii disponere possint de ullis beneficiis praedictis, aliás sub concessione, & literis praedictis, comprehensis extra Ro. Cu. in mensibus praedictis quoquo modo vacantibus, vel vacaturis, de quibus intra dictum tempus trium mensium per Romanum Pontificem, ac dictam Sedem qualiscunque gratia, vel dispositio, aut concessio facta fuerit. Ne tamen cuiquam licitum sit factam a Sede praedicta dispositionem huiusmodi in longum obtegere: illi, quibus deinceps gratiae huiusmodi concedentur, earum concessionum fidem, & testimonium, intra tres menses a die notae vacationis in loco beneficii huiusmodi, vel dictis collatoribus significare, vel in ipso beneficii loco publicare quoquomodo teneantur. Decernentes omnes, & quascunque dispositiones de dictis beneficiis ab eisdem collatoribus post significationem, seu publicationem huiusmodi pro tempore factas, nullas, & invalidas, nulliusque roboris, vel momenti fore. Atque in quibusvis causis pendentibus, & futuris judicari debeant. Necnon irritum, & inane quicquid secus super his ab eisdem collatoribus, aut quibuscunque aliis scienter, vel ignoranter contigerit attentari. Quod si forte quisquam collatorum praedictorum fuerit praesentium violator, eum a beneficiorum, & officiorum collatione tandiu suspendimus, donec ipse veniam petens restitutionis gratiam a Sede praedicta meruerit obtinere. Caeterum volumus, ut praesentium transumptis, etiam impressis Notarii publici manu, & sigillo personae in dignitate Ecclesiastica constitutae obsignatis, eadem prorsus fides in judicio, & extra illud ubique locorum adhiberetur, quae adhiberetur ipsis praesentibus si essent exhibitae, vel ostensae. Nulli ergo omnium hominum liceat hanc paginam nostrae declarationis, decreti, suspensionis, & voluntatis infringere, vel ei ausu temerario contraire. Si quis autem hoc attentare praesumpserit, indignationem Omnipotentis Dei, ac Beatorum Petri, & Pauli Apostolorum ejus se noverit incursurum. Datum Romae apud Sanctum Petrum, Anno Incarnationis Dominicae, millesimo quingentesimo septuagesimo sexto, Kal. Novembris, Pontificatus nostri anno quinto.
units.tr: Nicholas V decreed that ordinaries may dispose of benefices vacant in the months reserved to the Apostolic See, unless provision has been made by the said See, as above in his constitution, to the brothers, or it must be done at the said See, so that the life, morals and teaching of those to whom the said benefices are to be provided by the See may be completed; or before the provisions themselves, or the mandates which are sought from the same See for making such inquiries and provisions, or Apostolic letters issued by its own motion, are drawn up; or even before the mandates themselves are received by the judges to whom they are addressed, or, once received, are carried out; sometimes also when Apostolic letters have been issued and grace has been secured, or the mandates have been received and the inquiry completed, but before full execution is accomplished, because of various impediments which frequently arise, the period of three months from the day the vacancy of the benefice became known in its place expires; and therefore the ordinaries of the places, or others to whom the disposition of such benefices belongs once the Apostolic reservations have ceased, claim to confer them from that same time, even though, before it lapsed, a provision or other disposition of them had already been granted by the said See (which, to establish and seek a right, has often been declared by a sufficiently certain interpretation of the law to be more than enough). For this reason, men distinguished by religion and piety, when after showing the proof of their virtue and learning, and after immense labours and expenses, they ought to obtain the benefices, are opposed by others who got in first under the pretext of such ordinary collation. We, thinking it unworthy that a delay of time, which must intervene in order to examine more carefully the uprightness, diligence and other requisites of such men for the good of the Church, should open a way for wrongs, and considering that the words above which immediately precede (in the place of the benefice, with the words (notice of the vacancy)) are to be joined together and referred only to these, and that the will of the grantor and the sense of the grant and of the aforesaid letters are such that the disposition of the benefice must be made by the said See within three months from the day of the notice of the vacancy, and that the grant made must appear somewhere, as the interpreters of both laws have long since judged, with the most sound reasoning, in a matter of controversy: for it is scarcely possible that anyone, travelling from such distant regions to the said See, and having remained there even briefly to expedite the business, should be able to return within so short a space of time, not only when the roads are dangerous or closed, which almost always happens somewhere, but even when they are open. Wherefore, as equity and justice require, we declare by the authority of these presents that the concession of Nicholas V and the aforesaid letters do not at all apply, so that the ordinaries or other collators mentioned may, after the lapse of three months from the day of notice of the vacancy in the place of the benefice, dispose of any of the aforesaid benefices, otherwise the concession and the aforesaid letters being included, outside the Roman Curia, in the aforesaid months, in whatever way vacant or about to be vacant, of which within the said period of three months some grace, disposition or concession has been made by the Roman Pontiff and the said See. Yet lest it be lawful for anyone to conceal for long a disposition of this kind made by the said See, those to whom such graces are henceforth granted are bound, in whatever way, to signify the evidence and testimony of those concessions to the said collators within three months from the day of notice of the vacancy in the place of such a benefice, or to publish them in the place of the benefice itself. We decree that all and any dispositions of the said benefices made by the same collators after such signification or publication are null, invalid, and of no force or weight. And they ought to be judged so in all pending and future causes. Likewise, whatever else may be attempted by the same collators, or by any others, in these matters, knowingly or unknowingly, is void and of no effect. But if perchance any of the aforesaid collators should violate these presents, we suspend him from conferring benefices and offices until, seeking pardon, he deserves to obtain the grace of restitution from the said See. Furthermore we will that, to copies of these presents, even printed, signed by the hand of a public notary and sealed with the seal of a person constituted in ecclesiastical dignity, the same full faith be given in court and out of court everywhere, as would be given to these presents if they were exhibited or shown. Let it therefore be lawful for no one of all men to infringe this page of our declaration, decree, suspension and will, or to contravene it with rash daring. If anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of Almighty God and of the Blessed Apostles Peter and Paul. Given at Rome, at St Peter's, in the year of the Lord's Incarnation one thousand five hundred and seventy-six, on the Kalends of November, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

units.la: M. Dat.
units.tr: M. Dat.

units.la: C. Glorierius. A. de Alexiis.
units.tr: C. Glorierius. A. de Alexiis.

units.la: Maximiliani Imperatoris Romanorum edicto cautum est, ut Concordata Germanicae Nationis sedulo servantur, apud Leodienses, ita ut nihil pactis & concordatis illis derogetur: si vero quispiam Caesareo edicto & voluntati suo temerario contravenire praesumpserit, multabitur, quemadmodum latius patet in diplomate, Augustae die 11. Julii. Anno 1518.
units.tr: By an edict of the Emperor Maximilian of the Romans it is provided that the Concordats of the German Nation are diligently observed at Liège, so that nothing is taken away from the agreements and concordats; if indeed anyone should presume to contravene rashly the imperial edict and its will, he shall be fined, as is more fully set out in the diploma, at Augsburg, 11 July, 1518.

units.la: Similimodo per Carolum Romanorum Imperatorem cautum est, ut & Cameracenses servent suprascripta Concordata sub indignationis poena, & multa, quae ex literis latius patet. Dat. Bruxellae, Anno 1554. 9. Februarii.
units.tr: In a similar way, by Charles, Emperor of the Romans, it is provided that the people of Cambrai also observe the aforesaid Concordats under penalty of indignation and a fine, as is more fully set out in the letters. Given at Brussels, 9 February, 1554.

units.la: FRIDERICI III. IMPERAT. AUG. ET MAXIMILIANI I. CÆS. RESCRIPTUM AD REGEM ANGLIÆ, S. IMPERII GERMANICI SOCIUM, PRO VINDI- CANDIS injuriis à Rege Gallorum S. Cæs. Majestati & eidem Imperio illatis in rapienda a sponsa Cæsaris & occupando Britanniæ Ducatu.
units.tr: The rescript of Emperors Frederick III Augustus and Maximilian I Caesar to the King of England, an ally of the Holy Roman Empire, for avenging the injuries inflicted by the King of the French on His Imperial Majesty and on the same Empire, in seizing the bride of the Caesar and occupying the Duchy of Brittany.

units.la: MAximilianus divina clementia Romanorum Rex Semper-Augustus; Hungariæ, Dalmatiæ, Croatiæ, &c. Rex; Archidux Austriæ, &c. Wilhelmus Episcopus Eistetensis, ac Fridericus Comes de Zollern, Capitaneus Dominii de Hohenberg, S. Imperii Majestatis in hoc generali Conventu Confluentiæ habito Vicesgerentes; necnon S. Rom. Imperii Electores, ac alii Principes utriusque status, in eodem Conventu personaliter comparentes, aliique Imperii Principum & Communitatum Oratores ac Vicesgerentes, Serenissimo Principi, Domino Hainrico Regi Angliæ & Franciæ, ac Domino Hiberniæ, &c. Nobis Romanorum Regi carissimo, nobisque aliis Domino & amico observandissimo, salutem & prosperitatis incrementa.
units.tr: Maximilian, by divine clemency King of the Romans, ever Augustus; King of Hungary, Dalmatia, Croatia, etc.; Archduke of Austria, etc.; Wilhelm, Bishop of Eichstätt, and Frederick, Count of Zollern, Captain of the lordship of Hohenberg, vicegerents of His Imperial Majesty at this general assembly held at Koblenz; likewise the Electors of the Holy Roman Empire and the other princes of both estates, personally present at the same assembly, and the other envoys and vicegerents of the princes and communities of the Empire, to the most serene Prince, Lord Henry, King of England and France, and Lord of Ireland, etc., our most dear Roman King, and to us, his other lord and most observant friend, greeting and increase of prosperity.

units.la: 1. Serenissime ac potentissime Princeps; Cum egregius vir, Magister Franciscus de Puys Oratorque ac Secretarius vester, nobis omnibus in hoc Imperiali Conventu congregatis indicaverit, vestram Serenitatem non solum ob fraternam confœderationem, qua nobis Romanorum Regi constanter de conjungitur, verum etiam ob singularem affectum & amicitiam, quæ S. Rom. Imperio omnibusque Principibus ejus, & unicè Illustrissimo Archiduci Philippo Imperiali ac Regio filio vehementer afficitur, cum magna ac potenti classe mare trajecisse, multaque armatorum millia cum machinis ac cæteris quibuscunque castrensibus instrumentis traduxisse, tam in maximarum injuriarum nobis Regi ac sacro Imperio per Francorum Regem (ut nostis) illatarum ultionem, quam in ipsius Illustrissimi Archiducis patriarumque ejus defensionem; sanè omnes, ut debuimus, summopere gavisi sumus, vestraque Serenitati ex tam strenuissimis ac præclarissimis gestis nos omnes plurimum debere censuimus; atque propterea ingentes gratias agimus, non inferiora, cum usus feret, pariter redditurum, eandem vestram Serenitatem cum studio exhortantes, ut secundum jam diu concepta perseverare & continuare, ut eam facturam confidimus, non desistat.
units.tr: 1. Most serene and most powerful Prince: Since the distinguished man, Master Francis de Puys, your orator and secretary, has informed us all, gathered at this Imperial assembly, that Your Serenity has crossed the sea with a great and powerful fleet, and has brought over many thousands of armed men with siege engines and all other military equipment, both to avenge the greatest injuries inflicted on us, the King, and on the Holy Empire by the King of the Franks (as you know), and to defend this most illustrious Archduke himself and his lands, we have all indeed rejoiced greatly, as we ought, and we judge that we all owe Your Serenity very much for such most vigorous and distinguished deeds. We therefore give immense thanks, and we will likewise return no lesser favours when occasion requires, exhorting the same Your Serenity earnestly to persevere in what you have long intended and to continue, as we trust you will, and not to desist.

units.la: 2. Nos autem Romanorum Rex nostros jam antea in limitibus hostium ad præoccupandas angustias missos totis copiis sequimur, tot suscepturarum injuriarum justam ultionem Deo propicio profecuturi. Speramus enim æquissimos superos tam æquæ causæ nostræ minimè defuturos.
units.tr: 2. We, the Roman King, however, follow with all our forces those whom we had already sent earlier to the borders of the enemy to seize the narrow passes in advance, hoping, with God favouring, to carry out just vengeance for so many injuries yet to be inflicted. For we hope that the most just gods will by no means fail our equally just cause.

units.la: 3. Nos verò tam Imperialis Majestatis Vicesgerentes ea injuria præfato Domino nostro Regi illata affecti percitique, quam non immeritò molestè ferimus, eidem celerem expeditionem tam equitum quàm peditum in præsentiarum fecimus, ac propterea omni cura, fide, solertia, omni denique studio apud universos & singulos S. Rom. Imperii ac Germanicæ Nationis nostræ subditos pro longe ampliori ac communi per Imperium auxilio ferendo nos laboraturos sollicitaturosque; pollicitti sumus: dubitantes, vestræ Serenitatis simul accedentibus copiis, omnipotentem Deum, exercituum Domnum, de tam detestabilibus injuriis manifestam vindictam justumque triumphum concessurum; vestram Serenitatem indies feliciorem conservet.
units.tr: 3. We, indeed, the vicegerents of the Imperial Majesty, moved and stirred by that injury inflicted on our aforesaid Lord the King, and taking it no less than justly amiss, have for the present made a swift dispatch of both horse and foot to him; and accordingly we have promised that with all care, faith, diligence, and every zeal we will labour and press all and each of the subjects of the Holy Roman Empire and of our German Nation to bring far greater aid, common throughout the Empire. Trusting that, with Your Serenity's forces joining at the same time, Almighty God, the Lord of Hosts, will grant manifest vengeance for such detestable injuries and a just triumph; may He keep Your Serenity ever more fortunate day by day.

units.la: 4. Ex Imperiali Conventu generali Confluentiæ habito, sub sigillis Regiæ nostræ, & Wilhelmi Episcopi Eistetensis Cæsarei Oratoris ac Vicesgerentis, nostrorum quoque Berchtoldi Dei gratia Archiepiscopi Moguntini, Principis Electoris ac S. Rom. Imperii in Germania Archicancellarii, & Sigismundi eadem gratia Marchionis Brandenburgensis, Stetinensis, Pomeraniæ, Cassuborum ac Slavorum Ducis Burggravii Nurbergensis, ac Rugiæ Principis, nomine Principum Electorum aliorumque Principum, totiusque illius præmemorati Conventus, die VIII. Mensis Octobris, Anno Domini MCCCCXCII.
units.tr: 4. Given from the general Imperial assembly held at Koblenz, under the seals of our royal majesty and of Wilhelm, Bishop of Eichstätt, Imperial orator and vicegerent, and also of our Berchtold, by the grace of God Archbishop of Mainz, Prince Elector and Archchancellor of the Holy Roman Empire in Germany, and of Sigismund, by the same grace Margrave of Brandenburg, of Stettin, Pomerania, the Kassubians and the Slavs, Duke, Burgrave of Nuremberg, and Prince of Rügen, in the name of the Electoral Princes and the other princes, and of the whole of that aforementioned assembly, on the 8th day of the month of October, in the year of our Lord 1492.

units.la: PROCESSUS ET ORDINATIO IN UNCTIONE IMPERATO- RIS ROMANORUM, ET IMPERATRICIS, in eorum coronatione & consecratione Romana.
units.tr: The Procedure and Order in the Anointing of the Emperor of the Romans and of the Empress, in their Roman Coronation and Consecration.

units.la: CAPUT I.
units.tr: CHAPTER I.

units.la: De adventu & coronatione electi in Imperatorem Romanorum.
units.tr: Concerning the arrival and coronation of the one elected as Emperor of the Romans.

units.la: Electus Rex futurus Romanorum Imperator primum consuevit electionem suam per solemnes oratores Pontifici summo intimare, & decretum electionis ostendere, devotionem ac fidelem reverentiam exhibere, favorem & gratiam Apostolicæ sedis implorare, offerre quæcunque fidelitatis juramenta Romanæ Ecclesiæ præstanda, & demum unctionem coronationem & Imperii diadema humiliter postulare. Pontifices verò consueverunt viso decreto, & terminata electione in sacro senatu, habitaque sufficienti informatione tam super forma electionis quam super idoneitate & habilitate personæ electi, per commissarios à se constitutos ad instantiam electi ipsum electum in spiritualem filium suum & Ecclesiæ Romanæ suscipere, illique favorem gratiam concedere, & ipsius Regis electi persona idonea reputata, eum nominare, denuntiare, assumere, & declarare Regem Romanorum, ac etiam habilem & sufficientem declarare ad suscipiendâ Imperialis celsitudinis dignitatem, decernere consecrationem & coronationem per manus suas esse impendendas, & supplere omnes defectus &c. Hoc servatum legimus in Carolo IIII. à Clemente VI. & antea in Henrico VII. à Clemente V. & in Alberto ejus prædecessore, & Rodolfo patre à Bonifacio VIII. & à pluribus aliis, & in Wenceslao Caroli IIII. filio, quem pater adhuc vivens in Romanorum Regem ab Electoribus designari procuraverat: cujus rei approbationem cum Gregorius XI. ad quem delata erat, morte præventus decernere non posset, Urbanus VI. ejus successor legitime confecit.
units.tr: The king-elect of the Romans, who is to become Emperor, has customarily first announced his election through solemn envoys to the supreme Pontiff, shown the decree of election, paid devoted and faithful reverence, implored the favour and grace of the Apostolic See, offered whatever oaths of fidelity are to be sworn to the Roman Church, and finally humbly asked for the unction, the coronation and the diadem of the Empire. The Pontiffs, however, having seen the decree and the election being concluded in the sacred senate, and having obtained sufficient information both on the form of the election and on the fitness and ability of the person elected, have customarily, at the petition of the elected man, received him through commissioners appointed by them as their spiritual son and son of the Roman Church, granted him favour and grace, and, judging the person of the king-elect to be suitable, named, proclaimed, adopted and declared him King of the Romans; they have also declared him able and sufficient to receive the dignity of the Imperial majesty, decreed that the consecration and coronation are to be conferred by their own hands, and supplied all defects, etc. We read that this was observed in Charles IV by Clement VI, and earlier in Henry VII by Clement V, and in Albert, his predecessor, and in Rudolf, his father, by Boniface VIII, and by many others, and in Wenceslaus, son of Charles IV, whom his father, while still living, had brought about to be designated King of the Romans by the Electors. When Gregory XI, to whom the matter had been referred, was prevented by death from being able to decree approval of this, Urban VI, his successor, lawfully completed it.

units.la: CAPUT II.
units.tr: CHAPTER II.

units.la: Quomodo veniente Imperatore mittantur Legati Apostolici.
units.tr: How Apostolic legates are sent when the Emperor is approaching.

units.la: Electus igitur Rom. Rex cum statuerit Urbem petere ad imperiale diadema de manu summi Pontificis suscipiendum, primum convenit per nuncios suos cum Romano antistite de modo & tempore intrandi, ut Pontifex rebus oportune consulere posset. Deinde cum Pontifex noverit Cæsarem jam Italiam intrasse, mittit illi obviam duos Legatos de latere, qui illum conveniunt, antequam terras Romanæ Ecclesiæ ingrediatur. Et post gratulationes, salutationem & benedictionem, nomine Pontificis honesto modo exigunt ab illo juramentum solitum præstari ab electis Imperatoribus, antequam intrent agrum Romanæ Ecclesiæ, in forma quæ in Decretis cavetur, videlicet: Ego R. Rex Romanorum promitto & juro per Patrem & filium & Spiritum sanctum, & per lignum vivificæ crucis, & per barreliquias Sanctorum, quod si permittente Domino Romam venero, sanctam Romanam Ecclesiam, & sanctitatem suam rectorem ipsius, exaltabo secundum posse meum, & nunquam vitam, membrum, neque honorem quem habet, mea voluntate, meo consilio, meo consensu, aut mea exhortatione perdet. Et in Roma nullum placitum aut ordinationem faciam de omnibus quæ ad sanctitatem suam aut ad Romanos pertinent, sine vestro consilio. Et quidquid deterra S. Petri ad nostram potestatem pervenerit, sua sanctitati reddam. Et cuicunque Italicum regimen committo, juraret faciam illum ut adjutor suæ sanctitatis sit ad defendendam terram S. Petri secundum suum posse. Sic me Deus adjuvet, & hæc sancta Evangelia. Aliquando Oratores electi, quando veniunt ad mutandum electionem, & ad petendum approbationem nomine electi Regis, solent præstare supra dictum juramentum si ad hoc habent speciale mandatum. Hoc juramentum Fridericus III. Imp. dum Senis esset, in manibus legatorum Apostolicorum anno salutis M. CCCC. LI. præstitit, & ante eum plures alii.
units.tr: When the elected King of the Romans has decided to make for the City to receive the imperial crown from the hand of the supreme Pontiff, he first agrees, through his messengers, with the Roman bishop on the manner and time of entry, so that the Pontiff may be able to provide for matters in good time. Then, when the Pontiff learns that the Caesar has already entered Italy, he sends to meet him two legates from his side, who meet him before he enters the lands of the Roman Church. After greetings, salutation and blessing, they demand in the Pontiff's name, courteously, the oath customarily taken by elected emperors before they enter the territory of the Roman Church, in the form laid down in the Decretals, namely: I, R., King of the Romans, promise and swear by the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, and by the wood of the life-giving cross, and by the relics of the saints, that if, the Lord permitting, I come to Rome, I will exalt the holy Roman Church and its holy rector, His Holiness, to the best of my power, and I will never allow his life, limb, or the honour which he has to be lost, by my will, my counsel, my consent, or my urging. And in Rome I will make no decree or ordinance concerning all matters which pertain to His Holiness or to the Romans, without your counsel. And whatever comes into my power from the lands of St. Peter, I will restore to His Holiness. And to whomever I entrust the government of Italy, I will cause him to swear that he will be an aid to His Holiness in defending the land of St. Peter to the best of his ability. So help me God, and these holy Gospels. Sometimes envoys of the elect, when they come to change the election and to seek approval in the name of the elected King, are accustomed to take the above oath, if they have a special mandate for this. Frederick III, Emperor, while he was at Siena, took this oath in the hands of the Apostolic legates in the year of salvation 1451, and before him many others did.

units.la: Dehinc, ut primum Ecclesiæ territorium ingressus est Cæsar, consuevit cum sua familia impensis Pontificis ali, quandiu & Romæ & in agro Romano fuerit. Nicolaus verò quamvis Frederico prædicto cum familiaribus quingentis tantum expensas promiserit, longè tamen plures ære suo aluit.
units.tr: Next, as soon as the Caesar has entered the first territory of the Church, he is accustomed to be maintained at the Pontiff's expense, with his household, for as long as he is in Rome and in the Roman territory. Nicholas, indeed, although he promised Frederick, mentioned above, only five hundred retainers' expenses, nevertheless maintained far more at his own cost.

units.la: Ut Sutrium venit Cæsar, vel locum Urbis vicinum, ita ut paucis post applicare ad urbem posset, legati Apostolici illum cum aliquibus Prælatis à Pontifice missis, qui necessaria curent, dimittunt & Romam perveniunt.
units.tr: When the Caesar comes to Sutri, or to a place near the City, so that he can arrive at the city a few days later, the Apostolic legates, with some prelates sent by the Pontiff to attend to necessary arrangements, dismiss him and go on to Rome.

units.la: Sequenti die electus Imperator Romam missus carpit iter: cui honoris gratia obviam mittuntur Pontifice Prælati, Barones, & curiales hoc ordine, ut in Fridericiadventu servatum est. Primi ad lextum lapidem Columnenses proceres cum suis amicis, & clientelis, & mox Ursini atque alii Barones urbis: tum Pontificis copiæ, quæ adsunt cum illarum præfecto: inde Vicecamerarius cum præfecto Urbis, Senatore, conservatoribus officialibus, & aliis nobilibus civibus Romanis: deinde ordines Curiæ, cum regente Cancellariæ, sive alio aliquo Prælato: demum alii Prælati domestici Pontificis cum omni ejus familia: & tandem sacrum Cardinalium Collegium, ad radices montis juxta domum leprosorum Cæsarem expectabunt. Hi omnes distinctis intervallis Imperatori electo obviam bunt. Oratores verò Principum si qui in urbe erunt, pro suo libitu obviam procedent. Cardinales ut Cæsarem convenient, congratulationibus & oblationibus factis nomine Pontificis & Collegii, illum habentes medium inter duos primos Episcopos Cardinales, deducet usque ad tentorium, sive alium locum sibi deputatum extra urbem. Nam Cæsar non consuevit ea die qua appulit, Urbem intrare, sed pernoctare saltem una nocte extra mænia in campis. Cardinales & alij omnes postquam Cæsar ad locum deputatum pervenerit, in Urbem reverterunt.
units.tr: On the following day the elected Emperor sets out on his journey to Rome. To do him honour, the Pontiff's prelates, barons and courtiers go out to meet him in the order observed at the arrival of Frederick. First, at the sixth milestone, the Colonna nobles with their friends and clients, and soon afterwards the Orsini and the other barons of the City; then the Pontiff's troops, who are present with their commander; after them the Vice-Chamberlain with the prefect of the City, the Senator, the conservators, officials and other noble citizens of Rome; then the orders of the Curia, with the regent of the Chancery or some other prelate; last, the other domestic prelates of the Pontiff with his whole household; and finally the sacred College of Cardinals, who will await the Caesar at the foot of the hill near the house of the lepers. All of these will go out to meet the elected Emperor at distinct intervals. The envoys of the princes, if any are in the city, will go out to meet him at their own pleasure. The Cardinals, when they meet the Caesar, having made congratulations and offerings in the name of the Pontiff and the College, will hold him between the two senior Cardinal bishops and escort him as far as the tent, or other place assigned to him outside the city. For the Caesar is not accustomed to enter the City on the day on which he arrives, but at least to spend one night outside the walls in the fields. The Cardinals and all the others, when the Caesar has reached the assigned place, return to the City.

units.la: Consueverunt etiam electi Imperatores hac die antequam ponticulū, qui primus ante ingressum Urbis post descensum montem occurrit, pertransceant, præstare juramentum Romanis in hanc formam. Ego Rex Rom. futurus Imp. juro me servaturum Romanis bonas consuetudines suas, sic Deus me adjuvet.
units.tr: Elected emperors are also accustomed on this day, before they cross the little bridge which first meets them before the entrance to the City, after descending the mountain, to take an oath to the Romans in this form: I, the future Emperor and King of the Romans, swear that I will keep for the Romans their good customs. So help me God.

units.la: CAPUT III.
units.tr: CHAPTER III.

units.la: De Urbis ingressu Imperatoris.
units.tr: On the Emperor's entry into the City.

units.la: Postera die Cæsar per portam, quæ est sub arce S. Angeli hoc ordine quasi triumphans ingreditur. Primo die equites vexilla duo Cæsaris portant, alterum S.Georgii, quod ad Suevorum pertinet custodiam, Aquilæ alterum. Hos sequuntur Cæsaris cohortes armatæ, tum nobiles proceres & togati ejus: inde Oratores Regum & Principum, qui adsunt. Tum si quis adest Rex aut maximus Princeps, ut fuit cum Friderico Rex Ungariæ & Bohemiæ Ladislaus. Et tunc sequitur Præfectus Urbis, & Senator. Et ad Præfectum quidem pertinebat nudum ensem ante Cæsarem ferre: Frederico tamen Marescallus suus, non Præfectus, gladium prætulit. Inter istos autem & Cæsarem nemo equitare debet, nisi Marescallus, si Præfectus non præfert ensem. Incedit Cæsar solus equitans, & post eum Prælati, Consiliarii, proceres inermes, & alii togati sui. Deinde dico intervallo Imperatricis familia, si uxor virum sequitur, succedere debet. Ante illam nobiles prælati: & post matronæ, virgines & pedisequæ: circa eam verò solam equitantem pedites multi timò incedunt Ecclesiasticæ copiæ pompam claudentes. Portam ipsam quæ sub arce ingreditur, nostri Codices falsò Collinam appellant. Collina autem porta non est in novis Leonis Papæ libris, sed in antiqua Roma, Quirinalis primum dicta, deinde Collina (ut scripsit Varro) à pluribus montibus qui in Quirinali monte continebantur: hodie Salaria nuncupatur, quia inde via Salaria. In porta igitur quæ sub arce est, non Collina clerus urbis sacris vestibus ornatus, cum crucibus & sanctorum reliquiis, præsidente Vicario urbis & aliis Ecclesiarum prælatis infulatis Cæsarem exspectant, advenienti cruces deosculandas offerunt, & cum incensant, ac cantantes, Ecce mitto Angelum meum procedunt usque ad gradus Basilicæ principis Apostolorum. Principes autem digniores baldachinum supra Cæsaris caput portant, Conservatores freno equum ducunt. Cum verò est in magna area gradus, Præfectus & Senator id gerunt: & descendente ex equo Cæsare Præfectus stapham tenet, inde ante cum præcedit. Inter equitandum autem Cæsaris Camerarius pecuniam spargere consuevit. In plano supra gradus Basilicæ ante primum porticum ad dextram ascendentibus erigitur suggestus ornatus cum throno Pontificali, & sedibus Cardinalium Prælatorum, & aliorum officialium: quem suggestum Pontifex pluviali & mitra preciosis indutus ascendit cum ordinibus cum iaspaulo tea quàm Cæsar apparet. Electus Imperator cum suis omnibus servato ordine, ut equum descendit per gradus ascendit suggestum. Et ut primum pontificem videt, detecto capite illum genu terram tangens veneratur: & iterum cum appropinquat ad gradus sedis, genu flectit: demum ad Pontificis pedes pervenit, illos in reverentia salvatoris devotè osculatur. Pontifex hilari vultu Cæsarem aspicit ad osculum manus & oris recipit. Tum Cæsar iterum genu flexus auri massam ad pedes Pontificis fert, habetque verba ad Pontificem, gratias agens pro honore suscepto, prout ei videbitur. Pontifex benignè respondens illum sublevat, & summæ caritatis declaratione amplectitur. Et statim ibi ad dextram Pontificis Cæsare, Pontifex recipit Imperatricem ad osculum pedis & manus. Reges verò quis adest, ad osculum pedis, manus & oris: alios autem Prælatos, proceres & nobiles Cæsar ad osculum pedis tantum. His finitis surgit Pontifex, & manu sinistra Cæsarem capiens è suggestu descendit, & pariter ad secundum usque Ecclesiæ porticum cum eo progreditur. Deinde Palatium ascendit, ad Cameram suam reversurus, & Cæsar duobus aut quatuor Cardinalibus sociatus templum ingreditur, Apostolorum sacras reliquias veneraturus cum suis omnibus. Inde ad loca cuique destinata revertuntur. Cæsar postera die oportuno tempore ad Pontificem accedet, & cum eo de incumbentibus ad solennitatem pertractabit. Statuent de die coronationis, & si qua erunt prius peragenda, deliberabunt. Et notandum quod Cæsar, antequam coronetur Imperiali diademate, sedet post primum Episcopum Cardinalem: & si quis Rex adest, sedet tunc post primum presbyterum Cardinalem. Cum verò Cæsar erit coronatus, tunc sedebit in sede sibi parata inter Papam & primum Episcopum Cardinalem: & tunc Rex erit post primum Episcopum Cardinalem.
units.tr: On the following day the Caesar enters the city through the gate beneath the castle of St Angelo, in this order, like a triumphal procession. First, horsemen carry two standards of Caesar: one of St George, which belongs to the guard of the Swabians, and the other the Eagle. These are followed by Caesar's armed cohorts, then his noble lords and his gowned attendants, then the envoys of the kings and princes who are present. Next, if any king or very great prince is present (as there was with Frederick, Ladislaus, King of Hungary and Bohemia), then follow the Prefect of the City and the Senator. It was the Prefect's right to carry a bare sword before Caesar, but for Frederick his Marshal, not the Prefect, carried the sword. No one should ride between these and Caesar except the Marshal, if the Prefect does not carry the sword. Caesar rides alone, and after him come the prelates, councillors, unarmed nobles and his other gowned men. Then, after a short interval, the Empress's household should follow, if the wife accompanies her husband. Before her ride the noble prelates; after her come the matrons, virgins and attendants; and around her alone many foot soldiers walk, the ecclesiastical forces closing the procession. The gate which he enters beneath the castle is wrongly called the Collina gate by our manuscripts. But the Collina gate is not in the new books of Pope Leo; it belongs to ancient Rome, where it was first called Quirinalis and then Collina (as Varro wrote), from the several hills contained in the Quirinal hill. Today it is called Salaria, because the Salarian Way leads from it. So at the gate beneath the castle, which is not the Collina gate, the clergy of the city, adorned with sacred vestments, with crosses and relics of the saints, presided over by the Vicar of the city and other prelates of the churches wearing mitres, await Caesar. As he arrives they offer crosses for him to kiss, and with incense and singing, "Behold, I send my angel," they proceed as far as the steps of the basilica of the Prince of the Apostles. The more distinguished princes carry a canopy over Caesar's head, and the Conservators lead his horse by the bridle. When there is a large open space at the steps, the Prefect and the Senator perform these duties. When Caesar dismounts, the Prefect holds the stirrup and then goes before him. While riding, Caesar's Chamberlain is accustomed to scatter money. On the level ground above the steps of the basilica, before the first portico, on the right as one goes up, a decorated platform is erected with the pontifical throne and seats for the Cardinals, prelates and other officials. The Pope mounts this platform, clothed in a precious cope and mitre, with the orders, when Caesar appears. The Elect Emperor, with all his people, keeping their order, dismounts from his horse and climbs the platform by the steps. As soon as he sees the Pope, he uncovers his head and venerates him, touching the ground with his knee; and again, when he approaches the steps of the seat, he bends the knee. At last he reaches the Pope's feet and devoutly kisses them in reverence for the Saviour. The Pope looks upon Caesar with a cheerful countenance and receives him to the kiss of hand and mouth. Then Caesar, kneeling again, brings a mass of gold to the Pope's feet and speaks to him, giving thanks for the honour received, as he thinks fit. The Pope responds kindly, raises him up and embraces him with a declaration of the greatest affection. At once, with Caesar at the Pope's right, the Pope receives the Empress to the kiss of foot and hand. The kings who are present he receives to the kiss of foot, hand and mouth; the other prelates, nobles and lords Caesar kisses only on the foot. When these things are finished, the Pope rises, takes Caesar by the left hand, descends from the platform and goes with him as far as the second portico of the church. Then the Pope ascends the Palace to return to his chamber, while Caesar, accompanied by two or four Cardinals, enters the temple to venerate the sacred relics of the Apostles, with all his people. From there they return to the places assigned to each. On the following day, at a suitable time, Caesar will come to the Pope and discuss with him the matters pertaining to the solemnity. They will settle the day of the coronation and deliberate on whatever must be done beforehand. It should be noted that Caesar, before he is crowned with the Imperial diadem, sits after the first Cardinal Bishop; and if any King is present, he then sits after the first Cardinal Presbyter. But when Caesar has been crowned, he will sit in the seat prepared for him between the Pope and the first Cardinal Bishop, and then the King will sit after the first Cardinal Bishop.

units.la: CAPUT IIII.
units.tr: CHAPTER IV.

units.la: Processio Pontificis & Caesaris per Urbem.
units.tr: The Procession of the Pope and the Emperor through the City.

units.la: Caesar cum corona in capite, sceptro & pomo in manibus ad latus Pontificis incedens, nisi illius manu ducatur (quia tunc pomum vel sceptrum tantum in sinistra retineret) cum ad finem gradum pervenerit, traditis sceptro & pomo uni ex suis, praevenit ad equum Pontificis, & in honorem Salvatoris nostri Jesu Christi, cujus vices Pontifex in terris gerit, tenet stapham, quo ad Pontifex equum ascenderit. Et deinde accepto equi freno per aliquot passus ducit equum Pontificis. Pontifex, dum Imperator haec civilitatis officia vult exhibere, debet aliquantulum modeste recusare: & tandem cum aliquibus bonis verbis honorem non in personam suam, sed illius cujus locum tenet, net, recipiendo permittit illum aliquantulum progredi. Tum firmat se, & nullo pacto permittit Cæsarem ulterius ire. Qui mox conscenso equo suo accedit ad sinistrum latus Pontificis, & sub eodem baldachino equitat, & hoc ordine procedunt. Primum præcedant familiæ Cardinalium, cum suis valilIiis: & simul mixtæ familiæ Prælatorum, Principum, & omnium curialium tam Cæsaris quàm Pontificis. Deinde duo cum valisiis Pontificis. Inde familiares domestici Imperatorns, & post eos familiares Papæ. Tum Nobiles, & Barones, & Comites minores utriusque, equus cum scala Papæ tum vexilla rubea, quæ duodecim cursores portant; Deinde vexillum Populi Romani, vexillum Imperii, vexillum Papæ, vexillum Ecclesiæ, vexillum Crucis, cum vexilliferis armatis & ornatis, utin coronatione Papæ. Hos sequuntur duodecim equi phalerati sine sessoribus: deinde quatuor nobiles portantes pilea ex cramisino quatuor Papæ cum baculis. Quibus succedunt advocati & secretarii mixtim, secundum prioritatem officii procedentes, cum suis capuciis circa collum; quos etiam præcedunt Secretarii Imperatoris. Tum sequuntur Cubicularii etiam cum suis capuciis: inde Acolythi clerici Camerae Apostolicæ, & post eos statim Auditores cum rochetis & cappis. Deinde Subdiaconi cum cruce Papali, cum galero indici coloris, & cum aliis Subdiaconis cum cappis, ut alii. Duo portantes laternas cum lumine ante Sacramentum equitantes: deinde equus albus phaleratus cum tintinnabulo portans Sacramentum; & supra illud Sacramentum baldachinum percives Romanos portatur, & circa duodecim intorticia quæ portantur per duodecim familiares Papæ, sive per decem beneficiatos S. Petri cum superpelliciis, post Sacramentum equitat Sacrista cum feriulis alba. Inde si qui sunt maximi Domini, Principes, aut Duces. Principes Electores immediatè ante Cardinales procedunt: & si quis adsit frater aut filius Imperatoris, iret medius inter juniores Diaconos Cardinales. Rex erit à ministris Episcopi Cardinalis: & si plures adessent Reges, locarentur cum Episcopis Cardinalibus. Sequuntur duo Diaconi Cardinales assistentes Pontifici. Et si cum essent duo Principes Electores, qui præferrent gladium & pomum Cæsaris, isti deberent ire diatè ante Cæsarem, sicut Diaconi ante Pontificem: & quando via esset arcta, irent ante ipsos Diaconos assistentes. Si vero non sint Principes Electores, qui portent illa, videlicet gladium, pomum, seu sceptrum (nam alterum istorum duorum portabit Imperator) illi duo vadant timul cum Subdiacono qui portabit crucem, & illum in medio habeant. Sequitur Pontifex sub baldachino, & imperator cum sua corona & imperiali habitu à ministris. Post Pontificem sequuntur duo Cubicularii secreti cum sceptro vacante & mitra: & duo Medici cum secretario, si non sit Prælatus. Et post Imperatorem duo Camerarii sint cum uno secretario cum umbella. Deinde Prælati assistentes Papæ. Et si quis Archiepiscopus Elector Imperatoris adesset, iret ante assistentes Papæ. Post quos ibunt Praelati assistentes sive Consiliarii Imperatoris, cum cappis & galeris, ut alii Prælati: alias non irent inter cappatos. Sequuntur deinde Prælati, Oratores, Archiepiscopi, Episcopi, Protonotarii & Abbates, Cappati & Pileati: & demum alii curiales togati, tam Papæ quàm Cæsaris. Hoc ordine recta via per campum Florae & Judæorum plateam ad Ecclesiam S. Mariæ in Cosmedin. Et ibi Pontifex, si rosam habet, dat equo Imperatori equiti donandum: & ad dextram conversus trans Tiberim cum suis omnibus ad Palatium revertitur. Cæsar autem via quæ sibi melius placet, rosam manu gestans, ad pontem Adriani redit: ubi viros complures & de se optimè meritos equestri dignitate insignire solet.
units.tr: The Emperor, with the crown on his head and the sceptre and orb in his hands, walks at the Pope's left side, unless the Pope leads him by the hand (since he would then hold only the orb or the sceptre in his left hand). When he has come to the end of the steps, he hands the sceptre and orb to one of his men and hurries to the Pope's horse. In honour of our Saviour Jesus Christ, whose vicar the Pope bears on earth, he holds the stirrup until the Pope has mounted. Then, taking the bridle, he leads the Pope's horse for a few paces. While the Emperor wishes to perform these courtesies, the Pope should modestly decline for a little while. At last, with some kind words, he allows the Emperor to lead the horse a little way, accepting the honour not for his own person but for the one whose place he holds. Then he stands firm and by no means allows Caesar to go any further. The Emperor then mounts his own horse, comes to the Pope's left side, and rides under the same canopy. They proceed in this order. First come the households of the Cardinals with their valises, together with the households of the prelates, princes and all the courtiers of both the Emperor and the Pope. Next come two men with the Pope's valises, then the Emperor's household familiars, and after them the Pope's familiars. Then the nobles, barons and lesser counts of both, with the Pope's horse and ladder, and then the red banners carried by twelve couriers. Next come the banner of the Roman People, the banner of the Empire, the banner of the Pope, the banner of the Church and the banner of the Cross, with armed and decorated standard-bearers, as at the coronation of the Pope. These are followed by twelve caparisoned horses without riders, and then four nobles carrying the Pope's crimson caps and staves. After them come advocates and secretaries, mixed together, proceeding according to the precedence of their office, with their hoods around their necks; the secretaries of the Emperor precede them. Then come the chamberlains, also with their hoods, then the acolytes of the Apostolic Chamber, and immediately after them the auditors in rochets and copes. Next come the subdeacons with the Papal cross, wearing an indigo-coloured galero, and the other subdeacons in copes like the rest. Two men carrying lanterns with light ride before the Sacrament. Then comes a white caparisoned horse with a bell, carrying the Sacrament; over the Sacrament a canopy is carried by Roman citizens. About it are twelve torches carried either by twelve familiars of the Pope or by ten beneficed men of St Peter in surplices. Behind the Sacrament rides the sacristan with a white wand. Then come the greatest lords, princes or dukes, if any are present. The Electoral Princes proceed immediately before the Cardinals; and if a brother or son of the Emperor is present, he should walk between the junior Cardinal deacons. A king will be placed among the ministers of the Cardinal bishop, and if several kings were present, they would be placed with the Cardinal bishops. Two Cardinal deacons assisting the Pope follow. If there are two Electoral Princes to carry the sword and the orb or sceptre of the Emperor, they should go directly before the Emperor, just as the deacons go before the Pope; and when the way is narrow, they should go before the assisting deacons. If there are no Electoral Princes to carry those things, namely the sword, the orb or the sceptre (for the Emperor will carry one of these two), then those two should go together with the subdeacon who carries the cross, and have him between them. The Pope follows under the canopy, and the Emperor, with his crown and imperial vestments, is attended by the ministers. Behind the Pope follow two secret chamberlains with a vacant sceptre and mitre, and two physicians with a secretary, unless a prelate is present. And behind the Emperor there should be two chamberlains with one secretary carrying the umbrella. Then come the prelates assisting the Pope. If an Archbishop who is an Elector of the Emperor were present, he would go before the assisting prelates of the Pope. After them go the prelates assisting, or counsellors of the Emperor, in copes and galeros like the other prelates; otherwise they would not walk among those in copes. Then follow the prelates, orators, archbishops, bishops, protonotaries and abbots, both those in copes and those wearing caps, and finally the other courtiers in gowns, both of the Pope and of the Emperor. In this order they proceed straight through the Field of Flora and the Jews' square to the Church of St Mary in Cosmedin. There, if the Pope has the golden rose, he gives it to the Emperor, who is mounted, to be given away; and turning to the right, he returns across the Tiber with all his people to the Palace. The Emperor, however, by whichever way pleases him best, carrying the rose in his hand, returns to the Bridge of Hadrian, where he is accustomed to honour several men who have deserved well of him with the dignity of knighthood.

units.la: Quo facto ad Lateranum cum suis progreditur. Canonici & Capitulum Ecclesiæ supplicabunt Cæsari in porta principali occurrentes, illum honorificè suscipiunt, & postquam Crucem & quias osculatus fuerit, incensant, & præcedentes atque cantantes; Te Deum laudamus, ad altare deducunt: ubi procumbens supra saldisterium orat detecto capite. Deinde surgens osculatur tum resumpta corona recipitur in Canonicum & fratrem Ecclesiæ Lateranensis, & Canonicos omnes recipit ad osculum pacis. Quibus finitis, ascendit ad Palatium Lateranense, & cum suis celebrat solenne convivium suis moribus & ceremoniis. Deinde si placet, recurrit ad Palatium Apostolicum ad cameras suas.
units.tr: Having done this, he proceeds with his people to the Lateran. The canons and chapter of the church, meeting the Emperor at the main gate, supplicate him, receive him with honour, and after he has kissed the cross and the relics, they incense him; going before him and singing "We praise thee, O God," they lead him to the altar. There he kneels upon the faldstool and prays with his head uncovered. Then, rising, he kisses the altar, and after the crown is taken up again, he is received as a canon and brother of the Lateran church, and he gives the kiss of peace to all the canons. When these things are finished, he goes up to the Lateran Palace and celebrates a solemn banquet with his people, according to their customs and ceremonies. Then, if he pleases, he returns to the Apostolic Palace, to his chambers.

units.la: CAPUT V.
units.tr: CHAPTER V.

units.la: De Coronatione Imperatricis sine Imperatore.
units.tr: On the Coronation of an Empress without the Emperor.

units.la: Imperatrix si venit Romam pro corona Imperiali suscipienda sine Imperatore, vel quod non potuit venire cum eo, vel quod post ejus coronationem ei est conjuncta, hoc ordine coronatur. Die qua Urbem intrabit, procedentes obviam nobiles & officiales Urbis, & ordines Curiæ, ut do Cæsare dictum est. Sacer Senatus ante portam Urbis eam expectabit, & media inter duos Cardinales Diaconos introducetur. In fine autem & sub baldachino, clero cum processione in porta illi occurrente, ducetur ad Pontificem: qui eam in publico consistorio in prima aula ad pedis & manus osculum recipiet, ut alii Reges recipi consueverunt. Non tamen sedebit inter Cardinales; sed post osculum pedis & manus discedet ad suum hospitium. Deinde parabitur in Ecclesia S. Petri suggestus extra cancellos pro Imperatrice: & dicta die Pontifex procedet ad Ecclesiam, supplicatione præcunte sub baldachino, & paramentis temporiqu congruis ascendit ad altare, orat, sedet. Interim duo juniores Diaconi Cardinales cum suis cappis laneis ducunt Augustam ad Ecclesiam. Et prior Episcopus Cardinalis cum pluviali, stola & mitra accedens in tempore expectat eam in porta Ecclesiæ principali, ibi super eam genu flectentem depositæ mitra legit hanc orationem: Omnipotens sempiterne Deus, sponsi origo totius bonitatis, qui fœminei sexus fragilitatem nequaquam reprobando avertu, sed dignanter comprobando pertinet. tim eligis; & qui infirma mundi quaeque, ut fortia confunderet, eligenda decreuit; quisque etiam gloriae virtutisque nec triumphu in manu foeminae Iudaica olim plebis de hoste sceleratissimo assignare voluisti: Respice quaesumus ad preces hu-militatis nostrae, ut supra hanc famulam tuam N. quam supplici devotione Imperatricem eligimus, benedictionum tua-rum dona multiplices, eamque dextera tua potentia semper & ubique circumda: & ut dono tui numinis undique firmi-ter adjuta, ut visibilis seu invisibilis hostis nequitias triumphaliter expugnare valeat; ut una cum sacra Rebecca, Lea, atque Iudith, beata reverendiqe foeminae, fructu uteri sui foecundari seu gratulari mereatur, ad decorem totius Imperii, sta-tumque S. Ecclesiae regendum nec non protegendum. Per Christum Dominum nostrum qui ex intemerata B. Mariae virginis utero nasci, vivere, & renovare dignatus est mundum. Qui tecum vivit & gloriatur Deus in unitate Spiritus S. per immor-talia saecula saeculorum, Amen. Ducitur deinde ad confessionem B. Petri, & procumbit supra faldistorium sibi loco paratum. Et a Subdiacono Apostolico fit Litania: & ea finita prior Presbyterorum cum suis paramentis ad confessionem descendens, stans sine mitra, dicit super eam, Pater noster: & deinde: Et ne nos inducas in tentationem. Respond. Sed libera nos a malo. Verf. Salvam fac ancillam tuam Domine. Respond. Deus meus sperantem in te. Verf. Esto ei quae sumus Domine turris fortitudinis. Respond. Nihil proficiat inimicus in ea. Respond. Et filius iniquitatis non apponat nocere ei. Verf. Domine exaudi orationem meam. R. Et clamor meus ad te veniat. Verf. Dominus vobiscum. Resp. Et cum spiritu tuo. Oremus. Praetende quaesumus Domine famulae tuae caelestis dexteram auxilii, ut te toto corde perquirat, & quae digne postulat, consequi mereatur. Actiones nostras quaesumus Domine adjuvando praeveni, & adjuvando prosequere, ut cuncta nostra operatio & oratio a te semper incipiat, & per te coepta finiatur, per Christum Dominum nostrum. Amen. Finitis orationibus revertitur Presbyter ad locum suum, & prior Episcoporum Cardinalium procedit ad altare S. Mauritii, quem Augusta media inter Diaconos sequitur. Et ibi aute altare Episcopus ipse inungit illam stantem de oleo exorcizato brachium dexterum & scapulas, stans cum mitra dicens: Spiritus Sancti gratia nostrae humilitatis officio copiosa in te descendat, ut sicut manibus nostris licet indigna oleo materiali oblimita pinguescit extrinsecus, ita ejus invisibili unguine delibuta impinguaret mentem mentis, ejusque Spiritali unctione perfectissime semper imbuta, & illucita declinaretur tota mente & spernere dulcias & valeas & ulla animae tuae juguer opitare atque operari queas, et operetur auxiliante Domino nostro Jesu Christo: quoniam Patre per id regnat in unitate, etc. Reducitur deinde ad suggestum suum Imperatrix, & Cardinales tever.untur ad Pontificem, & Diaconi quidem depositis cappis capiunt paramenta sibi convenientia, & faciunt reverentiam Pontifici. Deinde Pontifex procedit ad altare per supplicationem, occurrunt tres Presbyteri, cantantur introitus a cantoribus, & procediturin Missa usque ad graduale. Imperatrix a Diaconis illis quamvis paratis ducitur aute Pontificem: qui surgens depositia nuda super eam ante se genuflexam dicit hanc orationem: Deus qui solus habes immortalitatem, lucemque habitas inaccessibilem, cujus prudentia in sua dispositione non fallitur, qui fecisti ea quae futura sunt, & vocas ea quae non sunt, qui superbos aqua mo-deramine de principatu eicit, atque humiles dignanter in sublime provehis, mirabili misericordiam tuam supplicis exoramus, ut sicut Hester reginam Israelitica causa salutis de captivitate sua compede solutam ad Regis Assueri thalamum regniqui suis consortium transfere fecisti, ita hanc famulam tuam N. humilitatis nostrae benedictione Christiana plebis salutis gratia, ad dignam sublimemque Imperatoris nostri copulam & Imperii sui participatum transfere concedas, & ut Imperialis sedere conjugii semper permanens pudicitia proximam virginum palmam consequi queat: tibi viro ac vero in omnibus & super omnia jugiter placere desideret, & te in parante quae tibi placita sunt, toto corde facere, per Christum Dominum nostrum, Amen. Deinde sedens cum mitra, imponit illi tiaram cum corona Imperiali allatam sibi ex altari, ut diximus de Imperatore, & dicit: Officio nostrae indignitatis in Imperatricem solemniter benedicta, accipe coronam Imperialis excellentiae; quae licet ab indignis, Episcopalibus tamen mantis capiti tuo imponitur. Undefficiat auro & gemmis redimita nites, ita & interna auro sapientia virtutumque gemma decorari concedat: quatenus posti occasionem hujus saeculi cum prudentibus Virginibus sponso perenni Domino Jesu Christo digne & laudabiliter occurrens regni coelestis aulae ingredi mereatis famulari, eodem Domino nostro auxiliante, quem Patre, etc. Coronata Imperatrix mox osculatur pedem Pontificis cum corona, & surgens reducit a Diaconis ad suggestum: & cum canturur deinde offertorium, revertatur ad Pontificem, & offerat aurum quantum placet. Deinde si vult communicare de Sacramento altaris (ut congruum est) procumbat supra faldistorium ad partem convenientem sitem (ut superius diximus) & orent quousquesit tempus, sine corona tamen: & cum Pontifex in sede sua eminenti communicaverit, ducitur Imperatrix sine corona ad ejus pedes, & communicet, osculaturque manum Pontificis, & descendens ad altare purificet cum vino. Deinde assumpta corona reducetur ad suum suggestum. Et quod Imperatrix deducetur semper eundo, & redeundo ab illis duobus Diaconis, sive paratis sive non paratis: & illam sociabunt sui Praelati, & proceres, atque matronae & aliae mulieres. Finita missa Imperatrix deducitur ad suum hospitium.
units.tr: If the Empress comes to Rome to receive the Imperial crown without the Emperor, either because she could not come with him or because she was joined to him after his coronation, she is crowned in this order. On the day she enters the City, the nobles and officials of the City and the orders of the Court go out to meet her, as was said concerning the Emperor. The Sacred Senate waits for her before the gate of the City, and she is led in between two cardinal deacons. Then, under a canopy, with the clergy coming in procession to meet her at the gate, she is taken to the Pontiff, who receives her in public consistory in the first hall with the kissing of foot and hand, as other kings are customarily received.
