She does not, however, sit among the cardinals; after the kissing of foot and hand she withdraws to her lodging. Then a platform is prepared in the church of St Peter, outside the rails, for the Empress. On the appointed day the Pontiff proceeds to the church, with the litany going before him under a canopy, and, in vestments suitable to the season, ascends to the altar, prays, and sits. Meanwhile the two junior cardinal deacons, in their woollen copes, lead the Augusta to the church. The senior cardinal bishop, in cope, stole and mitre, comes forward at the proper time and waits for her at the main door of the church, where, as she kneels before him, he lays aside his mitre and reads this prayer: Almighty and eternal God, origin of all goodness, who, far from rejecting the frailty of the female sex, graciously approves it, and who chose the weak things of the world to confound the strong, and who once willed that the triumph and glory over the most wicked enemy should be given into the hand of a Jewish woman: we beseech you, look upon the prayers of our lowliness, and, over this your servant N., whom we choose as Empress with humble devotion, multiply the gifts of your blessings, and encompass her always and everywhere with your mighty right hand; and, being strengthened on every side by the gift of your divine power, may she be able to overcome triumphantly the wickedness of the visible and invisible enemy; so that, together with the holy Rebecca, Leah and Judith, blessed and reverend women, she may deserve to be made fruitful in the fruit of her womb and to rejoice in it, for the honour of the whole Empire and for the ruling and protecting of the state of the holy Church. Through Christ our Lord, who deigned to be born, to live and to renew the world from the undefiled womb of the blessed Virgin Mary; who with you lives and reigns, God, in the unity of the Holy Spirit, for ever and ever. Amen. She is then led to the confession of St Peter and kneels upon a faldstool prepared for her there. The litany is sung by the Apostolic subdeacon; when it is finished, the senior of the elders goes down to the confession in his vestments and, standing without a mitre, says over her: Our Father; and then: And lead us not into temptation. Response: But deliver us from evil. Verse: Save your handmaid, O Lord. Response: My God, who trusts in you. Verse: Be to her, we beseech you, Lord, a tower of strength. Response: Let the enemy have no advantage against her. Response: Nor let the son of iniquity presume to harm her. Verse: O Lord, hear my prayer. Response: And let my cry come to you. Verse: The Lord be with you. Response: And with your spirit. Let us pray. Stretch forth, we beseech you, Lord, the right hand of heavenly help to your servant, that she may seek you with her whole heart and deserve to obtain what she worthily asks. Go before our actions, we beseech you, Lord, with your help, and follow them with your help, so that all our work and prayer may always begin from you and be finished through you; through Christ our Lord. Amen. When the prayers are finished the elder returns to his place, and the senior of the cardinal bishops goes to the altar of St Maurice, and the Augusta follows him between the deacons. There, in front of the altar, the bishop himself anoints her, standing with his mitre, on the right arm and shoulders with exorcised oil, saying: May the grace of the Holy Spirit descend upon you abundantly through the office of our unworthy lowliness, so that, as our hands, though unworthy, are smeared with material oil and become fat outwardly, so your mind may be anointed by its invisible unction and made fat inwardly, and may be always perfectly imbued with its spiritual unction, and may be turned wholly from evil to shun sweet things and ... and may be able to labour and act for the good of your soul, with the help of our Lord Jesus Christ, who with the Father, etc. The Empress is then led back to her platform, and the cardinals turn to the Pontiff; the deacons, laying aside their copes, take up vestments suited to them and make reverence to the Pontiff. Then the Pontiff proceeds to the altar with the procession; the three elders meet him; the introit is sung by the cantors, and the Mass proceeds as far as the gradual. The Empress is led by the deacons, who are now vested, before the Pontiff; he rises, and, with mitre laid aside, standing over her as she kneels before him, says this prayer: God, who alone has immortality and dwells in light unapproachable, whose wisdom is not deceived in his disposition, who made those things which are to come and calls those things which are not, who casts the proud from their dominion by the measure of your rule and kindly raises the humble to high station: we humbly beseech your wondrous mercy, that as you caused Esther, queen of Israel, for the sake of the salvation of her people, to be loosed from the fetters of her captivity and brought to the bed of King Ahasuerus and to the fellowship of his kingdom, so you may grant that this your servant N., by the blessing of our lowliness and for the saving grace of the Christian people, may be brought to the worthy and high union of our Emperor and to the sharing of his Empire; and that, remaining always in the chastity of the imperial marriage, she may be able to attain the palm next to that of virgins; and that she may desire always to please you, the true husband, in all things and above all things, and to do with her whole heart what is pleasing to you; through Christ our Lord. Amen. Then, seated and wearing his mitre, he places upon her the tiara with the Imperial crown, brought to him from the altar as we said concerning the Emperor, and says: By the office of our unworthiness, accept, solemnly blessed Empress, the crown of imperial excellence; which, though placed upon your head by unworthy hands, is nevertheless Episcopal. May it grant that, as you shine adorned with gold and jewels, so you may also be adorned within with the gold of wisdom and the gem of virtues; so that, when the occasion of this age has passed, you may worthily and praiseworthily go to meet the eternal Lord Jesus Christ with the prudent virgins, and may deserve to enter and serve in the hall of the heavenly kingdom, with the same Lord our Lord helping, who with the Father, etc. The crowned Empress straightway kisses the foot of the Pontiff, still crowned; and rising, she is led back by the deacons to her platform. When the offertory is sung, she returns to the Pontiff and offers as much gold as she pleases. Then, if she wishes to communicate of the Sacrament of the altar (as is fitting), she kneels upon the faldstool at the proper place on the side (as we said above) and prays for as long as is the custom, but without the crown; and when the Pontiff has communicated in his high seat, the Empress, without her crown, is led to his feet and communicates, and kisses the hand of the Pontiff, and, going down to the altar, purifies her fingers with wine. Then, taking up the crown again, she is returned to her platform. The Empress is always escorted, both going and returning, by those two deacons, whether vested or not; and her prelates, nobles, matrons and other women accompany her. When the Mass is finished the Empress is led to her lodging.

units.la: CAPUT VI. De Coronatione Imperatoris absente Papa.
units.tr: Chapter 6. On the Coronation of the Emperor When the Pope Is Absent.

units.la: Si quando autem acciderit, quod propter absentiam summi Pontificis ab Urbe Caesar non possit ab ipso Pontifice coronari, consuevit Pontifex mittere ad Urbem aliquem Episcopum Cardinalem, qui simul cum legato Apostolico qui Urbi praeest, Imperatorem electum coronet. Si autem ille Episcopus Cardinalis, non esset necessarium mittere alium Episcopum, sed quemcumque vellet alium Presbyterum Cardinalem. Et tunc procederetur hoc modo.
units.tr: If, however, it should happen that, because the supreme Pontiff is absent from the City, the Emperor cannot be crowned by the Pontiff himself, the Pontiff is accustomed to send to the City some Cardinal Bishop, who, together with the Apostolic legate who presides over the City, crowns the elected Emperor. If, however, that Cardinal were not available, it would not be necessary to send another Bishop, but any other Cardinal Priest he wished might be sent. And then the procedure would be as follows.

units.la: Electus Imperator ad Urbem veniens pro corona Imperiali, habebit obviam Barones, nobiles, officiales, civesque Urbis, & officiales curiae Romanae, & remanebit extra moenia illa nocte, ut supra dictum est. Sequenti die intrabit per portam sub arce S. Angeli, quae (ut diximus) non est Collina cum Principibus ordine praedicto. Et in porta recipietur à vicario Pontificis, cum Praelatis, & clero Urbis in modum supplicantium paratis. Et deducetur ut supra ad gradus Basilicae S.Petri, ibique non per suggestum sed ante primas portas recipietur ad osculum tantum per Episcopum Cardinalem coronatorem, & legatum, qui ibi aderunt cum aliis Praelatis curiae parati cum pluvialibus & mitris. Aderunt etiam cum Cardinalibus officiales curiae, Subdiaconi, Auditores, Acoluthi, & si qui sunt, & etiam Barones, aliique nobiles Romanae Ecclesiae. Et electus statim post osculum offeret duobus Cardinalibus, quod offerre debet Pontifici, & dicat haec verba: Si sanctissimus Pater noster N. Pontifex praesens hic esset, offerrem illi aurum istud praesens: sed per ejus absentiam offero ipsum vobis Episcopo & Legato Cardinalibus, recipientibus illud vice & nomine dicti Domini nostri Papae.
units.tr: The elected Emperor, coming to the City for the Imperial crown, will have the barons, nobles, officials and citizens of the City, and the officials of the Roman curia, meet him, and he will remain outside the walls that night, as has been said above. On the following day he will enter through the gate below the castle of St. Angelo, which (as we have said) is not the Collina gate, with the princes in the order described. At the gate he will be received by the Pope's vicar, with the prelates and clergy of the City arranged in the manner of suppliants. He will be led, as above, to the steps of the Basilica of St. Peter, and there, not from a platform but before the first doors, he will be received only with a kiss by the Cardinal Bishop who is to crown him and by the legate, who will be there with the other prelates of the curia, prepared with copes and mitres. The Cardinals will also be present, together with the officials of the curia, the subdeacons, auditors, acolytes and whoever else there may be, and also the barons and other nobles of the Roman Church. Immediately after the kiss, the elect shall offer to the two Cardinals what he ought to offer to the Pope, and say these words: If our most holy Father N., the Pontiff, were present here, I would offer this gold to him in person; but since he is absent, I offer it to you, the Cardinal Bishop and Legate, to receive in the place and name of the said Lord Pope.

units.la: Quo facto intrabunt porticum, & si tunc erit procedendum ad solemnitatem coronationis, quod commodè & decenter fieri potest, ibi supra altare S. Mariae in Turribus praestabit juramentum fidelitatis in manibus Cardinalium. Et similiter si aliud juramentum esset innovandum seu confirmandum, tunc immediatè innovabit. Deinde recipietur ad Canonicum Ecclesiae S.Petri, ut supra dictum est. Intrabit deinde Ecclesiam, & ibi ante portam argenteam Episcopus Cardinalis dicet per eum primam orationem. Deinde ducitur ad capellam S.Gregorii ad capienda sua ornamenta & Episcopus Cardinalis vadit ad altare majus, & ibi super faldisterium capit landalia, & omnia Pontificalia. Et nota quod debet habere expresse facultatem à Pontifice super altare B. Petri celebrandi, ut moris est. Caesar induetus imperialibus indumentis venit ad medium Ecclesiae, & ibi super eum legatus Apostolicus dicet secundam orationem. Veniet deinde ad confessionem B.Petri, & procumbet in faldisterio: & Diaconus qui servit in Missa facit super eum Litaniam, orationem autem cum versiculis & Pater Noster dicet legatus Apostolicus. Deinde ducetur ad altare S. Mariae, & ibi inungetur à Cardinali celebrante, tam ipse quàm Augusta, si adest, cum orationibus opportunis. Revertentur deinde ad altare, ut facta confessione Imperator ad suggestum sine osculo pacis, ad sua disterum suum revertitur. Et proceditur in missa usque ad graduale. Dum cantatur graduale, Imperator descendit ad altare, & celebrante Cardinali ante altare stans cum mitra, gladium sumit de altari, & illum nudum Imperatori tradit, dicens: Accipe gladium, &c. Et idem dicit Legatus, submissa voce: Det tibi idem mox pomum & sceptrum cum sua oratione Ecclesiae modo. Mitras autem & coronas imperiales ambo imponent Caesari & Augustae. Sed legatus alta voce profert verba: Accipe signum, &c. Et celebrans dicit eadem voce submissa.
units.tr: When this is done, they shall enter the portico, and if the solemnity of the coronation is then to proceed, which can be done conveniently and decently, he will there, above the altar of St. Mary in Turribus, take the oath of fidelity into the hands of the Cardinals. Likewise, if another oath is to be renewed or confirmed, he will renew it at once. Then he will be received at the canons' house of the Church of St. Peter, as has been said above. Then he will enter the church, and there, before the silver door, the Cardinal Bishop will say the first prayer for him. Then he is led to the chapel of St. Gregory to take up his vestments, and the Cardinal Bishop goes to the high altar and there takes from the faldstool the sandals and all the pontifical vestments. And note that he must have express faculty from the Pope to celebrate at the altar of St. Peter, as is customary. The Emperor, clothed in imperial garments, comes into the middle of the church, and there the Apostolic legate says the second prayer over him. He then comes to the confession of St. Peter and kneels on the faldstool, and the deacon who serves at Mass says the Litany over him; the legate says the prayer with its versicles and the Our Father. Then he is led to the altar of St. Mary, and there he is anointed by the celebrating Cardinal, both he and the Augusta, if she is present, with suitable prayers. They then return to the altar, and, the confession having been made, the Emperor returns to his platform without the kiss of peace, to his faldstool. And the Mass proceeds as far as the gradual. While the gradual is sung, the Emperor goes down to the altar, and the celebrating Cardinal, standing before the altar with his mitre, takes the sword from the altar and hands it bare to the Emperor, saying: Receive the sword, etc. The legate likewise says, in a low voice: may he presently give him the orb and the sceptre, with their prayer, in the manner of the Church. Both of them place the mitres and the imperial crowns on the Emperor and the Augusta. But the legate pronounces the words in a loud voice: Receive the sign, etc. And the celebrant says them in the same low voice.

units.la: Coronati Augustus & Augusta revertuntur ad suos suggestus sine osculo pacis: & ad offertorium veniunt cum coronis & habitu Imperiali. Et oblato auro revertuntur ad suggestus, neque ministrabit Imperator calicem & ampullam, sed tempore congruo veniet ad communionem sine manto & coronis. Post communionem Imperatori non dabitur osculum pacis à celebrante, sed revertetur ad suum suggestum.
units.tr: The crowned Augustus and Augusta return to their platforms without the kiss of peace, and they come to the offertory with their crowns and imperial dress. When the gold has been offered, they return to their platforms; the Emperor does not minister the chalice and cruet, but at a suitable time he comes to communion without mantle and crowns. After communion the celebrant does not give the Emperor the kiss of peace, but he returns to his platform.

units.la: Imperator finita missa ipse cum suis & cum Legato si placebit, ibit Lateranum, & ibi perficiet suas solennitates. Ceremoniae omnes, quae pertinent ad personam Pontificis, dimittantur, ut oculum pedum, manuum, & oris. Quin etiam nec in missa illi deserviet Imperator, quod Pontifici praesenti: nec stapham illi, dum equum inscendit, tenet, nec equum ducit.
units.tr: When Mass is finished, the Emperor, with his people and with the legate if he is willing, goes to the Lateran and there completes his solemnities. All the ceremonies that pertain to the person of the Pontiff are omitted, such as kissing the feet, hands and mouth. Indeed, the Emperor does not even serve him at Mass, as he would the reigning Pontiff, nor does he hold the stirrup for him when he mounts his horse, nor lead his horse.

units.la: * Cujus etiam exstant super coronatione Romana tam Imperatoris, quam Imperatricis Constitutiones unae atque alterae, quas a Frehero expectamus edendas.
units.tr: * There also survive, concerning the Roman coronation both of the Emperor and of the Empress, one or another constitution, which we await from Freher for publication.

units.la: Haec fere omnia servata fuerunt, cum * Carolus IIII. coronatus fuit Romae per Dominum Episcopum Hostiensem, quem ex Avione Innocentius VI. nuncium Apostolicum ad hoc miserat per Dom. Aegidium de Albornozio Tit. S. Clementis Presbyterum Cardinalem ac Legatum Apostolicum in Italia, Anno Salutis M.CCC.LVI. sexto nonas Aprilis: ut ex literis ipsius Caroli adhuc extant, & registratae sunt in archivis Ecclesiae, publicè patet. Voluit tamen Idem Pontifex, quod Cardinales praedicti publicè protestarentur Domino Imperatori, quod propter omissionem verentiarum, obsequiorum, & multarum ceremoniarum, quae pertinent ad personam Romani Pontificis, non esset aliquo modo derogatum privilegiis & honorificentiis Romanae sedis & suorum successorum, cessorum: & de hac protestatione & consensu Imperatoris exigerent quadruplices literas regalibus & Imperatoris sigillis munitas, sicut & factum est.
units.tr: Nearly all of these things were observed when * Charles IV was crowned at Rome by the Lord Bishop of Ostia, whom Innocent VI sent from Avignon as Apostolic nuncio for this purpose, through Lord Giles of Albornoz, Cardinal Priest of the title of St. Clement and Apostolic legate in Italy, in the year of salvation 1356, on the sixth day before the nones of April, as is publicly evident from the letters of Charles himself, which still survive and are recorded in the archives of the Church. Nevertheless, the same Pontiff wished that the aforesaid Cardinals should publicly protest to the Lord Emperor that, on account of the omission of the reverences, the obsequies, and many ceremonies which pertain to the person of the Roman Pontiff, nothing was in any way derogated from the privileges and honours of the Roman See and of its successors; and that, concerning this protest and the Emperor's consent, they should obtain letters in quadruplicate, fortified with the royal and imperial seals, as was indeed done.

units.la: MAXIMILIANI I. IMP. AUG. GRAVAMINA Adversus Sedem ac Curiam Romanam.
units.tr: The Gravamina of the Emperor Maximilian I, August, against the See and Court of Rome.

units.la: ARTICULUS LI. De idololatrico ritu in baptisandis campanis.
units.tr: Article 51. Concerning the idolatrous rite in baptizing bells.

units.la: Tem suffraganei excogitaverunt, ut solum ipsi, & nullus alius sacerdos, campanas baptizent. Credunt deinde simpliciores, ita affirmantibus Suffraganeis, tales campanas baptizatas, Daemones & tempestates pellere. Quapropter innumeri plerumque adhibentur Compatres, praecipuè verò, qui fortunâ pollent, exorantur, qui baptizationis tempore funem, quâ campana ligata est, tangunt, ac Suffraganeo praecinente (quemadmodum in parvulorum baptizatione fieri solet) omnes pariter respondent, ac campanæ nomen ingeminant, vestéque nova (quemadmodum à Christianis fieri solet) campana induitur. Inde ad sumptuosa properatur convivia, quibus praecipuè Compatres, ut eò largius munera offerant, adhibentur: necnon Suffraganei, & eorum Capellani, cum multis aliis ministris, regaliter pascuntur. Nec hoc satis est, sed & Suffraganeo mercedem persolvere necesse est, quam illi munusculum vocare solent. Inde evenit, ut aliquando etiam in parvis villis, centum floreni in tali absumantur & expendantur baptizatione. Quæ res non solùm superstitiosa, sed etiam Christianæ religioni contraria, ac simpliciorum seductio, & mera est exactio. Verùmtamen Episcopi, ut Suffraganeos vel vilissima obærare possint mercede, talia, & adhuc absurdiora, tolerant. Res igitur tam nefanda & illicita, merito aboleri debet.
units.tr: The suffragan bishops have devised a practice whereby only they, and no other priest, may baptize bells. The simpler folk then believe, since the suffragans so affirm, that bells baptized in this way drive away demons and storms. Therefore countless godparents are often called in, especially those who are wealthy and are entreated to do so. At the time of the baptism they touch the rope by which the bell is hung, and when the suffragan intones the responses (as is customary at the baptism of infants), they all answer together and repeat the bell's name. The bell is also dressed in a new garment, as Christians are customarily dressed. Then they hurry to sumptuous feasts, to which the godparents are especially invited so that they may give their gifts more generously. The suffragans and their chaplains, together with many other ministers, are feasted royally. Nor is this enough: it is also necessary to pay the suffragan a fee, which they customarily call a little gift. As a result, sometimes even in small villages a hundred florins are spent on such a baptism. This practice is not only superstitious but also contrary to the Christian religion; it is a deception of the simple and sheer extortion. Yet the bishops tolerate such things, and even more absurd ones, so that the suffragans may be kept in debt by even the lowest fee. Such a wicked and unlawful practice should therefore rightly be abolished.

units.la: ARTICULUS LXVII. Quemadmodum plus pecuniæ, quàm pœnitentiæ, peccatoribus imponant.
units.tr: Article 67. How they impose more money than penance upon sinners.

units.la: PATRUM canonibus sancitum est, spiritualibus ac manifestis peccatis spiritualem pœnitentiam seu satisfactionem esse imponendam: ut sic non pecuniæ lucrum, sed potius animarum salus quæri intelligatur. At Ecclesiastici Judices & Officiales perperam animadversis Canonibus, dictam spiritualem pœnitentiam in tantum exasperant, aggravant & augent, ut Laici plerique pœnitentiis, quàm eam satisfactionem acceptare velint, pecunia malint sibi ab ipsis immunitatem comparare. Quare Laici multùm premuntur: Ecclesiastici contrà multùm ditantur, utputa qui in suum privatum commodum & partis agunt munus & judicis; quod tamen omnibus juribus dissonum est.
units.tr: By the canons of the Fathers it has been decreed that for spiritual and open sins a spiritual penance or satisfaction is to be imposed, so that it is understood that the aim is not gain of money but rather the salvation of souls. But the ecclesiastical judges and officials, wrongly twisting the canons, so exasperate, aggravate and enlarge the said spiritual penance that most laymen, preferring money to penance, would rather buy exemption from them than accept that satisfaction. Hence the laity are greatly burdened, while the ecclesiastics are greatly enriched, since they act in their own private interest and perform the office both of party and of judge, which is nevertheless contrary to all laws.

units.la: timus q; Princeps Maximilianus I. Imp. adversus Curiam Romanam colligi ad annum Dom. 1510. curavit olim. Verba gravaminis haec sunt, Articulo 67. &c.
units.tr: ...Prince Maximilian I, Emperor, once had this collected against the Roman Curia in the year of our Lord 1510. The words of the grievance are these, in Article 67, etc.

units.la: MAXIMILIANI I. IMPER. AUG. ET LUDOVICI XII. REGIS FRANCORUM EDICTA
units.tr: THE EDICTS OF MAXIMILIAN I, EMPEROR AUGUSTUS, AND LOUIS XII, KING OF THE FRANKS

units.la: De convocatione & celebratione Concilii Pisani, pro necessitate & utilitate Reipublicæ Christianæ, contra Julium II. Papam, in Anno Domini MDXI.
units.tr: Concerning the convocation and holding of the Council of Pisa, for the necessity and benefit of the Christian commonwealth, against Pope Julius II, in the year of the Lord 1511.

units.la: EDICTUM MAXIMILIANI IMPERATORIS.
units.tr: THE EDICT OF THE EMPEROR MAXIMILIAN.

units.la: MAXIMILIANUS, divina favente clementia electus Rom. Imperator Semper-Augustus, ac Germaniæ, Hungariæ, Dalmatiæ, Croaciæ, &c. Rex, Archidux Austriæ, Dux Burgundiæ, Brabantiæ, &c. Comes Palatinus, &c. Conspicientes immensas calamitates quas universa respublica Christiana & ipsa nostra sancta mater Ecclesia ubique patitur, ex quo & decremetum orthodoxæ fidei, & incrementum omnium malorum subsequitur, & in dies major confusio in omnibus rebus, ac bella intestina inter Christianos oriuntur, & effusio sanguinis Christiani, ad quæ cum non videamus aliud remedium, quam quod juxta sanctorum patrum instituta, Concilium & congregatio universalis fierent, ut ibidem communi Concilio possit omnibus commodè provideri: expectantes igitur dictum Concilium debere indici & convocari per beatissimum Pontificis, & reverendissimorum dominorum S.R.E. Cardinalium, ac alios praelatos, juxta ordinationem Concilij Constantiensis, & votum ac debitum eorumdem, cessantibus ipsis (ne & nos ab omnipotenti Deo negligentiæ redarguamur) noluimus nos cessare: quum illis negligentibus, nos tanquam Imperator & ejusdem sanctæ matris Ecclesiæ advocatus & protector, & quantum in nobis est subvenire his tantis necessitatibus teneamur. Ideo obviare tot inconvenientibus, sicut tenemur, cupientes etiam sanctæ matri Ecclesiæ operam ferre, confisi de fide, prudentia, dexteritate, & rerum gerendarum experientia magnificorum & honorabilium Don Ferdinandi Tochi ex despotibus Arthae: & Cephaleæ, Matthæi Kuen Vicecancellarij in Purgk Viti de Furst Comitis, Hieronymi Nogaroli, Antonii de capitibus Vaccæ, & Ludovici Faclæ Consiliarorum fidelium nobis dilectorum, motu proprio, & ex certa nostra scientia, ac animo deliberato, & omni meliori modo, via, jure, forma, & causa, quibus melius possumus & debemus, ipsos omnes & partem eorum & quemlibet ex eis insolidum, constituimus, fecimus, creavimus, & nominavimus, ac tenore praesentium constituimus, facimus, creamus, ordinamus, & nominamus nuncios nostros, & negotiorum infrascriptorum gestores generales: ac procuratores speciales ita tamen, quod generalitas specialitati non deroget, nec è converso, & quod unus ipsorum inceperit alteri eorum prosequi, mediare, & finire valeat, & quod non sit melior conditio primitus occupantis: nec deteriora subsequentis, spiritualiter & expresse, ad requirendum nostro nomine, & cum ea qua decor decet reverentia instandum, & procurandum apud beatitudinem Pontificis, & R. D. Cardinalem sua Sanctitas, de illorum consilio, convocare & indicere velit Concilium generale universalis Ecclesiae, in loco convenienti & tuto: ac intra brevius tempus, quod fieri possit, juxta constitutionem Concilii Constantiensis (spiritualis juramenti), & voti suae Sanctitatis: & beatitudine sua id negligente, vel tardante, item apud R. Dominos Cardin. instare, ut ipsi hoc Concilium convocent & indicant: In casu, quo eadem beatitudo Pontificis, & R. Domini Cardin. dictum Concilium congregare renuerint, vel differrent, aut locum tutum & convenientem non assignarent, ad faciendum protestationes notorias, & convocationem aut indictionem generalis Concilii, simul cum procuratoribus, vel curatore serenissimi Principis Domini Ludovici Francorum Regis consanguinei, & fratris charissimi, & reliquorum qui huic intimationi adhaerere voluerint: dantes & concedentes procuratoribus nostris, quod si constaret eis de non tuto accessu vel alias legitime suspicarentur personali eorum comparitione coram Beatitudine sua, & R. D. Card. talem actum possint, practicum, vel affixionem in aliquo loco convenienti facere, ita quod verisimiliter possit pervenire ad notitiam suae Sanctitatis, & ipsorum R. D. Cardinalium & caeterorum, etiam hoc omni meliori via & modo possibilibus, supplentes omnes & singulos defectus tam juris quam facti, qui in aliquo modo intervenire potuerunt, promittentes quoque, quod nos omnia & singula acta, gesta, per dictos Procuratores nostros, vel partem eorum, aut unum ex eis, rata, grata, & tenebimus, & servabimus, harum testimonio literarum sigilli nostri appensione munitarum. Datum in oppido nostro Triburgi, die XVI. mensis Januarii, Anno Domini millesimo quingentesimo quinto, Regnorum nostrorum Ro. XXV. Hungariae vero XXI.
units.tr: MAXIMILIAN, by the favour of divine clemency elected Roman Emperor, ever Augustus, and King of Germany, Hungary, Dalmatia, Croatia, etc., Archduke of Austria, Duke of Burgundy, Brabant, etc., Count Palatine, etc. Seeing the immense calamities which the whole Christian commonwealth and our own holy mother the Church suffer everywhere, from which both the decline of the orthodox faith and the increase of all evils follow, and greater confusion in all affairs day by day, and internal wars arise among Christians and the shedding of Christian blood; since we see no other remedy for these things than that, according to the institutions of the holy Fathers, a Council and a universal assembly should be held, so that at that Council provision might be made conveniently for all: therefore, expecting that the said Council ought to be announced and summoned by the most blessed Pontiff and the most reverend lords, the Cardinals of the Holy Roman Church, and the other prelates, according to the ordinance of the Council of Constance and the vow and duty of the same, and they being negligent (lest we too be charged by almighty God with negligence), we have not wished to be idle, since, while they are negligent, we, as Emperor and advocate and protector of the same holy mother Church, are bound to come to the aid of such great necessities, so far as lies in us. Therefore, wishing to meet so many difficulties, as we are bound to do, and also wishing to render service to the holy mother Church, trusting in the faith, prudence, dexterity, and experience in affairs of our magnificent and honourable faithful councillors, whom we love: Don Ferdinand Tochi, of the lords of Arta and Cephalonia; Matthew Kuen, Vice-Chancellor, of Purgk; Vitus de Fürst, Count; Jerome Nogarola; Anthony de Capitibus Vaccae; and Louis Facla; of our own motion, and from our certain knowledge, and with deliberate mind, and by every better means, way, law, form, and cause by which we best can and ought, we have constituted, made, created, and named all of them, and any part of them, and each of them for the whole, and by the tenor of these presents we constitute, make, create, ordain, and name them our envoys and general managers of the affairs written below, and special procurators, so however that the general power does not derogate from the special, nor the reverse, and that whichever of them has begun may be able to pursue, mediate, and finish with the other, and that the condition of the first occupant is not better nor of the later one worse; spiritually and expressly, to require in our name, and to press and procure with that reverence which befits, before the Beatitude of the Pontiff and the most reverend Cardinals, that His Holiness, with their counsel, be willing to convoke and announce a general Council of the universal Church, in a convenient and safe place, and within the shortest time that can be done, according to the constitution of the Council of Constance (the spiritual oath) and the vow of His Holiness; and if his Beatitude is negligent or delays in this, likewise to press before the most reverend lords Cardinals that they convoke and announce this Council; in the case that the same Beatitude of the Pontiff and the most reverend lords Cardinals refuse or defer to assemble the said Council, or do not assign a safe and convenient place, to make notorious protests and the convocation or announcement of a general Council, together with the procurators, or the curator, of the most serene Prince, the lord Louis, King of the Franks, our kinsman and most dear brother, and of the others who wish to adhere to this intimation; giving and granting to our procurators that, if it should be established to them that access is unsafe, or they otherwise have legitimate suspicion of their personal appearance before His Beatitude and the most reverend lords Cardinals, they may make such an act, a placard, or an affixing in some convenient place, so that it may probably come to the notice of His Holiness and of the same most reverend lords Cardinals and the rest, by every better way and means possible, supplying all and each of the defects, both of law and of fact, which may in any way have intervened; promising also that we will hold and keep as valid, pleasing, and ratified all and each of the acts and deeds done by our said procurators, or by a part of them, or by one of them, witness these letters fortified by the appending of our seal. Given in our town of Trent, on the 16th day of the month of January, in the year of the Lord 1505, in the 25th year of our reign as Roman king, and of Hungary the 21st.

units.la: Ad mandatum Caesareae Majestatis proprium.
units.tr: By the proper command of His Imperial Majesty.

units.la: Quo lecto, Procuratores Christianissimi Regis Francorum, similiter mandatum suum legendum exhibuerunt, in authentica forma & sigillo regali munitum, tenoris infrascripti.
units.tr: When this had been read, the procurators of the most Christian King of the Franks likewise exhibited their own mandate, to be read, in authentic form and fortified with the royal seal, of the tenor written below.

units.la: EDICTVM REGIS GALLIARVM.
units.tr: THE EDICT OF THE KING OF THE FRENCH.

units.la: LUdovicus Dei gratia Francorum Rex, Dux Mediolani, &c. Notum facimus omnibus & singulis praesentibus & futuris, quod cum majores nostri semper non solum fautores & auxiliatores, verum & pervigiles propugnatores & defensores acerrimi ac constantissimi Christianae fidei & S.R.E. In arduis quibuscumque extiterint, nullis parcendo laboribus & periculis: nos vestigiis majorum nostrorum inhaerentes, & considerantes quantam reipublicae Christianae utilitatem generalia Concilia attulerint, quantumque detrimenti ex eorum intermissione universalis Ecclesia acceperit: quodque in praesentia magna adest necessitas ipsius Concilii generalis universalis Ecclesiae contra gadi, pro extirpatione haereseum, schismatum, ac divisionum in diversis mundi partibus, ac pro reformatione morum Ecclesiae; & nimium scandalizantium notoriorum continuorum & incorrigibilium tam in capite quam in membris criminum eversione; pro pace Christianorum stabilienda, & bello contra infideles procurando. Quumque tempus decennii post ultimum universale Concilium jamdudum sit effluxum, & salutaerrima decretali constitutione Ecclesiae, in sacratissimo Constantiensi Concilio edira, quae incipit, Frequens, singulis decenniis universale Concilium fit congregandum, quod unicum remedium, ab universali Ecclesia inventum, & sancitum est, pro medela omnium morborum Ecclesiae, & summus Ro. Pontifex cui primo curae esse deberet, illud convocare hoc tempore neglexerit, (maxime cum juraverit & voverit post biennium a creatione sua illud tenere) & non solum negligens, sed & voti & juramenti hujus transgressor, illud non tenuerit, temptatque interpellet pro homine, & nunquam sua auctoritate aut voluntate futurum Concilium celebrandum: cumque de ejus criminibus notoriis, universam Ecclesiam scandalizantibus, & de quibus est incorrigibilis etiam agatur, juxtaque Canonicas sanctiones, sacri Basilensis decreta Concilii, ad eum hoc casu convocatio Concilii non attineat, divisumque etiam sit R. D. Cardinalium Collegium, & hi qui cum S. D. N. moram trahunt, vel quia non sunt liberi, aut alia ex causa, non existimantur convocationi hujusmodi velle assistere: pluresque R. D. Cardinales, qui a Curia Romana legitimis ex causis sunt absentes, & in Mediolano congregati hujusmodi congregationem Concilii effagitent, & enixe deposcant: nos pro debito quo obligamur Christo Domino Redemptori nostro, sponte ex nostra certa scientia, animoque deliberato, omnibus melioribus, jure, via, modo, causa, forma, quibus melius & efficacius possumus & debemus, dilectos nostros Magistrum Joannem de Birago Juris utriusque Doctorem, ac procuratorem nostrum fiscalem in Ducatu nostro Mediolani, & Balthasarem Platum pariter procuratorem nostrum fiscalem: necnon magistrum Franciscum de Vaccis Advocatum nostrum, omnes doctores & Consiliarios nostros, constituimus, creamus, & solemniter ordinamus indubitatos procuratores nostros generales, & nuncios speciales, & eorum quemlibet insolidum, absentes tanquam praesentes; ita tamen quod specialitas generalitati non deroget, nec e converso, & quod unus eorum inceperit, alter ipsorum mediare, prosequi, atque terminare, & ad effectum perducere valeat & finire, ita quod non sit melior conditio primitus occupantis, nec deterior subsequentis, a nomine nostro tantum, seu una cum charissimo fratre nostro Maximiliano sacratissimo Ro. Imperatore electo, necnon cum R. D. Cardinalibus. Multis in Lombardia degentibus, aut cum aliis principibus, Cardinalibus, & praelatis, qui in hac convocatione nobiscum adhaerere voluerint, aut alteri ex ipsis per se, seu simul, conjunctim vel divisim; & prout melius, decentius, & convenientius fore videbitur indicendum, seu convocandum generale Concilium, seu assistendum illi, seu illis, & cuilibet supradictorum. étorum, qui illud indicendum & convocandum esse existimaverint, seu procuraverint, in loco tuto, & honesto, anno, mense, & die quibus videbitur, sicut praefatis nostris Procuratoribus, seu eorum alteri, aut ipsi sacratissimo Imperatori fiat nostro, seu dictis R. Cardinalibus, eorum cuilibet, qui Colonium ipsum convocandum procuraverit, melius videbitur: necnon per se simul, vel divisim & ut supra ad intimandum, notificandum, & insinuandum ejusmodi deliberationem, ipsi S.D.N. Ipsumque monendum, hortandum, & rogandum, & eidem humiliter supplicandum, quatenus in dicto loco, ut supra eligendo, tempore, anno, & mense quibus supra, ipsi Concilio per se, seu legatos suos speciales, interesse, & cum eis dominis Principibus, Cardinalibus, & Praelaris quibus ipsa deliberatio intimabitur, convenire velit: necnon admonendum & hortandum R.D. Cardin. Patriarchas, Archiepiscopos, Episcopos, ac principes universalis Ecclesiae, ac omnes habentes facultatem consulendi, & definiendi in Conciliis generalibus, & venire solitos, & obligatos ad universale Concilium per se, aut per solemnes oratores, seu Procuratores (si personaliter interesse non poterint) ad Concilium ipsum, loco & tempore quibus supra, accedant; procuraturi quantum in eis est honorem Dei, Ecclesiae splendorem, pacem Christianorum, et bellum contra infideles, necnon conjunctim vel divisim monendum, hortandum, & requirendum S.D.N. & R.D. Cardinales, ut a tribus, quae maxime possent congregationem hujusmodi impedire dignetur abstinere, videlicet a creatione novorum Cardinalium, & a publicatione creatorum (si qui sunt creati) & processu contra antiquos Cardinales ex justis causis absentes, aliosque praelatos, & personas Ecclesiasticas, quae ad ipsum Concilium accesserint, seu accedere voluerint, & ab impediendo congregationem hujusmodi Concilii, directe vel indirecte, palam vel occulte, quovis quaesito colore, & abalienatione feudorum & terrarum S.R.E. alioquin protestandum de nullitate actus, & quod nos processum seu processus contra memoratos, seu eorum alterum factos, seu per eum, aut mandato suo faciendos (quod non credimus) alienationem terrarum & feudorum hujusmodi, ac creationem Cardinalium, si quam forte fieri contingeret, creationumque si qui sunt publicationem, pro nulla, & nullis haberi ac nullius valoris, roboris, ac momenti esse existimus, ac per Concilium ipsum seu futurum Rom. Pontificem, annullari, cassari, & irritari procurabimus: & quia tutum non esset ipsis oratoribus, Nuncii, & Procuratoribus, dictam protestationem, intimationem, & convocationem in praesentia S.D.N. facere, quia S.R.E. Cardinales, confratres suos, carceribus mancipare, Oratoresque principum Christianorum, vi capere, & funis ictibus torquere, carceribus, aliisque totmentis macerare non erubescit; ideo decrevimus, per affixionem monitorios hujusmodi (quam ipsi Procuratores nostri facere dixerunt) in valvis aliquarum Ecclesiarum, & aliis locis propinquis, ex quibus verisimiliter ad notitiam Sanctitatis suae, & R.D. Cardinalium, & aliorum Praelatorum, venire poterit (quam vim publici edicti habere decernimus) eos petinde arcari, & ad veniendum obligatos esse, aut si personaliter fuisset illis intimata, ac exhibita ipsa nuntio: cum non sit verisimile ipsis fore incognitum, quod tam patenter omnibus publicatur. Unum quoque vel plures Procuratorem seu Procuratores, loco ipsius & cujuslibet ipsorum, cum simili aut limitata potestate substituendum, eosque revocandum, & onus Procurationis ejusmodi, se recassumendum toties quoties opus fuerit, & iplis vel eorum alteri videbitur expedite (praesenti procuratorio nihilominus in suo robore duraturo) & generaliter ad faciendum, dicendum, agendum, gerendum & procurandum omnia & singula, quae in praemissis & circa ea necessaria fuerint, seu quomodolibet oportuna, & quae nos ipsi facere possemus, si praemissis & cuilibet praemissorum praesentes personaliter essemus, etiamsi mandatum exigeretur magis speciale, &c. ac quorumdam verbo ad verbum expressa, & individua hic esset facienda mentio specialis. Promittentes in verbo regio, nos rata & firma habituros omnia & singula, quae in praedictis & eorum circumstantiis ac dependentiis, per praefatos nostros Procuratores, & Oratores, & eorum quemlibet acta, gesta, & facta fuerint. In quorum fidem & testimonium, has praesentes manu nostra propria subscripsimus, & sigilli nostri appensione muniri fecimus. Datum Blesis, die xv. mensis Februarii, Anno a nativitate Domini M.D.XI. regni vero nostri decimo tertio. Loys. Per Regem Mediolani Ducem.
units.tr: Louis, by the grace of God King of the French, Duke of Milan, etc. We make known to all and each, present and future, that since our forebears have always been not only supporters and helpers but also watchful and most zealous defenders of the Christian faith and of the Holy Roman Church, and have in every difficult matter stood firm, sparing no labours or dangers, we, adhering to the footsteps of our forebears, and considering how great a benefit general councils have brought to the Christian commonwealth, and how much harm the universal Church has suffered from their omission, and that at present there is a great need of that general and universal Council of the Church against the enemies (gadi), for the extirpation of heresies, schisms and divisions in the various parts of the world, for the reform of the morals of the Church, for the overthrow of the notorious, continual and incorrigible crimes, which cause great scandal, both in the head and in the members, for establishing peace among Christians, and for procuring war against the infidels; and since the period of ten years since the last universal Council has long since passed, and the most salutary decretal constitution of the Church, issued at the most sacred Council of Constance, which begins "Frequens", ordains that a universal Council be convened every ten years, a remedy which the universal Church has discovered and sanctioned as the only cure for all the ills of the Church; and since the Supreme Pontiff, to whom this should have been the first concern, has neglected to convene it at this time (especially since he swore and vowed to hold it within two years of his creation), and not only has he been negligent but, being a transgressor of this vow and oath, has not kept it, and he tries to delay and to put off the matter, and never intends the future Council to be celebrated by his own authority or will; and since, concerning his notorious crimes, which scandalise the whole Church, and for which he is incorrigible, this is also in question, and according to the canonical sanctions and the decrees of the sacred Council of Basel, the convocation of a Council does not in this case pertain to him; and since the College of the most reverend Cardinals is also divided, and those who delay with our Most Holy Lord, whether because they are not free or for some other reason, are not thought to wish to be present at such a convocation; and since several most reverend Cardinals, who for lawful reasons are absent from the Roman Curia, and have gathered at Milan, strongly demand and earnestly press for the convening of such a Council: we, out of the debt by which we are bound to Christ our Lord and Redeemer, of our own accord, from our certain knowledge and deliberate intention, by all the best means, by right, by way, by method, by cause and by form by which we are able and ought most effectively to do so, have constituted, created and solemnly appointed as our indubitable general procurators and special envoys our beloved Master John of Birago, Doctor of both laws and our fiscal procurator in our Duchy of Milan, and Baldassare Platus, likewise our fiscal procurator, and also Master Francis of Vacca, our advocate, all our doctors and counsellors, and each of them for the whole, as if absent as present; provided that the special does not derogate from the general, nor the reverse, and that whichever of them has begun, the other may take up, pursue, bring to an end, and complete and finish, so that the condition of the one who first took it up is not better, nor that of the one who follows worse; in our name alone, or together with our most dear brother Maximilian, the most sacred Roman Emperor-elect, and also with the most reverend Cardinals residing in Lombardy, or with other princes, cardinals and prelates, who wish to join us in this convocation, or with any one of them, either singly or together, jointly or separately; and to appoint, as shall seem best, most fitting and most convenient, a general Council to be proclaimed or convened, or to attend it or them, and to any of the above-named, who have judged or undertaken that it ought to be proclaimed and convened, in a safe and honourable place, in the year, month and day that shall seem good, as shall seem best to our aforesaid procurators, or to one of them, or to the most sacred Emperor himself, or to the said most reverend Cardinals, or to whichever of them shall have undertaken to convene the Council at Cologne; and likewise, either singly or together, and as above, to intimate, notify and insinuate this resolution to our Most Holy Lord, and to admonish, exhort and ask him, and humbly to beseech him, that at the place to be chosen as above, at the time, year and month stated above, he be willing to attend the Council himself or through his special legates, and to meet there with those lords, princes, cardinals and prelates to whom this resolution shall be intimated; and likewise to admonish and exhort the most reverend Cardinals, Patriarchs, Archbishops, Bishops and princes of the universal Church, and all who have the power to consult and to decide in general Councils, and who are accustomed and obliged to come to a universal Council, to repair to the same Council, at the place and time stated above, either in person or through solemn orators or procurators (if they cannot attend in person), there to procure, as far as in them lies, the honour of God, the splendour of the Church, the peace of Christians and war against the infidels; and likewise, jointly or separately, to admonify, exhort and require our Most Holy Lord and the most reverend Cardinals that he deign to abstain from three things which could chiefly hinder such a congregation, namely from the creation of new Cardinals, from the publication of those created (if any have been created), and from proceedings against the old Cardinals who are absent for just causes, and against other prelates and ecclesiastical persons who have come, or wish to come, to the same Council; and from hindering such a convocation of a Council, directly or indirectly, openly or secretly, under whatever pretext; and from the alienation of the fiefs and lands of the Holy Roman Church; otherwise to protest that the act is null, and that we shall consider as null and void, of no validity, strength or force, and shall procure to be annulled, quashed and rendered invalid by the Council itself or by the future Roman Pontiff, any proceeding or proceedings made against the said persons or any of them, or to be made by him or at his command (which we do not believe), and any alienation of such lands and fiefs, and the creation of Cardinals, should any such be made, and the publication of creations, if any there be; and because it would not be safe for the said envoys, messengers and procurators to make the said protestation, intimation and convocation in the presence of our Most Holy Lord, since the Cardinals of the Holy Roman Church are not ashamed to consign their brother Cardinals to prisons, to seize the envoys of Christian princes by force, and to torment them with blows of the rope, to waste them away with prisons and other torments; therefore we have decided, by the posting of these monitory letters (which our said procurators have said they will do) on the doors of certain churches and in other nearby places, from which it may likely come to the notice of His Holiness and of the most reverend Cardinals and of the other prelates (which we decree shall have the force of a public edict), that they are summoned thereby and are bound to come; or, if they had been personally intimated and presented to them by a messenger, since it is not likely that what is so openly published to all should be unknown to them. We also grant power to substitute one or more procurators in place of him and of each of them, with similar or limited power, and to revoke them, and to take up again the burden of such procuration as often as there is need, and as shall seem expedient to them or to one of them (the present procuratory nevertheless remaining in its full force); and generally to do, say, act, manage and procure all and each of the things which shall be necessary in and about the foregoing matters, or in any way fitting, and which we ourselves could do if we were personally present at the foregoing and at each of them, even if a more special mandate were required, etc.; and it would be necessary to make special mention here, word for word and individually, of certain matters. Promising on our royal word that we shall hold valid and firm all and each of the things which have been done, transacted and performed in the aforesaid matters and their circumstances and dependencies by our said procurators and orators, and by each of them. In witness and testimony whereof we have subscribed these presents with our own hand and caused them to be fortified by the appending of our seal. Given at Blois, the 15th day of the month of February, in the year of our Lord's nativity 1511, and in the thirteenth year of our reign. Louis. By the King, Duke of Milan.

units.la: COTEREAV.
units.tr: COTEREAV.

units.la: Quibus mandatis lectis, videntes R. Domini Cardinales praefati, utriusque Principis Procuratores, adea quae in mandatis continebantur exequenda, sufficienti facultate munitos, petierunt primo a Procuratoribus Caesareis praenominatis ut vellent ore tenus sacratissimi domini Caesaris mentem super hoc & mandata ipsius a Majestate sua Caes. tradita aperire. Tunc assurgens nobilis dominus Comes Hieronymus Nogarolus, petita a reverendissimis dominis Cardinalibus praefatis & Collegis suis, quorum etiam nomine loquebatur licentia, haec vel similia verba proposuit videlicet, Quod cum sacratissimo domino suo non esset aliqua spes per medium summi moderni Pontificis, nec R.D.S.R.E. Cardinalium apud Sanctitatem suam moram trahentium, debere congregari generale Concilium universale Ecclesiae, pro pace Christianorum, bello contra infideles, & reformatione morum Ecclesiae & extirpatione haeresum, ac errorum: nec eis etiam esset tutum hoc in praesentia a summo Pontifice exquirere, ideo videntes Ecclesiae maximam necessitatem, & memores praecepti Concilii Constantiensis, de tenendo generali Concilio singulis decennis, recurrebant ad ipsos dominos Card. in Insubria congregatos, quos intelligebant zelo Dei & Ecclesiae sanctae ferventes, defiderantesq. restitutionem pristini splendoris ipsius, & ut juxta antiquam tempora & consuetudinem superiorum patrum, ad medicinam omnium morborum Ecclesiae, & orbis deveniatur (generale videlicet Concilium) Idcirco quantum melius jure poterant, & debebant, requirebant eorum D.R. & alios S.R.E.Car. quos intelligebant in hac causa eis adherentes, ut dignarentur intendere courocationi & congregationi generali Concilii universalis Ecclesiæ, in quo, ut & officio quo Ecclesia tenerentur satisfacerent, & sacratissimo D. Cæsari, ac Christianissimo Regi Francorum charissimo fratri ejus maximè complacerent, quoque parati erant similiter cum eis, prout jure melius poterant, convocationem etiam hujusmodi Concilii facere, & intimare, & de hoc requirebant notarios & testes præsentes de testimonio, & instrumentis, &c.
units.tr: When these mandates had been read, the aforesaid Most Reverend Lords Cardinals, and the Procurators of both Princes, being provided with sufficient authority to carry out what the mandates contained, first asked the aforesaid Imperial Procurators to declare orally the mind of the most sacred Lord Emperor on this matter and the mandate delivered to him by His Imperial Majesty. Then the noble lord Count Girolamo Nogarola rose, with the permission of the most reverend lords Cardinals and his colleagues, which he requested and on whose behalf he spoke, and set forth words to this effect: that since his most sacred lord had no hope, through the agency of the present supreme Pontiff or of the Cardinals of the holy Roman Church who were lingering at his Holiness's court, that a general universal Council of the Church could be convened for the peace of Christians, war against the infidels, the reformation of the morals of the Church, and the extirpation of heresies and errors; nor was it safe for them to ask the supreme Pontiff about this at present; therefore, seeing the very great need of the Church, and mindful of the decree of the Council of Constance, that a general Council be held every ten years, they had recourse to those lords Cardinals gathered in Insubria, whom they understood to be fervent in the zeal of God and the holy Church, and desirous of the restoration of its former splendour, and that, as in the ancient times and custom of the earlier fathers, recourse be had to a general Council as the remedy for all the ills of the Church and the world. Accordingly, as best they could and ought by right, they asked their most reverend lordships, and the other Cardinals of the Holy Roman Church whom they understood to be adhering to them in this cause, to deign to attend to the convocation and gathering of a general Council of the universal Church, in which they would both satisfy their duty, to which the Church is bound, and most greatly please the most sacred Lord Caesar and the Most Christian King of the Franks, his dearest brother; and they said that they were likewise ready, as far as they could rightly do so, to make and announce the convocation of such a Council together with them; and on this they asked the notaries and witnesses present to bear witness, with instruments, etc.

units.la: Expósito hoc majestatis Cæs. sanctissimo propósito, spectabilis Jurisconsultus dominus Jo. Birgus, Christianissimi D. Ludovici Regis Francorum Procurator nomine suo, & Collegarum, accepta a reverendissimis dominis Cardinalibus dicendi licentiâ, hæc vel similia verba propósuit: quod in ponenda principis sui Christianissimi mente, & commissionibus eius verbis & sententiis utebatur quibus usus est Procurator prænominatus Cæsareus, quorum repetitio quia futura esset tædiosa, propter brevitatem omittebatur. Unde ... summodo dixit Christianissimum dominum Regem motum causis eisdem quibus sacratissimus dominus Cæsar movebatur, ejusdemque esse, cum majestate sua Cæsarea, in convocatione hac sancta, & notoria Concilii generalis universalis Ecclesiæ, propositi: & propterea hortabatur & requirebat D. Cardin. Reverendissimos, ut vellent hujusmodi convocationi pro definitione causarum à Procuratore Cæsareo nominatarum intendere, quam convocationem etiam erat cum D. ipsis reverendissimis & sacratissimo domino Cæsare, prout jure melius poterat facturus, & inti-matur.
units.tr: After this most holy proposal of His Imperial Majesty had been set forth, the distinguished jurisconsult, lord Jean Birague, Procurator of the Most Christian Lord Louis, King of the Franks, on behalf of himself and his colleagues, having received from the most reverend lords Cardinals permission to speak, set forth words to this effect: that in stating the mind of his Most Christian Prince and his commissions, he used the words and opinions which the aforesaid Imperial Procurator had used; since repeating them would be tedious, they were omitted for brevity. Hence ... he said only that the Most Christian lord King was moved by the same causes that moved the most sacred lord Caesar, and that it was his purpose, together with His Imperial Majesty, to take part in this holy and well-known convocation of a general universal Council of the Church; and therefore he urged and asked the most reverend lords Cardinals to be willing to attend to such a convocation for the settlement of the causes named by the Imperial Procurator; and he declared that he would make this convocation, as best he could by right, together with their most reverend lordships and the most sacred lord Caesar.

units.la: Tunc R.D. Cardinales prædicti audita conformitate horum principum Christianitatis circa sanctissimum hoc propositum concurrentium expetentes similem aliorum esse mentem, & timentes dilatione aliquod periculum, modicum ad partem secedentes, eadem hora per organum Reverendiss. Domini B. Cardinalis sanctæ Crucis responderunt prælatis utriusque principis Procuratoris habentes gratias Deo omnipotenti, quod tam firmum & generosum animum inspiraverit sacratissimo domino Max. E. Ro. Imperatori, Semper-Augusto; & Christianissimo domino Ludovico Regi Francorum, & eundem sperabant aliis Christianis Principibus inspirari, & communicari debere: ipsisque principibus agebant gratias ingentes, quod meliores essent officii sui, & conservaturi ac splendoris Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: Then the aforesaid most reverend lords Cardinals, having heard the agreement of these princes of Christendom concerning this most holy proposal, and wishing that the others share the same mind, and fearing some danger from delay, withdrew a little apart and that same hour, through the mouth of the Most Reverend lord B., Cardinal of Santa Croce, replied to the prelates and Procurators of both princes, giving thanks to Almighty God that He had inspired so firm and generous a spirit in the most sacred lord Maximilian, Emperor of the Romans, ever Augustus, and in the Most Christian lord Louis, King of the Franks; and they hoped that the same would be inspired and communicated to the other Christian princes; and they gave the princes very great thanks, because they were the better for their office and would preserve the splendour of the Church.

units.la: Ad hunc tamen actum convocationis Concilii, pro quo potissimum ad insubriam secedere petebant à suis nobilitatibus & magnificentiis, ut ea procuratorio nomine suorum principum promitterent servare, & realiter tenere.
units.tr: Yet for this act of convoking the Council, for which they chiefly asked to withdraw to Insubria, they asked of their nobilities and magnificences that they would promise, in the name of procuration of their princes, to observe these things and truly keep them.

units.la: Primò, quod promitterent nomine Imperatoris & Regis, in eventum convocationis Concilii generalis, quod eorum Majestates realiter & cum effectu erunt fautores dicti Concilii, & membrorum ejusdem: & cum omnibus viribus eos juvabunt, & custodient, usque ad ultimam Concilii definitionem.
units.tr: First, that they would promise in the name of the Emperor and the King that, in the event of the convocation of a general Council, their Majesties would in actual fact and effectively be supporters of the said Council and of its members; and that they would assist and protect them with all their strength until the final decision of the Council.

units.la: Secundò, quod nunquam erunt in voto nec consentient aliorum sententiæ, in dissolutione aut translatione dicti Concilii, sine consensu majoris partis congregandorum in eo.
units.tr: Second, that they would never give a vote, nor consent to the opinion of others, toward the dissolution or transfer of the said Council without the consent of the greater part of those gathered in it.

units.la: Tertiò, quod procurabunt quantum in eis erit, dictum Concilium esse liberum, tutum, & securum, & ad nullius confusionem (nisi secundum justitiæ terminos) & quod in eo teneatur forma Concilii Constantiensis. Et quamvis ipsi domini Cardinales à principibus ipsis plura essent petituri, prodirectione dicti Concilii, quia tamen ad illa non videbatur mandatii oratorum se extendere, petebant solum hæc tria, sine quibus & oratorum requisitio, & Cardinalium convocatio, irrita videretur.
units.tr: Third, that they would take care, as far as lies in them, that the said Council be free, safe, and secure, and not subject to the confusion of anyone (except according to the terms of justice), and that in it the form of the Council of Constance be observed. And although the lords Cardinals themselves would have asked the princes for more in order to direct the said Council, yet, since it did not seem that the mandate of the envoys extended to those things, they asked only these three, without which both the request of the envoys and the convocation of the Cardinals would seem void.

units.la: Tunc domini Commissarii, & Procuratores Cæsarei, & Regii, responderunt se verè intellexisse mentem sacratissimi Cæsaris, & Christianissimi Regis, esse inclinatissimam ad veram universalem Ecclesiæ directionem, in dicto Concilio, & cum ista tria sint annexa, & necessaria eorum mente & essectui, & comprehendantur sub requisitione & mandatis eorumdem, ideo pure, realiter & bona fide, nomine & auctoritate dominorum suorum principalium præfatorum, ista tria sunt polliciti, & promiserunt in verbo fidei & veritatis, Principum eorumdem.
units.tr: Then the lords Commissioners and the Imperial and Royal Procurators replied that they had truly understood the mind of the most sacred Caesar and the Most Christian King to be most inclined toward the true direction of the universal Church in the said Council; and since these three things are joined to and necessary for their intention and effect, and are included in their request and mandates, therefore they purely, actually, and in good faith, in the name and by the authority of their aforesaid principals, promised these three things and pledged them, in the word of faith and truth, of the same Princes.

units.la: Deinde, Reverendiss. domini Cardin. habita promissione ista, modicum secedentes, communicato consilio, ne incurrerent maledictum illius qui opus Dei tractat negligenter, per organum Reverendissimi Domini B. Episcopi Sabinensis Cardinalis Sanctæ Crucis, Patriarchæ Hierosolymitani, accepto themate.
units.tr: Then the most reverend lords Cardinals, having received this promise, withdrew a little, and after consulting together, so that they would not incur the curse of one who does the work of God negligently, through the mouth of the Most Reverend lord B., Bishop of Sabina, Cardinal of Santa Croce, Patriarch of Jerusalem, took the theme.

units.la: Confirma hoc Deus quod operatus es in nobis, à templo sancto tuo, quod est in Hierusalem, tibi offerent reges munera: Psalm. LXVII. ubi notata inspiratione ipsorum dominorum Cardinalium, & Principum, circa splendorem & directionem Ecclesiæ, quæ inspiratio effectivè à triumphante Hierusalē dependebat, & objectivè militantem respiciebat, & cum factores operum semper illa amentur, & conservari accon-firmari procurent, credebat hoc divinum opus à Domino confirmandum, à quo mirabiliter procedebat, & tantæ Majestatis & utilitatis erat: & hoc continebat prima pars illius versiculi (orationem videlicet pro confirmatione istius sanctissimæ inspirationis, pro qua nomine universalis Ecclesiæ cum David ab omnibus esset orandum) & in secunda parte versiculi, pro isto divino opere, notabatur gratarum actio, quæ fiebat cum omni genere munerum, & signanter per Principes Ecclesiæ, & orbis: quorum potissima cura esse debet ista publica & divina (tanquam Deo propinquiores, & immediatores) curare, & nullum majus munus esse poterat offerendum Deo, quàm ista fides, & devotio principum & ipsorum Reverendiss. D. Cardinalium, qui rejectis multis promissionibus, spretisque multis minis, & periculis postpositis, tam ferventer, tam solidè, hanc Dei inspirationem suis actionibus adjuvabant.
units.tr: Confirm, O God, what you have wrought in us; from your holy temple which is in Jerusalem, kings shall offer gifts to you: Psalm. LXVII. Here the inspiration of the lords Cardinals and Princes themselves was noted, concerning the splendour and direction of the Church; this inspiration depended effectively on the triumphant Jerusalem and was directed objectively toward the Church militant; and since the authors of works are always loved and their works are procured to be preserved and confirmed, they believed that this divine work was to be confirmed by the Lord, from whom it proceeded wonderfully and was of such majesty and usefulness. The first part of that verse contained this (namely, a prayer for the confirmation of this most holy inspiration, for which, in the name of the universal Church, all should pray with David); and in the second part of the verse, for this divine work, thanksgiving was noted, which was made with every kind of gift, and especially by the Princes of the Church and of the world, whose chief care ought to be these public and divine matters (as being nearer to God and more immediate to Him), and no greater gift could be offered to God than this faith and devotion of the princes and of the most reverend lords Cardinals, who, having rejected many promises, scorned many threats, and set aside many dangers, so fervently and so firmly aided this inspiration of God by their actions.

units.la: Invocato igitur nomine Dei omnipotentis, ista inspirantis, cum auxilio sancti Spiritus, quem Dominus promisit Ecclesiæ assistentem, visis prius mandatis infrascriptorum aliorum reverendiss. D. Cardinalium, ad convocationem Concilii generalis universalis Ecclesiæ, sub una schedula, quam exhibuerunt, suis & nomine omnium Cardinalium, quorum habentur mandata, aliorumque D. Cardinalium, & aliorum adhaerere volentium, devenerunt sub his verbis videlicet.
units.tr: Therefore, invoking the name of Almighty God, who inspires these things, with the help of the Holy Spirit, whom the Lord promised to the assisting Church, and first having seen the mandates of the other most reverend lords Cardinals written below, concerning the convocation of a general universal Council of the Church, they came, in a single schedule which they produced for themselves and in the name of all the Cardinals whose mandates are held, and of the other lords Cardinals and others willing to adhere, to the following words, namely:

units.la: CONVOCATIO GENERALIS CONCILII EX PARTE CARDINALIUM, qua una cum sequenti convocatione principum (ut probabita diligenti informatione ex aliis hentlicis relationibus probatum est; & notorium exstitit) per omnes quatuor nationes divulgata & publicata fuit.
units.tr: CONVOCATION OF A GENERAL COUNCIL ON THE PART OF THE CARDINALS, which, together with the following summons of the princes (as was proved by diligent inquiry from other trustworthy reports, and was notorious), was published and made known through all four nations.

units.la: TEnore praesentis schedulae aut instrumenti, cunctis pateat evidenter, & sit notum, quod anno a nativitate Domini M.D.XI. Indictione quartadecima, die vero Veneris XVI. Mensis Maij, Pontificatus sanctissimi domini nostri Domini Iulij, divina providentia Papae II. anno octavo: Constituti coram nobis notariis publicis, & testibus infrascriptis, reverendissimi in Christo patres & domini, Domini B. Episcopus Sabinensis & G. Episcopus Praenestinus & F. tt. Sanctorum Nerei & Achillei Cusentinus, S.R.E. Cardinales, suis nominibus, & pro sex aliis dominis Cardinalibus sufficiens mandatum habentes, pro aliis eis adhaerentibus, & adhaerere volentibus dixerunt, & protestati sunt sequentia verba, videlicet quod considerantes quantam reipublicae Christianae militantis Concilia generalia universalis Ecclesiae attulerint, quantumque ex eorum intermissione Christiana res publica sit passa, cumque imprae sentiarum conspiciantur clare, magnam instare necessitatem universalis Concilii congregandi pro vera pace Christianorum fundanda, & sufficienti bello contra infideles stabiliendo: necnon potissime pro reformatione morum universalis Ecclesiae in capite & in membris plurimum collapsorum, ac emendatione criminum gravissimorum notoriorum, continuorum, ac incorrigibilium universalem Ecclesiam scandalizantium, quorum omnium Ecclesiae morborum salutaris & unica medicina congregatio universalis Concilii semper fuit habita: quumque tempus decennii postultimum universale Concilium iurisdictum sit effluxum, & salubertima decreta Constitutionis constitutione edita, quae incipit Frequens, singulis decennis universale Concilium congregari debeat, & sanctissimus dominus noster Dominus Julius Papa II. cui primo curae esse debuerit illud convocandi, tanto tempore hoc neglexerit, maxime cum voverit & juraverit post biennium a creatione sua illud tenere, & nedum negligens in praecepto Ecclesiae & Concilii, sed & voti, & juramenti hujusmodi transgressor illud non tenuerit, tempusque interpellet pro homine, cumque nunquam sine authoritate aut volantate futurum Concilium credatur celebrandum: & cum de gravibus Ecclesiae standalisin capite agendum sit, quo casu, juxta patrum sanctiones, & ipsius sacri Constantiensis Concilii decreta, ad summum Pontificem congregatio Concilii non attineat, sed secundo loco, ad reverendissimos D. Card. qui Pontifici, in ejusmodi sua negligentia non adhaeserint: in similibus casibus, convocatio Concilii spectat, non ad eos qui sunt participes continuae negligentiae ejus: zelo domus Dei, quo nos maxime accendimur, post Missam sancti Spiritus invocato, ac reformationem Ecclesiae in capite & in membris vehementer effiagitantes, & depositentes ex nostra certa scientia: & spontanea voluntate quantum jure melius possumus, & debemus, nomine sacri R.D. Card. Collegii, quod in nobis repraesentatur, in hoc casu jure & etiam particulariter nomine nostro, & aliorum Cardinalium, quorum habemus mandata, & aliorum Card. & Praelatorum nobis adhaerentium, & adhaerere volentium, una cum Consiliariis & Procuratoribus sacratissimi domini Maximiliani electi Rom. Imperatoris Semper Augusti, & Christianissimi domini Ludovici Francorum Regis, Ducis Mediolani, caeterisque nobis in hoc adhaerentibus, & adhaerere volentibus, Concilium generale universalis Ecclesiae indicimus & convocamus, et quantum in nobis est effectualiter congregari monemus, & hortamur futurum, in civitate Pisana, & in choandum in Calendis Septemb. proximè futuri & ibi continuandum & terminandum, usque ad definitionem superiorum causarum: nisi de consensu majoris partis congregatorum in Concilio aliqua legitima causa ad alium locum commodiorem translatum sit. Quapropter cum unanimi reverentia, humilitate, ac instantia, sanctissimum dominum nostrum Julium Papam securidum supplicamus, & per viscera misericordiae Dei nostri hortamur, acre quia imus, ut huic congregationi Concilii, pro dictis causis, assentire dignetur, & illud personaliter, vel per suos legatos honorare & confirmare. Similiter & R.D.S.R.E. Card. Patriarchas, Archiepiscopos, Episcopos, Reges, Principes & Potentates, ac communitates, & Collegia, universitatesque studiorum generalium, ac Religiosorum generales, & magistros, necnon omnes alios Ecclesiae Praelatos, & in Conciliis generalibus, authoritatem definiendi aut consulendi habentes, & ad Concilium de jure aut consuetudine venire solitos, & obligatos, convocamus & requirimus: ut per se, vel solemnes oratores, vel Procuratores, (si commode, personaliter interesse non poterunt ad Concilium ipsum, loco & tempore quibus supra) accedere dignentur, procuraturi quantum in eis erit, ut Concilium sit libertum, tutum & securum, & in omnia forma Constantiensis Synodi procedatur ad honorem Dei, & Ecclesiae splendore, pacem Christianorum; & infidelium expugnationem; quod nos S.R.E. Cardinales pro viribus offerimus Deo & Ecclesiae effectualiter procuraturos; & pro viribus facturos. Quare sanctissimum dominum nostrum, & Reverendissimos dominos Cardinales, juxta formam aliorum Conciliorum, enixe supplicamus & hortamur, ut a quatuor cedusis quae maxime possent hujusmodi sanctam congregationem impedire, et nunc abstinere dignentur; videlicet a creatione novorum Cardinalium & a publicatione creatorum (si qui forsan sunt) & processu contra antiquos Cardinales, alios, jure praelatos, & personas ad Concilium ipsum accedere volentes; & illi prout decet consentientes, necnon ab impediendo hujusmodi convocationem Concilii directe, vel indirecte, publice vel occulte, quovis quæsito colore, & abalienatione feudorum seu terrarum S.R.E. In quibus omnibus causis, cum omni humilitate protestamur de nullitate actus (nisi à Sanctissimo domino nostro in dicto Concilio hujusmodi fieri contingeret) & aliter facta vel facienda irrita haberi, ac per Concilium seu prout juris fuit annullari, & cassari debere protestamur & requirimus. Insuper vos omnes R.D. Cardinales, & Prælatos, Principesque, ac dominos temporales, & personas alias, cujuscumque status, gradus, conditionis, vel præeminentiæ existant, hortamur, & monemus, quatenus hujusmodi bono proposito nostro annuere, opportunosque favores præbere, & à quibuscumque molestationibus, & impedimentis, ac prohibitionibus, contra venientes & venire volentes, ad dictum generale Concilium, quomodocumque, & qualitercumque directe, vel indirecte, sive alio quovis quæsito colore, vel ingenio, publice vel occulte desistant, atque desistere velint & debeant; & ab omnibus censuris, cujuscumque qualitatis (præextu hujusmodi congregationis Concilii) abstineant. Et si secus super his, à quoquam quavis auctoritate scienter vel ignoranter hactenus contigerit, protestamur de nullitate taliter gerendorum, & de omni remedio habendo, in dicto generali Concilio, ut talia irrita, & nulla declarentur, & de omnibus aliis remediis nobis comperientibus, maxime ex forma dictæ Synodi Constantiensis, prout coram notabilibus personis, notariis, & testibus, etiam in scriptis pro nobis adhærentibus, ac volentibus adhærere protestati fuimus, & reclamavimus, prout etiam tenore præsentium protestamur, & provocamus. Et quia tutum non est nobis dictam convocationem Concilii, ac protestationem in præsentia sanctissimi domini nostri facere, qui S.R.E. Card. fratres suos & Ecclesiæ universalis principes carceribus mancipari, & eis minari fecit, oratoresque principum contra jus gentium detinen: Ideo decrevimus per affixionem hujusmodi schedulæ, sive instrumenti convocationis, monitionis, & protestationis, in valvis Ecclesiarum Mutinensis Rhegiensis & Parmensis (ex quibus veniminiter ad notitiam sanctitatis tuæ, & reverentiam D. Cardinalium, ac Principum Christianorum, & aliorum Prælatorum venire poterit, quam vim publici edicti habere petimus) perinde atctare ad veniendum ad Concilium supra requisitos, & monitos, ac si personaliter illis intimata fuisset ipsa convocatio, monitio, & protestatio: cum non sit verisimile, ipsis fore incognitum vel occultum, quod tam patenter omnibus publicatur. Alioqui dictis Calendis Septembris advenientibus, & etiam elapsis, in dicta Civitate Pisana, vel alio loco, in quo, ut præfertur, de consensu majoris partis congregandorum, transferri contigerit, ad celebrationem & perfectionem dicti generalis Concilii gradatim & successive procedemus, & procedetur unà cum illis reverendiss. D. Cardinalibus, Patriarchis, Archiepiscopis, Episcopis, ac dominis, aliisque ut supra citandis, qui nobiscum in dicto generali Concilio convenerint, juxta statuta & decreta in dicto Concilio Constantiensi: aliorum, sicut supra requirendorum & citandorum absentia, seu negligentia, aut contumacia, in aliquo non obstante, eisque propter hoc ulterius non citatis vel monitis. De cujus præsentis instrumenti, hujusmodi convocationem, monitionem, protestationem, & decreta in se continentis, in locis prædictis & aliis ubi expediens fuerit publicatione, præsentatione, & in valvis prædictis affixione, & dimissione cuilibet hujus instrumenti latori, nuncio, in hac parte nostro, cum juramento aut instrumento publico, manu notarii publici consecto, plenam dabimus fidem. Quia vero fidelibus, non est tam de solicita intentione quacumque fidendum, quàm de instantia orationis humilis & devotæ (perandum: cum non simus sufficientes etiam cogitare aliquid ex nobis quasi ex nobis sed sufficientia nostra), juxta verbum Apostoli, ex Deo fit, ideo omnium vestrum charitates precamur in Domino, quatenus & per vos, & per fideles vestræ solicitudini commissos, humiles preces fundantur ad dominum, & devotis orationibus insistatur, ut ipse qui concordiam operatur in sublimibus, dignetur efficere, ut debita hujus sanctæ nostræ deliberationis, & convocationis provisio & executio, concors, & celer, ac canonica subsequatur, ut Ecclesiæ salus exigit, & totius orbis pax, & utilitas desideret, & expoleit. Et novissime vos R.D. Archiepiscopos hortamur in Domino, ne in tempore hujusmodi convocationis litis deficientes, sed interim suffragancos vestros, exemptos, & non exemptos, ac alias notabiles personas provinciarum vestrarum requiratis, ut in tempore ac loco designatis, absque dilatione, etiam cum deliberationibus, & avisamentis vestris, & suis circa fidem, pacem, & mores fidelium instructi compareatis, & compareant, quasi coram Domino rationem vestrae villicationis reddituri. De quibus omnibus prædicti R.D.S.R.E. Cardinales petierunt à nobis Notariis infrascriptis, unum vel plura instrumentum atque instrumenta fieri, atque confici debere. Acta fuerunt hæc Mediolani in domo moderna residentiæ prædicti reverendissimi D. Cardinalis Episcopi Prænestini, sita in porta Ticinensi, parrochiæ Sancti Georgii in palatio, sub anno, indictione, die, mense, & Pontificatu quibus supra, præsentibus ibidem illustribus dominis Carolo Jafredo, Præsidente reverendissimi Senatus Regii Mediolani, & Galeatio Vicecomite milite, & Senatoribus gio, testibus idoneis ad prædicta vocatis specialiter & rogatis.
