units.tr: BE IT EVIDENT to all, and made known by the tenor of this present schedule or instrument, that in the year of the Lord's nativity 1511, the fourteenth indiction, on Friday the 16th day of May, in the eighth year of the pontificate of our most holy lord, Lord Julius, by divine providence Pope II, there appeared before us, the undersigned public notaries and the witnesses below, the most reverend fathers in Christ and lords: Lord B., Bishop of Sabina; G., Bishop of Palestrina; and F., cardinal priest of the Holy Martyrs Nereus and Achilleus, of Cosenza, cardinals of the Holy Roman Church. Holding a sufficient mandate in their own names and on behalf of six other lord cardinals, and on behalf of those adhering to them and wishing to adhere, they declared and protested the following words: that, considering how greatly the general councils of the universal Church have benefited the Christian commonwealth militant, and how much the Christian commonwealth has suffered through their intermission; and seeing clearly that there is now a great necessity to summon a universal council, to found a true peace among Christians and to establish sufficient war against the infidels; and especially for the reform of morals in the universal Church, which has greatly collapsed in head and members, and for the amendment of most grave, notorious, continual and incorrigible crimes scandalizing the universal Church, the one healthful remedy for all these diseases of the Church has always been held to be the assembly of a universal council; and since the decade since the last universal council has passed, and the most salutary decrees of the constitution issued which begins Frequens, that a universal council ought to be assembled every ten years; and since our most holy lord, Lord Julius II, to whom the care of convoking it should first have fallen, has neglected this for so long, especially since he vowed and swore to hold it within two years of his creation, and, not only negligent of the precept of the Church and of the council, but also a transgressor of his vow and oath, has not held it; and since time calls out for the man, and a future council is never believed to be celebrated without authority or will; and since grave matters touching the head of the Church must be dealt with, in which case, according to the sanctions of the Fathers and the decrees of the sacred Council of Constance itself, the convocation of a council does not belong to the supreme Pontiff, but in the second place to the most reverend lord cardinals who have not adhered to the Pontiff in such negligence; in similar cases the convocation of a council belongs not to those who take part in his continued negligence: moved by zeal for the house of God, which especially kindles us, having invoked the Mass of the Holy Spirit, and vehemently demanding the reform of the Church in head and members, and declaring from our certain knowledge and spontaneous will, as far as we can and ought by right, in the name of the sacred College of Cardinals which is represented in us, and in this case by right, and also particularly in our own name and in the name of the other cardinals whose mandates we hold, and of other cardinals and prelates adhering to us and wishing to adhere, together with the councillors and procurators of the most sacred lord Maximilian, elected Roman Emperor, ever august, and of the most Christian lord Louis, King of the Franks, Duke of Milan, and of the others adhering to us in this and wishing to adhere, we indict and convoke a general council of the universal Church, and, as far as in us lies, we effectually admonish and exhort that it be assembled, to begin on the Calends of September next to come, in the city of Pisa, and there to continue and be concluded until the determination of the above causes; unless, by consent of the greater part of those gathered in council, some lawful cause requires its transfer to another, more convenient place. Wherefore, with united reverence, humility and insistence, we beseech our most holy lord Pope Julius II a second time, and through the bowels of mercy of our God we earnestly and urgently exhort him to deign to assent to this assembly of the council for the said causes, and to honour and confirm it, either in person or through his legates. Likewise we convoke and require the most reverend lords the cardinals of the Holy Roman Church, patriarchs, archbishops, bishops, kings, princes and potentates, communities, colleges and universities of the general studies, the general superiors and masters of religious orders, and all other prelates of the Church who have authority to define or advise in general councils, and who are accustomed or bound by right or custom to come to a council, that they deign to attend, either themselves, or through solemn orators or procurators (if they cannot attend in person at the place and time stated above), taking care, as far as in them lies, that the council be free, safe and secure, and that everything proceed in the form of the Council of Constance, to the honour of God, the splendour of the Church, the peace of Christians and the overthrow of the infidels; which we, the cardinals of the Holy Roman Church, offer to God and the Church that we will effectually procure, and will do so as far as we can. Wherefore we earnestly beseech and exhort our most holy lord and the most reverend lord cardinals, according to the form of other councils, that they deign to abstain from four things which could most impede such a holy assembly: namely, from the creation of new cardinals and the publication of those created (if any there are); from proceedings against the old cardinals, and against other prelates and persons who by right are entitled to come to this council and who consent to it as is fitting; from impeding this convocation of the council, directly or indirectly, publicly or secretly, under whatever pretext; and from the alienation of fiefs or lands of the Holy Roman Church. In all these matters we protest with all humility that any act (unless it should happen to be done by our most holy lord in the said council) and anything done or to be done otherwise are to be held void; and we protest and require that they be annulled and quashed by the council, or as the law provides. Further, we exhort and admonish all of you, most reverend cardinals and prelates, princes and temporal lords, and other persons of whatever state, rank, condition or pre-eminence, to consent to this our good purpose and to afford fitting favours; and to desist from all molestations, impediments and prohibitions against those coming, or wishing to come, to the said general council, however and in whatever way, directly or indirectly, under any other pretext or device, publicly or secretly; and to abstain from all censures of whatever kind, under pretext of this convocation of the council. And if anything has hitherto been done otherwise about these matters by anyone, by whatever authority, knowingly or unknowingly, we protest the nullity of such acts, and that every remedy to be had in the said general council be applied, so that such things be declared void and null; and we protest of all other remedies known to us, especially from the form of the said Synod of Constance, as we have protested and objected before notable persons, notaries and witnesses, also in writing, on our own behalf and on behalf of those adhering or wishing to adhere; and so we protest and challenge by the tenor of these presents. And since it is not safe for us to make the said convocation of the council and this protest in the presence of our most holy lord, who has had his brothers the cardinals of the Holy Roman Church and the princes of the universal Church cast into prisons and threatened, and who detains the envoys of princes against the law of nations, therefore we have decided, by posting this schedule or instrument of convocation, admonition and protest on the doors of the churches of Modena, Reggio and Parma (from which it may easily come to the notice of your holiness, and to the reverence of the lord cardinals, the Christian princes and the other prelates, and which we ask to have the force of a public edict), that they be required and summoned to come to the council as above, just as if this convocation, admonition and protest had been intimated to them personally; since it is not likely that what is so openly published to all would be unknown or hidden from them. Otherwise, when the said Calends of September arrive, or even have passed, we shall proceed, and shall be proceeded with, step by step and successively, in the said city of Pisa, or in another place to which it happens to be transferred, as stated, by consent of the greater part of those to be gathered, to the celebration and completion of the said general council; together with those most reverend lord cardinals, patriarchs, archbishops, bishops and lords, and others to be cited as above, who shall have assembled with us in the said general council, according to the statutes and decrees of the said Council of Constance; the absence, negligence or contumacy of others who are to be required and cited as above notwithstanding in any way, and those not being further cited or admonished on this account. Of this present instrument, containing this convocation, admonition, protest and decrees, we will give full faith by publication in the said places and others where it may be expedient, by presentation, by affixing on the said doors, and by delivery to any bearer, messenger or agent on our behalf in this matter, whether under oath or by public instrument made by the hand of a public notary. Since the faithful must trust not so much in any solicitous intention as in the prayer of humble and devout entreaty (for we are not sufficient even to think anything of ourselves, as of ourselves, but our sufficiency is from God), according to the word of the Apostle, we therefore beseech the charity of all of you in the Lord, that through you and through the faithful committed to your care, humble prayers be poured out to the Lord, and that you persist in devout prayers, so that He who works concord in the heights may deign to bring it about that the due provision and execution of this our holy deliberation and convocation follow in harmony, swiftly and canonically, as the salvation of the Church requires and the peace and welfare of the whole world desire. And lastly, we exhort you, most reverend archbishops, in the Lord, not to be wanting at the time of this convocation, but meanwhile to summon your suffragans, exempt and non-exempt, and other notable persons of your provinces, so that they may appear without delay at the designated time and place, instructed, with your deliberations and advice and their own, concerning the faith, peace and morals of the faithful, as those who must render an account of your stewardship, as before the Lord. Concerning all these things, the aforesaid most reverend lord cardinals of the Holy Roman Church asked us, the undersigned notaries, to draw up one or more instruments. These things were done at Milan, in the modern residence of the aforesaid most reverend Lord Cardinal, Bishop of Palestrina, situated at the Porta Ticinese, in the parish of St George in Palatio, in the year, indiction, day, month and pontificate stated above; in the presence there of the illustrious lords Carlo Jafredo, President of the most reverend Royal Senate of Milan, and Galeazzo Visconti, knight, and other senators, as suitable witnesses specially summoned and requested for the aforesaid.

units.la: Nomina autem R.D.Cardinalium, à quibus & quorum mandato hujusmodi convocatio facta fuit sequuntur.
units.tr: The names of the most reverend cardinals, by whom and by whose mandate this convocation was made, follow.

units.la: Bernardinus Episcopus Sabinensis, Cardinalis sanctæ Crucis. Guillermus Episcopus Prænestinus, Cardinalis Narbonensis, Philippus Episcopus Tusculanus, Cardinalis Cœnomanensis, Franciscus tt. sanctorum Nerei & Archilei, Cusentinus. Hadrianus tr. sancti Chrysogoni, de Corneto; Renatus tt. sanctæ Sabinæ, Bajocensis. Carolus tt. sancti Viti in Marcello de Finario, presbyteri Cardinales, necnon Dominus Federic. sancti Angeli de Sancto Severino, ac Dominus Hypolitus sanctæ Luciæ in silice Estensis S.R.E. Diaconi Cardinales.
units.tr: Bernardinus, Bishop of Sabina, Cardinal of Santa Croce; Guillermus, Bishop of Palestrina, Cardinal of Narbonne; Philippus, Bishop of Tusculum, Cardinal of Le Mans; Franciscus, Cardinal of the title of Saints Nereus and Achilleus, of Cosenza; Hadrianus, Cardinal of the title of St Chrysogonus, of Corneto; Renatus, Cardinal of the title of St Sabina, of Bayeux; Carolus, Cardinal of the title of St Vitus in Macello, of Finario: these are priest cardinals. Also Lord Federic, Cardinal of St Angelo, of San Severino, and Lord Hippolytus, Cardinal of St Lucy in Silice, of Este, deacon cardinals of the Holy Roman Church.

units.la: Ego Gentilis ex gentilibus Fulginas, publicus Apostolica auctoritate notarius, de prædictis omnibus rogatus. gatus, hanc schedulam seu instrumentum fideliter impressum subscripsi & publicavi signo meo apposito consueto in fidem praemissorum rogatus & requisitus.
units.tr: I, Gentile of the Gentili of Foligno, public notary by apostolic authority, asked about all the above, have subscribed and published this leaflet or instrument, faithfully printed, and have marked it with my customary sign in witness of the foregoing, as I was asked and requested.

units.la: Ego Petrus Rebc, Clericus Heduensis diocesis, auctoritate Apostolica notarius publicus, de praemissis rogatus, hanc schedulam sive instrumentum fideliter impressum una cum praenominato notario subscripsi, & publicavi, signoque meo manuali signavi, in testimonium praemissorum.
units.tr: I, Peter Rebc, clerk of the diocese of Autun, public notary by apostolic authority, asked about the foregoing, have subscribed and published this leaflet or instrument, faithfully printed, together with the aforenamed notary, and have signed it with my hand-mark in testimony of the foregoing.

units.la: CONVOCATIO GENERALIS CONCILII EX PARTE Principum.
units.tr: GENERAL CONVOCATION OF THE COUNCIL ON THE PART OF THE PRINCES.

units.la: ENORE praesentis schedulae seu instrumenti, cunctis pateat evidenter & sit notum, quod anno a nativitate Domini M.D.XI. Indictione XIV. die vero Veneris XVI. mensis Maii, Pontificatus S.D.N. Domini Julii divina providentia Papae II. anno VIII. constituti coram nobis notariis publicis, & testibus infrascriptis, nobiles viri domini Comes Hieronymus Nogarolus, Anto. de Capitibus vaccae, & Ludovicus Faella omnes equites sacratissimi ac Serenissimi Domini Maximiliani Romanorum electi Imperatoris Semper-Augusti Procuratores, necnon spectabiles Jurisconsulti Do. Jo. Bitagus, Franciscus de Vaccis, & Balthasar Platus Christianissimi & serenissimi Domini Ludovici Francorum Regis, & ducis Mediolani similiter Procuratores, & procuratoriis nominibus ad infrascripta sufficienti mandato suorum principalium muniti, proposuerunt & dixerunt sequentia verba, videlicet, quod cum Imperatores Romani & Francorum Reges fuerint semper fautores constantissimi Christianae fidei, & S.R.E. & propugnatores indefessi ac defensores acerrimi contra omnia catholicae fidei & Ecclesiae Romanae obstacula ac scandala, nullis laboribus, nullisque periculis in illarum extirpatione parcentes: & sacratissimi moderni Ro. Imperator, & Francorum Rex supra nominati domini nobis observandissimi, officii sui praedicti non immemores, sed majorum suorum inhaerendo vestigiis, & considerantes, quantam Reipublicae Christianae utilitatem generalia Concilia universalis Ecclesiae attulerunt, quantumque detrimenti ex eorum intermissione Christiana respublica sit passa, quamque impraesentiarum clare conspiciant, magnam instare necessitatem universalis Concilii congregandi, pro vera pace Christianorum fundanda, & sufficienti bello contra infideles stabiliendo, & pro extirpatione haeresum, & errorum, in diversis mundi partibus, superiorum negligentia pullulantium: & similiter schismatum ac divisionum; necnon potissime, pro reformatione morum universalis Ecclesiae in capite & in membris, plurimum collapsorum, ac emendatione criminum gravissimorum, notoriorum, continuorum, aut incorrigibilium, universalem Ecclesiam scandalizantium: quorum omnium Ecclesiae morborum, salutaris & unica medicina, congregatio universalis Concilii semper est habita: quumque tempus decennii, post ultimum universale Concilium, jamdudum sit effluxum, & saluberrima decretali constitutione universalis Ecclesiae irrevocabili ac irrevocata in sacrosanto Constantiensi Concilio edita, quae incipit Frequens, singulis decenniis universale Concilium congregari debeat: & summus Romanus Pontifex modernus, cui primo curae esse deberet, illud convocandi, tanto tempore hoc neglexerit, maxime cum juraverit & voverit post biennium a creatione sua illud tenere debere: & nedum negligens in praecepto Ecclesiae & Concilii, sed & voti & juramenti hujusmodi transgressor, illud non tenuerit: tempusque interpellet pro homine, quum nunquam sua auctoritate aut voluntate futurum Concilium credatur celebrandum, cumque de gravibus Ecclesiae scandalis in capite agendum sit: quo casu juxta patrum sanctiones, & ipsius facti Constant. Concilii decreta, ad summum Pontificem, Concilii convocatio non attineat, & R.D.S.R.E. Cardinales ad quos secundo loco in similibus casibus convocatio Concilii spectaret, divini videantur; & hi qui cum summo Pontifice moram trahunt, vel quia vere non sunt liberi, aut forsan ex negligentia, vel alia ex causa non existimentur convocationi hujusmodi pro nunc velle assistere, seu assentire, pluresque R.D. Card. qui a Curia Romana legitimis ex causis sunt absentes, & aliqui eorum in Lombardia congregati, hujusmodi convocationem Concilii pro superioribus causis, sicuti zelatores domus Dei cordialiter effl agitent, & enixe deposcant, quod etiam a nobis Procuratoribus instanter requisiti convocaverunt, & indixerunt. Prodebuto ergo, quo principes nostri supradicti Christo domino Creatori & redemptori tenentur, ac splendori sanctissimae sponsae suae Romanae & universalis Ecclesiae, ac paci & incremento fidei obligantur, eorum auctoritate & mandato, & de eorum certa scientia, & spontanea voluntate, quantum jure melius possumus & debemus, nomine supradictorum dominorum Concilium generale universalis Ecclesiae indicimus, & convocamus, & quantum in nobis est effectualiter congregati monemus, & hortamur futurum, in civitate Pisana, ad Calendas Septembris proxime futuri, inibi inchoandum, continuandum, actque terminandum, usque ad definitionem superiorum causarum, nisi de consensu majoris partis congregandorum in Concilio, alia legitima causa ad alium locum commodiorem transferendum sit. Quapropter cum omni reverentia & humilitate ac instantia S.D.N. Julium Papam II, nomine quo supra, supplicamus, & per viscera misericordiae Dei nostri requirimus, ut huic vocationi Concilii pro dictis causis assentire dignetur, & illud per se naliter vel per legatos suos honorare, & confirmare: similiter & R.D.S.R.E. Cardinales, Patriarchas, Archiepiscopos, Episcopos, Reges, & Principes, & potentatus, necnon alios Ecclesiae praelatos, communitates, & universitates studiorum generalium, Collegia ac Religionum generales, & magistros, & in Conciliis generalibus auctoritate defiendi aut consulendi habentes, & ad Concilium de jure venire solitos, & obligatos convocamus; & requirimus ut per se, vel per solemnes oratores vel procuratores (si commode personaliter interesse non poterunt) ad Concilium ipsum, loco & tempore quibus supra, accedere dignentur: procura quantum in eis erit, ut Concilium fit liberum, tutum, & securum, & in eo juxta formam Constantiensis Synodi procedatur, ad honorem Dei, & Ecclesiæ splendorem, pacem Christianorum, & exterminationem infidelium, quod observandissimi ipsi nostri principes, & domini nobis merito reverendissimi, pro viribus suis offerunt Deo & Ecclesiæ se effectualiter procuraturos & factiros. Necnon eorum nomine & auctoritate S.D.N. & R.D. Cardinalium juxta formam aliorum Conciliorum hortamur, & requirimus, ut a quatuor causis, quæ maxime possent hujusmodi sanctam congregationem impedire, abstinere etiam dignentur, videlicet a creatione novorum Cardinalium, & a publicatione creatorum (si qui forsan sunt) & processu contra antiquos Cardinales, aliosque prælatos, & personas ad Concilium ipsum accedere volentes, & illi prout decet consentientes, necnon ab impediendo hujusmodi convocationem Concilii directe vel indirecte, publice vel occulte quovis quæsito colore, & abalienatione feudorum seu terrarum S.R.E. in quibus omnibus casibus, protestantur domini nobis observandissimi principales, de nullitate actus (nisi a S.D.N. in dicto Concilio hujusmodi fierent) & alias facta, vel facienda, irrita haberi, ac per Concilium ipsum annullari, & cassari debere protestantur, & requirunt. Et quia tamen non esset nobis Procuratoribus dictam convocationem Concilii & protestationem in præsentia S.D.N. facere, qui S.R.E. Card. fratres suos & Ecclesiæ universalis principes carceribus aliquando mancipandos minari fecit, Oratoresque principum contra jus gentium detinen, pro notorium est, & pro notorio allegatur; ideo decrevimus, per affixionem hujusmodi schedulæ, sive instrumenti convocationis, monitionis, seu protestationis hujusmodi, in valvis Ecclesiarum Mutinensis, Rhegiensis & Parmensis (ex quibus verisimiliter ad notitiam sanctitatis suæ & R.D. Cardinalium ac principum Christianorum & aliorum prælatorum venire poterit, quam viin publici edicti habere petimus & principales domini nobis observandissimi habere decreverunt & voluerunt) perinde attractare ad veniendum ad Concilium supra requisitos, & monitos, ac si personaliter illis fuisset intimatus, vel exhibita ipsa convocatio, monitio, & protestatio: quum non sit verisimile, ipsis fore incognitum vel occultum, quod tam patenter omnibus publicatur. De quibus omnibus dicti domini Consiliarii, Commissarii & Procuratores, petierunt a nobis notariis infrascriptis unum vel plura instrumenta vel instrumenta fieri atque confici debere. Acta fuerunt hæc Mediolani in domibus habitationis moderoæ residentiæ R.D. domini G. Episcopi Cardinalis Prænestini, sitis in porta Ticinensi, pro... S.G. in palatio, sub anno, indictione, die mense & Pontificatu quibus supra, præsentibus ibidem illust. Dominis Galeatio Vicecomite milite magnifico J.U.D. Domino Hieronymo Morono, filio quondam D.Jo.Re. Senatoris Mediolani; magnifico D. Bernard. Guacio, filio quondam D. Anto. Prætor. Papiæ, & D. Benedicto Abriono, filio quondam Domini Christ. Vicarii D. Capitanei justitiæ Mediolani, ac domino Principivallo de Monte Regio, Secretario Mediolani, testibus idoneis ad præmissa vocatis, & specialiter rogatis.
units.tr: By the tenor of this present leaflet or instrument, let it be plain and known to all that in the year from the birth of the Lord 1511, in the fourteenth indiction, on Friday the sixteenth day of May, in the eighth year of the pontificate of our most holy lord Julius II, by divine providence Pope, there appeared before us, the undersigned public notaries and the witnesses below named, the noble men Count Hieronymus Nogarolus, Antonius de Capitibus Vaccae, and Ludovicus Faella, all knights and procurators of the most sacred and most serene lord Maximilian, elected Emperor of the Romans, ever August; and likewise the distinguished jurists Johannes Bitagus, Franciscus de Vaccis, and Balthasar Platus, procurators of the most Christian and most serene lord Louis, King of the French and Duke of Milan, who, provided with sufficient mandate from their principals for the matters below written, proposed and said the following words, namely: that since the Emperors of the Romans and the Kings of the French have always been most constant supporters of the Christian faith and of the Holy Roman Church, and tireless defenders and most fierce champions against all obstacles and scandals to the Catholic faith and the Roman Church, sparing no labours or dangers in their eradication; and since the most sacred present Roman Emperor and the King of the French, the lords named above, our most observant masters, mindful of their aforesaid office, and keeping to the footsteps of their ancestors, and considering how great a benefit to the Christian commonwealth the general councils of the universal Church have brought, and how much harm the Christian commonwealth has suffered from their discontinuance, and seeing clearly at present that there is a great necessity of gathering a universal council, both to establish a true peace among Christians, and to set up a sufficient war against the infidels, and for the extirpation of heresies and errors which, through the negligence of superiors, spring up in various parts of the world, and likewise of schisms and divisions; and above all for the reformation of morals of the universal Church, in head and in members, which has greatly collapsed, and for the correction of the most grave, notorious, continual or incorrigible crimes which scandalize the universal Church: for all these diseases of the Church the one wholesome remedy has always been held to be the gathering of a universal council; and since a period of ten years has long since passed since the last universal council, and by the most salutary decretal constitution of the universal Church, issued at the holy Council of Constance, which begins Frequens, an universal council ought to be gathered every ten years, irrevocable and unrevoked; and since the present supreme Roman Pontiff, whose first care ought to be to convoke it, has neglected this for so long a time, especially since he swore and vowed that he would hold it within two years of his creation, and not only is negligent of the precept of the Church and of the Council, but is also a transgressor of this vow and oath, in not having held it; and since time urges on the matter, as the future council is not believed ever to be held by his authority or will, and since grave scandals of the Church must be dealt with at the head; in which case, according to the sanctions of the Fathers and the decrees of the Council of Constance itself, the convocation of a council does not belong to the supreme Pontiff, and the most reverend cardinals of the Holy Roman Church, to whom in such cases the convocation of a council would belong in the second place, seem to be of divine right; and those who delay with the supreme Pontiff, either because they are not truly free, or perhaps through negligence, or for some other reason, are not thought to wish to assist or assent to such a convocation for the present; and several most reverend cardinals who are absent from the Roman Curia for lawful reasons, and some of them gathered in Lombardy, zealously urge and earnestly demand, for the above causes, as zealots of the house of God, this convocation of a council, which they also, being instantly requested by us procurators, have convoked and proclaimed. Therefore, since our aforesaid princes are bound to Christ the Lord, Creator and Redeemer, and are obliged to the splendour of his most holy spouse, the Roman and universal Church, and to the peace and increase of the faith, by their authority and mandate, and with their certain knowledge and spontaneous will, as well as we best can and ought by law, in the name of the aforesaid lords we indict and convoke a general council of the universal Church, and as far as lies in us we effectually admonish and exhort that it be assembled in the city of Pisa at the Kalends of September next, there to be begun, continued, and brought to an end, until the decision of the above causes, unless by the consent of the greater part of those to be gathered in the council, another lawful reason requires that it be transferred to another more convenient place. Wherefore, with all reverence and humility and insistence, in the name aforesaid, we beseech our most holy lord Pope Julius II, and by the bowels of mercy of our God we require, that he deign to assent to this convocation of the council for the said causes, and to honour and confirm it, either in person or through his legates; likewise we convoke and require the most reverend cardinals of the Holy Roman Church, patriarchs, archbishops, bishops, kings, princes, and powers, as well as other prelates of the Church, communities and universities of general studies, colleges and general orders of religion, and masters who have authority to define or to advise in general councils, and who are accustomed and bound by law to come to the council; and we require that they deign to come to the council itself, at the place and time aforesaid, in person or through solemn orators or procurators (if they cannot conveniently be present in person); and that they take care, as far as lies in them, that the council be free, safe, and secure, and that in it proceedings be carried on according to the form of the Synod of Constance, to the honour of God and the splendour of the Church, the peace of Christians, and the extermination of the infidels; which our most observant princes and lords, deservedly most reverend to us, offer, according to their strength, that they will effectually procure and do for God and the Church. Furthermore, in their name and by their authority, we exhort and require our most holy lord and the most reverend cardinals, according to the form of other councils, that they also deign to abstain from the four causes which could most of all impede such a holy gathering: namely from the creation of new cardinals, and the publication of those created (if any there are), and from proceedings against the old cardinals and other prelates and persons who wish to come to the council itself, and who consent to it as is fitting; and likewise from impeding this convocation of the council, directly or indirectly, publicly or secretly, under any pretext whatever; and from the alienation of fiefs or lands of the Holy Roman Church. In all of these cases our most observant principals protest and require that any act done or to be done otherwise, except by our most holy lord in the said council, be held void and be declared null and annulled by the council itself. And because it would not be possible for us procurators to make the said convocation of the council and this protest in the presence of our most holy lord, who has caused the cardinals of the Holy Roman Church, his brothers, and the princes of the universal Church to be threatened at times with being cast into prison, and who has detained the orators of princes contrary to the law of nations, as is notorious and is alleged as notorious; therefore we have decided, by the posting of this leaflet or instrument of convocation, admonition, or protest on the doors of the churches of Modena, Reggio, and Parma (from which it may probably come to the notice of his holiness and of the most reverend cardinals, of the Christian princes and of other prelates, which we ask to have made known as by public edict, and which our principal and most observant lords have decided and wished to have), to summon those required and warned to come to the council, just as if the convocation, admonition, and protest had been intimated to them personally or presented to them: since it is not probable that these things would be unknown or hidden from them, when they are so openly published to all. Concerning all of which the said lords, counsellors, commissioners and procurators asked us, the undersigned notaries, that one or more instruments be made and drawn up. These things were done at Milan, in the house of the present residence of the most reverend lord G., Bishop and Cardinal of Palestrina, situated at the Ticino gate, in the parish of St George in palatio, in the year, indiction, day, month and pontificate written above, the following being present there: the illustrious lords Galeazzo Visconti, knight; the magnificent J.U.D. Lord Hieronymus Moronus, son of the late Lord Johannes Re, senator of Milan; the magnificent Lord Bernardus Guacius, son of the late Lord Antonius, praetor of Pavia; and Lord Benedictus Abrionus, son of the late Lord Christophorus, vicar of the captain of justice of Milan; and Lord Principivallus de Monte Regio, secretary of Milan; suitable witnesses called and specially requested for the premises.

units.la: Ego Gentilis ex gentilibus Fulginas, publicus Apostolica auctoritate notarius, de præmissis rogatus, hanc schedulam seu instrumentum fideliter impressum subscripsi, & publicavi signo meo appositio, confucto, in fidem præmissorum rogatus & requisitus.
units.tr: I, Gentile of Foligno, a public notary by Apostolic authority, having been requested in the matters set out above, have subscribed and published this schedule or instrument, faithfully printed, and have affixed my sign, the mark of confirmation, as requested and required, in witness of the foregoing.

units.la: Ego Petrus Rebe, Clericus Heduensis Diocesis, auctoritate Apostolica Notarius publicus, de præmissis rogatus, hanc schedulam sive instrumentum fideliter impressum, una cum prænominato Notario subscripsi, & publicavi, signoque meo manuali signavi, in testimonium præmissorum.
units.tr: I, Pierre Rebe, clerk of the diocese of Autun, a public notary by Apostolic authority, having been requested in the matters set out above, have subscribed and published this schedule or instrument, faithfully printed, together with the aforesaid notary, and have signed it with my hand-sign, in witness of the foregoing.

units.la: SERENISSIMI ROMANORUM IM- PERATORIS ELECTI MAXIMILIANI SEM- PER-AUGUSTI EPISTOLÆ, quibus prælibata generalis Concilii indictio recipitur & approbatur.
units.tr: THE LETTERS OF THE MOST SERENE MAXIMILIAN, ELECTED EMPEROR OF THE ROMANS, EVER AUGUST, BY WHICH THE PREVIOUSLY ANNOUNCED GENERAL COUNCIL IS RECEIVED AND APPROVED.

units.la: A TERGO
units.tr: ON THE REVERSE

units.la: Reverendissimis in Christo patribus domino Cardinalibus Mediolani constituta amicis charissimis.
units.tr: To the most reverend fathers in Christ, the lord Cardinals established at Milan, our dearest friends.

units.la: MAXIMILIANUS, divina favente clementia electus Rom. Imperator Semper-Augustus, &c. Reverendissimi patres, amici charissimi salutem, cum incremento omnis boni. Accepimus complures literas V. Reverendiss. D. quibus nobis significant, quomodo una cum nobis serenissimi Regis Franciæ fratris nostri charissimi procuratoribus, indixerunt Concilium, & cum eadem literis suis accepimus schedulas ejusmodi denunciationis, & copias literarum datarum, ad serenissimum Regem Aragonum fratrem nostrum charissimum, quæ omnia nobis summopere placuerunt, & ea approbamus, sicuti aliquanto latius scribimus procuratoribus nostris, ibidem apud D.V. Reverendiss. existentibus, & quoniam jam primo rediit ad nos venerabilis Mathæus Episcopus Gurgensis Princeps & Consiliarius noster devotus dilectus, intellecto ab eo successu omnium rerum, litius scribemus D.V. Reverendiss. & eisdem Procuratoribus nostris, quibus circa omnia resolute mea firma nostram signisicabimus, quæ erit ad omnimodam prosecutionem hujusmodi Concilii, ad laudem Dei, & incrementum suæ sanctæ fidei, & confusionem hostium ejus, datum in oppido Muldors die quinta mensis Julii, Anno Domini M.D.XI. Regni nostri Romani XXVI. Per Regem. Ad mandatum Cæs. Majestatis proprium, Jacobi de Bannissis.
units.tr: Maximilian, by the favouring grace of God elected Roman Emperor, ever August, etc. To the most reverend fathers, our dearest friends, greeting, with the increase of every good. We have received several letters from your Reverences, in which they inform us how, together with the procurators of our most serene and dearest brother, the King of France, they have declared the Council, and with the same letters we have received copies of the notices of such a declaration and of the letters dated to our most serene and dearest brother, the King of Aragon. All of these things have greatly pleased us, and we approve them, as we write more fully to our procurators, who are present there with your Reverences. And since our trusted and beloved councillor and prince, the venerable Matthew, Bishop of Gurk, has already returned to us, and we have learned from him the outcome of all matters, we will write further to your Reverences and to the same procurators of ours, and we will make known to them our firm and settled will on all points, which shall be for the full prosecution of this Council, to the praise of God, the increase of his holy faith, and the confusion of its enemies. Given in the town of Mühldorf, on the fifth day of July, in the year of the Lord 1511, in the twenty-sixth year of our Roman reign. By the King. By the express command of His Imperial Majesty, Jacob de Bannissis.

units.la: A TERGO. Nobilibus, fidelibus, nobis dilectis Consiliariis, & Commissariis nostris Me- diolani.
units.tr: On the back: To our noble, faithful and beloved councillors and commissioners at Milan.

units.la: MAXIMILIANUS, divina favente clementia E.R.o. Imperator Semper-Augustus, &c. Nobiles, fideles, dilecti, accepimus literas vestras, die XVI. Et postea die XXIII. praeteritis, & ex illis intelleximus tractata per vos nomine nostro, cum Reverendiss. D. Card. Mediolani existentibus, ac venerabili Episcopo Parisiensi in causa Concilii universalis Ecclesiae, cujus indictionis schedulas ad nos transmissas, pariter percepimus, simulque ordinem & modum servatum ad illud indicendum, quae nobis omnia valde placuerunt, nec satis probare & laudare possumus prudentiam & dexteritatem vestram, quam adhibuistis in explicando tanto negotio, quodque in omnibus secuti fueritis consilium praefati Episcopi Parisiensis, ut vobis erat injunctum, gratum habuimus.
units.tr: MAXIMILIAN, by the favour of divine clemency elected Roman Emperor, always Augustus, etc. Noble, faithful and beloved: We have received your letters of the 16th and afterwards of the 23rd of last month, and from them we have learned of the business you have transacted in our name with the most reverend Lord Cardinals who are at Milan, and with the venerable Bishop of Paris, concerning the council of the universal Church. We have likewise received the copies of the notice of its convocation sent to us, and the order and method observed in calling it. All these things have pleased us greatly, and we cannot sufficiently commend or praise the prudence and skill you have shown in handling so great a matter. We are also pleased that in all things you have followed the counsel of the aforesaid Bishop of Paris, as you were instructed to do.

units.la: Volumus insuper, & ita vobis committimus, ut a R.D. Cardinalibus praefatis, & ab aliis quibus vobis videbitur, exactam capiatis informationem, & vos ipsi, judicium vestrum nobis perscribatis, de omnibus quae videntur esse per nos agenda in prosecutione dicti Concilii, quae & quales literae per orbem Christianum scribendae, & ad quos, quove pacto sit a nobis procedendum, tam in hoc principio quam in progressu, & quomodo cum Papa progredi debeamus, redigatisque omnium opiniones, & consilium de omnibus in scriptis, per bonum ordinem, ut juxta illum procedere habeamus, sicut nostra est intentio. Literas etiam per nos ut supra scribendas, curetis ab eis formari (licet nos aliquas scripserimus & emiserimus) in eam quam voluerint sententiam, ad nosque mittetis, ut juxta formulam expediri facere ea valeamus, ad quoscumque opus fuerit. Sed ante omnia, agetis nostro nomine gratias R.D. Cardinalibus, quod ad nostram requisitionem & exhortationem tam prompte & voluntarie reipublicae Christianae & universalis Ecclesiae periclitantis causam amplexi fuerint, denuo hortando eos, ut quo animo inceperunt, sic velint prosequi, pollicendo nos eis fautores, & auxiliatores constantissimos, usque ad finalem Concilii terminationem, de qua, Deo dante speramus eos mentum apud Deum & laudem apud homines reportaturos, manebitisque. Mediolani, apud reverendiss. D. eorum & praefatum Parisiensem, quandiu ipsi necesse duxerint vos sibi esse, pro rebus dicti Concilii, in quibus vos ea prudentia & fide semper gubernabitis, quam de vobis praesumimus: pro certo habentes nos benemeritorum vestrorum memoriam, & rationem habituros. Agetis insuper gratias praefato Parisiensi Episcopo nomine nostro, de bona intelligentia habita in proximo tractatu, cum venerabili Episcopo Gurgensi, principe & Consiliario nostro devoto dilecto, & de bonis ac sinceris officiis, & operibus quae praestitit in communibus rebus nostris, & serenissimi Regis sui, respiciendo honorem & utilitatem nostram aeque ac praefati regis sui, sicuti a praefato Gurgenli nobis scriptum est, & postea relatum, ostendendo nos eorum memores futuros, ac gratos, ubicumque contigerit nos aliquid posse efficere, quod ad dignitatem & commodum pertineat. Rediit jam ad nos idem Gurgensis, qui inter alia retulit nobis singularem prudentiam vestram, qua cum omni fide & affectu erga nos, astitisse sibi in negotiis nostris, quod & si jampridem pro comperto habeamus, gratum tamen multum fuit, ab eodem Gurgensi intelligere, hortamurque vos ut sicuti nobis certo persuademus, ita continue persistere velitis in omnibus rebus nostris, & nos condignam rationem habituri simus virtutum & meritorum vestrorum. Datum in oppido Muldorff. V. die mensis Junii, Anno Domini M.D.XI. Regni nostri Romani XXVI.
units.tr: Furthermore we wish, and so commit to you, that you obtain from the aforesaid most reverend Lord Cardinals, and from others whom you see fit, a thorough report; and that you yourselves send us your judgement on all those matters which seem to require action on our part in the furtherance of the said council: what letters ought to be written through the Christian world, and to whom, and in what manner we ought to proceed, both at the outset and in the course of the business, and how we ought to deal with the Pope. You are to gather their opinions and counsel on all these matters in writing, in good order, so that we may proceed in accordance with them, as is our intention. As for the letters which, as above, are to be written by us (although we have already written and sent some), you are to see to it that they are drawn up by them in whatever sense they wish, and send them to us, so that we may have them dispatched according to the form, to whomever it may be necessary. But above all, you shall offer our thanks in our name to the most reverend Lord Cardinals, for having embraced the cause of the Christian commonwealth and of the universal Church, which is in peril, so promptly and willingly at our request and exhortation. Urge them again to pursue it with the same spirit with which they began, promising that we shall be their steadfast supporters and helpers until the final conclusion of the council, from which, God willing, we hope they will win merit before God and praise among men. You shall remain at Milan, with their most reverend lordships and the aforesaid Bishop of Paris, for as long as they judge it necessary to have you with them for the affairs of the said council, in which you will continue to govern matters with that prudence and fidelity which we presume of you, being firmly assured that we shall keep in mind and reward your good services. You shall also offer our thanks to the aforesaid Bishop of Paris in our name, for the good understanding reached in the recent negotiations with the venerable Bishop of Gurk, our devoted and beloved prince and councillor, and for the good and sincere offices and labours which he has performed in our common affairs and those of his most serene King, having regard to our honour and advantage no less than that of the said King, as has been written to us by the aforesaid Gurk and afterwards reported. Show that we shall be mindful and grateful of them, wherever it may befall us to be able to do anything that pertains to their dignity and advantage. The same Bishop of Gurk has now returned to us, and among other things has reported to us your singular prudence, by which, with all loyalty and goodwill towards us, you have stood by him in our affairs. Although we have long held this to be certain, it was nonetheless very welcome to hear it from the same Bishop of Gurk. We exhort you to continue, as we are firmly persuaded you will, in all our affairs, and we shall give due regard to your virtues and merits. Given at the town of Muldorf, on the fifth day of the month of June, in the year of the Lord 1511, in the twenty-sixth year of our Roman reign.

units.la: JACOBUS DE BANNISSIS.
units.tr: JACOBUS DE BANNISSIS.

units.la: CHRISTIANISSIMI FRANCORUM REGIS D. LUDOVICI EPISTOLAE QUIBUS EADEM indictio approbatur & acceptatur.
units.tr: THE LETTERS OF THE MOST CHRISTIAN KING OF THE FRANKS, LORD LOUIS, BY WHICH THE SAME INDICTION IS APPROVED AND ACCEPTED.

units.la: A TERGO. Reverendissimis in Christo patribus, & dominis sanctae Crucis, Narbonensi, & Cusent. S.R.E. Cardinalibus, fratribus nostris charissimis.
units.tr: On the back: To the most reverend fathers in Christ and lords, the Cardinals of the Holy Cross, of Narbonne and of Cusa, of the Holy Roman Church, our most beloved brothers.

units.la: EVERENDISSIMI in Christo patres, & fratres nostri charissimi, recepimus literas quibus nos certioratis de indictione sacri Concilii, facta per D.V. reverendiss. una cum Procuratoribus serenissimi Rom. Imperatoris E. Semper-Augusti, fratris & consanguinei nostri honorandi, & nostris, accepimusque schedulas dictae indictionis, quas cum nobis plurimum placuerint alacri animo approbamus. Ut autem praelibatae D.V. reverendiss. intelligant quanti facimus hujusmodi indictum Concilium, optemusque illud ad laudem & servitium omnipotentis Dei, utilitatemque reformationem, & exaltationem Ecclesiae sanctae, ac confusionem inimicorum ejus, debitum sortiri effectum, elegimus copiosum numerum Praelatorum, Theologorum, & jurisperitorum, de almis Universitatibus Galliarum, ad eumdem, & assistendum in ipso sancto Concilio nomine Gallicanae Ecclesiae. Nos quoque pro ipso sacrosancto Concilio, omnes necessarias provisiones, pro virili nostra ministrare curabimus, sicuti a praesentium tabellario & nuncio nostro diffusius intelligere poteritis. Valeant D.V. reverendiss. quas Deus omnipotens assidue custodiat. Datum Valentiae, die XVIII. Julii M.D.XI.
units.tr: Most reverend fathers in Christ and our most beloved brothers: we have received your letter informing us of the indiction of the holy Council, made by your Reverences together with the procurators of the most serene Roman Emperor, Elected Augustus, our honoured brother and kinsman; and we have received the schedules of the said indiction, which, since they have pleased us greatly, we approve with a willing mind. Moreover, so that your aforesaid Reverences may understand how highly we value this indicted Council, and how earnestly we wish it to attain its due outcome, to the praise and service of almighty God, the benefit and reformation and exaltation of the holy Church, and the confusion of her enemies, we have chosen a considerable number of prelates, theologians and jurists from the nourishing universities of France to go to the same and to attend in the holy Council itself in the name of the Gallican Church. We too shall take care to supply, as far as in us lies, all the necessary provisions for the holy Council, as you may learn more fully from the bearer of these presents and our messenger. May your Reverences be well, whom almighty God constantly keep. Given at Valence, the 18th day of July, 1511.

units.la: MAXIMILIANI I. IMP. AUG. EDICTUM
units.tr: Edict of the Emperor Maximilian I, August

units.la: De vitio ingluviei & ebrietatis.
units.tr: On the vice of gluttony and drunkenness.

units.la: INN institutis à MAXIMILIANO I. Imper. Trevirensibus Comitiis anno supra millesimum quingentesimum duodecimo, postea Coloniæ finitis, uti de gravissimis alioquin Imperii negotiis, de pace nimirum publica conservanda: de auxiliis Imperatori, communi subditorum Imperii contributione præstandis: de schismate Cardinalium non tolerando: de proscriptione Edezardi Comitis Emdani, Imperatoris mandatis non parentis: de Groninga Phrysiæ metropoli, Georgio Duci Saxoniæ restituenda: ita quoque de vitio ingluviei & ebrietatis, radice omnium flagitiorum, præsentibus omnibus Septemviris & Ordinibus Imperii, consultatio diligens instituta est, de qua gravissime conclusum, edictoq; publico confirmatum talem in modum.
units.tr: Instituted by Maximilian I, Emperor, at the Diet of Trier in the year 1512 after the thousandth five hundredth and twelfth, and afterwards concluded at Cologne: where, among the other most weighty affairs of the Empire, namely the maintenance of public peace, the aids to be furnished to the Emperor by the common contribution of the subjects of the Empire, the non-toleration of the schism of the Cardinals, the proscription of Edzard, Count of Emden, who did not obey the Emperor's commands, and the restoration of Groningen, metropolis of Friesland, to Duke George of Saxony, so too careful deliberation was undertaken concerning the vice of gluttony and drunkenness, the root of all wickedness, with all the Electors and Estates of the Empire present; and it was resolved in the most serious manner, and confirmed by public edict in the following form.

units.la: Nos MAXIMILIANUS I. Dei gratia, electus Romanorum Imperator, &c. Quamvis ante hac tempora aliquibus in Conventibus aliquoties de ingluviei vitio, ipsaque adeo ebrietate vitanda pronunciatum gravissimè sit, tamen id in effectum hactenus nondum deductum.
units.tr: We, Maximilian I, by the grace of God elected Emperor of the Romans, etc. Although on several occasions in earlier times, at various Assemblies, it has been declared most seriously that the vice of gluttony, and indeed drunkenness itself, is to be avoided, yet this has so far not been carried into effect.

units.la: Quocirca cum ex immoderata & vitiosa ingluvie cibi potusque ebrietas: ex ebrietate vero, tanquam uberrimo fonte & scaturigine plenissima, omnis generis impietas, blasphemia, injuriæ, cædes, aliaque scelera quamplurima, promanent & exoriantur, ac revera ea sit litium propagatio, suorum genitrix, petulantiæ magistra: experientia insuper testetur, quòd ebrii ex se quasi rapti, non solùm omnem præeminentiæ, existimationis, dignitatis, aliorumq; honorum fastigio, summo cum dedecore, & ignominia haud contemnenda, seipsos privent, verùm etiam animæ, rationis, sensuum, fortunarum, bonorum, vitæ denique, corporis, ac salutis æternæ jacturam faciant certissimam, irreparabilem quenam harum universis ac singulis nostris, & S. Rom. Imperii, Regnorum, Dominiorum, Provinciarum, nostrarum hereditariarum subditis, cujuscunque status, gradus, ordinis, conditionis, dignitatis aut præeminentiæ existant, tam Ecclesiasticis quàm Saecularibus, serio mandamus & injungimus, ut contumaces ac violatores hujus nostri Cæsarei mandati, si quos forte deprehenderint, pœna non contemnenda multati, aliisq; idoneis ac opportunis mediis coerceri curent, nec id quenquam impune violare, spernere aut transgredi permittant. Si qui verò è Nobilibus, aut Equestris Ordinis viris ab hoc vitio sibi temperare minimè velint, eos cane pejores & angue abominandos, ac ab officiis & muneribus S. Romani Imperii publicis, aliisque dignitatum tam ecclesiasticarum quàm politicarum fastigiis removendos ac abdicandos sancimus & volumus, remotosque & abdicatos, neque promovendos, neque ampliùs dignitatibus præficiendos ullis esse, censemus & statuimus. Tenuioris autem fortunæ homines pœna afficiendos capitali pronunciamus. Si quis porrò Magistratus superior aut inferior, in exequenda hac pœna, negligentior aut remissior exiterit, nostram & S. Rom. Imperii indignationem gravissimam, acque multam fisco sive ærario nostro Imperiali, omni spe veniæ sublata, ii remissibiliter solvendam, ipso facto se noverit incurrisse. Iis verò in locis, ubi hoc ingluviei gulaeque vitium consuetudine veteri introductum perspiciant, summa cum animadversione, simili pœna proposità capitali, illud declinent.
units.tr: Therefore, since from immoderate and vicious gluttony in food and drink comes drunkenness, and from drunkenness, as from a most abundant spring and fullest fountain, every kind of impiety, blasphemy, injuries, murders and many other crimes proceed and arise, and indeed this is the breeding-ground of quarrels, the mother of them, the teacher of wantonness; and since experience further shows that drunkards, as if carried away out of themselves, deprive themselves not only of the summit of all pre-eminence, esteem, dignity and other honours, with great disgrace and no small ignominy, but also incur the most certain and irreparable loss of soul, reason, senses, fortunes, goods, indeed of life, body and eternal salvation: we seriously command and enjoin all and each of our subjects, and those of the Holy Roman Empire, of our kingdoms, dominions, provinces and hereditary lands, of whatever state, rank, order, condition, dignity or pre-eminence they may be, whether ecclesiastical or secular, that they take care to restrain by punishment, not to be despised, and by other suitable and fitting means, any transgressors and violators of this our Imperial mandate whom they may happen to detect, and that they permit no one to violate, despise or transgress it with impunity. If any of the nobles or men of the equestrian order are wholly unwilling to refrain from this vice, we decree and will that they be worse than dogs and abominable as serpents, and removed and dismissed from public offices and duties of the Holy Roman Empire, and from the heights of ecclesiastical as well as political dignities; and we judge and decree that, once removed and dismissed, they are neither to be promoted nor again placed over any dignities. Men of humbler fortune, however, we declare are to be punished with capital punishment. Furthermore, if any magistrate, superior or inferior, shall be more negligent or lax in carrying out this penalty, let him know that he has incurred, by the very fact, our most grave indignation and that of the Holy Roman Empire, and a fine to be paid without remission to our fisc or Imperial treasury, with all hope of pardon removed. In those places where the officials perceive that this vice of gluttony and carousing has been introduced by long-standing custom, they are to avoid it with the greatest vigilance, under the same proposed penalty of capital punishment.

units.la: MAXIMILIANUS divina favente clementia Electus Romanorum Imperator Semper Augustus, ac Germaniarum, Hungariæ, Dalmatiæ, Croatiæ, &c. Rex; Archidux Austriæ; Dux Burgundiæ, Lotharingiæ, Brabantiæ, Stiriæ, Carinthiæ, Carniolæ, Limburgiæ, Lucemburgiæ & Geldriæ; Landgravius Alsatiæ; Princeps Sueviæ; Palatinus in Habspurg & Hannoniæ; Princeps & Comes Burgundiæ, Flandriæ, Tirolis, Goritiæ, Arthesii, Holandiæ, Selandiæ, Frireris, in Kiburg, Namurii & Dusburgi; Marchio Sacri Romani Imperii Antuerpiæ, Super Anasum, & Burgoviæ; Dominus Phtisiæ, Marchiæ Sclavonicæ, Mechliniæ & Salinarum.
units.tr: MAXIMILIAN, by the favour of divine clemency, elected Emperor of the Romans, ever Augustus, and King of Germany, Hungary, Dalmatia, Croatia, etc.; Archduke of Austria; Duke of Burgundy, Lorraine, Brabant, Styria, Carinthia, Carniola, Limburg, Luxemburg and Guelders; Landgrave of Alsace; Prince of Swabia; Count Palatine of Habsburg and Hainault; Prince and Count of Burgundy, Flanders, Tyrol, Gorizia, Artois, Holland, Zeeland, Friesland, in Kyburg, Namur and Dusburg; Margrave of the Holy Roman Empire, of Antwerp, Upper Ems and Burgau; Lord of Pfirt, the Slavonic March, Mechlin and the Saltworks.

units.la: 1. Gloria Reipublicæ decusque totius Romani Imperii, & subditorum utilitas, in quorum prosperitate utique proseperamur, Nos, qui superna providione, & non nostris meritis, ad culmen Imperialis seu Cæsareæ Dignitatis, & plenitudinem potestatis, sublimati sumus, inducunt, ut non solùm ad ea, quæ ad augmentum & sublimationem Imperii, sed & ea, quæ ad reformationem deformitatum, correctionem errorum, & defectuum emendationem pertinent, ac periculorum submotionem, quæ in Republica aliquando contingunt, & subditis quotidiè imminent, aciem nostræ considerationis dirigamus, hinc in initio regiminis nostri, & susceptæ administrationis in Imperio pro justitia & pace conservanda, quæ tunc quodammodo in finibus Imperii exulaverunt, certas, per quas celerius cau in justitia expediantur, & illi qui pacem turbare conantur, acrius quàm antè coherceantur & compnmantur, edidimus Ordinationes.
units.tr: 1. The glory of the commonwealth, the honour of the whole Roman Empire and the welfare of the subjects, in whose prosperity we ourselves certainly prosper, lead us, who by higher providence and not by our own merits have been raised to the summit of the Imperial or Caesarean dignity and the fullness of power, to direct the attention of our consideration not only to those things which pertain to the increase and elevation of the Empire, but also to those which pertain to the reform of deformities, the correction of errors and the amendment of defects, and to the removal of those dangers which at times arise in the commonwealth and daily threaten the subjects. Therefore, at the beginning of our reign and of the administration we have undertaken in the Empire, for the preservation of justice and peace, which at that time had in some measure been banished from the borders of the Empire, we have issued certain ordinances, by which cases may be decided more swiftly in justice, and those who attempt to disturb the peace may be restrained and suppressed more sharply than before.

units.la: 2. Verùm quia nedum pro justitia & pace manutenenda, sed etiam quæ quotidiè in Republica & subditis occurrunt, tabellionatus seu tabellariorum officium perutile & necessarium existat, per quod placita, vota & gesta hominum (ne memoriæ labiliati seu oblivioni subdantur) per scripturæ ministerium certæ & perpetuæ memoriæ traduntur, publicisque firmantur documentis. Et quamplurimi Notarii seu Tabelliones & se saltem officio Notariatus ingerentes in Imperio (ut per experientiam didicimus, multorumque accepimus clamore) defectuosi & indigni inveniantur: tamen ratione conditionis & qualitatis personæ, tum ratione defectus etiam scientiæ & morum, ac quia aliis multipliciter inutiles existunt, utpote aliqui servili conditioni astricti, alii de falso, præsertim etiam circa tale officium Notariatus convicti, aut etiam aliis criminibus irretiti, seu publice diffamati, alii negligentes, nonnulli indocti & imperiti, & quorum imperitia, negligentia & malitia innumeros homines defraudari, negligi & gravari non est dubium. Ad obviandum igitur hujusmodi periculis & defectibus, necessarium esse putamus desuper fieri provisionem, vitisque doctrina & harum rerum experientia suffultis mandavimus, qui nostra autoritate præsentem ordinationem compilaverunt. Quam cum nobis obtulissent, eamque diligenti studio perlegissemus, animadvertissemusque multiplicem ejus fructum & utilitatem, ipsamque nostra Imperiali autoritate de nostrorum ac sacri Romani Imperii Electorum, Principumque & Statuum aliorum, consilio confirmamus, approbamus, atque plenissimum robur attribuimus, atque per universum Romanum Imperium divulgari præcipimus.
units.tr: 2. But since the office of scriveners or notaries is not only very useful and necessary for maintaining justice and peace, but also for the matters that daily occur in the commonwealth and among the subjects, namely that the agreements, vows and deeds of men (lest they slip from memory or fall into oblivion) may be handed down by the ministry of writing to a sure and perpetual memory and confirmed by public documents; and since very many notaries or scriveners, and those who thrust themselves into the notarial office in the Empire (as we have learned by experience and have heard from the outcry of many), are found to be defective and unworthy, both by reason of the condition and quality of their persons, and by reason of defect in learning and morals, and because they are in many ways useless to others: some being bound by servile condition, others convicted of forgery, especially in such notarial office, or entangled in other crimes or publicly defamed, others negligent, some unlearned and inexperienced, and it is beyond doubt that countless men are defrauded, neglected and burdened by their inexperience, negligence and malice. Therefore, to meet such dangers and defects, we judge it necessary to make provision in this matter, and we have commissioned men supported by learning and experience in these affairs, who by our authority have drawn up the present ordinance. When they had presented it to us, and we had read it through with diligent care, and had observed its manifold fruit and usefulness, we confirm and approve it by our Imperial authority, with the counsel of our Electors and of the Princes and other Estates of the Holy Roman Empire, grant it full force, and command that it be made known throughout the whole Roman Empire.

units.la: 3. Hanc igitur salubertimam reformationem & ordinationem studeant Notarii publici, ad quos præcipuè pro Notariatu, officiorum exercitio, & practica ipsa porrigetur, humili devotione ampleCti, summaque diligentia servare, ac juxta eandem & alia, quæ suis in juramentis super hujusmodi officiis præscriptis, vel etiam à jure communi, vel locorum laudabilibus consuetudinibus, tradita introduCtaque sunt, officia sua legaliter, fideliter & sincerè exercere, prout ultra damna & interesse, ad quæ aliis partibus à se neglectis vel defraudatis tenebuntur, nostræ Imperialis Majestatis severam evitare velint correctionem.
units.tr: 3. Let public notaries, to whom this reform and ordinance is especially addressed with regard to the notarial office, the exercise of their offices and the practice itself, study to embrace it with humble devotion and to observe it with the greatest diligence; and, in accordance with it and with the other things prescribed in their oaths concerning such offices, or handed down and introduced by the common law or by the laudable customs of the places, let them wish to exercise their offices lawfully, faithfully and sincerely, so that they may avoid the severe correction of our Imperial Majesty, in addition to the damages and interest to which they will be bound toward those parties whom they have neglected or defrauded.

units.la: CAPITULUM I.
units.tr: CAPUT I.

units.la: DE PERSONARVM QVALITATE, ET GENERALIBVS NOTA- RIORUM REGULIS.
units.tr: CONCERNING THE QUALITY OF PERSONS, AND THE GENERAL RULES FOR NOTARIES.

units.la: I N primis igitur ordinamus, quòd circa personas approbandorum vel denuò instituendorum habeatur ratio conditionum & qualitatum earundem, ne approbentur vel instituantur prohibiti, utpote infideles, servi, infames, præsentis ordinationis & aliorum tequisitorum non informati: Item vel excommunicatione majoris vel Imperialis banni censuris innodati. Et in summa qui à testimonio jure repellantur, quoniam testium vice fungantur.
units.tr: First, therefore, we ordain that, with regard to the persons to be approved or newly appointed, account be taken of their conditions and qualities, so that those who are prohibited are not approved or appointed: namely, unbelievers, slaves, the infamous, those not informed of the present ordinance and of the other requisites, likewise those bound by the censures of greater excommunication or of the Imperial ban, and, in short, all who are by law debarred from giving testimony, since they stand in the place of witnesses.

units.la: 2. Et cum sit de jure communi quæ practica & consuetudine introductum, ut servetur circa publica instrumenta eorumque solennitates talis forma, ut videlicet à principio invocato divino nomine, à quo cuncta bona progrediuntur, imponatur annus salutis, indictio, nomen ac annus Principis, dehinc Mensis, dies, hora, locus, loci locus, deinde facti seu actus gesti series, hinc testium adhibitio, quorum singulorum nomina & cognomina clarè designentur, & finaliter signetum, subscriptioque Notarii, qui semper debet de hoc rogari, seu requiri, & de rogatu suo attestati.
units.tr: 2. And since it is established by common law, and introduced by practice and custom, that the following form be observed in public instruments and their solemnities: namely, that at the beginning the divine name be invoked, from whom all good things proceed; then the year of salvation, the indiction, and the name and regnal year of the prince be set down; next the month, day, hour, place, and the place of the place; then the sequence of the fact or act performed; after that the presence of witnesses, whose individual names and surnames are to be clearly designated; and finally the seal and subscription of the notary, who must always be asked or required to do this and must attest it at the request made of him.

units.la: 3. Mandamus ergò, præcipimus & ordinamus hujusmodi formam ulterius servari, salvis non minus aliis de cujusvis loci consuetudine servandis: Ita tamen, ut saltem in tetris sacri Romani Imperii nomen & annus regiminis, seu Imperii Romanorum Imperatoris vel Regis pro tempore existentis, nullo modo sicut hactenus à nonnullis & male neglectum est, de cætero omittantur.
units.tr: 3. We therefore command, enjoin, and ordain that this form be further observed, saving also any other customs of any place that are to be kept. Provided, however, that at least in the titles of the Holy Roman Empire the name and year of the reign of the Roman Emperor or King then reigning are in no way omitted henceforth, as has hitherto been wrongly neglected by some.

units.la: 4. Deinde mandamus, ut quivis Notarius studeat omnimodo habere, & quidem summa cum custodia conservare, ac post se relinquere unum protocollum, in quo per seipsum, non alium, singulos actus coram se gestos, & de quibus rogatur, ordine in scriptis redigantur, instrumentorumque quæ inde edita fuerint, copias de verbo ad verbum concordanter registratas rerineat & conservet, ut de perditis antea editis instrumentis, sive ante sive post mortem suam, quando, & quotiens alia instrumenta de novo fuerint edenda, vel prætextu editorum suspicio, error, dubium, vel altercatio occurrit, ad tale protocollum tegistrumque possit haberi recursus. Hoc autem usque adeo servetur, ut hujusmodi protocollata etiam partibus quæ contraxerunt vel egerunt consentientibus, vel pro infectis nullisque habeni volentibus, seu deleti ex libro vel cancellati petentibus, non falsem pro tanto deleant seu cancellentur, quin non minus legibilia maneant & retineantur. Quid enim si alterius tertii, sive fisci, sive privati interfit, seu interesse cœperit, tem sic esse gestam, & ex Protocollo vetitatem apparere posse.
units.tr: 4. Next we command that every notary strive to have, and indeed keep with the greatest care, and leave behind him, one protocol, in which, by his own hand and not another's, the individual acts done before him, and concerning which he is asked, are written down in order; and that he keep and preserve copies of the instruments drawn up from them, registered word for word and in agreement, so that, if the instruments previously issued are lost, whether before or after his death, whenever other instruments are to be issued anew, or suspicion, error, doubt, or dispute arises from those issued, recourse can be had to such a protocol and register. This is to be observed to such an extent that protocolled acts are not to be struck out or cancelled, even if the parties who made the contract or transaction consent, or wish them to be regarded as undone and void, or ask that they be deleted or cancelled from the book; but they remain and are kept just as legible. For what if it is, or begins to be, in the interest of another third party, whether the treasury or a private person, that the thing was done in this way, and that the truth can appear from the protocol?

units.la: 5. Caveant etiam Notarii, ne quis ad quantumcunq; fide dignam relationem quicquam aliud plus vel minus quam quod coram se & testibus ad hoc adhibitis actum gestumve, atq; de quibus tempore actus hujusmodi non antea vel post ex intervallo rogarus fuerit, atque etiam quod corporeis sensibus perceperit, eò quòd officium seu autoritas sua ad alia se non extendat, in Protocollo suo scribat, vel desuper instrumentum edat. Sed in his sensibus est habenda distinctio. Nam in visu & auditu sufficit, Notarius in præsentia testium videat & audiat; in aliis verò, ut gustu, tactu vel odoratu requiritur, quòd testes coram se gustet, tangant vel odorent, & de qualitatibus eorum quæ per hujusmodi sensus perceperint, coram partibus, testibus, & se Notario attestentur. De eisdem enim sic attestari non autem de proprio suo gustu, tactu vel odoratu Notarius efficaciter potest testificari. Si tamen Notarius se similiter sic gustasse, tetigisse, vel odorasse, atque percepisse addiderit, non modicum dei facit.
units.tr: 5. Notaries shall also take care not to write into their protocol, or draw up an instrument upon, anything more or less than what was done before themselves and the witnesses summoned for this purpose, and concerning which they were asked at the time of the act, and not before or after at an interval; nor even what they perceived by the bodily senses, since their office or authority does not extend to other matters. But a distinction must be made in these senses. For in sight and hearing it is enough that the notary sees and hears in the presence of the witnesses; but in the other senses, such as taste, touch, or smell, it is required that the witnesses taste, touch, or smell in his presence, and that they attest before the parties, the witnesses, and the notary to the qualities of what they have perceived by these senses. For the notary can effectively testify to such things only through the attestation of others, not to his own taste, touch, or smell. If, however, the notary adds that he himself likewise tasted, touched, or smelled it and perceived it, this adds no small weight.

units.la: 6. Potest autem & Notarius rogari de actu multi, & scribere signa seu nutus ejus, ut potest sic talis propter accidens loqui non potuerit, interrogatus à me humeris vel capite innuendo confitetur & similia.
units.tr: 6. A notary may also be asked to record an act by signs or nods, as when someone, because of some accident, could not speak, but when questioned by me confesses by shrugging the shoulders or nodding the head, and the like.

units.la: 7. Et licet ex consuetudine Notarius tolleretur petalium fidelem (quando est aliis impedimento) ad mundum scribere instrumentum à se dictatum & completum, postea perseipsum subscribendum & signandum, tamen Protocollum suum seu extensionem ejus per seipsum, non per alium accipere: vel si ex aliquo accidenti pro tunc scribere non possit, ea vice alteri extendendum de verbo ad verbum pronunciare, & in subscriptione de hujusmodi impotentia & alterius ingroffatura attestari debet.
units.tr: 7. And although by custom a notary may (when hindered by others) have a trusted person make a clean copy of the instrument that he has dictated and completed, to be afterwards subscribed and signed by himself, nevertheless he must take his protocol, or its extension, from himself and not from another. Or if, for some accident, he cannot write at that time, he must dictate it word for word to another to be extended on that occasion, and in the subscription he must attest to such inability and to the other's engrossing.

units.la: 8. Et quamvis non requiratur plena, & tanta extensio Protocolli, sicut instrumenti indemnitas, tamen Notarii debent saltem brevibus & summariis verbis substantiales clausulas ipsius contractus, etiam juxta cujusque contractus seu actus naturam, vel loci consuetudinem solitas, & generaliter clausulas renunciationum praejudicialium attingere.
units.tr: 8. And although a full and complete extension of the protocol is not required, as for the completeness of an instrument, notaries must nevertheless set out, at least in brief and summary words, the substantial clauses of the contract itself, including those customarily used according to the nature of each contract or act, or the custom of the place, and generally the clauses of prejudicial renunciations.

units.la: 9. Nam cum consensus & intentio contrahentis vel agentis sit de substantia contractus seu actus celebrati, singulorumque, de quibus convenerunt partes, etiamsi solita sint apponi, neque talis sensus porrigatur ad ea quae quis ignorat, requiritur quod Notarius coram se & testibus saltem mariè reciter ac legat partibus pacta, renunciationes & clausulas singulas, super quibus fundatur ipsius coram se gesti, ac consensum deinde exprimi curet. Licet enim Jus praesumat contractus singulis quae secundum contractus naturam vel loci consuetudinem solent apponi, consensi, etiam si ex Protocollo non apparearent, neque a partibus exprimantur, nonnulliaque velint à Notario hoc requiri: tamen tutius & aequius est sic observari propter multa. Praeterea Judicis est, non Notarii praesumptionem scribere, sed de his solis, quae corporeis sensibus percipiuntur, ut supra dicitur, quam ad instar testis Notarius scribere debeat.
units.tr: 9. For since the consent and intention of the contracting or acting party is of the substance of the contract or act performed, and of each of the matters on which the parties have agreed, even if they are usually added, and since such consent does not extend to things that someone is ignorant of, it is required that the notary, in the presence of himself and the witnesses, at least read out and recite in summary the agreements, renunciations, and each clause on which the act done before him is founded, and then take care that consent is expressed. For although the law presumes that consent is given to those clauses that are usually added to each contract according to its nature or the custom of the place, even if they do not appear in the protocol and are not expressed by the parties, and although some would have this required of the notary, nevertheless it is safer and fairer to observe it this way, for many reasons. Moreover, it is for the judge, not the notary, to write down a presumption; the notary ought to write, as a witness would, only those things that are perceived by the bodily senses, as said above.

units.la: 10. Maximè autem ista sunt servanda in contractibus & actibus, in quibus scriptura est de substantia, imò etiam requiritur ut coram contrahentibus & testibus de verbo ad verbum singula relegantur: quia antequam scriptura complea-tur, & à partibus pro completa habeatur, contractus non censetur perfectus vel efficax: Postea verò quicquam addi, detrahi, vel mutari, etiam de partium consensu non potest.
units.tr: 10. These things are above all to be observed in contracts and acts in which the writing is of the substance, and indeed it is required that each item be reread word for word before the contracting parties and the witnesses; for until the writing is completed, and is held by the parties to be complete, the contract is not considered perfected or effective. Afterwards nothing can be added, removed, or changed, not even with the consent of the parties.

units.la: 11. Poterit tamen Notarius de his, quae partes mutare, addere vel detrahere vellent, denuò rogari & desuper facere instrumentum, prioribus gestibus manentibus in Protocollis.
units.tr: 11. Nevertheless, the notary may be asked again about those matters that the parties wish to change, add, or remove, and may make a new instrument on them, the earlier acts remaining in the protocols.

units.la: 12. Praecipuè autem sint cauti Notarii à fraudibus & fallacis aliquorum, sive coram eis contrahentium, sive aliorum, qui simulantes se Notarios à laborum prolixitate relevare velle per se vel alios subordinatos dictant instrumenta ex inbreviatura ipsis edenda, & ad mundum scribi facere ac postea offerunt Notariis subscribenda & signanda. In eis enim saepè dolose & in praejudicium aliorum secum contrahentium rei gesti detrahunt, vel addunt quae sensum vel substantiam mutant, quod facile quandoque uno verbo, una syllaba, imò interdum una litera fieri potest, & tamen advertenter & subtiliter, quòd vel Notarii, vel alii secum contrahentes vix, vel nullo modo sentire possunt. Ex quo ipsi Notarii intelligant quàm periculosum esset Protocolla seu inbreviaturas suas peralios, maximè alteri parti suspectos, vel qui actibus protocollatis non interfuerunt, extendi facere.
units.tr: 12. Notaries should be especially cautious of the frauds and deceits of certain persons, whether those contracting before them or others who, pretending that they wish to relieve notaries of the tedium of their labours, dictate, through themselves or through subordinates, instruments to be drawn up from abbreviations supplied to them, and then have them written out in clean copy and offer them to the notaries to be subscribed and signed. For in these they often fraudulently, and to the prejudice of others contracting with them, remove from or add to the transaction matters that alter its sense or substance, which can sometimes be done with a single word, a single syllable, or even a single letter, and so cunningly and subtly that the notaries or the other contracting parties can hardly, or in no way, perceive it. From this the notaries themselves may understand how dangerous it would be to have their protocols or abbreviations extended by others, especially by a party suspected by the other side, or by persons who were not present at the protocolled acts.

units.la: 13. Secus tamen esset, si antequam contractus seu actus absolveretur, seu concluderetur talis extensio sive ab ambobus contrahentibus, sive altero eorum fieret, & postea coram ipsis & Notario & testibus legeretur, & ubi sic placeret contrahentibus, extunc Notarius rogaretur. Posset enim tunc Notarius secure scribere, partes juxta illam extensam formam ipsis lectam & approbatam coram se & testibus requisitis contraxisse & egisse, ac caeteris protocollis suis adjungere atque postea publicare.
units.tr: 13. It would be otherwise, however, if, before the contract or act was completed or concluded, such an extension were made either by both contracting parties or by one of them, and afterwards read out in the presence of them, the notary and the witnesses, and, where the contracting parties are pleased with it, the notary is then asked to act. For the notary may then write securely that the parties contracted and acted according to that extended form, read and approved by them in his presence and that of the required witnesses, and may add it to his other protocols and afterwards publish it.

units.la: 17. In summa maximo studio advertant Notarii, ne circa protocollorum seu abbreviaturarum impositionem festinent seu praecipitanter agant, sed cum diligentia & consideratione clausulas vis protocollent. Nam tota officiorum, juramentorumque suorum desuper praestitorum vis & substantia in hoc consistit, ut bene diligenterque advertant & intelligant coram se gesta, & de quibus rogantur, & ea quae visu auditúque propriis in testium similiter animadvertentium praesentia perceperint protocollent, & publicent, sincerè ac fideliter, sive vel veritatis occultatione, vel falsitate mixtione quavis, adhibitis solennitatibus à Jure vel locorum, in quibus instrumenta facient, consuetudinibus introductis, ut supra dicitur.
units.tr: 17. Above all, notaries should take the greatest care not to hurry or act rashly when making their protocols or abbreviations, but should draw up the clauses with diligence and consideration.
