Domini nostri, avi nostri clementissimi, alius Romanorum Rex sive Imperator sit eligendus, & faciat Romani Imperii Electores pro hujusmodi electione faciēda, fide dignorū testimonio covenire intelligimus. possletq; contingere, cū nos è Germano sanguine ortissimus, & tot tantaque dominia nunc in Germania, tanquam Archidux Austriæ, possideamus, & prædecessores nostri Romanorum Imperatores hoc ipsum Romanum Imperium in multis annis bene & feliciter administraverunt, atque etiam quòd nos, si hanc Imperialem dignitatem Regnis atq; opibus nostris conjunctam haberemus, non solum sacrum Romanum Imperium augere & sustentare, sed universæ Reipubl. Christianæ, cui nunc Selimus Turcarum Rex, Asiæ Africaq; devictis, hostis imminet, saluti prospicere & consulere possimus, ut iidem sacri Romani Imperii Principes de nobis electionem in Regem Romanorum facerent, & ex antiqua consuetudine quilibet Rex, Princeps sive Dominus, qui per eosdem Electores Romanorum Rex electus fuerit, futurum Romanorum Imperatorem coronandus, quàm primùm post electionem factam absque omni protractione & mora immediatè debeat in electionem hujusmodi consentire, ac decretum ea ab eligentibus petere, & acceptare, juramentū debitum & consuetum præstare; necnon ipsis Principibus Electoribus, priusquàm se ingerat administrationi Regni sive Imperii, omnia eorum privilegia confirmare & approbare: necnò quædam alia obire, facere & adimplere, quæ approbata sunt frequenti & solito usu circa hujusmodi tempus electionis fieri debere.
units.tr: Charles, by the grace of God King of Castile, Aragon, León, both Sicilies, Jerusalem, Navarre, Granada, Toledo, Valencia, Galicia, Majorca, Seville, Sardinia, Córdoba, Corsica, Murcia, Jaén, the Algarve, Algeciras, Gibraltar, and of the Canary Islands, and likewise of the Indies and the mainland of the Ocean Sea; Archduke of Austria; Duke of Burgundy, Lorraine, Brabant, Styria, Carinthia, Carniola, Limburg, Luxembourg, Guelders, Calabria, Athens and Neopatras; Count of Flanders, Habsburg, Tyrol, Barcelona, Artois and Burgundy; Count Palatine of Hainault, Holland, Zeeland, Ferrette, Kyburg, Namur, Roussillon, Cerdagne and Zutphen; Landgrave of Alsace; Margrave of Burgau, Oristano and Gociano, and Prince of the Holy Roman Empire, Catalonia, Asturias, etc.; Lord of Friesland, Bruges, Mohna, Salins, Mechlin, etc. By the tenor of these presents we make known to all and each, to whom these letters shall come, that since, after the most grievous death of His Imperial Majesty, our most merciful lord and grandfather, another King of the Romans or Emperor is to be elected, and we understand, on trustworthy testimony, that the Electors of the Roman Empire are assembling for this election; and since it could come about that we, who are born of German blood and now hold so many and such great dominions in Germany, as Archduke of Austria, and since our predecessors, the Roman Emperors, have administered this same Roman Empire well and happily for many years, and also because, if we held this imperial dignity joined to our kingdoms and resources, we could not only augment and sustain the Holy Roman Empire, but also provide for and look after the welfare of the whole Christian commonwealth, which now, with Selim, King of the Turks, having conquered Asia and Africa, is threatened by an enemy; therefore the same Princes of the Holy Roman Empire might make their election of us as King of the Romans, and, according to ancient custom, any King, Prince or Lord whom the same Electors shall have elected King of the Romans, being about to be crowned future Emperor of the Romans, should, as soon as possible after the election has been made, without any delay or postponement, immediately consent to such an election, and ask for and accept the decree from the electors, and swear the due and customary oath; and also, before he takes up the administration of the kingdom or empire, confirm and approve all the privileges of the same Princes Electors; and also perform, do and fulfil certain other things which, by frequent and customary usage, have been approved as ought to be done at such a time of election.

units.la: Nos verò admoniti divino oraculo; Honorem tuum alterius nedederis, si & in quantum electio prefata de nobis facta fuerit, divina aspirante gratia, à qua omnis emanat dignitas & potestas, pro benedicto totius Christianæ Reipublicæ, pace & tranquillitate ac decore Nationis Germanicæ, hujusmodi honorem & fastigium solii Romanorum Regis acceptare, omniaq; & singula præmissa & alia facere & præstare, quæ fieri debent & consueverunt ratione electionis, deliberavimus. Et cùm id propria persona nequeamus, de probitate fidei, constantia atq; rerum experientia Reverendissimi in Christo Patris, Domini Matthei Sancti Angeli sacræ Rom. Ecclesiæ Diaconi Cardinalis Gurcensis, Coadjutoris Salzburgensis, ac Illustrium Principum Friderici Comitis Palatini & Ducis Bavariæ, & Casimiri Marchionis de Brandenburg, & Reverendorum Dominorum in Christo Patrum Principum Episcopi Leodiensis, Ducis de Bullon ac Comitis de Los, & Bernhardi Episcopi Tridentini, & Heinrici Comitis de Nassavv, Consanguineorum nostrorum; ac etiam Magnificorum, Nobilium, Spectabilium, fidelium nobis dilectorum, Maximiliani de Berges Domini de Senenbergen, Militis Ordinis nostri Aurei velleris, Bucardi de Plana Domini de Larocha, Cipriani de Serentein Cancellarii nostri Tyrolensis, Pauli de Arnsdorff Commendator Ordinis S. Jacobi de Spata, Jacobi Villinger, Nicolai Ziegler, & Joannis Renner, Camerariorum, Consiliariorum & Oratorum nostrorum, plenam habentes & indubitatam confidentiam, ex certa nostra scientia, omnibus melioribus modo, via, jure, casu atq; fortuna, quibus meliùs & efficacius possumus & valemus, fecimus & constituimus & ordinavimus, ac facimus & constituimus tenore præsentium eos & quoslibet tres eorum in solidum nostros veros, certos & legitimos ac indubitatos mandatarios, procuratores, actores, factores, & præmissorum ac infrascriptorum negotiorum gestores ac nuncios generales & speciales, cum plena facultate substituendi totiens, quotiens eis oportunum visum fuerit, & quicquid magis & melius dici & esse potest, ita quòd ipsi omnes aut major pars, vel tres saltem ipsorum, vel alii ab eis substituti nostro nomine, loco & vice (sicut eis vel saltem tribus eorum nostram omnimodam & plenam potestatem, facultatem, auctoritatem, tenore præsentium damus, concedimus, elargimur, & datam, concessam & elargitam esse dicimus & volumus) in præfatorum sacri Imperii Principum Electorum omnium vel eligentium sive majoris eorum partis de nostra persona factam electionem & creationem in Romanorum Regem liberè & aperte consentiant, & voluntatem nostram præstent, decretumq; super hujusmodi electione petant & exigant, petitumq; & obtentum acceperint, & super acceptato in animam nostram corporale juramentum in Romanorum Regem Electo cum omnibus & singulis clausulis, articulis & verborum expressionibus in tali juramento comprehensis, debitis & consuetis, ac etiam quæcunq; alia-ce ssaria juramenta præstent & faciant: circaque administrationem & Regni gubernationem tempore absentiæ nostræ cum eisdem Electoribus prosequantur & conveniant.
units.tr: We, indeed, admonished by the divine oracle, Do not give your honour to another, have resolved, if and insofar as the aforesaid election shall be made of us, with divine grace breathing upon us, from whom all dignity and power flows, for the good of the whole Christian commonwealth, and for the peace, tranquillity and honour of the German nation, to accept this honour and the eminence of the throne of the King of the Romans, and to do and perform all and each of the things mentioned above and the others which ought to be done and are customary by reason of the election. And since we cannot do this in person, and trusting in the integrity of faith, steadfastness and experience in affairs of the Most Reverend Father in Christ, Lord Matthew Lang of Sankt Angelo, Deacon Cardinal of the Holy Roman Church, Bishop of Gurk, Coadjutor of Salzburg, and of our illustrious Princes Frederick, Count Palatine and Duke of Bavaria, and Casimir, Margrave of Brandenburg, and of the Most Reverend Fathers in Christ, the Princes Bishop of Liège, Duke of Bouillon and Count of Los, and Bernard, Bishop of Trent, and Henry, Count of Nassau, our kinsmen; and also of our Magnificent, Noble, Honourable and faithful beloved ones, Maximilian von Berges, Lord of Senenbergen, Knight of our Order of the Golden Fleece, Burkhard von der Plana, Lord of Larocha, Cyprian von Serentein, our Chancellor of Tyrol, Paul von Arnsdorf, Commander of the Order of St. James of the Sword, Jacob Villinger, Nicholas Ziegler and John Renner, our Chamberlains, Councillors and Envoys: having full and undoubted confidence, from our certain knowledge, we have made, constituted and appointed, and by the tenor of these presents we do make, constitute and appoint them, or any three of them jointly, as our true, certain, lawful and undoubted mandatories, procurators, agents, factors and managers of the aforesaid and undermentioned business, and general and special envoys, with full power of substitution as often as it seems fitting to them, and in whatever way it can best be said and done, so that they all, or the greater part of them, or at least three of them, or others substituted by them, in our name, place and stead (as we give, grant and bestow upon them, or at least three of them, our complete and full power, faculty and authority by the tenor of these presents, and declare and wish that it has been given, granted and bestowed), may freely and openly consent to the election and creation of us as King of the Romans, made by all or by the electing or greater part of the aforesaid Princes Electors of the Holy Roman Empire, and may give our assent; and may seek and demand the decree upon such election, and, having sought and obtained it, may accept it; and, upon having accepted it, may swear the bodily oath, due and customary, upon our soul, as King of the Romans elect, with all and each of the clauses, articles and forms of words contained in such an oath; and may also make and perform any other necessary oaths; and may negotiate and agree with the same Electors concerning the administration and government of the kingdom during our absence.

units.la: Quodq; omnium Principum Electorum tam Ecclesiasticorum quàm Secularium, omnium eorum privilegia, literas, jura, libertates, gratias, immunitates & consuetudines, dignitates & prerogativas, & omnia quæ ipsi & quilibet eorum pro se usq; ad diem electionis de sacro Romano Imperio obtinuit, consecutus est, possedit, & in usu habuit, obtinent, possident & utuntur per literas sub nomine & sigillo nostro, quòd eorum fidei commisimus, confirment, approbent & roborent. Nosq; obligant & devinciant, quòd nos, postquam Imperiali diademate coronati fuerimus, iterum hujusmodi firmationem sub titulo Imperialis Majestatis nostræ renovare, ac etiam tanquam Romanorum futurus Imperator prænominatos Principes Electores Ecclesiasticos & Seculares in communi, & quemlibet eorum in speciali, in eorum privilegiis, juribus, jurisdictionibus, minimè impedire, aut ea diminuere, sed potiùs omnia & singula clementer adaugere juxta continentiam Aureæ Bullæ, & obligationum desuper factarum. Et quòd hæc omnia præmissa quàm primùm ad sacri Imperii loca in Germania pervenerimus, denuò confirmare, renovare & ratificare per manus nostræ subscriptionem ad beamus & velimus.
units.tr: And we bind and oblige ourselves that, once we have been crowned with the imperial diadem, we shall renew such confirmation under the title of our Imperial Majesty, and also, as future Emperor of the Romans, we shall in no way impede or diminish the aforesaid Princes Electors, Ecclesiastical and Secular, collectively, and each of them individually, in their privileges, rights and jurisdictions, but rather shall graciously increase all and each of them, in accordance with the content of the Golden Bull and of the obligations made thereupon. And that all the foregoing we wish and desire to confirm, renew and ratify again, by the signature of our hand, as soon as we have come to the places of the Holy Empire in Germany. All of the privileges, letters, rights, liberties, favours, immunities and customs, dignities and prerogatives, and all that they, and each of them, have obtained, acquired, possessed and held in use from the Holy Roman Empire up to the day of the election, the Ecclesiastical and Secular Princes Electors, all of them, shall have, possess and enjoy; and we shall confirm, approve and strengthen them by letters under our name and seal, which we shall entrust to their good faith.

units.la: Et generaliter omnia alia & singula, quæ ad augmentū sacri Imperii & Germaniæ nationis, ac conservationem & securitatem liberæ electionis præfatorum Electorum exnunc inantea perpetuis futuris temporibus concernunt, spectant & attinent, faciant, promittant, obligent, gerant, adimpleant in præmissis omnibus & singulis, & eorum quolibet, necnon connexis eorundē & emergentibus, quaven, legitimi & indubitati mandatarii, procuratores, negociorum gestores & nuncii tam generales quas iàm speciales, & amplam potestatem habentes, facere & gerere possunt, & quæ nos ipsi, si personaliter adessemus, prout negociorum merita, status & conditiones ac obligationum qua tumcunq; tenor requirunt, facere & gerere possemus. Et si mandatum exigant magis speciale, quod eisdem vel tribus eorum in solidum, ac si de verbo ad verbum in debitis & requisitis clausulis præsentibus insertum foret, traditum & concessum esse volumus, promittentes in verbo Regio, & sub bona fide nostra, ratum & gratum habituros, quicquid per præfatos nostros mandatarios, procuratores & nuntios, vel ab eisdem substitutos, in præmissis vel circa, actum, factum, promissum & conventum, obligatum & gestum fuerit, fideliter observaturos, nec ullo tempore directè vel indirectè, clam vel palam, contraventuros. Harum testimonio literarum manu nostra subscriptarum, & sigilli nostri appensione roboratarum. Datæ in civitate nostra Barchinone, die octava mensis Martii, Anno Domini MDXIX. Regnorum nostrorum quarto.
units.tr: And, in general, all and each of the other matters which, from now on and in perpetual future times, concern, pertain to and relate to the increase of the Holy Empire and of the German nation, and to the preservation and security of the free election of the aforesaid Electors, they shall do, promise, oblige, manage and fulfil in all and each of the foregoing matters, and in any of them, and in whatever is connected with or arises from them, as far as our lawful and undoubted mandatories, procurators, managers of business and envoys, both general and special, having ample power, can do and manage them; and as we ourselves, were we personally present, could do and manage them, as the merits of the business, its state and conditions, and the tenor of any obligations may require. And if they should demand a more special mandate, we wish that the same, or any three of them jointly, be considered as though it had been inserted word for word, in its proper and required clauses, in these presents, handed over and granted; promising in the word of a King, and under our good faith, that we shall hold as valid and acceptable whatever has been done, made, promised, agreed, obliged and managed in the foregoing matters, or concerning them, by our aforesaid mandatories, procurators and envoys, or by those substituted by them; that we shall faithfully observe it, and at no time, directly or indirectly, secretly or openly, shall we act against it. In witness whereof, we have given these letters, subscribed by our hand and strengthened by the appending of our seal. Given in our city of Barcelona, on the eighth day of March, in the year of the Lord 1519, in the fourth year of our reigns.

units.la: CAROLVS.
units.tr: CHARLES.

units.la: per Regem.
units.tr: By the King.

units.la: Hannart.
units.tr: Hannart.

units.la: CAROLI V. IMPER. AUG.
units.tr: Of Charles V, Emperor Augustus

units.la: IVRAMENTVM POST IMPOSITAM SIBI CORONAM Regiam Aquisgranensem.
units.tr: The oath taken after the royal crown was placed upon him at Aachen.

units.la: PROFITEOR & promitto coram Deo & Angelis ejus, amodò & deinceps legem & justiciam pacemq; sanctæ Dei Ecclesiæ servare, populoque mihi subjecto prodesse, & justitiam facere, & conservare jura Regni salvo condigno divinæ misericordiæ respecta, sicut cum consilio Principum & fidelium Regni atq; meorum melius invenire potero.
units.tr: I profess and promise before God and his angels that from now on I will keep the law, justice and the peace of the holy Church of God, will serve the people subject to me, will do justice and preserve the rights of the kingdom, saving the due mercy of God, as I shall be able to determine best with the counsel of the princes and faithful of the kingdom and of my own.

units.la: 1. Sanctissimo Romano Pontifici, Ecclesiæ Romanæ, cæterisque Pontificibus & Ecclesiis Dei condignum & canonicum honorem volo exhibere.
units.tr: 1. I wish to show due and canonical honour to the most holy Roman Pontiff, to the Roman Church, and to the other Pontiffs and Churches of God.

units.la: 3. Ea etiam, quæ Imperatoribus & Regibus, Ecclesiis seu Ecclesiasticis personis collata sunt, & ergata, inviolabiliter ipsis conservabo, & faciam conservari.
units.tr: 3. Likewise, I will inviolably preserve for them, and will cause to be preserved, those things which have been bestowed on emperors and kings, on churches or on ecclesiastical persons, or granted to them.

units.la: 4. Abbatibus & Ordinibus, vasallis Regni honorem congruum volo exhibere, Domino nostro Jhesu Christo mihi præstante auxilium, fortitudinem & decorem.
units.tr: 4. I wish to show fitting honour to abbots and orders, and to the vassals of the kingdom, with our Lord Jesus Christ granting me help, strength and dignity.

units.la: CAROLI V. IMPER. AUG.
units.tr: CHARLES V, EMPEROR AUGUSTUS

units.la: EDICTUM CONTRA LVTHERVM, PROMVLGATVM IN COMITIIS VVormatiensibus, Anno Domini, M.D.XXI.
units.tr: EDICT AGAINST LUTHER, PROMULGATED AT THE DIET OF WORMS, IN THE YEAR OF OUR LORD 1521

units.la: CAROLUS Quintus, divina favente Clementia electus Romanorum Imperator, semper Augustus, ac Germaniæ, Hispaniarum, utriusq; Siciliæ, Hierusalem, Ungariæ, Dalmatiæ, Croatiæ, &c. Rex: Archiducx Austriæ, Dux Burgundiæ, Brabantiæ, Styriæ, Charinthiæ, Carniolæ: Comes Habspurgi, Flandriæ, & Tyrolis, &c. Universis & singulis sacri Romani Imperii Electoribus, aliisque Principibus, tam Ecclesiasticis quàm Sæcularibus: Archiepiscopis, Episcopis, Præla-tis, Ducibus, Marchionibus, Comitibus, Baronibus, Nobilibus, Militibus, Clientibus, Præfectis, Præsidibus, Judicibus, Sculteris, Burgimagistris, Consulibus, Scabinis: Civitatum, Oppidorum, Villarum, Terrarum, & quorumvis aliorum locorum Communitatibus: necnon Universitatum, Studiorum sive Gymnasiorum Rectoribus, & Locumtenentibus, seu Officialibus eorundem, ac cæteris quibuscunq; nobis, tam jure sacri Imperii quàm hæreditario, aut alio quocunq; modo subjectis: & fidelibus dilectis, cujuscunque status, gradus, aut conditionis sint, & ad quos præsentes, vel earundem exemplum, nostro, vel alicujus Præl̃ati Ecclesiastici sigillo, sive etiam publici Notarii manus subscriptione, communitum pervenerit, gratiam Cæsaream, & omne bonum.
units.tr: CHARLES the Fifth, by the favourable clemency of God elected Roman Emperor, ever Augustus, and King of Germany, Spain, both Sicilies, Jerusalem, Hungary, Dalmatia, Croatia, etc.; Archduke of Austria, Duke of Burgundy, Brabant, Styria, Carinthia and Carniola; Count of Habsburg, Flanders and Tyrol, etc. To all and each of the Electors of the Holy Roman Empire, and to the other princes, both ecclesiastical and secular: archbishops, bishops, prelates, dukes, margraves, counts, barons, nobles, knights, vassals, prefects, presidents, judges, schultheiss, burgomasters, consuls, aldermen; to the communities of cities, towns, villages, lands and any other places; and likewise to the rectors, vice-rectors or officials of universities, schools or gymnasia, and to all others who are subject to us, whether by the law of the Holy Empire, by hereditary right or in any other way, and to our faithful and beloved, of whatever rank, degree or condition they may be, and to whom these present letters, or a copy of them, bearing our seal or that of some ecclesiastical prelate, or the signature of a public notary, may come: grace from Caesar and every good.

units.la: 1. Ad veri Romanorum Imperatoris officium pertinet, non solum fines hujus sacri Imperii; quod prædecessores nostri, Germaniæ Principes, ob defensionem sanctæ Romanæ & Universalis Ecclesiæ, suo suorumque sæpius effuso sanguine, per divinam gratiam, sibi quæsierunt, ad Orthodoxam viam adductis, vel expulsis infidelibus, propagare: verumetiam, ne qua hæreseos labes aut suspicio, in jam sibi subditis Nationibus sacrosanctâ Religionem nostram commaculet, summo studio providere: ac si qua jam oriri cœperit, cam omni ope, omnique cura, juxta normam, à Sancta Romana Ecclesia hactenus observatam, delere penitus & extinguere. Quod si quis aliusè Majoribus nostris, tanto nos magis præstare debemus, quanto Dei Opt. Maximi immensa benignitas Nobis plura Regna & Dominia, pluresque & magis bellicosos populos, majoresque vires, quàm jam multis sæculis alicui Principi, qui hisce titulis sit potitus, ad suæ sanctæ fidei tutelam & incrementum, elargiri dignata est. Accedit, quòd quum ex paterno genere, è Christianissimis Imperatoribus & Archiducibus Austriæ, Ducibusque Burgundiæ: Ex materno vero, Catholicis, Hispaniarum, Siciliæ, & Hierusalem Regibus, simus orti: quorum omnium, pro fide Christiana, res præclare gestas,
units.tr: 1. It belongs to the duty of a true Roman Emperor not only to extend the borders of this Holy Empire, which our predecessors, princes of Germany, have often won for themselves by the shedding of their own blood and that of their people, in defence of the holy Roman and universal Church, by God's grace, bringing infidels to the orthodox way or driving them out; but also to take the greatest care that no stain or suspicion of heresy should defile our sacred religion among the nations already subject to us; and if any such thing begins to arise, to root it out and utterly extinguish it with every resource and every care, in accordance with the rule hitherto observed by the holy Roman Church. And if anyone expects this of our ancestors, we ought to do so all the more, since the immense goodness of God, the best and greatest, has deigned to bestow on us more kingdoms and dominions, more and more warlike peoples and greater forces than on any prince who has held these titles for many centuries, for the protection and increase of his holy faith. Moreover, since we are sprung on our father's side from the most Christian Emperors and Archdukes of Austria and Dukes of Burgundy, and on our mother's side from the Catholic Kings of Spain, Sicily and Jerusalem, the splendid deeds which all of them performed for the Christian faith will never be erased by any oblivion.

units.la: Vulgò Edictum VVormaciense, Interprete Johanne Cochlæo. gestas, nulla unquam delebit oblivio: Non sine gravi conscientiæ nostræ onere, & perpetua quadam nota, quadamq; veluti nebula, fœlicibus meunis Principatus nostri auspiciis offusa, factum cideritur, si, quæ jam ab hinc triennium pullulare in Germania cœperunt, novas quasdam hæreses, iamq; verius jam sæpe olim per Concilia, & summorum Pontificum decreta, approbante Ecclesia, damnatas, & nunc denuo, veluti ab Inferis, erutas, altiores jacere radices, ulla nostra negligentia patiamur, deamur.
units.tr: Commonly called the Edict of Worms, translated by Johannes Cochlaeus. Deeds, which no oblivion will ever erase. It would be done not without a heavy burden on our conscience, and with a lasting mark, as it were a cloud spread over the happy beginnings of our reign, if we were to allow, through any negligence of ours, certain new heresies, which for three years now have begun to sprout in Germany, and which have often been condemned before, more truly, by Councils and by decrees of the supreme Pontiffs with the approval of the Church, and now, as if brought back from the dead, to strike deeper roots.

units.la: 2. Sane, vestrum neminem ignorare existimamus, quibus erroribus & hæresibus, ab Orthodoxa fide longe alienis, quidam frater Martinus Lutherus, Ordinis S. Augustini, Religione Christiana in hac præsertim Inclyta Germanica Natione, omnis infidelitatis & hæresum perpetua oppugnatrice, ita inficere conetur, ut nisi mature occurratur, tota hæc Natio, & deinde serpente contagione universa Christiana Respublica, in abominandum schisma, & bonorum morum pacisque, ac tandem stándam sui perniciem, prolapsura videatur. Quapropter, non immerito commotus Sanctissimus in Christo Pater, Dominus Leo X. Sacrosanctæ Romanæ & Universalis Ecclesiæ Summus Pontifex, quem fidem Catholicam, & Ecclesiæ Sacramenta curare spectat, prædictum Martinum a primo clementer & paterne monuit, & hortatus est, ut a nephandis hujusmodi inceptis desisteret, & sparsos errores revocaret. Quod cum ille neglexisset, & pejora semper prioribus adderet; Beatissimus Pater, ad opportuna, neque tamen insuetá remedia procedere statuit. Itaque convocatis sæpius Reverendissimis sanctæ Romanæ Ecclesiæ Cardinalibus, Episcopis, ac aliis Prælatis, necnon Regularium ordinum Prioribus seu Ministris generalibus, accersitisque plurimis probitate præstantibus viris, & in omni doctrinarum & linguarum genere eruditis, ac eorum Christianorum Nationum Doctoribus & Magistris: prædicto tamen Martino prius vocato ac citato, ac in contumacia persistente, ipsius scripta, tam Alemanico quam Latino sermone edita & edenda, ut perniciosa, & fidei unitatique Ecclesiæ contraria, authoritate sua Apostolica prohibuit; ad hoc accedente Cardinalium consilio & assensu, ac Episcoporum & Prælatorum, Doctorumque & Magistrorum matura deliberatione, damnavit, & ubique locorum comburenda, proscribenda censuit & decrevit. Martinum vero ipsum, nisi infra certum expressum terminum, a publicatione Decreti sanctitatis suæ, mutata sententia, se errores suos revocasse, & ad pœnitentiam ediderit, docuisset: ut inobedientiæ & iniquitatis filium, ut schismaticum & hæreticum ab omnibus evitandum, & prout jura postulant, puniendum declaravit, sub pœnis & censuris, quæ in Apostolicis literis, Bulla plumbea communitis, & super hac re additis, latius continentur. Quas ad Nos, utpote Christianæ fidei verum & supremum propugnatorem, & Sedis Apostolicæ, sanctæq; Romanæ & Universalis Ecclesiæ Primarium filium, & Advocatum, per suum, & dictæ Sedis spiritualem Nuncium & Oratorem, honorabilem virum nobis dilectum, Hieronymum Aleandrum, ejusdem Sedis Proconotarium, & Apostolicæ Bibliothecæ Præfectum, deditaque ad hoc opera, misit: petens atq; requirens, ut pro officio ac debito Imperialis dignitatis, in universo primum Romanorum Imperio, deinde (quod Catholicum Regem & Christianum Principem decet) in ceteris etiam Regnis, Dominiis, & Provinciis nostris, & præsertim in Germania, præstito in auxilium fidei Catholicæ brachio sæculari, omnia & singula in jam dictis literis Apostolicis contenta, inviolabiliter observari, & executioni mandari jubeteramus.
units.tr: 2. Indeed, we think that none of you is ignorant with what errors and heresies, far removed from the orthodox faith, a certain brother Martin Luther, of the Order of St Augustine, seeks to infect the Christian religion, especially in this famous German nation, which has always opposed every infidelity and heresy; so that, unless it is quickly checked, this whole nation, and then the entire Christian commonwealth through the spreading contagion, seems likely to fall into an abominable schism, into the ruin of good morals and peace, and at last into its own destruction. Therefore, not without good reason, the most holy Father in Christ, Lord Leo X, supreme Pontiff of the holy Roman and universal Church, to whom it belongs to care for the Catholic faith and the sacraments of the Church, being moved, first admonished the said Martin mildly and paternally, and exhorted him to desist from such nefarious undertakings and to revoke the errors he had spread. When he neglected this, and always added worse things to earlier ones, His Blessedness decided to proceed to suitable remedies, yet not unusual ones. So, having often summoned the most reverend Cardinals of the holy Roman Church, bishops and other prelates, as well as the priors or general ministers of the regular orders, and having called in many men outstanding in integrity and learned in every kind of doctrine and language, as well as teachers and masters of those Christian nations; the said Martin having first been called and cited, and persisting in contumacy, he forbade by his own apostolic authority his writings, whether published or to be published in German or in Latin, as pernicious and contrary to the faith and unity of the Church; and, with the counsel and assent of the Cardinals, and after mature deliberation of the bishops, prelates, doctors and masters, he condemned them and decreed and ordered that they be burned and proscribed wherever they might be found. As for Martin himself, he declared him, unless within a certain stated term from the publication of his Holiness's decree he should change his opinion, revoke his errors and show himself penitent, to be a son of disobedience and iniquity, a schismatic and heretic, to be avoided by all and, as the laws demand, punished, under the penalties and censures more fully set out in the apostolic letters sealed with a leaden bulla and added on this matter. These things were sent to us, as the true and supreme defender of the Christian faith, the first son and advocate of the Apostolic See and of the holy Roman and universal Church, through its spiritual nuncio and envoy, our beloved and honourable man Hieronymus Aleander, protonotary of that See and prefect of the Apostolic Library, who was employed for this purpose; asking and requiring that, in accordance with the duty and obligation of the imperial dignity, first throughout the whole Roman Empire, then (as befits a Catholic King and Christian Prince) in our other kingdoms, dominions and provinces, and especially in Germany, with the secular arm given in aid of the Catholic faith, we should order that everything and each thing contained in the said apostolic letters be inviolably observed and carried into effect.

units.la: 3. Post quas quidem prædicto Martino factas à Summo Pontifice, Monitionem, Vocationem, Citationem, & ipsius tandem Condemnationem, necnon præsentatas Nobis ejusdem Beatissimi Patris literas, Bullamq; Apostolicam, per varia & diversa loca Germaniæ publicatam, & nostro jussu & mandato, non solum Lovanii in Inferioribus Dominiis nostris: verum & Coloniæ, Trevirensi, Moguntiæ, Leodii, executioni demandatam, tantum abfuit, ut idem Martinus resipisceret, erraturus revocaret, & petita absolutionis venia, in gratiam cum Summo Pontifice & sancta Ecclesia procuraret, ut etiam deterstabiliores perversi ingenii sui fructus indies ederet, & perinde, ac ad Ecclesiæ perniciem, furens rueret, complures acervatim libros, non modo novarum à sacris Conciliis olim condemnatarum hæresum plenos: nec solum Latino, verumetiam, ut factus vulgus perverteret, Alemanico sermone à se compositos, vel saltem suo nomine editos, ferè quotidie divulgaret. In quibus (bone Deus) observatum ab Ecclesia jam tot sæculis, septem Sacramentorum numerum, ordinem, usum, dissipat, confundit, deturpat: inviolatas Matrimonii leges, miris fœdissime inficit: Extremam Unctionem cum Wiclepho fictionem dicit: Communicandæ tissimæ Eucharistiæ ritum, ad damnata Bohemorum revocat instituta. Ad salubérrimam confessionis peccato mentibus Confessionem primum ita involvit, ut confusionem eam è Confessione cerit, mox etiam magna in parte convellit: postremo, adhuc pejora se de ea scripturum minatur. Unde nonnulli jam (ut accepimus, quod vel auditu est intolerabile) sumpta hinc occasione, de Confessionis institutio & modo cœperint subdubitare. Alii mutilatam & truncam fecerint: Alii vero (scelus) & confiteri ipsi desiterint, & nequaquam esse confitendum publice afferere sint ausi. Sacerdotalem ordinem, & per quas sacrosanctum Christi corpus sanguisq; conficitur, divinum illud nus claviumq; cœlestium potestatem, non solum vilissimi pendit Lutherus, & Laicis pueris, atque eo feminis ipsis, communia facit: sed & eosdem Laicos, ad lavandas sibi in Sacerdotum sanguine nus, incitat. Ipsum vero summum nostræ Religionis Sacerdorem, divi Petri successorem, & veru terris Christi Vicarium, non nisi infamibus & probrosis nominat verbis, & frequentissimis atq; inditis invectivis contumeliis, & blasphemus insectatur. Liberum arbitrium prorsus nullum esse, (ed-mus.
units.tr: 3. After the admonition, summons, citation and finally condemnation of the said Martin made by the Supreme Pontiff, and after the letters of that most Blessed Father, and the apostolic bull, were presented to us and published in various places in Germany, and by our command and order were carried into effect not only at Louvain in our Lower Dominions but also at Cologne, Trier, Mainz and Liège, Martin was so far from coming to his senses, from revoking his errors and seeking absolution and reconciliation with the Supreme Pontiff and the holy Church, that he produced ever more detestable fruits of his perverse mind, and, as if rushing to the ruin of the Church in a frenzy, almost daily poured out heaps of books, full not only of new heresies long ago condemned by the holy Councils, but composed by himself in Latin and also, so that he might pervert the common people, in German, or at least published under his own name. In these books (good God!) he scatters, confuses, disfigures and dissipates the number, order and use of the seven sacraments observed by the Church for so many centuries; he most foully defiles the inviolable laws of matrimony with his wonders; he calls Extreme Unction a fiction, with Wycliffe; he restores the rite of communicating in the most holy Eucharist to the instituted practices of the condemned Bohemians. As for the most salutary confession of sins, he first so entangles it in confusion that he removes confession, and soon also tears much of it down; finally, he threatens to write even worse things about it. Hence some people (as we have heard, which is intolerable even to hear) have, taking occasion from this, begun to doubt the institution and manner of confession; others have mutilated and maimed it; and others (the crime!) have stopped confessing altogether and have dared to assert that one must not confess in public. The priestly order, and the power through which the holy body and blood of Christ is consecrated, and that divine power of the keys and of the heavenly authority, Luther not only holds in the lowest contempt and makes common to laymen, boys and women alike, but also urges these same laymen to wash their hands in the blood of the priests. But the supreme Priest of our religion, successor of St Peter and true Vicar of Christ on earth, he names only with infamous and disgraceful words, and attacks with the most frequent and abusive invectives and blasphemies. That free will does not exist at all, and that all things stand by a certain necessary law, he draws from the store of the Manichaeans and Wycliffe, but he confirms it as an irrefutable argument with the verses of the heathen poets.

units.la: {y} Lutheri dogmata. mnia certa lege stare, ex Manichaei quidem & Wiclephi penu depromit: sed tanquam irrefragabili argumento Ethnicorum Poëtarum carminibus confirmat. Missae venetabile Sacramentum neq; defunctis, neq; vivis aliis, quam soli celebranti suffragari scribit. Jejuniorum & Orationum institutionem, & consuetudinem, ab Ecclesia observatam, invertit & corrumpit.
units.tr: The dogmas of Luther. He draws everything into a fixed law from the storehouse of Manichaeus and Wycliffe, but he confirms it with the poems of the pagan poets, as if they were an unanswerable argument. He writes that the venerable sacrament of the Mass benefits neither the dead nor the living, but only the priest who celebrates it. The institution and custom of fasts and prayers, as observed by the Church, he overturns and corrupts.

units.la: 4. De Purgatorio, & Animarum, quae in eo expiantur, statu, deq; divini sacrificii & veniarum suffragiis, quae à nobis fideles defuncti expectant, cum Waldensibus & Wiclephistis contra Ecclesiam sentit. De Ecclesia vero ipsa militante, cum Pelegianis & Hussitis. At Sanctorum Patrum authoritates & scripturae, ab Ecclesia recepta, pro nihilo habet. Est ubi etiam saepe derident, debirumq; illis cultum & devotionem detrect & diminuit. Obedientiam, & Regimen omne prorsus tollit. Unde populi ad defectionem & rebellionem à suis, tam spiritualibus quam temporalibus Dominis faciendam, ad rapinas; caedes, incendia, cum magno & manifesto Christianae Reipublicae discrimine, provocentur. Quininimo, quum vitam quantam solutam, licentiosam, atque ab omni lege explicitam, & vere ferinam inducere conetur, ita ex lex homo, leges ipsas omnes damnat & contemnit, ut Decreta sanctorum Patrum, & sacros Canones, publico igni comburere non formidavit: facturus pejora Civili jurisdictioni non magis saeculi gladium, quam Pontificis excommunicationes & censuras nictuisset.
units.tr: 4. On Purgatory, the state of the souls purged there, and the suffrages of the divine sacrifice and of indulgences which the faithful departed look for from us, he thinks against the Church, with the Waldenses and Wycliffites. On the Church militant itself, he thinks with the Pelagians and Hussites. He counts as nothing the authority of the holy Fathers and the Scriptures as received by the Church. In places he even mocks them, and he diminishes and disparages the worship and devotion owed to them. He utterly removes all obedience and all government. Hence peoples are provoked to revolt and rebellion against their lords, both spiritual and temporal, to plunder, slaughter and arson, with great and manifest danger to the Christian commonwealth. Indeed, while he tries to bring in a life so loose, licentious, free of all law and truly brutish, he, so lawless a man, condemns and despises all laws, so that he did not hesitate to burn publicly the decrees of the holy Fathers and the sacred canons, and he would do worse. He no more winks at the jurisdiction of the civil power or the sword of the age than at the excommunications and censures of the Pontiff.

units.la: 5. Jam vero sacrosanctis Conciliis palam contradicere, & pro suo arbitratu detrahere, non erubescit. E quibus potissimum Constantiense illud, quod cum perpetua Inclytae Germanicae Nationis gloria, pacem & tranquillitatem diffidenti Ecclesiae dedit: ita ubique moriter, & impuro scelerato que ore lacerat, ut in magnum universalis Ecclesiae dedecus & offendiculum, sed Germanicae praesertim Nationis opprobrium & ignominiam Concilium ipsum nunc pessime omnium errasse scribat: nunc Synagogam Sathanae quinque in eo convenerant, & Joannem Hussitam haereseiarcham comburi jusserant. Sigismundum utique foelicis recordationis Imperatorem, & Sacri Imperii Principes, Antichristum, & suos Apostolos, homicidasque & Pharisaeos, vocet. Quid, quod damnata in eodem Concilio omnia Joannis Hussitae errata, Evangelica & Christiana esse, & se recipere, probaturumque profitetur: Approbatos vero ejusdem Hussitae articulos, nequaquam admittit. In tantamq; prorupit mentis vaesaniam, ut si semel Joannes Hussita fuerit haereticus, se plus decies haereticum Martinus glorietur: homo usq; adeo novarum rerum ac potius perditionis humanae cupidus, ut nihil fere scripserit, vel saltem suo nomine divulgaverit, cui non aliqua pestis, aliquis lerhalis infir aculeus: praeter illos libros, ne nominandos quidem, ob execrandam eorum materiam, ipsius tamen titulo additos, & ab eo cum reliquis ut suos agnitos, quorum singula verba, singula venena merito quis dicat. Et ne omnia, quae innumerabilia sunt Lutheri errata, singulatim percenseantur, tanquam si hic unus, non homo, sed Diabolus ipse, sub hominis specie, ad perniciem humani generis, assumpta. Monachi cuculla, quam plurimorum haereticorum damnatissimas haereses, jamdiu sepultas, in unam sententiam congesserit, & aliquas etiam novissime de suo excogitaverit, sub simulata praedicatione fidei, quam ad praetexendos suos dolos, tam saepe, tantoque opere objicit: Fidem veram prorsus destruit, sub libertatis, quam promittit, specie: Diaboli jugum & servitutem inducit, & sub Evangelicae professionis nomine, omnem Evangelicam pacem & charitatem, omnemque rerum ordinem, & pulcherrimam denique totius Ecclesiae faciem invertere, labefactare, & penitus pessundare molitur.
units.tr: 5. Now he does not blush openly to contradict the most sacred Councils and to disparage them as he pleases. Chief among them is the Council of Constance, which gave peace and tranquillity to the troubled Church, to the everlasting glory of the famous German nation. He tears it apart with such a filthy and wicked mouth that, to the great disgrace and stumbling-block of the universal Church, and especially to the reproach and shame of the German nation, he writes that the Council itself has now erred most badly of all. He says that the synagogue of Satan had gathered there and had ordered John Hus, the heresiarch, to be burned. He calls the Emperor Sigismund of happy memory, and the Princes of the Holy Empire, Antichrist, his apostles, murderers and Pharisees. What of the fact that he professes that all the errors of John Hus condemned in the same Council are evangelical and Christian, and that he will receive them and prove them so; yet the articles of the same Hus that were approved he by no means admits. He has broken into such a frenzy of mind that, if John Hus was once a heretic, Martin boasts that he is more than ten times a heretic. He is a man so eager for novelties, or rather for the ruin of the human race, that he has hardly written anything, or at least published under his own name, which does not carry some plague or deadly sting. Besides those books, which are not even to be named because of their accursed matter, yet which were added under his title and acknowledged by him with the rest as his own, one may rightly say that each of their words is a poison. And, not to list individually the countless errors of Luther, it is as if this one man were not a man but the Devil himself, assumed under the form of a man for the destruction of the human race. Under the monk's cowl, he has gathered into one opinion the most damnable heresies of very many heretics, long buried, and has devised some new ones of his own. Under the pretence of preaching the faith, which he so often and with such effort puts forward to cover his tricks, he utterly destroys the true faith under the appearance of the liberty he promises. He introduces the yoke and servitude of the Devil, and under the name of the evangelical profession he labours to overturn, shake and utterly ruin all evangelical peace and charity, all order of things, and finally the most beautiful face of the whole Church.

units.la: 6. Quibus omnibus per Nos, & consilia nostra omnium Nationum nobis subditarum, saepius & diligenter attentis & consyderatis, & praesertim in hac parte ab eodem Beatissimo Patre requisiti: absq; insigni macula nostra, arq; Orthodoxae Religionis injuria & detrimento, rem tanti ponderis negligere nequaquam potuimus, ut etiam nō debuimus, neque voluimus: sed potius praedecessorum nostrorum, Romanorum Imperatorum, vestigiis insistentes, eorumq; pro libertate Catholicae & Apostolicae Ecclesiae perpetuo laudabilia facta, ac pias & sanctas, super puniendis & exterminandis haereticis, constitutiones observantes, convocatis, iisque ad praesentiam nostram, propter hoc praecipue, Electoribus: necnon universis sacri Romani Imperii Ordinibus & Statibus, in hoc Wormaciensi Conventu congregatis, de eorum omnium & singulorum unanimi consilio, matura deliberatione & consensu, in hanc tandem devenimus sententiam & conclusionem; Ut quamvis hominem, ita à Summo Pontifice & Sede Apostolica condemnatum, & in sua obstinata perversitate obduratum, atque ab usu Catholicae Ecclesiae alienum, & notorium haereticum audire, omni jure exceptum esset: tamen ad tollendam omnem cavillandi ansam (idq;, quia nonnulli plurosq; libros Martino ascriptos, ipsius sepapertissime inficiebantur) complures audiendum à Nobis prius hominem, quam in eum ad executionem Pontificii Decreti ulterius procederemus, asseverabant, Martinum saepedictum, misso ad ipsum, dedira opera, uno è Caduceatoribus seu Praeconibus & Heraldis nostris, Sub libero huc veniendi & hinc recedendi salvo conducto, accersiri juberemus: Quod & factum fuit. Non ut nos de hoc negocio judicaremus, aut cognosceremus (quum id dubio procul ad Romanum Pontificem, & Sedem Apostolicam pertinear) neq; ut res sacrosanctae fidei nostrae, nunc tandem, post tot saecula, per novas altercationes, cum magno fidelium scandalo & perturbatione, ac infidelium derisione, in controversiam revocari pateremur: sed ut cum vulgi & plurimorum ita petentium satisfactione, hominis animum perconranres, eum bonis monitionibus & suasionibus, ad rectam sententiam (si fieri posset) reducetemus.
units.tr: 6. Having weighed and considered all these things often and carefully, by ourselves and by the counsel of all the nations subject to us, and especially as the same most Blessed Father asked in this matter, we could not, and indeed we ought not and did not wish, to neglect a matter of such weight without a notable stain on ourselves and injury and loss to the Orthodox Religion. Rather, following in the footsteps of our predecessors, the Roman Emperors, who for the liberty of the Catholic and Apostolic Church performed deeds of perpetual praise, and observing their pious and holy constitutions concerning the punishment and extermination of heretics, we summoned to our presence, and for this reason especially, the Electors and all the Orders and Estates of the Holy Roman Empire gathered at this Diet of Worms. By the unanimous counsel, mature deliberation and consent of all of them and of each, we came at last to this opinion and conclusion: that although a man so condemned by the Supreme Pontiff and the Apostolic See, hardened in his obstinate perversity, alien to the practice of the Catholic Church, and a notorious heretic, might by all right have been denied a hearing, nevertheless, to remove every occasion for cavilling (since some people, and many, asserted that many books ascribed to Martin were utterly denied by him), we ordered Martin, whom we had summoned by a special messenger, one of our heralds and criers, with a safe conduct to come here and to leave freely, to be brought before us. This was done. Not that we would judge or examine this business (since it undoubtedly belongs to the Roman Pontiff and the Apostolic See), nor that we would allow the matters of our most sacred faith to be called into controversy again, now at last after so many centuries, through new disputes, with great scandal and disturbance to the faithful and derision from unbelievers. Rather, to satisfy the common people and the many who asked it, we wished to hear the man, and by good warnings and persuasions to bring his mind back to the right opinion, if that could be done.

units.la: 7. Itaq; Lutherum in nostra, & sacri Imperii Electorum, Principum, Praelatorum, & Statuum, praesenpræsentia constitutum, juxta formam Imperialis mandati, super hac re nuper ædiri, interroganmus. Primum; Nunquid ipse multos libros sibi ob oculos adductos, & titulatim nominatos, & item, qui sub suo nomine circumferuntur, composuisset. Deinde, an ea, quæ in ipsis libris contra ea Concilia, Decreta Patrum, ritus & consuetudines, à nostris majoribus ad hunc usque præteritam diem observatas, scripserit, revocare vellet, & ad finem & unitatem universalis Ecclesiæ redire, adhibitis ad hoc nostro & Imperii nomine admonitionibus & adhortationibus, quæ obstinatissimam hominem (etiam lapide duriorem) emollire, & convertere potuissent. Qui sane statim libros ipsos ut suos agnovit, & confessus est, & nunquam se id negaturum protestatus: immo & adversarios se compositsse dixit, quorum copia cum nobis non fuisset facta, idcirco in medium non allati. Quantum vero ad revocationem attinet, terminum sibi ad respondendum dari petiit, quippe vis merito negari potuisset, tum quia novitates & errores in fide nulla sunt dilatione tractandi, sed statim penitus resecandi: tum quia ex mandato nostro sibi legitime insinuato, necnon etiam quas ad eum dederamus, optimè admonitus, quam ob causam vocaretur, non nisi statim responsurus paratus, ad tantum Imperialis Conventus conselsum venire debuisset: tamen ex nostra clementia & benignitate, unius adhuc diei termino ad respondendum sibi dedimus. Quo elapso, rursus coram Imperii et prædictis Ordinibus Imperii comparens, & similibus adhortationibus sæpius, ut ad cor redeat, effigitatus, pollicentibus etiam nobis, si respiceret, erroresque suos agnosceret, & quæ in suis libris damnata & mala essent, revocaret: facile nos impetraturos, ut à Beatitudine Pontificis in gratiam benigne reciperetur, & adhibito fideli, æquo, & diligenti examine, ex ipsius libris, quæ mala scripta recenserentur: quæ vero bona, Authoritate Apostolica approbarentur. Sed ne verbum quidem suis libris mutaturum, imprudentibus simul & impudentibus verbis, orisque, & corporis gestu, quod potius, quam religiosum aut sanum hominem præ se ferente, apertissime negavit. Quinimmo etiam & sacri Imperii faciem, Summorum Decreta Pontificum, & Concilia ipsa sacrulanctæ, et sæpius, & sibi ipsis contradixisse, & tandem nullius apud se momenti fore, afflaveravit: seq; nihil et his, quæ se ipserat revocaturum, nisi evidenti sibi ratione, & sacræ scripturæ authoritatibus, ad sur conscientiæ animiq; satisfactionem & assensum fuerit convictus: illud subinde repetens & inculcans quod fraudulum suarum virus, jam multis detegi coeptum, occultaret) conscientia sibi illæsa & integra neque velle se, necposse verbum Dei immutare. Mala mens, malus animus. Quasi vero Nos id ab eo petere-mus, ut verbum Dei immutaret, ac non potius, ut juxta verbum Dei verum, ad gremium sanctæ matris Ecclesiæ, à qua tam impie quam turpiter defecerat, rediret. Cujus authoritatem, quum tantam voluerit esse Dominus, idemq; Deus noster Jesus Christus, ut qui Ecclesiam non audierit, tanquam Ethnicus & Publicanus sit habendus. Idcirco non immerito vel eam solam omnibus inventionibus, & vaframentis hæreticorum longe anteferendam nemo nunquam, nisi perditissimus & vere hæreticus, & Lutherus judicavit, qui ut tandem egregia sua hica-cta condigno fine clauderet, & quod pessime incoeperat, pejus terminaret, & quid animi habeat, & quam fidelium clade exultet, vel in nostro & sacri Imperii conspectu dissimulare non potuit. Nam de orta (ut hæreticis mos est) à vero sensu ad suam pietatem Evangelica illa sententia: Non veni mittere pacem sed gladium. Omnium sibi, dixit, jucundamam iltam in rebus faciem videri, ob verbum Dei, itudia, & dissensiones fieri: Id est (quod ut nunc experientia videremus) ob diffidentes ab Ecclesiæ ritu Lutheri opiniones, quas verbi Dei falso præterexit, vere studia contraria, & dissensiones, & dissidia, & schismata, & bella, & cædes, & rapinas inter Christianos concitari. Tali igitur, & tam subdola, atq; hæreticis omnibus peculiari responsio Nobis, & sacro Imperio à Luthero data, etsi decreveramus, ipso statim remisso, ad ulteriora progressa (id quod ex sententia nostra, manu nostra scripta, & postera die publicata, nemini non constat potest) Tamen ad preces omnium Imperii Ordinum inclinati, adhuc ipsi triduum ad respiscendum concessimus. Quo tempore duo Electores, duo Episcopi, duo Principes Sæculares, duoq; Civitatum nomine, Universos Ordines, & Status sacri Romani Imperii repræsentantes, & ad hoc communi omnium jussu & nomine deputati, vocato ad se Martino prædicto, nullum non admonedi & adhortandi eum, ut iandé respiscere; & nisi id faceret, quæ ipsum à Nobis, & sacro Imperio, legumq; constitutionibus poenæ manerent, declarandi officium frustra insumpserunt. Unus etiam ejusdem sacri Imperii Electorum, adhibitis secum duobus Doctoribus, pietate & scientia præclaris, non solum adhortationibus sed etiam multorum errorum evidentibus redargutionibus, ad ipsius usque obmutescentiam mox seorsim ipsum prudenter & humane commonefecit, ut ad Summi Pontificis, & Sedis Apostolicæ, Nostrumq; & sacri Imperii Statuum, & cæterarum fidelium Nationum, sanam sententiam continuatum tot sæculis Ecclesiæ ritum, potius, quam ad suam unius opinionem, respiceret. Aqui recedens, in ordinem redire vellet, id se primum nonnullorum sanctorum patrum, qui & ipsi aliquando erraverunt, laudabili exemplo, deinde salvis, anima, corpore, & honore, facturum cognoscere. Ad quæ Martinus antedictus, etsi varia plæraq; & diversa, cumq; cis, quæ scripserat, pugnantia: tamen meliora, aut saniora, privatim respondit, quam publice, coram Nobis, & sacro Imperio, ferret. Atq; adeo se, non omnes modo supra memoratos, sed & Concilium ipsum generale (si quod iret) suspectum habere protestatus est. Et (ut certissimo, & omni exceptione majori testimonio constat) pollutissimo & sceleratissimo ore profari non est veritus, res Evangelii & Catholicæ fidei nunquam fuisse in Conciliis generalibus bene tractatas. Unde non injuria plurimum nobis subiret, cur nam à Summi Pontificis sententia, ad generale Concilium nuper provocarit, quum impie de Conciliis ipsis loquatur & scribat, nisi manifeste sciremus, ut nihil est hæreticis æque fore dabit. dabile, atq; œcumenicum Concilium: ita nihil illis iisdem magis proprium esse, quàm ut dictis factisque & scriptus, secum ipsi dissideat. Quod si usquam alibi, præcipuè in Lutheri libris (divina providentia sic operante, quo ipsius vana ædificia per se ruant) passim legere & videre est.
units.tr: 7. Accordingly, we questioned Luther, who was present before us and before the Electors, Princes, Prelates and Estates of the holy Empire, in accordance with the form of the Imperial mandate issued recently on this matter. First, we asked whether he had written the many books placed before his eyes, which are listed by title, and likewise those that circulate under his name. Second, we asked whether he was willing to retract what he had written in those books against the councils, the decrees of the Fathers, and the rites and customs observed by our ancestors up to this day, and to return to the unity and fellowship of the universal Church, with admonitions and exhortations offered in our name and that of the Empire, which could have softened and turned even this most obstinate man, harder than stone. He at once acknowledged the books as his own, confessed it, and declared that he would never deny it. Indeed, he said that he had also written against his opponents, whose number had not been made available to us, and so they were not brought forward. As for retraction, he asked for a term in which to reply. We could rightly have refused this, both because novelties and errors in faith admit no delay in dealing with them but must be cut out at once, and because he had been duly notified of our mandate and of the letters we had sent him, and so, well aware of why he was summoned, he ought to have come to the assembly of the Imperial Diet ready to answer at once. Nevertheless, out of our clemency and kindness, we gave him a term of one more day in which to reply. When it had passed, he appeared again before the Empire and the aforesaid Estates of the Empire, and was urged many times by similar exhortations to come to his senses, while we promised that, if he returned and acknowledged his errors, and retracted what was condemned and evil in his books, we would easily obtain for him a gracious reception from His Holiness the Pope, and that, after a faithful, equitable and diligent examination, the books would be sorted: those writings that were evil would be listed, and those that were good would be approved by apostolic authority. But he did not even say that he would change a word in his books, and he most plainly refused, with imprudent and shameless words, voice and bodily gesture, more like a man who shows himself impious than religious or sane. Moreover, he went so far as to insult the face of the holy Empire, the decrees of the supreme Pontiffs, and the councils themselves, saying that they had often contradicted themselves and had at last no authority with him; and he declared that he would retract nothing of what he had written unless he was convinced by clear reason and by the authority of Holy Scripture, so as to satisfy and win the assent of his conscience and mind. Again and again he repeated and impressed the point that his conscience was unharmed and intact (he concealed the poison of his deceits, which had already begun to be exposed in many places), and that he neither wished nor was able to change the Word of God. An evil mind, an evil spirit! As if we were asking him to change the Word of God, rather than to return, according to the true Word of God, to the bosom of holy mother Church, from which he had fallen away so impiously and so shamefully. Since our Lord and God Jesus Christ willed her authority to be so great that whoever does not hear the Church is to be regarded as a heathen and a tax collector, no one has rightly judged her, or placed her far above all the inventions and tricks of heretics, except one most depraved and truly heretical, and Luther. In order to bring his outstanding heresies to a fitting end, and to make worse what he had begun most wickedly, he could not conceal, even in our presence and that of the Empire, what he has in mind and how he rejoices in the ruin of the faithful. For, as heretics commonly do, he twisted that evangelical saying, "I came not to send peace but a sword," from its true sense to his own piety. He said that it seemed to him a most pleasant thing that, on account of the Word of God, there should be strife and dissensions among all men; that is (as we now see by experience), on account of the opinions that differ from the rite of the Church, which Luther falsely draws from the Word of God, contrary zeals, dissensions, discords, schisms, wars, slaughters and plunderings are stirred up among Christians. Therefore, although we had decided, once he had been dismissed, to proceed to further measures (as is plain to anyone from our sentence, written in our hand and published the following day), nevertheless, inclining to the prayers of all the Estates of the Empire, we granted him three more days to come to his senses. In that time, two Electors, two Bishops, two secular Princes, and the representatives of the cities, acting for all the Orders and Estates of the holy Roman Empire and deputed to this task by the common command and name of all, summoned the aforesaid Martin and spent their effort in vain, admonishing and exhorting him in every way to come to his senses now, and, if he would not, declaring the penalties that awaited him from us, the holy Empire, and the constitutions of the laws. One of the Electors of the same holy Empire also, with two Teachers of distinguished piety and learning at his side, not only by exhortations but by clear refutations of many errors, soon, in private and with courtesy and prudence, admonished him until he was silent, that he should turn his mind rather to the sound judgment of the supreme Pontiff and the Apostolic See, of ourselves and the Estates of the holy Empire, and of the other faithful nations, and to the rite of the Church continued for so many centuries, rather than to his own single opinion. He was to say that, if he wished to return to order, he would first acknowledge this, following the praiseworthy example of some holy Fathers who also at times erred, and then he would do so with life, body and honour safe. To these things the aforesaid Martin replied privately, though with many varied and diverse answers, some of them contrary to what he had written, yet perhaps better or saner than what he afterwards offered publicly before us and the holy Empire. And indeed he protested that he held in suspicion not only all those mentioned above but also a general Council, if one should be held. And (as is established by the most certain testimony, beyond any exception) he was not ashamed to say with a most polluted and wicked mouth that the matters of the Gospel and of the Catholic faith were never well handled in the general Councils. Hence we could not help but wonder, not without reason, why he has recently appealed from the sentence of the supreme Pontiff to a general Council, since he speaks and writes impiously about the Councils themselves, unless we knew clearly that, just as nothing is more fitting for heretics than to appeal to a general and ecumenical Council, so nothing is more characteristic of them than to disagree with themselves in what they say, do and write. And if this is found anywhere else, it is read and seen everywhere in the books of Luther, (divine providence so working that his vain buildings may fall of themselves).

units.la: 8. His omnibus & singulis, sic omnino, ut præmittitur, se habentibus, quum prædictus Martinus, tam perversè & obstinatè, in suis adeo manifestè hæreticis opinionibus perseveraret, ut ab omnibus iis, qui sapiunt, partim demens, partim etiam malo aliquo obsessus spiritu, judicaretur. Nos, juxta tenorem salvi conductus, ipsum statim à conspectu nostro missum fecimus, datoq; sibi in comitatu uno ex Heraldis nostris, & præscripto termino, à die vicesima quinta mensis Aprilis, qua ex Wormacia discesserit, ad viginti deinde proximè futuros dies, quibus peractis, unà salvus conductus peractus & extinctus censeretur. Nunc tandem ad reliquas opportunas medelas, huic pestilentissimo morbo necessarias, in hunc, qui sequitur modum, procedere decrevimus.
units.tr: 8. Since all and each of these things stand exactly as has been set out, and since the aforesaid Martin persevered so perversely and obstinately in his manifestly heretical opinions that he was judged by all who have sense to be partly mad and partly possessed by some evil spirit, we, in accordance with the tenor of the safe-conduct, dismissed him at once from our presence, and gave him, with one of our heralds as escort, a fixed term from the twenty-fifth day of April, when he left Worms, for the following twenty days; when these had passed, the safe-conduct was to be regarded as completed and extinguished. Now at last we have decided to proceed, in the following manner, to the remaining fitting remedies necessary for this most pestilent disease.

units.la: 9. Primum omnium, ad honorem Dei omnipotentis, Romanæ Pontificis, & sanctæ Sedis Apostolicæ debitam reverentiam, pro Imperialis dignitatis officio ac debito, necnon zelo & studio, quo nostrorum majorum more, & ingenita etiam nobis vi, ad defensionem Catholicæ fidei, sanctæque Romanæ & universalis Ecclesiæ honorem, tutelam & protectionem, omnes nostras vires & facultates, Imperium, Regna, Dominia, amicos, vitam denique & animam ipsam nostram, exponere sumus parati: Ex Imperiali & Regia authoritate, necnon consilio & assensu Electorum, & omnium sacri Rom. Imp. Principum, Ordinum, & Statuum, in hac celeberrima & frequentissima Imperiali Dieta Wormaciæ congregatorum, ad perpetuam rei memoriam. Exequendo sanctissimi domini nostri Papæ, veri in hac parte judicis, sententiam, decretum & condemnationem, in literis Apostolicis (ut supra dictum est) ad Nos directis, contentam, Martinum Lutherum, ut membrum ab Ecclesia Dei abalienatum, ut obstinatum schismaticum & notorium hæreticum, à Nobis haberi declaramus, & ut talem à vobis omnibus & singulis habendum decernimus & edicimus: Mandantes de eorundem Statuum consilio & consensu, sub criminis læsæ Majestatis, Nostræque & sacri Imperii gravissimæ indignationis, ac etiam amissionis feudorum, Dominiorum, & bonorum omnium, gratiarum quoq; & omnium Privilegiorum, à Nobis, & sacro Imperio dependentium, quæ obtinuistis hactenus, aut prædecessores vestri quomodolibet obtinuerunt: necnon proscriptionis ac Banni, & interdicti Imperialis, pœnis: ne quis vestrum præfatum Martinum Lutherum, receptare, defendere, sustentare, fovere, dicto, facto, aut scripto præsumat. Quinimmo post elapsum supradictū viginti dierum terminum, contra eum, ubicunq; deprehensus fuerit, & in manu, aut facultate vestra erit, juxta formam Imperialis Banni procedatis, vel saltem personaliter captum, tam diu custodiatis, donec Nos, à vobis de hac re certiores facti, de legitima in eum prosecutione facienda vobis significemus, & vos tam sancti operis & laboris debita præmia, & mercedem etiam uberem, cum impensis ob hanc causam factis, reportetis. Et nihilominus ejusdem Martini complices, adhærentes, receptatores, & quomodolibet fautores & fectatores (nisi se iniquitatis semitam deseruisse, & authoritate Apostolica absolutionis remedium consecutos esse, fidem condignam fecerint) necnon eorum omnia & singula bona, mobilia & immobilia, juxta sacras constitutiones, ac interdicti & Banni Imperialis legem & ordinem, liberè & absque ulla contradictione prosequamini, illosq; & illa capiatis, & in usus vestros, optimo & pleno jure convertatis.
units.tr: 9. First of all, for the honour of Almighty God, of the Roman Pontiff and of the holy Apostolic See, we are prepared to expose all our forces and resources, our Empire, kingdoms, dominions, friends, and finally our very life and soul, in fulfilment of the duty and obligation of our Imperial dignity, and out of the zeal and eagerness which, after the custom of our ancestors and by the force inborn in us, we feel for the defence of the Catholic faith and for the honour, protection and safeguarding of the holy Roman and universal Church. By Imperial and royal authority, and with the counsel and assent of the Electors and of all the princes, orders and estates of the Holy Roman Empire, assembled in this most celebrated and well-attended Imperial Diet at Worms, for perpetual remembrance: in carrying out the sentence, decree and condemnation of our most holy lord the Pope, who is the true judge in this matter, contained in the Apostolic letters addressed to us (as stated above), we declare Martin Luther, as a member alienated from the Church of God, an obstinate schismatic and notorious heretic, to be held as such by us, and we decree and command that he be held as such by all and each of you. We command, with the counsel and consent of the same estates, under the charge of injured majesty, under our and the Holy Empire's most grave displeasure, and under the loss of fiefs, dominions and all goods, and of the favours and all privileges depending on us and the Holy Empire, which you have hitherto held or your predecessors have held in any way; and likewise under the penalties of proscription, ban and Imperial interdict: that none of you presume to harbour, defend, sustain or foster the said Martin Luther, by word, deed or writing. Moreover, after the aforesaid term of twenty days has elapsed, wherever he is found and is within your hand or power, you shall proceed against him according to the form of the Imperial ban, or at least take him captive in person and keep him in custody until we, being informed of this by you, signify to you the lawful prosecution to be undertaken against him; and you shall receive the due rewards of so holy a work and labour, and also an ample recompense, together with the expenses incurred for this cause. And likewise the accomplices, adherents, harbourers and any supporters and followers of the same Martin (unless they have shown that they have abandoned the path of iniquity and obtained the remedy of absolution by Apostolic authority) and all and each of their goods, movable and immovable, you shall freely and without any contradiction pursue according to the sacred constitutions and the law and order of the Imperial interdict and ban; and you shall seize them and those goods, and convert them to your own use with the best and full right.

units.la: 10. Mandamus insuper vobis omnibus & singulis præfatis, sub eisdem prænominatis pœnis, ne quis Martini Lutheri scripta, à Summo Pontifice authoritate sua Apostolica (ut præmittitur) damnata, aut alia quæcunque, tam Latino quàm Alemanico, seu alio quovis idiomate, ab eo hactenus cóposita, vel in posterum componenda, utpote mala, suspecta, & à notorio & pervicacissimo hæretico proveniêtia, emere, vendere, tenere, legere, describere, imprimere, aut describi vel imprimi facere, afferre, sustentare, prædicare, defendere, præsumat: non obstante, quod in illis etiam aliqua bona (ad fallendas simplicium mentes) immixta essent. In quo præter justam Sedis Apostolicæ sententiam, etiam laudatissimam veterum Patrum institutionem & consuetudinem omnino exequendam duximus: Qui Arrianorum, Priscillianistarum, Nestorianorum, Euthychianorum, & aliorum hæreticorum libros, & in illis contenta omnia, tam bona quam mala, promiscuè exusserunt, & adnihilarunt. Neque id immerito. Nam si optimi quique cibi, unius tantum guttæ veneni (quo humanum corpus læderetur) infusione suspecti, penitus sunt abjiciendi: quanto magis ea scripta, quibus tanta & tam noxia animabus venena passim inserta sunt, non solum nobis cavenda sunt, sed etiam (ne aliis noceant) prorsus destruenda & corrumpenda, atq; ab omni hominum memoria veniunt oblitteranda. Accedit ad id, quod quicquid boni in Martini libris reperitur, id antea à sanctis Patribus, quos Ecclesia recepit & approbavit, sæpe dictum & sæpius repetitum, absq; ullius periculi aut mali suspitione, legi, & haberi poterit.
units.tr: 10. We further command all and each of you named above, under the same penalties, that no one presume to buy, sell, keep, read, copy, print, or cause to be copied or printed, bring in, uphold, preach or defend any writings of Martin Luther condemned by the Supreme Pontiff with his Apostolic authority (as has been said), or any others, whether in Latin, German or any other language, composed by him hitherto or to be composed in future, as evil, suspect, and proceeding from a notorious and most obstinate heretic, notwithstanding that some good things may be mixed into them to deceive the minds of simple folk. In this matter, besides the just sentence of the Apostolic See, we have thought fit to carry out in full the most praiseworthy institution and custom of the ancient Fathers, who together burned and utterly destroyed the books of the Arians, Priscillianists, Nestorians, Eutychians and other heretics, with all that was contained in them, both good and bad. Nor did they do so without good reason. For if the finest foods must be entirely cast away when merely suspected of having a single drop of poison infused into them (by which the human body would be harmed), how much more must those writings, into which such great and harmful poisons for souls are everywhere inserted, not only be avoided by us, but also (lest they harm others) be utterly destroyed and corrupted, and be blotted out from the memory of all men. Add to this that whatever good is found in Martin's books was previously said and often repeated by the holy Fathers, whom the Church has received and approved, and can be read and held without any danger or suspicion of harm.

units.la: 11. Ea propter, sub eisdem pœnis omnibus & singulis supradictis, vos omnes, & quilibet vestrum, tam Principes quàm alii, ad quos justitiam quomodolibet pertinet ministrare: & alii quicunque in universo Imperio, Regnis, & Dominiis nostris constituti, hujusmodi pestiferos Martini libros, tam Alemanicos quam Latinos, impressos & imprimendos, aut etiam manu scriptos, ubicunque reperiantur (utpote magnæ seditionis, schismatis, hæreseos, in Ecclesia Dei fomites) diripiendos, & publico igni consumendos, penitusque abolendos cum effectu curetis, Apostolicisque Nunciis, seu eorum Commissariis, si operam vestram ad hanc rem requisierint, fideliter & diligenter assistatis: & nihilominus in eorum absentia, per vos ipsos hæc sic fieri, nostro nomine & jussu, omnino & reipsa faciatis. ciatis. In quo omnibus fidelibus, dilectis, subditis nostris, ut vobis ac Nobis metipsis adsistant & parent, tenore praesentium sub eisdem poenis injungimus & mandamus.
units.tr: 11. Therefore, under the same penalties, all and each of you above-named, both princes and others to whom the administration of justice in any way belongs, and all others of whatever station established throughout our Empire, kingdoms and dominions, shall effectively see to it that such pestilent books of Martin, German and Latin, printed and to be printed, or even handwritten, wherever they are found (as the seedbeds of great sedition, schism and heresy in the Church of God), are torn to pieces, consumed by public fire and utterly abolished. You shall faithfully and diligently assist the Apostolic nuncios or their commissaries, if they seek your help in this matter; and in their absence you shall yourselves do these things in our name and by our command, fully and in fact. In this we enjoin and command all our faithful and beloved subjects, by the tenor of these presents and under the same penalties, to assist and obey you and us.

units.la: 12. Verum, quia maxime cavendum est, ne Martini libri, aut ex illis excerpta mala, supposita, aut etiam mutato authoris nomine, publicentur: quia etiam non sine magna animi nostri offensa multos quotidie videmus & audimus, cum alibi, tum maxime in Germania, componi & impressos libros, pluribus malis traditionibus & exemplis refertos: & ne non omni astu & dolo, humanae naturae hostis, Christianis laqueos tendat multos, passim divulgari picturas & imagines, non in opprobrium modo privatarum personarum, sed & ipsius Summi Pontificis, & Sedis Apostolicae contumeliam, cogitatas: ex quibus omnibus libris & picturis, Christi fideles in maximos, tam in fide quam in moribus, prolabuntur errores, & non solum privata odia, scandala, & simultates (pro ut experientia docet) multis in locis exorta fuerunt: verumetiam seditiones, tumultus, rebelliones, schismata, bella, Provincias, & populos, atque universa Dei Ecclesia (nisi provideatur) jamjam excitanda formidatur: Idcirco, ad hanc perniciosissimam pestem extinguendam, & supradictorum Electorum & eorum concordia animo & sententia, omnibus & singulis supradictis, tam Imperiali quam haereditario jure nobis subditis, sub jam saepedictis omnibus poenis praecipimus & mandamus, ne quis hujusmodi famosos & pestilentes libros, seu quascunque alias schedas, scripturas, imagines, picturas, contra Ouri-doxam fidem, bonos mores, & id quod sancta Romana Ecclesia hactenus observavit: atque vectivas criminationes & ignominias, contra Summum Pontificem, Sedem Apostolicam, Principes, Universitates & studiorum, & eorum facultates honestasque personas, componere, scribere, imprimere, depingere, vendere, emere, tenere, habere; aut imprimi, describi, depingi, vel facere, quavis arte aut dolo audeat, aut attentet. Quinimmo sub eisdem poenis jubemus omnibus singulis supradictis, & praesertim iis, qui justitiae ministerio praesunt, ut ejusmodi libros quoscunque hactenus impressos, vel posthac imprimendos, necnon etiam manu scriptos, cujuscunque linguae aut ubicunque locorum per sacrum Imperium, atque etiam nostra haereditaria Regna & Dominia degentes, similiter etiam picturas hujusmodi & imagines, nostro jussu & nomine occupent, diripiant, & publico igni comburant. Et nihilominus hujusmodi detestabilium librorum, codicum, schedarum, scripturatum, & picturarum, authores & inventores, ac etiam post praesentis mandati publicationem, Impressores, Emptores, & Venditores, qui contra jussa nostra facere praesumpserint (si modo id legitime constiterit) necnon eorum jura, & bona omnia & singula capiant, apprehendant, & detineant, ac jure bono quicquid sibi libitum fuerit de illis disponant: ita, quod de hoc nulli hominum, tam in judicio quam extra, respondere sint obligati.
units.tr: 12. But since it must be especially guarded against that Martin's books, or evil excerpts from them, be published under a false title or even with the author's name changed; since we also see, not without great offence to our mind, that many books full of pernicious teachings and examples are composed and printed daily, both elsewhere and above all in Germany; and since the enemy of human nature, with every cunning and guile, lays many snares for Christians, pictures and images devised not only to the reproach of private persons but also to the insult of the Supreme Pontiff himself and of the Apostolic See are everywhere spread abroad. From all these books and pictures the faithful of Christ slip into the greatest errors, both in faith and in morals; and not only private hatreds, scandals and quarrels (as experience teaches) have arisen in many places, but seditions, tumults, rebellions, schisms, wars, provinces and peoples, and the whole Church of God, are feared to be stirred up at any moment unless provision is made. Therefore, to extinguish this most pernicious plague, and with the mind and opinion of the aforesaid Electors in agreement, we command and order all and each of the aforesaid, both those subject to us by Imperial right and those subject by hereditary right, under all the penalties already often mentioned, that none dare or attempt, by any art or guile, to compose, write, print, paint, sell, buy, keep or have such infamous and pestilent books, or any other leaflets, writings or images or pictures against the orthodox faith, good morals and what the holy Roman Church has hitherto observed, or abusive accusations and insults against the Supreme Pontiff, the Apostolic See, princes, universities and seats of learning, and their faculties and honourable persons; or to cause them to be printed, copied or painted. Moreover, under the same penalties we order all and each of the aforesaid, and especially those who preside over the administration of justice, to seize, snatch up and burn in public fire, by our command and in our name, all such books, in whatever language and wherever they have been printed or are to be printed hereafter, and likewise handwritten ones, held by those living throughout the Holy Empire and also in our hereditary kingdoms and dominions, and similarly such pictures and images. And nevertheless the authors and inventors of such detestable books, codices, leaflets, writings and pictures, and also, after the publication of the present mandate, the printers, buyers and sellers who presume to act against our commands (if this has been lawfully established), together with all their rights and goods, each and all, shall be seized, apprehended and detained, and may dispose of whatever they wish of them by good right, so that they are not bound to answer to anyone for this, either in court or out of it.

units.la: 13. Atque ut omnis ejuscemodi & aliorum errorum occasio tollatur, & ne talia scribentium venena longe lateque diffundantur, sed praeclarum imprimendi libros artificium in bonos tantum, & laudabiles usus exerceatur: ex certa nostra scientia, animoque deliberato, ac Imperiali Regia authoritate, de maturo supradictorum Electorum, & aliorum sacri Rom. Imp.
