Statuum, consilio, deliberatione, & unanimi consensu, volumus & sub Banni, & Interdicti Imperialis, ac aliis antedictis poenis praecipimus & jubemus, tenore praesentis Edicti, quod vim inviolabilis legis habere decernimus: Ne quis de caetero Chalcographus, & librorum Impressor, aut alius quivis ubilibet per sacrum Imperium atque nostra praedicta Regna & Dominia constitutus, libros ullos, seu aliam quamcunque scripturam, in quibus de sacris literis, aut fide Catholica aliquid vel minimum tractatur, non habito prius consensu & voluntate Ordinarii loci, aut ejus ad hoc substituti & deputati, cum authoritate etiam facultatis Theologicae alicujus propinquae Universitatis, pro prima videlicet impressione: alios vero cujuscunque rei, & facultatis libros, schedas, & picturas, de consensu saltem Ordinarii, aut ejus ad hoc substituti, illo pacto imprimere, vel vendere, aut imprimi, vel vendi facere, directe vel indirecte, quoquo modo praesumat aut attentet.
units.tr: 13. And so that every occasion of this kind of error, and of others, may be removed, and that the poisons of such writers may not be spread far and wide, but that the excellent art of printing may be used only for good and laudable purposes: by our certain knowledge and deliberate intention, and by Imperial Royal authority, with the mature counsel, deliberation and unanimous consent of the above-mentioned Electors and of the other Estates of the Holy Roman Empire, we will, and under the ban and Imperial interdict, and the other penalties mentioned above, we command and order, by the tenor of this present Edict, which we decree to have the force of inviolable law: that no one henceforth, whether a printer or bookseller or anyone else anywhere established throughout the Holy Empire and our aforesaid kingdoms and dominions, shall presume or attempt, in any way, directly or indirectly, to print or sell any books or other writings whatsoever, in which anything at all, even the smallest matter, concerning Holy Scripture or the Catholic faith is treated, without first having the consent and will of the ordinary of the place, or of his substitute and deputy, together with the authority of the faculty of theology of some nearby university, namely for the first printing; and that he shall print or sell, or cause to be printed or sold, other books, papers and pictures of any subject or faculty on that same condition, with at least the consent of the ordinary or of his substitute.

units.la: 14. Quod si quis cujuscunque sit dignitatis, gradus, aut conditionis, hanc nostram decretum, statutum, legem & ordinationem, in omnibus & singulis supradictis, tam Lutheranam quam impressoriam materiam concernentibus, inviolabiliter observandam, ullo pacto, aut quaesito colore vel ingenio, contrafacere, aut venire, ausu temerario praesumpserit: praeterquam quod illud irritum decernimus & inane, etiam in laesae Majestatis crimen, ac nostram, & Sacri Imperii vehementissimam indignationem, proscriptionisque & Banni, ac interdicti Imperialis, necnon alias saepe dictas poenas, se ipso facto incurrisse cognoscat.
units.tr: 14. But if anyone, of whatever dignity, rank or condition, has rashly presumed to contravene this our decree, statute, law and ordinance, which must be inviolably observed in all and each of the above-mentioned matters, concerning both Lutheran and printed material, in any way, or under any pretext or cunning device whatsoever, or to act against it, let him know that, apart from our declaring such an act void and null, he has thereby incurred, by the very fact, the charge of high treason, our most severe indignation and that of the Holy Empire, proscription and the ban and Imperial interdict, and the other penalties often mentioned.

units.la: Harum testimonio literarum, Sigilli nostri munimine roboratarum. Datum in Civitate Imperiali Wormacia, die Octava Mensis Maij, Anno Domini Millesimo Quingentesimo Vicesimo Primo, Regnorum nostrorum: Romani secundo: Caeterorum vero omnium Sexto.
units.tr: Given under our seal as a witness to these letters, in the Imperial City of Worms, on the eighth day of May, in the year of our Lord one thousand five hundred and twenty-one, in the second year of our reign as King of the Romans, and the sixth of all our other reigns.

units.la: Ad mandatum Domini Imperatoris proprium.
units.tr: By the proper command of the Lord Emperor.

units.la: CAROLVS
units.tr: CHARLES

units.la: CAROLI V. IMPER. AUG. ET COMMUNIUM S. IMPE- RII ORDINUM GRAVAMINA
units.tr: CHARLES V, EMPEROR AUGUSTUS, AND THE GRIEVANCES OF THE ORDERS OF THE HOLY ROMAN EMPIRE

units.la: Adversus Papæ Romani, & universæ Curiæ Romanæ, ejusq; afflictarum, injustas usurpationes & tyrannides.
units.tr: Against the unjust usurpations and tyrannies of the Pope of Rome, of the whole Roman Curia, and of its dependants.

units.la: CAROLUS V. IMPERATOR AUG. HADRIANO VI. PONT. ROM.
units.tr: CHARLES V, EMPEROR AUGUSTUS, TO HADRIAN VI, POPE OF ROME

units.la: BEatissime Pater, Domine Reverendiss. Erfi ea est Sanctitatis vestræ erga nos benignitas, amorq; paternus, sitq; contrà hostra erga S. Vestram ea observantia & veneratio, ut majora esse non possint: illa tamen omnes & nostræ maximè ditionis populi longè majora, tantaq; existimant, ut & nos nihil à beatitudine vestra frustra posse petere, & S. vestram nobis non omnia libenter concessuram esse arbitrentur. Quæ res nos ea, quæ alioqui non nisi verecundè petere auderemus, liberè, confidenter à B. vestra postulare facit, & maximè, si talia fuerint, quæ publicæ salutis causa à nobis efflagitata videantur.
units.tr: Most blessed Father, most reverend Lord. Your Holiness shows us such kindness and paternal love, and we show Your Holiness such observance and veneration, that neither could be greater. Yet all the people of our dominions think both far greater still, and so they believe that we can ask nothing of Your Beatitude in vain, and that Your Holiness will readily grant us almost everything. This is why we dare to ask Your Beatitude freely and confidently for things which otherwise we would seek only with great restraint, especially when they are things which seem to be demanded by us for the sake of the public welfare.

units.la: 1. Cum itaq; superioribus mensibus in civitate nostra Imperiali Nurnbergensi omnes ordines Sacri Rom. Imperii pro tutela defensioneq; Regni Hungariæ convenissent, & Electores cæteriq; Principes ac aliorum ordinum Status seculares inter cætera animadverterent, Germaniam ad eam egestatem rerum inopiam redactam esse, ut nō modò ipsi quidquam contra Christi fidei hostes truculentissimos Turcas digne gerere possint: Sed nec tantulas superesse S. Rom. Imperii opes & facultates, unde justitiam & pacem tueri & conservare, ac nephariorum hominum scelera & in inferenda injuria audaciam possint cohibere, nisi etiam S. V. liberalitate & paterno favore atq; auxilio adjuti fuerint.
units.tr: 1. When, therefore, in recent months all the orders of the Holy Roman Empire had assembled in our Imperial city of Nuremberg to plan the protection and defence of the Kingdom of Hungary, the Electors and the other princes and the secular estates of the other orders observed, among other things, that Germany had been reduced to such want and poverty of resources that they could not act worthily themselves against the most savage Turks, enemies of the Christian faith. Nor do the Holy Roman Empire's remaining means and resources suffice to uphold and preserve justice and peace, and to restrain the crimes and audacity of wicked men in inflicting injury, unless they are also aided by the generosity, paternal favour and help of Your Holiness.

units.la: 3. Itaq; inter cætera cum meminissent annatas, quas novi antistites Rom. Pontifici solvere consueverunt, ab origine ea maximè ratione concessas esse, ut hujusmodi pecuniis Christi fidei hostes arcerentur: Nunc autem ipsi Turcæ magna parte inferioris Pannoniæ occupata, Germaniæ inhient: æquum esse, ut hujusmodi annatæ in Germania retineri, & illic in hunc usum converti debeant. Præterea cum inter mortales nihil sit sanctius, Deo nihil gratius, quam justitiæ & æquitatis cultus; Quæ de re etiam cæsuerunt, neq; Deo ingratū, neq; ulla ratione imperium dici posse, & si ea quæ solum divinæ Majest. cultui dedicata consecrataq; existimatur, ad justitiæ pacisq; constituendæ usum in parte convertantur: Propterea cuperent, nostraq; intercessione à S. V. obtinere posse sperant, inprimis ut pensiones, quæ ex sacerdotiis Germanicis curiæ S. V. & Romanæ urbis hominib. perfolvūtur, posthac in Germania detineantur. Adhæc cujuslibet Ecclesiæ majoris sive minoris Collegium quotannis decimam proventuum suorum contribuerit, vel saltem proximè vacaturæ præbendæ proventus, uti mortuæ & assiduè vacantis conservarentur, nec non cùm Germania ditissimorum monasteriorum plena sit, ut illis quoq; tributum imponeretur: Atq; etiam ut reliquorum sacerdotum ordines quisq; pro facultate & fortunis suis aliquid penderet: Præterea Mendicantium ordinum monasterium quodlibet floremos quinq; quotannis conferret. Quodq; hujusmodi proventus omnes ad Turcarum imperus reprimendos, ac pro justitia & pace in Germania ac S. Rom. Imperio stabiliēda, & in nullum prorsus alium usum converterentur: usq; S. V. suprà memorata omnia ad quadriennium concedere & clementer admittere dignaretur.
units.tr: 3. Accordingly, among other things, they recalled that the annates which new bishops have customarily paid to the Roman Pontiff were originally granted chiefly for this reason: that by such money the enemies of the Christian faith might be kept off. Now the Turks themselves, having occupied a large part of Lower Pannonia, are aiming at Germany, and it is right that such annates be retained in Germany and applied there to this purpose. Moreover, since nothing among mortals is holier or more pleasing to God than the cultivation of justice and equity, and since they have also agreed on this matter, it is neither ungrateful to God nor can it in any way be called unlawful, if what is thought to be dedicated and consecrated solely to the worship of the divine Majesty is in part turned to the establishment of justice and peace. They therefore wish, and hope through our intercession to obtain from Your Holiness, above all, that the pensions which are paid from German benefices to Your Holiness's Curia and to the people of the city of Rome be kept in Germany from now on. In addition, that the chapter of every greater or lesser church contribute yearly a tenth of its revenues, or at least the revenue of a prebend about to fall vacant, or else that the revenue of a prebend which has become vacant through death and remains perpetually unfilled be preserved for this use. Since Germany is full of very rich monasteries, they also wish a tax to be laid on these. Likewise, that each order of the remaining clergy pay something according to its means and resources. Furthermore, that each monastery of the mendicant orders contribute five florins yearly. And that all these revenues be used solely to repress the Turkish onslaught and to establish justice and peace in Germany and the Holy Roman Empire, and not be turned to any other use at all. They ask that Your Holiness deign to grant all the aforesaid things for four years and graciously allow them.

units.la: 4. Nobis verò diligenter considerantibus, perpetuos reip. Christianæ hostes Turcas, Hungarorum munitionibus locis & quodammodo propugnaculis captis, jam soli Germaniæ maximè imminere. Præterea S. Imperii proventus & vectigalia tum indulgentiā, tum prædecessorum nostrorum liberalitate, Ecclesiastico ordine locupletando, adeò esse extenuata atq; distracta, ut non modò Turcis relinq; sed nec pax aut justitia in Germania diutius confirmari possit, nisi his atq; aliis tributis, quæ Imperii ordines sibi præter hæc cultro impositu sunt: ea Beatitudinis V. & munificentia & mitissimo animo subleventur.
units.tr: 4. We, considering carefully, see that the Turks, perpetual enemies of the Christian commonwealth, having captured the Hungarian fortifications and, as it were, the bulwarks, now threaten Germany above all. Moreover, the revenues and tributes of the Holy Empire have been so reduced and dispersed, both through indulgences and through the liberality of our predecessors in enriching the ecclesiastical order, that not only can nothing be left for the Turks, but neither peace nor justice can be secured in Germany for any length of time, unless these and other tributes, which the orders of the Empire have been burdened with beyond these, are relieved by the bounty and most gentle spirit of Your Beatitude.

units.la: 5. Adhortatur nos & nephariam illam Lutherianam sectam, quam ut tolleremus nullum officium præter misimus, ita multorum Germanorum animis uti pestiferum virus paulatim obrepsisse, obsedisse, ut inde quoq; incendium Reip. Christianæ extinguerent, nisi prædictis tributis justicia itaq; boretur fulciaturq; ut aliquando in virulentæ illius doctrinæ sectatores distracto gladio possit animadverti. Ad quam rem etiam multorum Germanorum animos, & horum præsertim, qui honestissimi sunt ordinis, pro universalis Rom. Ecclesiæ tranquillitate & auctoritate conservanda erectos incensos; cognoscimus.
units.tr: 5. Moreover, we are urged on by that accursed Lutheran sect, which we have left no duty undone to suppress. Like a pestilent poison it has gradually crept into, and taken possession of, the minds of many Germans, so that it may kindle a fire even for the Christian commonwealth, unless justice is supported and strengthened by the aforesaid tributes, so that at last the followers of that virulent doctrine may be punished with the sword drawn. We know that the minds of many Germans, and especially of those of the most honourable rank, have been roused and inflamed to preserve the tranquillity and authority of the universal Roman Church.

units.la: 6. Quapropter B.V. summopere rogamus, ut divina illa sua mente & mitissimis oculis, quibus Christianum orbem irradiasse videant, hæc omnia clementius intueatur, ponatq; ante oculos Turcarum infesta signa aciesque jam pene invictas, perniciosi Lutherani dogmatis incendium, quod pestimi cujusque mentem obcedit. Præterea nostram à Germania absentiam: Quodque tantorum malorum imminentes flammæ nullo alio, quàm B.V. æterno illo benignitatis & munificentiæ fonte reflingui poterunt: & hæc nobis, deinde S. Romano Imp. & nationi Germanicæ, alioqui de sancta Apostolica sede optime meritae, pro tot tantisq; malis coercendis clementer ad quadriennium & indulgere dignetur. Quod si S.V. fecerit, uti speramus, feret genti bello invictae ad furorem Turcum refrenandum dignas atq; optatas suppetias in amplissimo Christiani orbis populo, & qui inquieto iustitiae cultum & pacem constituet: unico beneficio sibi innumeros & clarissimos principes conciliabit, Germanis autem reliquis, qui nunc ab ista sancta sede, Lutheriana haeresi corrupti, nonnihil alieni animi esse videntur, uberem occasionem praebebit, hoc munificentissimo S.V. beneficio illectis, ut quicquid studio, labore, observantia, quicquid fide, diligentia & quicquid viribus atq; opibus possunt, hoc totum pro B.V. & sacrosancta sedis Apostolicae authoritate tuenda deferant & polliceantur. Quemadmodum haec omnia S.V. ex Ostro, & Dn. Johanne Emanuele Duce Saxeae extensius intelliget: & S.V. valere, ac sanctae Romanae Ecclesiae diu feliciter praesse cupimus.
units.tr: 6. Therefore we earnestly beseech Your Beatitude to look more mercifully upon all these things with that divine mind and most gentle eyes with which you are seen to illumine the Christian world, and to set before your eyes the hostile standards and armies of the Turks, now almost invincible, and the burning of the pernicious Lutheran dogma, which besieges the mind of every wretch. Please consider also our absence from Germany; and that the threatening flames of such great evils can be quenched by no other source than the eternal fountain of kindness and munificence of Your Beatitude. Deign to grant these things for four years, first to us, then to the Holy Roman Emperor and to the German nation, which has otherwise deserved well of the holy Apostolic See, so that such great and grave evils may be restrained. If Your Holiness does so, as we hope, you will bring to a nation unconquered in war worthy and desired aid for checking the fury of the Turk, among the most extensive peoples of the Christian world, a people who will establish the cultivation of justice and peace in these restless times. By this one benefit you will win to yourself countless and most illustrious princes. To the rest of the Germans, who now seem somewhat estranged from this holy See, corrupted by the Lutheran heresy, it will offer a rich opportunity: enticed by this most generous benefit of Your Holiness, they will place at the disposal of Your Beatitude, and promise, whatever they can give of zeal, labour, devotion, faith and diligence, and whatever of strength and resources, all of it for defending the authority of the most sacred Apostolic See. Your Holiness will understand all these things more fully from Ostro and from Lord John Emanuel, Duke of Saxony. We wish Your Holiness well, and that you may long and happily preside over the holy Roman Church.

units.la: Datum in oppido nostro Vallisoleti, ultim. Octobr. Anno MDXXII. Regnorum Rom. quarto, &c.
units.tr: Given in our town of Valladolid, on the last day of October, in the year 1522, the fourth of our reign, etc.

units.la: CAROLVS
units.tr: CHARLES

units.la: divina favente clementia electus Romanorum semper Augustus.
units.tr: by the favouring clemency of God elected Emperor of the Romans, ever Augustus.

units.la: ADRIANUS PAPA VI. VENE- RABILIBUS FRATRIBUS, DILECTIS FILIIS, NOBILIBUS VIRIS, SACRI ROMANI IMPERII PRINCIPIBUS ELECTORIBUS, ET ALIIS PRINCIPIBUS tam Ecclesiasticis quam Secularibus, ac etiam Communitatum omnium Inclitae Germanicae Nationis Oratoribus in Dieta Nurnbergensi congregatis, salutem & Apostolicam bene- dictionem.
units.tr: POPE ADRIAN VI, TO OUR VENERABLE BRETHREN, BELOVED SONS, NOBLE MEN, THE PRINCES ELECTORS OF THE HOLY ROMAN EMPIRE AND THE OTHER PRINCES, BOTH ECCLESIASTICAL AND SECULAR, AND ALSO THE ENVOYS OF ALL THE COMMUNITIES OF THE RENOWNED GERMAN NATION, GATHERED AT THE DIET OF NUREMBERG: GREETING AND APOSTOLIC BLESSING.

units.la: VENERABILES fratres & dilecti filii: Postquam ad Apostolatus Officium, divina disposente providentia assumpti sumus, testis nobis est ille, qui nos ut immeritos, ita nul tale expectantes, promovit, ... cogitasse, quam ut in custodido grege nobis credito, tam in universum, quam singulatim bonis pastoris partes, modis omnibus impleremus: atq; adeo nullam existimasse nostri ovibus tam morbosam, quam non pro viribus curamus, nullam tam vagam, & a caeteris errantem, quam non perquirere, & ad dominicam caulam reducere summopere cupiemus.
units.tr: VENERABLE BRETHREN AND BELOVED SONS: Since we were taken up into the office of the apostolate by the disposing providence of God, he who promoted us, though we were unworthy and expected nothing of the kind, is our witness that we have thought of nothing more than fulfilling in every way the duties of a good shepherd, both toward the whole flock entrusted to us and toward each sheep individually. Accordingly, we have considered no sheep so diseased that we do not care for it to the best of our strength, and we most earnestly desire to seek out and lead back to the Lord's fold no sheep so wandering and straying from the rest.

units.la: Et sane ab ineunte statim Pontificatu nostro, (quod tum potissimum expedire videbamus) Christianorum principum animos, heu nimis iam inter se dissidentes, ad pacem & concordiam ineundam, deponendaq; arma (aut hostium dum esset, ea in fidei hostes convertenda) tam per diversos nuncios nostros, quam per quotidianas fere literas hortamare, precari, hactenus nunquam destitimus.
units.tr: And indeed, from the very beginning of our pontificate (which we then saw to be especially expedient), we have never ceased to urge, beseech and entreat the minds of Christian princes, alas now too divided among themselves, to enter into peace and concord and to lay down their arms (or, if they must still be at war with an enemy, to turn them against the enemies of the faith), both through our various nuncios and through letters nearly every day.

units.la: Et ne verbo tantum, sed & re ipsa hujus nostri desiderii ederemus exempla, Deus scit, quanto rei nostrae fuerit, hac praesertim temporibus incommodo, pecunias, & alia subsidia ad Rhodienses milites strenuos fidei propugnatores immanissimo Turcarum tyranno atrociter obsessos, ac in alia etiam loca in eamdem hostis faucibus periclitantia, mutuo. Mox vero ab externis ad intestina animum advertentes, non sine gravi animi molestia percepimus, Martinum Lutherum (quem sua culpa jam filium nostrum vocare non posse dolemus) hominem veterum, & jam dam-natae haeresum suscitatorem, post sedis Apostolicae paterna primum monita, deinde etiam sententiam, non absque ... morum & doctissimorum virorum, & diversarum universitatum legitime contra eum latam: post charissimi filii Caroli nostri Romanorum & Hispaniorum Regis Catholici, in Imperatorem electi, & vestrum ... ium, super ejusdem sententia executione, in proximis comitiis Wormaciae habitis, mature decretum; ... Germaniam promulgatum: non modo per quos deceret, non punitum, aut per se cohibitum, a pravissimis desistere, sed omnis Christiana charitatis & pietatis Evangelica non oblitum modo, sed & impie contemnentem quotidie libros, errorum, haeresum, contumeliarum, ac seditionum plenos, sive de suo, sive ab aliis adjutum, divulgari veluti pestem quandam Germaniam, & vicinas regiones longe lateq; pervadentem, venenata lingua spiculum animas & mores inficere & corrumpere conari: &, quod pejus est, borum fautorum facinorum non plebejos modo, sed Nobiles plerosq; habere fautores: adeo, ut (quae fortasse illorum tumultuum primaria fuit causa) in Sacerdotium, & obedientiam tam ecclesiasticis quam secularibus debitam, vilipendi coeptum sit, & tandem inter nonnullos ad civilia bella deventum.
units.tr: And so that we might give examples of this desire not only in words but in deeds, God knows how much of our own resources, especially inconvenient in these times, we have lent in money and other aid to the Rhodian soldiers, brave defenders of the faith, fiercely besieged by the most savage tyrant of the Turks, and to other places likewise endangered by the enemy's jaws. But soon, turning our attention from external to internal affairs, we learned, not without great distress of mind, that Martin Luther (whom, through his own fault, we grieve we can no longer call our son), a man who revives old and long-condemned heresies, after the first paternal admonitions of the Apostolic See and then also its sentence, lawfully pronounced against him by [...] learned men and various universities; after our dearest son Charles, elected Emperor of the Romans and Catholic King of the Spaniards, and yours [...] had maturely decreed at the recent diet held at Worms, concerning the execution of that sentence, and [...] promulgated throughout Germany: not only has he not been punished by those who ought to punish him, nor restrained by them, so that he might desist from his most depraved courses, but he, neglecting not only Evangelical Christian charity and piety but even impiously scorning them, daily publishes books full of errors, heresies, insults and sedition, whether from his own pen or aided by others, and tries, like a pestilence spreading far and wide through Germany and the neighbouring regions, to infect and corrupt souls and morals with his venomous tongue. And, what is worse, these perpetrators have as supporters not only commoners but most of the nobles as well, so that (which was perhaps the primary cause of those tumults) the priesthood and the obedience owed to both ecclesiastical and secular authorities began to be held in contempt, and at last among some it came to civil wars.

units.la: Quod quam male cadat Christianae reipub. hoc praesertim tempore, mente & cogitatione facile prospicere videtis tempus huic rei magis importunum, quam hoc: aut quod citius ab haeresibus si quaeortae sint, necessario purgandum. Quum enim humani generis perpetuum hostis diabolus, sub leonis rugientis specie per Turcarum vires... ... ... bolum sub draconis subdoli forma, iflas haereses domi nostra disseminantem, interq; fortissimos Germanos nostros dias & seditiones suscitantem, fovebimus. Atq; ut etiam debellare externos hostes maxime possimus, irritus labor, impensaq;, & animarum salutis minime utilis, foris hostes vincere, & domi haeresibus, schismatibus... Meminimus, quum etiam in minoribus constituti, in Hispania essemus, multa ad nos & varia de Luthero, & quae...
units.tr: How badly this falls upon the Christian commonwealth, especially at this time, you can easily see by thinking about it. There is no time more unseasonable for this matter than the present one, or rather, heresies, if they have arisen, must be cleansed away as quickly as possible. For since the devil, the perpetual enemy of the human race, under the appearance of a roaring lion, through the forces of the Turks ... [and] under the form of a deceitful dragon, spreading these heresies at home and stirring up discords and seditions among our most brave Germans, we would be fostering him. And so that we may be able to defeat external enemies most of all, it is a futile labour and expense, and of no use at all for the salvation of souls, to conquer enemies abroad while heresies and schisms at home ... For this reason, His Holiness earnestly desires that this plague be met more swiftly, so that worse consequences do not follow from it; with an explanation of certain necessary reasons which can, and ought, to move the German Princes especially to undertake this as quickly as possible; and above all by urging that the sentence against Luther lawfully passed by the Apostolic See, and the decree made after the edict of the Sacred Caesarean and Catholic Majesty, at the forthcoming Diet held at Worms, concerning the execution of that sentence, be committed to due execution.

units.la: 4. Ad hæc sacræ Cæsareæ majestatis Locumtenens, & Principes, aliique ordines dicunt, se non minùs, quàm Beatitudinem Pontificis ex animo dolere de impietatibus, animarum periculis & incommodis, quæ in Christiana religione, ex Lutherana secta, aliisve provenerint. Quicquid enim auxilii & consilii pro extirpandis erroribus & animarum periculis amovendis sua moderatione præstare unquam poterint, sunt pro summa sua in Christi religionem devotione & pietate paratissimi: ingenueque agnoscunt, se, & Beatitudini Pontificis, & sacræ Cæsareæ Majestati, ut Christianos decet Principes, ad omnem obedientiam esse obnoxios.
units.tr: 4. In addition, the Locum tenens of the Sacred Caesarean Majesty, the Princes, and the other estates say that they grieve from the heart no less than His Holiness the Pope over the impieties, the dangers to souls, and the troubles that have arisen in the Christian religion from the Lutheran sect and others. For whatever aid and counsel they are ever able to give, by their own moderation, for rooting out errors and removing dangers to souls, they are most ready, in their great devotion and piety toward the religion of Christ. And they frankly acknowledge that they, like Christian princes, are bound to every obedience both to His Holiness the Pope and to the Sacred Caesarean Majesty.

units.la: 5. Sed quòd sedis Apostolicæ sententia in Lutherum lata, simulque sacræ Cæsareæ majestatis edictum, non sit debitæ executioni demandatum, non sine maximis, urgentissimisque rationibus, ut puta, ne pejora inde causarentur, &c. hactenus prætermissum est.
units.tr: 5. But that the sentence of the Apostolic See against Luther, and at the same time the edict of the Sacred Caesarean Majesty, have not been committed to due execution, has so far been overlooked, not without very great and pressing reasons, for example, lest worse things be caused thereby, and so on.

units.la: 6. Majori namque populi parti jam pridem persuasum est, & modò Lutheranis libris ac dogmatibus populorum opinio sic informata, ut jam pro comperto habeant, nationi Germanicæ à Curia Romana per certos abusus, multa & magna gravamina & incommoda illata esse: ob id, si pro executione Apostolicæ Sedis sententiæ, vel Imperatoriæ Majestatis edicti, quidpiam acerbius attentatum esset, mox popularis multitudo sibi hanc suspicionem animo concepisset, ac si talia fierent pro evertenda Evangelica veritate, & sustinendis, manu tenendisque malis abusibus, impietatibusque. Unde indubiè aliud nihil, quàm gravissimi tumultus populares, intestinaque bella speranda essent. Quemadmodum ex multis ac variis rerum argumentis Principes, aliique Ordines jam plane didicere, & cognovere. Opportunioribus itaque remediis his malis, in hac potissimum temporum difficultate, succurrendum esse existimant.
units.tr: 6. For it has long been persuaded to the greater part of the people, and now the opinion of the people has been so shaped by Lutheran books and doctrines, that they now hold as certain that many great grievances and troubles have been inflicted on the German nation by the Roman Curia through certain abuses. Therefore, if anything rather harsh were attempted in execution of the sentence of the Apostolic See or of the imperial edict, the popular crowd would at once conceive this suspicion, as if such things were done to overthrow the evangelical truth and to uphold and maintain abuses and impieties. Hence nothing else is undoubtedly to be expected than the most serious popular tumults and internal wars, as the Princes and the other Estates have now plainly learned and recognised from many and various indications of affairs. They therefore think these evils must be met with more suitable remedies, especially in this difficulty of the times.

units.la: 7. Nam quemadmodum & reverendissimus Dominus Nuncius Apostolicus, nomine beatiss. Pontificis, in sua instructione inter alia pie, Christiane, & vere fatetur & agnoscit, quòd Deus hanc Ecclesiæ suæ persecutionem inferri permittit, propter peccata hominum; polliceturque beatitud. Pontificis omnem adhibiturum operam, ut primùm Romana Curia, unde forte omne hoc malum processit, reformetur, ut sicut inde corruptio in omnes inferiores emanavit, ita etiam ab eadem sanitas & reformario omnium emanet.
units.tr: 7. For just as the Most Reverend Lord Nuncio, in the name of the Most Blessed Pope, in his instruction, among other things, piously, Christianly and truly confesses and acknowledges that God permits this persecution to be brought upon His Church on account of the sins of men; and promises that His Holiness will apply every effort so that first the Roman Curia, whence perhaps all this evil has proceeded, be reformed, so that just as corruption has flowed from it into all the lower orders, so too soundness and reformation may flow from it to all.

units.la: 8. Ad hæc beatissimus Pontifex pio ac paterno amore testatur, sibi etiam dum in minoribus esset, plurimum displicuisse, quotiens Concordatis Principum per curiam Rom. derogaretur, suæque Beatitudini hanc certissimam esse sententiam, etiamsi Principes nunquam requirerent, sui Pontificatus tempore penitus abstinere, unicuique, & maximè nationi Germanicæ, jus suum conservare, illique nationi peculiares favores impendere. Quis itaque ex his omnibus non videt, sanctissimum Pontificem nihil penitus illorum omittere, quæ vel pius pater & verus pastor ovibus suis unquam vel præstare posset, vel debeat? Quis etiam per hæc ad veram pietatem, filialem amorem, & erratorum suorum emendationem non moveretur, maximè ubi sua Sanctitas hæc tam pia, sanctaque instituta opere ipso, uti coepit, præstiterit: quemadmodum Serenissimus Dominus Locumtenens, cæterique Principes, & omnium hujus Imperii Ordinum Proceres indubiè sperant, idque pro summa immortalis Dei gloria, animarum salute, ac publica pace & tranquillitate servanda fieri ex animo effla-gitant, orantque.
units.tr: 8. Moreover, the Most Holy Pontiff testifies with holy and paternal love that, even while he was still among the lesser clergy, it greatly displeased him whenever the concordats of the Princes were infringed by the Roman Curia; and that it is his most certain opinion that, even if the Princes never asked, during his pontificate he would entirely refrain from this, would preserve the right of each, and especially of the German nation, and would bestow special favours upon that nation. Who, then, from all these things does not see that the Most Holy Pontiff omits nothing of those things which a pious father and true shepherd could ever either grant or ought to grant to his sheep? Who would not also be moved by these things to true piety, filial love, and the amendment of his own errors, especially when His Holiness has carried out these so pious and holy arrangements in actual deed, as he has begun; just as the Most Serene Lord Locum tenens, the other Princes, and the nobles of all the Orders of this Empire undoubtedly hope, and earnestly ask and pray that this be done from their hearts, for the highest glory of immortal God, the salvation of souls, and the preservation of public peace and tranquillity.

units.la: 9. Nam nisi istiusmodi abusus & gravamina, simulque certi articuli, quos seculares Principes extra hæc speciali-ter designatos, scriptis exhibebunt, fideliter reformentur, vera pax & concordia inter Ecclesiasticos, secularesque ordines, hujusque tumultus & errorum extirpatio per Germaniam minime speranda est. Nam ex longis & variis bellorum tumultibus, quibus Germania nostra multis annis vexata est, item ob alia gravamina & incommoda, quæ huic nationi hactenus incubuerunt, hæc natio pecuniis ac divitiis adeò est extenuata & exhausta, ut etiam jam pro necessaria justitiæ ac pacis conservatione in his deficiat. Multo majori itaque incommodo & difficultate Hungarorum regno & Croatis petita auxilia contra Turcam præstare poterit.
units.tr: 9. For unless abuses and grievances of this kind, together with certain articles which the secular Princes will set out in writing, separately designated beyond these, are faithfully reformed, true peace and concord between the ecclesiastical and secular orders, and the extirpation of these tumults and errors throughout Germany, are by no means to be hoped for. For from the long and various tumults of wars, by which our Germany has been vexed for many years, and likewise from other grievances and troubles which have so far weighed upon this nation, this nation has been so worn down and drained of money and wealth that it is now failing even in the necessary maintenance of justice and peace at home. Therefore it will be able to furnish aid against the Turk to the kingdom of Hungary and to the Croats, when asked, only with much greater inconvenience and difficulty.

units.la: 10. Cum autem Ordines sacri Romani Imperii nihil dubitent, beatitudinem Pontificis pro comperto habere, Principes Germaniæ in solutionem Annatarum ad aliquot annos sedi Apostolicæ solvendarum, ea lege ac conditione consensisse, ut illa in oppugnationem perfidissimi Turcæ, & defensionem fidei Catholicæ converterentur: Ex quo autem numerus annorum, intra quos annatæ illæ solvi debeant, nunc longo intervallo transfactus sit, neque annatæ illæ à beatitudinis sive prædecessoribus Pontificibus Romanis in hunc usum, in quem decretæ sunt, conversæ: Ob id, si modò necessitate exigente, communia auxilia in oppugnationem Turcæ per Germaniam ellent decernenda & colligenda, causatur inde populus Germanicus, quare Annatæ priùs jam multis annis in hunc usum reservatæ, ad hoc opus applicentur, aversaturque alia in se ob hanc causam gravamina recipere. Ex quo Prælati Ecclesiastici pro annatis sedi Apostolicæ solvendis, ut plurimum suis subditis supposita, & collectas inponere, & talia ab eisdem recuperare causaverunt. Quare Illustrissimus Princeps Dominus Locumtenens, aliique Principes, & Imperii Romani Ordines vehementer orant, orant, ut beatitudo Pontificis velit haec & alia paterno affectu considerare, & illas Annatas, quae post obitum Episcoporum, aliorumque praelatorum, seu Ecclesiasticorum, ad Curiam Romanam invendae fuerint, in futurum non exigere, sed illas fisco sacri Romani Imperii applicandas relinquere, ut eo commodius justitia, pax & tranquillitas nationi Germanicae conservari, & respublica eo melius per haec ordinari, possintque per Germanicam nationem aliis Christianis potentatibus contra Turcam communem hostem auxilia & praesidia praestari: quod alias & absque eo, minime sperandum erit.
units.tr: 10. Since the Orders of the Holy Roman Empire doubt nothing, namely that His Holiness the Pope holds it as certain that the Princes of Germany consented to the payment of the annates to the Apostolic See, to be paid for some years, on this law and condition: that they should be turned to the attack on the most faithless Turk and to the defence of the Catholic faith; and since the number of years within which those annates ought to be paid has now passed by a long interval, and those annates have not been turned by his predecessors, the Roman Pontiffs, to the use for which they were decreed; therefore, if now, by pressing necessity, common aids were to be decreed and collected throughout Germany for the attack on the Turk, the German people complain that the annates, long reserved for this use, should first be applied to this work, and they shrink from taking upon themselves other burdens on this account. Hence the ecclesiastical prelates, who for the most part have placed upon their subjects the burden of paying the annates to the Apostolic See, have caused taxes to be imposed and such things to be recovered from them. Therefore the Most Illustrious Lord Locum tenens, the other Princes, and the Orders of the Roman Empire earnestly pray, pray, that His Holiness may be willing to consider these and other matters with a fatherly affection, and in future not to exact those annates which are to be sent to the Roman Curia after the death of bishops and other prelates or ecclesiastics, but to leave them to be applied to the treasury of the Holy Roman Empire; so that justice, peace and tranquillity may be the more conveniently preserved for the German nation, the commonwealth may be the better ordered by these means, and aids and defences may be furnished by the German nation to other Christian powers against the common enemy, the Turk. Otherwise, and without this, such things can by no means be hoped for.

units.la: 11. Item cum beatitudo Pontificis inter alia desideret informari, quibus mediis huic Lutherano errori commodius obviari possit, ut ea, quae per suam Beatitudinem providenda fuerint, celeriter curari possint: Ad haec Illustriss. Princeps Dominus Locumtenens, aliisque Principes & Ordines decunt, quicquid hac in re pro pietate & Christianae religionis devotione utilitatis & auxilii praestare poterint, sunt, eruntque semper ex animo paratissimi. Ex quo autem hoc saeculum in omni statu, tam Ecclesiastico, quam saeculari, corruptissimos habeat mores, sintque non tantum ex parte Lutherana secta, sed ex aliis causis multi errores, abusus & corruptelae, quae ita inoleverunt, ut istis opportunis remediis providen summopere necessarium sit, ob id simulque propter immensam tyrannidem crudelissimi Turcae, qua multis jam annis Christianitati multa incommoda & calamitates varias inferre, hodieque majora inferre molitur. Nullum itaque commodius, efficacius & opportunius remedium Illustriss. Dominus Princeps Locumtenens, caeterique Principes & Ordines cogitare possunt, quod beatitudo Pontificis, accedente ad haec sacrae Caesareae Majestatis consensu, liberum Christianum Concilium ad locum convenientem in natione Germanica, quanto ocyus & celerius, quod fieri possit, videlicet vel in Argentoratum, vel Moguntiam, Coloniam Agrippinam, vel ad civitatem Merenscem, vel alium convenientem locum in Germania indiceret: nec ultra unius anni spatium (quod possibile foret) haec Concilii convocatio & designatio differretur: & quod in tali concilio eis qui interesse deberent, Ecclesiastici, vel laicalis ordinis, non obstantibus quibuscunque juramentis & obligationibus, liberè liceret loqui & consulere pro gloria summi Dei, & salute animarum, pro republica Christiana, absque aliquo impedimento: quinimò quilibet ad haec debeat esse obnoxius, ut non dulcia, sed vera & meliora consulat, summa cura & diligentia per salutem animae suae, & absque aliqua adulatione doli vel fraudis suspicione.
units.tr: 11. Likewise, since His Holiness the Pope, among other things, desires to be informed by what means this Lutheran error may more conveniently be met, so that those things which are to be provided by His Holiness may be quickly set in order: To this the Most Illustrious Lord Locum tenens and the other Princes and Orders say that whatever help and aid they are able to give in this matter, out of piety and devotion to the Christian religion, they are, and always will be, most ready from their hearts. But since this age has most corrupt morals in every state, both ecclesiastical and secular, and there are many errors, abuses and corruptions arising not only from the Lutheran sect but from other causes, which have so taken root that it is most necessary to provide suitable remedies for them; and likewise on account of the immense tyranny of the most cruel Turk, by which he has for many years already inflicted many troubles and various calamities on Christendom, and even today is striving to inflict greater ones. Therefore the Most Illustrious Lord Locum tenens and the other Princes and Orders can think of no more convenient, effective and opportune remedy than this: that His Holiness, with the consent of the Sacred Caesarean Majesty added to this, should appoint, as quickly and speedily as possible, a free Christian Council in a convenient place in the German nation, namely either at Strasbourg, or Mainz, Cologne, or the city of Merseburg, or another suitable place in Germany; and that this convocation and designation of the Council should not be deferred beyond the space of one year (which would be possible); and that in such a council those who ought to take part, whether of the ecclesiastical or lay order, notwithstanding any oaths and obligations whatsoever, should be freely permitted to speak and advise, without any hindrance, for the glory of almighty God, the salvation of souls, and the Christian commonwealth; nay rather, each one ought to be bound to this, to give advice not pleasing but true and better, with the greatest care and diligence for the salvation of his own soul, and without any suspicion of flattery, deceit or fraud.

units.la: 12. Verùm quibus modis & rationibus interim, & medio tempore isti tumultus & populi errores poterint pacari, interteneri, & compesci, maxima cura & diligentia Illustriss. & Serenissimus Dominus Locumtenens, & alii Principes consuluerunt, cùm non minima pars istius negotii ex hac medii temporis intercapedine pendeat.
units.tr: 12. But by what means and reasons, in the meantime and during this interval, these tumults and the errors of the people can be calmed, restrained, and checked, the most illustrious and most serene Lord Lieutenant and the other Princes have considered with the greatest care and diligence, since not the least part of this business depends on this interval of time.

units.la: 13. Itaque deliberaverunt in primis, ex quo Lutherus, & aliqui illius sectatores in ditione ac territorio Illustrissimi ducis FRIDERICI, Saxoniae Principis Electoris, &c. agant: Ob id Illustriss. Princeps Locumtenens, & alii Ordines Imperii, apud praedictum Principem Saxoniae summa diligentia curare volunt, & per eundem Principem efficere sperant, ne Lutherus & sui sectatores aliquid amplius scribat, edat, & typis excudi faciat: indubieque sibi persuadent, quod praedictus Illustrissimus Princeps Saxoniae, pro sua in religionem Christianam pietate, & in sacrum Romanum Imperium observantia & obedientia, ut virtute praeditum decet Principem Electorem, omnem operam in hac re sit adhibiturus.
units.tr: 13. Accordingly, they have first deliberated on how Luther and some of his followers, in the dominion and territory of the most illustrious Duke Frederick, Elector Prince of Saxony, etc., are to be dealt with. For this reason the most illustrious Lord Lieutenant and the other Estates of the Empire wish to take the greatest care with the aforesaid Prince of Saxony, and they hope to bring it about through the same Prince that Luther and his followers write, publish, and have printed nothing further. They are fully persuaded that the aforesaid most illustrious Prince of Saxony, out of his piety toward the Christian religion and his observance and obedience toward the Holy Roman Empire, as befits a prince and elector endowed with virtue, will apply every effort to this matter.

units.la: 14. Curabuntque simul Illustrissimus Dominus Locumtenens, Principes, & Imperii Ordines, ut per omnem Germaniam cum divini verbi concionatoribus, sive praedicatoribus, diligenter agatur, ne in populum Christianum spargant, vel dicant ea, per quae posset popularis multitudo ad tumultum vel rebellionem moveri, aut in aliquem errorem induci; sed quod nihil praeter verum, purum, sincerum, & sanctum Evangelium, & approbatam scripturam, pie, manseurè & Christianè, juxta doctrinam & expositionem approbatae, & ab Ecclesia Christiana receptae scripturae doceant & praedicent, omniaque ab illa omittant, quae à populo doctius & sanctius ignorantur, quàm sciantur, quaeve subtilius indagare, & ad imum usque exigere, minimè expedit: nihilque in populo per concionem disputationum moveant, sed quicquid controversiae fuerit, usque ad determinationem futuri Concilii referent.
units.tr: 14. At the same time the most illustrious Lord Lieutenant, the Princes, and the Estates of the Empire will take care that throughout all Germany, with the preachers of the divine Word, or those who proclaim it, it be diligently arranged that they not scatter among the Christian people, or say, anything by which the common multitude could be moved to tumult or rebellion, or led into some error; but that they teach and proclaim nothing except the true, pure, sincere, and holy Gospel and approved Scripture, piously, gently, and in a Christian manner, according to the doctrine and exposition of approved Scripture as received by the Christian Church; and that they omit all those things which the people are better and more holily ignorant of than informed about, or which it is in no way fitting to investigate more subtly and to pursue down to the bottom. Nor should they stir up any disputations in the people through sermons; but whatever controversy there is, they shall refer it until the determination of a future Council.

units.la: 15. Ordinabunt praeterea Archiepiscopi & Episcopi, ac alii Praelati per suas dioeceses viros doctos, probos, & sacris literis peritos, qui praedicantibus fideliter & diligenter intendere debebunt, si quid ab illis vel erratum, vel minùs idoneè dictum esse offenderint, pie, manseurè, ac modeste eos corrigent, & informabunt, in hunc modum, ne quispiam suspicari possit, ut veritas Evangelica per hoc impediri quaeratur. Qui praedicatores, si tales monitores audire nollent, necá suis ineptis abstinere, debebunt per locorum Ordinarios congruis poenis coerceri & puniri.
units.tr: 15. Moreover, the archbishops and bishops and other prelates shall appoint, throughout their dioceses, learned, upright men skilled in sacred letters, who ought faithfully and diligently to attend to the preachers; if they notice that anything has been said by them in error or less fittingly, they shall correct and instruct them piously, gently, and modestly, in such a way that no one may suspect that the Evangelical truth is sought to be hindered by this. If those preachers were unwilling to hear such admonishers, and to refrain from their unfit utterances, they shall be restrained and punished by the local ordinaries with suitable penalties.

units.la: 16. Praeterea in omnibus bibliothecis, & apud typographos diligentissimè, quantum possibile erit, providebunt, ne in futurum aliquid novi typis excudatur: maximè, ne libelli famosi, neque publicè, neque secretè vendantur. Et ordinabuntur apud omnes Potestates, ut si quispiam aliquid nove edere, vendere, vel typis excudere voluerit, ut priùs per aliquos viros probos, doctos, & literarum peritos ista revideantur & recognoscantur: & nisi per eosdem admissum, improbatum fuerit, minime vendatur, excudatur, vel publicetur.
units.tr: 16. Furthermore, in all libraries and among the printers they shall take the most careful provision, as far as possible, that nothing new be printed in future; above all, that defamatory pamphlets be sold neither publicly nor secretly. And it shall be ordained among all the authorities that if anyone wishes to publish, sell, or print anything new, such things shall first be reviewed and examined by some upright, learned, and literate men; and unless they have been admitted by these men, they shall not be sold, printed, or published.

units.la: 17. Et per haec media speriant, quòd hoc tempore poterit istis tumultibus, erroribus, & offendiculis commodiùs mederi: maximè, ubi beatitudo Pontificis in istis gravaminibus congruam & detractam tam faciet reformationem, & provisionem, atque liberam & Christianam designabit Concilium. Per haec enim maxime satisfieret populari, & nunc fluctuanti multitudini. Et si hic tumultus tam illico in totum forsan per ista sedari non posset; nihil tamen dubitant, quod major pars istius per hunc modum ad tranquillitatem & pacem moveretur. Indubie enim multi probi & boni viri Christiani futurum & proxime indicendum Concilium magno desiderio essent expectaturi.
units.tr: 17. And by these means they hope that at this time these tumults, errors, and stumbling-blocks can be remedied more conveniently; especially if his Holiness will make a suitable and thorough reformation and provision for these grievances, and the Council which is to be freely and Christianly appointed will be designated. For by these means the populace, and the multitude now wavering, would be chiefly satisfied. And even if this tumult could perhaps not at once be wholly calmed by these measures, they nevertheless doubt not that the greater part of it would be moved to tranquillity and peace in this way. For indeed many upright and good Christian men will await the future Council, which is to be announced shortly, with great longing.

units.la: 18. Postremo de Presbyteris, qui matrimonium contrahunt, & de religiosis, qui relictis monasteriis, ad seculum redeunt, de quibus reverendissimus Dominus Nuncius Apostolicus, etiam inter cetera meminit, considerant Principes, & Imperii Ordines: ex quo in legibus civilibus nulla poena specialiter super his sit statuta, ob id congruum & justum ipsis visum est, ut tales per eorum Ordinarios debita poena, factis canonum constitutionibus super hoc expressa, utputa amissione Beneficiorum, & privilegiorum, & aliis condignis poenis puniantur, & coerceantur: & quod Ordinarii illi a Potestatibus secularibus in ista animadversione & punitione minime impediantur: Sed quod pro tuitione jurisdictionis Ecclesiasticae eis auxilium & favorem impendant, & super his omnibus publica mandata & edicta faciant, ne quispiam Ordinarios in punitione & coercitione talium impediat: sed quando alias illi votorum transgressores in ditione & territorio alicujus Principis vel Potestatis secularis delinquerent, quod extunc debitis & congruis poenis puniantur & coerceantur.
units.tr: 18. Finally, concerning the priests who contract marriage and the religious who, having left their monasteries, return to the world, of whom the most reverend Lord Apostolic Nuncio also made mention among other things, the Princes and Estates of the Empire have considered the matter: since no penalty specifically concerning these things has been established in the civil laws, it has therefore seemed fitting and just to them that such persons be punished and restrained by their ordinaries with the due penalty, according to the constitutions of the canons expressed on this matter, for instance by loss of benefices and privileges and other fitting penalties; and that those ordinaries not be hindered in this punishment and correction by the secular authorities, but rather that they lend them aid and favour in defending ecclesiastical jurisdiction, and issue public mandates and edicts on all these matters, so that no one hinder the ordinaries in punishing and restraining such persons. But when, on the other hand, those transgressors of vows offend within the dominion and territory of some Prince or secular authority, they shall then be punished and restrained with due and suitable penalties.

units.la: 19. Postremo super his omnibus Illustrissimus & Serenissimus Princeps Dominus Locumtenens, aliique Principes & Ordines vehementer, & ex animo iterum atque iterum orant, ut beatitudo Pontificis, simulque reverendus Dominus orator, ista omnia non aliter accipere & intelligere velint, quam a bono, pio, sincero, & Christiano animo professa, cogitata, & dicta esse. Nihil enim est, quod omnes isti Principes & ordines tam ex animo velint, atque cupiant, quam statum sanctae, Catholicae, & Romanae Ecclesiae, beatitudinisque Pontificis felicem, incolumem, & salvum; ad cujus vota, desiderata, & obedientiam, ut fideles filii, se paratissimos offerunt, atque commendant.
units.tr: 19. Finally, concerning all these matters, the most illustrious and most serene Lord Lieutenant, and the other Princes and Estates, earnestly and from the heart beg again and again that his Holiness, and likewise the reverend Lord Orator, be willing to accept and understand all these things in no other way than as having been professed, thought, and said from a good, pious, sincere, and Christian mind. For there is nothing which all these Princes and Estates desire and wish for so heartily as the happy, safe, and sound condition of the holy, Catholic, and Roman Church and of his Holiness; to whose wishes, desires, and obedience, as faithful sons, they offer and commend themselves most readily.

units.la: REPLICATIO.
units.tr: REPLY.

units.la: Serenissime Caesarea M. Locumtenens, Reverendissimi Patres, Illustrissimi Principes, & totius sacri Caesarei senatus Ordines amplissimi, cum pridie mihi longo tempore expectanti, datum fuerit tandem a vobis responsum, in re Lutherana; volui illustrissimis dominationibus vestris non solum verbo, sed & literis indicare, quam parum mihi illud satisfaciat, & per subsequens Pontifici maximo, ac universae Christianitati sit minus satisfacturum. Et omisiu multis, quae de pietate, fide, & observantia vestra erga sanctissimum Dominum nostrum & sanctam sedem Apostolicam in proemio vestri responsi habentur, de quibus tamen nomine sua Sanctitatis vestris illustrissimis dominationibus gratias ago, veniam tandem ad ea, quae suppletione, correctione & declaratione indigere videntur: reliqua prout stant, quatenus placeant sanctissimo Domino nostro acceptanda.
units.tr: Most Serene Imperial Lieutenant, Most Reverend Fathers, Most Illustrious Princes, and most distinguished orders of the whole sacred Imperial Senate: since the day before yesterday, when I had waited a long time, you at last gave me your response concerning the Lutheran affair. I wished to make known to your illustrious lordships, not only by word but also in writing, how little it satisfies me, and how much less it will satisfy the Supreme Pontiff and the whole Christian world. Passing over the many things said in the preface of your response about your piety, faith and observance toward our most holy Lord and the Holy Apostolic See, for which indeed in the name of His Holiness I thank your illustrious lordships, I come at last to those points which seem to need supplement, correction and clarification. The rest, as they stand, are to be accepted by our most holy Lord, insofar as they please him.

units.la: Et primo, quantum pertinet ad id, quod illustrissima dominatione vestra dicunt, & se excusando asserunt, quod attento, quod populus Germaniae sit persuasum, quod ipsis multa gravamina a Curia Romana sint illata, & ab ipsa multa scandala & incommoda indies patiantur, non fuisse visum, sibi expedire, ut sententia Apostolica sedis, & Imperiale decretum, debita executioni mandetur, ne inde contingat, pejora & acerbiora mala provenire. Ad hoc replicatur, quod nec sanctissimus Dominus noster, nec Caesarea Majestas, nec ullus Christianorum Principum expectavit unquam tale a vobis responsum in hac re dari. Nam si Lutherus ante sententiam Apostolicam, tot clarissimorum virorum, ac Universitatum judiciis fundatam, & denique ante Caesarem decretum ipsiusque edictum erraverat in uno; post eandem sententiam & decretum erravit in longe pluribus, & nihil reliquum fecit, quo minus tota orthodoxa religio a fundamentis everta fit. Quapropter cum poenae debeant de jure commensurari delicto, attento, quod indies magis cum suis sequacibus erravit, & errat, ut notorium; debent poenae ipsae augeri, atque gravari, & non diminui, prout ex praesenti vestro decreto fit. Et quantum ad responsum ipsum, ex eo in primis offenditur divina majestas, cujus causa tam seniter curanda proponatur. Offenditur Pontificis & Apostolicae sedis dignitas: offenditur postremo Imperialis culminis celsitudo, quorum decreta & ordinationes tam impune suspenduntur, abrogantur, deprimunturque: offenditur & pariter communis honor vester, cum omnes unanimes interfuerint eidem Imperiali decreto decernendo, & vestram auctoritatem praestando. Nec satisfacit illa ratio, quod propter scandala evitanda, dicta Apostolica sententia, & imperiale edictum, exequi non debeant. Nam non sunt toleranda mala, ut proveniant bona: & magis sunt curanda ea, quae pertinent ad animae, quam ad corporis salutem. Neque videntur excusandi, qui Lutherum sectari velint, quod propter sibi inflicta scandala & gravamina a Curia Romana (etiamsi verum illud esset) deberent ab unitate Catholica fidei propterea resilire, & in profundum malorum se praecipitare. Nam omnia potius mala deberent aequo animo & patienter sustinere, quam se & animam suam, cum animae periculo in praecipitium dare. Et si illud in omni tempore praestare debuissent, quanto magis deberent respicere, cum intelligant, Deum optimum maximumque dedisse Ecclesiae suae sanctae pastorem optimum: pastorem (inquam) sanctissimum, eundemque Germanum, qui non solum universam Ecclesiam sit curaturus & instauraturus, sed etiam Germaniam suam ad pristinam pietatem restituturus, ac pluribus & insignibus donis, in his quae honeste poterit, illustratus. Quare Principes illustrissimi & excellentissimi, vos tanto affectibus rogo, & vehementer obtestor, ut his rationibus veris simis adducti, velitis, antequam hujusmodi celeberrimus vester conventus dissolvatur, omnino statuere, & firmiter deliberare, quod eadem Apostolica sententia, ac Imperiale edictum exequatur, & executioni mandetur, fine aliqua diminutione: cum ex hac magna parte, quinimo tota Germania salus dependeat. Et si in aliquibus Germani populi, ut asseritur, sunt a Curia Romana gravati, illud declarent. Nam semper Apostolica sedes, quae est mater pusillorum omnium oppressorum, parata erit, illos subleware, & pro viribus juvare, & tueri.
units.tr: And first, as to what your illustrious lordships say, excusing yourselves and asserting that, since the people of Germany are persuaded that they have suffered many grievances from the Roman Curia, and daily endure many scandals and inconveniences from it, it did not seem expedient to you that the sentence of the Apostolic See and the Imperial decree be carried out, lest worse and more bitter evils follow. To this I reply: neither our most holy Lord, nor His Imperial Majesty, nor any Christian prince ever expected such a response from you in this matter. For if Luther had gone astray in one point before the apostolic sentence, founded on the judgments of so many distinguished men and universities, and finally before the Emperor's decree and edict, then after that sentence and decree he has gone astray in far more points, and has left nothing undone that might prevent the whole orthodox religion from being overthrown from its foundations. Therefore, since punishments ought by right to be proportioned to the offence, and since, as is notorious, he has erred and errs more and more daily along with his followers, the punishments themselves ought to be increased and made heavier, not diminished, as your present decree does. As to the response itself, the divine majesty is offended by it, for whose cause such a matter is proposed to be treated so lightly. The dignity of the Pontiff and of the Apostolic See is offended; lastly, the majesty of the Imperial crown is offended, whose decrees and ordinances are so easily suspended, abrogated and set aside. Your common honour too is offended, since all of you unanimously took part in enacting that Imperial decree and lent it your authority. Nor does that reason satisfy, that the Apostolic sentence and the Imperial edict ought not to be executed in order to avoid scandals. For evils must not be tolerated so that good may come of them, and those things which concern the health of the soul ought to be more carefully attended to than those which concern the health of the body. Nor do those seem to deserve excuse who wish to follow Luther, on the ground that, because of the scandals and grievances inflicted on them by the Roman Curia (even if that were true), they ought on that account to leap away from the Catholic unity of the faith and hurl themselves into the abyss of evils. Rather, they ought to bear all evils with an equal mind and with patience than to cast themselves and their souls headlong into ruin, at the peril of their souls. And if they ought to have done this at every time, how much more ought they to have considered, since they know that God, the best and greatest, has given to his holy Church a good shepherd: a most holy shepherd, I say, and one who is also a German, who will not only care for and restore the whole Church, but will also restore his Germany to its former piety, and is distinguished by many outstanding gifts, in those matters which he can honourably undertake. Therefore, most illustrious and most excellent Princes, I urge you with all earnestness and vehemently entreat you, that, moved by these most true reasons, you will be pleased, before this most celebrated assembly of yours is dissolved, to resolve firmly and deliberate carefully that this same Apostolic sentence and Imperial edict be carried out and put into execution without any diminution, since the salvation of this great part, indeed of the whole of Germany, depends on it. And if, as is alleged, some of the German people are burdened by the Roman Curia, let them declare it. For the Apostolic See, which is the mother of all the little and oppressed, will always be ready to raise them up, and to help and protect them as far as it can.

units.la: Quo ad seditiones & discordias, quae sunt inter Ecclesiasticos, & seculares Principes Germaniae, pacandas, ac ad articulos & eandem modum andos: respondetur, quod sanctissimus D.N. ubi eas seditiones, discordias intellexerit, pro officio hunc vestrum sua incumbentis, curabit, ut omnino componantur, & extinguantur: cum non minus habeat in filios suos & Ecclesia temporales Principes, ac habeat eosdem Ecclesiasticos. Pariformiter moderabitur omnia inter eos, ut unusquisque habeat quod suum est, & neutri injurietur.
units.tr: As to the seditions and discords which exist between the ecclesiastical and secular princes of Germany, which are to be pacified, and as to the articles and the manner of doing so: the response is that our most holy Lord, when he has learned of those seditions and discords, will, in accordance with the duty incumbent on him, take care that they are altogether composed and extinguished, since he has no less care for his temporal princes, sons of the Church, than for its ecclesiastical ones. In the same way he will moderate all matters between them, so that each has what is his own, and neither is wronged.

units.la: Quo ad Annatas non persolvendas Romae, sed in Germania retinendas, pro sustentatione Imperialis gubernationis data declaratione, quae facta est verbo difficultate, quae fieri possit ad eam concedendam: reservatur responsio ad tempus, quo dabitur, vel Imperiali regimini, vel futuro Principum conventui, prout magis expedire suae Sanctitati videbitur.
units.tr: As to the annates not being paid to Rome but being retained in Germany for the support of the Imperial government: the declaration given in words, concerning what difficulty could be made in granting it, is reserved; the response will be given at a time when it is given, either to the Imperial government or to a future assembly of the Princes, as His Holiness shall think more expedient.

units.la: Quo ad Consilium, quod datur per illustrissimas dominationes vestras, quod attentu legitimus causis, quae sunt, sanctissimus Dominus noster debeat convocare oecumenicum generale Concilium: replicatur, quod illud non debere displicere suae Sanctitati, ob omnes praecipue illas causas: tamen petitur, ut illud Concilium alio vero idoneo reformetur: & quod tollantur ea, quae possent aliquam umbram facere suae Sanctitati, prout est, quod debeat convocare Concilium de consensu Caesarea Majestatis, quod sit liberum, & quod relaxentur juramenta quod ponatur magis in una civitate, quam in alia, & similia, &c. Quia nisi tollerentur ista, videretur sanctitati gari manus per illustrissimas D. vestras, prout in voce declaratum est.
units.tr: As to the counsel which your illustrious lordships give, that, since the lawful causes that exist, our most holy Lord ought to convene an ecumenical general Council: it is replied that this should not displease His Holiness, on account of all those causes especially; yet it is requested that this Council be reformed in another true and suitable way, and that those things be removed which could cast some shadow upon His Holiness, such as that he should convene the Council with the consent of His Imperial Majesty, that it be free, that the oaths be relaxed, that it be held more in one city than in another, and similar matters, etc. For unless these things were removed, His Holiness would seem to have his hands bound by your illustrious lordships, as has been declared in speech.

units.la: Quo ad praedicatores, qui imposterum fidelibus habebunt praedicare verbum Dei: replicatur, quod servari illud, quod sanctissimus Dominus noster nuper pie, & sancte statuit, & ordinavit, de venerabilium fratrum suorum filio & assensu. Quod est, ut stante ista perniciosa secta in Germania, nullus deinceps possit praedicare verbum Dei per tatem vel dioecesim alicujus; nisi ille talis prius fuerit examinatus per Episcopum, vel Officialem suum de doctrina & sufficientia sua, & eadem fuerit ab eo approbata, vel pro pia & Christiana reputata. Et pariformiter, nisi ille ad munus praedicandi, per eundem Episcopum, vel suum Officialem institutus: qui habeat etiam illum amovere & castigare, quando a recta via cecideritIn caeteris placet, quantum de dictis praedicatoribus per illustrissimas D.V. respondere est, quod praedicent Evangelium cum interpretatione scriptura, quae fit per Ecclesiam approbata.
units.tr: As to the preachers who henceforth are to preach the Word of God to the faithful: it is replied that what our most holy Lord recently and piously and holily decreed and ordained, with the advice and assent of his venerable brothers, should be observed. This is, that while this pernicious sect remains in Germany, no one may henceforth preach the Word of God in any city or diocese unless he has first been examined by the Bishop, or his Official, on his doctrine and sufficiency, and has been approved by him or judged pious and Christian. Likewise, unless he has been appointed to the office of preaching by the same Bishop or his Official, who shall also have the power to remove and rebuke him when he has fallen from the right way. As to other matters, insofar as it is to be answered concerning the said preachers by your illustrious lordships, it is pleasing that they preach the Gospel with an interpretation of Scripture that is approved by the Church.

units.la: Quo ad impressores & venditores, seu alios divulgatores Lutheranorum librorum, & aliorum, qui sectam suam fustiuent & fovent; replicatur, quod nullo pacto placet data responsio, quod curabunt illustrissimae dominationes providere, quantum possibile erit, ne tales libri imprimantur, vel vendantur, &c. Sed dico in hoc, prout in aliis, debere exequi sedis Apostolica & Imperialis celsitudinis sententiam: id est, quod libri impresi & imprimendi tur: imprimentes vero & vendentes, seu aliás invulgantes dictos libros, juxta easdem sententias puniantur. Et maxime peto, debere adverti: nam in hoc stat tota vis, pro ista perniciosa secta comprimenda. ne tales libri amplius imprimantur. Nam ex illorum lectione omnia haec mala profecta sunt. Et quantum pertinet ad id, quod nullus possit imprimere libros novos imprimere, nisi illi tales libri prius videantur & examinentur per aliquem virum doctum. dico, in hoc non debere recedi a constitutione moderni Concilii Lateranensi, quae jam est in usu: & est, ut nullus, sub poena in ea contenta, possit aliquos libros imprimere, nisi per ordinarium Episcopum loci vel ejus officialem tales libri lecti & examinati, ac pro Christianis reputati & habiti sint.
units.tr: As to the printers and sellers, or other distributors, of the Lutheran books and of others which support and foster their sect: it is objected that the response given, namely that your illustrious lordships will take care to provide, as far as possible, that such books are not printed or sold, etc., pleases in no way. But I say that in this, as in other matters, the sentence of the Apostolic See and of the Imperial majesty must be carried out: that is, that the books that have been printed and are to be printed are to be suppressed, and that the printers and sellers, or otherwise those who spread the said books, are to be punished according to the same sentences. And I especially ask that this be noted, for in this lies the whole force for restraining this pernicious sect, namely that such books be printed no more, since all these evils have proceeded from reading them. And as to what is said, that no one may print new books unless such books have first been reviewed and examined by some learned man, I say that in this one ought not to depart from the constitution of the recent Lateran Council, which is now in use, namely that no one, under the penalty contained in it, may print any books unless such books have been read and examined by the ordinary Bishop of the place or his official, and been judged and held to be Christian.

units.la: Quo ad Clericos, qui uxorem ducunt: replicatur, quod illa quae pro responsione scripta sunt, non displicere videntur, quando in causa aculeum non habeant. Propter quod petuntur illa verba declarari, quae sunt in fine capituli dicitur sponsi sub eisdem verbis: Sed quando aliás illi votorum transgressores in ditione & territorio alicujus Principis, vel potestatis secularis delinquerent, quod ex tunc debitis & congruis poenis puniantur, & coerceantur, &c. Dico, quod sint talia verba intelligi debent secundum praedicta, id est, quod tales puniantur a suis judicibus Ecclesiasticis, bene stant: si firmentur, quod seculares Principes vel potentes illos punire debeant: in hoc dico, & instantissime peto tale responsum, utpote, contra libertatem & jus Ecclesiae, omnino corrigi debere, & reduci ad verum sensum. Nam si Principes seculares audierent tales judicare, & in eos jurisdictionem exercere, esset ponere falcem in messem alienam & tangere eos, qui sunt peculiariter Christo reservati. nec ob transgressionem voti, seu ob apostasiam praesumant credere Principes, tales ad iuam potestatem, vel jurisdictionem devolutos esse, si delinquent in suis dominiis, vel territoriis: cum propter talem transgressionem, vel abusum ordinis sui, non desinant propterea esse de jurisdictione Ecclesiae. Quia cum remaneant illa character & ordo, semper sunt in ejusdem Ecclesiae potestate. Unde in tali casu, quod in dominiis Principum delinquant, ipsi Principes denuncient illos suis Episcopis, vel aliis superioribus, qui eos castigent, corrigant: & si opus fuerit, pro viribus suis dictos Episcopos seu superiores brachio suo juvent, & aliis praesto sint.
units.tr: As to the clergy who take wives: the reply says that what was written in response does not seem objectionable, provided it does not have a sting in the matter. For that reason it is asked that those words be explained which are at the end of the chapter, beginning "sponsi," under the same wording: "But if otherwise those transgressors of vows should offend within the dominion and territory of some prince or secular power, let them be punished and restrained by fitting and appropriate penalties, etc." I say that these words ought to be understood according to what has been said above, that is, that such persons are to be punished by their ecclesiastical judges; this stands well. But if it is affirmed that secular princes or powers ought to punish them, then I say, and most earnestly ask, that such a reply must be wholly corrected and brought back to its true sense, since it is contrary to the liberty and right of the Church. For if secular princes were to hear such cases and exercise jurisdiction over them, it would be to put the sickle into another's harvest and to touch those who are reserved peculiarly to Christ. Nor should princes presume to believe that such persons, if they offend in their dominions or territories, have passed to their power or jurisdiction because of a transgression of vow or apostasy; for on account of such a transgression, or abuse of their order, they do not on that account cease to be under the jurisdiction of the Church. For since that character and order remain, they are always in the power of the same Church. Therefore in such a case, when they offend in the dominions of princes, let the princes themselves report them to their bishops or other superiors, who are to chastise and correct them; and if need be, let them with their strength support the said bishops or superiors with their arm, and stand ready to assist.

units.la: Super quibus omnibus & singulis petitur per me nuncium Apostolicum, habita matura deliberatione, ab illustrissimis dominationibus vestris, melius, clarius, sanius, & consultius responderi.
units.tr: Concerning all of these matters, and each one of them, I, the apostolic messenger, ask that your most illustrious lordships, after mature deliberation, reply better, more clearly, more soundly, and more advisedly.

units.la: DUPLICATIO ILLUSTRISSIMORUM ET REVE- RENDISSIMORUM Principum, &c.
units.tr: DUPLICATIO OF THE MOST ILLUSTRIOUS AND MOST REVEREND Princes, etc.

units.la: QUamvis Principes, & reliqui ordines Germanicae nationis, iterum pro verbis verba dixerunt: quum tamen aliis magis necessariis occupati essent negotiis, Pontificium oratorem pro responsione contentu esse jusserunt; donec gravamina nationis Germanicae summo Pontifici manifesta forent, acinde manifestum fieret, num verba ejus tam blanda, facta etiam debita sequutura essent.
units.tr: Although the Princes and the other estates of the German nation had again answered word for word, yet, since they were occupied with other and more pressing business, they ordered the Papal orator to remain content with this reply, until the grievances of the German nation should be made plain to the supreme Pontiff, and it should then become clear whether his very flattering words would be followed by deeds that were owed.

units.la: SACRI ROMANI IMPERII PRINCIPUM AC PRO- CERUM gravamina centum, quae adversus Sedem Romanam, ac totum Ecclesiasticum ordi- nem, Oratori Pontificiae Sanctitatis, in Comitiis Germanorum Principum Norembergae, Anno &c. XXII. proposuerunt.
units.tr: ONE HUNDRED GRIEVANCES OF THE PRINCES AND NOBLES OF THE HOLY ROMAN EMPIRE, which they presented against the See of Rome and the whole ecclesiastical order to the Orator of His Papal Holiness, at the Diet of the German Princes at Nuremberg, in the year 1522.

units.la: POSTQUAM relatio per Oratorem Sanctitatis Pontificiae Comitiis praedictis, coram Majestatis Caesareae Locum tenente, Electoribus caeterisque Principibus, ac Imperii Statibus, ibidem congregatis, habita, a Breve, quod vocant, Apostolicum, ejusdem Romani Pontificis, consultationem forent deducta, desuperque responsio consulta & conclusa, ac eidem Oratori & Legato Pontificio, inscriptis, nomine totius Romani Imperii tradita, factaque esset, forte inter alia, mentio non infrequens, gravaminum atque onerum Romani Imperii Procerum, quibus iniquius, quàm par sit, ab Romanæ Ecclesiæ Clero premerentur: placuit Principibus, ac cæteris Imperii ordinibus, hæc ipsa, quæ contra Ecclesiæ Romanæ Primores, se in medium adducturos polliciti erant, gravamina, paulo altius à Principibus, sigillatim per classes, & quàm potuit maximum per ordinem digesta, repetere, recenseréque, ac ita descripta fusius Legato Romano, ferenda secum trans Alpes, dare, rogareque hunc, ut apud Sedem Apostolicam curare velit, quatenus onera hæc, non ferenda Germanis, e medio tollere, emendaréque Sanctitas sua non dedignetur. Quemadmodum prædicta hæc in responsione supra memorata, omnia latius continentur. Itaque per compendium, ut sequitur, Germanicæ nationis onera hæc iusto graviora, digesta, ac oratori Pontificio, qui se nomine Sanctissimi Rom. Præsulis, ita syncerè ac Christianè obtulerat, tradita sunt; quo sæpe dictus orator ac Legatus Pontificius. hæcinde Sanctitati legantis referre, ac apud eundem pro Germanis Principibus & Proceribus, totius Imperii Romani ordinibus, interpellare possit. Sunt autem gravamina supra memorata, quæ per capita nunc sequuntur.
units.tr: After the report had been delivered by the Orator of the Papal Holiness to the aforesaid Diet, in the presence of the Locum tenens of His Caesarean Majesty, the Electors and the other Princes and estates of the Empire gathered there, and after the Apostolic Brief, as they call it, of the same Roman Pontiff had been brought into discussion, and a reply had been considered and concluded upon and delivered in writing to the same Orator and Papal Legate in the name of the whole Roman Empire, it happened that, among other matters, there was frequent mention of the grievances and burdens of the nobles of the Roman Empire, by which they were oppressed more unjustly than is fitting by the clergy of the Roman Church. The Princes and the other orders of the Empire resolved to take up again, somewhat more fully, these very grievances which they had promised to bring forward against the chief men of the Roman Church, arranging them one by one by classes and in as good an order as possible, and, so described, to give them more fully to the Roman Legate to carry with him across the Alps, and to ask him to see to it, with the See Apostolic, that His Holiness would not disdain to remove and amend these burdens, which the Germans cannot bear.
