units.la: DE INSIGNIBVS SIVE ARMIS GENTILITIIS.
units.tr: CONCERNING INSIGNIA, OR COATS OF ARMS

units.la: CAROLUS Quintus divina favente clementia Romanorum Imperator Augustus; & Rex Germaniæ, Hispaniarum, utriusque Siciliæ, Hierusalem, Hungariæ, Dalmatiæ, Croatiæ, Insularum Balearium, Sardiniæ, Fortunatarum & Indiarum, ac Terræ firmæ, Maris Oceani, &c. Archidux Austriæ, Dux Burgundiæ, Lothrici, Brabantiæ, Limburgiæ, Lucenburgiæ, Geldriæ, Wirtenbergæ, &c. Comes Habspurgi, Flandriæ, Tyrolis, Arthesiæ, & Burgundiæ; Palatinus Hanoniæ, Hollandiæ, Zelandiæ, Ferreti, Kiburgi, Namurci, & Zutphaniæ; Lantgravius Alsatiæ; Marchio Burgoviæ, & Sacri Romani Imperii, &c. Princeps Sueviæ, &c. Dominus Frisiæ, Molinæ, Salinarum, Tripolis, & Mechliniæ, &c. Nostro & Imperii Sacri fideli dilecto N.N. gratiam nostram Cæsaream & omne bonum.
units.tr: CHARLES the Fifth, by the favour of divine clemency Emperor of the Romans, Augustus, and King of Germany, Spain, both Sicilies, Jerusalem, Hungary, Dalmatia, Croatia, the Balearic Islands, Sardinia, the Fortunate Isles and the Indies, and of the mainland, the Ocean Sea, etc.; Archduke of Austria, Duke of Burgundy, Lorraine, Brabant, Limburg, Luxemburg, Guelders, Württemberg, etc.; Count of Habsburg, Flanders, Tyrol, Artois and Burgundy; Count Palatine of Hainault, Holland, Zeeland, Ferrette, Kyburg, Namur and Zutphen; Landgrave of Alsace; Margrave of Burgau, and of the Holy Roman Empire, etc.; Prince of Swabia, etc.; Lord of Friesland, Molin, Salins, Tripoli and Mechlin, etc. To our and the Holy Empire's faithful and beloved N.N., our Caesarean grace and every good.

units.la: 1. Etsi omnibus & singulis Sacri Romani Imperii subditis & fidelibus ad gratiam propensi sumus, eosque meritis honoribus & ornamentis honestare consuevimus, Cæsarei tamen est officii, & animi nostri, eos cæteris præferre, qui non solùm fide & observantia erga nos & Sacrum Romanum Imperium, verùm etiam animi moribus clari, & eximiis virtutibus præstantes habiti sunt.
units.tr: 1. Although we are inclined to grace toward all and each of the subjects and faithful of the Holy Roman Empire, and are accustomed to honour them with deserved dignities and distinctions, it is nonetheless the duty and the purpose of our Caesarean office to prefer above the rest those who are regarded as outstanding not only in loyalty and obedience toward us and the Holy Roman Empire, but also in the distinction of their character and in their singular virtues.

units.la: 2. Quapropter attendentes in primis egregias animi tui dotes, probatos mores, industriamque & vigilantiam, quam optimorum authorum monumentis in gratiam studiosorum ædendis publico bono impendis. Præterea tuam erga nos & Sacrum Imperium fidem & obsequium, quæ nobis hactenus, præsertim in rebus hanc expeditionem nostram in Galliam concernentibus, tuis labore & industria curandis præstitisti, & etiamnum præstas, haud abs re nostra Cæsarea liberalitate & clementia dignum judicamus, te peculiari ornamento cohonestare, atque una filios & successores tuos, quò & ipsi nostræ ergà te beneficentiæ participes efficiantur, hujusmodi pariter Cæsareæ gratiæ tecum reddere consortes.
units.tr: 2. Wherefore, considering above all your outstanding gifts of mind, your approved character, and the diligence and vigilance which you devote to the public good in publishing the works of the best authors for the benefit of students; and also your loyalty and obedience toward us and the Holy Empire, which you have hitherto shown, especially in matters concerning this our expedition into France, which you have managed with labour and diligence, and which you still show, we judge it fitting, out of our Caesarean liberality and clemency, to honour you with a particular distinction, and at the same time to make your sons and successors, so that they too may share in our beneficence toward you, partakers with you in this same Caesarean grace.

units.la: 3. Motu itaque proprio, ex certa scientia, animoq; deliberato, tibi præfato N.N. hæc infrà scripta armorum insignia, videlicet scutum azurei seu cœlestini coloris, in cujus medio gallus nigri coloris, extensis alis, exerta lingua, corona aurea coronatus conspicitur. Et supra scutum galeam communem sive clausam, azurei sive cœlestini, & aurei seu crocei, argenteique sive albi colorum redimitam laciniis, in cujus cono è fascia tortili azurei sive cœlestini, & albi seu argentei colorum, galli caput coronatum, ut in scuto, eminet; quemadmodum hîc omnia in medio præsentium accuratius depicta sunt, de novo dedimus, concessimus, & clargiti sumus, prout tenore præsentium damus, concedimus & clargimur, volentes & decernentes, quòd tt præfate N. ac filii, hæredes & descendentes tui legitimè nati & nasciturî, eorundemque hæredes & successores in infinitum utriusque sexus, ex thoro legitimo seriatim descendentes, prædicta arma & insignia habeatis & deferatis, illisque in omnibus & singulis honestis decentibusque actibus & expeditionibus, tam serio quàm joco, cæterorum armigerorum more, in torneamentis, hastiludiis, bellis, duellis, singulari certamine, & quibuscunq; pugnis, vexillis, tentoriis, annulis, signis, sigillis, signetis, aulæis, tapetis, peristromatibus, monumentis, ædificiis, picturis, sculpturis, sepulchris, clenodiis, & universa supellectili vestra, aliisque in rebus omnibus pro libitu, arbitrio vestro uti frui possitis & debeatis.
units.tr: 3. Therefore, of our own motion, from certain knowledge and deliberate intent, we have newly given, granted and bestowed upon you, the aforesaid N.N., the following coats of arms: namely, a shield of azure or sky-blue colour, in the middle of which a cock of black colour is seen, with spread wings, tongue protruding, and crowned with a golden crown. And above the shield a common or closed helmet, bordered with mantling of azure or sky-blue, and of gold or saffron, and of silver or white, on whose crest, made of a twisted band of azure or sky-blue and of white or silver, rises the crowned head of a cock, as on the shield; just as all these things are depicted more precisely here in the middle of these presents. By the tenor of these presents we give, grant and bestow them, willing and decreeing that you, the aforesaid N., and your sons, heirs and descendants, lawfully born and to be born, and likewise your heirs and successors in perpetuity of either sex, descending in order from lawful marriage, shall have and bear the aforesaid arms and insignia, and may and ought to use and enjoy them in all and each honourable and becoming acts and undertakings, both serious and in jest, after the manner of other armigers, in tournaments, jousts, wars, duels, single combats and all kinds of fights, on banners, tents, rings, seals, signets, hangings, carpets, cloths of state, monuments, buildings, paintings, sculptures, tombs, jewels and all your household furnishings, and in all other matters at your pleasure and discretion.

units.la: 4. Apriqué sitis & idonei ad ineundas & recipiendas omnes exemptiones, libertates, privilegia, feuda, vacationes à muneribus & oneribus quibuscunque realibus, personalibus, sive mixtis: jura quoque & consuetudines, quibus cæteri ejusmodi armorum ornamentis insigniti gaudent, utuntur & fruuntur, absque alicujus contradictione & impedimento.
units.tr: 4. You shall be fit and entitled to enter upon and receive all exemptions, liberties, privileges, fiefs, release from any public or private burdens and charges, whether real, personal or mixed; and likewise the rights and customs which the others so adorned with such coats of arms enjoy, use and profit by, without any opposition or hindrance from anyone.

units.la: 5. Quapropter mandamus universis & singulis Principibus, tam Ecclesiasticis quàm Secularibus, Ducibus, Marchionibus, Comitibus, Baronibus, Nobilibus, Militibus, Clientibus, Capitaneis, Præfectis, Procuratoribus, Advocatis, Officialibus, Quæstoribus, Civium Magistris, Judicibus, Consulibus, Armorum regibus, Heroldis, Caduceatoribus, Civibus, Communitatibus, & denique omnibus nostris & Imperii Sacri subditis, & fidelibus dilectis, cujuscunque status, gradus, ordinis vel dignitatis fuerint, ut te præfatum N.N. filiosque, hæredes & descendentes tuos antedictos, in perpetuum in hujusmodi armorum fruitione, nec turbent nec impediant, verùm illis liberè & absque ullo impedimento & contradictione uti frui, & in iis permanere sinant & permittant: quatenus gratiam nostram charam habeant, ac præter nostram & Imperii sacri indignationem gravißimam, pœnam viginti marcharum auri puri cupiant evitare; quarum medietatē sisco ærario nostro Imperiali, reliquam vero partem injuriam passi aut passorum usibus, toties quoties contrafactum fuerit, irremissibiliter decernimus applicandam.
units.tr: 5. Wherefore we command all and each of the princes, whether ecclesiastical or secular, dukes, marquises, counts, barons, nobles, knights, vassals, captains, prefects, procurators, advocates, officials, quaestors, masters of citizens, judges, consuls, kings of arms, heralds, caduceators, citizens, communities, and finally all our and the Holy Empire's subjects and beloved faithful, of whatever estate, rank, order or dignity they may be, that they neither disturb nor hinder you, the aforesaid N.N., and your sons, heirs and descendants mentioned above, in the enjoyment of such arms in perpetuity; but that they allow and permit you to use and enjoy them freely and without any hindrance or opposition, and to remain in them. Let them hold our grace dear, and, on pain of our and the Holy Empire's most grave displeasure, let them wish to avoid a penalty of twenty marks of pure gold; half of which we decree shall be irrevocably applied to our imperial treasury, and the remaining part to the use of the party injured, as often as this shall be done contrary to this grant.

units.la: Harum testimonio literarum manu nostra subscriptarum, & sigilli nostri Cæsarei appensione munitarum. Datum in oppido nostro. N. Die quarta mensis Octobris; anno Domini millesimo quingentesimo quadragesimo primo, Imperii nostri vigesimo primo, & Regnorum nostrorum vigesimo sexto.
units.tr: In witness whereof we have given these letters, signed with our own hand and secured by the appending of our Caesarean seal. Given in our town of N., on the fourth day of October, in the year of the Lord one thousand five hundred and forty-one, in the twenty-first year of our reign, and the twenty-sixth of our kingdoms.

units.la: CAROLVS divina favente clementia Romanorum Imperator semper Augustus, rex Germaniæ, Castellæ, Legionis, Arragonum, Navarræ, Neapolis, Siciliæ, Majoricarum insularum, Indiarum, & terræ firmæ maris Oceani. Archidux Austriæ, Dux Burgundiæ, Lotharingiæ, Brabantiæ, Limburgiæ, Luxemburgiæ & Geldriæ. Comes Flandriæ, Arthefii, Burgundiæ Palatinus & Hannoniæ, Hollandiæ, Zelandiæ, Ferrettis, Hagenaldi, Namurci & Zutphaniæ. Princeps Zwveviæ. Marchio sacri Romani Imperii. Dominus Frisiæ, territorii Trajectensis citra & ultra Insulam, Mechliniæ, Salinarum & Groningæ. Et dominator in Asia & in Africa. Universis præsentes literas inspecturis, salutem.
units.tr: CHARLES, by the favour of divine clemency Emperor of the Romans, always Augustus, King of Germany, Castile, León, Aragon, Navarre, Naples, Sicily, the Balearic Islands, the Indies, and the mainland of the Ocean Sea; Archduke of Austria; Duke of Burgundy, Lorraine, Brabant, Limburg, Luxembourg and Guelders; Count of Flanders, Artois, Burgundy (Palatine), Hainault, Holland, Zeeland, Ferrette, Hainaut, Namur and Zutphen; Prince of Swabia; Margrave of the Holy Roman Empire; Lord of Friesland, of the territory of Utrecht on both sides of the Ijssel, of Mechelen, Salins and Groningen; and ruler in Asia and Africa. To all who shall see these present letters, greeting.

units.la: Cum pro nostro erga Deum Optimum Maximum, Christianamque Rempublicam officio, quieteque & tranquillitate subditorum, in nostris inferioribus regionibus consistentium extirpationi perniciosorum dogmatum, hæresium & errorum, in prætactis regionibus (proh dolor) pullulantium & grassantium, diligentissime semper invigilaverimus ac incubuerimus. Quod ut commodius faciliusque fieret, et de noxiis supplicium sumeretur, pleraque salubria ædiderimus, publicaverimusque statuta, frequenter illa innovando, ampliandoque: apposita etiam nonnunquam gravium pœnarum comminatione. Certiores attamen effecti sumus, quod prætactis remediis non proficientibus, naturæ inimico male suggerente, hæreses antedictæ, iniquaque dogmata, neque extincta aut sedata extant, imo publice & privatim magis atque magis indies gliscunt. Quod quidem evenire maxima ex parte compertum est, ob doctrinarum diversitatem, quam concionatores, & alii ad quorum officium spectat verbum domini ad populum enunciare, spargunt & effundunt. Nonnullis eorundem de literis sacris, uno modo, aliis aliter sentientibus: unde indoctu vulgus persæpe ambiguu, in certu & sæpenumero deceptum fuit. Quibus malis ut obviam eatur, & quantum in nobis est, detur opera, quod sacrosanctâ mater nostra Ecclesia (quam puram & immaculatam esse oportet) nullis diversarum traditionum maculis aspergatur, utque Christiana nostra pietas & religio, certa constansque, in publicis concionibus de cætero in dubium non revocetur, prædicatorefque determinatam habeant resolutionem, quam populo annunciare teneantur, nonnullos per Decanum aliosque sacrarum literarum professores nostræ Lovaniensis Academiæ, filiæ nostræ, articulos deligi curavimus, quibus dubia per hæreticos in controversiam disputationemque circa Orthodoxam fidem, religionemque nostram hactenus vocata, resolvuntur diluunturque, tenoris infrascripti.
units.tr: Since we have always most diligently watched over and laboured, out of our duty to God the Best and Greatest and to the Christian commonwealth, and for the quiet and tranquillity of our subjects living in our lower regions, to root out the pernicious doctrines, heresies and errors which (alas) have sprouted and spread in the aforesaid regions, we have issued and published many salutary edicts, renewing and enlarging them frequently, and sometimes attaching the threat of severe penalties, so that this might be done more conveniently and easily, and that punishment might be exacted from the guilty. Yet we have been informed that, since these remedies have not prevailed, the evil suggestions of our enemy, nature, have kept the aforesaid heresies and iniquitous doctrines alive; they have not been extinguished or quelled, but grow ever more rampant day by day, both publicly and privately. This has been found to happen for the most part because of the diversity of teachings which the preachers, and others whose office it is to proclaim the Word of the Lord to the people, scatter and pour out. Some of them hold one view about the sacred letters, others another, so that the untaught crowd is often left uncertain and very often deceived. To meet these evils, and to take such pains as lies in us, so that our holy mother the Church (which ought to be pure and spotless) may not be stained by any blemishes of differing traditions, and so that our Christian piety and religion, being sure and steadfast, may no longer be called into doubt in public sermons, and so that preachers may have a settled resolution which they are bound to announce to the people, we have taken care to have certain articles chosen through the Dean and other professors of sacred letters of our Academy of Louvain, our daughter. By these articles the doubts which heretics have hitherto raised into controversy and dispute concerning the Orthodox faith and our religion are resolved and refuted, of the tenor written below.

units.la: DECANUS ET FACULTAS THEOLOGORUM LOVANIENSIUM OMNIBUS in Christo fidelibus, Salutem.
units.tr: DEAN AND FACULTY OF THEOLOGIANS OF LOUVAIN TO ALL THE FAITHFUL IN CHRIST, GREETING.

units.la: MAgnas quotidie vires in his regionibus accipit hæreticæ pestis contagium, ac nisi occurratur, futurum prospicimus, ut hic brevi plena sint omnia, non solum Lutheranorum, Oecolampadianorum & Anabaptistarum, sed istorum etiam, qui nuper adhuc obscuris nominibus cemergere cœperūt, nec dici potest, quanto studio teneantur multi clanculū monstra ista alēdi. Quare pro officio, quod in Ecclesia Dei gerimus, verbis paucis cōplexi sumus articulos certos dogmatū, quæ propter hæreses dictas, valde expedit hoc tempore, à bonis & catholicis cōcionatoribus populo (nam populi causa operam hanc suscepimus) exponi, fideliterque & diligenter explicari. Quos quidem articulos titulos aliquando fusius, pauloque altius repetitis principiis, ampliare exponereque potuissemus, verum hoc necessarium nobis visum non est. Quinimo utilius fore credidimus, si quam simplicissime proponerentur, ad captum etiam imperitissimorum. Porro eo libentius rem hanc curavimus, quia certo intelligebamus, eandem Caesareae M. magnae curae esse, et quae ipsius egregia pietas est, ultro etiam istiusmodi quippiam expetere.
units.tr: The contagion of the heretical plague gains greater strength every day in these regions, and we foresee that, unless it is checked, everything here will soon be full of it: not only of the Lutherans, the Oecolampadians and the Anabaptists, but also of those who have recently begun to emerge under obscure names; and it cannot be said how eagerly many people secretly strive to nourish these monsters. Therefore, in discharge of the office we bear in the Church of God, we have summed up in a few words certain articles of doctrine which, on account of the heresies named, it is very expedient at this time that good and Catholic preachers set forth to the people (for it is for the people's sake that we have undertaken this labour) and explain faithfully and diligently. We could indeed have expanded these articles, treating them at greater length and going back to first principles, but we did not think this necessary. Rather, we believed it would be more useful if they were put forward as simply as possible, so that even the most unlearned can grasp them. Moreover, we undertook this matter the more willingly because we clearly understood that it is a great concern of His Imperial Majesty, and that by his remarkable piety he himself also seeks something of this kind.

units.la: ARTICULUS PRIMUS.
units.tr: ARTICLE I.

units.la: Credendum est septem esse Ecclesiae sacramenta a Christo instituta, quae sunt, Baptismus, Confirmatio, Eucharistia, Poenitentia, Extrema unctio, Ordo & Matrimonium. Per quae, quamvis externa & corporalia signa, Deus invisibiliter, sive per bonos, sive per malos ministros, nostram salutem operatur.
units.tr: It is to be believed that there are seven sacraments of the Church instituted by Christ, which are: Baptism, Confirmation, Eucharist, Penance, Extreme Unction, Orders, and Matrimony. Through these, although they are external and bodily signs, God invisibly works our salvation, whether through good or through bad ministers.
II.

units.la: Baptismus ad salutem omnibus est necessarius, etiam infantibus, per quem peccata plene tolluntur, & fiunt filii Dei, ac haeredes vitae aeternae: nec unquam est iterandus.
units.tr: Baptism is necessary to salvation for all, even for infants; through it sins are fully taken away, people become sons of God and heirs of eternal life, and it is never to be repeated.
III.

units.la: Poenitentiae Sacramentum (quod post Baptismum omnibus relapsis est ad salutem necessarium) complectitur Contritionem, Confessionem, & Satisfactionem.
units.tr: The sacrament of Penance (which, after Baptism, is necessary to salvation for all who have fallen back) comprises Contrition, Confession, and Satisfaction.
IV.

units.la: Contritio, est dolor de peccatis propter Dei offensam susceptus, cum proposito confitendi & satisfaciendi, non autem (ut quidam hoc saeculo perniciose docent) terror conscientiae, propter apprehensum gehennae supplicium peccatis debitum. Praeparat tamen hic terror & gehennae metus, ad veram animi contritionem.
units.tr: Contrition is sorrow for sins undertaken on account of the offence against God, together with the purpose of confessing and making satisfaction; it is not, as some teach perniciously in this age, the terror of conscience arising from the apprehended punishment of hell owed to sins. Yet this terror and fear of hell prepare the way for true contrition of heart.
V.

units.la: Confessurus diligentiam legitimam adhibere debet, quo sacerdoti iudici suo, manifestet omnia peccata sua mortalia, etiam occulta cordis, ut ab eis per illum absolvatur: cujus absolutionis minister est solus sacerdos, secundum Ecclesiae ritum consecratus.
units.tr: The one who is to confess must take care to bring to his priest, his judge, all his mortal sins, even the hidden sins of the heart, so that he may be absolved of them through him. The minister of this absolution is the priest alone, consecrated according to the rite of the Church.
VI.

units.la: Satisfactio, est persolutio poenae, plerunque adhuc debitae, remissa jam culpa. Nam omnem poenam peccato debitam semper condonari culpa remissa, erroneum est, & scripturis sacris adversatur.
units.tr: Satisfaction is the payment of the punishment, often still owed, once the guilt has been remitted. For it is erroneous, and contrary to the holy Scriptures, to hold that all punishment owed to sin is always pardoned along with the remission of guilt.
VII.

units.la: Certa fide tenendum est, hominem habere liberum arbitrium, quo potest male, & cum gratia Dei bene agere, & post mortale peccatum admissum, Deo adjuvante poenitere, & peccatorum remissionem consequi.
units.tr: It is to be held with certain faith that man has free will, by which he can act badly, and with the grace of God act well, and after a mortal sin committed, with God helping, repent and obtain the remission of sins.

units.la: VIII.
units.tr: VIII.

units.la: Ad justificationem ante omnia necessaria est in adultis fides, qua certo credimus Christum Jesum Dei filium, nobis propiciatorem a patre propositum esse pro peccatis nostris in sanguine ipsius, sine qua nullis nostris operibus, nullaque poenitentia justificatio obtineri potest. Sicut nec fide sola, sine poenitentia & proposito vivendi secundum mandata Dei.
units.tr: For justification, faith is above all necessary in adults, by which we firmly believe that Jesus Christ, the Son of God, has been set forth by the Father as our propitiator for our sins in his blood; without this faith, justification cannot be obtained by any of our works or by any repentance. Nor by faith alone, without repentance and the purpose of living according to the commandments of God.
IX.

units.la: Fides qua quis firmiter credit, & certo statuit propter Christum sibi remissa esse peccata, sequeque possessurum vitam aeternam, nullum habet in scripturis testimonium, imo eisdem adversatur, etiam si firma & certa spe expectare debemus in hac quidem vita, per Sacramentum baptismi & poenitentiae, peccatorum remissionem, in saeculo autem futuro, vitam aeternam.
units.tr: Faith by which someone firmly believes, and with certainty determines, that his sins are remitted for Christ's sake and that he will possess eternal life, has no testimony in the Scriptures; indeed it is contrary to them. Yet we ought to await, with a firm and certain hope, in this life, through the sacrament of baptism and of penance, the remission of sins, and in the future age, eternal life.
X.

units.la: Itaque, quamdiu inter hostes nostros, & adversarias potestates hic vivimus, nulla nobis est securitas: sed cum timore & tremore juxta sententiam Apostoli nostram salutem operari debemus. Et secundum varias animorum nostrorum affectiones, nunc magis sperare, nunc magis timere, simpliciter tamen magis & frequentius de misericordia domini sperandum est, quā formidandū de severitate.
units.tr: Therefore, as long as we live here among our enemies and hostile powers, we have no security; but, according to the saying of the Apostle, we must work out our salvation with fear and trembling. And according to the various dispositions of our minds, now to hope more, now to fear more; yet, speaking simply, we ought to hope more and more often in the mercy of the Lord than to dread his severity.
XI.

units.la: Opera bona omnibus adultis sunt ad salutem necessaria, & cum ex fidei & charitatis spiritu proficiscuntur, ita grata sunt Deo, ut eis tanquam justam mercedem vitam retribuat aeternam.
units.tr: Good works are necessary to salvation for all adults, and since they proceed from the spirit of faith and charity, they are so pleasing to God that he rewards them with eternal life as a just recompense.
XII.

units.la: Confirmatio & extrema Unctio Sacramenta sunt a Christo instituta: sed non ut duo praecedentia ad salutem necessaria. Ex contemptu tamen illa omittere, mortale peccatum est.
units.tr: Confirmation and Extreme Unction are sacraments instituted by Christ, but not, like the two preceding, necessary to salvation. Yet to omit them out of contempt is a mortal sin.

units.la: XIII.
units.tr: XIII.

units.la: In Eucharistiae Sacramento est re ipsa verū corpus domini nostri Jesu Christi, illud ipsum, quod de virgine natum, & in cruce passum est.
units.tr: In the sacrament of the Eucharist there is, in very fact, the true body of our Lord Jesus Christ, that same body which was born of the virgin and suffered on the cross.
XIV.

units.la: In Eucharistia non manent panis & vinum, sed haec in corpus & sanguinē Christi admirabili potentia verbi ipsius sunt conversa: manentibus tantum panis vinique speciebus. unde certa fide tenendum est, sacram Eucharistiam sancte a nobis adorari, sive in Missa, sive extra Missam, ubicunque repositæ fuerit: aut quotiescunque supplicationibus publicis a sacerdote circumfertur, XV. Non
units.tr: In the Eucharist the bread and wine do not remain, but by the wonderful power of his own word they are changed into the body and blood of Christ, the appearances alone of bread and wine remaining. Hence it is to be held with certain faith that the holy Eucharist is to be adored by us, whether in the Mass or outside the Mass, wherever it has been reserved; or whenever it is carried about by the priest in public processions. XV. Not
XV.

units.la: Non est laicis necessaria ad salutem communio sub utraque specie, justisque de causis ab Ecclesia sancitum est, ut illis sub una tantum panis specie Sacramentum communicetur: in quo carnem & sanguinem, atque ita totum Christum sub una specie sumunt.
units.tr: Communion under both kinds is not necessary to salvation for laymen; and for just reasons the Church has ordained that the sacrament be given to them under the one kind of bread only; in that kind they receive the flesh and blood, and so the whole Christ under one kind.
XVI.

units.la: Sacrificium Missæ ex institutione Christi, tam vivis prodest, quam defunctis.
units.tr: The sacrifice of the Mass, by the institution of Christ, benefits the living as much as the dead.

units.la: XVII.
units.tr: XVII.

units.la: Solis sacerdotibus secundum Ecclesiæ ritum ordinatis, data est à Christo potestas consecrandi verum corpus Christi & sanguinem.
units.tr: Only to priests ordained according to the rite of the Church has Christ given the power of consecrating the true body and blood of Christ.

units.la: XVIII.
units.tr: XVIII.

units.la: Matrimonium contractum & consummatum inter Christianos, est indissolubile, qualiscunque fiat alter conjugum, sive adulter, sive sterilis, sive haereticus.
units.tr: Matrimony contracted and consummated among Christians is indissoluble, whichever spouse it may be, whether adulterer, barren, or heretic.
XIX.

units.la: Nunquam licet Christiano post divortium contrahere matrimonium, vivente eo cum quo prius legitime contraxerat.
units.tr: It is never lawful for a Christian to contract marriage after divorce, while the one with whom he had previously lawfully married is still living.
XX.

units.la: Matrimonia contracta contra Canones ipsa dirimentes, simpliciter sunt irrita & nulla.
units.tr: Marriages contracted contrary to the canons that invalidate them are simply void and null.
XXI.

units.la: Firma fide tenendum est, unam esse in terris veram atque catholicam Christi Ecclesiam, eamque visibilem, quæ ab Apostolis fundata, in hanc usque nostram ætatem perdurans, retinet & suscipit, quicquid de fide & religione tradidit, tradit & traditura est cathedra Petri, super quam ita à Christo suo sponsio est ædificata, ut in his, quæ fidei sunt & religionis, errare non possit.
units.tr: It must be held with firm faith that there is one true and catholic Church of Christ on earth, and that it is visible. Founded by the Apostles and enduring until our own age, it retains and accepts whatever it has handed down, hands down, and will hand down concerning faith and religion. The chair of Peter, upon which Christ, its bridegroom, has built it, so that it cannot err in matters of faith and religion.

units.la: XXII.
units.tr: XXII.

units.la: Extra hanc nulli speranda est salus: suntque extra eam haeretici, schismatici & excommunicati: unde vehementer formidanda est excommunicatio: nec humana, sed divina est excommunicandi potestas.
units.tr: Outside this Church no one may hope for salvation. Heretics, schismatics and the excommunicated are outside it. Hence excommunication is to be greatly feared. The power of excommunication is not human but divine.

units.la: XXIII.
units.tr: XXIII.

units.la: Unus est ecclesiæ summus pastor, cui omnes obedire tenentur: ad cujus judicium controversiæ, quæ super fide & religione exstiterint, sunt referendæ.
units.tr: There is one supreme shepherd of the Church, whom all are bound to obey. Controversies that arise concerning faith and religion are to be referred to his judgment.

units.la: XXIV.
units.tr: XXIV.

units.la: Summam hanc præposituram primus omnium gessit sanctus Petrus, verus Christi in terris vicarius, & totius familiæ ejus pastor. Post Petrum vero ex Christi institutione omnes deinceps Pontifices, Petri in cathedra successores.
units.tr: The first of all to hold this supreme headship was Saint Peter, the true vicar of Christ on earth and shepherd of the whole of his family. After Peter, by the institution of Christ, all the Pontiffs who succeed him in the chair of Peter hold the same office.
XXV.

units.la: Certa fide tenenda sunt, non solum quæ scripturis expresse sunt prodita, sed etiam quæ per traditionem Ecclesiæ Catholicæ credenda accepimus, & quæ definita sunt super fidei & morum negociis per cathedram Petri, vel per concilia generalia legitime congregata.
units.tr: We must hold with certain faith not only what is expressly handed down in the Scriptures, but also what we have received as to be believed through the tradition of the Catholic Church, and what has been defined concerning matters of faith and morals by the chair of Peter, or by lawfully assembled general councils.

units.la: XXVI.
units.tr: XXVI.

units.la: Constitutiones Ecclesiasticæ de jejuniis, festis, & abstinentia ciborum, aliisque multis, obligant in conscientia: etiam extra casum scandali.
units.tr: Ecclesiastical constitutions concerning fasts, feasts, abstinence from foods, and many other things bind in conscience, even apart from the case of scandal.

units.la: XXVII.
units.tr: XXVII.

units.la: Recte fit in Ecclesia, quod sanctos in cœlis cum Christo agentes veneramur & invocamus, ut pro nobis orent: quorum etiam meritis & intercessione, Christus nobis hic multa largitur, alias non largiturus: per quos etiam miracula multa in terris operatur.
units.tr: It is right in the Church that we venerate and invoke the saints who reign with Christ in heaven, that they may pray for us. Through their merits and intercession Christ bestows many gifts on us here, which he would not otherwise bestow. Through them he also works many miracles on earth.

units.la: XXVIII.
units.tr: XXVIII.

units.la: Quapropter sancte & religiose faciunt, qui loca eis dicata, una cum ipsorum reliquiis religiosa pietate visitant, & hoc modo ab ipsis opitulationem quaerunt.
units.tr: Therefore those who visit the places dedicated to them, together with their relics, with religious devotion, and in this way seek their help, act holily and religiously.

units.la: XXIX.
units.tr: XXIX.

units.la: Gratus est etiam Deo imaginum usus, rectèque coram eis procumbimus, invocaturi sanctos, quos repræsentant.
units.tr: The use of images is also pleasing to God, and we rightly bow down before them, intending to invoke the saints whom they represent.
XXX.

units.la: Firmiter credendum est, post hanc vitam purgatorium esse animarum: in quo solvitur poena peccatis adhuc debita. Eisdem tamen subvenitur, sacrificio altaris, oratione, jejunio, eleemosyna, aliisque bonis operibus vivorum, sicut: & indulgentiis, quo citius ab ea liberentur.
units.tr: It must be firmly believed that after this life there is a purgatory for souls, in which the punishment still owed for sins is paid off. Yet these souls are helped by the sacrifice of the altar, prayer, fasting, almsgiving and other good works performed by the living, and also by indulgences, so that they may be freed from it more quickly.

units.la: XXXI.
units.tr: XXXI.

units.la: Animæ defunctorum purgatæ, mox regnant cum Christo in cœlis. Et animæ impiorum hinc migrantes, sempiternis inferni tradLuntur supplicis.
units.tr: The souls of the dead who have been cleansed reign at once with Christ in heaven. The souls of the impious who depart hence are handed over to everlasting punishments of hell.

units.la: XXXII.
units.tr: XXXII.

units.la: Recte vota Deo facimus, tam monastica quam alia, & facta obligant apud Deum, nec advertsantur libertati Evangelicæ: quæ à peccatis libertas est, & iis quæ spiritum nostrum quoquomodo impediunt, quo minus totis Deo serviat: non autem à voti vel juramenti obligatione, nec ab obedientia magistratus Ecclesiastici vel secularis.
units.tr: We rightly make vows to God, monastic and others alike, and vows made are binding before God. They do not conflict with evangelical liberty, which is liberty from sins and from whatever in any way hinders our spirit from serving God wholeheartedly. It is not liberty from the obligation of a vow or oath, nor from obedience to ecclesiastical or secular magistrates.

units.la: Ergo quod unum nostræ facultatis est, mandamus Theologiæ studiosis omnibus, quacunque ratione nobis subjectis, & in posterum subjiciendis. Primum, ne quid usquam docentaur profiteantur, quod dogmatibus his contrarium sit: deinde, ut eadem fideliter, cum locus & occasio postulabit, tueantur & explicent ad veteris & orthodoxæ fidei custodiam & ædificationem Christiani populi. Si qui vero contraria, eos pro modo facultatis nostræ omnino punire decrevimus.
units.tr: Therefore, what lies within our power, we command all students of theology, whoever is subject to us in any manner, and whoever shall be subject in future: first, that they teach or profess nowhere anything contrary to these doctrines; second, that when place and occasion demand, they faithfully defend and explain the same, for the keeping of the old and orthodox faith and for the edification of the Christian people. If any teach the contrary, we have decreed that they be punished fully, according to the measure of our power.

units.la: Anno à nativitate domini M. D. XLIIII. Mensis Decembris, die sexta, Facultas Theologiæ congregata per juramentum in collegio Theologorum super articulis præcedentibus, probavit hos articulos sub forma, qua scripti sunt. Sic subscriptum de mandato dominorum Decani & Facultatis. Iudocus de Langhenhove Notarius subscripsit.
units.tr: In the year of our Lord 1544, on the sixth day of December, the Faculty of Theology, gathered under oath in the college of theologians, approved these articles in the form in which they were written. Signed thus by order of the lord Dean and the Faculty. Judocus de Langhenhove, notary, subscribed.

units.la: Hac proinde causa, cumq; articuli peracti in nostro concilio accurate perlecti, catholici & sancti comperti fuerint, eosdem, quantum in nobis situm est, harum testimonio literarum nostra auctoritate decretoque firmamus. Omnes & singulos Episcopos, Ecclesiarumq; prælatos, cujuscunque gradus dignitatisve fuerint, requirentes & exhortantes. Et quantum protectionis & conservationis sanctissimæ fidei nostræ nobis incumbentis provincia exigit, illis mandantes, quatenus singulis eorum vicariis, officialibus & officiatis, articulorum prædictorum authenticum exemplar transmittant Parochialib. Presbyteris, & monasteriis mendicantium, & non mendicantium; & aliis quibuscunq;, ad quos verbum Christi populo annunciare pertinet, in eorundem Prælatorum diocesibus constitutis tradendum & porrigendum, aperteq; & absq; verborum involucro populo è suggestu exponendum. Juxta quorum articulorum contenta tam Episcopi, quam clerus, exemptus & non exemptus, non modo in publicis concionibus, verum etiam in privatis communicationibus sese accommodare studebunt. Non permittentes quicquam, ab eisdem articulis dissonum, seu contrarium à suis evulgari, proponi, aut fustineri: adhibita diligenti, de transgressoribus, contraria, pugnantia, seu his discordantia, prædicantibus aut sententiabus, inquisitione: & de noxiis (ut aliis cedant in exemplum) debita animadversione sequuta. Omnibus itaque nostris, nostrorumque vasallorum officiatis, & justitiæ præfectis, districte præcipiendo mandamus, quatenus Episcopis prædictis, Prælatis, & aliis eorundem officiatorum operam egentibus, circa præmissa faveant & assistant, impertito eis, ubi exinde fuerit requisiti, auxilii secularis brachio. Insuper dilectis & fidelibus nostris, supremo capiti, Præsidenti, & nostris consiliorum privati magnique Consiliariis, Cancellario & Consiliariis, consilii nostri Brabantiæ gubernatori. Cancellario & Consiliariis Geldrensibus, Gubernatoribus, Præsidentibus & Consiliariis Luxemburgensibus, Flandriæ, Arthesii, Insulensis, Duacensis, & Orchiarum. Magno nostro Hannoniæ Ballivo, & Consiliariis nostris in Montibus Hannoniæ. Gubernatori, Præsidenti, Consiliariis Hollandiæ, Frisiæ & Trajecti, Gubernatori & supremo Ballivo Namurcensi, Locumtenenti Transfulano, & Groningæ, receptoribus Zelandiæ Meridionalis & Orientalis, Schaldæ, Præposito Comitis in Valenchenis, Ballivo Tornacensi & Tornacesii, Sculteto Mechliniensi, omnibusque aliis nostris, nostrorumque vasallorum officiatis, & justitiæ præfectis, quibus literæ nostræ diligentur, & ad quos negocium hoc pertinet & spectat, Damus in mandatis, quatenus præmissa servent, sectentur, & adimpleant, & ab omnibus servari, sectari, & adimpleri, absque contradictione aut contraventione quacunque procurent. In quorum robur, fidemque præmissorum, præsentes literas nostro fecimus sigillo communiri. Datum Bruxellæ, die XIIII. Mensis Martii. Anno Domini M. D. XLV. Imperii nostri XXVI. Regnorumque nostrorum Castellæ, Legionis & aliorum XXIX. Subscriptum per Imperatorem in suo concilio, & signatum Vertteyken.
units.tr: For this reason, since the articles, once drawn up, were carefully read through in our council and found to be Catholic and holy, we confirm the same, as far as lies in us, by the testimony of these letters, with our authority and decree. We require and exhort all and each of the bishops and prelates of the churches, of whatever rank or dignity they may be, and, as far as the duty of protecting and preserving our most holy faith, which falls to us, requires, we charge them that they send an authentic copy of the aforesaid articles to each of their vicars, officials and those under them, and to the parish priests, and to the monasteries of mendicant and non-mendicant orders, and to all others to whom it belongs to announce the word of Christ to the people, established within the dioceses of these same prelates, to be delivered and handed over, and to be set forth openly and without wrapping of words to the people from the pulpit. In accordance with the contents of these articles, both bishops and clergy, exempt and non-exempt, shall strive to conform themselves not only in public sermons but also in private conversations, not permitting anything at variance with or contrary to these articles to be published, proposed or defended by their subjects. A diligent inquiry is to be made concerning transgressors who preach or hold opinions contrary, conflicting or discordant with them, and due punishment is to follow against the guilty, so that others may take warning from it. Therefore, to all our officials and to the officials of our vassals, and to the prefects of justice, we give strict command that they favour and assist the aforesaid bishops, prelates and the other officials of the same who need their help in these matters, granting them, whenever they are requested, the aid of the secular arm. Moreover, to our beloved and faithful ones: our chief, president, and the privy and great councillors of our council; the chancellor and councillors; the governor of our council of Brabant; the chancellor and councillors of Guelders; the governors, presidents and councillors of Luxemburg, Flanders, Artois, Lille, Douai and Orchies; our great bailiff of Hainaut and our councillors in the Mons region of Hainaut; the governor, president and councillors of Holland, Friesland and Utrecht; the governor and chief bailiff of Namur; the lieutenant of Overijssel and of Groningen; the receivers of South and East Zeeland and of the Scheldt; the provost of the count at Valenciennes; the bailiff of Tournai and Tournaisis; the schout of Mechelen; and all other officials of ours and of our vassals, and prefects of justice, to whom these our letters are addressed and to whom this business pertains and belongs: we command that they observe, follow and fulfil the aforesaid matters, and that they see to it that they are observed, followed and fulfilled by all, without any contradiction or contravention whatever. In witness and confirmation of which matters we have caused these present letters to be fortified with our seal. Given at Brussels, on the 14th day of March, in the year of the Lord 1545, the 26th of our reign and the 29th of our kingdoms of Castile, León and the others. Signed by the Emperor in his council, and sealed by Vertteyken.

units.la: CAROLI V. IMPER. AUG. MANDATUM
units.tr: Mandate of Charles V, Emperor Augustus

units.la: Quo jubetur Dux VVirtenbergius rebellionis reus, seq. suaq. omnia ultro dedere, aut læsæ Majestatis indignationem pænamq. perferre.
units.tr: By which Duke Wirtemberg, guilty of rebellion, is ordered to surrender himself and all his possessions unconditionally, or to bear the indignation and punishment of injured majesty.

units.la: Quamvis aliquot ante annis propter bellum, abste & Lantgravio adversus fratrem meum motum, & agrum Wirtenbergensem, quo multatus fueras, receptum, in vos exemplum edere jure potuissem; noxam tamen omnem & injuriam clementer, quia supplex petebas, tibi remisi, omnemque, quam potui, munificentiam atque humanitatem præstiti. Nuper etiam ante hoc bellum suscepntum, pan benevolentia te minime meritu prosequutus fui, cum tyrannide in tuos finitimosq; Imperii Ordines immaniter exerceres, neq; legib. humanis neq; rationis habenis coerceri posses. Legatos ad te misi, a quib. quia ob causa arma ego sumpserim, cognoscetes, quiq; tibi, ut ab armorum societate abstineres, ediceren. Tu his omnib. ludibrio habitis, violata fidei qua mihi debes, religione, societate & amicitia cum ho-
units.tr: Although some years ago, on account of the war which you and the Landgrave waged against my brother, and the recovery of the land of Württemberg, by which you were punished, I could rightly have made an example of you; nevertheless I mercifully remitted to you all offence and injury, since you begged as a suppliant, and I showed you all the generosity and humanity I could. Recently too, before this war was undertaken, I treated you with no small goodwill, although you were savagely exercising tyranny over your neighbours and the Estates of the Empire, and could be restrained neither by human laws nor by the reins of reason. I sent envoys to you, so that you would learn why I had taken up arms, and they were to order you to abstain from alliance in arms. You, having treated all these things with mockery, violated the faith, obligation, alliance and friendship you owe me, and joined with my enemies

units.la: Interprete Lamberto Hortensio. cum hostib. meis inisti; quos proscripsi, quorū urbes, oppida, arces, agrosque non hastiled armis jeci, cum his arma ac vires consociasti. Et ne qua contumelia ludibriumque pietatis mitteretur, confœderatorum tuorum opibus fretus, fratris mei primum, deinde quorundam ex Ordinibus Imperii adeoque mea, quae ad Imperium pertinent, oppida armis non petivisti modo sed etiam navali ... nondum, quamvis gravibus & atrocibus flagitiis, expletus bellum insuper, qua fuisti ... fecisti: Majestatem meam, dictis virulentis imminuisti: meam authoritatem decusque ... mnemque in id operam sedulo navasti, ut me Imperatorio splendore exueres, renunciaret ... hi obnoxius es, fide, quam sociorum conjurationi posthabuisti. Super haec copias cum ... juratis sociis in me armasti, & conscriptas mihi frequenti acie objecisti, prius multis & ... clientibus memorabili rerum suarum naufragio afflictis. Eadem proinde multa & ... rum, ut Majestatis reum, quae alios, te quoq; manet.
units.tr: Translated by Lambert Hortensius. whom I had proscribed, whose cities, towns, citadels and fields I had not seized with a spear but with arms, and you joined arms and forces with them. And lest any insult or mockery of piety be sent forth, relying on the resources of your confederates, you not only attacked by arms first the towns of my brother, then those of certain members of the Imperial Estates, and indeed those which belong to me and to the Empire, but also by naval [...] not yet satisfied, although by grave and atrocious crimes, you moreover waged war, in which you [...] did. You diminished my majesty with virulent words; you diligently laboured to strip me of my imperial authority and splendour [...] you are guilty, by the faith which you have set aside in favour of the conspiracy of your allies. Besides these things, you armed troops against me with your sworn allies, and you set them against me in a dense battle line, after many [...] clients, afflicted by the memorable shipwreck of their affairs. Therefore many of the same [...] as a guilty party against majesty, which await others, await you too.

units.la: Haec quanquam ita se habent, & causae, cur in te ultimo humanorum supplicio ... possem, comparent, uti meritus es: ne tamen plebs insons, cui plus misericordiae quam tuae ... debetur, rei Principis peccatum hoc (huic omnino parcere statui sententia) edico, ut ... meas literas acceperis, te ultro mihi dedas: omnem tuam provinciam, urbes, agros, ... denique fortunatum tibi est, in jus meum tradas, ut de his ex meo arbitrio consulam. Et ... feceris, ferro & igni potius labor omnia, teq; bello, donec oppressero, usq; perequar. ... expurgatoriae, quas quatuor hinc diebus ad me dederis, non faciunt mihi satis, neq; ejusmodi hoc tuum facinus vel extenuare vel excusare queant. Datae Rotenburgi ad Neccarum, ... mense Decembri.
units.tr: Although these things are so, and the causes by which I could justly condemn you to the ultimate human punishment are present, as you deserve; nevertheless, lest the innocent common people, to whom more mercy is owed than to you, suffer for the crime of their prince, I have resolved wholly to spare them. I declare that, upon receiving my letter, you surrender yourself to me unconditionally; that you hand over to my jurisdiction your whole province, cities, fields [...] and finally whatever belongs to you, so that I may decide about these matters at my own discretion. And if you do not do this, I will rather labour all things with sword and fire, and pursue you with war until I have overcome you. [...] the purgatory letters which you have sent to me within these four days do not satisfy me, nor can they lessen or excuse this your deed. Given at Rottenburg on the Neckar, [...] in December.

units.la: CAROLI V. IMPER. AUG. INTERIM SIVE Declaratio Religionis, hoc est, constitutio præscribens, qua ratione sacrosancti Imperii Romani Status in negocio Religionis usq; ad decisionem Concilii generalis, se se mutuo gerere ac excipere debeant, in habito Augustæ Conventu, 15. Maii à Caes. Majest. publicata, & a Statibus Imperii acceptata, A. D. 1548.
units.tr: Charles V, Emperor Augustus: the Interim, or Declaration of Religion; that is, the constitution prescribing in what manner the Estates of the Holy Roman Empire ought to conduct themselves towards one another and receive one another in matters of religion, until the decision of a general Council, published by His Imperial Majesty in the assembly held at Augsburg on 15 May, and accepted by the Estates of the Empire, A.D. 1548.

units.la: Sacra Cæsarea Majestas, Dominus noster Clementissimus, sacri Rom. Imperii Electoribus, Principibus, & cæteris Statibus, absentiumque Legatis sequentia jubet intimari.
units.tr: His Sacred Caesarean Majesty, our most merciful Lord, orders the following to be intimated to the Electors, Princes and other Estates of the Holy Roman Empire, and to the envoys of those who are absent.

units.la: QUanquam sacra Cæsarea Majestas ab initio sui regiminis nihil magis in votis habuit, quam ut ea tractarentur & promoverentur, quae universo orbi Christiano, & in primis sacro Imperio Germanicæ nationis, tanquam dilectae patriae suae, ad honorem, utilitatem, ac felicem statum ipsius, conservandamq; sub aliis & felici Majest. suae administratione, omniū ordinū pacem, concordiam, & tranquillitatem ullo modo conducere possent: tamen sua Majest. jamdudum satis perspicuis indiciis, & ipsa experta est, absq; Christiana compositione, vel legitima determinatione hujus exitii perniciosissimi controversiæ religionis dissidii, ex quo hactenus omnes discordiae, rancores, bella, angustiae, & gravamina statuum processerunt, ullam hujusmodi firmæ pacis, justitiæ & publicæ tranquillitatis spem non superesse: Ideo sua Majest. antea variis super ea re institutis colloquiis & tractatibus nullum non movit lapidem, quo exitiale hoc dissidium ad Christianam concordiam, vel saltem intellectum promoveretur.
units.tr: Although His Sacred Caesarean Majesty, from the beginning of his reign, had nothing more at heart than that those things be treated and promoted which could in any way conduce to the whole Christian world, and above all to the Holy Empire of the German nation, as to his beloved fatherland, to its honour, advantage and happy condition, and to the preservation of peace, concord and tranquillity of all orders under his other and happy administration; nevertheless His Majesty has already learned, by sufficiently clear signs and by experience itself, that without a Christian settlement or a lawful determination of this most pernicious dissension of the religious controversy, from which all the discords, rancours, wars, distresses and grievances of the Estates have hitherto arisen, there is no hope of any such firm peace, justice and public tranquillity. Therefore His Majesty, having earlier held various colloquies and negotiations on this matter, left no stone unturned by which this deadly dissension might be advanced towards Christian concord, or at least towards mutual understanding.

units.la: Verum cum in prosecutione illius operis res ipsa declararet, illud dissidium adeo altas radices, ut jam non solum Germanicam, verum etiam multas alias Nationes attingeret, omnque eis commune esse coeperit, ita ut visum sit, huic tam gravi morbo ullo alio convenientiori remedio, quam per viam universalis catholici Concilii, subveniri non posse: impetravit ... preces Statuum, sua Majest. post multas in ea re habitas tractationes, quod generale Concilium in Germanica natione Tridenti convocatum & celebrati coeptum sit. Quapropter & horum Conventus initio cum Statibus ita egit, eosq; permovit, ut in sequentes sanctorum patrum majorumq; vestigia, qui in negociis fidei semper ad sacra Concilia recurrere, eisdemq; obtemperare solerent, in adhaesionem & submissionem hujus Concilii communiter consenserint, ac ulterius suæ Majest. ... Herum permiserint, de Christianis ac convenientibus mediis cogitare, quibus medio ... finem ac determinationem Concilii omnes Status pie & pacifice simul vivere & habitare ... ut nemo contra jus ac æquitatem gravetur. Et sicut sua Majest. tunc temporis hujusmodi Statuum sensum ac remissionem clementissimo animo suscepit, ita & nunc non minus suscipit.
units.tr: But when, in the pursuit of that work, the matter itself showed that this dissension had struck such deep roots that it now touched not only the German nation but also many other nations, and had begun to be common to all, so that it seemed this so grave a disease could be remedied by no other more suitable remedy than by way of a universal and catholic Council; His Majesty, after many negotiations held on this matter, granted the prayers of the Estates, that a general Council be convened and begun at Trent in the German nation. Wherefore at the beginning of these assemblies he dealt with the Estates in such a way, and so moved them, that, following the footsteps of the holy Fathers and of our ancestors, who in matters of faith were always wont to have recourse to sacred Councils and to obey them, they agreed in common to adhere and submit to this Council, and further, they permitted His Majesty [...] to think about Christian and suitable means, by which all the Estates, until the end and determination of the Council, might live and dwell piously and peacefully together, so that no one be burdened against right and equity. And just as His Majesty at that time received the opinion and concession of these Estates with a most merciful mind, so now he receives them no less.

Item: Euntes docete omnes gentes, et ecce ego vobiscum sum omnibus diebus usque ad consummationem sæculi. Item: Ego rogabo Patrem, et alium Paracletum dabit vobis, ut maneat vobiscum in æternum, Spiritum veritatis.
units.tr: spread to the ends of the earth according to the promises of God: He shall possess the nations as your inheritance, and the ends of the earth as your possession. Likewise: He will send his angels with a great trumpet, and they shall gather his elect from the four winds, from the uttermost part of heaven to the ends of it. Likewise: Go and teach all nations, and behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age. Likewise: I will ask the Father, and he will give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you forever, the Spirit of truth.

units.la: Hæc itaque significat Ecclesiam Christianorum, Scripturarum atque Harmonia, quod mihi in præcipuis, et de quibus Ecclesiæ auctoritas.
units.tr: These things therefore signify the Church of Christians, according to the Scriptures and their harmony, which to me are among the principal points, and on which the authority of the Church rests.

units.la: CAP. XI. De authoritate & potestate Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: Chapter XI. On the authority and power of the Church.

units.la: ET Scriptura ad Christianos, quæ solutionem potest, & ideo immobilis. Ecclesia est, cum sit quia pietas Ecclesiam authoritas differendi sententias, et non habet haec Canon Scripturarum, quæ permanet, et falsa, quæ sub nomine Apostolorum et sepulcrorum Domino obtrudebantur, discernere.
units.tr: And Scripture, which can be neither dissolved nor altered, is for Christians the rule of faith. The Church has the authority to distinguish the true canon of Scriptures, which endures, from the false writings that were foisted on the world under the names of the Apostles and of the disciples of the Lord.

units.la: 2. Et ut Ecclesia tantum rem authoritatem potestatemque habet semper, ut crederemus quæ docet et exhibet, et sic per doctrinam et exhortandi dogmata quæque cum baptismo, sicut quod in Christo veritatem quam ad mundum Christus præcepit. Hæc item per Spiritum sanctum in Apostolis et, sed per Spiritum sanctum ut ait, Ecclesia, hæc.
units.tr: 2. The Church therefore always has this authority and power over the matter, so that we believe what she teaches and sets forth, and so through her teaching and exhortation she brings to faith those who are baptized, as Christ commanded the world. These things were likewise given through the Holy Spirit to the Apostles, and the Church has them through the same Holy Spirit, as he says.

units.la: 3. Hæc non Ecclesia traditiones Christo & Apostolis per manus Episcoporum quæ sunt, quam non vellit, ita non est eandem columnam esse & fundamentum. Hoc genus est nam baptismi partes eorum aliis.
units.tr: 3. The Church does not hold the traditions of Christ and the Apostles through the hands of bishops in such a way that she is not the same pillar and foundation of truth. The same holds for the parts of baptism, which differ from one another.

units.la: 4. Cum vero sint potestas coercendi atque excommunicandi esse potest Ecclesia contra eos qui Christo de portum, ut quod hanc concordia verum est illud Apostoli: Potestas Domini data est.
units.tr: 4. Since indeed there is a power of restraining and excommunicating, the Church can act against those who depart from Christ, and so that agreement holds true, the saying of the Apostle: "The power has been given by the Lord."

units.la: 5. Habet enim per omnia potestatem judicandi. Nam cui competit pœnas coercendi, is potest etiam decidere non potest.
units.tr: 5. For it has power of judging in all things. For he to whom it belongs to restrain punishments can also decide matters, and cannot fail to do so.

units.la: 6. Ac si quæ in Ecclesia haberet quidem hæc potestatem, quid tamen quam, atque decernere, si quod per Synodum & quod hæc in Spiritu sancto, legitime congregata Spiritus, ut quæ sunt decernere videtur, juxta illud Concilii Hierosolymitani: Visum est Spiritui sancto et nobis, quæ talia ut quia cum sit auctoritatem, dubitare debet nemo.
units.tr: 6. And if this power is in the Church, what else is it to decide and determine than what is decided through a synod, and what seems good to the Holy Spirit, when lawfully gathered in the Spirit, according to that saying of the Council of Jerusalem: "It seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us." Since such decisions carry authority, no one ought to doubt them.

units.la: 7. Et quod ex eodem Concilio Hierosolymitano intelligitur, est etiam potestas Ecclesiæ ad cogendum ad coarctandum, ad constitutionem ecclesiæ, cujus potestas omnis est ad ædificationem et non ad destructionem.
units.tr: 7. What is also understood from the same Council of Jerusalem is that the Church has the power to compel and to restrain for the building up of the congregation; and all her power is for edification and not for destruction.

units.la: CAP. XII. De Ministris Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: Chapter XII. Concerning the Ministers of the Church.

units.la: HÆC Ecclesia doctrinam divinam traditam, quæ populo explicanda est. Hæc sunt ministri ... Christianorum tractabatur, ... ad Ecclesiæ ministerium.
units.tr: This Church teaches the divine doctrine handed down, which is to be explained to the people. These are the ministers ... of Christians was treated ... to the ministry of the Church.

units.la: 2. Ipsque cum sit Apostolorum non omnibus data fuit potestas ad fundandas Ecclesias, sed ad eosdem ipsos legatos. Nam cum Antiochiæ essent Barnabas et Saulus, ministrantibus illis Domino, et Lucas in Actibus Apostolorum ... Segregate mihi Saulum et Barnabam in opus ad quod assumpsi eos. Ceteros nobis, ne ipsi ... ad ædificationem.
units.tr: 2. And since this belongs to the Apostles, the power to found churches was not given to everyone, but to those same legates. For when Barnabas and Saul were at Antioch, ministering to the Lord, and Luke in the Acts of the Apostles ... "Separate me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them." The rest ... lest they ... for edification.

units.la: CAP. XIII. De Pontifice Summo & Episcopis.
units.tr: CHAPTER XIII. On the Supreme Pontiff and the Bishops.

units.la: ATQUE in Ecclesia, quæ est unum corpus, Christi unum caput, ita ut ... pontifex summus, qui Episcopus est. Hæc ... per Ecclesiam et ad ædificationem.
units.tr: And in the Church, which is one body with Christ as its one head, so that ... the supreme pontiff, who is the bishop. These things ... through the Church and for its building up.

units.la: 2. Quapropter Christianorum Pontificem Summum Romanum sive Episcopum, qui Petrum successorem Christi ... Papam sive episcopum et sacerdotem et gubernatorem, et gubernandi debet.
units.tr: 2. Therefore the supreme pontiff of Christians, the Roman bishop, who (as) Peter, the successor of Christ ... pope or bishop, and priest and governor, and ought to govern.
