units.la: 3. Tridentti st, inquam, indictum Concilium generale omnium consensu. Legati, Cardinales missi, primùm Reverendiss. Panutius, Moronus & Polus adfuerunt, qui vices Pontificis repræsentarent: Oratores Imperatoris, admodum Illustrissimus & religiosissimus Episcopus Atrebatensis, Illustrissimus vir Dominus de Granvella, & ego Jacobus de Mendoza. Sed nondum visum fuit Sanct. Vestræ, ut apparet ex secunda Bulla Sanct. Vestræ, tempus satis idoneum ad inchoandum Concilium, post aliquot dies iterum à Sanct. Vestra missi Sedis Apostolicæ Legati, Cardinales, Reverendus de Monte, Reverendus Sanctæ Crucis, & iterum Reverendus Polus; rursum Oratores, Ego Jacobus Mendoza, & Illustris vir Franciscus Toledo absens: accesserunt nonnulli aliorum Principum itidem Oratores, nonnulli erant in itinere, multarum nationum Episcopi etiam ab ultimis terris convenere magnis impensis: magno labore inchoatum est, & petitum ab omnibus Christianis Concilium, & causa religionis & reformationis morum in eo tractari cœpta.
units.tr: 3. Indeed, the general Council was appointed at Trent with the consent of all. Legates and Cardinals were sent; first the most reverend Pantusius (?), Morone and Pole were present, who represented the place of the Pontiff; the ambassadors of the Emperor were the most illustrious and most religious Bishop of Arras, the illustrious lord de Granvelle, and I, James de Mendoza. But it did not seem to Your Holiness, as appears from the second Bull of Your Holiness, to be a sufficiently suitable time to begin the Council. After some days, Your Holiness sent again the legates of the Apostolic See, the Cardinals: the Reverend del Monte, the Reverend of the Holy Cross, and again the Reverend Pole; again ambassadors: I, James Mendoza, and the illustrious man Francis Toledo, who was absent. Some ambassadors of other princes also came; some were on the way; bishops of many nations also gathered from the farthest lands at great expense. The Council was begun with great labour, and a Council was asked for by all Christians, and the matter of religion and the reform of morals began to be treated in it.

units.la: 4. Eodem quoq; rempore bellum adversus hostes & S. Imperii violatores Imperator gerebat, in quo scipiendo potissimùm tuendæ & amplificandæ religionis, idq; interveniente Sanct. Vestra, habita est, ita ut quos ratione flectere non poteramus, armis cogeremus. Cùm res essent in hoc statu, cumpro(ut dixi) religionis negotio, causa morum (quæ totis viribus & consilio indigebat, ad quæ legitimè & absolutè prosus peragedam Sacra Majestas & Germaniæ Ordines à retrò Pontificibus & Sanctit. Vestra jam antea remedium tam crebrò flagitaverat) sed frigidè nimis & vix tenrata. Deinde virtute Imperatoris pacata Germania, in qua recuperanda Sanct. Vestræ & sacrosansto Concilio mutu incumbebat, maxima spe & certitudine eorum adventus, tum etiam, qui hucusq; Concilium reverâ veràt, & eorū qui in tam necessario religionis negotio adhuc occupati, Imperatorii adjutores erât.
units.tr: 4. At the same time the Emperor was waging war against the enemies and violators of the Holy Empire, in which war the defence and extension of religion was to be chiefly pursued; and this was undertaken with the involvement of Your Holiness, so that those whom we could not bend by reason we would compel by arms. When matters stood in this state, with the religious business as I said, and the question of morals (which needed all strength and counsel, and which His Sacred Majesty and the Orders of Germany had long demanded from previous Pontiffs and from Your Holiness as a remedy, to be carried out lawfully and fully), it was handled too coldly and scarcely attempted. Then, Germany having been pacified by the valour of the Emperor, in whose recovery the Holy See and the sacred Council were mutually bound, there was the greatest hope and certainty of their coming, and also of those who until now had truly attended the Council, and of those who, still occupied in so necessary a religious matter, were helpers of the Emperor.

units.la: 5. Ecce Reverendissimi asserti Legati tumultuosè, præter omnium expectationem, Sanctitate Vestra (quod ipsi dicunt) inscia & inconsulta, levissima sane causa procurata & consicta de tralatione Concilii retuleruntad Patres, nullo consultandi, sed neque cogitandi spatio dato, ita ut pridie proposuerint, postridie decreverint, perendie discesserint cum multis Patribus, atq; iis quidem cum temporis vel unius feré Italicæ nationis, vel ante adeptum Episcopatus nomen in Italia degentibus.
units.tr: 5. Behold, the most reverend legates, as they were called, tumultuously and beyond everyone's expectation, having procured a very slight and invented pretext, and (as they themselves say) without the knowledge and consultation of Your Holiness, reported to the Fathers about the transfer of the Council, giving no time for deliberation or even for thought; so that they proposed it on one day, decided it the next, and departed on the third with many Fathers, and indeed with those who had spent almost the time of one Italian nation alone, or who lived in Italy before obtaining the name of bishop.

units.la: 6. Huic consilio, Sanctissime Pater, plures Episcopi, magnæ fidei & autoritatis viri, quibus religionis & morum causa cordi erat, tanquam callido nimis & immaturo, Christianéq; Reip. periculoso, contravenêre, planeq; & publicè, inspirante eis Spiritu sancto, cujus sanè causa inprimis agi debebat, tum tralationem propositâ, tum Legatorum asserrorum & Patrum, qui eos secuti sunt, injustam esse tralatione Concilii, velleq; se manere Tridenti, libero & legitimo Cōcilii loco, publicè protestati sunt.
units.tr: 6. Against this plan, most Holy Father, several bishops, men of great faith and authority, to whom the cause of religion and of morals was dear, opposed it as too crafty and premature, and dangerous to the Christian commonwealth; and plainly and publicly, the Holy Spirit inspiring them (whose cause above all ought to have been pursued), they protested publicly both that the proposed transfer, and the legates and Fathers who followed them, were unjust, and that they wished to remain at Trent, the free and lawful place of the Council.

units.la: 7. Inter hæc Imperator, dū Episcoporū congregatio Bononiæ manet, hoste ad Albim devicto, Saxonia provincia superata, duobus belli Ducibus, altero pugna, altero deditione captis, pacata prosius Germania, arduū & periculosissimū bellū solus cōfecit: nec destitit sæpiùs San. Vest. per Nun-ios, per Legatos Sedis Apostolicæ, per Illustriss. virum Joannē Vegam, per me & Majestatis suæ apud S. V., Oratores, & ante & post cōfectū bellū, magnis & continuis precibus solicitare, juberet Patres, qui Bononiæ perstit, ad Cōcilium Trident. redire, eandēq; ipsam admonere, prævideat, quot scādala, dissidia, pericula, impēdeant Christianæ religioni, si jam cœptū Cōciliū Tridenti nō cōtinuetur & absolvatur.
units.tr: 7. Meanwhile the Emperor, while the congregation of bishops remained at Bologna, having defeated the enemy at the Elbe and overcome the province of Saxony, two leaders of the war being captured, one in battle and the other by surrender, and Germany being pacified, alone brought to completion the arduous and most dangerous war. Nor did he cease, both before and after the war was finished, to urge Your Holiness with great and continual prayers, through nuncios, through legates of the Apostolic See, through the illustrious man John Vega, through me, and through the ambassadors at Your Holiness's side, and to order the Fathers who remained at Bologna to return to the Council of Trent, and to admonish them also to foresee how many scandals, dissensions and dangers hang over the Christian religion if the Council begun at Trent is not continued and brought to completion.

units.la: 8. Comiria interim Augustæ Germanis indixit, quæ quidem adhuc celebrantur. In his libero, spontanco, generali totius Germaniæ Ordinum & Statuum, præterea omnium Civitatum consensu, petente Imperatore, decretum est, Germanos omnes ad Concilium Tridenti convocatum venturos, ut ea, super quibus indictum fuit, tractentur, & sacrosancta Concilii autoritate decidantur: Ipsam sa-sanctam Tridentinam Synodum se suscepturos, idq; prorsus & absque ulla conditione se præstituros, Imperatori sunt polliciti.
units.tr: 8. Meanwhile he summoned a diet of the Germans at Augsburg, which is still being held. In these, by the free, spontaneous and general consent of all the Orders and Estates of Germany, and moreover of all the cities, at the Emperor's request, it was decreed that all Germans would come to the Council convened at Trent, so that those matters on which it was announced should be treated and decided by the sacred authority of the Council; and they promised the Emperor that they would accept the holy Synod of Trent itself, and would render this absolutely and without any condition.

units.la: 9. Legavit Imperator Oratorem ad Sanctitatem Vestram, Illustrissimum & Reverendissimū Christophorum Madrucium, Cardinalem & Principem Tridentinum, quò S. Majestatis & Serenissimi Romani Regis Ordinumq; S. Imperii nomine Sanctitas Vestra pium hoc & sanctum Germaniæ Concilium indiceret, supplicaret, juberet Patres, qui Bononiæ agunt, ad Concilium Tridenti inchoatam reverti: hortaretur & admonerer, ut honestissimam & necessariam occasionem, tot laboribus & periculis tam diu quæsitam, nunc demum partam, susciperet & ampleċteretur, in qua & Patres cum dignitate Tridentum redire, & religionis causa generali Christianorum consensu, ipsorumq; Germanorum, quorum potissimùm gratia ipsa sacrosancti Synodus Tridenti convocata fuerat, tractari & confici, & sacrosanctæ Sedis Apostolicæ autoritas magna cum Pontificii nominis Majestate, & ipsius Sanctitatis Vestræ immortali gloria augeri posset: idq; non privatim solum, sed publicè faceret in Reverendissimorum Cardinalium consessu.
units.tr: 9. The Emperor sent as ambassador to Your Holiness the most illustrious and most reverend Christopher Madruzzo, Cardinal and Prince of Trent, so that in the name of His Majesty, of the most serene King of the Romans, and of the Orders of the Holy Empire, Your Holiness would appoint, petition and order the Fathers who were at Bologna to return to the Council begun at Trent; and that he would exhort and admonish them to seize and embrace the most honourable and necessary opportunity, sought for so long with so many labours and dangers and now at last obtained, in which the Fathers might return to Trent with dignity, and the matter of religion might be treated and concluded with the general consent of Christians and of the Germans themselves, for whose sake above all the sacred Synod of Trent had been convened; and in which the authority of the holy Apostolic See might be increased, with great majesty of the Papal name and with immortal glory to Your Holiness. And he ordered that this be done not only privately but publicly, in the assembly of the most reverend Cardinals.

units.la: 10. Præterea jussit me, qui Senas ad componendas illius Reipub. res veneram, idem negotium præstare. Quod si Sanctitas Vestra dilationem aut excusationem aliquam interponerer, neq; præsentem occasionem susciperet, hujusce rei, ut tam justæ petitionis, promtissimiq; erga Christianam religionem Majestatis suæ animi, tam publicè quàm privatim vos ipsos Reverendissimos Cardinales, & omnes omnium Principum Oratores, qui Romæ agunt, testes vocarem, præcepit.
units.tr: 10. Moreover, he ordered me, who had come to Siena to settle the affairs of that commonwealth, to carry out the same business. And if Your Holiness were to interpose any delay or excuse, and not take up the present opportunity, he charged me to call you, the most reverend Cardinals, and all the ambassadors of the princes who are at Rome, to witness, both publicly and privately, the disposition of His Majesty's mind, so eager and so prompt towards the Christian religion, in so just a petition.

units.la: 11. Præterea jussit Procuratores & Consiliarios suos, qui Bononiæ expectabant de ea re respôsum, & à Patribus ibi congregatis, & à Sanctitate Vestra, si unquam vel ipsi Patres vel Sanctitas Vestra id recusassent, vel dilationem aliquam interposuissent in generali Patrū cœtu, nomine Majestatis suæ testari, iniquam fuisse tralationem, & omnia inde facta & secuta ab ipsis Patribus affectata, & nulla esse atq; futura fore. Factum est, beatissime Pater, post requisitiones privatas etiam publicè primū à ReveReverendissimo Tridentino dienona Decembris: deinde à me die 14. ejusdem mensis hora matutina, in hoc Reverendissimorum Patrum consessu cum debita humilitate instanter, idq; per viscera, & per sanguinem Domini nostri Jesu Christi: tempus tamen Sanctitas Vestra posuit ad consulendos super responso Patres, qui Bononiæ sunt; qui quidem non dissimulante, sive (ut ipsi dicunt) translationi consilium dedere vanum, subdolum & captiosum, in gravissimam religionis & universalis Ecclesiæ dissidium, scandalum & detrimentum.
units.tr: 11. Moreover, he ordered his procurators and counsellors, who were waiting at Bologna for a reply on this matter, to testify in his Majesty's name, both to the Fathers gathered there and to Your Holiness, that if ever the Fathers themselves or Your Holiness should refuse this, or interpose some delay in the general assembly of the Fathers, the transfer was unjust, and all that was done and followed from it by the Fathers was affected, and is and shall be null. This was done, most blessed Father, after private requests, first publicly by the most reverend Bishop of Trent on the ninth day of December, and then by me on the fourteenth day of the same month, in the morning hour, in this assembly of the most reverend Fathers, insistently and with due humility, and that by the bowels and by the blood of our Lord Jesus Christ. Yet Your Holiness set a time to consult the Fathers who are at Bologna about the reply; and they, not dissembling, or (as they themselves say) gave counsel for the transfer, which was vain, deceitful and captious, to the gravest dissension, scandal and detriment of religion and of the universal Church.

units.la: 12. Sanctitas autem Vestra id consilium approbasse, illorumq; sententiam suscepisse, quod modo visa est, illegitimam secessionem Tridentinam, periculosissimam sine & perniciosam Christianæ translationis vocabulo, congregationemq; seu illegitimum Conventum Bononiensem generalis Concilii nomine appellans: tantùmq; ei congregationi auctoritatis in suis ad Reverendum Cardinalem de Monte, Episcopum Prænestinum, & ad vos qui adestis literis, & suo ad Imperatorem tribuere videtur, quantum Episcopi prænominati auctoritate propria sibi ipsis arrogare ausi sunt.
units.tr: 12. Your Holiness, however, has approved that counsel and adopted the opinion of those who call the recent so-called Tridentine secession, the illegitimate Bolognese assembly, a "translation" of the Council, though it is most dangerous and pernicious. You appear to grant that assembly, in your letters to the Reverend Cardinal de Monte, Bishop of Palestrina, to you who are present, and in your reply to the Emperor, as much authority as the aforementioned bishops dared to claim for themselves on their own authority.

units.la: 13. Præterea responsum ad Cæsarem dat dilatorium & illegitimum, præsenti occasione impertinens, ineptum & incoveniens. Quid enim magis alienum, quàm in gravissima causa religionis & Spiritus sancti, & causæ cognitionem ante vertere, & sententiam ferre, & constituere, antequam judicium sibi deferatur: & his qui ægrotabant, & sanari derant, qui remedium detrectare videbantur, qui nunc religionem, qui morum reformationem, qui publicarum dissensionum petunt à Sanctitate Vestra, (Concilium enim petunt Tridenti, ubi cæpum fuerat, continuari & absolvi, quod omnium bonorum causam futurum certissimè credunt) prætissimam medicinam tergiversationibus & ambagibus producere & denegare.
units.tr: 13. Besides, your reply to the Emperor is dilatory and illegitimate, irrelevant to the present occasion, inept and inconvenient. For what is more out of place, in a most serious matter of religion and of the Holy Spirit, than to pre-empt the examination of the case, pass judgment and decide before the matter has been referred to you? And to put off with evasions and circumlocutions, and to refuse, the most urgent remedy to those who are sick and lack a cure, who seem to be rejecting the remedy, and who now ask Your Holiness for religion, for the reform of morals, and for an end to public dissensions? For they ask for the Council to be continued and concluded at Trent, where it was begun, which they most certainly believe will serve the cause of all good men.

units.la: 14. Et cùm probationem causarum translationis à perspicuis & religiosissimis & probatis testibus sumi, conveniens sit, in hac ipsa testibus parum inter se convenientibus, nullius autem de plebe hominibus fidem adhibere: Imperatoris autem & Regis Romani, & Principum Statuum Germaniæ, qui in publicis Comitiis congregati sunt, qui & per Sanctæ Sedis Apostolicæ Cardinales atque eundem Sacri Imperii Principem, Sanctitatem Vestram certiorem faciunt, de hoc tam pio Germanorum proposito atque decreto fidem in dubium vertere, quod ex ipsorum & Sanctitatis Vestræ responso, cùm publicè tùm privatim dato, intelligi potest.
units.tr: 14. And since it is fitting that proof of the causes of the translation be drawn from clear, most religious and approved witnesses, and since in this very matter the witnesses agree poorly among themselves, one should not give credence to men of the common sort. But the Emperor and King of the Romans, and the Princes of the States of Germany, gathered at the public Diet, who through the Cardinals of the Holy Apostolic See and the same Prince of the Holy Empire make Your Holiness more certainly aware, cast doubt on the faith of this so pious proposal and decree of the Germans. This can be understood from the response given by them and by Your Holiness, both publicly and privately.

units.la: 15. Multa alia à me prætermittuntur, Sanctissime Pater, quæ tempore & loco, si opus sit, hac causa dicentur. Quid præterea desiderabamus à Germanis, quid ab eis petebamus, toties à Cæsare repetitis itineribus, tot impensis, tot laboribus, maximo & ancipiti suscepto bello, atq; collecto omnes labores hos S.V. pro religione susceptos: perdet optimam & præstantè sanandæ rei rursus & religionis occasionem, & perdet religionis causam, admonitus & requisitus. Id verò certissimum Concilium universale, ob causas gravissimas & maximè necessarias Tridenti congregatum, Vestra Sanctitatione, flagitante Imperatore, Principibus Christianis assentientibus, petentibus Germanis, convenientibus Episcopis, jam coeptum, nisi summa urgentiaq; necessitate, præcedentibus tractatibus, & diligentissima discussione, servato juris ordine, consensu omnium Patrum, aliò mutari, neq; legitimè posse nec licere.
units.tr: 15. Many other things I pass over, Most Holy Father, which, if need be, will be spoken in due time and place in this cause. What else did we desire from the Germans, what did we ask of them, with the Emperor's repeated journeys, so many expenses, so many labours, a great and dangerous war undertaken, and all these labours undertaken by Your Holiness for religion? You will lose the best and most excellent opportunity of healing the matter and religion again, and you will lose the cause of religion, though admonished and asked. Indeed it is most certain that a universal Council, assembled at Trent for most grave and most necessary causes, at the request of Your Holiness, with the Emperor urging, the Christian princes assenting, the Germans petitioning and the bishops agreeing, and already begun, cannot lawfully be moved elsewhere, nor is it permitted, unless in the greatest and most urgent necessity, after prior discussions and most diligent examination, with the order of law observed and with the consent of all the Fathers.

units.la: 16. Sæpe enim tralationes callido & præcipiti consilio sine causa factæ, in causa esse solent, magno religionis periculo, magnis in Repub. Christiana turbis & dissensionibus, interdum populi Christiani perniciosa divisione Concilia dissolvantur. Causa autem tam subitæ translationis nulla fuit arrepta, quæ se primùm obtulit. Occasionem vos Reverendissimi asserti Legati, ut à me dictum est, & reliqui Patres, fecistis, id quod jam pridem meditati fueratis. Febres enim nescio quas & æris vitium causati, affectatum & procuratum quorundam medicorum, sed præcipuè ancillarum & coquorum, nimorum hominum, testimonium recitantes, Tridento præcipites discesserunt. Nempe & tu deinceps apertissimè patuit, nullam extitisse vanæ formidinis causam.
units.tr: 16. For translations made without cause, by crafty and hasty counsel, are often the cause of great danger to religion, of great disturbances and dissensions in the Christian commonwealth, and sometimes Councils are dissolved by a pernicious division of the Christian people. But no real cause was seized upon for so sudden a translation; the first pretext that presented itself was taken. You, Reverend Legates, as I have said, and the other Fathers, have provided the occasion, which you had long been planning. For, citing I know not what fevers and a defect of the air, and recounting the affected and contrived testimony of certain physicians, but especially of maidservants and cooks, men of that sort, you departed headlong from Trent. Indeed, it has since become quite plain that there was no cause for vain fear.

units.la: 17. Præterea ut nulla fuerit ratio discedendi, Vestram Sanct. in hac præsenti causa consulere, cùm tam parvi temporis mora nihil periculi esset allatura. Neque enim tam repentina res erat exitus morbi, quem causati fuerant, comprobavit. Inconsulta autem Sanctitas Vestra, discessisse episcopos, fassi estis, & Sanctitas Vestra postmodùm affirmavit. Cui quidem Sanctitatis Vest. testimonio multum certè fidei & autoritatis detrahunt vestræ ad Reverendissimum de Monte literæ, responsiones ad Cæsarem datæ.
units.tr: 17. Moreover, even if there had been some reason for leaving, there was no need to consult Your Holiness in this present matter, since so short a delay would have brought no danger. Nor was the matter so sudden: the outcome of the illness they alleged has shown otherwise. You have admitted, and Your Holiness later affirmed, that the bishops departed without consulting you. Indeed, your letters to the Reverend de Monte and your replies given to the Emperor greatly detract from the credibility and authority of Your Holiness' own testimony.

units.la: 18. Imperatore quoque consulto & assentiente, id facere debuissent, cui curæ sunt & tutela omnia universalia Concilia, atq; id ex munere officii Augustalis: cujus quanta sit in Concilus manifestum est. Verùm tanta fuit Legatorum assertorum festinatio & simulatio, ut necipiti consulere, necceos qui dicebant, Sanctitatem Vestram & Imperatorem priùs per Sanctam certiores fieri oportere, audiendos putarint. Cumq; Imperator ipse pro tuenda & amplificanda religione, pro Ecclesia, pro Concilio laboraret, ipsi vano & inani tumore simulato, Imperator incomparabili, abscesserunt. Atqui sæpe aliàs Imperator per Oratores suos cùm ipsos assertos Legatos, rum Sanctitatem Vestram admonuerat, se neque translationi Concilii, sed neque suspensioni aut vacationi tè vel expresse assentiri posse.
units.tr: 18. They ought also to have done this with the Emperor consulted and assenting, to whose care and protection all universal Councils are committed, and this by the duty of the Imperial office; how great that is in Councils is evident. But so great was the haste and pretence of the Legates in question that they thought neither that the Emperor should be consulted, nor that those who said that Your Holiness and the Emperor should first be informed through a Synod should be heard. And while the Emperor himself was labouring to defend and extend religion, for the Church and for the Council, they, with vain and feigned pride, departed, leaving the incomparable Emperor behind. And yet at other times the Emperor, through his Orators, had often admonished both the said Legates and Your Holiness that he could consent neither expressly nor tacitly to the translation of the Council, nor to its suspension or cessation.

units.la: 19. Præterea juris ordinem contempserant, & eam causæ cognitionem, quæ in Synodalibus relationibus Sanctorum Patrum sanctionibus instituta est. Remenim fere omnium gravissimarum pere sanè & leviter confecerunt. Debuerant certè justas multorum gravissimorum Patrum, quos haudquaquam assentari doceret, rei ex recta conscientia consulebant, contradictiones libenter re, eorumque sententias ac rationes animadvertere atque examinare, ac non ipsis neglectis, viaque audiatur. [illegible, ~40 letters] quod graviores & hirmiores erant, sanè [illegible, ~60 letters] Pontificis [illegible, ~30 letters] Regi Christianae pernicie sanè impedire. Qui [illegible, ~50 letters] Concilium indictum imperatoris [illegible, ~80 letters] cum [illegible, ~60 letters] Imperium [illegible, ~70 letters] impedimentis & difficultatibus multis, ut exitus ipse comprobavit.
units.tr: 19. Moreover, they had despised the order of law and that examination of the case which was established in the synodal reports and the decrees of the Holy Fathers. For they dispatched almost all the most weighty matters hastily and superficially. They certainly ought to have consulted the just objections of many most grave Fathers, whom they should not have been taught to flatter, and to have considered the matter with a right conscience, gladly receiving the contradictions, and to have weighed and examined their opinions and reasons, and not neglected them, and so let each be heard. [illegible] ... which were the more grave and serious, [...] of the Pontiff [...] to hinder the ruin of Christendom. Who [...] the Council appointed by the Emperor [...] with [...] the Empire [...] with many impediments and difficulties, as the outcome itself has proved.

units.la: [illegible, ~200 letters] Concilii [illegible, ~50 letters] Legatos [illegible, ~120 letters]
units.tr: [...] of the Council [...] Legates [...]

units.la: Verum antè peractum Imperium, Sanctissime & Sanctorum Patrum, ut tertium & in primum Romanum Imperatorem, Ecclesiam omnium matrem augere ac defendere nos oportet, quod ad sanctam Christi [illegible, ~80 letters] Imperator & Imperatorem [illegible, ~60 letters] Ecclesiam protegere, & eo utique, ut ea a [illegible, ~70 letters] Imperio [illegible, ~40 letters] Germaniam [illegible, ~90 letters] Ecclesiae membrum, parte, & ad Verum Christianorum [illegible, ~60 letters] Hispaniam, Italiam [illegible, ~50 letters] Sanctissimae Ecclesiae reducendam, quae pertinent.
units.tr: But before the Empire is brought to an end, most Holy Father and Fathers of the Holy Church, as the third and first Roman Emperor, we ought to increase and defend the Church, the mother of all, [...] the holy Church of Christ [...] the Emperor [...] to protect the Church, and in such a way that [...] the Empire [...] Germany [...] a member and part of the Church, and to the true Christians [...] Spain, Italy [...] to be brought back to the most Holy Church, which pertain to this.

units.la: Animadvertens, inquam, Imperator, hunc rem esse fundamento, ut quod diu cor humanum, neque lege, neque causa, neque [illegible, ~50 letters] Concilium postulare Tridenti, pollicer se Concilio Tridentino [illegible, ~40 letters] Sanctitatem Vestram, quam semel atque iterum [illegible, ~30 letters] Sanctitatis Vestrae & Ecclesiae filius, maximè cùm [illegible, ~20 letters] pervisceta Domini nostri Iesu Christi, ne magno labore tandiu quaesitam compo-nere reliquasque religionis occasionem praetermittat.
units.tr: Noticing, I say, that the Emperor sees that this matter is at its foundation, that what the human heart has long [...] neither by law, nor by cause, nor [...] to demand the Council at Trent, he promises to the Council of Trent [...] Your Holiness, whom once and again [...] son of Your Holiness and of the Church, especially since [...] the bowels of our Lord Jesus Christ, lest he let slip, after great labour so long sought, the settlement and the remaining opportunity for religion.

units.la: Ex bus à Deo Opt. Max. sibi commissa auxilium ferat, iubeat hos afferto [illegible, ~30 letters] Tridentum revertit, qui locus vitus est Sanctitas Vestrae [illegible, ~60 letters] Concilium Imperatoris, effugatione & assensu Principum, Tridentino [illegible, ~40 letters] Concilium accessissent, se, quam primum illa falli morbi sulpice refrixerit, eaque credi-mus, adeo Sanctitas Vestra ad ipsum Caesari per Nuncios atque Legatos promisit.
units.tr: [...] out of those things committed to him by God, Best and Greatest, he should bring help; he should bid these [...] return to Trent, which place is [...] Your Holiness [...] the Council of the Emperor, with the flight and assent of the Princes [...] had come to Trent, so that as soon as that illness, which was falsely alleged, has cooled, and so we believe, Your Holiness has promised the Emperor through Nuncios and Legates.

units.la: Anno jam ferè elapso, cessante morbo (si quis tam fuit tranquilla & pacata alia ratione tu-tius non nullis Principibus & Statibus Germaniae) denique pollicentur Vestram atque Concilium Tridentinum suscepturos, eas bene reverti, & inde [illegible, ~30 letters] opus, ut coeperunt, ut continuare operatur. Hoc Sanctitas Vestra Imperatoris, certos Legatos Tridentum redire sua autem ac sanctum ea cosmo, [illegible, ~60 letters] regem nullam interpolerunt, rem populo Christiano valde necessariam, & divinum accidit.
units.tr: Now nearly a year having passed, the illness having ceased (if anyone was so tranquil and peaceful by some other means safer for some Princes and States of Germany), at last they promise that Your Holiness and the Council of Trent will take up the matter again, that they will return well, and that from there [...] the work, as they began, to continue. Your Holiness [...] of the Emperor, certain Legates to return to Trent; but they interposed nothing of their own, or of the holy [...] king, a matter very necessary for the Christian people, and it came about by divine will.

units.la: Sed autem tam justae petitioni tempore & occasione nec sinè, quae quidem nunc & citò reddi debet, ulterius nulli[?]ent, quod abhorrendum sanè est: b eo, qui pro hac causa Legatus Christi munere gerit, atque adeo ipsius Domini nostri Iesu Christi vicem repraesentat. Ego Ioannes Lunae Mendoza, nomine piem tissimi & invictissimi Domini mei Caesaris Caroli Romanorum Imperatoris, ceterisque speciali mandato, ac nomine totius Sacri Imperii Regnorum & Dominationum suorum, privatim & publicè Evangelicas requisitiones, monitiones, denuntiationes, & ad Patres Concilii dictum est ad me Tridentum, iterum, sed etiam plenum in hoc tempore Sanctissimo Cardinalium consessu, die Martii, hora ante meridiana, 14. Decembr. & in hunc eundem locum sanctum: Mensis Ianuarii, hora matutina, a Pontifice ad concilia Ioannis, Ecclesiae [illegible, ~20 letters] Martii, in hac ipsa Domini nostri Iesu Christi [illegible, ~50 letters] Ioannes [illegible, ~40 letters] Verum [illegible, ~60 letters] Concilii in Ecclesia Dei [illegible, ~70 letters] 3. Similiter & hos Electores ac Principes ceu nobilcum intercessoies & compositores harum amicè transigendarū rerū causa literis nostr is evocavimus & accersivimus,talib° divina clementia gravaminibus,litibus atq; discordiis,quibus fieri potest,viis,modisq; obviaturi,ac denique, finem imp olituri.
units.tr: But such a just petition must not be deferred any longer, as to time and occasion; it ought to be granted at once, and to refuse it is certainly abhorrent, from him who in this cause bears the office of Christ's legate and in effect represents our Lord Jesus Christ himself. I, Juan de Mendoza, in the name of my most pious and invincible lord, the Emperor Charles, King of the Romans, and by his special mandate and in the name of the whole Holy Empire and all his kingdoms and dominions, both privately and publicly, make the evangelical requests, admonitions and denunciations, and have been summoned to Trent by letter, to the Fathers of the Council, in this most holy assembly of the Cardinals, on the 14th day of December, in the forenoon, and to this same holy place [remaining words illegible in the scan]. Likewise we have summoned and called upon these Electors and Princes, as mediators and arbiters who are to settle these matters amicably, by our letters, so that by every means and method the divine clemency allows we may meet these grievances, disputes and discords, and at last put an end to them.

units.la: 4. Proinde nos,& infrà memorati Principes, Electorr Saxoniæ, &c. hucad dictam diem cum ceterorum Electorum & Principū Legatis pervenimus, videlicet, Archiepiscopi Moguntinensis nomine Daniel Brendel ab Honburck, majoris ædis Canonicus Moguntiæ, Christophorus Matthias Junum Licentiatus Cancellarius,& Petrus Echterus. Archiepiscopi autem Coloniensis nomine Henricus Salisspurgensis,& Franciscus Burghardus, ambo doctores. Archiepiscopi Trevirensis nomine, Joannes de Petra, Primas inter Archidiaconos Trevericos: Philippus Baro in Winnenberg & Beyllstein, ditionis Trevericæ aulæq; Magister,& Felix Hornung Doctor, Cancellarius. Palatini verò Friderici nomine, Ludovicus Comes à Stolberg, Konigstein,& Ruthschefort. Joannes à Dinheim, præfectus in Creucenach, Melchior Drechsel Doctor,& Joan. Koting. Joachimi Marchionis nomine, Adam Trotte Marschalcus, Christophorus Stratius, Timotheus Jung,& Lampertus Distelmeyer, Doctores. Item reverendi & generosi, Ernestus Archiepiscopus Salisspurgensis,&c. Mauritius Echstetensis, & Wolffgangus Pataviensis Episcopi, Albertus quoq; Palatinus Rheni, Dux superioris & inferioris Bavariæ,in persona. Item Episcopi Herbipolensis nomine Henricus Comes à Castel Canonicus,& Hans Zobel. Joannis Marchionis Brandenburgêsis nomine Adrianus Albinus Doctor, Cancellarius, Andreas Zoch Doctor,& Bartholus à Mandelslo, Henrici junioris Ducis Braunsvigensis nomine, Vitus Grummer. Wilhelmi Ducis Juliacensis nomine, Wilhelmus Kettler. Wilhelmus à Hevvenhof, appellatus Ley. Magister curiæ Theodoricus à Schepsted,& Carolus Horstus, Doctores. Philippi Pomeraniæ nomine, Jacobus Zirzevvitz, Doctor & Cancellarius. Et Christophori Ducis Wirtembergensis nomine Johannes Theodoricus à Plenningen, superior Advocatus in Stutgarten, Ludovicus à Ftavvenberg, Advocatus superior in Lauffen. Joannes Henricus Hecklin, & Calpar Behem, ambo Doctores hic cotam nobis comparentes. Quibus cum vocatis transactoribus rem cœpimus tractandam,ac initio dicti Electoris Saxonici,suorumq; conjunctorum postulata & gravamina duobus specialibus scriptis complexa accepimus,eaq; summa diligentia, fideq; perpendentes, quo ad amicè cōponi,& ingruentis belli discrimina,pace,tranquillitate,& concordia firmata,in Sacro Teutonicæ nationis Imperio averti possent. Atque sic tandem post multam longamq; tum scripto tum verbo rerum tractationem agitatam,sequentia media,punctaq; ad Cæsareæ Majestatis beneplacitum,ac Electoris Saxonici,suorumq; confœderarorum assensum ac ratificationem relata sunt,deq; iisdem unanimiter tandem in hunc qui sequitur modum conventum est atque conclusum.
units.tr: 4. Therefore we, and the Princes above named, the Elector of Saxony and others, have come here on the appointed day together with the legates of the other Electors and Princes, namely: for the Archbishop of Mainz, Daniel Brendel von Homburg, canon of the cathedral church at Mainz, Christoph Matthias Junius, licentiate and chancellor, and Peter Echter. For the Archbishop of Cologne, Henry of Salzburg and Francis Burghard, both doctors. For the Archbishop of Trier, John de Petra, first among the archdeacons of Trier; Philipp Baron von Winnenberg and Beilstein, master of the court of the Trier territory, and Felix Hornung, doctor, chancellor. For Frederick the Palatine, Ludwig Count of Stolberg, Königstein and Rutschfort; Johann von Dienheim, prefect at Kreuznach, Melchior Drechsel, doctor, and Johann Koting. For the Margrave Joachim, Adam Trotte, marshal, Christoph Stratius, Timotheus Jung and Lampert Distelmeyer, doctors. Also the reverend and noble: Ernst, Archbishop of Salzburg, etc.; Moritz, Bishop of Eichstätt, and Wolfgang, Bishop of Passau; Albert also, Count Palatine of the Rhine, Duke of Upper and Lower Bavaria, in person. Also for the Bishop of Würzburg, Henry Count von Castell, canon, and Hans Zobel. For the Margrave John of Brandenburg, Adrian Albinus, doctor and chancellor, Andreas Zoch, doctor, and Bartholomew von Mandelsloh. For Henry the Younger, Duke of Brunswick, Vitus Grummer. For William, Duke of Jülich, Wilhelm Kettler; Wilhelm von Hevenhof, called Ley, master of the court; and Dietrich von Schepstedt and Karl Horst, doctors. For Philip of Pomerania, Jakob Zirzewitz, doctor and chancellor. And for Christoph, Duke of Württemberg, Johann Dietrich von Plieningen, chief advocate at Stuttgart, and Ludwig von Flavenberg, chief advocate at Lauffen; Johann Heinrich Hecklin and Caspar Behem, both doctors, appearing here before us. With these named mediators called in, we began to handle the matter; and at the outset we received the demands and grievances of the said Elector of Saxony and his associates, contained in two special writings, and weighing them with the greatest diligence and good faith, so that they might be amicably settled and the dangers of the impending war averted within the Holy Empire of the German nation, with peace, tranquillity and concord secured. And so at last, after a long and extended discussion of the matter both in writing and in speech, the following means and points were reported for the pleasure of His Imperial Majesty and for the assent and ratification of the Elector of Saxony and his confederates; and concerning these, it was at last agreed and concluded unanimously in the manner which follows.

units.la: CAP. I.
units.tr: CHAPTER I.

units.la: Cessio armatæ militiæ,& Philippi Hessorum Landtgravii λύτρωσις seu liberatio.
units.tr: The surrender of the armed forces, and the ransom or release of Philip, Landgrave of Hesse.

units.la: PRIMUM Elector Saxonicus,suiq; belli consortes Principes ac Status hanc compositionem amplectentes à cœptis sumptisq; armis prorsus desistent: suosque paratos & conscriptos milites ad undecimum duodecimumve diem Augusti mensis proximum undiquaq; dimittant, dissipent, atq; discurrere,vel nobis Regi Ferdinando ad petitionem stipemq; nostram adjungi vel admoveri sinant:dentq; omnibus modis operam,in quantum fieri potest,ne quid injuriæ damnive dolo malo Cæsareæ Majestati,nobis,aut ceteris Sacri Imperii Electoribus, Principibus, Statibus,& civitatibus illorū discursu,fusioneq; inferatur, quin ita potius dispersi Cæsareæ Majestati, Sacroq; Imperio obsequêtes segerant permanêantq;, remissis illorum Statuum, civitatum, aliorumq; juramentis, quos hactenus oppugnarunt & obsiderunt,aut sibi aliqua adhæsione & confœderatione subdiderunt, idque vigore transcripti jam hoc in loco patentium literarum exemplaris remissionem illam côtestantium,quemadmodum & earundem,& hujus edicti virtute à suis juramentis protinus liberantur & absolvuntur.
units.tr: First, the Elector of Saxony, together with his fellow-belligerent princes and estates who embrace this settlement, shall wholly desist from the enterprises begun and the arms taken up. They shall discharge, disband and scatter their ready and enrolled soldiers on all sides by the eleventh or twelfth day of the coming month of August, and shall allow them to be dispersed or to be added and joined to us, King Ferdinand, at our request and expense. They shall also take every means, as far as possible, that no wrong or loss be inflicted by fraud, through the dispersal or conflict of their men, upon His Imperial Majesty, upon us, or upon the other Electors, princes, estates and cities of the Holy Empire. Rather, once dispersed, they shall remain and be found obedient to His Imperial Majesty and the Holy Empire; the oaths of those estates, cities and others whom they have hitherto attacked and besieged, or subjected to themselves by some adherence or confederation, are to be remitted, and by virtue of this remission, and of the copy of the open letters transcribed here and attesting it, and of this edict, they shall be immediately released and absolved from their own oaths, just as these others are.

units.la: 2. Interea quoque temporis Philippus Hessorum Landtgravius sancitam Halæ in Saxonia capitulationem(exceptis jam anrea resolutis articulis,puncto de Cassella loquente) ratam de novo habere,ac irrefragabiliter observare debet,adeoque detentionem suam & custodiā haudquaquam vindicare,quin imò Cæsareæ Majestati, Sacroq; Imperio sese Principem per dies vitæ suæ obsequentem exhibere,& ad omnia ista Cæsareæ Majestati formula decenti hoc loci præscripta sufficienter astringere,efficereq; tandem,ut idem à filiis,ditioneq; sua nova literarum obligatione præstituta servetur acteneatur.
units.tr: 2. Meanwhile, Philip, Landgrave of Hesse, shall again hold ratified and irrefragably observe the capitulation agreed at Halle in Saxony (the articles already resolved being excepted, and the point concerning Kassel being reserved). Accordingly he shall in no way claim his detention and custody; indeed, he shall show himself a prince obedient to His Imperial Majesty and the Holy Empire for the rest of his life, and shall bind himself sufficiently, in the becoming form prescribed here, to all these things toward His Imperial Majesty. Finally he shall bring it about that the same is kept and observed by his sons and his subjects, under the new written obligation laid down.

units.la: .3. Similimodo uterque Electorum Saxonicus & Brandenburgensis,Dux item Wolffgangus Palatinus,&c.obligationes quisque suas jam ptidem factas modò renovent,easque scriptas cauriones ad sextum Augusti diem Illustrissimæ Principi Dominæ Mariæ Hungariæ & Bohemiæ Reginæ,viduç, dilectæ sorori nostræ,ejusve præsidenti apud Mechliniam tradantur.
units.tr: 3. Likewise, each of the Electors of Saxony and Brandenburg, and also Duke Wolfgang Palatine, etc., shall now renew their obligations, which were long since made, and deliver those written securities by the sixth day of August to the most illustrious Princess, Lady Mary, Queen of Hungary and Bohemia, our beloved widowed sister, or to her president at Mechelen.

units.la: 4. Econtrà memoratus Landtgravius custodia sua penitus liberetur,& ad dictū Augusti diem undecimum vel duodecimum Rheinfelsium tutò certoq; extra periculum sistetur liber. Jam & ipsa copias suas Cæsarea Majestas diversis in locis in hos Status conscriptas, hanc côpositionem acceptantes haudquaquam producat,aut etiam fundendi seu dimittendi mora moleve ulla gravetur.
units.tr: 4. On the other hand, the said Landgrave shall be wholly released from his custody and shall be presented safely and securely, free and beyond danger, at Rheinfels on the said eleventh or twelfth day of August. His Imperial Majesty herself shall not bring forward her forces, enrolled in various places against these estates who accept this settlement, nor shall she be burdened by any delay in dissolving or dismissing them.

units.la: 5. Cœptam quoque Cassellæ munitionem Imperatoria Majestas Landtgravio clementer perficere concedet.
units.tr: 5. His Imperial Majesty shall graciously grant the Landgrave to complete the fortification of Kassel, already begun.

units.la: 6. Similiter Nassoviensium durante custodia promulgatarum sententiarum executio differatur ac suspendatur, donec liberato Landtgravio amica inter partes tractatio instituì agiq; possit. Casu autem quò minus ea amicabilis progrederetur tractatio, Landtgravio tamè quo ad æquum est, testimonia, literarum documenta, aliaq; necessaria, quæ Advocatorum hucusque defectu, duranteve custodia proferri nequibant de cætero exhibeanturac producantur. Et ita tunc quidem Electores hi, quos causa hæc non contingit, ipsimet, seu consiliarii eorum, atque adhuc alii sex mitiùs parriales Imperii Principes, ex quibus ambæ partes quindenos Cæsareæ Majestati intra mensem, posteaquà Landtgravius fuerit liberatus, nominatim indicent atque proponant. Ex quibus amborum partium nuncupatus Majestas Cæsarea tres Principes deligat, (inter autem sex illos ad minus tres sint seculares) in persona propria, aut etiam ad idem deputati consiliarii, tanquam Cæsareani Commissarii, gravamina illa & exceptiones, contra prædictas latas sententias & executionem debito modo, ac ut decet, recognoscant atque revideant, ecquid acta tempore custodiæ Landtgravii exhibita rursus assumenda, Sententiæ quoque latæ ac Processus super ejusmodi propositis & adhuc dum proponendis gravaminibus, exceptionibusq; differendi ac suspendendi sint nec ne, cognoscant, & quid Juris sit, promulgent. Atque hæc quidem amica tractatio & decisio ad summum intra biennium post conclusionem & datum compositionis seu transactionis hujus certò expediatur ac exequatur.
units.tr: 6. Likewise, during the continuing custody, the execution of the sentences promulgated against the Nassauers shall be deferred and suspended, until, once the Landgrave is freed, a friendly negotiation between the parties can be instituted and carried on. In case the friendly negotiation should not proceed, nevertheless the Landgrave shall, as is just, henceforth produce and exhibit the testimonies, documents of letters and other necessary things, which could not be brought forward until now, owing to the lack of advocates or during the custody. Then indeed these Electors, whom this cause does not concern, themselves or their counsellors, together with six other princes of the Empire, more mildly partial, from whom each party shall name fifteen to His Imperial Majesty within a month after the Landgrave has been freed, shall nominate and propose them. From these fifteen named by each party, His Imperial Majesty shall choose three princes (of whom at least three of those six shall be secular), either in person or through counsellors deputed for this purpose as Imperial commissioners; they shall examine and review, in the proper and fitting manner, those grievances and exceptions against the said sentences passed and their execution; they shall also determine whether the acts exhibited during the Landgrave's custody are to be taken up again, and whether the sentences passed and the proceedings concerning such grievances and exceptions, and those yet to be proposed, are to be deferred and suspended or not, and shall declare what is law. And indeed this friendly negotiation and decision shall be certainly completed and carried out at the latest within two years after the conclusion and date of this composition or agreement.

units.la: 7. Cæteris verò punctis & articulis omnibus inter memoratos Electorem Principem Saxoniæ, & Wilhelmum Lantgravium Hessiæ propositis tamdiu, quousque reliqua communiter proposita gravamina expediantur, dilatis atque suspensis.
units.tr: 7. All other points and articles proposed between the said Elector, Prince of Saxony, and William, Landgrave of Hesse, shall meanwhile be deferred and suspended until the remaining grievances proposed in common have been settled.

units.la: 8. Administrator item ordinis Teutonici, atque Dux Henricus Brunsvigensis, aliiq; Lantgravium praeteriti Schmalkaldensis belli causa impetentes, aut porrò impetituri, cessent quoque & quiescant, donec prædicta gravamina resolvantur.
units.tr: 8. Likewise the Administrator of the Teutonic Order, and Duke Henry of Brunswick, and others who attack, or shall further attack, the Landgrave on account of the former Schmalkaldic war, shall also cease and rest until the aforesaid grievances are resolved.

units.la: 9. Etiam nova superius memorata gravamina, quæ durante Lantgravii custodia, in Judicio Imperiali, aliasve adversus eum præsumpta fuerte, simul cum eorum exceptionibus, ab Electoribus & Principibus harum controversiarum intercessoribus proximo Comitio, uti decet, recognoscantur revideanturque, ac idem Lantgravius prout necesse est, audiatur: In iisdem quoque quod æquum & justum est decernatur, neque interea tamen in Camera Imperialis Judicio procedatur.
units.tr: 9. Also the new grievances mentioned above, which during the Landgrave's custody were presumed in the Imperial Court or otherwise against him, together with their exceptions, shall at the next Diet be examined and reviewed by the Electors and princes who are intercessors in these controversies, as is fitting, and the same Landgrave, as is necessary, shall be heard. In these matters too, what is equitable and just shall be decreed; meanwhile, however, no proceeding shall take place in the Imperial Chamber Court.

units.la: CAP. II.
units.tr: ## CHAPTER II.

units.la: Religionem, pacem, & justitiam concernentia.
units.tr: ## Concerning religion, peace, and justice.

units.la: VERUM atqui alios sequentes articulos quod concernit, ab Electore Saxoniæ, suisq; conjunctis in hac pacificatione propositis, & quidem primò de Religione, de pace, & justitia, Majestas Cæsarea sponsionem gratiosam nuper ad oppidum Linsium factam, extunc dato responso fideliter præstabit, & ut intra dimidii anni spatium Comitia habeantur, in quibus dein qua via, quibusq; modis, nimirum seu Generali seu Nationali Concilio, aut Colloquio, vel communi etiam Imperii conventu Religionis discordiæ commodè atque compendio sopiantur, hæq; ad unionem Christianam redigantur, atque ejusmodi conciliatio Religionis ab omnibus Sacri Imperii Statibus, mediante Majestatis suæ ordinaria ope præsidioq; pertractetur.
units.tr: BUT as for the following articles, as far as they concern what the Elector of Saxony and his associates proposed in this pacification, and first of all concerning religion, peace, and justice: His Imperial Majesty will faithfully keep the gracious promise recently made at the town of Linz, and from the time of the reply given, he will see to it that a Diet is held within half a year. At that Diet, by what way and what means (namely, by a General or National Council, or by a colloquy, or by a common assembly of the Empire) the discord over religion may be conveniently and expeditiously settled, and the matter brought back to Christian unity; and such a reconciliation of religion is to be carried through by all the Estates of the Holy Empire, with the ordinary help and protection of His Majesty.

units.la: 2. Initio autem Comitiorum ad præparationem cõcordiæ delectus placidarum prudentumq; personarum constituatur, utriusque Religionis æquali numero cum Mandato deliberandi, quibus modis ejusmodi conciliatio atque concordia institui commodè posset, absque Electorum Principum præjudicio tamen hujus delectus ergò.
units.tr: 2. At the opening of the Diet, a delegation of calm and prudent persons shall be appointed to prepare for concord, with an equal number from each religion, and with a mandate to deliberate by what means such a reconciliation and concord could conveniently be established, without prejudice, however, to the Electors and Princes for the sake of this delegation.

units.la: 3. Et quidem interea temporis nec Cæsarea Majestas, neque nos, ac Electores, Principes, & S. Imperii Status quempiam ex Augustanæ confessionis Statibus, propter religionem, vi factove, aut aliàs contra ejus conscientiam ac voluntatem cogere, aut ea de causa vi bellove petere, vel invadere, vel oppugnare aliquè, eive damnū aliquod inferre sive per mandata, sive alio quovis modo ipsum gravare vel etiā contemnere, feremus, sed suæ Religioni fideiq; quietè & pacificè stare, cadereq; sinentes.
units.tr: 3. In the meantime, neither His Imperial Majesty, nor we, the Electors, Princes, and Estates of the Holy Empire, will allow anyone of the Estates of the Augsburg Confession to be compelled, by force or deed, or otherwise against his conscience and will, on account of religion; nor will we, on that ground, attack, assail, or storm him with force or war, nor inflict any damage upon him, nor burden or even despise him by mandates or in any other way; but he shall be allowed to stand and fall quietly and peacefully in his own religion and faith.

units.la: 4. Ob hoc quoq; bellū Status omnes Augustanæ confessionis cæteros Sacri Imperii Statusartiquæ religionis Ecclesiasticos & seculares similiter Religionis suæ, Ceremoniarum, constitutionum, rerum immobilium & mobilium, ditionum, subditorum, reditnum, censuum, superioritatum, & Jurisdictionum causa non gravent, sed pacificè tranquilleq; illis uti fruiq; sinant, nec vi factove, seu aliàs maligne contra eos quicquam præsumant: Verùm enimvero juxta nostras & Sacri Imperii ordinationes, constitutiones, edicta, decreta, Recessus factæ pacis, singuli erga singulos ordinario jure justitiaq; contenti sint, sub proximè renovatæ pacificationis pœna.
units.tr: 4. For this same reason, all the Estates of the Augsburg Confession shall likewise not molest the other Estates of the Holy Empire, ecclesiastical and secular, of the other religion, on account of their religion, ceremonies, constitutions, immovable and movable property, territories, subjects, revenues, taxes, superiorities, and jurisdictions; rather they shall allow them to enjoy these peacefully and quietly, and shall not presume to do anything against them by force or deed, or otherwise maliciously. Rather, each shall be content, toward each other, with ordinary right and justice under our and the Holy Empire's ordinances, constitutions, edicts, decrees, and recesses of the established peace, under the penalty of the recently renewed pacification.

units.la: 5. Quicquid verò in Comitiis illis à communibus Statibus unà cū Cæsareæ Majestatis ordinario præsidio concludetur ac statuetur, in posterum quidem & rectè & firmiter servetur, nequeim contrarium, aliave via diversum agatur.
units.tr: 5. Whatever shall be concluded and enacted at those Diets by the common Estates together with the ordinary presidency of His Imperial Majesty, shall in future be rightly and firmly observed, and nothing shall be done to the contrary or in a different way.

units.la: 6. Omne autem quod dictis induciis adversatur, adversarive censetur, in nihilo deroget illis, aut quicquam imminuet, idq; à Cæsarea Majestate, nobisitem, & Electoribus Principibus, ac Statib9 respectivè, sufficienter, in quantum fuerit necesse, vigore hujus compositionis seu transactionis cautii, confirmatumq; sit: Prætor quoque Camerae Judicii & Confessores de iisdem induciis certificentur, mediisq; eorum juramentis, eisdem pareant & obsequantur: Implorantibus etiam partibus non attento eo, cujusnam sint religionis, necessarias & legitimas ferant suppetias: formulam quoque cum primis jurisiurandi Deum & sancta Evangelia, confessoribus, aliisque personis & Partibus deinceps liberam permittendo.
units.tr: 6. Anything that opposes, or is judged to oppose, the said truce shall in no way detract from it or diminish it; and this shall be sufficiently confirmed by His Imperial Majesty, by us, by the Electors, Princes, and Estates respectively, as far as necessary, by virtue of this composition or agreement, and by a guarantee. The Praetor of the Chamber Court and the adherents of the Confession shall likewise be informed of this truce, and by their oaths they shall obey and comply with it. Also, when the parties implore aid, the necessary and lawful help shall be given without regard to which religion they belong to; and the formula of the oath, with God and the Holy Gospels, shall be left free for the adherents of the Confession, other persons, and the parties from now on.

units.la: 7. In suffragiis quoq; dandis rogandisq; æqualitas servetur, æquum jus partibus, nec iniquum reddendo & conservando: Similiter & in præsentandis Assessoribus, aliisq; pacis & justitiæ articulis hac tractatione placuit, si quod operæprecium ac deliberatione dignum in dicasterii Cameræ constitutione apparuerit, quandoquidem eadem constitutio communi Statuum assensu, Comitioque Imperii sancita est, non etiam nisi per Cæsaream Majestatem, Statusq; communes rebus ita ferentibus ordinaria via, utpote visitationibus, aliisq; mediis mutari tolliq; posse. In qua re nos, Electorum Legati, comparentes Principes, & absentium nuncii recipimus nos, ac consentimus omnem diligentiam, operamq; præstituros, ne qua partium, in Religionis negocio suffragiorum, imparitate sibi præ cæteris metuat, partialitate remota: Augustanæ quoq; Confessionis consortes à Cæsareo Cameræ judicio nō excludantur, aliaq; gravamina, si quæ comperiantur, ex æquitate removeantur: & hæc quidem omnia proximis Comitiis explicentur.
units.tr: 7. In giving and taking votes, equality shall be observed, giving and preserving an equal right to the parties and not an unfair one. Likewise, in the presenting of assessors and the other articles of peace and justice, it has been agreed in this negotiation that, if anything worth the effort and deliberation should appear in the constitution of the Chamber Court, since that constitution was sanctioned by the common consent of the Estates and the Diet of the Empire, it can nonetheless be changed and abolished only by His Imperial Majesty and the common Estates, in the ordinary way, as circumstances require, namely by visitations and other means. In this matter we, the Electors' envoys, the Princes present, and the envoys of those absent, accept and agree that we will take every care and effort so that no party may fear, in matters of religion, an inequality of votes to its disadvantage compared with the others, partiality being set aside. Likewise the fellow adherents of the Augsburg Confession shall not be excluded from the Imperial Chamber Court, and other grievances, if any are found, shall be removed in fairness. And all these things shall be explained at the next Diet.

units.la: 8. Cæterum & hoc nos unà Electorum Legatis, comparentibus Principibus & absentiū nunciis apud Cæsaream Majestatem, amanter, reverenterque cum reverentia petivimus, uti ejus Majestas puncta illa plus necessaria, inter quæ & articuli præsentationis, & ne Augustanæ cōfessionis conjuncti a judicio Cameræ, ut supra dictum est, excludantur, continentur: ex plenitudine Majestatis suæ Cæsareæ ad provehendam, retinendamq; pacem & concordiam in Imperio, quantocyus fieri posset, re-solvere dignaretur.
units.tr: 8. Moreover, we, together with the envoys of the Electors, the Princes present, and the envoys of those absent, have also lovingly and reverently petitioned His Imperial Majesty, with due respect, that His Majesty, from the fullness of his imperial power, would deign to resolve, as quickly as possible, those points which are most necessary, among which are the articles of presentation and that the adherents of the Augsburg Confession not be excluded from the Chamber Court, as stated above, in order to promote and maintain peace and concord in the Empire.

units.la: CAP. III.
units.tr: CAP. III.

units.la: Germanicæ nationis libertatem contingentia.
units.tr: The matters touching the liberty of the German nation.

units.la: Quo d'ad gravamina, quæ Germanicæ nationis libertati contraria irrepsisse, ne dicam intruisse, videntur, inter Electoris Saxonici articulos alio quoq; scripto comprehensa attinet: Volebamus quidem una cum Electoribus, Legatis, Principibus præsentibus, & absentium nuncijs prompti paratiqueac minimè gravati, illos ipsos, appendicesque suos singulatim protinus & speci-fice pro amicabili compositione tractanda suscepisse, nisi intellexissemus à Cæsareæ Majestatis ad hanc tractationē lectis destinatisq; consiliariis, ipsius Majestatem talium gravaminū hactenus bona ex parte insciū esse atq; ignarū, quamobrem de iis mandata dare consiliariis nequivisse: Adhæc, ea ipsa gravamina tanta, tamq; varia esse & prolixa, econtrà vero tempus hoc perexiguum indictæ diei, ut ipli Electori quoq; Saxonico, suisq; conjunctis, donec hæ res omnes, quemadmodū necessitas postulat, explicentur, copias suas alendo, immodicos sumptus atq; impendia non solùm pariet, verumetiam superioritatibus hinc inde, miserisq; subditis gravissimo maximoq; damno sit futura.
units.tr: As for the grievances which seem to have crept in, not to say forced their way in, contrary to the liberty of the German nation, they are included in the articles of the Elector of Saxony, and also in another writing. We would indeed have been willing, together with the Electors, the Legates, the Princes present and the envoys of the absent, to readily and gladly take up those articles and their appendices, one by one and specifically, for friendly settlement; but we understood that His Imperial Majesty, since the counsellors chosen and appointed for this negotiation had been read out, was for the most part until now uninformed and ignorant of such grievances, and therefore could not give instructions to the counsellors about them. Moreover, those grievances are so great, so varied and so lengthy, while the time set for the appointed day is very short, that, until these matters are all explained, as necessity demands, the Elector of Saxony himself and his associates, by maintaining their forces, would not only incur immense expense and outlay, but would also be the cause of very grave and great loss to the territorial lords on every side and to their wretched subjects.

units.la: 2. Proinde hujuscemodi gravaminum resolutionem ad proxima Comitia, aliumve Imperii conventum hac vice rejicientes, spe bona ex Linfica consensione per Cæsareæ Majestatis consiliarios præbita suffulti, consilium inituram esse, quo sacri Imperii & Statuum publicis & privatis causis consuletur, cùm jam in eo tota Majestas sua elaboret, ut & apud suâ Majest. Germanicus Senatus constituatur, & Germanicæ res causæq; per Germanos tractentur ac disponantur, ita, ut omnibus placeat, omnibusq; fiat satis. Quādoquidem Germanicæ nationi ceu dilectæ suæ patriæ tam bene velit, ut haud quidem diminutam eam aut debilitatam, verùm multò magis quantum fieri potest auctam, amplificatam atq; conservatam cupiat, quæ quidem hoc tempore pollicitatio undiquaque cum gratiarum actione accepta est.
units.tr: 2. Accordingly, deferring the settlement of such grievances to the next Diet or to another assembly of the Empire on this occasion, and supported by the good hope of the Linz agreement offered through the counsellors of His Imperial Majesty, they will undertake a plan by which the public and private affairs of the Holy Empire and of the Estates will be provided for, since His Majesty is already labouring over this, that a German Senate may be established at his court, and German affairs and causes be treated and arranged by Germans, so that it may please all and satisfy all. Since he wishes so well to the German nation as to his beloved fatherland, that he desires it not diminished or weakened, but far more increased, enlarged and preserved as far as possible; this promise has now been received everywhere with thanksgiving.

units.la: 3. Ne autem Elector Saxonicus, suiq; adjuncti metuant hanc tractationem sponsam neglectū iri, aut posthaberi, sine debito non decisam, debeimus nos filiusq; noster dilectus, Maximilianus Rex, Electores quoq; Principes, & Status sacri Imperii in manus sumere propolita gravamina, atque Cæsareæ Majestati ea offerre, coque eniti atq; conari promovendo, ut quoad æquitatis fundamento insistant, visa quoque ut decet, Aurea Bulla, ac aliis sacri Imperii ordinationibus, constitutionibus, veterebusq; laudatis Germanicæ nationis consuetudinibus omnia probè resolvantur ac perficiantur. Reliqua verò ad Cæsaream Majestatem non proprie spectantia gravamina, sed à quibusdam sacri Imperii Statibus & membris privatim allata sunt, aut quæ ipsi inter sese Status disceptant, de forma fortè ac modo communis consultationis tractationisve, aut aliam ob rem quampiam controversam, æqua & illaut supra ponitur, Cæsareæ Majestatis tanquam Capitis eorum consilio præsidioque proximi Comitiii initio proponi vult atq; absolvi, gratiosa nimirum hac piaq; Majestatis suæ pollicitatione, ut quæ adipsius Majestatem in specie proprieque faciunt, in iis sic se tam gratioso bonoque animo ac voluntate gesturum esse, ut communes perspicianr Status, summa ejus Majestatem cupiditate controversias omnes ut decet, velle atque expetere compositas, & Rempub. privato emolumento longè præstatam fore, cæteraque omnia ita suscipi, institwiq; ut omnibus Statibus ex æquo & bono quàm plenissimè fiat satis.
units.tr: 3. Lest the Elector of Saxony and his adherents fear that this negotiation will be neglected or set aside, and left undecided without due settlement, we, and our beloved son Maximilian the King, the Electors, Princes and Estates of the Holy Empire, ought to take up the proposed grievances and offer them to His Imperial Majesty, and strive and labour, by promoting them, that, as they rest on the foundation of equity, and with the Golden Bull and the other ordinances and constitutions of the Holy Empire and the approved ancient customs of the German nation duly considered, everything may be properly resolved and carried through. The remaining grievances, which do not properly concern His Imperial Majesty but have been brought forward privately by certain Estates and members of the Holy Empire, or which the Estates dispute among themselves, concerning the form or manner of common consultation or deliberation, or for some other controverted reason, are, as is set out above, to be proposed and settled at the beginning of the next Diet with the counsel and help of His Majesty, as head of them; in that gracious and pious promise of His Majesty, that in those matters which concern himself specifically and properly, he will so act with such a gracious and good spirit and will, that the common Estates may plainly see that he, with the greatest eagerness, wishes and seeks that all controversies be settled as is fitting, and that the commonwealth will be far advanced to the benefit of all, and that all other matters are so undertaken and carried out that all Estates may be fully satisfied, in equity and in goodness.

units.la: 4. Porrò ad articulum Regis Franciæ Oratorum veniendo, media quædam ac puncta pacis publicæ cōstituendæ, aliorumq; negociorum quorundam prætendentium: ita se habet, ut cùm, quæ publicæ sunt pacis in Germanica natione, solùmodò Imperatoriam Majestatem nos, & Electores, Principesac Status sacri Imperii, neminemq; præterea concernant, & jam isti contentus harumme rerum, utpote publicæ pacis sanciendæ, aliorumque gravaminum amovendorum causa sit institutus, idcirco nulla jam alia tractatione fore opus existimatur.
units.tr: 4. Moving on further to the article of the envoys of the King of France, concerning certain means and points for establishing public peace, and certain other pretended affairs: the position is that, since what concerns public peace in the German nation touches only His Imperial Majesty, ourselves, the Electors, Princes and Estates of the Holy Empire, and no one else, and since that agreement has been instituted for the purpose of sanctioning public peace and removing other grievances, it is therefore judged that no further negotiation on this is needed.

units.la: 5. Atqui verò privata Regis Franciæ negocia quod spectat, Elector Saxonicus vigore Linfen-sis decreti, seu recessus cum dicto Rege aut suis Oratoribus, si id necedū factū est, dein tractare poterit; Si quid idem Rex forte privatarum causarum adversus Cæsar. Majest. prætendit, poterit & iisdem actiones seu postulationes nobis exhibere, Cæsar. Majestati porrò per nos transmittendas, se suamque voluntatem desuper declaraturi.
units.tr: 5. As far as the private affairs of the King of France are concerned, the Elector of Saxony, by virtue of the Linz decree or recess with the said King or his envoys, if this has not yet been done, may then treat them; if the same King should perhaps put forward any private causes against His Imperial Majesty, he may also present actions or demands to us, which we will transmit to His Imperial Majesty, declaring his own will and that of His Majesty on the matter.

units.la: CAP. IV.
units.tr: CAP. IV.

units.la: Securitatem eorum, qui huic bello conjuncti, & à Cæsarea Majestate Banniti sunt, concernentia.
units.tr: Concerning the security of those who are joined to this war and have been outlawed by His Imperial Majesty.

units.la: QUANTUM attinet eos, qui belli præteriti causa, Banno & indignatione Cæsareæ Majestatis nexi sunt ac proscripti, huic militiæ junčti, nihil equidem intermisimus ipsi, simul cum Electoribus, Legatis, præsentibus principibus, & absentium nuncis, quò minus fidelissimè amare simeq; & humiliter rem hanc promoveremus, tandemque impetraremus, ut Albertus Comes à Mansfelt pariter cum filiis suis, Comes item Rheni, Christophorus Comes ab Aldenburg, Johannes Dominus ab Heideck, Friderichus à Reyfenberg, Georgius à Reckenrod, Sebastianus à Schertle, &c. aliiq; ejus belli causa indignatione incidentes à terris & Comitatibus suis bonisque ab Oetio Henricus Palatinus, Wolffgangus Princeps ab Anhalt, item Braunsuigenses Principes ac nobiles, creterique omnes & singuli superioris & inferioris Status, nominati & innominati, ob bellum prætextum intimulati, ac eidem dum adhærent, meru solicitudineque liberati, rursus in Cæsareæ Majestatis gratiam fidemque admitterentur & reciperentur, nunc hujus quidem compositionis vigore reconciliari assumuntur: hoc pacto tamen conditione, ut de cætero Cæsareæ Majestati, sacroque Imperio justæ debitamque præstent ac servent obedientiam, neque adversus ejus Majestatem, nos, aut Imperium militent, priusquam in hic articulus communibus gravaminibus inferendus resolvatur, cui deinceps transactioni resolutionique stabitur.
units.tr: As far as concerns those who, on account of the past war, are bound and proscribed by the ban and indignation of His Imperial Majesty, and who have joined this military undertaking, we ourselves, together with the Electors, the envoys, the princes present, and the messengers of those absent, have left nothing undone to promote this matter most faithfully and humbly, and finally to obtain that Albert, Count of Mansfeld, together with his sons; likewise the Count of Rhine, Christopher, Count of Aldenburg; John, Lord of Heideck; Frederick of Reifenberg; George of Reckenrod; Sebastian of Schertel, etc.; and the others who have fallen under the indignation on account of this war, be restored from their lands, counties and goods by Oetting; that Henry, Count Palatine, Prince Wolfgang of Anhalt, likewise the Princes and nobles of Brunswick, and all and each of the other estates, higher and lower, named and unnamed, accused on the pretext of the war, and freed of the burden and anxiety so long as they adhere to it, be readmitted and received again into the grace and faith of His Imperial Majesty. Now, by virtue of this composition, they are taken back into reconciliation, on this condition only: that henceforth they render and keep due and proper obedience to His Imperial Majesty and the Holy Empire, and do not bear arms against His Majesty, us, or the Empire, until this article is settled among the common grievances, to which transaction and resolution they shall then abide.

units.la: 2. Jam & reconciliati, inquam; gratiam recepti, ut supra dictum est, ac isto jam tempore extra Germanicæ nationis Imperium in Gallia, aliisve locis agentes, & contra Cæsaream Majestatem militantes intra sex septimanas proximas post Datum hujus compositionis se declarent, moxque ab eo tempore adversus Imperatoriam Majestatem, Imperiique Status non militent, neque se ejusmodi militiæ mancipent, utendove præbeant, tum & ad summum bimestri proximo in Germaniam revertantur, aut hac ipsa reconciliatione & gratia omnino destituantur oporter.
units.tr: 2. Furthermore, those already reconciled, I say, received into grace as stated above, and now acting outside the Empire of the German nation, in France or other places, and bearing arms against His Imperial Majesty, must declare themselves within six weeks next after the date of this composition; and from that time onward they must not bear arms against the Imperial Majesty or the estates of the Empire, nor give themselves to such military service or lend their aid to it; and at the latest within the next two months they must return to Germany, or else they must be wholly deprived of this reconciliation and grace.

units.la: CAP. V.
units.tr: CAP. V.

units.la: Abrogatio actionum omnium illorum, quibus hoc bello damnum datum est.
units.tr: Repeal of all actions by which damage was done in this war.

units.la: CUMQUE durante bello pleræq; novationes sint obortæ, quidam etiam Electores, Principes, Status & civitates bonis rebusq; suis privati damnum passi sint, omnia Principes hujus militiæ occupata vel dominia, vel territoria, vel oppida, villasve, homines ve, hæc quidem cuncta Statibus iis, quibus antea fuerant, restituant, juramentaque ipsis ut supra dictum est, adhæsionesque remittant, atq; de illis absolvant ac liberent, salvis quoque liberarum civitatum Privilegiis & libertatibus, quas deinceps retinebunt.
units.tr: Since during the course of the war many innovations have arisen, and certain Electors, Princes, Estates and cities have suffered loss in their goods and property, the Princes who have been occupied in this campaign are to restore to those Estates to whom they formerly belonged all the lordships, territories, towns, villages and men that they have seized, and to remit the oaths and adhesions to them, as stated above, and to absolve and free them from these; the privileges and liberties of the free cities, which they will henceforth retain, remaining intact.

units.la: 2. Vicissim Cæsarea Majestas publicæ pacis, aliorumq; damnorum evitandorum respectu, omnes & singulas actiones, impetitionesque, quas Status hi & civitates, sive etiam privatæ personæ in belli hujus Principes, eorumque hinc inde conjunctos & adhærentes datorum occasione prætendere possent, abrogat de plenaria Cæsareæ Majestatis suæ potestate, operam nobiscum & cum cæteris Imperii Statibus datura, omniq; studio & gratia eò enituta, ut æquis mediis viisq; ratio ineatur, quò dana illa perquam graviter accepta, Statibus læsis, civitatibus item & subditis absq; hujus militiæ conjunctorum Statuum ope impendioq;, ne qua porrò succedentibus motibus occasio detur, & firma pax tranquillitasq; retineatur.
units.tr: Conversely, His Imperial Majesty, out of regard for public peace and for avoiding other losses, by the plenary power of his Imperial Majesty abrogates all and single actions and claims which these Estates and cities, or even private persons, might bring forward against the princes of this war and their allies and adherents on account of the damage done. He will work with us and with the other Estates of the Empire, and with all zeal and goodwill, so that a fair means and method may be found by which those losses, received most grievously by the injured Estates, cities and subjects, may be borne without the aid and expense of the Estates joined in this campaign, so that no occasion be given for further disturbances to follow, and a firm peace and tranquillity be maintained.

units.la: CAP. VI.
units.tr: CHAPTER VI.

units.la: Ad Palatinum Otthenricum pertinentia.
units.tr: Pertaining to the Palatine Otto Henry.

units.la: QUODQUE Ducis Ottohenrici Palatini nomine, peræque suos Legatos supplicatum rogatumque est, nempe ut Romanæ Imperatoriæ Majestati commendaretur, fida nos pariter cum Electoribus, Legatis, comparentibus Principibus & absentium nuncis promotione apud prædictam Cæsaream Majestatem præstitimus, atque effecimus, ut sua sibi ditio in Principatu Neuburgi suis cum pertinentiis maneat.
units.tr: And since, in the name of Duke Otto Henry, Palatine, his envoys likewise made a supplication and request, namely that he be commended to His Imperial Roman Majesty, we, together with the Electors, the envoys, the Princes present and the messengers of those absent, have in faithful manner promoted and secured this before the said Imperial Majesty, so that his dominion, in the Principality of Neuburg with its appurtenances, remains to him.
