units.la: 3. Tridenti est, inquam, indictum Concilium generale omnium consensu. Legati, Cardinales missi, primùm Reverendiss. Panutius, Moronus & Polus adfuere, qui vices Pontificis repraesentarent: Oratores Imperatoris, admodum Illustrissimus & religiosissimus Episcopus Arrebatensis, Illustrissimus vir Dominus de Granvella, & ego Jacobus de Mendoza. Sed nondum visum fuit Sanct. Vestrae, apparet ex secunda Bulla Sanct. Vestrae, tempus satis idoneum ad inchoandum Concilium, post aliquot dies iterum à Sanct. Vestra missi Sedis Apostolicae Legati, Cardinales, Reverendus de Monte, Reverendus Sanctae Crucis, & iterum Reverendus Polus: rursum Oratores, Ego Jacobus Mendoza, & Illustris vir Franciscus Toledo absens: accesserunt nonnulli aliorum Principum itidem Oratores, nonnulli erant in itinere, multarum nationum Episcopi etiam ab ultimis terris convenere magnis impensis magno labore inchoatum est, & petitum ab omnibus Christianis Concilium, & causa religionis & reformationis morum in eo tractari coepta.
units.tr: 3. Trent was, I say, appointed as a general council with the consent of all. The legates, cardinals sent for the purpose, first the most reverend Pannucio, Morone and Pole, were present, to represent the place of the Pontiff. The orators of the Emperor were the most illustrious and most religious bishop of Arras, the illustrious lord de Granvelle, and I, James de Mendoza. But it did not yet seem to Your Holiness, as appears from the second bull of Your Holiness, a sufficiently suitable time to begin the council. After some days, Your Holiness again sent the legates of the Apostolic See, the cardinals: the most reverend de Monte, the most reverend of Santa Croce, and again the most reverend Pole. Again there were orators: I, James Mendoza, and the illustrious man Francis Toledo, who was absent. Some other princes' orators also came, and some were on the way. Bishops of many nations came even from the furthest lands, at great expense and great labour. The council was begun, a general council was requested by all Christians, and the cause of religion and the reform of morals began to be treated in it.

units.la: 4. Eodem quoq; tempore bellum adversus hostes & S. Imperii violatores Imperator gerebat, in quo capiendo potissimum tuendae & amplificandae religionis, idq; interveniente Sanct. Vestra, ratio habita est, ita ut quos ratione flectere non poteramus, armis cogeremus. Cùm res esset in hoc negotio, causa morum (quae totis viribus & consilio indigebat, ad quam ... absolutè prorsus peragedam Sacra Majestas & Germaniae Ordines à retrò Pontificibus & Sanctitate. Vestra jam antea temedium tam crebrò flagitaverat) sed frigidè nimis & vix tentata. Deinde virtute Imperatoris pacata Germania, in qua recuperanda Sanct. Vestrae & sacrosancto Concilio muniendum incumbebat, maxima spe & certitudine eorum adventus, tum etiam, qui hucusq; Concilium reverat, & eorum qui in tam necessario religionis negotio adhuc occupati, Imperatori adjutores erat.
units.tr: 4. At the same time the Emperor was waging war against the enemies and violators of the Holy Empire. In carrying this war through, the chief aim was the protection and enlargement of religion, and this with the intervention of Your Holiness was taken into account, so that those whom we could not bend by reason we might compel by arms. While the matter stood thus, the cause of morals (which needed all our strength and counsel, and which His Sacred Majesty and the estates of Germany had long before asked the Pontiffs and Your Holiness to settle absolutely, so often and so urgently) was handled far too coldly and barely attempted. Then, Germany having been pacified by the valour of the Emperor, the recovery of Germany and the strengthening of the most holy council rested on the greatest hope and confidence in the arrival of those who had hitherto revered the Council, and of those who, still occupied in so necessary a matter of religion, were helpers to the Emperor.

units.la: 5. Ecce Reverendissimi afferri Legati tumultuosè, praeter omnium expectationem, Sanctitate Vestra (quod ipsi dicunt) inscia & inconsulta, levissima sanè causa procurata & confecta de translatione Concilii retulerunt ad Patres, nullo consultandi, sed neque cogitandi spatio dato, ita ut pridie proposuerint, postridie decreverint, perendie discesserint cum multis Patribus, atq; iis quidem tum temporis vel unius ferè Italicae nationis, vel ante adeptum Episcopatus nomen in Italia degentibus.
units.tr: 5. Behold, the most reverend legates came back in a tumult, contrary to everyone's expectation. They reported to the Fathers, on a very slight cause (as they themselves say) without the knowledge or consent of Your Holiness, that the council was to be transferred, and this was arranged and carried through. No time was given for consultation, or even for thought, so that they proposed it the day before, decreed it the next day, and departed the day after, with many Fathers. And these were at that time mostly of one Italian nation alone, or men who, before obtaining the name of bishop, lived in Italy.

units.la: 6. Huic consilio, Sanctissime Pater, plures Episcopi, magnae fidei & auctoritatis viri, quibus religionis & morum causa cordi erat, tanquam callido nimis & immaturo, Christianeq; Reip. periculoso, contravenêre, planeq; & publicè, inspirante eis Spiritu sancto, cujus sanè causa imprimis agi debebat, tum translationem propositam, tum Legatorum assertorum & Patrum, qui eos secuti sunt, injustam esse translationem Concilii, velleq; se manere Tridenti, libero & legitimo Cocilii loco, publicè protestati sunt.
units.tr: 6. Against this plan, most holy Father, several bishops, men of great faith and authority, to whom the cause of religion and morals was dear, openly and publicly opposed it as too crafty and premature, and dangerous to the Christian commonwealth. Inspired by the Holy Spirit, by whom the cause above all ought to have been pursued, they publicly protested both that the proposed translation was unjust, and that the assertions of the legates and of the Fathers who followed them were unjust, and that they wished to remain at Trent, the free and lawful place of the council.

units.la: 7. Inter haec Imperator, dum Episcoporum congregatio Bononiae manet, hostem ad Albim devicto, Saxonia provincia superata, duobus belli Ducibus, altero pugna, altero deditione captis, pacata provinciis Germania, arduo & periculosissimo bello solus cofecit: nec destitit saepius San. Vest. per Nuncios, per Legatos Sedis Apostolicae, per Illustriss. virum Joannem Vegam, per me & Majestatis suae apud S. V. Oratores, & ante & post confectum bellum, magnis & continuis precibus solicitare, juberet Patres, qui Bononiae persistunt, ad Concilium Tridentinum redire, eandemq; ipsam admonere, praevideat, quot scandala, dissidia, pericula, impedient Christianae religioni, si jam coeptum Concilium Tridenti nō continuetur & absolvatur.
units.tr: 7. Meanwhile the Emperor, while the congregation of bishops remained at Bologna, having defeated the enemy at the Elbe and conquered the province of Saxony, with two leaders of the war taken, one in battle and one by surrender, and Germany pacified in its provinces, carried through alone a hard and most perilous war. Nor did he cease, by frequent and continual prayers, to urge Your Holiness both before and after the war was finished: through nuncios, through the legates of the Apostolic See, through the illustrious man John Vega, and through me and His Majesty's orators before Your Holiness. He asked that the Fathers who remain at Bologna be ordered to return to the council of Trent, and he admonished them to consider how many scandals, dissensions and dangers they would bring upon the Christian religion if the council, now begun at Trent, were not continued and brought to completion.

units.la: 8. Comitia interim Augustae Germanis indixit, quae quidem adhuc celebrantur. In his libero, spontaneo, generali totius Germaniae Ordinum & Statuum, praeterea omnium Civitatum consensu, petente Imperatore, decretum est, Germanos omnes ad Concilium Tridenti convocatum venturos, ut ea, super quibus indictum fuit, tractentur, & sacrosanctae Concilii auctoritate decidantur: Ipsam sacrosanctam Tridentinam Synodum se suscepturos, idq; prorsus & absque ulla conditione se praestituros, Imperatori sunt polliciti.
units.tr: 8. Meanwhile he summoned a diet of the Germans at Augsburg, which is still being held. There, by the free, spontaneous and general consent of all the orders and estates of Germany, and moreover of all the cities, at the Emperor's request, it was decreed that all Germans would come to the council convened at Trent, so that the matters for which it was announced might be treated and settled by the authority of the holy council. They promised the Emperor that they would themselves accept the most holy Synod of Trent, and that they would present themselves for this absolutely and without any condition.

units.la: 9. Legavit Imperator Oratorem ad Sanctitatem Vestram, Illustrissimum & Reverendissimum Christophorum Madrucium, Cardinalem & Principem Tridentinum, quò S. Majestatis & Serenissimi Romani Regis Ordinumque S. Imperii nomine Sanctitas Vestra pium hoc & sanctum Germaniae Concilium indiceret, supplicaret, juberet Patres, qui Bononiae agunt, ad Concilium Tridenti inchoatum reverti: hortaretur & admoneret, ut honestissimam & necessariam occasionem, tot laboribus & periculis tam diu quaesitam, nunc demum partam, susciperet & amplecteretur, in qua & Patres cum dignitate Tridentum redire, & religionis causa generali Christianorum consensu, ipsorumq; Germanorum, quorum potissimum gratia ipsa sacrosancti Synodus Tridenti convocata fuerat, tractari & confici, & sacrosanctae Sedis Apostolicae auctoritas magna cum Pontificii nominis Majestate, & ipsius Sanctitatis Vestrae immortali gloria augeri posset: idq; non privatim solum, sed publicè faceret in Reverendissimorum Cardinalium consessu.
units.tr: 9. The Emperor sent as his orator to Your Holiness the most illustrious and most reverend Christopher Madruzzo, cardinal and prince of Trent. In the name of His Majesty, of the most serene King of the Romans, and of the estates of the Holy Empire, he was to request and beseech Your Holiness to announce this pious and holy German council, and to order the Fathers who are at Bologna to return to the council begun at Trent. He was to exhort and admonish Your Holiness to take up and embrace the most honourable and necessary opportunity, so long sought with so many labours and dangers and now at last gained. In this way the Fathers could return to Trent with dignity, and the cause of religion could be treated and concluded by the general consent of Christians, and of the Germans themselves, for whose sake the holy Synod had been convened at Trent. The authority of the holy Apostolic See could thus be increased, with great majesty for the pontifical name and immortal glory for Your Holiness. He was to do this not only privately but publicly, in the assembly of the most reverend cardinals.

units.la: 10. Praeterea jussit me, qui Senas ad componendas illius Reipub. res venerarum, idem negotium praestare. Quod si Sanctitas Vestra dilationem aut excusationem aliquam interponeret, neq; praesentem occasionem suscipteret, hujusce rei, ut tam justae petitionis, promptissimiq; erga Christianam religionem Majestatis suae animi, tam publicè quàm privatim vos ipsos Reverendissimos Cardinales, & omnes omnium Principum Oratores, qui Romae agunt, testes vocarem, praecepit.
units.tr: 10. Moreover, he ordered me, who had been sent to Siena to settle the affairs of that commonwealth, to perform the same task. And if Your Holiness were to interpose some delay or excuse and not take up the present opportunity, he commanded me to call to witness, both publicly and privately, you yourselves, the most reverend cardinals, and all the orators of the princes who are at Rome, concerning this matter, and concerning so just a petition and the most ready disposition of His Majesty's mind toward the Christian religion.

units.la: 11. Praeterea jussit Procuratores & Consiliarios suos, qui Bononiae expectabant de ea re respondere, & à Patribus ibi congregatis, & à Sanctitate Vestra, si unquam vel ipsi Patres vel Sanctitas Vestra recusassent, vel dilationem aliquam interposuissent in generali Patrum coetu, nomine Majestatis suae protestari, iniquam fuisse translationem, & omnia inde facta & secuta ab ipsis Patribus affectata, & nulla esse atq; futura fore. Factum est, beatissime Pater, post requisitiones privatas etiam publicè primū à ReveReverendissimo Tridentino die nona Decembris: deinde à me die 14. ejusdem mensis, horâ [?] ridiana, in hoc Reverendissimorum Patrum consessu cum debita humilitate instanter [?] idq; per viscera, & per sanguinem Domini nostri Jesu Christi: tempus tamen Sanctitas Vestra [?] posuit ad consulendos super responso Patres, qui Bononiæ sunt; qui quidem non dissimulecta sive (ut ipsi dicunt) translationi consilium dedere vanum, subdolum & captiosum, in gravissimam [?] ligionis & universalis Ecclesiæ dissidium, scandalum & detrimentum.
units.tr: 11. Moreover, he ordered his procurators and counsellors, who were waiting at Bologna for a reply in this matter, to protest in his name, both to the Fathers gathered there and to Your Holiness, that if ever the Fathers themselves, or Your Holiness, refused, or interposed any delay in the general assembly of the Fathers, the translation was unjust, and all things done and following from it by the Fathers were presumptuous, and were and would be null. This was done, most blessed Father, after private requests, and now publicly: first by the most reverend Tridentine on the ninth day of December, then by me on the fourteenth day of the same month, at the hour [?], in this assembly of the most reverend Fathers, with due humility and urgently, and that by the bowels and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ. Yet Your Holiness set a time to consult the Fathers who are at Bologna about the response. They indeed did not conceal that the counsel they gave concerning the translation (as they themselves say) was vain, deceitful and captious, and would bring the gravest dissension, scandal and loss upon religion and the universal Church.

units.la: 12. Sanctitas autem Vestra id consilium approbasse, illorumque sententiam suscepisse quodammodo visa est, illegitimam secessionem Tridentinam, periculosissimam sane & perniciosam Reipublicæ Christianæ, translationis vocabulo, congregationemque seu illegitimum Conventum Bononiensem generalis Concilii nomine appellans: tantùmque ei congregationi auctoritatis in suis ad Reverendissimum Cardinalem de Monte, Episcopum Prænestinum, & ad vos qui adestis literis, & suo ad Imperatorem relationi tribuere videtur, quantum Episcopi prænominati auctoritate propria sibi ipsis arrogareausi sunt.
units.tr: 12. Your Holiness, however, seems to have approved that counsel and in some way to have adopted their opinion, calling the illegitimate secession from Trent, very dangerous and pernicious to the Christian commonwealth, by the name of translation, and the gathering or illegitimate assembly at Bologna by the name of general council. In your letters to the most reverend Cardinal de Monte, Bishop of Palestrina, and to you who are present, and in your report to the Emperor, you seem to grant that assembly as much authority as the aforementioned bishops had presumed to arrogate to themselves by their own authority.

units.la: 13. Præterea responsum ad Cæsarem dat dilatorium & illegitimum, præsenti occasioni non pertinens, ineptum & inconveniens. Quid enim magis alienum, quàm in gravissima causa religionis & Spiritus sancti, & causæ cognitionem anteverte re, & sententiam ferre, antequam judicium sibi deferatur: & his qui ægrotabant, & sanari erant, qui remedium detrectare videbantur, qui nunc religionem, qui morum reformationem, qui unitatem publicarum dissensionum petunt à Sanctitate Vestra, (Concilium enim petunt Tridenti, ubi coeptum fuerat, continuari & absolvi, quod omnium bonorum causam futurum certissimè credunt) præstantissimam medicinam tergiversationibus & ambagibus producere & denegare.
units.tr: 13. Moreover, the reply he gives to the Emperor is dilatory and unlawful, irrelevant to the present occasion, inept and inappropriate. For what could be more out of place than, in a most grave matter of religion and of the Holy Spirit, to anticipate the hearing of the case and pass judgment before the judgment has been referred to you? And to hold out and deny the most excellent remedy, through evasions and circumlocutions, to those who were sick and wanted to be healed, who seemed to refuse the remedy, and who now seek from Your Holiness the restoration of religion, the reform of morals, and the unity of the public dissensions. (For they ask that the Council be continued and concluded at Trent, where it had begun, which they most certainly believe will be to the advantage of all good men.)

units.la: 14. Et cùm probationem causarum translationis à perspicuis & religiosissimis & probatissimis testibus sumi, conveniens sit, in hac ipsa testibus parum inter se convenientibus, nullius auctoritatis de plebe hominibus fidem adhibere: Imperatoris autem & Regis Romani, & Principum Status Germaniæ, qui in publicis Comitiis congregati sunt, qui & per Sanctæ Sedis Apostolicæ Cardinalem atque eundem Sacri Imperii Principem, Sanctitatem Vestram certiorem faciunt, de hoc tanto pio Germanorum proposito atque decreto fidem in dubium vertere, quod ex ipsorum & Sanctitatis Vestræ responso, cùm publicè tum privatim dato, intelligi potest.
units.tr: 14. And since proof of the grounds for the translation ought to be drawn from clear, most religious and most approved witnesses, it is fitting that no faith be given to men of the common people, whose testimony agrees poorly among themselves. But the Emperor and King of the Romans, and the Princes of the Estates of Germany, who have assembled in the public Diet, and who through the Cardinal of the Holy Apostolic See and the same Prince of the Holy Empire inform Your Holiness, call into doubt the faith due to this so great pious purpose and decree of the Germans, as can be understood from the reply given by them and by Your Holiness, both publicly and privately.

units.la: 15. Multa alia à me præretermittuntur, Sanctissime Pater, quæ tempore & loco, si opus fuerit, in hac causa dicentur. Quid præterea desiderabamus à Germanis, quid ab eis petebamus, toties à Celsitudine repetitis itineribus, tot impêsis, tot laboribus, maximo & ancipiti suscepto bello, atque collecto Perdet omnes labores hos S.V. pro religione susceptos: perdet optimam & præstantem sanandæ rei tuendæque religionis occasionem, & perdet religionis causam, admonitus & requisitus. Id verò certissimum Concilii universale, ob causas gravissimas & maximè necessarias Tridenti congregatum, Vest. Sanctitate, flagitante Imperatore, Principibus Christianis assentientibus, petentibus Germanis, convenientibus Episcopis, jam coeptum, nisi summa urgentiaque necessitate, præcedentibus tractatibus, & diligentissima discussione, servato juris ordine, consensu omnium Patrum, aliò mutari, neque legitimè posse nec licere.
units.tr: 15. Many other things are passed over by me, most holy Father, which, if need be, will be said in this cause at the proper time and place. What else did we desire from the Germans, what did we ask of them, so often, by repeated journeys of the Highness, at such expense and such toil, after undertaking a great and dangerous war? It will lose all these labours undertaken by Your Holiness for religion; it will lose the best and most excellent opportunity of healing and safeguarding the state of religion, and it will lose the cause of religion, though admonished and urged. Most certainly, a universal Council, gathered at Trent for very grave and most necessary causes, begun already with Your Holiness urging, the Emperor pressing, the Christian princes assenting, the Germans asking and the bishops coming together, cannot lawfully or rightly be moved elsewhere, unless in a case of highest and most pressing necessity, with prior discussions and most diligent examination, the order of law being observed, and with the consent of all the Fathers.

units.la: 16. Sæpe enim tralationes callido & præcipiti consilio sine causa factæ, in causa esse solent magno religionis periculo, magnis in Repub. Christiana turbis & dissensionibus, interdum populi Christiani perniciosa divisione Concilia dissolvantur. Causa autem tam subitæ translationis nulla fuit, arrepta, quæ se primùm obtulit. Occasionem vos Reverendissimi asserti Legati, ut à me dictum est & reliqui Patres, fecistis, id quod jam pridem meditari fueratis. Febres enim nescio quas & ærius vitium causati, affectatum & procuratum quorundam medicorum, sed præcipuè ancillarum & coquorum, nimiorum hominum, testimonium recitantes, Tridento præcipites discesserunt. nempe & tunc & deinceps apertissimè patuit, nullam exitiosæ vanæque formidinis causam.
units.tr: 16. For transfers made without cause, by crafty and hasty counsel, are often wont to be the cause of great danger to religion and great disturbances and dissensions in the Christian commonwealth, and sometimes Councils are dissolved with the harmful division of the Christian people. But there was no cause for so sudden a transfer; whatever presented itself first was seized upon. You, the most reverend Legates aforesaid, as has been said by me and by the other Fathers, made the occasion, which you had long been planning. For, alleging I know not what fevers and some airy ailment, and reciting the testimony of certain physicians, put on and arranged, but chiefly of maidservants and cooks, men of no account, you headlong departed from Trent. Indeed, then and afterwards it became most plainly evident that there was no cause for a deadly and vain fear.

units.la: 17. Præterea ut nulla fuerit ratio discedendi, Vestram Sanct. in hac præterensa causa confulerunt, cùm tam parvi temporis morâ nihil periculi esset allatura. Neque enim tam repentina res erat exitus morbi, quem causati fuerant, comprobavit. Inconsulta autem Sanctitas Vestra, discesserunt Episcopos, fassi estis, & Sanctitas Vestra postmodùm affirmavit. Cui quidem Sanctitatis Vest. tanto nio multum certè fidei & auctoritatis detrahunt vestræ ad Reverendissimum de Monte literæ, responsiones ad Cæsarem datæ.
units.tr: 17. Moreover, even if there had been some reason for leaving, they consulted Your Holiness in this matter, which, as they said, would bring no danger in so short a delay. For the outcome of the illness they alleged was not so sudden as to make such haste necessary, as the event proved. But the bishops departed without consulting Your Holiness, as you yourselves confessed, and Your Holiness afterwards affirmed it. Your letters to the most reverend de Monte, and the replies given to the Emperor, certainly detract much from the faith and authority of Your Holiness' so great name.

units.la: 18. Imperatore quoque consulto & assentiente, id facere debuissent, cui curæ sunt & tutela omnia universalia Concilia, atque id ex munere officii Augustalis: cujus quanta sit in Concilus manifestum est. Verùm tanta fuit Legatorum assertorum festinatio & simulatio, ut necipti consulere, nec eos qui dicebant, Sanctitatem Vestram & Imperatorem priùs per Sanctam certiores fieri oportere, audiendos putarint. Cumq; Imperator ipse pro tuenda & amplificanda religione, pro Ecclesia, pro Concilio laboraret, ipsi vano & inani timore simulato, Imperator consulto, abscesserunt. Atqui sæpe aliàs Imperator per Oratores suos cùm ipsos asserentes Legatos, tuam Sanctitatem Vestram admonuerat, se neque translationi Concilii, sed neque suspensioni aut vacationi tè vel expresse assentiri posse.
units.tr: 18. They ought also to have done this with the Emperor's counsel and assent, to whom the care and protection of all universal Councils belong, and this by virtue of the duty of the Imperial office, whose extent in councils is manifest. Yet so great was the haste and pretence of the Legates aforesaid that they neither sought counsel nor thought that those who said that Your Holiness and the Emperor ought first to be informed through the Holy See should be heard. And while the Emperor himself was labouring for the defence and extension of religion, for the Church and for the Council, they, with a feigned empty fear, departed with the Emperor deliberately kept in the dark. And yet, at other times, the Emperor, through his own envoys, had often admonished Your Holiness, through these very Legates asserting it, that he could give no express assent either to the transfer of the Council or to its suspension or interruption.

units.la: 19. Præterea juris ordinem contempserant, & eam causæ cognitionem, quæ in Synodalibus lationibus Sanctorum Patrum sanctionibus institutæ est. Remenim ferè omnium gravissimam ferè sanè & leviter confecerunt. Debuerant certè justas multorum gravissimorum Patrum, qui haudquaquam assentari docti, rei ex recta conscientia consulebant, contradictiones libenter ad re, eorumque sententias ac rationes animadvertere atque examinare, ac non ipsis neglectis, audire. [illegible, ~40 letters] fenteatiæ, quod graviores & firmiores erant, sanè omnes sacerdotes [illegible, ~60 letters] Petri, cum multis aliis Episcoporum Christi & Regis Christiani sententiam impedire. Quia [illegible, ~50 letters] Germaniæ pro ponendis & ordinandis rebus, ad maximè fieri potest, de de Concilio [illegible, ~30 letters] Germanorum [illegible, ~20 letters] ad Concilium veteri & proceffionibus fortiter [illegible, ~40 letters] vt exitus [illegible, ~25 letters].
units.tr: 19. Furthermore, they had despised the order of law and that manner of hearing a cause which has been established by the sanctions of the Holy Fathers in the synodal decrees. For they dispatched almost all the most grave matters hastily and lightly. They certainly ought to have considered in good conscience the just objections of many most grave Fathers, who, being learned and in no way inclined to flatter, consulted the matter in good conscience; they ought willingly to have attended to those objections, and to have examined their opinions and reasons, and to have heard them, not neglecting them. [illegible] ...the opinions, because they were weightier and firmer, certainly all the priests [illegible] of Peter, together with many other bishops of Christ and Christian kings, to impede the opinion. Because [illegible] of Germany, for setting forth and ordering affairs, as far as it can most be done, concerning the Council [illegible] of the Germans [illegible] to the Council of old and with processions bravely [illegible] that the outcome [illegible].

units.la: Ob haec ergo [illegible, ~30 letters] ad Ecclesiæ delegationes, quam Germanorum Germaniæ, Locum fuisse Consiliorum ac Ecclesiastico, quam quidem [illegible, ~60 letters] Conciliorum & Concilium, quod est Tridenti Concilium pro re publica & alii iussus, [illegible, ~50 letters] Conciliorum, Cæsaris Iesu Christi, ne magno labore tandem quæritur cum pœnitentiæ fugam emperet ex tali corrigamus, ad eundem Ecclesiam, quam in habitatur, sed ætatis ita tantum Concilium eum fuit Sanctissimo Concilii consultatione.
units.tr: Therefore, for these reasons, [illegible] to the delegations of the Church, which of the Germans of Germany, there was a place of councils and ecclesiastical...; of councils and of the Council, which is the Council at Trent for the commonwealth and others ordered, [illegible] of councils, of Caesar, of Jesus Christ, lest after great labour one should at last seek, when he avoids repentance, from such a state we correct, to the same Church in which he dwells, but so only the Council was for him with the most holy consultation of the Council.

units.la: Animadvertens, inquam, Imperator, hunc recessum [illegible, ~20 letters] tractam, neque lege, neque ratione, neque causa, neque concilio [illegible, ~30 letters] perturbare præterea totam Germaniam, ad quam hæc potissimum causa pertinet, Concilium postulare Tridenti, polliceri se Concilio Tridentino affuturum, Sanctitatem Vestram, quam semel atque iterum offensus est, quod quam sanctitatis Vestræ & Ecclesiæ filius, maximè coërcitur debita humilitate & Christi membrorum per viscera Domini nostri Iesu Christi, ne magno labore tandiu quæritur cum pœnitentiæ occasionem præterinitat.
units.tr: Noticing, I say, the Emperor, this withdrawal [illegible] handled, neither by law, nor by reason, nor by cause, nor by counsel [illegible] to disturb moreover all Germany, to which this cause chiefly pertains, to demand a Council at Trent, to promise that he would be present at the Council of Trent, Your Holiness, by whom he has been offended once and again, who, as a son of Your Holiness and of the Church, is most restrained by due humility and by the bowels of our Lord Jesus Christ, lest after great labour one should at last seek the occasion of repentance and let it pass.

units.la: Ob hæc ergo Deo Opt. Max. sibi commissis auxilium feratis, jubeat suos ad Patres Legatos, ibi exire, qui recesserunt sine mora Tridentum reverti, qui locus vilis est Sanctitati Vestræ, qui ab Imperatore & liberi, ipsi atque invictissimi & pientissimi Imperatoris tutatur, quod et Caesaris Conciliorum Imperatoris, et Iesu Christi Ecclesiæ, ut decet ac necessarium est, ad Concilium Ecclesiæ, quod Concilium ex Imperatoris et Principum Tridenti inchoatum, quod ibi, et Ecclesiæ proseguntur: quod nullo pacto recusare possunt, & sancti jam antiqui pollicitis tuis, ut Concilium accesserunt, se, quam primum, ab illis morbi se pœnitentia recitare fierent, ut essent, ut Sanctitas Vestra id ipsum Cæsari per Nuncios & Legatos promisit.
units.tr: For these reasons, then, to God, the Best and Greatest, bring help to those committed to you; let them order their Legates, who withdrew without delay, to go out there and to return to Trent, which place is dear to Your Holiness, and which is protected by the Emperor, the most invincible and most pious Emperor, as is fitting and necessary, to the Council of the Church, which Council was begun at Trent by the Emperor and the Princes, and is there and by the Church continued. This they cannot refuse in any way; and the holy men of old, by your promises, as they came to the Council, [declared that] as soon as possible they would be freed from that sickness of repentance, so that they might be, as Your Holiness promised the same to the Emperor through Nuncios and Legates.

units.la: Anno jam ferè elapso, cessante morbo (si quis fuit) & tranquillitate, aliquot sunt in Principibus & Statibus Germaniæ, qui deinde pollicentur [illegible, ~20 letters] rebus, & quod conditione aut prætextu Synodum sanctam Tridentinam, qui non revertuntur, ut quo modo Civitas Ecclesiæ urbis ut ceperant, ut continuo opera bellorum ad Sanctam Vestram Legatos Tridentum redire, [illegible, ~30 letters] Concilium ex authoritate & imperio Caesaris, neque ab omnibus [illegible, ~20 letters] Ecclesiæ, ex inter politos, sive populo Christiano, tale ecclesiasticum, & erunt suspicioni [illegible, ~10 letters].
units.tr: Now that nearly a year has elapsed, the sickness having ceased (if there was any) and tranquillity restored, some of the Princes and Estates of Germany, who then promised [illegible] matters, and on what condition or pretext the holy Council of Trent, which they do not return to, as the city of the Church, as they had undertaken, that continually by the works of wars, to Your Holiness the Legates should return to Trent, [illegible] the Council by the authority and command of the Emperor, nor by all [illegible] of the Church, among the polity, or the Christian people, such an ecclesiastical [council], and they will be an object of suspicion [illegible].

units.la: Sed quæ tam iustæ petitioni tempore & occasione nec illi se, quæ quidem mea sit, ad idem rediturus, ut nolueritis, quod abhorrendum sit, est abjiciendum quod aliud intuendum est, qui iudicat sequi gratia nostra Concilio, atque adeo ipsius Domini nostri Iesu Christi vices repræsentans. Ego Iacobus Iohannes, nomine plenissimo & invictissimi Domini mei Caroli Quinti Romanorum Imperatoris, ex speciali mandato ac nomine totius Sacri Imperii Regnorum & Dominorum, [illegible, ~30 letters] privatim & publicè Evangelicas æquitatis, tranquillitatis, dicta Christi Conciliorum, & de, cum sanctis Ecclesiæ ad Concilium conscriptum, dic Mercurii hora antemeridiana, 4. Decemb. & [illegible, ~20 letters], hora pomeridiana, 27. eiusdem Decemb. præsente eo Ecclesiæ Patrum deputatio Sanctissimo Papæ Pio, eodem Pontifice. Sanctorum & Consiliarii Imperatoris Majestatis, pactum in generali sua Ecclesiæ tantum protestor, dicit enim Ecclesiam sanctam seu conventionem nullum Ecclesiæ diligentiam, & [illegible, ~60 letters] Ecclesiæ Dei indicatur, aperte sanctum, ac [illegible, ~40 letters] populis Christianis, fidei [illegible, ~30 letters] Ecclesiæ & Concilia [illegible, ~30 letters]. 3. Similiter & hos Electores ac Principes ceu nobilcum intercessiones & compositores harum amicè transfigendarū rerū causa litteris nostris evocavimus & accersivimus, talib° divina clementia gravaminibus, litibus atq; discordiis, quibus fieri potest, viis, modisq; obviaturi, ac denique, finem imponi-turi.
units.tr: But since such a just petition, at a time and on an occasion that ... I, who am to return to the same matter, should not refuse, which is to be abhorred, must be set aside; another point must be considered: he who judges that our grace follows the Council, and so represents the very place of our Lord Jesus Christ. I, Jacob John, in the full name and by the special mandate and in the name of the most unconquered lord, my lord Charles the Fifth, Emperor of the Romans, and of the whole Holy Empire, of the kingdoms and lords, [illegible] privately and publicly, the Evangelical [matters] of equity and tranquillity, the sayings of Christ and of the councils, and concerning the holy Church, as written for the Council, on Wednesday in the morning hour, 4 December, and [illegible] in the afternoon hour, 27 December of the same month, the deputation of the Fathers being present, with Pope Pius of the same name. Of the saints and counsellors of His Imperial Majesty, I protest in his general [assembly] only; for he says that the holy Church, or the assembly, does not [admit] any diligence of the Church, and [illegible] is declared the Church of God, openly holy, and [illegible] to Christian peoples, [illegible] of the faith, of the Church and of the councils [illegible]. 3. Likewise we have summoned and invited these Electors and Princes, as intercessors and mediators, by our letters, for the sake of settling these matters amicably; and by the divine clemency we shall meet, by whatever means and ways are possible, the grievances, lawsuits and discords, and finally bring them to an end.

units.la: 4. Proinde nos, & infrà memorati Principes, Elector Saxoniæ, &c. hucad dictam diem cum exterorum Electorum & Principū Legatis pervenimus, videlicet, Archiepiscopi Moguntinensis nomine Daniel Brendel ab Honburck, majoris ædis Canonicus Mogūtiæ, Christophorus Matthias Jurium Licentiatus Cancellarius, & Petrus Echterus. Archiepiscopi autem Coloniensis nomine Henricus Salisburgensis, & Franciscus Burghardus, ambo doctores. Archiepiscopi Trevirensis nomine, Joannes de Petra, Primas inter Archidiaconos Trevericos: Philippus Baro in Winnenberg & Beylstein, ditionis Trevericæ aulæq; Magister, & Felix Hornung Doctor, Cancellarius. Palatini verò Friderici nomine, Ludovicus Comes à Stolberg, Konigstein, & Ruthschefort. Joannes à Dinheim, præfectus in Creucenach, Melchior Drechsel Doctor, & Joan. Koting. Joachimi Marchionis nomine, Adam Trotte Marischalcus, Christophorus Straiius, Timotheus Jung, & Lampertus Distelmeyer, Doctores. Item revetendi & generosi, Ernestus Archiepiscopus Salisburgensis, &c. Mauritius Echstetensis, & Wolffgangus Pataviensis Episcopi, Albertus quoq; Palatinus Rheni, Dux superioris & inferioris Bavariæ, in persona. Item Episcopi Herbipolensis nomine Henricus Comes à Cattel Canonicus, & Hans Zobel. Joannis Marchionis Brandenburgensis nomine Adrianus Albinus Doctor, Cancellarius, Andreas Zoch Doctor, & Bartholus à Mandelslo, Henrici junioris Ducis Braunsvigensis nomine, Vitus Grummer. Wilhelmi Ducis Juliacensis nomine, Wilhelmus Kettler. Wilhelmus à Hevvenhof, appellatus Ley. Magister curiæ Theodoricus à Schepsted, & Carolus Horstus, Doctores. Philippi Pomeraniæ nomine, Jacobus Zitzewitz, Doctor & Cancellarius. Et Christophori Ducis Wirtembergensis nomine Johannes Theodoricus à Plenningen, superior Advocatus in Sturgarten, Ludovicus à Fravvenberg, Advocatus superior in Lauffen. Joannes Henricus Hecklin, & Caspar Behem, ambo Doctores hic coram nobis comparentes. Quibus cum vocatis transactoribus rem cœpimus tractandam, ac initio dicti Electoris Saxonici, suorumq; conjunctorum postulata & gravamina duobus specialibus scriptis complexa accepimus, eaq; summa diligentia, fideq; perpendentes, quo ad amicè cōponi, & ingruentis belli discrimina, pace, tranquillitate, & concordia firmata, in Sacro Teutonicæ nationis Imperio averti possent. Atque sic tandem post multam longamq; tum scripto tum verbo rerum tractationem agitatam, sequentia media, punctaq; ad Cæsareæ Majestatis beneplacitum, ac Electoris Saxonici, suorumq; confœderatorum assensum ac ratificationem relata sunt, decq; iisdem unanimiter tandem in hunc qui sequitur modum conventum est atque conclusum.
units.tr: 4. Therefore we, and the Princes above named, the Elector of Saxony, etc., have come to the said day together with the legates of the foreign Electors and Princes, namely: on behalf of the Archbishop of Mainz, Daniel Brendel von Homburg, canon of the cathedral of Mainz, Christoph Matthias, licentiate in law, chancellor, and Peter Echter. On behalf of the Archbishop of Cologne, Henry of Salzburg and Francis Burghard, both doctors. On behalf of the Archbishop of Trier, John von der Petra, first among the archdeacons of Trier; Philip, Baron of Winneburg and Beilstein, master of the court of the Trier domain; and Felix Hornung, doctor, chancellor. On behalf of Frederick the Palatine, Ludwig Count of Stolberg, Königstein and Rossfort; John von Dienheim, prefect at Kreuznach; Melchior Drechsel, doctor; and John Koting. On behalf of the Margrave Joachim, Adam Trott, marshal; Christoph Strauss, Timotheus Jung, and Lampert Distelmeyer, doctors. Likewise the reverend and noble: Ernest, Archbishop of Salzburg, etc.; Maurice, Bishop of Eichstätt, and Wolfgang, Bishop of Passau; also Albert, Count Palatine of the Rhine, Duke of Upper and Lower Bavaria, in person. Likewise on behalf of the Bishop of Würzburg, Henry Count of Kattel, canon, and Hans Zobel. On behalf of John, Margrave of Brandenburg, Adrian Albinus, doctor, chancellor; Andreas Zoch, doctor; and Bartholomew von Mandelsloh. On behalf of Henry the Younger, Duke of Brunswick, Vitus Grummer. On behalf of William, Duke of Jülich, Wilhelm Kettler; Wilhelm von Hevenhof, called Ley, master of the court; and Dietrich von Schepstedt and Karl Horst, doctors. On behalf of Philip of Pomerania, Jacob Zitzewitz, doctor and chancellor. And on behalf of Christoph, Duke of Württemberg, Johann Dietrich von Plieningen, chief advocate at Stuttgart; Ludwig von Frauenberg, chief advocate at Lauffen; John Henry Hecklin and Caspar Behem, both doctors, appearing here before us. With these mediators called in, we began to treat the matter, and at the beginning we received the demands and grievances of the said Elector of Saxony and his associates, comprised in two special writings; and weighing them with the greatest diligence and good faith, so that they might be amicably settled, and the dangers of the impending war averted, and peace, tranquillity and concord established in the Holy Empire of the German nation. And so at last, after a long and extended treatment of the matters, both in writing and by word of mouth, the following means and points were referred to the pleasure of His Imperial Majesty and to the assent and ratification of the Elector of Saxony and his confederates; and on these, unanimously, at last, it was agreed and concluded in the manner that follows.

units.la: CAP. I.
units.tr: CHAPTER I.

units.la: Cessio armatæ militiæ, & Philippi Hessorum Landtgravii λύτρωσις seu liberatio.
units.tr: The surrender of the armed forces, and the ransom [λύτρωσις] or liberation of Philip, Landgrave of Hesse.

units.la: PRIMUM Elector Saxonicus, suiq; belli consortes Principes ac Status hanc compositionem amplectentes à cœptis sumptisq; armis prorsus desistent: suosque paratos & conscriptos milites ad undecimum duodecimumve diem Augusti mensis proximum undiquaq; dimittant, dissipent, atq; discurrere, vel nobis Regi Ferdinando ad petitionem stipemq; nostram adjungi vel admoveri sinant: dentq; omnibus modis operam, in quantum fieri poterit, ne quid injuriæ damnive dolo malo Cæsareæ Majestati, nobis, aut cæteris Sacri Imperii Electoribus, Principibus, Statibus, & civitatibus illorum discursu, fusioneq; inferatur, quin ita potius dispersi Cæsareæ Majestati, Sacroq; Imperio obsequentes gerant permaneantq;, remissis illorum Statuum, civitatum, aliorumq; juramentis, quos hactenus oppugnarunt & obsiderunt, aut sibi aliqua adhæsione & confœderatione subdiderunt, idque vigore transscripti jam hoc in loco patentium literarum exemplaris remissionem illam cōtestantium, quemadmodum & earundem, & hujus edicti virtute à suis juramentis protinus liberantur & absolvuntur.
units.tr: FIRST, the Elector of Saxony, and the other princes and estates who are his companions in the war, accepting this settlement, shall wholly desist from the arms they have begun and taken up. They shall dismiss, disband and scatter their soldiers, both those ready and those enlisted, on all sides by the eleventh or twelfth day of the coming month of August, or allow them to disperse, or to be added or transferred to us, King Ferdinand, at our request and expense. They shall use every means, as far as possible, to ensure that no harm or loss is inflicted through the dispersal and gathering of those troops, whether by fraud or otherwise, upon His Imperial Majesty, upon us, or upon the other Electors, princes, estates and cities of the Holy Empire. Rather, once dispersed, they shall conduct themselves and remain obedient to His Imperial Majesty and the Holy Empire, with the oaths of those estates, cities and others which they have attacked and besieged, or subjected to themselves by some adherence or confederation, remitted. This shall be done by virtue of the copy of the open letters transcribed here, which attest that remission, and by the power of these letters and of this edict, they are at once freed and absolved from their oaths.

units.la: 2. Interea quoque temporis Philippus Hessorum Landtgravius sanctam Halæ in Saxonia capitulationem (exceptis jam antea resolutis articulis, puncto de Cassella loquente) ratam de novo habere, ac irrefragabiliter observare debet, adeoque detentionem suam & custodiā haudquaquam vindicare, quin imò Cæsareæ Majestati, Sacroq; Imperio sese Principem per dies vitæ suæ obsequentem exhibere, & ad omnia ista Cæsareæ Majestati formula decenti hoc loci præscripta sufficienter astringere, efficereq; tandem, ut idem à filiis, ditioneq; sua nova literarum obligatione præstituta servetur acteneatur.
units.tr: 2. Meanwhile, Philip, Landgrave of Hesse, must again hold as ratified the holy capitulation made at Halle in Saxony, with the articles already resolved set aside (the point concerning Kassel excepted), and must observe it without fail. He shall in no way claim his detention and custody as a right. Rather, he shall present himself as a prince obedient to His Imperial Majesty and the Holy Empire for the rest of his life, and shall sufficiently bind himself to all these matters by the fitting formula prescribed here for His Imperial Majesty. He shall also bring it about that the same is kept and observed by his sons and his territory, by a new written obligation laid down.

units.la: 3. Simili modo uterque Electorum Saxonicus & Brandenburgensis, Dux item Wolffgangus Palatinus, &c. obligationes quisque suas jam ptidem factas modò renovent, easque scriptas cautiones ad sextum Augusti diem Illustrissimæ Principi Dominæ Mariæ Hungariæ & Bohemiæ Reginæ, viduq, dilectæ sorori nostræ, ejusve præsidenti apud Mechliniam tradantur.
units.tr: 3. In the same way, each of the Electors of Saxony and Brandenburg, Duke Wolfgang Palatine, etc., shall now renew the obligations each has long since made, and deliver those written securities by the sixth day of August to the most illustrious Princess, Lady Mary, Queen of Hungary and Bohemia, our beloved widowed sister, or to her president at Mechlin.

units.la: 4. Econtrà memoratus Landtgravius custodia sua penitus liberetur, & ad dictū Augusti diem undecimum vel duodecimum Rheinfelsium tutò certoq; extra periculum sistetur liber. Jam & ipsa copias suas Cæsarea Majestas diversis in locis in hos Status conscriptas, hanc cōpositionem acceptantes haudquaquam producat, aut etiam fundendi seu dimittendi mora moleve ulla gravetur.
units.tr: 4. On the other hand, the said Landgrave shall be wholly released from his custody and, on the said eleventh or twelfth day of August, shall be presented safely and securely at Rheinfels, free and beyond danger. Likewise, His Imperial Majesty shall not bring forward her forces, raised in various places against these estates which accept this settlement, nor be burdened by any delay or hindrance in pouring out or dismissing them.

units.la: 5. Cœptam quoque Cassellæ munitionem Imperatoria Majestas Landtgravio clementer perficere concederet.
units.tr: 5. His Imperial Majesty shall graciously grant the Landgrave permission to complete the fortification begun at Kassel.

units.la: 6. Suniliter Nassoviensium durante custodia promulgatarum sententiarum executio differatur ac suspendatur, donec liberato Landtgravio amica inter partes tractatio institui agiq; possit. Casu autem quò minus ea amicabilis progrederetur tractatio, Landtgravio tamè quo ad æquum est, testimonia, literarum documenta, aliaq; necessaria, quæ Advocatorum hucusque defectu, duranteve custodia proferri nequibant de cætero exhibeantur ac producantur. Et ita tunc quidem Electores hi, quos causa hæc non contingit, ipsimet, seu consiliarii eorum, atque adhuc alii sex minimè partiales Imperii Principes, ex quibus ambæ partes quindenos Cæsareæ Majestati intra mensem, posteaquâ Landtgravius fuerit liberatus, nominatim indicent atque proponant. Ex quibus amborum partium nuncupatis Majestas Cæsarea tres Principes deligat, (inter autem sex illos ad minus tres sint seculares) in persona propria, aut etiam ad idem deputati consiliarii, tanquam Cæsareani Commissarii, gravamina illa & exceptiones, contra prædictas latas sententias & executionem debito modo, ac ut decet, recognoscant atque revideant, ecquid acta tempore custodiæ Landtgravii exhibita rursus augmenda, Sententiæ quoque latæ ac Processus super ejusmodi propositis & adhuc dum proponendis gravaminibus, exceptionibusq; differendi ac suspendendi sint nec ne, cognoscant, & quid Juris sit, promulgeant. Atque hæc quidem amica tractatio & decisio ad summum intra biennium post conclusionem & datum compositionis seu transactionis hujus certò expediatur ac exequatur.
units.tr: 6. Likewise, the execution of the sentences pronounced against the Nassau men during the Landgrave's custody shall be deferred and suspended, until, once the Landgrave is freed, a friendly negotiation between the parties can be instituted and carried on. But if that friendly negotiation should not proceed, then the Landgrave shall, as is just, henceforth produce the testimonies, documentary letters and other necessary items which, owing to the lack of advocates or during his custody, could not hitherto be produced. In that case, these Electors, whom this matter does not concern, either in person or through their counsellors, together with six other princes of the Empire who are wholly impartial, shall each be named and proposed by both parties, within a month after the Landgrave is freed, fifteen from each side, to His Imperial Majesty. From the names put forward by both parties, His Imperial Majesty shall choose three princes (at least three of those six shall be secular), who, in person or through counsellors deputed for this purpose as Imperial Commissioners, shall examine and review, in the proper and fitting manner, the grievances and exceptions against the said sentences and their execution. They shall determine whether the acts presented during the Landgrave's custody should be further augmented, and whether the sentences pronounced, and the processes concerning grievances already proposed or still to be proposed, are to be deferred and suspended or not, and they shall declare what the law is. This friendly negotiation and decision shall certainly be concluded and carried out within two years at most after the conclusion and date of this settlement or agreement.

units.la: 7. Cæteris verò punctis & articulis omnibus inter memoratos Electorem Principem Saxoniæ, & Wilhelmum Lantgravium Hessiæ propositis tamdiu, quousque reliqua communiter proposita gravamina expediantur, dilatis atque suspensis.
units.tr: 7. All the other points and articles proposed between the said Elector, Prince of Saxony, and William, Landgrave of Hesse, shall be deferred and suspended until the remaining grievances proposed in common have been settled.

units.la: 8. Administrator item ordinis Teutonici, atque Dux Henricus Brunsvigensis, aliiq; Lantgravium præteriti Schmalkaldensis belli causa impetentes, aut porrò impetituri, cessent quoque & quiescant, donec prædicta gravamina resolvantur.
units.tr: 8. Likewise, the administrator of the Teutonic Order, Duke Henry of Brunswick, and others who attacked the Landgrave on account of the past Schmalkaldic war, or who shall attack him in future, shall also cease and rest until the aforesaid grievances are resolved.

units.la: 9. Etiam nova superius memorata gravamina, quæ durante Lantgravii custodia, in Judicio Imperiali, aliasve adversus eû præsumpta fuerte, simul cum eorum exceptionibus, ab Electoribus & Principibus harum controversiarum intercessoribus proximo Comitio, uti decet, recognoscantur revideanturque, ac idem Lantgravius prout necesse est, audiatur: In iisdem quoque quod æquum & justum est decernatur, neque interea tamen in Camera Imperiali Judicio procedatur.
units.tr: 9. Also, the new grievances mentioned above, which were presumed to have been brought against him during the Landgrave's custody, in the Imperial Court or elsewhere, shall be examined and reviewed together with their exceptions at the next Diet, as is fitting, by the Electors and princes who act as intercessors in these controversies. The Landgrave himself shall be heard, as necessary. In these matters too, what is fair and just shall be decreed, and meanwhile no proceeding shall take place in the Imperial Chamber Court.

units.la: CAP. II.
units.tr: CAP. II.

units.la: Religionem, pacem, & justitiam concernentia.
units.tr: Concerning religion, peace, and justice.

units.la: VErum atqui alios sequentes articulos quod concernit, ab Electore Saxoniæ, suisq; conjunctis in hac pacificatione propositis, & quidem primò de Religione, de pace, & justitia, Majestas Cæsarea sponsionem gratiosam nuper ad oppidum Linsium factam, extunc dato responso fideliter præstabit, & ut intra dimidii anni spatium Comitia habeantur, in quibus dein qua via, quibusq; modis, nimirum seu Generali seu Nationali Concilio, aut Colloquio, vel communi etiam Imperii conventu Religionis discordiæ commodè atque compendio sopiantur, hæcq; ad unionem Christianam redigantur, atque ejusmodi conciliatio Religionis ab omnibus Sacri Imperii Statibus, mediante Majestatis suæ ordinaria ope præsidioq; pertractetur.
units.tr: Indeed, as for the other articles that follow, proposed in this pacification by the Elector of Saxony and his associates, and first of all concerning religion, peace, and justice: His Imperial Majesty will faithfully keep the gracious promise recently made at the town of Linz, once the answer has been given, and will ensure that within the space of half a year a Diet be held, at which it may then be settled by what way and by what means—namely whether by a General or National Council, or by a colloquy, or indeed by a common assembly of the Empire—the dissensions of religion may be conveniently and expeditiously quieted, and these matters brought back to Christian unity; and that such a reconciliation of religion be handled by all the States of the Holy Empire, with the ordinary aid and support of His Majesty.

units.la: 2. Initio autem Comitiorum ad præparationem cõcordiæ delectus placidarum prudentumq; personarum constituatur, utriusque Religionis æquali numero cum Mandato deliberandi, quibus modis ejusmodi conciliatio atque concordia institui commodè posset, absque Electorum Principum præjudicio tamen hujus delectus ergò.
units.tr: 2. At the beginning of the Diet, for the preparation of concord, peaceable and prudent persons shall be appointed, of each religion in equal number, with a mandate to deliberate by what means such a reconciliation and concord could conveniently be established, provided that this appointment be without prejudice to the Electors and Princes.

units.la: 3. Et quidem interea temporis nec Cæsarea Majestas, neque nos, ac Electores, Principes, & S. Imperii Status quempiam ex Augustanæ confessionis Statibus, propter religionem, vi factove, aut aliàs contra ejus cõscientiam ac voluntatem cogere, aut ea de causa vi bellove petere, vel invadere, vel oppugnare aliquê, sive damnû aliquod inferre sive per mandata, sive alio quovis modo ipsum gravare vel etiâ contemnere, feremus, sed suæ Religioni fideiq; quietè & pacificè stare, cadereq; sinentes.
units.tr: 3. And meanwhile, neither His Imperial Majesty, nor we, the Electors, Princes, and States of the Holy Empire, will compel anyone of the States of the Augsburg Confession, on account of religion, by force or deed, or otherwise against his conscience and will; nor on that ground will we seek by force or war, attack or assail anyone, or inflict any loss, or burden or even despise him, whether by mandates or in any other way; but we shall allow him to stand and fall quietly and peacefully in his own religion and faith.

units.la: 4. Ob hoc quoq; bellû Status omnes Augustanæ confessionis cæteros Sacri Imperii Status antiquæ religionis Ecclesiasticos & seculares similiter Religionis suæ, Ceremoniarum, constitutionum, rerum immobilium & mobilium, ditionum, subditorum, redituum, censuum, superioritatum, & Jurisdictionum causa non gravent, sed pacificè tranquilleq; illis uti fruiq; sinant, nec vi factove, seu aliâs malignè contra eos quicquam præsumant: Verum enimvero juxta nostras & Sacri Imperii ordinationes, constitutiones, edicta, decreta, Recessus factæ pacis, singuli erga singulos ordinario jure justiq; contenti sint, sub proximè renovatæ pacificationis pœna.
units.tr: 4. For this reason too, all the States of the Augsburg Confession shall not burden the other States of the Holy Empire of the ancient religion, ecclesiastical and secular alike, in respect of their religion, ceremonies, constitutions, immovable and movable goods, lordships, subjects, revenues, rents, superiorities, and jurisdictions; but they shall allow them to use and enjoy these peacefully and quietly, and shall presume nothing against them by force or deed, or otherwise maliciously. Indeed, in accordance with our and the Holy Empire's ordinances, constitutions, edicts, decrees, and the recesses of the established peace, each shall be content with his ordinary right and what is just, under the penalty of the peace which has just been renewed.

units.la: 5. Quicquid verò in Comitiis illis à communibus Statibus unà cũ Cæsareæ Majestatis ordinario præsidio concludetur ac statuetur, in posterum quidem & recte & firmiter servetur, neque in contrarium, aliave via diversum agatur.
units.tr: 5. Whatever, however, shall be concluded and decreed at that Diet by the common States together with the ordinary presidency of His Imperial Majesty, shall in future be rightly and firmly observed, and nothing shall be done to the contrary or by any other way.

units.la: 6. Omne autem quod dictis induciis adversatur, adversarive censetur, in nihilo derogeri illis, aut quicquam imminuer, idq; à Cæsarea Majestate, nobis item, & Electoribus Principibus, ac Statibus respectivè, sufficienter, in quantum fuerit necesse, vigore hujus compositionis seu transactionis cautü, confirmatumq; sit: Præator quoque Cameræ Judicii & Consessores de iisdem induciis certificentur, mediusq; eorum juramentis, eisdem parcant & obsequantur: Implorantibus etiam partibus non attento eo, cujusnam sint religionis, necessarias & legitimas ferant suppetias: formulam quoque cum primis jurisiurandi Deum & sancios, aut Deum & sancta Evangelia, confessoribus, aliisque personis & partibus deinceps liberam permittendo.
units.tr: 6. Anything that is opposed to, or is deemed to be opposed to, the said truce shall in no way be taken away or diminished; and this shall be sufficiently confirmed by His Imperial Majesty, and likewise by us, and by the Electors, Princes and States respectively, as far as necessary, by virtue of the security of this composition or agreement. The President of the Chamber Court and the Assessors shall also be informed of this truce, and by their oaths shall spare and obey the same; likewise, when the parties implore aid, they shall bring necessary and lawful help, regardless of which religion they belong to; also, the formula of the oath, above all "God and the saints," or "God and the holy Gospels," shall be freely permitted to confessors and other persons and parties henceforth.

units.la: 7. In suffragiis quoq; dandis rogandisq; æqualitas servetur, æquum jus partibus, nec iniquum reddendo & conservando: Similiter & in præsentandis Assessoribus, aliisq; pacis & justitiæ articulis hac tractatione placuit, si quod operæprecium ac deliberatione dignum in dicasterii Cameræ constitutione apparuerit, quandoquidem eadem constitutio communi Statuum assensu, Comitioque Imperii sancita est, non etiam nisi per Cæsaream Majestatem, Statusq; communes rebus ita ferentibus ordinaria via, utpote visitationibus, aliisq; mediis mutari tolliq; posse. In qua re nos, Electorum Legati, comparentes Principes, & absentium nuncii recipimus nos, ac consentimus omnem diligentiam, operamq; præstituros, ne qua partium, in Religionis negocio suffragiorum, imparitate sibi præ cæteris metuat, partialitate remota: Augustanæ quoq; Confessionis confortes à Cæsareo Camerae judicio non excludantur, aliaq; gravamina, si quæ comperiantur, ex æquitate removeantur: & hæc quidem omnia proximis Comitiis explicentur.
units.tr: 7. Equality shall also be observed in giving and asking for votes, rendering and preserving an equal right for the parties and not an unfair one. Likewise, in presenting Assessors and other articles of peace and justice, it has been agreed in these negotiations that, if anything worthy of effort and deliberation appears in the constitution of the Chamber tribunal—since that constitution was sanctioned by the common assent of the States and the Diet of the Empire—it may be changed and removed only by His Imperial Majesty and the common States, in the ordinary way when circumstances require, namely by visitations and other means. In this matter we, the Legates of the Electors, the Princes present, and the envoys of the absent, accept and agree that we will take all diligence and effort so that no party, in matters of religion, may fear for itself an inequality of votes beyond the others, partiality being set aside. The partners of the Augsburg Confession shall also not be excluded from the Imperial Chamber tribunal, and other grievances, if any are found, shall be removed in fairness; and all these matters shall be explained at the next Diet.

units.la: 8. Cæterum & hoc nos unà Electorum Legatis, comparentibus Principibus & absentiū nunciis apud Cæsaream Majestatem, amanter, reverenterque cum reverentia petivimus, uti ejus Majestas punctatilla plus necessaria, inter quæ & articuli præsentationis, & ne Augustanæ confessionis conjuncti a judicio Camerae, ut suprà dictum est, excludantur, continentur: ex plenitudine Majestatis suæ Cæsareæ ad provehendam, retinendamq; pacem & concordiam in Imperio, quantocyus fieri posset, resolvere dignaretur.
units.tr: 8. Moreover, we, together with the Legates of the Electors, the Princes present, and the envoys of the absent, have also petitioned His Imperial Majesty, lovingly and reverently, with reverence, that His Majesty would deign, from the fullness of his imperial authority, to resolve as quickly as possible the points that are more necessary, among which are the articles of presentation and that the partners of the Augsburg Confession are not excluded from the judgment of the Chamber, as was said above, for the advancement and preservation of peace and concord in the Empire.

units.la: CAP. III.
units.tr: CAP. III.

units.la: Germanicæ nationis libertatem contingentia.
units.tr: Concerning the liberty of the German nation.

units.la: Quod ad gravamina, quæ Germanicæ nationis libertati contraria irrepsisse, ne dicam intrusisse, videntur, inter Electoris Saxonici articulos alio quoq; scripto comprehensa attinet: Voluebamus quidem una cum Electoribus, Legatis, Principibus præsentibus, & absentium nuncii prompti paratique ac minime gravati, illos ipsos, appendicesque suos singulatim protinus & specifice pro amicabili compositione tractanda suscepisse, niti intellexissemus à Cæsareæ Majestatis ad hanc tractationem lectis destinatis; consiliariis, ipsius Majestatem talium gravaminum hactenus bona ex parte in scium esse atq; ignarū, quamobrem de iis mandata dare consiliariis nequivisse: Adhuc, ea ipsa gravamina tanta, tamq; varia esse & prolixa, econtra vero tempus hoc perexiguum indicta dici, ut ipsi Electori quoq; Saxonico, suisq; conjunctis, donec hæ res omnes, quemadmodum necessitas postulat, explicentur, copias suas alendo, immodicos sumptus atq; impendia non solum pariet, verumetiam superioritatibus hincinde, miserisq; subditis gravissimo maximoq; damno sit futura.
units.tr: As for the grievances which seem to have crept in, not to say been thrust in, contrary to the liberty of the German nation, which are also contained in a separate writing among the articles of the Elector of Saxony: we indeed considered, together with the Electors, the envoys, the Princes present, and the messengers of those absent, who were ready and willing and not at all reluctant, that they should take up those articles and their appendices one by one, and specifically, for a friendly settlement. But we understood from the councillors appointed by His Imperial Majesty for this negotiation that His Majesty has hitherto been largely unaware of and ignorant of such grievances, and therefore the councillors could not give instructions concerning them. Moreover, these grievances are so great, so varied and so lengthy, while on the other hand this time is very short and has been fixed for other business, that, while the Elector of Saxony and his associates are maintaining their forces, unless all these matters are explained, as necessity demands, they will not only cause immoderate expense and outlay but will also be a most serious and grievous loss to the superiorities on every side and to the wretched subjects.

units.la: 2. Proinde hujuscemodi gravaminum resolutionem ad proxima Comitia, aliumve Imperii conventum hac vice rejicientes, ipsa bona ex Linsica consensione per Cæsareæ Majestatis consiliarios præbita suffulti, consilium inituram esse, quo sacri Imperii & Statuum publicis & privatis causis consuletur, cùm jam in eo tota Majestas sua elaboret, ut & apud suâ Majest. Germanicus Senatus constituatur, & Germanicæ res causæq; per Germanos tractentur ac disponantur, ita, ut omnibus placeat, omnibusq; fiat satis. Quādoquidem Germanicæ nationi ceu dilectæ suæ patriæ tam bene velit, ut haud quidem diminutam eam aut debilitatam, verùm multò magis quantum fieri potest auctam, amplificatam atq; conservatam cupiat, quæ quidem hoc tempore pollicitatio undiquaque cum gratiarum actione accepta est.
units.tr: 2. Therefore, rejecting for the present the resolution of such grievances to the next Diet or to another assembly of the Empire, supported by the very good agreement reached at Linz and offered through the councillors of His Imperial Majesty, they will undertake a plan by which the public and private affairs of the Holy Empire and of the Estates will be looked after, since His Majesty is already labouring toward this end: that a German Senate be established at his court, and German affairs and causes be handled and arranged by Germans, so that it pleases all and satisfies all. Since he wishes so well to the German nation as to his beloved fatherland, he desires it to be preserved and increased and enlarged as far as possible, not diminished or weakened. This promise has now been received everywhere with thanks.

units.la: 3. Ne autem Elector Saxonicus, suiq; adjuncti metuant hanc tractationem sponsam neglectu iri, aut posthabere, sine debito non decisam, debemus nos filiusq; nostes dilectus, Maximilianus Rex, Electores quoq; Principes, & Status sacri Imperii in manus sumere propositā gravamina, atque Cæsareæ Majestati ea offerre, eoque eniti atq; conari promovendo, ut quoad æquitatis fundamento insistant, visa quoque ut decet, Aurea Bulla, ac aliis sacri Imperii ordinationibus, constitutionibus, veteribusq; laudatis Germanicæ nationis consuetudinibus omnia probè resolvantur ac perficiantur. Reliqua vero ad Cæsaream Majestatem non proprie spectantia gravamina, sed à quibusdam sacri Imperii Statibus & membris privatim allata sunt, aut quæ ipsi inter se Status disceptant, de forma forte ac modo communis consultationis tractationisve, aut aliam ob rem quampiam controversam, æqua & illa ut suprà ponitur, Cæsareæ Majestatis tanquam Capitis eorum consilio prælidioque proximi Comitiis initio proponi vult atq; absolvi, gratiosa nimirum hac piaq; Majestatis suæ pollicitatione, ut quæ ad ipsius Majestatem in specie propriéque faciunt, in iis sic se tam gratioso bonoque animo ac voluntate gesturum esse, ut communes perspiciant Status, summa ejus Majestatem cupiditate controversias omnes ut decet, velle atque expetere compositas, & Rempub. privato emolumento longè prælatam fore, cæteraque omnia ita suscipi, instituique, ut omnibus Statibus ex æquo & bono quàm plenissimè fiat satis.
units.tr: 3. Lest the Elector of Saxony and his adherents fear that this matter, not yet settled, will be neglected or postponed, we, and our beloved son Maximilian the King, together with the Electors, Princes and Estates of the Holy Empire, are obliged to take up the grievances proposed and to present them to His Imperial Majesty, and to strive and endeavour to promote that, as they rest on the foundation of equity, and as is fitting, with the Golden Bull and the other ordinances and constitutions of the Holy Empire and the praiseworthy old customs of the German nation kept in view, everything be properly settled and completed. The remaining grievances, which do not properly concern His Imperial Majesty but have been brought forward privately by certain Estates and members of the Holy Empire, or which the Estates themselves dispute among themselves, concerning perhaps the form or manner of common consultation or negotiation, or some other controversial matter, which likewise, as stated above, are fair, His Imperial Majesty, as head of them, wishes to be proposed and settled at the beginning of the next Diet, with his counsel and protection. By that gracious and pious promise of His Majesty, namely, that in those matters which pertain specifically and properly to His Majesty he will so act with such a gracious and good mind and will, that the common Estates may perceive that His Majesty with the greatest desire wishes and seeks that all controversies be settled, as is fitting, and that the commonwealth will be set far above private advantage, and that all other matters will be undertaken and arranged so that all Estates may be fully satisfied in equity and goodness.

units.la: 4. Porrò ad articulum Regis Franciæ Oratorum veniendo, media quædam ac puncta pacis publicæ constituendæ, aliorumq; negociorum quorundam prætendentium: ita se habet, ut cùm, quæ publicæ sunt pacis in Germanica nat̃ione, solùmodò Imperatoriam Majestatem nos, & Electores, Principes ac Status sacri Imperii, neminemq; præterea concernant, & jam isti contentus harummer rerum, utpote publicæ pacis sanciendæ, aliorumq̃ue gravaminum atq; ovendorum causa sit instituturus, idcirco nulla jam alia tractatione fore opus existimatur.
units.tr: 4. Moving on further to the article of the envoys of the King of France, concerning certain means and points for establishing the public peace and of some other pending business: the matter stands thus, that since those things which concern the public peace in the German nation concern only His Imperial Majesty, we, the Electors, Princes and Estates of the Holy Empire, and no one besides, and since he, being content with these matters, will institute them for the sake of confirming the public peace and settling other grievances and duties, therefore it is thought that no further negotiation is needed.

units.tr: All these things written above, both individually and as they concern the Imperial Majesty itself, the Imperial Majesty ought to declare by virtue of its dignity in its own language, and it ought to observe them faithfully and carry them out justly and rightly, and it shall not act, either now or in the future, to the contrary, under any other appearance or pretext, by whatever name it may be called, in any way, nor allow any other party to do so on its own account, notwithstanding any other decrees whatsoever. Whatever is opposed to this agreement in any respect, we desire to maintain, defend and uphold; rather, all the terms of this composition, these truces and the other articles included herein.

units.la: 2. units.la: SEQUNTUR ARTICULI DE RELIGIONE, PACE, & justitia, per Regiam Majestatem, Electorum Legatos, praesentes Principes, & absentium nuncios designati.
units.tr: THE FOLLOWING ARTICLES CONCERNING RELIGION, PEACE, AND JUSTICE, DRAWN UP BY HIS ROYAL MAJESTY, THE ELECTORS' ENVOYS, THE PRINCES PRESENT, AND THE DEPUTIES OF THOSE ABSENT.

units.la: Vno ad Religionis, pacis, & justitiae articulum, Regia Majestas cum Electorum Legatis, praesentibus Principibus, & absentium nunciis inter Caesarem & Regiam Majestates, Electores, & Principes, & Status Germanicae nationis, donec controversia Religio tandem concorderur, inducias fieri firmas exiítimant, sic quidem, ut Caesarea & Regia Majestates, Electores quoq; Principes & Status sacri Imperii, nullum ex Augustana confessione Statum, aut qui sectis publicè per Imperii decreta damnatis non adhaereat, vi factove, aut aliis contra conscientiam ac voluntatem rationibus, modisq; de sua religione & fide deturbet, dejiciat, propellat, aut bello petat, laedatve, gravetve, aut etiam reprehendat, quinimò Religione quemq; sua fideq; tranquillè pacificeq; vivere agereq; sinat, neq; religionis controversiam aliter quàm amicis placidisq; mediis modisq; ad Christianum concordem intellectum unionemq; perduci ferat suftineatq;. Conjuncti quoq; hujus belli, aliiq; Status omnes, caeteros sacti Imperii Status tum Ecclesiasticos, tum seculares suâ Religione, Ecclesiastico usu, ordine & ceremoniis, atque facultatibus, bonis, dioecesibus, subditis, reditibus, censibus, dominiis, & jurisdictionibus non privent aut gravent, sed uti frui illis pacificè sinant, neq; vi, facto, aliasve malignè advertsus eos praesumant: sed per omnia sacri Imperii juri, ordinationibus, decretis, edictis, recessibus, atq; publicae pacis constitutioni quisq; stet, pareatq; ordine suo, sub interminatione poenae in proximè renovata publicae pacis sanctione comprehensae.
units.tr: On the first article concerning religion, peace, and justice, His Royal Majesty, with the envoys of the Electors, the Princes present, and the deputies of those absent, judge that, between the Emperor and the royal majesties, the Electors, Princes and States of the German nation, until the controversy over religion is at last settled, a firm truce shall be made. In such a way, namely, that neither His Caesarean and Royal Majesties, nor the Electors, Princes and States of the Holy Empire, shall by force or deed, or by other means contrary to conscience and will, drive out, dislodge, expel, or attack with war, harm, burden, or even rebuke any State adhering to the Augsburg Confession, or to those sects publicly condemned by decrees of the Empire, concerning its religion and faith. Rather, they shall let each person live and act in his religion and faith quietly and peacefully, and shall not allow or endure the controversy over religion to be pursued in any other way than by friendly and peaceable means, aiming at a Christian, harmonious understanding and union. Likewise, the allies in this war and all other States shall not deprive or burden the other States of the Holy Empire, whether ecclesiastical or secular, in their religion, ecclesiastical use, order and ceremonies, or in their revenues, goods, dioceses, subjects, rents, taxes, domains and jurisdictions. Rather, they shall let them enjoy these things peacefully, and shall not presume to act maliciously against them by force, deed, or otherwise. Instead, each person shall abide in all things by the law, ordinances, decrees, edicts, recesses and the constitution of public peace of the Holy Empire, and obey in his own rank, under the threat of the penalty included in the sanction of public peace to be shortly renewed.

units.la: 1. Acquacunq; saepe dictis inducis adversari videbuntur aut exiítimentur, nihil tamen derogent, sed à Caesarea & Regia Majestatibus, Electoribus, item Principibus ac Statibus respectivè sufficienter, & ut necesse est, provideri caveriq; debent mediante hujus transactionis Caesareo quoq; judicio Camerae, & Assessoribus inducię praedictae intimentur ac innotescant, ad earum observationem jurejurando suo adactis, omnino illis se ut conformes obtemperantesq; gerant, Partibusitem implotantibus nulla religionis differentia respectuve habito, prout decebit, opusq; fuerit, opè juris justitiąq; ferant. Assessorum quoq; aliarumq; personarum jurisjurandi per Deum sanctosque, aut Deum, sanctumq; Evangelium, formula juraturis liberè concessa.
units.tr: 1. Whatever things may seem or be judged to be opposed to the aforesaid truce, they shall nevertheless derogate nothing from it. Rather, the Caesarean and Royal Majesties, the Electors, likewise the Princes and States, shall respectively and sufficiently provide and take care as necessary, by means of this agreement and with the Emperor's judicial authority. The aforesaid truce shall be intimated and made known to the Chamber Court and its assessors, who shall be bound by oath to observe it, and they shall conduct themselves wholly in conformity with it and obey it. Likewise, in suits brought by the parties, without any regard to difference or respect of religion, they shall, as is fitting and necessary, bring help by means of law and justice. The form of oath for assessors and other persons who are to swear is freely granted: either "by God and the saints," or "by God and the holy Gospel."

units.la: 3. Pro unione autem & pace controversiae Religionis constituenda, Regia Majestas & Electorum consiliarii, tum & praesentes Principes absentiumq; nuncii exiítimant, Caesaream Majestatę proximo semestri post conclusionem & data harum induciarum & compositionis, Comitia habituram esse, in quibus cum Electoribus, Principibus, & Statibus Imperii rationem ineat, an Generali aut nationali Concilio, aut Colloquio, aut alio Imperii conventu & congregatione dissectae Religionis causa instituenda, concordanda, ac definienda sit, & quòd per Caesarem Majestatem communesq; tam Augustanae quàm contrariae confessionis Status pro usu ac bono publico statuetur, cum gratia passim omnibus concedatur.
units.tr: 3. For establishing union and peace in the controversy over religion, His Royal Majesty, the Electors' councillors, and likewise the Princes present and the deputies of those absent, judge that His Caesarean Majesty will hold a Diet within the next six months after the conclusion and date of this truce and agreement. At this Diet, with the Electors, Princes and States of the Empire, he shall consider whether the matter of the divided religion is to be instituted, agreed upon and settled by a General or national Council, or by a Colloquy, or by another assembly and gathering of the Empire. And what is decided by His Caesarean Majesty and the common States, both of the Augsburg and of the opposing confession, for public use and welfare, shall be granted with grace to all everywhere.

units.la: 4. Ethocin mentem venit, ad praeparationem ejusmodi unionis incundae, in initio eorundem Comitiorum nonnullorum tranquillitatis amantium ac prudentium personarum utriusq; Religionis pati numero haberi, quibus injungatur, quomodo concordia talis melius rectiusque suscipiatur, absque tamen Electorum Principum propter huncipsum delectum superioritatis ac praeeminentiae praejudicio.
units.tr: 4. Moreover, it has come to mind that for the preparation of such a union, at the beginning of the same Diet, some persons of both religions who love tranquillity and are prudent should be appointed in a number, to whom it shall be enjoined how such concord may be better and more rightly undertaken, yet without prejudice to the superiority and preeminence of the Electors and Princes arising from this very selection.

units.la: 5. Ubi autem nulla talibus viis concordia consequeretur, nihilo tamen secius praedictae inducad supremum concordiae terminum suas habeant vires, perpetuoq; valeant atq; constant.
units.tr: 5. But if no concord were achieved by such ways, the aforesaid truce shall nevertheless keep its force until the final term of concord, and shall remain and stand in perpetuity.

units.la: 6. Ad suffragiorum autem & justitiae aequaliter, tum & praesentationem Assessorum, aliorumque articulorum pacis & justitiae conservandae quod attinet, deliberatum est, si quid grave meditatione cogitaruq; dignum in ordinatione judicii Camerae oboriatur, cùm ea constitutio cómuni Statuum assensu facta sit, eam quoq; absq; communi Statuum voluntate conditionum respectu, non nisi ordinana visitationis judicii via, aliasve unà cum praetensis gravaminibus mutari non posse. Cuirei juvandae Regia Majestas unà cum Electorum Legatis, comparentibus Principibus, & absentium nunciis est operam datura, ne in religionis causa altera partium vel suffragiorum vel partialitatis ergò praealtera gravatam queri possit, aut etiam Augustanae confessionis adhaerentes & conjuncti à Caesareo Camerae judicio secludi se vereantur. Aliaq; gravamina, si quae innotuerint, ex aequitate proximis Comitus decíduntur.
units.tr: 6.
