As for the equal voting and justice, and likewise the presentation of assessors and the other articles for preserving peace and justice, it has been resolved that if anything grave and worthy of reflection should arise in the ordinance of the Chamber Court, since that constitution was made with the common assent of the States, it likewise cannot be changed without the common will of the States, regardless of conditions, except by the ordinary way of visitation of the court, or otherwise together with the grievances put forward. To help in this matter, His Royal Majesty, together with the Electors' envoys, the Princes present and the deputies of those absent, shall take care that in the cause of religion neither party may complain of being burdened by the votes or by partiality of the other, nor that the adherents of the Augsburg Confession and those allied with them should fear being excluded from the Caesarean Chamber Court. Other grievances, if any become known, shall be decided at the next Diet according to equity.

units.la: 7. Dabit quoq; hic operam Regia Majestas unà cum Electorum Legatis, comparentibus Principibus, & absentium nunciis Caesaream Majestatem amanter juxtà ac reverenter interpellando oranDoque, ut puncta cum primis necessaria, inter quae & articulus praesentationis atque Augustanae Consessionis, conjuncti, à Caesareo Camerae judicio (ut supra dictum est) ne excludantur, ex plenitudine Caesareae ejus Majestatis, pro retinenda confervandaq; in Imperio pace & concordia, quantocyus fieri poterit, resolvantur atq; expediantur.
units.tr: 7. His Royal Majesty, together with the Electors' envoys, the Princes present and the deputies of those absent, shall also take care to ask and entreat His Caesarean Majesty lovingly and at the same time reverently, that the points most necessary above all, among which is the article of presentation and of the Augsburg Confession, and those allied with it, shall not be excluded from the Caesarean Chamber Court (as has been said above). Out of the fullness of His Caesarean Majesty's power, for retaining and preserving peace and concord in the Empire, they shall be resolved and settled as quickly as can be done.

units.la: FERDIReverendissimo Tridentino die nona Decembris: deinde à me die 14. ejusdem mensis, hora tertia meridiana, in hoc Reverendissimorum Patrum consessu cum debita humilitate in stantibus, genibus flexis, idq; per viscera, & per sanguinem Domini nostri Jesu Christi: tempus tamen Sanctitas Vestra interposuit ad consulendos super responso Patres, qui Bononiæ sunt; qui quidem non dissimile (ut ipsi dicunt) translationi consilium dedere vanum, subdolum & captiosum, in gravissimam religionis & universalis Ecclesiæ dissidium, scandalum & detrimentum.
units.tr: FERDINAND ... To the Most Reverend [Cardinal] of Trent, on the ninth of December; then from me, on the fourteenth day of the same month, at three in the afternoon, in this assembly of the Most Reverend Fathers, standing, with knees bent, with due humility, and that through the bowels and through the blood of our Lord Jesus Christ. Your Holiness, however, interposed a delay in order to consult the Fathers who are at Bologna about the response. They have given a counsel, which (as they themselves say) is not unlike the translation: a vain, deceitful and captious counsel, to the gravest discord and scandal and detriment of religion and of the universal Church.

units.la: 12. Sanctitas autem Vestra id consilium approbasse, illorumq; sententiam suscepisse quamodo visa est, illegitimam secessionem Tridentinam, periculosissimam sane & perniciosam Reipublicæ Christianæ, translationis vocabulo, congregationemq; seu illegitimum Conventum Bononiensem generalis Concilij nomine appellans: tantumq; ei congregationi auctoritatis in suis ad Reverendissimum Cardinalem de Monte, Episcopum Prænestinum, & ad vos qui adestis literis, & suo ad Imperatorem responso tribuere videtur, quantum Episcopi prænominati auctoritate propria sibi ipsis arrogare auditur.
units.tr: 12. Your Holiness, however, seems to have approved that counsel and to have adopted their opinion, as it has been seen, calling the Tridentine secession, which is indeed most dangerous and pernicious to the Christian Commonwealth, by the name of "translation," and the gathering, or illegitimate assembly, at Bologna by the name of a General Council. And in your letters to the Most Reverend Cardinal de Monte, Bishop of Palestrina, and to you who are present, and in your response to the Emperor, you seem to grant that gathering as much authority as is heard that the aforesaid bishops have arrogated to themselves by their own authority.

units.la: 13. Præterea responsum ad Cæsarem dat dilatorium & illegitimum, præsenti occasioni & negotio impertinens, ineptum & inconveniens. Quid enim magis alienum, quàm in gravissima causa, in negotio religionis & Spiritus sancti, & causæ cognitionem anteverte-re, & sententiam ferre, & judicium sibi deferatur: & his qui ægrotabant, & sanari did erant, qui remedium detrectare videbantur, qui nunc religionem, qui morum reformationem, qui publicarum dissensionum petunt à Sanctitate Vestra, (Concilium enim petunt Tridenti, ubi coepi fuerat, continuari & absolvi, quod omnium bonorum causam futurum certissimè creduntur) præstantissimam medicinam tergiversationibus & ambagibus producere & denegare.
units.tr: 13. Moreover, you give to the Emperor a response that is dilatory and illegitimate, irrelevant to the present occasion and business, inept and unsuitable. For what is more alien than to anticipate the examination of a most grave cause, in a matter of religion and of the Holy Spirit, and to pronounce sentence and pass judgment before the case is heard? And to bring forward, and deny, the most excellent remedy by evasions and circumlocutions for those who were sick and were to be healed, and who seemed to refuse the cure: those who now ask Your Holiness for the reform of religion, for the reform of morals, and for the end of public dissensions. For they ask for a Council at Trent, where it had begun, to be continued and concluded, which they are most certainly believed to be the cause of all good men.

units.la: 14. Et cùm probationem causarum translationis à perspicuis & religiosissimis & probatissimis testibus sumi, conveniens sit, in hac ipsa testibus parum inter se convenientibus, nullius autoritatis de plebe hominibus fidem adhibere: Imperatoris autem & Regis Romani, & Principum Statuum Germaniæ, qui in publicis Comitiis congregati sunt, qui & per Sanctæ Sedis Apostolicæ Cardinalem atque eundem Sacri Imperii Principem, Sanctitatem Vestram certiorem faciunt, de hoc tam Concilio tam pio Germanorum propositio atque decreto fidem in dubium vertere, quod ex ipsorum & Sanctitatis Vestræ responso, cùm publicè tùm privatim dato, intelligi potest.
units.tr: 14. And since it is fitting that proof of the causes of the translation be taken from clear, most religious and most approved witnesses, and since in this very matter the witnesses agree poorly among themselves, no faith should be given to men of no authority from the common people. But the Emperor and King of the Romans, and the Princes and States of Germany, who are gathered in public Diet, who through the Cardinal of the Holy Apostolic See and the same Prince of the Holy Empire make Your Holiness certain of this, have called into doubt the faith in this so pious proposal and decree of the Germans concerning this Council. This can be understood from their response and from that of Your Holiness, given both publicly and privately.

units.la: 15. Multa alia à me prætermittuntur, Sanctissime Pater, quæ tempore & loco, si opus fuerit, in hac causa dicentur. Quid præterea desiderabamus à Germanis, quid ab eis petebamus, toties à Cæsare repetitis itineribus, tot impësis, tot laboribus, maximo & ancipiti suscepto bello, atq; collecto: Perdet omnes labores hos S.V. pro religione susceptos: perdet optimam & præstantè sanandæ restituendæq; religionis occasionem, & perdet religionis causam, admonitus & requisitus. Id verò certissimi Concilii universale, ob causas gravissimas & maximè necessarias Tridenti congregatû, Vest. Sanctitatis dictione, flagitante Imperatore, Principibus Christianis assentientibus, petentibus Germanis, convenientibus Episcopis, jam cœpiû, nisi summa urgentiq; necessitate, præcedentibus tractatibus, & diligentissima discussione, servato juris ordine, consensu omniû Patrû, aliò mutari, neq; legitimè posse nec licere.
units.tr: 15. Many other things I pass over, Most Holy Father, which, if need be, will be spoken of in this cause at the proper time and place. What else did we desire from the Germans, what did we ask of them, when the Emperor so often repeated his journeys, with so many expenses, so many labours, after undertaking and gathering a great and dangerous war? All these labours undertaken by Your Holiness for religion will be lost; the excellent and outstanding opportunity of healing and restoring religion will be lost, and the cause of religion will be lost, once admonished and asked. Indeed, that most certain universal Council, convened at Trent for the most grave and most necessary causes, by the direction of Your Holiness, at the request of the Emperor, with the assent of the Christian Princes, at the petition of the Germans, with the bishops agreeing, has already begun. It cannot lawfully be moved elsewhere, nor is it lawful, unless in the greatest and most pressing necessity, with prior negotiations and most diligent discussion, with the order of law observed and with the consent of all the Fathers.

units.la: 16. Sæpe enim tralationes callido & præcipiti consilio sine causa factæ, in causa esse solent, ut magno religionis periculo, magnis in Repub. Christiana ruinis & dissensionib°, interdum populi Christiani perniciosa divisione Concilia dissolvantur. Causa autem tam subitæ translationis nulla fuit, sed arrepta, quæ se primùm obtulit. Occasionem vos Reverendissimi asserti Legati, ut à me dictum est & reliqui Patres, fecistis, id quod jam pridem meditati fueratis. Febres enim nescio quas & aëris vitium causati, affectatum & procuratum quorundam medicorum, sed præcipuè ancillarum & coquorum, vel- limmorum hominum, testimonium recitantes, Tridento præcipites discesserunt. nempe & rursus deinceps apertissimè patuit, nullam exitiosam formidinis causam.
units.tr: 16. For transfers made by a crafty and hasty plan, without cause, often prove to be the reason why councils are dissolved, with great danger to religion, great ruin and dissension in the Christian commonwealth, and sometimes the sundering of the Christian people. But there was no cause for so sudden a transfer; it was seized upon, whatever first presented itself. You, most reverend Legates of the aforesaid, as has been said by me and by the other Fathers, provided the occasion, which you had long been planning. For you, pleading I know not what fevers and a fault of the air, and reciting the testimony of certain physicians, contrived and procured, but chiefly of maids and cooks and worthless men, departed headlong from Trent. Indeed it has since become quite plain that there was no deadly cause for fear.

units.la: 17. Præterea ut nulla fuerit ratio discedendi, Vestram Sanct. in hac præterensa causa consulilent, cùm tam parvi temporis mora nihil periculi esset allatura. Neque enim tam repentina res erat quod exitus morbi, quem causati fuerant, comprobavit. Inconsulta autem Sanctitas Vestra, discessistis illos Episcopos, fassi estis, & Sanctitas Vestra postmodùm affirmavit. Cui quidem Sanctitatis Vest. testimonio multum certè fidei & autoritatis detrahunt vestræ ad Reverendissimum de Monte litteræ, & responsiones ad Cæsarem datæ.
units.tr: 17. Moreover, that there was no reason for departing, you should have consulted Your Holiness in this matter, since so brief a delay would have brought no danger. The matter was not so sudden as the outcome of the illness you had alleged made plain. But without consulting Your Holiness, you dismissed those bishops, as you confessed, and Your Holiness afterwards affirmed it. Indeed your letters to the most reverend de Monte, and the replies you gave to the Emperor, greatly detract from the credit and authority of that testimony of Your Holiness.

units.la: 18. Imperatore quoque consulto & assentiente, id facere debuissent, cui curæ sunt & tutela omnia universalia Concilia, atq; id ex munere officii Augustalis: cujus quanta sit in Concilius manifestum est. Verùm tanta fuit Legatorum assertorum festinatio & simulatio, ut nec ipsi valuerint consulere, nec eos qui dicebant, Sanctitatem Vestram & Imperatorem priùs per Sanctam Sedem certiores fieri oportere, audiendos putarint. Cumq; Imperator ipse pro tuenda & amplificanda religione, pro Ecclesia, pro Concilio laboraret, ipsi vano & inani timore simulato, Imperatore incontrà fulto, abscesserunt. Atqui sæpe aliàs Imperator per Oratores suos cùm ipsos assertos Legaros, tum Sanctitatem Vestram admonuerat, se neque tralationi Concilii, sed neque suspensioni aut vacationi vel expresse assentiri posse.
units.tr: 18. The Emperor too should have been consulted and have assented, since the care and protection of all ecumenical councils belong to him, and this from the duty of the Augustal office, whose extent in councils is manifest. But the haste and pretence of the Legates were so great that they neither could consult, nor thought that those who said Your Holiness and the Emperor ought first to be informed through the Holy See should be heard. Although the Emperor himself was labouring to defend and extend religion, for the Church and for the Council, they, with feigned and empty fear, departed while the Emperor, on the contrary, was held fast. Yet often at other times the Emperor, through his envoys, had admonished both the said Legates and Your Holiness that he could assent neither to the transfer of the Council, nor expressly to its suspension or vacancy.

units.la: 19. Præterea juris ordinem contempserant, & eam causæ cognitionem, quæ in Synodalibus translationibus Sanctorum Patrum sanctionibus instituta est. Rem enim fere omnium gravissimam perèsanè & leviter confecerunt. Debuerant certè justas multorum gravissimorum Patrum, qui illa haud quaquam assentari docti, rei ex recta conscientia consulebant, contradictiones libenter audire, eorumque sententias ac rationes animadvertere atque examinare, ac non ipsis neglectis, vi-que audire. [illegible, ~60 letters] quidem sententiae quod graviores & firmiores essent, fauto- [illegible, ~40 letters] Christiana principiorum nopedire. Quod enim sui sapientia Concilio decreta fuerunt, ne dissideret a termino ejus regni Germaniae hujus praesumeret, & opprimeret impedidas. [illegible, ~120 letters] Concilium Tridentinum quod nomine Ecclesiae deliberat, quod illi resistit, Germanos. [illegible, ~300 letters] Trident. Concilium Christiana ad Concilium Tridentinum vocant, tradatur Concilium perdet.
units.tr: 19. Moreover, they had disregarded the order of law and that examination of the case which the sanctions of the holy Fathers established for synodal transfers. For they dispatched an affair almost the most weighty of all very lightly and hastily. They ought certainly to have gladly heard the just objections of many most grave Fathers, who by no means assented to that course, and who consulted on the matter from a right conscience; they ought to have noted and examined their opinions and reasons, not neglecting them and simply hearing the rest. [illegible] For the decrees were made by their own authority, so that they would not dissent from the border of this kingdom of Germany, and would not presume to oppress those who were hindered. [illegible] The Council of Trent, which deliberates in the name of the Church, which resists it, the Germans [illegible] they call to the Council of Trent; the Council will be given up.

units.la: Verum tam pollicitus Imperator, Sanctissimae & Sanctae Ecclesiae, ut verus & legitimus Romanus Imperator, Ecclesiam omnium matrem augere ac defendere rem sicut semper ab initio Imperii & Imperatorum, quod antiquitus mos fuerat, Concilia protegere, & eo modo, nunquam & salvam esse, quam in quo id ita in aliquo bonum esse [illegible, ~200 letters] Trident. Concilium postulare Tridenti, pollicitus est Concilio Tridentino adfuturum, Sanctissimo Pontifici, ut ad Sanctitatem Vestram, quam semel atque iterum obtestatus est, nunc quoque, ac Sanctitatis Vestrae & Ecclesiae filius, maxime cotidie [illegible, ~80 letters] per viscera Domini nostri Jesu Christi, ne magno labore tandem quaesitam unitatem religionis occasionem praetermittat.
units.tr: But the Emperor, having promised, as a true and lawful Roman Emperor, to increase and defend the Church, the mother of all, and to protect the councils, as the custom was from the beginning of the Empire and of the Emperors, and in such a way that it is never safe except where it is so good in some respect [illegible] ... He promised to attend the Council of Trent, and asked the Council of Trent to ask the Most Holy Pontiff, that he would for the sake of Your Holiness, whom he has once and again entreated, and who is now, as a son of Your Holiness and of the Church, most of all daily [illegible] through the bowels of our Lord Jesus Christ, that he not let slip the occasion of religious unity, sought at last with great labour.

units.la: Ut ibus a Deo Opt. Max. sibi commissis auxilium ferat, jubeat suos allertos legatos, tam religiosos qui recesserunt sine mora Tridentum reverti, qui locus ipsis ab Sanctitate Vestrae appositus est, & Ecclesiae ipsius. Invictissimi & piissimi Imperatoris, sub tutela inquit, sed licet, ut decet ac nec etiam ... Concilia protegere atque tueri: ibique, ut decet ac necessarium est, sacrosancta claret Concilium auctoritate Imperatoris, effigiatione & sublimi Principum, Tridenti indicatum, itaque cumque prosequatur quod nullo pacto recusare potuit, & sane id jam ante a pollicitis sunt, si utique Germaniae Concilium accessissent, se quam primum illa falsa morbi fulgida tollisset, eliciendi tur a deo sanctitas Vestra idipsum Caesari per Nuncios saepe & Legatos probavit.
units.tr: That he may bring help to those committed to him by God, most good and most great, let him order his legates, so religious, who withdrew, to return to Trent without delay, the place appointed for them by Your Holiness and by the Church itself. The most invincible and most pious Emperor, under the protection, says he, but it is fitting and not even ... to protect and defend the councils; and there, as is fitting and necessary, the most sacred council shines forth under the authority of the Emperor, through the splendour and high rank of the Princes, indicated at Trent; and so, whatever it pursues, it could by no means refuse; and indeed they had already promised this, if they had come to the Council in Germany, that as soon as possible he would remove that false and shining sickness; Your Holiness has often proved this to Caesar through nuncios and legates, that it is drawn forth from God.

units.la: Anno jam fere elapso, cessante morbo (ut quis fuit) in tranquillitate & pacata, ablata ratione corrigi, illudantibus Principibus & Statibus Germaniae, qui ... pollicentibus, sed nihil ... ab his, aut praetextu Synodum sanctam Tridentinam a suscepta ... eorum reverterunt, & in ... ut quod ... Legatos Tridentum reduc. ... nunc postea, Caesar ... rem populo Christiano valde necessarium, & dare ... adjici, pollicitum fecit.
units.tr: Now that nearly a year has passed, the sickness having ceased (as it was), in tranquillity and peace, with reason removed, to be corrected, the Princes and States of Germany mocking, who ... promised, but nothing ... from these, or under the pretext of the holy Synod of Trent undertaken ... of them they returned, and ... that ... the Legates back to Trent ... now afterwards, Caesar ... a matter most necessary for the Christian people, and to give ... added, he promised.

units.la: Sed earum tam justae petitioni tempore & occasione necessaria, quae quidem nunc ... ... offerunt, ... decretum ... nobiscum ... Concilium ... Ecclesiae Christi vicem repraesentantis; Deo fundatum; Concilio ... nomine ... Caroli Caesaris Romanorum Imperatoris ... illius speciali mandato, ac nomine totius Sacri Imperii & Ingenuorum Dominorum nostrorum ... religiosus ... Evangelicas quasdam ... dictum est a me semel atque iterum, sed etiam plures in hunc ... Concilii ... Ecclesiae ... Decembris ... 16. Januarii ... 27. Decemb. ... Ecclesiae. Concilium ... Concilium ... Ecclesiae ... Maximum ... bonis ... prorsus ... Jesu Christi ... 3. Similiter & hos Electores ac Principes ceu nobilcum intercessores & compositores harum amicè transfigendarũ rerũ causa literis nostris evocavimus & accersivimus, talib9 divina clementia gravaminibus, litibus atq; discordiis, quibus fieri potest, viis, modisq; obviaturi, ac denique, finem imposituri.
units.tr: But to such a just petition, at a necessary time and occasion, which now ... offer, ... decree ... with us ... Council ... of the Church representing the vice of Christ; founded by God; for the Council ... in the name of Charles, Caesar, Emperor of the Romans, by his special mandate, and in the name of the whole Holy Empire and of our noble lords ... pious ... certain Evangelical ... said by me once and again, but also several more times in this ... of the Council ... of the Church ... December ... 16 January ... 27 December ... of the Church. The Council ... the Council ... of the Church ... greatest ... goods ... entirely ... of Jesus Christ ... 3. Similarly, we have summoned and called these Electors and Princes, as noble intercessors and mediators for the sake of settling these matters amicably, by our letters, intending to meet, by whatever ways and means are possible, these burdens, quarrels and discords which the divine clemency has permitted, and finally to put an end to them.

units.la: 4. Proinde nos, & infrà memorati Principes, Elector Saxoniæ, &c. huc ad dictam diem cum ceterorum Electorum & Principũ Legatis pervenimus, videlicet, Archiepiscopi Moguntinensis nomine Daniel Brendel ab Honburck, majoris ædis Canonicus Moguntiæ, Christophorus Matthias Junum Licentiatus Cancellarius, & Petrus Echterus. Archiepiscopi autem Coloniensis nomine Henricus Salisburgensis, & Franciscus Burghardus, ambo doctores. Archiepiscopi Trevirensis nomine, Joannes de Petra, Primas inter Archidiaconos Trevericos: Philippus Baro in Winnenberg & Beylstein, ditionis Trevericæ aulaeq; Magister, & Felix Hornung Doctor, Cancellarius. Palatini vero Friderici nomine, Ludovicus Comes à Stolberg, Konigstein, & Ruthschefort. Joannes à Dinheim, præfectus in Creutzenach, Melchior Drechsel Doctor, & Joan. Koting. Joachimi Marchionis nomine, Adam Trotte Marischalcus, Christophorus Srratius, Timotheus Jung, & Lampertus Distelmeyer, Doctores. Item reverendi & generosi, Ernestus Archiepiscopus Salisburgensis, &c. Mauritius Echstetensis, & Wolffgangus Pataviensis Episcopi, Albertus quoq; Palatinus Rheni, Dux superioris & inferioris Bavariæ, in persona. Item Episcopi Herbipolensis nomine Henricus Comes à Castel Canonicus, & Hans Zobel. Joannis Marchionis Brandenburgensis nomine Adrianus Albinus Doctor, Cancellarius, Andreas Zoch Doctor, & Bartholus à Mandelslo, Henrici junioris Ducis Brunsvigensis nomine, Vitus Grummer. Wilhelmi Ducis Juliacensis nomine, Wilhelmus Kettler. Wilhelmus à Hevvenhof, appellatus Ley. Magister curiæ Theodoricus à Schepsted, & Carolus Horstus, Doctores. Philippi Pometaniæ nomine, Jacobus Zitzewvitz, Doctor & Cancellarius. Et Christophori Ducis Wirtembergensis nomine Johannes Theodoricus à Plenningen, superior Advocatus in Stutgarten, Ludovicus à Fravvenberg, Advocatus superior in Lauffen. Joannes Henricus Hecklin, & Caspar Behem, ambo Doctores hic coram nobis comparentes. Quibus cum vocatis transfactoribus item cœpimus tractandam, ac initio dicti Electoris Saxonici, suorumq; conjunctorum postulata & gravamina duobus specialibus scriptis complexa accepimus, eaq; summa diligentia, fideq; perpendentes, quo ad amicè cõponi, & ingruentis belli discrimina, pace, tranquillitate, & concordia firmata, in Sacro Teutonicæ nationis Imperio averti possent. Atque sic tandem post multam longamq; tum scripto tum verbo rerum tractationem agitatam, sequentia media, punctaq; ad Cæsareæ Majestatis beneplacitum, ac Electoris Saxonici, suorumq; confœderatorum assensum ac ratificationem relata sunt, deq; iisdem unanimiter tandem in hunc qui sequitur modum conventum est atque conclusum.
units.tr: 4. Therefore we, and the Princes above named, the Elector of Saxony, etc., have arrived here on the said day with the Legates of the other Electors and Princes, namely: on behalf of the Archbishop of Mainz, Daniel Brendel von Homburg, canon of the cathedral of Mainz, Christophorus Matthias Junus, licentiate, chancellor, and Petrus Echterus. On behalf of the Archbishop of Cologne, Henricus Salisburgensis and Franciscus Burghardus, both doctors. On behalf of the Archbishop of Trier, Joannes de Petra, first among the archdeacons of Trier; Philippus, Baron of Winnenberg and Beilstein, master of the court of the Trier domain, and Felix Hornung, doctor, chancellor. On behalf of Frederick the Palatine, Ludovicus Count of Stolberg, Königstein and Rothschild; Joannes von Dienheim, prefect at Kreuznach, Melchior Drechsel, doctor, and Joan. Koting. On behalf of the Margrave Joachim, Adam Trotte, marshal, Christophorus Srratius, Timotheus Jung, and Lampertus Distelmeyer, doctors. Likewise the reverend and noble men, Ernestus, Archbishop of Salzburg, etc., Mauritius of Eichstätt, and Wolfgangus of Passau, bishops; Albert also, Palatine of the Rhine, Duke of Upper and Lower Bavaria, in person. Likewise, on behalf of the Bishop of Würzburg, Henricus Count of Castell, canon, and Hans Zobel. On behalf of Margrave Johann of Brandenburg, Adrianus Albinus, doctor, chancellor, Andreas Zoch, doctor, and Bartholus von Mandelsloh. On behalf of Henry the Younger, Duke of Brunswick, Vitus Grummer. On behalf of William, Duke of Jülich, Wilhelmus Kettler; Wilhelm von Hevenhof, called Ley, master of the court; and Theodoricus von Schepstedt and Carolus Horstus, doctors. On behalf of Philip of Pomerania, Jacobus Zitzewitz, doctor and chancellor. And on behalf of Christoph, Duke of Württemberg, Johannes Theodoricus von Plenningen, chief advocate at Stuttgart, and Ludovicus von Frauenberg, chief advocate at Lauffen. Joannes Henricus Hecklin and Caspar Behem, both doctors, appearing here before us. With these called mediators we likewise began to deal with the matter; and at the beginning we received the demands and grievances of the said Elector of Saxony and his associates, embraced in two special writings, and weighing them with the greatest diligence and good faith, so that they might be amicably settled, and the dangers of the impending war might be averted within the Holy Empire of the German nation, and peace, tranquillity and concord be firmly established. And so at last, after a long and extended treatment of the matter, both in writing and by word, the following means and points were referred for the approval of His Imperial Majesty and the assent and ratification of the Elector of Saxony and his confederates; and concerning these, at last unanimously, it was agreed and concluded in the following manner.

units.la: CAP. I.
units.tr: CHAPTER I.

units.la: Cessio armatæ militiæ, & Philippi Hessorum Landtgravii Λύτρωσις seu liberatio.
units.tr: The surrender of the armed soldiery, and the Lytrosis, or liberation, of Philip, Landgrave of Hesse.

units.la: PRIMUM Elector Saxonicus, suiq; belli consortes Principes ac Status hanc compositionem amplectentes à ceptis sumptisq; armis prorsus desistent: suosque paratos & conscriptos milites ad undecimum duodecimumve diem Augusti mensis proximum undiquaq; dimittant, dissipent, atq; discurrere, vel nobis Regi Ferdinando ad petitionem stipemq; nostram adjungi vel admoveri sinant: denique omnibus modis operam, in quantum fieri potest, ne quid injuriæ damnive dolo malo Cæsareæ Majestati, nobis, aut cæteris Sacri Imperii Electoribus, Principibus, Statibus, & civitatibus illorum discursu, fusioneq; inferatur, quin ita potius dispersi Cæsareæ Majestati, Sacroq; Imperio obsequentes segerant permaneantq;, remissis illorum Statuum, civitatum, aliorumq; juramentis, quos hactenus oppugnarunt & obsiderunt, aut sibi aliqua adhæsione & confœderatione subdiderunt, idque vigore transscripti jam hoc in loco patentium literarum exemplaris remissionem illam cõcestantium, quemadmodum & earundem, & hujus edicti virtute à suis juramentis protinus liberantur & absolvuntur.
units.tr: First, the Elector of Saxony and his fellow-confederate princes and estates, accepting this settlement, shall wholly desist from the arms they have taken up and begun to use. They shall disband, dismiss and scatter on all sides their soldiers, already paid and enrolled, by the eleventh or twelfth day of August next, and they shall allow them to disperse and go away, or to be joined or added to us, King Ferdinand, at our request and expense. Finally, they shall do everything possible, so far as it can be done, to ensure that no injury or loss is inflicted by fraud or malice on His Imperial Majesty, on us, or on the other Electors, princes, estates and cities of the Holy Empire through their dispersal and withdrawal; rather, once dispersed, they shall remain and continue obedient to His Imperial Majesty and the Holy Empire. The oaths of those estates, cities and others whom they have hitherto attacked and besieged, or subjected to themselves by some alliance and confederation, shall be remitted, and by virtue of the remission granted in the copy of the open letters here transcribed, and of this edict, they shall at once be freed and absolved from their oaths, in the same way as the former.

units.la: 2. Interea quoque temporis Philippus Hessorum Landtgravius sanctam Halæ in Saxonia capitulationem (exceptis jam antea resolutis articulis, puncto de Cassella loquente) ratam de novo habere, ac irrefragabiliter observare debet, adeoque detentionem suam & custodiam haudquaquam vindicare, quin imò Cæsareæ Majestati, Sacroq; Imperio se se Principem per dies vitæ suæ obsequentem exhibere, & ad omnia ista Cæsareæ Majestati formula decenti hoc loci præscripta sufficienter astringere, efficereq; tandem, ut idem à filiis, ditioneq; sua nova literarum obligatione præstituta servetur acteneatur.
units.tr: 2. Meanwhile, too, Philip, Landgrave of Hesse, must again hold the holy capitulation made at Halle in Saxony as ratified, and observe it without fail (the articles already settled earlier being excepted, the point concerning Kassel being the exception), and so he must not claim his detention and custody at all. Rather, he must show himself to His Imperial Majesty and the Holy Empire as a prince obedient for the rest of his life, and bind himself sufficiently to all these things by the fitting form prescribed here for His Imperial Majesty. He must also bring it about that the same is observed and kept by his sons and his territory, under the new written obligation set down.

units.la: 3. Simili modo uterque Electorum Saxonicus & Brandenburgensis, Dux item Wolffgangus Palatinus, &c. obligationes quisque suas jam pridem factas modò renovent, easque scriptas cautiones ad sextum Augusti diem Illustrissimæ Principi Dominæ Mariæ Hungariæ & Bohemiæ Reginæ, viduæ, dilectæ sorori nostræ, cjusve præsidenti apud Mechliniam tradantur.
units.tr: 3. In like manner, each of the Electors of Saxony and Brandenburg, and likewise Duke Wolfgang Palatine, etc., shall now renew the obligations each has long since made, and these written securities shall be handed over by the sixth day of August to the most illustrious princess, Lady Maria, Queen of Hungary and Bohemia, widow, our beloved sister, or to her president at Mechlin.

units.la: 4. Econtrà memoratus Landtgravius custodia sua penitus liberetur, & ad dictũ Augusti diem undecimum vel duodecimum Rheinfelsium turò certoq; extra periculum sistetur liber. Jam & ipsa copias suas Cæsarea Majestas diversis in locis in hos Status conscriptas, hanc cõpositionem acceptantes haudquaquam producar, aut etiam fundendi seu dimittendi mora moleve ulla gravetur.
units.tr: 4. On the other side, the aforesaid Landgrave shall be wholly freed from his custody, and by the said eleventh or twelfth day of August he shall be presented at Rheinfels, surely and certainly outside danger, as a free man. Also, His Imperial Majesty shall not bring forward her forces, raised in various places against these estates which accept this settlement, nor shall she be hindered by any delay or difficulty in disbanding or dismissing them.

units.la: 5. Cœptam quoque Cassellæ munitionem Imperatoria Majestas Landtgravio clementer perficere concedet.
units.tr: 5. His Imperial Majesty shall graciously grant the Landgrave permission to complete the fortification begun at Kassel.

units.la: 6. Similiter Nassoviensium dutante custodia promulgatarum sententiarum executio differarur ac suspendatur, donec liberato Landtgravio amica inter partes tractatio institui agiq; possit. Casu autem quò minus ea amicabilis progrederetur tractatio, Landtgravio tamè quo ad æquum est, testimonia, literarum documenta, aliaq; necessaria, quæ Advocatorum hucusque defectu, durante vel custodia proferri nequibant de cætero exhibeanturac producantur. Et ita tunc quidem Electores hi, quos causa hæc non contingit, ipsimet, seu consiliarii eorum, atque adhuc alii sex minimè partiales Imperii Principes, ex quibus ambæ partes quindenos Cæsareæ Majestati intra mensem, posteaquam Landtgravius fuerit liberatus, nominatim indicent atque proponant. Ex quibus ambarum partium nuncupatis Majestas Cæsarea tres Principes deligat, (inter autem sex illos ad minus tres sint seculares) in persona propria, aut etiam ad idem deputati consiliarii, tanquam Cæsareani Commissarii, gravamina illa & exceptiones, contra prædictas latas sententias & executionem debito modo, ac ut decet, recognoscant atque revideant, ecquid acta tempore custodiæ Landtgravii exhibita rursus assumenda, Sententiæ quoque latæ ac Processus super ejusmodi propositis & adhuc dum proponendis gravaminibus, exceptionibusq; differendi ac suspendendi sint nec ne, cognoscant, & quid Juris sit, pronunciant. Atque hæc quidem amica tractatio & decisio ad summum intra biennium post conclusionem & datam compositionis seu transactionis hujus certò expediatur ac exequatur.
units.tr: 6. Likewise, while the custody of the Nassauers lasts, the execution of the sentences promulgated shall be deferred and suspended, until, once the Landgrave is freed, a friendly negotiation between the parties can be instituted and carried on. But if that friendly negotiation should not go forward, then the Landgrave shall nevertheless, as is just, be given in future the testimonies, written documents and other necessary things which, owing to the lack of advocates hitherto, could not be produced while he was in custody, and shall be shown and produced. And then indeed these Electors whom this cause does not touch, themselves or their counsellors, together with six other wholly impartial princes of the Empire, shall each be named and proposed by name by both parties, fifteen from each side, to His Imperial Majesty within a month after the Landgrave has been freed. From the names of both parties His Imperial Majesty shall choose three princes (of the six at least three shall be secular), either in person or through counsellors deputed for this purpose as Imperial Commissioners. They shall examine and review in due manner, and as is fitting, the grievances and exceptions against the said sentences passed and their execution; they shall consider whether the acts exhibited during the Landgrave's custody are to be taken up again, and whether the sentences passed and the proceedings concerning such grievances and exceptions, both already raised and still to be raised, are to be deferred and suspended or not, and they shall pronounce what the law is. This friendly negotiation and decision shall certainly be concluded and carried out within two years at the most after the conclusion and date of this settlement or agreement.

units.la: 7. Cæteris verò punctis & articulis omnibus inter memoratos Electorem Principem Saxoniæ, & Wilhelmum Lantgravium Hessiæ propositis tamdiu, quousque reliqua communiter proposita gravamina expediantur, dilatis atque suspensis.
units.tr: 7. All other points and articles proposed between the said Elector, Prince of Saxony, and William, Landgrave of Hesse, shall be deferred and suspended for as long as the other grievances proposed in common are not settled.

units.la: 8. Administrator item ordinis Teutonici, atque Dux Henricus Brunsvigensis, aliiq; Lantgravium præteriti Schmalkaldensis belli causa impetentes, aut porrò impetituri, cessent quoque & quiescant, donec prædicta gravamina tesolvantur.
units.tr: 8. Likewise the Administrator of the Teutonic Order, and Duke Henry of Brunswick, and others who attack or will attack the Landgrave on account of the former Schmalkaldic war, shall also cease and be quiet until the aforesaid grievances are resolved.

units.la: 9. Etiam nova superius memorata gravamina, quæ durante Lantgravii custodia, in Judicio Imperiali, aliasve adversus eū præsumpta fuerè, simul cum eorum exceptionibus, ab Electoribus & Principibus harum controversiatum intercessoribus proximo Comitio, uti decet, recognoscantur revideanturque, ac idem Lantgravius prout necesse est, audiatur: In iisdem quoque quod æquum & justum est decernatur, neque interea tamen in Camera Imperialis Judicio procedatur.
units.tr: 9. Also, the new grievances mentioned above, which were alleged against him in the Imperial Court, or elsewhere, during the Landgrave's custody, shall, together with their exceptions, be duly examined and reviewed at the next Diet by the Electors and princes who intervene in these disputes, and the same Landgrave shall be heard as necessary. In these matters too, what is equitable and just shall be decreed; meanwhile, however, no proceeding shall be taken in the Imperial Chamber Court.

units.la: CAP. II. Religionem, pacem, & justitiam concernentia.
units.tr: CAP. II. Concerning religion, peace, and justice.

units.la: VERUM atqui alios sequentes articulos quod concernit, ab Electore Saxoniæ, suisq; conjunctis in hac pacificatione propositis, & quidem primò de Religione, de pace, & justitia, Majestas Cæsarea sponsionem gratiosam nuper ad oppidum Linsiuni factam, extunc dato responso fideliter præstabit, & ut intra dimidii anni spatiū Comitia habeantur, in quibus dein qua via, quibusq; modis, nimirum seu Generali seu Nationali Concilio, aut Colloquio, vel communi etiam Imperii conventu Religionis dissidia commodè atque compendio sopiantur, hæq; ad unionem Christianam redigantur, atque ejusmodi conciliatio Religionis ab omnibus Sacri Imperii Statibus, mediante Majestatis suæ ordinaria ope præsidioq; pertractetur.
units.tr: But as for the other articles that follow, proposed in this pacification by the Elector of Saxony and his associates, and first of all concerning religion, peace, and justice: His Imperial Majesty will faithfully fulfil the gracious promise recently made at the town of Linz, and, from the time of the reply given, will ensure that a diet is held within the space of half a year. At that diet it shall be deliberated by what way and by what means the dissensions of religion may be conveniently and expeditiously settled, namely whether by a General Council, a National Council, a colloquy, or even a common assembly of the Empire, and by what means these matters may be brought back to Christian unity; and that such a reconciliation of religion shall be pursued by all the Estates of the Holy Empire, with the ordinary help and support of His Majesty.

units.la: 2. Initio autem Comitiorum ad præparationem cõcordiæ delectus placidarum prudentumq; personarum constituatur, utriusque Religionis æquali numero cum Mandato deliberandi, quibus modis ejusmodi conciliatio atque concordia institui commodè posset, absque Electorum Principum præjudicio tamen hujus delectus ergò.
units.tr: 2. At the opening of the Diet, a selection of peaceable and prudent persons shall be appointed to prepare for concord, equal in number from each religion, with a mandate to deliberate on the ways by which such a reconciliation and concord might conveniently be established, yet without prejudice to the Electors and Princes for the sake of this selection.

units.la: 3. Et quidem interea temporis nec Cæsarea Majestas, neque nos, ac Electores, Principes, & S. Imperii Status quempiam ex Augustanæ confessionis Statibus, propter religionem, vi factove, aut aliàs contra ejus conscientiam ac voluntatem cogere, aut ea de causa vi bellove petere, vel invadere, vel oppugnare aliquè, eive damnū aliquod inferre sive per mandata, sive alio quovis modo ipsum gravare vel etiā contemnere, feremus, sed suæ Religioni fideiq; quietè & pacificè stare, cadereq; sinentes.
units.tr: 3. Meanwhile, neither His Imperial Majesty, nor we, the Electors, Princes, and Estates of the Holy Roman Empire, will compel any of the Estates of the Augsburg Confession, on account of religion, by force or deed, or otherwise against his conscience and will, nor for that reason will we seek, attack, or assault him with war or violence, nor inflict any damage on him, nor burden or even despise him by mandates or in any other way; but we will allow him to stand and fall quietly and peacefully in his religion and faith.

units.la: 4. Ob hoc quoq; bellū Status omnes Augustanæ confessionis cæterosq; Sacri Imperii Statusanti quæ religionis Ecclesiasticos & seculares similiter Religionis suæ, Ceremoniarum, constitutionum, rerum immobilium & mobilium, ditionum, subditorum, tributuum, censuum, superioritatum, & Jurisdictionum causa non gravent, sed pacificè tranquilleq; illis uti fruiq; sinant, nec vi factove, seu alias maligne contra eos quicquam præsumant: Verum enimvero juxta nostras & Sacri Imperii ordinationes, constitutiones, edicta, decreta, Recessus factæ pacis, singuli erga singulos ordinario jure justitiaq; contenti sint, sub proximè renovatæ pacificationis pœna.
units.tr: 4. For this same reason, all the Estates of the Augsburg Confession and the other Estates of the Holy Roman Empire, whatever their religion, ecclesiastical and secular alike, shall likewise not burden one another on account of their religion, ceremonies, constitutions, immovable and movable property, lordships, subjects, tributes, rents, superiorities, and jurisdictions, but shall allow them to use and enjoy these peacefully and quietly, and shall presume nothing against them by force or deed, or otherwise maliciously. Rather, in accordance with our ordinances and those of the Holy Roman Empire, its constitutions, edicts, decrees, and the recesses of the established peace, each shall be content with ordinary law and justice towards every other, under the penalty of the peace that has just been renewed.

units.la: 5. Quicquid verò in Comitiis illis à communibus Statibus unà cū Cæsareæ Majestatis ordinario præsidio concludetur ac statuetur, in posterum quidem & rectè & firmiter servetur, nequeum contrarium, aliave via diversum agatur.
units.tr: 5. Whatever shall be concluded and decided at that Diet by the common Estates together with the ordinary aid of His Imperial Majesty shall indeed be rightly and firmly observed in future, and nothing contrary to it, or any other different course, shall be pursued.

units.la: 6. Omne autem quod dictis induciis adversatur, adversarive censetur, in nihilo derogetillis, aut quicquam imminuer, idq; à Cæsarea Majestate, nobis item, & Electoribus Principibus, ac Statib* respectivè, sufficienter, in quantum fuerit necesse, vigore hujus compositionis seu transactionis cautū, confirmatumq; sit: Prætor quoque Camerae Judicii & Confessores de iisdem induciis certificentur, mediusq; eorum juramentis, eisdem pareant & obsequantur: Implorantibus etiam partibus non attento eo, cujusnam sint religionis, necessarias & legitimas ferant suppetias: formulam quoque cumprimis jurisjurandi Deum & sanctos, aut Deum & sancta Evangelia, confessoribus, aliisque personis & Partibus deinceps liberam permittendo.
units.tr: 6. Moreover, everything that opposes or is judged to oppose the said truce shall be in no way derogated from or diminished by it, and this shall be sufficiently secured and confirmed by His Imperial Majesty, and likewise by us, the Electors, Princes, and Estates respectively, as far as necessary, by virtue of this composition or agreement. The praetor of the Chamber Court and the assessors shall also be informed of the same truce, and by their oaths shall obey and comply with it. Likewise, when the parties implore aid, the necessary and lawful assistance shall be given, without regard to what religion they belong to; and the form of oath, especially "by God and the saints" or "by God and the holy Gospels," shall be freely permitted henceforth to the assessors and to the other persons and parties.

units.la: 7. In suffragiis quoq; dandis rogandisq; æqualitas servetur, æquum jus partibus, nec iniquum reddendo & conservando: Simuliter & in præsentandis Assessoribus, aliisq; pacis & justitiæ articulis hac tractatione placuit, si quod operæprecium ac deliberatione dignum in dicasterii Cameræ constitutione apparuerit, quandoquidem eadem constitutio communi Statuum assensu, Comitioque Imperii sancita est, non etiam nisi per Cæsaream Majestatem, Statusq; communes rebus ita ferentibus ordinaria via, utpote visitationibus, aliisq; mediis mutari tolliq; posse. In qua re nos, Electorum Legati, comparentes Principes, & absentium nuncii recipimus nos, ac consentimus omnem diligentiam, operamq; præstituros, ne qua partium, in Religionis negocio suffragiorum, imparitate sibi præ cæteris metuat, partialitate remota: Augustanæ quoq; Confessionis consortes à Cæsareo Camerae judicio non excludantur, aliaq; gravamina, si quæ comperiantur, ex æquitate removeantur: & hæc quidem omnia proximis Comitiis explicentur.
units.tr: 7. In giving and taking votes, equality shall also be preserved, giving and maintaining an equal right to the parties and not an unjust one. Likewise, in presenting assessors and in the other articles of peace and justice, it has been agreed in these negotiations that, if anything worthy of effort and deliberation appears in the constitution of the Chamber court, since that constitution was sanctioned by the common assent of the Estates and the Diet of the Empire, it may not be changed or abolished except by His Imperial Majesty and the common Estates, in the ordinary way, when circumstances require, namely by visitations and other means. In this matter, we, the envoys of the Electors, the Princes present, and the messengers of the absent, accept and agree that we will make every diligent effort so that no party, in matters of religion, may fear for itself an imbalance of votes against the others, partiality being removed. The fellow members of the Augsburg Confession shall also not be excluded from the Imperial Chamber Court, and other grievances, if any are found, shall be removed in fairness. And all these matters shall be explained at the next Diet.

units.la: 8. Cæterùm & hoc nos unà Electorum Legatis, comparentibus Principibus & absentiū nunciis apud Cæsaream Majestatem, amanter, reverenterque cum reverentia petivimus, uti ejus Majestas puncta illa plus necessaria, inter quæ & articuli præsentationis, & ne Augustanæ confessionis conjuncti à judicio Camerae, ut supra dictum est, excludantur, continentur: ex plenitudine Majestatis suæ Cæsareæ ad provehendam, retinendamq; pacem & concordiam in Imperio, quantocyus fieri posset, re-solvere dignaretur.
units.tr: 8. Furthermore, we, together with the envoys of the Electors, the Princes present, and the messengers of the absent, have also humbly and respectfully asked His Imperial Majesty, with reverence, that His Majesty might deign, from the fullness of his imperial power, to resolve, as quickly as possible, those points that are most necessary for advancing and preserving peace and concord in the Empire, among which are the articles of presentation and that the members of the Augsburg Confession not be excluded from the Chamber court, as was said above.

units.la: CAP. III.
units.tr: CHAPTER III.

units.la: Germanica nationis libertatem contingentia.
units.tr: Concerning the liberty of the German nation.

units.la: Quod ad gravamina, quæ Germanicæ nationis libertati contraria irreprisse, ne dicam ituisse, videntur, inter Electoris Saxonici articulos alio quoq; scripto comprehensa attinet: Volebamus quidem una cum Electoribus, Legatis, Principibus præsentibus, & absentium nuncijs prompti paratiqueac minimè gravati, illos ipsos, appendicesq; suos singulatim protinus & specificè pro amicabili compositione tractanda suscepisse, nisi intellexissemus à Cæsareæ Majestatis ad hanc tractatione lectis destinatisq; consiliariis, ipsius Majestatem talium gravaminum hactenus bona ex parte insicium esse atq; ignarũ, quamobrem de iis mandata dare consiliariis nequivisse: Adhæc, ea ipsa gravamina tanta, tamq; varia esse & prolixa, e contrà vero tempus hoc perexiguum indicta dici, ut ipsi Electori quoq; Saxonico, suisq; conjunctis, donec hæ res omnes, quæ madmodum necessitas postulat, explicentur, copias suas alendo, inumodicos sumptus atq; impendia non solum patiet, verum etiam superioritatibus hinc inde, miserisq; subditis gravissimo maximoq; damno sit futura.
units.tr: As for the grievances which seem to have crept in, not to say gone in, contrary to the liberty of the German nation, and which are also included in the articles of the Elector of Saxony and in another writing: we indeed wished, together with the Electors, the legates, the Princes present and the envoys of those absent, to be ready and prepared, and in no way reluctant, to take up those articles and their appendices one by one, promptly and specifically, for amicable settlement. But we understood that the counsellors of His Imperial Majesty appointed to this negotiation had hitherto been, for the most part, unaware of and ignorant of such grievances, so that they could not give them instructions about them. Moreover, those grievances are so great, so varied and so lengthy, while the time allotted is very short and has not been announced, that the Elector of Saxony himself and his associates will, until all these matters are explained as necessity demands, not only suffer the expense and great outlay of maintaining their troops, but it will also be a very grievous and very great loss to the superiorities on every side and to the wretched subjects.

units.la: 2. Proinde hujuscemodi gravaminum resolutionem ad proxima Comitia, aliumve Imperii conventum hac vice rejicientes, spe bona ex Linfica consensione per Cæsareæ Majestatis consiliarios præbita suffulti, consilium initurum esse, quo sacri Imperii & Statuum publicis & privatis causis consuleretur, cùm jam in eo tota Majestas sua elaboret, ut & apud suâ Majest. Germanicus Senatus constituatur, & Germanicæ res causæq; per Germanos tractentur ac disponantur, ita, ut omnibus placeat, omnibusq; fiat satis. Quâdoquidem Germanicæ nationi ceu dilectæ suæ patriæ tam bene velit, ut haud quidem diminutam eam aut debilitatam, verùm multò magis quantum fieri potest auctam, amplificatam atq; conservatam cupiat, quæ quidem hoc tempore pollicitatio undiquaque cum gratiarum actione accepta est.
units.tr: 2. Therefore, deferring the resolution of such grievances to the next Diet or to another assembly of the Empire on this occasion, and supported by the good hope given through the counsellors of His Imperial Majesty in the Linz agreement, they will undertake a plan by which the public and private affairs of the Holy Empire and of the States may be looked after, since His Majesty is already labouring toward this: that a German Senate be established at His Imperial Majesty's court, and German affairs and causes be handled and arranged by Germans, so that it pleases all and satisfies all. Since he so wishes well to the German nation as to his beloved fatherland, he desires it not diminished or weakened, but much rather increased, enlarged and preserved as far as possible. This promise has indeed been received everywhere with thanksgiving.

units.la: 3. Ne autem Elector Saxonicus, suiq; adjuncti meruant hanc tractationem sponsam neglectu ni, aut posthaberi, sine debito non decisam, debemus nos filiusq; nostér dilectus, Maximilianus Rex, Electores quoq; Principes, & Status sacri Imperii in manus sumere propositá gravamina, atque Cæsareæ Majestati ea offerre, eoque enim atq; conari promovendo, ut quoad æquitatis fundamento insistant, visa quoque ut decet, Aurea Bulla, ac aliis sacri Imperii ordinationibus, constitutionibus, veteribusq; laudatis Germanicæ nationis consuetudinibus omnia probè resolvantur ac perficiantur. Reliqua verò ad Cæsaream Majestatem non proprie spectantia gravamina, sed à quibusdam sacri Imperii Statibus & membris privatim allata sunt, aut quæ ipsi inter sese Status disceptant, de forma fortè ac modo communis consultationis tractationisve, aut aliam ob rem quampiam controversam, æqua & illaut supra ponitur, Cæsareæ Majestatis tanquam Capitis eorum consilio præsidióque proximu Co-mitiiniitio proponi vult atq; absolvi, gratiosa nimirum hac piaq; Majestatis suæ pollicitatione, ut quæ adipsius Majestatem in specie proprieque faciunt, in iis sic se tam gratioso bonoque animo ac voluntate gesturum esse, ut communes perspiciant Status, summa ejus Majestatem cupiditate controversias omnes ut decet, velle atque expetere compositas, & Rempub. privato emolumento longè præstaram fore, cæteraque omnia ita suscipi, institutiq;que, ut omnibus Statibus ex æquo & bono quàm plenissimè fiat satis.
units.tr: 3. Lest the Elector of Saxony and his adherents deserve that this negotiation, promised, be neglected or set aside, not decided without due consideration, we, and our beloved son Maximilian the King, must take up the proposed grievances, the Electors also, the Princes and the States of the Holy Empire, and offer them to His Imperial Majesty. For we shall strive to promote this, so that, insofar as they rest on the foundation of equity, and with the Golden Bull and the other ordinances, constitutions and old praised customs of the German nation duly regarded, all things may be properly resolved and completed. The remaining grievances, which do not properly concern His Imperial Majesty but have been brought forward privately by certain Estates and members of the Holy Empire, or which the Estates dispute among themselves concerning the form or manner of common consultation or negotiation, or for some other controversial reason, His Majesty wishes to be proposed and settled at the next Diet, with his counsel and help as head of them. He does so by this gracious and pious promise: that in those matters which concern His Majesty in particular and properly, he will so act with such a gracious and good spirit and will that the common Estates perceive that His Majesty, with the greatest eagerness, as is fitting, wishes and seeks all controversies to be settled; and that the Commonwealth will be far advanced beyond private advantage; and that all other matters be undertaken and arranged so that all the Estates may be satisfied as fully as possible, with equity and goodness.

units.la: 4. Porrò ad articulum Regis Franciæ Oratorum veniendo, media quædam ac puncta pacis publicæ cōstituendæ, aliorumq; negociorum quorundam prætendentium: ita se habet, ut cùm, quæ publicæ sunt pacis in Germanica natione, solùmodò Imperatoriam Majestatem nos, & Electores, Principesac Status sacri Imperii, neminemq; præterea concernant, & jam isti contentus harummet rerum, tupote publicæ pacis sanciendæ, aliorumque gravaminum atnovendorum causa sit institutus, idcircò nulla jam alia tractatione fore opus existimatur.
units.tr: 4. Moreover, coming to the article of the orators of the King of France, concerning certain means and points for establishing public peace, and of certain other pretended affairs: it stands thus, that since the matters of public peace in the German nation concern only His Imperial Majesty, us, the Electors, Princes and States of the Holy Empire, and no one else, and since this assembly has been instituted for the sake of sanctioning public peace and resolving other grievances, it is therefore judged that no other negotiation is needed.

units.la: 5. Atqui verò privata Regis Franciæ negocia quod spectat, Elector Saxonicus vigore Linsen-sis decreti seu recessus cum dicto Rege aut suis Oratoribus, si id necedū factū est, dein tractare poterit; [illegible, ~20 letters] Imperium [?]. Ad haec, Caesar Majestatem, ergo nos sacrumque Imperium lege aut consuetudine obstricti.
units.tr: 5. As for the private affairs of the King of France, the Elector of Saxony may then negotiate them with the said King or his orators, by virtue of the Linz decree or recess, if this has not yet been done [illegible, ~20 letters]. Furthermore, His Caesarean Majesty, we and the Holy Empire are bound by law or custom.

units.la: 2. Praeterea quaeque a Summo Caesare sunt facta, exterisque omnes utrinque captiad praesentem diem ad concordiam et damnationem dagmatis, in ea rebus de libertate donentur.
units.tr: 2. Moreover, whatever has been done by the Supreme Caesar, and all foreigners on both sides up to the present day, for concord and the condemnation of the dogma, in those matters concerning liberty are to be granted.

units.la: 3. Quod si Alberto Mansfeldio aut quibusdam cuiusdam, et iam tempus praefixum, transigatur, ut ipse cuiquam nolens, seu dominum, detrimentum esse reddat.
units.tr: 3. If Albert of Mansfeld, or certain others, and the time now fixed be concluded, so that he, unwilling, shall make restitution of the damage to anyone or to the lord.

units.la: 4. Quod ita pulchrum et Brunsuigensem Deum Henricum, qui ex Duce Henrico Brauns uigensi, ad carceres, et simul liberum ad carcerem ad Gosleriam et ad ea maxime vinculis unitate offensus.
units.tr: 4. Likewise, Henry, Duke of Brunswick, from Duke Henry of Brunswick, to the prisons, and at the same time free to the prison at Goslar, and especially offended by these bonds of union.

units.la: 5. Caesarea Majestas, atque, ac requisitis Electores, Principes, dictos praetores seu Commissarios, quod ad mandato ut ex eo, et publicer pacis prodesse putentur, gratia atque omni tuebimur, defendemus ac manutenebimus.
units.tr: 5. His Caesarean Majesty, and the Electors, Princes and said praetors or commissioners, as required, by the mandate, and as public peace may be thought to profit, we will protect, defend and maintain with grace and every...

units.la: 6. Ad haec grande sub poena proscriptionis interminatione edictum exire in Ducem Henricum a Caesarea Majestate, ne qua procerum corpori, rebus ac bonis, praesertim autem sylvis cum Dux, obsint, diuturnis ab intercessoribus tota audiatur ac componatur, et illi quoque restituantur.
units.tr: 6. Moreover, a great edict under penalty of proscription, with a threat, is to go out from His Caesarean Majesty against Duke Henry, that no harm be done to the body, goods and property of the nobles, especially the forests, since the Duke ... for a long time be heard and settled by the intercessors, and that those things be restored to him as well.

units.la: CAP. VIII. Civitates Goslariam & Brauns fugam concernentia.
units.tr: Chapter VIII. Concerning the cities of Goslar and Brunswick and the flight.

units.la: Sanctissimi praedictis quatuor Electoribus & Principibus, tanquam delegatis sanctis Commissariis, quoque in jungetque Caesarea Majestas, & Ducis Henrici & aliorum civitatum Brunsuigensium & Goslariensium actiones ac petitiones quantum necesse fuerit examinandas atque exbendas, ac quo utrinque sunt componi, publico Caesareae Majestatis edicto propositio, ut a coepto armis desistant, et omnibus inde mutuo abstineant, Caesareanorum delegatorum tractationi parendo, aut omnino aliis jure ordinario atque Imperii constitutionum vigore explicando.
units.tr: The Emperor's Majesty also joins the aforesaid four Electors and Princes, as delegated commissioners, in examining and settling, as far as necessary, the actions and petitions of Duke Henry and of the other cities of Brunswick and Goslar, and in determining how they may be reconciled on both sides. By public edict the Emperor proposes that they lay down their arms and abstain from mutual harm, either by submitting to the treatment of the imperial delegates or by having the matter fully decided through ordinary law and the force of the imperial constitutions.

units.la: CAP. IX. Ut ad servandam hanc transactionem Caesarea Majestas fidelitatem obliget.
units.tr: CHAPTER IX. That His Imperial Majesty binds himself to keep this agreement.

units.la: Haec omnia & singula supra scripta, sicut singuli articuli nominatim specificati, Caesarea Majestas, quo ad pfammet concernunt, vi virtutis, rationis, et Maiestatem dignitate nuncupata lingua proximo, sumque posterius firmiter, et tracte, cunctisque contra dictam servare juste, rectéque exequi debet, nec in contrarium vel nunc vel in futurum. Si ex hoc aliqua ... volumus.
units.tr: All these things, written above in full and in each part, as the individual articles name them, His Imperial Majesty must, insofar as they concern him, by the force of virtue, reason and his dignity, firmly and faithfully observe and justly and rightly carry out, and must not act contrary to them either now or in future. If from this any ... we will.

units.la: 2. Si quis quive Status, unus pluresve, aliquem alioque quovis modo, quovisve specie seu jure exmittere, oppugnare, laedere, aut gravare suave dirtipere tentaret, quod tamen nullo ratione fieri potest, Caesarea Majestas in unum cum altera parte, in quantum eos actio ... non tenebitur, Caesarea ope consilioque; vel alio ex officio sua Majestatis addecet, aequum; et ad ... gravamina amovere satagat.
units.tr: 2. If any Estate or Estates, one or more, should attempt to expel, attack, injure, burden or harm any of them in any way or by any species or right (which indeed can in no way be done), His Imperial Majesty, together with the other party, insofar as the action ... does not bind them, shall by Imperial aid and counsel, or by some other duty befitting his Majesty, fairly strive to remove the grievances.

units.la: CAP. X. Consensio Principum Hallensium in hanc transactionem seu compositionem.
units.tr: CHAPTER X. Consent of the Princes of Halle to this transaction or composition.

units.la: Nos quoque Elector Saxonicus, Otto Dux Palatinus, Joannes Albertus Dux Mecklenburgensis, Ernestus Ludovicus Landgravius Hassiae, & ceterorum publicum, omnium ac singuli, sequentes punctis et articulos nostrae mentis & voluntate corporis, decrevimus, & consensum ... [illegible, ~10 letters].
units.tr: We also, the Elector of Saxony, Otto Duke Palatine, John Albert Duke of Mecklenburg, Ernest Louis Landgrave of Hesse, and of the rest of the public, all and each, following the points and articles of our mind and will, have decreed and given consent ... [illegible].

units.la: SEQVVNTVR ARTICVLI DE RELIGIONE, PACE, & justitia, per Regiam Majestatem, Electorum Legatos, praesentes Principes, & absentium nuncios designati.
units.tr: The following articles concerning religion, peace, and justice, designated by His Royal Majesty, the Electors' envoys, the princes present, and the messengers of those absent.

units.la: Quo ad Religionis, pacis, & justitiae articulum, Regia Majestas cum Electorum Legatis, praesentibus Principibus, & absentium nuncliis inter Caesareani & Regiam Majestates, Electores, & Status Germanicae nationis, donec controversia Religio tandem concordetur, inducias fieri firmas existimant, sicquidem, ut Caesarea & Regia Majestates, Electores quoq; Principes & Status sacri Imperii, nullum ex Augustana confessione Statum, aut qui sectis publice per Imperii decreta damnatis non adhaereat, vi factove, aut alius contra conscientiam ac voluntatem rationibus, modisq; de sua religione & fide deturbet, dejiciat, propellat, aut bello petat, laedatve, gravetve, aut etiam reprehendat, quinimo Religione quemq; sua fideq; tranquille pacificeq; vivere agereq; sinat, neq; religionis controversiam aliter quam amicis placidisq; mediis modisq; ad Christianum concordem intellectum unionemq; perduci ferat sustineatq;. Conjuncti quoq; hujus belli, aliiq; Status omnes, caeterosq; sacri Imperii Status tum Ecclesiasticos, tum seculares sua Religione, Ecclesiastico usu, ordine & ceremoniis, atque facultatibus, bonis, dioecesibus, subditis, redditibus, censibus, dominiis, & jurisdictionibus non privent aut gravent, sed uti frui illis pacifice sinant, neq; vi, facto, aliasve malignè adversus eos praesumant: sed per omnia sacri Imperii jun, ordinationibus, decretis, edictis, recessibus, atq; publicae pacis constitutioni quisq; stet, pareatq; ordine suo, sub interminatione poenae in proximè renovata publicae pacis sanctione comprehensae.
units.tr: Concerning the article of religion, peace, and justice, His Royal Majesty, together with the Electors' envoys, the princes present, and the messengers of those absent, between His Caesarean and Royal Majesties, the Electors, and the Estates of the German nation, judge that truces are to be made firm until the controversy over religion is finally settled. Thus, neither His Caesarean and Royal Majesties, nor the Electors, princes and Estates of the holy Empire, shall by force or deed, or by any other means against conscience and will, drive out, expel, or drive away from his religion and faith any Estate adhering to the Augsburg Confession, or any who do not adhere to the sects publicly condemned by the decrees of the Empire; nor shall they attack, harm, burden, or even rebuke them by war. Rather, they shall allow each person to live and conduct himself in his religion and faith quietly and peacefully, and shall neither permit nor bear that the controversy over religion be brought to a Christian, harmonious understanding and union by any means other than friendly and peaceful ones. Likewise, the allies in this war and all other Estates, and the rest of the Estates of the holy Empire, whether ecclesiastical or secular, shall not deprive or burden them of their religion, ecclesiastical use, order and ceremonies, or of their faculties, goods, dioceses, subjects, revenues, incomes, domains, and jurisdictions, but shall allow them to enjoy these peacefully; nor shall they presume to act maliciously against them by force, deed, or otherwise. Instead, in all things each shall abide by and obey the ordinances, decrees, edicts, recesses of the holy Empire and the constitution of public peace, each in his own rank, under threat of the penalty comprised in the public peace sanction soon to be renewed.

units.la: 2. Acquaecunq; saepe dictis induciis adversari videbuntur aut existimentur, nihil tamen derogent, sed à Caesarea & Regia Majestatibus, Electoribus, item Principibus ac Statibus respective sufficienter, & ut necesse est, provideri caveriq; debent mediante hujus transactionis Caesareo quoq; judicio Camerae, & Assessoribus induciae praedictae intimentur ac innotescant, ad earum observationem jurejurando suo adactis, omnino illis se ut conformes obtemperantesq; gerant, Partibus item implotantibus nulla religionis differentia respectuve habito, prout decebit, opusq; fuerit, opeque juris justitieq; ferant. Assessorum quoq; aliarumq; personarum junsjurandi per Deum sanctosque, aut Deum, sanctumq; Evangelium, formula juraturis liberè concessa.
units.tr: 2. Whatever things seem or are thought to be contrary to the aforesaid truces, nevertheless shall not derogate from them; but these shall be sufficiently and, as necessary, provided for and guarded by His Caesarean and Royal Majesties, the Electors, and likewise the princes and Estates, respectively, by means of this agreement and the Caesarean judgment of the Chamber. The aforesaid truces shall be announced and made known to the assessors, who shall be bound by oath to observe them, and they shall conduct themselves wholly in conformity and obedience to them. Likewise, when the parties implore aid, no difference or regard for religion shall be had; the assessors shall render help of law and justice as becomes and is needed. The form of oath by God and the holy ones, or by God and the holy Gospel, is freely granted to the assessors and to other persons who are to swear.

units.la: 3. Pro unione autem & pace controversiae Religionis constituenda, Regia Majestas & Electorum consiliarii, tum & praesentes Principes absentiumq; nuncii existimant, Caesarem Majestate proximo semestri post conclusionem & data harum inducatum & compositionis, Comitia habituram esse, in quibus cum Electoribus, Principibus, & Statibus Imperii rationem ineat, an Generali aut nationali Concilio, aut Colloquio, aut alio Imperii conventu & congregatione dissectae Religionis causa instituenda, concordanda, ac definienda sit, & quod per Caesarem Majestatem communesq; tam Augustanae quàm contrariae confessionis Status pro usu ac bono publico statuetur, cum gratia passim omnibus concedatur.
units.tr: 3. For establishing union and peace in the controversy over religion, His Royal Majesty and the Electors' counsellors, as well as the princes present and the messengers of those absent, judge that His Majesty the Emperor will hold an Assembly within the next half-year after the conclusion and date of these truces and agreement, in which he shall consider with the Electors, princes, and Estates of the Empire whether the matter of the divided religion is to be instituted, agreed upon, and settled by a general or national Council, by a Colloquy, or by another assembly and gathering of the Empire. Whatever is decided by His Caesarean Majesty and the common Estates, both of the Augsburg and of the contrary confession, for public use and good shall be granted with grace to all everywhere.

units.la: 4. Et hoc in mentem venit, ad praeparationem ejusmodi unionis ineundae, in initio eorundem Conuentorum nonnullorum tranquillitatis amantium ac prudentium personarum utriusq; Religionis pari numero haberi, quibus injungatur, quomodo concordia talis melius rectiusque suscipiatur, absque tamen Electorum Principum propter hunc ipsum delectum superioritatis ac praeminentiae praejudicio.
units.tr: 4. It has also occurred to us that, in preparation for entering into such a union, at the beginning of these same assemblies some persons of both religions, lovers of tranquility and prudent, shall be appointed in equal number, to whom it shall be enjoined how such concord may be undertaken better and more rightly; yet without prejudice to the superiority and preeminence of the Electors and princes on account of this very selection.

units.la: 5. Ubi autem nulla talibus viis concordia consequeretur, nihilo tamen secus praedictae inducia ad supremum concordiae terminum suas habeant vires, perpetuoq; valeant atq; consistant.
units.tr: 5. But if no concord were to follow by such ways, the aforesaid truces shall nevertheless retain their force until the final term of concord, and shall remain valid and in force forever.

units.la: 6. Ad suffragiorum autem & justitiae aequalitem, tum & praesentationem Assessorum, aliorumque articulorum pacis & justitiae conservandae quod attinet, deliberatum est, si quid grave meditatione cogitaruq; dignum in ordinatione judicii Camerae oboriatur, cùm ea constitutio communi Statuum consensu facta sit, eam quoq; absq; communi Statuum voluntate conditionum respectu, non nisi ordinaria visitationis judicii via, aliasve unà cum praetensis gravaminibus mutari non posse. Cuirei juvandae Regia Majestas unà cum Electorum Legatis, comparentibus Principibus, & absentium nuncis est operam datura, ne in religionis causa altera partium vel suffragiorum vel partialitatis ergo praealtera fe gravatam queri possit, aut etiam Augustanae confessionis adhaerentes & conjuncti à Caesareo Camerae judicio secludi se vereantur. Aliaq; gravamina, si quae innotuerint, ex aequitate proximis Comitiis decidantur.
units.tr: 6. As for equality of votes and of justice, and likewise the presentation of assessors and the other articles for preserving peace and justice, it has been resolved that if anything grave and worthy of serious consideration arises concerning the ordering of the Chamber's court, since that constitution was made by the common consent of the Estates, it likewise cannot be changed without the common will of the Estates, with regard to conditions, except by the ordinary way of visitation of the court or otherwise together with the alleged grievances. To help this matter, His Royal Majesty, together with the Electors' envoys, the princes present, and the messengers of those absent, shall take care, lest in the cause of religion one of the parties may complain of being burdened by the other in votes or partiality, or lest the adherents of the Augsburg Confession and their allies fear being excluded from the Caesarean Chamber court. Other grievances, if any become known, shall be settled at the next Assembly according to equity.

units.la: 7. Dabit quoq; hic operam Regia Majestas unà cum Electorum Legatis, comparentibus Principibus, & absentium nuncis Caesaream Majestatem amanter juxtà ac reverenter interpellando orandoque, ut puncta cum primis necessaria, inter quae & articulus praesentationis atque Augustanae Confessionis, conjuncti, à Caesareo Camerae judicio (ut supra dictum est) ne excludantur, ex plenitudine Caesareae ejus Majestatis, pro retinenda conservandaq; in Imperio pace & concordia, quantocyus fieri poterit, resolvantur atq; expediantur.
units.tr: 7. His Royal Majesty, together with the Electors' envoys, the princes present, and the messengers of those absent, shall also take care to entreat and beg His Caesarean Majesty, lovingly and reverently, that the points most necessary above all, among which is the article of the presentation and of the Augsburg Confession, and of the allies, shall not be excluded from the Caesarean Chamber court (as stated above), but shall be resolved and dispatched as quickly as possible, from the fullness of His Caesarean Majesty's power, for the sake of retaining and preserving peace and concord in the Empire.

units.la: VOdego opus tibi offero, VIR ILLVSTRIS, Consuetudinum & Legum Imperialium, quas huiusce Collectionis inscriptio profitetur, id ad officium dignitatis tuae proprie spectat atque attinet. Necalium sibi patronum optare debuit, praeter te maximum, interque maximos eximium Magnae Germaniae, quam Franciam dixere, Cancellarium, hoc est, Sacri Palatii Imperialis Logothetam, Custodem & Capellanum, penes quem Legum omnium sacrarum sigillum, tutela & publicatio, sacratissimi muneris auctoritate sanciure igitur atque merito hoc meum votiuum munus publice in sacra Cancellorum tuorum, quam Sacristiam mediae aetatis scriptores appellant, suspendo, ut patrocinio tuo fretum & saluti communi commendet, & simul libere versari per ora clientum Imperii tutumque esse ab insidiis possit. Confido in diligentia & dexteritate iudicii tui, cuius gratia in universo sacro Imperio ab utriusque religionis Ordinibus frequenter celebratis & constanter adamaris, te id facturum esse cum libentium studiose. Etenim Leges sunt, eaedemque sacrae ac Imperiales, quae (ut dictum est) ratio, quae aequitatem illarum & iustitiam dirigit, ad libertatem tuum & amplissimum pertinet officium, quod nobis Iurisconsulti illi hisce versibus eleganter descripserunt: Hic est, qui leges Regni cancellat iniquas, Et mandata piy Principis aequa facit: Si quid obest populo, vel legibus est inimicum, Quidquid obest, per eum definit esse nocens.
units.tr: I offer you this work, most illustrious sir, a collection of the customs and imperial laws that its title announces. It belongs properly to the duty of your dignity. Nor should it wish for any other patron than you, outstanding among the greatest men of Greater Germany, which they called Francia, that is, the Chancellor, the Logothete, Custodian and Chaplain of the Imperial Palace, in whose keeping are the seal of all sacred laws, their safekeeping and their publication, by the authority of a most sacred office. I therefore rightly hang up this votive gift of mine publicly in your sacristy of the Chancellors, which the writers of the Middle Ages call the Sacristy, so that, supported by your protection and commended to the common welfare, it may move freely through the mouths of the clients of the Empire and be safe from ambushes. I trust in the diligence and skill of your judgment, for which you are often and constantly admired in the whole Sacred Empire by the orders of both religions, that you will do this with a willing and zealous mind. For these are laws, and both sacred and imperial, and the reason which (as has been said) directs their equity and justice belongs to the liberty and the very wide office of yours. Those jurists described it elegantly for us in these verses: "He is the one who cancels the unjust laws of the realm, and makes the commands of the pious Prince just. If anything is harmful to the people or hostile to the laws, whatever is harmful is by him made to cease to be harmful."

units.la: Verum ipsa etiam consignatio, per quam leges recimauctorum, in iure potestatis tuae consistit. Siquidem vsu hodierno Auctor Historiae, quae de B. Ausberto conscripta le- ... Scriba, doctus conductorque Regalium privilegiorum, & gerulus. lus annuli Regalis, quo eadem signabantur privilegia. Et Ioannes Cotonalas libro de Officiis sacri Palatii Constantinopolitani, sol. 60, Magnus Cancellarius (id est, Cancellarius) diffomat Mandata & Bullas aureas, quas ... mittuntur ad Reges, Sultanos & Toparchas, atque hoc quidem proprium Magnae Logothetae munus esse. Videre profecto habes, ne ulla Principis constitutio, ulla sanctio, ullum diploma, ullum rescriptum, ulli Codicilli Imperatorii non e Republica, atque etiam ex dignitate Imperatoris Ordinum, concedantur aut excant.
units.tr: But the very sealing too, by which laws are renewed, lies within the right of your power. For in present-day usage the author of the History, which was written about St. Ausbert ... scribe, learned and keeper of the royal privileges, and bearer of the ... of the royal ring, by which those same privileges were sealed. And John Cotonalas, in his book on the offices of the sacred palace of Constantinople, page 60, says that the Great Chancellor (that is, the Chancellor) signs the mandates and golden bulls which ... are sent to kings, sultans and toparchs, and that this is indeed the proper duty of the Great Logothete. You see clearly that no constitution of a prince, no sanction, no diploma, no rescript, no imperial codicil is issued or put out that is not in keeping with the public good and also with the dignity of the Emperor and of the Orders.

units.la: Custodiam quoque Legum ad muneris tui amplitudinem attinet satis apparet ex Ordinatione Caroli Magni Imperatoris, quam Hincmarus Archiepiscopus Rhemensis in Epistola ad Carolomannum Regem Principes Francorum refert his verbis: Apocrisiario sociabatur Summus Cancellarius, qui a Secretis olim appellabatur, erantque illi subtiles prudentes & meliores ac fideles viri, qui praeceptis Regia absque immoderata cupiditatis venalitate sciberent & secreta illis fideliter custodirent.
