Are you not ashamed of vanity? And what, I beg you, did the Prussians, Rugians and Saxons, of the same (as ... origin and kindred peoples), ever have in fellowship, whether in war or in peace? Let us look at the rest. "The Thuringians having been put to flight ... lords," etc. The Thuringians never held our Saxony so as to be put to flight; but the Saxons, invited by the Franks ... Thuringians, received as their pay for service a part of Thuringia (as we shall show in its place). From this came the fable about the Thuringians. And lest he seem ignorant of all letters, he adds about the Latin and the Dediticii, so as to show that the Imperial constitutions were known to him. Most inept ... what, I beg you, do the Latins have a part in Saxony? I do not wish to linger on a matter which even boys can correct. ... you will find such things, so that we may plainly prove that the Mirror is not an edition of Charles's.

units.la: Ad Gloffatorem veniamus, virum aliquot iuris peritissimum, et cui plurimum debent eius Constitutionis seruato- ... Sed fabulas narrationi plurimas contemptu dignas inscrit. Non est longe vagandum, vt tale aliquid ostendamus. In ... explanatione, quem diximus. Vide quam puerile est, quod ait, Pompeium Consulem voluisse Imperatorum Leges ... um Codicem redigere: eius temporibus et ante, nulli erant Imperatores, qui leges ferrent. Cum autem Romani fa- ... Consules aut Praetores, quum exercitum deducerent, victoriam assecuti, Imperatores ea tempestate dicebantur, sed Leges ... ibant. Rogabant Consules in Senatu, vt si probarentur, fierent senatusconsulta: et Tribuni plebem, vt plebiscita fierent.
units.tr: Let us come to the Glossator, a man very skilled in law, and to whom his constitution's preservation owes very much ... But he inserts very many fables worthy of contempt in his narrative. There is no need to wander far to show something of this kind. In ... the explanation which we have mentioned. See how childish it is that he says Pompey the Consul wished to reduce the laws of the emperors into a Code: in his times and before, there were no emperors who proposed laws. When the Romans ... consuls or praetors, leading out an army, had won a victory, they were then called emperors, but they did not propose laws ... They asked the Consuls in the Senate that, if approved, they might become senatusconsults; and the Tribunes asked the plebs that they might become plebiscites.

units.la: )( )( fierent, ferant. Mirum, quod vir iuris doctissimus, Constantino tribuat initium legum, & non Pandectis & Iustiniano missa sint hac. Quid est, quod asserit, Karolum fecisse constitutionem de eligendo Imperatoribus? Qua re put tamen Tertium anni ducentu post Karolum. Quid, quod ait, per eundem Karolum sparos Wandalos pro eorum regnum? Quum latissima natio Bohemiam, Poloniam, Russiam, Dalmatiam, & litora Germanici maris longe ante Karolum. Quid, quod Suevos ait expulsos per eos, qui de Anglia redierunt? Quum revera de iis loquuntur, qui hoc fecere. Infinita sunt eius generis. De quibus pauca attigi, eo consilio, non ut virum laude dignissimum reprehendam, sed ut ostendam Lectori, iuribus ab eo introductis, non narrationibus, fidem adhibendam esse. Quod idem accidit cursio diligentissimo Glossatori.
units.tr: It is strange that a man most learned in law should ascribe the beginning of laws to Constantine, and not to the Pandects, and that these things were sent forth by Justinian. What does he mean by asserting that Charles made a constitution on the election of emperors? For instance, it was in the three hundredth year after Charles. And what of his saying that the Vandals were scattered through the realm by the same Charles? Since the very widespread nation held Bohemia, Poland, Russia, Dalmatia and the shores of the German sea long before Charles. And what of his saying that the Suevi were expelled by those who returned from England? Since in truth they speak of those who did this. Things of this kind are endless. I have touched on a few of them, with the aim not of censuring a man most worthy of praise, but of showing the reader that faith should be placed in the legal enactments he introduces, not in his narratives. The same thing happens, too, to the most diligent Glossator, in passing.

units.la: Georg FABRICIVS Origin. Saxonicar. lib. 1. anno sol. 61. Hanc historiam temporum ignorantia, & Auctoripsa, & Interpres iuris Saxonici, quod Speculum appellant, confundit: quod est a diligente viro Alb. Crantzio non prud. nter observatum.
units.tr: Georg Fabricius, Origines Saxonicae, book 1, year 1561 (?). Ignorance of the times confuses this history, both the author himself and the interpreter of Saxon law, which they call the Mirror. This was observed, and not unwisely, by the diligent man Albert Krantz.

units.la: Quid de hoc Krantziano iudicio sentiendum sit, diximus in praefatione Reichenbachii a nobis Germanico editarum. Namque Glossator exsertissimis verbis, & quae mirorat Krantzius termissa, aut non lecta esse, testatur, non Karolum Magnum, sed Eckonem esse huius Speculi auctorem; idque collectum esse partim ex Constantini & Karoli Magni, partim ex Ottonum & Friderici constitutionibus, quorum nomina subiungit. Quod ad Historicas narrationes attinet, in eodem errorem lapsus impegit, quem Tribonianus, Gratianus, & consimiles alii eorum temporum Compilatores. Igitur illa. Nunc pergemus illorum testimonia recensere, qui nobis veritatem & autoritate in huius Speculi penitius comprobant.
units.tr: What is to be thought of this judgment of Krantz, we have said in the preface to Reichenbach's work, which we published in German. For the Glossator states in the plainest words, and on those points which Krantz wonders were omitted or not read, that the author of this Mirror is not Charles the Great but Eike (Eckon). He also states that it was gathered partly from the constitutions of Constantine and Charles the Great, and partly from those of the Ottos and Frederick, whose names he adds. As for the historical narratives, he has fallen into the same error into which Tribonian, Gratian and other compilers of their times fell. So much for those points. Now we shall go on to review the testimonies of those who more thoroughly confirm for us the truth and authority of this Mirror.

units.la: Ioannes AVENTINVS de Ludovico I. Rege, & postea III. Imperatore, scribit: In Synodo Conventum iuridicum ad annum Visurgim agit, &c. Leges Saxonum emendat. Spangenbergius scribit, in Reichstag zu Minden an der Weser id est, Minda ad Visurgum in Comitiis Imperialibus, anno 850. in Chron. Saxon. cap. 100.
units.tr: John Aventinus writes of King Louis I, and afterwards Emperor III: "In a synod he holds a juridical assembly at the Visurgis (Weser)... he emends the laws of the Saxons," etc. Spangenberg writes that it was at the Reichstag at Minden on the Weser, that is, Minda on the Visurgis, in the imperial diet, in the year 850, in his Saxon Chronicle, chapter 100.

units.la: Idem SPANGENBERGIVS in eodem Chron. scribit: Anno 937 hat Kenser Otto auff dem Reichstag zu Stela der Sachsen Recht uberseben lassen, und ihnen stattlich confirmirt, bestätigt: hoc est, anno 937. Stela in Comitiis Imperialibus recensuit Otto Primus Imperator iura Saxonum, & leniter confirmavit & ratificavit.
units.tr: Spangenberg again, in the same Chronicle, writes: "In the year 937 Emperor Otto had the law of the Saxons reviewed at the Reichstag at Stela, and graciously confirmed and ratified it for them." That is, in 937 at Stela, in the imperial diet, Otto I, Emperor, reviewed the laws of the Saxons and gently confirmed and ratified them.

units.la: Idem in eodem Chronico, cap. 247. scribit: Anno 1213. hat Keyser Friderich der Ander auff dem Reichstag zu Merseburg gehalten, den Sachsenspiegel vermehret: hoc est, Imperator Fridericus II Augustus Speculum Saxonum auxit & additis constitutionibus locupletavit, anno Domini 1213. Marburgi in Comitiis Imperialibus. Cui consonat, quod notat Glossa ad l.b.4. Speculi Sax. attic. 87. Constitutio praesens de Pacis Ricardi de Stupsen (lego, Stouffen) Imperatoris. Cui etiam sequentes ad finem usque attribuuntur; tamen Friderico Barbarossae, ut nos opinati in textu praefati ipsimus.
units.tr: Spangenberg, in the same Chronicle, chapter 247, writes: "In the year 1213 Emperor Frederick II held a Reichstag at Merseburg and enlarged the Saxon Mirror." That is, the Emperor Augustus Frederick II enlarged the Mirror of the Saxons and enriched it with added constitutions, in the year of the Lord 1213, at Marburg in the imperial diet. This agrees with what the Gloss notes on book 4 of the Saxon Mirror, article 87: "This present constitution concerning the peace is of Richard of Stupsen (read Stouffen), Emperor." The following ones down to the end are also attributed to him; yet they belong to Frederick Barbarossa, as we ourselves supposed in the text of the preface.

units.la: CAROLVS IV. Imperator Augustus in Aurea Bulla, cap. 5 §. 2. Et eodem iure provisum Ducem Saxoniae sicut Imperii Archimareschallum sui volumus in illo loco, ubi Saxonica iura servantur, &c.
units.tr: Charles IV, Emperor Augustus, in the Golden Bull, chapter 5, §2: "And by the same right we wish that the Duke of Saxony, as Archmarshal of the Empire, be provided for in that place where the Saxon laws are observed," etc.

units.la: GLOSSA Polonica in Wichbild. artic. 1. Ius Provinciale dicitur, quod homines unius Provinciae statuunt, & inter se tenent: ut est ius Provinciale Saxonicum, quod Speculum Saxonum nuncupatur: vel ius Provinciale seu Terrestre Nobilitatis Regni Poloniae, &c.
units.tr: The Polish Gloss on the Wichbild, article 1: "Provincial law is said to be that which the men of one province lay down and keep among themselves, as the Saxon provincial law, which is called the Mirror of the Saxons; or the provincial or territorial law of the nobility of the Kingdom of Poland," etc.

units.la: Arnoldus HVITFELDIVS Magnus Cancellarius Regni Daniae, in praefat. Legum Provincialium terrae Scaniae; Omnes tamen hae leges magna ex parte originem habent ex iure Saxonico: quod causam fuisse credere liceat, qui eas cum libro Saxenspiegel vulgo dicto, contulerit. Sed in Legum Scanicarum & Sialandicarum auctor est Valdemarus Primus Rex Daniae, easque publicavit anno Domini 1163. Credetur Hoc dius, vir caeteris prudens nec indoctus, eorum opinione esse secutus, qui Speculum Saxonum Carolo Magno adscribunt. Cymbricas tamen Leges, quas Valdemarus II. Rex, anno 1241. in Comitiis Vordingborgensibus protulit, non dubito originem suam ex Speculo illo trahere, quod tamen ut ei esse coeperat, indeque ab Vffone Archiepiscopo Lundensi collectas. Quas dabimus (ut Gloss. Anglicus) in Collectione Constitutionum Regiarum.
units.tr: Arnold Huitfeldt, Grand Chancellor of the Kingdom of Denmark, in the preface to the Provincial Laws of the land of Scania: "Yet all these laws for the most part have their origin in Saxon law, which one may believe was the reason for those who compared them with the book commonly called the Saxenspiegel." But the author of the Scanian and Zealandic laws is Valdemar I, King of Denmark, who published them in the year of the Lord 1163. Huitfeldt, a man prudent in other matters and not unlearned, is believed to have followed the opinion of those who ascribe the Mirror of the Saxons to Charles the Great. However, I do not doubt that the Cimbrian laws, which King Valdemar II published in 1241 at the Diet of Vordingborg, derive their origin from that Mirror, and were afterwards collected by Uffo, Archbishop of Lund. We shall give them (as the English Gloss does) in the Collection of Royal Constitutions.

units.la: DE WICHBILDO MAGDE- BVRGENSI
units.tr: On the Wichbild of Magdeburg

units.la: S Vper hoc exstat OTTONIS I. cognomento Magni Imperatoris constitutio in Collectione Constitutionum Imperialium, tom. 1. sol. 215. & OTTONIS II. cognomento Rufi, Imperatoris constitutio, ibidem sol. 215.
units.tr: On this subject there exists a constitution of Otto I, surnamed the Great, Emperor, in the Collection of Imperial Constitutions, vol. 1, p. 215, and a constitution of Otto II, surnamed the Red, Emperor, in the same place, p. 215.

units.la: Burchardus MANGELHELDIVS Compilator huius Iuris, aitarticul. 3. Recitatur pore FRIDERICI Imperatoris statutum fuit, si liber homo seruam superduxerit, vel ingenua seruum, quod ... utriusque sexus matrem sequi deberet, & non patrem. Hic est Fridericus I. Imperator, cognomento Barbarossa. Sequitur iubinde: A temporibus vero Vickmanni Episcopi, iure frequentatum est, & per HENRICVM filium statutum, quod utraque proles, filius & filia, nascuntur secundum matrem, &c. Hic est Henricus VI. Imperator, Barbarossae filius & successor. Wigmanus autem anno 1152. a Friderico illo in ecclesiam, ... obiit anno 1194. sub Henrico. Unde satis manifestum fit, nec huius quidem libri Compilatorem ... Ottonis II. Imperatoris temporibus, sed quadringentis ferme annis post illum sub Lothario Imperatore & Duce Saxoniae Brunsuicensi Comiteque Pictaviensi in Regno Aclarano ... Compilator Constitutiones nonnullas interiecit, quibus nomen eius praescriptum est. Unde appa-ret Mangelpheldium non multum esse posse Eckoue Speculi compositorem posteriorem.
units.tr: Burchard Mangelheld, the compiler of this law, says in art. 3: "Under Emperor Frederick it was enacted that if a free man took a female slave, or a freeborn woman a male slave, the child should follow the mother, not the father, whichever the sex." This is Frederick I, surnamed Barbarossa. He then continues: "From the time of Bishop Wigmann the law was frequently applied, and it was enacted through Henry, his son, that both offspring, son and daughter, are born according to the mother, etc." This is Henry VI, Emperor, son and successor of Barbarossa. Wigmann, who in 1152 passed over into the church under that Frederick, died in 1194 under Henry. From this it is quite clear that the compiler of this book did not live in the time of Otto II the Emperor, but some four hundred years after him, under Lothar the Emperor and Duke of Saxony of Brunswick and Count of Poitou in the kingdom of Aclaran(?)... The compiler inserted some constitutions, which bear his name. From this it appears that Mangelpheld cannot have been the later compiler of the Mirror of Eike.

units.la: IDEM artic. 10. Maydenburgensis civitatis locatio declaranda sequitur. Imperatoris etenim Ottonis Magni con-cessu, accedente etiam Senatorum totius provinciae consensu, primum fundata est & erecta, iureque municipali praesenti confirmata.
units.tr: The same, in art. 10, sets out the founding of the city of Magdeburg to be explained. For by the grant of the Emperor Otto the Great, with the consent also of the senators of the whole province, it was first founded and established, and confirmed in the present municipal law.

units.la: Glossa in proœmio circa sin. Praeterea Imperator ille gloriosus Otto, inter alia praeclara opera, Magdeburgum erexit, Iusque Municipale, quod pre manibus habemus, ex Speculo Saxonum, seu iure Provinciali excerptum, approbavit, illudque tenendum privilegio confirmavit. Sed & eius etiam nonnullis iuxta eorum arbitrium plebiscitis, civitati flatuit, illudque tenendum privilegio confirmavit. Sed & eius Otto Rvssvs, circa annum DCCCC V. Imperator Romanorum creatus, Ecclesiam Cathedralem Magdeburgi fundavit, amplis proventibus eandem dotando: Iusque Municipale praesens, per patrem eius Magnum Ottonem civitati datum confirmavit, nonnulla superaddendo, iuxta tenorem privilegii desuper dati.
units.tr: Gloss on the preface, near the end. Moreover, that glorious Emperor Otto, among his other famous works, founded Magdeburg and approved the municipal law which we have before us, excerpted from the Saxon Mirror or provincial law, and confirmed it by privilege to be kept. He also established for the city some plebiscites according to their judgment, and confirmed it by privilege to be kept. Moreover his son Otto the Red, created Emperor of the Romans about the year 905, founded the cathedral church at Magdeburg, endowing it with ample revenues; and he confirmed the present municipal law, granted to the city by his father Otto the Great, adding some things according to the tenor of the privilege given on that matter.

units.la: Eadem, ad art. 10. de Ottone Magno: Imperator tandem ibidem circa Albim fluvium, Ducatu fundavit Sobarr-ne communiter: sed & civitatem Maydeburgum ibidem locavit, communique privilegio Iuris Municipalis de consensu to-tius provinciae dotavit. Filius eius tandem Otto Russus privilegium Iusque Municipale, per patrem eius Ottonem Magnum civitati concessum, auctoritate Imperiali confirmavit, nonnulla etiam iuxta eorum plebiscita, ac de consilio prudentium il-lustri, exiure Provinciali, quod Speculum Saxonum vocatur, extrahendo addidit. Quum immo illa, quae in Speculo provinciae, ex iure Provinciali, quod Speculum Saxonum vocatur, extrahendo addidit, obscure habebantur, hic clarius enodatae. Hunc quoque operi ac provinciae praefecerat Sequestratorem sacri sui Palatii Ottonis, Burchardum de Manphelt (alii rectius habent, Mangelfeld) Professorem sacrae Theologiae, ac Utriusque Iuris Doctorem, ex mandato Imperatoris, in Ius Provinciale, seu Speculum Saxonum Commentarium fecit, legibusque & canonibus adornavit, idque in conclusi sedendo facere coactus. Praefensetiam privilegium, ut supra tactum est, congestis glossis & interpretationibus lucidius declaravit. Sed & processum Iuris (Richtsteig) compilavit, quem tandem Gerko de Kerta-w ...
units.tr: The same, on art. 10, concerning Otto the Great: the Emperor at last founded the Duchy commonly called Saxony there, by the river Elbe, and he also established the city of Magdeburg there, and endowed it with a common privilege of municipal law, by the consent of the whole province. His son Otto the Red at last confirmed by imperial authority the privilege and municipal law granted to the city by his father Otto the Great, and added some things, drawn from the provincial law called the Saxon Mirror, according to the plebiscites of the citizens and on the advice of learned men. Indeed, those things in the Mirror of the province, which were drawn from the provincial law called the Saxon Mirror, and which were obscure, are here more clearly explained. He also placed over this work and the province Burchard of Manphelt (others more correctly Mangelfeld), sequestrator of his sacred palace, Professor of Sacred Theology and Doctor of Both Laws, who by the Emperor's command made a commentary on the provincial law, or Saxon Mirror, and adorned it with laws and canons, being compelled to do this while sitting in confinement. He also explained the aforesaid privilege more clearly, with glosses and interpretations heaped together, as was touched on above. He also compiled the Process of Law (Richtsteig), which Gerko of Kertaw...

units.la: [illegible, ~40 letters] Henrici de Phalkenstein in Germanicum traduxit. Corpusque ut sic, Iuris Maydeburgensis congestum, reui-dilgenterque interpretatum, per Imperatorem Ottonem confirmatum sunt. Sed & per successores eius illa, se custodie-runt quaedam superaddebantur pro commodo & utili civitatis Maydeburgensis. Privilegium etiam, quod Otto Russus de Maydeburg, ac provinciae, quaedam istis reportant, largius est, hic subinferre consulto videbatur. Id habes, ut diximus, Constitutionum Imperialium, com.a.sol.215. Pergit deinde Glossator recitato privilegii textu, in haec verba: Et haec est gene-ralium libertatum Maydeburgensium confirmatio per Imperatorem Ottonem Russum facta, omniaq; Maydeburgen-sium Municipalia iura ex eo dependent. Unde in testimonium huius Maydeburgensis habent insigne, seu effigiem eius sculp-tam in pro stantem una cum Electoribus Imperii, quae pro ornamento civitatis servatur. Civitasque praetacta, ut supra ha-bitum est, in suis iuribus, & significanter Municipali iure, de consensu totius provinciae confirmata: estque antiquior omnium Maydeburgensium ...
units.tr: [illegible, about forty letters] of Henry of Falkenstein translated into German. And the body of Magdeburg law, thus assembled, carefully revised and interpreted, was confirmed by Emperor Otto. Also, by his successors, those things were preserved, and certain additions were made for the convenience and benefit of the city of Magdeburg. It seemed right to me to insert here, deliberately, the privilege which Otto the Red gave to Magdeburg and the province, which contains some further provisions. You have it, as we said, in the Imperial Constitutions, vol. a, p. 215. The gloss then goes on, after reciting the text of the privilege, in these words: "This is the confirmation of the general liberties of Magdeburg made by Emperor Otto the Red, and all the municipal law of Magdeburg depends on it. Whence, in testimony of this, Magdeburg has its emblem, or its image carved standing together with the Electors of the Empire, which is kept as an ornament of the city. And the aforesaid city, as stated above, was confirmed in its rights, and especially in its municipal law, with the consent of the whole province; and it is the oldest of all the Magdeburg..."

units.la: Alexander Rex Poloniae: Primum vero posuimus libros, qui a nonnullis titulatur Ottonis Caesaris.
units.tr: Alexander, King of Poland: "We have placed first the books which are by some entitled those of Otto Caesar."

units.la: Iohannes a Lasko Cancellarius Regni Poloniae: Quod quidem Ius Maydenburgense, etsi Imperiali Ma-gistro Ottonis Russi Caesaris constitutum fuerit, &c.
units.tr: John of Łask, Chancellor of the Kingdom of Poland: "This Magdeburg law, although it was established by the imperial master Otto the Red Caesar, etc."

units.la: Nicolaus Iaskierus Secretarius Cracouiensis in glossa marginali ad prologum lib. 1. Spec. Ecke translator fuit praesentis Privilegii Saxonicis Latino in Germanicum. Ex mandato vero Imperatoris Ottonis Russi-Burchardus de Manphelt fecit Palatij Sequestratot, Privilegium praesens illuminavit, legibusque & canonibus adornavit. Idem etiam Ius Municipale in luculentam ...formam.
units.tr: Nicholas Jaskier, Secretary of Kraków, in a marginal gloss on the prologue to book 1 of the Mirror of Eike: he was the translator of the present privilege from Saxon Latin into German. By command of Emperor Otto the Red, Burchard of Manphelt, sequestrator of the palace, illuminated the present privilege, and adorned it with laws and canons. The same man also set the municipal law into a clear form...

units.la: Idem in glossa margin. ad Wichbild, artic. 11. Articulus praefens, & sequentes quatuor, parum afferunt vi-tae (lc. Polonis.) Appellatio etenim in Hallam vel Maydeburgum ex Regno Poloniae abolita est in anno Domini Diuum olim Casimirum Magnum Poloniae Regem: locatumque est Ius Provinciale in castro Cracouiensi, ut illic appellando recurrant habeant. Ab illo vero tandem pro instantia ultima, ad tribunal Regium, vel Communi-ariosfex Ciuitatum ad id deputatos pronunciatio fit, iuxta priuilegia desuper data, & diuersos super eo processus habetur, quam hic, ut ex communi praxi liquet.
units.tr: The same, in the marginal gloss on the Wichbild, art. 11: "This article and the following four bring little life (to the Poles). For appeal to Halle or to Magdeburg was abolished in the kingdom of Poland in the year of the Lord..., in the time of Casimir the Great, King of Poland; and provincial law was placed in the castle of Kraków, so that they might have recourse there by appeal. From there, at last, for the final instance, judgment is pronounced by the royal tribunal, or by the commissioners of the common towns deputed for this, according to the privileges given on the matter, and various proceedings are held on it, as is clear from common practice here."

units.la: Spangenbergius in Chronic. Saxon. cap. 150. Anno 937. Imperator Otto Magnus Magdeburgensibus dedit Wichboldum, sive Ius Municipale.
units.tr: Spangenberg, in the Saxon Chronicle, ch. 150: "In the year 937 Emperor Otto the Great gave the Magdeburgers the Wichbold, or municipal law."

units.la: Albertus Krantzius Saxoniae lib. 3. cap. 24. de instauratione Magdeburgi ab Ottone Magno facta: Extant litere, quibus testatur etiam nunc Imperator, quas dederit immunitates novas urbi. Innuit indubio Constitutionem, quam supra diximus tom. 1. sol. 215. Constitutionum Imperialium continere.
units.tr: Albert Krantz, Saxony, book 3, ch. 24, on the restoration of Magdeburg by Otto the Great: "There exist letters in which the Emperor, even now, testifies to the new immunities he gave the city." He undoubtedly points to the constitution which, as we said above, is contained in vol. 1, p. 215, of the Imperial Constitutions.

units.la: Glossa Polonica ad Wichbild, artic. 1. Ius Civile seu Municipale dicitur, quod quisque populus vel civi-tas habitare incipit, causa constituit, quasi in proprium illud civitatem vel fori. Pasquam enim populus habitare in-capit, ciuitatis ..., quae erigi & constitui coeperat; quidquid inter se iuxta eorum arbitrium constituerunt, ius illorum erat: vt ius Athenensium, Lacedaemoniorum; ut est ius Aquisgranense, Coloniense, a D. Carolo Imperatore confirma-tum; ut etiam in praesens est Ius Magdeburgense, quo Cracoviae, & multae civitates Regni utuntur.
units.tr: Polish gloss on the Wichbild, art. 1: "Civil or municipal law is called that which each people or city, when it begins to inhabit, establishes by its own cause, as if for its own city or forum. For when a people begins to inhabit a city which had begun to be built and established, whatever they settled among themselves according to their judgment was their law: such as the law of the Athenians and the Lacedaemonians; such as the law of Aachen and Cologne, confirmed by Emperor Charles; and as now the Magdeburg law, which Kraków and many cities of the kingdom use."

units.la: Glossa ordinaria ad eundem artic. 1. Dubitare quae possit; quandoquidem Saxonibus ante hac Ius Pro-vinciale
units.tr: Ordinary gloss on the same art. 1: "One may doubt, since formerly provincial law was given to the Saxons,

units.la: 2 Municiale datum sit, & provinciae eorum confirmatum, an per iam praesens privilegium posterius lini eorum Speculum Saxonum vocitatur, derogatur necne? Iure enim novo, seu constitutione posteriore superveniente tollit & annullatur. Pro exsoluenda hac dubietate respondendum, quod postquam civitas Maydeburgensis ... legio, quod & breve quoddam modo in se est, dotata & confirmata fuerat, de consensu Imperatoris, Principum & Ordinum ... tatis; ex iure Provinciali, quod Speculum vocatur, extractum est, certis quibusdam plebiscitis superadditis per id derogatum est iuris Provinciali, nec etiam Civitas renunciari Speculo Saxonum per id voluit: verum hoc ... ex certis & rationabilibus causis. Primo, quia hic quaedam constitutiones speciales habentur, quae in Speculo Saxonico non sunt: ut quando increpatur ortu legum in Maydeburgo, non appellatur praecise ad Regem, sed ad Palatinum ... dum vero ius Provinciale appellatio praecise ad Regem fit. Secundo, Privilegium praesens sanciunt est ad supplementum ... vinciali Iuris: ut si quid breviter in iure Provinciali complexum habetur, hic expressius enodatur. Tertio, quod sen ... declaratio iurium, quae in iure Provinciali sparsim in diversis locis habentur, hic summatim & breviter exprimuntur.
units.tr: and their province confirmed in municipal law, whether by this present later privilege their so-called Mirror of the Saxons is derogated or not. For a later law, or a subsequent constitution, takes it away and annuls it. To resolve this doubt it must be answered that after the city of Magdeburg was endowed and confirmed by this privilege, which is in itself also a kind of brief document, with the consent of the Emperor, the Princes and the Orders of the city, and extracted from the provincial law called the Mirror, with certain plebiscites added, the provincial law has indeed been derogated in part by this, yet the city did not wish to renounce the Saxon Mirror by it; rather this was done for certain and reasonable causes. First, because here certain special constitutions are held which are not in the Saxon Mirror: as when appeal is made from the sources of the laws in Magdeburg, it is not made directly to the King but to the Palatine... whereas under provincial law appeal is made directly to the King. Second, the present privilege sanctions, as a supplement to the provincial law, that whatever is briefly comprehended in the provincial law is here set forth more fully. Third, the declaration of rights which are scattered in various places in the provincial law are here expressed summarily and briefly."

units.la: Alius causis praesens Privilegium confirmatum est, nec contradicit Speculo Saxonum, sed est declaratio eius. In privilegio praesenti, quod ... minus & facilius intelligi faciliter Ius Provinciale poterit. Est enim Prima ... fluta seu elementa iuris Provinciali sicut institutae Imperialia sunt elementa legum.
units.tr: This privilege, confirmed by the present charter, does not contradict the Saxon Mirror but is a declaration of it. In the present privilege, which ... the Provincial Law can be understood more easily and readily. For it is the first ... the rudiments or elements of the Provincial Law, just as the Institutes are the elements of the laws.

units.la: Eadem, ad artic. 6. Ex declaratis itaque liquet, Ius Municipale ex Babylone originem habere. Omnes etiam ... inhabitantes uno & eodem iure locati erant, quod Ius Municipale seu Ciuile ducebatur. Urbsque illa initium & radices Imperii & Iuris Municipalis. Constitutiones tamen in Babylone & Persia fancita, omnes pertinere, & in ... Municipale pretactum. Privatum ius etiam dicitur, sicut & praesens Ius Magdeburgense, privatum Ius ... natur. Ideo in etiam Speculum Saxonum ius privatum Provinciae Saxonicae est, & pro privilegio apud illos habetur.
units.tr: Likewise, on article 6. From what has been declared it is clear that Municipal Law has its origin in Babylon. All ... inhabitants were settled under one and the same law, which was called Municipal or Civil Law. That city was the beginning and the roots of the Empire and of Municipal Law. Nevertheless, the constitutions enacted in Babylon and Persia ... pertain to the aforesaid Municipal Law. It is also called private law, just as the present Magdeburg Law is. Therefore the Saxon Mirror is also the private law of the Province of Saxony, and it is held among them as a privilege.

units.la: Eadem, ad art. 9. Non aliud intendit, nisi ut ostendat, unde liber praesens nomen sumpsit, quod videlicet Wichbildum, id est, Ius Municipale, vocitatur. Sortitur etenim nomen (nam a iure ... quod populus sibi fecit, ut ... habitum & non est aliud, nisi Curia Imperii in ( des Sächsischen Kaysers Hofgerichts Recht ) quod Imperator in ... quentabat communiter sua.
units.tr: Likewise, on article 9. He intends nothing other than to show whence this book took its name, namely that it is called Wichbild, that is, Municipal Law. For it takes its name (for from the law ... which the people made for itself ...) and is nothing other than the court law of the Empire (the law of the Saxon Emperor's court of justice), which the Emperor ... commonly ... his own.

units.la: Wig seu munitio in propositio, quae in Saxonico antiquo vocabulo Wighus nuncupatur, triplici interpretatur ... m habet. Primo dicitur esse propugnaculum in muris civitatis constructum, nullum habens tectum. Secundo, dicitur esse domus ... civitate, in qua iudex iudicium exercet suum. Tertio, dicitur esse locus, ubi executio iudicii fit, vel ubi poena ... Primo modo accepta munitio dicitur ex eo, quia inimicis civitatis nocere volentibus, ex illa coercentur ... Secundo modo accepta nuncupatur, quae & Praetorium (Rathhaus) appellatur, est ex eo, quia homines ... convenientes, arceri debent a praviis consuetudinibus, confulerec, continue ad seruandum vera iuris praecepta, & ... ut alia iura; ut nemini nocere, alteri tribuere quod suum est, honeste vivere, &c. Tertia vero munitionis ... ratapatet. Accipi enim debet pro loco, ubi poenae infliguntur, & qui in terrorem confluuntur seu praefigurent, ut homines ... pracustodiant se: & accipitur locus ille pro praecustodietione seu poenae comminatione.
units.tr: Wig or munitio, which in old Saxon is called Wighus, is interpreted in three ways ... It is first said to be a bulwark built on the walls of the city, having no roof. Second, it is said to be the house in the city in which the judge exercises his judgment. Third, it is said to be the place where the execution of judgment takes place, or where punishment ... The first sense of munitio is so called because, when enemies wish to harm the city, they are restrained by it ... The second sense, which is also called the Praetorium (Rathhaus), is so called because men gathering there ought to be kept from wicked customs, and to take counsel continually for keeping the true precepts of law, and ... like the other laws: that no one harm another, that each render to another what is his own, that one live honourably, etc. The third sense of munitio ... is clear. For it must be taken as the place where punishments are inflicted, and where people flock together in terror or are warned beforehand, so that men ... guard themselves in advance; and that place is taken for the forewarning or threat of punishment.

units.la: In vocabulario Iuris Saxonici, quid sit Wich, & Wichbild, hisce verbis exponitur: Weichbild, so viel nach altem Sächsischen Teutschen, als iuris dictio, Gericht oder Gebiet.
units.tr: In the glossary of Saxon Law, what Wich and Wichbild are is explained in these words: Weichbild, in old Saxon German, means as much as iuris dictio, court or territory.

units.la: Item: Weichbild: heist so viel, als weit ein Gebiet rimb ein Statt ist. Und ist vor alters dahin gewesen, dass man ein groß hülzen Creutz in einer Statt oder Flecken hat auffgericht, darauff ein Hau ... und Schwert geflecht, zum Zeichen der Gericht über Halß und Haupt.
units.tr: Likewise: Weichbild means as much as the area that lies around a town. And in former times it was the custom that a large wooden cross was set up in a town or village, on which a hand and sword were fixed, as a sign of the court's jurisdiction over neck and head.

units.la: DE IVRE FEVDALI.
units.tr: CONCERNING FEUDAL LAW.

units.la: Glossa in Specul. Saxon lib. 1. artic. 14. Carolus Magnus Ius Provinciale Saxonibus statuit: Frederic ... Imperator Ius Feudale, ut in auth. de vsi feud. coll. 10.
units.tr: Gloss on the Saxon Mirror, book 1, article 14. Charles the Great established the Saxons' provincial law: Frederick ... Emperor [established] feudal law, as in the authentic text "de usu feudorum," collation 10.

units.la: Eadem, d. lib. 1. artic. 26. Articulus est, non est ex Privilegio, sed est constitutio Frederici Imperatoris ... feud. c. 1 ... mandatoque ipsius hoc inserti est.
units.tr: The same gloss, on book 1, article 26. The article is not from a privilege but is a constitution of Emperor Frederick ... feudal title 1 ... and was inserted here by his command.

units.la: Glossa posteriora ad lib. 3. Specul. Saxon. artic. 78. (Vasallus insequi potest dominum.) Caute ... debet paragraphus ille, nec ita grosse, ut in se sonat. Magna enim praemeditatione intigit vasallus, ut ad aggressionem ... tus suadet. Dictum est enim supra lib. 2. art. 12. quod vasallus contra dominum sententiam murmure non potest ... tolerabilius est, quam quod dominum detinere debeat. Si ergo et facere non licet illud, quod est minus, nec ci ... manus, ut luftit, quib alteu licet vel non, & ff. de reg. iur. d. non debet: etiam habetur in lib. 1. ... Ex quo ... vbi iuratur domino esse auxilio contra unumquemque, quod non esset, si eum detineret, ut hic textus ... 12. q. vlt. de forma. quod vasallus dominum tueri debet ab omni damno; quod hic non esset. ... corrigit & derogat aliis legibus in contrarium. Respondeo tamen, quod nova lex corrigit ... rius est iure Saxonico, quare illud non derogat illi. Dicunt etiam quidam, quod Ius Feudale ... constituta, qua est contraria priori, derogat illi, dato, quod metio aliqua ibidem non fit, ut de consil ... [illegible, ~10 letters] nulla facta est. Abrogationem enim iuris, in probationibus maxime, vitare debemus, in quantum possumus. C. de appell. I. praecipimus, in sin, & in auth. quib. mod. natur. effic. fili. §. tribus. coll. 7.
units.tr: Later gloss on book 3 of the Saxon Mirror, article 78 (the vassal may pursue his lord). That paragraph must be taken cautiously, and not in the crude sense its words suggest. The vassal touches on it with great forethought, so that ... advises an attack. For it was said above, book 2, article 12, that a vassal may not murmur against his lord's sentence ... it is more tolerable than that he should be obliged to detain the lord. If, then, it is not lawful to do the lesser thing, neither ... hands, as the saying goes, by which it is permitted to one or not, and in the Digest, "de regulis iuris" [it is said] it ought not [be done]; this is also held in book 1 ... Hence ... where an oath is sworn to aid the lord against everyone, which would not be the case if he detained him, as this text [says] ... 12, q. last, "de forma": that a vassal ought to defend his lord from all harm, which here would not be the case. ... corrects and derogates from other laws to the contrary. I answer, however, that the new law corrects ... is more appropriate under Saxon law, so it does not derogate from that one. Some also say that feudal law ... a constitution enacted, which is contrary to the earlier one, derogates from it, given that no mention is made of it there, as in the consilium ... [illegible, ~10 letters] was made. For we ought, as far as we can, to avoid the abrogation of law, especially in proofs. C. "de appellationibus," l. "praecipimus," in the final part, and in the authentic text "quibus modis naturales effici sui" §. "tribus," collation 7.

units.la: Glossa Iuris Feudalis, in proœmio: Und darumb hat adscribo verba Germanica, quod glossa hęc Latine non exstet, so hat der Hochgelobt und Hochgeboren (deß Gott ewiglich gedenck) diese gegen-wertigen Buchs Außgeber Keyser Friderich von Stauffen das da lehenrecht genant ist, wol erkannt, dann warum dieses Recht so maniger Hand was, dyes kein Mann zu ende erkunden kunde, darumb daß ein jegliches Herr vnd Fürst, Geistlich vnd Weltlich, seinen Mannen vnd sonderliche Satzung machen, vt C. de negot. gest. l. 1. Und darumb ward er zu Rath, daß er durch deß gemeinen Nutzes wolt, daß zu der Ritterschafft gehört, diß gegenwertig Buch, zu einer ewigen Gedächtniß der Ritterschafft gelassen hat, daß sie wissen, was Recht sie antreffen sey, vt C. qui mil. possl. l. i.
units.tr: Gloss on feudal law, in the preface: Und darumb hat ich die deutschen Worte eingesetzt, weil diese Glosse nicht lateinisch vorliegt. So hat der hochgelobte und hochgeborene Kaiser Friedrich von Staufen, dessen Gedächtnis Gott ewiglich bewahren möge, der Herausgeber dieses gegenwärtigen Buches, der das Lehenrecht genannt wird, dies wohl erkannt. Denn weil dieses Recht bei manchen Leuten in Gebrauch war, konnte es kein Mann vollständig erforschen, weil jeder Herr und Fürst, geistlich wie weltlich, seinen Mannen besondere Satzungen gab, wie im C. "de negotiis gestis," l. 1. Deshalb wurde er beraten, dass er zum gemeinen Nutzen wollte, dass dieses Buch, das zur Ritterschaft gehört, zu ewigem Gedächtnis der Ritterschaft überlassen werde, damit sie wissen, welches Recht sie betrifft, wie im C. "qui milites possint," l. 1.

units.la: SPANGENBERGIVS in Chronic. Saxoniae, cap. 247. Anno 1213. Imperator Fridericus Secundus in Comitiis Merseburgi celebratis dedit Saxonibus Ius Feudale. & Speculam etiam Saxonum adiectis constitutionibus adauxit.
units.tr: SPANGENBERG in the Saxon Chronicle, chapter 247. In the year 1213, Emperor Frederick II, at the Diet held at Merseburg, gave the Saxons feudal law, and he also enlarged the Saxon Mirror by adding constitutions.

units.la: Etica quidem isti hactenus commemorati, videntur Ius Feudale Saxonum ad Imperatorem Fridericum Secundum auctorem retulisse. Qua auctoritate, aut quo iudicio, non disputo. Reperio namque & alios Fridericos de feudis constitutiones edidisse.
units.tr: Indeed, the authorities so far mentioned seem to have referred the Saxon feudal law to Emperor Frederick II as its author. I do not dispute on what authority, or by what judgment, they do so. For I find that other Fredericks also issued constitutions on fiefs.

units.la: RADEVICVS Canonicus Frisingensis, de Friderico Primo Imperatore, cognomento Barba-rossa, scribit, eum de iure feudorum, quia apud Latinos scripto nondum sufficienter expressum fuerat, & pene omnes eam ignorantium iustitiam converterant, leges promulgasse. Sed earum legum certa tantum capitula fuerunt, in nullios tributa, quae idem Radevicus, & postea Guntherus in Lingurino, ordine suo recensent: sive postea ab Hugolino vetere Feudorum interprete (ut testatur Odofredus) fuerunt Usibus feudorum partim inserta, partim adiuncta. Nihil ergo hic locus ad Consuetudines feudorum vulgatas, multo minus ad Ius iustum Feudale Saxonum attinere potest.
units.tr: RADEVICUS, canon of Freising, writes of Frederick I, Emperor, surnamed Barbarossa, that he promulgated laws concerning the law of fiefs, because it had not yet been sufficiently set forth in writing among the Latins, and almost all had corrupted that justice through ignorance. But these laws consisted only of certain chapters, not assigned to any books, which the same Radevicus, and afterwards Guntherus in the Ligurinus, list in their own order; or afterwards they were partly inserted into and partly added to the Usus feudorum by Hugolinus, the old interpreter of the Feuds (as Odofredus attests). Nothing, therefore, in this place can pertain to the commonly published customs of fiefs, much less to the true feudal law of the Saxons.

units.la: CVSPINIANVS quoque in Friderico III. Imperatore affirmat, enim Iuriperitus mediocriter dile-ctus iuris aequitatem diceret ab iuvenum, iustitiam q. sedari; ob idque novum de Usibus feudorum librum fieri iussisse.
units.tr: CUSPINIAN also states, in his account of Emperor Frederick III, that a moderately learned jurist, when he spoke of the equity of law, said that justice had been lulled by the young; and for that reason he ordered a new book on the Usus feudorum to be made.

units.la: Et Iacobus SPIEGELIVS in Catalogo Imperatorum scribit in hunc modum: Friderikus III. Austriacus, ut Haloander indicat, Feudorum Consuetudines, quas veteres appellare solebant Iura militarium, & Imperator nominat specialem ac adpreces Bononiensis Collegii confirmavit. Nos dubio proculiam habueramus eas ordinis suo restitutas, mi-rum quo Principi per tam celebre Collegium fuerunt exhibitae, si per inusitatam fari licuisset, ne quid gravius dicam, de ulti-ma morte Haloandri nostri. Qui tamen non est ille, quem nuper Nicol. Rigaltius publicavit, Bartholomaeus Bunterius C. Placentini, qui non est ad auctoritatem Friderici III. Imperatoris relatus, sed per- meo errore ad Philippi Mariae Ducis Mediolanensis, vasalli ligii in Imperio. Fuit autem (quemodum hi persuadeo) libri illius, ad Academiae Bononiensis preces ab Imperatore confirmati, auctor Antonius de Prato veteri, Doctor Bononiensis, cuius ipse Rigaltius in praefatione facit mentionem.
units.tr: And Jacob SPIEGEL, in his Catalogue of the Emperors, writes to this effect: Frederick III of Austria, as Haloander points out, confirmed the customs of fiefs, which the ancients were accustomed to call the laws of the soldiers, and which the Emperor names specially, and at the request of the college of Bologna. We, without doubt, had thought them restored to their order, and it is a wonder that they were presented to the Prince through so famous a college, if it were permitted to speak of unusual things, not to say anything more serious, about the recent death of our Haloander. He, however, is not that man whom Nicolaus Rigaltius recently published, Bartholomaeus Bunterius of Piacenza, who is not referred to the authority of Emperor Frederick III, but through my error [is referred] to Philip Mary, Duke of Milan, a liege vassal in the Empire. The author of that book (as I am persuaded), confirmed by the Emperor at the request of the Academy of Bologna, was Antonius de Prato Vetus, Doctor of Bologna, whom Rigaltius himself mentions in his preface.

units.la: Marquardus Ficherus Consiliarius Archipalatinus, amicus noster, in Commentario ad constitutionem Caroli III. Imperatoris de expeditione Romana, subinde laudat & adducit codicem Iuris Feudalis, sub nomine Vetustissimi Auctoris de Beneficiis. Qui Codex, hic ipsissimus est, quem nunc tibi exhibemus, liber Iuris Feudalis Saxonum. Omnia enim illa fragmenta, quae ex suo MSS. Codice Ficherus refert, in hoc nostro libro verbatim exstant, ut appareat cuius ea cum nostro libro conferre volenti.
units.tr: Marquard Fichard, Archpalatine Councillor, our friend, in his commentary on the constitution of Emperor Charles III concerning the Roman expedition, repeatedly cites and adduces a codex of feudal law under the name of the Most Ancient Author concerning Benefices. This codex is precisely the one we now present to you, the book of the feudal law of the Saxons. For all those fragments which Fichard reports from his manuscript codex are found word for word in this our book, so that it may be evident to anyone who wishes to compare them with our book.

units.la: Hactenus singulorum Tractatuum sua sibi testimonia & elogia, quoad eorum potui commemorasse, elucidavimus. Nunc generatim apponam, quae de omnibus tribus Iuris Saxonici voluminibus in Corpore Iuris Polonici leguntur, auctoritates Regias, quibus in usum Regni & Provinciarum Poloniae Ius Saxonicum confirmatur & stabilitur.
units.tr: So far I have, as far as I could, set out and clarified the individual treatises' own testimonies and commendations. Now I will set down in general what is read in the Body of Polish Law concerning all three volumes of Saxon Law, the royal authorities by which Saxon Law is confirmed and established for the use of the Kingdom and the Provinces of Poland.

units.la: Ea autem habent in hunc modum.
units.tr: They have it in this manner.

units.la: PRIVILEGIVM IVRIS THEVTONICI PROVINCIALIS SVPREMI CASTRI CRACOVIENSIS, PER KAZIMIRVM MAGNVM CONSTITVTVM, QVOD VLADISLAVS IAGELLO, ET Vladislaus Iagellonis Reges confirmarunt, cuius tribunal est in castro Cracouiensi, ad quod in causis tam magnis, quam parvis iuris ciuilis prouocatur & appellatur.
units.tr: The Privilege of the Provincial Teutonic Law of the Supreme Castle of Kraków, established by Kazimierz the Great, which Władysław Jagiełło and King Władysław confirmed, whose tribunal is in the castle of Kraków, to which appeal is made and recourse had in civil causes both great and small.

units.la: NNomine Domini, Amen. Nos Vladislaus Dei gratia Rex Poloniae, Hungariae, Dalmatiae, Croaciae, Rasciae, Seruiae, necnon terrarum Cracouiae, Sandomiriae, Siradiae, Lanciciae, Cuiianiae Lithuaniaeque Princeps supremus, Pomeraniaeque Russiaeque Dominus & haeres, &c. Ad perpetuam rei memoriam significamus tenore praesentium, quibus expedit, universis praesentibus & futuris, praesentium notitiam habituris. Quomodo pro parte famosorum Aduocati & iuratorum iuris nostri supremi Theutonici provincialis castri Cracouiensis, oblata petitio continebat in effectu, quatenus de innata nostrae benignitatis clementia diuae memoriae serenissimi Principis Domini Vladislai Regis Poloniae, nostri immediati praedecessoris & genitoris charissimi, literam pergamenam confirmationis priuilegii Illustris Principis & Domini Kazimiri Regis Poloniae &c. de & super institutione iuris supremi Theutonicalis provincialis in castro nostro Cracouiensi, vice & loco iuris Magdeburgensis editi & concessi factam & donatam, sigillo sancti genitoris nostri mediocri in cerea forma impendente sigillatam, sanam, saluam & integram, non viciatam, non cancellatam, nec in aliqua sui parte suspectam, sed omni prorsus vitio & suspicione carentem, & pro parte praefatorum Aduocati & iuratorum coram nobis praesentatam confirmare, approbare, ratificare, & innouare dignaremur, cuius quidem literae una cum contentis in eadem tenor de verbo ad verbum sequitur & est talis.
units.tr: In the name of the Lord, Amen. We, Władysław, by the grace of God King of Poland, Hungary, Dalmatia, Croatia, Rascia and Serbia, and also Prince supreme of the lands of Kraków, Sandomierz, Sieradz, Łęczyca, Kujavia and Lithuania, and lord and heir of Pomerania and Russia, etc., make known by the tenor of these present letters, to whom it may concern, to all present and future persons who shall have knowledge of these present letters, for the perpetual memory of the matter, that the humble petition presented on behalf of the famous advocates and sworn men of our Supreme Provincial Teutonic Law of the castle of Kraków contained in substance this: that, by the innate clemency of our kindness, we would deign to confirm, approve, ratify and renew the parchment letter of confirmation of the privilege of the illustrious Prince and Lord Kazimierz, King of Poland, etc., concerning and upon the establishment of the Supreme Teutonic Provincial Law in our castle of Kraków, issued and granted in place and stead of Magdeburg Law, made and given, sealed with the middling seal of our holy father, King Władysław of blessed memory, our immediate predecessor and most dear father, hanging in wax form, sound, safe and whole, not spoiled, not cancelled, nor suspect in any part, but free of every defect and suspicion, and presented before us on behalf of the aforesaid advocates and sworn men. The tenor of that letter, together with its contents, follows word for word, and is as follows.

units.la: In nomine Domini, Amen. Ad perpetuam rei memoriam. Non consenuit, ut imperatorum casibus profectus rerum subiicere, & pia vota cum cadente fortuna deputare, quorum memoria debet esse assertio & constitutio perpetuo subsistere roboreque firmitatis. Proinde nos Vladislaus Dei gratia Rex Poloniae, necnon terrarum Cracouiae, Sandomiriae, Siradiae, Cuiianiae, Lanciciae, Lithuaniaeque Princeps supremus, Pomeraniae, Dominus & haeres, &c. significamus tenore praesentium, quibus expedit universis praesentibus & futuris praesentium notitiam habituris. Quomodo licet dudum diuae memoriae Dominus Kazimirus Rex Poloniae, praedecessor noster, Regali prouisione & communi utilitate suadente, in Regno Poloniae ius Theutonicum supremum instituisset, & ordinasset, ut omnibus oppressis & grauamen coram iudicibus secularibus iudicij eiusdem Theutonicalis patientibus totum ad illud appellandi & euocandi patuisset refugium, ne subditi Regni nostri ob defectum iuris supremi ad terras alienas per loca incognita non sine gravibus periculis, damnis & expensis pro iustitia recurrere arcerentur, quemadmodum ante huiusmodi constitutionis decretum: & haec talis modi constitutio tempore felicis nostri regiminis sub ratihabitione nostra & hactenus tenta fuisset custodita & seruata in & sub forma per certa capitalia tradita & literis authenticis sub appendentibus sigillis maiestatis eiusdem Regis Kazimiri confirmata.
units.tr: In the name of the Lord, Amen. For the perpetual memory of the matter. It has not been customary to subject the advance of affairs to the chances of emperors, or to assign pious wishes to a falling fortune, whose memory ought to be preserved by assertion and constitution, and to endure forever with the strength of firmness. Therefore we, Władysław, by the grace of God King of Poland, and also Prince supreme of the lands of Kraków, Sandomierz, Sieradz, Kujavia, Łęczyca and Lithuania, lord of Pomerania and heir, etc., make known by the tenor of these present letters, to whom it may concern, to all present and future persons who shall have knowledge of these present letters, that although our predecessor, Lord Kazimierz, King of Poland, of blessed memory, long ago, moved by royal foresight and the common good, established and ordained in the Kingdom of Poland a Supreme Teutonic Law, so that to all the oppressed who suffered under the judgment of the secular judges of that Teutonic court there might lie open a whole refuge for appeal and summons to it, lest the subjects of our kingdom, for lack of a supreme law, be hindered from seeking justice in foreign lands, through unknown places, not without grave dangers, losses and expenses, just as before the decree of this kind of constitution; and this sort of constitution, in the time of our happy reign, with our ratification, had until now been kept and observed in and under the form handed down in certain chapters, and confirmed by authentic letters under the hanging seals of the majesty of that same King Kazimierz.

units.la: Tandem huiusmodi literae apud iudices & conseruatores praefati iuris nescitur, quae forte & utique infausta perierunt. dignum itaque arbitrantes hanc concessionem & constitutionem extare, ut antea, viribus debere subsistere, praefatas literas & priuilegia, quorum tenor de copiis sumptis originalibus in certis codicibus dictorum iudicum remansit integer conseruatus, renouamus ac robur ipsis in vigore perpetuo adiicimus. Volentes, ut in omnibus suis capitulis, punctis, conditionibus & articulis iugem semper & irrefragabilem obtineant firmitatem, prouidentes specialiter, ut quotiescunque ciuitates in hac priuilegij copia descripta & contenta, veleorum alias in huiusmodi supremi iuris iudicio causam vel causas proprias vel suorum coincolarum & concilium coram iudicio praefati iuris per appellationem introductas habuerint, illis amotis & exclusis alia ciuitates pro eis ad iudicium cum aliis remanentibus surrogentur. Tenor autem praedictarum literarum, & forma siue copia sumpta ex originali, ut praefertur, sequitur & est talis.
units.tr: Finally, such letters are not known to be held by the judges and conservators of the aforesaid law; perhaps they have perished, and indeed unhappily. Therefore, judging it worthy that this grant and constitution should stand, and should, as before, have force, we renew the aforesaid letters and privileges, the tenor of which has remained whole and preserved from copies taken from the originals in certain codices of the said judges, and we add strength to them for perpetual validity. Wishing that in all their chapters, points, conditions and articles they may always obtain a lasting and irrefragable firmness, we provide especially that, whenever cities described and contained in this copy of the privilege, or others, shall have in the judgment of this supreme law, by appeal, introduced before the tribunal of the said law their own causes or the causes of their co-residents, or a council, then those cities being removed and excluded, other cities shall be substituted in their place for the judgment with the remaining ones. The tenor of the aforesaid letters, and the form or copy taken from the original, as has been said, follows and is as follows.

units.la: In nomine Domini, Amen. Quia humana conditio dominantis sibi iugo libenter carere, ut homines libertatem minime abdicassent: si non impunita vitia grauis perniciae scelerum reduxissent. Ideo diuina sententia dati sunt Reges populo, & domini subiecti, ut necessario infirma & iudicio ac imperio Regum subessent universi. Ut cuilibet aequo libramine statera lance appendantur Regis iustitiam ministrarent. Et proinde nos Kazimirus Dei gratia Rex Poloniæ, necnon terrarum Cracoviæ, Sandomiriæ, Lanciciæ, Siradiæ, Cuiaviæ, Pomeraniæque Dominus & heres Russiæ, &c. ad extollenda iustorum praeconia, & transgressorum insolentias reprimendas, animadvertentes nostri Regno contra decorem & honorem illibata eiusdem Regni nostri praeter scientiam nostram Regiæ Maiestatis verfasse corruptelas. quod cum Advocati, Scultetii, Scabini iurati iudiciorum bannitorum iuris Theutonici, aut litigantibus in iudiciis eorum bannitis contendentibus sententias interlocutorias & diffinitivas in causis quam pluribus promulgant. Dicti contendentes ad partes remotas Rinenses th Maydemburg civitatem, cui nullo iure subsunt, & ultra fines Regni nostri; appellationes & provocationes interponuntur, nostra Maiestatis proprio solio & tribunali, nec non proprij Principis & domini iure & iurisditionem omissis & contemptis, & in detrimentum Regni nostri damnum, & regnicolarum nostrorum gravamen. Advocati vero, scultetii & alij scabini iurati praedicti nostri Regni a contendentib. eisdem pro emendis sententiis & scultetis in Magdeburg per nouem ferrones latorum grossorum Pragensium, & nonnullas summas pecuniarum pro expensis exigunt, & extra Regnum nostrum in Maydemburg, pro praedictis sententiis emendis transmittunt, per quae honori, decori, iurisditioni, solio, tribunali illibatis nostris praedictis detrahatur, & turpitudinis reructur, & quod deterius est dicti Advocati, scultetii, scabini iurati iurisditionem Theutonicalium cum more litigantes iustitia reddere deberent complementum, difficiles se in hoc reddentes ad eiusdem nonnullarum dicti Regni nostri Consules, Advocatos, scabinos iuratos. Quibus nulla a nobis super iure supremo & dandis sententiis iuris Maydemburgensi a nostra Regali Maiestate, nulla proprius fuit velet eis specialis ad talia loca ipsorum extra eorum loca constituta, ultra terminos iurisditionis eorum attributa potestas ad vendendum ius supremo nostro solio & tribunali de iure duntaxat annexum, & sententias aliquas dandum extra fines eorum iurisditionis ad alias civitates, villas & loca, nulla eis a nostra Regia Maiestate auctoritas est concessa, sed ex quadam temeritate contendentes coram eis in causis tam magnis; quam parvis pecunias ponere compulerunt non paucas, pro quibus sententiis a dictis civitatum Regni nostri Consulibus, Advocatis, scabinis iuratis nulla prorsus ad hoc auctoritate fruentibus sententias extraxerunt & ius emerunt, quod viribus earum & non subsisteat, insontesque contendentes deludebant sumptibus, laboribus, impensis & expensis fatigando minus iuste. Contra quae in regno nostro clamor ascendit, & insinuatio manifestauit, quod maiestas nostra fama deferente & clamore incitante sine periculo pertransfire & sine scandalo tolerare per nostram serenitatem oculis conniventibus pertransfirenon potuerint. Cum reverendis in Christo patribus Ioraslao Archiepiscopo Gnesnensi, Bodzanta, Cracoviensi, Sbiluthu, Vladislaviensi, Iohanne Poznaniensi, Nicolao Ploczensi, Iohanne Lubucensi, Episcopis, necnon Abbatibus, Præpositis, Decanis, Archidiaconis, caterisque Prælatis & Canonicis tam Cathedralium, quam Collegiatarum & aliarum Ecclesiarum Capitulis & Beneficiatis, tam secularibus, quam regularibus, exemptis & non exemptis; necnon magnificis Castellanis, Palatinis, Camerariis, Succamerariis, Iudicibus, Subiudicibus, Baronibus, Militibus & Nobilibus, Consulibus, Advocatis, scabinis iuratis civitatum, Scultetis & Officialibus villarum & locorum singulorum universis synodum, conuentionem & concilium celebrauimus, de quorum omnium & singulorum consilio, appellationes, provocationes indictis iudiciis faciendas a litigantibus praedictis pro pecuniis praedictis emendas, exigendas, admittendas sententias, & ius in Maydemburg emendum, & ab civitatum aliquarum dicti Regni Iudicibus, Advocatis, scabinis iuratis ius aliquod absque nostra speciali auctoritate per quospiam Iudices, Advocatos, scabinos iuratos, litigantes emendum & recipiendum sententias aut ius aliquod, & receptis aliqualiter standum, aut ea pro iure habendum, sub poena amissionis omnium bonorum suorum auctoritate nostra Maiestatis Regia inhibemus. Volentes, praedictis nostris regnicolis damna, gravamina, fatigas & sumptus remouere, profectum quoque & utilitatem eis, nostro quoque Regio & Regia maiestatis honorem & decorem ampliare, libros iuris Maydemburgensi ordinauimus, & in thesauro nostro Cracoviensi depositum, in eodem, castro nostro Cracoviensi constituimus ius supremum Theutonicale provinciale, vice & loco iuris Maydemburgensis, de libris eisdem promulgari debere sententias & iura per Advocatum nostrum & septe scultetos, seu Advocatos & iuratos dicti iuris provincialis peritos iuris praedicti. Quos nostra maiestatis Procurator generalis, qui pro tempore fuit, dicti castri terra nostra Cracovien. unum Advocato nostro, & locis infra scriptis, inter advocatos & scultetos, seu alios iuris peritos potiores, duxerit recipiendos, nominandos, eligendos, & ad loca tempore vitae eorum pro iudicio nostro supremo provinciali castri Cracovien. banniendo more consueto, temporibus competentibus & locis, videlicet de Bochnia & Vjelyczka, de Robczyce & Lipnicza, de Miły linyczę, de Ilkusch, de Volbram civitatibus, Advocatis de Lypnik, de Sulazowa, de Irmanowicze, de Przeczyny, de Sandumman, de Balyn, de Czubrowicze Scultetis maiestatis nostrae regia de Bodzanow, de Igolomia, de Lapsicze,
units.tr: In the name of the Lord, Amen. Because the human condition would gladly be free of the yoke of a master, men would never have renounced liberty, unless unpunished vices of grievous ruin had led back the crimes. Therefore by divine judgment kings were given to the people, and lords set over subjects, so that all the weak would necessarily be subject to the judgment and rule of kings, that they might administer justice to each one, the balance weighed with equal scale. And therefore we, Kazimierz, by the grace of God King of Poland, and also lord of the lands of Kraków, Sandomierz, Łęczyca, Sieradz, Kujavia and Pomerania and heir of Russia, etc., considering in order to extol the praises of the just and to repress the insolence of transgressors, that corruptions have arisen in our kingdom, contrary to the decorum and unimpaired honour of our kingdom, without the knowledge of our Royal Majesty, because the advocates, sheriffs and sworn aldermen of the courts of the Teutonic law, banned, or the litigants contending in their banned courts, pronounce interlocutory and definitive sentences in very many causes. The said contending parties interpose appeals and provocations to the distant parts of the Rhineland and to the city of Magdeburg, to which they are subject by no right, and beyond the borders of our kingdom, the proper seat and tribunal of our Majesty and the right and jurisdiction of our own Prince and lord being omitted and contemned, to the detriment of our kingdom and the grievance of our subjects. Moreover, the advocates, sheriffs and other sworn aldermen of our aforesaid kingdom, from the same contending parties, demand for buying sentences and sheriffs in Magdeburg nine ferrons of Prague groschen and some sums of money for expenses, and send them out of our kingdom to Magdeburg to buy the aforesaid sentences, whereby the honour, decorum, jurisdiction, seat and tribunal of our aforesaid unimpaired majesty are detracted from and brought to shame; and what is worse, the said advocates, sheriffs and sworn aldermen, who ought to render full justice to litigants according to the custom of Teutonic law, make themselves difficult in this matter, along with certain consuls, advocates and sworn aldermen of the said cities of our kingdom. To them no power was given by us, nor by our Royal Majesty, concerning the supreme law and the giving of sentences under the law of Magdeburg; no special power was granted to them to go to such places outside their own seats, beyond the limits of their assigned jurisdiction, to sell to another the right annexed to our supreme seat and tribunal, and to give any sentences outside the bounds of their jurisdiction to other cities, villages and places; no authority was granted to them by our Royal Majesty. But through a certain rashness, they have compelled the contending parties before them, in causes both great and small, to lay down not a few sums of money, for which sentences from the said consuls, advocates and sworn aldermen of the cities of our kingdom, who enjoy no authority whatever for this, they have extracted sentences and bought the law, which ought not to subsist by their force, and they deluded innocent contending parties, wearing them out unjustly with costs, labours, outlays and expenses. Against these things a cry has risen in our kingdom, and information has made it plain that our majesty, with fame bearing it and clamour inciting, could not pass by without danger, nor tolerate without scandal, with our serenity turning a blind eye. With the reverend fathers in Christ, Jaroslaw, Archbishop of Gniezno, Bodzanta of Kraków, Sbiluth of Włocławek, John of Poznań, Nicholas of Płock, John of Łubusz, bishops, and also abbots, provosts, deans, archdeacons, and other prelates and canons, both of the cathedral and collegiate churches and of other chapters and beneficed clergy, both secular and regular, exempt and non-exempt; and also with the magnificent castellans, palatines, chamberlains, sub-chamberlains, judges, sub-judges, barons, knights and nobles, consuls, advocates, sworn aldermen of the cities, sheriffs and officials of the single villages and places, we have celebrated a synod, convention and council, and by the counsel of all and each of them, we, by our royal authority, forbid that appeals and provocations, to be made from the said litigants in the courts declared, be bought, exacted or admitted for the said sums of money, and that any judges, advocates or sworn aldermen of certain cities of the said kingdom, without our special authority, shall sell or receive any law for the litigants to buy and receive sentences or any law, and that, when they have been received in any way, they shall be stood by, or held as law, under penalty of the loss of all their goods. Wishing to remove from our said kingdom's subjects damages, grievances, toils and expenses, and to enlarge for them profit and utility, and also the honour and decorum of our Royal Majesty, we have ordained the books of the law of Magdeburg, deposited in our treasury at Kraków, and in the same castle of Kraków we have established the Supreme Provincial Teutonic Law, in place and stead of the law of Magdeburg, so that sentences and laws should be promulgated from those books by our advocate and seven sheriffs, or advocates and sworn men of the said provincial law, skilled in the aforesaid law. These, whom our Procurator General of Majesty, who was for the time being, shall have thought fit to be received, named and chosen, one for our advocate of the castle and land of Kraków, and for the places written below, among the advocates and sheriffs or other more eminent experts in law, and to be banned by the customary manner to the places and at the appropriate times for the lifetime of each for our supreme provincial court of the castle of Kraków, namely from the cities of Bochnia and Wieliczka, Radoszyce and Lipnica, Myślenice, Ilkusz, Wolbrom, advocates from Lipnik, Sułkowa, Irmanowice, Przeczyny, Sandomierz, Balin, Czubrowice, royal sheriffs of Bodzanów, Igołomia, Łapsze,

units.la: Lapsziczc, de Scavvyjna, de Rybna, de Lyski, Tiniczenst, de Brzesko, de Goney, Brosse, de Lubotza, de Pubyedny, de Tubyicze, Suvertmensi Praepositi monasteriorum ... sculteti necnon aliis locis, Scabinis & aliis honestis & circumspectis personis de ... denburgensi peritis, & quisque Scabinali fuerint digni, quod sint septem in numero semper praesentes perpetui, & quod septenarius numerus non excedatur. Ad quod quidem tandem nostrum supremum provinciale Theutonicale castri nostri Cracoviensis Aduocatum vestrum, necnon Aduocatos, sculteros & alios septem praesidentes eidem nostro iudicio, loco praedictarum prematiorum & appellationum in Maydemburg prorumpi confuerunt, locum erit eis ... bus Iudicibus, Aduocatis, Sculteis, Scabinis, invitatis tam ciuitatum quam villarum, qui ... contendentibus & litigantibus appellare & provocare, & coram eisdem prosequi, finire & ... re suam appellationem seu super eisdem & alius per simplices propositiones sive appellationes ... sententias postulare, de libris nostris praedictis iuris Maydemburgensi. Quibus sententiis ... per eosdem promulgatis, auctoritate nostra Regia Maiestatis decernimus, vel ut ... vel tanquam legem observandum. Nisi aliqui contendentium praedictorum duxerint ... quaestionibus & causis suis melius & sententias meliores in oppositum ipsorum prono... ru & sententiarum proponendum, eisdem ab ipsis ad tribunal & solum nostrae Maiestatis ... appellare, & infra tempus dicti iuris Maydemburgensis librorum nostrorum, a nobis ... rum pronunciatione obtinere certos Commissarios, quos volumus & determinamus fore Consu... tatum, unde ipsi appellantes nominauerint alteri parti non (in)spectos, de qualibet ciuitate per consules, vel dicet de Cracovia & Sandecz, de Bochnia & Vyelnicza, de Kasimiro & ... qui ex nostra speciali commissione decident appellationem & finem negotii appellationis ... ponent. Et ne praefati Aduocatus nostri, & alii Aduocati, Sculteti, Scabini, ... tui praesidentes circa iudicium nostrum & iura praedicta danda & laborandum ... exponant, & litigantes praedictis laboribus, fatigu & expensis more priori ... mus observandum in antea pro qualibet sententia danda duntaxat per sex Scabinos ... fisco nostro mediatatem, aliam praedictis praesidentibus septem Scabinis, inter ipsos ... rum diuidendos, praeter Notarii salarium, memorialia, & priuilegiorum literas coram ... de quibus iuxta eorum moderationem disponere debebunt, rationem onerum leuandum. De ... tem dicti iudicii nostri, pro nobis Aduocatus nostri quatuor poenas, & quintam pro Scabinis ... dictis exigere debebit. Et ut praefati Aduocatus nostri & septem Scabini dicti iudicii no... mi eo fortius & cum exacta diligentia iudicio supremo praedicto & sententiis promulgandis ... gentium consistant & continuent. Ipsos Aduocatum & Scabinos Maiestatis nostrae ... praerogativa fauoris & gratia speciali, ipsos eximimus & liberamus ab omnibus exactionibus ... tributis, contributionibus & aliis collectis, laboribus, seruitiis, expeditionibus, ad quaecunque, per nos & per nostros successores fiendis & obedientiis quibuscunque, tam nostrarum quam ... rum dominorum, nec non a iudicis & iurisdictionibus ipsorum dominorum, castellanorum, pal... tinorum, Iudicum, subiudicum, Camerariorum, caeterorumque Officialium terrestrium, ... Aduocatorum, Consulum, Scabinorum & quarumcunque potestatum, quibus nulla ratione... diant, neque citati in magnis vel parvis causis coram ipsis comparere & respondere tenea... Sed duntaxat cum ad praesentiam nostram, & per speciale sigillum nostrum citati fuerint, ... ram nobis aut coram speciali commissario nostro ad hoc deputando respondere tenebuntur, ... Maydenburgensi. & quilibet eorum respondebit. Vt autem praemissa omnia robur obtineant, per... petua firmitatis, praesens priuilegium de consilio & consensu praedictorum omnium ... strorum scribi & sigilli nostri Maiestatis Regalis maioris appensione fecimus communiri, & datum Cracouiae, Anno Domini 1356. in crastino S. Francisci, praesentibus praefatis ... scopo, & Episcopis, nec non magnificis viris, Dominis Iura Castellano, Imramo palatino ... Iudice Cracouiensi, Vyelczkone Sandomiriensi, Raphaele Vislicensi, Petro Sandecensi ... & aliis quam pluribus testibus fide dignis.
units.tr: Lapsziczc, of Scavvyjna, of Rybna, of Lyski, Tiniczenst, of Brzesko, of Goney, Brosse, of Lubotza, of Pubyedny, of Tubyicze, Suvertmensi, provosts of the monasteries ... sculteti, and also other places, scabins and other honourable and circumspect persons of ... Denburg, skilled in the law, and whoever are worthy to be scabins, so that there shall be seven in number, always present and permanent, and that the number seven shall not be exceeded. To this end, our supreme provincial Teutonic court of our castle of Kraków, its advocate, and the advocates, sculteti and the other seven presiding over the same our court, in place of the aforesaid premiums and appeals, have been accustomed to resort to Magdeburg; there shall be room for them ... the judges, advocates, sculteti, scabins, and those invited from both the towns and the villages, who ... contending and litigating parties to appeal and challenge, and to prosecute and conclude before the same, and ... to seek his appeal, or concerning the same, by simple propositions or appeals ... sentences, from our aforesaid books of the law of Magdeburg. By our royal authority we decree that these sentences, as promulgated by the same ..., shall be observed as law. Unless any of the aforesaid contending parties have thought that their questions and causes can be better settled, and better sentences proposed against their opponents and against the sentences, they may appeal to them from the tribunal of our Majesty alone ..., and within the time of the said law of Magdeburg from our books, after the pronouncement ..., obtain certain commissioners, whom we wish and determine to be the consuls ..., whom the appellants shall have named, not suspected by the other party, from each town through the consuls, or the said [men] of Kraków and Sandecz, of Bochnia and Wieliczka, of Kazimierz and ... who by our special commission shall decide the appeal and bring to an end the matter of the appeal. And lest the aforesaid advocates of ours, and the other advocates, sculteti, scabins, ... presiding over our court and the aforesaid laws, in giving and labouring over them, be exposed to the aforesaid labours, fatigue and expenses, as before ... we shall observe in future that for each sentence to be given, only six scabins ... half to our treasury, the other half to the aforesaid seven presiding scabins, to be divided among themselves, apart from the notary's salary, the memorials, and the letters of privilege ..., which they shall have to dispose of according to their moderation, so as to lighten the burden of expenses. Concerning ... of our said court, our advocate shall be bound to exact four penalties for us, and a fifth for the scabins ... And so that the aforesaid advocates of ours and the seven scabins of our said court may stand and continue with greater strength and with exact diligence in the aforesaid supreme court and in the sentences to be promulgated ... nations. By the prerogative of our Majesty's favour and special grace, we exempt and free the same advocate and scabins from all exactions, tributes, contributions and other levies, labours, services, expeditions, for whatever purposes are to be made by us and our successors, and from all obediences whatsoever, both of ours and of the lords ..., and likewise from the judges and jurisdictions of those lords, castellans, palatines, judges, subjudges, chamberlains, and the other terrestrial officials, advocates, consuls, scabins, and of whatever powers, by whom in no way ... they are to be summoned or to appear and answer before them in great or small causes. But only when they have been summoned into our presence and by our special seal, they shall be bound to answer to us or before our special commissioner appointed for this purpose ... of Magdeburg, and each of them shall answer. And so that all the foregoing may have force and perpetual firmness, we have had this present privilege written with the counsel and consent of all the aforesaid, and have caused it to be fortified with the greater appendage of our royal Majesty's seal; given at Kraków, in the year of the Lord 1356, on the day after the feast of St. Francis, the aforesaid being present ... bishops, and also the magnificent men, lords Jura, castellan, Imram, palatine ... judge of Kraków, Wyelczko of Sandomierz, Raphael of Wiślica, Peter of Sandecz ... and many other trustworthy witnesses.

units.la: Petitionibus itaque praefatorum iudicum & conseruatorum praefati iuris Theutonici supe... mi benigniter annuati, & subditorum nostrorum commodis & profectibus commanentes ... deliberas, constitutionem, gratiam & concessionem grata & rata habentes, atque ... tenore mediante. Actum feria quinta post conductum paschae, Anno Domini 1421 ... reuerendissimis in Christo patribus, Dominis Nicolao dicta Gneznensi Ecclesiae Archiepiscopo ... Praeposito, Alberto Cracouiensi, Andrea Posnaniensi, Iacobo Plocensi, Ioanne Chelmensi Ecclesiae ... Episcopis, nec non magnificis validisque viris Christino de Ostrouo Castellano Cracoviensi ... nogio de Ostroroh Posnaniensi, Ioanne de Tarnouv Cracouiensi, Nicolao de Ochu ...
units.tr: Therefore, with the petitions of the aforesaid judges and conservators of the aforesaid Teutonic law being graciously granted by us, and having regard to the advantages and profit of our subjects ... we deliberate, and hold the constitution, grace and concession pleasing and ratified, and ... by this tenor. Done on the Thursday after the Octave of Easter, in the year of the Lord 1421 ... the most reverend fathers in Christ, lords Nicholas called of Gniezno, archbishop of the church, ... provost, Albert of Kraków, Andrew of Poznań, Jacob of Płock, John of Chełm, bishops of the church, and also the magnificent and vigorous men, Christin of Ostrów, castellan of Kraków, ... Nogi of Ostroróg, Poznań, John of Tarnów, Kraków, Nicholas of Ochna ...

units.la: Sinienf. Matthia de Vanszoszno Calissiensf. Nicolao de Opporovv Lancicien s. Iacobo de Conyecz-le Siradiensf. Matthia de Labyszniyn Brestens. Iohanne de Coszyjelecz Gnevveonien s. Palati-nos: Michaele de Cissovv Sandomirien s. Mislino Poznanien s. Martino de Clenovv, Cristino deCoszyeglovvy Sandeceń s. Floriano de Corythnyicza Vislicien s. Ioanne de Scekoczyn Lublinen s. Castellanis: Sbigneo de Brzeźye Regni Poloniæ Marscalco, Petro Schafraniecz Succamerario Cracovien s. Andrea Czyolek de Zelecho, Dapifero Sandomirien s. & aliis quam pluribus fide dignis, nostris fidelibus dilectis. Datum per manus reuerendi in Christo Patris Domini Alberti Episcopi Cracovien s. supremi Cancellarij, & Ioannis Decani Cracovien s & Vice Cancellarij Regni Poloniæ, sincere nobis dilectorum.
units.tr: Sieniawa; Matthias of Wąsosz, Kalisz; Nicholas of Opporów, Łęczyca; Jacob of Coniecpol, Sieradz; Matthias of Łabiszyn, Brześć; John of Koziejówek, Gniezno; palatines: Michael of Ciszów, Sandomierz; Mislino, Poznań; Martin of Kleno; Christin of Ciężkowice(?), Sandecz; Florian of Korytnica, Wiślica; John of Skoczów, Lublin; castellans: Sbignew of Brzeźnica, Marshal of the Kingdom of Poland; Peter Szafraniec, Chamberlain of Kraków; Andrew Czyżek of Żelechów, Steward of Sandomierz; and many other trustworthy persons, our faithful and beloved subjects. Given by the hand of the reverend father in Christ, lord Albert, bishop of Kraków, supreme chancellor, and of John, dean of Kraków and vice-chancellor of the Kingdom of Poland, sincerely beloved by us.

units.la: Nos vero Vladislaus Dei gratia Rex prefatus de consilio consiliariorum nostrorum ad latus nostrum, tunc assistentium, petitionibus taliter coram nostra Maiestate oblatis tanquam iustis, rationabilibus, & rationi consonis acclinati, huiusmodi literam, ratificationem, innouationem Priuilegij præscripti cum contentis in eodem confirmamus, ratificamus, approbamus & innouamus, decernentes ipsam in omnibus suis punctis, clausulis, conditionibus & articulis robur obtinere perpetua firmitatis per præsentes. Harum, quibus est appensum sigillum nostrum, testimonio literarū.
