Actum in insula Czyepel oppido Coniın alias Racze, die Dominico post festum Sancti Stanislai tempore Maii proximo, Anno Domini millesimo quadringentesimo quadragesimoquarto, præsentibus ibidem venerabilibus, magnificis, strenuis & generosis Laurentio de Edervvar Regni Hungariæ, Nicolao de Naszoki Luca de Gorka Poznanien s Hinkone de Pomorzani terra Podo-lia Palatinis; Nicolao de Zakrzovv Marscalco, Creslao de Voischeck de VVoiźa Dapifero Curiæ nostræ, Petro de Schamotuli; Paulo de Siienno; Nicolao de Czessavv, & Hinkone de Baliczye, familiaribus nostris, & aliis fide dignis testibus circa præmissa. Datum per manus Magnificorum Ioannis de Coniecz pole Cancellarii & Petri de Scekoczyn, Vicecancellarii Regni Poloniæ, sincere nobis dilectorum.
units.tr: We, Vladislaus, by the grace of God, the aforesaid King, with the counsel of our councillors at our side, then in attendance, being inclined by the petitions thus presented before our Majesty as just, reasonable and consonant with reason, confirm, ratify, approve and renew this letter of ratification and renewal of the aforesaid privilege with its contents, and by these presents we decree that the same shall have the force of perpetual firmness in all its points, clauses, conditions and articles. In witness whereof this letter is sealed with our seal. Done at the island of Czepel, at the town of Konin, otherwise Racz, on the Sunday after the feast of St. Stanislaus, in the month of May next, in the year of the Lord one thousand four hundred and forty-four; present there the venerable, magnificent, valiant and noble Lawrence of Edervár, palatine of the Kingdom of Hungary; Nicholas of Nasozki; Luke of Górka, palatine of Poznań; Hinko of Pomorzany, palatine of the land of Podolia; Nicholas of Zakrzew, marshal; Kriesław of Wojszyce of Wojża, steward of our court; Peter of Szamotuły; Paul of Sieniawa; Nicholas of Czesawa; and Hinko of Baliczyce, our familiars, and other trustworthy witnesses to the aforesaid matters. Given by the hand of the magnificent John of Koniecpol, chancellor, and Peter of Skoczów, vice-chancellor of the Kingdom of Poland, sincerely beloved by us.

units.la: SVMMVS PONTIFEX GRE- GORIVS REPROBAT CERTOS ARTICV- LOS IVRIS SAXONICI ET MAGDEBURGENSIS, tanquam iuri diuino contrarios.
units.tr: THE SUPREME PONTIFF GREGORY REJECTS CERTAIN ARTICLES OF THE SAXON AND MAGDEBURG LAW, AS CONTRARY TO DIVINE LAW.

units.la: REGORIVS Episcopus seruus seruorum DEI venerabilibus fratribus Archiepiscopo Rigensi eiusdem suffraganeis salutem & Apostolicam benedictionem. Ad reuerentiam DEI, extirpationem errorum, & exaltationem Catholicae fidei, que iustitiae & animarum salutem. Quaedam execrabilia scripta, Legis Saxonum appellata, multa examinatione & maturitate in hac parte praeuia, authoritate Apostolica reprobamus, damnamus, & decernimus irrita & inania, & carere omni robore firmitatis, prout continetur in nostris confectis, quarum tenor est talis.
units.tr: Gregory, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brothers, the Archbishop of Riga and his suffragans, greeting and the Apostolic blessing. For the reverence of God, the rooting out of errors, and the exaltation of the Catholic faith, which is the salvation of justice and of souls: we, by Apostolic authority, after a careful examination and mature deliberation in this matter, reprobate and condemn certain execrable writings, called the Laws of the Saxons, and decree them null and void, lacking all force of validity, as is contained in our letters, whose tenor is as follows.

units.la: Gregorius Episcopus seruus seruorum DEI, ad perpetuam rei memoriam. Sathanas humani generis Dominus noster Iesus Christus, cuius licet indigne vices gerimus, cernens ipsum eum de manu, quod ad delicias paradisi creauerat, ex lapsu protoplasti diabolica fraude decipi, peccatum inobedientiae corruisse. Et quod futurorum praescius praeuidebat inter statutum triticum hostem inuidum seminaturum zizania, & inter sacra prophana; inter sincera et corrupta, & inter recta, iniqua hostilibus callidisque machinationibus & astutiis polituram, cuius oreis videlicet beati Petri principis Apostolorum, cui & successoribus suis, per eundem tradidit pascendam potestatem, aliorum Apostolorum & Discipulorum successores, scilicet Ecclesiarum omni supernatum eyellerent lolium, ne inficeret semen bonum. Ideoque ad nostrum principium aliorumque praelatorum Ecclesiae sanctae DEI spectat officium, vt animarum salutem neintendentes, & agrum huiusmodi, prout expedit, saepius expurgantes: Ea quae noueritis contraria salutis, studio pastoralis solicitudinis euellamus. Sane fide digna & admodum pluriesque inculcata relatio plurimorum ad nostrum perduxit auditum, quod in Saxonia, nullis aliis partibus, quaedam detestabilia scripta, Leges seu speculum Saxonum vulgo vocata, & inferius annotata, apud nonnullos Nobiles atque plebeios reperiuntur, quorum colae partium earundem, omissis Canonibus aliisque scripturis Sacris contemptis, quae non ad bonos ac ciuilibus & bonis moribus procul pulsis & longis retroactis temporibus obseruantur, seruant etiam de praesenti. Ex quorum quidem obseruantia Deus offendirur, proximus gravia iustitia & aequitas dissipatur, canones & leges contemnuntur. Etenim iudicium enormiter peruertitur, veritas impugnatur, contra bonos mores & legem naturae agitur, dehonestatur libertasque Ecclesiastica conculcatur, & quod est deterius, apostolica denegatur potestas, veritas catholicae fidei derogatur. Nos igitur de his tanto dolentes amarius, quanto exindeque animae longioribus temporibus, strictioribus laqueis fuerunt alligari. Et propterea parentes affectibus tot & tantis malis periculis obuiare. Ne nobis praedicta dissimulantibus ipsa peccantium de nostris manibus a domino requiratur, ipsa scripta seu leges, quae nouerunt, & per nonnullos ex fratribus nostris sanctae Romanae Ecclesiae Cardinales & aliquos magistros ac virtusque iuris Doctores diligenter examinari fecimus. Habita super ea dilatione matura, tanquam falsa, temeraria, iniqua & iniusta, & in quibusdam haereticam & ideo contra bonos mores existentia periculosaque animabus de ipsorum fratrum nostrorum conditione tantate Apostolica, tenore praesentium reprobamus, damnamus, & decernimus irrita & inania carere omni robore firmitatis, necnon processus & sententias, si quas forsan iplarum scriptarum legum praetextu fieri contigit, in posterum penitus non valere. Vnuctis Carolo Ludouico per Apostolica scripta mandamus, quatenus ipsis scriptis & legibus repulsari de cetero non urantur, sed Domini terrarum tam ecclesiastici quam seculares, suos vti subditos non permittant. Aliquin contrarium praesumentes, cuiuscunque praeeminentiae, dignitatis, status vel conditionis existant, etiam si Pontificali, vel Imperiali, aut Regali, vel alia qualibet praefulgeant dignitate, excommunicationis sententiam incurrere volumus ipso facto. Et vt reprobatio, damnatio & irritatio nostrum huiusmodi, tam salubrem effectum irrefragabiliter consequatur, vniuersos ... dominos temporales tam ecclesiasticos quam etiam seculares, per praesentes requirimus et rogamus, vt per eorum constitutiones & statuta perpetua ordinent & mandent sub grauioribus temporalibus poenis, quod nullus subditorum suorum deinceps vtatur his reprobatis scriptis, sed legibus emoratis, ipsaque in contrarium facientes taliter exequantur, quod eorum scriptorum legum detestanda iniquitas de terris eorum totaliter extirpetur. Nulli ergo hominum omnino liceat hanc paginam nostrae damnationis, prohibitionis, constitutionis, mandati, voluntatis & requisitionis infringere, vel eius temerario contraire. Si quis autem hoc attentare praesumpserit, indignationem omnipotentis Dei omnipotentis & beatorum Petri & Pauli Apostolorum eius se nouerit incursurum. Datum Auinione, 6. idus Aprilis, pontificatus nostri Anno tertio.
units.tr: Gregory, bishop, servant of the servants of God, for the perpetual memory of the matter. Satan, the adversary of the human race, whereas our Lord Jesus Christ, whose vices we unworthily bear, saw that man, whom he had created for the delights of paradise, had fallen into the sin of disobedience through the fall of the first-formed man, deceived by diabolical fraud. And as he foresaw in advance of future events, that the hostile enemy would sow tares among the wheat that had been sown, and would polish, by hostile and crafty devices and cunning, the profane among the holy, the corrupt among the sincere, and the wicked among the upright; so that the sheep of the blessed Peter, the prince of the Apostles, to whom and to whose successors he had handed over, through the same, the power of feeding, and the successors of the other Apostles and disciples, that is, of the Churches, should root out every tare, lest it infect the good seed. Therefore, it belongs to our office and to the office of the other prelates of the holy Church of God, caring for the salvation of souls and cleansing such a field, as is fitting, very often, to root out by pastoral zeal those things which you know to be contrary to salvation. Indeed, a reliable report, and one often pressed upon us, has reached our hearing from many people: that in Saxony, and in no other regions, certain detestable writings, commonly called the Laws or Mirror of the Saxons, and noted below, are found among some nobles and commoners, whose adherents of those parts, despising the canons and other Holy Scriptures, which are not observed in the ancient times, now long past, by good and civil people, with good morals put far away, still keep them even at present. By the observance of these, God is offended, justice and equity are scattered abroad to the neighbour's harm, canons and laws are despised. For judgment is grossly perverted, truth is assailed, things are done against good morals and the law of nature, ecclesiastical liberty is trampled underfoot, and, what is worse, apostolic power is denied and the truth of the Catholic faith is derogated. We, therefore, grieving over these things the more bitterly, because souls have for a long time been bound with tighter snares thereby, and so that we may meet with our affections such and so great evils and dangers, lest, by ignoring the aforesaid things, the souls of sinners be required at our hands by the Lord, have had these writings or laws, which they know of, carefully examined by some of our brothers, the holy Roman Church's Cardinals, and by certain masters and doctors of both laws. After a mature delay in this matter, we reprobate, condemn, and decree by the tenor of these present letters, as false, rash, iniquitous and unjust, and in some respects heretical, and therefore contrary to good morals and dangerous to souls, by the authority of the Apostolic office, and of the condition of our said brothers, that they be null and void and lack all force of validity; and furthermore that the processes and sentences, if by any chance any have been made under the pretext of these written laws, shall henceforth be wholly without effect. We command by Apostolic letters to the Charles Louis [the Elector Palatine?], that these writings and laws shall no longer be used, and that the lords of the lands, both ecclesiastical and secular, shall not permit their subjects to use them. Moreover, we will that those presuming to act to the contrary, of whatever pre-eminence, dignity, status or condition they be, even if they shine with Pontifical, or Imperial, or Royal, or any other dignity, shall incur the sentence of excommunication by the very fact. And so that this our reprobation, condemnation and annulment may irrefragably achieve so salutary an effect, we request and beg, by these present letters, all the temporal lords, both ecclesiastical and also secular, that by their constitutions and statutes they ordain and command in perpetuity, under heavier temporal penalties, that no one of their subjects henceforth use these reprobated writings, but the laws rejected, and that those acting against this be so punished that the detestable iniquity of those written laws be wholly rooted out from their lands. Let no one of mankind at all, therefore, be permitted to infringe this page of our condemnation, prohibition, constitution, command, will and request, or to contravene it with rash daring. If anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of the blessed Apostles Peter and Paul. Given at Avignon, on the sixth day before the Ides of April, in the third year of our pontificate.

units.la: Ad Idem.
units.tr: To the same effect.

units.la: Gregorius Episcopus seruus seruorum Dei charissimo in Christo filio Carolo Romanorum Imperatori, & semper Augusto salutem & apostolicam benedictionem: Fili charissime, tempus est & praeteritum, quod de erroribus & de execrabilibus quorundam scriptorum de ... am, quae leges seu speculum Saxonum appellantur, quibus nonnulli de partibus tuarum Imperii regni terrarum vel seu potius abuti dicebantur, per fidem dignas, & intelligentes personas summo formati, & petitum fuit a nobis, ad quos spectat de talibus prouidere, ut super eis ad salutem animarum prouisionem adhibere digharemur. Nos scripta ipsa mature vidimus, & per nonnullos tam fratres nostros sanctae Romanae Ecclesiae Cardinales, quam per alios in sacra Theologia solennes magistros ac virtuosque iuris Doctores examinari fecimus diligenter, & illa ex eis, quae falsa, temere ratione, ichismatica contra bonos mores existentia & periculosa nimium animabus fore reperimus, auctoritate apostolica reprobamus, condemnamus, & decernimus irrita & inania, & carere omni roboris firmitatis, prout ex nostris literis inde confectis, quarum tenorem praesentibus inclusum, quasi venerabilibus fratribus nostris Moguntinensi, Coloniensi, Bremensi, Magdeburgensi, Pragensi & Rigensi Archiepiscopis, eorumque suffraganeis dirigimus, videte poteritis plenius contineri.
units.tr: Gregory, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his dearly beloved son in Christ, Charles, Emperor of the Romans and ever Augustus, greeting and apostolic blessing. Dearest son, it is some time since it was reported to us, and our attention was drawn, that errors and detestable writings of certain men, called the laws or mirror of the Saxons, by which some people in parts of your empire and kingdom of lands were said to be misled, had been brought before trustworthy and discerning persons of high standing, and it was requested of us, to whom it belongs to provide for such matters, that we should take measures concerning them for the salvation of souls. We have examined these writings carefully, and have had them scrutinised diligently by some of our brothers, the Cardinals of the holy Roman Church, and by others who are learned masters in sacred theology and distinguished doctors of law. We have found that those among them which are false, rashly reasoned, schismatic, contrary to good morals and exceedingly dangerous to souls, we reprobate and condemn by apostolic authority, and we decree them void and null, and deprived of all force and firmness. You will be able to see this more fully from our letters drawn up on this matter, whose tenor, enclosed with these present letters, we send to our venerable brothers, the Archbishops of Mainz, Cologne, Bremen, Magdeburg, Prague and Riga, and to their suffragans.

units.la: QVATVORDECIM ARTICVLI ERRONEI IVDIS SAXONICI SEV THEVTONICI ET MAYDENBVRGENSIS, PER eundem Apostolicam condemnati, tanquam iuri naturali & diuino contrarii, quos etiam nos Alexander, Rex Poloniae, &c. Apostolico decreto nitentes reprobamus, condemnamus, nulliusque roboris & momenti decernimus perpetuo, ac per quoslibet iudices & subditos nostros, vbilibet in dominiis nostris constitutos, distinctius sub poenis nostris eosdem teneri inhibemus.
units.tr: FOURTEEN ERRONEOUS ARTICLES OF THE SAXON, OR TEUTONIC, AND MAGDEBURG LAW, condemned by the same apostolic authority as contrary to natural and divine law. We, too, Alexander, King of Poland, etc., relying on the apostolic decree, reprobate and condemn them, and decree them to be of no force or weight forever. We also forbid, under our penalties, that they be upheld in any more particular way by any judges and subjects of ours, wherever they are established in our dominions.

units.la: PRIMVS Articulus continet; Quod quicquid homo fecerit extra iudicium, quantumcunque hoc sit notorium, se liberare poterit per suum iuramentum, nec contra talem valet aliquod testimonium.
units.tr: The FIRST article contains: whatever a man has done outside judicial proceedings, however notorious it may be, he can free himself by his own oath, and no testimony is valid against such a person.

units.la: Secundus Articulus; Papa non potest, nec aliquo alius, Dominum Imperatorem excommunicare, postquam confessratus est, & vicius, nisi solum in tribus casibus, si dubium fit in fide, si repudiat uxorem suam legitimam, si destruat Ecclesiam.
units.tr: Second article: the Pope cannot, nor anyone else, excommunicate the Lord Emperor after he has been crowned and consecrated, except in only three cases: if there is doubt in the faith, if he repudiates his lawful wife, or if he destroys the Church.

units.la: Tertius Articulus; quod excommunicatio neminem debilitat in iure terrae seu feudi, nisi sequatur regularis proscriptio.
units.tr: Third article: excommunication does not deprive anyone of rights in the land or fief, unless it is followed by a formal outlawry.

units.la: Quartus Articulus; quod Papa non potest aliquo modo in condere vel statuere, per quod valeat in nostrum, hoc est, statutum terra vel feudi Saxonicum deteriorari.
units.tr: Fourth article: the Pope cannot in any way enact or establish anything by which the Saxon law, that is, the statute of our land or fief, could be made worse.

units.la: Quintus Articulus; Quod nulla sententia tam iusta dari potest in Saxonem coram Rege vel iudicio Regali, quam si Saxo talem sententiam reprehendit, tellans in manum suam dextram, & maiorem communitatem metiseptimus pu-art volens, contra septem alios pro dicta sententia, tunc vbi maior pars triumphauerit, talis sententiam obtinebit.
units.tr: Fifth article: no sentence can be given against a Saxon before the King or royal court so just that, if the Saxon rejects such a sentence, stretching out his right hand and, wishing to be the seventh man of a larger company against seven others, in support of the said sentence, then, where the greater part has prevailed, such a sentence shall be upheld.

units.la: Sextus Articulus; Quod si quis fuerit interfectus ipsius vel fratris pro quo consanguineus interfecti se praebeat ad duellum, talis per duellum reductus omne testimonium, ne talis mortuus sine duello potest vinci seu conuinci.
units.tr: Sixth article: if anyone has been killed, and the kinsman of the slain man, either himself or on behalf of a brother, offers himself for a duel, such a person, once brought to a duel, cannot be overcome or convicted without a duel, and this excludes all testimony.

units.la: Septimus Articulus; Quod si duo dicti in iudicio simul contrarias sententias, tunc quicunque talium habuerit maiorem, sequelam talis sententiam obtinebit.
units.tr: Seventh article: if two such men in a court pronounce contrary sentences at the same time, then whichever of them has the greater following shall obtain his sentence.

units.la: Octavus Articulus; Quod quicunque fuerit appellatus ad duellum secundum istius libri formam, talis non potest declinare duellum, nisi appellatus eum fuit thurus bene natus, quam appellatus.
units.tr: Eighth article: whoever has been summoned to a duel according to the form of this book cannot decline the duel, unless the one summoned was more nobly born than the one who summoned him.

units.la: Nonus Articulus; Quod quicunque perdat tus suum rationem furti vel spolii, talis accusatus secundo de furto vel spolio non potest se liberare iuramento suo, sed dilationem habet ad ferrum ignitum aut aquam bullientem, vel ad duellum: huius quidem articuli pars ultima, quae ad ferrum ignitum & caetera electionem concedat, est erronea.
units.tr: Ninth article: whoever loses his case for theft or robbery, if he is accused a second time of theft or robbery, cannot free himself by his oath, but is given a delay for the hot iron or boiling water, or for a duel. Indeed the last part of this article, which grants the choice of the hot iron and the rest, is erroneous.

units.la: Decimus Articulus; Quod quicunque cognouerit aliquam feminam, si postea ducat eam in matrimonium, nunquam pro lem legitimam generare.
units.tr: Tenth article: whoever has known a woman carnally, if he afterwards takes her in marriage, shall never beget lawful offspring by her.

units.la: Undecimus Articulus; Quicunque cognouerit publice uxorem alicuius viuente marito, si post mortem mariti illius ducat in uxorem, nunquam ex ea prolem legitimam generabit.
units.tr: Eleventh article: whoever has publicly known the wife of another man while her husband is living, if after the husband's death he takes her as his wife, shall never beget lawful offspring by her.

units.la: Duodecimus Articulus; Quod heres non tenetur de furto vel spolio perpetrato per illum, cui successit in hereditate, redere; quod erroneum est falsum in foro conscientiae.
units.tr: Twelfth article: an heir is not bound to make restitution for theft or robbery committed by the one whose inheritance he has taken up; this is false and erroneous in the court of conscience.

units.la: Tredecimus Articulus; Quod quicunque succinctus cum gladio, clipeum tenens non potest de ligno vel lapide pollicibus quantum ad altitudinem habentem supra dextrarium scandere, talis non potest cedere, dimittere, vel infeudare, vel exuere mobilia bona alicui dare, sic quod ipse custoditus sit, qui talia post mortem danda expectat. Ille Articulus est erroneus, quantum Eleemosynas, testamenta & alia pietatis opera prohibet.
units.tr: Thirteenth article: whoever, girt with a sword and holding a shield, cannot mount a horse from a log or stone of a height of a thumb's breadth, cannot yield, transfer, enfeoff, or give away movable goods to anyone, so that he himself is kept under guardianship, who awaits such gifts to be made after his death. This article is erroneous, in so far as it forbids alms, wills and other works of piety.

units.la: Quartusdecimus Articulus est; Quod nullus sine licentia suorum heredum sine iudicio bannito, quod Saxonis dicitur dare proprietatem suam vel suos homines. Et si talia daret alicui, heredes acquirent ipsa per iudicium dans illa mortuus effet, ipsi duo articuli sunt erronei, in quantum Eleemosynas & alia pietatis opera prohibent.
units.tr: Fourteenth article: no one, without the consent of his heirs, may give his property or his men without a judgment of outlawry, which is called Saxon; and if he should give such things to anyone, the heirs shall acquire them by the judgment, if the giver should die. These two articles are erroneous, in so far as they forbid alms and other works of piety.

units.la: Haec in quadam extravagante beati Gregorij Papae Noni ponuntur, & reprobata sunt pro eo, quod non continent contenti suppositas ad legem requisitas, sed magis militant contra pietatem & salutem animarum.
units.tr: These articles are set down in a certain extravagant decretal of blessed Pope Gregory IX, and have been rejected because they do not contain the provisions required by law, but rather militate against piety and the salvation of souls.

units.la: CONTINVATIO DECRETI REGII IN PRIVILEGIO COMMVNI.
units.tr: CONTINUATION OF THE ROYAL DECREE CONCERNING THE COMMON PRIVILEGE.

units.la: De uniuersis Regni nostri priuilegiis, etsi nos Alexander Rex dudum ad praefens Communia inferctris mus, habemus tamen & habemus numerosiora in publico Regni Thesauro ad communem tam Rempub. eorum nostrorum statum feliciter dirigendum & instituendum, ac tutelam pertinentia. Verum, ita praecipue pendimus, maioris efficacitas esse, idcirco per haec finem damus eius modi processui laboriqe n[?] fiat. Et nihilominus privilegia certas summorum pontificum bullas tam errores & nonnullas constitutionum leges non exorbitantes contra pietatem & salutem animarum militantes, quam fragilitatem humanae excessus corrigentes, per praefatum de Lasko Regni nostri Cancellarium scribi, sic etiam constitutionis iuris civilis, Saxonici Maydenburgensis Cancellarii ante proximum Privilegij communis meminit, quam vigilantissime de eorum Theutonicis sylvis libris per eum ipsum Cancellarium caesigatas, emendatas & novis rubricis distinctis titulatas, in eis infimis, eundem iuris Civilis constitutiones nusquam correctas & in suis sententiis integras, immo in toto earum tenore ... originalibus longe vagantes inuenimus. Postremo vero sumuntur doctissimi Raymundi Parshonopes, quae ... per nonnullos prudentes subditos nostros pro singulari eruditione, & suorum subditorum gubernaculis ... quod eorum practica communiter sit incerta Regni nostri loco ius Maydenburgense ac Theutonicum habentes a privato illorum usu sumentes ad communem vniuersorum subditorum nostrorum cognitionem eruditionem ... legauimus & tradidimus. Primum vero posuimus librum, qui a nonnullis titulatur Octonis Caesaris Provincialis & Feudalis iurium libros, qui diuorum Caroli & Conflantini Imperatorum constitutiones ... vt legentibus patebunt singulariter insertis & inserta.
units.tr: Concerning all the privileges of our Kingdom: although we, King Alexander, some time ago inserted the present common [privileges], we nevertheless have, and have in greater numbers, in the public treasury of the Kingdom, the matters pertaining to the protection and the happy direction and establishment of the common state of our Republic and of our subjects. But we weigh especially that such things be of greater efficacy, and therefore by these [words] we put an end to that kind of procedure and labour, so that it not be done. And nevertheless, the privileges, certain bulls of the supreme pontiffs, and some laws of the constitutions that do not exceed [their bounds], fighting against piety and the salvation of souls, as well as correcting the frailty of human excess, were written down by the aforesaid de Lasko, Chancellor of our Kingdom. So also he mentions the constitution of civil law of the Saxon Magdeburg Chancellor, before the next Common Privilege, which most carefully ... were corrected by that same Chancellor in their Teutonic books, emended and entitled with new distinct rubrics; in them the same constitutions of civil law are nowhere corrected and are not whole in their sentences, indeed in the whole tenor of them ... we found them wandering far from the originals. Finally, the most learned Raymund Parshonopes are taken up, which ... by some of our prudent subjects, for singular erudition and for the government of their subjects ... since their practice is commonly uncertain, having the Magdeburg and Teutonic law in place of the law of our Kingdom, taking [them] from the private use of those [books], we have bequeathed and handed down for the common knowledge and erudition of all our subjects. But first we have set down the book which is called by some the Books of the Provincial and Feudal Rights of Octo Caesar, which [contain] the constitutions of the divine emperors Charles and Constantine ... as will be clear to the readers, singly inserted and inserted.

units.la: IOHANNES DE LASKO REGNI POLONIAE CANCELLARIVS IN PRAEFATIONEM IN PRIVILEGIVM CONSTITVTIONVM REGNI POLONIAE, &c.
units.tr: John of Łasko, Chancellor of the Kingdom of Poland, in the Preface to the Privilege of the Constitutions of the Kingdom of Poland, etc.

units.la: LIQVAS etiam Leges externas in priuilegiis Apostolicis ordinariis Ecclesiasticis &Imperialibus, ad optimos tamen Chranoe mores scriptas, & nonnullas prouinciis editas, vt iunt Leges ciuiles siue iuris Maydemburgensis, etsi Imperiali Maiestate Ottonis Rom. Caesaris institutum fuerit, tamen quia illud Serenissimus olim Kazimirus M. ad vtilitatem & profectum regnicolarum Reges Poloniae accepit, repositum in thezauro Regni communi, vt de hoc priuilegium iuris supremi Caesari Cracouiensis perstringit. Cuius iuris ac Legum Ciuilium in oppidis & villis Regni Poloniae Ius Ciuile fit practica & obseruatio. Iccirco innata eiusdem Serenissimi Principis ac Domini, Domini Alexandri Regis gratiosissimi pietas, intelligens iura ipsa atque leges Reipub. quam communiter ad pietatem cuiuslibet iustitiae, vtiles & pernecessarias, decreuit eas ordine intrascripto colligere, &c.
units.tr: Furthermore, although the foreign laws contained in the ordinary Apostolic, Ecclesiastical and Imperial privileges, written in the best manner of Chranoe and some issued for provinces, as well as the so-called civil laws or the law of Magdeburg, were instituted by the Imperial Majesty of Otto, Roman Emperor, nevertheless, because the most serene Casimir the Great once took them up for the benefit and advancement of the inhabitants of the kingdom, and deposited them in the common treasury of the Kingdom, so that the privilege of supreme law of the Emperor of Kraków might be touched upon concerning this matter... The practice and observance of this law and of the civil laws in the towns and villages of the Kingdom of Poland is civil law. Therefore the innate piety of the same most serene Prince and Lord, Lord Alexander, most gracious King, understanding that these laws and rights of the Commonwealth, which are commonly useful and altogether necessary for the piety of every kind of justice, has decided to gather them together in the order written below, etc.
